Such "improved" American cocktails from the period are also distinguished by using European ingredients, particularly maraschino liqueur and/or absinthe.

name: Stone Wheel
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with cider.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄6 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄4 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
1⁄4 shot	Ginger syrup
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 1⁄2 shot	Dry cider
review: Herbal tequila, refreshing lime and mild ginger heat mellowed with creamy vanilla, all lengthened and flavoured with apple cider. An exceptionally good and interesting long drink.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in July 2021 at Lobby Bar at The London Edition Hotel in London, England. This cocktail was sold in aid of S.A.C.R.E.D., a charity that helps improve lives in the rural communities in Mexico.

name: Fresh Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Monkey Shoulder Fresh Monkey
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
4 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters (optional)
review: Scotch new make spirit replaces light rum in this Daiquiri riff which also benefits from a combination of lime and lemon juices.
history: Recipe by yours truly in July 2022.

name: Firecracker
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Crema de Mezcal
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄3 shot	Pimento dram/Allspice liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Agave syrup
review: Allspiced pineapple fruit with delicate caramel-like agave richness and grape fresh pisco spirituous spice.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Ivan Radulovic at Macao Trading Co. in New York City, USA.

name: 50:50 Margarita
garnish: Orange juice and salt rim, garnish with lime wedge
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
5⁄6 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
5⁄12 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
5⁄12 shot	Agave syrup
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
4 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters
review: I was tempted to also split the citrus juice to also bring lemon or even pink grapefruit juice into this cocktail but when I made the recipe above it was so tasty that I opted to leave well alone.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in February 2023 by Simon Day, a fellow Discerning Drinker, and shared via a comment on our Margarita on-the-rocks page. As Simon says, "Quite excellent." I added a split tequila base to Simon's recipe and slighted upped the volumes.
Margarita cocktail history

name: Mezcal Manzanilla Margarita
garnish: Rim glass with equal parts mix of Tajín, paprika and salt (moistened with either orange or lime juice).
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into pre-rimmed ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1 shot	Manzanilla sherry
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Agave syrup
6 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters
review: Manzanilla sherry contributes dry, delicate, minerally salty notes to this mezcal-forward aperitivo. If you don't have Difford's Margarita Bitters (shame on you!), then instead, this dry sherry-influenced Margarita benefits from a few drops of saline solution.
history: Adapted from a recipe, originally named the "50/50 Margarita" created circa 2020 by Natasha Bermúdez, Head Bartender at Llama San in New York City, USA.

name: Daiquiri Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
8 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Flavoursome and sweet 'n' sour with an almost creamy mouthfeel.
history: Created by yours truly in April 2023 at The Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Blood and Sand (Difford's recipe)
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
3⁄4 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky (optional)
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: The equal parts Blood and Sand (scotch, cherry brandy, sweet vermouth, and orange juice) formula from the 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book is the accepted classic Blood & Sand recipe but results in a cocktail that's a tad sweet for hardened whisky drinkers. This formula, with slightly increased Scotch and orange juice, is dryer and fresher. Those with a taste for Scotch and a slightly drier drink may also appreciate the additional spoon of Islay malt.
history:
Probably the best-known Scotch whisky-based cocktail, the Blood & Sand was created in 1922 and is named after Rudolph Valentino's Blood & Sand bullfighter movie which was released the same year.

Based on the 1909 Spanish novel Sangre y arena (Blood and Sand) by Vicente Blasco Ibáñez and the play by Thomas Cushing, the silent film was a box office hit. It tells the dramatic story of Juan Gallardo (Valentino), a poor village boy who grows up to become one of the greatest matadors in Spain. He marries his childhood sweetheart, the beautiful and virtuous Carmen, but once rich and famous, is seduced by a wealthy widow. They embark on a torrid affair, but feeling guilty he tries to end the affair. Furious at his rejection, his lover exposes their affair to his wife. Distracted and depressed, he becomes reckless in the arena and, somewhat predictably, is killed in a bullfight. However, in true Hollywood style, just moments before his death, he manages to reconcile with his wife, Carmen, who is naturally grief-stricken. The end.

Who was inspired by the film to make the cocktail is unknown, but it first appears in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book. The deep amber-red cherry brandy is said to represent blood and the orange juice, the sand of the arena.

name: East India No.2
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄6 shot	Pineapple sugar syrup
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: The bitters are crucial in balancing this after-dinner brandy and pineapple cocktail.
history:
An East India (No. 2) classically has pineapple syrup or pineapple juice, while an East India No. 1 instead calls for raspberry syrup. Pineapple syrup is first recorded in an East India in Robert Vermeire's 1922 Cocktails: How to Mix Them and is repeated in Frank Meier's 1936 The-Artistry of Mixing Drinks and it's Meier, who worked at Ritz Bar, Paris from 1921 to 1947, who is said to have introduced pineapple to this cocktail.

In his 1923 Harry of Ciros ABC-of-mixing-cocktails, Harry MacElhone also uses pineapple syrup in his East India, which, like the above, is otherwise pretty much the same as Harry Johnson's 1882 East India No. 1 - indeed, MacElhone credits the recipe to Johnson.

Harry Craddock's influential 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book stipulates pineapple juice in place of pineapple syrup, and this is repeated in other cocktail books which follow, including William James "Billy" Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Cocktail Book. I've honoured all the above by using both pineapple juice and syrup in my version of an East India.

name: Royal Bermuda Yacht Club
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A full-flavoured, tangy Daiquiri with faint clove spice.
history: Created at the eponymous club, established in Bermuda in 1844 and largely frequented by British Army Officers. Royal Bermuda Yacht Club cocktail first appears in Crosby Gaige's 1941 Cocktail Guide & Ladies' Companion as the favourite cocktail of Mary Mabon, then a writer for Harper's Bazaar fashion magazine.

name: Royal Mojito
preparation: Add the first 4 ingredients to the glass, and two-thirds fill with crushed ice. CHURN (stir) with bar spoon and then FILL glass with more crushed ice. TOP with sparkling wine and serve.
ingredients:
14 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: A mojito topped with a splash of fizz instead of soda water. There's posh!
history: Mojito cocktail history and other variations.

name: Twentieth Century
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
2⁄3 shot	Americano bianco
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review:
Strike a balance between spirituous strength, citrus acidity, herbal complexity, bitterness from the aromatised wine and rich chocolate, and this cocktail justifies its longevity and rightful place in our Cocktail Hall of Fame .

Sadly, Kina Lillet, one of the original ingredients, is no longer available and its modern-day replacement, Lillet Blanc, lacks the quinine bitterness and associated balancing sugar of the original Lillet.

This cocktail's original 2:1:1:1 specs, published in Billy Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Cocktail Book, translate as 40ml (1⅓oz) Gin, 20ml (⅔oz) white crème de cacao, 20ml (⅔oz) Kina Lillet, and 20ml (⅔oz) lemon juice. However, as Kina Lillet is no longer available, I offer my interpretation using Americano Bianco (see recipe above) as well as this version using a blend of aromatised wines:

40ml (1⅓oz) Dry gin
20ml (⅔oz) White crème de cacao
15ml (½oz) Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
2.5 (1/12) Kina aromatised wine
2.5 (1/12) Gomme syrup
20ml (⅔oz) Lemon juice
3 drop Saline solution (4:1)

Your choice of white cacao liqueur will significantly impact the finished cocktail, so much so that Joerg Meyer created Dutch Cacao liqueur specifically with this cocktail in mind. (It's also the liqueur I used to test both recipes.)
history: The recipe for a Twentieth Century was first published in William J. "Billy" Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Cocktail Book so this cocktail is thought to have originated in the 1930s. Thanks to Tarling's book, it's known to have been created by "C. A. Tuck."

name: Frank Sullivan Cocktail
garnish: Orange juice and sugar rim & lemon zest twist
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Blanc quinquina/kina (e.g. Mattei Cap Corse or Kina L'Aéro d'Or)
1⁄3 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: If you like Sidecars, then you'll love the Frank Sullivan. Just on the tart side with a touch of quinine bitterness which makes sipping through a sugar-crusted rim a delight.
history: Adapted from the Frank Sullivan Cocktail recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book. The same book also features two other cocktails with the exact same recipe: the Hoop La! Cocktail and Odd McIntyre Cocktail.

name: Rum Old Fashioned
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄3 shot	White overproof rum
1⁄4 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: The flavour of the overproof rum greatly adds to the character of this Old Fashioned. There are many rum Old Fashioned riffs but this is the recipe that made this cocktail both special and famous.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2009 by Gonçalo de Sousa Monteiro in Berlin, Germany.
See: Old-Fashioned cocktail history and variations

name: Succulent Blood
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1 shot	Blood orange juice
1⁄4 shot	Cinnamon syrup
1⁄6 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Mezcal and blood orange juice with sweet spice added with cinnamon syrup and clove-rich falernum.
history:
Created in February 2014 by yours truly after misreading the recipe for the Sangre Dulce cocktail by Regina Butler at Blackbird Bar in San Francisco. I used Velvet Falernum in place of Fernet Vallet but the resulting drink tasted good. Then, in May 2022, updated to add a splash of lime juice thanks to a comment by Ulysses Grand.

Mezcal is distilled from agave plants which are categorised 'Succulents' - plants which are thickened and fleshy, allowing them to retain water in arid climates - hence, coupled with blood orange juice, this cocktail's name.

name: Enrico Pallazzo
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into carbonator. CARBONATE and pour into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1⁄4 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
2 dash	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
review: A bittersweet Manhattan-style lightly sparkling cocktail.
history: Named after the fictional acclaimed Italian opera singer that Leslie Nielsen's Lt. Frank Drebin impersonates at the start of a baseball game in The Naked Gun film. Later in the movie, Drebin goes undercover on the pitch as the game's umpire. When he unmasks himself, a spectator shouts, "Hey, it's Enrico Pallazzo!" The crowd then jubilantly chant Pallazzo's name.

name: Brooklyn's Finest
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Light vermouth amaro (e.g. Cardamaro)
1⁄3 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A delicately spiced riff on the classic Brooklyn cocktail.
history: Created in 2016 by Seth Brammer at Filament in Dallas, Texas, USA.

name: Grappa Espresso Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Bepi Tosolini Grappa di Moscato
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1⁄12 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Grappa is made to go with espresso coffee and adds its distinctive flavour to this cocktail originally made with vodka.
history: See the story behind the Espresso Martini.

name: Carlton Banks
preparation: STIR first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. Top with chilled champagne.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
2 dash	Boker's bitters
1 1⁄2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Reminiscent of a classic champagne cocktail with cognac, champagne and zesty orange flavours dominating. It's surprising how little cherry brandy notes are evident in the finished drink given the recipe calls for a whole shot.
history: Created in 2016 by Seth Brammer at Filament, Dallas, Texas, USA. Seth's original recipe uses the same proportions shown here but with Paul Beau VS cognac,Luxardo Sangue Morlacco, Regan's Orange Bitters, Bakers bitters and Val de Mer Brut.

name: Bamboo (Joaquín Simó's recipe)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Dry, delicate. Aromatic and complex.
history:
Adapted from a recipe by Joaquín Simó, New York City, USA.
Bamboo Cocktail history

name: Banana Calling
garnish: None (but perhaps serve with banana chips)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄12 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Fino sherry
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: This short, sharp cocktail is best described as a Banana & Fino Sherry Gin Sour. The fino and banana notes are subtle, so subtle that it is not obviously a banana cocktail – although the name should serve as a clue.
history: Created August 2018 by Cameron Attfield at Dandelyan, London, England, this is a riff on the popular London Calling cocktail created by Chris Jepson in 2002.

name: Garden Sour
garnish: Rhubarb ribbon around inside of glass
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda water. and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Rhubarbe Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Celery bitters
review: Delicately smoky mezcal forms the backbone of this delicious, bittersweet refreshing cocktail.
history: Created in 2017 by Giffard USA to celebrate the launch of Giffard Rhubarbe liqueur in the USA.

name: Old Cuban Highball
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with sparkling wine.
ingredients:
7 fresh	Mint leaves
1 1⁄3 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 2⁄3 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
review: A tasty bite-sized alternative to a Mojito.
history: Adapted from a 2017 recipe discovered at Boilerman Bar, Hamburg, Germany.

name: Nuclear Banana Daiquiri
garnish: Banana slice & star anise on rim with mint sprig bouquet & straws
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with a 7oz-sized scoop of crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 shot	White overproof rum
2⁄3 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
2⁄3 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 fresh	Banana (preferably overripe)
review: To quote our friends at Hawksmoor, where we discovered this delicious and indulgent cocktail, "Our take on a drink that doesn't take itself too seriously by the late, great Gregor de Gruyther. We've just added half a banana and blitzed it. Silly, but tasty."
history: Adapted from a riff on the Nuclear Daiquiri discovered in 2013 at Hawksmoor, Spitalfields, London, England.

name: Christmas Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
4 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters
review: Fruit,y rum-laced, cleansing citrus with delicate Christmassy spice.
history: Created in October 2020 by yours truly at the Clocktower in Rye, Sussex.

name: Aged Grappa Espresso Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bepi Tosolini I Legni Rovere grappa
3⁄4 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1⁄6 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: You've almost certainly enjoyed the modern classic that is the Espresso Martini but switch the base spirit from vodka to aged grappa and you've an even more delightful drink. Grappa has a more intense flavour that does more than fortify, it stands up to espresso coffee's robust flavours to emerge triumphant in the finished cocktail.
history: See the story behind the Espresso Martini

name: Bronx (Difford's)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: The challenge, and indeed the opportunity, with the Bronx is to strike the perfect balance between the botanical flavours of the gin, vermouths and zesty fresh orange. Classically, where the vermouths are concerned that's between rosso (sweet) and dry vermouth. However, I find it better with bianco in place of dry vermouth. If you prefer a less orangy, more punchy Bronx, then you may prefer to cut the orange juice back to 15ml( ½oz).
history: An interpretation of the classic Bronx recipe using bianco vermouth in place of dry vermouth formulated by yours truly in January 2023.

name: Call Mexico
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Fino sherry
2⁄3 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Agave syrup
4 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters
review: Dry, sour, delicately smoky and delicious.
history: A reversed and volumized mezcal-based riff on a London Calling, I created this after making a Call London at the suggestion of Jennifer Spencer via a comment on our London Calling cocktail page.

name: Keoke Coffee
preparation: POUR first 3 ingredients into a pre-heated toddy glass. TOP with hot coffee and then FLOAT lightly whipped (and preferably heated) cream.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Overproof/bonded brandy (50-55% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
2 shot	Filter coffee (hot)
1 shot	Double cream / heavy cream
review: Sip brandy-laced chocolate coffee through a velvety layer of cream. For best results use a milk frother (e.g. Nespresso Aeroccino) to whip and heat your cream.
history:
The creation of Keoke Coffee is credited to George Bullington in 1967, then owner of Bully's North steakhouse in Del Mar, California, USA. Long since closed, Bully's was described as being a "time-tested little steakhouse with the feel of an English pub and racehorse-themed decor." The story goes, George created the new coffee drink late one night at the bar and named it at the suggestion of a colleague who shared the fact that "George" was "Keoki" in Hawaiian (pronounced kee-OH-kee) and was sometimes spelt with an "i".

The Keoke Coffee is enjoying a revival thanks to being resurrected and rejuvenated by influential bartender Jeffrey Morgenthaler in February 2023. Jeffrey's recipe calls for a bonded 50% alc./vol. American brandy and omits the coffee liqueur in the original recipe.

name: Sea O La
garnish: Skewered cherries & mist with 3 sprays of peated whisky from an atomiser
preparation: POUR all ingredients into a pre-chilled, ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄3 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
6 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
4 shot	Cola (e.g. Coca Cola or Pepsi Cola)
review: Oh my Lola, it's just like smoked cherry cola!
history: Created in March 2023 by yours truly at The Clocktower, Rye, England for Caisteal Chamuis. Inspired and named after Lola, the Kinks song written by Ray Davies, particularly the live "just like cherry cola" recording. "Sea" is also a reference to the salinity of the peaty Scotch whisky.

name: Californie Palace
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
6 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters
review: Vermouth-based and wonderfully aromatic with maraschino and monastic herbal complexity. Delicious as an aperitivo, digestive or nightcap.
history: Adapted from a recipe first published in Ted Saucier's 1951 Bottoms Up and takes its name from the the luxurious California Hotel in Cannes, France. Built in 1876, the hotel was renamed Californie Palace in 1925 when acquired by a new owner. During WWII, the hotel was requisitioned by the Germans and then by the Americans. After the war the building became a private residence.

name: Affinity
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 shot	Vermouth amaro - medium (e.g. Cocchi Vermouth Amaro)
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A spirituous aperitivo-style cocktail, or an after-dinner sipper, which can be made with numerous different sweet vermouths or indeed a vermouth amaro as per our recipe. Equal parts produces a balanced drink but those after a more spirituous cocktail may want to up the Scotch a tad. Also, consider using a single malt Scotch - your choice could dramatically change this drink's profile.
history: Fashionable in the 1920s, the Affinity first appears in The New York Sun on Monday 28th October 1907.

name: Aged Honey Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Rich, flavoursome honey replaces sugar syrup in this delicious Daiquiri. The fuller the honey, perhaps the bigger the rum.
history: Dedicated Daiquiri cocktail information, including variants, history and best recipes is available in our Daiquiri cocktail area.

name: Barbary Coast
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
3⁄4 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: Cream and a touch of rich chocolate smooth scotch whisky and gin without smothering them. This may be a creamy drink but it remains 'serious' and far from being a sweetie.
history: A Prohibition-era cocktail (1920-1933) of unknown origin, the term Barbary Coast referred to a nine-block area was cantered around Pacific Street (now Pacific Avenue) between Montgomery and Stockton Streets, which during the second half of the 19th and early 20th centuries was a red-light district popular with sailors.

name: Blood and Sand (Classic formula)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
3⁄4 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: One of the best classic Scotch cocktails, the Blood & Sand is said to be the Scotch whisky-based cocktail that whisky haters will like. Some may find this equal part's recipe a tad on the sweet side and if this is the case then our Blood & Sand recipe ups the Scotch notes with reduced sweet ingredients.
history: Created in 1922, this cocktail is named after Rudolph Valentino's Blood & Sand movie.

name: Honeysuckle Daiquiri
garnish: Float mint leaf (or honeysuckle flower pegged to the rim when in season)
preparation:
SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

If using honey rather than pre-diluted honey syrup, then STIR 3 spoons of runny honey with citrus juices in base of shaker until honey dissolves. Add the rum, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: A Daiquiri made with flavoursome honey in place of sugar, or a Bee's Knees with rum in place of gin. However you view this, it's damn tasty.
history: Adapted from a recipe in David A. Embury's 1948 Fine Art of Mixing Drinks.

name: Irish Coffee
garnish: Dust with freshly grated nutmeg and/or float 3 coffee beans
preparation:
1. Select a heat-proof glass and pre-warm by filling with very hot water and leave to stand.
2. Separately prepare cream by lightly warming and whipping or shaking (ideally use a milk frother to heat and whip your cream).
3. Empty the now warmed glass.
4. POUR whiskey, sugar syrup and hot coffee into pre-warmed glass and briefly stir.
5. FLOAT heated and aerated cream over the back of a warmed spoon.
ingredients:
1 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1⁄3 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
2 shot	Filter coffee (hot)
1 shot	Double cream / heavy cream
review:
Sometimes called a Gaelic Coffee and properly known by its Irish name 'Caife Gaelach', the Irish Coffee is traditionally served in a stemmed heatproof glass known as a toddy glass and comprises hot filter coffee, Irish whiskey and sugar (preferably brown sugar) topped with lightly whipped cream. The sweetened whiskey-laced coffee should be topped with a luxurious moustache inducing inch thick layer of cream to sip through.

To ensure your cream floats rather than sinks into the coffee, lightly whip, shake, or blend your cream before pouring over the bowl of a spoon. It also helps if the cream and the spoon are gently warmed. Sweetening the coffee with sugar also amplifies the drink's flavours and helps the cream float. I prefer to use demerara or muscovado sugar syrup.
history:
The history of alcoholic hot coffee drinks topped with cream dates back to the mid-19th Century with the best-known examples being the Fiaker and Pharisäer served in Viennese coffee houses. By the turn of the 20th-century variations called Kaisermelange, Maria Theresia and Biedermeier-Kaffee could also be found on menus at Viennese coffee houses. Combining coffee and spirits was also popular in 19th-century France where such drinks were called a Gloria.

The relatively modern Irish Coffee (originally named Sheridan's Gaelic Coffee) was created in late 1944 - early 1945 by Joe Sheridan, a chef turned bartender originally from Castlederg, County Tyrone while working at Foynes' Port. Sheridan added whiskey to hot coffee to warm a group of American passengers disembarking from a Pan Am flying boat at Foynes on a cold and wet winter evening. The passengers are said to have asked if they were being served Brazilian coffee to which Sheridan answered, "It's an Irish coffee".

Early planes lacked sufficient flying range to make Atlantic crossings and from 1937 onwards, flying boats were used to make the journey with Foynes' Port on the west coast of Ireland the last refuelling point for the Sikorsky S-42 and Boeing 314 planes. The first non-stop New York service started on 22 June 1942 and took 25 hours 40 minutes. The planes were comparatively primitive and the flight was arduous so the restorative boozy coffees were well received by cold weary travellers.

The demise of Foynes Port was sealed in 1942 with the opening of nearby Shannon Airport, built on bogland on the northern bank of the Estuary. Foynes Flying Boat Museum is all that remains of the old port but the tradition of serving Irish Coffees to transatlantic travellers continued at the new airport, and it is here, in 1947, that Stanton Delaplane, a travel writer for the San Francisco Chronicle, enjoyed his first Irish Coffee.

Back home in San Francisco, at one of his favourite local bars, the Buena Vista Café (purportedly late on 10th November 1952), Delaplane recounted travel stories to Jack Koepple, the bar owner, and the two of them set about trying to recreate Sheridan's Gaelic Coffee. Despite numerous attempts, the drink did not quite taste right and the cream would not float. This prompted Koepple to travel to Shannon Airport to see how the drink was made.

Upon returning back to San Francisco he continued his experimentation and also discussed the issues he was having floating the cream with the city's mayor, who was also a dairy owner. Koepple discovered that the cream whipped better and so floated when it was two days old rather than being fresh. After further experimentation, Koepple arrived at the method, recipe and 6oz heat-treated goblet still used at the Buena Vista today, where some 2,000 Irish Coffees are reputedly sold every day.

name: Manhattan (Sweet)
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo Maraschino Cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: I prefer my Manhattans served "Sweet", or "Perfect " at a push. The Manhattan is complex, challenging and moreish. Best of all, it's available in a style to suit every palate. For me, it's this recipe or the brilliantly simple High Ryeser Manhattan.
history: See Manhattan cocktail history

name: Polish Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Bison grass vodka
3⁄4 shot	Krupnik spiced honey liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review:
In Poland, Bison Grass vodka and apple juice are a classic combo, here also with an additional splash of Polish honey liqueur.

Adjust the quantity of apple juice and honey liqueur to suit your palate. We've played around with this recipe a lot over the years (it's one of our favs) and for us, equal parts (preferably with freshly pressed green apple juice) is perfectly balanced.
history: Created by Dick Bradsell, for his (Polish) father-in-law, Victor Sarge. Dick's original formula was equal parts and he specified sweet clear pasteurised apple juice in preference to cloudy fresh juice.

name: Tommy's Margarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Agave syrup
4 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters (optional)
review: The flavour of agave is king in this simple Margarita, made without the traditional orange liqueur.
history:
Created in circa 1987/88 by Julio Bermejo and named after his family's Mexican restaurant and bar in San Francisco, the self-proclaimed "premier tequila bar on earth".

Tomas and Elmy Bermejo set up Tommy's in 1965 and Julio is one of their five children, all of which are involved in what is truly a family business. Julio has become a legend in the drinks industry for the Tommy's Margarita, his knowledge of tequila and his evangelistic quest to promote good tequila.

Tommy's Margarita now appears on the menus of bars all around the world, and in turn, the small family restaurant where the drink was created has become something of a mecca for bartenders and barflies wanting to experience the now famous cocktail in the bar where it was invented. Their journey is well-rewarded. At Tommy's, the classic Margarita trio of tequila, triple sec and lime is enhanced by using agave syrup in place of the triple sec and hand-squeezed Persian limes. The drink is served accompanied by plentiful tortillas and salsa. The bar's shelves groan with one of the largest selections of 100% agave spirit in the USA, and drinkers are encouraged to sample how different tequilas taste in the bar's signature cocktail.

Margarita cocktail history and variations

name: Daiquiri No. 1 (Embury's 8:2:1 formula)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
4 drop	Bob's Vanilla bitters (optional)
review: Traditionally a Daiquiri should always be based on light rum but if I should feel like breaking with tradition and using aged rum, I find Embury's 8:2:1 formula works particularly well with a sweet aged rum. However, with drier aged rums, depending on the sourness of the limes, I up the sugar from 7.5ml (representing 1 part from the 8:2:1 formula) towards 10ml (as in the recipe above). So, depending on your rum and limes, 12:3:2 may be better than 8:2:1.
history:
According to David A. Embury's 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks the classic proportions of a daiquiri are: 8 parts (2 shots) white label Cuban rum, 2 parts (1/2 shot) lime juice and 1 part (1/4 shot) sugar syrup.
See: Daiquiri cocktail history

name: Anejo Manhattan
garnish: Salami wrapped Luxardo Maraschino cherry on a pick
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Añejo tequila
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Añejo tequila rather than American whiskey dominates this Manhattan riff.
history:
A much-adapted version of a recipe created by Ryan Magarian, Seattle, USA. Ryan's original recipe called for the addition of Licor 43 liqueur.
Manhattan cocktail history

name: Breakfast Club
preparation: STIR honey and marmalade with rum until dissolved. Add tea, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 barspoon	Orange marmalade
1 barspoon	Honey
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Lapsang Souchong tea (cold)
review: Slightly smoky with incredible depth of flavour. A perfectly balanced delight.
history: Recipe courtesy of DrinkBoy.com in 2008.

name: Daiquiri (on-the-rocks)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
4 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters (optional)
review: Light and refreshing. No one flavour predominates - sweet and sour are in harmony with the rum.
history: See: Daiquiri cocktail history

name: Ford Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: The Ford Cocktail is a Martini-style cocktail sweetened by both the use of old tom gin and Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur (not Bénédictine B&B) served 'wet' with a generous splash of dry vermouth. The orange bitters and zest are essential to the drink's success.
history: Adapted from a recipe in George J. Kappeler's 1895 Modern American Drinks – How to mix and Serve All Kinds of Cups and Drinks.

name: Negroni Spumante
preparation: POUR first 3 ingredients into ice-filled glass. TOP with spumante and lightly STIR.
ingredients:
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
Top up with	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
review: A Negroni lengthened with sparkling wine. Every Negroni drinker should try this variation
history: The history and other recipes for the Negroni cocktail can be found on our Negroni cocktail page.

name: Smokey Joe
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Akashi-Tai Daiginjo Genshu sake
1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄4 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1 shot	Sauternes dessert wine
review: Sake sweetened with Sauternes and flavoured with cognac and Islay whisky.
history: Created in August 2008 by yours truly at The Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Vesper Dry Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄6 shot	Blanc quinquina/kina (e.g. Mattei Cap Corse or Kina L'Aéro d'Or)
1⁄6 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
review:
Yes, yes, it's a spirituous drink without fruit juices that best shows its crystalline beauty when stirred rather than shaken. However, it's the one Martini that no bartender should lecture a drinker who prefers, like James Bond, their Martinis "shaken not stirred".

Vespers should be shaken! An action that aerates the cocktail, making it colder and more dilute than simply stirring. Surprisingly, shaking (rather than stirring) a Martini also amplifies the aromatised wine/vermouth. Shaking also gives the drink a slightly clouded appearance and can leave tiny shards of ice on the cocktail's surface. The clouded appearance impacts visual appeal, but the ice shards are easily removed using a fine strainer when pouring.
history: A cocktail with the name "Vesper" appears in William "Cocktail Bill" Boothby's posthumously published 1934 World's Drinks And How To Mix Them (see below), but is very different to the Dry Martini variation that, thanks to James Bond's "shaken, not stirred", is so famous and revered today.

name: Special Brew Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 1⁄4 shot	Byrrh Grand Quinquina
1 1⁄4 shot	Akashi-Tai Daiginjo Genshu sake
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Hopefully, it's 'Special'! 'Brew' refers to both the use of Byrrh (pronounced beer) and sake (which is brewed). To be a true 'Martini' a cocktail should have both gin and vermouth – we tried gin but vodka worked so much better. Byrrh doesn't qualify as a vermouth as while an aromatised wine it lacks wormwood – an omission made up for in this drink with a dash of absinthe.
history: Created 21st February 2015 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Blooded Knees Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. (If using honey rather than honey syrup then use 3 spoons of honey.)
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
3⁄4 shot	Blood orange juice
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Tart lemon and orange citrus notes are balanced by rich and flavoursome honey with the gin fortifying and adding botanical complexity.
history: Adapted from the classic Bee's Knees, made bloody using blood orange juice.

name: 20th Century Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1 shot	Americano bianco
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: When, as originally, this cocktail is made with Rutte Celery Gin, then celery notes are very obvious in the final cocktail - perhaps more so than in the gin itself. Whatever gin you favour, this contemporary version of the 20th Century is fabulously expressive of the gin with subtle rich chocolate notes.
history: Created in 2016 by Joerg Meyer at Le Lion Bar de Paris, Hamburg, Germany this is a riff on the classic Twentieth Century.

name: Velasco and Sand
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
3⁄4 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Mezcal adds a faintly smoky note to this riff on the classic Blood & Sand. The proportion of spirit and orange juice is slightly raised from the usual equal parts formula – the extra nip of mezcal adds an uplifting kick to the drink while more orange adds zippy freshness and lightens what can otherwise be a heavy cocktail.
history:
Sadly, I can't claim to have created this mezcal-based riff on the classic Blood & Sand – indeed, Adéle Robberstad of Cherry Heering hinted that a "Mezcal Blood & Sand" was a drink that should be on Difford's Guide. However, I felt it needed a fitting name. But why Velasco?

The Battle of Velasco, fought on 26th June 1832, was a prelude to the Texas Revolution and was the first military conflict between Mexico and the settlers in Texas. After two days of battle, the Texans prevailed after the Mexicans, who were running out of ammunition, surrendered. Not only was this a bloody Mexican battle, but the name seemed apt for a Blood & Sand due to Fort Velasco standing in what is now the city of Surfside Beach, approximately 140 meters/150 yards from the Brazos River. The stockade had inner and outer walls with the 1.8 meters/6 feet between the two filled with earth and sand. Sand also featured in this bloody battle as the Texans were forced to dig trenches in the sandy ground to protect themselves from the Mexicans' fire.

name: Red Grape Caipirinha
garnish: Stirrer (spoon, wooden lolly stick or stick cut from sugar cane)
preparation:
1. Cut lime in half (from pole to pole) and then slice one of the halves into eight 3-4mm thick half-moon shaped segments and drop into the base of a robust rocks glass.

2. Add 3 bar spoons caster sugar (or ½oz / 15ml sugar syrup 2:1) and MUDDLE.

3. Add grapes and MUDDLE some more.

4. When sure fruit juice is fully extracted and the sugar dissolved, transfer the muddled fruit and sugar into serving glass (preferably a 30cl / 10oz hi-ball glass).

5. POUR cachaça (stored in the freezer) into the rocks glass (used to muddle) and swirl to rinse glass before pouring cachaça into serving glass. STIR to ensure all ingredients are well mixed.

6. Crack (rather than crush) four to five large ice cubes and drop into serving glass. STIR before topping with more ice and serve with a stirrer (but no straws).
ingredients:
1⁄2 fresh	Lime (fresh) (chopped)
3 barspoon	Caster/ Superfine/Baker's special sugar (white)
8 fresh	Red grapes (seedless)
2 shot	Cachaça (from freezer)
history: For information on the history and other variations of the Caipirinha, please see our Caipirinha cocktail page.

name: Cherry Martinez
garnish: Orange zest twist & Luxardo maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Luxardo Sour Cherry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄12 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Spirit-led and very slightly sweet, this makes for a delicious late-night tipple.
history:
Created in 2018 by Gareth "G" Franklin, Luxardo Global Brand Ambassador.

Our Martinez cocktail page provides a detailed history of this style of drink.

name: Apple Jack (by Sasha Petraske)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Applejack brandy bottled-in-bond (50% alc./vol)
1⁄2 shot	Medium dry apple cider
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Sweet and sour with rich apple flavours and a brandy backbone.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created by the late Sasha Petraske at his famous Milk & Honey bar, New York City, USA. Sasha was inspired by the Apple Jack Rabbit in The Savoy Cocktail Book.

The Apple Jack features in Georgette Moger-Petraske's 2016 Sasha Petraske Regarding Cocktails.

name: Sloegroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
2⁄3 shot	Rosé/rosato vermouth
review: Lighter in colour and more mellow in flavour than a classic Negroni with sloe gin adding richness and subtle berry flavours.
history: A riff on the classic Negroni which emerged circa 2018.

name: Loaded Pistol
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strega liqueur
4 drop	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
review: Mezcal provides the firepower, tamed by sweet vermouth and rich herbal liqueur. A great late-night sipper.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Erick Castro at Polite Provisions, San Diego, USA. Erick's original recipe calls for a "grasshopper salt rim" made by blending ½ cup sea salt and 2 spoons dehydrated grasshoppers.

name: Gin Blossom Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Apricot (abricot) eau-de-vie
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Fragrant apricot eau-de-vie nestles alongside piney gin botanicals with faint sweetness from herbal vermouth.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2009 by Julie Reiner at the House Martini for the opening menu of her Clover Club bar in Brooklyn, New York City, USA.

name: Macunaíma
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass (no ice).
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cachaça
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄4 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
review: A cachaça sour given additional bittersweet herbal depth of flavour by a dash of fernet.
history:
Pronounced 'Ma-cu-nayma', this is adapted from a recipe created in 2014 by Arnaldo Hirai at his Boca de Ouro bar in São Paulo, Brazil. According to Arnaldo, his recipe started to take shape in 2014 and was almost called Caxirola, after the rattle created by Carlinhos Brown to be the official musical instrument for the World Cup in Brazil later that year.

Many considered the 2010 World Cup, held in South Africa, to be marred by the oppressively noisy Vuvuzela and the Caxirola was intended to be a quieter alternative. The instrument not only failed to catch on but was banned in football stadiums. Fortunately, rather than an unsuccessful Brazilian musical instrument, Arnaldo chose to name his cocktail after the 1928 novel by Brazilian writer Mário de Andrade, considered one of the founding texts of Brazilian modernism.

The Macunaíma quickly became the most popular cocktail at Arnaldo's Boca de Ouro bar, with 500 to 600 sold each month. The ingredients remained constant, but Arnaldo says that the proportions have evolved to make the cocktail less sweet. The recipe used at the bar:

50ml (1 2⁄3oz) Cachaça
20ml (2⁄3oz) Lime juice
20ml (2⁄3oz) Sugar syrup (1:1)
7ml (1⁄4) Fernet Branca

When I first translated this recipe from Portuguese, I mistook lime juice for lemon. But when corrected by a Brazilian friend, I retried this cocktail made with both citrus juices alongside each other and concluded that I much prefer the lemon. It's delicious with lime but even better with lemon. That said, I find limes in Brazil sweeter and more fragrant than those shipped to the UK, so my preference may differ if making this cocktail in Brazil.

I've also taken the liberty of swapping out 20ml of 1:1 sugar syrup for 15ml of 2:1 sugar. However, with 12.5ml of 2:1 sugar syrup and 2.5ml of 3:1 honey syrup, this cocktail is even more divine.

name: Warday's Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
review: Apple brandy with complex botanical influences from both gin and Chartreuse mellowed by botanically enriched fortified wine. If you like spirit-forward cocktails, then this Yale Fence on monastic steroids takes some beating.
history:
An exhumed classic recommended to us by Jason E. Clapham who says "the war of the name rhymes with bar, at one time as a slang word for working day.

This cocktail notably features in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Another Sunken Boat
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
3⁄4 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
1⁄2 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Far from being a wreck, this boat is worthy of re-floating, indeed cruising upon. Its displacement is perfectly balanced and it handles well. However, beware, it may sink you!
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2022 by Phil Ward at Long Island Bar in New York City, USA.

name: Not So Perfect Manhattan
garnish: Orange zest twist (expressed & discarded) and skewered Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Not so imperfect – indeed this is one of the most delicious Manhattans I've had the pleasure of drinking.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created by Frank Caiafa, bars manager of the celebrated Peacock Alley and La Chine restaurants at New York's The Waldorf Astoria Hotel from 2005 until its closure.
Manhattan cocktail history

name: Anchorage
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄2 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Fino sherry brilliantly tames and shapes this "slightly less intense Alaska Cocktail."
history: Created in 2017 by Sam Ross at his Attaboy bar in Manhattan, New York City. Adapted from a recipe in Sam Ross' own Bartender's Choice app.

name: Canchànchara
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: Your choice of honey and rum will greatly affect the flavour and, indeed, the success of the finished cocktail. More flavoursome honey demands a more robust rum, so best you're guided by what your local beekeeper supplies. Achieve the perfect balance between sweet honey and sour lime and this is a truly great cocktail.
history:
Known as the forerunner of the Daiquiri and drunk by Cuban revolutionaries fighting off the Spanish at the end of the nineteenth century, the Canchànchara is a simple mix of honey, citrus and rum (originally aguardiente de caña rather than rum).

Although there is some debate as to its origins, most historians favour the Ten Years War, 1868-78. Anistatia Miller and Jared Brown, in their book Cuban Cocktails, say it was certainly present at the height of the 1898 Spanish-American Civil War.

name: Añejo Old Fashioned
preparation: STIR one shot of tequila with three ice cubes (dry to the touch frozen ice, not wet ice) in a glass. Add agave syrup and bitters and two more ice cubes. STIR some more and add another two ice cubes and the rest of the tequila. STIR some more, and if you have room, add more ice.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Añejo tequila
1⁄4 shot	Agave syrup
8 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters
review: A hint of agave syrup sweetness and dilution from the stirred ice knocks back the spirit's fire while opening and releasing agave flavours. (If you don't have Margarita bitters then Angostura Aromatic Bitters will do.)
history: See Old-Fashioned cocktail history.

name: Dry Ice Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Canadian icewine
review: Icewine has fabulously rich concentrated flavours due to being made using grapes frozen on the vine in Canada's harsh and early winters. Thanks to icewine, despite the name, this Martini is slightly honeyed rather than being bone dry.
history:
Created in 2004 by yours truly in London, England.
Martini cocktail and its evolution

name: Addington
preparation: STIR first 2 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. TOP with a splash of chilled soda from a bottle/can or just the merest squirt from a chilled soda siphon.
ingredients:
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water (chilled)
review: Substituting vermouths (go high-end) dramatically alters the character of this light and easy aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Hi Falutin
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Swedish Punsch liqueur
1 shot	Byrrh Grand Quinquina
review: Forceful and Manhattan-like in style but with sweet delicate influences from France and Sweden.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2012 at Tooker Alley Bar, Brooklyn, USA by owner Del Pedro. To quote the menu, “This brash American Whippersnapper has been nattily clad by a classy old-world tailor. A puttin'-on-aits, high-steppin', diamond-pink-ed, cane-twirlin' dandy of a cocktail. Whippersnapper American Whiskey, Swedish Punsch, Byrrh and lemon essence."

name: Gen'tonique
preparation: Pour all ingredients into ice-filled glass and lightly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
5⁄12 shot	Byrrh Grand Quinquina
3 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: A refreshing apéritif with a mouth-salivating bitterness. Makes a Spritz seem bland.
history: Created in 2017 by Sullivan Doh at the Le Syndicat in Paris, France, who says of his drink, "I was looking for a nice bitter and refreshing drink with a hint of complexity. The gentian of the Suze marries perfectly with the wine and quinine flavour of the Byrrh."

name: Millionaire's Martini
preparation: STIR first 2 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. TOP with Champagne.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2⁄3 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Usually, we'd follow convention and honour the Martini name with a V-shaped glass. However, due to the splash of champagne, a coupe seems more in keeping for this dangerous champagne-charged riff on a Fifty-Fifty Dry Martini.
history: A Prohibition-era cocktail introduced to us by the chaps at London's Sipsmith Distillery.

name: Irish Boulevardier
preparation: STIR all ingredients in ice-filled serving glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: Blended Irish whiskey replaces richer bourbon in this mellow yet dry riff on the classic Boulevardier.

name: Three Gulps Martini
garnish: Gorgonzola (or Roquefort) cheese stuffed large olive (well chilled)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
5⁄12 shot	Ambrato/ambre/amber vermouth
1⁄12 shot	Fino sherry
review: This delicious four to one ratio martini with both vermouth and sherry has a tasty treat to savour with the last gulp.
history: A volumized adaption of the delicious One Sip Martini at Tayēr + Elementary, London, England.

name: Old Gal
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
review: This Negroni-style cocktail is a riff on the Old Pal with bianco vermouth, which has a more mellowing effect on the whiskey than the dry vermouth traditionally used in the Old Pal.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Phil Ward at Long Island Bar, Brooklyn, New York City, USA.

name: Toffee Negroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1 shot	Amontillado sherry
1 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
review: There's no toffee in this "Toffee Negroni" in the same way there's no coffee in the "Coffee Cocktail" yet both drinks are aptly named and delicious.

name: Queen's Jubilee Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
review: Classically a three-equal parts Perfect Martini is called the Queen. My Jubilee rendition of a Queen Martini uses Dubonnet Red (said to be one of the Queen's favourite tipples) in place of sweet vermouth. It later transpired that great minds think alike - my recipe is identical to Jacques Straub's Coronation Cocktail, only the choice of garnish differs.
history: Created in March 2022 by yours truly in honour of Queen Elizabeth II's Platinum Jubilee.

name: Smoky Cokey
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
4 drop	Bob's Abbotts bitters
3 1⁄2 shot	Cola (e.g. Coca Cola or Pepsi Cola)
review: Just as it says on the tin – a smoky malt and cola. This simple but delicious drink perhaps doesn't need bitters or even a twist but it's better with these subtle embellishments.
history:
Jack & Coke is a famous combo but until the Smoky Cokey, Scotch whisky was restricted to soda water or perhaps ginger ale. So for his 2014 book, Whisky: The Manual, Dave Broom set out to discover the best mixer for various Scotch whiskies, trying everything from soda water to green tea. His discovery that Lagavulin is delicious with cola is the origin of the Smoky Cokey.

Dave's discovery was picked up by Colin Dunn, Diageo's whisky ambassador who served 35ml of Lagavulin 16 Year Old in a Martini glasses topped with almost flat cola at the 2000 Feis Ile (Islay whisky festival). Collin presented them on a silver tray to his guests on Lagavulin pier.

I remember Collin talking about what he'd by then christened the "Smoky Cokey" at a Diageo World Class event, circa 2016. Dave Broom discovered this delicious combination of whisky and cola but it is Colin Dunn who made the Smoky Cokey a contemporary classic.

name: Beatnik
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Averna Amaro
3⁄4 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Tawny port
review: This whiskey-laced, bittersweet red wine-like, three-ingredient cocktail is best appreciated as an after-dinner digestive or late-night refresher.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Duggan McDonnell in San Francisco, USA.

name: Beer on-the-rocks
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass and stir.
ingredients:
2 shot	Byrrh Grand Quinquina
2 shot	British bitter ale
review: I love a good beer and I love Byrrh (also pronounced 'beer') – a marriage made in Bermondsey. Best served as an apéritif cocktail.
history: Created by yours truly on 14th March 2015 at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Highball (Generic Name)
garnish: Orange, lime or lemon slice (as appropriate to the spirit or the carbonate)
preparation: POUR spirit into ice-filled glass and TOP with a carbonated soft drink (ginger ale, soda or tonic water).
ingredients:
2 shot	Brandy, whisk(e)y, gin, rum etc.
Top up with	Ginger ale, soda, tonic water or other carbonated mixer
review: Simple, but simplicity can be beautiful.
history: Information on Highball cocktails, their history and tips on the perfect serve can be found on our page.

name: New Orleans Gin Fizz
preparation:
1. Vigorously SHAKE first seven ingredients with ice and pour back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass (no ice in glass). TOP with soda from siphon.

ALTERNATIVELY, 2. Flash BLEND first seven ingredients without ice (to emulsify mix). Then pour contents of blender into shaker and SHAKE with ice. Strain into chilled glass (no ice in glass) and TOP with soda from siphon.
ingredients:
2 1⁄4 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix) (2 sugar to 1 water)
1⁄6 shot	Orange blossom water / Orange flower water
1 shot	Egg white
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
Top up with	Soda from siphon
review: The full flavour of Old Tom gin adds an extra dimension to this classic Gin Fizz. Indeed, it is probably the original Gin Fizz.
history: Said to be the original name and recipe of the Ramos Gin Fizz, created in 1888 by Henry C. Ramos at the Imperial Cabinet Saloon on the corner of Gravier and Carondelet Streets in New Orleans. Today, a New Orleans Gin Fizz is made with Old Tom gin while a Ramos Gin Fizz is made with London Dry gin. While today's Ramos Gin Fizz always has added rose water and sometimes vanilla essence, the New Orleans Gin Fizz usually relies on the use of Old Tom gin for its flavour nuances.

name: Martinez (with Old Tom gin)
garnish: Orange zest twist expressed & discarded. Adorn with skewered Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Use an authentic-tasting distilled old tom gin that's balanced rather than overly sweet, and you'll have a fabulous cocktail.
history: See Martinez cocktail history

name: Pina Colada (Difford's recipe)
garnish: Parasol, pineapple wedge & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with half scoop crushed ice and serve with paper straws.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Cachaça
3 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
3⁄4 shot	Cream of coconut (e.g. Coco Lopez, Re'al etc.)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A splash of cachaça adds some Latin funk, lime adds a citrusy bite while a splash of fresh cream makes this Piña Colada creamy white.
history: Piña Colada history

name: Improved Improved Pendennis Club Cocktail
garnish: Lime slice or wedge (or apricot) on rim
preparation: SHAKE first 6 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with sparkling wine.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Apricot (abricot) eau-de-vie
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
1 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Dry sparkling wine dilutes and adds pleasing biscuity notes to this apricot gin sour.
history: Adapted from a riff on Toby Cecchini's Improved Pendennis Club Cocktail created in 2022 by Phil Ward, fellow bartender at the Long Island Bar in Brooklyn, New York City.

name: Satan's Whiskers (Straight)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Dry and citrusy with underlying piney gin and herbal complexity.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book. A variation on the classic Bronx.

name: Carta Switchel
garnish: Mint sprig bouquet & grapefruit zest twist
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Bacardi Gold rum
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄6 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Apple cider vinegar
review: Complex and very refreshing. Rum is the predominant flavour but is brilliantly accentuated with grapefruit, fernet and vinegar.
history: Adapted from the British Bacardí Legacy 2016 winning cocktail created by Iain Griffiths at Dandelyan, London> Originally based on Bacardí Carta Blanca rum and Bacardí Carta Oro .

name: Haiti Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredient with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Ferro China Baliva
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Rubino vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Navy rum (54.5% alc./vol.)
3 drop	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: This vintage aperitivo is lightly bitter and wonderfully complex with distinctive ferro china, vermouth and Demerara rum favours.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Elveio Grassi's 1936 book Mille Misture.

name: Winter
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Jamaican aged blended rum with funk
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄6 shot	Ginger liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Pimento dram/Allspice liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: This vintage cocktail was recommended to us by Jason E. Clapham who aptly describes it as "a Jamaican daiquiri with Christmas spices."
history: The Winter Cocktail appears in Albert Stevens Crockett's 1935 Old Waldorf Astoria Bar Book.

name: Christmas Negroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk or block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Becherovka liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
1⁄12 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
review: A classic Negroni turned festive with added Christmassy flavours. A proper Christmas cracker!
history:
Adapted from a recipe shared with us on Christmas Day 2021 by Andreas Beil who, on our Negroni page, told us, "I would like to share a variety replacing half (or even the full amount) of Campari with Becherovka liqueur. It makes a great sipper for winter times with spicy cloves and cinnamon. To be honest, I came up with it on Christmas eve 2020 when I ran out of Campari and was looking for a bitter replacement. Because of that true story and the gingerbread taste, I suggest calling it a Christmas Negroni. Cheers and Merry Christmas to all discerning drinkers."

To amplify fruity festive spice, I couldn't resist adding sloe gin and falernum. After all, Christmas is a time for overindulgence!

name: Crosstree
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	White overproof rum
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
5⁄6 shot	Pineapple juice
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Vanilla sugar
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Like a rum-laced pineapple cream soda served with a wedge of lime.
history: Adapted from a recipe by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England. Jason originally made this with frozen cubes of pineapple and lime juice, in a blender.

name: Gem
garnish: Float dehydrated lemon slice wheel & dust with freshly grated cinnamon
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Pineapple sugar syrup
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
4 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters
review: Pineapple shines in this cognac-influenced Daiquiri. Best when made with an aged Jamaican blended rum to impart a touch of funk.
history: Adapted from a recipe in William Schmidt's 1892 The Flowing Bowl: What and When to Drink.

name: Martinique Fizz
preparation: STIR lemon juice and sugar in base of shaker until all the sugar is dissolved. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda water.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 barspoon	Powdered sugar (white sugar ground in mortar and pestle)
1 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
2⁄3 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Rhum J.M. Terroir Volcanique
1 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Select the right glass [a "highball glass" means no larger than 10oz], appropriate and delicious rums, and take time to properly dissolve your powdered sugar, and you've a banging "short cocktail served long."
history: An adaptation of a 1930s cocktail from New York City's Hotel Martinique.

name: Old Fashioned Cocktail (Difford's recipe)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄3 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
8 drop	Bob's Abbotts bitters
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review:
Achieving balance, ideal dilution and a good chill are essential to the enjoyment of this spirituous sublime classic.

Pre-batched bottled version serves 7 people:
315ml (10.5oz) Bourbon
210ml (7oz) Rye
75ml (2½oz) Brown sugar syrup
135ml (4.5oz) Water
48 drops Abbots bitters
18 drops Saline solution
Measure ingredients into a 75cl bottle, seal, label, turn bottle a few times to mix and place in refrigerator. Ideally, move into a freezer for 30 minutes prior to serving.
history: Old-Fashioned Whiskey Cocktail history.

name: San Francisco (Café Royal)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Fruity, aromatic and complex. This is one of my favourite sloe gin cocktails, made all the more appealing by its bijou serve.
history: First published in William James "Billy" Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Bar Book.

name: Punch (Generic Name)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Freshly squeezed lemon or lime juice
1 1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 1⁄4 shot	Brandy, whisk(e)y, gin, rum etc.
3 shot	Fruit juice or water
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Two traditional punches remain on today's cocktail lists, the 'Rum Punch' and the 'Hot Whisky Punch', now better known as the 'Hot Toddy'. Also bear in mind that the Gin Punch probably led to the creation of the Collins.
history:
Long before the Martini, the V-shaped glass and the cocktail shaker, the drink of choice at society gatherings was punch and the punch bowl was the centre of activity at every party.

Our Punch page details the history of Punch.

name: Barney Barnato Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Blanc quinquina/kina (e.g. Mattei Cap Corse or Kina L'Aéro d'Or)
3⁄4 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄12 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Dry, with bittersweet undertones, and aromatic. I've tried this recipe with modern-day Caperitif but prefer the above blend of two apéritif wines in its place.
history:
Adapted from Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book which calls for a South African aromatised wine called Caperitif.

This cocktail is named after Barney Barnato, who was born Barnett Isaacs in 1852 in the Whitechapel slum of London and traded on his Jewish-Cockney wit and humour. With only a box of cigars to his name, in 1873 Barney fled poverty to join his brother in the South African diamond rush and changed his name. He formed the Barnato Diamond Mining Company and within ten years he had become a millionaire. He and his brother were eventually forced to sell out to Cecil John Rhodes for $5,338,650, then the single largest cheque that had been written. The fortune was little compensation for being beaten in the battle to control the Cape diamond mines - Rhodes went on to form the now mighty De Beers.

After a brief spell in South African politics Barnato died in 1897 when he was lost overboard near the island of Madeira, whilst on a passage home to England. It is still questioned as to whether he jumped, fell or was pushed. His body was recovered but the mysterious circumstances of his death were never resolved. He is buried at Willesden Jewish Cemetery, London.

His vast fortune was divided between his family, including his sister Sarah and her husband Abraham Rantzen, great-grandparents of English TV presenter Esther Rantzen. Another beneficiary was his son, Woolf Barnato, who used part of this inheritance to become one of the so-called Bentley Boys racing drivers in the 1920s.

name: General Harrison's Nogg
preparation:
BEWARE, shaking with fizzy ingredients such as cider tends to be explosive. Hence, use a still/less fizzy cider and hold both ends of your shaker firmly. (If you have to hand, use a specially designed 'fizz' shaker such as Perlini, which is designed to be carbonated).

SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass (without ice). Be sure to shake well to completely emulsify the egg.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
2 shot	Dry cider
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Pimento bitters
1 fresh	Egg (white & yolk)
review: A whole raw egg contributes body to this filling, flavoursome, wintry, delicate cocktail. The retained CO2 fizz of the cider adds essential body and balancing acidity but demands the use of a specialised shaker.
history:
We were sent this recipe by Dale DeGroff in December 2012 who said: "A personal favourite, adapted from a recipe from Jerry Thomas' 1862 How to Mix Drinks: a totally different take on eggnog – made as a single-serve drink it includes a raw egg, so you need to shake the hell out of it."

This cocktail is named after General William Henry Harrison, the American president to hold office for the shortest period. He was elected 4th March 1841 and died a month to the day later of pneumonia. Harrison was known for his drinking and cider was one of his preferred tipples. It is said that this eggnog was his favourite drink.

name: Haberdasher
garnish: Dust with cocoa & garnish with a mint leaf
preparation:
1. STIR first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
2. SHAKE Chartreuse and cream with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and LAYER by carefully pouring over surface of drink.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
1⁄4 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: Chocolaty bourbon with a freshening herbal blast of Fernet Branca, smoothed by sipping through a Chartreuse cream head. Like meeting the devil hidden beneath a thick white velvet blanket, this is the ultimate after-dinner cocktail.
history: Discovered in January 2013 at Pouring Ribbons, New York City, USA.

name: Brooklyn (Grohusko's original)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Amer Picon
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water
review: Despite the generous dose of Italian 'sweet' vermouth, rye whiskey shines in this harmonious Sweet Manhattan-like dry cocktail.
history: Brooklyn cocktail history

name: Te Anaka
garnish: Sea salt and lemon spritz with a dehydrated lemon wheel
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
1 shot	Honey water (1:1)
1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
