preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: After the Whisky Sour, this is the most requested sour. Try it and you'll see why - but don't omit the egg white.

name: Army & Navy
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water) (optional)
review: Almond and lemon flavoured gin. Subtle, citrus and, despite generous orgeat, fairly dry.
history:
This cocktail first appears in David A. Embury's 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks so establishing a 'made before' date. Little else is known but based upon its name, folk suggest it originated at The Army and Navy Club in Washington, D.C.. The club's lounge is also said to be "where the famous Daiquiri cocktail was introduced to the United States."

Thanks to Embury, we know the original recipe comprised a 2:1:1 formula, but the lawyer-turned-cocktail writer opts for an 8:2:1 formula, describing the original formulation as "horrible". I've ended up with an 8:3:2 formula in the quest for balance and deliciousness.

name: Florida Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
review: This classic blend of rum, lime and sugar, but with a hint of freshly squeezed grapefruit juice and maraschino. A user-friendly version of a Hemingway Special.
history: The shaken version of the Daiquiri No.1 refined and made famous Constantino Ribalaigua Vert at El Florida bar (later renamed El Floridita) in Havana, Cuba.

name: GE Blonde
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 3⁄4 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 1⁄4 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
1 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: This delicate drink demands freshly pressed apple juice and flavoursome Scotch with subtle peat.
history: A combined effort by the staff of London's GE Club in January 2002, this was named by Linda, a waitress at the club who happens to be blonde. She claimed the name was inspired by the cocktail's straw colour.

name: Gin Sour
garnish: Lemon slice & Luxardo Maraschino cherry on stick (sail)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: This 4:2:8 formula is a tad sourer than the classic sour proportions of 3:4:8: three-quarter part of the sour ingredient (lemon juice), one part of the sweet ingredient (sugar syrup) and two parts of the strong ingredient (gin). However, dependent on your lemons, this should be perfectly balanced, or even a tad on the sweet side. Hit the right balance and this is a delicious cocktail.

name: Japanese Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients (inc. 2 slivers of lemon peel in stirring glass) with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (reduce if wet ice)
3 dash	Boker's bitters
2 twist	Lemon peel
review: Lightly sweetened and diluted cognac, flavoured with almond and a hint of spice.
history: Adapted from a recipe first published in Jerry "The Professor" Thomas' 1862 Bartender's Guide. This is one of the few cocktails in the book which is believed to be his own creation.

name: Major Bailey #1
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE (only to bruise) mint with gin in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into glass half filled with crushed ice. CHURN (stir) drink with ice using a barspoon. Top the glass to the brim with more crushed ice and churn again. Serve with straws.
ingredients:
12 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: As Victor says of this gin based Julep, "This is a hell of a drink."
history: Adapted from a recipe in the 1947 Trader Vic's Bartender Guide by Victor Bergeron.

name: Major Bailey #2
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with 6oz scoop of crushed ice and serve with straws.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Made well this is a long, fruity, brilliant frozen Daquiri.
history: Adapted from a drink created by Victor Bergeron.

name: Menehune Juice
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. Serve with straws.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Slightly sweet and strong. According to Vic, "One sip and you may see a Menehune."
history: Adapted from a recipe in Victor Bergeron's 1947-72 Trader Vic's Bartender's Guide.

name: Milly Martini
garnish: Pineapple wedge on rim &/or float basil leaf boat
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE basil (just to bruise) in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
6 fresh	Basil leaves
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Gin and pineapple with a pleasing hint of basil.
history: Created in 2003 by Shelim Islam at the GE Club in London, England.

name: Oh Gosh!
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: A subtley orange twist on a classic Daiquiri.
history: Created by Tony Conigliaro in 2001 at Isola, London, England. A customer requested a Daiquiri with a difference - when this was served he took one sip and exclaimed "Oh Gosh!".

name: Opal
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 1⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄24 shot	Orange blossom water / Orange flower water
review: Fresh, fragrant flavours of zesty orange and gin with a subtle floral note.
history: Thought to have originated in the 1920s, the Opal notably appears in in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Pineapple Mojito
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE mint (just to bruise) in glass. POUR other ingredients into glass and half fill with crushed ice. CHURN (stir) with barspoon. Fill glass with more crushed ice, churn and serve with straws.
ingredients:
12 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
3⁄4 shot	Licor 43 Original liqueur
2 shot	Pineapple juice
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A fruity, vanilla-ed twist on the classic Mojito.
history:
Discovered in 2003 at Apartment 195, London, England.

Mojito Cocktail hostory.

name: Pinky Pincher
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
review: Fruity, sweetened bourbon. What's not to like.
history: Adapted from a drink created by Victor J. Bergeron (Trader Vic) and published in his 1972 Trader Vic's Bartender's Guide Revised.

name: Sidekick
garnish: Quarter orange wheel slice on the rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Rich ripe pear (actually, there's no pear in this cocktail) and orange with a stabilising and cleansing hint of sour lime.
history: Adapted from a drink discovered in 2003 at Temple Bar in New York City, USA.

name: Whiskey Collins
garnish: Orange slice & Luxardo Maraschino cherry on stick (sail)
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda water and briefly stir.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 1⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A whiskey-based twist on the classic Tom Collins .
history: A classic Collins variation.

name: Wink
preparation: POUR absinthe into ice-filled glass. TOP with chilled water and set to one side. Separately, SHAKE other ingredients with ice. DISCARD contents of glass (absinthe, water and ice) and strain drink into empty absinthe-coated glass.
ingredients:
1⁄3 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Reminiscent of a Sazerac but with gin and triple sec. Delicate, remarkably fruity and very sippable.
history: Created in 2002 by Tony Conigliaro at The Lonsdale, London, England.

name: Gin Punch No. 1
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and stain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 2⁄3 shot	Chilled water
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Light and refreshing, akin to alcoholic real lemonade (not fizzy.
history: This is a version of the cocktail for which Limmer's Hotel in London was most famed: a Captain Gronow recalled it in his 1860s memoirs as one of the top, if filthy and seedy, sporting hangouts of 1814, thanks in part to its 'famous gin-punch'. A bartender named John Collins worked there later in the 19th century, and was famous enough to inspire a limerick. Hence, many believe he created the Collins, which is similar to gin punch.

name: Mint & Honey Daiquiri
preparation: STIR honey and rum in base of shaker until honey dissolves. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 barspoon	Honey
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
3 fresh	Mint leaves
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: A fresh-breath-tastic riff on the classic Daiquiri.
history: Created in 2006 by yours truly (Simon Difford).

name: Colony
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix) (optional)
4 drop	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
review: Grapefruit and maraschino balance each other in this gin-based classic.
history: Created during the Prohibition period at New York's Colony speakeasy, possibly by bartender Marco Hattem. The Colony attracted an upmarket clientele, including the Vanderbilts and Windsors. The liquor was kept in an elevator which would be sent to either the attic or the basement if federal agents raided.

name: Wild Blossom
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Aptly named - it is indeed blossom-like with subtle floral elderflower, yet also balanced with assertive gin notes.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2007 by James Scarito at BLT Market in New York City, USA.

name: Periscope
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Fabulously light, almost creamy, and floral.
history: Created by Matt Gee at Milk & Honey in New York City, USA.

name: Wisecrack Fizz
preparation: SHAKE first four ingredients with ice and strain into an ice-filled glass. TOP with soda and serve with straws.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Light, balanced and refreshing. The pisco character shines through.
history: Created in 2007 by Matt Gee at Milk & Honey, New York City, USA.

name: Greyhound's Tooth
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
8 drop	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
review: Fresh grapefruit flavours form the backbone of this summer-fresh cocktail.
history: Created in 2010 by Brandon Clements, San Francisco, USA.

name: Lady's Sidecar
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix) (optional)
review: The addition of orange juice and an orange zest twist supposedly gives this otherwise classic Sidecar a feminine twist. Classically, this cocktail does not contain sugar syrup, so it is a touch sourer. Hence, if you have a dry palate, omit the sugar, and if you have a sweet palate, consider increasing the sugar syrup to 5ml (1/6oz).
history: Sidecar cocktail history

name: Ruby Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄3 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A well-balanced, almond-influenced Daiquiri.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2008 by Wrigley "Oz" Osbourne at Goldbrick House in Bristol, England.

name: Gennaro's Sidecar
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: My version of the established Jamie's Italian Gennaro's Sidecar is a tad boozier than the original, but retains the balance between sweet limoncello liqueur and tart lemon juice.
history:
Adapted from a popular drink on the menu of Jamie's Italian restaurant and bar chain.
See: Sidecar cocktail history

name: Club Cocktail (Difford's recipe)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄6 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
5⁄12 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Pineapple juice
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Cognac and pisco brandies with maraschino and pineapple adding fruity tropical freshness and a foamy head.
history:
I merely added a splash of pisco to the classic Club Cocktail which first appeared in W.C. Whitfield's 1939 Just Cocktails' book to arrive that this delicious recipe:
60 ml Cognac
7.5 ml Pisco
15 ml Maraschino liqueur
22.5 ml Pineapple juice
2 dash Peychaud's/Creole-style bitters
While delicious, this recipe is boozy so in June 2020 I rained this back to the recipe above.

name: Cold Whisky Punch
preparation: SPRAY lemon zest twists into shaker and drop in. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 slice	Lemon peel
2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 1⁄2 shot	Chilled water
review: A balanced – not sweet, nor sour or strong – refreshing short whisky cocktail.
history: The godfather of bartending, Jerry Thomas, offered both a hot and cold version of his Scotch Whisky Punch in his 1862 Bartender's Guide and it is in the cold form that the drink has survived. Modernity dictated that we streamline the recipe and ingredients which originally called for boiling water and an extended chilling period.

name: London Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
2 1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Our thanks to Brent Evans for pointing us towards this tasty cocktail which he describes as "Scotch whisky blended with fresh oranges, lemons and a whisper of almond." We tried with egg white, usually our preference in a sour, but prefer this one without the resulting foam. We also found upping the orange juice and serving long preferable.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Trader Vic himself for the opening of the Hyde Park Hilton, London branch of his eponymous restaurant chain in 1963. This cocktail features in his 1972 Trader Vic's Bartender's Guide.

name: MGM Grand
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Nail the perfect balance and this cognac-based cocktail sings on the palate with cognac, richly subtle cherry, and zesty lemon acidity.
history:
A riff on the classic Casino Cocktail, hence the name referencing one of the most famous Las Vegas resort casinos.

Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Andrew Loudon at Satan's Whiskers in London, England.

name: Dama Blanca
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Agave syrup
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: This tequila (in place of gin) based riff on a White Lady is basically a straight-up Margarita made with lemon rather than lime, softened and smoothed by egg white. This is a delightful drink. Go easy spraying the zest, as this can overly dominate the drink. It also works best with light agave syrup, as the darker versions affect its virgin-like hue and can add unwanted caramel notes.
history: Created in February 2017 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Ginger Last Word
preparation: MUDDLE ginger with gin in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 slice	Fresh ginger root (thumbnail-sized slice)
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
3⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: As the name suggests this is simply a Last Word with a hint of ginger. Simple can be beautiful.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2016 by Riccardo Aletta (AKA 'Ricky D Wing') at Holy Birds, London, England. Ricky calls this drink a "Vegan Last Word," but we thought 'Ginger' better said what was in the tin.
Last Word history

name: The Waysider
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with ginger beer.
ingredients:
5 fresh	Mint leaves
1 2⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
5⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: A cross between a bourbon-based Southside and a bourbon mule. Packs a gingery bourbon punch.

name: Old Acquaintance
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Dry, bitter, very refreshing and mouth-puckering with grapefruit and gin bittered and coloured by red Italian bitters.
history: Adapted from a recipe by Henrik Buus Larsen, which in turn is a riff on the Old Friend cocktail.

name: Inside Job
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe (omit for Cocktails Made Easy)
review: This is a deliciously subtly absinthe (anise) and maraschino (cherry) influenced fresh take on the classic Manhattan/Old Fashioned. Serve on the rocks, as illustrated here, or serve straight-up strained into a chilled coupe. It's boozy and surprisingly dry.

name: Eastern Standard (Soho House Tonic)
preparation: MUDDLE cucumber in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3 slice	Cucumber (fresh)
3 fresh	Mint leaves
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄12 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Fresh and refreshing with gin-laced mint, cucumber and lime.
history: One of the Soho House groups' House Tonic cocktails, the Eastern Standard is based on the Eastside, a drink which in turn was inspired by the Southside.

name: Saturn
garnish: Cut a slice of lemon and remove inside to leave a round ring of zest. Skewer ring and Luxardo maraschino cherry with a stick to form a cherry planet encircled by a lemon zest ring. Rest on top of drink.
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with 7oz scoop crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄4 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄4 shot	Passion fruit syrup
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A Tiki-influenced frozen gin sour with passion fruit and almond.

name: Old Maid
garnish: Cucumber slice speared with mint sprigs bouquet
preparation: MUDDLE cucumber in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
3 slice	Cucumber (fresh)
8 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Zings with freshness. Lime, mint and cucumber make this gin-laced cocktail a veritable health tonic.
history: Created in 2004 by Sam Ross at Milk & Honey in New York City, USA.

name: Jeez Louise
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Averna Amaro
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
5⁄12 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Bittersweet with zesty citrus and subtle carbonation lifting and enlivening deeper rooty and herbal notes.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Chris McMillian at Revel Cafe & Bar in New Orleans, USA.

name: Vodka Mojito
preparation: Add first 4 ingredients to glass and two-thirds fill with crushed ice. CHURN (stir) with bar spoon and then FILL glass with more crushed ice. TOP with splash of soda, briefly stir and serve.
ingredients:
14 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: More usually made with rum but superbly fresh and refreshing with vodka.

name: Sunflower
preparation: RINSE chilled glass with absinthe and set to one side. SHAKE other ingredients with ice and fine strain into absinthe-rinsed glass.
ingredients:
1⁄12 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Elderflower liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Elderflower liqueur replaces aromatised wine in this riff on a classic Corpse Reviver No.2. This means the bitter oils from the lemon zest twist are crucial to the balance of this aromatic floral and citrusy cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2008 by Sam Ross at Milk & Honey in New York City, USA.

name: Mezcalero
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄3 shot	Ginger syrup
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
8 drop	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
review: Lightly smoky mezcal with ginger spice and zesty citrus.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by David Roth at Cask Bar & Kitchen in New York City, USA.

name: Christmas Cosmopolitan
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄3 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A brandy-based Cosmo with a hint of mellow warming Christmasy spice.
history:
Created in November 2020 by yours truly, and revisited with a brandy base in November 2023. The original 2020 recipe:
30ml (1oz) Vodka
20ml (⅔oz) Triple sec
10ml (⅓oz) Falernum
45ml (1½oz) Cranberry juice
15ml (½oz) Lime juice

name: Ernest + Rita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄6 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1 1⁄6 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A relatively low-alcohol, floral, grapefruit-laced and aperitivo-style Margarita.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2014 by Jamie Lewis at Bath & Bottle in Douglas, Isle of Man.

name: Gin Mezcal Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄4 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A pineapple and gin sour made more interesting by a splash of mezcal.
history: Adapted from a recipe called "Mezcalero" by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England.

name: High Noon (Mezcal-based)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
4 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: There's something about the more assertive style of mezcal that suits this cocktail better than its original tequila-based incarnation.
history: A riff on Naren Young's 2013 tequila-based High Noon cocktail. When I say "riff" the only change is swapping tequila for mezcal. This mezcal-based version was popular and is identified with New York City's Empellón Cocina Mexican-restaurant before its closure in 2017.

name: Rising Sun
garnish: Float dehydrated lime or blood orange slice wheel
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Lovechild of the Mezcal Margarita and the Hemingway Special Daquiri.
history: My thanks to fellow Discerning Drinker, Erik Smith, for introducing me to this cocktail which is adapted from a recipe created circa 2018 at Toro Bravo restaurant in Portland, Oregon, USA.

name: Green Eyes No. 2
garnish: Lime slice and Luxardo Maraschino cherry sail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Reminiscent of a Last Word served as a sour.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Andrew Volk at Portland Hunt & Alpine restaurant in Portland, Maine, USA.

name: Smoky Mountain Rain
preparation: POUR all ingredients into glass. Fill with ice and briefly stir.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
2⁄3 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
7 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
4 shot	Chilled water
review: An unlikely but very tasty combination of peated whisky and absinthe.
history: Created in March 2023 by yours truly at The Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Yes Dear!
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
2⁄3 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
2⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water
review: A pisco-based riff on the classic The Last Word cocktail. Most make this with equal parts but I find it better with a touch more pisco.
history: Last Word history

name: Sleeping Lotus
garnish: Edible flowers (preferably orchid) & mint sprigs bouquet
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into glass filled with crushed ice. Churn to integrate and top with more crushed ice.
ingredients:
10 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: An Army & Navy-style almond and mint gin sour served tall and frappe.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Sierra Kirk, bar manager at Hale Pele in Portland, Oregon, USA.

name: Vodka Sidecar
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄4 shot	Chilled water
review: Some will question the use of vodka in a Sidecar but it contributes to the clean freshness of this aperitivo.
history: Recipe by yours truly.

name: Galatoire Special
garnish: Cut lemon string zest twist over cocktail, knot and drop into glass
preparation: DASH absinthe (or Herbsaint) into the inside of a chilled glass then rotate glass to coat its inside and set aside. (Alternatively, use an atomiser to mist the inside of glass.) Separately, STIR rest of ingredients with ice and fine strain into absinthe-coated glass (no ice in the glass).
ingredients:
3 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
4 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Bourbon, made easy by a little sugar and dilution with extra interest courtesy of a subtle touch of freshening anise.
history: A bourbon-based Sazerac that has been the house cocktail at Galatoire's 33 Bar & Steak on Bourbon Street in New Orleans for "as long as anyone can remember", perhaps since Jean Galatoire opened his French cuisine-inspired restaurant in 1905.

name: Grapefruit Gin Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
4 drop	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Not a very imaginative name for a delicious sour.
history: Recipe by yours truly in August 2023.

name: Hemingway Daiquiri (by Anders Erickson)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice (including a swath of grapefruit peel, which should be expressed and dropped in the tin for a "regal shake") and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄4 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Tart, as a Hemingway Special Daiquiri (Papa Doble) should be, with rum-laced bright grapefruit and lime, kissed with flavoursome maraschino liqueur.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Anders Erickson in Chicago, USA.

name: Johnny's Dream
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: I tried this dry, bittersweet, apertivo cocktail with blanco and then reposado tequilas to discover how much better it is with the more youthful tequila.
history: Urban myth has it, backed up by reports in mainstream media in 2023, that this cocktail features on a business card printed with only the recipe and a photograph of the lurid orange drink presented to bartenders in Los Angeles, presumably by Johnny himself, accompanied by the request, "Make this if you can."

name: High Five
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A gin-based riff on the Hemingway Daiquiri with delicate bittersweetness influencing the sweet 'n' sour balance. Light and refreshing – perfect for summer.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2010 by Alex Day at his Death & Co. bar in New York City, USA.

name: Infante
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
6 drop	Orange blossom water / Orange flower water
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A Margarita riff with orgeat replacing the usual orange liqueur, so disguising it with alluring almond/marzipan notes. Some versions call for rose rather than orange blossom water, but floral orange seems more appropriate than rose to replace the orange liqueur.
history:
Named after Mexican actor and singer Pedro Infante Cruz (1917-1957), who acted in more than 60 films and recorded over 350 songs.

Adapted from a recipe created in 2009 by Giuseppe González at Dutch Kills bar in Long Island City, NYC, USA.

name: Gaby des Lys
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Absinthe delicately influences this almond gin sour.
history:
An adaptation of a classic which first features in Charles H. Baker, Jr.'s 1939 The Gentleman's Companion volume II – An Exotic Drinking Book., originally without both lemon juice and bitters. This rather better rendition is by Jason E. Clapham of the St. Ewards MCR, Oxford, England.

Named after the French singer and actress Gaby Deslys (born Marie-Elise-Gabrielle Caire, 1881-1920) Renowned for her beauty, to quote Charles H. Baker, " Gaby the lovely, Gaby the delightfully mad, Gaby the free soul – who died too young and gave a fortune in pearls to the Paris poor!". Her will, in fact, left her villa and all of her other property in Marseilles, to the poor of Marseilles.

name: Amaretto Sour
garnish: Spray aromatic bitters over foaming cocktail from atomiser and then garnish with lemon & cherry sail (lemon slice & Luxardo Maraschino cherry on stick)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Sweet 'n' sour - frothy with an almond buzz. An extra couple of dashes of bitters help balance the drink and add an extra burst of flavour. When made with freshly squeezed lemon juice this can be a great cocktail.
history: Notably absent from 1970s encyclopaedia-style books listing pretty much all known cocktails of the day, including the comprehensive Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide, the Amaretto Sour is a cocktail of the 1980s, when it starts to appear in books such as Mark Torre's 1987 The Bartender's Cherry. (It may well also be in the 1984 first edition but sadly I don't own a copy.)

name: Chimayo
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
3⁄4 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: I used to make this cocktail with reposado tequila, but it's cleaner and better with blanco tequila. Either way, cassis and apple juice mellow tequila.
history: Named after El Potrero de Chimayo in northern New Mexico, USA.

name: Cowboy Hoof Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients (including mint) with ice and syuper fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5 fresh	Mint leaves
2 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Lightly sweetened gin shaken with fresh aromatic mint.
history: Created in the early 1990s by Dick Bradsell at Detroit in London, England.

name: Between The Sheets (by David Wondrich)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Bénédictine takes the place of rum in this variation on the classic Between The Sheets cocktail.
history: Adapted from a version of the classic Between The Sheets by David Wondrich.

name: Earl Grey MarTEAni
preparation:
1. Infuse gin with black tea (preferably Earl Grey). Rather than infuse a whole bottle, you can instead pour just 120ml (4oz) dry gin (enough for two cocktails) into a small glass with one Earl Grey tea bag for five minutes at room temperature to achieve the desired flavour extraction. (Any longer and tannins can be overly dominant.)

2. DRY SHAKE all ingredients (without ice) to emulsify. SHAKE again with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin (tea infused)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: A fantastic and very English drink created by a New Yorker. The gin botanicals combine wonderfully with the flavours and tannins of the tea.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2000 by Audrey Saunders at Bemelmans Bar at the Carlyle, New York City.

name: Fancy Free
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
5⁄12 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Aromatised, tamed bourbon with complex maraschino notes. Basically, a Whiskey Old Fashioned with maraschino in place of sugar syrup. Surprisingly dry, helped by generous dashes of orange and aromatic bitters.
history: The first known reference to the Fancy Free appears in Crosby Gaige's 1940 Cocktail Guide and Ladies' Companion.

name: Gin Fizz
garnish: Lemon slice on rim & mint sprig
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass (without ice). TOP with soda to create frothy head.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Everyone has heard of this clean, refreshing cocktail, but few have actually tried it.
history: A mid-19th century classic Which appears in Jerry "The Professor" Thomas' 1876 Jerry Thomas' Bar-tenders Guide.

name: Jalisco Espresso
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water) (optional)
review: A tequila-laced wake-up call.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2005 by Henry Besant and Andres Masso in London and named after the Mexican state where the tequila industry is centred.
Espresso Martini story

name: Julep Martini
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE mint in base of shaker (just to bruise). Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
8 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: A short variation on the classic Julep: lightly sweetened bourbon and mint.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in the mid 1990s by Dick Bradsell.

name: Lazarus
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
review: A splash of brandy adds an extra dimension to this riff on Dick Bradsell's Espresso Martini.
history: Created in 2000 by David Whitehead at Atrium in Leeds, England.

name: Lotus Espresso
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1⁄3 shot	Maple syrup
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
review: Coffee to the fore but with complex, earthy bittersweet notes.
history:
Adapted from a drink discovered in 2005 at Lotus Bar in Sydney, Australia.
See: Espresso Martini story.

name: Mainbrace
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Tangy grapefruit laced with gin and a hint of orange. Tart finish.
history:
This gin-based cocktail takes its name from a Navy term, usually associated with rum. However, while the ratings on British Navy ships drank rum, their officers sipped gin.

Braces are the ropes that control the angle of the sails on square-rigged ships, and the mainbrace is the longest rope in the rigging. If the mainbrace were shot away during a battle, then the ship would be rendered unmaneuverable. The mainbrace runs through blocks, so it cannot be repaired with a short splice or a knot. Instead, a long splice is needed, so even outside of battle, this is a difficult and skilled job. Hence, it was customary for the men who spliced the mainbrace to be rewarded with an extra ration of rum. Over time, the order to "splice the mainbrace" came to mean that the whole crew would receive an extra ration of rum, issued after victory or to celebrate a special occasion such as a royal birth.

name: Margarita (frozen)
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with flat 7oz scoop of crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Citrus freshness with the subtle agave of tequila served frozen.
history: Margarita cocktail history

name: Mona Lisa
preparation: SHAKE first three ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with tonic water.
ingredients:
1 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: Chartreuse fans will appreciate this drink, which is also an approachable way for novices to acquire a taste for the green stuff. It's also a great brunch cocktail.

name: Pineapple & Cardamom 'Martini'
preparation: MUDDLE cardamom in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into a chilled glass.
ingredients:
3 whole	Green cardamom pods
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Pineapple and cardamon are a spectacular pairing of fruit and spice in this vodka laced 'Martini'.
history:
Created in 2002 by Henry Besant at The Lonsdale, London, England.

Our Martini cocktail page details its evolution and other common variants.

name: Pineapple Daiquiri (on-the-rocks)
garnish: Skewered pineapple wedge or dehydrated pineapple slice & Luxardo maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 1⁄4 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Rum and pineapple are just meant to go together. A simple but pleasingly fruity cocktail with ripe pineapple and sugar richness balanced by cleansing dry white rum and lime citrus acidity.

name: Pineapple Daiquiri (Frozen)
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with a scoop of crushed ice and serve with a straw.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A tad fluffy but very tasty.

name: Pisco Sour (blended)
garnish: Float three drops of Amargo Chuncho or Angostura aromatic bitters to signify health wealth and happiness.
preparation: BLEND lime and sugar to dissolve sugar. Add pisco, egg white and 6oz scoop crushed ice and BLEND again. Serve with paper straws.
ingredients:
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
6 barspoon	Powdered sugar (white sugar ground in mortar and pestle)
2 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: This blended version of a Pisco Sour is the authentic Peruvian and indeed Chilean serve.
history: See: Pisco Sour history.

name: Seventh Heaven No.2
garnish: Mint sprigs bouquet pegged to rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Grapefruit citrus bitterness balances rich floral maraschino liqueur in this delicately balanced gin-based cocktail.
history:
Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book:
"SEVENTH HEAVEN COCKTAIL. (No.2)
1 Tablespoonful Grapefruit Juice.
¼ Maraschino
¾ Dry Gin.
Stir well and place a sprig of green Mint on top."

name: Swizzles Cocktail
garnish: Crown with a few dashes of aromatic bitters over ice peak, plus juniper or blueberries
preparation: POUR all ingredients into chilled glass and two-thirds fill with crushed ice. SWIZZLE with a swizzle stick (or churn with a barspoon). Add more crushed ice to fill and SWIZZLE some more. Serve with straws.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Somewhat reminiscent of a frozen gimlet – the combination of gin and lime shines in this freshening swizzle.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Tropic
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
2 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A light, satisfying cooler.
history: Based on a recipe believed to date back to the 1950s.

name: Turkish Coffee Cocktail
preparation: MUDDLE cardamom pods in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5 whole	Green cardamom pods
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Turkish and Arabic coffee is made with lightly roasted coffee beans that are very finely ground and boiled in water, usually with a little sugar, in a special pot called cezve in Turkey or ibrik elsewhere. It is sometimes flavoured with some cardamom and this vodka-based coffee cocktail harnesses the aromatic eucalyptus and citrus notes of this spice.
history: Created in 2003 by yours truly.

name: USB Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy) (infused with vanilla)
1 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
1 1⁄4 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Vanilla notes in the cognac sit beautifully with the pineapple juice while the acidity of the wine balances rich fruity sweetness.
history:
A brandy-driven riff on the Palermo cocktail created in 2003 by yours truly in London, England.

Named, not after the Universal Serial Bus used to connect PCs and peripheral devices, but after the grape varieties Ugni and Sauvignon Blanc. Ugni Blanc is the most common grape variety in Cognac, while Sauvignon Blanc wine seems to suit this drink, (although it also works well with Chardonnay and other grape varieties).

name: Vodka Espresso
garnish: Float 3 coffee beans in the centre of the drink, arranged in a flower petal formation.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Vodka and coffee combine in this tasty wake-up call.
history: Created circa 1983 by Dick Bradsell while bartending at the Soho Brasserie on Old Compton Street, London who created his Vodka Espresso for a woman, said to be an "American model," who famously asked for "Something that's gonna wake me up, then fuck me up."

name: Chartreuse Swizzle
garnish: Pineapple wedge, Luxardo Maraschino cherry & dusting of freshly grated nutmeg
preparation: POUR ingredients into chilled glass and two-thirds fill with crushed ice. SWIZZLE with a swizzle stick (or churn with a barspoon). Add more crushed ice to fill and SWIZZLE some more. Serve with straws.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A swizzle for people like me - Chartreuse lovers. Best enjoyed on a hot summer's evening.
history: Created in 2002 by Marco Dionysos at Tres Agaves, San Francisco, USA.

name: Fitzgerald
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A Tangy and fresh Gin Sour without the egg white. A juniper heavy gin and dashes of bitters are key to the success of this sour.
history: Adapted from a drink created in the early 1990s by Dale DeGroff at the Rainbow Room in New York City, USA.

name: In-Seine
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Elderflower liqueur
3 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Elderflower liqueur mellows and boosts the brandy's floral notes, while dashes of absinthe balance sweetness and add aniseed notes.
history:
Created in 2006 by yours truly at The Cabinet Room, London, England.

The name is a reference to the Parisian district of St-Germain, lying on the left bank of the River Seine, and a nod to the use of absinthe and its pre-war ban in France partly due to the belief that it induced insanity.

name: Old Mexican Friend
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Bittersweet and sweet 'n' sour with smoky mezcal, zesty grapefruit and faint floral elderflower, particularly on the long smoky finish.
history: A riff on Jim Meehan's usually gin-based Old Friend created in October 2020 by yours truly as a result of a comment left by a Discerning Drinker on our Old Friend page saying, "Swapped out gin for mezcal and would highly recommend for the more adventurous."

name: Elderflower Mojito
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE (just to bruise) mint in base of glass. Add other ingredients, half fill glass with crushed ice and CHURN (stir) with bar spoon. Fill glass to brim with more crushed ice and churn some more. Serve with straws.
ingredients:
12 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: The enduring classic benefits from a touch of elderflower.
history: See: Mojito origins and history.

name: Gypsy #1
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Dominic Venegas, this cocktail's creator, describes it as "a little homage to the Last Word cocktail".
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2007 by Dominic Venegas at Bourbon & Branch in San Francisco, USA.

name: Parisien Mojito
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE mint (just to bruise) in base of glass. Add other ingredients, half fill glass with crushed ice and CHURN (stir) with bar spoon. Fill glass to brim with more crushed ice and churn some more. Serve with straws.
ingredients:
12 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Those with a sweet tooth may want to add a dash of sugar syrup.
history:
Created in 2006 by yours truly.
See: Mojito Cocktail history

name: Peruvian Elder Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: This tasty sour combines the aromatics of pisco and elderflower in an intriguing variation on the Margarita. Consider smoothing with fresh egg white.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2006 by drinks writer Gary "gaz" Regan

name: Gin Twist
preparation: POUR ingredients into pre-warmed glass and STIR.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
Top up with	Boiling water
review: Gin botanicals flavour this delicate, citrusy, warming drink.
history:
This classic English cocktail dates back to at least the early 1800s and was so popular at the time that it is frequently referred to in novels and periodicals from the time. In Sir Walter Scott's 1823 novel St Ronan's Well, the character Captain MacTurk says, "Sir Binco, I will beg the favour of your company to the smoking-room, where we may have a cigar and a glass of gin-twist; and we will consider how the honour of the company must be supported and upholden upon the present conjuncture."

William Makepeace Thackeray mentions the Gin Twist in his 1869 Miscellanies: The Book of Snobs. Sketches and Travels in London. "About eleven men in white neckcloths drop in from dinner-parties, and show their lacquered boots and shirt-studs with a little complacency - and at midnight, after the theatres, the young rakes and viveurs come swaggering in, and call loudly for Gin-Twist."

name: Hi Ladies!
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
8 fresh	Mint leaves
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: This tasty cocktail is basically a Vodka Mojito served straight-up.
history: From Ted Saucier's 1951 book, Bottoms Up!.

name: Easy Speak
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix) (2 sugar to 1 water)
4 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: Originally served in a chilled old-fashioned glass without ice but I prefer this cocktail with the dilution that comes with ice. Don't worry if you don't have any chocolate bitters, this drink has enough complexity without the extra bitterness.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2012 by Scott Diaz, Beverage & Cafe Manager at Elliott's Oyster House & Seafood Café, Seattle, USA.

name: Closing Argument
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
3⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
3⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A mezcal-based Last Word. It works! End of argument.
history: Last Word history

name: Gin Basil Smash
preparation: MUDDLE basil sprigs (no need to pluck leaves from stem) in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
12 fresh	Basil leaves
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Jörg, the creator of this cocktail, says, "Better too much than not enough basil in this drink". He also specifies that the basil is muddled rather than just broken by the action of shaking as this produces a greener drink. He adds "Keep in mind: 5 cl Gin is not enough; 6 cl Gin is the recipe; 7 cl Gin is LOVE!"
history: Created in the summer of 2008 by Jörg Meyer at Le Lion • Bar de Paris, Hamburg, Germany and originally named Gin Pesto. Jörg blogged about his new creation on the 10th of July 2008 and from that point, it started to quickly grow in popularity to become internationally known, also becoming better known as the Gin Basil Smash.

name: Whiskey Smash
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
8 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A mint-influenced Whiskey Sour.
history: Adapted from a recipe created 1998-99 by Dale DeGroff at The Rainbow Room in New York City, USA.

name: Club Cocktail (Whitfield's recipe)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Pineapple juice
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Pineapple juice adds fruity tropical freshness and a foamy head to this cocktail. Fortified with cognac and aromatised with a splash of maraschino cherry liqueur and a couple of dashes of New Orleans bitters.
history: The Club Cocktail first appeared in W.C. Whitfield's 1939 Just Cocktails book (although does not appear in his 1941 Here's How Mixed Drinks by the same Three Mountaineers Inc. publishers).

name: Division Bell
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
3⁄4 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A mezcal inspired variation of the Last Word with a refreshing, spirit-forward blend of ingredients.
history:
Created in 2009 by Phil Ward at Mayahuel, New York City, USA.
Last Word history

name: Gin Pahit
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water
review: The balance of bitters to sugar is key to the success of this cocktail. Use a Japanese dasher bitters bottle and measure your 2:1 sugar syrup judiciously and you'll have made something special. Go easy while spraying the lemon zest over the drink – too much lemon oil will wreck its fine balance.
history: The name of this vintage variation on a Pink Gin cocktail is pronounced 'Gin Fight' in the Malay language ("pahit" means bitter).

name: Chepari
garnish: Orange foam (prepared beforehand with 50cl orange juice, 5cl sugar, and 3 egg whites).
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila (infused with cherry & tonka)
2⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
history: Adapted from a recipe created for Campari by Bettina Kupsa in Germany.

name: Pineapple Martini (1990s recipe)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: This cocktail is deliciously simple, fruity, and ridiculously easy to drink. The quality and freshness of your pineapple juice are key to this cocktail's success, so muddling fresh pineapple instead of using juice also works well.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 1997 by Ben Reed at the Met Bar in London, England. Ben has appointed, or should I say anointed, the 26th June as International Pineapple Martini Day.

name: Old Friend
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Elderflower liqueur
review:
Tart, dry and lightly bitter, but with just enough underlying sweetness to stroke the palate and make another sip so very desirable – a complex, bittersweet taste sensation. Brilliant as an aperitif on a hot summer's evening.

Jim's original recipe calls for 7.5ml (¼oz) elderflower liqueur, but in October 2020, due to popular demand (see comments below), I amended the above recipe to have twice the volume of elderflower liqueur. Then, in June 2022, also in the pursuit of balance and pleasing the tastes of as many as possible, I nudged this back to 10ml (1/3oz). Given variations in citrus, I believe this is my final amendment.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Jim Meehan in 2012 for the cocktail menu at Chef's Club in Aspen, Colorado.

name: Boston Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Bourbon whiskey soured with lemon juice and smoothed by egg white.
history:
Whereas the addition of egg white to a Whiskey Sour is optional, egg white is a requisite in a Boston Sour – a Boston Sour is simply a Whiskey Sour with egg white.
See: Whiskey Sour cocktail History

name: Last Flight
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: This appropriately named boozy cocktail is a cross between a Last Word and a Paper Plane.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in January 2018 by Callum Rixson, General Manager at Hideout in Bath, England.

Callum's original recipe used Wild Turkey 101 for the bourbon and he told us that he created this cocktail for "one of our old locals who was moving to Toronto and he still drinks it in his local bar." Callum sought to create a drink that could be ordered and replicated pretty much anywhere.

Also see Last Word history

name: Sidecar
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Spirituous and just on the sour side, the sugar rim is considered by some to be integral to this classic cocktail. Dilution is key to perfecting a Sidecar so if using ice straight from a freezer (rather than an ice machine) then consider adding 10 to 15ml chilled water. In place of a sugar rim, some may want to add 2.5ml or more sugar syrup or see my Sidecar recipe.
history:
In his 1948 Fine Art of Mixing Drinks, David A. Embury says of the Sidecar's origin: "It was invented by a friend of mine at a bar in Paris during World War I and was named after the motorcycle sidecar in which the good captain customarily was driven to and from the little bistro where the drink was born and christened."

Embury doesn't name the bar, but it's commonly assumed that he meant Harry's New York Bar and that the cocktail was created by its owner, Harry MacElhone. However, in his own 1922 ABC of Cocktails, Harry credits the cocktail to Pat MacGarry, "the Popular bar-tender at Buck's Club, London." However, in later editions of ABC of Cocktails he appears to take credit for the cocktail himself. The fact that MacElhone worked alongside Malachi "Pat" MacGarry at Buck's Club when it first opened just a few years earlier in June 1919, may have some bearing on this.

MacGarry being the originator of the Sidecar is further reinforced by the first printed recipe appearing in Robert Vermeire's Cocktails How To Mix Them, published in May 1922, just a few months prior to Harry MacElhone's ABC of Cocktails.

name: Combustible Edison
preparation: STIR first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. Warm cognac in a metal ladle and ignite before pouring (from a height) as a flaming stream into the glass already containing other ingredients. PLEASE EXERCISE CAUTION!
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
review: The variation, the non-combusted merely "Edison" or "The Edisonian", which calls for all the ingredients (inc. brandy) to be stirred together with ice, is a bitter drink but lacks the theatre. Opt for showmanship or discernment – your call. Whichever, this bittersweet cocktail is suited to the aperitivo moment.
history: Adapted from a recipe by Robert "Brother Cleve" Toomey, a regarded bartender, DJ and musician. Brother Cleve was a member of the band Combustible Edison and this cocktail was created in the 1990s by Michael "The Millionaire" Cudahy, the band's leader. The drink appeared on the back cover of the band's first CD, I, Swinger.

name: Zara
garnish: Lemon zest twist (expressed & discarded) & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
2⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄6 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
4 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Gareth describes his creation as, "Bold and smoky with chocolate notes, perfect for after dinner." It is!
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2014 by Gareth Franklin, better known as "G.", Luxardo's global ambassador.

name: Dead Man's Handle
garnish: Dust surface of drink with Tajín seasoning
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
review: Tequila charged, delicately bittersweet undertones sit with rich almond syrup.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Tiffany Kirk at Miss Carousel bar in Houston, USA. Perhaps named after the dead man's switch designed to activate or deactivate if a human operator becomes incapacitated due to loss of consciousness or being physically removed from control. Also known as a dead man's handle, such switches were originally used on trains, other vehicles and machines, but the term is now used to describe other fail-safe devices or computer software.

name: Gargoyle No. 2
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) and float half a fresh passion fruit
preparation: Cut a passion fruit in half and scrape the flesh and seeds from both halves into shaker. Add other ingredients, shake with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 fresh	Passion fruit (fresh)
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Some might describe this as being a grown-up/vintage Porn Star Martini. It's spirituous and yet dry – despite the generous spoon of sugar which serves to amplify flavour and take the edge of the spirit.
history:
Named after and created at The Gargoyle Club in London, England circa 1930 by its head bartender, George White. This cocktail appears in several cocktail books published in England around the time of its presumed creation:
- R. de Fleury's 1934 1700 Cocktails For The Man Behind the Bar
- William James "Billy" Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Bar Book
- The United Kingdom Bartenders' Guild's 1937 The UKBG's Approved Cocktails.

name: Mexican El Diablo
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with ginger beer.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄2 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: Mezcal's assertive flavours stand up well, indeed sit in harmony with richly flavoured blackcurrant liqueur, lime juice and fiery ginger beer.
history: The original name for Trader Vic's tequila-based El Diablo. As fellow Discerning Drinker, Erik Maloney suggests, more appropriate names would perhaps be Smoky Devil, Diablo Ahumado, or Diablo Humeante.

name: Sir Knight
garnish: Orange or lemon zest twist (classically lemon)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Don't be tempted by bartending convention to stir this late night sipping cocktail, it's classically shaken and all the better for it.
history: Adapted from a recipe in the 1938 book The How And When by Hyman Gale and Gerald F. Marco.

name: White Cuban
preparation: STIR first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. Carefully FLOAT lightly whipped cream (shake sealed cream container before pouring).
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
5⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
5⁄6 shot	Double cream / heavy cream
review: A White Russian based on rum rather than vodka. Tends to be better with a charcoal-filtered light white rum rather than a more characterful golden rum. Depending on how dry your coffee liqueur is, and your palate, you may prefer to omit the sugar syrup or increase the measure.

name: Pantheon
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Honeyed herbal Scotch whisky freshened by lemon sourness.
history: Created in 2019 by Daisuke Ito at his Land Bar Artisan in Tokyo, Japan.

name: Salmoncito
garnish: Grapefruit zest twist expressed & discarded. Adorn with a grapefruit supreme wedge
preparation: POUR all ingredients into glass and then fill glass with ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
3 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: A bittersweet pink grapefruit-flavoured riff on the G&T.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2013 by Khristian de la Torre at Maison Artemisia in Mexico City.

Salmoncito means 'little salmon', a reference to this cocktail's colour, particularly its grapefruit supreme (a wedge of grapefruit with pith and membrane removed) garnish, reminiscent of a salmon swimming into the ice.

name: Naked In The Rain
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
3⁄4 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
3⁄4 shot	Elderflower liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A riff on the Naked & Famous with elderflower liqueur in place of Yellow Chartreuse.
history: Adapted from a cocktail discovered in June 2024 at Attaboy in New York City.

name: Blue Blazer
preparation:
You will need a pair of large silver-plated tankards (blazer mugs) with handles. Preheat these with boiling water and warm the whisky. POUR the whisky into one tankard and fresh boiling water into the other. Ignite the whisky using a long match and while still blazing pour the whisky into the other tankard. Then mix ingredients by pouring them from one tankard to the other. The foolhardy increase the distance between the tankards as they pour, thus creating a spectacular long blue flame between the two. Extinguish flame by covering flaming tankard with base of the other tankard, pour into glass and sweeten to taste by stirring in powdered sugar.

WARNING - please practice with water first to perfect your method. Stand on a non-flammable floor and have suitable fire-fighting equipment nearby. The following recipe makes two drinks.
ingredients:
4 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
4 shot	Boiling water
1 barspoon	Powdered sugar (white sugar ground in mortar and pestle)
review: The showy way to make a simple hot whisky punch.
history: For the full story behind the origins of the Blue Blazer variations on this drink see our Blazer cocktails page.

name: Brandy Flip
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 fresh	Egg (white & yolk)
review: A serious alternative to advocaat for those without raw egg inhibitions.
history: A forgotten classic.

name: Brandy Milk Punch
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. (Don't dry shake a Milk Punch as this produces something redolent of an Egg Nog.)
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 5⁄6 shot	Milk (whole milk/full 3-4% fat)
1⁄3 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
review: This traditional New Orleans hangover cure beats your bog-standard vanilla milkshake.
history: A classic which was popular during America's Prohibition era and dates back to colonial times. It is still widely served in New Orleans where it is commonly consumed with Sunday brunch.

name: Call Me Old-Fashioned
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: An Old-Fashioned made with cognac instead of whiskey. Works well.
history: A Cognac Old-Fashioned cocktail created in 2001 by yours truly, London, England.

name: English Martini
preparation: Strip rosemary leaves from stem and MUDDLE in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 fresh	Rosemary sprig
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄6 shot	Elderflower liqueur
review: Rosemary and sweet elderflower combine wonderfully with the gin botanicals to make an interesting and approachable, if slightly sweet "Martini".
history:
Adapted from a drink created in 2003 at MJU at the Millennium Hotel, London, England.
Martini cocktail

name: Maple Old Fashioned
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄3 shot	Maple syrup
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A spirit-forward sipper that's rich and easy with bourbon mellowed and sweetened by maple syrup.
history: I first encountered the bourbon-based Maple Old Fashioned in 2004 at Indigo Yard in Edinburgh, Scotland but in more recent years, rum seems to have taken over as the preferred spirit base to make a Maple Rum Old Fashioned. Whichever spirit base you use, makes a delicious riff on the classic Old-Fashioned.

name: Old Fashioned
