preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
5⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Rich (medium-dry and spirituous this old-fashioned is all too easy to drink and fortunately, easy to make.
history: As with the Martini, the glass this cocktail is served in has taken the name of the drink. Its origin stems from the adaptation and renaming of a similar drink known as the Whisky Cocktail, which was shaken and served up. Who did the adapting and renaming is unknown. For the full story, see Old-Fashioned cocktail history.

name: Passion Fruit Martini
preparation: Cut passion fruit in half and scoop out flesh into shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 fresh	Passion fruit (fresh)
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Passion fruit syrup
review: Simple but tasty, harnessing the flavour of passion fruit.

name: Elderflower Spritz
preparation: POUR wine and then elderflower liqueur into an ice-filled glass. TOP with soda (or champagne).
ingredients:
2 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
1 1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A long, easy drinking summer cooler.
history:
Created in 2006 by yours truly ahead of the launch of St-Germain elderflower liqueur. It went on to become the brand's signature cocktail.
See: Spritz cocktail history

name: Gypsy Queen
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Vodka both fortifies this complexly spiced honeyed and herbal cocktail.
history:
Drinks historian David Wondrich discovered the earliest known reference to the Gypsy Queen in a 1938 booklet published by New York City's famed The Russian Tea Room. This makes it one of the earliest vodka-cocktails in the USA.

In his seminal 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks, David Embury says, "The original recipe calls for a proportion of 1 to 2. This, however, is rather sweet. About 5 top 6 parts vodka to 1 of Benedictine makes a much better drink." [The above recipe is 3 to 1.]

Embury's "Gypsy or Gypsy Queen" recipe of 1-part Benedictine and 2 to 6 parts Vodka stipulates "1 dash Orange Bitters to each drink" but Angostura or similar aromatic bitters produce a rounder cocktail.

name: King's Jubilee
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) & skewered maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review:
If there is such a thing as a 'Rum Aviation', then this is surely it.

The proportions of the original 1935 recipe stipulate equal amounts of maraschino and lemon juice but even my recipe with a third less lemon is on the tart side. Don't be tempted to drop the cherry garnish into the drink or both appearance and balance will be muddied. Skewer the cherry and reserve for a sweet treat at the end.

My original take on this classic (up until July 2020) was 60ml light rum, 22.5ml maraschino liqueur and 15ml lemon juice but this packs a whopping 80ml of alcohol. The above recipe scales this back by a third to still pack a double shot punch, but in a drink that hopefully won't be a killer blow to the night.
history:
Created in 1935 to celebrate the Silver Jubilee of King George V by Harry Craddock, then head bartender of The American Bar at London's The Savoy Hotel. Craddock was also President of the United Kingdom Bartenders' Guild and this cocktail appears in the U.K.B.G. Approved Cocktails book published in 1937, as well as William James "Billy" Tarling's Cafe Royal Cocktail Book – Coronation Edition, published the same year.

Tarling was also in the top echelon of the Guild and the royalties of his book were equally divided between the U.K.B.G. Sickness Benefit Fund and The Café Royal Sports Club Fund.

name: London Gypsy
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: The botanicals in the gin and the herbal Bénédictine combine well in this cocktail, which is balanced by the addition of bitters.
history: A riff on the classic Gypsy Queen by yours truly and then revisited in January 2023 thanks to feedback from fellow Discerning Drinkers and a tweak to my formulation by John Hinojos.

name: Flying Frenchman (Absinthe Espresso Martini)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
review: Best described as an energy drink on steroids - equal parts absinthe, coffee liqueur and espresso. However, unlike most caffeine-laden energy drinks the Flying Frenchman is very tasty.
history:
Adapted from a drink created in 2014 for La Fée Parisienne by Andy Mil at the London Cocktail Club. Andy's recipe originally called for Patron XO Café and an additional 15ml of sugar syrup.
Espresso Martini history

name: Milanese G&T
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly STIR.
ingredients:
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
4 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: Depending on how you view this, it's a traditional Gin & Tonic with a splash of bitter liqueur adding colour and herbal fruity complexity. Or a G&T take on the classic Negroni cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2016 at Campari's then-London office in The Shard.

name: Espresso Martini (simple 3 equal parts recipe)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
review: Balanced, tasty and enlivening, this cocktail is incredibly quick and easy to make using just three ingredients that should be every day essentials in every domestic kitchen.
history: This simplified version of Dick Bradsell's Espresso Martini (or Vodka Espresso) is preferred to the original recipe by some due to its simple equal parts formula and omission of sugar syrup. (If using a dry coffee liqueur, you'll need to add 5ml to 7.5ml sugar syrup, preferably demerara syrup.)

name: Gin Sonic Highball
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
1 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A lower alcohol and lower sugar version of a Gin & Tonic with a smaller serve of gin topped with equal parts tonic water and soda water so reducing the alcohol and sugar associated with the tonic in a regular G&T.
history: Originating in Tokyo, Japan in the Noughties, "Sonic" is a combination of soda and tonic.

name: Spanish Espresso Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Licor 43 Original liqueur
1 1⁄3 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
review: This riff on Dick Brasell's classic Espresso Martini introduces rich vanilla and faint and delicate herbal notes.
history: A cocktail promoted by Licor 43 Liqueur and added to Difford's Guide in 2019.

name: Bicicletta Spritz
preparation: POUR all ingredients into an ice-filled glass. If poured in the following order there should be no need to stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
1 1⁄3 shot	Pinot Grigio white wine
1 1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review: Basically the same as a Veneziano Spritz but with equal proportions wine to Italian red bitter liqueur, we like to further distinguish the Bicicletta from the spritz by serving it with less volume in a tall slim highball glass rather than the larger glassware associated with spritz. Much more appropriate for the ride home.
history: Bicicletta (Italian for bicycle) is another name for Veneziano Spritz and is one of many examples of regional differences across Italy in the name of what is essentially the same drink. The name is said to have originated due to old men wobbling home on their bikes after an evening of Biciclettas with their friends.

name: Italian Chocolate Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
1 1⁄2 shot	Averna Amaro
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
review: There may be some chocolate in your coffee liqueur and perhaps cocoa beans play a role in the amaro, but like the Coffee Cocktail (which has no coffee) this delicious riff on an Espresso Martini is chocolaty without really featuring the headline chocolate in the recipe.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Nicholas Boden at Tavernonna Italian Kitchen, Kansas City, USA.

name: Comte de Sureau
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄6 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review: Sprays of oils from both orange and lemon zest twists aid the fine balance of this bittersweet aperitivo, which fittingly has become known by many as an Elderflower Negroni.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2007/8 by Gonçalo de Sousa Monteiro at Le Lion in Hamburg, Germany.

name: The Original Margarita
garnish: Rim glass with lime juice and sea salt before making cocktail. Add a lime wheel slice to finished drink.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 2⁄3 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review:
There's debate as to who created the original Margarita recipe and when with a Dallas socialite called Margarita Sames most often credited (see below). However, there is universal acceptance that the recipe comprised just three ingredients: tequila, Cointreau triple sec, and lime juice.

The classic proportions, dating back to 1937, are 2oz (60ml) tequila, 1oz (30ml) Cointreau, and 1oz (30ml) lime juice. The recipe we've adopted slightly reduces the proportion of tequila and sour lime juice to the rich liqueur to create a better-balanced cocktail. Depending on your palate you may still want to add a teaspoon of agave syrup in addition to the three "original" ingredients.
history:
The first written reference to this cocktail appears in the 19th July edition of the Albuquerque Journal as a "Tequila Daisy" but the proportions are not stated. The 2 parts tequila, 1 part Cointreau, 1 part lime juice recipe we recognise as today's Margarita first appears in W. J. Tarling's 1937 Cafe Royal Cocktail Book but under the name "Picador".

Tarling's 1937 recipe doesn't specify a brand or style of tequila and his recipe calls for lime or lemon juice, but he does name Cointreau as his liqueur of choice.

Who added the salt rim and renamed the Picador a Margarita is debated by cocktail historians. Perhaps read the full story of the Margarita cocktail while you sip on one.

name: Spritz Le Fizz
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
1 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Crisp and grassy Sauvignon Blanc wine balances the rich, zesty orange invigorated with sparkling soda water
history: Adapted from the Cointreau Fizz- a cocktail comprising of 2 parts Cointreau, 1 part lime juice and 3 parts soda water, created in the early 1950s by Jean Lupoïu who was a famous Parisian bartender. The Cointreau Fizz is turned into the Fizz Spritz by swapping out and rebalancing the acidity of lime juice with that of dry white wine.

name: Vodka Sonic Highball
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
1 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: A lower alcohol and lower sugar version of a Vodka & Tonic (VAT). Light and refreshing. One for a hot summer's afternoon.
history: Originating in Japan's Tokyo with gin as the base, "Sonic" is a combination of soda and tonic.

name: Sonic Surfer
preparation: POUR first 2 ingredients into ice-filled glass. Carefully pour cognac so it floats to form a gold layer over the clear soda and tonic. Add a wooden lollipop stick as the drinker should stir before enjoying.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
1 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
review: A light and refreshing way to enjoy cognac. Best appreciated as a summertime aperitif.
history: Created in April 2021 by yours truly, this builds on the Japanese "Sonic" (a combination of soda and tonic) with cognac surfing the bubbles.

name: Iced Creamy Mocha
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Chocolate cream liqueur
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
review: A dessert-style cocktail that's just as its name suggests.
history: Created in March 2023 by yours truly at The Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Daiquiri Frappé
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review:
Not to be confused with a Frozen Daiquiri, which is blended with crushed ice, a Daiquiri served frappé is shaken with cubed ice and then strained over crushed ice. The result is very different and this frappé serve amplifies the flavour of the rum so suits a light white rather than a more characterful rum. Also, while I'd obviously advocate the use of Difford's Daiquiri Bitters when serving straight-up, the chilled simplicity of the frappé is serve best kept simple – rum, lime, sugar and water/ice.

If you've good crushed ice and start with a well-chilled glass, you should be able to take your time sipping this cocktail and once finished you be left with a glass at least half filled with pebbles of ice. The trick is to crush cubes of ice taken directly from a freezer immediately before serving.
history: Recipe created in June 2023 by yours truly using the same proportions I favour for a classic Daiquiri No.1.

name: Scotch Whisky Highball
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Simple, refreshing and brilliant. One of the best ways to appreciate a good scotch whisky.
history: Whisky Highball history and in-depth info on Highballs

name: Gin Tonica
garnish: Lemon zest twist, lime wedge & 3 cardamom pods
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and lightly stir.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: Something of a Spanish phenomenon, where the G&T (which in England has been traditionally served in a tall slim Collins glass) tends to be served in a huge goldfish bowl of a glass – big enough to house garnishes ranging from cardamom pods and juniper berries to fruit peels and slices of ginger.

name: Vodka & Tonic (VAT)
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
4 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: Dry, crisp, refreshing and cleansing. Sip, contemplate and say to yourself, "The world is my lobster."
history: During the 1980s the Vodka & Tonic knocked the G&T off the top spot as Britain's signature drink, its popularity helped by frequent appearances in television series such as ITV's Minder, broadcast 1979 to 1994. The comedy-drama series stared the affable but unscrupulous entrepreneurial trader, Arthur Daley who was a regular at the Winchester Club where his usual was "a large V.A.T", a wordplay on Value Added Tax. Arthur never paid for drinks, so "stick it on the slate" would evitable follow his bar call.

name: Kentucky Colonel
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
review: If you like Old Fashioneds then there's a good chance you'll appreciate the Kentucky Colonel.
history: The Kentucky Colonel first appears in Jacques Straub's 1914 Manual of Mixed Drinks. This recipe is adapted from a recipe in Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide.

name: Dark & Smoky
garnish: Orange slice or lime slice wheel or wedge
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
4 1⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: Where there's smoke there's fire – in this case peat smoke and fiery ginger spice.
history: Adapted from a drink created by the mysterious folk at Caisteal Chamuis.

name: Brave Cow
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
review: If your coffee liqueur is on the sweet side, then add six drops of vanilla bitters to help the balance and complexity. However, with a good coffee liqueur and dry gin, this two-ingredient cocktail is surprisingly tasty and wonderfully simple.
history:
The Brave Cow emerged during the 1970s/80s on the back of the then popular Black Russian cocktail.

Recipe adapted from John J. Poister's, The New American Bartender's Guide.

name: Clarified Vodka Milk Punch
preparation:
Milk Punch Base pre-batch (scale-up recipe according to requirement)
1. POUR first 7 ingredients (with peels from the zests lemons & orange) into a sealable container and leave to infuse for 12 hours in a refrigerator.
2. Hot milk method HEAT milk until just starting to simmer and pour (while still simmering) the vodka tea and juice mix into the milk while stirring. As soon as the milk curdles, stop stirring. Chill for at least 2-3 hours and up to 24 hours.
OR 2. Cold milk method POUR vodka tea and juice mix into cold milk while stirring. As soon as the milk curdles, stop stirring. Chill for at least 2-3 hours and up to 24 hours.
3. Fine STRAIN mixture through cheesecloth or Superbag into a large jar or another container. Ideally, this should be in a refrigerator (I removed a shelf in ours) with the cheesecloth/bag hung over the jar.
4. Repeat step three, without removing curds from the filter or move to a finer strainer (e.g. from a 400-micron bag to a 100-micron bag) or coffee filter.
5. Stored in the refrigerator, this will keep for a week (and potentially months), but be sure to sterilise containers, etc.

Cocktail itself
STIR 50ml pre-prepared Milk Punch Base with 50ml vodka and 7.5ml sugar syrup and strain into an ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice)
ingredients:
6 2⁄3 shot	Cold black breakfast tea
6 2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
fresh	Lemon peel
6 2⁄3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
fresh	Orange peel
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
6 2⁄3 shot	Milk (whole milk/full 3-4% fat)
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: This cocktail requires starting preparation at least a day before you want to drink it, but with its velvety texture and delicate citrus flavour, it's worth the faff. This recipe works with Lactose-free milk, but it must be whole-fat milk.
history: Popular in eighteenth-century England, the earliest known clarified brandy milk punch recipe, by housewife Mary Rockett, dates back to 1711. The milk punch became so highly regarded that in 1838, Queen Victoria awarded a Royal Warrant to Nathaniel Whisson & Co. as "Purveyors of Milk Punch to Her Majesty" for their bottled version.

name: Peligroso
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Averna Amaro
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄12 shot	Pimento dram/Allspice liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄4 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Bittersweet and spicy this is a warming, comforting winter aperitivo.
history: Named after the Spanish word for dangerous and much adapted from a recipe that originated in 2019 at La Factoría bar in Old San Juan, Puerto Rico.

name: Fog Cutter
preparation: SHAKE first 7 ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. FLOAT sherry on top of drink.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄12 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1 1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Oloroso sherry
review: Don't be fooled by this seemingly innocuous orange-yellow long, fruity cocktail. It packs a serious punch with sweet almond notes masking its rum, gin and brandy.
history: A Tiki classic credited to Victor Bergeron. It appears in his 1972 Trader Vic's Bartender's Guide (revised edition) accompanied by his "TV" logo signifying that this is a Trader Vig signature cocktail. Above the recipe, he remarks, "Fog Cutter, hell. After two of these, you won't even see the stuff."

name: Absinthe Makes The Heart Grow Fonder
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄6 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Absinthe and gin delicately lead this subtle cherry-flavoured cocktail. Bitter liqueur adds more colour than flavour, while pink grapefruit freshens.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created by Scott Diaz in Seattle, Washington State, USA.

The phrase "absence makes the heart grow fonder" is first attributed to English poet Ernest Dowson (1867-1900) as part of a February 1899 letter to Arthur Moore. However, it was another poet, Thomas Haynes Bayly, who popularised the phrase in his poem Isle of Beauty published in his two-volume 1844 Songs, Ballads, and Other Poems.

name: Espresso Breakfast Martini
garnish: Express orange zest twist and discard. Float 3 coffee beans.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 barspoon	Orange marmalade
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: As the name suggests, a mashup of the Espresso and Breakfast Martinis, delivering gin-laced coffee and marmalade citrus.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2024 by Scott Baird, beverage manager at the Starlite in San Fransico, USA.

name: Morning Glory Fizz
preparation:
SHAKE first 6 ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and slowly pour 2/3rds of the contents of the shaker from a higher than normal height into a chilled empty glass (no ice in glass) while simultaneously pouring soda with your other hand. The cocktail and soda should form a single stream of liquid falling into the glass.

As when pouring a Guinness, to achieve a perfect head on a fizz, the cocktail should be left to settle for at least a minute before topping off with what remains in the shaker. Ideally, during the settling period, the glass should be placed in a glass froster/fridge/freezer. As the final contents of the shaker are poured into the glass so the head should rise like a souffle.
ingredients:
2 shot	Speyburn 10yo Speyside single malt (from freezer)
1⁄12 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2⁄3 shot	Egg white
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: This classic, sour and aromatic cocktail is traditionally considered a morning after a pick-me-up / rejuvenative 'hair-of-the-dog'.
history:
This restorative fizz features in two 1884 books, George Winter's How to Mix Drinks and O.H Byron's The Modern Bartenders' Guide

Byron says of this drink, "To be drank immediately, or the effect will be lost. It is a morning beverage, a tonic and a nerve quieter."

name: Angel's Draft
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄4 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Agave syrup
1 dash	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
3 fresh	Mint leaves
1⁄4 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: A refreshing, minty, light cocktail with herbal complexity.
history: Adapted from the Bacardí Legacy 2010 winning cocktail, created in 2009 by Matthew Dakers at The Hoxton Pony in Shoreditch, London, England.

name: Maid in Cuba
preparation: POUR absinthe into ice-filled glass, TOP with water and leave to stand. Separately SHAKE other ingredients with ice (Don't muddle cucumber). DISCARD contents of glass (absinthe, water and ice) and STRAIN contents of shaker into absinthe-coated glass. TOP with splash of soda.
ingredients:
1⁄4 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix) (2 sugar to 1 water)
7 fresh	Mint leaves
2 slice	Cucumber (fresh)
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Tom Walker, the originator of this cocktail explains, "With the origins and popularity of the Daiquiri and the Mojito firmly rooted in the 19th and 20th century, and taking inspiration from an American-style of drink making which spawned the 'Maid' category, it was time the 21st century contributed its own version..."
history: The British Bacardí Legacy 2014 winning cocktail created by Tom Walker at The American Bar, Savoy Hotel, London, England. Tom went on to win the 2014 Bacardí Legacy Global Final with this cocktail.

name: Give Me Fever
preparation: SHAKE first 6 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. Top with a splash of tonic water.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
5⁄12 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Lavender sugar syrup
1⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: This drink combines the fever quenching G&T with medicinal lavender and flavoursome mezcal from the Mexican territories where us Brits are susceptible to "fever... give me fever. What a lovely way to burn."
history: Created 3rd May 2014 by yours truly while Fever by Peggy Lee was playing.

name: Stone Sour
garnish: Orange zest twist expressed & discarded. Adorn with skewered Luxardo Maraschino Cherry.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. (Or strain into an ice-filled old-fashioned glass.)
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review:
This Whisky Sour with a splash of orange juice is often also served over ice. It's uncommon to see stone fruit in a Stone Sour in the form of apricot liqueur, and regrettably, I didn't note where I discovered this version. However, its addition benefits this orange-influenced bourbon sour. This was my original recipe:
45ml (1½oz) Bourbon
15ml (½oz) Apricot brandy liqueur
22.5ml (¾oz) Lemon juice
15ml (½oz) Orange juice
10ml (⅓oz) Sugar syrup
3 drop Saline solution
history: The first known recipe for a "Stone Sour" appears in Jacques Straub's 1914 book Drinks, but that first iteration is a gin-based Stone Sour without the orange juice that in later decades became part of this cocktail's DNA. Straub's Stone Sour is also differentiated from later renditions by its being frappé.

name: Nuka Nuka
garnish: Pineapple & Luxardo Maraschino cherry-charged fruit stick with mint sprigs bouquet
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
3⁄4 shot	Pineapple juice
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Bitters and a touch of salt play a crucial role in this almond and pineapple fruity Rum Sour.

name: Grapefruit Whisky Fizz
preparation:
SHAKE first 6 ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and slowly pour 2/3rds of the contents of the shaker from a higher than normal height into a chilled empty glass (no ice in glass) while simultaneously pouring soda with your other hand. The cocktail and soda should form a single stream of liquid falling into the glass.

As when pouring a Guinness, to achieve a perfect head on your fizz, the cocktail should be left to settle for at least a minute before topping off with what remains in the shaker. Ideally, during the settling period, the glass should be placed in a glass froster/fridge/freezer. As the final contents of the shaker are poured into the glass so the head should rise like a souffle.
ingredients:
2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2⁄3 shot	Egg white
3 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
2 1⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Pink Grapefruit soda
review: Scotch and grapefruit sit harmoniously together in this very refreshing fizz. Be decadent, try it with breakfast.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Sam Ross at Attaboy in New York City, USA.

name: Fleur de Paradis
garnish: Edible flower (preferably elderflower when in season)
preparation: SHAKE first 6 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with sparkling wine.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
2⁄3 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Sparkling wine charged elderflower gin with a freshening touch of grapefruit and lemon juice acidity.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Kenta Goto in New York City, USA. Apparently, inspired by the bird of paradise plant (Strelitzia).

name: Negroni Amaro Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Perhaps more an Amaro Sour than it is a Negroni Sour but this a very tasty bittersweet aperitivo nonetheless.
history: Adapted from a recipe created at Farmers & Distillers restaurant in Washington DC, USA.

name: Absinthe Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄3 shot	Rhum Clément Blanc
1⁄4 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (chilled)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: It's surprising both how much absinthe you can use in this bite-sized cocktail and then how much sugar is needed to tame it. Hit the balance and all these huge flavours play together harmoniously.
history: Adapted from a cocktail made for me in September 2022 by Nate at Lulu White bar in Paris, France. Nate used a blend of light white rum and Clarin Communal Rum telling me this funky rum was key to balancing the huge favours of the absinthe. In an effort to keep my back bar in check, I used rhum blanc agricol for my funk.

name: Pauline
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄24 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
1⁄4 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: A delicate and cleansing lemon Daiquiri subtly infused with absinthe.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: B-Side
garnish: Lemon & lime slice wheels and mint sprigs bouquet
preparation: Gently MUDDLE mint in base of shaker (just to bruise). Add next 5 ingredients and SHAKE with ice. Open the shaker, add soda and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 fresh	Mint leaves
1 1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A low alc./vol. South Side Fizz pepped up and much-improved thanks to a generous splash of fino sherry.
history: Adapted from a recipe created crica 2015 by Gracy Ramirez, head bartender at Dominick's Italian restaurant in Los Angeles, California, USA.

name: Stars & Garters
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
3⁄4 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Pamplemousse liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: An agave-laced example of harmonious bittersweet and sweet 'n' sourness. Reminiscent of a Naked & Famous.
history: Adapted from a cocktail served at Atchafalaya Restaurant in New Orleans, USA.

name: Famous Last Word No. 3
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
2⁄3 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
2⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Chilled water
4 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: There are more mezcal riffs on the Last Word but tequila also works well in this classic in place of gin.
history: Adapted from a recipe discovered by Betsy Larey, a fellow Discerning Drinker, in 2023 at Pacci restaurant in the Kimpton Brice Hotel in Savannah, Georgia, USA.

name: Fall Forward
garnish: Drops of aromatic bitters dragged through the foam with a cocktail pick.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) to emulsify and fine into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Ginger liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: An autumnal-coloured apple brandy sour with warming ginger spice.
history: Adapted from a created by Julia Tunstall, the co-founder of A Bar Above, the website where this cocktail was first aired.

name: Apricot Cosmo
preparation: STIR apricot preserve with vodka until preserve dissolves. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 barspoon	Apricot jam (preserve)
1 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: The apricot preserve adds a flavoursome tang to the contemporary classic.
history: A riff on the classic Cosmopolitan cocktail created in 2004 at Aura Kitchen & Bar in London, England.

name: Barbara West
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄4 shot	Amontillado sherry
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Your choice of amontillado sherry may dramatically affect the balance of this gin and sherry sour. Choose well and you're in for a treat.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide. This classic could date from the 1930s.

name: Charles Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Navy rum (54.5% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Navy rum and triple sec add special interest to this Daiquiri.

name: Cosmopolitan Cocktail (Difford's recipe)
garnish: Flamed coin-sized orange zest twist expressed and floated on surface
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Citroen Vodka
1 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water) (optional)
review: The Cosmopolitan was originally made with citrus vodka, but it's great with unflavoured vodka or a combination of the two vodkas - my preference. For this recipe, as long as your combined vodka totals 37.5ml (1¼oz) or a splash more, you should end up with a tasty, balanced cocktail. I've previously added orange bitters, but the combination of triple sec liqueur and the bitter oil from the garnish is orangy enough. Like so many cocktails, two or three drops of saline solution help meld all harmoniously.
history: The origins of the Cosmo seem to originate in the gay bars of 1970s San Francisco, but this contemporary classic cocktail was perfected and popularised in 1990s New York City. Along the way, several bartenders played their part in its success, but perhaps TV's Sex and the City was the most influential. For the full story, see Cosmopolitan cocktail history.

name: Aku Aku
garnish: Pineapple wedge, Luxardo Maraschino cherry and mint sprig
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with a small scoop of crushed ice and fine strain into glass (push through sieve using back of a bar spoon).
ingredients:
1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Peachtree peach schnapps
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
10 fresh	Mint leaves
review: This Tiki classic looks a little like frozen stagnant pond water but tastes minty fresh and rather good.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Victor Bergeron's 1972 Trader Vic's Bartender's Guide (revised edition).

name: Brass Rail
garnish: Flamed orange zest twist (discarded) & light dusting of ground cinnamon on surface of drink
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: The cinnamon dusting which crowns this cocktail adds light spice to what is a mellow Aged Rum Daiquiri with subtle herbal complexity.
history: Adapted from a recipe by Tony Abou-Ganim who was inspired by his late cousin Helen David's penchant for a nightcap after a special occasion; her favourite was Bénédictine. Appropriately, Tony named this drink after Helen's bar, the Brass Rail in Port Huron, Michigan, USA. Helen's memory is also commemorated by the Helen David Spirit Award recognising lifetime achievements at the annual Tales of the Cocktail festival.

name: Corpse Reviver No.2 (Savoy Recipe)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix) (optional)
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review:
Well-balanced, with zesty lemon and absinthe just shining through. We've cheekily added the merest dash of sugar, but depending on your personal tastes, citrus juice and triple sec, you may want to omit this.

Harry originally stipulated Kina Lillet, but as this is no longer available, I've used Lillet Blanc. You can also use dry vermouth or preferably a kina aromatised-wine.
history: Adapted from Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Fog Cutter (Bramble style)
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. DRIZZLE cherry brandy over drink and serve with straws.
ingredients:
1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄4 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
review: A well-balanced (neither too strong nor too sweet), short, fruity drink which is reminiscent of the modern-day Bramble.

name: Georgia Mint Julep
preparation: ADD first 5 ingredients to glass and two-thirds fill with crushed ice. CHURN (stir) with bar spoon and then FILL glass with more crushed ice. TOP with soda, briefly stir and serve.
ingredients:
12 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Peachtree peach schnapps
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Bourbon, peach and mint flavours combine harmoniously in this cooling cocktail.
history:
This classic was originally made with peach brandy in place of peach liqueur. It is also sometimes made with apricot brandy.

The contentious history of the Julepand variantions on the classic Mint Julep.

name: Grapefruit Julep
preparation: STIR honey with vodka in base of shaker until honey dissolves. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 barspoon	Honey
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
4 fresh	Mint leaves
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: Wonderfully refreshing. Bring on the sun.
history:
Created by Dale DeGroff, New York City, USA.

The contentious history of the Julep, along with its variants can be found on our page.

name: Hot Toddy (Hot Scotch & Lemon)
garnish: Lemon slice on rim with cinnamon stick in glass
preparation: POUR all ingredients into pre-warmed glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 dried	Clove
2 shot	Boiling water
review: The faintly smoky flavours of Scotch add spice to this warming drink that's great when you're feeling down with a cold or the flu.
history: Lost in time but Dickens refers to a "Whisky Toddy" in The Pickwick Papers.

name: Lemongrad
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with tonic and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Citroen Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: A great summer afternoon drink. Fresh lemon with elderflower and tonic.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2002 by Alex Kammerling in London, England.

name: Liquorice Whisky Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄4 shot	Liquorice liqueur
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Liquorice dramatically changes the classic Sour, working harmoniously with the Scotch. I have also tried with bourbon and the result is not nearly so pleasing.
history: Created in 2006 by Tony Conigliaro at Shochu Lounge, London, England.

name: Pear & Cardamom Sidecar
preparation: MUDDLE cardamom in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 whole	Green cardamom pods
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Pear & cognac liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A wonderful meld of aromatic ingredients. The combination of delicate cardamom spice and rich pear gives this cocktail an autumnal/winter feel.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2002 by Jason Scott at Oloroso in Edinburgh, Scotland.
See: Sidecar history and variations

name: Pineapple & Cardamom Daiquiri
preparation: MUDDLE cardamom in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
4 whole	Green cardamom pods
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 3⁄4 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
4 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters (optional)
review: One of the tastiest Daiquiris we've tried.
history: Adapted from Henry Besant's excellent Pineapple & Cardamom Martini.

name: Pineapple Margarita
garnish: Lime juice and Tajín seasoning rim. Float a dehydrated pineapple slice wheel or adorn with a pineapple wedge on rim.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄6 shot	Pineapple sugar syrup (optional)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: As advertised, a Margarita with pineapple fruitiness. If you have it, a splash of pineapple syrup helps balance while amplifying the pineapple flavour.

name: Stairs Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Pear juice (freshly pressed)
1 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: In London's cockney rhyming slang 'apples and pears' means stairs. Thus this tasty cocktail is appropriately named.
history: Created in 2000 by Ian Baldwin at the GE Club, London, England

name: Union Club
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Balanced sweet and sour with bourbon to the fore. Some, including my hero David Embury, stipulate making this cocktail with a straight rye whiskey. However, having tried rye against bourbon in this cocktail and I prefer the richness of a wheat-rich bourbon over a spicy rye.
history: Adapted from a recipe in David A. Embury's 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks.

name: Zamboanga 'Zeinie'
garnish: Lime zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Pineapple sugar syrup
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: I described our previous version of this classic as "Reminiscent of a tropical Sidecar." The recipe above is more fitting for this classic, but if you preferred the tropical version, it comprised 60ml cognac, 7.5ml maraschino cherry syrup, 30ml pineapple juice, 15ml lime juice, and 2 dashes of aromatic bitters.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Charles H. Baker, Jr.'s 1939 The Gentleman's Companion volume II – An Exotic Drinking Book. He describes this as "another palate twister from the land where the Monkeys Have No Tails. This drink found its way down through the islands to Mindanao from Manila..."

name: Daiquiri No. 2
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄6 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water) (optional)
review: A Daiquiri with subtle orange notes, but far from being a mere Orange Daiquiri.
history: Created circa 1915 by created by Constantino "Constante" Ribalaïgua Vert, who owned Havana's famous El Floridita from 1918 to 1952, this is the second of four numbered daiquiris in the 1934 1st edition Bar La Florida Cocktails, menu book.

name: Daiquiri No. 4
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with finely crushed ice and strain into chilled glass. (Classically blended rather than served straight-up.)
ingredients:
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Lime (fresh)
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water) (optional)
review: Maraschino cherry liqueur adds delicate notes to this finely balanced golden rum-based Daiquiri.
history: Created by Constantino "Constante" Ribalaïgua Vert, who bartended at Havana's famous El Floridita (originally Bar Florida) from circa 1914 to his death in 1952. (He purchased the bar in 1918.) This is the fourth of four numbered daiquiris in the 1934 1st edition Bar La Florida Cocktails menu book from his bar.

name: Don's Delight
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Patrón Añejo tequila
1⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄4 shot	Disaronno amaretto
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Named due to originally being made with Don Julio 1942.
history: Created in 2008 by Brian Van Flandern in New York City, USA.

name: Fallen Angel
garnish: Mint leaf or float tip of mint sprig
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	Giffard Peppermint Pastille crème de menthe
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Gin-laced zesty citrus with subtle freshening mint with aromatic bitters adding depth of flavour and complexity.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Pastis Whisky Sour
garnish: Lemon slice & Luxardo Maraschino cherry on stick (sail)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄3 shot	Pastis
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Pastis adds a pleasing hint of anise and liquorice to a classic Scotch Whisky Sour.
history: Created in 2006 by yours truly.

name: Lorraine
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Kirschwasser (cherry) eau-de-vie
2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
2⁄3 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Sweet and sour with fruity, herbal notes.

name: Sol Ardiente
preparation: MUDDLE peppercorns in base of shaker. Add next four ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with splash soda.
ingredients:
1 barspoon	Pink peppercorns
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Pineapple juice
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Red pepper and pineapple influences this twisted Daiquiri.
history: Created in 2008 by Anthony Farrell, San-greal Bartending Ltd, Belfast, Northern Ireland. The name translates from Spanish as 'Burning Sun'.

name: Will Of Alan
preparation: DRY SHAKE all ingredients without ice. Add ice, SHAKE again and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Pineapple juice
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Old-fashioned / old time bitters
1⁄4 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Fantastic, spiced, tiki-style twisted Daiquiri.
history: Discovered in 2008 at Tonic, Edinburgh, Scotland.

name: Corpse Reviver No.2 (Duffy's recipe)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Swedish Punsch liqueur
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: For an equal parts recipe, this Corpse Reviver variation is brilliantly balanced. It's also a delicious cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Patrick Gavin Duffy's 1956 Official Mixer's Manual. This recipe features Swedish Punch whereas the recipe in his 1934 first edition calls for Kina Lillet.

name: The Bird Is The Word No. 2
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Bepi Tosolini Grappa di Moscato
3⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
4 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: A grappa-based Last Word by way of Denmark.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2009/10 Mikael Melzer Nilsson while a bar manager at Salon 39 in Copenhagen, Denmark.
See: Last Word history

name: The Hac
preparation: MUDDLE cardamom in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 fresh	Green cardamom pods
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Agave syrup
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Perhaps better billed as being a 'Pineapple and Cardamom Margarita'.
history: Discovered in 2009 at Cloud 23, Manchester, England.

name: Highland Sazerac
preparation: POUR Chartreuse into glass and twirl to coat inside with liqueur, fill glass with ice and stand to one side. Separately, STIR other ingredients with ice in mixing glass. DISCARD contents of glass (Chartreuse and ice), fill with fresh ice and strain contents of mixing glass.
ingredients:
1⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Speyburn 10yo Speyside single malt
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A dash of malt gives a Highland influence to the Sazerac, also given a herbal note due to a generous splash of Chartreuse.
history:
Adapted from a recipe crearted by Don Lee at PDT in New York City, USA. Don's original recipe calls for yellow Chartreuse.
Sazerac cocktail history

name: Money Penny
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
4 drop	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Dry gin soured with a splash of fresh grapefruit juice and balanced with the merest touch of sugar.
history: Adapted from a recipe discovered in 2010 at the Blue Owl in New York City, USA.

name: Sourise
preparation: DRY SHAKE all ingredients (without ice) to emulsify. SHAKE again with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5 fresh	Raspberries
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Almond, cognac and raspberry harmoniously sit together to flavour this sour-style cocktail.
history: Created in 2010 by David Wondrich and named 'Sourise' after the French for 'smile'.

name: Holland House (Craddock's London dry gin-based)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Without the optional addition of sugar syrup, this cocktail is very dry. Even with sugar, this cocktail is on the dry side and makes for a great aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Sharman-Cox Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Blue Curaçao
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: A foam-topped blue riff on two classic cocktails which honours two men named Cox as well as our friend Hannah Sharman-Cox.
history:
Adapted from a drink created in 2013 at the Rum Kitchen, Notting Hill, London. The name 'Cox' is a common theme to this drink:

1. It is inspired by the Perfect Lady, a classic cocktail created in 1936 by Sidney Cox, a bartender at the Grosvenor House, London for The British Empire Cocktail Competition where it took the 1st Prize.

2. The original Daiquiri, said to be created in 1898 by Jennings Cox, an American mining engineer working at a tin mine near the Cuban town of Daiquiri.

3. Most importantly, this drink was created and named to honour the fabulous Hannah Sharman-Cox of London Cocktail Week fame.

name: Blood Orange Margarita
garnish: Half salt rim and blood orange slice
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄6 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Blood orange juice
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Notes of tequila, orangey triple sec, bittersweet liqueur, blood orange and lime juice all sit in perfect kilter in this tasty riff on the classic Margarita.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2000 by Ben Davidson in Sydney, Australia.
Margarita cocktail history.

name: New York Sour cocktail
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into ice-filled glass. DRIZZLE red wine around the surface of the drink.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
1⁄2 shot	Claret red wine (chilled)
review:
A classic bourbon-based Whiskey Sour made more interesting – both visually and in flavour by the addition of a float of red wine.

Egg white is not classically used in a New York Sour but some prefer this drink with the mouthfeel and change of appearance egg white imparts.

British bartenders may prefer the following formula based on UK measures:
50 ml Bourbon whiskey
25 ml Lemon juice
12.5 ml Sugar syrup (2:1)
1 dash Angostura bitters
12.5 ml Egg white (optional)
12.5 ml Claret red wine
history:
Thought to have been first made in the 1880s by a bartender in Chicago, this drink was originally named the Continental Sour and then Southern Whiskey Sour, also masquerading as a Brunswick Sour and Claret Snap before becoming best known as the New York Sour, probably after a bartender in Manhattan started serving the drink and made it popular. It first appears in print under the New York Sour name in print in the 1934 Mr. Boston Bartender's Guide.
History of Sours family of cocktails and more recipies

name: Other Word
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Agave syrup
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Mezcal fortifies this Californian riff on the Last Word.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created by Eric Alperin at The Varnish in Los Angeles, California. Eric's original recipe, as published in his 2020 book Unvarnished, calls for:
60ml (2oz) Mezcal
30ml (1oz) Lime juice
7.5ml (¼oz) Yellow Chartreuse
7.5ml (¼oz) Maraska Maraschino Cherry Liqueur
5ml (barspoon) Agave syrup.

name: English Marmalade (a.k.a. Hawksmoor Marmalade Martini)
preparation: STIR 4 flat barspoons marmalade with other ingredients in base of shaker to dissolve the marmalade. SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
4 barspoon	Orange marmalade
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄6 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: The addition of bitter liqueur and aromatic bitters to the classic 1930 recipe from The Savoy Cocktail Book, lifts the Marmalade Cocktail to a new level of bittersweet complexity.
history: Adapted from a recipe discovered in 2013 at Hawksmoor in Spitalfields, London, England. Huw Gott, Hawksmoor's co-founder, says the cocktail went on the menu soon after the restaurant and bar opened in 2006.

name: Mountain Man
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Crème de Pêche de Vigne liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Maple syrup
1⁄6 shot	Ginger syrup
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: A peachy Whiskey Sour with a mild ginger kick.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Natasha David at Nitecap in New York City, USA.

name: The Saint
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄6 shot	Ginger syrup
review: A riff on the classic Brown Derby, this is a refreshing bourbon sour with zesty citrus and subtle warming earthy ginger.
history: Created in 2015 by Karen Grill at Sassafras Saloon in Los Angeles, USA

name: The Cab
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
8 fresh	Mint leaves
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 2⁄3 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: A minty limey cognac sour invigorated with champagne.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Andres Walters at The Lobo Plantation in Sydney, Australia.

name: Parmenides
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
2⁄3 shot	Chardonnay (Chablis) white wine
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
4 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: A sour-style drink served straight-up combining cognac, Green Chartreuse, white wine and lemon.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Fabiano Latham when he was at The Natural Philosopher, London, England. Parmenides was a 6th century BC Greek philosopher, appropriate considering the name of Alban’s bar.

name: Triomphe d'Anis (Triumph of Aniseed)
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & float star anise
preparation: RINSE glass with absinthe. STIR other ingredients with ice and strain into absinthe rinsed glass.
ingredients:
1⁄6 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 dried	Star anise
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1⁄4 shot	Fino sherry
review: A boozy stirred sipper, perhaps after-dinner cognac-based cocktail, with hints of anise coffee and dry sherry complexity.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Isaac Windsor at The Milk Thistle, Bristol, England.

name: Perfume Daiquiri
preparation: POUR all ingredients into shaker and STIR to incorporate honey. SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
5⁄6 shot	Elderflower liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
4 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
4 fresh	Mint leaves
1 barspoon	Honey
history: Argentinean Bacardí Legacy 2015 winning cocktail by Ezequiel Rodríguez, Victoria Brown Bar, Buenos Aires.

name: Kentucky Buck
preparation: MUDDLE strawberry in base of shaker. Add next 4 ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with ginger beer.
ingredients:
1 fresh	Strawberries (hulled, small & ripe)
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
Top up with	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: A tall, strawberry influenced bourbon sour with a subtle spicy hint of ginger.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2009 by Erick Castro at Bourbon & Branch, San Francisco, USA.

name: Sour Grapes
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineau des Charentes blanc
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 fresh	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A bourbon whiskey sour with a splash of pineau des charentes providing the grape influence.
history: Adapted from a straight-up bourbon based recipe created by Robb Jones at Bellecour Bar in Wayzata, Minnesota, USA.

name: Suze-Ann Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: A bittersweet, gentian-influenced riff on a classic White Lady.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2017 by Dom Saunders and Simone Nelli at Cinnamon Club in London, England. (I took the liberty of adding egg white to their recipe.)

name: Mariposa
garnish: Half cherry tomato & small basil sprig on rim
preparation: MUDDLE tomato in base of shaker and then muddle basil leaves. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 fresh	Cherry tomato (fresh) (chopped)
4 fresh	Basil leaves
1 2⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄6 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: This rum-laced cocktail has attractive savoury flavours with a tangy sourness and floral elderflower.
history: Created by Robb Collins, Group Head Bartender at London Cocktail Club, London, England, who told us he made it for the 2015 Bacardi Legacy UK Finals. "Inspired by a fictional love story of an American soldier who falls in love with a French Cuban girl called 'Mariposa' during WWII."

name: First Post
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a spear of ice). TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Pale green in colour with a refreshing bitter/sour sweet profile.
history:
This cocktail was published in an article called The Golden Cocktail Mile for the release of the 2013 World's End film comic science fiction film. It is named after the first pub on the bar crawl that Simon Peg and co. embark on in the film.

Created in 2013 by Alastair Walker, then at The Everleigh in Melbourne, Australia.

name: Tropicalia
garnish: Bouquet of Gypsophila (Baby's Breath) & cocktail umbrella
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
1⁄2 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Banana tea
2⁄3 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Delicately spiced with cacao and coffee sitting atop a basket of fruit (overripe banana, pineapple and lime).
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Sufian Mahmoud, Sugar Sand (Hotel Indigo Seminyak), Bali, Indonesia.

name: Ce Soir (This Evening)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
5⁄12 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Brandy-based, bittersweet and herbal. A good after-dinner digestif.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2010 by Nicole Lebedevitch at The Hawthorne, Boston, USA.

name: Tsipouro Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 5⁄6 shot	O/Purist Tsipouro
1⁄3 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Falernum adds delicate clove spice to this delicious sour which as the name suggests beautifully harnesses the complex flavour of tsipouro.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Thanos Prunarus at Baba Au Rum in Athens, Greece.

name: Maria Soto Robbins
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & float 3 coffee beans
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 dash	Bob's Chocolate bitters
3 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: We've added a splash of water to 'open' up this subtly coffee and cacao riff on a classic Daiquiri.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Ian Burrell.

name: 100 Year Old Cigar
preparation: RINSE chilled glass with absinthe and set to one side. STIR other ingredients with ice and fine strain into pre-prepared glass.
ingredients:
1⁄12 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 2⁄3 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1⁄6 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Stirred down and boozy so suited to late night sipping. This cocktail has broader appeal when served on-the-rocks in an old-fashioned glass, either way it is cigar-like and suits being accompanied by one.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Carey Jones' 2016 Brooklyn Bartender: A Modern Guide to Cocktails and Spirits.

name: Clean Aviation
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 3⁄4 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Crème de violette liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄4 shot	Chilled water
review: Named in homage to the laudable quest for a clean aviation fuel, this is a classic Aviation (usually based on gin) but made with vodka and given a touch of extra complexity with the merest hint of absinthe.
history: Created in November 2020 by yours truly as a result of a comment left by Julie Kovar on our Aviation page.

name: Mr. Bali Hai
garnish: Pineapple wedge, mint sprigs bouquet & 3 coffee beans
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass/mug filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Jamaican aged blended rum with funk
1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Full-flavoured rum and pineapple with delicate coffee and a refreshing zing of lemon citrus.
history:
This cocktail takes its name from, and was originally served in a mug modelled after, the carved wooden statue that still stands (restored in 2010) proudly at the entrance to the Bali Hai Restaurant in Shelter Island, San Diego, USA.

Meaning "Your own special island" and perhaps named after the song titled Bali Ha'i from the 1949 musical, South Pacific, Bali Hai opened in 1955 after Tom Ham, an accountant, took on the task of saving the last outpost of The Hut restaurant franchise. This remains the restaurant's signature cocktail.

To quote Jeff "Beachbum" Berry's 2010 Remixed, "Since the Bali Hai opened in 1955, this drink has gone through several incarnations." The recipe above, like so many other adaptations, is based on one from Jeff's book.

A more recent tribute to the original is by Kevin Beary at Chicago's Three Dots and a Dash:

Mr. Bali Hai
Serve in: Tiki mug/Collins glass
Garnish: Pineapple wedge, mint sprigs bouquet & 3 coffee beans
Method: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass/mug filled with crushed ice.
25 ml Black Strap rum
25 ml Madeira Malmsey
25 ml Coffee liqueur
7.5 ml Spiced rum
7.5 ml Dark Jamaican rum
7.5 ml Falernum
25 ml Pineapple juice
25 ml Lemon juice
2 dashes Tiki bitters

name: Night Cap (Sloppy Joe's 1935)
garnish: Express and then float coin-sized orange zest twist
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water) (optional)
review: This sweet 'n' sour, gin and cognac-laced cocktail is perhaps more suited to be enjoyed as an aperitivo, or even with breakfast, than the nightcap the name suggests. Unless you have a very sweet white cacao then the recipe needs the bar spoon of sugar syrup I've added for balance.
history: Adapted from a recipe in a 1935 souvenir pamphlet from the famous Sloppy Joe's bar in Havana, Cuba (courtesy of Beachbum Berry's Potions of the Caribbean).

name: Cardamom Daiquiri
garnish: Lime zest twist (discarded) & lime wedge on rim
preparation: Cut zest from your lime for garnish prior to squeezing for juice. MUDDLE cardamom in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3 dried	Green cardamom pods
1 2⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
4 drop	Bob's Cardamom bitters
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water
review: A charcoal-filtered light rum works best as more full-bodied rums simply don't sit well with the cardamon. Hit the right balance with the right rum and this delicately cardamon-influenced daiquiri is delicious.
