history: Adapted from a recipe created in January 2021 by Richard Godwin in Bristol, England this recipe is based on yours truly's 10:3:2 Daiquiri formula.

name: Ether
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	O/Purist Tsipouro
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄6 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Tsipouro combines harmoniously with pineapple juice supported by complex herbal notes from Chartreuse with a hint of orange.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Argyris Mastrogianidis at Funky Monkey in Kozani, Greece, this was one of ten winning recipes in the 2021 O/Purist Quest. He says, "The inspiration of the cocktail comes from what the O/Purist Tsipouro stands for, a Greek modern distillate that wants to give a new point of view and proposal for our traditional distillate, tsipouro."

name: Slow & Unsteady
garnish: Basil leaf and 3 drops of aromatic bitters
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and finer strain into a chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
5 fresh	Basil leaves
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Basil-infused herbal sour perhaps best enjoyed as an after-dinner digestif.

name: Whiskey Daisy No.3
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. TOP with a slash of soda.
ingredients:
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
5⁄6 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A Whiskey Sour made Daisy-like with a hint of almond.

name: Steel Drum
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	White overproof rum
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Rum funk and maraschino influences this Daiquiri's beat. Jason calls for this to be served straight-up in a coupe but I prefer with the dilution afforded by serving on-the-rock(s), perhaps in a drum-shaped old-fashioned glass.
history: Adapted from a recipe by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford.

name: The Smoke Also Rises
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Rabarbaro liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A bittersweet riff on a Hemingway Special .
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2020 by Orestes Cruz at Empire State South restaurant in Atlanta, Georgia, USA. Originally made with Cappelletti Sfumato Rabarbaro.

name: Cutter
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Amaro CioCiaro
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A riff on a Paper Plane.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Alec Bales at the Ticonderoga Club in Atlanta, USA. Originally based on St. George Spirits' B&E American Whiskey.

name: The Carlsbaek
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄2 shot	Averna Amaro
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1⁄3 shot	Bigallet China China Amer
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Mezcal and bittersweet coffee, freshened with zesty citrus.
history: Adapted from a recipe left by Morten Carlsbaek, a fellow Discerning Drinker, who shared this recipe on our Pura Vida cocktail page. I named the cocktail after its creator.

name: Albemarle Fizz
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker (no need to muddle raspberries). DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain half the contents of the shaker into chilled glass (no ice in glass). POUR half the soda water into glass and then STRAIN the rest of the contents of the shaker into glass. Leave to stand until the white frothy head forms a clear line above the pale red base. Then POUR rest of soda water to raise the soufflé-like foaming head.
ingredients:
3 fresh	Raspberries
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white
2 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Light, fluffy and fruity. Like drinking gin-laced Angel Delight.
history: The Albemarle Fizz first appears in the 1934 Old Mr. Boston Bartender's Guide.

name: Mist & Mysterious
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
5⁄6 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Floral peaty whisky with bittersweet gentian and refreshing lemon juice, invigorated with a splash of soda.
history: Created in April 2023 by yours truly at The Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Misty Auld Fashioned
garnish: Mist with 3 sprays of peated whisky
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
2⁄3 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
8 drop	Bob's Ginger Bitters
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A splash of lemon juice mystifies this peated whisky Old Fashioned with delicate warming ginger spice.
history: Created in April 2023 by yours truly at The Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Vino Orancio Margarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
3⁄4 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
3⁄4 shot	Savoia Orancio
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Agave syrup
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Bittersweet notes from Savoia Orancio sit brilliantly with mezcal and tequila in this Margarita riff.
history: Created in September 2023 by yours truly after Roberta Mariani, Italspirits Advocacy Director, professed how well Savoia Orancio combines with agave spirits.

name: J & Tony's Hot Negroni
preparation: POUR all ingredients into pre-warmed heat-proof glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 2⁄3 shot	Boiling water
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Ewan Bennie at J & Tony's Discount Cured Meats And Negroni Warehouse in San Diego, California, USA. Originally made with Cocchi Storico Vermouth di Torino.

name: Sidecar Royale
garnish: Orange juice and sugar rim (on one side of glass). Adorn with an orange zest twist.
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with sparkling wine.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
1⁄2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: A classic Sidecar with an added splash of sparkle, and all the better for it.
history: The Sidecar cocktail first appears in Robert Vermeire's 1922 Cocktails How To Mix Them with a fizz invigorated Sidecar following in the United Kingdom Bartenders' Guild's 1937 Approved Cocktails.

name: Pink Margarita
garnish: Pink grapefruit juice and sea salt rim
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. TOP with pink grapefruit soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
1 1⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Pink Grapefruit soda
review: This Margarita with pink grapefruit soda is made pink and flavoured with a couple of dashes Creole bitters.
history: Adapted from a similar recipe promoted by Cointreau by yours truly in February 2024.

name: Industry Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) to emulsify and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Herbal, bittersweet and sour. Being a 'Sour', it seemed fitting to add a few drops of saline and a splash of egg white.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2011 by Ted Kilgore at Taste by Niche in St. Louis, USA, for a fellow bartender visiting the bar. His original recipe is equal parts Fernet-Branca, Green Chartreuse, lime juice and simple syrup.

name: Plaza Vieja
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1 shot	Lucano amaro
1⁄3 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A spirit-forward and bittersweet digestive with pleasing herbal overtures.
history:
Plaza Vieja is Spanish for 'old square' and this cocktail is a riff on the classic Vieux Carré, old square in French.

Adapted from a recipe created in 2013 by Joe Cammarata and Sam Treadway at Backbar, Somerville, MA, USA. Originally made with Braulio Amaro.

name: Kiss the Boys Goodbye
garnish: 3 drops aromatic bitters drawn through foam head
preparation: DRY SHAKE all ingredients (without ice) to emulsify. SHAKE again with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
3⁄4 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: A sour showcasing how well cognac and sloe gin play together.
history: Named after the 1941 musical comedy film of the same name, starring Mary Martin, Don Ameche and Oscar Levant, released in August 1941. This cocktail was probably created soon after the film's release and features in the 1949 book Esquire's Handbook for Hosts.

name: Cherry Blossom Daiquiri
garnish: Skewered Luxardo Maraschino cherry with cherry blossom when in season
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Cherry blossom/sakura syrup
1⁄4 shot	Chilled water
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: As the name suggests, a Daiquiri with cherry and floral notes.
history: Created by yours truly in April 2024 at the Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: Negroni Flip
preparation: DRY SHAKE all ingredients (without ice) to emulsify. SHAKE again with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
1 whole	Egg (white & yolk)
review:
Bittersweetness rounded and made wholesome by the addition of an egg. If you like Negronis, be sure to sample this cocktail's flip side.

Depending on your tolerance for bitterness, you may want to up the rich sugar syrup to 5ml (1 barspoon).

name: North Beach Cooler
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 1⁄4 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: As the name suggests, this low-alcohol, tequila-laced, bittersweet Cooler is suited to summer drinking. All the better when enjoyed on the beach.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2018 by Priscilla Leonga bartender from Melbourne who won that years Australian Speed Rack competition with this cocktail. The North Beach Cooler is one of more than 100 Speed Rack recipes featured in the 2024 book North Beach Cooler.

name: Tequila Stone Sour
garnish: Skewered half orange slice wheel and Luxardo cherry (sail)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Agave syrup
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: I prefer a reposado tequila in this sour but I'm sure others will argue for the freshness and purity of a blanco.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Vincent Sardi Jr. & George Shea's 1988 Sardi's Bar Guide.

name: Rum Stone Sour
garnish: Skewered half orange slice wheel and Luxardo cherry (sail)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A great sour with one rum, but perhaps try a split base of rums.
history:
Adapted from a recipe in Vincent Sardi Jr. & George Shea's 1988 Sardi's Bar Guide.
As for the origins of this cocktail, David Wondrich says "in 1972, the O.J.-and-Bacardi version starts appearing in the Chicago suburbs, whence it spreads to the rest of the Midwest, California, and eventually Sardi's, right there on little old West 44 Street. Back in Greater Chicago, it apparently began as a golf course and country club drink, but beyond that its origin was unknown.

name: Césaire's Last Word
garnish: Lime zest twist expressed and discarded. Adorn with skewered Luxardo Maraschino Cherries.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Rhum Clément Blanc
2⁄3 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
2⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A rhum agricole-based Last Word.
history:
Created in August 2024 by your truly to a recipe suggested by Chris Brislawn, a fellow Discerning Drinker, on our Wordsmith page.
Named after Martinique's most famous writer, Aimé Césaire (1913-2008). Poet, playwright, and politician, he co-founded the Négritude movement, which sought to reclaim black identity and culture in the face of colonialism. His works, including the book-length 1939 poem Cahier d'un retour au pays natal (Notebook of a Return to the Native Land), had a profound influence on Francophone literature and post-colonial thought. His influence extended beyond Martinique, making him a central figure in Caribbean literature and politics.

name: Apple Brandy Sour
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) and garnish with a skewered lemon slice wheel and Luxardo Maraschino cherry sail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Sour by name - balanced sweet and sour apple by nature.

name: Applesinth
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2⁄3 shot	Apple Schnapps liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Hints of apple and liquorice combine to make a very moreish cocktail.
history: Created in 1999 by Alex Kammerling in London, England.

name: Autumn Cocktail
preparation: Cut passion fruit in half and scoop out the flesh into shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. (You shouldn't need to dry shake to achieve desired foam head.)
ingredients:
1 fresh	Passion fruit (fresh)
2 shot	Bison grass vodka
1 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Passion fruit syrup
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: An easy-drinking, fruity cocktail with grassy hints courtesy of bison vodka.
history: Created in 2004 by yours truly and inspired by Max Warner's excellent Autumn Punch. In keeping with every cocktail served straight-up and in a Marting glass in those days, this was originally named Autum Marini, it was an Alternatini.

name: Aviation Cocktail (Difford's recipe)
garnish: Lemon zest twist (& optional sugar rim)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Crème de violette liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review:
Citrus, floral gin with a slightly sour finish.

The recipe above has been my preferred recipe for some years. However, in early 2020, I decided that the maraschino and violet were overly dominant so in a quest for harmony I reduced these to allow botanical gin notes to emerge. I then rebalanced with 5ml sugar:
- 45 ml Dry gin
- 12.5 ml Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
- 5 ml Crème de violette
- 15 ml Lemon juice
- 5 ml Sugar syrup
- 10 ml Chilled water (omit if wet ice)
Thanks to the emails and comments below, I came to my senses and reverted to my original recipe.
history: An adaptation of Hugo R. Ensslin's Aviation Cocktail from his 1916 Recipes for Mixed Drinks by yours truly.

name: Basil Bramble Sling
preparation: MUDDLE basil in base of shaker. Add rest of ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. Serve with straws.
ingredients:
7 fresh	Basil leaves
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Crème de Mûre liqueur
review: Wonderfully refreshing and balanced.
history: Created in 2003 by Alexandra Fiot at Lonsdale House bar in London, UK. Inspired by Dick Bradsell's Bramble cocktail

name: Big Apple Sour Martini
garnish: Skewered Luxardo Maraschino cherry & green apple slices
preparation: SHAKE All ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 1⁄4 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A delicious and beautifully balanced apple sour, all the better when made with freshly pressed Granny Smith apple juice.

name: Blimey
garnish: Fresh blackberry sat heroically atop crushed ice summit (it survived the muddler to reach its peak)
preparation: MUDDLE blackberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into glass filled with crushed ice. Serve with a cut-down paper straw.
ingredients:
5 fresh	Blackberries
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: This vodka-laced "Blackberry and lime(y) summer cooler is both fruity and (hopefully) aptly named.
history: Created in 2002 by yours truly in London, England.

name: Brandy Fix
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄6 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
review: This wonderful classic is slightly on the tart side of well-balanced.

name: Angel's Share No.1
preparation: STIR heaped spoon of orange marmalade with cognac in base of shaker until marmalade dissolves. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 barspoon	Orange marmalade
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄4 shot	Licor 43 Original liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Tangy citrus fruit and cognac smoothed with a hint of vanilla.
history: Created in 2005 by Milo Rodriguez, London.

name: Bajan Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 barspoon	Powdered sugar (white sugar ground in mortar and pestle) (optional)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water
review: A full-flavoured Daiquiri with a delicate touch of clove.
history: Created in 2006 by yours truly in London, England.

name: Basil Gimlet
preparation: MUDDLE basil in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
6 fresh	Basil leaves
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Lime cordial (sweetened lime juice)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Balanced tangy citrus, fresh basil and gin botanical complexity.
history: Greg Lindgren is credited with creating the basil-infused riff on the classic Gimlet in 2006 at Rye in San Francisco, but this recipe is adapted from the Basil Gimlet we discovered the same year at Stella in Boston, USA. This recipe combines fresh lime and lime cordial (part of a Gimlet's DNA) while Greg's used fresh lime juice and simple syrup.

name: Daiquiri De Luxe
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Caribbean Pineapple liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
review: A standard Daiquiri turned premium and given a touch of Tiki with added notes of almond and pineapple.
history: Adapted from a recipe in David Embury's 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks which calls for "1 part Orgeat or Crème d'Ananas; 2 parts Citrus Juice made by mixing the juice of one large Lemon with that of three or four large Limes; 8 parts Cuban White Label Bacardi or Havana Club Rum."

name: Dino Sour
garnish: Lemon slice & Luxardo Maraschino cherry on stick (sail)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Dark/black/blackstrap rum
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Two diverse rums combine brilliantly in this classic sour.
history: A detailed history of the Sours family of cocktails is available on our Sours cocktails page.

name: Four W Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Maple syrup
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: The oomph of rum, the sourness of grapefruit and the richness of maple syrup, all aromatised by bitters.

Cosmopolitan cocktail history and recipe variations

name: Greta Garbo
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Aniseed (anise) liqueur
review: A deliciously clean and cleansing Daiquiri with delicate notes of maraschino and anise.
history:
The origins of this cocktail are unknown but it is named after the Swedish film actress and Hollywood star. Born Greta Lovisa Gustafsson on the 18th September 1905, Greta Garbo received three Academy Award nominations for Best Actress and an honorary one in 1954. She was ranked the fifth greatest female star of all time by the American Film Institute in 1999, behind Katharine Hepburn, Bette Davis, Audrey Hepburn, and Ingrid Bergman.

Garbo's career launched with the 1924 Swedish film, The Saga of Gosta Berling. Although her role was minor, her performance caught the attention of Louis B. Mayer, chief executive of Metro Goldwyn Mayer (MGM) who signed her to his studio in 1925. The next year she appeared in MGM's silent film, Torrent, then Flesh and the Devil in 1926, which propelled her to international stardom. Garbo's first talking film was Anna Christie (1930) which MGM marketed with the catch-phrase "Garbo talks!". Garbo retired from the screen after the failure of Two-Faced Woman in 1941 at the age of 35 having appeared in 28 films. An avid art collector, she never married, had no children and lived alone shunning publicity. Greta Garbo died 15th April 1990.

name: Harvey Wallbanger
preparation: STIR first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. FLOAT Galliano on the surface.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
2 1⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
5⁄12 shot	Galliano L'Autentico liqueur
review:
One of the most famous cocktails from the 1970s, the Harvey Wallbanger is a Screwdriver (vodka and orange juice served tall over ice) with a float of Galliano liqueur. It was a huge cocktail in its era, but its reign barely made it into the 1980s as it fell prey to changes in fashion, packaged juice and even Galliano.

The original style of Galliano, Galliano L'Autentico, was changed by marketeers who reduced its alcohol content from a robust 42.3% to 35% alc./vol., in the 1970s and then eventually to 30% alc./vol., in the 1990s when the flavour profile was also changed with vanilla predominating. Thankfully Galliano L'Autentico was reintroduced in 2006 and now sits alongside the more modern version Galliano Vanilla. Both are fine liqueurs, but it is Galliano L'Autentico that you'll need for an authentic Harvey Wallbanger.

This is a cocktail that must be made with freshly squeezed orange juice. You may be too lazy to squeeze orange juice for breakfast, but at a hotel or bar you'll have experienced how good freshly squeezed juice can be. It's a very different experience from the comparatively sweet and marmaladey packaged orange juices. Add a splash of vodka and the aromatic herbal peppermint freshness the float of Galliano brings to this tall, refreshing cocktail, and you can start to see why the Harvey Wallbanger was such a hit in the 1970s.

A Harvey Wallbanger is traditionally made without sugar syrup or bitters but is a better drink with them. And beware, shaking (rather than stirring) the first four ingredients makes the drink too thin.
history:
Legend has it that 'Harvey' - Tom Harvey was a surfer at Manhattan Beach, California. His favourite drink was a Screwdriver with added Galliano - the ingredients that comprise a Harvey Wallbanger. One day in the late 1960s, while celebrating winning a surfing competition, he staggered from bar to bar, banging his surfboard on the walls, leading to the name of this contemporary classic cocktail.

However, a competing story credits the drink's creation to Bill Donner, the host of a house party held in the mid-1960s in Newport Beach, California. One of the guests, Harvey, was found banging his head the next morning, complaining of the hangover this drink induced.

We have booze historian Robert Simonson to thank for his investigations into the true origins of what was one of the most popular drinks of the 1970s. He unearthed a piece in The Hartford Courant published 3rd September 1977 titled Retired Mixologist To Teach Tunxis Drink-Making Class at Tunxis Community College which goes on to say, "... it's not the mix that makes a drink, but the mixer, says the instructor of the noncredit course, Donato 'Duke' Antone. He is the creator of the Harvey Wallbanger and more than 50 nationally consumed drinks."

So there you have it, written evidence. However, Robert Simonson expresses some scepticism but does theorise that Antone created the cocktail while working as a drinks marketing consultant for George Bednar, the Marketing Director of McKesson Imports Co. during the late 1960s, the then US importers of Galliano Liqueur. This theory is helped by a sentence in the same 1977 Hartford Courant piece, "Antone...has not limited himself to mixing drinks. Rather, he has been active in all aspects of the liquor industry, ranging from restaurant design to marketing". Simonson surmises that Bednar approached Antone in 1966 to create a cocktail to market Galliano. After all, Antone was noted for creating a Galliano-heavy cocktail called the Italian Fascination and is credited with inventing the Freddy Fudpucker, a Harvey Wallbanger with tequila.

So it is Donato "Duke" Antone who is not only said to have created the Harvey Wallbanger, but legend (or good marketing) has it that he also made the coctail for that surfer called Tom Harvey while bartending at Blackwatch Bar on Sunset Boulevard in Hollywood way back in 1952.

George Bednar was undoubtedly a good marketeer who commissioned a commercial artist named Bill Young to design a poster to promote Galliano via the Harvey Wallbanger cocktail. Bednar is credited with penning the tagline for the advertisement himself: "Harvey Wallbanger is the name. And I can be made!".

The pop-art advert featuring a sandal-wearing, monk-like hippy with attitude proved a massive hit. As the Sixties turned to the Seventies, the character was reproduced on T-shirts, mugs and bumper stickers while the cocktail it advertised flew across bar counters.

By the summer of 1973, advertisements appeared for a pre-mixed canned version of the Harvey Wallbanger, "The Club Wallbanger" made with Smirnoff Vodka. Perhaps the canned version is what helped eventually kill the Harvey Wallbanger. After all, made with fresh orange juice, it's a great drink - as is the Screwdriver. However, made with pasteurised orange juice, it is just another Disco Drink that was best forgotten in the Seventies.

name: Hemingway Special Daiquiri (Papa Doble)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review:
This drink is also known as a Papa Doble for good reason, it's twice the size of a regular cocktail. Hence the above recipe will fill one oversize Martini or two regular coupe glasses.

If you've a bone dry palate and would like to sample a true Hemingway Special without the addition of sugar then try the following authentic recipe given to me by Alejandro Bolívar Rodriguez, Head Bartender at El Floridita, Havana, Cuba where this cocktail is blended and not shaken. Indeed, blending rather than shaking Daiquiris is the default at El Floridita.

Daiquiri Hemingway (El Floridita's recipe)
Glass: Hurricane
Garnish: Straw
Method: BLEND all ingredients with crushed ice for five seconds.
90ml (3oz) Light Cuban rum
5ml (1 spoon) Maraschino liqueur
30ml (1oz) Grapefruit juice
15ml (½oz) Lime juice
history:
Created by Constantino (Constante) Ribalaigua Vert, the legendary head bartender of El Floridita, Havana, Cuba for Ernest Hemingway, after the great man wandered into the bar to use the toilet. When Hemingway tried the Floridita's standard frozen Daiquiri, he is quoted as saying, "That's good but I prefer it without sugar and with double rum" - so the Hemingway Special was born.

Hemingway suffered from haemochromatosis (a rare hereditary disease that can lead to diabetes) from which his father also suffered, hence his aversion to sugar. The original version was exactly as Hemingway requested a Daiquiri without sugar and heavy on the rum, basically, rum shaken with a splash of lime juice.

Years later after he took over the position of Head Bartender at El Floridita, Antonio Meilan added maraschino and grapefruit juice into the drink. Today sugar is commonly also added to balance this drink and make it more palatable to people with less sour palates than Hemingway.

Hemingway was affectionately known as 'Papa' in Cuba and this drink was originally named 'Daiquiri Like Papa' and then later 'Papa Doble'. After Meilan added maraschino and grapefruit the drink changed its name again to the Hemingway Special we recognise today.

Daiquiri cocktail history

name: Linstead

name: London Calling

history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2002 by Chris Jepson at Milk & Honey, London, England. Originally made for a Drinks International Magazine competition, this cocktail has gone on to be a much-copied contemporary classic, inspiring riffs such as the Banana Calling.

We also discovered a quite different stirred cocktail named London Calling in 2003 at London's Oxo Tower Bar & Brasserie (50ml dry gin, 31.25ml sloe gin, 12.5ml sweet vermouth and 2 dash orange bitters).

name: Latest Word
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

2⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: A Last Word made with genever in place of London dry gin. The distinctive flavour of genever stands up well to the other very characterful ingredients.
history: Last Word history

name: Martini Special

name: Honey Rum Grog

history: This Grog traces its origin back to the British Navy and Admiral Edward "Old Grog" Vernon's 1740 Order to Captains No.349 instructing that the daily ration of high-proof Navy rum was diluted with water and that where possible lime juice and sugar was made available.

name: New Yorker

name: North Pole

name: No. 10 Lemonade

ingredients:
12 fresh	Blueberries (fresh)
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)

1 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Basically a long blueberry Daiquiri.
history: Adapted from a drink discovered in 2006 at Double Seven, New York City, USA.

name: Paloma
garnish: Salt rim (optional) & pink or red grapefruit wedge
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with grapefruit soda and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
5⁄6 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Agave syrup
1 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Pink Grapefruit soda
review: Reminiscent of a long fruity Margarita with refreshing effervescence.
history: Paloma is Spanish for 'dove'. Its origins are unknown although it is reputed to date back to the 1950s. Some attribute its creation to the legendary Don Javier Delgado Corona, the former owner/bartender of La Capilla (The Chapel) in Tequila, Mexico, who created the Batanga.

name: Passion Fruit Margarita
garnish: Lime juice and salt rim if desired. Float half passion fruit
preparation: Cut passion fruit in half and scoop out the flesh from one half into your shaker (retain the other half for garnish). Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice, and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 fresh	Passion fruit (fresh)
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Agave syrup
review: Subtle passion fruit flavour and tartness influence rather than dominate this Margarita, allowing the tequila and other ingredients to also shine. Fruity yet sophisticated.

name: Pini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
5⁄12 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄4 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Use a great pisco and you'll have a wonderfully complex drink.

name: Brazil 66
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cachaça
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Reminiscent of an orange-influenced Caipirinha.
history:
Adapted from a drink created at Absinthe Brasserie & Bar, San Francisco, USA.

The name perhaps refers to Sérgio Mendes' band Brazil 66, best known for their 1966 hit Mas Que Nada. One of the best-known Brazilian songs, the name translates as a sarcastic 'Yeah, right!' and reached 47 on the US Billboard Hot 100 and six on the Official UK Top 40.

This cocktail name may also remember 1966 when Brazilians had much to be bitter about. The country's team had done well in the two previous World Cups, and during their first match in the 1966 Cup against Bulgaria, Pele, the world's most famous footballer, became the first player to score in three World Cups with a goal from a free kick. The Bulgarians spent the rest of the match fouling Pele, making him unable to play in Brazil's next game against Hungary. Without their star player, Brazil lost, meaning they needed a win in their next and final group game against Portugal. The Portuguese players followed the bad example set by the Bulgarians and repeatedly fouled Pele, resulting in him hobbling through much of the game. The Bulgarians won, and Brazil were eliminated from the World Cup at the group stage.

name: Esmeralda
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cachaça
1⁄3 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Cachaça, lime and elderflower with a smoky hit of Islay whisky.
history: Adapted from a recipe originally created by Ben Sandrof at Drink, Boston, USA.

name: Planter's Punch
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Jamaican-style overproof aged pot still rum
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 shot	Chilled water
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A tangy punch that harnesses the strength and rich flavours of the rum.
history:
Invented in the late 19th century by the founder of Myers's rum, Fred L. Myers. The recipe on the back of each bottle of his rum is known as the "Old Plantation formula" and uses the classic rum punch proportions: 1 sour (lime), 2 sweet (sugar), 3 strong (rum), and 4 weak (water).

Rather than this, or the American formula: 1 sour, 2 sweet, 3 weak, and 4 strong, I've followed David A. Embury's recommendation (in his 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks) of 1 sweet, 2 sour, 3 strong and 4 weak.

name: Pompanski Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Zesty with the sharp freshness of grapefruit and a hint of orange rounded with dry vermouth.

name: Rude Cosmopolitan
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)

review: Don't let the pink appearance of this Cosmopolitan (made with tequila in place of vodka) fool you into thinking it's a fluffy cocktail. It's both serious and superb.
history: Cosmopolitan cocktail history and development

name: Rum Punch-Up
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	White overproof rum
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2⁄3 shot	Chilled water (reduce if wet ice)
review: Exactly what the name promises - a Rum Punch served straight-up, Daiquiri style.
history: Adapted from a drink discovered in 2006 at Albannach, London, England.

name: Rum Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) to emulsify and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
5⁄6 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Smooth and sour - well balanced.

name: Turf Club (1895, George Kappeler)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
3 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Reminiscent of a Martini but sans vermouth, sweetened with dash of sugar and balanced by heavy use of bitters.
history: Adapted from a recipe in George J. Kappeler's 1895 book, Modern American Drinks.

name: Turf Club (1900, Harry Johnson)
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur

history: Harry Johnson, tellingly, doesn't list the Turf cocktail in the 1882 first edition or the 1888 second edition of his Bartenders' Manual but does include it as the last drink in his revised 1900 New and Improved edition. Johnson reflects on changing tastes and fashions by calling for Plymouth gin rather than old tom gin in his turn-of-the-century recipe.

name: Stanley Cocktail

review: Salmon pink and reminiscent of a Daiquiri with a splash of gin and grenadine.

name: Tailor Made

5⁄6 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)

review: Bourbon-laced cranberry and grapefruit with light honeyed richness and a faint touch of clove spice.

name: Vante Cocktail

name: Vodka Gimlet
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

2 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄4 shot	Lime cordial (sweetened lime juice)
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
