1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Dry grainy vodka, delicately flavoured and softened by subtly sweetened lemon and lime juice.
history: A vodka-based riff on the classic gin-based Gimlet. Recipe by yours truly, London, England.

name: Irish Maid
preparation: MUDDLE cucumber in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 slice	Cucumber (fresh)
2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Fresh, juicy cucumber and elderflower with Irish whiskey and zesty lemon.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Jack McGarry at The Dead Rabbit, New York City, USA, this is an Irish-whiskey-based riff on Sam Ross' Kentucky Maid cocktail which is considered a contemporary classic.

name: Larchmont
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: I share Embury's appreciation of this fine, delicate Orange Daiquiri. However, I've tweaked his formulation as we found the original somewhat rich and over citrusy.
history: Created by David A. Embury, who in his 1948 Fine Art of Mixing Drinks writes of this drink: "As a grand finale to cocktails based on the Rum Sour, I give you one of my favorites which I have named after my favorite community." Larchmont is a village in Westchester County, New York where he lived for many years.

name: Amarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
4 drop	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: The name of this bitter bittersweet and sour Margarita riff references amaro (meaning bitter) and the use of an Italian bitter liqueur. Many will want to add 5ml (1 bar spoon) of agave syrup to rebalance this cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2007 by Neyah White in San Francisco, USA.

name: Amber Room
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Serious and packed with bold flavours. Fellow Chartreuse fans will approve.
history:
This vintage cocktail originated from a layered or 'pousse-café' style drink called a Bijou. The original drink was so named after the French word meaning 'jewel' due to its trio of ingredients being coloured after the three most precious jewels: diamond (gin), ruby (sweet vermouth) and emerald (Green Chartreuse).

Stir rather than layer and the colours combine to make this an aptly named amber coloured drink.

name: Apple Blossom
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A Gin & Juice with a little extra interest courtesy of a splash of apple brandy.
history: In W. J. Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Cocktail Book the invention of this cocktail is credited to one R. G. Buckby.

name: Biggles Sidecar
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Ginger liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: The idea was to make a riff on an Aviation (see Biggles Aviation) but ginger cries out for cognac so I also ended up with this ginger Sidecar.
history: Created in 2008 by yours truly at The Cabinet Room, London, England. As a kid, I was an avid reader of the Biggles books.

name: Black Rose
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into (empty - no ice) chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
3 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Sazerac-like but with fruitiness.

name: Casino
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
2⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: This recipe is a broad interpretation of Jacob A. Didier's 1909 original and the Casino recipes that follow in Hugo R. Ensslin's 1916 book and other subsequent tomes. Although, as Didier merely specifies "dashes" of lemon juice, his recipe may not be so far removed from mine.
history: Until March 2014, when Henry Duke, a fellow discerning Drinker, made me aware that the Casino first appeared in Jacob A. Didier's 1909 book The Reminder: Up-To-Date Bartender' Vest Pocket Guide [thanks, Henry], I and most others credited Hugo R. Ensslin for debuting the recipe in his 1916 Recipes For Mixed Drinks, written when he was head bartender at New York City's Hotel Wallick which stood at the corner of Broadway and 43rd Street. It would appear that Ensslin copied Didier as the recipes in both books are almost identical.

name: Fumigator Flip
garnish: Dust with grated nutmeg & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄4 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 fresh	Egg yolk
review: Smoky Islay malt adds a distinctive aroma and flavour to this appropriately named cocktail with cherry fruitiness and smoothing egg yolk.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2008 by Julian de Feral at Bureau, London, England. Julian's original recipe rinsed the glass with Islay whisky but his drink was based on aged rum rather than Scotch.

name: Looks Familiar
preparation: STIR malt with ice and then strain and discard excess to leave the ice and mixing glass coated. Add other ingredients and STIR with the coated ice. Strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	Agave syrup
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄4 shot	Amer Picon
review: I defy you not to love this herbal bittersweet tequila-laced concoction.
history: Created by Jake Burger at Jake's Bar, Leeds, England.

name: Moonlight Cocktail (Gaz Regan's)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Crème de violette liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Basically an Aviation but with triple sec in place of maraschino and lime instead of lemon juice. Gaz used lime juice because he didn't have any lemons but in this adaptation of his recipe I've mellowed the citrus sourness by using a combination of both lime and lemon juice.
history:
This riff on the classic Aviation was created by Gary "gaz" Regan and first published in his The Cocktailian column in the San Francisco Chronicle on 27 September 2007. Gaz wrote, "After making my new baby I took it for a stroll around my deck and gazed up at the moon. It was off-white that evening, but it had a faint purplish hue to it. Just like my drink. The Moonlight Cocktail was born."

For the story behind the origins of the Aviation and its many other variations see our Aviation cocktail page.

name: Pernelle
preparation: SHAKE first four ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. TOP with soda and serve with straws.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1 shot	Poire William eau-de-vie
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: This long clear drink has a grassy, alpine aroma and a fresh pine finish.
history: Created in 2007 by Colin Asare-Appiah, London, England. Colin named this drink after the wife of the 14th-century alchemist Nicolas Flamel, who supported her husband in his search for the Philosopher's Stone.

name: English Breakfast Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Elderflower liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Cold black tea
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water
review: Light and fragrant with black tea, elderflower and the botanical influence of gin.
history: Created in 2006 by yours truly, London, England.

name: Nuclear Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	White overproof rum
2⁄3 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: A great way to inflict mutually assured destruction, although there will be fallout the morning after.
history: Created in 2005 by the late great Gregor de Gruyther at LAB bar in London, England.

name: Old Flame
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: As Dale DeGroff, this cocktail's creator, says, it's a Negroni softened by fresh orange juice and a splash of triple sec.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2001 by Dale DeGroff in New York, USA.

name: Rock 'n' Rye
garnish: Orange zest twist (expressed & discarded). Adorn with a skewered Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Syrup from Luxardo Maraschino Cherries
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Great rye whiskey notes with hints of orange and cherry. Slightly sweet but all too easy to quaff.
history:
Rock & Rye is a generic term for a style of traditional American liqueur made with a rye whiskey base infused with fruit and sugar, often bottled with pieces of fruit in the bottle. This was inspired by the flavour of one of these liqueurs: Jacquin's Rock & Rye, produced by Charles Jacquin et Cie Inc., "America's Oldest Cordial Producer" until circa 2009.

Classically, a "Rock & Rye Cocktail" is mixed with rock & rye liqueur as an ingredient. For example, Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide includes a Rock & Rye Cocktail, a Rock & Rye Cooler, and a Rock & Rye Toddy, all made with rock & rye liqueur as an ingredient.

name: Smoked Maple
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Maple syrup
1⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: This peaty-whisky-laced cocktail won't be to everybody's taste, but an Islay malt fan will most definitely approve.
history: Adapted from a cocktail discovered in 2009 at Dylanbar, Dublin, Ireland.

name: Hollywood
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄3 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: This drink is deliciously different. Rum, grapefruit, and pomegranate are smoothed with egg white and spiced with nutmeg.
history: Adapted from a recipe in William "Cocktail Bill" Boothby's 1930 Swallows : World Drinks and How to Prepare Them.

name: Improved Holland Gin Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. [To measure 1.25ml and how many dashes in 1.25ml, please see Measuring cocktail ingredients.]
ingredients:
2 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
1⁄24 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄24 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄24 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Salmon-pink with subtle juniper, rounded by maraschino liqueur, aromatic bitters and absinthe.
history: The classic Holland House "improved" due to the use of genever.

name: Submarine Kiss
preparation: POUR liqueur into base of chilled glass. SHAKE the rest of the ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and carefully fine strain into the liqueur-primed glass so contents of shaker float over liqueur.
ingredients:
1⁄3 shot	Crème Yvette liqueur
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Looks stunning and gives the drinker the option to sip or swirl to mix the sweet liqueur base into the body of the drink.
history: This cocktail is mentioned in O. O. McIntyre's New-York-Day-By-Day column in The Washington Herald on the 24th November 1915, "Sailors who come to Broadway for a touch of high life have invented a new drink called the Submarine Kiss." "The liquid combination is a milky white above and purple below and the submarine effect is secured after drinking about three."

name: Bernice
garnish: Mint leaf pegged to rim or float very tip of mint sprig
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄4 shot	Galliano L'Autentico liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Best described as "A vodka daiquiri with a hint of herbal peppermint courtesy of Galliano."
history: Created by "C. S. Berner", this cocktail first appears as the winning cocktail at a 1950 bartender's competition in The U.K.B.G. Guide to Drinks 1st edition published 1953 [and not in Ted Saucier's 1951 Bottoms Up! as we were previously led to believe. Having checked, I can't see it in Saucier's book.]

name: Fogerty No. 2
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Spirit-forward, fruity and bittersweet with a balance that makes another sip compelling.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2010 by Ryan 'Jesus' Fitzgerald at Beretta in San Francisco, USA. According to my notes, when at Beretta in 2010, Ryan's original recipe comprised 60ml (2oz) Rye whisky, 15ml (½oz) Campari, 7.5ml (¼oz) crème de cassis, and 2 dash orange bitters. However, it transpires that Ryan's Fogerty is made with white crème de cacao and not crème de cassis.

name: Tequila Basil Lemonade
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda and gently stir.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3 fresh	Basil leaves
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Just as it says on the tin, tequila charged with lemonade and flavoured with basil.
history: Created in 2011 by Chris Stave.

name: Rhine Wine Cobbler
garnish: A grape, orange and pineapple slice
preparation: MUDDLE grapes and pineapple in base of shaker and fine strain (without shaking) into glass filled with crushed ice. POUR other ingredients into glass and cobble (churn/stir) with barspoon to thoroughly mix.
ingredients:
3 fresh	Green grapes (seedless)
2 wedge	Pineapple (fresh) (cored, skinned and chopped)
3 shot	Riesling wine
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Light, fruity and very refreshing. A fruity alternative to a spritz.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Johnson's 1882 New And Improved Bartender's Manual.

name: Smoke and Mirrors No.1
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
3⁄4 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Byrrh Grand Quinquina
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: This spirit-forward cocktail has subtle smoky peatiness with herbal complexity provided by Bénédictine and Byrrh.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2011 by Erik Lorincz at the Savoy's The American Bar in London, England where it was made with 45ml (1½) Speyside single malt Scotch whisky (and no peated whisky) and 'smoked' in a decanter in front of the customer and served at the table.

name: Satan's Whiskers (Marcelled)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 1⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: This riff on the Satan's Whiskers (in turn a Bronx variation) calls for it not to be 'curled' (as is the case when you use orange curaçao), but to be "marcelled", apparently a deep soft wave in one's hair (for those that still have some) created with curling tongs and popular in the 1920s and 1930s.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2011 by William "Chili Bill" Eichinger at Finnegan's Wake in San Francisco, USA, and courtesy of Gaz Regan's Ardent Spirits.

name: Amaretto Sour (by Jeffrey Morgenthaler)
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo Maraschino Cherries on stick.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and pour into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: As the name suggests, this cocktail is dominated by amaretto, with lemon juice providing the sour balancing element and a slug of bourbon giving backbone.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2012 by Jeffrey Morgenthaler in Oregon, USA. Jeffrey's original formula calls for
45ml (1½oz) Amaretto
22.5ml (¾oz) Cask-strength bourbon
30ml (1oz) Lemon juice
5ml (1 spoon) Sugar syrup (2:1)
15ml (½oz) Egg white

name: Hawaiian Stone Sour
garnish: Skewered pineapple wedge or dehydrated pineapple slice & Luxardo maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Pineapple juice
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Pimento bitters
review: A Stone Sour is usually a sour cocktail with orange juice, and Dale DeGroff replaced the orange juice with pineapple juice in this "tropical" riff on a Bourbon Stone Sour.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2000 by Dale DeGroff "as a poolside drink for a regular guest at the Rainbow Room's Promenade Bar" in New York City, USA.

name: Monet's Moment
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably with one large hand-cracked cube)
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Byrrh Grand Quinquina
1⁄6 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Cognac and aromatised wine lifted with a splash of absinthe. Complex and refreshing.
history: Created in 2013 by Erik Lorincz, then Head Bartender at The American Bar, The Savoy Hotel, London. Erik was inspired after seeing a work by Claude Monet that hung in the hotel's Monet Suite, the room where, in 1901, the French impressionist originally sketched the pastel work entitled Waterloo Bridge.

name: My Sherry Amore
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
2⁄3 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: A bittersweet, salmon-pink, light, delicate balance of gin, herbal complexity, grapefruit and dry sherry.
history: Created in 2011 by Nick Van Tiel and named after the 1969 soul classic by Motown singer-songwriter Stevie Wonder. Originally titled Oh My Marcia, the song was originally about Wonder's girlfriend whilst he was at the Michigan School for the Blind in Lansing, Michigan. After they broke up, the lyrics and title were changed to 'My Cherie Amour'.

name: Randy Old-fashioned
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Tawny port
1⁄4 shot	Maple syrup
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Port and brandy (rhymes 'Randy') are traditionally consumed at Christmas and used to be a popular British pub combo. I've used maple syrup in place of brown sugar syrup to lightly sweeten this festive after-dinner combo. The Sazerac was the inspiration for the choice of bitters and use of absinthe.
history:
Created December 2014 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.
Old-Fashioned cocktail history and recipes

name: Game Set Match
garnish: Half lemon slice & Luxardo Maraschino cherry on stick
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A Sweet Manhattan with Cynar and orange bitters. What's not to like?
history: Created in 2013 by Juan 'J.P.' Caceres-Rojas while working in Washington D.C., USA.

name: Lemon Tart
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) & half lemon or half lime wheel on rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. SHAKE again without ice (dry shake) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: This bittersweet aperitif cocktail harnesses the herbal bitterness of gentian root with gin's botanical notes and sweetened freshly squeezed lemon juice.

name: Smokey Boat
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄3 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Andrea created this drink "for enjoying the flavour of smoky whisky with calvados adding to apple fruitiness." The amount of Peychaud's used makes or breaks this drink so beware of how generous your 'dash' is.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2014 by Andrea Buttier, an Italian bartender from Bologna working at The Loft, Clapham Common. Andrea originally used Laphroaig 10 year old for his malt with equal parts calvados, 2 shots apple juice, 2/3rd shot vanilla syrup and 1 dash Peychaud's.

name: Mediterranean Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Kleos Mastiha liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: This tasty sour features the distinctive flavour of mastiha.

name: The Other Woman
garnish: Spray absinthe mist over drink (or pre-rinse glass)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Byrrh Grand Quinquina
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Lucy Horncastle at Nola Bar, London, England.

name: Salvatore Meets
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
2⁄3 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: A refreshing zesty lemon Daiquiri topped with a splash of champagne.
history: Created in 2015 by Salvatore Calabrese at his bar in the Playboy Club, London, England.

name: Lion's Tail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄3 shot	Pimento dram/Allspice liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A heavily allspice dram liqueur influenced, Daiquiri-like, bourbon-based cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe that first appeared in William James "Billy" Tarling's Café Royal Cocktail Book, published in London in 1937. However, the drinks creator is likely to have been an American bartender driven to London by Prohibition. "Twisting the lion's tail" was an American slang expression for provoking the British which emerged during the period of American Anglophobia between the World Wars.

name: Medicina Latina
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. FLOAT mezcal.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Ginger syrup
1⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄6 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
review: A ginger spiced and honeyed Tequila Sour.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2009 by Marcos Tello at The Varnish in Los Angeles, USA.

In January 2022 I updated the recipe above. The previous after-dinner version comprised:
60ml (2oz) Blanco tequila
10ml (1/3oz) Honey syrup (3:1)
10ml 1/3oz) Ginger syrup
SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled old-fashioned glass. Garnish with candied ginger and spray of mezcal.

name: Élysée Treaty
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Jägermeisteror other German amaro
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
2 twist	Orange peel
review: Cognac-laced, zesty and bittersweet. Delicious as a late-night after-dinner digestive.
history: Created in 2015 by Ivan Mandaric at Oxbo Urban Bar & Grill, DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel, Zagreb, Croatia.

name: C'est la Vie (That's Life)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Cinnamon syrup
review: A tasty apple and cognac sour with delicate herbal and cinnamon spice.
history: Created in 2015 by Saverio Vicari at The Rib Room Bar at The Jumeirah Carlton Tower Hotel, London, England.

name: Excuse My French
garnish: Lemon zest encircling the inside rim of glass with crusted sugar coated rim.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Crème de Framboise
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Raspberry flavours characterise this cognac sour which is served crusta-style.
history: Created in 2015 by Daniele Francini at Salvatore's Bar at Playboy Club, London, England.

name: Homely Smoke
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1⁄4 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1 barspoon	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Honey and amaretto's rich almond flavours brilliantly balance and marry with cognac and Islay single malt whisky.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2015 by Sam Fraser for the menu at The Lickfold Inn in West Sussex, England

name: Smoke & Mirrors (by The Bon Vivants)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
4 fresh	Mint leaves
1 1⁄2 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Genever and mezcal sit surprisingly well together in this very refreshing drink with mint and lemon.
history: Created in 2016 by The Bon Vivants, USA for Rutte Old Simon Genever.

name: Smoked Old Fashioned Godfather
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
3⁄4 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1⁄4 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
review: A quartet of whiskies: bourbon, rye, blended Scotch and Islay single malt, stirred with, and lightly sweetened and flavoured by amaretto liqueur. The result is a complex, balanced and lightly nutty after-dinner cocktail. If you like this, then also consider a Madurised Almond Old Fashioned.
history:
Created in June 2016 by yours truly at The Cabinet Room, London, England.
See: Old-Fashioned cocktail history

name: Optimist
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Fino sherry and Creole bitters brilliantly set this riff on a classic Daiquiri apart. Beautifully balanced and delicately flavoured. If you apply the charcoal rim, perhaps leave a lipstick saving space rather than encircling the rim.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2014 for Bacardi Legacy by Roman Foltan at the Artesian Bar at The Langham Hotel, London, England.

name: Oaxacan Negroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Mancino Vermouth di Torino Chinato
1 dash	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: Mezcal lends a characterful smoky note to this complex riff on a classic Negroni.
history: Recipe adapted from one created by William Aporih at Añejo Tribeca. William’s original recipe called for ¾ Espolon Reposado mezcal, 1 oz Botanist Gin, ¾ oz Campari, ¾ oz Barolo Chinato and a splash of Cola Nut Extract.

name: Cadáver Reviver
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: The combination of tequila and triple sec make this riff on the classic Corpse Reviver remarkably Margarita-like, only with added complexity and subtlety due to the aromatised wine and faintest hint of absinthe.
history: Created in February 2017 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Sin Limites
preparation: MUDDLE cardamom in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 dried	Green cardamom pods
1 1⁄2 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
1⁄6 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review: Some huge flavours presented in a comparatively delicate drink – think bittersweet and spiced Vanilla Daiquiri.
history:
Created for Bacardí Legacy 2017 by Péter Gózon at Warmup RUSTIC bar in Budapest, Hungary.

Péter makes his own vanilla syrup by mixing 0.5 kg sugar & 2.5 ml water, simmered with 2 vanilla pods.

Peter says, "When I was a child my father was a journalist so we were always on the move; I lived in many countries and often found when we returned to Hungary that the local children treated me as a foreigner. I used to dream of being an actor, but lost my confidence because of this.

"Three years ago I walked into my first bar and saw the bartenders at work. I was amazed - I wanted to be like them - like actors on a stage – but needed first to overcome my fear. Now, a few years later, I am part of this amazing competition, which has helped me realize that bartending is my life. When I heard my name at the BLGCC semi-final, I felt invincible - I realized that if you do what you really love, then you are Sin Limites."

name: Lemon Sherbet Margarita
garnish: Float lemon sorbet balls (made with melon baller)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
3⁄4 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Agave syrup
1 scoop	Lemon sorbet
review: This Margarita does indeed have a sherbet flavour with a lemony citrus bite.

name: Pineapple Daiquiri (simple but tasty recipe)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Light rum provides vibrancy while aged rum adds rich complexity. Pineapple juice adds tropical fruitiness and replaces the dilution necessary to open and amplify a classic Daiquiri.
history: Recipe by yours truly in July 2017 at the Cabinet Room in London, England.

name: Macca Margarita
garnish: Half salted rim with split lime & orange wheels on rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Agave syrup
review: Orange juice adds fruity dilution to what could also be called a Breakfast Margarita. Sir Paul McCartney (yup of Beatles fame) likes his Margaritas made with a splash of freshly squeezed orange juice (preferably clementine juice), hence this recipe is named in his honour.
history: A riff on the classic Margarita created in 2017 by yours truly.

name: Beelzebub
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄2 shot	Lucano amaro
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Whoever created this bittersweet drink is clearly in league with Beelzebub himself – it's devilishly good. With rich bourbon, a hint of smoky mezcal, amaro bitterness and lemon freshness balanced by almond syrup. Also, try substituting all or at least half of the amaro with Ferro China to put a bit of iron into this devil.

name: Egg Sour
garnish: Float 3 small dashes Angostura bitters on surface of drink
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 whole	Egg (white & yolk)
review: A well-balanced sour with brandy and orange zestiness shaken with a whole egg. Try it. This combo is tastier than it sounds.
history: A vintage cocktail of unknown origin.

name: Tuxedo Cocktail No.2 (Savoy & Duffy's recipe)
garnish: Lemon zest twist & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 dash	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe (omit for Cocktails Made Easy)
review: A Fifty-Fifty Martini with added flavour and aroma thanks to the addition of a trio of bitters, liquor and liqueur.
history:
Adapted from recipes in The Savoy Cocktail Book (1930) by Harry Craddock, The Official Mixer's Manual (1934 & 1940) by Patrick Gavin Duffy.
Also see: Tuxedo cocktail history

name: Oh Snap!
garnish: Lemon zest twist & Luxardo maraschino cherry
preparation: MUDDLE peas in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
4 fresh	Sugar snap peas
1 1⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: The light green colour comes from the sugar snap peas and their delicate flavour sits well in this floral Aviation-style cocktail.
history: Created in 2018 by Gareth "G" Franklin, Luxardo global brand ambassador, this cocktail was originally called Howard Hughes, but given the recipe includes sugar snap peas, G thought "Oh! Snap!" more appropriate.

name: Champagne Julep
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) & mint sprigs dusted with icing sugar
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice. Add champagne and more to shaker, then throw twice before straining into julep tin filled with crushed ice. Serve with a metal straw.
ingredients:
8 fresh	Mint leaves
1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
3 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Lower in strength than most old-school julep cocktails, champagne adds a zing if not a sparkle.
history: The contentious history of the Julep, along with its variants can be found on our page.

name: Mojito (no added sugar & low-calorie)
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE mint (just to bruise) in base of glass. Add rum, lime juice and sugar free sweetener. Half fill glass with crushed ice and CHURN (stir) with bar spoon. Fill glass with more crushed ice and CHURN some more. TOP with soda, stir and serve with environmentally friendly straws.
ingredients:
8 fresh	Mint leaves
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar-free sweetener
1 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
history:
Adapted from the classic serve by yours truly (Simon Difford) in January 2019.

For more recipes, its origins and history, see the Mojito Cocktail.

name: Sazerac (no sugar & low-calorie)
preparation: POUR absinthe into ice-filled glass, TOP with water and leave to stand. Separately THROW other ingredients with ice. DISCARD contents of glass (absinthe, water and ice) and STRAIN drink into absinthe-coated glass.
ingredients:
1⁄3 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 2⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄4 shot	Sugar-free sweetener
3 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters (optional)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters (optional)
review:
A Sazerac just isn't a Sazerac without dashes of bitters but beware: Peychaud's contains low amounts of caramel and Angostura Aromatic bitters contain sugar. So include these and your finished cocktail will have trace amounts of sugar.

The weight and flavour of the spirits in this cocktail are such that I defy anybody to call this out as being sugar free – or even very very low sugar.
history: Adapted from the classic Sazerac by yours truly in January 2019.

name: Vodka Sour (no added sugar & low-calorie)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Sugar-free sweetener
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters (optional)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: As with most sours, adding a couple of dashes aromatic bitters greatly contributes to the cocktail's flavour but this also adds trace amounts of sugar.
history:
Adapted from the classic serve by yours truly (Simon Difford) in January 2019.

Also see Sours - history, recipes and glassware.

name: Whiskey Sour (no added sugar & low-calorie)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Sugar-free sweetener
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters (optional)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review:
This Whiskey Sour isn't very sour and those wanting a drier drink should consider reducing the sweetener to nearer 15ml (1/2oz).

Adding a couple of dashes aromatic bitters greatly contributes to the cocktail's flavour but this also adds trace amounts of sugar.
history:
Adapted from the classic serve by yours truly (Simon Difford) in January 2019.

A history of the Whiskey Sour cocktail can be found on our page.

name: Vanilla Espresso Martini
garnish: Float 3 coffee beans (and if feeling extravagant, also half, or even a full vanilla bean)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1⁄6 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: If you're the kind to opt for a splash of flavoured syrup at the coffee shop, then this variation on Dick Bradsell's original Espresso Martini is for you. And with the range of flavoured vodkas and sugar syrups available, why stop at vanilla?
history: See the story behind the Espresso Martini.

name: Dutch Mule
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with ginger beer.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
3 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: Ginger spice invigorates this long refreshing cocktail with a splash of genever adding to the Dutch influence.
history:
A signature cocktail for Ketel One Dutch vodka.

A detailed history of the Moscow Mule cocktail, of which this drink is a variant, can be found on our page.

name: Egg Nog
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Cognac (brandy)
5⁄6 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
5⁄6 shot	Milk (whole milk/full 3-4% fat)
1 fresh	Egg (white & yolk)
review: This vintage cocktail is literally a thickened alcoholic milkshake flavoured with cognac and rum. Yum!
history: Egg Nog is a vintage Christmas libation and George Washington, America's first President famously made his own. It is traditionally made by whisking the egg yolks with sugar; separately stirring the milk, cream, rum and bourbon; and finally combining these two mixtures along with beaten egg white. This is obviously best made in batches and is a faff. Our quick and easy single-serve version delivers on flavour and if you seek a thicker consistency then opt for cream in place of milk.

name: Aigua de València
preparation: STIR first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass that has first been charged with Cava.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
2 1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 1⁄2 shot	Cava sparkling wine (chilled)
review: This boozier Spanish take on a Mimosa is authentically made with the juice of oranges from the Valencia region. Perfect for a lazy hot afternoon, preferably served with some Spanish sun.
history:
Aigua de València (Valencian Water) is often made and served as a punch in pitchers and is a popular drink in the tapas bars of the eponymous Spanish city.

Aigua de València was first made in 1959 by Constante Gil at Café Madrid in Valencia and the story goes that a group from the Basque Country had become regulars at the bar with their usual order being "Agua de Bilbao", meaning Water of Bilbao and referring to cava. (The majority of cava is produced in Catalonia, but there is also some production in the Basque Country.) Challenged to devise an alternative for the group, Gil created "Agua de Valencia" by adding local orange juice and then fortifying the mixture with gin and vodka. This proved a hit with the group and became a staple at the bar before finding broader appeal in other Valencian bars during the 1970s.

name: Harvest Moon (1930s recipe)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Applejack brandy bottled-in-bond (50% alc./vol)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water
review:
Described as being an "applejack sour with orgeat," we've adapted the recipe to use commercially available orgeat. If using a more artisan orgeat then you may want to use as much as 30ml/1oz orgeat and forgo the sugar and water.

There is no orange in the cocktail but it's surprising how much the orange zest twist influences this drink and adds complexity.
history: We have Robert Hess and his The Cocktail Spirit podcast to thank for the Harvest Moon and drawing our attention to its feature in a list of the Top 10 Most Popular Cocktails in the December 1934 edition of Esquire Magazine.

preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
3⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Mezcal and cognac fuel this stirred and strong nightcap sipper.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2014 by Ezra Star at Drink in Boston, USA, this Martinez riff is named after the year the half-decade long The Mexican Revolution (Mexican Civil War) started. This had a transformative effect on both Mexican culture and government.

name: Bitter Giuseppe
garnish: Lemon zest twist (in addition to twist used in the recipe)
preparation: SPRAY oils from lemon zest twist into stirring glass and drop zest into glass. Add other ingredients, STIR with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 twist	Lemon peel
2 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
6 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: It's bitter Giuseppe, best you enjoy this as an aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2007 by Stephen Cole at The Violet Hour, Chicago, USA.

name: Cotillion
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄4 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A dry bourbon-based, citrussy sour lifted by rich aged rum complexity.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Lucius Beebe's 1946 The Stork Club Bar Book.

name: Lemon Drop Crusta
garnish: Select a small wine or flute glass with a rim diameter that will snugly accommodate a small lemon tightly enough to act as a watertight extension to the glass. Cut off both ends of the fruit and carefully remove the pulp to leave a barrel-shaped shell of skin. Place in the top of the glass. Wet the edge of the glass and exposed fruit shell with sugar syrup and dip in caster sugar to frost the edge of both peel and glass. Leave for a couple of hours to form a hard crust.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass with pre-crusted rim.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Lemon bitters
review: Zesty lemon with a sugar-crusted rim. This tasty drink's name aptly describes it.
history: This riff on a vodka sour, inspired by the hard candy sweet, may have earlier origins but rose from the popularity of the 1990s, a time when pretty much every cocktail came in a v-shaped glass and was called a "Martini". Then it was usually garnished with a lemon zest twist, and was sometimes also served in a glass with a sugar crusted rim, in which case it is a bona fide Crusta (although it was never a true Martini). This version by yours truly.

name: Rum Dum Sour
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into ice-filled glass. FLOAT pot still rum.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
1⁄2 shot	Jamaican-style overproof aged pot still rum
review: A light rum sour sipped through a float of pungent pot still rum.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 1971 by Wilfred Sands while bartending at the Lyford Cay Club in New Providence, Bahamas. Wilfred apparently made the drink at the request of a member who sought a short rum cocktail that was not overly sweet.

name: Holy Smokes No.1
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Light vermouth amaro (e.g. Cardamaro)
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
4 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: Bourbon-laced and spirit-forward but mellowed by bittersweet amaro and herbal liqueur with a hint of Islay smokiness.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Whistle Pig brand ambassador Tony Devencenz in USA.

name: Greek Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	O/Purist Tsipouro
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: This delicately sharp sour is indeed redolent of a rum-based Daiquiri and is a great showcase for Tsipouro's vinous flavours.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Kostas Ignatiadis at Schuman's Bar in Munich, Germany.

name: The Field Marshal
garnish: Split grapefruit coin zest on rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 2⁄3 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
1 shot	Pineapple juice
2⁄3 shot	Celery saccharum (celery syrup)
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Sauvignon blanc wine, celery, pineapple and rum all sit harmoniously in this cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Ed Belshaw at World Service Nottingham, England, this cocktail earned him a place in the UK final of Bacardi Legacy 2019 (held in February 2020).

name: Brandy Old Fashioned (Wisconsin-style)
garnish: Orange wheel slice & Luxardo maraschino cherry sail
preparation: MUDDLE first 4 ingredients in base of glass. Add brandy and 6oz scoop crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 wedge	Orange (fresh)
1 whole	Maraschino cherry (from jar in syrup)
1⁄6 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
review:
Fruity and lightly sweetened brandy cooled and diluted with crushed ice. What's not to like?

The Brandy Old-Fashioned is usually made using Californian bandy or another domestic brandy, and depending on the sweetness of your brandy you may want to reduce the sugar syrup in this recipe. Use a wedge, rather than a slice, of orange as when muddled a slice breaks up too much leaving unsightly debris in the drink.

In Wisconsin, the Brandy Old Fashioned is also usually finished with a splash of 7-Up or Sprite (if ordered "sweet"), or Squirt (if the bar call is "sour") or a combination of 7-Up/Sprite and soda water (if requested "press").
history: The muddled fruit Old-Fashioned seems to have arisen due to masking poor quality whiskey during Prohibition and in America lingered as the prevailing way to make an Old-Fashioned into the mid-1990s. Helped by Jeffrey Morganthaler, as muddling fruit in the whisky-based Old-Fashioned has faded so muddling fruit in the brandy brandy-based version has grown in popularity, particularly in Wisconsin where a Brandy Old-Fashioned is the state drink.

name: Silver Pineapple

2 shot	Bourbon whiskey

history: Adapted from a recipe called Peach Me created by Jason Shullo of Golden Entertainment, Nevada, USA. Jason's original Peach Me recipe calls for a larger slug of bourbon.

1 dash	Bob's Chocolate bitters

name: Monte Whiskey Sour

history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2006 by Audrey Saunders at the Pegu Club, New York City, USA. This cocktail is a tribute to late 1800s French architecture, a period when sipping absinthe was fashionable in Paris, represented by pastis in this cocktail.

review: Select the right rum (see Jason's recommendations below) and you have what he aptly describes as "a Last Word Jamaica daiquiri."
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2022 by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford. Jason recommends this cocktail is made using "a medium-ester rum such as the Berry Bros Jamaica rum from their Classic Range, or Plantation Xaymaca."

Also known as Tropicbirds, Bosun Birds are medium-sized white tropical seabirds found in all the major oceans across three varieties: Red-billed; Red-tailed and White-tailed. They own their Bosun Bird name to the era of the sailing ship when their call was said to resemble the sound of a bosun's whistle.

Bosun is the oldest rank in the Royal Navy, the most senior rate of the deck department and responsible for the components of a ship's hull. As the deck foreman, the boatswain plans the day's work and assigns tasks to the deck crew.

A bosun's whistle is a pipe with a hole opened and closed by the hand of the player to change its pitch. Historically the high pitch boatswain's call was used by the bosun to pass commands to the crew when their voice could not be heard over heavy seas. In modern-day use, it's best known for piping aboard an important guest. Part of this ceremony, "manning the side", originates in summoning a party of sailors, known as "side boys", to hoist the visitor aboard using a bosun's chair when the weather was too rough for the use of ladders.
