3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Maple syrup
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: A classic Rattlesnake with maple syrup and Creole-style bitters. Delicious!
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2010 by Thad Vogler at Beretta restaurant in San Francisco, California. USA.

name: Calvados Espresso
garnish: Float 3 coffee beans in centre of cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Calvados adds its distinctive flavour to this well-balanced riff on a classic Espresso Martini.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in February 2023 by Kaitlin Wilkes for Avallen Calvados.

name: Clan MacLeod
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with lemonade.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Ginger syrup
1 2⁄3 shot	Lemonade
review: A peaty Whisky Collins with orange and ginger.
history: Created in May 2023 by yours truly. I named this riff on the Auld Alliance after the MacDonalds, the clan whose stronghold was Knock Castle, better known as Caisteal Chamuis (Castle Camus), now the name of the peaty whisky I based this cocktail on.

name: Tim Bin
garnish: Squeeze lemon wedge in cocktail and drop in as garnish
preparation: POUR all ingredients into glass and the n add ice to fill.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Monkey Shoulder Fresh Monkey
1⁄6 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄3 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
1 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Any G & T drinker should appreciate this brilliantly simple yet complex cocktail. The funky new-make spirit, peated whisky and falernum combine brilliantly with the quinine notes of the tonic water.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Rob McHardy of The Lab in Nantes, France.

name: Daisy Marie
garnish: Lime juice and Tajin seasoning rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
3⁄4 shot	Passoã passion fruit liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
6 drop	Hot pepper sauce (red)
review: A cross between a Porn Star Martini and a chili-spiced Mezcal Margarita.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Rye Patton, bar manager at the Tango Room in Dallas, Texas, USA.

name: Constantine
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄24 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A Martinez with pleasing aniseed notes from absinthe.
history: A classic, published in the 1933 book Pioneers of Mixing at Elite Bars, brought to my attention and rejuvenated by Jason E. Clapham of St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England.

name: Young Man's Delight
garnish: Lemon zest twist expressed and then discarded. Garnish with quarter orange slice wheel on rim
preparation: DRY SHAKE (without ice) first 4 ingredients. Add ice, SHAKE again and fine strain into chilled glass (no ice in glass) along with 30 of the ginger ale. Place in freezer to stand for at least 3 minutes. TOP with the rest of the ginger ale poured from a height to raise the head (fizz style).
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
3 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
review: A double shot of tequila presented in a wonderfully light cocktail.
history: The first known recipe for a Young Man's Delight appears in the second, 1934 edition of G. F. Steele's My New Cocktail Book.

name: Rum Collins
garnish: Skewered Luxardo Maraschino cherry and lemon slice (sail)
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: It's more common to find rum mixed with lime juice, but the Rum Collins calls for lemon, and this combines brilliantly with the aged rum in this long refreshing cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe featured in the 1932 menu of Sloppy Joe's Bar in Havana, Cuba.

name: Improved Gin Cocktail
garnish: Express lemon zest twist over surface of the drink, rub lemon zest oils on rim, and discard
preparation: Express oils from lemon zest twist into shaker and discard. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄6 shot	Gomme syrup
1⁄12 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2 dash	Boker's bitters
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Fabulously complex and spirit-forward. A delicious cocktail on which to sip and contemplate. Some may want to stir this cocktail but it's better shaken. Expressing lemon oils over the surface enhances the aroma and clears the bubble slick produced by shaking.
history: The Gin Cocktail first appears in Jerry "The Professor" Thomas' 1862 The Bar-Tender's Guide & Bon Vivant's Companion with this "Improved" version debuting in his 1876 The Bar-Tender's Guide 2nd Edition. This also includes "Improved" versions of the Brandy Cocktail, and Whiskey Cocktail, which are all what we today call Old Fashioned cocktails. In the words of Jerry Thomas, they have been "improved by moistening the edge of the cocktail glass with a piece of lemon." Such "improved" American cocktails from the period are also distinguished by using European ingredients, particularly maraschino liqueur and/or absinthe.

name: Pomegranate Cosmopolitan
garnish: Flamed coin-sized orange zest twist expressed and floated on surface
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 shot	Pomegranate juice
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Made with freshly squeezed pomegranate juice, this riff on a classic Cosmopolitan is both flavoursome and striking in colour.
history: Created in November 2023 by yours truly at The Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Rust & Bone
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Lucano amaro
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A bittersweet Old Fashioned with pleasing herbal complexity.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Sandy de Almeida at The Drake Hotel in Toronto, Canada. Originally made with cedar-infused Four Roses Bourbon (a small handful of cedar chips infused in 75cl of bourbon for 4 hours) and Amaro Nonino.

name: Southern Border
garnish: 3 drops of Creole bitters dropped on and pulled through foam with a cocktail stick.
preparation: DRY SHAKE all ingredients (without ice) to emulsify. SHAKE again with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Blue Curaçao
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: This cocktail's border is delineated by the line between the pisco-laced citrusy base and its foaming white head.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Pamela Wiznitzer at the Dead Rabbit in New York City, USA.

name: Apple Grass
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Bison grass vodka
1⁄3 shot	Licor 43 Original liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Ginger syrup
2⁄3 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Bison grass vodka and apple juice are a classic and tasty combo. Here, they are paired with ginger and spiced vanilla, freshened with lemon juice.
history: This was a new cocktail to me when Ollie Sagerström Blom at London's Satan's Whiskers kindly made it for us in March 2024, and (thanks to Kevin Armstrong) I now know it was created circa late-2004 by Michele Tuveri, when a bartender at London's Milk & Honey where it featured on the menu for a period and also a couple of Match Bar menus thereafter.

name: Famous Last Word No. 2
garnish: Lime zest twist expressed and discarded. Adorn with a skewered Luxardo Maraschino Cherry.
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
3⁄4 shot	Americano bianco
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Americano Bianco replaces maraschino liqueur to bring quinine notes to this aperitivo rendition of the classic Last Word.
history: We have Jason E. Clapham from the St. Ewards MCR at Oxford to thank for this cocktail, who says, "I can't really claim to have invented it-the original Famous Last Word, a great drink from Red Light in Manchester, is exactly the same, but made with a Irish whiskey as the spirit base instead of gin, a cross between the Last Word and the Tipperary."

name: Cosmicus
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Italicus liqueur
1 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Why have a bog-standard Cosmo when you can have a Cosmicus? A Cosmopitan with a sophisticated Italian touch of bergamot.
history: This cocktail was served as the "Sliving Cosmo" at Cocenella music festival in California in April 2024 but amongst the cognoscente, this cocktail is known as the Cosmicus.

name: Margarita Soda
garnish: Optional lime juice and salt rim. Adorn with lime wedge.
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda water.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Agave syrup
6 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A Tommy's Margarita lengthened with soda. Tasty and refreshing.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2023 by Tony Milici, when beverage director at Hellbender Nighttime Café in Queens, New York City, USA.

name: Marianito
garnish: Skewered orange zest twist and olive
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. (Or strain into chilled coupe.)
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A vermouth-forward Spanish variation on the Negroni, which is great served over ice or straight-up.
history: Traditionally made with Spanish vermouth, the Marianito originated and is still popular in Northern Spain, particularly in the Basque Country, La Rioja and the city of Burgos.

name: Cock N' Bull
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 dash	Orange Curaçao liqueur
review: Some modern interpretations call for orange curaçao in place of triple sec. I stirred both versions alongside each other to sample what each liqueur brings to this cocktail, and I find myself much preferring triple sec, as per the original recipe.
history:
This cocktail was created at and took its name from the famous Cock 'n Bull British-style pub on Hollywood's Sunset Strip, founded in 1937 by Jack Morgan. An anglophile, he covered the walls with cutting from framed cuttings from English newspapers, portraits of British monarchs, and prints of English landmarks and countryside. The 'pub' is famed for being where head bartender Wes Price created the Moscow Mule, so cementing his name and that of Jack and the Cock 'n Bull in cocktail history. When Jack died in 1974, his son John took over the running of the bar, which finally closed after 50 years in 1987.

This cocktail features in Ted Saucier's Bottom's Up as the "Cock 'N Bull Special," meaning it was created sometime between the bar opening in 1937 and the publication of this Saucier's book in 1951.

name: Abbey
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Americano bianco
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A dry, orangey, herbal, gin-laced aperitivo, closely related to the better known Bronx.
history:
Adapted from a recipe first published in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book and repeated in William James "Billy" Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Bar Book.

Although one of the earliest cocktails on our database (the third), the Abbey was brought to our attention for a long overdue update by Jason E. Clapham of St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England who recommends making it with Cocchi Americano as a substitute for the now sadly discontinued Kina Lillet used in the 1930 recipe.

name: Almond Old Fashioned (tequila based)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄4 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1⁄6 shot	Agave syrup
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: One to please fans of both tequila and the Old Fashioned cocktail genre with amaretto adding the headline hint of almond.
history:
Created in 2005 by Mark Prat at Maze, London, England.
See: Old-Fashioned cocktail history

name: Bacardi Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: This classic salmon-pinky cocktail perfectly combines and balances the light rum with the assertive sourness of lime juice and rich sweetness of pomegranate syrup.
history:
The Bacardi Cocktail originated in Cuba in 1917 and quickly grew in popularity with the growth of the cocktail culture in the USA after Prohibition, so much so that it became known simply as 'the Bacardi'.

There are two schools of thought over the original ingredients, some believe it was simply a Daiquiri but made using Bacardi rum and that the now ubiquitous grenadine version originated in New York sometime after Prohibition. Others hold that the grenadine was there at inception, after all the earliest known Daiquiri recipe was made with Bacardi rum so grenadine must be the distinguishing factor. However, the number of vintage cocktail books listing a Bacardi Cocktail without grenadine would seem to back up the inclusion of grenadine being a later addition.

Like the Daiquiri, The Bacardi Cocktail was sometimes served frozen and talking about the iced version, Jack Doyle, former barman at Sloppy Joe's in Key West, then Bacardi Imports Inc. barman in New York, explained, "The secret to the iced version was to shake the flaked iced until it looked like sherbet." This technique became known as frappé.

As the Bacardi Cocktail rapidly grew in popularity a small number of establishments neglected to use Bacardi rum as the base ingredient. In 1936, this led the Bacardi Company to take the Barbizon-Plaza Hotel and the Wivel Restaurant in New York's West Fifty-Fourth Street to court to ensure that when a customer asked for "Bacardi" by name they were given Bacardi Rum, so protecting the company's trademark.

Bacardi's case at New York's Supreme Court involved the premise that theirs was a unique rum and Bacardi family members travelled from Cuba to New York to appear as witnesses. Even Enrique Schueg, the third President of the Bacardi Company, took to the witness stand. When asked by Justice Walsh, "Well, how is this Bacardi Rum of yours made?" he replied, "Oh! That is my secret." Despite this secrecy, after deliberation, Justice John L. Walsh eventually affirmed that "Bacardi Rum is unique and uncopyable" and issued a ruling that a Bacardi Cocktail must legally be made with rum manufactured by the Compania Ron Bacardi.

name: Blue Lady
garnish: Express coin-sized orange zest twist and float in the centre of cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Blue Curaçao
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Vivid blue with a pale blue head, this is a striking cocktail. It also packs a whopping 45ml (1½oz) of blue curaçao but is far from being a "disco drink". It is a balanced colourful and vintage riff on the even older White Lady.
history: Recipe adapted from W. J. Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Cocktail Book (Coronation Edition) which says this drink was "Invented by Victor." Victor Cabrin is widely credited with creating the White Lady.

name: Bourbon Milk Punch
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
2 1⁄2 shot	Milk (whole milk/full 3-4% fat)
4 drop	Bob's Vanilla bitters
review: Truly the milk of the Gods! Delicate bourbon with a touch of vanilla. Balanced rather than sweet, and milky rather than creamy.
history: This classic was popular during America's Prohibition era and is still widely served in New Orleans where it is commonly consumed with Sunday brunch.

name: Bramble
garnish: Blackberry & lemon slice dusted with icing sugar
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. Top with more crushed ice and compact ice to form a volcano-shaped mound. DRIZZLE liqueur over this mound to create a 'bleeding' effect in the glass. Serve with short sustainable straws.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
5⁄12 shot	Giffard Crème de Mûre liqueur
review: One of the best and most popular drinks to come out of the 1980s.
history:
Created in the mid-80s by Dick Bradsell at Fred's Club, Soho, London, England.

In 2001 and again in 2015, Dick wrote about how he came to create this contemporary classic and you can read the Bramble Cocktail - its inception told by its creator here.

name: Breakfast Martini
garnish: Orange zest twist & slice of toast on rim
preparation: STIR marmalade with gin in base of shaker until it dissolves. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 barspoon	Orange marmalade
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: The success or failure of this tangy drink is partly reliant on the quality of marmalade used. For ease of use, choose "fine cut" or even "no peel"/"shredless" orange marmalade.
history:
This neo-Martini was created in 1996 by bartender and long-term President of the United Kingdom Bartender's Guild, Salvatore Calabrese.

Being of proud Italian descent, Salvatore usually has little more than a swift espresso for breakfast. However, one morning, Sue, his English wife, insisted he sit down for breakfast and served him toast and marmalade. Salvatore came up with the idea for his Breakfast Martini while enjoying the tangy preserve-covered toast and took the jar to work with him. Later that day, at London's Library Bar in the Lanesborough Hotel, he perfected his signature cocktail.

Coincidentally, Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book includes a recipe for a "Marmalade Cocktail" that's very similar to Salvatore's Breakfast Martini. However, Salvatore says that the inspiration for his drink was the hearty English breakfast and not the classic English bartending book.

name: Chin Chin
preparation: STIR honey with Scotch in base of shaker. Add apple juice, SHAKE with ice and strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
1⁄2 barspoon	Honey
1 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
Top up with	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Golden honey in colour and also in flavour. An unusual and great tasting Champagne cocktail.
history: Created in 2002 by Tony Conigliaro at Isola, Knightsbridge, London, England.

name: Cosmopolitan Cocktail (Dale DeGroff's recipe)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Citroen Vodka
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: This is the definitive Cosmo recipe from the man most associated with the drink's development and popularity.
history: In his 2002 The Craft of the Cocktail, Dale DeGroff explains that while he did not invent the Cosmopolitan, "What I did do was popularize a definitive recipe that became widely accepted as the standard." He also gives the above recipe but with just ½oz (15ml) Cointreau, a measure which he increased to ¾oz (22.5ml) for the 2020 Revised Edition of his book. This could be as much due to a reduction of sugar in Cointreau to conform with fashion since Dale created his recipe at Manhattan's Rainbow Rooms in the mid-1990s as his revisiting and polishing an old recipe.

name: Batanga
preparation: STIR salt with lime juice in base of glass to dissolve salt. Add ice and other ingredients and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 pinch	Salt (sea salt)
5⁄12 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
3 1⁄2 shot	Cola (e.g. Coca Cola or Pepsi Cola)
review: Basically a Cuba Libre made with tequila in place of rum and an all-important pinch of salt.
history:
Created in 1961 by the legendary Don Javier Delgado Corona, owner/bartender of La Capilla (The Chapel) in Tequila, Mexico. Don Javier famously ritualistically stirred this drink with the knife he used to cut the limes, something he did into his eighties.

The Batanga is a popular drink in Mexico, helped by being featured in an advertising campaign by El Tequileño, a tequila made close to Don Javier's bar.

name: Bonnie Prince Charlie
garnish: Half lime slice wheel on rim or float dehydrated lime slice
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Drambuie liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Honeyed, spiced cognac with a touch of citrus. Fit for a Prince?
history: The Bonnie Prince Charlie Cocktail's first appearance in a recipe book is Hyman Gale and Gerald F. Marco's 1937 The How and When.

name: Cosmopolitan cocktail (Toby Cecchini's recipe)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Citroen Vodka
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
review: This 2:1:1:1 original Cosmopolitan is on the tart side of balanced with the citrus-flavoured vodka shining over the other ingredients. Indeed, Toby describes his Cosmo as being "kind of a brutal sour, it's very very tart."
history:
The original Cosmopolitan cocktail recipe as created in 1988 by Toby Cecchini at The Odeon in New York City. Toby's recipe used the then newly launched Absolut Citron and Cointreau triple sec.
Cosmopolitan cocktail history and development

name: Double Grape Martini
preparation: MUDDLE grapes in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
10 fresh	Green grapes (seedless)
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
2⁄3 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: The wine adds complexity to this simple grape cocktail - hence "Double" Grape Martini.
history: Created in 2004 by yours truly, London, England.

name: Dawa
preparation:
1. Cut a ripe lime in half (from pole to pole) and remove the core from each half by cutting a V-shape grove. (You'll need one-half of the lime per cocktail). Chop a cored half into 3 wedges, then slice each wedge in half to produce 6 chunks of lime and drop these into the serving glass.
2. MUDDLE lime chunks in the base of the glass.
3. Add vodka and honey-loaded honey dipper stick (or bar spoon of honey) and use the dipper stick (or spoon) to STIR until the honey is dissolved.
4. Add sugar syrup and fill the glass with crushed ice leaving the dipper stick as a garnish for the drinker to continue stirring.
ingredients:
1⁄2 fresh	Lime (fresh) (chopped wedges)
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 barspoon	Honey
1⁄3 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
review: Similar to the Caipirovska in its use of vodka and lime, but the Dawa is sweetened with honey.
history:
Inspired by the Brazilian Caipirinha and originally made and named during the 1980s at the Carnivore Restaurant in Nairobi, this cocktail is particularly popular in upscale hotel bars in Kenya where it's enjoyed by the safari set. The name translates from Kiswahili as 'medicine'.

It should be noted that in Kenya, a Dowa is also the name for a non-alcoholic drink made with honey, ginger and lime juice, made with hot water.

name: Gold Rush
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. (Some like to Regal Shake with a swath of pink grapefruit zest.)
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A Whiskey Sour made with honey syrup in place of sugar.
history: Recipe envisaged by T. J. Siegel one night in 2001 at Milk & Honey, New York City, USA, where it was first made by Sasha Petraske.

name: Dry Orange Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Bone dry, orangey, aptly named Martini.
history: Created in 2003 by Wayne Collins for Maxxium UK.

name: Espresso Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water) (optional)
review: A rum-based twist on the ubiquitous and very tasty Espresso Martini.

name: Flying Scotsman
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters

history:
Named after what is perhaps the world's most famous steam locomotive, The Flying Scotsman set two world records, the first steam locomotive reach 100 miles per hour and the longest non-stop run by a steam locomotive (422 miles in 1989 whilst in Australia). The Flying Scotsman was built in 1923 for the London and North Eastern Railway (LNER) at Doncaster and took its name from London to Edinburgh Flying Scotsman express service which it ran. This cocktail was apparently originally served to first-class passengers on board the train.

Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Golden Retriever

1⁄2 shot	Licor 43 Original liqueur

history: Adapted from a recipe created by Dick Bradsell at Alfred's, London, England. Dick's original recipe was equal parts without the water and was served straight-up in a Martini glass.

The Harlem Cocktail first appears in print in the 1934 book Old Mr. Boston Bartender's Guide and then in Charlie Conolly's The World Famous Cotton Club: 1939 Book of Mixed Drinks.

Adapted from a drink discovered in 2001 at Teatro, London, England.

Sours cocktails history

At his receptions, he served an aperitif made with the locally produced crème de cassis and Bourgogne Aligoté white wine. The concoction eventually became known as Kir Apéritif.

name: Passion Fruit Caipirinha
garnish: Stirrer (spoon, wooden lolly stick or stick cut from sugar cane)
preparation:
1. Cut lime in half (from pole to pole) and then slice one of the halves into eight 3-4mm thick half-moon shaped segments and drop into the base of a robust rocks glass.

2. Add 3 bar spoons caster sugar (or ½oz / 15ml sugar syrup 2:1) and MUDDLE.

3. Chop passion fruit in half and scoop flesh into the rocks glass and MUDDLE some more.

4. When sure fruit juice is fully extracted and the sugar dissolved, transfer the muddled fruit and sugar into serving glass (preferably a 30cl / 10oz hi-ball glass).

5. POUR cachaça (stored in the freezer) into the rocks glass (used to muddle) and swirl to rinse glass before pouring cachaça into serving glass. STIR to ensure all ingredients are well mixed.

6. Crack (rather than crush) four to five large ice cubes and drop into serving glass. STIR before topping with more ice and serve with a stirrer (but no straws).
ingredients:
1⁄2 fresh	Lime (fresh) (chopped)
3 barspoon	Caster/ Superfine/Baker's special sugar (white)
1 fresh	Passion fruit (fresh)
2 shot	Cachaça (from freezer)
review: A very tasty fruity Caipirinha.
history: For information on the history and other variations of the Caipirinha, please see our Caipirinha cocktail page.

Spritz history

name: Pink Gin
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
1 shot	Chilled water (reduce if wet ice)
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review:
This is a cocktail that likes dilution, hence the shot of water in my recipe. And, a spoon full (or ½ spoon) of sugar certainly helps the medicine go down where the Pink Gin is concerned. However, the more sugar you add, the less dilution you'll need. Hit the perfect balance (hopefully my recipe) and this is a great cocktail, but it's an equilibrium that's down to personal taste so tricky to attain.

I've opted for more characterful old tom gin, but London dry gin also works well, especially if you double the sugar to 5ml (1 bar spoon).
history:
The Pink Gin cocktail is so named due to aromatic bitters giving the main ingredient, gin, a pink tinge.

Originally, gin at room temperature was simply poured into a glass that had been primed with a few dashes of bitters and swirled to coat the inside. No ice was used. Ice simply wasn't available.

The creation of this cocktail is said to have started with the discovery of Angostura Bitters by Henry Workshop, an English ship's surgeon serving on H.M.S. Hercules. In 1826, his ship was patrolling the Caribbean on watch for slave trader vessels when he came across the bitters which had been created two years earlier by Johann Gottlieb Benjamin Siegert (1796-1870), a German doctor who had settled in Venezuela where he was Surgeon-General of a military hospital in the town of Angostura. Siegert had created the now famous bitters to treat stomach disorders and indigestion of his fellow settlers, not to make cocktails.

Now the city of Ciudad Bolivar (renamed in 1846 in honour of Simon Bolivar), the town of Angostura sits on the mighty Orinoco River, connecting it with the Caribbean basin and it is via this river, and its trade, that Siegert's bitters found their way around the islands of the Caribbean with sailors being likely customers for any potion believed to treat upset stomachs and sea sickness.

The British Admiralty already prescribed the use of chinchona bark (quinia) to ward against tropical diseases and, as a medical man, Workshop was interested in Angostura as he had heard the preparation included chinchona and many other herbal remedies. He procured a couple of bottles of the bitters while on shore leave in George Town, a port in the Cayman Islands. Back onboard ship, he and the ship's captain, Jack Bristow, mixed a small amount of the medicinal bitters with their gin ration and found the pink drink produced agreeable. They served their new creation to the other officers on the ship. Word spread and 'Pink Gin' as it became known, became popular with officers of the Royal Navy. By the mid-19th century, the drink became widely served throughout England.

A riff on a classic Dry Martini.
Dry Martini history and recipe variations

name: Tom Collins
garnish: Skewered orange slice wheel & Luxardo Maraschino cherry (sail)
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda and briefly stir.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A medium-dry Gin Collins based on old tom gin. There is much confusion between Tom Collins and John Collins; arguably, the two names are interchangeable [see history below]. However, I follow the convention that a Tom Collins is based on old tom gin while a John Collins is made with London dry gin (although a John Collins was originally made with genever. Today, that's a Dutch or Genever Collins).
history: In his 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks, David A. Embury says "The original Collinses were always made with gin but, strangely enough, never with London dry gin - the very liquor that is practically always used in making a Collins today. The Tom Collins was made with Old Tom gin and the John Collins with Holland gin [jenever]." He goes on to explain the confusion/difference between a Tom and John Collins:

name: Treacle No.1
preparation: STIR half of the rum, sugar syrup and bitters with two ice cubes in glass. Add rest of rum, another couple of ice cubes and STIR again. Fill glass with ice and STIR again. Finally FLOAT apple juice.
ingredients:
2 shot	Jamaican-style overproof aged pot still rum
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Richly flavoured, almost like molasses.
history: This twist on the Old-Fashioned was created by Dick Bradsell in the 1990s' London. Like the original, it takes a few minutes to make and there are no shortcuts. The apple juice Dick originally used is the cheap clear stuff rather than the posh pressed cloudy apple juice. In this drink, cheap is best.

name: Vanderbilt
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) & skewered Luxardo maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review:
Tangy, rich cherry and hints of vanilla fortified with brandy.

My previous specs for this cocktail were to serve in a coupe glass and called for a generous 67.5ml (2¼oz) cognac, 22.5ml (¾oz) cherry brandy, 5ml (1 bar spoon) sugar syrup, and aromatic bitters. In July 2022, in a quest for some semblance of sobriety, I reduced the volume of this boozy late-night treat back by a third to better suit a Nick & Nora glass.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Robert Vermeire's 1922 Cocktails: How to Mix Them which gives the origin of this cocktail as being at "the Kursaal" in Ostend, Belgium, where, as the name would suggest, it was made for a member of the wealthy Vanderbilt family. However, Colonel Cornelius Vanderbilt, the American railroad tycoon cited by Vermeire died in 1877 so this cocktail is more likely to have been made for his great-grandson, Alfred Gwynne Vanderbilt (1877–1915) who died as a passenger on the RMS Lusitania ocean liner when it was sunk by a German U-boat torpedo during WWI.

name: Vanilla Daiquiri

name: Yellow Belly

review: Lemon, lemon and lemon, but well-balanced, refreshing and tasty. A great early summer's evening cocktail.
history: Originally named Yellow Belly Martini, this was a popular neo-martini in London during the 1990s.

name: Bee's Knees
preparation:
SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

Alternatively, if making with raw honey (rather than syrup), STIR 4 spoons honey with 22.5ml (¾oz) lemon juice and 10ml (⅓oz) orange juice in base of shaker until honey is dissolved. Add 60ml (2oz gin), SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review:
The combination of honey and lemon suggests flu relief but don't wait for an ailment before trying this soothing concoction.

The beneficial addition of a splash of orange juice to a Bee's Knees (classically it's just gin, lemon and honey) comes from David Embury's 1948 book The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks where he says, "The addition of a small amount of orange juice makes for an interesting variation".
history: For years, thanks to David A. Embury, the Bee's Knees was thought to have emerged in America during Prohibition when it was said the lemon juice and honey in this cocktail masked the poor quality of gin. However, the Bee's Knees actually originated on the other side of the Atlantic in Paris, France.

name: Amber Room No. 2

1 1⁄3 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄3 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Too many, and you're in it.
history:
Created in 2007 by Ted Kilgore at Monarch Restaurant, Maplewood, USA. This recipe is an adaptation from an adapted recipe by Gary Regan and first published in his column in The San Francisco Chronicle. Apparently, Kilgore created this drink as a pick-me-up, but perhaps better suited to being a (put-you-down) late-night nightcap.
Comment: Too many and you're in it.

name: Sherry Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Palo cortado sherry
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: The huge flavour of sherry is freshened by lemon juice and rounded by egg white.
history: Adapted from a cocktail discovered in 2007 at Suba in New York City, USA.

name: Italian Margarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
2⁄3 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A liberal dash of amaretto adds very Italian subtexts of apricot and almond to a classic Margarita.
history: Discovered in 2005 at the Club Bar in The Peninsula Beverly Hills, USA.

name: Apple Martini (with apple schnapps)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Apple Schnapps liqueur
1 2⁄3 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review: There are as many different recipes for this drink as there are varieties of apple and brands of apple liqueur: this one was popular in the UK during the Noughties.

name: Japanese Maple
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 3⁄4 shot	Japanese blended whisky
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Maple syrup
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: This excellent Japanese whisky-based sour is balanced with maple syrup.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2009 by Damian Windsor at The Roger Room, Los Angeles, USA.

name: Negroni Tredici
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄4 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: A amaro riff on the Negroni.
history:
Adapted from a drink created in 2009 by Toby Maloney of Alchemy Consulting, USA.
Negroni cocktail history and recipe variations

name: Smoke and Mirrors No.2
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Averna Amaro
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A hardcore but sublime drink.
history: Adapted from a drink discovered in 2010 at Raines Law Rooms in New York City, USA.

name: The Quad
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Oranje Vodka
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Four different, orange-flavoured ingredients combine in this complex bittersweet citrusy cocktail.
history: Created in 2010 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Green Deacon
preparation: MIST chilled glass with spray or rinse of absinthe to coat the inside and set aside. SHAKE other ingredients with ice and fine strain into absinthe-rinsed chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄24 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Actually, a shade of orange-red rather than green, the name is a reference to the absinthe in this unusual combination of ingredients. The absinthe-rinse is a subtle addition to the Rosy Deacon but propels this classic into a more interesting place.
history: Created in 2009 by Jim Meehan at PDT in New York City, USA, this is a riff on the Rosy Deacon in Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide.

name: Millennium Cocktail
garnish: Orange zest twist & dust with grated nutmeg
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
5⁄6 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Somewhat reminiscent of a cognac-laced Hawaiian pizza. Yum!
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Dale DeGroff, New York City, USA.

name: Oaxaca Old-Fashioned
preparation: STIR tequila with three ice cubes in a glass. Add other ingredients and STIR with more ice. Top up ice and STIR some more.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄4 shot	Agave syrup
4 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review:
An agave-based old-fashioned with a wonderful hit of smokiness from the mezcal.

Like many cocktails, Philip's original recipe (of 45 ml Reposado tequila, 15 ml Mezcal, 7.5 ml Agave syrup and 1 dash Angostura bitters) has morphed with chocolate bitters now favoured by many in place of Angostura (as per the recipe above). If using a "sweeter" style glycerine-based (rather than alcohol-based) chocolate bitters, such as Fee Brothers, or you have a bone-dry palate, then consider reducing the agave syrup to 5ml.
history:
Created 2007 by Philip Ward at Death & Co., New York City, USA.

See: Old-Fashioned cocktail history

name: Smoky Old Bastard
preparation: STIR half the bourbon, tea bag and four ice cubes in glass for 60 seconds. Remove tea bag, add maple syrup and bitters, and STIR some more. Add more ice and the rest of the bourbon. STIR lots more and add more ice.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 bag	Lapsang Souchong tea (cold)
1⁄4 shot	Maple syrup
2 dash	Boker's bitters
review: Lapsang souchong flavours and dry tannins are balanced by maple syrup and fortified with bourbon.
history: Created in 2011 by Craig Toone at Glovers Bar in Merseyside, England who says of his drink, "'Smoky' obviously refers to the distinctive tea flavour and the bastard refers to the bastardisation of the classic drink [Old Fashioned]."

name: Applejack Rabbit
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Maple syrup
review: Apple brandy, orange and tart lemon enriched with maple syrup. Strike the perfect balance and this is a delicious combination. This cocktail's name alone suggests making it with American applejack brandy rather than French calvados, and when made with 45ml (1½oz) straight bottled-in-bond 50% alc./vol. applejack in place of the calvados, it's arguably a better cocktail.
history: The Apple Jack Rabbit appears in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book and in David A. Embury's 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks where he tells us "This drink is also sometimes, for no reason at all, called the Applejack Dynamite. The same cocktail made with a gin base plus a dash of Angostura is called the Old Vermont."

name: Vodka Daisy
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. CHURN (stir) drink with ice and serve with straws.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Raspberry (framboise) sugar syrup
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Dependent on your raspberry syrup (homemade is best) you'll either have a beautifully fruity and refreshing drink, or one that's a tad on the sweet side. Adjust to taste.

name: Fino Flip
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 fresh	Egg yolk
review: Salty tang of fino balanced and given extra richness by the egg.

name: The Ansonia
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄12 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Scotch with delicate notes of sweet vermouth, maraschino and absinthe. Subtle and refined.
history:
Adapted from a recipe by Charles Christopher in his 1934 Pioneers of Mixing at Elite Bars and named after a luxurious residential hotel on Manhattan's Upper West Side. The Ansonia was built in 1904 and was the permanent home of the rich and famous including baseball player Babe Ruth, composer Igor Stravinsky, writer Theodore Dreiser and operatic tenor Enrico Caruso. The first air-conditioned hotel in New York, the hotel's opulence was legendary and included a lobby pool and fountain which was home to a family of live seals.

The original recipe called for dashes of Ojen bitters rather than absinthe. However, absinthe was banned in the USA at the time and Ojen was a Spanish brand of absinthe, so this was a way to communicate the use of absinthe to other bartenders without highlighting the fact to authorities.

name: Bijou Cocktail (Difford's recipe)
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) & skewered Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: It is not uncommon to see this drink stipulated with equal parts gin, Chartreuse and sweet vermouth, as called for in Harry Johnson's Bartender's Manual. In fact, that's the norm. Equal parts works, but it makes for a drink strong enough to drop a rhinoceros with Chartreuse overly dominant (and I love Chartreuse).
history:
Recipe adapted from Harry Johnson's 1900 Bartender's Manual which calls for "1/3 wine glass Chartreuse (green); 1/3 wine glass vermouth (Italian); 1/3 wine glass of Plymouth gin; 1 dash orange bitters". The Bijou first appeared in C. F. Lawlor's 1895 book The Mixicologist as equal parts gin, Grand Marnier and sweet vermouth.

Good story: The word 'bijou' is French for 'jewel', and this cocktail's name was inspired by the jewel-like colours of the ingredients: diamond for gin; ruby for rosso vermouth and emerald for Chartreuse Verte.

name: The Lone Ranger
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Very slightly sweet tequila and lemon, lengthened and dried with brut sparkling wine.
history: Created in 2012 by Jeffrey Morgenthaler, Oregon, USA.

name: Amber Nectar
preparation: STIR honey with Scotch in base of shaker until honey dissolves. ADD other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄4 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
2 barspoon	Honey
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: Honey lifts and enhances this blend of Scotch whisky, single Islay malt and dry vermouth.
history: Adapted by yours truly from a cocktail promoted in 2013 by Bols, the Dutch liqueur producer. Originally based on vodka with Bols honey liqueur, the honey cried out for blended Scotch whisky and then some Islay single malt. It's called the Amber Nectar after all.

name: Marvin's Last Word
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Kleos Mastiha liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: The distinctive notes of mastiha and Chartreuse shine in this Greek riff on the classic Last Word.
history:
Created by Christos Chouseas at 42 Bar in Athens, Greece – a bar where The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy and the work of Douglas Adams influences many of the drink names.

In The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy book, the number 42 is the "answer to the ultimate question of life, the universe, and everything", while 'Marvin' is a paranoid, depressive android.

See also Last Word history

name: La Poire des Bénédictines
garnish: Pear wedge speared with cube of Roquefort cheese
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Poire William eau-de-vie
3⁄4 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Pear and cognac are a match made in heaven. Bénédictine adds honeyed sweetness and herbal complexity to this after-dinner cocktail.
history: Adapted from a drink promoted by Grey Goose in 2013 and originally using their La Poire vodka.

name: Negroni and the Goat
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
3⁄4 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Averna Amaro
review: Negroni in name and Negroni in style with the sweetness of Aperol countered by the use of amaro.
history: This riff on a Negroni was originally served straight-up in a coupe and comes from The Girl And The Goat restaurant in Chicago, USA where it was created in 2014.

name: Petanque cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Fino sherry
1 shot	Disaronno amaretto
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: The game this drink is named after is French while the main ingredients are Spanish and Italian, but they do play Pétanque in the Basque region of Spain. However, both the creator of this drink and the Creole-style bitters used originate from the USA – perhaps it took a non-European to bring these ingredients - fino sherry and amaretto - harmoniously together.
history:
Adapted from a drink created in 2014 by Andrew Bohrer at Mistral Kitchen, Seattle, USA, and named after the French game where hollow metal balls are thrown as close as possible to a small wooden jack ball.

Inspired by playing Petanque in France whilst sipping on pastis, I tried Andrew's original spec but with an additional float of absinthe. To be honest, I tried pastis first but the liquorice notes detracted from the cocktail. A couple of dashes of absinthe merge with the body of the cocktail to add harmonious additional complexity. Hope you agree.

name: Roman Highball
preparation: SHAKE first three ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Averna Amaro
3⁄4 shot	Ginger liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water (chilled)
review: Refreshing and Pimm's Cup-like. A great long drink to come home to.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created by Danny Gil at Weather Up, New York City, USA.

Information on Highball cocktails, their history and tips on the perfect serve can be found on our page.

name: Smoky Tears cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1 1⁄2 shot	Kleos Mastiha liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Best described as being a mezcal, mastiha and pink grapefruit Margarita. It’s a great combo. Mastiha freshness with a hint of smoky mezcal is balanced by slightly acidic pink grapefruit juice.

name: Sakura Martini
garnish: Fresh cherry blossom (or make do with an olive if out of season)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Akashi-Tai Daiginjo Genshu sake
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄12 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: This Reverse Martini-style cocktail originally featured a floating salted cherry blossom as a garnish. This is not just for looks, the hint of saltiness it lends this delicate drink replaces the savoury note which an olive typically brings to a Martini.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Kenta Goto. This is the house Martini at his Bar Goto in New York City, USA where it is garnished with a salted cherry blossom (rather than including saline solution in the recipe).

See: Martini cocktail and its evolution

name: Joy Division
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: A 2:1 Dry Martini with a slug of triple sec and dashes of absinthe contributing zesty orange and subtle aniseed respectively.
history: Recipe created in 2008 by Phil Ward at Death & Co., New York, USA.

name: Bennett Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into a chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: The judicious dashing of bitters makes or breaks this Gimlet-like cocktail which tastes good when made with a dry gin but better when made with an old tom gin, as per the original 1922 recipe. (If your old tom gin is sweet, reduce the sugar syrup.)
history:
The Bennett Cocktail was first published in Robert Vermeire's 1922 Cocktails: How to Mix Them and then repeated in the 1930 book Cocktails by "Jimmy" Late of Ciro's London written by the mysterious Jimmy. Both recipes are based on old tom gin and without the addition of sugar.

Most modern versions of the Bennett, including that made in 2015 by Meaghan Dorman at The Bennett in New York City, USA call for dry gin rather than old tom.

name: Pour Me Another
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄4 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
1⁄6 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water
review: Raisiny pedro ximénez sherry adds subtle richness to the cognac with hints of flavour from the absinthe and lemon zest. This drink benefits from generous dilution so consider adding a splash of water.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Noel Ekstrand at Astrum Grill & Raw Bar, Trondheim, Norway.

name: Celebration
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Reminiscent of a brandy-based Negroni served straight-up.
history: Created in 2015 by Devis D'Ercole at Imperial Beach, San Benedetto del Tronto, Marche, Italy. Originally with Martini Rubino vermouth.

name: Three Hundred Poems
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 barspoon	Blackcurrant jam (preserve)
review: Blackcurrant jam adds rich concentrated berry notes to this attractive crimson red cognac laced cocktail.
history: Created in 2015 by Konrad Kaczmarzyk at ECC Chinatown, London, England.

name: The Addington
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1 dash	Boker's bitters
review: A beautifully balanced, spirit-forward, stirred, cognac-based cocktail with Vermouth di Torino and herbal liqueur.
history: Created in 2015 by Guy Butler at Muddlers in Sydenham, London, England.

name: The Good, The Bad and the Ugni
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably block of ice). Lastly, FLOAT Chartreuse.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Canadian icewine
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
review: Perhaps it's the holier-than-thou Chartreuse that is playing the part of the bad guy in this tasty drink. The cognac (made with Ugni Blanc grapes) play the strong, characterful part.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Alex Mills at Lab 22 in Cardiff, Wales. Alex's original recipe calls for Martell Cordon Bleu.

name: Toasted Old Fashioned Godfather
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Disaronno amaretto
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Rye whiskey spice and Angostura bitters offset bourbon's richness and amaretto's sweetness in this complex, dry and boozy after-dinner drink. If you like this, then also consider a Smoked Almond Old Fashioned.
history:
Created in June 2016 by yours truly at The Cabinet Room, London, England.
See: History of the Old-Fashioned cocktail

name: Almond Old Fashioned (bourbon based)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄3 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1⁄6 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Bourbon's sweet notes are lifted and amplified by amaretto's almond flavours. For a slightly drier, more complex version of this drink try a Toasted Almond Old Fashioned.
history: See history of the Old-Fashioned cocktail.

name: Tuxedo Affumicato
garnish: Orange zest twist and a mist of Liquore Strega from an atomizer over drink
preparation: STIR first four ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
2⁄3 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Mezcal lends a lightly smoky note to this riff on the classic Tuxedo. This boozy Martini-esque cocktail makes for a great aperitif.
history:
Created in 2016 by Riccardo Aletta (AKA 'Ricky D Wing') at Holy Birds in London, England.
See: Tuxedo cocktail history

name: Via Roma
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2⁄3 shot	Ferro China Baliva
review: This aperitivo cocktail will appeal to lovers of Italian amari.
history: Created in 2017 by Mattia Conti at London Cocktail Club, Shoreditch, London, England. Originally named Bartender's Elixir.

name: Dramble
preparation: POUR first 3 ingredients into glass filled with crushed ice and STIR/SWIZZLE. Lastly, DRIZZLE crème de mûre around surface of drink.
ingredients:
2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Crème de Mûre liqueur
review: Basically, a whisky sour served over crushed ice with a dash of rich crème de mûre. For whisky drinkers this Scotch whisky riff on Dick Bradsell’s classic Bramble is even better than the original gin based cocktail.
history: Created in 2013 by Jacob Briars at Aberfeldy Distillery during a tasting session, this is a Dewar’s whisky twist on the on the Bramble, hence the name Dramble. The name is also fitting as Tommy Dewar, one of the two brothers who built the Aberfeldy Distillery and the Dewar’s whisky brand, being known for his Ramble Round the Globe book, so there’s a pun at play there too.

name: Kiwi Caipirinha
garnish: Stirrer (spoon, wooden lolly stick or stick cut from sugar cane)
preparation:
1. Cut lime in half (from pole to pole) and then slice one of the halves into eight 3-4mm thick half-moon shaped segments and drop into the base of a robust rocks glass.

2. Add 3 bar spoons caster sugar (or ½oz/15ml sugar syrup 2:1) and MUDDLE.

3. Add slices of kiwi and MUDDLE some more.

4. When sure fruit juice is fully extracted and the sugar dissolved, transfer the muddled fruit and sugar into serving glass (preferably a 30cl / 10oz highball glass).

5. POUR cachaça (stored in the freezer) into the rocks glass (used to muddle) and swirl to rinse glass before pouring cachaça into serving glass. STIR to ensure all ingredients are well mixed.

6. Crack (rather than crush) four to five large ice cubes and drop into serving glass. STIR before topping with more ice and serve with a stirrer (but no straws).
ingredients:
1⁄2 fresh	Lime (fresh) (chopped)
3 barspoon	Caster/ Superfine/Baker's special sugar (white)
1⁄2 fresh	Kiwi fruit (fresh) (chopped)
2 shot	Cachaça (from freezer)
review: Fruity and refreshing, perfect for a summer afternoon.
history: Caipirinha cocktail history.

name: Jäger Old-Fashioned
garnish: Luxardo Maraschino cherry and orange zest twist
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Jägermeisteror other German amaro
2⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄6 shot	Maple syrup
3 dash	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: Rewarding, chocolaty and boozy with complex herbal and fruity notes.
history:
Created in 2017 by Florian Beuren, Jägermeister's UK brand ambassador.

For a more detailed history of the Old-Fashioned cocktail, along with additional recipes, see our page.

name: Bijou (by Jamie Gordon)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review: This bittersweet digestivo is one of those drinks that becomes easier and gets better as dilution, from the melting ice, opens and softens.
history: Adapted from a 2018 recipe by Jamie Gordon, San Francisco, USA.

name: Pineapple Caipirinha
garnish: Stirrer (spoon, wooden lolly stick or stick cut from sugar cane)
preparation:
1. Cut lime in half (from pole to pole) and then slice one of the halves into eight 3-4mm thick half-moon shaped segments and drop into the base of a robust rocks glass.

2. Add 3 bar spoons caster sugar (or ½oz / 15ml sugar syrup 2:1) and MUDDLE.

3. Add pineapple and MUDDLE some more.

4. When sure fruit juice is fully extracted and the sugar dissolved, transfer the muddled fruit and sugar into serving glass (preferably a 30cl / 10oz hi-ball glass).

5. POUR cachaça (stored in the freezer) into the rocks glass (used to muddle) and swirl to rinse glass before pouring cachaça into serving glass. STIR to ensure all ingredients are well mixed.

6. Crack (rather than crush) four to five large ice cubes using an Ice Tapper and drop into serving glass. STIR before topping with more ice and serve with a stirrer (but no straws).
ingredients:
1⁄2 fresh	Lime (fresh) (chopped)
3 barspoon	Caster/ Superfine/Baker's special sugar (white)
1⁄2 slice	Pineapple (fresh) (chopped)
2 shot	Cachaça (from freezer)
review: Natural acids from the pineapple make this tarter in flavour than some other fruit Caipirinhas, those with a sweet tooth may want to add an extra ½ spoon of sugar.
history: For information on the history and other variations of the Caipirinha, please see our Caipirinha cocktail page.

name: French 75 (Judge Jr's 1927 recipe)
preparation: STIR powdered sugar with lemon juice in base of shaker until sugar dissolves. Add gin, SHAKE with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with champagne and lightly stir.
ingredients:
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3 barspoon	Powdered sugar (white sugar ground in mortar and pestle) (or use 5ml of 2:1 sugar syrup per spoon)
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Judge Jr's original 1927 recipe calls for "2 jiggers Gordon water; 1 part lemon juice; a spoonful of powdered sugar; cracked ice. Fill up the rest of a tall glass with champagne!" I've loosely interpreted this recipe to the one above (with the 3 spoons of powdered sugar being flat 5ml measuring spoons). The result is dangerously quaffable gin spiked champagne with a zesty lemon bite. The powered sugar adds an attractive sherbet note, but if you prefer to use sugar syrup then substitute with ½oz/15ml (2:1).
history:
Adapted from a recipe in the 1927 book Here's How by Judge Jr..
See: French 75 history.

name: French 95 (a French '75' with bourbon)
preparation: STIR powdered sugar with lemon juice in base of shaker until sugar dissolves. Add bourbon, SHAKE with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with champagne and lightly stir.
ingredients:
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3 barspoon	Powdered sugar (white sugar ground in mortar and pestle) (or use 5ml of 2:1 sugar syrup per spoon)
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
2 1⁄2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Jones' original 1977 recipe, which consists: 2oz/60ml bourbon, 1oz/30ml lemon juice and 2 spoons sugar, topped with champagne, is built in the glass. This makes for a very powerful drink. Hence, we hope Jones would approve of our tweaking his recipe and shaking to mix. The result still has some oomph, but with the extra dilution of shaking, is a tad more harmonious.
history:
Adapted from a recipe in Stanley M. Jones' 1977 book Jones Complete Barguide.

More information on the history and variants of the French 75 can be found on our page.

name: Red Earl
preparation: MUDDLE raspberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
10 fresh	Raspberries
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: This vodka-laced, rich (but not overly sweet) raspberry cocktail is a crowd-pleaser.

name: French 125 (French '75' with cognac) Jones' 1977 recipe
preparation: STIR powdered sugar with lemon juice in base of shaker until sugar dissolves. Add cognac, SHAKE with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with champagne and lightly stir.
ingredients:
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3 barspoon	Powdered sugar (white sugar ground in mortar and pestle) (or use 5ml of 2:1 sugar syrup per spoon)
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Jones' original 1977 built in the glass recipe, which consists: 2oz/60ml cognac, 1oz/30ml lemon juice and 2 spoons sugar, topped with champagne, is a powerful drink. Hence, we hope Jones would approve of our tweaking his recipe. The result still has plenty of oomph behind it, but with the extra dilution of shaking, is a tad more harmonious.
history:
A cognac-based version of the gin-based French 75 cocktail, which was named after the French 75mm field gun used by the French army during WWI. This cognac version is appropriately named after another gun, the tank mounted Soviet 2A46 (also called D-81T) 125mm/L48 smoothbore cannon. This recipe is adapted from a recipe in Stanley M. Jones' 1977 book Jones Complete Barguide, modern French 125 recipes tend to be served straight-up in a flute glass.

French 75 history and variations

name: Swiss Account
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄3 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
2 dash	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
review: A vodka charged bittersweet aperitif with herbal notes laced with grainy vodka.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2017 by Griffin Cox at Lot Six, Halifax, Canada.

Griffin says, "Hailed as a venerable French bitter, the story of Suze veritably began to the west in Switzerland before it was brought across the border by Fernand Moureaux in 1885. The Swiss Account pays homage to that beginning and shows how Suze finds its home alongside other French spirits just as it found its home in French palates over a century ago."

Griffin's original recipe calls for 45ml Grey Goose Vodka, 15ml Suze, 5ml Bénédictine and 2 dash Bittermens Hopped Grapefruit Bitters.

name: Black Manhattan
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Averna Amaro
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A classic Manhattan with amaro in place of sweet vermouth. Heavier in style and with distinctive bitter chocolate and light spice.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Todd Smith at Bourbon & Branch in San Francisco, USA.

See: Manhattan cocktail history

name: Death Star
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1 shot	Strega liqueur
1 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1 dash	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
review: This equal-parts stirred cocktail is either a spirit-forward aperitivo or a bittersweet digestif come nightcap. Whatever classification it falls into, it's tasty.

name: Purpurina Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco (Jalapeño chilli infused)
1 shot	Watermelon sugar syrup
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: With a whole measure of watermelon syrup, you may expect this cocktail to be on the sweet side. Instead, it is beautifully balanced with delicate Jalapeño heat – at least it is if you go easy with the amount of Jalapeño you infuse in your pisco.
history: Created by David Osborne at Bellota tapas bar, San Francisco, USA. Incidentally, purpurina is Spanish for glitter / tinsel.

name: Thyme Will Tell Sour
garnish: Lemon zest twist (expressed and discarded) & thyme sprig
preparation: MUDDLE thyme (strip leaves from stem) in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 fresh	Fresh thyme
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Maple syrup
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Thyme and maple syrup add extra interest to a Whiskey Sour. Some may want to add egg white.
history: Adapted from a recipe discovered at The Sea Fire Grill, New York City, USA.

name: Iron & Sand Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
3⁄4 shot	Ferro China Baliva
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: This dark bittersweet aperitivo also works well when served on-the-rocks in an old-fashioned glass. A riff on the classic Blood & Sand, made distinctive by the use of Ferro China.
history: Created March 2018 by yours truly at The Cabinet Room in London, England.

name: Sorrentino Cocktail
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly STIR.
ingredients:
1 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Bittersweet with pleasing rich lemon zestiness from the limoncello.
history: A well-established and popular cocktail in southern Italy (Mezzogiorno), the home of limoncello.

name: Black Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Dark/black/blackstrap rum
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: More deep golden amber than black in appearance, this Daquiri takes its name from the black rum (well, dark brown rum) it's made with. Pungent rum notes sit well with zingy citrus.

name: Gin Sling (no added sugar & low-calorie)
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda water.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar-free sweetener
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Light and refreshing with lemon freshening gin while a splash of sugar-free sweetener provides balance.
history:
Adapted from the classic serve by yours truly (Simon Difford) in January 2019.

You may also be interested in the story behind the Singapore Sling.

name: Daiquiri (no added sugar & low-calorie)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar-free sweetener
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Light and delicate, and not overly citrusy so allowing the rum to shine. And it's sugar-free! At least it is if you choose your rum carefully.
history:
Adapted from the classic serve by yours truly (Simon Difford) in January 2019.

name: Espresso Martini (no sugar & low-calorie)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
5⁄12 shot	Sugar-free sweetener
1⁄2 pinch	Salt (sea salt)
review: Slightly thinner in mouthfeel than a regular sugar loaded Espresso Martini but equally as tasty.
history:
Recipe adapted from Dick Bradsell's contemporary classic by yours truly (Simon Difford) in January 2019.

Also see the origin and story behind the Cosmopolitan cocktail.

name: Gin Basil Smash (no added sugar & low-calorie)
preparation: Gently MUDDLE basil in base of SHAKER with Gin. ADD other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
8 fresh	Basil leaves
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Sugar-free sweetener
review: Herbal and refreshing. Basil, gin and lemon sit harmoniously, balanced by sugar-free sweetener.
history: Adapted from Joerg Meyer's original Gin Basil Smash by yours truly (Simon Difford) in January 2019.

name: Mint Julep (no sugar & low-calorie)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into julep cup half filled with crushed ice. STIR the drink with the crushed ice using a bar spoon. Top up the cup with more crushed ice and STIR again. Repeat this process so the drink fills the cup and frost forms on the outside.
ingredients:
12 fresh	Mint leaves
1 2⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Sugar-free sweetener
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters (optional)
review:
Bourbon with minty freshness served ice cold with the hint of sweetness amplifying flavours provided by sweetener rather than sugar.

This drink is better with the addition of dashes of aromatic bitters but this will add trace amounts of sugar.
history:
Adapted from the classic serve by yours truly (Simon Difford) in January 2019.

For more Julep recipes, its origins and history, see Julep cocktails

name: Tom Collins (no added sugar & low-calorie)
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Sugar-free sweetener
3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: If opting to make this Tom Collins with an Old Tom gin (as it should be), beware which brand you choose as many Old Tom gins contain sugar.
history:
Adapted from the classic serve by yours truly (Simon Difford) in January 2019.

Also see Collins Cocktails - recipes & history.

name: Weekly Special
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Mentzendorff Kümmel liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Not far removed from an Aviation. Depending on your grapefruit juice, this particular Special may be very slightly on the sweet side but it's fantastically aromatic. If you find too sweet, then slightly up the grapefruit juice.
history: Adapted from a recipe first published in William James "Billy" Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Bar Book.

name: Double Black
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
1 1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1 1⁄3 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
3 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: Dark bitter chocolate and rich espresso with delicate spice.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 Wilson Hernandez at El Del Frente, Havana, Cuba.

name: Highland Highball
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
