1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Bénédictine and sweet vermouth add richness and herbal complexity to this scotch whisky highball.
history: Highball cocktail history and perfect serve.

name: Ad Astra
garnish: Float one drop of castor oil
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. (Ideally, use strained lemon juice. Otherwise, fine strain cocktail when pouring.)
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Crème de violette liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Ad Astra is a Latin phrase meaning "to the stars", an apt name for this spirituous and complex riff on a classic Aviation.
history:
Created by Ben Simpson of Smoke & Oakum Manufactory Ltd, Wellington, New Zealand and the name behind Gunpowder Rum. Ben shared his "spin on the old Aviation cocktail" with us in May 2019 saying, "Somewhere along the line I got it into my head that the Aviation was, at heart, a martini variant (I think I even found some gin/maraschino type cocktails to back my argument). For this reason, the lemon juice is vastly reduced, and the drink is stirred.

"To this idea, I added the suggestion that the washed-out purple colour of crème de violette in the finished drink references aviation fuel (or 'Av-Gas' as they used to call it when I did my basic flight training). Then I kept making stuff up as I prepared the drink: the spinning of the ice within the mixing glass is similar to the action of the rotary engine that dominated the early years of flight, with the mixing spoon being the propeller shaft. Finally, the drop of castor oil on top harks back to the use of this in rotary engines to keep the whole hot, spinning mass from seizing. Unfortunately, the result of this was a slipstream saturated in castor oil, including both the plane and the pilot (hence the image of the leather trenchcoat-wearing pilot wiping his goggles with his silk scarf)."

name: Oakenshield
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1⁄3 shot	Walnut (Nocino) liqueur
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Bittersweet, herbal and subtly nutty with delicate notes of smoky whisky. A tasty late-night sipper.
history: Adapted from a recipe by Pip Hanson at Marvel Bar at The Bachelor Farmer, in Minneapolis, USA.

name: Apple Business
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: Rich honey balances zesty lime in this flavoursome gin and apple sour.
history: Adapted from a 2017 recipe by Theo Lieberman, New York City, USA.

name: Devil's Margarita
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. Carefully FLOAT wine.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Claret red wine
review: Due to a lack of orange liqueur, this is not strictly a Margarita. However, the red wine float fits the name and sipping the underlying 'margarita' through this layer makes for a devilishly good drink.

name: Five Keys
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
review: A bourbon-laced, spirit-forward after-dinner digestive.

name: Bucket List
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
2⁄3 shot	Bigallet Genepi Grand Tetras
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: Floral, honeyed, herbal and vodka-laced.

name: Life is Beautiful
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ambrato/ambre/amber vermouth
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄4 shot	Elderflower liqueur
4 drop	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
review: This dry herbal aperitif cocktail is enriched with the floral tones of elderflower liqueur.
history:
Adapted from a 2019 recipe created by Andy Keir at Bruach, Dundee, Scotland. Andy's original recipe calls for Star of Bombay Gin.

"This drink was inspired by my La Classica experience, the places we visited, and drinks shared with friends. The name is taken from an Italian movie of the same name, which was filmed in Arezzo, of course the starting point for La Classica 2019. The name reflects the feeling we all shared that 1st morning.

This cocktail is essentially a reverse Martinez, chosen to showcase Martini Ambrato. I've paired it with Star of Bombay as the higher ABV and intensity of flavour ensure the presence of gin isn't lost. I discounted using an Old Tom gin here as there is enough sweetness from the other ingredients, and it also keeps the cocktail 'on brand'. The addition of elderflower helps to balance the cocktail and adds a floral finishing note."

name: Good Cork
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1 shot	The Busker Single Pot Still Irish Whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Dry and boozy, this delicious late-night sipper unusually mixes two different single pot-still spirits, one smoky Mexican agave and the other characterful Irish barley
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2013 by Phil Ward at his Mayahuel bar in New York City, USA.

name: Irish Old Fashioned
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Dry and yet smooth and refined as Old-Fashioneds go.

name: Sweetheart
garnish: Serve accompanied by a bunch of flowers
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Lanique Spirit of Rose liqueur
1 3⁄4 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review:
A floral riff on a classic Cosmopolitan. The quality of rose liqueur used makes or breaks this romantically themed cocktail.

Photographed in a glass from the Gibson Bar, London.

name: Florence Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bepi Tosolini Grappa di Moscato
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Floral and aromatic grappa shines in this citrusy fresh cocktail.

name: Grappa Sour
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) and lemon slice
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bepi Tosolini Grappa di Moscato
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Omit the lemon garnish and instead float a few dashes of bitters and this tasty, aromatic cocktail is a ringer for a Pisco Sour.

name: Grapefruit Drop
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Grapefruit flavoured vodka
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: The grapefruit lovers Cosmopolitan. Refreshing and enlivening zesty citrus.

name: Blackberry Fruitini
preparation: MUDDLE blackberries in base of shaker, add other ingredients and SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5 fresh	Blackberries
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
5⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Vodka-laced rich blackberry fruit with faint zest orange.
history: Created in May 2020 by yours truly in Rye, England.

name: Vermouth Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄24 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2 dash	Boker's bitters
review: Well-balanced bitter-sweetness dominated by vermouth (hence the name) with faint maraschino but perhaps the most important ingredient is the most hidden, the dashes of bitters. Hence, dash well and judiciously.
history: Fittingly, the "Vermuth Cocktail" is the first cocktail with vermouth to appear in a recipe book. Although this 1869 recipe in J. Haney's 1869 Steward and Barkeeper's Manual is not so much a cocktail, but simply vermouth served with ice and a lemon zest twist.

name: Drunk Uncle
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
review: Not the most endearing of names but this spirituous late-night sipper has broad family appeal beyond just uncles, so long as they have a taste for bittersweet peaty whisky. OK, perhaps just the discerning among the family circle.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Shawn Soole in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada.

name: St. Stephen's Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
history: Adapted from a 2014 recipe created by Jeffrey Morgenthaler at Clyde Common in Portland, Oregon, USA.

name: Espresso Rumtini
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) & float 3 coffee beans on surface of drink
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Naturally, this also works well with well-aged rums, but I prefer the cleaner bite of a rum with a mere three years or so age in this delicious cocktail.
history: A riff on Dick Bradsell's classic Espresso Martini.

name: Green Isaac's Special
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3 shot	Coconut water
1⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Ernest Hemingway was a hardened drinker who also suffered from haemochromatosis (a rare hereditary disease that can lead to diabetes) so avoided sugar. With this in mind, I've subtly softened and mellowed his creation. It's still on the dry side and plenty strong enough, but hopefully better balanced.
history: Named after the small Bahamian island of Great Isaac Cay, the Green Isaac's Special appears in Ernest Hemingway's autobiographical novel Islands in the Stream where the great author wrote, "Thomas Hudson tasted, took a swallow and felt the cold that had the sharpness of the lime, the aromatic varnishy taste of the Angostura and the gin stiffening the lightness of the ice-cold coconut water."

name: Gin Quarantini
garnish: Lemon juice & powdered vitamin C rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Described by its creator as "the most delicious way to boost your immunity. The alcohol kills the germs. The local honey and lemon boost your immunity."
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Jessica Segarra A.K.A. The Novice Chef.

name: Vodka Quarantini
garnish: Lemon juice & powdered vitamin C rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Described by its creator as "the most delicious way to boost your immunity. The alcohol kills the germs. The local honey and lemon boost your immunity."
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Jessica Segarra A.K.A. The Novice Chef.

name: L'Ultima Parola (by David Wondrich)
garnish: Lime zest twist (discarded) and Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Strega liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Strega replaces Chartreuse in this learned American in Italy take on a classic Last Word.
history:
Adapted from a riff on a Last Word created in April 2018 by David Wondrich at The Jerry Thomas Project bar in Rome, Italy.
Last Word history

name: Elderflower Champagne Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: An Elderflower Collins with champagne in place of soda water.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in February 2021 by Dr John Davies in Newbury, England.

name: Rosalia Margarita
garnish: Lemon juice & Himalayan pink salt rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled salt-rimmed glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Rose sugar syrup
review: Delicately bittersweet with balancing citrus sourness and rich floral rose which combine brilliantly with the agave notes of the blanco tequila.
history: Created by Chiara Mascellaro for Margarita Day 2021. Votes by Discerning Drinkers on Difford's Guide led to this cocktail being declared the 2021 Margarita of the Year. (Chiara's original recipe used Martini Riserva Speciale Bitter as the red bitter liqueur.)

name: Ronan Collins
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Not just a Collins made with Irish whiskey but a Ronan Collins. There's some Irish logic as to why this cocktail is garnished with a pineapple wedge, but that's what sets it apart.
history:
Classically known as a Mike Collins, but in more recent years, this Irish whiskey-based Collins has been eponymously named for Ronan Collins, the Senior Brand Ambassador for Irish Whiskey at Pernod Ricard UK.

See the history of the Collins cocktail on our Tom Collins page.

name: Santa Maria (by Dani Umoette)
preparation: Makes 2 drinks STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into two chilled shot glasses, ideally Vaso Veladora glasses.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
2⁄3 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1⁄6 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1⁄12 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
review: Best described as a mezcal-based Godfather with amaro and crème de banana adding depth of flavour.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in May 2021 by Daniele Umoette as a parting gift to us. What inspired him, "The other day I was listening to Blondie's "Maria" and it is indeed one of my favourite songs and that did the trick. The song talks about this multifaceted woman called Maria, so I tried to reinterpret her qualities through my personal imagination."

name: Devil Smoked Margarita
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. Carefully FLOAT wine.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Claret red wine
review: A Margarita 'smoked' by mezcal and 'blooded' with red wine. Devilishly good!
history: Created by Stacey Harvard who, in December 2020, commented on our Devil's Margarita page saying "I used Del Maguey Mezcal instead, the smokiness seemed more appropriate. Was lovely."

name: Chip Err O
preparation: STIR first 3 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with splash soda.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	O/Purist Tsipouro
2⁄3 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Vinious and loosely Martini in style.
history: Created in December 2020 by yours truly to highlight and promote Greek Tsipouro, pronounced "Chip Err O" or thereabouts.

name: Piña Verde
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with scoop crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
3⁄4 shot	Cream of coconut (e.g. Coco Lopez, Re'al etc.)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Green Chartreuse blended with coconut and pineapple – yummm.
history: 'Green Pineapple' in Spanish, the Piña Verde was created by Erick Gastro at his Polite Provisions bar in San Diego, USA.

name: Barribault
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Island single malt Scotch whisky
3⁄4 shot	Averna Amaro
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Whisps of characterful whisky lace this spirit-forward bittersweet late-night sipper.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England. Jason's recipe calls for Talisker single malt whisky.

name: Storm King
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Walnut (Nocino) liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Damon Boelte at his Grand Army bar and restaurant in Brooklyn, New York City, USA.

name: Banker's Lunch
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
review: I also tried this fruity vodka-based aperitivo with orange curaçao but it works better with triple sec.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2016 by Eric Alperin at The Varnish in Los Angeles, USA.

name: Burnt Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄12 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
5⁄12 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A stirred Dry Martini influenced by a smoky splash of Islay single malt scotch whisky, flamed with a flamed orange zest twist.

name: Baltimore Bang
garnish: Orange slice wheel and Luxardo maraschino cherry sail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: An apricot flavoured Whiskey Sour.

name: Pomme
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 2⁄3 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: This cocktail's fruitiness and slug of vanilla syrup gives it broad appeal, particularly for those who like Porn Star Martinis.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Merlin Griffiths, publican and First Dates TV star bartender.

name: Randy's Old Fashioned
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Canadian blended whisky
1⁄3 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Maple syrup
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Does the choice of whisky coupled with maple syrup suggest Randy, the drinker this cocktail was created for, was/is Canadian? Grapefruit freshens while maple syrup adds deep flavoursome richness.
history: Adapted from a cocktail on the menu of the Dragonfly Cocktail Bar in Edinburgh, Scotland circa 2015-18. Brought to my attention thanks to a comment by a fellow Discerning Drinker, Charl Engela on our Maple Old Fashioned page.

name: Quintessential Royal
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Savoia Americano Rosso
5⁄6 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄3 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
2 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: The cacao powder rim echoes the subtle chocolate flavours in this tasty bittersweet aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Andrea Kollcaku at Annabell's in Mayfair, London, England.

name: Bridal
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Richly aromatic and somewhat reminiscent of a Martinez.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Albert Stevens Crockett's 1931 Old Waldorf Bar Days. This rejuvenated classic was brought to my attention by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England. Jason's recipe is as above but with 60ml (2oz) Plymouth Gin.

name: Añejo Almond Old Fashioned
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Añejo tequila
1⁄4 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1⁄6 shot	Agave syrup
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Añejo has notes of almond, here amplified by a splash of amaretto liqueur.
history: Adapted from Mark Prat's 2005 Almond Old Fashioned. Back then, Mark almost certainly didn't have access to añejo tequila, but if had he'd surely have used it rather than reposado.

name: Maximilian Affair
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Mezcal leads, underpinned by floral elderflower, rich herbal vermouth and sour lemon.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2008 by Misty Kalkofen at Green Street Gill in Boston, USA.

name: Yellow Cab
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Sage gin
1⁄3 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Agave syrup
review: Sage-led gin with assertive and refreshing zesty citrus balanced with honeyed caramel agave syrup.
history:
The Checker A11 Marathon Taxi manufactured 1959–82 by Checker Motors is the archetypal American yellow cab, as iconic as a London black taxi.

The Yellow Cab cocktail, promoted by Engine Gin, pays homage to Marathon Taxi driven by Robert De Niro in the movie directed by Martin Scorsese, Taxi Driver. Engine Gin describe this cocktails as "a mash-up between a classic Margarita and Julio Bermejo's modern classic Tommy's Margarita."

name: Olympic Class
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Rhum Clément Créole Shrubb liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Créole shrubb replaces orange curaçao in this riff on the classic, equal parts, Olympic cocktail which was named after the RMS Olympic, an Olympic-class ocean liner and sister ship to the ill-fated Titanic and Britannic.
history: The produce of the French mainland meet that of a French Caribbean island in this delicious brandy and rum-laced orange cocktail.

name: Safe Word
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
review: The Last Word meets the 20th Century.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2022 by Matt Lofink at Cure in New Orleans, USA. Matt's original recipe call for Sweet Gwendoline French Gin.

name: Left Hand
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
4 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: The Negroni meets a Manhattan in this straight-up riff on a Boulevardier.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2006 by Sam Ross at Milk & Honey in New York City, USA. Originally made with mole (spiced chocolate) bitters, (indeed this cocktail was first made soon after the release of Bittermens Xocolatl Mole Bitters ), but I prefer with regular chocolate bitters.

name: Mistaken for Strangers
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass (no ice in glass).
ingredients:
1 shot	Bepi Tosolini Grappa di Moscato
1 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Grappa nestles supportively alongside Chartreuse in this Last Word-like cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created late in 2012 by Misty Kalkofen at Brick & Mortar bar in Cambridge, Massachusetts, USA. Originally for the holiday menu and named 'The Grinch' but, in January/February 2013, Misty renamed her creation to be less seasonal with the name 'Mistaken for Strangers' referencing the unexpected combination of grappa and Green Chartreuse.

name: Stiletta
preparation:
MUDDLE (smash) a star anise in base of stirring glass. Add other ingredients, STIR with ice and extra fine strain into chilled glass.

OR Omit the muddled star anise and instead pre-prepare Star anise-infused Italian red bitter liqueur by infusing 18-20 star anise pods into a 70-75cl bottle. Seal and shake periodically over 8 hours, then strain through a dampened coffee filter or cheesecloth.
ingredients:
1 dried	Star anise
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
review: Negroni-like with tequila rather than gin and a touch of star anise spice.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Phil Ward at Mayahuel in New York City, USA.

name: Calvados Appletini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A tangy apple sour alternatini served straight-up in that all important "tini" 'V'-shaped glass.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Tim Etherington-Judge of Avallen calvados.

name: La Frangipane
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Almond is an essential element of any frangipane, here with zesty lemon and apple brandy.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Anya Lily Montague for Avallen calvados.

name: Pippin No. 1
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review: A delicious bittersweet aperitivo. Don't be tempted to stir, "shake it to wake it," and add dilution and an attractively foamy head.
history: Adapted from a recipe by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England. Named after one of the beloved Royal Pembroke Welsh Corgi dogs: Queen Elizabeth II owned more than 30 corgis from her accession in 1952 until her death in 2022.

name: Stardust
garnish: Lemon zest twist – either discarded and float edible viola flowers or use lemon zest twit for garnish
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with 60z scoop of crushed ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Parfait Amour liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A riff on a Royal Daiquiri with lemon juice in place of lime.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by the legendary Robert "Brother Cleve" Toomey for B-Side Lounge Bar in Cambridge, MA, USA.

name: Donegal Donkey
preparation: POUR first 3 ingredients into copper mug/glass and stir. Two-thirds fill vessel with cubed ice. TOP with ginger beer and crown with crushed ice.
ingredients:
2 shot	Poteen/Poitín
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: Poteen adds an appealing almost oily, new leather-like flavour to a Moscow Mule .
history: Created in 2023 by Stephen Curtin and shared via a comment on our Moscow Mule page: "Might I suggest an Irish Poteen variation... The Donegal Donkey. Donegal not just for the alliteration, but because Donegal was once famous for the quality of its Poteen."

name: Frozen Jägerita
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with two-thirds a 6oz scoop crushed ice and pour into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Jägermeisteror other German amaro
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: There is so much about this digestivo cocktail that's wrong that it's brilliant.
history: Created in 2014 by David Cordoba for the menu at 28 HongKong Street in Singapore, this is a frozen version of his 2008 Jägerita.

name: Lioness
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Crème de Pêche de Vigne liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 1964 by J. "Popo" Galsini, a bartender at the Palms In The Jungle restaurant in Anaheim, California, USA. This recipe courtesy of Jeff "Beachbum" Berry's Total Tiki.

name: Commodore No. 3
garnish: One-third lemon slice wheel 'fan' on rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A short, sharp, pleasing rye whiskey sour.
history:
We have the Commodore No. 1 and No. 2 from Albert S. Crockett's 1931 Old Waldorf Bar Daysbut as David A. Embury says in his 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks, "Another version of the Commodore calls for whisky instead of rum, omits the egg white, and uses orange bitters in place of the grenadine. Obviously, the two Commodores command two different fleets."

Embury is perhaps referring to this "Commodore Cocktail" which appears in Harry McElhone's 1922 Harry's ABC of Mixing Cocktails and Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Fresh No. 1
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Monkey Shoulder Fresh Monkey
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: If you like a Florida-style Daiquiri then this Fresh could be for you.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Léa Longayrou of Little Red Door in Paris, France.

name: The O. G.
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
4 drop	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
review: Spiritous gin supported by herbaceous and bitter botanical notes with a touch of citrus freshness and rich vanilla.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England. Jason describes this cocktail as being "an Old Gin cocktail, updated with amaro and grapefruit bitters." Originally made with Cocchi Storico Vermouth di Torino.

name: Three of a Kind
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Americano bianco
1 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
8 drop	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
review: Maraschino shines in this bittersweet aperitivo/digestivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Weisi Basore, beverage director at Bar Cleeta in Bentonville, Arkansas, USA.

name: Rose Noble
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Speyburn 10yo Speyside single malt
3⁄4 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Bittersweet and sweet 'n' sour, A whisky-based riff on the Division Bell.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Jason E. Clapham of St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England. Jason says it's "a very popular Burns Night serve in the MCR!"

name: A Quiet Word
garnish: Lime zest twist (expressed & discarded) and skewered Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
2⁄3 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
2⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A Last Word with Light rum in place of gin, hence initially named Light Word, but A Quiet Word had more of a ring to it.
history: Last Word cocktail history

name: Rum Cow
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Jamaican aged blended rum with funk
2 shot	Milk (whole milk/full 3-4% fat)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A wholesome and very tasty milky dessert Tiki cocktail. Be generous with your dusting of nutmeg.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 1937 by Don The Beachcomber at his Los Angeles bar where it featured in the postprandial section of the menu.

name: Pumpkin Sazerac
preparation: POUR absinthe into chilled glass and rotate glass to coat the inside with absinthe. Shake out excess and place glass to one side. STIR other ingredients with ice and strain into absinthe-rinsed glass.
ingredients:
1⁄12 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	Pumpkin spice syrup
3 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Don't feel bad if you add a cube or two of ice to this spirituous cocktail –it's perhaps all the better for it.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by US bartending veteran Naren Young.

name: Golden Glove
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Jamaican aged blended rum with funk
1⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Funky rum and zesty citrus tamed and refreshed by being served over ice chippings.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Constante Ribalaïgua Vert and published in the 1934 Bar La Florida Cocktails, the menu of his famous bar, now El Floridita in Havana, Cuba.

name: Sunshine No. 3
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
3⁄4 shot	Strega liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Mezcal is the characterful backbone to this aperitivo with rich herbal notes balanced by delicate bitterness and citrus freshness.
history: Created by the good folk at Strega and discovered at BCB Berlin 2023.

name: Italian G&T
preparation: POUR all ingredients into chilled glass and then fill with ice.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: The Gin & Tonic meets the Negroni.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Alex Smith at Whitechapel in San Francisco, USA.

name: Black Widow's Bite
garnish: Orange juice and black salt rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine stain into chilled and rimmed glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Blue Curaçao
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Essentially a Screwdriver blued (not quite blackened) by blue curaçao and served straight-up.
history: Named after the character played by Scarlett Johansson in eight Marvel movies, including two which also starred Jeremy Renner. In 2023, Renner featured a Black Widow's Bite cocktail in a promotional video for delivery firm Drizly. His version of this cocktail was made with orange rather than blue curaçao and based on Sweet Grass Vodka, a brand he co-owns.

name: Winterised Negroni
garnish: Quarter orange slice wheel on rim
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄12 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
history: Adapted from a recipe created by New York City bartender Brian Evans, originally made with Cocchi Storico Vermouth di Torino.

name: Brazil Basil Smash
preparation: MUDDLE basil in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
12 fresh	Basil leaves
2 shot	Cachaça
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Basil flavours combine brilliantly with cachaça's funky notes in this frappé served riff on Joerg's contemporary classic Gin Basil Smash.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2011 by Joerg Meyer at his Le Lion Bar de Paris in Hamburg, Germany. A tribute to Brazil's famous Caipirinha cocktail, Joerg created this for a bar show in Rotterdam and says, "I did a fun talk, playing John Garuku was my Head Bartender on Stage. :)"

name: Almond Margarita
preparation: DRY SHAKE all ingredients (without ice) to emulsify. SHAKE again with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Adriatico Bianco almond milk liqueur
1 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
review: Just as it says on the tin, recognisably a Margarita in style, loaded with almond nutty milky goodness, which also gives it an attractive frothy head (hence the use of a dry shake).
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2022 by our friends at Bellaventura Brands, the folk behind Adriatico Amaretto Bianco.

name: Wiffin
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: A little dilution from a good stir helps tame this spirit-forward aperitivo or late-night sipper, which mellows and becomes more pleasurable as you sip.
history: The Wiffin was kindly brought to our attention by Jason E. Clapham and is David Wondrich's interpretation of the un-named cocktail P. G. Wodehouse had in mind when he wrote a short story called The Passing of Ambrose. Wiffin is the surname of Ambrose, the protagonist).

name: Smokey Almond
garnish: Place a roasted almond on the ice
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice.)
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Adriatico Bianco almond milk liqueur
1 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Agave syrup
review: Almond freshened by lime and fortified by mezcal.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2022 by our friends at Bellaventura Brands, the folk behind Adriatico Amaretto Bianco.

name: Tripole
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water) (optional)
review: A three-ingredient [saline doesn't count!] riff on a classic Metropole, so obviously a Tripole! Basically, a brandy Manhattan is best appreciated during a late-night Manhattan moment.
history: Created in December 2023 by yours truly at The Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Doctor No. 2
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄4 shot	Swedish Punsch liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Funky notes from Swedish punch vie with piney gin, freshened by zesty lemon.
history: David A. Embury's 1948 Fine Art of Mixing Drinks lists a cocktail called a Doctor No.2 (consisting of equal parts lemon juice, Swedish Punch and gin) and states, "This is also known as a Gretta Garbo." Not anymore, it's not! A Gretta Garbo is a very different, rum-based cocktail.

name: Haymaker
garnish: Dust with a dollop of freshly whipped double/heavy cream, a pinch of sea salt and a light dusting of instant coffee powder
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
5⁄6 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
5⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
5⁄6 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
review: If the Espresso Martini could be taken in a Tiki direction then this cream-topped, almond-influenced riff is it.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Vince Stipo at Enswell café bar & diner in Philadelphia, USA.

name: Margarita Royal
garnish: Dehydrated lime powder on outside of glass
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. TOP with sparkling wine.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Agave syrup
1 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: A Tommy's Margarita topped with a splash of fizz.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Dre Masso in 2005, the year he was part of the team behind the opening of Green & Red Mexican Cantina in Shoreditch and while creating cocktails for his book, Margarita Rocks.

name: Sakura Vesper
garnish: Lemon zest twist expressed and discarded. Adorn with skewered Luxardo Maraschino Cherry and cherry blossom if in season.
preparation: THROW all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Mancino Vermouth di Torino Sakura
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A delicious, delicately floral Vesper.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Ramón Clark, bar manager at Deep Dive in Seattle, USA. Originally made with Haku Vodka, Roku Gin and Mancino Sakura vermouth.

name: Money in the Bank
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄2 shot	Meletti amaro
1⁄2 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
review: A characterful bittersweet aperitivo or digestive. A wisp of mezcal sits brilliantly with the London dry gin base.
history: Created late-2023/early 2024 by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edwards MCR, Oxford, England.

name: Old Money No. 2
garnish: Orange zest twist and mist with allspice dram sprayed from an atomiser
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1⁄3 shot	Walnut (Nocino) liqueur
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Best described as a nutty, delicately bittersweet Old Fashioned. A tasty digestivo or late-night sipper.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2009 by Benjamin Schiller for BOKA Restaurant Group in Chicago, USA.

name: Americano
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Bittersweet, lightly effervescent, long and refreshing.
history:
Meaning "American-style" in Italian, the name references this cocktail's origins. Italian vermouth producers, picking up on the trend for cocktails in the USA to be based on vermouth and bitters, started marketing vermouths with bitters added under the name "vermouth Americano." Italian bars then started making their own versions by adding various bittersweet style liqueurs, including Fernet Branca, to vermouth. Some also added soda to turn this cocktail into a long drink. Then the popularity of the Milano Torino led to red bitter liqueur (e.g. Campari) being used in preference to amari in an Americano.

Mazzon Ferruccio's 1920 book Il Barista Guida del Barman, a "collection of American and International Recipes", includes two "Americano" recipes, a single serve and a "Americano (grandi quantità)" (large quantities). Both illustrate the Americano's origins as vermouth adjusted by adding bitters or bitter liqueurs and other flavourings such as "5 drops of cognac".

name: Black Diamond
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
review: This flavoursome mix of coffee and chocolate is further enhanced if vanilla-infused rum is used.
history: Created in March 2004 by yours truly in London, England.

name: Bobby Burns (Craddock's recipe)
garnish: Lemon zest twist expressed and discarded. Adorn with skewered Luxardo Maraschino cherry.
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
review: Rich and slightly sweet, laced with spice liqueur - an excellent dram to enjoy alongside the ritualistic serving of haggis.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book which calls for equal parts rosso vermouth and scotch whisky with three dashes of Bénédictine. Craddock adds that this is "One of the very best Whisky Cocktails and "A very fast mover on Saint Andrew's Day."

name: Canary Flip
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Warninks Advocaat liqueur
1 2⁄3 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A delightful balance of egg, spirit and wine. Looks creamy and sweet but is sharp and citrusy.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2002 by Alex Kammerling, London, England.

name: Death in the Afternoon
garnish: Rose petal or lemon zest twist
preparation: POUR first 2 ingredients into chilled glass and STIR. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
1⁄3 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
4 1⁄2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Bravado (absinthe) dominates this drink, alongside hints of biscuity champagne. I've added a touch of sugar to tame this hardman's cocktail.
history:
Created by Ernest Hemingway (not just named after his book), this recipe was the author's contribution to a 1935 cocktail book titled So Red the Nose, or Breath in the Afternoon. I've toned down the maestro's original recipe a little as it included a whopping ounce-and-a-half of absinthe. The book stipulates: "Pour 1 jigger of absinthe into a champagne glass, add iced champagne until it attains the proper opalescent milkiness. Drink 3 to 5 of these slowly."

This is followed by a note about the drink's origin by Hemingway, "This was arrived at by the author and three officers of H.M.S. Danae after having spent seven hours overboard trying to get Capt. Bra Saunders' fishing boat off a bank where she had gone with us in a N.W. gale." The book continues with a paragraph by its compilers, "It takes a man with hair on his chest to drink five Absinths and Champagne Cocktails and still handle the English language in the Hemingway fashion. But Ernest has proved his valour, not alone in his cups. Captain of the swimming team at Oak Park high school - first American to be wounded on the Italian front during the World War (with 227 individual wounds to his credit) - tossed by a bull in the streets of Pamplona while rescuing his friend Donald Ogden Stewart - deep sea fisherman - big game hunter - and one of the first citizens of Key West - Hemingway is the man who can hold his Absinthe like a postwar novelist."

name: Delmonico
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A Sweet Manhattan with cognac substituted for the whiskey.
history:
Named after and likely created at New York's Delmonico's Steakhouse Restaurant, the history of which dates back to 1837 when the Delmonico brothers opened "the first fine dining restaurant in the country." There is still a Delmonico's in New York City but the restaurant owned by the Delmonico family at 44th Street and Fifth Avenue closed in 1923.

The Delmonico Cocktail appears in Albert Stevens Crockett's 1935 Old Waldorf-Astoria Bar Book.

name: Dickens' Dry Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄12 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄12 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A 5:1 Dry Martini served without any garnish (i.e. no olive or twist). The name is a reference to Charles Dicken's novel Oliver Twist.
history: Evolution of the Dry Martini

name: Downhill Racer
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
review: Aged rum sweetened, softened and flavoured with pineapple and amaretto. A crowd pleaser.

name: Duke's Dry Martini - The 'Naked' or 'Direct' Martini
garnish: Chilled olive on stick or lemon zest twist
preparation:
1. Place glass and bottle of gin in freezer for at least two hours before making drink.
2. An hour before making drink POUR water into frozen glass, swirl around to coat and place back in freezer. Preferably do this with a little of the water at a time. Continue to swirl around during freezing process to coat the sides of the glass.
3. When ready to serve drink, POUR chilled vermouth into icy glass and swirl to coat with vermouth.
4. POUR frozen gin into glass, garnish and serve immediately.
ingredients:
1⁄6 shot	Chilled water
1⁄12 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
review: The quantities of gin and vermouth stated in this recipe produce a Dry Martini with a 30:1 ratio of gin to vermouth. A small amount of dilution is achieved as the ice coating the frozen glass melts. Both glass and gin must be freezing cold so that the temperature masks the strength of the alcohol. Thus the drink does not taste nearly as strong as it is – you have been warned.
history: Giuseppe Cipriani documents his use of a freezer to make Dry Martinis in his 1978 book L'angolo dell'Harry's Bar, seven years before what is now known as the Duke's Martini was introduced to the bar at London's Dukes Hotel by Salvatore Calabrese who served it first to American journalist, Stanton Delaplane.

name: Estilo Viejo
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄3 shot	Agave syrup
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Basically, a Tequila Old-fashioned, it's even better when made with añejo tequila.
history: The name of this drink literally translates from Spanish as 'Old Style'.

name: Flip Cocktail (generic recipe)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with the ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and pour into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Brandy, whisk(e)y, gin, rum etc.
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 fresh	Egg (white & yolk)
review: Made with a full-bodied and flavoursome base spirit or fortified wine, this is a tasty cocktail. Those perhaps put off by a whole raw egg per drink should give flips a chance. (Health concerns relating to raw eggs taken into account of course.)
history:
Flips basically consist of any fortified wine or liquor shaken with a whole egg and sweetened with sugar. They are typically garnished with a dusting of nutmeg and served in a sour glass or small coupe. They can be served hot or cold.

Flips, emerged in the early 1600s and Charles Dickens includes this popular drink of the day in his 1861 novel Great Expectations. Early flips consisted of a tankard of ale to which a mixture made from sugar, eggs and spices was added before being heated with a red-hot iron poker from the fire. Later they came to mean any fortified wine or liquor shaken with a whole egg and sweetened with sugar.

name: French Martini
garnish: Pineapple wedge on rim or float raspberry in centre of cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
review: Raspberry and pineapple laced with vodka. Easy drinking and very fruity.
history:
The French Martini is based on one of the most straightforward recipes: base, modifier, and juice. Liqueurs burst onto the scene as cocktail modifiers during Prohibition when homemade spirits needed to be masked. Having been so well embraced, they never declined after liquor became more refined and once again legal.

Vodka, particularly during the late 1980s-90s when this cocktail was created, had, and perhaps still does have, the broadest consumer appeal, while pineapple is crucial to both the drink's flavour and texture: frothy without being heavy.

Despite what you may have heard, the French Martini wasn't invented by Chambord as part of a marketing campaign, although it would be hard to deny that the French Martini has done a lot to promote the brand of black raspberry liqueur.

Named for its use of French blackberry and raspberry liqueur and the fact that it was served in a V-shaped glass, this Neo-Martini doesn't contain vermouth and is a long way from being a true Martini. However, during the late 1980s, when this fruity cocktail emerged in New York City, pretty much any drink served in a V-shaped glass was named Martini, and the name has stuck. Just as it has for the Espresso Martini. [See Martini cocktail and its evolution]

In 1996, Dale DeGroff put the French Martini on the menu of Keith McNally's vodka-themed New York bar, Pravda. However, it was later that year, when the cocktail appeared at McNally's renowned Balthazar restaurant in New York's Soho, that it started to fly.

By 1997-8, the French Martini made it onto the menu at London's Met Bar, then the favoured hangout of the glitterati and a bar which championed this style of fruity vodka-based cocktails, dubbed "fresh fruit Martinis".

But it was Dick Bradsell, then Europe's most influential bartender, who made me my first French Martini at London's Quo Vadis in November 1997. In the editor's letter of the following month's CLASS magazine, I gushed, "My favourite Martini of the moment has to be the French Martini, a drink that looks set to be the hit cocktail of 1998. The French Martini resembles a Sex on the Beach, but without the sex - i.e. no peach schnapps or melon liqueur".

CLASS was a newly established magazine and needed funding. I knew both the UK distributors of Chambord and Absolut Vodka were looking for a cocktail to promote their products so I had a full-page advertisement designed and approached both of them to support jointly. The ad ran for the first time in that December issue and every issue for months after. So, in a way, the French Martini helped establish my magazine, and I helped establish the French Martini in the UK.

name: Bonaparte
preparation: POUR chilled soda water into an ice-filled glass. Add freshly brewed hot espresso coffee so it layers on the sparkling water. Lastly, pour the mandarin liqueur (the tasty part of the Bonaparte), which will sink through the coffee layer, pulling the drink together while leaving the coffee's crema on the surface.
ingredients:
3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
1 1⁄2 shot	Mandarine Napoleon liqueur
review: Zesty mandarin orange and espresso coffee served as a tall, refreshing cocktail. A tall drink named after a short man!
history: Created 20th February 2014 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Gimlet (Schumann's recipe)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄4 shot	Lime cordial (sweetened lime juice)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Schumann uses fresh citrus sourness to balance rich lime cordial but opts for lighter lemon juice rather than lime as is classic with a Gimlet.
history: A riff on the classic Gimlet created in 1983 by the famous bartender and cocktail author Charles Schumann of Munich, Germany. This "Schumann's Gimlet" is one of several Gimlet recipes in his 1995 book American Bar book.

name: Gin & It
garnish:
Lemon zest twist
(Or if serving on-the-rocks garnish with an orange slice wheel.)
preparation:
STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
(Or if serving on-the-rocks, strain into ice-filled old-fashioned glass, preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review:
Remembering both vermouth and gin are flavoured with similar botanicals, they obviously have an affinity for each other. This drink may be simple but made with a full-bodied Vermouth di Torino it's a fabulously tasty combination of botanicals, wine and spirit.

My own preference for proportions comes from Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide (see below).
history:
Adapted from a recipe in Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide.

"It" is short for Italian, a reference to the 'sweet' (rosso) vermouth, which was traditionally Italian, while French vermouth was dry.

In his 2002 Craft of the Cocktail, Dale DeGroff states that the Gin and It was originally known as a Sweet Martini and as such was a popular drink during the 1880s and 1890s at the Hoffman House and other Manhattan bars. Later it became known as 'Gin & Italian', until during Prohibition it was shortened to 'Gin & It'. The first print reference to this cocktail by the "Gin & It" name appears in Frank Meier's 1936 The Artistry of Mixing Drinks.

During American Prohibition, the Gin & It made its way to London, where due to the British love of gin, the Gin & It became a popular drink and pub staple.

The popularity of the Gin & It waned along with both that of vermouth and gin in the late 1980s but is now enjoying a renaissance with a new generation of gin and vermouth drinkers.

name: Grand Sidecar
garnish: Half sugar rim (if you must) & orange zest twist
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review:
A riff on the classic Sidecar that's even simpler to make but equally tasty.

Grand Marnier Cordon Rouge consists of 51% cognac so there is no need to add cognac to make a great Sidecar, simply add lemon juice. This drink benefits from a touch of dilution so also works well served on-the-rocks in an old-fashioned glass.
history:
Created June 2005 by yours truly, London, England.
Sidecar history

name: Ice 'T' Knee
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Jasmine tea (cold)
3⁄4 shot	Canadian icewine
review: Honeyed palate topped off with tannin and jasmine.
history: Created in 2004 by yours truly (Simon Difford), London, England

name: Manhattan (Dry)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A bone dry Manhattan for those with dry palates. If you like Dry Martinis then be sure to try one of these.
history: Manhattan cocktail history

name: Very French Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
review: Cognac, pineapple juice and black raspberry liqueur. OK, so France is not known for its pineapples but I said 'very' not 'totally' French. And yes I know it's not really a Martini.
history: A riff on the French Martini created in January 2015 by yours truly and Matthias Lataille at the Cabinet Room, London, England. I subsequently found I'd created an almost identical drink, the French Cocktail back in 2011. However, I prefer the Very French Martini name - even though it's far from being a Martini.

name: Milano
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: A vodka-based Negroni.

name: Pink Gin & Tonic
preparation: POUR gin and bitters into ice-filled glass, TOP with tonic and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
4 shot	Aromatic tonic water
review: Basically a G&T with an extra pop of flavour, this has a broader appeal than the original Pink Gin.
history:
When I sampled my first Pink Gin, made with generous dashes of bitters I found this classic tough to appreciate, so in 2002, I added another medicinal ingredient - tonic water, also containing quinine from cinchona bark. Or, looking at this another way, I simply added dashes of bitters to a G&T.

I'm sure I wasn't the first to add Angostura Bitters to a G&T but I've not found an earlier reference to a "Pink Gin & Tonic". Others soon cottoned on and the gin graze, soda boom, and ready-to-drink market have combined to produce a plethora of pre-mixed Pink G&Ts as well as tonic waters specifically designed for such a serve. Hence, in 2021, I swapped out classic 'Indian' tonic water in this recipe for an aromatic tonic while also reducing the bitters dose accordingly.

name: Caneflower cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cachaça
3⁄4 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
review: Rust coloured and bittersweet with cachaça and elderflower.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2009 by Jeffrey Morgenthaler in Portland, Oregon, USA. Jeff's original recipe calls for a "generous twist of lemon" rather than orange. On JeffreyMorgenthaler.com, he says this cocktail was "Inspired in part by a gorgeous cocktail created by my good friend Gonçalo de Souza Monteiro, the Comte de Sureau."

name: Scotch Negroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review: On the bitter side of bittersweet and, depending on your Scotch, faintly smoky.
history: See: Negroni history and variations

name: Sicilian Negroni
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 shot	Blood orange juice
review: Blood orange juice replaces sweet vermouth in this fruity Negroni.
history:
Discovered in 2006 at The Last Supper Club, San Francisco, USA.
Negroni cocktail history

name: Silver Bullet
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Mentzendorff Kümmel liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: If you like Aviations then this caraway influenced sour may appeal. It's powerfully flavoured so also consider serving in an old-fashioned over ice to allow dilution to tame the flavours.
history: Thought to have been created in the 1920s.

name: Slow Screw
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3 1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Reminiscent of a fruity screwdriver with a botanical gin character. When made with a good slow gin and freshly squeezed orange juice this is a great brunch cocktail.
history: More information on the Slow Screw family of cocktails is included on our Slow Screw cocktails page.

name: Tequila Smash
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
7 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄4 shot	Agave syrup
review: Simple, not too sweet - a great way to appreciate quality tequila.
history: Adapted from the classic Brandy Smash.

name: Twinkle
preparation: SHAKE first two ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with dry sparkling wine.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: It's hard to believe this floral, dry, light golden tipple is so loaded with alcohol. Go easy twinkle toes!
history: Adapted from a recipe Created in 2002 by Tony Conigliaro at The Lonsdale in London, England. Originally made using prosecco and elderflower cordial but now mostly made with elderflower liqueur and often champagne.

name: Dry Martini (2:1 ratio) Wet
garnish: Chilled olive on stick or lemon zest twist
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura (optional)
review: Reputed to be a favourite of HRH Prince Charles.
history:
A generous measure of vermouth to two of gin, hence the name 'Wet' Martini.
Dry Martini history

name: Tahitian Honey Bee
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: Basically a lemon honey Daiquiri or a lemon Canchànchara - very tasty it is too.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Victor Bergeron's 1972 Trader Vic's Bartender's Guide (Revised Edition).

name: TNT (Tequila 'N' Tonic)
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and STIR.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
Top up with	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: A simple but very tasty way to enjoy tequila.
history: Adapted from Victor Bergeron's Trader Vic's Bartender's Guide (1972 revised edition).

name: Chrysanthemum
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth (chilled)
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
4 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Herbal and aromatic, this benefits from the dilution that comes with a good long stir.
history: The Chrysanthemum appears in Hugo R. Ensslin's 1917 Recipes for Mixed Drinks (and may well have been in his 1916 First Edition).

name: Flipping Good
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1 fresh	Egg yolk
review: Simply an aged rum flip with falernum replacing sugar syrup and egg white omitted.
history: Created in December 2008 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room in London, England.

name: Kangaroo
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura (optional)
review: Temperature is key to the enjoyment of this modern classic. Consume while icy cold.
history: Bartending legend has it that "Kangaroo" was the original name for a Vodka Martini. It wasn't: the first known printed reference to a Vodka Martini predates that of what was originally called the "Kangaroo Kicker" in Oscar Haimo's 1943 Cocktail Digest by ten years.

name: Monte Carlo
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ive and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: When served straight-up the Monte Carlo fits into the Scaffa family of cocktails but it's much better and more usually served on-the-rocks, so best described as being a Manhattan with Bénédictine in place of vermouth. My hero, the tax lawyer and cocktail writer, David Embury, says in his 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks, "This drink is a bit on the sweet side. It can be improved by adding 2 parts lemon juice and increasing the rye from 2 parts to about 4 or 5." Embury had a dry palate approaching that of Hemingway's and most palates will appreciate the extra touch of sweetness in this cocktail that's best enjoyed as an after-dinner tipple or nightcap.
history: The Monte Carlo first appears in print in David Embury's 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks as "1 part Bénédictine, 2 parts Rye, 1 or 2 dashes Angostura to each drink. Shake with cracked ice".

name: Tenner Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2 dash	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
review: Very wet, aromatic Martini.
history: There is considerable debate around the origin of the Martini and the best way to make this drink. Detailed information can be found on our Dry Martini page.

name: Waldorf Cocktail No.2
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Swedish Punsch liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Lime works better than lemon but like the Astor, using a combination of lime and lemon produces an even better drink.
history: This is the later of the two versions of this vintage cocktail from New York's Waldorf-Astoria Hotel [Waldorf No.1]. It appears in the 1939 Café Royale book and in the 1955 United Kingdom Bartender's Book. Both books offer a choice between using lemon or lime juice and the original recipe calls for two parts Swedish punch to one part gin but with most modern-day Swedish punches this makes for an overly sweet drink.

name: Obituary
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin (from freezer)
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄12 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: What a way to go. A Dry Martini with a dash of the green fairy.
history: This absinthe-laced Dry Martini was popularised during the 1940s at Lafitte's Blacksmith Shop in New Orleans and is regarded as one of the Crescent City's cocktails.

name: Tijuana Brass
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. Top with cucumber foam. (Top make cucumber foam: fill a cream whipper two-thirds full with equal parts cucumber juice, 1:1 simple syrup and egg white, then charge with two nitrous oxide (N2O) cartridges and chill.)
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	Agave syrup
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Pronounced "Tea-You-One-Na" this is basically a Tommy's Margarita topped with cucumber foam.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2009 by Damian Windsor at The Roger Room in Los Angeles, USA.

name: Tip Top Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: The lemon zest twist is essential to the fine balance of this vermouth (note; no spirit) cocktail.
history: Recipe adapted from Albert S. Crockett's 1935 Old Waldorf Bar Days.

name: Aperol Spritz / Aperitivo Spritz
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
3 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
2 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review:
Slightly sweet, herbal, refreshing and quaffable.

The good folk at Aperol, the aperitivo liqueur brand most identified with the Spritz, recommend equal parts prosecco and liqueur topped with a splash of soda. However, we've stuck with our preferred 3:2:1 ratio which is a little lighter on aperitivo liqueur and noticeably fizzier. Hence, along with specifying how you want your steak done and preferred Dry Martini ratio, perhaps also stipulate your Spritz ratio.
history: Spritz cocktail history (and other recipes)

name: Boulevardier Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review: Basically a Negroni with bourbon replacing gin. The original 1927 recipe calls for equal parts, but I've previously favoured a 3:2:2 (45ml bourbon, 30ml rosso vermouth, 30ml Italian red bitter liqueur) recipe. Popular demand (see comments) has led me to adopt a 2:1:1 recipe as I have to concede it's better balanced.
history: The Boulevardier first appears in Harry McElhone's Barflies and Cocktails, not among the book's A-Z listing of recipes but in a piece called "Cocktails Round Town" contributed by Arthur Moss, the "Around the Town" columnist of the New York Herald, Paris.

name: French Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
review: A simple riff on the French Martini swapping the usual vodka for the more French cognac. Fruity and easy drinking.
history: Created in June 2011 by yours truly at The Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: The Business
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: As the name suggests, The Business is a riff on a classic Bee's Knees with lime juice. It's snappier with lime instead of lemon juice.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created by Sasha Petraske at his famous Milk & Honey bar in Manhattan, New York City, USA.

The Business features in Georgette Moger-Petraske's 2016 Sasha Petraske Regarding Cocktails.

name: Dry Martini (3:1 ratio)
garnish: Chilled olive on stick or lemon zest twist.
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura (optional)
review: Three to one may be unfair odds in a fight but vermouth shines in this stirred off-dry Martini. Through experimentation we have found that 3:1 Martinis are better stirred rather than shaken. Conversely 15:1 Martinis are better shaken rather than stirred.
history: There is considerable debate around the origin of the Martini and the best way to make this drink. Detailed information can be found on our Dry Martini page.

name: The Cappa Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineau des Charentes blanc
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
review: Dry, balanced and delicate with a balanced marriage of gin, fortified wine and maraschino.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2012 by Franky Marshall at 15 Romolo, San Francisco, USA.

name: Paloma (Simple)
garnish: Salt rim (optional) & pink or red grapefruit wedge
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass and gently stir.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
4 shot	Thomas Henry Pink Grapefruit soda
review: Long, fruity and refreshing.
history: Paloma is Spanish for 'dove', and this well-known cocktail in Mexico is rumoured to have been created by the legendary Don Javier Delgado Corona, owner/bartender of La Capilla (The Chapel) in Tequila, Mexico. Don Javier notably stirred his drinks with a huge knife.

name: Rocky Left Bank
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄6 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1 1⁄3 shot	Chardonnay (Chablis) white wine
review: A slightly sweet, hopefully crowd-pleasing, combo of gin, elderflower and white wine.
history: Created in 2006 by yours truly at The Cabinet Room in London, England.

name: Double Grape
preparation: STIR ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 3⁄4 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1 3⁄4 shot	Byrrh Grand Quinquina
1 dash	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
review: The aromatics of the distilled wine of pisco combine harmoniously with the aromatised wine’s sweet grapey notes.
history: Created by yours truly (Simon Difford) at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Islay Old Fashioned
preparation: STIR whisky with three ice cubes (dry to the touch frozen ice, not wet ice) in a glass. Add sugar syrup, bitters and two more ice cubes. STIR some more and add another two ice cubes. STIR a bit more, and if you have room, add more ice.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄3 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
3 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
