review: Given its name, obviously, this cocktail was originally based on Islay peated malt whisky, but as they'd say on the BBC, "other peated whiskies are available". Choose judiciously, and this Old Fashioned will be delicious.
history:
In late 2014, Eliot Cole sent me an email saying, "one of my favourite drinks ever was an Old Fashioned made with Laphroaig (possibly quarter cask)... it was made at Hotel Delmano in Williamsburg, Brooklyn". Thanks to Eliot I took to the bar and, with a nod to David Embury's preference for Peychaud's bitters with whisk(e)y in my mind, made this tasty Old Fashioned.
See: Old-Fashioned cocktail history

name: Fat Godfather
preparation: Fat-wash a bottle of peaty Scotch whisky with smoky bacon fat. POUR the now clarified smoky bacon-flavoured Scotch and other ingredients into mixing glass, STIR with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky (bacon fat washed)
1 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1 dash	Whiskey barrel-aged bitters
history: Created in 2016 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England for Disaronno's Mixing Star project.

name: Carnaghino
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Dark chocolate liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Pistachio liqueur
review: Cognac, luxurious chocolate and pistachio. What’s not to like?
history: Created in 2015 by Gabriele Carnaghi at Sky Bar Birmingham Resort World, England.

name: Gin Old Fashioned
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A couple of shots of bready genever with a spoon of sugar and a couple of dashes of bitters - incredibly simple, equally classic, and with the right genever, incredibly tasty.
history: For a detailed history of the Old-Fashioned cocktail, along with additional recipes, see our page.

name: Med Mex Cocktail
garnish: Long strip of cucumber peel around inside of glass.
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filed glass and lightly stir.
ingredients:
1 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
Top up with	Aegean Tonic Water
history: Created in 2015 by Dimitris Dafopoulos, Athens, Greece.

name: Kula Negroni
garnish: Orange zest twist and fresh strawberry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass, preferably over a large chunk of block ice.
ingredients:
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur (infused with strawberry)
1 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
history: Created by Julie Reiner at Clover Club, New York City, USA.

name: Whisky Mac Toddy
preparation: POUR ingredients into pre-heated glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 shot	Ginger wine
3 1⁄2 shot	Boiling water
review: Simple, warming and comforting – rich ginger wine, gently spices and mellows Scotch whisky.
history: A Whisky Mac, made into a long warming toddy by simply adding boiling water.

name: Gimlet (no added sugar & low-calorie)
garnish: Express lime zest or two into glass and discard before pouring cocktail. Then place lime wedge on rim.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar-free sweetener
review: Fresh lime juice replaces cordial in this vitamin C-loaded, almost healthy gin-laced sugar-free version of a classic Gimlet.
history: Created by yours truly in January 2019.

name: Le Frog
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
review: A tasty Islay whisky-influenced riff on a French Martini.
history: One of many riffs on the French Martini.

name: Vodka Silver Bullet
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Mentzendorff Kümmel liqueur
8 drop	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
review: Perhaps best described as a Kümmel Martini with kümmel liqueur's strong caraway flavours fortified with vodka, freshened and made more complex by the addition of grapefruit bitters.
history: A classic with unknown origins.

name: Gin Spider Highball
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
review: A Pink Gin & Ginger would also be a fitting name for this tasty alternative to a Gin & Tonic.
history: As part of his long section on Highballs, in his 1948 The Fine Art Of Mixing Drinks David Embury notes, "Gin and ginger ale, with a dash of Angostura, is sometimes called a Gin Spider."

name: Darkside
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Mancino Vermouth di Torino Chinato
3 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: This gin, Barolo Chinato and Peychaud's bitters trio is remarkably reminiscent of a Negroni.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Adam Bernbach at Bar Pilar, Washington, D.C., USA. Adam's original recipe calls for a boozy 75ml of gin and 22.5ml Barolo chinato.

name: Explorer 'Martini'
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1 shot	Amontillado sherry
review:
The choice of sherry greatly impacts the Explorer. Made with cream sherry, as per the original recipe, brings out the rich marzipan notes in the amaretto to produce a richer after-dinner cocktail.

In contrast, a fino sherry dries this cocktail to make it more apéritif in style with nutty flavours to the fore.

Amontillado sherry (as in our rendition) amplifies butterscotch and is best served on the rocks in an old-fashioned as a late-night tipple. An extremely versatile equal parts recipe to appeal to all palates.
history: Adapted from a cocktail discovered by a fellow Discerning Drinker in 2019 at Sandals Resort in Barbados, where it's made with Harvey's Bristol Cream Sherry rather than Amontillado sherry.

name: Absinthe Spider Highball
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
4 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
review: Absinthe and ginger ale combine well in this refreshing highball.

name: Dry Martini (4:1 ratio)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura (optional)
review: A stirred four-to-one Martini is indeed a delicious thing. But is a five-to-one Martini even more delicious? Try both, and perhaps also a three-to-one. What a wonderful way to lose an evening.

name: Jean Harlow
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura (optional)
review: Reminiscent of a Martinez but a tad lighter.
history: Adapted from a recipe in the 1933 book Hollywood Cocktails published by the wonderfully named, Buzza-Cardozo, a Hollywood-based company that specialised in illustrated cards and books.

name: De Rigueur
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
3⁄4 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: Delicately peaty Scotch whisky with rich rounding honey balancing tart zesty grapefruit. This recipe will stand a much bigger slug of bourbon, particularly if using a more mellow honey.
history: This recipe is adapted from Judge Jr.'s 1927 Here's How! where its name is spelt "De Riguer" with one 'u'.

name: Fair Harvard
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
3 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: This wonderfully aromatic cocktail; benefits from dilution so consider adding a splash of chilled water or serving on-the-rocks.
history: A recipe created in 2016 by drinks writer Robert Simonson to serve at a reception at Yale School of Architecture. The speaker was from Harvard so a classic dark liquor based Harvard Cocktail seemed appropriate but the venue was an all-white room, so, in case of spillage, Robert created this clear riff on the classic.

name: Cosmonaut
preparation: STIR all ingredients in base of shaker to dissolve jam, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3 barspoon	Raspberry jam
review: It's rich in both colour and flavour. Don't scrimp on the quality of raspberry jam; use three flat barspoons (15-20ml). Sasha's original recipe specifies Bonne Maman Raspberry Conserve.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created by Sasha Petraske at his Milk & Honey bar in New York City, USA.

In Georgette Moger-Petraske's 2016 Sasha Petraske Regarding Cocktails, Michael Madrusan, who worked alongside Sasha at Milk & Honey, says of the Cosmonaut, "Sasha named it as a jab towards the popularity of the Cosmopolitan, which this drink, Emphatically, is not."

name: Peach Me
garnish: Orange slice wheel or fresh peach wedge
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
5⁄12 shot	Peachtree peach schnapps
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: It's peachy baby! Well, subtly peachy. Most of all it's a whiskey-forward, Old Fashioned-style sipping cocktail that demonstrates just how harmoniously bourbon and peach sit together.
history: Adapted from a cocktail by Jason Shullo, beverage director at Golden Entertainment, Las Vegas, USA. We've taken the liberty of renaming Jason's original Peach Me recipe as Peach Old-fashioned (Wisconsin-style).

name: Full Monte No.2
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Amaro replaces vermouth in this delectably bittersweet Reverse Manhattan.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Jenelle Engelson at Gertie's Bar at The 404 Kitchen in Nashville, USA.

name: Remember the Alimony
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Fino sherry
1 1⁄4 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
review: Fino sherry adds a cleansing mineral note to this delicious riff on a classic Negroni.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2012 by Dan Greenbaum at The Beagle bar, New York City, USA.

name: Cherry Fruitini
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded), & fresh cherry or Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Cherry juice
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Cherry juice laced with vodka and the merest hint of sweetness. Almost a healthy "Martini".
history: Created in May 2020 by yours truly in Rye, England.

name: Watermelon Fruitini
preparation: Cut watermelon into 16 segments, chop the flesh from one segment into cubes and MUDDLE in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 slice	Watermelon (fresh)
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: So fruity, you could almost convince yourself this is a health drink.
history: This cocktail emerged in London, England during the 1990s. Thought to have been created at The Met Bar.

name: Cin-Cyn
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: A slightly sweeter, less bitter, artichoke-influenced riff on a classic Negroni.
history: Cin-Cyn is a play on 'cin-cin', Italian for cheers and reflects the use of Cynar as the artichoke amaro in the original recipe. Cin-cin (pronounced 'chin-chin') is a toast used in casual and informal settings as an alternative to the more formal 'salute'.

name: Adriatique
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
1⁄2 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Bittersweet zesty orange with deep herbal complexity. Great for a summer afternoon or an evening aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2013 by Jackson Cannon at Island Creek Oyster Bar in Boston, USA.

name: Calvados & Tonic
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters (optional)
3 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: Crisp dry apple with delicate quinine tonic bitterness.

name: Bourbon Old Fashioned
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into Ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄4 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Generous dashes of bitters add spice to delicately sweetened bourbon.

name: Pink Witch
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄6 shot	Strega liqueur
3 1⁄3 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Depending on your grapefruit this drink may indeed be lightly pink, and, again, depending on your grapefruit, hopefully it will be balanced and superbly refreshing.

name: Mexican Jumping Bean
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
1⁄2 shot	Agave syrup
review: The lovechild of Dick Bradsell's Espresso Martini and Tommy's Margarita.
history:
Perhaps better known by some as the Mexpresso Martini, this cocktail likely emerged in the mid-noughties in London. However, it was made famous when created and named the Mexican Jumping Bean by Richard Godwin of The Spirits fame. Here's how he tells the story:

"One afternoon a few years ago, I ran into my friends Cleo and Stewart in a bar near my old work in Kensington. Cleo and Stewart make Aqua Riva tequila for a living and I always had the impression they drank it for a living too - as it is generally impossible to spend more than three minutes in their company without a tray of Tommy's Margaritas arriving. We took up residence at a table. We drank Margaritas. And then some more. And after five or six, I felt the need to mix things up a bit. All that lime juice - I'm sure it was the lime juice - began to have a slightly pixelating affect. So I asked the bartender if he could make a Margarita with fresh espresso in place of the lime. The result was a Mexican take on the Espresso Martini."

name: Speyside Single Malt Old Fashioned
preparation: STIR ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Speyburn 10yo Speyside single malt
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Some may want to use a Demerara sugar syrup but pure cane sugar delicately mellows the malt whisky without masking its flavour, indeed it amplifies its character.
history: History of the Old-Fashioned Whiskey Cocktail.

name: Cowboy Derby
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Horse with No Name habanero bourbon
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Maple syrup
review: Habanero-infused whiskey adds a touch of Cowboy spirit to this riff on the classic 1930s' Brown Derby, with maple syrup balancing grapefruit tart freshness.
history: Created in August 2021 by yours truly in Rye, England.

name: Crowbar Hotel
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Horse with No Name habanero bourbon
5⁄6 shot	Elderflower liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A riff on Philip Spee's 2007 Beverly Hills Hotel Cocktail. Apparently, in cowboy lingo, a "crowbar hotel" is a jail, so when presented with a renegade whiskey I went in search of a suitably hospitable cocktail.
history: Created in September 2021 by yours truly at the Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: Poet's Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
review: A three-to-one Dry Martini enriched by a splash of herbal liqueur.
history: A riff on the equal parts Poet's Dream vintage cocktail by Damon Boelte at his Grand Army bar and restaurant in Brooklyn, New York City, USA.

name: Belafonte
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 shot	Dry white port
3 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: A Portuguese apéritif (Porto Tonico) influenced by a bittersweet Italian aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a cocktail created in 2o14 by London bartender Cas Oh. This features in his excellent 2020 Co-Specs cocktail book where he explains that Belafonte is the name of Steve Zizzou's boat in Wes Anderson's film The Life Aquatic starring Bill Murray as the eccentric oceanographer.

name: Bergamot Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
5⁄6 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Italicus liqueur
review: Rosolio di Bergamotto liqueur adds zesty complexity to clean grainy vodka and delicately gin botanicals.
history: Created at the suggestion of Nick Hopewell-Smith who advocates "75ml of the hard stuff and around 10ml of the adulterant" and says "for a lemony variant, I use Nardini Acqua Di Cedro."

name: Artillery
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A 2:1 Sweet Martini with aromatic bitters.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Queen Elizabeth Wine
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Zest lime and dry vermouth balance the rich herbal and saffron notes of Bénédictine liqueur.
history:
Cocktail historian, David Wondrich, discovered this cocktail in an advertisement form Bénédictine liqueur published in the February 1935 edition of Esquire Magazine that reads "Here is the prize-winning recipe in a recent nation-wide cocktail contest."

The Queen Elizabeth was the winning cocktail in US cocktail competition organised by the liqueur brand. It was created the preceding year by Herbert L. Quick, then the head bartender at the Benjamin Franklin Hotel in Philadelphia. Herbert named his cocktail, not after any monarch, but after his wife, Elizabeth.

Adapted from a recipe in Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide.

name: Arnaud's Special
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
5⁄6 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Chocolatey notes emerge from this Rob Roy-like cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Ted Saucier's 1951 Bottoms Up book, this was the signature cocktail at the eponymous New Orleans restaurant during the 1940s and 50s.

name: CIA
preparation: POUR all ingredients (preferably chilled) into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1⁄2 shot	Applejack brandy bottled-in-bond (50% alc./vol)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: My own preference is to sip half-sized serves of CIA from a Copita cup – it's too tasty to appreciate in a gulp.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in circa 2012 by Tonia Guffey at Dram bar in New York City, USA. Originally named the Triple A for amaro, Angostura and applejack, the CIA name, an acronym of Cynar In Applejack, was the idea of broadcaster and bar entrepreneur Sother Teague.

name: Peachy Peat
garnish: Skewered peach wedge & spray with peated whisky mist
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
6 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
4 1⁄3 shot	White peach & jasmine soda
review: Faintly smoky and salty peach, ideally served by the beach.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by the mysterious folk at Caisteal Chamuis.

name: Negronic
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filed glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice) and briefly stir to combine.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: A cocktail which Robert Simonson, the creator's partner, aptly describes as Negroni crossed with a Gin & Tonic. It is surprisingly delicious with the bitter quinine notes in the tonic water going some way to balance the sweet vermouth.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in September 2022 by Mary Kate Murray while visiting her parents on Long Beach Island in New Jersey, USA.

name: Chocolate Tequila Alexander
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Chocolate cream liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Añejo tequila
1⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: A rich, indulgent, tequila-laced riff on the classic Alexander cocktail.
history: Created in March 2023 by yours truly at The Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Monte Carlow
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Honeyed, toasty, oaky notes from the whiskey shine in this lightly herbal Old Fashioned-style late-night sipper.
history: A riff on the classic rye whiskey-based Monte Carlo created by Stephen Curtin and shared via our Monte Carlo page in January 2023.

name: Rose Petal 'Martini'
preparation: STIR all ingredients and stain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Lanique Spirit of Rose liqueur
1 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
review: Rose and cranberry sit together surprisingly harmoniously in this gin-laced Neo-Martini.

name: The Clansman
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice.)
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
2⁄3 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1⁄2 shot	Amontillado sherry
review: A Godfather based on peated scotch whisky in place of blended scotch and with a splash of sherry to accompany the amaretto in the classic recipe.
history: Created in April 2023 by yours truly using Caisteal Chamuis peated whisky which is named after Caisteal Chamuis (AKA Castle Camus) which was built on the east coast of Sleat, Isle of Skye by the MacLeod clan. A riff on the Godfather, this cocktail is named for these industrious builders and the MacDonald clan for which this castle became a stronghold.

name: Knock Almond Highball
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
5⁄6 shot	Disaronno amaretto
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
review: Rich almond and delicate ginger spice mellow the whisky's peaty strength.
history: I named this riff on the Loch Almond after Knock Castle, also known as Caisteal Chamuis (Castle Camus), the former stronghold of the MacDonalds. Now in ruins, the castle stands on the east coast of Sleat, some five miles north of Armadale on the Isle of Skye.

name: El Capitán
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A popular Peruvian riff on a Sweet Manhattan. A tad drier than a bourbon-based Manhattan.
history:
The combination of vermouth and pisco probably dates back to soon after vermouth arrived in Peru during the 1850s-60s with Italian immigrants. Pisco being the dominant spirit, it was a natural progression to mix this with the newly available fortified wine. However, the ingredients would have simply been combined without ice.

The origin of El Capitán is unknown, but it is said to date from the 1920s when it was apparently popular with army captains in the city of Puno in southeastern Peru.

name: Intercontinental
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Armagnac brandy
3⁄4 shot	Averna Amaro
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
review: Bittersweet spirituous armagnac with nutty fruity maraschino.
history: Adapted from an originally equal parts cocktail created by Duggan McDonnell in San Francisco, USA.

name: Mezcaletti
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1 shot	Meletti amaro
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A drier mezcal-based riff on the M & M.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Richard Boccato at Bar Clacson in Los Angeles, USA.

name: Sunstone
preparation: STIR all ingredients and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1 shot	Americano bianco
review: Bittersweet and herbal. Enjoy as an aperitivo or digestivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Lindsay Matteson at Barnacle in Seattle, USA.

name: Big Chief
garnish: Flamed coin-sized orange zest twist (expressed and then floated)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄3 shot	Averna Amaro
1⁄3 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
review: A spirit-forward (bourbon) Manhattan-style digestivo.
history:
Named after the big chief Mardi Gras Indians that lead their tribes in New Orleans' St. Joseph's Day parade.

Adapted from a recipe created in 2016 by Abigail Deirdre Gullo at SoBou in New Orleans, USA. This is a riff on Abigail's own Longshoreman, which in turn was inspired by the Red Hook, one of a series of Manhattan-style cocktails named after districts of New York City.

name: Holy Smoke
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Manzanilla sherry
1⁄4 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
review: This delightful cocktail is light and yet complex with dry, lightly salty sherry, a touch of herbal liqueur, and subtle peaty whisky. Finishes with faint green apple notes, hence the garnish.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Yanni Kehagiaras at Stoa in San Francisco, USA.

name: Secrets of Savoy
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1 shot	Lucano amaro
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
review: Mezcal has an affinity to bittersweet liqueurs, here with an almost imperceptible slug of maraschino.
history: Adapted from a recipe discovered in March 2024 on barfaith.com.

name: Adjournment
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
review: A Dry Martini with a freshening zesty lemon burst, courtesy of limoncello. Don't let the generous splash of limoncello deceive you into thinking this is a sweet cocktail. It is surprisingly dry with the spirituous bite of a proper Martini.
history: Created by David Teager, a fellow Discerning Drinker who shared this recipe via a comment on our Procrastination cocktail page (which is the same but with Green Chartreuse added and the measures of the vermouth and limoncello reversed.)

name: Marsala Negroni (Sicilian Negroni)
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and gently STIR. Add an additional ice cube or two after stirring.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Marsala semisecco (medium)
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review: Rich marsala replaces sweet vermouth in this Sicilian-influenced Negroni.
history: Chef Sandra Lotto, owner of Toscana Saporita Cooking School in Tuscany, Italy, created her version of this cocktail, "The Lost Sailor," with 45ml sweet marsala, 45ml Campari, and 45ml dry gin.

name: Caracalla Jazz Club
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice & DRY SHAKE and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Adriatico Bianco almond milk liqueur
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Gin-laced almond milk liqueur balanced and freshened with lemon juice.

name: Irish Godfather
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into an ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
2⁄3 shot	Disaronno amaretto
2 drop	Boker's bitters
review: Amaretto adds delicate richness and toasted almond flavours to Irish whiskey in this old-fashioned-style cocktail. Your choice of bitters will profoundly influence the finished cocktail.
history: Recipe by yours truly.

name: Fergroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review: Serving a Negroni garnished with lemon rather than orange zest twist is normally an act of heresy, but the Fergroni does indeed benefit, adding zesty vitality to what otherwise could be a heavyweight cocktail.
history: A Negroni variation created by chef Fergus Henderson. The Fergroni is served at all his St John's restaurants across London.

name: Boilermaker
preparation: POUR whiskey to brim of shot glass and then manoeuvre shot glass so it is held tight up against the inside base of an upturned Boston glass. Then quickly flip the Boston glass over so that the bourbon is trapped in the now upside-down shot glass. Now pour beer into Boston glass over the whiskey-filled shot glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 pint	Pilsner lager
review:
When you get to the end of the beer the shot glass lifts and the whiskey is released as a chaser.

I should point out that in these days of discernment, a Boiler Maker is most commonly a glass of beer served with a shot glass of whiskey alongside – NOT one inside the other. It is also increasingly common for the beer and the whiskey to be specifically selected due to their flavours complementing one another. Beer and whiskey matchmaking.
history: Unknown but in his book The Joy of Mixology Gary Regan credits steelworkers in western Pennsylvania.

name: Coquetail Au Vanille
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. Serve with straws.
ingredients:
2 shot	Vanilla rum/vanilla-infused light rum
1⁄4 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
review: This drink may look fluffy and sweet but it's dry and lightly spiced. Perfect for a sunny afternoon.
history: An adaptation of a classic by yours truly, London, England.

name: Gibson Dry Martini
garnish: Pair of skewered pickled cocktail onions
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄12 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄12 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: A classic Dry Martini without bitters and garnished with cocktail onions in place of an olive or a twist. On those two distinctions, all are agreed. However, this cocktail's history and the best proportions of the two ingredients are topics of bar debate. I believe two different Mr Gibsons, a decade apart, were involved in creating and defining this cocktail. As for the proportions, I favour my go-to 5:1 Dry stirred Martini ratio.
history:
As David Embury says in his 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks, "The distinction between the Martini and the Gibson is simple. The Martini is served with an olive, the Gibson with a small pickled cocktail onion."

However, what differentiated a Gibson Martini was originally not its garnish but the lack of orange bitters in its recipe at a time when dashes of bitters in Martinis were the norm. The onion garnish came decades later.

The first written reference to a Gibson appears in a piece written by Edward W. Townsend in the Sunday 13th February 1898 edition of New York's The World newspaper, titled "Major Max Philosophizes. A Recent Society Function Discussed by the Major and His Wife." The salient section:

name: Stinger
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe
review: Classically the Stinger is shaken and served straight-up in a chilled coupe. However, I think it makes for a more refreshing peppermint and brandy digestif when served over crushed ice.
history:
In the 1956 American musical comedy film High Society, Bing Crosby explains to Grace Kelly how the Stinger gained its name. "It's a Stinger. It removes the sting."

The Stinger appears in Jacques Straub's 1913 Straub's Manual of Mixed Drinks but owes its popularity during the 1920's to Reginald "Reggie" Vanderbilt, an American millionaire and father of fashion designer Gloria Vanderbilt.

In his 2015 Updated & Revised Imbibe David Wondrich recounts a 1923 newspaper gossip page story crediting the invention of The Stinger to Reggie, a keen cocktail maker who "was observed in all its pomp and glory in the bar of [his] home, and he himself was the high priest, the host, the mixer." The bar in his Fifth Avenue mansion was apparently modelled after the one in the William the Conqueror tavern in Normandy. The article claims "the 'Stinger' was his own invention, a short drink with a long reach, a subtle blending of ardent nectars, a boon to friendship, a dispeller of care."

Reggie's enthusiasm for cocktails, particularly the Stinger helped contribute to his death from liver failure on 4th September 1925.

Similar cocktails, under various names, date back to 1890 when Reggie was only ten. That said, the name Stinger, after the boxing term for a jab to the head, only emerged in 1913 and although a bartender named James B. Regan at New York's Knickerbocker Hotel is implicated, I like to believe that Reggie didn't just adopt the Stinger as his own but also christened it.

name: Vodkatini / Vodka Martini
garnish: Chilled olive on stick or lemon zest twist
preparation: SHAKE (or STIR) all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: Temperature is key to the enjoyment of this modern classic. Consume while icy cold and you'll enjoy a clean and crisp Martini.
history: Exactly where the Vodkatini fits in the vexed question of the origins of the Dry Martini are unknown but it's certain that 'Vodka Martinis' were being served in New York after the repeal of Prohibition in 1933. It's first known print appearance is a 1935 Smirnoff marketing pamphlet:

name: Whisky Mac
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 shot	Ginger wine
review:
When a teenage pub-goer in the early 1980s, the Whisky Mac was my drink of choice after I'd had my fill of ale – Courage Directors in those days. I hit upon the Whisky Mac mostly because I liked the name and it pushed the boundaries of what could be ordered at The Pickhurst Pub. I remember the drink comprising a jigger of scotch whisky and an equal measure of green ginger wine served in a tumbler over a few cubes of bad pub ice. You paid for each measure - two drinks served in one glass.

I was young with a sweet tooth, so equal parts whisky to wine suited. Now middle-aged/old with drier tastes, I prefer at least one-and-half times as much whisky to green wine. The resulting cocktail is gently spirituous with subtle ginger spice and an off-dry velvety mouthfeel. As a teenager I was onto a good thing!
history:
This cocktail's full name is Whisky MacDonald, and legend has it that it was named after Major General Sir Hector Archibald MacDonald (4th March 1853 - 25th March 1903). Then better known as Fighting Mac due to his military exploits, MacDonald was a distinguished Victorian soldier who became something of a folk hero.

MacDonald is said to have first made the eponymously named drink in 1899 while serving in India, during a period of unrest over a proposed demarcation between China and British India - a border known as the Macartney-MacDonald Line (which is still the basis of the border between China and Pakistan). A cholera breakout hit the troubled area, and due to the perceived medicinal properties of ginger, so green ginger wine became popular among serving officers. MacDonald combined his love for whisky and medicinal ginger wine to create the Whisky Mac.

One should never let the truth stand in the way of a good story, and our hero may well have mixed scotch whisky with green ginger wine whilst in India, but the Macartney-MacDonald Line is named after George Macartney, the British consul at Kashgar, and Sir Claude MacDonald, the British envoy in Peking who presented the proposed border to the Chinese in a letter to the Qing government. That doesn't necessarily throw doubt on the relationship between Sir Hector Archibald MacDonald and the Whisky Mac, but the two MacDonalds have been confused in various tellings of this legend.

But what of our hero, Fighting Mac? He was the son of a Ross-shire crofter who left school before he was 15 and, at the age of 17, enlisted as a private in the Gordon Highlanders. He quickly rose through the ranks after distinguishing himself in action at Omdurman in 1898. He then became a popular hero in Scotland and England and was knighted for his service in the Second Boer War.

Sir Hector MacDonald became a Major General, then one of only a few British Army generals to have risen through the ranks, "from stable boy to general," merely on merit and success in the field. Such was his notoriety that his likeness appeared on the labels of Camp Coffee as the moustached, dark-headed officer being offered a tray of coffee.

MacDonald's final posting was to Ceylon (Sri Lanka) as Commander-in-Chief of British forces, but tragically, he shot himself in a hotel room in Paris on 25 March 1903 "following unsubstantiated accusations of homosexual activity with local boys." Was his suicide proof of his guilty conduct while in Ceylon? Or was MacDonald the victim of a class-ridden conspiracy? This blog makes a compelling argument for his merely falling foul of the British Establishment.

Sir Hector MacDonald may or may not have created the Whisky Mac, but it is fitting that a cocktail is named after him.

name: Z Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 1⁄4 shot	Tawny port
review: Grainy vodka with dry, wine-like notes. The garnish makes the drink.
history:
Discovered in 2004 at Les Zygomates, Boston, USA.

Our Martini cocktail page details its evolution and other common variants.

name: Dry Martini (1:1 ratio) Fifty-Fifty
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: A very 'wet' but wonderfully Dry Martini which demands an olive, not a twist. Before you start - Craddock calls for it to be shaken, but it's better stirred. Shaking tends to suit Martinis with a low vermouth ratio.
history: First published in Hugo R. Ensslin's 1917 Recipes for Mixed Drinks and then repeated, like so many of Ensslin's cocktails, in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book. Both Ensslin and Craddock call for the "Fifty-Fifty Cocktail" to be stirred and both also list a Dry Martini cocktail with the addition of "1 dash orange bitters." However, while Ensslin's 2:1 Martini is stirred, Craddock's 1:1 Martini is shaken, so according to Craddock, a Fifty-Fifty should be stirred while an equal parts Dry Martini is shaken. Remember, this is 23 years before Fleming's first Casino Royale Bond novel.

name: Valencia Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
review: A Martini-style drink but using fino sherry instead of vermouth. Crisp and dry.
history: See Martini cocktail and its evolution

name: Nick & Nora
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: A classic Three-to-One Dry Martini served in bijou proportions.
history:
Created in circa 1934 and named after Nick and Nora Charles, the flirtatious married couple at the centre of Dashiell Hammett's 1933 The Thin Man story serialised in Redbook Magazine. Published as Prohibition was ending, Nick is a hard-drinking retired detective and his wife Nora a wealthy heiress, both embrace cocktail culture. The Thin Man was published as a novel in 1934 and then a series of movies.

In the novel, Nick and Nora shake their Martinis and Nick tells a bartender, "The important thing is the rhythm. Always have rhythm in your shaking. Now a Manhattan you shake to fox-trot time, a Bronx to two-step time, a Dry Martini you always shake to waltz time." Hence, some insist a Nick and Nora Martini should be shaken rather than stirred.

In the movie, the detective duo drink from what has become known as a Nick & Nora glass so this has become the default for this scaled-down to fit Dry Martini.

name: Bohemian Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: A regular Four-to-One Dry Martini garnished with a caperberry.
history:
Created circa 2002 by Tim Stones and Ross Simon while bartending at LAB Bar on Old Compton Street in Soho, London, England. The name comes from Café Bohéme, the late-opening restaurant practically opposite, where the LAB crew would go for sustenance after a shift.
Martini history

name: Buckeye
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: A standard Dry Martini - but a Buckeye is always garnished with a black olive instead of a green one.

name: Roosevelt Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: A regular Martini, but garnished with two olives instead of one.
history:
Named after Franklin Delano Roosevelt (1882-1945), the 32nd President of the United States. Roosevelt is remembered for leading his country into World War II to fight alongside the Allies against Germany and Japan: he died just as victory was in sight.

Also see our Dry Martini page.

name: Sweet Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: A 5:1Dry Martini made with sweet vermouth - sweet in name but drier than the cherry garnish might indicate.

name: Mamie Taylor Highball
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
3 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
review: Faintly smoky malty Scotch and subtly sweet ginger are flavours that are simply made for each other. Simple but delicious.
history:
Bartenders apparently became so sick of making Mamie Taylors in the 1900s that they hiked up the price of the cocktail to discourage customers from ordering it.

Mamie Taylor was invented in 1899 in Rochester, New York, and it spread like wildfire. The name is a bit of a mystery, but there are several versions of a tale linking this cocktail to the Broadway star of the same name.

Thirty years after its creation, the Mamie Taylor appears in Albert Stevens Crockett's 1935 The Old Waldorf-Astoria Bar Book with the juice of half a lime served in a Collins glass. Sadly, the cocktail never managed to recover from Prohibition and has since faded from the limelight.

name: Milano Torino (Mi-To) Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: The drink that led to both the Negroni and the Americano. Pause and enjoy its simplicity before progressing.
history: Created at Milan's Caffè Camparino in the 1860's, the Milano-Torino is named after its original ingredients: Campari is from Milan (Milano in Italian) and sweet vermouth traditionally comes from Turin (Torino in Italian). It is said that later soda water was added to the Milano-Torino to create the Americano. The Milano-Torino also morphed into the Negroni with gin added.

name: Rebujito cocktail
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass and stir.
ingredients:
3 1⁄2 shot	Lemon-lime soda (Sprite/7-Up)
2 1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
review: Dry characterful sherry with sweet zesty lemonade – a combo made for a hot summer’s day.
history: Named after the Spanish word 'arrebujar' meaning to mix, the recipe for a Rebujito changes from region to region in Spain and is often as simple as equal parts fino sherry and soda or equal parts fino sherry and Sprite or Seven-up. It is popular in Seville and the south of Spain, particularly during April’s Seville Fair (La feria de Abril).

name: Grapefruit & Rose Seltz
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Grapefruit & Rose
5 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review:
Very refreshing and light. Perfect for a summer's afternoon. Our own favourite of the three initial Ketel One botanical serves.

Also, consider serving as a Spritz: Pour 90ml/3oz Prosecco, 45ml/1.5oz Botanical Grapefruit & Rose and 60ml/2oz soda water into an ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
history: One of three signature serves launched in the summer of 2018 to accompany the launch of Ketel One Botanicals.

name: White Sting
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Acqua Bianca liqueur
review: This riff on a classic Stinger brings in floral rose notes which sit alongside delicately freshening mint.
history: Created in 2020 by Salvatore "The Maestro" Calabrese at the Donovan Bar, London, England.

name: White Spider
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Acqua Bianca liqueur
review: A cleansing Martini-style cocktail with sophisticated citrus, rose and mint notes.
history: A White Spider is another name for a Vodka Stinger (vodka and white crème de menthe) and in 2020 Salvatore Calabrese, at London's Donovan Bar, adapted this vodka-based classic cocktail to use his Acqua Bianca, an alternative white crème de menthe liqueur.

name: Rhubarb & Tonic Highball
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Rhubarb flavoured vodka
Top up with	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: Surprisingly tasty and very refreshing. Forget rhubarb & custard.

name: Monte & Tonic
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
4 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: Bittersweet and very refreshing with hints of zesty citrus freshness.

name: Porto Tonico (White Port & Tonic)
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Dry white port
3 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: Portugal's answer to the G&T is tasty, balanced, superbly refreshing and has a relatively low alcohol strength.
history: A traditional Portuguese aperitivo that's particularly popular during the summer months.

name: Vodka Stinger
garnish: Float mint leaf or peg to glass rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe
review: A vodka-based version of the classic Stinger. Fresh, clean and cleansing.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Stan Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide

name: Less is More Negroni
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Savoia Americano Rosso
5⁄6 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
review: Looks like a Negroni, tastes like a very good and interesting Negroni, yet only has two ingredients – hence the name. Also, quicker to make than a three-ingredient Negroni and with one less bottle to buy.
history: Giuseppe Gallo, the creator of Savoia Americano.

name: Casa Savoia Garibaldi
preparation: Squeeze orange juice using pillar or elbow press and fine strain to remove any flesh. BLEND the freshly squeezed juice at high speed (without ice) to make "fluffy". POUR Americano and half of the orange juice into glass over 2 cubes of ice and STIR. Fill glass with more ice (3 cubes) and TOP up with rest of fluffy orange juice.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Savoia Americano Rosso
3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: The success of this cocktail is reliant upon your oranges and how you fluff their juice. Fluff well and this is delicious.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Giuseppe Gallo, the creator of Savoia Americano.

name: Casa Savoia Boulevardier
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or junk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Savoia Americano Rosso
5⁄6 shot	Bourbon whiskey
review: A delicious riff on a classic Boulevardier with just two ingredients.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Giuseppe Gallo, the creator of Savoia Americano.

name: Peaty Monte
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1 1⁄3 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
review: Peated whisky replaces mezcal in this riff on the bartenders' favourite M&M.
history: Created by Asher Günther who, on Christmas Day 2022, left this comment on our M&M page; "I've tried this drink a few times and very much enjoyed it. Tonight I thought I'd try subbing the mezcal for the other smokey bottle in my cabinet - an Islay single malt. Oh man. Someone needs to give this a name and get it on a menu ASAP." I've tentatively named this delicious combo "Peaty Monte" but I'm sure somebody will come up with a better name.

name: Winged Hussar
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) & skewered green grape
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
4 1⁄3 shot	Energy drink (carbonated)
review: With the peaty whisky, the energy drink takes on an almost smoked white grape flavour.
history: Created in March 2023 by yours truly for Caisteal Chamuis.

name: Core Blimey
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) and lemon slice wheel
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
4 1⁄3 shot	Sparkling apple juice
review: Wisps of smoky peated whisky-infuse carbonated apple juice to produce a deliciously refreshing long drink.
history: Created in April 2023 by yours truly at The Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Poleaxe
garnish: Mist with spray of peated whisky
preparation: POUR all ingredients into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky (chilled)
3⁄4 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro) (chilled)
review: Peated whisky replaces mezcal in this riff on the bartenders' favourite M&M.
history: Adapted from Asher Günther's Peaty Monte cocktail by your's truly in April 2023.

name: Hebridean
garnish: Orange slice or lime slice wheel or wedge
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
4 1⁄3 shot	Red bitter soda
review: Italian red bitter soda mixes brilliantly with peaty whisky.
history: Created in April 2023 by yours truly for Caisteal Chamuis. The name is a reference to this whisky's Hebridean home on the Isle of Skye.

name: Amaro Caldo
garnish: Lemon zest twist, expressed and dropped into glass
preparation: POUR All ingredients into pre-warmed heat-resistant glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Amaro Braulio
3 shot	Boiling water
review: A winter's hot digestivo or warming late-night toddy.
history: Amaro Caldo means 'hot bitter' in Italian, which describes this traditional Italian serve consisting of amaro (bitter liqueur) and hot (caldo) water.

name: Tom & Jerry
preparation:
1. Pre-warm six 20cl (6.75oz) toddy glasses or Tom & Jerry mugs with hot water.
2. Using a whisk, BEAT the yolks in a mixing bowl "until they are thin as water." Add sugar, Jamaican rum, spices and STIR thoroughly with whisk.
3. In a separate bowl, use a whisk to BEAT the egg whites "to a stiff froth."
4. Use a tablespoon to FOLD the frothy egg whites into the spiced and beaten yolk mixture. This produces the gloopy base mixture known as 'Tom & Jerry batter'.
5. To make individual drinks, to each of the warmed glasses or mugs, POUR cognac and rum, and add two table spoons of Tom & Jerry batter. STIR each glass/mug thoroughly with a barspoon while topping with boiling water.
6. Each should end up with frothy head ready to receive the garnish of grated nutmeg. Serve and enjoy.
ingredients:
2 fresh	Egg white
2 fresh	Egg yolk
6 barspoon	Caster/ Superfine/Baker's special sugar (white)
1⁄2 shot	Jamaican-style overproof aged pot still rum
2 pinch	Cinnamon powder (ground)
2 pinch	Clove
3 pinch	Freshly grated nutmeg
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
Top up with	Boiling water
review: A warming and filling winter's meal in itself. This recipe will fill six small toddy glasses or Tom & Jerry mugs (each 20cl capacity to brim), and given the faff involved you might as well double or treble the recipe and make for a crowd, or enjoy several each.
history: See history of the Tom & Jerry cocktail.

name: Bermuda Rum Swizzle
preparation: POUR ingredients into glass and two-thirds fill with crushed ice. SWIZZLE with a swizzle stick or CHURN (stir) with a bar spoon. Fill glass with more crushed ice and repeat. Serve with straws.
ingredients:
1 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 shot	Dark/black/blackstrap rum
3⁄4 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1 shot	Pineapple juice
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Your five-a-day fruits in a glass, laced with pungent rums and spice infused sweet Falernum.
history: This recipe is adapted from one by Del Pedro, originally from Bermuda but now resident in New York City. It came my way (in 1997) courtesy of LeNell Smothers, and apparently it originally heralds from the Swizzle Inn in Bermuda where their rather appropriate slogan is "Swizzle Inn, Swagger Out".

name: Billionaire
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
2⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄6 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 fresh	Mint leaves
review: Why have a Millionaire when you can stretch to a Billionaire? A suitably luxuriant whiskey sour with absinthe, aromatic bitters and mint.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2011 by Dushan Zarić and Jason Kosmas at Employees Only in Manhattan, New York City, USA. The original was quite different and was based on Wild Turkey Rare Breed Bourbon without the rye and (in place of absinthe, bitters and mint) called for Employee Only's housemade 'Absinthe Bitters', a blend of absinthe, Green Chartreuse, Peychaud's bitters, Angostura bitters and Fee Brothers Mint bitters.

name: Pegu Club Cocktail (Difford's recipe)
garnish: Coin-sized lime zest twist (expressed & discarded). Garnish with a lime wedge on rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄3 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Lime cordial (sweetened lime juice)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄4 shot	Chilled water
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review:
Whatever you think of modern-day Rose's Lime Cordial (other brands are available as well as homemade recipes), as with the Gimlet, I believe lime cordial is an essential part of this cocktail's DNA so should be included. Also, in keeping with the Gimlet, I like to use fresh lime juice to add fresh citrus zing alongside the 'cooked' notes of the cordial.

The other moving part of a Pegu Club is the orange curaçao liqueur. A dry 40 alc./vol. versus a very sweet 20-27% orange curaçao will impact the overall alcohol and sugar content very differently. I use a dry 40% curaçao so this dictates the need to balance with a smidgen of sugar syrup.

Strike the perfect balance and a Pegu Club is citrusy, bracing, and refreshing with the gin base providing the backbone while rich zesty orange curaçao, accentuated by tart lime, drives the flavour.
history:
Created in the 1920s at the Pegu Club, an ex-pat gentlemen's club in British colonial Rangoon, Burma.

The Pegu Club first appears in Harry McElhone's 1923 "Harry" of Ciro's ABC of Mixing Cocktails and notably in Harry Craddock's seminal 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book where he notes, "The favourite cocktail at the Pegu Club, Burma, and one that has travelled, and is asked for, round the world."

Despite The Savoy's influence, it's the recipe published just months before Craddock's, in Cocktails by Jimmy Late Of Ciro's London, written by the mysterious "Jimmy" (like McElhone another bartender who worked at Ciro's in London), which calls for fresh lime rather than cordial that's nearer to most other modern-day interpretations of this venerable classic. [Mine respects the use of lime cordial so is perhaps a tad more authentic!]

name: Courtside
preparation: MUDDLE berries in base of shaker. Add next five ingredients (all but soda), SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 fresh	Strawberries (hulled, small & ripe)
3 fresh	Raspberries
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Easy drinking, fruity, refreshing and lightly sweet. Bring on the summer's afternoon.

name: Vieille Place
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Bourbon whiskey
5⁄6 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Spirit-forward and bittersweet yet balanced and eminently drinkable. Reminiscent of an old-fashioned but with the option to enjoy as an aperitif.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2018 by Robbie Neskens at Bruut, Hasselt, Belgium. Robbie says, "This cocktail is a twist on the classic Vieux Carré. Vieux Carré and Vieille Place both have the same meaning: Old Square. With the difference Vieux Carré being masculine and Vieille Place feminine."

name: Ramos Greek Fizz
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and strain into chilled (empty) glass, while at the same time pouring soda water with your other hand so both liquids form a single stream to slowly fill the glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	O/Purist Tsipouro
1⁄2 shot	Kleos Mastiha liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2⁄3 shot	Egg white
2 barspoon	Yoghurt (natural)
3 1⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: This clever riff on a classic Ramos Gin Fizz harnesses a trio of Greek specialties: tsipouro, mastiha and yoghurt.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Aristotelis Makris.

name: High King
preparation: MUDDLE raspberries in base of shaker. Add next 6 ingredients (all but soda), SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
2 fresh	Raspberries
1 1⁄3 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1⁄3 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Berry fruit and citrus gently caressed by mellow Irish whiskey with a splash of enlivening soda.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Joaquín Simón at Pouring Ribbons in New York City, USA.

name: Espress Ya'self
garnish: Dust with black, green & red stripes of edible glitter
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
1⁄3 shot	Agave syrup
1⁄24 shot	Vanilla extract/essence
1 dash	Xocolatl mole bitters
1 dash	Chili tincture (firewater bitters)
review: Boozed-up and spiced, a coffee espresso has never been so expressive.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Anthony A. Baker, a New York City bartender. Baker's original spec. calls for 30ml cold-brew coffee in place of espresso coffee accompanied by 30ml Mr Black cold-brew liqueur.

name: Mad Monk Monkey
garnish: Lime zest twist (discarded) and maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄3 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Monkey 47 tops a mad list of ingredients with a Monastic liqueur also influencing the name of this gin-laced herbal sour.
history: Created in March 2022 by yours truly. Originally based on Monkey 47 Gin

name: Midnight Caller
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄2 shot	Amaro Santoni
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄4 shot	Agave syrup
4 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Wondering what to wet your palate with before dinner? This bittersweet aperitivo with complex botanicals, zesty grapefruit and a touch of tropical fruit may just be what you're looking for.
history: Created in November 2022 by yours truly and eponymously named after the American television drama series based around talk radio which aired on NBC from October 1988 to May 1991.

name: Adios Amigos
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water) (optional)
review:
A trio of base spirits blend harmoniously in a cocktail of which Trader Vic himself said, "You know that adios means good-bye. You drink two or three of these, and it's adios, believe me, it's adios."

His original recipe calls for "light Puerto Rican rum" and I originally interpreted that as a charcoal-filtered light white rum. However, I've since found this cocktail works best with a light rum with a little more age and character.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Victor Bergeron's 1972 Trader Vic's Bartender's Guide.

name: Mint Daiquiri
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE (just to bruise) mint in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. (Even with a fine strainer, if your finished cocktail doesn't end up with tiny fragments of mint on the surface, you've not shaken hard enough.)
ingredients:
12 fresh	Mint leaves
1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Gold rum (1-3 years old pot & column blend)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
6 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters
review: Reminiscent of a short, concentrated Mojito, this Daiquiri works well with either a charcoal filtered 'carta blanca' style light rum or a lightly aged 'gold' rum. The former produces a brighter and fresher Daiquiri, while the latter arguably has more character. In a quest for the best of both worlds, I've used equal parts of both rums.
history: Created in 2006 by yours truly.

name: Orange Mojito
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE mint (just to bruise) in base of glass. Add other ingredients and half fill glass with crushed ice. CHURN (stir) with bar spoon. Fill with more crushed ice and churn some more. TOP with soda, stir and serve with straws.
ingredients:
8 fresh	Mint leaves
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Oranje Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Mandarine Napoleon liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Mint and orange combine to make a wonderfully fresh drink.
history:
Created in 2001 by Jamie MacDonald while working in Sydney, Australia.

For more recipes, its origins and history, see the Mojito Cocktail.

name: Pear Shaped
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chiiled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
3⁄4 shot	Pear & cognac liqueur
1 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
3 drop	Bob's Vanilla bitters (optional)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water) (optional)
review: Scotch, pear and apple combine wonderfully in this fruity and balanced cocktail. Pear juice in place of apple juice produces a richer and arguably tastier cocktail.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2003 by Jamie Terrell at the iconic Dick's Bar at the Atlantic Bar & Grill in London, England. The Atlantic Bar & Grill opened in 1994, and it, particularly Dick's Bar, is considered the birthplace of the cocktail renaissance.

Jamie's original recipe was shaken and strained into an ice-filled Collins glass and comprised:
60ml (2oz) Scotch whisky
30ml (1oz) Pear & Cognac liqueur
90ml (3oz) Apple juice
15ml (½oz) Lime juice
7.5ml (¼oz) Vanilla syrup

A "Deluxe Version" was shaken and strained into a chilled Martini glass:
Pulp of 1 fresh Passion fruit
45ml (1½oz) Scotch whisky
30ml (1oz) Pear & cognac liqueur
30ml (1oz) Apple juice
30ml (1oz) Pear juice
7.5ml (¼oz) Lime juice

name: Periodista Daiquiri
garnish: Lime zest twist expressed and discarded. Adorn with skewered lime wedge and Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄4 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: An orange and apricot Daiquiri. Like most Daiquiris, the Periodista benefits from a little additional dilution, hence the chilled water in my recipe.
history: Periodista (Spanish for 'journalist') originated in Havana, Cuba, where it is said to have been one of Ernest Hemingway's tipples at El Floridita. In keeping with the Cuban origin, the earliest known recipe appears in the 1948 El Arte de Cantinera, a bartenders' manual from the Club de Cantineros de la Republica de Cuba in Havana.

name: Red Lion (Difford's recipe)
garnish: Half rim glass with orange juice and sugar-coated rim & orange zest twist (discarded)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: The sophisticated drinker's answer to a gin and juice with dry gin and orange liqueur made all the more fruity with orange juice, lemon juice and pomegranate syrup.
history:
Adapted from Arthur Tarling's 1933 competition-winning Red Lion recipe by yours truly in August 2016.
See: Red Lion cocktail history

name: St. Patrick's Day
garnish: Mint leaf or shamrock pegged to the rim
preparation: SHAKE first 6 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with splash soda.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1⁄3 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Peppermint Pastille crème de menthe
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Verdant, vibrant, and virtuous - so virtuous that it's saintly! Faintly minty, herbal, and citrusy with whiskey making it a helluva craic.
history: Created in 2006 by yours truly in London, England. (Better if it had been Dublin or Belfast!)

name: Feather Duster Crusta
garnish: Sugar crusted rim & thick lemon zest twist
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Passion fruit syrup
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: In Gregor's own words, "based on the father of the Sidecar, the granddad of the Margarita, Laydeez an' Gennulmen! The Brandy Crusta."
history:
Created in 2006 by Gregor de Gruyther at Ronnie Scott's, London, England. It is "quite a light Crusta", hence the name.
Crusta cocktail info

name: Jamie's Mojito
preparation: POUR first 4 ingredients into glass with lime wedges and mint. Half fill glass with crushed ice and CHURN (stir). Fill glass with more crushed ice and TOP with Prosecco.
ingredients:
1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 wedge	Lime (fresh)
12 fresh	Mint leaves
Top up with	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
review: A light mojito made more complex with bianco vermouth.
history:
Adapted from a drink found on the menu of Jamie's Italian restaurant and bar chain.

Mojito cocktails, tips and history

name: Boozy Suzie
garnish: Pink grapefruit zest twist (discarded) & 3 spots of Peychaud's bitters drawn through foamy head
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄4 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
1⁄4 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Bittersweet gentian is the prevalent flavour (hence the 'Suzie' name), toned down by bianco vermouth and freshened with pink grapefruit over a fortifying grainy vodka base. Peychaud's subtly adds its distinctive flavour.
history: Created in August 2015 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: 49th Parallel
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄3 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Sidecar-esque with zesty citrus tartness.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Robert Wilson at Urban Farmer, Portland, Oregon, USA. Robert's original recipe (below) was served in a coupe glass but this packed almost 3 ounces of liquor so in July 2020 I scaled this back to fit a Nick & Nora glass, plus I added the merest touch of sugar to balance citrus tartness. Hopefully, I've maintained the cocktail's integrity.

1 1⁄2oz Cognac
1⁄2 oz Straight rye whiskey
1⁄2 oz Lemon juice
1⁄2 oz Triple sec
2⁄3 oz Lillet Blanc
3 dash Peychaud's bitters

name: Brazuca Remedy
garnish: Lemon zest twist & float basil leaf
preparation: MUDDLE basil in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3 fresh	Basil leaves
1 1⁄2 shot	Cachaça
2⁄3 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Bittersweet and complex with underlying cachaça character. Perfect as an aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Joao Paulo Balzani at Aqua Spirit in Hong Kong, China.

name: Stone Fence (by Venning Bros.)
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass charged with soda. TOP with cider.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Crème de Pêche de Vigne liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
1 1⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
5⁄6 shot	Dry cider
review: Peach and bourbon combine harmoniously in this easy-drinking well-balanced fizz.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2017 by Max and Noel Venning at Three Sheets, London, England.

name: Aventura
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
6 fresh	Raspberries
1 1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
3⁄4 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Elderflower liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Mezcal infused raspberry fruit with lemon, orange and lime citrus aromatised with delicate rich elderflower.

name: Efficacious
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄6 shot	Ferro China Baliva
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄12 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: Take one per day in the hope it will aid your health, wealth and happiness. OK, its efficacious effect is most likely to benefit the latter at a cost to your wealth and perhaps your health.
history: Created in January 2021, amid Covid-19 lockdown, by yours truly using ingredients with a proven or claimed efficaciousness.

name: Poison Dart
garnish: Orange zest twist expressed & then skewered with a dart-like cocktail pick
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄4 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1⁄6 shot	Cinnamon syrup
1⁄24 shot	Pimento dram/Allspice liqueur
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Bourbon-laced zesty lemon balanced by rich almond syrup with layers of herbal complexity and cinnamon spice.
history: Adapted from a recipe, originally served straight-up in a coupe, created circa 2010 by Craig "Colonel Tiki" Herman. Many thanks to David Selle for bringing to my attention and uploading his own Poison Dart recipe.

name: Evening Sun
garnish: Express & float coin-sized orange zest twist
preparation: SHAKE first 6 ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with sparkling wine by pouring in the centre of the cocktail and then cover the hole in the foam left by pouring with garnish.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄6 shot	Lanique Spirit of Rose liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: It's the dry sparkling wine that has the last word in this beautifully integrated and complex foaming sour.
history: Adapted from a recipe in William Schmidt's 1892 The Flowing Bowl.

name: Smoky Chili Margarita
garnish: Smoked salt rim and lime wedge
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
