ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
2⁄3 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Piment d'Espelette chile liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
4 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Having tried the Tommy's version of this cocktail, (which as it doesn't have an orange liqueur is actually a "Tequila Sour",) I wanted to make it into a 'real' Margarita with a triple sec liqueur and a touch of added chili spice.
history: Created in October 2021 by yours truly and inspired by Stelios Papadopoulos' Smoky Tommy's Margarita.

name: Naked & Infamous
preparation: Cut a passion fruit in half and scoop the flesh and seeds form each half into shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 fresh	Passion fruit (fresh)
2⁄3 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
2⁄3 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
2⁄3 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄3 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄3 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: The lovechild of Douglas Ankrah's Pornstar Martini and Joaquín Simó's Naked & Famous. Fresh ripe (yet still a little tart passion fruit) sits alongside mezcal to jointly anchor this fruity, yet balanced, cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 at Homeboy bar in London, England.

name: White Negroni Piña Colada
preparation: SHAKE first 6 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. FLOAT aromatic bitters.
ingredients:
1 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄2 shot	Coconut rum liqueur (35-40% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄24 shot	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Just as it says on the tin – a White Negroni crossed with a Piña Colada, but the delight of crossbreeding is a tasty mezcal-based mongrel of a cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2020 by Chris Amirault at Parm Boyz in Los Angeles, USA.

name: Catch-Up Fizz
preparation: DRY SHAKE first 6 ingredients. SHAKE again with ice and strain into chilled glass (without ice). TOP with soda, or, ideally, strain cocktail into glass as you pour the soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Monkey Shoulder Fresh Monkey
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2⁄3 shot	Egg white
1 shot	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A classic fizz freshened with new make spirit.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Oliver Sagerstöm Blom of Satan's Whiskers in London, England.

name: Alaska (Difford's recipe)
preparation: Express the oils of a coin-size orange zest into the base of stirring glass. Add other ingredients, STIR with ice (Regal Stir) and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 disc	Orange zest/swath
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
1⁄2 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄4 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: A classic Alaska mixed with a dash of absinthe and mixed with a Regal Stir.
history: Recipe by yours truly in August 2023.

name: Cosmarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄3 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1 1⁄4 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Either a cross between a Cosmopolitan and a Margarita or an extremely Rude Cosmopolitan.
history: Created in November 2023 by yours truly at The Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Anchor Heart
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) to emulsify and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄6 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Genever provides a bready spirituous base while triple sec adds a zesty citrus bite to this honey sour. In keeping with its Anchor name, peaty malt and saline solution add a subtle marine element.
history: Inspired by De Kuyper's anchor in a heart logo, I created this cocktail in March 2020 for De Kuyper Royal Distillers' 325th anniversary. However, the COVID-19 pandemic scuppered De Kuyper's anniversary celebrations, so this cocktail stayed in my notes until April 2024, when I was looking for a cocktail to honour the retirement of Mark de Witte, CEO of De Kuyper Royal Distillers. I've been lucky enough to have counted Mark as a friend since I met him in 2013. Happy retirement, Mark.

name: Lychee Rosé
garnish: Skewered, peeled & destoned lychee (fresh or from tin)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	Kwai Feh lychee liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Manzanilla sherry
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: I believe this cocktail works better with the freshness of blanco rather than lightly aged reposado tequila, or indeed rose-coloured tequila. The original recipe omits Creole bitters, but this addition contributes colour and complexity of flavour.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Adam George Fournier at Spago restaurant in Los Angeles, California, USA. The original recipe is based on Tequila Komos Reposado Rosa rose-coloured tequila, house-made salted lychee cordial, manzanilla sherry, elderflower liqueur, and fresh lime juice.

name: Velveteen
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1 shot	Pale cream sherry (medium/sweet)
1⁄4 shot	Licor 43 Original liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Averna Amaro
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Brilliantly integrated flavours led by Irish whiskey and cream sherry. An elegant digestivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2024 by Eliza Hoar at Equal Measure in Boston, USA.

name: Baby Turtle
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) to emulsify and fine strain into an ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	Cinnamon syrup
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
2 dash	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Bittersweet and sweet 'n' sour cinnamon-infused tequila mellowed and made to combine harmoniously.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2013 at Trick Dog in San Francisco, USA.

name: Apricot Mango Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Mango purée
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Just as it says on the tin. Rich tropical and orchard fruit, but not overly sweet with balancing lemon citrus acidity, orange bitters and underlying gin botanical complexity.
history: Originally named Apricot Mango Martini this drink was created by yours truly during the fresh fruit Martini craze that swept through London's bars in the mid-1990s. Name and recipe updated by yours truly in September 2014.

name: Cosmopolitan Delight
garnish: Orange zest twist (expressed & discarded) and skewered berry fruits
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with red wine.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄2 shot	Shiraz red wine
review: No relation to the modern Cosmopolitan, this is a mellow, balanced blend of citrus, brandy and red wine.
history: Adapted from Dale DeGroff's 2002 book, The Craft of the Cocktail. He, in turn, credits the original recipe to Charlie Paul's 1902 book American and Other Iced Drinks.

name: Cucumber Martini
preparation: (Ideally, cut skin from cucumber log before chopping). MUDDLE cucumber in base of shaker, add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 inch	Cucumber (fresh) (chopped)
1 shot	Bison grass vodka
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Cucumber has never tasted so good, helped by being vodka-laced and infused with notes of bison grass. The touch of sugar in this cocktail helps amplify flavours rather than sweetening the cocktail.
history: There are many different Cucumber Martini recipes; this is mine - much improved in July 2023 thanks to a comment by Marco, a fellow Discerning Drinker (below).

name: Doctor
garnish: Express orange and lemon zests but adorn with just an orange zest
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 1⁄3 shot	Swedish Punsch liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
4 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters (optional)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Lighter and arguably more satisfying than the various citrus-heavy Doctor Cocktail recipes (see Doctor No. 1 to No. 4). Obviously, with two such dominant ingredients, your choice of rum and Swedish punch will greatly influence the result.
history: There are earlier Doctor recipes combining Swedish punch and rum (see Doctor No. 1), but this recipe, which first appeared in Frank Meier's 1936 Artistry of Mixing Drinks, has proved the most enduring, helped by its being republished in Victor Bergeron's 1947 Bartender's Guide... by Trader Vic

name: Dr Zeus
preparation: POUR Fernet Branca into ice-filled glass. Separately MUDDLE raisins in base of shaker, add other ingredients and SHAKE with ice. Finally DISCARD contents of glass and strain contents of shaker into the Fernet Branca coated glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
20 dried	Raisins
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Not that far removed from a Sazerac cocktail, this is innovative and great tasting.
history: Created by Adam Ennis in 2001 at Isola, Knightsbridge, London, England.

name: Frisky Bison
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE mint in base of shaker (just to bruise). Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
6 fresh	Mint leaves
1 1⁄3 shot	Bison grass vodka
2⁄3 shot	Apple Schnapps liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Sweet 'n' sour, fruity, minty and fresh.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Tony Kerr in 1999 at Mash & Air in Manchester, England.

name: Ginger Cosmo
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Ginger liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Ginger syrup
1 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 drop	Bob's Ginger Bitters
review: Just what it says on the tin - your everyday Cosmopolitan but with extra vitality courtesy of a good whack of ginger spice.
history:
The Ginger Cosmo emerged during 2002 in New York City but this recipe is adapted from one we discovered in October 2019 at Soho House Barcelona where it reigned as the best-selling "House Signature" cocktail.
Cosmopolitan cocktail history and recipe variations

name: Green Swizzle
garnish: Crown with 3 dashes Angostura bitters over the drink's ice cap, a lime wedge and mint sprig
preparation: POUR ingredients into chilled glass two-thirds filled with crushed ice. SWIZZLE (or churn with a barspoon). Add more crushed ice to fill. Serve with straws.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄3 shot	White overproof rum
1⁄6 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
5⁄6 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Peppermint Pastille crème de menthe
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Robustly flavoured ingredients brought together harmoniously in a tall, most refreshing swizzle. Worthy of its legendary status.
history:
The Green Swizzle was popular between 1890s and the 1930s during a period when the grand hotels of the Caribbean, such as the Queen's Park Hotel in Trinidad, were in their prime. This drinks legendary status is partly due to its featuring in The Rummy Affair of Old Biffy by P.G. Wodehouse. Bertie Wooster sings its praises after enjoying a few at the Panter's Bar of the West Indian stand at the 1924 British Empire Exposition at Wembley, London.

We bow to David Wondrich, who in his 2015 Updated and Revised Imbibe says, "It is impossible to give a definitive recipe for the Green Swizzle" and he goes on to explain that there are versions based on rum, whiskey, old tom gin and genever. While the recipe has numerous variations, it is certain that this swizzle was originally made green by dashes of absinthe bitters, rather than the green crème de menthe used in some modern interpretations of the drink. That said we like the way the minty liqueur combines with the absinthe that we've used as a wormwood bitters substitute. As for the base spirit, given the Green Swizzle's Caribbean heritage, white rum seems most appropriate (aged rum dirties the drink's pale green hue).

name: Havana Special
garnish: Pineapple wedge on rim & speared Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
5⁄6 shot	Pineapple juice
5⁄12 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
4 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters
review: A Pineapple Daiquiri with an added something – a touch of flavoursome ash-aged maraschino liqueur. When garnishing the pineapple may be optional but the cherry is a must-have.

name: Hawaiian Eye
garnish: Orchid or other edible flower. Serve with a straw.
preparation: DRY BLEND (without ice) first 5 ingredients on slow setting and gradually add Xanthan gum while continuing to blend. Add half a 7oz scoop of crushed ice and blend again. Pour into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
2⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
2⁄3 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄4 barspoon	Xanthan gum (E415) (optional)
review: Subtle clove spice and lime juice sits harmoniously with a duo of rums. A much used flavour combo but still a great cocktail worthy of a fresh outing.
history: A famous Tiki cocktail created circa 1963 by Tony Ramos at China Trader restaurant in Toluca Lake, California, USA, for the cast of the TV series of the same name who were filming at the nearby Warner Brothers Studios. Originally served in an iconic and now very collectable Hawaiian Eye mug.

name: Income Tax Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A Bronx with equal parts rosso and dry vermouths and with Angostura in place of orange bitters.
history: A riff on the Bronx cocktail, the Income Tax cocktail first appeared in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Kava
garnish: Pineapple wedge & skewered Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 shot	Pineapple juice
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: A wonderfully fruity and kitsch Tiki cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe featured in Jeff Berry's 'Intoxica' and originally created circa 1942 by Trader Vic.

name: Millionaire
garnish: Dust with freshly grated nutmeg & optional small orange wedge on rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Raspberry (framboise) sugar syrup
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review:
Delicately sweet with whiskey-laced, zesty citrus, rich berry fruit and a hint of aniseed, is smoothed and rounded by egg white.

Your choice of grenadine or raspberry syrup (my preference) will significantly impact the flavour and colour of your Millionaire.
history: There are numerous cocktails that go by the name Millionaire but this cocktail (based on rye whiskey with curaçao, raspberry syrup/grenadine and egg white, usually with orange bitters &/or absinthe &/or lemon juice) first appears in Jacques Straub's 1914 Manual of Mixed Drinks.

name: Pan American Clipper
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Essentially, a Jack Rose with a couple of dashes of absinthe. (If making this with bonded-strength applejack in place of calvados, then knock back to 50ml.)
history:
This vintage cocktail first appeared in Charles H. Baker's 1939 The Gentleman's Companion in which Baker says the cocktail is "from the notebook of one of our pilot friends–when off duty–may seek one." His friend obviously was a pilot for Pan Am Airlines.

The Pan American Clipper's modern-day popularity is partly due to its being heroed by St. John Frizell at his Fort Defiance bar in Brooklyn, New York City, USA. Our version of this classic by yours truly.

name: Naranja Daiquiri
garnish: ¼ orange wheel slice on rim

1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)

review: An Orange Daiquiri with orange juice notes amplified by cognac orange liqueur.
history: Pronounced 'Na-Rahn-ha' (or thereabouts), Naranja is Spanish for 'orange', both the fruit and the colour.

name: Park Lane
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:

2⁄3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Gin, apricot and orange combine in this easy-drinking frothy topped cocktail.

name: Pink Lady
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Applejack brandy bottled-in-bond (50% alc./vol)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: A generous measure of gin and high-proof applejack provide spirituous spice which, along with lemon juice sourness, ensures that this cocktail is neither sweet nor weak. Indeed, this is a very tasty sour. So tasty, that to spare this Lady's blushes, our friend Ted "Dr Cocktail" Haigh would prefer you refer to it as "The Secret Cocktail".
history: The first known reference to the Pink Lady is in Jacques Straub's 1913 Manual of Mixed Drinks.

name: Playmate Martini
garnish: Orange zest twist and 2 drops of bitter on foamy head (spread with a cocktail stick)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Cognac-laced apricot and orange. Mellow and easy drinking.

name: Appletini (Sour Apple Martini)
garnish: Drop Luxardo Maraschino cherry into cocktail &/or float thin apple slice/dehydrated apple slice
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Sour apple liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄6 shot	Lime cordial (sweetened lime juice)
1⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: This "Martini" is unashamedly fun and brash with lurid green apple liqueur at its 'core'.
history:
Unlike the origins of so many cocktails, the date when this altern'atini was created and by whom is remembered by those involved and has been widely reported. It was the Fourth of July 1996 when Loren "Lola" Dunsworth, owner of Lola's in West Hollywood was encouraged to include a Ketel One signature Martini on her restaurant's cocktail list by a representative from Ketel One Vodka. Boasting one of L.A.'s first extensive Martini menus, Lola's, which sat at 945 N. Fairfax Avenue in West Hollywood, opened in July 1996 and closed 8th August 2013.

Seeing a bottle of DeKuyper Pucker Sour Apple Liqueur on the back bar, Lola asked bartender Adam Karston to make a cocktail with this and Ketel One. He mixed equal parts Ketel One and Pucker liqueur with a splash of house-made sweet-and-sour mix. The result, "Adam's Apple Martini" was an instant hit and under its simplified name, the "Appletini", quickly became hugely popular across North America in the Noughties earning it contemporary classic status and a place in our Cocktail Hall of Fame.

At Lola's, they garnished their Appletinis with slices of Granny Smith apple marinated in iced lemon juice mixed with water to keep fresh. In other bars, the attractive colour contrast and ease of simply dropping a maraschino cherry into the drink led to this becoming the more usual garnish. In recent years, floating a dehydrated apple slice has become popular.

name: Tuxedo Cocktail Original
garnish: Lemon zest twist & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 dash	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: I've tried this recipe with 2 to 3 dashes of Angostura and also orange bitters, but I prefer it with 2 dashes of both aromatic (Angostura) and orange bitters, so honouring Johnson, MacElhone, Mahoney and Grohusko. The result is a very aromatic semi-Dry Martini.
history:
Based on the earliest Tuxedo recipe I'm aware of in Harry Johnson's Bartenders Manual (1900 and later editions). The same recipe, bar the odd dash of bitters, also appears in Jack's Bar Manual by Jacob Abraham Grohusko (1910), Hoffman House Bartender's Guide by Charles Mahoney (1912) and Barflies & Cocktails by Harry MacElhone (1927).

All four of the revered bartenders stipulate equal parts old tom (sweet) gin and French (dry) vermouth with one dash each of maraschino and absinthe, but Grohusko's recipe adds 3 dashes Angostura Bitters; while MacElhone, Mahoney & Johnson call for orange bitters in place of the Angostura.
Also see: Tuxedo cocktail history

name: Vanilla & Grapefruit Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:

1⁄2 shot	Licor 43 Original liqueur

1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
4 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters
review: Reminiscent of a Hemingway Special, this citrusy, vanilla-laced Daiquiri has a tangy bittersweet finish.
history: Created in 2003 by yours truly in London, England.

name: Vanilla Margarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila

2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
4 drop	Bob's Vanilla bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A classic Margarita with a hint of vanilla.
history:
I first drank Vanilla Margaritas in 1998 at London's Café Pacifico and I drank a lot of them. I also drank VDQs (Vanilla Daiquiris) at Teatro on Shaftesbury Avenue - often on the same night. The former (Café Pacifico is an early evening haunt) was made with tequila infused with a vanilla pod while the latter (Teatro was most definitely a place to finish a night) was made with vanilla-infused Havana 3yo rum. And way before that, I drank McDonald's Vanilla shakes and ate vanilla ice-cream. Who doesn't like vanilla?

I used to, and sometimes still do, make my Vanilla Margaritas just the same way as my regular Margaritas, only based on vanilla-infused tequila (Café Pacifico-style) but thanks to a comment by Vincent Dufour on this very page, (on 5th December 2020) I developed this recipe (that's even better when also made with vanilla-infused tequila).

name: Wibble
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin

1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)

review: As Dick Bradsell once said to me, "It may make you wobble, but it won't make you fall down." Dick named this cocktail after the 1970s' Weebles children's roly-poly toys which were advertised with the catchphrase, "Weebles wobble, but they don't fall down."
history: Created in 1999 by Dick Bradsell at The Player, London, England for Nick Blacknell - a conspicuous lover of gin.

name: Zeus Cocktail
preparation: POUR fernet into chilled/frozen glass, swirl round to coat inside and DISCARD excess. MUDDLE raisins with cognac in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into fernet-rinsed glass.
ingredients:
1⁄6 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
24 dried	Raisins
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1⁄4 shot	Maple syrup
1 shot	Chilled water (reduce if wet ice)
review: Rich, pungent and not too sweet.
history: Adapted from Dr Zeus, a cocktail created by Adam Ennis in 2001 at Isola in London, England.

name: Golden Bronx

review: A Bronx made 'golden' by the addition of egg yolk.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide.

name: Blood Sage
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:

2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Blood orange juice
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Sage combines wonderfully with gin and orange in this well-balanced sour.

name: Clara Astié Cocktail
preparation: STIR jam with rum until jam dissolves. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 barspoon	Apricot jam (preserve)
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1 dash	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Tangy apricot with hints of maraschino dried by vermouth and fortified by light rum.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2008 by Ian McLaren of Bacardi. The name is in tribute to Doña Amalia's Godmother whose bequest revived the fortunes of Don Facundo Bacardi Massó allowing him to establish the rum brand we know today.

name: Clover Club
garnish: Express lemon zest twist over cocktail and discard. Float raspberry in centre of drink
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Raspberry (framboise) sugar syrup
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review:
Gin-laced, sweet 'n' sour with a fruity blast of rich raspberry toned by dry vermouth.

Depending on your raspberry syrup, the finished cocktail may range in colour from a shade of pale yellow to a tinge of pink through to pink red (the cocktail above was photographed made with homemade syrup). You may need to vary the measure of syrup from 12.5ml to as much as 20ml (2/3 oz): this is as much dependent on personal taste as your choice of raspberry syrup.
history:
The Clover Club cocktail is eponymously named after a club founded in 1896 by a group of prominent Philadelphia journalists who met regularly at Philadelphia's Bellevue-Stratford Hotel from when it opened in 1904. Over time, the club's membership expanded to include lawyers, bankers and prominent businessmen.

The Clover Club cocktail is ostensibly the same as the Clover Leaf cocktail, and historians trade newly unearthed quotations to argue one predates the other. The earliest recipe for a Clover Leaf (I have found) is in Jacob Abraham Grohusko's 1908 Jack's Manual. This 1908 origin is confirmed by a quote from 8th July 1908 New York Herald, "A party of Philadelphians introduced a new appetizer at the Plaza last evening called a clover leaf cocktail."

The Oxford Companion to Spirits And Cocktails references a 1901 recipe by Michael Killackey, head bartender at the Waldorf-Astoria in New York, published in the New York Press on 21st June 1901, but neither I nor others have been able to find this. [If you can help this newspaper's name, please let me know.]

The Clover Club Cocktail appears in Paul E. Lowe's 1909 book Drinks: how to mix and how to serve but with the lemon juice omitted from the recipe, although this is thought to be a transcription mistake. The cocktail does not feature in Lowe's earlier 1904 Drinks as they are Mixed but a toast from the club does feature in the book.

name: Clover Club (Difford's recipe)

preparation: MUDDLE raspberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5 fresh	Raspberries
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: It's a bit of a faff to make but it's worth the clogged sink drain from the raspberry shrapnel. Using raspberry syrup and especially raspberry jam in a Clover Club introduces cooked "jammy" notes, while this can be delicious (see Julie Reiner's Clover Club), I like to retain and hero fresh berry flavours.
history: My version of a classic .

name: Corpse Reviver No.2 (Contemporary Recipe)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:

history:
A riff on the classic Corpse Reviver No. 2, this was popular with London bartenders during the late noughties.
Corpse Reviver cocktail history

name: Dry Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)

name: Old Cuban

review: A luxurious, minty Daiquiri topped with a splash of fizz.

name: Shark's Tooth (by Don Beach)
preparation: BLEND first 5 ingredients with 4oz scoop of crushed ice and pour into an old-fashioned glass. POUR Jamaican rum into shot glass and serve alongside drink, instructing drinker to pour rum into cocktail prior to sipping (without straw).
ingredients:
1 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)

review: This cocktail should be blended so the ice is dissolved to chill and dilute the drink which should end up with a long-lasting frothy head.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Don Beach in the 1960s.

name: Apple Fool
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5 fresh	Basil leaves
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1 shot	Grapefruit juice (ruby red)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: There's no gold in 'Fool's Gold', a mineral called Iron Pyrite (FeS2) that looks like gold. Similarly, there's no apple in this Apple Fool although its crisp enlivening freshness is reminiscent of a good apple.
history: Adapted from a drink created by Aisha Sharpe in New York City, USA.

name: Four Aces
preparation: MUDDLE grapes in base of shaker. Add next 5 ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda water, stir and serve with straws.
ingredients:
6 fresh	Green grapes (seedless)
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka

1⁄2 shot	Ginger liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
4 fresh	Basil leaves (torn)
review: A summery, light, superbly balanced herbal fruit cocktail.
history: Created in 2009 by Damian Windsor at The Roger Room in Los Angeles, USA. Inspired by Table 8 in Los Angeles.

name: Precursory Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Tawny port

1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
3 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura (optional)
review: The winning cocktail from CLASS magazine Bartender of the Year 2009.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2009 by Tim Philips at Milk & Honey in London, England.

name: Velvet Threesome
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)

1⁄2 shot	Licor 43 Original liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: A trio of brandies with a dash of herbal vanilla, rounded with vermouth.
history: Created in 2010 by yours truly.

name: Melba Cocktail
garnish: Float mint leaf or peg to rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
3⁄4 shot	Swedish Punsch liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄12 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water
review: This would be better named, "Melba Daiquiri", as it is a Swedish punsch, absinthe, and grenadine influenced Daiquiri. I've dramatically changed the equal parts rum and Swedish punsch specified in The Savoy Cocktail Book original, and upped the grenadine, but hopefully for the better.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Sherry Cobbler
garnish: Pineapple wedge, orange slice, mint sprig bouquet & seasonal berry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into a glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
2 shot	Oloroso sherry
1⁄2 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄4 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: This age old cocktail is said to have been the drink for which the waxed paper straw was invented. To quote Harry Johnson, from his 1882 Bartender's Manual, "It is a very refreshing drink for old and young."
history: The origins of this cocktail are unknown but it is one of the oldest classic cocktails dating back to the mid-1800s. For the full history and more about the cobbler, see our Cobblers encyclopedia page.

name: The Gold Rush
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
2⁄3 shot	Ginger liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: The name refers to this sweet 'n' sour, zesty ginger cocktail's golden hue. Bourbon provides the base, while lemon and lime balance the warming, rich ginger liqueur and honey (which replaced sugar syrup in our previous version of this recipe in January 2024).

name: The Matinee
preparation: DRY SHAKE (without ice) all ingredients. SHAKE again with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth

1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
2 leaf	Kaffir lime (fresh fruit)
review: Created in 2010 by Metinee Kongsrivilai at The Bon Vivant, Edinburgh, Scotland.
history: Kaffir lime leaves add zest to this vanilla infused Rum Sour with added vermouth complexity.

name: Mixed Berry Julep
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE berries in base of glass. Add mint, bourbon, cognac, and sugar syrup into glass, add crushed ice and CHURN (stir) with bar spoon. Top up the glass with more crushed ice and CHURN again. Repeat this process until the drink fills the glass and serve.
ingredients:
12 fresh	Mint leaves
2 fresh	Blackberries
3 fresh	Raspberries
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A fruity, minty crowd pleasing Julep.
history:
Created by Dre Masso in Colombia 2009.

The contentious history of the Julep, along with its variants can be found on our page.

name: Christmas Margarita
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & rosemary sprig spiked with cranberries or float a dehydrated orange slice
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

A Christmas cocktail created in October 2011 by yours truly and then revisited in November 2020.

name: Death Flip
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) to emulsify and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	Jägermeisteror other German amaro
1⁄2 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄4 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup (2 sugar to 1 water)
