review: With a whole egg, a shot of tequila, bittersweet liqueur and Chartreuse, this is both a Death Flip and perhaps your last meal, for a while at least. Challenging herbal and bitter complexity yet with endearing sweet creaminess.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2010 by Chris "Hasselhoff" Hysted Hysted-Adams at the Black Pearl in Melbourne, Australia, where it was an immediate hit on the menu, despite its being listed without ingredients and the warning, "You don't wanna meet this cocktail in a dark alley."

name: Green Park
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE basil in base of shaker (just to bruise). Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
6 fresh	Basil leaves
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 dash	Celery bitters
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Lime green in colour under a frothy head, lemon fresh and botanical with gin, basil and a hint of celery.
history: Created in 2011 by Erik Lorincz white head bartender at The American Bar, The Savoy Hotel, London, England.

name: Jack Tar
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Navy rum (54.5% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
review: Characterful rum leads with gin and whiskey playing supporting roles with hints of citrus.
history: Jack is a generic name for all British sailors, derived from Jack Tar in the 18th and 19th centuries. Sailors in those years used high-grade tar in their clothing and hair for waterproofing. The term, "Jack-of-all-trades," described a sailor who could turn his hand to anything, and is widely used today.

name: Tomatini
preparation: MUDDLE tomato in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 fresh	Cherry tomato (fresh) (chopped)
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	White balsamic vinegar
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 pinch	Black pepper
review: A sweet and sour sipper that has to be tried. Delicate and yet assertive, this is an 'out there' recipe!
history: Created by Jimmy Barrat at La Petite Maison Dubai for the 2012 World Class Bartenders' competition.

name: The Heritage
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Anise / aniseed syrup
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Vodka fortifies and supports a well-balanced blend of orange zest, apple, lemon and star anise.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in May 2014 by Danish bartender (and winner of Diageo World Class 2012 Western Europe Final), Hasse Johansen from Apothex Bar. This cocktail was first made to celebrate the birthday of the creator of Ketel One Vodka, Carolus Nolet. If you'd like to make one and toast Carolus, his birthday is on the 15th of May.

name: New Orleans Minute
garnish: Lemon and orange zests (discarded) & three coffee beans floated on drink
preparation: POUR mezcal into chilled glass and swirl to coat. Discard excess mezcal. STIR other ingredients with ice and strain into mezcal rinsed glass.
ingredients:
1⁄4 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1 2⁄3 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
2⁄3 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Perhaps not a Bourbon Street staple but characterful nonetheless with tequila, mezcal, aromatised wine, maraschino and orange bitters.
history: Created by Sune Urth at Ruby bar in Copenhagen and adapted from the original New York Minute created by Luke Whearty at Der Raum bar in Melbourne.

name: Chanbanger
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
2⁄3 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
6 drop	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
review: Hard to classify, a hint of Singapore Sling oriental cherry with some Cuban aged rum Daiquiri and a splash of Papa's grapefruit citrus sourness.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2014 by Barney Chan at The Mayor of Scaredy Cat Town in London, England.

name: Pastry War Margarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄2 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Mezcal, amaro and elderflower liqueur all work together to set this Margarita apart.
history:
Adapted from a recipe discovered at Bastille Cafe & Bar in Seattle, USA.

The Pastry War of 1838–39 between Mexico and France was fought after a French pastry chef living in Tacubaya, near Mexico City, claimed some Mexican army officers had damaged his restaurant. The chef was one of a number of foreign nationals who claimed they'd suffered losses as a result of civil disturbances, and their respective governments had unsuccessfully sought compensation on behalf of their nationals from the Mexican government. The chef's grievances pushed the French to the war in support of his claim for 600,000 pesos and sent a fleet to the Mexican port of Veracruz. After bombarding the fortress of San Juan de Ulúa and occupying the city, thanks to a British-brokered peace, the French secured payment and withdrew their fleet.

Margarita cocktail history

name: Edison's Medicine cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
6 fresh	Basil leaves
1 1⁄2 shot	Cachaça
1⁄2 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Agave syrup
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Cachaça leads with basil and Chartreuse herbal notes, zesty lime and agave richness.
history: Adapted from a 2011 recipe created by Pete Gugni at The Bedford in Chicago, USA.

name: Malecon Cocktail
garnish: float chunk of block ice (or ice cube)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Ruby port
1⁄3 shot	Oloroso sherry
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Best described as a fortified wine rich Daiquiri.
history: Created in 2011 by Erik Lorincz at the American Bar, The Savoy, London, England.

name: Thuir Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Byrrh Grand Quinquina
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
3⁄4 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Perfectly balanced sweet and sour apricot with faint red wine notes.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2015 by Stuart Bale of 69 Colebrooke Row, London during a visit to Thuir in the South of France where Byrrh has been made since the 1870s. When Stuart asked what Thuir was famous for, apart from Byrrh, the locals claimed their apricots were the best in the world. Hence Stuart’s use of Byrrh and crème d’apricot in this cocktail.

name: Copenhagen Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
2⁄3 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Bready notes in the genever combine with the cherry brandy and the lime juice to produce a complex bittersweet, jammy cocktail.
history: In August 2009, Cherry Heering, a liqueur from Copenhagen, challenged local bartenders to create a signature cocktail for their city. This winning recipe was created by Gromit Eduardsen at Bar 1105 in Copenhagen, Denmark.

name: Sunny Disposition cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Boker's bitters
review: Slightly on the bitter side of bittersweet with gentian, jammy apricot and lemon juice over a tequila base.

name: Minty White Lady cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
4 drop	Bob's Peppermint Bitters
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: White crème de menthe and peppermint bitters bring minty freshness to this lady in white.
history:
A minty riff on the classic White Lady created by yours truly in August 2015 at the Cabinet Room in London, England.
White Lady cocktail history

name: The Nooner
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Vanille de Madagascar
1⁄4 shot	Ginger liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Maple syrup
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Charles Joly's original recipe called for Nevan liqueur (sadly no longer made) and fresh ginger. This simplified version has a flavour reminiscent of the original combining 'made for each other flavours' in the shape of bourbon, vanilla, maple syrup, ginger and orange.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2013 by Charles Joly at The Aviary, Chicago, USA.

name: Pinecone
preparation: MUDDLE cloves in base of shaker to crush. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 dried	Clove
1 1⁄2 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1 shot	Mead
1 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Licor 43 Original liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Pine liqueur
review: Honey and pineapple, laced with aromatic pisco and spiced with clove.
history: Created by yours truly at the Cabinet Room in London, England.

name: Je suis l'Amour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Ambrato/ambre/amber vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Ginger liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
4 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: Cognac and cask-aged dry vermouth form the base of this refined cocktail with complex ginger, pink grapefruit, and chocolate notes.
history: Adapted from a drink created by Walter Gosso at The Mad Dog Speakeasy, Turin, Italy.

name: Le Commerçant (The Merchant)
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. TOP with prosecco.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
5⁄6 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
1 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
review: A balance between citrus and berry sweetness forms the heart of this cognac-based cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Mark Velasquez at The Merchant Hotel, Belfast, Northern Ireland.

name: Repose' 1912
preparation: STIR first five ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. Top with champagne.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄6 shot	Balsamic vinegar of Modena
2 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
2 drop	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
Top up with	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Cognac with sharp balsamic notes and hints of chocolate, enlivened with champagne.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Simone Ditadi at Hilton Birmingham Metropole, Birmingham, England.

name: L'Heritage
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 1⁄2 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄3 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Also, try this apéritif-style, bittersweet cocktail served on the rocks.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2015 by Pierre-Marie Bisson at Basement Sate in London, England.

name: El Viajero
garnish: Dust side of glass with coconut dust and garnish with lime zest twist
preparation: THROW all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 1⁄2 shot	Coconut water
1⁄3 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
1⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
4 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: Rum, coconut water and Pedro Ximénez sherry are unusual bedfellows in a cocktail but work well together and are toned by lime juice and chocolate bitters.
history: Originally based on Bacardi Carta Blanca rum, this was the Hungarian Bacardí Legacy 2016 winning cocktail, created by Norbert Schök at the Four Seasons Gresham Palace in Kollázs, Budapest.

name: Empire of Dreams
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
15 whole	Roasted coffee beans
review: A Pineapple Daiquiri with apricot and almond shaken with coffee beans. With good ice and a brisk shake, you'll be surprised how much the coffee beans are broken up, so also impacting this fruity cocktail. (Be sure to have a strainer in your sink when you dump the spoils from your tin.)
history: Australian Bacardí Legacy 2014 winning cocktail created, originally using Bacardi Carta Blanca, by Fred Siggins at The Black Pearl in Melbourne, Australia.

name: Été Anisé
garnish: Dehydrated orange slice, star anise & edible flowers
preparation:
SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. Top with tonic water.

Special ingredient #1: Sour orange mix
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 1⁄6 shot	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 barspoon	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2 barspoon	Peach aperitif liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
history: Adapted from a recipe created for Campari by Jan & Hannah Van Ongevalle in Belgium.

name: Plaza Antigua
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Patrón Añejo tequila
1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄4 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review:
The sweet herbal punch you'll recognise from the classic Vieux Carré but given extra life and fresh vitality by the addition of a shot of tequila (I've halved the usual doses of cognac and bourbon to make way for the tequila).

Plaza Antigua is Spanish for Old Square, while Vieux Carré is in turn French for Old Square hence I first tried using añejo tequila as the sole base spirit, but while good, this drink strayed too far away from what's recognisable as a Vieux Carré.
history: Created in February 2017 by yours truly (Simon Difford) at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Celery Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Rutte Celery Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄12 shot	Celery bitters
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: This aptly named drink is beautifully balanced with delicate celery flavours.
history: A cocktail named the Celery Sour first appears in Tom-Bullock's 1917 book, The Ideal Bartender.

name: The Artist's Muse
garnish: Atomise absinthe over surface of cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Crème de Pêche de Vigne liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Bittersweet and fruity, with complex aromatics from the pisco and strong flavours of gentian liqueur.
history: Created in 2016 by Maggie Eckl at The Dead Rabbit, New York City, USA. The Artist's Muse is named due to its originally being made with Suze gentian, a brand identified with artists and the arts - a bottle of Suze is depicted in a painting by Pablo Picasso.

name: Slow Comfortable Screw Between the Sheets
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Southern USA-style liqueur 40% (e.g. Southern Comfort)
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
3 1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: The rum and cognac combo from Between the Sheets served as part of the Slow Comfortable genre. As with so many of the Slow Comfortable family of cocktails, when made with freshly squeezed orange juice, this is a tasty, fruity and balanced long drink.

name: Glass & Bottle
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
3⁄4 shot	Americano bianco
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 pinch	Salt (sea salt)
review: Sour, dry and fabulously complex with bittersweet herbal gentian notes over a gin base.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2017 by J Lynn at Lyons at Ace Hotel New Orleans, New Orleans, USA, who “wanted to create something more palatable for those new to gentian.” The name comes from the 1912 Picasso collage featuring a bottle of Suze.

name: Suzette au Bal (Suzette at the Ball)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄2 shot	Pear liqueur (Poire William)
1⁄3 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Dry and lightly bitter with a faint mezcal smokiness and delicate rich pear fruit.
history: Created in 2017 by Alexandre Girard at La Queue du Coq, Annecy, France, who told us, "Suzette is the name of French song. It's the story of a guy who falls in love with Suzette; a smart, smooth, incredible young woman. The scene takes place in a local dance in the middle of summer."

name: Back to Basics Cocktail
preparation:
SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

Special ingredient #1: Orange and red wine syrup - cube 1 orange, adding half the peel from a 2nd orange and soak in 300g sugar for up to 1.5 hours. Simmer with 330 ml red wine (Merlot) until the alcohol evaporates (around 10 mins).
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Aquafaba (chickpea water) or Egg white (pasteurised) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Irene Benjamin says of her drink, “Back to Basics is all about the simple things in life, the things that make me happy and keep me motivated through hard and busy times. I tried to capture memories and the people that affected me and made me who I am today - my friends, family and my partner in life. One of the things that really motivates me is the desire to take care of our planet. I put a lot of sustainable thinking into my cocktail, I believe we can all take care of our planet by maximising our products and extending their lifetime. My agenda is to help to create a better world and a greener future.”
history: Israel BACARDÍ LEGACY 2018 winning cocktail by Irene Benjamin, Zalame, Be'er Sheva, Israel.

name: Greenwich Sour
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and strain into ice-filled glass. DRIZZLE red wine around surface of the drink.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
3⁄4 shot	Shiraz red wine
review: A Whiskey Sour smoothed by the addition of egg white and made more visually appealing and interesting by red wine tannins.
history:
Although this egg white enriched Whisky Sour with a New York Sour red wine float was made in other numerous bars, particularly in London, prior to Manhattan's Employees Only opening in 2004, this cocktail is closely associated to EO and almost certainly owes its name to the bar's proximity to New York's Greenwich Villiage district.

A detailed history of the Sours family of cocktails is available on our Sours cocktails page.

name: Velvet Revolver
preparation: STIR strawberry conserve and cognac in base of shaker until conserve is dissolved. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 barspoon	Strawberry jam/preserve/conserve (heaped)
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Pinot Noir red wine
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: As Robb, the creator of this drink, says, it is "short strong and fruity, pulls out all the deeper notes from the cognac."
history: Created by Robb Collins when he was Group Head Bartender at London Cocktail Club, London, England. Developed for Cocktails in The City summer 2017.

name: Corleone
preparation: MUDDLE grapes in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5 fresh	Green grapes (seedless)
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Bepi Tosolini Grappa di Moscato
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Aromatic, floral and surprisingly dry with pleasing grape fruitiness and botanical complexity.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Ryan Magarian at Oven & Shaker, Portland, Oregon. Apparently, Ryan named this cocktail due to his being inspired by the Sicilian countryside.

name: Dynasty Margarita
garnish: Grapefruit salt rim (mix 100g sea salt with 10g grated grapefruit peel, spread over a paper towel and leave to infuse and dry overnight)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass pre-rimmed with grapefruit salt.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄4 shot	Patron Citronge
1⁄4 shot	Elderflower liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Lychee syrup
1⁄6 shot	Ginger syrup
review: Created by Jay Khan and inspired by Hong Kong, the Dynasty Margarita appropriately uses traditional Chinese ingredients of lychee and ginger and combines these with elderflower liqueur to make a distinctive floral Margarita.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Jay Khan in Hong Kong, China for Patrón Tequila's Margarita of the Year competition. This was the winning cocktail!

Jay's original recipe uses homemade lychee & ginger syrup. To make this blend fresh peeled and de-stoned lychees until smooth. Double strain this juice and combine with equal parts of freshly pressed ginger juice. Add equal amount of granulated sugar to the combined weight of lychee and ginger juice and blend until the sugar is completely dissolved.

name: Wild Rose Margarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
5⁄6 shot	Savoia Americano Rosso
1⁄3 shot	Rose sugar syrup
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
review: Bittersweet floral rose and faint gin botanical notes underpin this balanced riff on a classic straight-up Margarita.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Makina Labrecque in Calgary, Canada. Originally made with Patrón Silver tequila and Patrón Citrónge Orange (as the triple sec), this cocktail was the 2019 Patrón Margarita of the Year.

name: Dunkel & Stürmig
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with beer and ginger beer and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 2⁄3 shot	Dunkel / dark / black lager
1 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: Dunkel & Stürmig is German for Dark & Stormy and indeed this ia a tasty coffee and cacao spiced rum riff on the classic Dark 'N' Stormy.
history: Created by Dirk Hany at Bar am Wasser, Zurich, Switzerland.

name: Bird of Paradise Gin Fizz
preparation:
SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and slowly pour 2/3rds of the contents of the shaker from a higher than normal height into a chilled empty glass (no ice in glass) while simultaneously pouring soda with your other hand. The cocktail and soda should form a single stream of liquid falling into the glass.

As when pouring a Guinness, to achieve a perfect head on a fizz, the cocktail should be left to settle for at least a minute before topping off with what remains in the shaker. Ideally, during the settling period, the glass should be placed in a glass froster/fridge/freezer. As the final contents of the shaker are poured into the glass so the head should rise like a souffle.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Raspberry (framboise) sugar syrup
3 drop	Orange blossom water / Orange flower water
2⁄3 shot	Egg white
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A Gin Fizz with pleasing rich raspberry notes, discovered by Charles H. Baker at the Strangers Club in Panama.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Charles H. Baker's 1939 The Gentleman's Companion, a book of travel memoirs and recipes.

name: Three of Strong
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
2⁄3 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
2⁄3 shot	Passion fruit purée
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Cacao and coffee flavours from the rum shine in this fruity and delicately spicy Tiki influenced cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Dinos Constantinides at Lost + Found, Nicosia, Cyprus. Dinos original recipe calls for "Grandpa's Lemonade" made using a Thermomix (which we simplified by instead using with lemon juice and sugar syrup).

name: New York Stone Sour
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice). FLOAT wine on surface of the cocktail.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Claret red wine
review: Sip through dry red tannins to reach the rich apricot and orange fruity bourbon sour beneath.

name: Kingston Club
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass, adding soda as you pour.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Drambuie liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Pineapple juice with herbal attitude. Fernet contributes almost clove-like flavours to this fruity aperitivo cocktail.
history: Purloined from Jeffrey Morgenthaler's 2014 The Bar Book in which he says, "I've always loved working with herbal liqueurs such as Drambuie, and Fernet-Branca makes a solid chunk of their sales from the staff at our restaurant. And behold, the Kingston Club was born."

name: Astral Plane
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass while pouring soda.
ingredients:
1 shot	Dry white port
2⁄3 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A bittersweet, refreshing aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Tyson Buhler at Death & Company, New York City, USA.

name: Morning Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Cognac (brandy)
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄12 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 dash	Boker's bitters
review: A short, sharp and very satisfying bracer to prequal a good meal, or indeed chase such a meal.
history: This cocktail first appears in Harry Johnson's 1900 Bartenders' Manual. It also features in Harry Craddock's 1930 Savoy Cocktail Book where Bokers bitters is replaced with orange bitters. It's worth noting that Harry Johnson's recipe states "3 or 4 dashes of bitters (Boker's genuine only)."

name: Burning Bright
preparation: STIR lime and grapefruit juices with sugar in base of shaker until sugar is dissolved. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1 barspoon	Powdered sugar (white sugar ground in mortar and pestle)
1 2⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄3 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: There are hints of Hemingway Daiquiri to this multi-layered bittersweet and sweet 'n' sour aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Maxim Schulte at The American Bar at The Savoy, London, England.

name: Chicago Fizz
preparation:
Shake the first 5 ingredients with ice and strain back into the shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and slowly pour 2/3rds of the shaker's contents from a higher-than-normal height into a chilled empty glass (no ice in the glass) while simultaneously pouring soda with your other hand. The cocktail and soda should form a single stream of liquid falling into the glass.

As when pouring a Guinness, to achieve a perfect head on a fizz, the cocktail should be left to settle for at least a minute before topping off with what remains in the shaker. Ideally, during the settling period, the glass should be placed in a glass froster/fridge/freezer. As the final contents of the shaker are poured into the glass, the head should rise like a souffle.
ingredients:
1 shot	Dark/black/blackstrap rum
1 shot	Tawny port
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white
1 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Rum character shines, distinguishing this from lesser fizzes.
history: The Chicago Fizz first appears in Jacques Straub's 1914 book Drinks.

name: Downhill Daring
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Americano bianco
1⁄4 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A rich characterful and tasty riff on a Sweet Manhattan.
history: Named after a piece by American painter and illustrator, Norman Rockwell (1894-1978) and adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Brian Nixon at the Truxton Inn in Washington D.C., USA.

name: Frogroni
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with 6oz scoop crushed ice.
ingredients:
3 fresh	Strawberries (hulled, small & ripe)
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
7⁄12 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
7⁄12 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Gin-laced, bittersweet, sweet 'n' sour, and rich strawberry.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2017 by Julie Reiner at Clover Club in Brooklyn, New York City, USA.

name: Honey Cosmopolitan
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Grapefruit flavoured vodka
1 1⁄3 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄3 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
4 drop	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
review: Honey adds delicate flavour and richness to this grapefruit fresh riff on a classic Cosmopolitan.
history: Created in 2020 by yours truly at the Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: Sherry Valance
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Manzanilla sherry
1⁄2 shot	Armagnac brandy
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
3 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Armagnac-laced dry sherry and rich almond with zesty refreshing citrus and a touch of creole bitter complexity.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Robert Weeks, General Manager at The Coldroom bar in Montréal, Canada.

name: Frisky Whiskey Highball
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1 shot	Barenjager Honey liqueur
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 shot	Orange flavoured soda water
review: Rich honeyed Irish whiskey freshened by orange.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Allen Katz at his The Shanty bar in New York City, USA.

name: Mrs Daisy Robinson
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. Top with prosecco.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1⁄2 shot	Pineapple sugar syrup
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
1 2⁄3 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
review: Pisco and pineapple are a match made in heaven and sit at the centre of this prosecco-charged celebratory sour.
history: Created by yours truly in May 2021 for Mrs. Daisy Robinson (then soon to be) and inspired by the gin-based "Mrs. Robinson Cocktail" by Andrew Call, a bartender at Bacchus Bar in Portland, Oregon, USA.

name: Kroton Cup
preparation: THROW all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	O/Purist Tsipouro
1 1⁄2 shot	Shiraz red wine
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄12 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Reminiscent of a Cobbler, I like the connection and balance between the tsipouro and red wine in this recipe with triple sec, maraschino, and Creole biters extenuating as much as flavouring.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Petros Binas at Istioploikos restaurant in Mikrolimano, Pireaus, Greece, this was one of ten winning recipes in the 2021 O/Purist Quest. Petros explains, "Theano Thuria, the ancient Greek philosopher and mathematician who dealt with the harmony of the universe, came from Croton in southern Italy. My cocktail is my attempt to expand its theory into the world of drink. I created a cup which, guided by the O/Purist Tsipouro, brought in harmonious flavours and aromas from the enchanting mountain forests to the sunny plains of the Mediterranean."

name: Around The World
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	O/Purist Tsipouro
1⁄3 shot	Rhum Clément Blanc
1 shot	Pineapple juice
5⁄6 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Tsipouro and falernum shine in this long fruity cocktail with just enough Agricole to make this properly tropical in style.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Solon Liakos at Grappa Vino & Aperitivo in Volos, Greece, this was one of ten winning recipes in the 2021 O/Purist Quest. Solon says, "The inspiration for this cocktail comes from my love for tsipouro and obviously for my love for Tiki cocktails. As the O/Purist Tsipouro combines flavours and aromas, so do Tiki cocktails and I had to find a way to combine these two together as one. Through this combination, we have in our glass the "Around the world" a cocktail that has Greek culture in it but also encapsulates Tiki cocktail culture."

name: Mr Burns
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Speyburn 10yo Speyside single malt
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄6 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: A single malt whisky-based Bobby Burns, and all the more "excellent" for it.
history: We were introduced to the Mr. Burns by Richard Elgar, a fellow Discerning Drinker. Mr Charles Montgomery Burns is a character in The Simpsons television series, who is the wealthy owner of the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant so Homer Simpson's boss. Mr Burns is depicted as being greedy, wicked, and villainous, and the character is famous for his catchphrase expression, "Excellent", muttered slowly in a sinister voice while steepling his fingers.

name: Tia Mia
garnish: Mint sprigs bouquet, spent lime shell & fruit stick
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄4 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
review: This Mai Tai riff is equally good and becomes a Mexican Mai Tai when made with añejo tequila in place of aged rum.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2010 by Ivy Mix in New York City, USA.

name: Wogan
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water
review: Best described as an apricot-flavoured Irish whiskey Daiquiri.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created by Aaron Wall at his Homeboy bar in Islington, London, England. Originally made with Teeling Small Batch Irish whiskey, the Wogan remains one of Homeboy's signature cocktails.

Named after Sir Terry Wogan (1938-2016), the popular BBC television and radio presenter who was considered "a national treasure", originally from Limerick, Ireland.

Aaron Wall says, "What were trying to showcase with this cocktail is that Irish whiskey can sit in an aspect of a grassier rum, this is a formula for an Irish whiskey cocktail:
- 40ml Irish
- 10ml of a liqueur that complements or contrasts a tasting note of the whiskey
- 15ml lime
- 15ml 1:1 sugar
- 3 dashes saline or a pinch of salt to draw flavours together.
That's why in the Wogan we use apricot liqueur to complement the rum finish cask flavour of the Teeling Small Batch."

name: Grand Slam No.2
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice or large cube.)
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: Rum-laced zesty citrus with an appealing hint of subtle cognac richness.
history: In his The Fine Art Of Mixing Drinks, David Embury describes the Grand Slam as a...

name: Eeyore's Requiem
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄4 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1⁄4 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: On the bitter side of bittersweet with cleaning piney and herbal notes from gin, carciofo, and fernet.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created circa 2009 by Toby Maloney at his Violet Hour in Chicago, USA and featured in his 2022 book The Bartender's Manifesto

Originally made with 45ml Campari, 30ml Dolin Blanc Vermouth de Chambery, 15ml Junipero (Navy-strength gin), 7.5ml Cynar, 7.5ml Fernet Branca, and one dash of each Regan's Orange and Angostura Orange bitters.

This cocktail is named after Eeyore in Winnie the Pooh, which Toby is quoted as saying is "the most bitter character in literature" so appropriate for a bittersweet cocktail.

name: Clergyman's Lapse
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄2 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Crème de Pêche de Vigne liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water
review: Reminiscent of a Last Word and inspired by a Missionary's Downfall.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England (Jason's recipe calls for 22.5ml / ¾oz lime juice). Jason says, "the name of this drink is meant to evoke Donn Beach's wonderful Missionary's Downfall, which brings together lime and peach in a tiki context."

name: Improved Pendennis Club Cocktail
garnish: Lime slice or wedge (or apricot) on rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Apricot (abricot) eau-de-vie
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Fruity and sweet 'n' sour with gin-laced stone fruit and lime. If you have a dry/sour palate, and depending on your apricot liqueur and limes, then cut the sugar syrup back to 7.5ml (¼oz) if using 2:1 sugar syrup. (If using 1:1 "simple syrup" then 10ml will produce a dry cocktail.)
history: Adapted from a riff on the classic Pendennis Club Special created in 2013 by Toby Cecchini at his Long Island Bar in Brooklyn, New York City.

name: Mezcal Mule
garnish: Skewered candied ginger and dust with chili flakes
preparation: MUDDLE cucumber in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
4 slice	Cucumber (fresh)
1 1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
3⁄4 shot	Ginger liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Passion fruit purée
1⁄2 shot	Agave syrup
review: Sans ginger bee,r but this mule packs plenty of ginger kick. A sunshine cocktail.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2008 by Jim Meehan at PDT in New York City, USA. Jim's original recipe calls for 30ml (1oz) Ginger Wort syrup in place of liqueur.

To make Ginger Wort syrup
Pour 3 cups of boiling water into a large glass bowl containing 1 cup minced fresh ginger and 40 grams (1.5 ounces) light muscovado sugar. Stir to combine, cover and leave to stand for 90 minutes. Stir in 22.5ml (¾oz) lime juice and then strain, pressing the ginger to extract its juices, bottle and refrigerate. Use within 24 hours.

name: Single Village Fix
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Pineapple sugar syrup
1⁄3 shot	Pineapple juice
3 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: For the above recipe, depending on how ripe your pineapple, you may want/need to add a spoonful of agave syrup. I also like to boost lime and pineapple complexity with a few drops of our Daiquiri Bitters.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2008 by Thad Vogler at his bar Beretta in San Francisco, USA. Originally, comprising just mezcal, pineapple syrup, and lime juice.

name: Widow's Word
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
3⁄4 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
3⁄4 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A mash-up of the Widow's Kiss and Last Word or, as fellow Discerning Drinker, Andrew Gelb pointed out in a comment on our Last Word cocktail page, "a Monte Cassino with the rye replaced by calvados or apple brandy --> Delicious!"
history:
Created by Boston cocktail enthusiast, Eric Witz who shared his equal parts recipe via Instagram in late 2015. A drier, more apple brandy-forward, version was created by cocktail photographer, Chase Hoffman who shared his recipe via Flickr: "1.5 oz unaged apple brandy, 1.0 oz fresh lemon juice. 1.0 oz Yellow Chartreuse, 0.5 oz Bénédictine."

See also Last Word history

name: Brazilian Margarita
preparation: MUDDLE lime and sugar in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into glass filled with cracked (with an ice tapper – not crushed.
ingredients:
1⁄2 fresh	Lime (fresh)
3 barspoon	Powdered sugar (white sugar ground in mortar and pestle)
3⁄4 shot	Cachaça
3⁄4 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
4 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters
review: Brazil's national cocktail (the Caipirinha) meets Mexico's Margarita. The muddling of lime to release oils from the skin is key to the success of this cocktail.
history: Created in March 2023 by yours truly after trying Hugo Carvalho's excellent Brazilian Margarita.

name: Improved Brandy Cocktail
garnish: Express lemon zest twist over surface of the cocktail, rub lemon zest oils on rim, and discard
preparation: POUR first 5 ingredients into shaker. Express oils from lemon zest twist into shaker and discard. Add ice, SHAKE and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄6 shot	Gomme syrup
1⁄12 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2 dash	Boker's bitters
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 twist	Lemon zest oils
review: Yes, yes, I know modern convention calls for this cocktail to be stirred but Jerry Thomas stipulates to shake it and it's much "improved" by shaking. "Shake it to wake it" and brandy shines with the other ingredients, adding complexity rather than challenging its dominance. If you can't bring yourself to shake it, at least throw it!
history: The Brandy Cocktail first appears in Jerry "The Professor" Thomas' 1862 The Bar-Tender's Guide & Bon Vivant's Companion with this "Improved" version debuting in his 1876 The Bar-Tender's Guide 2nd Edition.

name: Calvados Sazerac
garnish: Lemon zest twist expressed & discarded. Garnish with a lemon zest knot
preparation: POUR absinthe into chilled glass and roll glass so as to coat the inside with absinthe. Discard excess and set glass aside. STIR other ingredients with ice and strain into absinthe-rinsed glass.
ingredients:
1⁄12 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 2⁄3 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
history: Adapted from a recipe created in February 2023 by Kaitlin Wilkes for Avallen Calvados.

name: The Project
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1 dash	Peach bitters
review: Huge herbal and fruit flavours combine in this whisky-laced Last Word-like aperitivo/digestive/late-night sipper.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Owen Westman at Bourbon & Branch in San Francisco, USA. For reasons of cost and sobriety, I've halved the quantities from the original cocktail which called for Laphroaig Quarter Cask (for peated whisky) and was served in a coupe.

name: Passion Fruit Mojito
garnish: Mint sprigs bouquet & spoon of fresh passion fruit flesh & seeds. Serve with a straw.
preparation: ADD first 5 ingredients to glass and two-thirds fill with crushed ice. CHURN (stir) with bar spoon and them FILL glass with more crushed ice. TOP with splash of soda, briefly stir and serve.
ingredients:
12 fresh	Mint leaves
1 2⁄3 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Passoã passion fruit liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Passion fruit syrup
1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Fruity, just as the name promises, but this Mojito is balanced rather than sweet.
history: This rendition of a Passion Fruit Mojito is by yours truly in May 2023.

name: Pample Mousse
garnish: Dash with Peychaud's bitters to form lines across the foaming head
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass (no ice). TOP with prosecco.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Monkey Shoulder Fresh Monkey
1 1⁄3 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
1 2⁄3 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
review: A dry and very fresh grapefruit fizz. Best as an aperitivo.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Callum Rixson
Monkey Shoulder Brand Ambassador for the south of the UK.

name: Funky Watermelon
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice. Open shaker, add soda and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Monkey Shoulder Fresh Monkey
1⁄6 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Agave syrup
1 1⁄2 shot	Watermelon juice
1 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Fruity watermelon and funky new-make spirit are harmonious with lime, bittersweet liqueur and agave syrup adding depth of flavour.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Rosie Patton of Dos Dedos in Bath, England.

name: Palladio
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Lanique Spirit of Rose liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
1 dash	Rhubarb bitters
review: A rose-flavoured gin sour made more special by the well-judged addition of rhubarb bitters.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England. Jason's original recipe calls for Briottet Rose liqueur.

Andrea Palladio (1508-1580) was an Italian Renaissance architect regarded as one of the most influential architects in Western architecture.

name: Absinthe Suissesse

1⁄3 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup

1 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer

history: The first known recipe for an absinthe Suissesse appeared in Frank P. Newman's 1904 book American Bar - Recettes des Boissons Anglaises et Américaines.

name: Près du Quai

1⁄3 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: We discovered the use of rum in place of cognac in a Vieux Carré thanks to a comment by Collin Westgate on our Vieux Carré page saying that he'd discovered how good this cocktail is with aged dark Jamaican rum after running out of cognac. This was followed by a comment by Roberto Brazzo saying he also prefers rum and refers to them as a 'Près du Quai', "since we moved away from the Vieux Carré 'old square' to a more nautical 'by the docks' or 'near the wharf'." We thank Collin and Roberto for suggesting such a tasty and appropriately named cocktail.

name: Crystal Ship
garnish: Ice shell and monkey on rim. Serve with a straw.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.

1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Blue Curaçao

1 shot	Pineapple juice

review: Sail through aquamarine waters to a happier place. In the original serve, there's even a monkey perched on the rim along for the ride.
history:
Adapted from a cocktail created by Jeff Berry at his Beachbum Berry's Latitude 29 in New Orleans, USA where the menu describes this cocktail as, "A marriage of smoky mezcal and grassy rhum agricole, blessed by lime, pineapple, orgeat and blue curaçao."

The Crystal Ship is a song from the 1967 American rock band The Door's debut album and was the B-side of their number-one hit single Light My Fire. The track's psychedelic, dreamlike vibe, coupled with the opening lines "Before you slip into unconsciousness, I'd like to have another kiss" have led some to suggest it references a drug trip. Indeed, a 1990 letter to the Los Angeles Times claimed the song was about crystal methamphetamine, with the ship representing a hypodermic needle and the kiss an injection. However, it is a love song composed by Jim Morrison after breaking up with his first serious girlfriend, Mary Werbelow.

name: Ghost of Smokey Joe
garnish: Deliver to guest with verbal garnish, "Hi De Hi De Hi De Ho", ideally as you lift a smoked choche dome covering this cocktail.
preparation: STIR first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. FLOAT peated whisky.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄12 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
review: Herbal notes shine, fortified with rye whiskey with character provided by absinthe, aromatic bitters and particularly peated whisky.
history:
A Halloween-appropriate riff on the classic Minnie the Moocher cocktail, created by fellow Discerning Drinker, John Champion and shared via a comment on our Minnie the Moocher recipe page.

The Ghost of Smokey Joe was one of Cab Calloway's follow up songs to his Jazz Age classic, Minnie the Moocher, performed in the 1930s at the famous Cotton Club. The lyrics, sung in the first-person by the ghost of Smokey Joe who "just climb right through the wall" to spook his fellow "cokies" (users of cocaine) bragging about his "A zillion dollar coffin" and his surprise to learn that Minnie the Moocher had "Quit kickin' the gong around" (kicked her opium habit).

name: Blackthorn No. 5
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Sloeberry fruit and gin form the backbone of this aperitivo/digestivo, which is freshened by a splash of lemon juice and opened by being shaken. (Other versions of the Blackthorne tend to be stirred.)
history: William "Cocktail Bill" Boothby features a version of this cocktail in his 1908 World's Drinks And How To Mix Them. By the 1930 Swallows edition of his book, Boothby adds three numbered variations to the original Blackthorn recipe, but this fifth version doesn't appear until the posthumously published 1934 edition.

name: Tequila Daisy
garnish: Half orange slice wheel on rim
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Orange curaçao and grenadine harmoniously balance lemon juice in this tequila-based Daisy.
history:
Recipe created in October 2023 by yours truly, based on historical recipes.

Daisy is the generic name of a family of cocktails which dates back to Victorian times. Such cocktails are made with citrus juice, sweetened with syrup or a liqueur, and fortified with a base spirit – in this case tequila. It's perhaps no coincidence that Margarita is the Spanish word for 'daisy' and that a Margarita cocktail is basically a Tequila Daisy

The first published recipe for a Daisy appears in Jerry Thomas' 1876 second edition of his Bar-Tender's Guide. He list the recipe for a Brandy Daisy in full followed by recipes for a Whisky Daisy, Gin Daisy and Rum Daisy with the base spirit substituted accordingly. That first Daisy recipe mixes the spirit (brandy) with gum syrup, orange cordial (liqueur) and lemon juice in an iced shaker strained into a glass then topped with seltzer water from a syphon. By 1910, both editions of Jacob Abraham's Jack's Bar Manual published that year boast numerous Daisy recipes with raspberry syrup relacing gum syrup.

Tequila was little known outside of Mexico but that changed as Prohibition led to tequila being smuggled into the US and so into the Daisy. The first specific mention of a Tequila Daisy appears in the Moville Mail newspaper on 23rd July 1936 (pg. 4, cols. 1-3) in a piece titled "Graham's Sightseeing". James Graham was the newspaper's editor and owner and in the piece, he recounts his visit to Tijuana and Augua [sic] Caliente, Mexico.

name: Turnpike

ingredients:

1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄6 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: This recipe is a third of the volume of the original, with the optional additional water only compensating for my use of rich 2:1 sugar syrup (in place of simple syrup).
history:
Adapted from a recipe created circa 2007 by Joseph Schwartz at Milk & Honey in New York City.

Joseph's original recipe called for Old Overholt Rye Whiskey from Pennsylvania and Laird's Applejack from New Jersey, so appropriately, this cocktail is named after the New Jersey Turnpike (I-95) connecting these two states with New York.

name: Harvest Sour

1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)

name: Ocean Shore

history: A vintage cocktail brought to our attention by Jason E. Clapham and first published in William Boothby's 1934 The World's Drinks and How to Mix Them.

name: Lost Souls
garnish: Orange juice & shaved dark chocolate rim

6 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: Mezcal and beet juice sit well together in this delicious riff on a Straight-up Margarita.
history: Adapted from a cocktail originally made with Lost Explorer Espadín Mezcal and promoted by the brand.

name: Blood Orange Daiquiri
garnish: Orange zest twist expressed and discarded. Adorn with blood orange wedge or dehydrated blood orange slice wheel.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)

1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)

2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Blood orange adds a delightful citrus fruitiness to this Daiquiri.
history: Recipe by yours truly in June 2024.

name: Private Island
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)

3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)

1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur

review: Delicate grassy agricole rum and apricot brandy dance in this beautifully balanced, Tiki-style cocktail.
history: Created late-2023/early 2024 by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Ewards MCR, Oxford, England.

name: Oaxacanite
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients, including grapefruit zest (Regal Shake), with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila

history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2012-14 by Ben Long when head bartender at the John Dory Oyster Bar in Manhattan, New York City. Named after Oaxaca, the Mexican state most identified with mezcal production, this cocktail was featured in Georgette Morger-Petraske's 2016 book .

name: Ruby Diamond
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Spirit-forward, bittersweet and sweet 'n' sour, this mezcal and gin sour is best enjoyed as an aperitivo or digestivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created 2015 by Matt Duckor, New York, USA.

name: Ancestor
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Blended Scotch whisky

1⁄2 shot	Ginger wine
1⁄2 shot	Maple syrup
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Looking at the recipe, with liqueur and a whopping 15ml (½oz) of maple syrup, I thought it would be overly sweet. However, as you'd expect from a Satan's Whiskers cocktail, it's beautifully balanced and refreshing and harnesses Scotch whisky's affinity for pear, ginger, and lemon.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Ollie Sagerström Blom at Satan's Whiskers in Bethnal Green, London, England.

name: Empire State of Mind

1 1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
3⁄4 shot	Meletti amaro
1 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A delicately bittered apple sour.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Joe Stinchcomb at Saint Leo in Oxford, Mississippi, USA.

1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)

review: Just as it says on the tin, an agricole rhum-based Cosmopolitan.

name: Alexander The Great

1⁄4 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: A tasty combination of coffee, chocolate and cream, laced with vodka.

name: Apple Cart

name: Apples 'n' Pears

name: Bahamas Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

3⁄4 shot	Coconut rum liqueur (35-40% alc./vol.)
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Totally tropical with a sweet tangy edge.
history: Adapted from the Bahamas Martini created in 2002 by Yannick Miseriaux at the Fifth Floor Bar, Harvey Nichols, London, England.

name: Bling! Bling!
preparation: MUDDLE raspberries in base of shaker. Add vodka, lime and sugar, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into glass. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
7 fresh	Raspberries
1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: An ostentatious little number.
history: Created in 2001 by Phillip Jeffrey at the GE Club, London, England.

name: Blood Orange Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 1⁄3 shot	Blood orange juice
1⁄6 shot	Disaronno amaretto (optional)
review: Fresh blood orange with a subtle gin backbone, bittersweet herbal notes and vermouth complexity.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2008 by Jeffrey Morgenthaler at Bel Ami Lounge in Oregon, USA. The optional addition of a barspoon (5ml) amaretto is thanks to a suggestion by Tibor Szentirmai, a fellow Discerning Drinker.

name: Bronx
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura (optional)
review:
A fairly dry, complex cocktail. Generous sweet vermouth and orange juice make the Bronx less bitter and fruitier than many of its era, but still challenging to delicate modern palates. A classic that needs a trio of something extras to give it zing;
1. Freshly squeezed orange juice
2. Orange bitters
3. Orange zest twist
history: Bronx history and variations

name: Cable Car
garnish: Orange juice, cinnamon & sugar powder rim (1 teaspoon cinnamon powder to ½ cup sugar). Coin-sized orange zest twist expressed and floated.
preparation: DRY SHAKE all ingredients (without ice) to emulsify. SHAKE again with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Chairman's Reserve Spiced Rum
3⁄4 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: A spiced-rum-based riff on a Sidecar. Vanilla and spice from the rum interact with the orange liqueur in this citrusy sour cocktail.
history:
Created in 1996 by Tony Abou-Ganim at the Starlight Room, a nightclub and cocktail lounge atop San Francisco's Sir Francis Drake Hotel (now the Beacon Grand Hotel). The Nob Hill cable cars pass by the bar, hence its catchphrase, "between the stars and the cable cars," and this contemporary classic cocktail's name.

Some say that Cory Reistad created the Cable Car, but Tony says of such claims, "Cory Reistad did indeed work at the Starlight Room with me although not as a member of the opening team. All the menus were created by myself and yes other bartenders were encouraged to participate but the Cable Car was one of my creations which did indeed go on the menu and was created in 1996."

Tony's original 1996 recipe: 1½ oz Captain Morgan Spiced Rum, ¾ oz Marie Brizard orange curaçao and 1½ oz fresh lemon sour mix (which is made with 2 parts freshly squeezed, filtered lemon juice with 1 part simple syrup).

name: Cachaça Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cachaça
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)

4 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters
review: Might not look like a Caipirinha but tastes like a Caipirinha - a very sophisticated refined Caipirinha.

name: Chiclet Daiquiri
garnish: Banana chunk or dried banana chip
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with 6oz scoop of crushed ice and serve in a chilled glass.

1⁄3 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe

review: A wonderfully refreshing drink on a summer's day with surprisingly subtle flavours.

name: Cox's Daiquiri

preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

2 shot	Vanilla rum/vanilla-infused light rum
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄6 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
3 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters (optional)

history: One of two cocktails with which I won Havana Club's The Best Daiquiri in London Competition back in 2002. It is named after Jennings Cox, the American mining engineer credited with first creating the Daiquiri.

name: Dark Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Navy rum (54.5% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)

review: The fine, sweet and sour balance of a great Daiquiri with hints of molasses.

name: Delmonico Special
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A very wet gin martini dried with a splash of cognac and two dashes of bitters.
history: Also known as Delmonico No. 1, Cocktail historian, David Wondrich, says it's probable this cocktail originated soon after the Delmonico restaurant near Madison Square opened in 1876. In his 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks, David Embury describes a Delmonico Special as "merely a Medium Martini with 1 teaspoon of brandy to each drink and a twist of orange peel."

name: East India No.1
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄6 shot	Red curaçao liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Raspberry (framboise) sugar syrup
1⁄12 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review:
A splash of floral red curaçao, raspberry syrup and the merest touch of maraschino delicately flavour and slightly sweeten this spirit-forward, brandy-based cocktail.

Beware making this cocktail with more widely available orange curaçao rather than red curaçao as this produces a very different tasting and looking cocktail.
history:
Named after the East India Company, this recipe is adapted from the earliest known reference to an East India cocktail in Harry Johnson's 1882 Bartender's Manual which stipulates the use of red curaçao rather than the now more commonplace clear or blue curaçao.

This recipe, including the use of red curaçao, is repeated in O.H. Byron's 1884 The Modern Bartender's Guide, and in the 1900 updated edition Johnson's Bartender's Manual, where he specifies "putting in a cherry or medium-sized olive" in addition to the lemon zest twist. Tellingly, he also adds, "This drink is a great favourite with the English living in the different parts of East India."

The East India doesn't appear in any notable cocktail books published after 1900 until Johnson's 1882 recipe appears almost verbatim in Thomas Stuart's 1904 Stuart's Fancy Drinks and How to Mix Them and then again in Tom Bullock's 1917 The Ideal Bartender.

The East India survives pretty much unchanged from Harry Johnson's 1882 recipe until the 1920s when the East India No.2 emerges.

name: Easter cocktail
garnish: Dust with chocolate powder &/or crumbled Cadbury's Flake bar, & mini chocolate eggs in orange zest nest on rim.
preparation: MUDDLE cardamom pods in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3 whole	Green cardamom pods
1 2⁄3 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
1 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Chocolate cocktail with extra interest thanks to vanilla and cardamom.
history: Created in 2003 by Simon King at MJU Bar, Millennium Hotel, London, England. The egg white was our addition to Simon's recipe - it seemed appropriate to add egg given this is an Easter cocktail. We also added the orange zest nest of chocolate eggs.

name: Eclipse
preparation: MUDDLE raspberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into glass filled with crushed ice. Serve with straws.
ingredients:
12 fresh	Raspberries
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
review: A fruity summer cooler which I challenge anyone not to like.
history: Signature cocktail at the chain of Eclipse Bars, London, England.

name: Elegante Margarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lime cordial (sweetened lime juice)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: One of the best Margarita recipes around. Richly endowed with flavour.
history: Created in 1999 by Robert Plotkin and Raymon Flores of BarMedia, USA.

name: Elle for Leather
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 shot	Giffard Vanille de Madagascar
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
Top up with	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: A long, cooling champagne cocktail pepped up with scotch whisky, smoothed with vanilla liqueur. Easy drinking - yet adult.
history: Created in 2001 by Reece Clark at Hush Up, London, England.

name: French Mojito
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE mint in base of glass (just to bruise). Add other ingredients. Half-fill glass with crushed ice and CHURN (stir) with bar spoon. Continue to add crushed ice and churn until drink is level with glass rim.
ingredients:
12 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A classic Mojito with a hint of berry fruit flavour and colour
history: For more recipes, its origins and history, see the Mojito Cocktail.

name: Grape Escape
preparation: MUDDLE grapes and mint in base of shaker. Add cognac and sugar, SHAKE with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. TOP with champagne, stir and serve with straws.
ingredients:
8 fresh	Green grapes (seedless)
5 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
Top up with	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: A cracking drink - subtle and refreshing.
history: Created in 2000 by Brian Lucas and Max Warner at Long Bar at The Sanderson, London, England.

name: Hanky Panky Cocktail
garnish: Orange zest twist (go easy - orange oils add unwanted bitterness if overdone)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄12 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
1⁄24 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed) (optional)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water) (optional)
review: This is basically a Sweet Martini influenced by the addition of bittersweet and aromatic fernet liqueur.
history:
Created in the early 1900s by Ada "Coley" Coleman at The Savoy's American Bar, London, for actor Sir Charles Hawtrey (1858–1923).

Recipe adapted from Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Harvard
preparation: STIR first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. TOP with a splash of soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄12 shot	Gomme syrup
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Old-school, but approachably so. Dry and herbal. A great apéritif.
history:
This recipe is faithful to the first known reference to this cocktail in George J. Kappeler's 1895 Modern American Drinks – How to Mix and Serve All Kinds of Cups and Drinks.

In his 1931 book Old Waldorf Bar Days, Albert Stevens Crockett notes of this drink, "Named after a school for young men, whose site is contiguous to the Charles River, in a suburb of Boston. Alumni who drunk it sometimes lost the 'Harvard accent'."

name: Havanatheone
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
10 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: A flavoursome Daiquiri featuring honey, apple and mint.
history: Adapted from a recipe discovered in 2003 at Hush in London, England.

name: Honey Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
2⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water
review: Rich flavoursome honey replaces sugar syrup in this natural Daiquiri. Try experimenting with different kinds of honey. We favour orange blossom honey.
history: Recipe by yours truly.

name: Irish Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1⁄24 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄24 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 dash	Boker's bitters
review: Stir well and strain into an icy cold glass and this subtly flavoured whiskey cocktail is a delicious way to chase a good evening.
history: Adapted from Harry Johnson's 1900 Bartenders' Manual.

name: Japanese Pear
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄3 shot	Poire William eau-de-vie
1 1⁄2 shot	Akashi-Tai Daiginjo Genshu sake
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Originally made with Poire William liqueur, hence this version calls for a little sugar. We've also taken the liberty of adding a dash of Peychaud's Bitters for added complexity and the merest salmon-pink tint of colour.
