history: Adapted in 2002 from a recipe originating at Grand Pacific Blue Room, Sydney, Australia.

name: Lemonhead
preparation: MUDDLE lemongrass in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 inch	Lemongrass stem (chopped)
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Delicately lemony and vodka-laced.
history: Created in 2006 by yours truly. This was originally a Lemon Martini; every cocktail was named "Martini" back then.

name: Lemongrass Cosmo
preparation: MUDDLE lemongrass in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 inch	Lemongrass stem
1 shot	Ketel One Citroen Vodka
1 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 1⁄2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Lemongrass adds complexity to this balanced Cosmo.
history:
Adapted from a cocktail discovered in 2005 at Opia in Hong Kong.
Cosmopolitan history and recipe variations

name: Lucky Lily Margarita
garnish: Pineapple wedge dusted with pepper on rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 shot	Pineapple juice
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
5 grind	Black pepper
review: Spicy tequila and pineapple tingle with balance and flavour.
history: Adapted from a honeyed pineapple and pepper riff on a classic Margarita discovered in 2006 at All Star Lanes, London, England.

name: Mai Tai (Trader Vic's)
garnish: Half lime shell, mint sprig and fruit stick (skewered pineapple cubes and Luxardo Maraschino cherry)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A Mai Tai is basically a Daiquiri based on aged rum, with orange curaçao liqueur and orgeat syrup contributing to its flavour and sweetness. Trader Vic's Mai Tai is the undisputed king of Tiki cocktails and one of the most enduring of all vintage cocktails. However, like most classics, there's controversy over its origin, while poor renditions have sadly tarnished its reputation.
history:
In 1934, Victor Jules Bergeron, or Trader Vic as he became known, opened his first restaurant in Oakland, California. He served Polynesian food with a mix of Chinese, French and American dishes cooked in wood-fired ovens. But he is best known for the rum-based cocktails he created, particularly for the Mai Tai.

The story goes that one evening in 1944, he tested a new cocktail on two friends from Tahiti, Ham and Carrie Guild. After the first sip, Carrie is said to have exclaimed, "mai tai-roa aé", which in Tahitian means 'out of this world - the best!'. Thus, Bergeron created and named the Mai Tai cocktail.

Others, particularly Ernest Raymond Beaumont-Gantt, then owner of a Hollywood bar called Don the Beachcomber's, have also laid claim to the creation of this drink. But as Vic says in his Bartender's Guide, "Anybody who says I didn't create this drink is a dirty stinker." Indeed, due to the controversy surrounding the origin, he says rather more in his 1972 Trader Vic's Bartender's Guide Revised Edition:

name: Toronto Cocktail
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 3⁄4 shot	Canadian blended whisky
1⁄4 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Maple syrup
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Originally with a dash of sugar syrup but, thanks to a comment by Yacha Han on Difford's Guide, presented here with maple syrup as a more appropriate sweetener. Whether you use sugar or maple syrup, both tame and amplify the flavour of the whiskey, but maple syrup contributes so much more. However, it's Fernet that dominates this Manhattan-style cocktail.
history: A previously forgotten classic resurrected in 2006 by Jamie Boudreau, Seattle, USA. The Toronto appears in David A. Embury's 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks but its earliest written incarnation is as the "Fernet Cocktail" in Robert Vermeire's 1922 Cocktails - How to Mix Them.

name: Mexico City
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A hint of flavoursome cranberry gives this tasty margarita a light pink hue.
history: Adapted from a cocktail discovered in 2002 at the Merc Bar in New York City, USA.

name: Livorno Sour
garnish: Lemon zest twist expressed & discarded. Adorn with a Luxardo Maraschino cherry dropped into cocktail.
preparation: DRY SHAKE all ingredients (without ice) to emulsify. SHAKE again with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
3⁄4 shot	Galliano L'Autentico liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Delicate anise and peppermint with citrus freshness. Old Tom gin fortifies and adds piney juniper while amplifying pleasing liquorice notes. A cleansing aperitivo.
history: Created in 2006 by yours truly and originally served on-the-rocks, but revisited and reformulated in 2023 as straight-up serve.

name: Pago Pago Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Pineapple juice
review: A Pineapple Daiquiri with two liqueurs giving a herbal chocolate influence.
history: Adapted from Jeff Berry's Beachbum Berry Remixed, and, according to Jeff, originally from a 1940 book called The How and When by Hyman Gale and Gerald F. Marco (although it doesn't appear under this name in our 1945 Third Revised Edition of the book).

name: Pineapple & Sage Margarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5 fresh	Sage leaves
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Agave syrup
review: Herbal tequila and sweet pineapple in harmony.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2005 at Green & Red Bar London, England.

name: El Mediterraneo
garnish: Drip 5 drops of olive oil on top
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. (There's no need to muddle basil if good ice and shake are used.)
ingredients:
3 fresh	Basil leaves
1 2⁄3 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
1⁄3 shot	Kleos Mastiha liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
history: Lebanese Bacardí Legacy 2015 winning cocktail by Jad Ballout, Bar Manager at Central Station Boutique Bar in Beirut, Lebanon.

name: Pisco Punch (Micheli's recipe)
preparation: MUDDLE orange and pineapple in base of shaker. ADD pisco and pineapple marinade. SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with no more than two shots of soda water.
ingredients:
2 slice	Orange (fresh)
3 fresh	Marinated pineapple wedges
2 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
3⁄4 shot	Pineapple marinade syrup
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: This Pisco Punch is very fruity and slightly on the sweet side but is so tasty that it justifies its legendary reputation.
history:
Alfredo Micheli (who went by the nickname Mike) was employed at the Bank Exchange and spied on Duncan Nichol to learn how to make this legendary drink. After he believed he'd learnt the secret he left to start serving at a newly opened competitor to the Bank Exchange, Paoli's on Montgomery Street.

Our Pisco Punch cocktail page gives a more detailed history of this drink and explains the different recipes.

name: Reggae Rum Punch
garnish: Pineapple wedge, Luxardo maraschino cherry & mint sprigs bouquet
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	White overproof rum
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1 1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Strawberry sugar syrup
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Jamaicans have a sweet tooth and love their rum. This drink combines sweetness, potent rum, and generous fruit.
history: The most popular punch in Jamaica, where it is sold under different names with slightly varying ingredients. It always contains orange, pineapple and most importantly, overproof rum.

name: Royal Smile
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: This balanced sweet and sour cocktail could put a smile on anyone's face. Unless that is, "one is not amused!" Calvados notes shine through.
history: Adapted from a recipe in David A. Embury's 1948 seminal book, The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks.

name: R U Bobby Moore?
garnish: Apple wedge or float apple slice (preferably dehydrated)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
5⁄6 shot	Bison grass vodka
2⁄3 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
5⁄6 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: It's common to pair Scotch whisky with apple, and Bison Grass vodka with apple juice, but combining these three with acidic wine and rich honey adds sweet 'n' sour complexity.
history:
Created in 2002 by yours truly and named after the rhyming slang for are you bloody sure? However, the Dictionary of Rhyming Slang claims 'bobby moore' means "door". Well, not in South London it bloody doesn't! And I'm bobby moore of it!

Just in case you're unenlightened, during the 1960s, Robert Frederick Chelsea "Bobby" Moore OBE (1941-1993) was the England football team captain, a national hero, and West Ham United defender.

name: Tequila Sour
preparation: DRY SHAKE (without ice). SHAKE again with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. (Or strain into an ice-filled old-fashioned glass.)
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Agave syrup
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
4 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters (optional)
review: A Margarita without orange liqueur (e.g. a Tommy's Margarita) is not a "margarita" at all but a tequila sour. The triple sec orange liqueur is one of the things that define the margarita (which sits within the Daisy cocktail family). The Tequila Sour may lack the ring of a Margarita, but it is a very tasty cocktail nonetheless.

name: Tipperary No.2
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE mint in base in stirring glass (just to bruise). Add other ingredients, STIR with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
7 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: Gin-laced and Martini-like with subtle mint and orange.
history:
This drink first appears (alongside Tipperary No.1) in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book where he stipulates to "Shake well" However, in his later, The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks, David Embury uses little less vermouth and instructs to "stir with cracked ice".

Shaking seems to amplify the bitter notes in the mint so I prefer to follow Embury's stirring method while leaning more towards Craddock's more generous vermouth proportions.

name: Tropical Caipirinha
garnish: Stirrer (spoon, wooden lolly stick or stick cut from sugar cane)
preparation:
1. Cut lime in half (from pole to pole) and then slice one of the halves into eight 3-4mm thick half-moon shaped segments and drop into the base of a robust rocks glass.

2. Add 3 bar spoons caster sugar (or ½oz/15ml sugar syrup 2:1) and MUDDLE.

3. When sure fruit juice is fully extracted and the sugar dissolved, transfer the muddled fruit and sugar into serving glass (preferably a 30cl / 10oz hi-ball glass).

4 POUR cachaça (stored in the freezer), coconut liqueur and pineapple juice (also chilled) into the shaker base or glass used to muddle and swirl to rinse before pouring into serving glass. STIR to ensure all ingredients are well mixed.

5. Use an Ice Tapper to crack (rather than crush) four to five large ice cubes and drop into serving glass. STIR before topping with more ice and serve with a stirrer (but no straws).
ingredients:
1⁄2 fresh	Lime (fresh) (chopped)
3 barspoon	Powdered sugar (white sugar ground in mortar and pestle)
1 1⁄2 shot	Cachaça (from freezer)
1⁄2 shot	Coconut rum liqueur (35-40% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Pineapple juice
review: In drink circles, tropical usually spells sweet. This drink has a tropical flavour but a definite adult sourness.
history:
Created in 2003 by yours truly.
Caipirinha cocktail history and variations

name: Verdant Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Bison grass vodka
1 1⁄3 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: What this cocktail lacks in verdant colour is made up by its grassy green favour.
history: Created in 2003 by yours truly.

name: Waltzing Matilda
preparation: Cut passion fruit in half and scoop out flesh into shaker. Add next 3 ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain (fine strain if you don't want passion fruit seeds in drink) into ice-filled glass. TOP with ginger ale.
ingredients:
1 fresh	Passion fruit (fresh)
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
1⁄6 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
review: Passion fruit, gin, wine and ginger ale all combine well in this fruity, yet dry, refreshing drink.
history: Adapted from a recipe from David Embury's 1948 book, The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks.

name: Fancy Brandy
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄6 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Gomme syrup
1⁄6 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
1 dash	Boker's bitters
review: This appropriately named brandy-based cocktail benefits from dilution, hence my addition of a splash of water. Modern bartending convention might lead you to stir rather than shake this cocktail, which would be a shame, as it's better shaken!
history: Adapted from a recipe by Charles Schumann, Munich, Germany, and published in his American Bar. Very similar to Jerry Thomas' Fancy Brandy Cocktail, published in the 1862 edition of his The Bar-tenders Guide.

name: Anejo Highball
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass charged with half ginger beer. TOP with rest of ginger beer.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: Orange and rum with a hint of ginger spice. Long and thirst-quenching.
history:
The Añijo Highball was created in the late 1990s by Dale DeGroff at The Rainbow Room, New York City, USA.
Highball cocktail history

name: Batida Rosa
preparation: POUR soda water into ice-filled glass. SHAKE other ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled and soda-charged glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
1 1⁄2 shot	Cachaça
3⁄4 shot	Pineapple juice
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: Fruity and tropical. A tall refreshing drink for a hot evening or an afternoon beside the pool.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2008 by Jeffrey Morgenthaler at Bel Ami Lounge, Oregon, USA.

name: Biggles Aviation
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Ginger liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄24 shot	Crème de violette liqueur
review: A ginger-influenced Aviation named after the fictional book Biggles in Borneo about WWII flying heroes Ginger, Algy, and Biggles. Originally inspired by the ginger used in Canton Ginger liqueur being sourced from Borneo.
history: A riff on the classic Aviation created in 2008 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England

name: Brandy Daisy
preparation: STIR first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. TOP with a splash of soda and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Soda from siphon
review: Chartreuse notes show strongly in this short refreshing cocktail, with cognac providing the base and lemon juice contributing to freshening citrus balance.
history: The Brandy Daisy appears in Jerry Thomas' 2nd edition of his Bar-Tender's Guide (1887) and then the 2nd edition of Harry Johnson's Bartenders Manual (1888). Tellingly, both bartenders omit the Brandy Daisy, and indeed Daisies in general from their first editions. We prefer Johnson's recipe.

name: Angels' Advocate
garnish: Orange zest twist (cut to be cross-shaped)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄6 shot	Warninks Advocaat liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Bob's Cardamom bitters
review: Advocaat, gin, and lemon juice harmoniously combine in this pale yellow cocktail. Vanilla syrup adds balance, and cardamom enlivens the blend.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Tess Posthumus, Amsterdam, The Netherlands.

name: Cornwall Negroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A Negroni-style cocktail served up. Heavy on the gin and relatively light on bitter liqueur and vermouth. It's a formula that works but like us, you may prefer yours served on the rocks.
history: Created in 2006 by Philip Ward, New York, USA after attending Gary "gaz" Regan's Cocktails in the Country workshop in Cornwall-on-Hudson.

name: Daiquiri Noir
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE mint in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
7 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Drambuie liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Drambuie adds herbal consistency to this minty fresh aged rum Daiquiri.
history: Discovered in 2008 at Hugos Bar Pizza, Sydney, Australia.

name: La Dolce Vita
preparation: MUDDLE grapes in base of shaker. Add vodka, honey and bitters, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with prosecco.
ingredients:
4 fresh	Green grapes (seedless)
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 barspoon	Honey
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
Top up with	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
review: Complex, yet easy to quaff, with a touch of fizz adding some sparkle.
history: Created in 2002 by Tony Conigliaro at Isola, London, England

name: Eighteen '97
preparation: MUDDLE kumquats in base of shaker. Add next three ingredients, shake and fine strain into a chilled glass. FLOAT wine.
ingredients:
5 fresh	Kumquats (chopped)
1 1⁄2 shot	Bepi Tosolini Grappa di Moscato
1 1⁄4 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄4 shot	Merlot red wine
review: Looks great and, with the citrus freshness of kumquat combined with the oily character of grappa, it also tastes great.
history: Created in 2008 by Raffaello Dante at Salvatore's at FIFTY, London, England.

name: Four Leaf Clover
preparation: MUDDLE clove in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 dried	Clove
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
3⁄4 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: Originally based on vodka but seemed a shame not to try it as a Daiquiri.
history: Created in 2008 by Denis Broci at Maze bar & Restaurant, London, England.

name: Ideal
garnish: Serve with almonds on the side
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
review: On the dry, tart side of bittersweet with hints of freshening zesty grapefruit and dry gin botanicals which cut through heavier vermouth notes. The maraschino is subtle but key.
history: The first known appearance of this classic cocktail is in Hugo R. Ensslin's 1917 Recipes for Mixed Drinks (2nd Edition) (It may have also appeared in his 1916 first edition.)

name: Matador Margarita (Tommy's Style)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Agave syrup
1 shot	Pineapple juice
4 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters
review: A Pineapple Margarita with agave syrup in place of a sweet liqueur.

name: Metropole
garnish: Orange zest twist expressed & discarded. Adorn with Skewered Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄12 shot	Gomme syrup
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A Cognac Manhattan mellowed by a dash of sugar.
history: The Metropole first appears in George J. Kappeler's 1895 Modern American Drinks and was the signature cocktail of the Hotel Metropole, located just off Times Square at Broadway and 42nd Street. It is a subtle adaptation of the 1884 Metropolitan Cocktail.

name: Prestige
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 3⁄4 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Aged rum, pineapple and lime with delicate but enlivening clove spice.
history: Created in 2002 by Dale DeGroff, New York City, USA.

name: Ranglum
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Dark/black/blackstrap rum
1⁄2 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	White overproof rum
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Estery rum with zesty lime and sweet clove spice. A Tiki-style cocktail for a full-on sunny afternoon or to lift a dull winter's day.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2006 by Gonçalo de Sousa Monteiro at Victoria Bar, Berlin, Germany. Gonçalo created this drink whilst listening to Ernest Langlin, so he used a combination of the guitarist's surname and falernum to name his new libation.

name: Daisy Cutter Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3 fresh	Mint leaves
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
5⁄6 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
review: Floral, minty and herbal with a dry finish.
history: Created in 2006 by yours truly. Named not for the bomb but after the English cricketing term for a ball bowled so incompetently that it skims along the ground.

name: Peto
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
review: APerfect Martini with a splash of orange juice and a touch of maraschino liqueur.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: The Puritan
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Gin contributes botanical strength, vermouth enhances the aromatics, while Chartreuse adds sweet herbal complexity.
history: An often overlooked classic which is thought to have originated at the end of the 19th century.

name: Queen's Park Swizzle
preparation:
1. Lightly MUDDLE mint with rum in base of glass. Use your bar spoon to raise the bruised mint up and around the inside of the glass to coat with fragrant mint oils.
2. Add other ingredients and two-thirds fill glass with crushed ice.
3. SWIZZLE with a swizzle stick or CHURN (stir) with a bar spoon.
4. Fill glass with more crushed ice.
ingredients:
8 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: This close relation to the Mojito is drier, more complex and tad less minty than its sibling. Some like to finish this cocktail with a hefty dose of bitters to colour the crushed ice atop the cocktail but as Martin Cate says in his 2016 book Smuggler's Cove, "even though the bitters look pretty when floated on top, the drink tastes much better when they are swizzled with the rest of the ingredients." Two dashes integrated with the other ingredients is plenty.
history:
Created at the Queen's Park Hotel, Port of Spain, Trinidad. The hotel opened on the 15th of January 1895 and it is likely that this cocktail emanated soon after. This luxury hotel was a fashionable stop for Hollywood types and well-heeled vacationers who spread the legend of its tall swizzled signature cocktail. The hotel was also famed for its Queen's Park Hotel Super Cocktail.

In this 1946, Trader Vics Book of Food and Drink, Victor Bergeron describes the Queen Park Swizzle as "the most delightful form of anesthesia given out today." A year later he also includes this swizzle in his Bartender's Guide By Trader Vic, adding, in the 1972 revised edition, "If you like to make and drink a real doozer of a rum drink that really is a rum drink, try this. It's from the Queen's Park Hotel in Trinidad."

name: Vancouver
garnish: Orange zest twist (or Luxardo Maraschino cherry)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: This cocktail, which is popular in the city from which it takes its name, was originally made with French dry vermouth but since the turn of the century has been made with Italian sweet vermouth. I've opted for the 'perfect' solution with 50% dry and 50% sweet vermouths.
history: Recipe adapted from the About Town Cocktail Book which featured popular food and drink recipes in Vancouver and was published in 1925 by Mitchell Publishing, a local publishing company.

name: Cajun Nail
preparation: POUR absinthe into ice-filled glass, TOP with water and leave to stand. Separately STIR whiskey, Drambuie and bitters with ice. DISCARD contents of glass (absinthe, water and ice) and STRAIN stirred drink into empty absinthe-coated glass.
ingredients:
1⁄3 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 shot	Tennessee whiskey
1 shot	Drambuie liqueur
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A riff on the classic Sazerac.
history: Created in 2010 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Mexican Nail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 shot	Drambuie liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
4 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water
review: Complex with obvious peated whisky and tequila notes, made more interesting with subtle spice and chocolaty notes.
history: Created in 2010 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Smokestack Lightning
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain with ice.
ingredients:
1 3⁄4 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄4 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Agave syrup
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
4 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters (optional)
review: Margarita-like with a wisp of Islay smoke.
history: Created in 2009 by yours truly for The Cocktail Hour at Tales of the Cocktail that year.

name: Daiquiri No. 1 (countdown 3:2:1 formula)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
4 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters (optional)
review: Made to the easy-to-remember 3:2:1 Daiquiri "countdown" formula (3 parts rum, 2 parts lime & 1 part sugar), this balanced and limey daiquiri suits a more characterful light rum.
history:
I'm indebted to Roger Vilalta who in 2010 at Banker's Bar in Barcelona, Spain made yours truly an excellent daiquiri using this formula.

See: Daiquiri Cocktail history

name: Weissen Sour
preparation: STIR marmalade with bourbon in base of shaker to dissolve marmalade. Add lemon juice and bitters, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with beer.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 barspoon	Orange marmalade
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
Top up with	Weisse (wheat) beer
review: Wheaty bourbon with wheat beer and marmaladey citrus notes - they all go hand in hand and so work harmoniously in this unusual long drink.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2010 by Kevin Diedrich at the Burritt Room in San Francisco, USA.

name: Tres Amigos Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
5⁄6 shot	Patrón Añejo tequila
1⁄6 shot	Navy rum (54.5% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Actually this is a Navy rum influenced Margarita made to Daiquiri proportions, but whatever it's called, it's damn good.
history: Adapted from Craig Toone's (8:2:1) interpretation of a cocktail that was doing the rounds in Manchester in 2003, originally under the name 'Triple Rum Daiquiri'.

name: Francophile Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄6 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1 shot	Pineapple juice
review: A simple variation on the vodka-based French Martini adding gin and vermouth to help justify its "Martini" name.
history: Created in June 2011 by yours truly at The Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Monte Cassino
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: The robust flavours of rye combine harmoniously with the other ingredients in this riff on the classic Last Word.
history:
Adapted from a drink created in 2010 by Damon Dyer at Louis 649, New York City. Damon won the Bénédictine 500th Anniversary Cocktail Competition with this drink.

Named after Monte Cassino, a rocky hill 80 miles southeast of Rome, Italy which is best-known for its historic monastery, built on the site where St. Benedict of Nursia established the Benedictine Order circa 529. The hilltop abbey was destroyed by Allied bombing during the World War II but was subsequently rebuilt and reconsecrated in 1964 by Pope Paul VI.

Last Word history

name: Oh Cecilie!
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Amer Picon
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A tasty Danish riff on the Negroni.
history: Created in 2010 by Carl Wrangel at the Oak Room, Copenhagen, Denmark and named after his girlfriend.

name: Red Manhattan
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Claret red wine
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: The tannins from the splash of red wine add complexity and depth of flavour to this Sweet Manhattan.
history:
Created in November 2010 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.
Manhattan cocktail history

name: Rusty To The Core
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
3⁄4 shot	Drambuie liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Honeyed herbal whisky liqueur with an apple brandy base, freshened with lemon juice and given a wisp of smokiness by a splash of Islay malt.
history: Created in 2010 by Julian de Feral at Lutyens Bar in London, England for his autumn menu.

name: Jenever Punch
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP up with soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
2 dash	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A more complex riff of a Collins with malty genever and brown sugar flavours considerably adding to the drink.

name: Velvet Maker
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
2 dash	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
review: Originally made with home infused vanilla vodka, zesty grapefruit, and dry vermouth which adds balancing botanical complexity.
history: Created by yours truly and named after Velvet Maker, the filly who won the 15:05 at the wonderfully named Fairyhouse racecourse in Ireland on 31st January 2015 - the day I first made this drink.

name: Strawberry Fields
garnish: Five drops of balsamic vinegar and a dusting of freshly ground black pepper
preparation: MUDDLE strawberry in base of shaker. Add vodka, honey syrup, lemon juice and egg white and SHAKE with ice. Strain back into shaker, DRY SHAKE (without ice) and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 fresh	Strawberries (hulled, small & ripe)
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: This refreshing vodka-based strawberry cocktail balances tart lemon juice with rich honey. Drops of balsamic and a dusting of black pepper add complexity.
history: Created by Trina Nishimura in 2014.

name: Fly Me The Flip To France
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Byrrh Grand Quinquina
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Grapefruit sugar syrup (2:1)
1 whole	Egg (white & yolk)
review: A bittersweet flip best enjoyed as a wholesome aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Ben Campbell at the Alchemist in Manchester, England.

name: Wood Sap & Sand cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 fresh	Mint leaves
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
3⁄4 shot	Kleos Mastiha liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Fresh and refreshing Greek mastiha replaces cherry liqueur in this riff on the classic Blood & Sand.
history: Created in August 2015 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Eccentrica Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Kleos Mastiha liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Birch water
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Daiquiris are refreshing but I believe this mastiha and birch water influenced example is particularly so.
history: Created in August 2015 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England. Named after a character in Douglas Adams' The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy by the name of Eccentrica Gallumbits.

name: Dried Meadow Flower
garnish: Lemon slice (& ideally a bouquet of edible flowers)
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
5⁄6 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Floral elderflower and tequila with bittersweet gentian and refreshing lemon.
history: Created in August 2015 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Reggatta de Blanc
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Dry and boozy.
history:
Created in August 2015 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

Reggatta de Blanc (White Reggae) was the second, and seminal, album by the English rock band The Police. The album's French name reflects the heavy influence of the country's products in this cocktail and happily, for approval by our naming committee (my missus), most of the ingredients are also decidedly "blanc".

name: Andean Dusk
garnish: Drop cold red grape into drink
preparation: MUDDLE grapes in base of shaker. Add next 3 ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
3 fresh	Red grapes (seedless)
1 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
Top up with	Rosé champagne
review: Dry, biscuity champagne adds sparkle to sweet red grapes while pisco fortifies and adds complex distilled grape flavours.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2011 by Meaghan Dorman at Raines Law Room in New York City. Named due to the use of Peruvian pisco and the cocktail hue due to rosé sparkling wine.

name: Pearl Button
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with lemonade.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cachaça
2⁄3 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 2⁄3 shot	Lemonade
review: Cachaça, aromatised wine, and citrus combine in this dry, refreshing drink.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2013 by John Deragon at PDT, New York City, USA. John's original recipe calls for San Pellegrino Limonata in place of lemonade.

name: Almond Atholl Brose
preparation: STIR honey with Scotch in base of shaker until honey dissolves. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 barspoon	Honey
1 1⁄3 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
2⁄3 shot	Oat milk / oatmeal water
1⁄2 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1⁄3 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
history: An almond riff on the classic Atholl Brose created in March 2016 by yours truly for Disaronno amaretto.

name: Art de Vivre (Art of Living)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Kleos Mastiha liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: Cognac freshened and flavoured with Mastiha, Fernet Branca and chocolate bitters.
history: Adapted from a drink created by Thanos Prunarus at Baba Au Rum, Athens. Originally with 50ml Martell Cordon Bleu cognac.

name: Lovelight
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain in ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Cinnamon syrup
2 dash	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: Reminiscent of a cognac-based Negroni with a hint of cinnamon spice.
history: Created in 2015 by John Stavroulakis at Zaxari kai Alati Bistrot Bar in Athens, Greece

name: L'Indochine
preparation: STIR all the ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1⁄3 shot	Lapsang Souchong tea liqueur
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1 dash	Boston Bittahs bitters
review: This stirred cognac-based cocktail is reminiscent of both an old-fashioned and a Godfather with notes of citrus, coffee and tea.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Trinh Quan Huy-Philip, Vietnam.

name: The Devil In Me
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Piment d'Espelette chile liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Akashi-Tai Shiraume Ginjo Umeshu
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1 dash	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: Plum sake, chilli spice and maraschino cherry delicately flavour cognac in this stirred, boozy after-dinner cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Grant Murray at Bar One, Inverness, Scotland.

name: Butler's Tipple
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄3 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Almost creamy with vanilla, bittersweet rootiness and cognac.
history: Created by Nicholas Gilmour at The Tippling House, Aberdeen, Scotland.

name: Derniere Minute (Last Minute)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1⁄4 shot	Drambuie liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Cognac stirred with rich herbal and heather honey Drambuie, along with aromatised wine. Aromatic bitters add complexity depth.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2015 by Jakub Bobcek at The Refectory Bar, Plymouth, England.

name: Love On Sale
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Unaged rye spirit
2⁄3 shot	Elderflower liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Spiritous and fresh – if you like Natural Daiquiris then perhaps try this. The unaged rye spirit sits brilliantly with the vermouth and maraschino with the lemon enlivening the drink.
history: Created by Dirk Gueldner at the Pine Room, Bar de Lion, Hamburg.

name: Colleen Bawn
garnish: Dust with freshly grated cinnamon & nutmeg
preparation: BEAT egg and pour into shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 fresh	Egg (white & yolk)
3⁄4 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
3⁄4 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A hearty drink that's best suited to a winter's night – perhaps a night with little food as it's something of a meal in itself.
history:
Colleen Bawn is an anglicization of the Gaelic 'cailín bán', meaning girl or young woman. The Colleen Bawn (or The Brides of Garryowen) is also the title of a melodramatic play written by Irish playwright Dion Boucicault and first performed on 27th March 1860 at Miss Laura Keene's Theatre, New York City.

The first recipe for the Colleen Bawn cocktail appears in print in Frederick and Seymour Davies' 1896 book Drinks of All Kinds For All Seasons and is repeated, almost verbatim, in Edward Spencer's 1903 The Flowing Bowl.

name: Patriota
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
1⁄3 shot	Brancamenta
1⁄3 shot	Chocolate cream liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
2 barspoon	Caster/ Superfine/Baker's special sugar (white)
review: A minty mocha coffee rum espresso. Tasty.
history: UAE Bacardí Legacy 2016 winning cocktail by Laura Marnich, Zuma Dubai, Dubai.

name: Anything Else
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably block ice). TOP up with beer.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1 shot	India pale ale (IPA) beer
review: Zesty lemon, bitter liqueur and tangy IPA makes for a zippy, refreshing drink. A characterful IPA and nailing exactly the right amount of honey are key to this drink's success.
history: Originally made with Bacardi Carta Blanca, this was the Belarus Bacardí Legacy 2016 winning cocktail and was created by Lizaveta Molyavka at News Café in Minsk.

name: Pickle Whack Cocktail
preparation:
SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and strain into ice-filled glass.

Special ingredient #1: Pickle Salt
- 500g Fine Sea Salt
- 20ml Pickle Juice
Add pickle juice to salt, break up any lumps, store in Kilner jar.
ingredients:
2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
1 pinch	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
review: An Irish Whiskey Sour made special and distinctive by a salty pickle influence. So much better than a Pickle Back and as it's from Mojo, much more rock and roll.
history: Adapted from a recipe discovered in June 2016 at Mojo in Manchester, England.

name: Bouteiller
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bacardi Gold rum
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Herbal and delicately spiced rum invigorated, aerated, and harmonised by shaking.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Alissa Gabriel at Manhattan Line in Brisbane. This was the Australian Bacardí Legacy 2015 winning cocktail. Alissa says, "The history of Bacardí is famous, but very few have heard the story of Jose Leon Bouteiller and his contributions to Bacardí. The Bouteiller cocktail flavors work hand in hand, just like Bacardí and Jose Leon."

name: Suze you, Sir
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄12 shot	Agave syrup
1 dash	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
review: We do like a pun and appropriately the original recipe for this cocktail specifies Suze gentian liqueur. The flavour of gentian combines brilliantly with tequila while dry vermouth adds herbal complexity.
history: Created Rufus Grantham at Demon, Wise & Partners, London, England. Rufus’ original recipe called for 2 Ocho blanco tequila, ½ Dolin dry vermouth, ½ Suze and 4 drops Bittermens hopped grapefruit bitters. The agave syrup was our own addition.

name: Yellow Cactus Flower
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
3⁄4 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
3⁄4 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
review: Jordan Smith, describes his creation as "bright, herbaceous, subtly smoky, and refreshingly bittersweet." We concur!
history:
Named after the 1929 Georgia O'Keefe painting due to both the shades of yellow, white and green, and for the inclusion of a southwestern ingredient - mezcal.

Adapted from a recipe created in 2017 by Jordan Smith, Head Bartender at Le Coucou French restaurant in SoHo, New York City, USA.

name: Duchess
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Aniseed and liquorice notes from absinthe pervade this vermouth-based cocktail, even though I have dramatically reduced the amount used from the original recipe which calls for equal parts of each ingredient. The Duchess is a cocktail for absinthe lovers.
history: Adapted from a recipe in the 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book which specifies one-third of each: absinthe, French vermouth and dry vermouth with the instruction to "stir well and strain into cocktail glass." The recipe for the Duchess Cocktail in the 1931 The Old Waldorf-Astoria Bar Book calls for the same trio of equal parts ingredients but with the addition of a dash of orange bitters and the indication that the drink should be served frappé. Interestingly, the instruction to serve "frappé" is omitted from the 1935 third edition of The Old Waldorf-Astoria Bar Book.

name: Dutch Coupe
preparation: STIR all ingredient with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Rutte & ZN 12 Oude Graan Jenever
1⁄2 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
4 drop	Orange blossom water / Orange flower water
review: Reminiscent of a genever Manhattan served on the dry side with notes of carciofo amaro.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created by Tess Posthumus, Amsterdam, The Netherlands. Originally based on Bols Barrel Aged genever.

Tess says, "I created this cocktail in honour of the Dutch Queen Beatrix abdicating the throne. She willingly resigned and passed the crown to her son, King Willem Alexander, but as the drink also comes in a coupe glass I thought the name 'Dutch Coupe' would fit perfectly. It's a slightly bitter drink with orange notes and genever based.

"I used Genever as it's the spirit of the Netherlands. Try to use an aged old genever or corenwyn style genever, as the drink needs the malty backbone to support the other ingredients. I've included orange because our royal family is called 'van Oranje', the House of Orange. Back in the days the Dutch would drink oranjebitter at royal celebrations, which is a bitter orange liqueur. So this celebration cocktail needed to have some bitter notes as well. Inspired by Ada Coleman's Hanky Panky, another great woman in history, I think this drink is fit for a Queen. The only thing missing was Queen Beatrix' feathery hat, a signature of her. So, try to replicate this by garnishing the Dutch Coupe with a pretty 'feathery' orange zest."

name: Bitter Jean
garnish: Two Luxardo Maraschino Cherries on stick
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Speyburn 10yo Speyside single malt
1⁄3 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
3⁄4 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
8 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Scotch malt whisky, and particularly peated malt, balance and work brilliantly with rich crème de cassis and full-bodied vermouth, helped by a generous dose of aromatic bitters.
history: Adapted from a recipe discovered in 2017 at Soho House in London, England.

name: Strawberry & Basil Caipirinha
garnish: Stirrer (spoon, wooden lolly stick or stick cut from sugar cane)
preparation:
1. Cut lime in half (from pole to pole) and then slice one of the halves into eight 3-4mm thick half-moon shaped segments and drop into the base of a robust rocks glass.

2. Add 3 bar spoons powdered caster sugar (or ½oz / 15ml sugar syrup 2:1) and MUDDLE.

3. Add strawberries and basil, and MUDDLE some more.

4. When sure fruit juice is fully extracted and the sugar dissolved, transfer the muddled fruit and sugar into serving glass (preferably a 30cl / 10oz hi-ball glass).

5. POUR cachaça (stored in the freezer) into the rocks glass (used to muddle) and swirl to rinse glass before pouring cachaça into serving glass. STIR to ensure all ingredients are well mixed.

6. Using an Ice Tapper, crack (rather than crush) four to five large ice cubes and drop into serving glass. STIR before topping with more ice and serve with a stirrer (but no straws).
ingredients:
1⁄2 fresh	Lime (fresh) (chopped)
3 barspoon	Powdered sugar (white sugar ground in mortar and pestle)
3 fresh	Strawberries (hulled, small & ripe)
3 fresh	Basil leaves
2 shot	Cachaça (from freezer)
review: Succulent ripe strawberries are delicious in a Caipirinha but so much better with basil.
history: See Caipirinha history and other variations.

name: Electric Avenue
preparation: POUR first 4 ingredients into ice-filled glass and CHURN to mix. TOP with port.
ingredients:
1 1⁄6 shot	Bacardi Gold rum
1 1⁄6 shot	Pineapple juice
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Ruby port
review: Slightly sweet and very fruity with pineapple and citrusy rum to the fore. A refreshing, easy drinking crowd pleaser.
history: Created for Bacardí Legacy 2017 by Conor Myers at The Exchequer in Dublin, Ireland. Conor says, "I wanted to create a drink that looked loud and fun, was efficient, low cost with a low alc./vol. and could potentially be a permanent fixture at Bacardí's festival circuit. I wanted to bring two subcultures closer together; Bacardí has always been a massive part of the whole underground music scene. 'Electric Avenue' represents all that is fun, large crowds and big venues – it pairs perfectly with loud thumping music and underground culture."

name: Gonzo
preparation: STIR first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with tonic water.
ingredients:
1 1⁄6 shot	Bacardi 8 year old rum
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Amontillado sherry
2 dash	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
4 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: Tall and refreshing with a delicate balance between tonic's quinine bitterness and maraschino's sweetness.
history: Adapted from a recipe created for Bacardí Legacy 2017 by Kaitlin Wilkes at Corner Club in Stockholm, Sweden, who says "I named my drink Gonzo as a tribute to Hunter S. Thompson – author of Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas and The Rum Diaries. His legacy was 'gonzo' journalism – a style of journalism where the writer injects themselves into the narrative. Thompson wrote The Rum Diaries whilst in his early 20s about his time in Puerto Rico writing for a newspaper and soaked in rum – quite possibly Bacardí rum as they built their flagship distillery the 'Cathedral of Rum' there around the same time."

name: Melon & Apple Caipirinha
garnish: Stirrer (spoon, wooden lolly stick or stick cut from sugar cane)
preparation:
1. Cut lime in half (from pole to pole) and then slice one of the halves into eight 3-4mm thick half-moon shaped segments and drop into the base of a robust rocks glass.

2. Add 3 bar spoons caster sugar (or ½oz / 15ml sugar syrup 2:1) and MUDDLE.

3. Add melon and MUDDLE some more.

4. When sure fruit juice is fully extracted and the sugar dissolved, transfer the muddled fruit and sugar into serving glass (preferably a 30cl / 10oz hi-ball glass).

5. POUR cachaça (stored in the freezer) into the rocks glass (used to muddle) and swirl to rinse glass before pouring cachaça into serving glass. Add apple juice and STIR to ensure all ingredients are well mixed.

6. Crack (rather than crush) four to five large ice cubes using an Ice Tapper and drop into serving glass. STIR before topping with more ice and serve with a stirrer (but no straws).
ingredients:
1⁄2 fresh	Lime (fresh) (chopped)
3 barspoon	Caster/ Superfine/Baker's special sugar (white)
1 slice	Melon (Cantaloupe) (chopped)
1⁄4 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
2 shot	Cachaça
review: Melon and lime dominate this deliciously fruity Caipirinha.
history: For information on the history and other variations of the Caipirinha, please see our Caipirinha cocktail page.

name: Czechmate
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with pilsner.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Becherovka liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 shot	Pilsner lager
review: The herbal notes of Becherovka are noted for combining harmoniously with beer, fittingly in this recipe a pilsner (Becherovka is Czech, as are the origins of pilsner). This combo is fortified with vodka and freshened with lemon juice to produce a long refreshing cocktail which makes a great alternative to merely drinking beer.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Jim Meehan in 2015 for a seminar he was presenting in Prague.

name: Eclipse Cocktail (by Leo Robitschek)
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice). FLOAT mezcal on surface of drink.
ingredients:
1 shot	Patrón Añejo tequila
3⁄4 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
review: Beautifully balanced bitter-sweetness with tequila and mezcal sitting harmoniously with cherry and aperitivo liqueurs, with lemon freshness. A perfect aperitivo cocktail.
history:
The colour of the moon during an eclipse inspired the name of this rusty-orange-red cocktail.

In Jim Meehan & Chris Gall's 2011 The PDT Cocktail Book, the creation of the Eclipse is credited to "Leo Robitschek, New York, Winter 2009."

name: Suzerac
preparation: Rinse glass with absinthe and set to one side. STIR other ingredients with ice and strain into rinsed glass.
ingredients:
1⁄6 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: A boozy and bittersweet aperitif-style cocktail.
history: Created in 2017 by Kevin Rigault at Le Forvm cocktail bar in Paris, France, who says, "My inspiration for this drink comes from the desire to mix old French apéritif Suze with the New Orleans cocktail culture. For the origin of the name, it's just a combination of Suze and Sazerac."

name: Marguerite No.2 (modern)
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into an ice-filled glass. TOP with splash of soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Tequila laced with rich maraschino balancing sour grapefruit and dry sherry – a very refreshing aperitif.

name: Mai Dutch Tai
garnish: Mint sprig, lime shell & fruit stick
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. Crown with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
1 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Wonderfully fruity with underlying bready genever replacing the almond notes from the orgeat syrup almond notes of a classic Trader Vic Mai Tai.
history: Created in February 2018 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Del Famoso (The Famous)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
3⁄4 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: The herbal spicy peppermint and liquorice notes of Fernet Branca dominate this digestif-style tequila laced cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in June 2017 by Nathan Hinze at 99 Hanover Street, Edinburgh, Scotland. The cocktail's name is inspired by the wording on the Fernet Branca label.

name: Corpse Reviver No.0824
garnish: Lemon zest twist (not expressed) & spray of absinthe
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Strega liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Americano bianco
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: A suitably Italian riff on the classic Corpse Reviver No. 2 with Strega liqueur.
history:
Adapted from a recipe by Matteo Rebuffo.
See: Corpse Reviver history and variations

name: Witches' Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into a chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
2⁄3 shot	Strega liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Aniseed, sweet almond and delicate spice subtly influence this tasty Daiquiri.

name: New York Sour (no added sugar & low-calorie)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain ice-filled glass. DRIZZLE red wine around the surface of the drink.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar-free sweetener
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters (optional)
3⁄4 shot	Claret red wine
review: The splash of Claret wine makes this cocktail – both in terms of flavour and visually. Adding the aromatic bitters will help the flavour but also adds trace amounts of sugar.
history:
Adapted from the classic serve by yours truly (Simon Difford) in January 2019.

Also see Sours - history, recipes and glassware.

name: Dunderstruck
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Jamaican-style overproof aged pot still rum
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strawberry sugar syrup
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Fruity in every sense of the word – not to mention estery with namesake dundery rum notes taking centre stage. (Flavours are somewhat reminiscent of a Reggae Rum Punch.)
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Matthew Roedel at The Public House, Bay City, Michigan, USA.

name: Envy Smith
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe
1⁄2 shot	Apple sugar syrup
1 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Sadly, there are few contemporary cocktails using crème de menthe, but this refreshing gin-laced, apple and mint cocktail is one of the stand-out exceptions.
history: Created by Shirmy Chan at 61 Monarchy bar, Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia for the Giffard West Cup 2018.

name: Mrs Hendrickx Lemonade Highball
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass charged with half of the soda water. TOP with rest of soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄6 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
5⁄6 shot	Mandarine Napoleon liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Bready genever fortifies and rounds this mandarin orange influence 'real' lemonade.
history: Created in 2019 and served at Boilerman Bars in Hamburg and Munich, this highball honours Myriam Hendrickx, Master Distiller of Rutte.

name: La Familia (by Ian Burrell)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Agave syrup
2 dash	Coffee bitters
2 dash	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: Tommy's Margarita meets a Daiquiri with spice, chocolate and coffee. Tasty!
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Ian Burrell, London, England.

name: Clockwork Orange No.2
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Akvavit / Aquavit
1 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1 shot	French press/cafetière coffee
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
8 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: Easy drinking, neither sweet or sour, this cocktail with its subtle coffee notes suits breakfast, teatime or aperitivo but was originally created as a dessert cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Taylor Hall at Tandem Bar, Newtown, Sydney, Australia. Taylor was inspired to create this dessert cocktail after eating a Jaffa Cake.

name: Grapefruit Drop Crusta
garnish: Sugar crusted rim & grapefruit zest around inside of rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass with pre-crusted rim.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Grapefruit flavoured vodka
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Pamplemousse liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
review: Easy-drinking vodka-laced refreshingly zesty grapefruit.
history: Created in October 2019 by yours truly (Simon Difford) at the Clocktower, Rye, Sussex, England.

name: Swedish Paloma
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda water.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Grapefruit flavoured vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Grapefruit juice (ruby red)
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Lighter and zestier than a Mexican Paloma.

name: Golden Fortune
preparation: STIR marmalade with vodka in base of shaker to dissolve marmalade. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 barspoon	Orange marmalade
1 1⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Kumquat liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Agave syrup
review: A golden kumquat-flavoured sour with bittersweet orange marmalade.
history: Adapted from a recipe, originally based on Kavka Vodka, by Karol Terejlis for Fortunella liqueur.

name: Sweet Liberty's Sherry Cobbler
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into a glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: Fino sherry's minerality sits beautifully with subtle pineapple and elderflower, freshened by zesty grapefruit.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by John Lermayer at Sweet Liberty Drinks & Supply Co. in Miami, USA.

name: Dunmore Cobbler
garnish: Two dashes of bitters to colour ice crown & pineapple wedge
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
2 shot	Amontillado sherry
1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Pineapple sugar syrup
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Blended scotch and sherry underpin this tangy fruit cobbler.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Ryan Fitzgerald and Todd Smith at ABV, San Francisco, USA. (Originally made with 20ml homemade pineapple syrup.)

name: Strawberry Margarita (frozen)
garnish: Half strawberry (or lime wedge) on rim
preparation:
BLEND all ingredients with 6oz scoop crushed ice.

Seasonal variation: 30 ml strawberry puree as substitute for fresh strawberries.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
4 fresh	Strawberries (hulled, small & ripe)
review: Slightly sweet but yummy with an interplay between tequila, rich strawberry and tart fresh lime.

name: Breakfast Margarita
garnish: Quarter orange slice wheel on rim
preparation: STIR marmalade with tequila in base of shaker until it dissolves. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 barspoon	Orange marmalade
1 2⁄3 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	Agave syrup
history: A Margarita with extra zesty orange tang courtesy of a spoon of bitter orange marmalade.

name: Summer of Matador
garnish: Fresh watermelon wedge on rim or watermelon slices sweets/candy
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Watermelon liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Giffard Caribbean Pineapple liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Agave syrup
review: Watermelon, lime and pineapple combine harmoniously in this very fruity, tequila-laced sour.
history:
Adapted from a cocktail created by Trinh Quan Huy-Philip in Ukraine. In November 2012, Philip won the Swizzle Masters competition with this cocktail which was originally served as follows:

Summer of Matador
Glass: Old-fashioned
Garnish: 3 ginger slices, pineapple & mint sprig
Method: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. Crown with DRIZZLE of watermelon liqueur.
30ml Tequila
20ml Green melon liqueur
20ml Pineapple juice
10ml Lime juice
10ml Agave syrup
10ml Watermelon liqueur

name: The Malagueña
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Dark/black/blackstrap rum
1 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
1⁄4 shot	Agave syrup
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Bittersweet dark pungent rum is lightly sweetened, aromatised and bittered by amaro and bitters duo. A sharpener of an aperitivo.
history: Pronounced "mah-lah-GAY-nyah", Malagueña is a Venezuelan folk music genre, a style of flamenco as well as the name of numerous pieces of music.

name: Robert Frost
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Amontillado sherry
3⁄4 shot	Dry white port
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: This complex cocktail is equally enjoyable as an aperitivo or after-dinner digestivo. If enjoying as an aperitivo, then consider using equal parts fino and amontillado sherries.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Derek Brown at Columbia Room, Washington D.C., USA. Apparently, this cocktail was served at the White House during a party hosted by the Obamas. How the President and First Lady regarded the libation is not recorded.

name: Monte Paloma
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass, while also combining with soda water.
ingredients:
1 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Agave syrup
1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: As you'd expect of a Paloma, refreshing grapefruit and tequila but with delicate bitter complexity.

name: Stonage
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄6 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1 1⁄6 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
1⁄6 shot	Italicus liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
review: Layers of sour citrus, bittersweet vanilla and cleansing Moscato grape spirit. Best enjoyed as an aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Giacomo Giannotti at Paradiso in Barcelona, Spain.

name: South Slope
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
3⁄4 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄2 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: This tasty aperitivo also works well with Americano Bianco used in place of Lillet Blanc.
history: Created by Michael Madrusan (of The Everleigh, Melbourne fame) in Summer 2007 and named for Brooklyn's South Slopes area where he was living at the time. This recipe is from Jim Meehan's 2011 The PDT Cocktail Book.

name: Drunken Helmsman
garnish: Orange zest twist & mint sprig bouquet
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Jamaican-style overproof aged pot still rum
1⁄2 shot	Meletti amaro
1⁄2 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Maple syrup
review: A tad debauched but very tasty.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Jason Alexander at Tacoma Cabana in Tacoma, Washington, USA.

name: Wardroom
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Tawny port
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A potent (pleasingly so) late-night sipping cocktail that's rendered less volatile by serving on-the-rocks.
history: Adapted from a 2020 recipe by Jason E. Clapham, Oxford, England, who says of this drink, "the Wardroom features port, cognac, and rum, the three favourite libations of the British Naval officer."

name: Chocolate Negroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
6 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: The chocolate in this riff on a classic Negroni seems to boost the orange notes in the Italian red bitter liqueur.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in the noughties by Naren Young in New York City, USA.

name: The Prospector
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Speyburn 10yo Speyside single malt
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water
review: Three ingredients combine brilliantly in this deliciously simple cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Lewis Cooke at Black Pearl in Melbourne, Australia. Originally based on The Glenlivet 12 Year Old Speyside single malt Scotch whisky.

name: Fall From The Tree
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Cinnamon syrup
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: An autumnal apple and delicately cinnamon-spiced sour.
history: Adapted from a recipe (originally based on applejack) created in 2019 by Jim Kearns at The Happiest Hour bar in West Village, New York City, USA.

name: Margarita del Diablo
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. Carefully FLOAT wine.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Piment d'Espelette chile liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Claret red wine
review: Sip a chili-spiced Margarita through a thin layer of devilishly red wine.
history: Adapted from a recipe (with Ancho Reyes Verde) created for Dia de los Muertos 2020 by Richard Elgar, a regular contributor to comments on Difford's Guide.

name: Mezcal Martinez
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄2 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2 drops	Angostura Cocoa Bitters
review: Bold flavours combine harmoniously in this characterful riff on a classic Martinez
history: Adapted from a recipe created on 21st October 2020 (Mezcal Day) by Richard Elgar who posted his Mezcal Martinez recipe with accompanying video as part of his own cocktail collection on Difford's Guide.

name: Chocolate Orange Espresso Martini
garnish: Quarter orange wheel slice on rim or float dehydrated orange wheel slice
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Oranje Vodka
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water) (optional)
review: As the name suggests, an orange and chocolate flavoured Vodka Espresso.
history: In November 2020 I came across a few chocolate and orange riffs on Dick Bradsell's classic Espresso Martini. This is mine.

name: Shamrock Sour Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 drop	Green food colour gel
review: Looks like it should be minty but don't be deceived by the verdant colour, it's actually a tasty whiskey citrus sour.

name: Red Echo
