preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	O/Purist Tsipouro
1 1⁄6 shot	Manzanilla sherry
1⁄4 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
1 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A pale shade of pink rather than red, Red Echo has delicate falernum spice which allows vinous notes from the tsipouro and sherry to shine.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Kostas Petropoulos at Lou.Ki Bar in Komotini, Greece, this was one of ten winning recipes in the 2021 O/Purist Quest. The name Red Echo derives from the Greek word: ēchō and Kostas says, "My inspiration comes from a quote: "Life is an echo. What you send out comes back. What you sow you reap." From Greece to the rest of the world, tsipouro has come a long way. O/Purist Tsipouro seems to be a strong advocate voice for the globalization of our national spirit, let us, the Greek bartending community, be the Echo!"

name: Bertram's Cap

review: Apple, honey and grapefruit presented as a harmonious trio.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Jessica Sanders at Drink.Well gastropub in Austin, Texas, USA.

name: Toasted Ginger Godfather
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).

1⁄3 shot	Ginger liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Disaronno amaretto
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters

history: A riff on my Toasted Old Fashioned Godfather, created in November 2021 by Linda Cooke, a Discerning Drinker, who reports that her version not only tastes good (we agree!) but is something of a cold remedy.

name: Vitamin C Cobbler
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.

history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Colin Bugbee at Cure bar in New Orleans, Louisiana, USA.

name: Tirreno

history: Adapted from a recipe created in December 2021 by Mattia Messina at City Social in London, England.

name: Vetiver

name: Pomegranate Negroni

name: Maria Margarita

name: Cherry Margarita

name: My Boy Blue

name: Twelve Mile Limit
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: Spirit-forward, sweet and sour with rich grenadine balancing lemon sourness, laced with a trio of spirits.
history:
In his Vintage Sprits and Forgotten Cocktails, Ted "Dr. Cocktail" Haigh affirms that Thomas Franklin Fairfax Millard (1868-1942), a war correspondent and journalist, is "the confirmed author of the Twelve Mile Limit Cocktail."

The Twelve Mile Limit is one of several Prohibition-era cocktails whose name references the distance from a shore that a nation's territorial waters. During the 18th century this was established as three nautical miles (5.6 km), the distance a cannonball could be shot from the shore to repel incursions. Hence, during Prohibition, US jurisdiction was limited to three miles offshore so allowing the legal supply of alcohol to parties on board boats just outside territorial waters.

As the number of offshore parties grew, the US negotiated agreements with countries such as the UK and France to recognize the right of the American authorities to enforce Prohibition and anti-smuggling laws to an extended 12-mile limit. Predictably, the parties moved further off-shore. On 29th December 1988, President Reagan extended the territorial waters of the United States to 12 miles from 3 miles.

The notoriety of the three-mile and then 12-mile limit to the reach of the Feds during Prohibition led to the Three Miller/Three Mile Limit the Twelve Miles Out, and the Twelve Mile Limit cocktails. The Twelve Mile limit is a rye whiskey laced Three Miller – as the limit was extended, so the cocktail was made stronger.

4 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters
review: Gin-forward with herbal notes shining through. Refreshing before or after a meal.
history: Created by yours truly in December 2022 at The Clocktower, Rye, England.

history: Adapted from a recipe in Ted Saucier's 1951 Bottom's Up where this cocktail is credited to Larry Denis, Head Bartender at the Seigniory Club, The Log Chateau, Quebec, Canada.

name: Performance Automobile

1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur

2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura

There are several versions of the Automobile and for their rendition, the folk at Engine Gin turned to Frank Meier's 1936 book, The Artistry of Mixing Drinks. They added "a typical Ibiza liquor which we also soaked our bolt" but as not widely distributed, I've replaced this with Bénédictine D.O.M..

name: Gilda

history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2009 by Brian Miller at Death & Co. in New York City, USA.

name: Rainbow Sour

preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into ice-filled glass.

name: Call London
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Fino sherry
2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
4 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters
review: Dry and slightly sour yet a delicious aperitivo.

name: Orléans
garnish: Orange zest twist (expressed and discarded) and dehydrated orange slice wheel
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄4 shot	American single malt whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Averna Amaro
1⁄4 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
review: There's a pleasingly bittersweet cola bite to this spirit-forward aperitivo/digestivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2022 by Hadi Ktari at the Chandelier Bar, Four Seasons Hotel in New Orleans, USA.

name: Don't Give Up The Ship
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.

history: Jason E. Clapham of the St. Edward's MCR, Oxford, rejuvenated this long lost classic from 1941 book, Crosby Gaige's Cocktail Guide and Ladies' Companion and says, "The name appears to be a patriotic reference to a naval engagement in the War of 1812 between Britain and the U.S.." I've used Jason's recipe but with Dubonnet, as per the original recipe, while Jason holds that "it works far better with vermouth", specifying Carpano Antica. Jason also specifies Fernet Menta.

name: Royal Daiquiri
garnish: Lemon zest twist – either discarded and float edible viola flowers or use lemon zest twist for garnish
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with 6oz scoop of crushed ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Parfait Amour liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 1950s by Don The Beachcomber.

name: Calvados Mojito
preparation: ADD first 4 ingredients to glass and two-thirds fill with crushed ice. CHURN (stir) with bar spoon and then FILL glass with more crushed ice. TOP with apple soda, briefly stir and serve.
ingredients:
12 fresh	Mint leaves
1 2⁄3 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 2⁄3 shot	Sparkling apple juice
review: This could have been named an "Apple Mojito", it's rather delicious and wonderfully refreshing.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in February 2023 by Kaitlin Wilkes for Avallen Calvados.

name: Rose Margarita
garnish: Salt rim & float edible rose petal
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
3⁄4 shot	Lanique Spirit of Rose liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Agave syrup
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
6 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters
review: As the name suggests, rose flavours imbue this riff on a classic straight-up Margarita.
history: Added to Difford's Guide in April 2023, this recipe is adapted from one promoted by Lanique Spirit of Rose.

name: Andalusian Buck
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice. Open shaker and slowly pour ginger beer over other ingredients in shaker, then strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Amontillado sherry
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: A 'Buck' is a tall spirit-based cocktail with ginger ale or ginger beer and lime juice. This particular Gin Buck is distinguished by also being based on sherry, which comes from Jerez in Andalucia, Spain – hence the name.
history: Created circa 2010 by Jeffrey Morgenthaler at Clyde Common in Portland, Oregon, USA.

name: Second Serve
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
1 shot	Fino sherry
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Fino sherry, amaro and lime juice drive this brilliantly refreshing cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2015 by Dan Greenbaum at Attaboy in New York City, USA.

name: Hazelnut Espresso Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1⁄4 shot	Hazelnut liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
review: Just as it says on the tin, an Espresso Martini with hazelnut. What's not to like? [Beware of using a too assertive muscovado or demerara sugar.)
history: A riff on the Espresso Martini to emerge circa 2022 on the back of the rise in popularity of Dick Bradsell's contemporary classic.

name: Pink Passion Fruit Margarita
garnish: Salt rim & float half fresh passion fruit
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	Passoã passion fruit liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄6 shot	Passion fruit syrup
review: A citrussy bite keeps this distinctly pink, fruity Margarita just on the tart side.
history: This rendition of a Passion Fruit Margarita by yours truly in May 2023.

name: Tropical Racer
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Monkey Shoulder Fresh Monkey
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄6 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
review: Subtle clove spice sits brilliantly with pineapple juice fruitiness and the grainy funk of new-make spirit
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Dillon Scott-Brodie of Mother Mercy in Newcastle, USA.

name: Frozen Passion Fruit Mezcalita
garnish: Lime slice wheel on rim, or float half a fresh passion fruit, or top centre of cocktail with a spoon of passion fruit seeds and flesh
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with ¾ of a 7oz scoop of crushed ice and pour into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
3⁄4 shot	Passoã passion fruit liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Passion fruit purée
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Delivers just as the name suggests – drier and tarter than you might anticipate.

name: Dry Pornstar Daiquiri
garnish: Add a barspoon of passion fruit seeds and flesh to cocktail. Serve with a shot of sparkling wine on the side.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Amaro Santoni
1⁄4 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
1⁄4 shot	Passion fruit syrup
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Fruity, bittersweet and sweet 'n' sour. More an aperitivo Daiquiri than a Porn Star Martini.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in February 2022 by Julian de Féral at the Kindred Club in Hammersmith, London. Julian created this as a tribute to West London cocktail culture, combining two of his favourite cocktails that originated in the area: Kevin Armstrong's Dry Daiquiri (Trailer Happiness) and Douglas Ankrah's Pornstar Martini (Townhouse).

Originally made with Bonanto Spanish aperitif liqueur and garnished by adding passion fruit 'popping pearls' (the kind that you might find for boba tea) in the shot of sparkling wine.

name: Negroni Frappé
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. Churn to redistribute ice and top with more crushed ice to fill glass if necessary.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Meletti amaro
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
3 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Bittersweet, herbal, fruity and wonderfully refreshing. A summertime aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Naren Young at Dante in New York City, USA.

name: Sea Moon
garnish: Mint sprigs bouquet pegged to rim
preparation: STIR ingredients in base of shaker until sugar is dissolved. Then SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 barspoon	Powdered sugar (white sugar ground in mortar and pestle)
4 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Rhum Clément Blanc
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe
review: Rhum agricole wit with lime and a subtle hint of mint. Patiently stir your sugar so it fully dissolves, strike the right balance, and this is a brilliant cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Jason E. Clapham of St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England (originally using Tempus Fugit Crème de Menthe.)

name: Gorgeous
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Fino sherry
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Cucumber syrup
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A delicately flavoured, summertime gin sour. Best served late afternoon to accompany cucumber sandwiches with the crusts cut off.
history: Adapted from a cocktail created by Adam Minegar at Hemlock Bar in Catskill, New York, USA. In place of the two sugar syrups, the original recipe calls for 22.5ml (¾oz) homemade cucumber syrup made with equal parts extracted and strained English cucumber juice and white sugar.

name: Frisco Cooler
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1⁄2 shot	Kirschwasser (cherry) eau-de-vie
1⁄2 shot	Spiced Pear liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Pisco and kirsch eau-de-vie shine in this delicately pear-flavoured sour.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England. Jason says, "The name refers to the Pisco Sour which travelled with Peruvians to San Francisco where, for a time, it rivalled the popularity of Pisco Punch."

name: Douglas Fairbanks
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Potent, sour, fruity, and surprisingly tasty.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Sloppy Joe's Cocktail Manual Season 1931 - 32. Named after the American actor Douglas Elton Fairbanks Sr. (1883 - 1939), famous for his swashbuckling roles in silent films. He married actress and film producer Mary Pickford in 1920 (who also has a cocktail named after her) and the couple soon became "Hollywood royalty" with Fairbanks being called "The King of Hollywood."

name: White Lotus
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with sparkling wine.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄4 shot	Coconut sugar syrup
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: A Piña Colada reimagined, made drier, and taken stratospherically upmarket by a splash of fizz.
history: Adapted from a recipe by an unknown bartender in 2022/23. Inspired by and named after the engaging and entertaining HBO television series White Lotus.

name: Maravilla
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
1⁄4 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
8 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Spiritous and delicately bittersweet, with mezcal and dark chocolate freshened by zesty orange.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2017 by José Cardenas at Raines Law Rooms in New York City, USA. Named after the Spanish word for 'marigold', an appropriate name as this is a riff on Becky McFalls' African Flower. (Originally made with Amaro Sfumato.)

name: Rebennack No. 2
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Ramazzotti amaro
1⁄4 shot	Strega liqueur
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: This after-dinner digestivo is lighter than the original Rebennack.
history: A variation on Chris Hannah's Rebennack No. 1.

name: Pumpkin Spice Old Fashioned
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
2⁄3 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Pumpkin spice syrup
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: I originally used a third less pumpkin spice syrup but the result, while tasty, lacked the headline pumpkin spice.
history: Created by yours truly in October 2023 ahead of Halloween.

name: Lynchburg Spritz
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Tennessee whiskey
2⁄3 shot	Amer Picon
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 5⁄6 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A Lynchburg Lemonade made more interesting and balanced due to Picon Amer replacing triple sec.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Cam Dawson, the longstanding UK Jack Daniel's brand ambassador.

name: Button Hook
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chill glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Brandy-led with supporting and influential crème de menthe and apricot brandy, freshened and rounded by absinthe and carciofo amaro.
history: Adapted from recipes in Hugo R. Ensslin's 1917 Recipes for Mixed Drinks (2nd Edition) (It may have also appeared in his 1916 first edition) and Crosby Gaige's 1944 The Standard Cocktail Guide by Jason E. Clapham in 2013. The original recipe specifies equal parts and omits Clapham's all-important addition of Cynar.

name: Elf On The Shelf
garnish: Float small leaf from the top of a mint sprig
preparation: STIR first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. POUR half-a-bar spoon of grenadine into centre of cocktail which should sink to form a suitably red Christmassy base.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄12 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review:
Elf (elderflower liqueur), On (orange liqueur), The (tequila), Shelf (sherry) is for naughty elves to share while planning mischievous enactments.

Judicious elves take delicate sips so as not to disturb this cocktail's rich, fruity red base, while naughty elves sip, swirl, and even stir their cocktail to turn it sweet and pink. However, very naughty elves enrich their Elf On The Shelf cocktail with red crème liqueurs such as cassis, framboise or fraise in place of non-alcoholic grenadine. They're so naughty!
history:
Not a product of Santa's workshop, but created in November 2023 by yours truly. (In the process, this elf fell off the shelf!)

Dreaded by parents but loved by their children, what started as a children's picture book in 2005 has become a nightly drama enacted by parents worldwide from Thanksgiving to Christmas Eve. The book The Elf on the Shelf: A Christmas Tradition was written by Carol Aebersold and her daughter Chanda Bell and illustrated by Coë Steinwart. Their Christmas-themed story revolves around elves who report to Santa which children are naughty and those who are nice during the lead-up to Christmas. Each night, parents dream up an elf-like act of mischief and then position an elf at the crime scene for their children to discover in the morning. However, children can't touch the elf, or it will lose its magic.

name: Vodka Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
5⁄6 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
4 drop	Bob's Abbotts bitters
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A lemon cherry vodka sour with added complexity thanks to the judicious use of bitters.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Grosby Gaige's 1944 Standard Cocktail Guide.

name: Cinnamon & Pomegranate Margarita
garnish: Float dehydrated orange slice to support a carefully placed star anise.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Cinnamon syrup
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Pomegranate juice
review: Just as the name promises, a cinnamon and pomegranate-flavoured Margarita.

name: Betty Carter
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
1⁄2 shot	Lucano amaro
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A sherry and amaro-influenced Whiskey Sour.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Jeremy Oertel at Berlyn restaurant & bar in Brooklyn, New York City, USA. Named as a tribute to Betty Carter, the famous jazz singer who lived nearby.

name: Bella Martini
garnish: Lime zest twist expressed & discard. Float tiny lime zest coin.
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Dry white port
2 dash	Rose water
review: Pisco, white port and a hint of rosewater influence this Dry Martini.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in January 2023 at Dante in New York City as the official cocktail for Yorgos Lanthimos' black comedy fantasy film Poor Things, starring Emma Stone who plays Bella Baxter. Each ingredient represents a city featured in the film: Gin = London, French (dry) vermouth = Paris, pisco = Peru, port = Lisbon, and rosewater = Alexandria.

name: Lucino's Delight
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Lucano amaro
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Bittersweet, herbal, and cleansingly refreshing, a delightful digestive. (Beware: a citrus zest twist knocks this cocktail off kilter.)
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2007 by Phil Ward at Death & Co. in New York City, USA.

name: French Blonde
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄3 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Lemon bitters
review: Lemon bitters and zestyness, along with tart grapefruit, add crucial balance to this gin-laced, delicately herbal floral cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe published in 2011 on Saveur.com and written by Caraline Bianchetto Chase.

name: 25th Hour
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
3⁄4 shot	Tawny port
1⁄2 shot	Lucano amaro
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A delicious bittersweet digestivo or late-night contemplative sipper.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Sandy de Almeida at The Drake Hotel in Toronto, Canada. (Originally made with Bowmore 12-year-old Islay scotch and Nonino Amaro.)

name: Banana Toronto
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: This tasty riff on the Old Dog, New Tricks is bourbon-forward with rich overripe banana balanced by herbal bitterness.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Ryan Polhemus, bar manager at Offsuit bar in Boston, USA. Ryan's original recipe called for Coffee-infused Angostura Bitters.

name: Tombstone
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄3 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Modern bartending conventions call for this cocktail to be stirred rather than shaken, but the bartender who it celebrates would say that stirring lacked theatre. Shaking also adds dilution and oxygenation. So if you can't bring yourself to shake, then please throw this cocktail, arguably more fitting of the bartender it celebrates.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Dave Wondrich and published in his 2007 book Imbibe!. However, its origins date back to 3rd October 2004, when David Wondrich took a group of bartenders and drinks writers to Woodlawn Cemetery in the New York's Bronx to find and pay their respects at Jerry Thomas' grave. Wondrich went with a bag of ice, glasses, and the ingredients required to make this cocktail. He combined all in a shaker, which was passed around to those present for a ceremonial shake.

name: 21st Century Negroni
garnish: Grapefruit zest twist and orange wedge
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Mancino Vermouth di Torino Chinato
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: A chinato-forward Negroni that's fit for the 21st Century. Indeed, I recommend it, particularly as a digestivo.

name: My Favorite Things
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1⁄2 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1⁄2 shot	Mancino Vermouth di Torino Chinato
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: It might not taste of "Raindrops on roses and whiskers on kittens" but after this cocktail you won't feel so bad. It is a delicious aperitivo or digestivo.
history: Created circa 2014 by Paul Manzell while bar manager at Bergamot Restaurant in Somerville, Massachusetts, USA.

name: Montana Club
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Anisette liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A spirit-forward cocktail that takes dilution well, so consider serving it in an old-fashioned glass over ice.
history: Adapted from a recipe in J. A. Grohusko's 1908 Jack's Manual.

name: Dynamite Dew Drop
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Meletti amaro
8 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: Gin and brandy combine harmoniously and are the backbone of this spirit-forward cocktail – as befits the name. Chocolate bitters play a crucial role alongside rosso vermouth and amaro.
history: Adapted from a recipe created late-2023/early 2024 by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Ewards MCR at Oxford, England, "An attempt to create the mysterious drink that features in the cocktail-fuelled Wodehouse classic, 'The Story of William'."

name: Wild Irish Rose
garnish: Lemon zest twist and skewered Luxardo Maraschino Cherry
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: An Irish Whiskey Sour invigorated with a splash of soda and given a tint of rose by a touch of grenadine.
history: A recipe for a Wild Irish Rose cocktail first appears Geo. R. Washburne and Stanley Bronner's 1911 book Beverages De Luxe, "As served at Auditorium Hotel, Chicago, Illinois and attributed to "Samuel Foote, Manager Liquor Department".

name: Ace Of Clubs Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A Daiquiri with a hint of chocolate.
history: Created in the 1930s at a Bermudian nightclub of the same name.

name: Velvet Old Fashioned
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄4 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
1⁄4 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: The use of a good Pedro Ximénez sherry and achieving the correct level of dilution is key to the success of this potentially brilliant cocktail.
history: History of the Old-Fashioned cocktail and more variations on the Old-Fashioned.

name: Banana Daiquiri
garnish: Banana chunk on rim (cut garnish from centre of banana and place the rest in the blender to make the drink)
preparation: BLEND ingredients with 6oz scoop of crushed ice.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 fresh	Banana (preferably overripe)
review: A tangy banana drink that's not overly sweet and is more sophisticated than the uninitiated may expect.
history: Legendary Tiki bartender Harry K. Yee is credited with being the first to add banana to a Daiquiri at Henry Kaiser's Hawaiian Village Hotel in Waikiki, Oahu, Hawaii.

name: Bebbo Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Blood orange juice
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review:
Fresh, clean and fruity with honeyed notes. Choose your honey wisely.

If using honey rather than honey syrup, stir 2 spoons of honey with the lemon juice in the base of the shaker to dissolve the honey. Then add the other 2 ingredients and shake.
history: A long lost relation of the Bee's Knees revived thanks to Ted Haigh's 2004 book Vintage Spirits & Forgotten Cocktails. Although not classically called for, this is best made with blood orange juice. I've also knocked back the lemon juice by 25% from the original recipe.

name: Bee's Tease
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Lapsang Souchong tea (cold)
review: Assam tea adds delicate tannins and a touch of smoke to this honey gin sour.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2018 by Jared Brown, who wrote the following about the origins of this cocktail.

"One night upstairs at Balthazar, London, I was hosting a large group and thought I had nearly lost my voice. Before they arrived, I set up a pot of Assam tea, with honey and lemon and asked the bartender to shake this ove ice, strain it into a chilled cocktail glass and serve it to me whenever my glass ran empty. I thought this would soothe my throat and keep me out of trouble - until the third one arrived and it dawned on me how much better the drink would be with a measure of gin. Thus, the Bee's Tease was born.

name: Blackthorn No. 3
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2 dash	Boker's bitters
review: As Robert Vermeire says in his 1922 Cocktails: How to Mix Them, "The Blackthorn is a very old cocktail, which is made in two different ways." The most popular way is with various combinations of sloe gin/dry gin and vermouth (see Blackthorn No. 1, 2, 4, 5 and Blackthorn English). This whiskey-based Blackthorn is the oddball in the long-running Blackthorn franchise. Dry and aromatic, it is whiskey's answer to gin's Dry Martini.
history: The whiskey-based "Black Thorn" first appears in Harry Johnson's 1900 Bartender's Manual.

name: Brooklyn Godfather
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: Described by some as being a Brooklyn but perhaps more a bourbon whisky-based Godfather with vermouth.
history: A history of the Brooklyn cocktail can be found on our Brooklyn cocktail page.

name: Kiss
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
review: Gin-forward with a kiss of aromatised wine and maraschino. For a more delicate "Kiss", cut the gin back to 45ml or even 30ml and add one or two dashes respectively of Creole-style bitters.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2019 by bartender Brian Miller in New York City, USA.

name: Champagne Cocktail
preparation: COAT sugar cube with bitters and drop into glass. POUR chilled cognac over soaked cube, then TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
1 cube	Sugar cube
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3 1⁄3 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review:
Starts bone dry and becomes slightly sweeter as you reach the dissolving cube at the bottom, depending on how briskly you drink of course.

Back in the 1940s, David Embury, an American attorney and amateur bartender, wrote the most succinct instruction on how to make a Classic Champagne Cocktail in his The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks: "This drink should be served in a pre-chilled saucer champagne glass. Place a medium-sized loaf of sugar in the glass and saturate it with Angostura bitters - about 2 dashes. Fill with thoroughly chilled champagne. Add a twist of lemon or orange peel, or both.."

Embury also added his opinion of the drink, "From every point of view, other than cost, this cocktail is a decidedly inferior drink, and no true champagne lover would ever commit the sacrilege of polluting a real vintage champagne by dunking even plain sugar - much less bitters - in it. So if you must... serve this incongruous mess just for the sake of 'putting on the dog,' then, in the name of all that a true lover of the grape holds sacred, use a cheap domestic champagne or even an artificially carbonated white wine."

Tips on how to make
Despite Embury's protestations, "this incongruous mess" of a drink remains, some 70 years later, one of the most popular champagne cocktails and one of the most enduring classics. So it can't be that bad! Like most cocktails, it's all about the quality of ingredients used and how you use them. Follows eight tips for making a perfect Champagne Cocktail:

1. Use a well-chilled, clean glass pre-chilled in a freezer. A flute gives a better drinking experience, but a saucer looks more decadent.

2. As cocktail historian David Wondrich says, "Don't use loose sugar or try to crush the cube - the whole point isn't so much to sweeten the drink as to create bubbles, which the cube will do as it slowly dissolves." I prefer a rustic looking brown sugar cube.

3. Place a small napkin (bevnap) over the glass and place the cube on top of the napkin. Dash the bitters over the cube to soak the surface thoroughly. The napkin handily absorbs excess bitters and then works, with some dexterous finger work, to act as a stylish chute to direct the soaked cube into the glass.

4. Use good quality cognac/brandy and store it in a refrigerator or even freezer prior to use. Consider decanting some into a small bottle for such occasions. Pour a measure of the chilled cognac into the glass over the sugar cube. Room-temperature cognac acts as a heat bomb to wreck this cocktail.

5. "Some prefer an ice cube in theirs, which will (to state the bleeding obvious) prolong the chill at the cost of a certain dilution," again, to quote Wondrich. Ice is unnecessary if the sparkling wine, brandy and glass are well chilled.

6. The dry biscuity and citrus flavour of a good brut champagne/sparkling wine is integral to this cocktail. Tip the glass at a slight angle and pour the chilled wine down the inside of the glass before straightening the glass to finish the pour to create as little foam as possible. The cube will continuously generate bubbles, so a careful pour will help retain CO2 in the drink and add to the drinking experience.

7. As Embury says, "Add a twist of lemon or orange peel, or both." Discard twist(s) after expressing citrus oils.

8. Enjoy with friends. This cocktail is not suited to solo consumption and lends itself to a crowd. Depending on the size of your glasses, expect 6 - 8 servings per bottle of sparkling wine, or stretch to 10 if you're a tightwad.
history:
One of the oldest cocktails, dating back to at least the mid-1800s. The Champagne Cocktail consists of a sugar cube doused in aromatic bitters, dropped into the base of a flute, over which a small measure of brandy is poured before the glass is topped up with champagne - hence the name. Although now often made with other brut sparkling wines, it remains one of the most popular 'champagne' cocktails.

The origins of the Champagne Cocktail are lost in the mists of bartending history, with Wondrich saying it "dates from the Iron Age of American mixology - that final prehistoric period between the invention of the cocktail, whenever that was, and 1862 when the first cocktail book was published."

The first written mention of the Champagne Cocktail appears in the 'Panama in 1855. An Account of the Panama Rail-road, of the cities of Panama and Aspinwall with sketches of life and characters on the Isthmus by Robert Tomes'. Published 1855 in New York by Harper & Brothers. On page 61, Tomes writes, "I profess the belief that drinking Champagne cock-tails[sic] before breakfast, and smoking forty cigars daily, to be an immoderate enjoyment of the good things of this world." On the following page, he handily goes on to describe in some detail how a Champagne Cocktail is made:

name: Cherry Martini
garnish: Luxardo maraschino cherry &/or lemon zest twist
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Rich cherry is balanced by botanically complex dry gin and citrus freshness, and further dried and deepened by vermouth.
history: Created in 2005 by yours truly in London, England. Originally based on citrus vodka, I amended this cocktail to be gin-based in May 2020 after the creation of my vodka-based Cherry Fruitini.

name: Chihuahua Margarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Agave syrup (optional)
4 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters (optional)
review: Tequila and grapefruit juice pepped up with a splash of agave nectar and dash of bitters. A tart and delicious tequila sour to pucker the palate.
history: Named after both the Mexican region of the same name and the dog breed, the Chihuahua is a Greyhound with tequila replacing gin.

name: Coronation Cocktail No.1
garnish: Lemon (or orange) zest twist expressed and discarded, plus garnish with a skewered olive
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Dry and wonderfully aromatic with faint notes of almond from the fino sherry and delicately fruity maraschino. Delicious.
history:
Created for, or soon after, the Coronation of England's King Edward VII, who became King on 22 January 1901, upon the death of his mother, Queen Victoria. His Coronation was set for 26 June 1902, but just two days before, an emergency operation required for an attack of appendicitis forced the investiture to be postponed until 9 August 1902.

The Coronation Cocktail first appears in Charles S. Mahoney's 1905 The Hoffman House Bartender's Guide, where it is credited to Joseph Rose of Murry Bros.' Café in Newark, New Jersey, USA. The date of its creation is not given but the cocktail won second prize in the 1903 Police Gazette Bartenders' Contest.

name: Cuba Libre
preparation: MUDDLE lime wedges in base of glass. Add other ingredients, fill glass with ice and briefly stir.
ingredients:
2 wedge	Lime (fresh)
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
4 shot	Cola (e.g. Coca Cola or Pepsi Cola)
review: Basically, a rum and coke with a squeeze of lime, but Cuba Libre has much more of a ring about it. Zesty lime and dashes of bitters add layers of complexity, balancing the sweetness of the cola.
history: In his 1939 The Gentleman's Companion, Charles H. Baker Jr. calls for the lime to be muddled to extract the oils in the skin:

name: Alaska (Straub's 1914 recipe)
preparation: STIR all the ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
3⁄4 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Made with an Old Tom gin with amplified botanicals and minimal sugar (some are way too sweet) this is a spiritous and, if you hit the right dilution, tasty and complex cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Jacques Straub's 1914 book Drinks. The proportions are exactly as per his recipe but Straub calls for his Alaska to be shaken rather than stirred.

name: Angel Face
garnish: Orange zest twist, or apple wedge on rim, or float (dehydrated) apple slice
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into a chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review:
Rich apricot and apple with a backbone of botanical gin. Balanced rather than dry or sweet.

This drink looks better when stirred but the Harry Craddock's original 1930 recipe is shaken and the extra dilution this brings helps mellow this boozy classic. Hence, I've added a splash of water to increase the dilution of the stirred recipe. Although an act of heresy, a splash of processed and packaged clear "apple juice drink" also works wonders in place of added chilled water.
history: Adapted from Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book which stipulates "Shake well and strain into cocktail glass" rather than to stir as modern convention dictates.

name: Angel's Share No.2
preparation: POUR the Chartreuse into glass and coat the inside of the glass with the liqueur by tilting and rotating it. DISCARD excess liqueur. Carefully set the liqueur on the inside of the glass alight and allow it to BURN for a few seconds. Extinguish flame by placing a saucer over the glass, add other ingredients and SWIRL to mix. Beware of hot glass rim.
ingredients:
1⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Walnut (Nocino) liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Tawny port
review: A fabulous drink, especially when VEP Chartreuse, family reserve cognac and 20 year old tawny port are used as per the original Starlight Room recipe.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2005 by Jacques Bezuidenhout at Harry Denton's Starlight Room in San Francisco, USA.

name: Ante
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
2⁄3 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Medium-dry, spiritous aromatised apple with delicate grape/berry fruit and faint orange.
history: The Ante notably features in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: The Atty Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄24 shot	Crème de violette liqueur
1⁄24 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: My recipe remains pretty faithful to Craddock's classic 1930s proportions, but in line with modern bartending conventions, I now disregard Craddock's instructions and stir rather than shake this cocktail. However, arguably, shaking yields an even more delicious cocktail, and if you decide to shake, consider doubling the measures of both crème de violette and absinthe. Shaken or stirred, this Martini-style cocktail is dry and aromatic with subtle floral and aniseed notes.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Bensonhurst
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
review: This riff on a Brooklyn is one of many to emerge since 2006 but is one of the more enduring.
history:
Adapted from a riff on the classic Brooklyn created in 2006 by Chad Solomon at Milk & Honey in Manhattan and named after a neighbourhood close to his home in Brooklyn, New York City, USA.
Brooklyn cocktail history

name: Creole Cosmo
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Rhum Clément Créole Shrubb liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Rhum Clément Blanc
1 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Dry tangy and perhaps more sophisticated than a classic Cosmo.
history: Cosmopolitan cocktail history and recipe variations

name: Damn-the Weather
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄4 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review:
Gin and herbal vermouth with zippy zesty orange.

My previous recipe comprised 30ml (1oz) gin, 15ml (½oz) orange curaçao, 30ml (1oz) rosso (sweet) vermouth, 45ml (1½oz) orange juice, and 1 dash orange bitters. In a quest for a recipe closer The Savoy's original, in January 2023, I amended to the above recipe – hopefully for the better.
history: This cocktail emerged during Prohibition in America and its modern-day notoriety is mostly due to its inclusion in Harry Craddock's influential 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: East Indian
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Dry and pretty flat (like much of India) but perfectly balanced with subtle hints of orange zest.

name: Escalator Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Poire William eau-de-vie
1⁄2 shot	Bison grass vodka
2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: This orchard-fresh concoction was originally made with Korte Palinka (Hungarian pear schnapps).
history: Created in 2002 by Kevin Connelly, England. It's called an escalator because the 'apples and pears', rhyming slang for 'stairs', are shaken.

name: Honey Bee
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Jamaican aged blended rum with funk
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed) (optional)
review: Rich honey balances tart lemon juice over a characterful rum-base. Most recipes omit the orange juice, but as David Embury says in his Bee's Knees recipe (more from him below), "The addition of a small amount of orange juice (about 1 to 2 parts) makes for an interesting variation." The additional subtle fruitiness also sits well with Jamaican rum funk.
history:
The 1949 edition of Esquire's Handbook for Hosts says a Honey Bee is "1 part honey, 4 parts Bacardi, 1 part lemon juice. Mix well, then add ice and shake."

However, in his 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks, under his recipe for a Bee's Knees, David Embury handily explains, "The same drink except for the use of white Cuban rum in place of gin, is known as the Honeysuckle. The same drink with Jamaica rum is the Honey Bee. The Honeysuckle is also sometimes called the Airmail. Since Embury's era, an Airmail has become accepted as being a Honeysuckle lengthened with champagne.

name: Honeymoon
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
review:
This equal parts apple brandy and Bénédictine recipe broadly follows Ensslin's 1916 (the first published) recipe and is not only faithful to the original but the best I've tried.

Most contemporary recipes call for:
60ml (2oz) apple brandy
15ml (½oz) Bénédictine
15ml (½oz) Orange curaçao
15ml (½oz) Lemon juice

My own previous recipe called for:
45ml (1½oz) apple brandy
22.5ml (¾oz) Bénédictine
7.5ml (¼oz) Orange curaçao
15ml (½oz) lemon juice
15ml (½oz) egg white
history: This pre-Prohibition cocktail was first published in Hugo R. Ensslin's 1916 Recipes for Mixed Drinks (1st Edition) and was popularised during the 1920s at the Brown Derby restaurant in Los Angeles, USA.

name: Kentucky Pear
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Pear & cognac liqueur
1 shot	Pear juice (freshly pressed)
1 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review: Pear, apple, vanilla and whiskey are partners in this richly flavoured drink.
history: Created in 2003 by Jes at The Cinnamon Club, London, England.

name: Kiwi Fresh Fruit Martini
preparation: Cut kiwi fruit in half and cut a slice to put aside for garnish. Scoop out flesh out of both halves into base of shaker and MUDDLE. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 fresh	Kiwi fruit (fresh)
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Kiwi sugar syrup
review: You may need to adjust the sugar depending on the ripeness of your fruit. Using kiwi sugar syrup helps boost this cocktail's flavour but, if your kiwis are good and ripe, it also works well just using standard sugar syrup.

name: Lolita Margarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A fittingly seductive Margarita.
history:
Named after the novel by Vladimir Nabokov which chronicles a middle-aged man's infatuation with a 12-year-old girl. Nabokov invented the word 'nymphet' to describe her seductive qualities.
Margarita cocktail history

name: Mandarintini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Oranje Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Mandarine Napoleon liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review: This bittersweet palate cleanser looks like pink grapefruit juice.
history: Adapted from a cocktail discovered in 2005 at Aqua Spirit in Hong Kong.

name: Manhattan (Perfect)
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
5⁄12 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
5⁄12 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: The medium-dry version of the classic Manhattan cocktail.
history: Manhattan cocktail history

name: Mary Pickford Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: When made correctly, this pale-pink cocktail has a perfect balance between the fruit flavours and the spirit of the rum.
history:
Created in the 1920s (during Prohibition) by Fred Kaufman at the Hotel Nacional de Cuba, for the silent movie star and wife of Douglas Fairbanks.

Mary was in Cuba filming a movie with her husband and his best friend, Charlie Chaplin, and this is recounted on page 40 of Basil Woon's 1928 book When It's Cocktail Time in Cuba, "The Mary Pickford, invented during a visit to Havana of the screen favourite by Fred Kaufman, is two-thirds pineapple-juice and one-third Bacardi, with a dash of grenadine. Both cocktails [The Presidenté is also mentioned] are sweetish and should be well shaken. The pineapple juice must be fresh-squeezed." Thus it would appear that the dash of maraschino liqueur, now viewed as an essential ingredient, is a later addition to the Mary Pickford.

name: Alabaster
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Gold rum (1-3 years old pot & column blend)
3⁄4 shot	Aloe liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Aloe liqueur sits brilliantly with clove-led falernum in this refined rum sour.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Jake Powell, bar manager at Death & Co. in Denver, USA. Originally made with Probitas rum.

name: Perfect Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Made with equal parts gin, rosso vermouth and dry vermouth the result is almost sherry-like and suits the aperitivo moment. However, if you want that spirituous Martini punch then gin-forward, as per above, is for you.
history: The Perfect Martini sits between a Dry Martini (with gin and dry vermouth) and a Sweet Martini (with gin and rosso vermouth) so is logically called a Medium Martini in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Pink Palace
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review:
This drink's sweet-sour balance and degree of pink hue is relative to how generous you are with the grenadine.

(When made with homemade fresh pomegranate syrup in place of grenadine, and you hit the perfect balance, this drink is delicious but sadly lacks the eponymous pink hue with the result being more golden-amber.)
history: The signature drink at the Polo Lounge, Beverly Hills Hotel, Los Angeles, USA. The hotel, which is lovingly termed the Pink Palace inspired The Eagles' Hotel California and graces the album cover.

name: Pear & Elderflower Martini
garnish: Pear slice on rim (& pegged elderflower bouquet when in season)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Pear-flavoured vodka
2⁄3 shot	Elderflower liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: With its blend of gin and vodka this fruity floral Martini is entering Vesper territory.
history: Created in February 2020 by yours truly.

name: Saturn 'Martini'
preparation: MUDDLE grapes in base of shaker. STIR honey with vodka and grapes to dissolve honey. Add wine, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
7 fresh	Green grapes (seedless)
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Citroen Vodka
2 barspoon	Honey
1 1⁄2 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
review: Delicate, beautifully balanced and subtly flavoured.
history: Created in 2001 by Tony Conigliaro at Isola, Knightsbridge, London, England.

name: The Scott
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
5⁄12 shot	Drambuie liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: This golden drink is dry and sophisticated, yet honeyed and approachable.
history:
Adapted from a cocktail discovered in 2006 at The Clift Hotel in San Francisco, USA.

My original recipe for this cocktail was 60ml (2oz) Scotch whisky, 15ml (½oz) Drambuie, and 30ml (1oz) dry vermouth which seemed to be liked with 5 ratings at 5/5. However, it was boozy so in June 2020, I reduced the volume of each ingredient to the above with the liqueur ratio very slightly increased and a dash of water added to aid dilution. Or, omit the water and serve over ice.

name: Sloe Gin Fizz
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass (without ice). TOP with champagne (or soda if you're cheap). Some like to add egg white to enhance foam. (The drink photographed here is without egg white and we prefer without.)
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 barspoon	Powdered sugar (white sugar ground in mortar and pestle) (or use 5ml of 2:1 sugar syrup per spoon)
4 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: With the right brand of sloe gin and champagne, this citrusy berry cocktail is just on the dry/tart side of balanced (add more sugar or choose your sloe gin according to taste). Obviously, when made with soda rather than sparkling wine this is a quite different but still tasty cocktail. There is no need to add egg white, and its addition detracts from this cocktail.
history: "Its haunting pink color and fruity opulence are topped with a handsome collar of natural foam which, if the sloe gin be of first quality, is gladsome aplenty." We have David Wondrich to thank for uncovering this quote about the Sloe Gin Fizz by Lawton Mackall in the August 1941 issue of Esquire.

name: 75 Cocktail (MacElhone's 1926 recipe)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Like the gun this cocktail is named after, this small cocktail packs a hell of a punch, and to ensure it does, MacElhone calls for a couple of dashes of absinthe in place of the lemon juice used in earlier Soixante-Quinze (Seventy-Five) recipes. The result is a dry, spirituous drink.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry MacElhone's's 1926 Harry ABC of Mixing Cocktails.

name: Strawberry Daiquiri (frozen)
garnish: Half strawberry (or lime wedge) on rim
preparation:
BLEND all ingredients with a 6oz scoop of crushed ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

Seasonal variation: 30 ml strawberry puree as a substitute for fresh strawberries.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
4 fresh	Strawberries (hulled, small & ripe)
review: Strawberry Mivvi for grown-ups.
history: Unknown but the earliest published recipe is said to be in home economist, Mabel Stegner's 1952 book Electric Blender Recipes.

name: Texsun
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Best made with a bottled-in-bond rye whiskey but also works well with bourbon. Depending on your whiskey and grapefruits, you may want to omit or even increase the sugar syrup. Strike the right balance and this is a refreshing bracer of an aperitif.
history: Adapted from a recipe in the 1949 edition of Esquire's Handbook for Hosts.

name: Widow's Kiss
garnish: Pair of skewered Luxardo Maraschino Cherries
preparation: STIR (or shake) all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Herbal with hints of apple, mint and eucalyptus. This classic is also often made with green Chartreuse, but we prefer, as per classic recipes, with half Yellow Chartreuse and half Bénédictine.
history: Created by George J. Kappeler at New York City's Holland House Hotel. This recipe is adapted from his 1895 book Modern American Drinks.

name: Brandy Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄4 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Gomme syrup
2 dash	Boker's bitters
review: Subtle mint and citrus lightly flavour the cognac.
history: One of the earliest cocktails, the Brandy Cocktail first appears in Jerry "The Professor" Thomas' 1862 The Bar-Tender's Guide & Bon Vivant's Companion.

name: Fair & Warmer Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Sure to warm and fairly good.
history: Adapted from Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Gin Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
1⁄3 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Boker's bitters
review: Bready genever with a hint of orange curaçao adding flavour and the merest touch of sweetness balancing Boker's Bitters. If you don't have Boker's to hand then use the more widely stocked Peychaud's Bitters which produce a different but very tasty drink. I'd go as far as to suggest that Peychaud's produces better cocktail, one with an attractive pale shade of salmon pink – if you like that kind of thing.
history: A close relation to the Martinez, and so by default also the Martini, this cocktail is adapted from one of the oldest known cocktail recipes. Some say this recipe dates back to 1824, coincidentally the same year Dr Siegert created Angostura Bitters. However, the first known recipe appears in Jerry Thomas' 1862 The Bartender's Guide.

name: Saratoga Cocktail
garnish: Orange zest twist (or Luxardo Maraschino cherry)
preparation: THROW (or stir) all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: This brandy-influenced Sweet Manhattan is best mixed by throwing and enjoyed when the odd bubble still rests on its surface.
history:
Recipe adapted from Jerry Thomas' 1887 The Bar-tenders Guide (it does not appear in 1862 or 1876 editions).

This cocktail takes its name from Saratoga Springs, a city in New York State, USA which became a popular resort town due to its natural mineral springs and the Saratoga and Schenectady Railroad which opened in 1832. Hotels sprung up and Saratoga became "the 19th century's east coast equivalent of Las Vegas." In its heyday, the city's Grand Union Hotel was the largest in the world.

name: The Montford
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄2 shot	Ambrato/ambre/amber vermouth
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A wonderfully wet Martini with the addition of Lillet and orange bitters.
history: Adapted from a drink created by Dan Warner at the Beefeater Distillery in London, England.

name: Myrtle Bank Special Rum Punch
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Jamaican-style overproof aged pot still rum
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A rich, fruity and spirituous Daiquiri.
history: Originally made at the Myrtle Bank Hotel in Kingston, Jamaica. Built in the mid-1800s, the Myrtle Bank was converted from a shipyard into a select boarding house. After the hotel was destroyed in the 1907 earthquake it was reconstructed in 1918 and was then the largest hotel in Jamaica, with 205 rooms and a filtered saltwater pool.

name: The Neutral Ground
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Amontillado sherry
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Sweet Manhattan-like with sherry and spiced notes.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2008 by Rhiannon Enlil at Bar Tonique in New Orleans, USA and named after the Median area on Canal Street in New Orleans that formerly separated the American district from the Spanish/French district (now known as the French quarter).

name: Orchard Crush
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into an ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 barspoon	Damson jam (preserve)
2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Apple brandy and damson jam combine brilliantly in this tangy but not at all sweet cocktail.
history: Created in 2008 by Jeffrey Morgenthaler at Bel Ami Lounge in Oregon, USA.

name: Perfect Regent
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
review: Fruity and easy, perhaps not what you would expect.
history: Recipe adapted in 2008 by yours truly.

name: Rose-Hyp Martini
garnish: Rose petal, edible flower or orange zest twist
preparation: THROW all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Lanique Spirit of Rose liqueur
review: Dry (but far from bone dry), aromatic and floral.
history: Created in 2006 by yours truly in London, England.

name: Waldorf No. 1
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: It may go against modern bartending etiquette, but this modern riff on the original equal parts Waldorf is best enjoyed shaken rather than stirred. The extra dilution and aeration benefits this Sazerac meets a Sweet Manhattan cocktail. Shake well, and the foam will last till it reaches the bottom of the glass.
history:
The eponymous cocktail from the Waldorf Hotel, which, until its demise in 1929, occupied the site on New York's Fifth Avenue where the Empire State Building now stands. The hotel was succeeded by the present Waldorf-Astoria New York Hotel, which occupies a landmark Art-Deco building at 301 Park Avenue built in 1931.

Consisting of equal parts rye whiskey, sweet vermouth and absinthe with 2 dashes of orange bitters, shaken and served frappé (over crushed ice), this cocktail first appeared in Jacques Straub's 1913 Manual of Mixed Drinks. It was repeated later in Albert Stevens Crockett's 1931 Old Waldorf-Bar Days .

The original recipe is tough for modern palates, but it's made more approachable by the addition of 2 spoons of sugar syrup:
15ml (½oz) Rye
15ml (½oz) Sweet vermouth
15ml (½oz) Absinthe
10ml (⅓oz) Sugar syrup (2 sugar : 1 water)
2 dashes Orange bitters
SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into a double old-fashioned glass filled with crushed ice.

name: Brunswick
garnish: Orange slice & Luxardo Maraschino cherry on stick (sail)
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. FLOAT claret wine on drink.
ingredients:
2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3⁄4 shot	Claret red wine
review: A rye whiskey-based New York Sour without egg white. This Sour has the good looks and also the flavour profile to back them up.
history:
The Brunswick Sour is simply a Whiskey Sour with a float of red wine, an embellishment that is thought to have first been added to a Whisky Sour by a bartender in Chicago in the late 1800s and is now better known as a New York Sour.

The Brunswick Sour appears in the 1935 Old Waldorf-Astoria Bar Book, in which A. S. Crockett notes under the recipe, "Invented at the Old Hotel Brunswick, once a resort for Fashion, and situated on the north side of Madison Square." The hotel is said to have been "particularly popular with visitors from England as well as wealthy young men about town" closed in 1896.

A detailed history of the Sours family of cocktails is available on our Sours cocktails page.

name: Delmarva Cocktail No.2
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Bourbon's distinctive character shines through but is softened and flavoured by cacao and a hint of citrus.
history: Gary Regan adapted Ted Haigh's original Delmarva Cocktail and published both versions in his 2003 Joy of Mixology. Garry's recipe calls for 2oz straight rye whiskey, ½oz dry vermouth, ½oz white crème de cacao and ½oz lemon juice but, depending on your crème de cacao, this can be on the sour side so I've opted for bourbon, bianco vermouth and reduced the lemon a tad.

name: Elderflower Martini No.2
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Bison grass vodka
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
2⁄3 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: Dry but not bone dry with aromatic hints of grass and elderflower.

name: Fat Tire
preparation:
SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.

(If you don't have Nardini Amaro then sub with Ramazzotti Amaro or Averna Amaro.)
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1 shot	Nardini Amaro
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
review: This flavourful, bittersweet fruity aperitivo won't be to everyone's taste but it's certainly to ours.
history: Discovered in San Francisco in 2006, hence the American spelling of 'tyre'.

name: Saúco Margarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 1⁄6 shot	Elderflower liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
4 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters
review: The floral notes of elderflower combine wonderfully with the herbaceous tequila and citrusy lime.
history: Created in 2006 by yours truly and named after 'flor saúco', which is Spanish for elderflower.

name: Chanticleer
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Clean, crisp, and fresh - gin-laced orange zesty citrus with herbal vermouth mellowed by smoothing egg white.
history:
Recipe adapted from Albert Stevens Crockett's 1935 The Old Waldorf-Astoria Bar Book which originally calls for "orange gin" rather than an orange liqueur. Crockett says the drink "celebrated the local opening of Edmond Rostand's Chanticler".

Edmond Rostand was a French poet and dramatist, best known for his play Cyrano de Bergerac. First released in 1910, Chantecler (correct spelling) is a story where the characters are based on barnyard animals, and whose eponymous protagonist is a rooster who believes that his song makes the sun rise.

By all accounts, the cocktail is rather better than the play. Incidentally, the Chantecler is actually a breed of chicken developed in the early 20th century by Brother Wilfred Chantelain, a Trappist monk at the Abbey of Notre-Dame du Lac in Canada.

name: Lazy Man Flip
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & dust with grated nutmeg
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ruby port
3⁄4 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 fresh	Egg yolk
review: Indulgent creamy mouthfeel but not too sweet, with a great balance between the port and the calvados.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2007 by Chris Jepson at Milk and Honey in London, England. Chris' original recipe also contained 3/4 shot of cream. However, strictly speaking, flips contain egg but not cream.

name: Roosevelt Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 3⁄4 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Hit the right proportions with freshly squeezed orange juice, and this drink is sublime.

name: Tapered Nail
garnish: Pineapple wedge cut into nail-like shards
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (cubes rather than a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
3⁄4 shot	Drambuie liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Rum takes over from Scotch as the base spirit in this riff on a Rusty Nail, but peated single malt adds interest and keeps it a true Nail (a cocktail with Drambuie and Scotch whisky).
history: Created in 2010 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Bobby Burns (Embury's recipe)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled cocktail glass
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Drambuie liqueur
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: As Embury says, there would seem to be some sense in using a Scotch-based liqueur and although this version of the Bobby Burns is rarely seen, it is worthy of a trial.
history: Recipe adapted from David A. Embury's 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks. His Rob Roy and Bobbie Burns recipe reference a footnote below, "An interesting variation of these drinks may be obtained by substituting Peychaud bitters for the Angostura. Peychaud, somehow seems to blend better than Angostura with the Scotch."

name: Breakfast in Manhattan
preparation: STIR marmalade with bourbon to dissolve marmalade. Add other ingredients, STIR with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 barspoon	Orange marmalade
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: The British Breakfast Martini comes to Manhattan.
history:
Discovered in 2009 at Bentley's, Dublin, Ireland.
Manhattan cocktail history

name: Swedish Ale Punch
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with beer.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
5⁄6 shot	Swedish Punsch liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
2 shot	British bitter ale
review:
The grapefruit hop notes in the beer are amplified by fresh grapefruit juice while the beer's cereal notes are fortified with bourbon. Meanwhile, Swedish Punch both sweetens and adds flavour.

Swedish Punch (also known as Arrack Punch, Caloric Punch or Punsch) is a style of liqueur popular in Sweden and other Nordic countries. It's based on Batavia arrack (and other spices) which was first introduced from Java by the East Indian Company in 1773.
history: Created in 2011 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Swedish Margarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 shot	Swedish Punsch liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A Swedish punch influenced Margarita. Tangy and oily.
history:
Created in 2010 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room in London, England.
