See: Margarita cocktail history

name: Praecocia Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Bourbon and apricot are a well-established match, and everybody who drinks Manhattan's will recognise how well sweet vermouth and bitters work with bourbon. Hence, it's perhaps not surprising that this spirit-forward cocktail is delicious.
history: Created in 2010 by Jamie Boudreau at Vessel, Seattle, USA. Jamie describes his 1½ spirit to ¾ vermouth and ¼ modifier as the "Mister Potato Head of Ratios."

name: Prospector
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
3⁄4 shot	Rainwater/Verdelho (med-dry) madeira wine
3⁄4 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1 dash	Whiskey barrel-aged bitters
review: Complex and strong with all three ingredients balancing and enhancing each other.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2010 by Thomas Waugh at Prospect, San Francisco, USA.

name: Corn 'n' Oil
garnish: Lime wedge squeezed and dropped into cocktail
preparation: STIR first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. (Optional: FLOAT black rum on surface of the drink.)
ingredients:
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄3 shot	Dark/black/blackstrap rum (optional)
review:
Rum, slightly sweetened and flavoured with the lime and clove flavours of falernum.

There is much debate over the Corn 'N' Oil, particularly the type of rum used, or even if a proportion of the base spirit should be brandy. The style of dark "black strap" rum is now often floated to give this cocktail an oil slick-like dark top, but this is not traditional in Barbados; this drink's home, but it does aid its appearance. To be authentic to its origin, you should use a Bajan rum and forego the oil slick. There does seem to be a consensus that whatever rum or combination of rums (and brandy) are used, the base spirit is usually a 60ml (2oz) measure mixed with 15ml (½oz) falernum. Once you decide on the base spirit, you have a choice of whether to add "red bitters" (aromatic bitters such as Angostura) or "green bitters" (absinthe) and how many dashes. Finally, you have a choice between cubed or crushed ice. As with all cocktails, I advise making your Corn 'N' Oils to suit your tastes or your guests.
history:
The Corn 'n' Oil is a traditional Barbadian planters' drink which, like the falernum liqueur it is sweetened and flavoured with, dates from the 1700s. Its 'Corn and Oil' name is derived from the Book of Deuteronomy, the fifth book of the Christian Old Testament. Chapters 1–30 are of sermons delivered to the Israelites by Moses on the plains of Moab, shortly before they enter the Promised Land. The salient verse being, "That I will give you the rain of your land in his due season, the first rain and the latter rain, that thou mayest gather in thy corn, and thy wine, and thine oil."

A recipe for falernum in Mrs. H Graham Yearwood's 1911 book [we don't have a copy to verify] is followed by with a notation on its use, "Rum and falernum constitute the drink known as Corn 'n Oil or 'Corning Oil'".

This cocktail's notoriety was helped by its appearing on the back label of John D. Taylor's Velvet Falernum, the best-selling brand of falernum:

name: Betsy Ross
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 1⁄2 shot	Tawny port
1⁄12 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Deep burgundy red and boozy. Based on the classic combination of port and brandy, this is a drink to finish a night. (Benefits from some dilution so stir well.)
history: This combination of brandy, port and curaçao is also known as the Imperial, indeed it first appears under that name in William "Cocktail Bill" Boothby's posthumously published 1934 World's Drinks And How To Mix Them.

name: Emerson
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
review: The botanical notes of old tom with herbal vermouth, zesty citrus and sweet maraschino. Reminiscent of a Last Word without Chartreuse.
history: Recipe adapted from Jacques Straub's 1913 Straub's Manual Of Mixed Drinks.

name: Preakness Cocktail
garnish: Lemon zest twist discarded & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A Sweet Manhattan with a herbal touch of Bénédictine.
history: Thanks to a 2009 article by Dave Wondrich in The Malt Advocate we know that this cocktail was created in 1936 by a chap called George who was the head bartender at Baltimore's Emerson Hotel. The Preakness Stakes is an American horse race held on the third Saturday in May annually at the Pimlico Race Course in Baltimore. George was the winner of a contest to come up with an official cocktail for the first Preakness Ball held that year. Incidentally, The Pimlico Racetrack is said to be named after Ben Pimlico's Tavern which once stood in the area.

name: Rhubarb Lucca Negroni
garnish: Orange zest twist (expressed & discarded) and rhubarb stirrer
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Rabarbaro liqueur
review: A rhubarb-influenced rift on the Negroni, which takes the classic from an aperitivo to a digestivo.
history:
Adapted from a cocktail created in 2011 by Jonathan Abarbanel at Quo Vadis, London, England. Jonathan originally used Rhubarb-infused London dry gin.
See: Negroni cocktail history

name: Voyager Vodka Martini
garnish: Frozen green grape on stick (place on stick then freeze)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Akashi-Tai Daiginjo Genshu sake
1⁄6 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
review: Why dampen your Martini with just vermouth when the Japanese and the Peruvians have so much more to offer?
history:
Created in 2013 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

See Martini cocktail and its evolution

name: Perfect Guest
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
2⁄3 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄3 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1 dash	Celery bitters
review: Clean grainy vodka forms the back bone of this floral and herbal delicate dessert Vodkatini-style drink.
history: Created by Giuseppe Santamaria during for the Spanish World Class 2012 bartender competition.

name: Honey Cobbler
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. Serve with a straw.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 shot	Claret red wine
1⁄4 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
1⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: Dry wine tannins and smoky scotch balance rich honey and blackcurrant liqueur.
history: See Cobbler cocktails history.

name: There It Is...
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1 shot	Blood orange juice
review: Genever is basically a blend of whiskey and gin and in this drink combines wonderfully with Scotch as a base to which maraschino and blood orange flavour lengthen.
history: Created by yours truly in March 2014 at the Cabinet Room in London, England.

name: Gin Colheita
preparation: THROW (pour from one vessel to another from a height) all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Rainwater/Verdelho (med-dry) madeira wine
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: The quality and style of your madeira is crucial to the success and balance of this cocktail - don’t skimp – buy a colheita.
history: Created on 20th August 2014 by yours truly (Simon Difford) to accompany ‘Beef, Juniper and Pistachio Canapés’ for the EBLEX Quality Standard Mark Scheme for beef and lamb. Tasty meat and a tasty cocktail.

name: Paddington Bear Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 barspoon	Orange marmalade
1 3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
review: Tangy orange marmalade with gin and pisco rounded with bianco vermouth.
history: Created on the 28th November 2014 by yours truly to celebrate the premiere of Paddington Bear the movie. Paddington is a Peruvian bear who has a penchant for marmalade sandwiches – hence the use of both marmalade and Peruvian pisco in this Martini.

name: Charente White Negroni
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and STIR.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
review: A riff on the White Negroni with the cognac replacing half of the gin. Fittingly 'Charente' references the Cognac area of France.
history: Created in January 2014 by Matthias Lataille and yours truly at the Cabinet Room in London, England.

name: Bloody Negroni
preparation: Briefly STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Blood orange juice
review: A classic Negroni consists of equal parts gin, Italian red bitters and sweet vermouth garnished with an orange slice. When in season, a splash of blood orange juice adds a refreshing citrusy tang.
history:
Made by yours truly in February 2014 at the Cabinet Room, London, England. (Although I'm sure someone came up with this combo years before.)
Negroni cocktail history and recipe variations

name: Londoner (Ward's recipe)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: As a born and bred Londoner, I'm slightly miffed that a New Yorker has applied the name of our great city to a drink using French and Italian products, but as it's Phil Ward and a great gin-based drink, I'll forgive him and mix up another.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Philip Ward while at Pegu Club, New York City, USA and brought to our attention by the super imbiber and scribe Gary "gaz" Regan, RIP.

name: Pisco Kid
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & Nestle's Milkybar or other white chocolate
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄3 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
1⁄6 shot	Fino sherry
review: This short pisco-based spirituous stirred drink was inspired by memories of Nestle's Milkybars and the 1980s British TV ads featuring the Milkybar Kid promoting the white chocolate bars. White crème de cacao's sweetness is balanced by dry sherry and the acidity of Sauvignon Blanc wine which also adds grassy floral notes. The discarded orange zest twist makes the first sip a white chocolate orange experience.
history: Created by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Mr Simon
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
2⁄3 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 barspoon	Agave syrup
review: Your choice of genever and orange curaçao greatly effects the balance of this cocktail. Salvatore uses Rutte Old Simon which is not only a fantastic genever with an attractive nutty character but also befits the name. The choice of a drier, high alcohol curaçao obviously produces a correspondingly drier drink.
history: Created in 2015 by Salvatore Calabrese at his bar in London's Playboy Club. Salvatore was inspired to make this drink both by the vintage 'Gin Cocktail' - perhaps the first ever gin cocktail - and Old Simon Rutte genever, which was being released across Europe at the time.

name: Chutes & Ladders cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 3⁄4 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1 shot	Swedish Punsch liqueur
1 shot	Americano bianco
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Citrusy tequila-led with Swedish punch and Cocchi Americano rounding and adding their distinctive flavours.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2014 by Frederic Yarm, Russell House Tavern, Cambridge, MA, USA.

name: Sloane Square cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Speyburn 10yo Speyside single malt
1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: An unusual pairing of single malt scotch whisky and tequila with herbal complexity courtesy of Bénédictine liqueur, freshened with orange zestiness.
history: Adapted from a 2013 recipe by Paige McCune of AroundOrTwo.com

name: To Be Oranged
garnish: Orange zest (discarded) & orange wedge on rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 1⁄4 shot	Byrrh Grand Quinquina
1 1⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
4 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: To be arranged - In the meantime shake your tangerine with this pleasing earthy tequila and zesty fruity number.
history: Created in August 2015 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Reverse Vesper Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Blanc quinquina/kina (e.g. Mattei Cap Corse or Kina L'Aéro d'Or)
1 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
review: More a subtly fortified wine than a true "three and under the guest" Martini, but delightfully so with sherry-like wine notes and faint botanical influences. Some will say this should be stirred despite the 'Vesper' name. Shake boldly on, but with good ice.
history: A riff on James Bond's preferred Vesper Martini by yours truly.

name: Blinker (Hawksmoor's Riff)
preparation: MUDDLE raspberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3 fresh	Raspberries
2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: The original Blinker from Patrick Gavin Duffy's 1934 The Official Mixer's Manual uses grenadine but the folk at Hawksmoor have switched this for a few fresh raspberries and a dash of sugar syrup, turning a good drink into a great cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe discovered in 2013 at Hawksmoor in Spitalfields, London, England.

name: Mon Dernier Mot (My Last Word)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Ginger liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Tangy lemon and cognac with sweet herbal and ginger notes. An interesting riff on The Last Word.
history:
Created in 2015 by Edward Godard at Berlin Bar, Melbourne, Australia.
Last Word history

name: Terroir
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Chardonnay (Chablis) white wine
1⁄2 shot	Nettle cordial
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Chablis' white wine acidity balances rich nettle cordial in this sweet 'n' sour cognac based cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Clotilde Lataille at Hawksmoor Spitalfields Bar, London, England.

name: Don Pone
garnish: Skewered crystalised ginger & dust with grated dark chocolate
preparation: RINSE glass with maraschino liqueur. STIR other ingredients with ice and strain into maraschino rinsed glass.
ingredients:
1⁄12 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄3 shot	Ginger liqueur
review: Maraschino cherry aromas strike you first as you enjoy this cognac-laced, subtly chocolate and ginger after-dinner cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Pascal Pone at W Hotel, Verbier, Switzerland.

name: Munich Negroni Western Style
garnish: Orange slice & square of dark chocolate
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Hazelnut liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
review: A nutty riff on a Negroni with a lingering bittersweet hazelnut finish. The dark (high cocoa content) chocolate and orange slice garnish brilliantly befits this cocktail.
history:
Created in 2015 by Mauro Mahjoub at his Negroni Bar in Munich, Germany.
Negroni cocktail history and recipe variations

name: Yuliya Martini
garnish: Grapefruit zest twist & drop eucalyptus oil
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄3 shot	Americano bianco
1⁄12 shot	Giffard Crème de Pêche de Vigne liqueur
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: It's surprising what influence just 2.5ml of Crème de Peche has on this subtly flavoured vodka-based cocktail, particularly if you omit the grapefruit twist.
history: Created in 2016 by Andrii Osypchuk at Gaucho, Dubai, UAE. Originally made using Belvedere vodka, this drink won the 2015 United Arab Emirates Belvedere cocktail competition.

name: The Milkman
preparation:
SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

*Special ingredient #1: Pineapple & browned butter syrup
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
5⁄6 shot	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Pineapple juice
review:
"The Milk shops in the early 1900s were the sellers of spirits during the Swedish prohibition era. The first milk shop ever opened in Stockholm was at the very same spot my bar, Corner Club, is located today. The order "a box of browned butter" was the code name for one wanting to buy booze. The bottles were concealed in butter in small wooden boxes and carried to your home in the open without any questions from the police. I wanted to find something truly Nordic that could not only reflect my geographical region, but also the bar I work at. Björn Frantzén is world famous for his food & one of his signature ingredients is browned butter."

We say: Tastes great but I'm not sure how many people are going to make "pineapple & browned butter syrup".
history: Swedish BACARDÍ LEGACY 2016 winning cocktail by Oskar Johansson, Corner Club, Stockholm.

name: Tara Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Poteen/Poitín
1⁄2 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3 dash	Bob's Abbotts bitters
review: Imagine a delicately clove influenced Daiquiri but with the bready influence of poitín, then you are some way towards imagining the taste of this refreshing and invigorating cocktail.
history: Adapted from a drink created by Tommy Cummins and discovered in January 2017 at The Sun Tavern, Bethnal Green, London, England.

name: Slow Negroni
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly STIR.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: As the name suggests, this is a classic Negroni with sloe gin introduced as a fourth ingredient. Its flavour is exactly as it says on the tin – a sloe berry flavoured Negroni.

name: Maximiliano
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
3⁄4 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: The subtly smoky notes of mezcal combine brilliantly with the aromatic bittersweetness of gentian liqueur in this fabulously complex White Negroni-like aperitivo. (If using dry vermouth in place of bianco vermouth, you'll need to add 2.5ml of rich sugar syrup.)
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2015 by Julio Xoxocotla at Ward III, New York City, USA.

name: Quintessenza
garnish: Dehydrated grapefruit slice & orange zest twist. Smoke the drink using a smoking gun filled with artichoke chips
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin (infused with prawns)
1 dash	Artichoke essence
history: Created by Nagore Arregui, Spain.

name: Jäger Negroni
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly STIR. (Ideally, pre-mix ingredients and age in medium toasted oak barrel for one week.)
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Jägermeisteror other German amaro
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review: A lightly spicy Negroni perfectly suited to the after-dinner "digestive" moment. If it doesn't aid your digestion it will aid your sleep.
history: This cocktail emerged in London in 2016, originally with equal parts Sacred Gin, Sacred Sweet Vermouth and Jägermeister (no Italian red bitter) aged for one week in medium toasted oak barrel.

name: Blueberry Caipirinha
garnish: Stirrer (spoon, wooden lolly stick or stick cut from sugar cane)
preparation:
1. Cut lime in half (from pole to pole) and then slice one of the halves into eight 3-4mm thick half-moon shaped segments and drop into the base of a robust rocks glass.

2. Add 3 bar spoons caster sugar (or ½oz / 15ml sugar syrup 2:1) and MUDDLE.

3. Add blueberries and MUDDLE some more.

4. When sure fruit juice is fully extracted and the sugar dissolved, transfer the muddled fruit and sugar into serving glass (preferably a 30cl / 10oz highball glass).

5. POUR cachaça (stored in the freezer) into the rocks glass (used to muddle) and swirl to rinse glass before pouring cachaça into serving glass. STIR to ensure all ingredients are well mixed.

6. Crack (rather than crush) four to five large ice cubes and drop into serving glass. STIR before topping with more ice and serve with a stirrer (but no straws).
ingredients:
1⁄2 fresh	Lime (fresh) (chopped)
3 barspoon	Caster/ Superfine/Baker's special sugar (white)
10 fresh	Blueberries (fresh)
2 shot	Cachaça (from freezer)
history: For information on the history and other variations of the Caipirinha, please see our Caipirinha cocktail page.

name: Old Hickory (Britten's recipe)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
4 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Heavy doses of Creole-style bitters and orange bitters work with dry vermouth to balance this drink's rich sweet vermouth base. A great aperitivo.
history:
Adapted from a 2017 recipe by Maxwell Britten at Maison Premiere, Brooklyn, NYC, USA. Britten's drink is riff from the Old Hickory cocktail in Stanley Clisby Arthur's 1937 Famous New Orleans Drinks and How to Mix 'Em.

'Old Hickory' was the nickname of Andrew Jackson, the seventh President of the USA (1829 to 1837) and founder of the Democratic Party. Before becoming president, Jackson was a general in the U.S. army who, despite orders to the contrary, in 1812 led his soldiers on a long march from New Orleans to Nashville with a toughness of discipline and resolve that drove his men to start calling him Hickory, a name that stuck and later became Old Hickory. To quote Famous Old New Orleans Drinks, "When General Andrew Jackson was in New Orleans helping pirate Jean Lafitte win the Battle of New Orleans in the winter of 1814-15, this was his favourite tipple."

name: Bamboo Cocktail (Boothby's 1908 recipe)
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) & olive - preferably pimiento-stuffed ('pimola' olive)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
2 drop	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: This bone dry cocktail makes for a great apéritif, but you may find the Bamboo 'Perfect' version of this cocktail easier going.
history:
Adapted from a recipe in William T. Boothby's 1908 World Drinks and How to Mix Them.
Bamboo Cocktail history.

name: Watermelon Caipirinha
garnish: Stirrer (spoon, wooden lolly stick or stick cut from sugar cane)
preparation:
1. Cut lime in half (from pole to pole) and then slice one of the halves into eight 3-4mm thick half-moon shaped segments and drop into the base of a robust rocks glass.

2. Add 3 bar spoons caster sugar (or ½oz / 15ml sugar syrup 2:1) and MUDDLE.

3. Add watermelon and MUDDLE some more.

4. When sure fruit juice is fully extracted and the sugar dissolved, transfer the muddled fruit and sugar into serving glass (preferably a 30cl / 10oz hi-ball glass).

5. POUR cachaça (stored in the freezer) into the rocks glass (used to muddle) and swirl to rinse glass before pouring cachaça into serving glass. STIR to ensure all ingredients are well mixed.

6. Crack (rather than crush) four to five large ice cubes using an Ice Tapper and drop into serving glass. STIR before topping with more ice and serve with a stirrer (but no straws).
ingredients:
1⁄2 fresh	Lime (fresh) (chopped)
3 barspoon	Powdered sugar (white sugar ground in mortar and pestle)
1⁄2 cupful	Watermelon (fresh) (chopped)
2 shot	Cachaça (from freezer)
review: The melon flavours are very subtle in this delicious Caipirinha.
history: For information on the history and other variations of the Caipirinha, please see our Caipirinha cocktail page.

name: Melon Caipirinha
garnish: Stirrer (spoon, wooden lolly stick or stick cut from sugar cane)
preparation:
1. Cut lime in half (from pole to pole) and then slice one of the halves into eight 3-4mm thick half-moon shaped segments and drop into the base of a robust rocks glass.

2. Add 3 bar spoons caster sugar (or ½oz / 15ml sugar syrup 2:1) and MUDDLE.

3. Add melon and MUDDLE some more.

4. When sure fruit juice is fully extracted and the sugar dissolved, transfer the muddled fruit and sugar into serving glass (preferably a 30cl / 10oz hi-ball glass).

5. POUR cachaça (stored in the freezer) into the rocks glass (used to muddle) and swirl to rinse glass before pouring cachaça into serving glass. STIR to ensure all ingredients are well mixed.

6. Crack (rather than crush) four to five large ice cubes using an Ice Tapper and drop into serving glass. STIR before topping with more ice and serve with a stirrer (but no straws).
ingredients:
1⁄2 fresh	Lime (fresh) (chopped)
3 barspoon	Caster/ Superfine/Baker's special sugar (white)
1 slice	Melon (Cantaloupe)
2 shot	Cachaça (from freezer)
review: Exactly as the name suggests, a fruity, melon flavoured Caipirinha.
history: For information on the history and other variations of the Caipirinha, please see our Caipirinha cocktail page.

name: Stiletto Manhattan
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo Maraschino cherry on stick
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Tennessee whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Disaronno amaretto
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Many make this drink with 30ml amaretto and 15ml dry vermouth and, as you'd expect, the result is sweet with amaretto predominating. This 2013 formula by yours truly is more in the style of a traditional Sweet Manhattan.
history: Manhattan cocktail history

name: Rhubarb Negroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Rabarbaro liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: Rabarbaro amaro influences this Negroni, making it a tad drier and punchier than standard three ingredient Negronis.
history: Created in 2009 by Paolo Tonellotto at The Hide Bar, London, England.

name: Montreal Cocktail (official city cocktail)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Canadian rye whisky
3⁄4 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
3⁄4 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
review: Stirred, spirituous and bittersweet, this aperitif-style cocktail reflects Montreal's French and English influences with London dry gin and gentian liqueur. Naturally this Canadian cocktail also features domestically produced rye whisky.
history:
Collaboratively created in summer 2017 by fifteen Montreal bartenders, with the "hope to not only inspire the people of our great city, but those of other communities across the globe, to give life and to embrace the Montreal Cocktail as a modern-day classic."

The initiative, to coincide with Montreal's 375th anniversary, was led by Kevin Demers, owner of Montreal's Coldroom. The other members of the team were: Brynley Leach, Charles Landry, Chris Natale, Drahos Chytry, Fabien Maillard, Graham Warner, Hugo Dallaire, Jason Griffin, Kate Boushel, Philippe Haman, Sabrina Mailhot, Sam Dalcourt, Tony Galdes, and Jean-Maxime Giguere.

name: Schnitzelburg
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Light vermouth amaro (e.g. Cardamaro)
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
review: Stirred down and bourbon-led with bittersweet amaro, and a hit of rich maraschino, lifted and enlivened by fernet's herbal complexity.

name: Renaissance
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄4 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2 dash	Peach bitters
review: Spirituous and bittersweet with a cleansing citrusy bite and underlying cognac complexity, this cocktail is suited to both aperitif and after-dinner occasions.

name: Archibald's Last Memory
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass (no ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
review:
This drink is so spirituous that it may have finished Archibald off, but at least his last drink was a proper sharpener. Then again, the perceived health-giving herbal benefits of Fernet and Bénédictine combined in such a dosage would have perhaps got him back on his feet.

We prefer this cocktail served on-the-rocks as the dilution takes the edge off the spirituous attack and opens the cocktail, releasing more of its delicate herbal complexity.
history: Adapted from a recipe which originated at the Flatiron Lounge in New York City circa 2010.

name: Fin de Siècle (End of Century) Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Amer Picon
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Dry, spirituous and zesty, this is a cocktail that lends itself equally to apéritif or after-dinner occasions.
history: In his 1935 The Old Waldorf Astoria Bar Book A.S. Crockett describes the Fin de Siècle as a very different drink to the above, a "Tom Collins with grenadine and raspberry syrup." He adds, "Name dates it back to 1899 or 1900, when the term was much used, but much mispronounced." In the "Baptismal" chapter he says, "The Fin de Siècle came toward the end of the century, when the expression became current in magazines and newspapers, and when lots of Americans were taking their first steps in French. What they said when they meant to order such a cocktail is another matter."

name: Port Old-Fashioned
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Tawny port
1⁄4 shot	Maple syrup
6 drop	Bob's Abbotts bitters
review: Bourbon and maple syrup somewhat overwhelm the headline port wine, although it does add an underlying fruitiness to this balanced and tasty riff on an Old-Fashioned.
history:
Adapted from a recipe discovered at Red Star Tavern in Portland, Oregon, USA.
Old-Fashioned cocktail history and recipe variations

name: Haystack Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredient with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
5⁄6 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Zesty, bittersweet and sweet 'n' sour, this Haystack will make you salivate – a tasty bittersweet & sour aperitivo. John didn't specify a garnish and although a dried apricot doesn't particularly suit the name, it goes well with the drink (which incidentally we prefer served on-the-rocks).
history: Created in 2017 by John Barraclough, London, England, who describes his drink as "a yellow version of Sam Ross's Paper Plane" that has "the perfume of a hayfield in late summer."

name: The Duchess Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: Gin’s light gin botanical spice combines with rich orange and complex vinous notes from the combination of Sauvignon Blanc wine and dry vermouth.
history: Created in February 2018 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Vanadis
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Birch spirit/birch eau-de-vie
1⁄2 shot	Mancino Vermouth di Torino Chinato
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 pinch	Salt (sea salt)
review: Dry and spirituous, yet (with the right dilution) complex and subtle – even delicate. An interesting aperitif alternative to a Dry Martini or a Negroni.
history: Created in 2017 by Thom Solberg at Black Rock, London, England.

name: The Queen's Steeple
preparation: STIR all ingredient with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
5⁄6 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1⁄2 shot	Italicus liqueur
3 drop	Boker's bitters
review: Amaro pleasantly dominates this bittersweet, delicately orangey aperitif cocktail.
history: Created in 2017 by Loris Carotenuto at The Dorchester Hotel in London, England.

name: Acapulco No.2
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 shot	Strega liqueur
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: This Margarita-like drink demonstrates what a great combo tequila and Strega are.

name: Witches' Grappa
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Bepi Tosolini Grappa di Moscato
1 shot	Strega liqueur
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: As the name suggests, grappa and Strega predominate in this citrusy cocktail.

name: Rusty Peach Cocktail
garnish: Lemon zest twist or peach slice
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Ferro China Baliva
1 1⁄3 shot	Peach aperitif liqueur
3 dash	Peach bitters
review: A dark, delicately bittersweet and light in alcohol aperitif cocktail.
history: A peachy riff on the classic Grassoide Ferro Cocktail in Elveio Grassi's 1936 book Mille Misture by yours truly.

name: Mancini Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Mancino Vermouth di Torino Chinato
1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Spirit-forward, lightly chocolaty and bourbon laced with subtle zesty orange and herbal notes.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2018 by Dominic Venegas and is named after Roberto Mancini the former Italian footballer who after a successful playing career went on to manage Italy’s national team.

name: Lost Plane
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Dark/black/blackstrap rum
3⁄4 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
3⁄4 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Amaro's distinctive flavours shine through alongside the dark rum in this aperitivo cocktail.
history: Created by Emily Gosling of Goslings Black Seal Rum, this is a riff on Sam Ross' contemporary classic, Paper Plane.

name: Fairbanks No.2
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & luxardo maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Crème de noyau liqueur
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Original Savoy and Vermeire recipes for this cocktail specify 2 dashes of crème de noyeaux. I've interpreted this as being a generous 5ml / 1/6oz measure to add a delicate pink hue and a fruity almond note to this Dry Martini-style cocktail.
history:
Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book where he notes, "We often wondered what Doug did it on. Now we know we are going to try and do it ourselves" in reference to the charisma of Douglas Fairbanks Sr., this drinks namesake.

However, the earlier, Robert Vermeire's 1922 Cocktails: How to Mix Them says, "This drink is named after Senator Fairbank, a personal friend of the late President Roosevelt, of America." Vermeire's recipe also differs from the Savoy in that it specifies equal parts gin and vermouth, and if you'd like to try this version, I suggest 45ml / 1.5oz of each.

name: Old Etonian
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄6 shot	Crème de noyau liqueur
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: This Wet Martini-style cocktail is basically, a Fairbanks No.2 but with Lillet in place of dry vermouth.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock’s 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Lily
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Crème de noyau liqueur
1 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Pinky red, gin laced delicate red fruit and almond nuttiness with light white wine and lemon acidity.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book. The original recipe calls for Kina Lillet in place of Lillet Blanc.

name: Aviazione
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bepi Tosolini Grappa di Moscato
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Crème de violette liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: An Italian influenced riff on the classic Aviation with fragrant grappa in place of the usual gin base and floral crème de violette very slightly dialled up to match the aromatics of the grappa.
history: Created February 2019 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room in London, England.

name: William Wallace
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
3 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Take a Rob Roy and switch some of the sweet vermouth for rich flavoursome PX sherry, add a dash or three of orange bitters and you've a William Wallace. A well-conceived cocktail that if you nail the dilution (hence the optional chilled water) is both spirituous and quaffable. Be warned!
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Manchester's Joe Schofield, who says, "The William Wallace is inspired by and takes elements from the Rob Roy and Bobby Burns and is named after another Scottish hero with an alliterated name."

Joe's original recipe specifies a Coupe glass but I felt the drink's volume better suited a Nick & Nora. It is also a cocktail that likes dilution, hence if using ice straight from a freezer consider adding a splash (7.5ml/¼oz) of chilled water prior to stirring.

name: Apricot Julep
garnish: Mint sprigs bouquet & wedge fresh apricot when in season
preparation: MUDDLE apricot in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into cup half filled with crushed ice. CHURN (stir) the drink with the crushed ice using a bar spoon. Top up with more crushed ice and CHURN again. Repeat this process so the drink fills the cup and frost forms on the outside.
ingredients:
1⁄2 fresh	Fresh or tinned apricot
12 fresh	Mint leaves
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
review: Apricot liqueur flavours and sweetens this tasty riff on a classic Bourbon Julep.
history:
Adapted from a recipe by Tony Abou-Ganim, Las Vegas, USA.

The contentious history of the Julep, along with its variants can be found on our page.

name: Tequila Manhattan
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Añejo tequila
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄24 shot	Syrup from Luxardo Maraschino Cherries
review: A Sweet Manhattan but with the distinctive herbal agave notes of tequila.
history: Manhattan cocktail history

name: Yellow Daisy
preparation: SHAKE (or stir) all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2⁄3 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
3 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: This is the kind of cocktail that many bartenders will want to stir rather than shake. However, it is classically shaken. Herbal, zesty and spirituous. Absinthe plays a key role but does not overwhelm.
history: Despite its name, the Yellow Daisy is not a member of the daisy family of cocktails. Best described as a sweetened and aromatised Martini, It was a popular drink in the early 20th century and featured in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book accompanied by a notation saying the drink was the favourite of, and perhaps invented by, Richard William "Deadwood Dick" Clark. He was a famous larger-than-life wild west character of the day who mixed with the likes of Buffalo Bill and Calamity Jane.

name: Isla de Piño
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: There's an interesting play between rum, vermouth and grapefruit which, with the right grapefruit, can be delicious. (Juice ripe pink or red grapefruit.)
history: This classic Cuban cocktail takes its name from the eponymous island off the Cuban coast which is famed (at least it is in Cuba) for the quality of the grapefruit grown there.

name: Home On The Range
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (or straight-up in a coupe).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 1⁄2 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Boozy and complex with delicate fruit, spice and bitterness. A very agreeable late-night tipple.
history: Adapted from a recipe (served straight-up) in the 1941 book Crosby Gaige's Cocktail Guide and Ladies' Companion.

name: Strawberry Caipirinha
garnish: Stirrer (spoon, wooden lolly stick or stick cut from sugar cane)
preparation:
1. Cut lime in half (from pole to pole) and then slice one of the halves into eight 3-4mm thick half-moon shaped segments and drop into the base of a robust rocks glass.

2. Add 3 bar spoons powdered caster sugar (or ½oz / 15ml sugar syrup 2:1) and MUDDLE.

3. Add strawberries and MUDDLE some more.

4. When sure fruit juice is fully extracted and the sugar dissolved, transfer the muddled fruit and sugar into serving glass (preferably a 30cl / 10oz hi-ball glass).

5. POUR cachaça (stored in the freezer) into the rocks glass (used to muddle) and swirl to rinse glass before pouring cachaça into serving glass. STIR to ensure all ingredients are well mixed.

6. Crack (rather than crush) four to five large ice cubes using an Ice Tapper and drop into serving glass. STIR before topping with more ice and serve with a stirrer (but no straws).
ingredients:
1⁄2 fresh	Lime (fresh) (chopped)
3 barspoon	Powdered sugar (white sugar ground in mortar and pestle)
3 fresh	Strawberries (hulled, small & ripe)
2 shot	Cachaça (from freezer)
review: Easy drinking, fruity and refreshing with cachaça's distinctive flavour.
history: For information on the history and other variations of the Caipirinha, please see our Caipirinha cocktail page.

name: Call me Ish
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Spanish brandy
1 shot	Meletti amaro
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Equal parts American whiskey, Spanish brandy and Italian amari produces an incredibly complex, spirit-forward, bittersweet Manhattan-like cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Drew Nemetz and Billy Nichols at Simon & The Whale, Freehand Hotel, New York City, USA. "The Whale" in the name of where this drink was first made helps explain the cocktail name inspired by the famous start to the opening chapter of Herman Melville's 1851 novel, Moby-Dick, "Call me Ishmael."

name: Queen Mother
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄6 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
2⁄3 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1⁄6 shot	Jamaican-style overproof aged pot still rum
review: Pot still Jamaican rum adds delicate but distinctive funky notes to this lightly sweet fruity gin-laced cocktail.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2014 by Jake Burger at The Portobello Star, London, England. Naturally, Jake's original recipe calls for Portobello Road Gin.

Elizabeth Angela Marguerite Bowes-Lyon (1900–2002), better known as Queen Elizabeth The Queen Mother, was the wife of King George VI and the mother of Queen Elizabeth II and Princess Margaret, Countess of Snowdon. During WWII her spirit gave moral support to her subjects while in her later years she was viewed as matriarch to the Royal Family, enjoying public popularity throughout. She remained publicly active until just before her death at 101 years old, perhaps helped by her reputed love of gin and Dubonnet Red.

name: Absolute Gangster
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
5⁄12 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
4 drop	Bob's Abbotts bitters
review: A mere four drops of Abbotts Bitters play a crucial role in this delicately sweetened and complex vodka-based cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2016 by Ricardo Dynan, global brand ambassador for Absolut vodka. Naturally, the name is a reference to this cocktail originally being based on Absolut vodka.

name: Persepolis
preparation: SHAKE All ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄3 shot	Strega liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Rose sugar syrup
5⁄12 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: With its strong rose flavour, the Persepolis is somewhat reminiscent of a Turkish Delight so is very appropriately garnished.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2018 by Sergio Leanza at Funkidory, Peckham, London, England. Sergio describes his drink as being "a Middle Eastern version of a Daiquiri, dedicated to Marjan Satrapi (novelist/illustrator)." Sergio's original recipe calls for 40ml Puerto Rican style rum, 10ml Strega, 15ml rose syrup and 15ml lime juice. He uses a homemade 1:1 rose syrup: 5g rose petals, 500ml water and 500gr caster sugar.

Incidentally, Pārsapura was the capital of the Achaemenid Empire (ca. 550–330 BCE), situated 60 km northeast of the modern-day Iranian city of Shiraz.

name: Vanessa Polk
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
3⁄4 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
6 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Cherry red, spirit-forward and dangerously quaffable as a late-night tipple.
history: Adapted from a 2019 recipe by Jason Clapham in Oxford, England. Jason named his cocktail after the "rather impressive heiress" in P.G. Wodehouse's A Pelican at Blandings. Jason's original recipe calls for Chairman's Reserve Rum.

name: Mezcal Jackson
garnish: Smoked almonds or a single flake of coconut
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
5⁄6 shot	Disaronno amaretto
5⁄6 shot	Coconut rum liqueur (35-40% alc./vol.)
4 drop	Bob's Abbotts bitters
review: Smoky almond and delicate coconut combine in this elegant after-dinner sipper.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Sean Lisik.

name: Hunter's Tea
preparation: STIR first 3 ingredients until maple syrup dissolves. Add Jägermeister, STIR with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cold black breakfast tea
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Maple syrup
1 2⁄3 shot	Jägermeisteror other German amaro
review: Liquorice, chocolate, black tea and citrus. Equally as good enjoyed as an aperitif or digestive.
history: Adapted from a signature cocktail promoted by Jägermeister.

name: Early Spring
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Rhubarb flavoured vodka
5⁄12 shot	Lavender sugar syrup
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Rhubarb flavours shine in this tall floral lavender sour.
history: A cocktail promoted in 2021 by Absolut to support their Absolut Juice: Rhubarb Edition.

name: Fumata Bianca
preparation: STIR first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Dry, lightly bitter and smoky – a thirst-quenching aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2016 by Timothy Miner, New York City, USA.

name: Witches' Flight
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Strega liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Amaro Nonino Quintessentia
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: This cocktail harnesses the flavour of Strega in an after-dinner cocktail and as its creator says, the sugar rim "brings out the tartness in the drink."
history: Created in 2020 by Eran Guter, "cocktail enthusiast from Haifa, Israel" who says, "It is a distant relative of Sam Ross' Paper Plane, with a very different, complex and bright flavor profile, which showcases the Strega yet in perfect harmony with the other ingredients. I named the cocktail Witches' Flight after the magnificent painting by Francisco Goya."

name: Brandy Manhattan
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Cognac is sweeter than the rye whiskey (or even bourbon) on which the Manhattan is classically based. Cognac is also usually slightly lower in alcohol, hence cognac suits a 'Perfect' rather than 'Sweet' Manhattan recipe.
history: Manhattan cocktail history

name: More Supreme Daiquiri
garnish: Grind black pepper over drink's surface
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Martinique V.S.O.P rum
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review: The grassy oaky favours of aged rhum agricole sit well with the fresh lime and bittersweet liqueur.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Alec Bales at Ticonderoga Club in Atlanta, USA. Alec's original recipe called for the first 3 ingredients to be shaken and fine strained into a chilled glass, then for the Italian bitter to be carefully poured down the inside of the glass. (The goal being for the bitter to sink to the bottom of the glass rather than meld with other ingredients.)

name: Pink Tsipouro Fizz
preparation: POUR first 3 ingredients into glass and STIR. Fill glass with ice and TOP with grapefruit soda.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	O/Purist Tsipouro
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3 1⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Pink Grapefruit soda
review: Rich almond with delicate zesty citrus packaged in a light pink refreshing drink.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by George Bagos, Co-owner of Three Cents, in Athens, Greece.

name: Blackberry Martini
preparation: MUDDLE blackberries in base of shaker, add other ingredients and SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3 fresh	Blackberries
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: "Berry nice!" Was the comment from the other side of the bar when this lightly fruity, botanically influenced fruitini was first bar tested.
history: Created in May 2020 by yours truly in Rye, England.

name: Low Rider
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass (no ice in glass).
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	Rabarbaro liqueur
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A tequila-laced bitter chocolate spirituous treat.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2012 by Misty Kalkofen at Brick & Mortar in Cambridge, Massachusetts, USA.

name: Midnight Marauder
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
5⁄6 shot	Bonal/Gentiane-Quina aperitif
5⁄6 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1 dash	Xocolatl mole bitters
review: A bittersweet after-dinner digestif with lightly a smoky hint of mezcal.
history: Adapted from a 2018 recipe created by Joaquín Simó at Pouring Ribbons, New York City, USA.

name: Monterita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 1⁄2 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	Agave syrup
review: Bittersweet citrusy Italian amaro replaces triple sec to make a Spaghetti Western of an aperitivo.
history: An established amaro riff on the classic Margarita by yours truly.

name: Piaggio Vespa Sidecar
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Italian Brandy
1 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A bittersweet Italian aperitivo riff on the classic Sidecar. Tasty it is too.
history: Created in July 2020 by yours truly.

name: Monte Manhattan
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
3⁄4 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Bittersweet herbal and citrusy notes influence this aperitivo-style riff on a classic Manhattan.
history: Manhattan cocktail history

name: Mount Rushmore
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
1 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
review: A bourbon-laced aperitivo that is an interesting alternative to a Boulevardier.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Patrick Pistolesi at Drink Kong in Rome, Italy.

name: Ocean Cable
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Canadian blended whisky
1 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
history: This cocktail originally appears in William Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Cocktail Book where its creation is attributed to one A. G. Scott. We've respected the proportions of the original recipe but as recommended by reader, Jason E. Clapham, we've switched the original Angostura Bitters for creole bitters.

name: Miracle Worker
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1⁄12 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Dry and spiritous but rounded and mellowed by subtle red grape and maraschino cherry fruitiness. Best enjoyed as a late-night sipper.
history: A 2020 riff on a Bushranger by Jason E. Clapham, Oxford, England (originally using Flora de Cana rum).

name: The Symphony No.2
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Malty notes from the genever shine in this complex and lightly sour cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2010-15 by Misja Vorstermans in Amsterdam, The Netherlands, originally based on Bols Genever.

name: The Fitzroy
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Speyburn 10yo Speyside single malt
1⁄6 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A Rob Roy with a delicate peaty note courtesy of a splash of peated single malt.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Sam Paech at The Baxter Inn in Sydney, Australia. Originally based on The Glenlivet 12yr Speyside single malt Scotch whisky.

name: Flannel
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
5⁄12 shot	Pimento dram/Allspice liqueur
5⁄12 shot	Apple sugar syrup
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Pimento dram adds a touch of Christmas spice to this cognac-laced apple and orange winter sipper.

name: Old Barrel
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Amontillado sherry
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Rye whiskey spice, herbal liqueur complexity and vinous sherry sit alongside each other in a harmonious trinity with dashes of aromatic bitters and lemon zest freshness in this riff on a classic Old Fashioned.

name: Bourbon Peach Tea
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Peachtree peach schnapps
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 1⁄2 shot	Cold black breakfast tea
review: Peach and bourbon are a match made in heaven, presented here with a touch of citrus (also classically great with black tea) and zesty orange. A classic pairing of harmonious flavours.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by William Little, a keen golfer from South Carolina, USA who was inspired to make an alcoholic version of an Arnold Palmer.

name: 19th Century
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
3⁄4 shot	Lillet-style Rouge light quinquina
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: If you like New York Sours then you should try this bourbon-laced, red aromatised riff on a classic 20th Century.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2016 by Brian Miller at Pegu Club in New York City, USA.

name: Iron Clad Old Fashioned
preparation: STIR ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄2 shot	Cachaça
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Ferro China Baliva
review: Spirituous with apple brandy leading a trio of aromatic cachaça, herbal Bénédictine and bittersweet Ferro China.
history: Created in October 2020 by yours truly and inspired by Mayur Subbarao's Ironbound.

name: It's All Greek To Me
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	O/Purist Tsipouro
1⁄3 shot	Kleos Mastiha liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A fresh and refreshing aperitivo or digestivo with vinous tsipouro, distinctive mastiha notes, and zesty lemon.
history: Created in January 2021 at The Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: Make It Count
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Blood orange juice
1⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1 1⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Delicately bittersweet honeyed blood orange with a splash of effervescence.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Pamela Wiznitzer at Seamstress in New York City, USA.

name: Rosé 75
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with sparkling wine.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄3 shot	Raspberry (framboise) sugar syrup
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3 1⁄2 shot	Rosé champagne
review: Raspberry fruitiness, rosé sparkling wine and a coupe glass serve set this French 75 apart and make it fitting for Valentine's Day.

name: Pied-à-terre
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Jägermeisteror other German amaro
1 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Cognac-laced and herbal with hints of liquorice, Pied-à-terre (which translates from French to mean 'foot on the ground') makes for a great after-dinner digestif.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Jason E. Clapham in Oxford, England.

name: Rosina Ferrario No. 203
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bepi Tosolini Grappa di Moscato
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Crème de violette liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Aromatic grappa notes shine in this fabulously floral, appropriately pale sky blue cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Joerg Meyer for the Sap Bar in Paris, this cocktail takes its name from the first Italian woman to qualify for a pilot's license. The number of her license was 203.

name: Brasil
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cachaça
2⁄3 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Citrus enlivens this lightly herbal cachaça cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in May 2021 by Will Ballantine, Bar Manager at Wild by Tart in London, England.

name: Weather Up
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Bepi Tosolini I Legni Rovere grappa
1 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
review: Grappa-laced sweet 'n' sour almond, somewhat reminiscent of a Daiquiri made with aged rum.

name: Gallnipper
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Horse with No Name habanero bourbon
1 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1⁄2 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Gallnipper is a large mosquito so an appropriate name for this habanero-infused whiskey riff on the bourbon-based Cicada cocktail.
history: Created in August 2021 by yours truly at the Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: Four-flusher
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Horse with No Name habanero bourbon
5⁄6 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
5⁄6 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: In cowboy lingo, a four-flusher is a cheat/swindler/liar but in this case, a Four-Flusher is a tasty bittersweet four equal parts aperitivo cocktail.
history: A riff on Sam Ross' Paper Plane by yours truly.

name: Yellow Jacket (Gin-based)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄12 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: Rich honey and herbal liqueur balance sour lemon juice in this tasty gin-laced sour.
history: A Yellow Chartreuse-influenced riff on a Bees Knees which instead of a bee is named after the American name for what we English call wasps.

name: Queen Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: The high proportion of vermouth makes this Martini almost sherry-like. And I like sherry!
history: A Martini made with both French (dry) and Italian (sweet) vermouths is called a Perfect Martini and to quote David A. Embury's 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks, "Someone once said that whoever named near-beer was a darned poor judge of distance. I say that whoever named the "Perfect" cocktail was a might poor judge of perfection. It is also sometimes called the Somerset and, if made with equal parts of French vermouth, Italian vermouth, and gin, the Queen."

name: Tunnel Negroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2⁄3 shot	Meletti amaro
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review: Bittersweet and delicately herbal.
history: Adapted from a recipe in the 1929 Cocktails de Paris Presents Par RIP. This 1929 recipe calls for Cora Amaro, an Italian amaro produced by G. & L. F.lli Cora, founded in 1835 by brothers Giuseppe and Luigi Cora. It's clear golden amber, not that bitter and flavoured with cinnamon and orange peel.

name: Topgallant
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄24 shot	Strega liqueur
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Reminiscent of a Martinez.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England. A topgallant is the sail immediately above the topsail(s) on a square-rigged boat. Originally made with Cocchi Storico Vermouth di Torino rosso vermouth.

name: Pineapple Express
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple rum
3⁄4 shot	Rhum Clément Blanc
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Although only one-part rhum agricole to two-parts pineapple rum, it's the agricole that dominates the delicious and spirituous sour.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2016 by Freddie Sarkis at the Broken Shaker in Chicago, USA.

name: Walnut Manhattan
garnish: Luxardo Maraschino cherry dropped into glass and walnut half on rim
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Walnut (Nocino) liqueur
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A Sweet Manhattan with subtle hint of walnut.
history: Manhattan cocktail history

name: Demosthenes Club
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1⁄6 shot	Lanique Spirit of Rose liqueur
1 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Two-parts cognac to one-part aromatised wine with the faintest note of rich aromatic rose. A late-night libation.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England.

name: Norman Conquest
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: An apple brandy-influenced Sweet Manhattan served on-the-rocks.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Erik Lorincz at The American Bar at The Savoy Hotel, London. A shaker containing this cocktail was buried in the counter of The American Bar at The Savoy Hotel when it was refurbished.

name: Nassau Street
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
1 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: A voluptuously flavoured nightcap that tastes boozier than it actually is. However, the residents of Nassau Street party hard.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Chris Frankel in Houston, Texas, USA.

name: D&B Shakerato
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Savoia Americano Rosso
2⁄3 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Delicately bittersweet and sweet 'n' sour with honeyed zesty grapefruit.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Matteo Carretta at Claridge's Hotel in London, England. Matteo's original recipe calls for 10ml acacia honey and xanthan gum syrup in place of the honey syrup I've used.

name: Murano Negroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Savoia Americano Rosso
5⁄6 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄6 shot	Hazelnut liqueur
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: The merest hint of hazelnut liqueur makes this relatively light and approachable Negroni.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Lucas Kelm at AMO Restaurant & Bar in Venice, Italy.

name: Faithfulness
preparation: STIR first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice). TOP with sparkling wine.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Savoia Americano Rosso
1⁄6 shot	Agave syrup
2⁄3 shot	Moscato d'Asti wine
review: Bittersweet and Negroni-like with a touch of rose.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in December 2021 by Michele Lombardi at Quaglino's in Mayfair, London, England.

name: Cold Brew Negroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Cold brew coffee
review: Just as it says on the tin, a Negroni with a splash of cold brew coffee. Simples! Whether you view this as an aperitivo or a breakfast cocktail says a lot about your lifestyle. A proper breakfast is a great way to start the day!
history: Created in December 2021 by yours truly after seeing a recipe for a Cold-Brew Negroni by Pamela Wiznitzer. Pam's recipe uses different proportions and includes coffee grounds infused Campari – seemed a faff so I created this version.

name: The Astor
garnish: Float mint leaf or peg to rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Gin-laced rich berry fruit freshened with lime and mint. Enjoy as a satisfying palate cleanser before or after a meal.
history: The cocktail first appears as the Astor Punch in Jacques Straub's 1913 Manual of Mixed Drinks and then in Jacob Abraham Grohusko's 1933 Jack's Bar Manual.

name: Prince Henry
garnish: Float mint leaf or peg to rim
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄12 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A Sweet Fifty-Fifty Dry Martini freshened with a splash of crème de menthe.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Albert Stevens Crockett's 1931 Old Waldorf Bar Days.

name: Banana Boulevardier
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) and dried banana chip
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
review: Some things are just so wrong that they're not only right, but deliciously so. This riff on a classic Boulevardier is such a cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2016 by Terry Williams, General Manager at Anvil Bar & Refuge in Houston, USA.

name: Spiced Mexican Old Fashioned
garnish: Skewered orange cube & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Añejo tequila
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Piment d'Espelette chile liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Agave syrup
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Just as it says on the tin, a chilli-spiced Tequila Old Fashioned.
history: Created in October 2023 by yours truly at the Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Bridal Suite
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Deeply flavoursome and aromatic with zesty orange freshness.
history: A riff on the classic Bridal cocktail created in March 2022 by yours truly.

name: Pamplemousse Margarita
garnish: Grapefruit or lime wedge on rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
2⁄3 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Giffard Pamplemousse liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: There is something about the flavour and cleansing mild tartness of pink grapefruit that screams breakfast and indeed this Pink Grapefruit Margarita would be delicious with breakfast.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by John Hinojos, a fellow Discerning Drinker, and shared via a comment on our Pink Grapefruit Margarita page.

name: Jägerdame
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice),
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Herbal coffee liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Rhum Clément Blanc
5⁄12 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
3 drop	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: This "dame" is best enjoyed after dinner or as a late-night pick-me-up/put you down.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England.

name: Salted Caramel Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Caramel Toffee liqueur
10 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Just as it says on the tin! A Vodkatini with salted toffee caramel.
history: Created in September 2020 by yours truly at the Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: North Sea Oil
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Akvavit / Aquavit
3⁄4 shot	Americano bianco
1⁄2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
review: A dry, characterful aperitivo with aquavit at its heart and whisps of peaty whisky freshened by herbal citrus.
history: Created in 2018 by Leo Robitschek at the NoMad Hotel in New York City and featured in his 2019 The NoMad Cocktail Book. Originally made with Laphroaig 10-Year Islay Scotch whisky.

name: Ciro's Special
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Dark/black/blackstrap rum
3⁄4 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
review: Characterful dark rum and huge fruity components sit harmoniously in this rum daisy.
