history: Created at Ciro's nightclub in Hollywood, USA, this cocktail appears Ted Saucier's 1951 book Bottoms Up.

name: Copper Bullet
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
2⁄3 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄3 shot	Mentzendorff Kümmel liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: This spirit-forward herbal cocktail may lack a copper hue but it has the lethal potential of a bullet to inflict a killer blow.

name: Rosina
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1 dash	Plum bitters
review: Fruity yet dry, almost earthy, with a delicate smokiness.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2022 by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England who says, this is a "Smokey revival of that Edwardian rarity, now far more widely known, the Zaza. (Named after Rosina Storchio, the lead in the premiere of the opera of Zazà.)

name: Last Lap
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Sage gin
5⁄6 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
5⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A lap of honour for the Last Word cocktail, here made with sage-forward gin and Yellow Chartreuse in place of the usual Green.
history:
A riff on the Last Word created in 2022 by the folk at Engine Gin.
Last Word history

name: 21st Century (Jim Meehan's recipe)
preparation: POUR anis liqueur into chilled glass, swirl, then pour contents out to leave the inside of the glass coated and set 'rinsed' glass aside. SHAKE other ingredients with ice and fine strain into pre-prepared glass.
ingredients:
1⁄6 shot	Aniseed (anise) liqueur
2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
3⁄4 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Jim Meehan is rightly proud of his ground-breaking tequila-based riff on the classic 20th Century and it is indeed both delicious and well-balanced. He created this before absinthe became available in the USA and now it is, I'd prefer to replace the anis liqueur rinse with a couple of dashes of absinthe incorporated with the other ingredients prior to shaking.
history: Jim Meehan created this tequila-based riff on the classically gin-based 20th Century Cocktail back in 2007 during his tenure at Manhattan's famous Pegu Club (subsequently recorded in his 2012 PDT Cocktail Book). Jim points out, "this cocktail was created before absinthe was legalized in the US- it was legalized that year- and in the same year the Oaxaca Old Fashioned was, as I had a sense that agave spirits would lead the zeitgeist in the 21st century- as they have." Jim was ahead of the popularity of absinthe and the rediscovery of the 20th Century Cocktail - he arguably dove it, especially State-side.

name: Campden
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄3 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄6 shot	Blanc quinquina/kina (e.g. Mattei Cap Corse or Kina L'Aéro d'Or)
review: Delicately bittersweet with herbal undertones freshened by zesty orange.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Chicago
garnish: Orange juice and caster sugar rim
preparation: STIR first 3 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with sparkling wine.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄12 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
3 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: A sugar-crusted rim replaces the sugar cube in the classic Champagne Cocktail with extra interest thanks to a splash of orange liqueur.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Cherry Bomb No. 1
garnish: Skewered Luxardo Maraschino cherry and lime slice wheel sail
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda water.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cachaça
1 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Cachaça's character brilliantly laces this cherry-flavoured lime Collins.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by bartender Aisha Sharpe in New York City, USA.

name: St. George's Negroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1⁄2 shot	Tawny port
review: Port and aromatised wine add red berry fruit flavours to this riff on a Negroni.
history: Adapted from a recipe discovered in February 2022 at the Library Bar at London's Landsborough Hotel under the "Robust Cocktails" section of their menu, described as a "Apothecary mix of Martini Bitters, French Aperitif Dubonnet, Graham's Port 10 years old & uplifted with Bombay Sapphire gin."

name: Fourth Degree
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Ambrato/ambre/amber vermouth
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
4 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: One of those cocktails where a 'bland' dry vermouth just won't do. Don't go big on the rosso but go for it on the dry vermouth. Dash your absinthe judiciously and you'll have a delicious variation on a Perfect Martini.
history: The Fourth Degree Cocktail first appears as a blanche absinthe-based cocktail (without gin) in Jacques Straub's 1914 book Drinksalong with the attentive name, "Feather Cocktail".

name: Sherry Kicker Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄3 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄6 shot	Manzanilla sherry
3 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Manzanilla sherry adds its characteristic dry faintly salty notes to this excellent 5:1 Dry Martini.
history: Adapted from a recipe created at the Gin Palace in Melbourne, Australia.

name: Three Citrus Garibaldi
garnish: Orange zest twist (expressed & discarded) and orange wedge rested across rim
preparation: Squeeze oranges and grapefruits (stored in a refrigerator) using pillar or elbow press and fine strain to remove any flesh. Then BLEND with amaro at high speed (without ice) to make "fluffy" and pour into chilled glass. Fill glass with ice cubes.
ingredients:
2 shot	Blood orange juice (chilled)
1 2⁄3 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed) (chilled)
1 1⁄2 shot	Amaro Santoni (chilled)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix) (optional)
review: Why pop vitamin C tablets when you can chuck this bittersweet riff on a classic Garibaldi . (Depending on your citrus, you may want to add as much as a barspoon of sugar syrup.)
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Luca Missaglia of Amaro Santoni.

name: Mexican Martini (Mex-Mart)
garnish: Lime juice & salt rim. Garnish with lime wedge on rim & 3 skewered three pimiento-stuffed green olives
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled (salt rimmed) glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Olive brine (from jarred olives)
review: Not another Neo-Martini but an olive brine-enriched Margarita.
history: Adapted from a cocktail served at the Cedar Door Patio Bar and Grill in Austin, Texas, USA, since the early 1980s after one of its bartenders, named Ellen, was served a Margarita while on vacation in Matamoros, Mexico. Ellen took the idea back to the Cedar Door's owners, Gus and Diane Koerner and their longstanding bartender, Jim LeMond, created the recipe and added what would become the bar's signature cocktail to the menu.

name: Misty Martini
garnish: Spray a mist of peated & lemon zest twist expressed & discarded and garnished with a skewered black olive
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄12 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄12 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
review: A peaty whisky-influenced 4.3 to 1 Dry Martini with the base spirit split between gin with a flavour-packed smidgeon of peated whisky, stirred with 2-parts dry vermouth to 1-part bianco vermouth.
history: Created in June 2022 by yours truly at The Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Tequila Matador
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
4 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters
review: Restrained in alcohol but not lacking in balance nor fruitiness. I've added a mere four drops of our Daiquiri Bitters to Trader Vic's original recipe but I feel he'd have approved.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Victor Bergeron's 1972 Trader Vic's Bartender's Guide.

name: Golden Boy
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄6 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Americano bianco
6 drop	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
review: Gin-forward, this pale golden cocktail is delicious as either an aperitivo or digestive. If you don't have a circa 47% alc./vol. citrus-forward gin to hand, perhaps try with 30ml London Dry Gin and 10ml citrus gin.
history: Adapted from a recipe create in 2023 by bartender Michele Di Firmo and his colleague Walter Boero at Dal Medico bar in the centre of Verona, Italy. Their original recipe calls for 35ml Tanqueray No. Ten Gin.

name: Triple Crown
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Pamplemousse liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A grapefruit Whiskey Sour made more interesting and bittersweet by amaro.
history: Adapted from a recipe created Jay Zimmerman of [bā'sik] bar in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, NYC, USA.

name: Frozen Passion Fruit Daiquiri
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with ¾ of a 7oz scoop of crushed ice and pour into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
1⁄2 shot	Passoã passion fruit liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: The success of this cocktail is all about striking the perfect balance between the strength of the rum, fruity sweetness of the liqueur and sugar syrup, and the sourness of the lime, coupled with the super chilled dilution from the slushy ice. Succeed and the result is delicious.

name: Darb
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Dry vermouth adds complexity and balance to this apricot gin sour.
history: A Rejuvenated classic from Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book brought to my attention and reformulated by Jason E. Clapham of St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England.

name: Depth Charge (Savoy recipe)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄4 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄2 shot	Blanc quinquina/kina (e.g. Mattei Cap Corse or Kina L'Aéro d'Or)
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review:
Wet Martini-like with pronounced quinine. A hot weather Martini, perhaps.

I tried the Depth Charge with various proportions of Lillet Blanc and Kina L'Aéro d'Or, starting with equal parts which was too dry, before arriving at the recipe above.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Chocolate Bourbon Stinger
garnish: Square of 70% cacoa chocolate & mint sprigs bouquet
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into a glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄4 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe
8 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: Best described as a cleansing, delicately chocolate-influenced Bourbon Old Fashioned served frappé.
history: Created by yours truly in July 2023 at The Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: Spring Green
garnish: Lime zest twist expressed and discarded. Garnish with a half-moon lime slice on rim.
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄2 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
4 drop	Lime bitters
review: A floral and herbal aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2007 by Kitty Gallisá at Nopa in San Franciso, USA – originally using V.E.P. Chartreuse. The original recipe calls for 45ml (1½oz) manzanilla sherry, 15ml (½oz) Green Chartreuse, and 15ml (½oz) elderflower liqueur.

name: Lento Negroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Pacharan liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: A riff of a Sloegroni/Slow Negroni with sloe gin replaced by Spanish pacharán, which adds a delicate aniseed note.
history: Created in December 2021 thanks to a comment (on our Slow Negroni page) by Melissa Demian, a fellow Discerning Drinker. Lento is Spanish for slow, a reference to this cocktail being made with pacharán in place of sloe gin.

name: Witches' Negroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Strega liqueur
review: A classic Negroni, bewitched by a splash of Strega liqueur.

name: Saint Sauvant
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Richly flavoured and brandy-laced. A delicious late-night libation.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England. Originally made with Merlet Soeurs Cerises, this is "A cognac version of the gin-based Copenhagen, without the lemon. Named after the Merlet HQ." The recipe also called for Cocchi Storico Vermouth di Torino.

name: Cel Rey
preparation: POUR first 3 ingredients into ice-filled glass. TOP with celery soda.
ingredients:
2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3 dash	Celery bitters
3 shot	Celery soda
review: Mezcal shines in this dry, savoury, refreshing, long, effervescent cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Danny Child for The Farm and Fisherman Tavern in New Jersey, USA. Originally based on Rey Campero mezcal and Dr. Brown's Cel-Ray celery soda, a combination that inspired this cocktail's name.

name: Pisco Cerenza
garnish: Skewered orange slice wheel & Luxardo Maraschino cherry (sail)
preparation: STIR first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda water.
ingredients:
1 1⁄6 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Cherry and rosso vermouth fortified with a spirit is a winning combination (see Blood & Sand), in this case with pisco, which being distilled from fermented grape juice sits brilliantly with the vermouth.

name: Ancho Problem
garnish: Lime slice wheel on rim or float dehydrated lime slice wheel
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1 shot	Giffard Piment d'Espelette chile liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
review: No problem! Unless that is you're out of chili liqueur, as that's the backbone to this spicy, low citrus Margarita.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Boston bartender Ezra Star.

name: Mandarine Negroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Mandarine Napoleon liqueur
review: Bittersweet with, as the name suggests, zesty mandarin freshness.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2022 by Dennis Stein at Le Lion Bar de Paris in Hamburg, Germany for Negroni Week. The Mandarine Negroni proved so popular it became a permanent addition to the bar's menu and is consistently one of the bestselling cocktails.

Dennis' original recipe: 30ml Rutte Dutch Dry Gin, 30ml Berto Bianco Vermouth, 20ml Campari, and 10ml Mandarine Napoleon.

name: Rebennack No. 1
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Averna Amaro
1⁄4 shot	Rhum Clément Créole Shrubb liqueur
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Spirit-forward with heavy herbal flavours lifted by zesty orange.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Chris Hannah at Arnaud's French 75 Bar in New Orleans, USA and named during the 2010 Mardi Gras when be served the cocktail to singer and song writer Mac Rebennack (a.k.a. Dr. John) at a Krewe de Vieux event.

name: Embassie
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
3⁄4 shot	Americano bianco
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A delicious, dry, herbal and citrusy Last Word riff.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Mal Spence at Kelvingrove Café in Glasgow, Scotland.

name: Brave Bull
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
6 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Your choice of coffee liqueur will dramatically affect how dry/sweet your Brave Bull is. Reposado or añejo tequila tend to sit more harmoniously with the coffee than blanco tequila.
history:
The Brave Bull emerged during the 1970s on the back of the then-popular Black Russian cocktail.
Recipe adapted from Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide.

name: Williams
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Herbal scotch whisky freshened by orange oils. One of those cocktails that's so spirit-forward that you may find it more enjoyable served on-the-rocks.
history: A vintage cocktail kindly bought to our attention by Jason E. Clapham who also proved us with the above recipe. The Williams cocktail first appears in Pioneers of Mixing at Elite Bars 1903-1933 published in 1934.

name: Amaro Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 3-5 years
1⁄2 shot	Averna Amaro
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	Pimento dram/Allspice liqueur
review: Bittersweet and lightly spicy notes from amaro play an important role in this cocktail well beyond just the name.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2017 by head bartender Julian Cox at Sotto restaurant in Los Angeles, USA.

name: King Street Negroni
garnish: Skewered thick cube of fresh orange flesh
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a ice ball or large cube).
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Island single malt Scotch whisky
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Ginger liqueur
review: A Scotch single malt whisky-based Boulevardier with a touch of ginger spice. Or, perhaps consider this a Negroni for a winter's eve by the fireside. Either way, it's tasty!
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2016 by Günter Windhorst at his Windhorst Bar in Berlin, Germany. Günter says this was his 36th riff of the Negroni , and his original recipe uses 40ml Talisker 10-year-old, 30ml Campari, 10ml Antica Formula, and 10ml Giffard Ginger of the Indies liqueur.

name: Meat Hook
preparation: STIR first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. FLOAT peated whiskey.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
review: This delicious but assertively spirit-forward late-night sipper is more approachable with the added dilution that comes with serving on-the-rock(s) in a small old-fashioned glass.
history: Adapted from a riff on the Red Hook with a splash of peated whiskey, created in 2014 by Shaun Layton at L'Abattoir restaurant in Vancouver, Canada.

name: The Haggis Horns
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 1⁄3 shot	Adriatico Bianco almond milk liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄6 shot	Drambuie liqueur
review: Shaking (rather than stirring) gives this Godfather riff a frothy head which dissipates to leave attractive beads around the edge of the glass. As well as appearance, the aeration that comes with shaking adds life and vitality to this almond and whisky cocktail.
history: Created by yours truly while listening to Naughty Buddha by UK funk band, The Haggis Horns.

name: Et Moi, Je Te Dis... Maud
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Armagnac brandy
5⁄12 shot	Izarra Jaune liqueur
5⁄12 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: An armagnac-laced after-dinner/late-night, spirit-forward sipper that harnesses herbal and maraschino liqueurs. Apologies if you are reading this recipe in ounces, 5/12oz is between 1/3oz (too little) and 15oz (too much).
history:
The name, which literally translates as "And me, I'd tell you... Maud," but should be read as "That's Maud for ya," celebrates a French comedienne, Maud Loty. Nicknamed "La Maud," she starred in dozens of hit vaudeville plays throughout the 1920s and '30s.

This cocktail appears in Georges Gabriel Thenon's 1929 book Cocktails de Paris followed by Maud Loty's signature and the notation, "Grand Prize of Honor at the Champonnal de Cocktail des Artistes de Paris, June 21, 1929. This cocktail was presented by Mile Maud Loty, surrounded by Miles Betty Spelle and Yama and Mr. Dorly."

name: Famous Last Word
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
2⁄3 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
2⁄3 shot	Americano bianco
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A cross between a Last Word and a Tipperary
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Deana Ferguson at her Red Light cocktail bar in Manchester, England.

name: Lord Lucan
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
3⁄4 shot	Lucano amaro
3⁄4 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A tamed and smoked Boulevardier. Lordy, it's good!
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2016 by Andy Aitken and first published on his Proof Cocktails blog.

Lord Lucan (Richard John Bingham), the 7th Earl of Lucan, was a British peer and an Anglo-Irish aristocrat who disappeared after being named as the prime suspect in the bludgeoning to death of his children's nanny and the attempted murder of his wife, Veronica Duncan. This followed the collapse of their marriage and a bitter custody battle, and Veronica named Lucan as the attacker. His blood-stained car was found abandoned, but the police failed to find Lucan or his body. Despite reported sightings around the world, he was declared legally dead in 1999.

name: Oliver South
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1 shot	Lucano amaro
1 shot	Light vermouth amaro (e.g. Cardamaro)
1 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: When I first tried this bittersweet tequila-laced cocktail, I intended to add a dash of orange bitters but mistakenly used Peychaud's and found I liked the extra layer of anis freshness it adds. Both styles of bitters work well, but the orange oils from the garnish are crucial.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Dan Zollman, Boston, MA, USA. Recipe courtesy of Kindred Cocktails.

name: Jabroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
review: Overripe banana delicately influences this tequila-based Negroni.
history: There are numerous riffs on the Negroni called Jabroni, and the origins of this recipe are unknown. However, as "jabroni" is famously one of Dwayne 'The Rock' Johnson's favourite insults, it's likely to have been created for his tequila brand, Teremana.

name: Lucky Luke
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Lucano amaro
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: An after-dinner digestive that you can keep remaking and enjoying into the late hours. Gin's botanicals, the rich vermouth and the amaro make this an invigorating alternative to a Sweet Manhattan.
history: Adapted from the Cocktail Lucano by New York bartender Natale Di Noia.

name: Monte Berico
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Nardini Amaro
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: This bittersweet Manhattan served on-the-rocks is best enjoyed as a digestivo or cleansing late-night tipple.
history: Created in late 2023/early 2024 by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edwards MCR in Oxford, England. Named after the location of the Nardini Distillery on Via Madonna di Monte Berico in Bassano del Grappa, Italy.

name: Classic Vermouth Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄12 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Gomme syrup
2 dash	Boker's bitters
review: As the name promises, this cocktail is all about the vermouth, with the addition of maraschino liqueur and bitters delicately modifying, so their influence is far from obvious. And don't be deceived into thinking the touch of gomme syrup makes this cocktail sweet; it merely contributes mouthfeel to this pleasing aperitivo.
history: Fittingly, the "Vermuth Cocktail" is the first cocktail with vermouth to appear in a recipe book. Although this 1869 recipe in J. Haney's 1869 Steward and Barkeeper's Manual is not so much a cocktail, but simply vermouth served with ice and a lemon zest twist.

name: Golden Pisco Tang
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1 shot	Strega liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Strega shines in this pisco-based riff on the vodka-based Golden Tang.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Zach Schwartz, a fellow Discerning Drinker and shared via a comment on our Golden Tang page.

name: Tobacco Oaxaca Old Fashioned
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Añejo tequila
1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄4 shot	Agave syrup
3 dash	Fee Brothers Turkish Tobacco Bitters
review: Tobacco bitters add a distinctive and very pleasant flavour to the modern classic Oaxaca Old Fashioned.
history: Made at the suggestion of Fee Brother's Jon Spacher who says, "my FAVORITE drink is a Oaxaca Old Fashioned with Fee Bros Tobacco bitters. And I'm not a tobacco guy!"

name: Fogerty
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review:
Spirit-forward and bittersweet. Sometimes that's what life calls for!

If you find Ryan's recipe, which originally calls for a high-strength rye, a tad on the spirituous/bitter side then try serving on-the-rocks to add some dilution, or try my split-whiskey base rendition with saline solution replacing orange bitters:
37.5 Rye whiskey (bottled in bond)
22.5 Bourbon
15 Red bitter liqueur
7.5 White crème de cacao
3 drops Saline solution
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2010 by Ryan Fitzgerald at Beretta in San Francisco and subsequently a popular cocktail at his ABV bar in San Francisco, USA.

name: Semi-Dry Martini
garnish: Lemon zest expressed and discarded. Adorn with skewered olive.
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄12 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
5⁄12 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura (optional)
review: A 3:1 Dry Martini made with a combination of bianco and dry vermouths.

name: Palabra Caliente
garnish: Lime zest twist expressed and discarded. Adorn with skewered Luxardo Maraschino Cherries.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
3⁄4 shot	Corn/maize liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Piment d'Espelette chile liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: As the name suggests, chilli heat adds spice to Last Word riff, inspired by Brent Roe's Taco Belle cocktail.
history: Created by fellow Discerning Drinker, Frederic D., who shared shred this recipe via a comment on our Nixta Liqueur page after being inspired by the Taco Belle recipe also left in a comment on the same page by Brent Roe.

name: Sake Negroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄6 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 1⁄6 shot	Akashi-Tai Daiginjo Genshu sake
1 1⁄6 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A bittersweet aperitivo with sake and vermouth.

name: Strawberry Negroni
garnish: Fresh strawberry, ideally with a mint sprig tip.
preparation: MUDDLE strawberries in base of mixing glass, add other ingredients, stir with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
3 fresh	Strawberries (hulled, small & ripe)
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: Just as it says on the tin, a classic Negroni with strawberry fruitiness. Be sure to use sweet, ripe, small strawberries. (You'll still need to be a Negroni aficionado to appreciate this cocktail's bittersweet fruity deliciousness.)

name: Pince-Nez
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1⁄4 shot	Kirschwasser (cherry) eau-de-vie
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A Zaza/Dubonnet Cocktail No. 1 with a splash of kirschwasser transporting it to a special place.
history: Created late-2023/early 2024 by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Ewards MCR at Oxford, England. Jason says this cocktail is related to the Blackthorn No. 4 in William "Cocktail Bill" Boothby's 1930 World Drinks and How To Prepare Them and the Merry Widow in Albert Stevens Crockett's 1935 The Old Waldorf-Astoria Bar Book.

name: Pear-fect Spritz
preparation: POUR all ingredients into chilled glass and fill glass with ice.
ingredients:
2 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco (chilled)
1 1⁄3 shot	Pear & cognac liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Spritz cocktails don't classically include citrus juice. They instead usually rely on the acidity in white wine to balance the sweetness from the liqueur. So this spritz is apart by its balanced sweet 'n' sourness, along with pear fruitiness.
history: Named due to its being made with pear liqueur, this Spritz was created by our friends at Rémy Cointreau USA.

name: Apple Manhattan
garnish: Apple wedge, apple fan or dehydrated apple slice
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 1⁄6 shot	Apple Schnapps liqueur
5⁄12 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: Rusty gold in colour, this is a flavoursome threesome for bourbon lovers.
history:
Our take on a drink created in the late 1990s by David Marsden at First on First in New York City and latterly popularised by Dale DeGroff. David's original recipe comprised just 2 ingredients, 2 oz Maker's Mark bourbon and 1 oz Berentzen Apfel Korn.
Manhattan cocktail history

name: Cold Comfort
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	White overproof rum
3⁄4 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Take at the first sign of a cold, and then retreat under your bed covers. Repeat dose regularly while symptoms persist. Warning - do not consume with other forms of medication.
history: Discovered in Jamaica in 2001.

name: Apple Blossom Cocktail
garnish: Apple wedge on rim or float dehydrated apple slice
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Concentrated lightly herbal apple with subtle zesty citrus. Quick to make and stupidly simple yet delicious.
history: Adapted from Victor Bergeron's Trader Vic's Bartender's Guide (1972 revised edition).

name: Dirty Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into a chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄12 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth (chilled)
1⁄3 shot	Olive brine (from jarred olives) (chilled)
review:
As with all Martinis, striking a perfect level of dilution and achieving an ice-cold serving temperature (helped by chilling/freezing all ingredients, the glass and garnish) is key. However, a Dirty Martini introduces another element, olive brine, and your choice of olives and accompanying brine will make or break this cocktail. (Beware, olives packed in oil produce a revolting emulsion.) Then there's the question of how much olive brine to use, and personal tastes see this vary from 5ml to 15ml. I've found that my taste is middle of the road at 10ml (⅓oz).
(In place of olive brine, five dashes of The Bitter Truth's Olive Bitters work well.)
history:
Cocktail historian David Wondrich has traced the origins of the Dirty Martini back to 1901 and a bartender called John E. O'Connor, who served a Dry Martini with muddled olives at New York's Waldorf Astoria.

The first written reference to brine being added to a Martini-style cocktail appears in G.H. Steele's 1930 My New Cocktail Book.

Good story: Franklin Delano Roosevelt, the 32nd President, a keen home bartender, is often connected to this cocktail. However, besides a story that Joseph Stalin recommended he sip pickle juice and vodka as a cure for a hangover at the Yalta Conference in 1945, there is no evidence that he used olive brine in his Martinis. Besides, his cocktails were reportedly "horrendous".

name: Freddy Fudpucker
preparation: STIR tequila and orange juice with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. Float Galliano.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3 1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Galliano L'Autentico liqueur
review:
A Harvey Wallbanger made with tequila in place of vodka. Squeeze quality oranges just before making and you'll be amazed just how good this cocktail is.

It's usual to build this drink and 'float' Galliano over the top. However, it's better to separately stir the tequila and orange and then strain over fresh ice. Then add the Galliano.
history:
Basically a Harvey Wallbanger with tequila, this drink is thought to have been created in the mid-1960s by Donato 'Duke' Antone, the bartender also often credited for the Harvey Wallbanger itself.

Read the full story and history of the Harvey Wallbanger.

name: Iced Sake Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Akashi-Tai Daiginjo Genshu sake
1⁄4 shot	Canadian icewine
review: Icewine adds interesting and wonderfully subtle honeyed notes to this Sake Martini.
history: Created in 2004 by yours truly (Simon Difford), London, England.

name: Kir Apéritif
preparation: POUR half the chilled wine into chilled glass. POUR cassis into glass and TOP with rest of the chilled wine.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Bourgogne Aligoté wine white
5⁄6 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
2 1⁄2 shot	Bourgogne Aligoté wine white
review: Traditionally made 1/3 cassis to 2/3 wine, that's too sweet for most modern palates. We recommend a ratio of one part cassis to between five and seven parts Bourgogne Aligoté white wine. The above formula is 6:1 and at this concentration, the mix of blackcurrant and wine is clean, crisp and not too sweet.
history:
The Kir Apéritif is thought to have first been mixed in 1904 by a waiter called Faivre at the Café George, 42 Rue de Montchapet, Dijon, France. It is named after Canon Félix Kir, who as the Mayor of Dijon promoted the drink by serving at civic functions.
Kir and Kir Royale history

name: High Ryeser

With thanks to Bob Cook, a Discerning Drinker, who on 27th October 2020 left a comment with the recipe for this delicious high-proof whiskey, equal parts Manhattan on our Sweet Manhattan page. Many thanks, Bob.

Short for High Proof Rye Manhattan, I originally unimaginatively named this cocktail High Rye Manhattan but another (sadly anonymous) Discerning Drinker commented on this page on this page (see comments below) suggesting "High Ryeser" was a better name. It is!

A truly collaborative cocktail.
history: See Manhattan cocktail history

name: Medium Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass

3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth

review: A classic Martini served perfect and very wet. I prefer mine shaken which is the method Harry specifies in his guide.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Mexican Tea (Hot)
preparation: Place bar spoon in warmed glass. POUR all ingredients into glass and stir.

1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
Top up with	Breakfast tea (hot)
review: Tiffin will never be the same again.

name: Twelve Miles Out Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
3⁄4 shot	Swedish Punsch liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
review: Stir or shake (as originally stipulated in The Savoy Cocktail Book) this cocktail is still boozy. However, it's also wonderfully aromatic with all three ingredients combining harmoniously.
history:
The Twelve Miles Out is one of several Prohibition-era cocktails whose name references the distance from a shore that a nation's territorial waters. During the 18th century this was established as three nautical miles (5.6 km), the distance a cannonball could be shot from the shore to repel incursions. Hence, during Prohibition, US jurisdiction was limited to three miles offshore so allowing the legal supply of alcohol to parties on board boats just outside territorial waters.

As the number of offshore parties grew, the US negotiated agreements with countries such as the UK and France to recognize the right of the American authorities to enforce Prohibition and anti-smuggling laws to an extended 12-mile limit. Predictably, the parties moved further off-shore. On 29th December 1988, President Reagan extended the territorial waters of the United States to 12 miles from 3 miles.

The notoriety of the three-mile and then 12-mile limit to the reach of the Feds during Prohibition led to the Three Miller/Three Mile Limit, the Twelve Miles Out, and the Twelve Mile Limit cocktails.

Recipe adapted from Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book where this cocktail is shaken rather than stirred.

name: Bamboo Cocktail (Stuart's 1904 recipe)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:

1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth

review: Balanced and complex, heavier than Bamboo recipes with dry vermouth.

Adapted from a recipe in Thomas Stuart's 1904 Stuart's Fancy Drinks and How to mix them.
Bamboo Cocktail history.

name: Sin Cyn
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass and lightly STIR.
ingredients:

1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: A single malt whisky laced twist on a Boulevardier with Cynar replacing the familiar Italian red bitter liqueur.
history: Created by Paul Dellevigne at the Red Owl Tavern, Philadelphia, USA.

name: Razzzzzzberry Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
review: Raspberry and vanilla with characteristic dry cranberry fruit.

name: Rob Roy Cocktail
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
8 drop	Bob's Abbotts bitters
review:
Scotch whisky's answer to the Manhattan. The Rob Roy is classically made with Angostura Bitters, but in his 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks, as a footnote below his recipe, David Embury attests "Peychaud, somehow, seems to blend better than Angostura with Scotch."

I find Abbott's Bitters combines more harmoniously with the whisky in this cocktail. Or if not to hand, I use one dash Angostura-style aromatic bitters and one dash Peychaud's/creole bitters. Whatever bitters you use, their inclusion is essential to the balance and complexity of this cocktail.
history:
Named after the Rob Roy operetta about the Scottish folk hero and outlaw Robert Roy MacGregor, which debuted on Broadway near where New York's Waldorf Astoria Hotel used to stand. (The Empire State Building occupies the site today.) Hence, it's not a stretch to believe this cocktail was created at the hotel to serve operagoers and that scotch whisky was appropriately swapped for the usual American whisky in the popular cocktail of the day, a Manhattan.

The New York Times 30th October 1894 review said "the latest work of Harry B. Smith and Reginald De Koven" was "clean, frank, manly, bright, and winesome." The same words could have been used to describe the cocktail, and before David Wondrich uncovered more about this cocktail, then the above was a neat, concise origin story.

It turns out there was a Rob Roy cocktail created some 20 years earlier by New York bartender Edward F. Barry, and this is documented in an interview he gave for the New York Sun 22nd August 1873. "The Rob Roy cocktail is made with a little gum syrup, two dashes of Angostura, a few drops of oychette cordial [orgeat], in a tumbler filled with fine ice, strained." - New York Sun. Sadly, the interview doesn't record what the base spirit was. This earliest known reference is just the first not to confirm or even cast doubt as to the original base spirit in a Rob Roy.

It's worth noting that the first recipe for a scotch whisky-based Manhattan, which appears in Charlie Paul's American and other Drinks, published 1884 in London, bares no reference to the cocktail also being known as a Rob Roy.

name: Roselyn Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

name: Sakini

history: The "Sake Martini" emerged in the 1980s. This recipe by yours truly in November 2016.

name: Turf Club (1935, Albert Stevens Crockett)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 3⁄4 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever

1 dash	Boker's bitters
review: Albert Stevens Crockett's original recipe calls for two-thirds genever to one-third sweet vermouth, but this produces an overly dry cocktail so I've upped the proportion of vermouth to genever. Made with a quality oude genever, this cocktail is almost nutty and makes for an interesting aperitif.
history: Recipe adapted from Albert Stevens Crockett's 1935 The Old Waldorf-Astoria Bar Book.

name: Snyder Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin

review: A 2:1 Dry Martini but with a splash of orange curaçao taking the dry edge off and adding more subtle complexity than orange bitters.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Sumo In A Sidecar
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
2 1⁄2 shot	Akashi-Tai Daiginjo Genshu sake
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Hints of sake but retains the Sidecar style.
history: See: Sidecar history.

name: Ti Punch
garnish: The lime disc in the drink is garnish enough but also consider expressing a lime zest twist over the drink and then discarding.
preparation:
Traditionally the limes used to make this drink are not cut into slices or wedges. Instead, a round disc is cut from the side of the fruit. These are cut large enough that some of the fruit's flesh backs the peel of the disc.

POUR the rum and sugar into glass. Then SQUEEZE the lime disc between finger and thumb before dropping into the drink. This expresses the oil from the skin and little of the juice into the Ti'Punch. STIR and consider adding ice - either one or two large cubes depending on glass size, or preferably, a small chunk of block ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Rhum Clément Blanc
1⁄4 shot	Clément Sirop de Canne
1 slice	Lime (fresh)
review: As the name suggests, Martinique's national cocktail is deliciously punchy – traditionally made with 50% alc./vol. rhum agricole. And, even if you choose to add ice, then dilution is negligible. However, the all-important sugar cane juice (not sugar syrup made from processed sugar) adds flavour and mellows the rum, so yes, it's punchy but it's also very pleasing to drink.
history:
Named "Ti", Creole for the French word 'petit', this is literally a small rum punch, and unlike most rum punches, it is not lengthened with water or juice – and often without ice, despite the warm climate from where it originates.

It is the national cocktail of the French islands of Martinique and Guadeloupe, where "Ti" is pronounced "Tee". It is also popular in Réunion, Maurice, Haiti, French Guiana and other French-speaking Caribbean islands. On these islands, it's often drunk straight without adding ice and chased by a large glass of chilled water (called a 'crase' in Martinique).

The earliest known written mention appears as a "yon Ti Punch" in an 1890 book, Two Years in the West Indies by Lafcadio Hearn, who was a travel writer and recounted his time in Martinique.

name: Tipperary No.1
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
review: Chartreuse fans will love this Irish whiskey-forward nightcap.
history: Adapted from a recipe that first appeared in Hugo R. Ensslin's 1916 Recipes for Mixed Drinks where he stipulates equal parts.

name: Turf Club
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Simple but very tasty, equal parts old tom gin and sweet vermouth with aromatic bitters. Winter's original 1884 recipe calls for "Peruvian bitters" - I found 3 dashes of Peruvian Cortesano Amargo Bitters Aromatic work well if you have them; alternatively, use a dash less of aromatic bitters (e.g. Angostura).
history:
A sibling, or at least cousin, of the Martinez and the Martini, the Turf Club is or could be, the first cocktail to combine gin and vermouth. It makes its first written appearance in George Winter's 1884 How To Mix Drinks–Bar-Keeper's Handbook as the "Turf Club" with later books most often merely titling the drink "Turf".

The name Turf Club refers to the gentlemen's clubs of the late 1800s-early 1900s, which operated as a combined restaurant, bar, meeting place, and gambling den for the gentlemen of the day. Captains of industry and the aristocracy have always liked horse racing, and where folk gather to watch racing, there is bound to be betting. Many a 'turf accountant' (bookmaker) frequented such clubs, and many a Turf Cocktail was consumed.

One of the most famous of these gentlemen's clubs, The Turf Club, stood at the corner of Madison Avenue and 26th Street in New York City. The building, Jerome Mansion, had pedigree, being the former home of Lady Randolph Churchill, the American mother of Winston Churchill - a man I suspect would have appreciated a well-made Turf Club cocktail.

name: Sake Martini

history: Adapted from a drink discovered in 2005 at Bellini, Auckland, New Zealand.

review: Vermouth adds depth of flavour to aromatic pear vodka and floral elderflower liqueur.

name: Pear Tree Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE first 2 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with sparkling wine.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Pear-flavoured vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
Top up with	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Aromatic pear vodka and elderflower liqueur paired with biscuity champagne.

name: Islander
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into a chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Blended Scotch whisky

review: Vermouth-based and bittersweet with anise and fennel, and depending on your scotch, also faint smokiness.

name: Little Italy
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.

1 3⁄4 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
review: This rye whiskey-based, Manhattan-like, bittersweet cocktail is a great digestivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2005 by Audrey Saunders for the opening menu of the Pegu Club in New York City, USA.

name: Starry Night
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.

1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
review: Delicate pear and aromatic maraschino over a dry wine base.
history: Created in 2008 by Jamie Boudreau at Vessel, Seattle, USA.

name: Red Hook
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
review:
This Manhattan-like cocktail is rightly recognised as being a contemporary classic cocktail. Also great served on-the-rocks in an old-fashioned glass.

Previous recipe (updated November 2023):
60ml (2oz) Straight rye whiskey
15ml (½oz) Punt E Mes
15ml (½oz) Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
history: A riff on the classic Brooklyn Cocktail created in 2003 by Vincenzo Errico at Milk & Honey, New York City, USA and named after a neighbourhood of Brooklyn.

name: Dutch Count Negroni
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass and STIR.
ingredients:
1 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: Genever's flavoursome character adds malty notes to an otherwise traditional Negroni.
history:
Discovered in 2011 at Vesper Bar, Amsterdam, Netherlands and a cocktail then promoted by Bols Genever.
See: Negroni cocktail history.

name: Mezzo E Mezzo
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Nardini Rosso
1 1⁄2 shot	Rabarbaro liqueur
2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Slightly on the bitter side of bittersweet, this classic aperitivo is light and palate cleansing. Best made with equal parts Nardini Rosso, Nardini Rabarbaro and soda.
history: Originally and properly made with equal parts Nardini Rosso, Nardini Rabarbaro and soda water, this drink originates from the famous Grapperia Nardini on the Ponte Vecchio where Nardini Rosso was first served with soda water in the 1920s. In the 1970s a drinker tried Nardini Rosso with a dash of Nardini’s rhubarb liqueur. The combination became increasingly popular, and as its popularity grew, so the dash became larger until the mixture reached equal parts Nardini Rosso and Rabarbaro.

name: Gin Sangaree (Sangre)
preparation: SHAKE gin and sugar with ice and strain into chilled glass. Lastly POUR the port wine which will sink through drink and mix, leaving a thin clear layer at the top.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 shot	Tawny port
review: Either drink through the layers or stir before consuming. Fabulously old-school in style, this sweetened port and old tom gin drink resembles chilled mulled wine.
history: The Sangaree takes its name from the Spanish word for blood, Sangre. The drink's origins date back to the early 1700s and it first appears in writing in a 1736 issue of the British Gentleman's Magazine, "... a punch seller in the Strand had devised a new punch made of strong Madeira wine and called Sangre".

name: White Negroni
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and STIR.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
review: Wayne Collins, this drink's creator, originally used equal parts as is usual for a classic Negroni and after trying various other formulations, I've found this works best. Wayne also specified a grapefruit zest twist and this makes the cocktail. However, be warned, this is a drink for aficionados of bittersweet aperitifs and gentian.
history: Created in 2001 by Wayne Collins at VinExpo. Bordeaux, France using Plymouth Gin for Nick Blacknell, then brand director of Plymouth Gin. Later, Simon Ford, who was the Plymouth Gin ambassador, introduced the drink to Audrey Saunders in the early days of her Pegu Club where the drink became a hit on the menu.

name: Violet Negroni cocktail
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and STIR.

1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2 shot	Byrrh Grand Quinquina
1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
review: Bittersweet with a strong hint of gentian. A great aperitif.
history: Created in 2013 by Mathieu Sabbagh of Pernod Ricard.

name: Grosvenor cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ginseng liqueur
1 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
1⁄6 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
review: On the bitter side of bittersweet, this is a great aperitivo cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe by Alex Kammerling. He originally used an extra 1/2 shot of Kamm & Sons but as it is his brand we'd not criticise him for a generous pour.

name: Bijou Cocktail (inspired by Lawlor's 1895 recipe)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review:
A boozy sipper of a cocktail that's medium dry with honeyed richness. Gin-based with zesty orange freshness and sweet vermouth adding deep herbal complexity. A great after-dinner cocktail that also works well on-the-rocks.

This should not be confused with the more commonplace equal parts gin, Chartreuse and vermouth Bijou which first appeared in Harry Johnson's 1900 Bartender's Manual.
history: Adapted from the original equal parts gin, Grand Marnier and sweet vermouth recipe in C. F. Lawlor's 1895 book The Mixicologist in which he describes this as "a delicious drink." Handily adding, "Grand Marnier can also be served in a pony-glass like any liqueur." Remember, Louis-Alexandre Marnier-Lapostolle only created Grand Marnier 15 years earlier and it must have taken a while for the new liqueur to find its way from France to the Grand Hotel in Cincinnati where Lawlor worked, so he was commenting on what was then an exciting new product.

name: Tribute
preparation: SPRAY violet liqueur onto inside surface of glass and set aside. STIR cognac with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄6 shot	Crème de violette liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3 1⁄2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Originally made with Martell Cordon Bleu, this sophisticated champagne cocktail has delicate floral notes.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Matthias Lataille at The Beat, London, England.

name: White Old Fashioned
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄3 shot	Clément Sirop de Canne

review: Joerg makes this cocktail using Bacardi Neo but it also works well with the easier to obtain Bacardi Carta Blanca. If you haven't any Sexy Bitters then try with a dash of orange bitters.
history:
Created in 2016 by Joerg Meyer at Le Lion - Bar de Paris, Hamburg, Germany.

For a more detailed history of the Old-Fashioned cocktail, along with additional recipes, see our page.

name: Apairoteef

preparation:

*Special ingredient #1 = Cardamom & Pear Shrub made as follows:
400ml Merlet pare

7g Cardamom pods
5ml Vanilla curd
75ml White balsamic
10g Citric acid
10g Tartaric acid
150g Caster sugar
100g Water
Blend for 5 minutes and super strain.
ingredients:
1 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1 shot	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)

review: Invigorating, refreshing and very amusing – we do like a pun.

name: Pink Americano

name: Harvest Cocktail

1 1⁄2 shot	Light vermouth amaro (e.g. Cardamaro)

review: Boozy with notes of spiced apple brandy. A great after-dinner sipper.

name: Three Blind Mice

1 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro

review: Stirred down and boozy, corn notes from the whiskey are amplified by the bittersweet aperitif liqueur and aromatised wine.

name: Negroni Bianco

review: This white Negroni is not quite as dry and bitter as a traditional red Negroni and has additional pleasing creamy honeysuckle notes.
history: The creation of this cocktail was inspired by Wayne Collins' White Negroni and made possible by the launch of Luxardo Bitter Bianco liqueur in 2016.

name: Amber Negroni (Difford's recipe)
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and lightly STIR.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Luxardo Bitter Bianco liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: As the name suggests, this riff on a classic Negroni is amber in colour with honeyed notes and is not quite as bitter as the classic red version.
history: Created in February 2017 by yours truly after the launch of Luxardo's Bitter Bianco liqueur.

name: Bamboo Cocktail (with Palo Cortado Sherry)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Palo cortado sherry
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Dry, vinous, and best enjoyed as an aperitif.
history: Bamboo Cocktail history.

name: Sbagliato With Tonic
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass and lightly stir.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3 1⁄3 shot	Tonic water (salty lemon)
review: Lightly bittersweet and superbly refreshing, a tasty aperitif cocktail.
history: This adaptation of a classic cocktail recipe is to a Tony Conigliaro 2017 formulation.

name: It's Hartnell Damn It!
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1 shot	Swedish Punsch liqueur
1 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
review: An equal parts riff on a Doctor No.1 using white wine acidity in place of lime juice. Tangy and slightly sharp in flavour with more than a hint of Swedish punch funkiness.
history: Created by yours truly as a thank you to Doctor Salt, who was left in a "pother of Whovian pedantry" due to my misspelling of another good Doctor's name on our Cocktail of the Day for 23rd November 2017. The actor who portrayed the first Dr Who is William Hartnell (not Hartness), who incidentally also played Sgt Grimshaw in the first-ever Carry-On film, Carry on Sergeant.

name: Youth & Treachery
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: This spirituous bittersweet aperitif is reminiscent of a White Negroni, but based on tequila rather than gin.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2017 by Jason Simplot at Rumba, Seattle, USA. Jason's original spec called for equal parts El Tesoro Platinum, Suze and Carpano Bianco.

Jason says, "Essentially a white Rosita, created for a guest who wanted a tequila cocktail on the bitter side. Slightly spicy, kinda sweet and gentian-heavy. I thought I named this after a 'Modern Life Is War' song, one of my favorite punk bands, but upon a little research, they never titled a song with the aforementioned phrase. Which is too bad. It's fitting for not only their casse-toi brand of aggressive punk but also for this slightly aggressive and feisty cocktail."

name: Smoky Mizu
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
2⁄3 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
2⁄3 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
review: Dry, lightly bitter and delicately spirituous. An aperitif-style sipper.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2017 by Andrew 'Drew' Chigorimbo at J Boroski, Hong Kong. Drew's original recipe calls for Chivas Mizunara, hence the drinks name.

name: Jersey's Best Dancers
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review:
Three equal-part ingredients, the holy grail of cocktail recipes, makes for a dry spirituous apéritif cocktail. This cocktail is very similar to a Maximiliano.

Incidentally, Jersey's Best Dancers is the third studio album by the New Jersey band Lifetime (released June 1997).
history:
Adapted from a 2017 recipe by Charlie Martin at Eclipse Restaurant, Saint Louis, USA, who says, "I wanted a version of the Negroni that used mezcal as the base spirit and Suze as the bittering agent. Whipped this drink up and now it's on our menu! Rarely you nail it on the first try but this one is perfect!"

Charlie's original recipe calls for equal parts: Suze, Vida Mezcal and Carpano Dry vermouth.

name: La Alianza
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1 shot	Lillet-style Rosé light quinquina
1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
review: Mezcal sings in this dry aperitif-style cocktail with delicate vinous notes and light gentian bitterness.

name: Lo Stregone
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 shot	Strega liqueur
1 shot	Red bitter soda
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Red bitter soda (originally Crodino) and Strega make a very tasty and very Italian aperitivo. Go easy on the aromatic bitters.
history: Adapted from a recipe by Matteo Schianchi.

name: Remind Me Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bepi Tosolini Grappa di Moscato
2⁄3 shot	Averna Amaro
1⁄2 shot	Mandarine Napoleon liqueur
review: A delicious stirred down, grappa laced aperitif or summertime digestif.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2018 by Andre Tarantino at Collage Cocktail Bar, Barcelona, Spain, who says "this cocktail was inspired by the song Remind Me by Patrice Rushen." His preference is Grappa Poli as it "gives a very sharp feeling to the cocktail."

name: High Kick
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
3⁄4 shot	Mentzendorff Kümmel liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: Plenty of dilution is key to this caraway and Scotch dominated cocktail that is sure to appeal to Kummel fanciers.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Arthur Tarling and first published in his brother's (William James "Billy" Tarling) 1937 Café Royal Bar Book.

name: Little Cuba
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
1⁄2 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: Chocolate and raisin flavours with delicate herbal spice add complexity to this Rum Negroni.
history: Created in 2019 by Lisa Kempen, Head Bartender at Deadshot in Auckland, New Zealand.

name: Count Mast
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Jägermeisteror other German amaro
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: This three equal part cocktail makes for a perfect aperitivo.
history: A signature cocktail promoted by Jägermeister.

name: Piña Clara
preparation: THROW all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄3 shot	Pineapple sugar syrup
1 2⁄3 shot	Coconut water
review: This delicious and light long drink harnesses the classic combination of coconut, rum and pineapple.
history: Adapted from a cocktail discovered in October 2019 at Soho House, 76 Dean Street, London, England.

name: Burnt Fuselage
garnish: Lemon zest twist (or orange zest twist)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: Cognac and Grand Marnier are well-suited bedfellows in this spirit-forward "stiff steadier". Dry vermouth combines with these surprisingly well. Adding balance and herbal complexity.
history:
The Burnt Fuselage first appears in the "Cocktails Around Town" section of Harry MacElhone's 1927 Barflies and Cocktails where he lists cocktails of regulars ("Men About Town") at his Harry's New York Bar.

To quote MacElhone, "Chuck Kerwood takes to the air so frequently that he likes a stiff steadier when he comes down to earth. The famous flying man calls his concoction the 'Burnt Fuselage'. And believe me, 1/3 Grand Marnier, 1/3 Cognac, and 1/3 French vermouth, and your own fuselage will be warm, to say the least." From Philadelphia, USA Colonel C.W. (Chuck) Kerwood, was President of the International League of Aviators and was apparently known as the "wild man of aviation."

name: Old Bank
garnish: Orange zest twist & Luxardo maraschino cherry on a spoon
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Bigallet China China Amer
1⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: Zesty orange, liquorice and honey combine with bourbon in this delicious riff on a classic Old Fashioned.
history: Adapted from a cocktail discovered in December 2019 at the Bank Hotel in Stockholm where this is the signature Old Fashioned at the Papillon Bar.

name: Perennial
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & orange wheel slice
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Rhubarb flavoured vodka
2⁄3 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄2 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
review: Gently bitter rhubarb - a very tasty aperitivo.

name: Honey Margarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: Strictly speaking, as this cocktail doesn't contain an orange liqueur it is not a Margarita but should properly be termed a "Honey Tequila Sour". We decided Honey Margarita had more of a ring to it. Very tasty it is too.

name: Holiday Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄6 shot	Americano bianco
review: A riff on the classic Tuxedo.
history: Adapted from a recipe purloined from Jared Brown/Sipsmith's 2019 Sip 100 Gin Cocktails with only 3 ingredients.

name: Tsipouro Negroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	O/Purist Tsipouro
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: Just as it says on the tin, it's a Negroni but based on Greek grape-based Tsipouro.
history: Adapted from a 2019 recipe created by Dimitris Kiakos at To Lokali, Athens, Greece.

name: Reverse Manhattan
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: This Reverse Sweet Manhattan is a delicious aperitivo while a regular Sweet Manhattan is more a late-night affair.
history: Manhattan cocktail history

name: Gnome
garnish: Float mint leaf or peg mint sprig bouquet to rim
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
2⁄3 shot	Fino sherry
review: An after-dinner tipple with gin botanicals and rich herbal flavours dried with fino sherry.
history: Created in May 2020 by yours truly while experimenting with David Embury's Nome Martini.

name: Lunes Aperitivo
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
2⁄3 shot	Americano bianco
1⁄6 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
review: On the dry side of bittersweet. As the name suggests this is intended to be drunk as the first aperitivo of the week, preferably accompanied by olives.
history: Created in June 2020 by yours truly and inspired by Jeremy Oertel's Cloud 9 cocktail .

name: Negroni del Professore
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Rabarbaro liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Centerbe liqueur
review: Bittersweet and Negroni-like with deep herbal, rooty, bark bitterness.
history: Created and made for us by Ivan Patrun, Bar Manager at Bulk, Milan, Italy when we were lucky enough to dine there in November 2019. A memorable aperitivo followed by an equally special meal.

name: MonteNegroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄6 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review:
While the proportions of the classic Negroni are accepted as being equal parts, with some boozehounds slightly upping the gin, the proportions of this amaro-dolce riff vary tremendously. Recipes include equal parts to twice as much amaro as the other ingredients, to one-and-a-half parts gin to one part each of the other ingredients. Having tried them all (well, all I could find/come up with). I've settled on this 7:6:5 formula which is amaro-forward, yet with assertive gin notes and not being overly sweet or boozy. However, you may prefer this recipe from Montenegro:
40ml (1⅓oz) Amaro Montenegro
20ml (⅔oz) Gin
20ml (⅔oz) Rosso (sweet) Vermouth
2 drops Aromatic bitters
history:
Rudi Carraro, global brand ambassador for Amaro Montenegro, has his own version of the MonteNegroni consisting:
40ml Amaro Montenegro
25ml Brooklyn Gin
20ml Select Aperitivo

name: Longshoreman
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (perhaps over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
1⁄2 shot	Averna Amaro
review: Big flavours combine harmoniously in this Manhattan riff which substitutes bitters for an amaro.
history: Adapted from a recipe (originally served straight-up) created by Abigail Deirdre Gullo at SoBou, New Orleans, USA. Inspired by the Red Hook, one of a series of Manhattan-style cocktails named after districts of New York City.

name: Ostend Fizz Royale
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Kirschwasser (cherry) eau-de-vie
5⁄12 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
3 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: As Jason, the reader who created this sent us this recipe says, "A champagne charged riff on the classic Ostend Fizz this is a good alternative to a Kir Royale."
history: Created in 2020 by Jason Clapham in Oxford, England.

name: After Supper
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: As the name suggests, this slightly sweet citrusy-apricot cocktail is best enjoyed after a hearty meal.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Hardy Grunter
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Amontillado sherry
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
review: Medium-dry sherry lightly sweetened and aromatised with sweet vermouth and maraschino liqueur. If you prefer a tad drier, then sub 15ml / ½oz of amontillado sherry for fino sherry. Or do like we do, and mix 50/50 amontillado and fino.
history: Created in 2020 by Neil Grayshon as "a nice way to help with an inventory problem." Neil's original recipe calls for 2oz Delicado amontillado, ¾oz Discarded vermouth, and ¼oz Luxardo maraschino.

name: Fantasticus
garnish: None or float one tiny mint leaf from the tip of a sprig
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Italicus liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Delicious bergamot zesty freshness with subtle underlying rum. Great as an after-dinner freshening digestivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Patrick Pistolesi from Drink Kong in Rome, Italy, originally with 30ml Italicus, 25ml Veritas rum and 5ml sugar syrup.

name: Whiskey Dry & Lime
garnish: Drop squeezed lime wedges into drink
preparation: POUR and squeeze ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
2 wedge	Lime (fresh)
4 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
review: Irish Whiskey and ginger ale with a couple of squeezes of lime. The hint of lime takes the sweet edge of the ginger ale to produce a light and refreshing long drink.

name: Amaroni
preparation: POUR all ingredients into chilled ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄6 shot	Angostura di Amaro
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: Piney notes in the gin are amplified in this bitter-bittersweet riff on a classic Negroni.
history: A cocktail promoted by The House of Angostura.

name: Pinga com Mel
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Cachaça
5⁄12 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: Cachaça-laced, bite-sized, and delicious with rich smoothing honey balancing sharp zesty lime.
history: Pinga com Mel is a popular drink in Brasil in work-a-day bars, especially on cold days. It's also drunk to help alleviate flu and some even add garlic. The Pinga com Mel is considered one of the possible origins of the Caipirinha and so popular is the drink that in Brasil there are also some bottled versions and Busca Vida (17% alc./vol.) is popular in nightclubs.

name: Dublin Spider Highball
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
3 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
review: Ginger ale and aromatic bitters lengthen and colour Dublin's finest – blended whiskey.

name: Dominicana
preparation: STIR first 2 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. Carefully float lightly whipped cream (shake cream in the container to aerate prior to pouring).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1 1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review:
Just three ingredients – rum-laced coffee liqueur topped by a velvety layer of indulgent chilled cream. Basically, a rum-based White Russian but that description doesn't do justice to this delicious cocktail that's best appreciated in place of a dessert after a meal.

Consider adding sugar syrup if using a very dry coffee liqueur.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Sasha Petraske during the early years of his iconic Milk & Honey bar in New York City, USA.

name: Lefkó Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	O/Purist Tsipouro
1⁄2 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
1⁄4 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: Martini-esque in style but gin's juniper-led botanical character is replaced by a Greek grape distillate (Tsipouro). Enhanced vinous notes and flavoursome acidity provided by a splash of dry white wine (ideally Dafni or even Assyrtiko but Sauvignon Blanc also works well). A spoon of honey (again preferably Greek orange blossom) provides the all-important balancing richness of flavour.
