history: Created by yours truly in January 2021. Due to the use of a grape spirit and white wine, this Martini-like cocktail was going to be called a Greek White Martini but then discovered "Lefkó" is the Greek word for the colour white. It is also appropriately a synonym for white Greek grape varieties used in winemaking.

name: Bali Rum Trader
garnish: Float banana chip or peg to rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
5⁄6 shot	Green banana liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Pineapple juice
review: Looks like swamp water but tastes delicious.
history: Created by yours truly thanks to the suggestion of David Porter in a comment on our Bali Trader page.

name: On the Med
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄6 shot	Italicus liqueur
4 shot	Mediterranean tonic water
review: For the complete "on the Med" experience, you may want to use a Mediterranean-style gin, but we prefer a London dry style so perhaps making this a Brit On The Med.
history: Created in March 2021 by yours truly at the Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: Irish Buck
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
review: Simple but surprisingly delicious and very refreshing thanks to cleansing lime sourness.
history: Bucks are a family of cocktails which emerged during Prohibition and always contain ginger ale or ginger beer. Incidentally, that's why we named our very fury ginger cat 'Buck'.

name: Occasion
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1 shot	Tawny port
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
review: A dessert cocktail designed to complement Cuban cigars.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Alejandro Bolivar, head bartender at El Floridita in Havana, Cuba for La Casa del Habano in Montreal, Canada, where Alejandro has visited during numerous summer trips.

name: Big Boss
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Disaronno amaretto
4 drop	Bob's Vanilla bitters
review: A Godfather made with bourbon is "The Boss" so it stands to reason that with bottled-in-bond rye, it is the Big Boss.
history: Created in April 2021 by yours truly.

name: Yale Fence
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: The combination of apple brandy, gin and vermouth produce a delicious spirit-forward cocktail with unexpected delicious creamy vanilla notes.
history:
An exhumed classic recommended to me by Jason E. Clapham of the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, who told us that this recipe was eponymously named after the Yale Fence which crossed the Yale University campus in Connecticut, USA. The three-rail fence was the main social hub for students at the university with various sections reserved for students of different years, clubs, teams and societies. A carved stone plaque, "The Old Yale Fence Stood Here", now commemorates the fence which stood for 51 years until its demise in 1888, leading to the formation of The Yale Fence Club. Jason surmises that the cocktail "was probably created at the Yale Fence Club in the early 1900s."

This cocktail first appears in David Embury's 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks.

name: Rye Boulevardier
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: A rye whiskey-based Boulevardier with both the generous measure of rye and its high alc./vol. making this a boozy but tasty aperitivo or digestivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Abigail Gullo at Ben Paris restaurant in The State Hotel, Seattle, USA.

name: L'agreste
garnish: Rosemary sprig and lime slice wheel
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bepi Tosolini Grappa di Moscato
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: A frozen Grappa Canchanchara – delicious.

name: Strawberry Inn Grappa Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bepi Tosolini I Legni Rovere grappa
1 shot	Giffard Fraise des Bois liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: As the name suggests, a sour laced with characterful grappa, flavoured with rich ripe strawberry. Dry and complex rather than sweet and one-dimensional.

name: S 'n' Emm
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Savoia Americano Rosso
5⁄6 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄2 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
review: So named due to originally being made with Savoia, Mezcal and Montenegro. On the bitter side of bittersweet but eases with the dilution that comes with contemplative consumption.
history: Created September 2021 by yours truly at the Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: Mezcal Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice or large cube).
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1 2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
4 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters
review: With gin, my go-to stirred Dry Martini recipe is five-to-one, but that's way too much when using mezcal – a Fifty-Fifty Martini is more befitting. Rather than straight-up, I also prefer my Mezcal Martinis on-the-rock(s).
history: Recipe by yours truly in September 2020.

name: Dunlop Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Amontillado sherry
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A punchy dry aperitivo – sherry-influenced rum with a dash of bitters.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Raimbaut
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
review: Beautifully balanced and aromatic. A cheeky little aperitif. This cocktail vaguely resembles The Savoy Corpse Reviver No. 2, though the absence of lemon juice and absinthe makes it a very different cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Ross Simmonds of the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England [I reduced volume by 33% to fit a Nick & Nora glass in place of the original coupe]. This cocktail is eponymously named after the 12th century troubadour, Count Raimbaut of Orange.

name: Fake I.D.
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Dark/black/blackstrap rum
2⁄3 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1⁄6 shot	Cinnamon syrup
review: An after-dinner late night sipper which harnesses rum's character and pairs it with artichoke amaro and a touch of rich cinnamon spice.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England. Jason's original recipe calls for Plantation Original Dark rum.

name: Sharon
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Manzanilla sherry
1 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review: A bittersweet vinious palate cleanser.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2018 by Tristan Willey at Momofuku Ssäm Bar in New York City, USA.

name: Quill Riff
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Luxardo Bitter Bianco liqueur
review: A gin-forward and bittersweet cleansing aperitivo.
history: A riff on the classic Quill cocktail created in 2020 by Keith Meicher, head bartender at Sepia restaurant in Chicago, USA.

name: Santana
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
3⁄4 shot	Amaro Santoni
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
review: Bittersweet, faintly floral flavours with characterful tequila.
history: Created in November 2021 by yours truly at the Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Tuscan Negroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Amaro Santoni
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: Floral amaro adds a subtle but distinctive note to this Negroni.

name: Rose (French style) No. 2
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Kirschwasser (cherry) eau-de-vie
1⁄2 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
review: I've reduced the proportions of this cocktail by one-third as I believe, where such richly flavoured spirituous cocktails are concerned, less is more.
history: Adapted from a recipe by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, in turn, an adaption of a recipe in William "Cocktail Bill" Boothby's 1930 Swallows : World's Drinks And How To Mix Them.

name: Zegroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	10+ year old blended rum
2⁄3 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review: Vinous bittersweet vanilla massaged oak rum.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Mark Huang of Taiwan while competing in the "Gentleman's Drinks & Fancy Tipples" round in Diageo's World Class Global competition in 2011. Mark won the round with this cocktail which was originally made with Zacapa 23 rum, hence the name for this riff on a classic Negroni.

name: Red Apple Manhattan
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄3 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
review: A calvados-based Red Hook. It has a touch of apple but a bit less bite than Vincenzo Errico's bottled-in-bond rye whiskey-based original.
history:
Created in March 2022 by yours truly after picking up a bottle of bottled-in-bond applejack when making a Red Hook rather than the intended rye whiskey. I then swapped applejack for calvados.
Manhattan cocktail history

name: Smok'n Rob Roy
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
4 drop	Bob's Abbotts bitters
review: As the name might suggest, a Rob Roy made with Islay single malt whisky.

name: Pendennis Club Cocktail
garnish: Luxardo Maraschino cherry dropped into cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: This bite-sized spirit-forward cocktail is as equally good as an aperitif as it is an after-dinner or late-night tipple.
history: Named after the Pendennis Club in Louisville, Kentucky, the first known reference to this cocktail appears in the "Seductive American Cocktails" appendix in William "Cocktail Bill" Boothby's 1908 The World's Drinks and How to Mix Them book.

name: Auto Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
5⁄6 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: A Dry Martini on steroids with flavours pumped-up yet harmonious.
history: Adapted from the Auto Cocktail recipe in Jacques Straub's 1914 Drinks.

name: Morning Dew
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Framboise/raspberry eau-de-vie
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe
1 2⁄3 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
review: Minty fresh with light white wine acidity and subtle ripe raspberry notes. A brilliantly refreshing cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created for Giffard's West Cup in 2022 by Claudio Bedini from Sydney, Australia. This cocktail won the Australian final of the competition to earn its originator a place in the final, where he came tantalisingly close to taking one of the top three places. Claudio's original recipe comprised: 35ml Giffard Menthe Pastille, 15ml raspberry eau-de-vie, and 70ml Val de Loire sauvignon blanc wine.

name: Savoy Corpse Reviver (by Joe Gilmore)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
review: A bite-sized brandy-laced after dinner mint chocolate. Refreshing, tasty and arguably, even aids digestion.
history: A riff on the classic Corpse Reviver created in 1954 by Joe Gilmore at The American Bar at The Savoy Hotel in London, England.

name: Wallick
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
review: An orange curaçao-influenced Fifty-Fifty Martini.
history: This cocktail first appears in Hugo R. Ensslin's 1916-17 Recipes for Mixed Drinks and is named after the hotel where he worked for the better part of his bartending career. Opened in 1910, The Wallick Hotel sat at the corner of 43rd Street and Broadway in New York City and was owned by the brothers Louis C. and Adrian L. Wallick.

name: Amalienborg
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
review: Tastes boozy but this aperitivo/digestivo is relatively light in alcohol.
history: Named after the official residence of the Danish royal family, this recipe comes from Axel Sørensen's black, bar notebook "Lommebogen" ISBN 978-87-995886-0-2. Axel Sørensen, was a bartender at Café de la Reine in Copenhagen during the late 1930s and his granddaughter inherited his pocketbook containing his cocktail recipes and other notes. Henrik Steen Petersen, from the former "Moltkes Bar" in Copenhagen, borrowed this notebook, photographed it and has since published the notebook to make it available to all.

name: Un-Ford-Gettable
garnish: Grapefruit zest twist (discarded) and skewered green olive
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄12 shot	Italicus liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Fino sherry
review: Bone dry and zesty – just like a Martini should be.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Ago Perrone at The Connaught Bar in London, England and originally based on Fords Gin, hence the name.

name: Old Martinique Special
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄12 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
review: Drinks writer, Robert Simonson describes this as "basically an Improved Martini Cocktail." He's right.
history: An adaptation of a 1930s cocktail from New York City's Hotel Martinique courtesy of The Mix with Robert Simonson, March, 2023.

name: Allies Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin (from freezer)
1 2⁄3 shot	Ambrato/ambre/amber vermouth (chilled)
1⁄24 shot	Mentzendorff Kümmel liqueur
review: A Fifty-Fifty Martini with a touch of kümmel. Your choice of dry vermouth (you need a characterful one) and temperature are key to this cocktail's success. Freeze/chill all ingredients and the glass prior to mixing and it can be brilliant.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Hugo R. Ensslin's 1917 Recipes for Mixed Drinks (2nd Edition).

name: Armour
preparation: THROW (or stir) all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A Bamboo but with rosso (sweet) vermouth in place of dry vermouth to produce a cocktail that's perhaps more digestivo than aperitivo.
history: The Armour first emerges in the anonymously written 1898 book Cocktails... How to make them with an equal parts sherry to Italian vermouth with orange bitters recipe.

name: Coronation Cocktail (Jacques Straub's)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: One-part gin to two-part aromatised wines produces an approachable vinous alternative to a Dry Martini.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Jacques Straub's 1914 book Drinks.

name: Me, Myself & I
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. (Better over good cubed ice than block ice.)
ingredients:
1 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
1 shot	Italicus liqueur
review: An M & M with Italian citrus-led self-indulgence.
history: Created in June 2023 by yours truly at the Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: Stregotto
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice). Briefly stir.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Strega liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
2 2⁄3 shot	Chinotto
review: Bittersweet and refreshing as either an aperitivo or digestivo.
history: Created by the good folk at Strega and discovered at BCB Berlin in November 2022.

name: Orancio Negroni
garnish: Orange zest twist expressed & discarded, adorn with 2 skewered green grapes and 1 red
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Savoia Orancio
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄3 shot	Italicus liqueur
review: Other Negronis are garnished with an orange slice or twist, but as the name suggests, this one has a complex orange medley at its core and is garnished with a trio of grapes.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in September 2023 by Roberta Mariani, Global Advocacy Director at Ital Spirits, London, England.

name: Pumpkin Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Pumpkin spice syrup
review: Pumpkin spice syrup works surprisingly brilliantly in an otherwise classic Daiquiri.
history: Created by yours truly in October 2023 ahead of Halloween.

name: Marconi Wireless
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into a glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A dry and refreshing calvados-based apéritif or digestif served frappé, adding to the cleansing nature of this cocktail.
history:
Named after Guglielmo Giovanni Maria Marconi (1874 – 1937), an Italian electrical engineer and inventor who's best-known for creating a radio wave-based wireless telegraph system and is credited for being the inventor of radio.

Recipe adapted from Albert Stevens Crockett's 1931 Old Waldorf Bar Days. Earlier in the book, under the heading "Big Events Spirituously Memorialized", Crockett says the Marconi Wireless "first sprang across the Bar of the Waldorf when the ancestor of the radio began to raise its ghostly voice". That's as maybe, but the Marconi Wireless is a riff on Jacques Straub's 1913 Marconi served frappé with the addition of a couple of dashes of orange bitters.

name: Orchid Thief
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
review: A Bamboo and Chrysanthemum mashup that makes for a delicious aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Chip Tyndale at Dutch Kills in New York City, USA.

name: Alchemystique
garnish: Orange zest twist expressed and discarded. Adorn with dried coconut (preferably toasted)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 shot	Lucano amaro
1 shot	Coconut water
review: Nutty coconut nestles harmoniously with Scotch whiskey and liquorice-forward amaro. Orange zest adds vitality and freshness.
history: Created in March 2024 by yours truly at The Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Montana (Albert Stevens Crockett, 1931)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 shot	Ruby port
review: Ruby port adds fruitiness to this dry, brandy-laced late-night sipper.
history: Adapted from an equal parts recipe in Albert Stevens Crockett's 1931 book Old Waldorf Astoria Bar Days with a higher proportion of brandy influenced by the Montana recipe in David A. Embury's 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks.

name: Montana Club Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Expressed oils from a lemon zest twist are essential to the freshness of this beautifully rounded, old-tom gin-based Sweet Martini.
history: Adapted from a recipe thought to have been created by Julian Anderson, who, from 1893 to 1953, was the bartender at The Montana Club, a private club in Helena, Montana, USA. As this is the club's signature cocktail, over his 60-year tenure, he certainly mixed thousands of Montana Club Martinis and included the recipe in his self-published 1919 book Julian's Recipes.

name: White Mezcal Negroni
garnish: Lemon zest twist expressed and discarded
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
review: Muscular notes of mezcal and gentian square up to each other but are softened and made to play nicely by bianco vermouth.
history: A mezcal riff on Wayne Collins gin-based White Negroni.

name: Fort Point
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
1⁄4 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
review: Like many of New York City's Manhattan variations, the rye whiskey-forward Fort Point is named after the Boston district that was home to the bar where it was created.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2008 by bar manager John Gertsen at Drink Bar, soon after the bar opened in Fort Point, Boston, USA. (Sadly, shuttered in January 2024.)

Fellow Discerning Drinker, Frederic Yarm, says, "It might have been the inspiration for the bar's 1919 Cocktail that got a bit more traction appearing on menus across town (rye split with Old Monk Rum, double the Punt e Mes & Benedictine, and addition of mole bitters)."

name: Blind Pilot
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Galliano L'Autentico liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: Best described as a Galliano Manhattan, I was sceptical when David Selle, a fellow Discerning Drinker, recommended this three equal-parts cocktail to me, but the herbal notes of the liqueur sit brilliantly with the whiskey and vermouth without making it overly sweet.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2008 by bartender Lance Mayhew in Portland, Oregon, for a patron who asked for a cocktail with whiskey and Galliano.

name: Rum Manhattan
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: This riff on a classic whiskey-based Sweet Manhattan beautifully showcases your choice of rum.

name: Kopstoot
preparation: POUR genever into shot glass and beer into beer glass. To enjoy, simply sip a shot of ice-cold genever from a small, tulip-shaped glass, then follow with a sip of beer.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever (chilled)
1⁄2 pint	Belgium dubbel abbey ale
review: In the worthy pursuit of responsible drinking I must stress that when enjoying a Kopstoot you should repeatedly take a sip from each glass – savour the combination rather than shooting the genever in one gulp.
history: The traditional Dutch way to drink genever, Kopstoot (pronounced 'Cop-Stoat') translates as 'headbutt'.

name: Byrrh Special
preparation: STIR ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Byrrh Grand Quinquina
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
review: The botanicals in gin combine brilliantly with Byrrh to create a cocktail that works as well as an apéritif as it does a digestif.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Ciao Bella
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Acqua Bianca liqueur
1 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
review: Use a great quality white crème de cacao alongside Aqua Bianca and you'll have a surprisingly well-balanced complex and delicately chocolaty freshening after-dinner cocktail.
history: Created in 2020 by Salvatore "The Maestro" Calabrese at the Donovan Bar, London, England.

name: Casa Savoia Spritz
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Savoia Americano Rosso
1 2⁄3 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
review: Easy-drinking and delicately bittersweet.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Giuseppe Gallo, the creator of Savoia Americano.

name: Fernandito
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
3 1⁄2 shot	Cola (e.g. Coca Cola or Pepsi Cola)
history:
Very popular in Argentina where the combination of fernet & Coke is as much a staple as the G&T is in England. The drink is most identified with the Argentinian province of Córdoba, where legend has it that a bartender by the name of Oscar "el Negro" Becerra mixed and served the Fernandito in the 1970s, although others say it dates from the 1950s.

Realising the Fernandito's growing popularity, in the 1990s, Fratelli Branca and the Coca-Cola Company launched a joint national advertising campaign in Argentina to help drive the drink's popularity.

name: The Reanimator
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain intio chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 1⁄2 shot	Amaro Nonino Quintessentia
review: Adapted from a recipe created in 2011 by David Wondrich, New York City, USA.
history: Deliciously simple. Great as a spirit-forward digestivo or late-night sipper.

name: Fernet con Coca (Fernet with Coke)
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
4 1⁄2 shot	Cola (e.g. Coca Cola or Pepsi Cola)
review: Herbal bittersweet cola for grownups. Two ingredients singing "In Perfect Harmony," to quote that famous TV ad.
history: A very popular drink in Argentina, particularly in the province of Córdoba in the centre of the country.

name: Diamante
preparation: POUR ingredients into chilled glass and fill with ice.
ingredients:
3 1⁄3 shot	Rosé champagne (chilled)
1 2⁄3 shot	Mancino Vermouth di Torino Sakura
review: Cherry blossom rose sparkling wine. Perfect for Valentine's Day.

name: The Very Last Word
garnish: Lime zest twist discarded and skewered maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
2⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
1⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄4 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄6 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄12 shot	Lavender sugar syrup
4 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: When it comes to riffs on the Last Word, this may not be the "Very Last" but at very least it has more ingredients. Why settle for a Last Word when you can have The Very Last Word?
history:
Created 28th October 2021 by yours truly at the Clocktower in Rye, England.
Last Word history

name: Le Coq d'Or (The Golden Rooster)
garnish: Grapefruit zest twist (discarded) & float star anise
preparation: Saturate sugar cube with Peychaud's in base of shaker and MUDDLE thoroughly. Add cognac and stir to ensure sugar is dissolved. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 cube	Demerara / dark Muscovado / brown sugar
3 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
2 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Galliano L'Autentico liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Pineapple juice
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
2 dash	Pimento bitters
1 fresh	Egg yolk
review: Perhaps substitute ¼ shot demerara sugar syrup for the sugar cube and all that muddling. Whether runny or dry sugar, this flip-style cocktail is balanced and complex.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Timothy Eshing who says "'Le Coq d'Or' means 'the golden rooster' (hence the use of 'golden' ingredients); it is the title of a 1907 opera by Nicolai Rimsky-Korsakov, after a story by Pushkin, itself after a story by Irving. Outside Russia, the work is usually performed in French (hence the name and reliance on French ingredients). Each major ingredient is associated with a major character in the opera: the cognac and liqueur for the Tsar and Tsaritsa, the fruit juices for the Tsar's two doomed sons, the yolk for the golden rooster, and the bitters for the astrologer."

name: Forbidden Fruit
preparation: SHAKE first 7 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with ginger beer and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄3 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
1 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: Given the name, don't expect a sweet 'fruity' cocktail, instead, this is dry, spicy and complex with zesty citrus over an appley spirituous base with enlivening ginger spice.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2012 by Aisha Sharpe in New York City, USA. The original recipe was based on bonded applejack rather than calvados and was more or less:
45ml Bottled-in-bond applejack
30ml Pimm's No. 1
15ml Lemon juice
7.5 Sugar syrup (1:1)
2 dashes Angostura Aromatic bitters
2 dash Peychaud's bitters
45ml Ginger beer

name: Long Island Iced Tea (no added sugar* & low-calorie)
preparation: SHAKE first 8 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with cola and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄3 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄3 shot	Agave Sec liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Sugar-free sweetener
5⁄12 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 shot	Cola (e.g. Coca Cola or Pepsi Cola)
review:
* BEWARE: Although free of cane sugar and beet sugar, this cocktail contains small amounts of fructose sugars from the agave nectar used in the Agave Sec orange liqueur as well as natural sugars in the lime and lemon juice.

As the cola falls and bleeds its way through the otherwise clear drink (it takes noticeably long to fall than full sugar cola), it does end up looking remarkably like week black tea and indeed the taste isn't so far removed from spirit laced weak tea with citrus fruit.
history:
Adapted from the classic serve by yours truly (Simon Difford) in January 2019.

For the origins of the Long Island Iced Tea see 1980s cocktails.

name: Bit Of An Animal
garnish: Lemon juice moistened sea salt-coated rim. Garnish with Pepperoni/beer stick, lemon wedge & skewered olive
preparation: ROLL (rotate rather than shake shaker) and strain into ice-filled glass. Use ice fresh from freezer (rather than ice-machine/ice-well) to fill glass so avoid unwanted dilution.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
2 1⁄4 shot	Tomato juice
1⁄3 shot	Amontillado sherry
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
3 grind	Black pepper
2 dash	Worcestershire sauce
8 drop	Hot pepper sauce (red)
review: Vodka is both traditional and works brilliantly as a base to a Bloody Mary but is far too tame for a 'Bit Of An Animal'.
history: Created in March 2023 by yours truly at The Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Double Barrel Winchester
garnish: Union Jack skewered parasol half grapefruit slice wheel and 2 slices ginger
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. (You may want to split the first ingredient into 22.5ml (¾oz) of two different gins if available.)
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
1⁄3 shot	Hayman's Navy Strength Royal Dock Gin
1⁄3 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Ginger syrup
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Ginger spice and citrus freshness shine in this quadruple gin-based, contemporary classic Tiki cocktail.
history:
Brian Miller created the Winchester cocktail while working at Death & Co. in 2009 and named it for Angus Winchester, then Tanqueray brand ambassador. The Winchester was based on a trio of gins: Hayman's Old Tom Gin, Martin Miller's Westbourne Strength Gin and Tanqueray Gin. Then, a decade later, Brian put his Double Barrel Winchester on the menu at The Polynesian in New York City with four gins: 15ml (½oz) Greenhook Ginsmith Old Tom Gin, 15ml (½oz) Perry's Tot Gin, 30ml (1oz) Millar's Westbourne Strength Gin, and 30ml (1oz) Monkey 47 Gin.

For reasons of sobriety and cost, my adaptation uses measures around a third smaller than the original recipe. If you'd prefer larger measures, reach for a Tiki mug and try:
30 London dry gin
30 Citrus-forward 47% alc./vol. gin
20 Old Tom gin
15 Navy strength gin 57% alc./vol.
15 Elderflower liqueur
22.5 Lime juice
22.5 Grapefruit juice
10 Grenadine
10 Ginger syrup

name: Hurricane
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
5⁄6 shot	Navy rum (54.5% alc./vol.)
5⁄6 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Lime cordial (sweetened lime juice)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄6 shot	Passion fruit syrup
review: A strong, tangy, refreshing drink packed with fruit and laced with rum.
history: Named after the shape of a hurricane lamp and served in the tall, shapely glass of the same name. Thought to have originated in 1939 at The Hurricane Bar in New York City, but made famous at Pat O'Brien's in New Orleans. Some old cocktail books list a much earlier Hurricane made with cognac, absinthe and vodka.

name: Jack Rose Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. (Consider dry shaking if using egg white.)
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄12 shot	Raspberry (framboise) sugar syrup
1⁄12 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1⁄4 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review:
In his 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks, David Embury says, "a Jack Rose is nothing but a Pink Apple Car", and when made with just calvados, lemon juice and one-dimensional sweet grenadine, he's right. Popular recipes tend to be:

45ml (1½oz) Calvados/apple jack
22.5ml (¾oz) Lime or lemon juice
15ml (½oz) Grenadine

However, the Jack Rose can be so much more with artisanal grenadine or raspberry syrup (as per the original recipe). I like to split the citrus juices between lemon and lime as per the original 1908 recipe, with a dash of bitters as a nod to the third citrus fruit in that recipe. I also add a dash of egg white to round the palate, although I can understand many choosing to omit this foam-inducing addition.
history:
The first known Jack Rose recipe appears in Jacob Abraham Grohusko's 1908 Jack's Manual with the following recipe:
"1 teaspoon sugar
10 dashes Raspberry syrup
10 dashes lemon juice
5 dashes orange juice
Juice ½ lime
75% cider brandy
Fill glass with cracked ice, shake and strain, fill with fizz water and serve.

By the time the Jack Rose reappears in Jacques Straub's 1914 Drinks it was reduced to just three ingredients, much closer to modern-day renditions:
"1 jigger Applejack.
½ lime
¼ jigger grenadine syrup. Shake well."

Like many great classics, this drink is served with numerous plausible origins for its name but given the 1908 appearance above, some are easily discounted:

1. The Jack Rose is named after the Jacqueminot rose, which in turn takes its name from the French general, Jean-François Jacqueminot. According to Albert S. Crockett's 1935 The Old Waldorf-Astoria Bar Book, it is so-called because of its pink colour, the exact shade of a Jacqueminot rose, when properly concocted.

2. Some credit this drink's creation to the Colt's Neck inn in New Jersey, which was originally owned by a member of the Laird's family of applejack distillers. His name was Jack and 'Rose' is said to be a reference to the drink's reddish-pink hue. However, this theory has been discredited by Lisa Laird-Dunn, a ninth-generation Laird family ancestor.

3. Others simply claim 'Jack' is short for 'applejack' and again hold that 'Rose' a reference to the drink's colour.

4. According to the Police Gazette of 1905, "Frank J. May, better known as Jack Rose, is the inventor of a very popular cocktail by that name, which has made him famous as a mixologist." Jack Rose, apparently also a wrestler, held bar at Gene Sullivan's Café, 187 Pavonia Avenue, Jersey City, New Jersey.

5. Jack Rose, a late 19th century New York small-time gangster, was the informant in a notorious 1912 murder case. "Bald" Jack Rose, whose favourite beverage is said to have been applejack brandy with lemon and grenadine, was heavily implicated in the 1912 shooting of Herman 'Beansy' Rosenthal, the owner of several New York gambling dens who was in throws of blowing the lid on police and municipal links to organised crime. Rosenthal had already squealed to the press and, on the evening of July 15, after the lengthy delivery of his affidavit, left D.A. Charles Whitman's office at around midnight. Fatally, he then headed to the Metropole Café at the Hotel Metropole on West 43rd Street, a favourite late-night gambler's haunt, for a nightcap. As he exited the Metropole, he was killed by four bullets, one to the chest and three to his head. The hit was pinned on Lieutenant Charles Becker of the NYPD's anti-gambling squad, and Rose was the star witness in what was the trial of the century. Becker went to the electric chair while Rose apparently entered the catering business, lending his name to his favourite drink.

6. Or, alternatively, it could be named after Jack Rose, an early 20th-century brand of small cigars which sold for five cents a pack. Interestingly, these little cigars became known by the nickname 'squealers' after the Rosenthal case.

Whatever, don't let the truth stand in the way of a good bar story.

name: Bruised Pomegranate
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo maraschino cherry
preparation: THROW all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 1⁄2 shot	Byrrh Grand Quinquina
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
4 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
3⁄4 shot	Chilled water
review: This cocktail sits somewhere in the East River between a Manhattan and a Brooklyn with some Thames Estuary thrown in.
history: Created in August 2015 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Quarantine Order
garnish: Mint sprig bouquet, lime wheel slice & Luxardo Maraschino cherry sail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Jamaican aged blended rum with funk
1 1⁄3 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
5⁄6 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Cinnamon syrup
1⁄4 shot	Passion fruit syrup
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
4 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Tangy, fruity, rum-laced and passion fruit-tastic. Doctor's order!
history:
Adapted from a recipe created circa 2014 by William Prestwood at The Tonga Room before leaving to run Pagan Idol, a Tiki bar in San Francisco, where he also put this cocktail on the menu. Consequently, the Quarantine Order is perhaps now more associated with the Pagan Idol.

Originally based on equal parts Appleton Estate Signature and Rum-Bar Gold rums.

name: Expense Account
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Dark/black/blackstrap rum
1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Maple syrup
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water (reduce if wet ice)
3 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: This particular Expense Account has a distinctly festive flavour with notes of sweet cinnamon (not an ingredient) and is best described as being an expensive "Festive Rum Old Fashioned."
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Peter Hill at the Albert Street Cocktail Company bar in Winnipeg, Canada.

name: Pinky Gonzales
garnish: Mint sprigs bouquet & fruit stick (skewered pineapple cubes and Luxardo Maraschino cherry)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄6 shot	Agave syrup
1⁄12 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A tequila-based Mai Tai variation created by Victor Bergeron, AKA "Trader Vic", creator of the original Mai Tai.
history: A Tiki classic created in 1964 by Victor Bergeron, AKA "Trader Vic" for his Señor Pico restaurant. This cocktail is included in his 1972 Trader Vic's Bartender's Guide accompanied by the 'TV' logo denoting that it is a Trader Vic original.

name: 3 Monkeys & a dash
garnish: Mist with 3 sprays of whisky and garnish with skewered pineapple wedge & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into glass filled with crushed ice. Chrun to redistribute ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄6 shot	Monkey Shoulder Fresh Monkey
1⁄2 shot	Blended/vatted Scotch malt whisky
1⁄4 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
4 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: There's more than a hint of Tiki to this 'you've been oranged' fresh and refreshing riff on a classic Three Dots and a Dash.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2022 by Joe Petch, the global Monkey Shoulder brand ambassador.

name: Satan's Whiskers (Kevin Armstrong's)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄3 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄6 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A classic Straight Satan's Whiskers with added freshness thanks to a splash of lemon juice, balanced with a touch of sugar.
history: This version of the classic Satan's Whiskers is adapted from a recipe created by Kevin Armstrong as the signature cocktail at his Satan's Whiskers bar in Bethnal Green, London, England. His recipe calls for Tanqueray London Dry Gin and Noilly Prat as the dry vermouth. Kevin's recipe is also mixed with a Regal Shake.

name: Spicy Margarita
preparation: MUDDLE chili and coriander/cilantro in base of shaker, Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 slice	Red chili pepper (jalapeño/fresno chili (10,000 SHU) deseeded)
3 sprig	Coriander/Cilantro leaves (optional)
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Agave syrup
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water) (optional)
4 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters (optional)
review: By the end of 2023 it was clear that the Spicy Margarita was going to be one of the big cocktails of 2024. Its popularity and origin are thanks to Soho House's Picante de la Casa, created in 2012 by Chris Ojeda of Soho House, West Hollywood as a simplification of another 'House' cocktail, the Margarita Picante from nearby Soho Beach House Miami. (Picante means 'spicy' in Spanish, Portuguese and Italian).

name: Daddy's Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Rhum Clément Blanc
1⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄4 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Gomme syrup
3 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Rhum agricole, Chartreuse and falernum add their flavoursome character to this Daiquiri.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2024 by Michael "Daddy Long Legs" George at Water Witch in Salt Lake City, USA.

name: Bloody Mary (Modern Recipe)
preparation: ROLL rather than shake all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. (Use double frozen ice freshly from freezer to fill glass.)
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
4 shot	Tomato juice
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
8 drop	Hot pepper sauce (red)
4 dash	Worcestershire sauce
2 grind	Black pepper
1 pinch	Celery salt
review: The classic brunch cocktail.
history: Bloody Mary cocktail history

name: Cherry Blossom
garnish: Skewered Luxardo Maraschino cherry with cherry blossom when in season
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄3 shot	Kirschwasser (cherry) eau-de-vie
1⁄3 shot	Bepi Tosolini Grappa di Moscato
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Cherry blossom/sakura syrup
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Kirsh eau-de-vie and grappa give depth of flavour to vodka as a base in this cherry blossom and maraschino sour.
history: Created by yours truly as a refresh of an old recipe. The refresh became a remake.

name: Commodore No. 1
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄12 shot	Raspberry (framboise) sugar syrup
1⁄12 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: A Daiquiri sweetened with raspberry and grenadine syrup and mellowed by egg white.
history:
The first of two Commodore cocktails in Albert S. Crockett's 1931 Old Waldorf Bar Days. (See Crockett's Commodore No.2 recipe).

David A. Embury also includes a Commodore cocktail in his 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks, where he writes, "Another version of the Commodore calls for whisky instead of rum, omits the egg white, and uses orange bitters in place of the grenadine. Obviously, the two Commodores command two different fleets." Embury is perhaps referring to the "Commodore Cocktail" recipe in Harry McElhone's 1922 Harry's ABC of Mixing Cocktails or in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book, both whisk(e)y based.

name: Delicious Sour
garnish: Lemon zest twist expressed & discarded. Adorn with dehydrated apple slice.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) to emulsify and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Applejack brandy
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Crème de Pêche de Vigne liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Licor 43 Original liqueur (optional)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
4 drop	Bob's Vanilla bitters
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Tis rather.
history: Adapted from a recipe in William Schmidt's 1892 The Flowing Bowl.

name: Ginger Margarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	Ginger liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Agave syrup
4 drop	Bob's Ginger Bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water) (optional)
review: Ginger liqueur replaces orange liqueur in this lightly spicy margarita.
history: Recipe by yours truly.

name: Goombay Smash
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Jamaican aged blended rum with funk
1 shot	Coconut rum liqueur (35-40% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review:
The classic pineapple and coconut combo with a touch of rum funk and subdued apricot.

Smashes are usually short drinks that include muddled mint. Strictly according to cocktail family rules, this drink might be misnamed, but like all the miss-named fruit "Martinis" that are not actually Martinis, it's tasty and has mass-market appeal.
history:
Created by Emily Cooper, better known as "Miss Emily" at the Blue Bee Bar in New Plymouth, Green Turtle Cay, Bahamas. Miss Emily passed away in 1977 but her daughter Violet Smith continues to run the now-famous bar and serve the infamous Smash to visitors from the world over.

Incredibly, while Miss Emily Cooper is the undisputed creator of a contemporary classic cocktail that appears on bar menus through the Bahamas and the wider world, she never sipped an alcoholic beverage during her entire life and was allergic to pineapples. so had two reasons never to sample her own invention. The rainy day she created her now famous cocktail she relied on men playing dominoes in the yard outside to gauge the success of her concoction and was told, "that is very good." So popular did her cocktail become that she experimented with ever quicker ways of making ever-larger batches, ending up mixing it in a gallon bottle. The method still employed in the bar to this day.

Miss Emily created her potent cocktail around the time that the annual Goombay Summer Festival hits the Bahamas, so inspiring the name.

The original recipe remains a secret but at Blue Bee Bar the coconut run of choice is Rico Bay Coconut Rum which is a full 40% (80° proof) so a low alc./vol. sweet coconut liqueur will not do for this cocktail. Miss Emily used "dirty rum", so obviously a dark characterful rum rather than charcoal filtered lighter style rum. The other known ingredients are apricot brandy and pineapple juice, although orange juice is also common to pretty much all recreations of the original. There is apparently a "secret ingredient" but being the Caribbean there's a good chance that's a couple of dashes of bitters.

name: Kamaniwanalaya
garnish: Pineapple wedge & Luxardo Maraschino cherry & mint sprig
preparation: SHAKE first 6 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled (cubed ice) tiki mug (or large Collins glass). Top with crushed ice and then top with prosecco.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1⁄2 shot	Navy rum (54.5% alc./vol.)
1⁄4 shot	White overproof rum
3 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
review: Try saying the drinks name after a few of these rum laced, tropical pineapple concoctions.
history: Adapted from a tropical drink recipe of unknown origin which appeared in Mark Torre's 1987 book The Bartender's Cherry.

name: Russian Spring Punch
preparation: SHAKE first 6 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass charged with champagne.
ingredients:
7 fresh	Raspberries
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Crème de Framboise
1⁄4 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 2⁄3 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Well-balanced, complex and refreshing.
history:
Created in the 1980s by Dick Bradsell, London, England. In the Dec-Jan 1998 edition of CLASS magazine (page 6), Dick wrote about his drink, "Many springs ago, I conceived the Russian Spring Punch which is basically a spiked Kir Royal over ice. This conforms to the punch formula of 1 sweet, 2 sour, 3 strong, 4 weak except the most of the 'weak' bit (normally soda or juice) is replaced with champagne, turning the recipe into a sledgehammer of a cocktail. To make, fill a Collins glass with ice. Add 50ml best vodka, 25ml lemon juice, two teaspoons of cassis and two teaspoons of sugar syrup. Top with champagne and stir. Garnish with a lemon slice and some berries."

In August 2015, Dick told us the full story: "I created this drink for friends of ours, Rebecca du Pont de Bie and Peter Kent, in the 80s. I think I was still working at Zanzibar at the time, but it might very well have been Fred's: it was before my daughter Beatrix was born in 1988.

Peter was a gay guy, who designed shops and married Hamish Bowles, who is editor-at-large for Vogue. They shared an extremely nice flat in the Knightsbridge end of Kensington, and they wanted to have a cocktail party but they didn't have enough money.

So I suggested that, as they didn't have quite enough cash for prestigious amounts of drink, they requested that everyone brought a bottle of bubbly. So if you brought rubbish, you got the drinks rubbish, and if you brought quality, you drank quality.

I stocked the bar with glasses, and in each glass was a shot of vodka, half a shot of lemon juice, two barspoons of sugar, one barspoon of cassis and ice. People got to drink their whole bottle of champagne and however many shots of vodka they felt they could manage.

It was lethal, that thing. We had people falling down the stairs and dancing around in wild abandon. I called it the Russian Spring Punch because it has vodka in it, which is Russian, and it's a Collins, or a Fizz, which is a spring drink."

name: Scofflaw
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters (optional)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water) (optional)
review: Just on the dry/tart side so crisp and superbly refreshing. For my version of this classic, I've used bonded strength rye whisky so you need to up the measure if using standard strength rye. I've also used a 'rich' 2:1 grenadine syrup. If using homemade 1:1 syrup pomegranate syrup for your grenadine, up the measure to 10ml (1/3oz) and omit the sugar syrup. Homemade syrup produces a rust-coloured cocktail while with commercial grenadine the result is likely to be more vibrant. The quality of your pomegranate syrup/grenadine will make or break the finished cocktail.
history:
The term "Scofflaw" emerged on 15th January 1924 as the winning word of a competition held by a campaigning teetotaller, named Delcevare King, during the height of Prohibition who offered a prize of $200 "for an epithet which would best express the idea of lawless drinker, menace scoffer, bad citizen, or what not, with the biting power of 'scab' or 'slacker'." The Chicago Tribune reported on the competition's launch and winners. "Two contestants proposed the word and the prize was divided between them. The winners are Henry Irving Shaw of Shawsheen Village and Miss Kate L. Butler of Dorchester."

It is also the Chicago Tribune, on Monday 21st January 1924, that reports on the creation of the Scofflaw Cocktail at Maxim's bar in Paris.

name: Yellow Bird
garnish: Banana carved to resemble a bird OR pineapple wedge, Luxardo maraschino cherry & half orange wheel.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
2⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Galliano L'Autentico liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄6 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: With its sunny colour and tropical fruity flavour and rum base, the Yellow Bird certainly evokes the Caribbean. Two rums and three fruit juices, but the ripe banana and peppermint freshness of the two liqueurs that most influence this lightly Tiki cocktail.
history: Perhaps simply named due to its golden yellow colour or possibly after the 19th-century Haitian tune Choucoune, rewritten with English lyrics as Yellow Bird in the mid-1950s. The song was first recorded with his calypso-style arrangement by Norman Luboff and his choir in 1957. A 1959 recording by the Mills Brothers became a minor hit but it was Hawaiian singer Arthur Lyman's recording that rose to No.4 on the Billboard charts in July 1961. Some say that this record was regularly played at Shell Bar in The Hawaii Village so inspiring the creation of this cocktail there.

name: Gun Club Punch No.1
garnish: Fruit stick (pineapple cubes & Luxardo Maraschino cherry on stick) & mint sprigs bouquet. Serve with straws
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into mug/glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
5⁄6 shot	Jamaican aged blended rum with funk
1⁄3 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Rum-laced fruit, as with most Trader Vic classics, balanced rather than sweet.
history: Victor Bergeron specified that this drink should be served in one of his bespoke green cartridge mugs (pictured here). This recipe is adapted from Trader Vic's Bartender's Guide (1972 revised edition).

name: Moo'lata
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
1⁄4 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Angostura Cocoa Bitters
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Scotch soured with lime (works better than lemon) and sweetened with a touch of chocolate liqueur.
history: Created in January 2011 by Yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England after mistakenly taking a bottle of Scotch from the speedwell to make a Mulata Daiquiri. It proved a tasty mistake.

name: Reality Check
glass: Rum barrel mug or pint glass
preparation: MUDDLE raspberries in base of large shaker tin. Add ice and other ingredients then THROW (strain from a height into a second strainer). Repeat four times and then strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
5 fresh	Raspberries
2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
2⁄3 shot	Becherovka liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 3⁄4 shot	Pilsner lager
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Raspberry fruit, herbal complexity and dry hoppy beer with a splash of zesty lime. Fabulously refreshing.
history: Created in 2013 by Simone Caporale at the Artesian Bar, Langham Hotel, London, England. One of five finalists in the Difford's Guide Beer-tail Competition held 9th August 2013 at Simon Difford's Cabinet Room in London.

name: Ramos Chocolate Fizz cocktail
preparation: SHAKE first six ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne slowly poured into glass from a height to create thick foamy head.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄6 shot	Orange blossom water / Orange flower water
1⁄6 shot	Vanilla extract/essence
1 shot	Egg white
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Creamy chocolate vanilla fudge with faint orange and a hint of gin.
history: Created 4th February 2014 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room in London, England.

name: Heisenberg Cocktail
garnish: Lime juice and blue-coloured salt rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. (Most appropriately served in a science beaker.)
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Patrón Añejo tequila
1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Lavender sugar syrup
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Blue Curaçao
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Like a suitably complex chemistry experiment, this Margarita-like cocktail has seven ingredients with mezcal adding smoky notes to tequila and a trio of liqueurs balancing lime sourness.
history: Adapted from a drink created in September 2013 at Mark's Bar, Soho, London to celebrate the last episode of Breaking Bad inspired by the show's blue crystal meth.

name: Zuzu's Petals cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bison grass vodka
1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Celery bitters
review: Bittersweet with fragrant bison grass vodka and fruity Maraschino cherry flavours supported by bitter gentian, rich elderflower and lime juice.
history: Chaim Dauermann at The Up & Up, Greenwich Village, NYC, USA. The name references It's A Wonderful Life.

name: Ambrosio Cup
preparation: SHAKE first 6 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with soda water.
ingredients:
8 fresh	Mint leaves
3⁄4 shot	Cachaça
3⁄4 shot	Bison grass vodka
3⁄4 shot	Manzanilla sherry
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Cachaça, Bison Grass vodka and manzanilla sherry combine harmoniously and are freshened with mint and lime in this refreshing cocktail.
history: Created in 2013 by Ann Robinson at PDT, New York City, USA

name: Sweet Manhattan (batched recipe)
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo maraschino cherry
preparation:
Combine all ingredients and stir (without ice). POUR into a litre bottle and leave to chill in a refrigerator. To serve, STIR 2 shots / 2oz / 60ml of the bottled mixture with ice and strain into chilled glass. Makes 16 drinks.

This recipe is also perfect for making a barrel aged Manhattan and will fill a one litre mini cask. Obviously, multiply recipe if using a larger cask.
ingredients:
10 shot	Bourbon whiskey
10 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
10 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
5⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄6 shot	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Bourbon and rye whiskies form a robust base with hints of both maraschino and cherry brandy liqueurs adding flavour and richness alongside Italian vermouth.
history:
Created in 2016 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.
See: Manhattan cocktail history

name: Sake Manhattan
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 3⁄4 shot	Akashi-Tai Daiginjo Genshu sake
3⁄4 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Lighter in style than your typical Manhattan Cocktail, with all the familiar flavours enhanced by extra sake complexity.
history:
Created in October 2016 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.
Manhattan cocktail history

name: Honey Badger
preparation: De-stalk a sprig of rosemary and MUDDLE the leaves with bourbon in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 sprig	Rosemary sprig
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄3 shot	Ginger syrup
1⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Lemon bitters
review: If you like the Penicillin Cocktail, then you'll also like this rosemary, ginger, lemon and honey infused bourbon cocktail, shaken and served on-the-rocks.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Liam Baer at Fish and Meat in Hong Kong. (Our thanks to Kshitiz Gurung at Stockton, Hong Kong for passing on this recipe.)

This drink takes its name from the eponymous honey badger, a carnivorous animal which despite its name bears more resemblance to an oversized weasel or polecat than it does to other members of the badger species. It is native to Africa, Southwest Asia, and the Indian subcontinent.

The original recipe uses rosemary-infused bourbon* and homemade ginger syrup.

*Rosemary infused bourbon: Drop 6 fresh rosemary sprigs into a bottle of bourbon. Leave to infuse for 48 hours shaking occasionally, then strain and rebottle.

Ginger syrup: Stir 1/3 cup water and ½ cup brown sugar and in a saucepan and gently heat until sugar is dissolved. Transfer the brown sugar syrup you have made into a blender and add 1 cup peeled and chopped fresh ginger. Blend into a paste and strain to remove solids. Bottle and refrigerate.

name: Pomegranate Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄6 shot	Rhum Clément Blanc
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Pomegranate juice
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Freshly pressed pomegranate juice is essential to the success of this deliciously fruity but dry Daiquiri. Sadly, packaged juice doesn't produce a cocktail of comparable quality.
history: Created in May 2017 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room in London, England.

name: Pan Galactic Gargle Blaster
garnish: Dust with lots of freshly grounded black pepper
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
10 fresh	Basil leaves
2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
2⁄3 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄6 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1 2⁄3 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1 2⁄3 shot	Strawberry puree
review: Orange, basil and red berries laced with vodka makes for a well-balanced, easy-drinking fruity cocktail - arguably too easy for a drink titled Pan Galactic Gargle Blaster which is said to be like "having your brains smashed in by a slice of lemon wrapped round a large gold brick." Remember, Beeblebrox advises, "never drink more than two Pan Galactic Gargle Blasters unless you are a thirty ton mega elephant with bronchial pneumonia."
history:
Based on the Basil Grande, this recipe for the legendary Pan Galactic Gargle Blaster was created circa 2011 by Christos Chouseas at his Bar 42 in Athens, Greece – a bar where the work of Douglas Adams influenced many of the drink names.

In Adams' thought-provoking and amusing book, The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, the number 42 is the "answer to the ultimate question of life, the universe, and everything", while the Pan Galactic Gargle Blaster is considered by the Guide to be the "Best Drink in Existence."

According to the guide, the original Pan Galactic Gargle Blaster was invented by ex-President of the Universe Zaphod Beeblebrox. "After two of those babies, the dullest, most by-the-book Vogon will be up on the bar in stilettos, yodeling mountain shanties and swearing he's the king of the Gray Binding Fiefdoms of Saxaquine."

name: Mean Fiddler
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	The Busker Single Pot Still Irish Whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Cinnamon syrup
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A riff on a classic Tipperary, with Islay single malt and Italian red bitter liqueur adding complexity.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Jack McGarry at the Dead Rabbit, New York City, USA.

Jack originally based this cocktail on Green Spot single pot still Irish whiskey.

name: Nui Nui
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with 6oz scoop of crushed ice. Place garnish in glass so hanging over the edge. Pour cocktail into glass and top with more crushed ice.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄6 shot	Pimento dram/Allspice liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Cinnamon syrup
1⁄6 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Cinnamon and pimento spiced golden rum with cleansing brightening citrus. Balanced, cooling and delicious.
history: Adapted from a 1930s recipe by Don Beach at his Don The Beachcomber, Restaurant.

name: Cold War Easier
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice)
ingredients:
1 shot	Bison grass vodka
1⁄3 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Pinot Noir red wine
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: The reds are turned a shade near pink in this aromatic sipper.
history: Adapted from a cocktail discovered circa 2015 at Danger of Death bar, London, England.

name: Jungle Hunt
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Jägermeisteror other German amaro
1⁄2 shot	Pineapple rum
1⁄2 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Cinnamon syrup
1 1⁄3 shot	Pineapple juice
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Herbal pineapple and spice with hints of Tiki.

name: Rum & Rye Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
2⁄3 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
2⁄3 shot	Tawny port
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Tawny port adds grape fruitiness to rum and rye whiskey with freshening tart zesty lemon and subtle bitters complexity.
history: Created in January 2021 by yours truly after remembering a cocktail discovered circa 2015 at Danger of Death bar in Brick Lane, London, England.

name: Viking Gimlet
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄6 shot	Akvavit / Aquavit
2⁄3 shot	Lime cordial (sweetened lime juice)
1⁄6 shot	Swedish Punsch liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: This Gimlet has a split spirit base of 50/50 gin and aquavit and 50/50 lime and lemon with lime cordial proving extra citrusy richness. A splash of Swedish punsch alongside the aquavit both adds to the flavour and Viking name.
history: Created in April 2021 by yours truly at the suggestion of fellow discerning drinker, Nicholas Fiennes.

name: Smoke & Mirrors (mezcal-based)
garnish: Dust with an equal mix of powdered sugar, salt and cayenne pepper
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE without ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄3 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Piment d'Espelette chile liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Ginger liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Pineapple juice
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: A Mezcal Margarita with chili, ginger and pineapple, mellowed by a splash of foaming egg white.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2018 by Melissa Yard at Joséphine Wine Bar, Charleston, South Carolina, USA. The original calls for homemade pineapple jalapeño syrup and omits chili liqueur.

name: Taoiseach
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1⁄6 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: The quality of your pomegranate (grenadine) syrup will make or break this cocktail. (Perhaps even better with groseille syrup.)
history:
Adapted from a recipe created by Aaron Wall at his Homeboy bar in Islington, London, the Taoiseach remains one of Homeboy's signature cocktails. Originally made with Redbreast 12 pot still Irish whiskey.

Pronounced 'Tee-shock', this cocktail is named after the title of the first minister of government in Ireland. Aaron says, "Literally translated the name would mean Chieftain and this drink is a twist on an old rum drink, El Presidente – the Irish word for president is Uachtarán na hÉireann, but we thought that might be a bit tricky for the Anglo Saxon vocabulary. This drink is the perfect example of how Irish whiskey can sit in many positions, like the age rum realm, when it comes to making cocktails."

name: Savoia Plane
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄6 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
5⁄6 shot	Savoia Americano Rosso
1⁄3 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Delicately smoky tart citrus enriched by subtle herbal complexity. A freshening aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Umberto Oliva at Bella Milano Bistrot in Milan, Italy. I've swapped the 5ml simple syrup in Umberto's original recipe for 10ml honey syrup, plus I've added drops of saline.

name: Matejcek 3-2-1 Manhattan
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. (If adding maraschino syrup then stir ingredients together before adding ice and stirring again.)
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Syrup from Luxardo Maraschino Cherries
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A rye-based Perfect Manhattan with an optional lift from maraschino syrup.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in January 2017 by Paul Matejcek, a fellow Discerning Drinker who shared his cocktail in a comment on our Fourth Regiment page. With 90ml of whiskey as its base, Paul's original recipe is best made to serve in two glasses.

name: Halekulani
garnish: Pineapple wedge on rim with Luxardo maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Adapted from a recipe in Shannon Mustipher's 2019 Tiki Modern Tropical Cocktails.
history: Originally made with a high proof bourbon, I prefer this cocktail with the spicy notes a bottled-in-bond rye whiskey delivers.

name: The Edge
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Licor 43 Original liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄4 shot	Disaronno amaretto
5⁄6 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1 dash	Xocolatl mole bitters
review: Creamy nutty vanilla whiskey with a hint of cleansing spice.

name: Roman Holiday
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 shot	Meletti amaro
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 shot	Cold brew coffee
3⁄4 shot	Pineapple juice
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
