1⁄6 shot	Demerara / dark Muscovado / brown sugar
4 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A sans rum, amari-forward, caffeine-loaded riff on the Jungle Bird.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Nandini Khaund at Cindy's Chicago Athletic Association Hotel in Chicago, USA.

name: Paloma Rosa
garnish: Grapefruit juice and Himalayan pink salt rim
preparation: SHAKE first 6 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with pink grapefruit soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
2⁄3 shot	Lanique Spirit of Rose liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Pamplemousse liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Bigallet Genepi Grand Tetras
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Pink Grapefruit soda
review: Recognisably a Paloma with tequila and grapefruit, but made "Rosa" with a delicate hint of rose.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2021 by Josh Goldman at Bar Caló in Los Angeles, California, USA.

name: L'Auberge Español
preparation: STIR first 6 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda water.
ingredients:
3 shot	Rosé wine
3⁄4 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
3⁄4 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
6 drop	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
1 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: If you like a spritz, then this refreshing rosé wine-based, citrussy tall cocktail may be just what you're looking for on a warm afternoon.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2018 by Susie Scott, Beverage Director at The Carillon in Austin, Texas, USA. L'Auberge Español translates to 'The Spanish Inn'.

name: Nightwish
garnish: Lemon zest twist, expressed and then skewered for garnish (preferably using a skull-topped pick)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
4 drop	Bob's Cardamom bitters
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Vodka may fortify this cocktail, but it's led by the interplay between fino sherry, banana liqueur and sweet 'n' sour.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2022 by Kelsey Ramage for Black Lagoon, the Halloween pop-up bar concept.

name: Pink Flamingo (by Eric Ochoa)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Rhum Clément Blanc
2⁄3 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1⁄2 shot	Pineapple sugar syrup
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Savoia Americano Rosso
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Bittersweet, sweet 'n' sour, and bristling with grassy rum-led flavour. This Pink Flamingo is a very expressive bird and one that may prove hard to handle for newbie twitchers.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2018 by Eric Ochoa at Over Proof (above ABV bar) in San Francisco, USA. Eric's original recipe uses house-made pineapple gum syrup (1:1) and ABV's signature Tiki-Tivo apéritif, which is made with 1 part Campari, 1 part Capelletti and ½ part Leopold Bros. Aperitivo).

name: Flannel Shirt
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Blended/vatted Scotch malt whisky
1⁄2 shot	Averna Amaro
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄6 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
1⁄12 shot	Pimento dram/Allspice liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: This whisky-laced, lightly spiced apple and lemon cocktail has an autumnal hue and is one to hunker down with on a winter's eve.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2018 by Jeffrey Morgenthaler, Portland, Oregon, USA.

name: Metropole (Difford's version)
garnish: Orange zest twist expressed & discarded. Adorn with skewered Luxardo Maraschino cherry.
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄24 shot	Gomme syrup
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: If bianco vermouth was available in 1889, when the opening bartending team at the Hotel Metropole lazily subtly tweaked the established Metropolitan to create their signature cocktail, they would have perhaps used it in preference to dry vermouth and gomme syrup. I've imagined that in my three-ingredient Tripole but the above recipe introduces bianco vermouth while doffing my hat to the original 1889 Metropol cocktail.
history: Created in December 2023 by yours truly.

name: Tussetto No. 2
garnish: Lemon zest twist expressed and discarded. Adorn with skewered Luxardo Maraschino Cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Manzanilla sherry
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄24 shot	Gomme syrup
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Dry, gin-laced and sherry-influenced with subtle salinity.
history: A Tuxedo with sherry in place of vermouth is a Tussetto and the original was first published in Jacques Straub's 1913 Straub's Manual of Mixed Drinks. The Tussetto No. 2 was created in January 2024 by yours truly at the Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Winter Solace
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Rhum Clément Blanc
3⁄4 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Blood orange juice
1⁄2 shot	Pomegranate juice
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: This tart citrusy cocktail brilliantly harnesses the character of rhum agricole.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2024 by Nick Stephens, a fellow Discerning Drinker. His original Winter Solace recipe is a little more generous in its proportions.

name: Pink Sakura
garnish: Skewered maraschino cherry with cherry blossom when in season
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Akashi-Tai Daiginjo Genshu sake
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄6 shot	Cherry blossom/sakura syrup
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A vodka-laced alternative to my more vermouth-forward, gin-influenced Cherry Blossom Sake Martini. This more subtly flavoured version allows the sake to shine.
history: Created by yours truly in April 2024 at the Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: Breakfast Special Marmalade Martini
preparation: STIR 3 flat barspoons (or 1 heaped spoon) of marmalade with gin in base of shaker to dissolve the marmalade. (It helps to break down if you push the marmalade into the sides of the tin.) Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3 barspoon	Orange marmalade
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Due to its inclusion of vermouth, this Neo Martini is more befitting the 'Martini' moniker than a standard Breakfast Martini. The name also pays homage to Harry Craddock's Marmalade Cocktail, which inspired this recipe. (And, a proper English breakfast should always be served with an egg. or at least an egg white!)
history: A riff on the Marmalade Cocktail in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book. Created by yours truly in April 2024 at The Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Big Apple Martini
garnish: Apple wedge on rim or float dehydrated apple slice
preparation: SHAKE All ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄6 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄6 shot	Sour apple liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review: Spirits-forward, with a trio of spirits, and vermouth as befits the Martini name. Apple notes are well integrated rather than in your face.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2022 by Julie Reiner at Milady's in New York City, USA. The original recipe omits sour apple liqueur and apple juice and instead combines the vodka and gin in a Granny Smith green apple infusion.

name: Apple Strudel
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Apple Schnapps liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄6 shot	Cinnamon syrup
review: Apple, vanilla and a hint of Scotch and cinnamon- reminiscent of the dessert but a good deal drier.
history: Created in 2006 by yours truly.

name: Atholl Brose
preparation: STIR honey with Scotch in base of shaker until honey dissolves. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 barspoon	Honey
1 1⁄3 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 shot	Oat milk / oatmeal water
1⁄6 shot	Drambuie liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1⁄3 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: Forget the porridge and kick start your day with an Atholl Brose. Consider using raw heather honey.
history:
Legend has it that Atholl Brose was created by the Earl of Atholl in 1475 when he was trying to capture Iain MacDonald, Lord of the Isles and leader of a rebellion against the king. Hearing rumours that MacDonald was drawing his drinking water from a particular well, the Earl ordered it to be filled with honey, whisky and oatmeal. MacDonald lingered at the well, enjoying the concoction, and was captured.

Three versions of the Athol Brose appear in Charles H. Baker, Jr.'s 1939 The Gentleman's Companion volume II – An Exotic Drinking Book which he describes as "an odd Scottish institution, which like many things Scottish, is founded on mighty good reason, & is guaranteed to profit its user."

name: Autumn Punch
preparation: Cut passion fruit in half and scoop out flesh into shaker. Add vodka, passion fruit syrup, pear and lemon juice, SHAKE with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
1 fresh	Passion fruit (fresh)
2 shot	Bison grass vodka
1⁄4 shot	Passion fruit syrup
1 shot	Pear juice (freshly pressed)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
Top up with	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Autumnal in colour with a wonderful meld of complementary flavours.
history: Created in 2001 by Max Warner at Baltic Bar, London, England.

name: Blackthorn (English)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A sloe berry-influenced fruity Perfect Martini.
history: The Blackthorn dates back to the 1890s and the Blackthorn No. 1 appears in William "Cocktail Bill" Boothby features a version of this cocktail in his 1908 World's Drinks And How To Mix Them. This version is adapted from one of five different Blackthorn recipes in Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide.

name: Especial Day
preparation: MUDDLE blackberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3 fresh	Blackberries
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Crème de Mûre liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
3 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Rum-laced, very fruity, and toned by vermouth and generous dashed of bitters. If you like a French Martini you'll also like this.
history: Created in 2005 by Tonin Kacaj at Maze in London, England.

name: Fish House Punch
garnish: Lemon slice & dust with grated nutmeg
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
2⁄3 shot	Giffard Crème de Pêche de Vigne liqueur
1 shot	Cold black breakfast tea
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Tea tannins and lemon juice dry and sour this cognac and rum-laced punch with rich peach liqueur balancing and adding fruit appeal.
history:
Probably the most famous of all punch recipes this is believed to have originated at a Philadelphia fishing and social club called the State in Schuylkill Fishing Corporation which was established in 1732 with a clubhouse built on the banks of Pennsylvania's Schuylkill River (pronounced Skoo-kul). When the drink was first made is unknown, but drinks historian David Wondrich says the first written reference to the Fish House Punch appeared in 1794.

Others say it was first made in 1848 by Shippen Willing of Philadelphia to celebrate women being allowed into the Fish House for the first time for a Christmas Party. Whatever the origin, as with all traditional punch recipes this should properly be made with oleo saccharum (rather than lemon juice and sugar) in larger quantities and served from a punch bowl. This recipe is our cheat's single-serve.

The inclusion of peach liqueur is a modern substitute for the traditional barrel-aged peach brandy. However, some believe the Schuylkill original omitted peach entirely.

The following poem may be recited when serving a Fish House Punch.

name: Missionary's Downfall
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE mint with rum in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
15 fresh	Mint leaves
1 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Peachtree peach schnapps
1⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review:
Recipes for this venerable Tiki classic vary enormously and are often confused with the Aku Aku which this drink morphed into at the hands of its creator, Donn Beach. The original recipe calls for peach brandy (distilled from fermented peaches) rather than peach liqueur (based on neutral spirit), but due to its clarity and clean flavour, I prefer peach schnapps as a substitute.

Many recipes blend fresh mint and pineapple, and while blending the mint gives the drink a vibrant green colour, it does resemble stagnant pond water and looks like something you'd only drink for the promise of perceived health-giving properties rather than for pleasure. Hence, my version is shaken, but be sure to muddle generous amounts of mint to impart colour and flavour.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in the late 1930s by Donn Beach at his Don The Beachcomber restaurant in Hollywood, California, USA.

name: Christmas Cheer-re
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
1 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1 shot	Mancino Vermouth di Torino Chinato
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Genever provides the yuletide spirit base, sweetened and flavoured by cherry liqueur, with Chinato drying and adding wine notes while gin adds freshness and botanical complexity. Maraschino and orange bitters complete this festive tipple.
history: Created in December 2014 by yours truly and christened by Paloma Alos.

name: Hotel Nacional Special
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
4 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters (optional)
review: A fruity but sophisticated riff on the classic Daiquiri with fresh pineapple and apricot liqueur. It would appear the Hotel Nacional was originally made with a charcoal filtered white rum but in his influential 1939 travel log, Charles H. Baker says, "We indicate Gold Label Bacardi for the simple reason that Carta Blanca is so delicate in flavour it barely comes through any rich drink. " This cocktail does indeed suit a more characterful rum, to the extent that it's also delicious when made with a well-aged rum.
history:
The flagship cocktail of Havana's famous Hotel Nacional de Cuba, this was created sometime during or after the hotels opening in 1930. The hotel's then elegant opulence was a magnet to the style-set and celebrities including Ava Gardner and Nat King Cole, as well as mobsters such as "Lucky" Luciano.

Such a hotel opening off the US coast during the height of Prohibition attracted some of America's greatest bartenders, including Will (or Wil) Taylor, Eddie Woelke and Fred Kaufman. All three of these have been credited with the creation of the Hotel Nacional Special and perhaps they all contributed. However, the first known reference to the cocktail, in Charles H. Baker's 1939 The Gentleman's Companion credits Wil P. Taylor, describing the drink as "one of the three finest Bacardi drinks known to science."

name: Remember the Maine
preparation: POUR absinthe and water into ice-filled glass and set to one side. Separately, STIR other ingredients in stirring glass. Discard absinthe and strain into absinthe-rinsed glass.
ingredients:
1⁄3 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2 shot	Chilled water
1 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
review: Charles H. Baker says of this twist on a Sazerac, "Treat this one with the respect it deserves, gentleman."
history:
Adapted from a recipe by Charles H. Baker Junior. In his 1939 The Gentleman's Companion he writes of this drink, "a Hazy Memory of a Night in Havana during the Unpleasantnesses of 1933, when Each Swallow Was Punctuated with Bombs Going off on the Prado, or the Sound of 3" Shells Being Fired at the Hotel NACIONAL, then Haven for Certain Anti-Revolutionary Officers".

The drink is named after the press slogan, "Remember the Maine, to Hell with Spain" blaming Spain for the unexplained sinking of the U.S.S. Maine off Cuba in 1898. This helped provoke the 1898 Spanish-American War.

name: Rosarita Margarita
garnish: salt rim (optional) & lime wedge on rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lime cordial (sweetened lime juice)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: This peachy coloured Margarita is well-balanced and flavoursome with zesty orange liqueur sitting well with cranberry.
history: Created in 1999 by Robert Plotkin and Raymon Flores of BarMedia, USA.

name: Suburban
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably with small or cracked cubes).
ingredients:
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
3⁄4 shot	Tawny port
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: An old-Fashioned with a splash of rum and port in place of sugar syrup. I favour tawny port, but if you've a sweet tooth, then use ruby port.
history: Created at New York's old Waldorf-Astoria Hotel (the Empire State Building occupies the site today) for James R Keene, a racehorse owner whose steeds ran in the Suburban Handicap at Brooklyn's Sheepshead Bay track. The Suburban features in Albert Stevens Crockett's 1931 Old Waldorf Bar Days.

name: Tequila Sunrise
preparation: POUR grenadine and cassis into ice-filled glass. SHAKE other ingredients with ice and carefully strain into glass to sit on red base layer (to create a sunrise effect).
ingredients:
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄6 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: This 1970s zesty citrus version of the Tequila Sunrise looks the part and comes with a sweet treat at the bottom of the glass.
history:
A variation on the original 1930s Tequila Sunrise, created in 1970 by Bobby "Robert" Lozoff, when a 22 year-old rookie bartender working at the Trident in Sausalito, California, USA.

The Trident was popular with rock 'n' roll stars and one Monday night in June 1972, when the Trident was normally closed, it was the venue for an intimate Rolling Stones American Tour kick-off party. While Mick Jagger was at the bar waiting for Lozoff to make the Margarita he'd just ordered, Lozoff asked if he had ever tried a Tequila Sunrise. Jagger replied, "no." So, Lozoff made one of his signature drinks. Jagger loved the taste and that it was simple enough for the band to make while on tour. In chapter nine of Keith Richard's 2010 book Life, he says "The '72 tour was known by other names-the Cocaine and Tequila Sunrise tour." The drink's notoriety led its being printed on the back label of Jose Cuervo bottles. Then, in April 1973, the Eagles released their song Tequila Sunrise.

name: Tiramisu Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1⁄2 fresh	Egg yolk
1 barspoon	Mascarpone cheese
review: Chef meets bartender in the rich dessert cocktail.
history: Created by Adam Ennis in 2001 at Isola bar in London, England.

name: Vacation Martini
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and strain into chilled glass. Then POUR liqueur into the centre of the drink. It should sink to create a blue base and leave a blue spot in the centre of this drink's frothy head.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
1⁄2 shot	Coconut rum liqueur (35-40% alc./vol.)
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄4 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
1⁄24 shot	De Kuyper Blue Curaçao
review: A great-looking holiday (Tiki-style) cocktail with vanilla, coconut and pineapple.
history: My 2003 adaptation of the then signature drink at the MercBar on Mercer Steet in Soho, New York City, USA.

name: Fairbanks No.1
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Apricot liqueur dominates this cocktail but dry vermouth, dry gin, lemon juice, and dilution save it from excessive sweetness.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Hearn Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
4 dash	Orinoco bitters
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Stirred and boozy with Green Chartreuse and bitters adding herbal spice to Irish whiskey.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Jack McGarry at The Dead Rabbit, New York City, USA.

name: Mulata Daisy
preparation: MUDDLE fennel seeds in the base of shaker. Add lime juice and powdered sugar and stir until sugar is dissolved. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 barspoon	Fennel seeds
1 barspoon	Powdered sugar (white sugar ground in mortar and pestle) (or use 5ml of 2:1 sugar syrup per spoon)
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 2⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄3 shot	Galliano L'Autentico liqueur
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
review: Delicately spiced and subtly chocolaty.
history: Created in 2008 by Ago Perrone at The Connaught, London, England. This drink, which is named after the classic Cuban Mulata Daiquiri, won the 2009 Bacardi Legacy.

name: Porn Star Martini
preparation:
Wash and cut 2 fresh passion fruits in half, SCOOP out the seeds and flesh of 3 halves into your shaker. (Keep last passion fruit half for garnish.) Add the next 4 ingredients (all but champagne), SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

Optionally, separately POUR champagne into chilled shot glass to serve on the side. Instruct drinker to sip alternately from each glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 fresh	Passion fruit (fresh)
2 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
1⁄2 shot	Passoã passion fruit liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine (optional)
review: A passion fruit and vanilla crowd-pleaser that's balanced with zesty lime, often served with sparkling wine on the side.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2002 by Douglas Ankrah at The Townhouse bar in Knightsbridge, London. Douglas also founded London's LAB bar which is perhaps more associated with this cocktail.

This cocktail was originally named the Maverick Martini after a nightclub in Cape Town, South Africa which Douglas frequented, a story he recounts in his 2004 book, Shaken & Stirred.

name: Satan's Whiskers (Enroulée)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Mandarine Napoleon liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Enroulée is the French word for 'curled' and this version of the classic Satan's Whiskers is "curled" by the use of mandarine liqueur in place of the Grand Marnier found in the 'straight' version.
history: Created in 2011 by Gary "gaz" Regan, New York, USA.

name: Satan's Whiskers (Curled)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: This variation on the 'Straight' Satan's Whiskers is made curly by the use of orange curaçao liqueur. It seems strangely counter-intuitive as you'd think the slightly richer Grand Marnier would be what made it curly.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book. (A variation on the classic Bronx.)

name: Love me flip
preparation: BEAT egg yolk with sugar in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 fresh	Egg yolk
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1 shot	Yoghurt liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
3 drop	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: The grated tonka bean adds a vanilla aroma to the surface of this drink.
history: Created in 2010 by Erik Lorincz at The Connaught Hotel, London, England.

name: Waldorf Daiquiri
garnish: A walnut, apple wedge and chunk of blue cheese on the side
preparation: MUDDLE celery in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 inch	Celery stick (fresh)
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review: Walnut, celery and apple are essential elements to both a Waldorf Salad and this tasty Daiquiri.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2010 by Julian de Feral at Lutyens Bar, London, England.

name: Spanish Eyes
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	Byrrh Grand Quinquina
3⁄4 shot	Pacharan liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
4 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: Reminiscent of a Mexican Blood & Sand, refreshing and complex.
history: Created in August 2015 by yours truly (Simon Difford) at the Cabinet Room, London, England. Why Spanish eyes? Tequila distillers speak Spanish, Byrrh is made close to the Spanish boarder, pacharan is very Spanish, as are the best oranges. Plus my missus is half Spanish so has brown eyes and this drink is brownish.

name: Gun Metal Blue cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Blue Curaçao
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Crème de Pêche de Vigne liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Cinnamon syrup
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Orange, peach and cinnamon delicately flavour this mezcal-based Margarita riff.
history: Created in February 2015 by Mike Shain and Nicholas Bennett at Porchlight, New York City, USA. At Porchlight the original is made with house-made cinnamon syrup infused with gentian root to add a slight bitterness so you may want to add 2.5ml gentian liqueur to the above recipe.

name: Queen's Park Hotel Super Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: It is perhaps best described as a Trinidadian Daiquiri due to its heavy use of Angostura Bitters. According to Owen Rutter, it was also originally made with Trinidad gold rum, Canning's Caroni Rum. (If using homemade 2:1 pomegranate syrup rather than grenadine, use 15ml (½oz) and omit sugar syrup.)
history: Recipe adapted from If Crab No Walk: A Traveller in the West Indies, a 1932 book written by British travel writer Owen Rutter, who writes of the Queen's Park Hotel, Port of Spain, Trinidad, "The cooking is good; the servants, though slow, are attentive; there is an excellent ballroom, a first-rate band, and a good bar: 'the Long Bar with the Brass Rail,' where you may drink the Queen's Park Hotel Super Cocktail."

name: Alcatraz
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Añejo tequila
3⁄4 shot	Oloroso sherry
1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄4 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄6 shot	Agave syrup
8 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: Dry and lightly bitter, this tequila-based sipper makes for a great apéritif cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Christin Wagner at La Petite Grocery, New Orleans, USA. Recipe courtesy of Gary "gaz" Regan's Ardent Spirits.

name: Banana Split
garnish: Lightly dust surface of drink with chocolate powder & banana chunk on rim
preparation: STIR first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. Shake a sealed container of cream and carefully POUR over the back of a spoon to form a small white spot floating in the centre of the drink.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
2 drop	Bob's Vanilla bitters
2 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
3⁄4 shot	Banana tea
1⁄6 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: A banana-flavoured after-dinner sipper of cocktail with coconut water subtly flavouring and smoothing cognac.
history: Created in April 2016 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room in London, England.

name: The Cheshire Cat
garnish: Lemon zest twist, rosemary sprig & smouldering cinnamon stick
preparation: THROW all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of ice block).
ingredients:
1 sprig	Rosemary sprig
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
1⁄6 shot	Cinnamon syrup
review: A twist of the classic Vieux Carré with scotch substituting rye whiskey and cherry wine in place of vermouth. The bitter balance is provided by aromatised wine.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Georgia Billing at The Looking Glass Cocktail Club in London, England. Georgia's original and authentic recipe calls for Gravino Cherry wine (not cherry brandy), Reina Lab Spiced Rosemary syrup (rather than cinnamon sugar syrup) and the addition of her own Reina Lab Sinner Bitters.

name: The Beloved
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄4 shot	Mozart Chocolate Vodka
1⁄4 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
1 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A wonderfully complex marriage of cognac, distilled chocolate, rich Pedro Ximénez and banana liqueur with aromatic bitters and a dash of brine.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by James Wall at Hawksmoor, Air Street, London, England.

name: Floral Daiquiri
garnish: Sprig of dried lavender pegged to rim
preparation: Rinse chilled glass with violet liqueur and set aside ready for drink. MUDDLE blueberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into rinsed glass.
ingredients:
1⁄12 shot	Crème de violette liqueur
3 fresh	Blueberries (fresh)
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lavender sugar syrup
1⁄3 shot	Elderflower liqueur
review: A floral riff on a classic Daiquiri with a hint of berry fruitiness and a lavender pink hue courtesy of a blueberry threesome.
history: Created in 2016 by Andrii Osypchuk at Gaucho, Dubai, UAE.

name: Simple Truth
garnish: Dehydrated grapefruit slice and sage leaf
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
3⁄4 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Honey sugar syrup
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
3 fresh	Sage leaves
review: Rum-laced honeyed pineapple and grapefruit with a hint of bitter liqueur and herbal sage notes.
history: Adapted from the South African Bacardí Legacy winning cocktail created by Nicholas Crouse at Lucky Shaker in Durban.

name: Under The Clouds
garnish: Grapefruit, bear grass, sweet potato & white radish
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
1⁄3 shot	Rosé/rosato vermouth
2⁄3 shot	Lapponia Lakka Cloudberry
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 barspoon	Caster/ Superfine/Baker's special sugar (white)
1 slice	Orange peel
review:
“The inspiration for my cocktail is an Estonian woman.
Her beauty, her nature and her spark all of which I've tried to bring out in my cocktail. Terviseks!”
history: Estonian BACARDÍ Legacy 2014 winning cocktail created by Angelika Larkina, Estonian Bartenders Association Training Center Manager, Estonia.

name: Catalizador
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1 1⁄6 shot	Camomile tea syrup
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review:
“Two inspirations: one of history, and one of a grandmother's love.

“Catalizador is inspired by a long and untold history between rum and tea that incited the American Revolution. What most people believed to have started with a tax on tea actually began with discord created by a tax on rum in 1733.

“The second inspiration for the Catalizador came from my grandmother’s natural remedy for my hyperthyroidism. She introduced me to camomile and its calming properties alleviated my condition.

“So, rum and tea were the CATALYST for the war leading the Americans to their freedom, tea was the CATALYST in aiding a heart condition, and BACARDÍ was the CATALYST that inspired and continues to inspire bartenders to create a whole new genre of light, crisp, refreshing, and legacy-worthy cocktails.”
history: UAE BACARDÍ Legacy 2014 winning cocktail created by Graziella Nieto at JW Marriott Marquis, Dubai.

name: Last Palabra
garnish: Lime zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
2⁄3 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Lavender sugar syrup
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
4 drop	Bob's Lavender Bitters
review: Tequila replaces gin in this riff on the classic Last Word, with the amount of maraschino slightly reduced to accommodate the introduction of lavender syrup, which in turn is also balanced by a dash of lavender bitters.
history:
Created in February 2017 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.
Last Word history

name: The Moment
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with prosecco.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 1⁄3 shot	Pomegranate juice
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Ramazzotti amaro
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
review: Take the time to juice a fresh pomegranate to make this dry fruity long drink and you'll be thankful you did. Pomegranate combines brilliantly with the rum and the other ingredients adding depth and complexity.
history: Adapted from a recipe created for Bacardí Legacy 2017 by Pawan Singh Rawat at Grappa Bar - Shangri-La Eros Hotel, New Delhi, India. Pawan's original recipe was based on Bacardi Carta Blanca rum.

name: Madame Lily
garnish: Lime zest twist & edible white flower
preparation: RINSE glass with absinthe and set aside. MUDDLE apple and sugar syrup in base of shaker. Add rum, calvados and lime juice, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into absinthe rinsed chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄6 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄4 fresh	Apple (fresh)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 1⁄2 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
3⁄4 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Best described as being an absinthe influenced Apple Daiquiri, and very good it is too.
history: Adapted from a recipe created for Bacardí Legacy 2017 by Noam Sharet at A23 Local Blend in Tel Aviv, Israel. Noma's original recipe calls for 22.5 ml (3/4oz) simple (1:1) sugar syrup. We swapped for richer 2:1 and we also found adding a dash or two of absinthe works well in place of absinth rinsing.

name: Pilar
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
1 shot	Peach aperitif liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Pineapple sugar syrup
8 fresh	Mint leaves
5⁄6 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: If you don’t have pineapple syrup, or the time to make the pineapple syrup as stipulated in Joseph’s recipe, then don’t worry - this drink also works well when made with 10ml / 1/3oz pineapple juice and 10ml / 1/3oz of sugar syrup (2:1).
history:
Adapted from a recipe created for Bacardí Legacy 2017 by Joseph Harper at Dakota Deluxe, Leeds, UK.

Joseph makes his own pineapple syrup with 2 parts sugar, 1 part pineapple juice, 1 part boiling water. Stir water and sugar until dissolved, add juice.

Inspiration: “Pilar is named after Ernest Hemingway’s fishing boat, which he used in a fishing competition the Bacardí family invited him to via airmail. This boat was a symbol of his own religious downfall, and so its name suits a drink that marries two classic cocktails: the ‘Missionary’s Downfall’ and the ‘Airmail,’ to bring together the opposing styles of Tiki and opulent drinks.”

name: Slow Comfortable Mexican Screw Against the Wall
preparation: STIR first four ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. FLOAT sloe gin on surface so it bleeds into drink. Finish with Galliano FLOAT.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
3⁄4 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Southern USA-style liqueur 40% (e.g. Southern Comfort)
3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
1⁄2 shot	Galliano L'Autentico liqueur
review: Tequila adds a Mexican touch to the Slow Screw family to create a tasty riff on a Screwdriver. Great for a lazy summer afternoon or a barbeque.

name: Fade To Black Cocktail
preparation: MUDDLE blackberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5 fresh	Blackberries
2 shot	Chairman's Reserve Spiced Rum
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
1 barspoon	Charcoal powder
review: A Rum Sour blackened with blackberries and charcoal powder. The black charcoal which makes this cocktail black does little for the taste and given the potential issues with charcoal this tasty cocktail is perhaps best appreciated without its addition (as illustrated photographed here).
history: A cocktail which was widely made to celebrate the total solar eclipse which worked its way across the USA on 21 August 2017 – the first for 38 years.

name: Castle Cobbler
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with pebble ice. Float Peychaud's on drink.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1 shot	Byrrh Grand Quinquina
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Crème de Pêche de Vigne liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
9 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: A fruity bittersweet apéritif with "orchard fruit, citrus and bittersweet gentian sipped through a sarsaparilla-like layer of Peychaud's Bitters."
history:
Created in 2017 by Taoufike Zrafi at Taology, Montreal, Canada, who says, "I was basically trying to work on a low proof cobbler style cocktail that really puts the flavor of Suze on the forefront of the flavor profiles. I went towards using only southern French ingredients and whilst tasting it behind the bar a guest asked me to try it, as soon as he did, he ordered one right away and demanded for it to be on the menu for next time he's going to come in. Enjoy this drink while you're castle hopping in your next trip to southern France!"

For information on the fascinating history of Cobblers please see our page.

name: Ernst Happel
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strega liqueur
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Kirschwasser (cherry) eau-de-vie
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Gin-laced, tangy, herbal, fruity and citrusy.
history: Ernst Franz Hermann Happel was a famous Austrian football player and coach, regarded by many as one of the most successful managers of all time.

name: Barracuda
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Galliano L'Autentico liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: There's a touch of Tiki to this pineapple rum sour that's made distinctive by peppermint and herbal flavours.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in the late 1950s by Italian bartender Benito Cuppari while working on the Cristoforo Colombo cruise liner. Benito perfected his tropical cocktail in 1965 soon after moving to Bar Lido, one of seven bars onboard the new SS Michelangelo cruise liner and re-named it after the Barracuda beach club in Portofino which was managed by a great friend of his and during the 50s and 60s was one of Europe's most famous nightclubs. Benito and his cocktail won the Long Drink category at the 1966 Italian AIBES National Cocktail Competition held in Saint Vincent so also helping the cocktail's notoriety.

Initially served in half a pineapple shell, after marketing support from Galliano, this was upgraded to a souvenir ceramic pineapple and quickly became the ship's signature cocktail. Galliano's promotional pineapple mug was imprinted with the Barracuda recipe, also using two other products from the same brand portfolio.

name: La Cola Nostra
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass pre-charged with prosecco.
ingredients:
2 shot	Martinique V.S.O.P rum
1 shot	Averna Amaro
1⁄4 shot	Pimento dram/Allspice liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 1⁄2 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
review: We do like a pun and this one is a particularly tasty aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2018 by Don Lee, New York City, USA.

name: José Marti Especial
preparation: MUDDLE cloves with rum in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 dried	Clove
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄12 shot	Pastis
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Aniseed and clove delicately influence this complex riff on a classic Daiquiri.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created by Andy Loudon at Satan's Whiskers, London, England. Andy won the Havana Club Cocktail Grand Prix in Cuba with this cocktail in in 2014.

José Julián Martí Pérez was a Cuban poet. Professor and publisher who is regarded as a Cuban national hero.

name: Tom & Cherry
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo Maraschino cherry on stick
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
1⁄3 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Cherry juice
1⁄6 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review: Old tom gin with layers of cherry, a hint of bitter-sweetness and a balancing zesty sourness.
history: Created in May 2020 by yours truly after our cherry farmer neighbour, Mike, brought a case of his cherry juice round during lockdown. We look over his cherry orchard but prior to this delivery and cocktail, we were not connected to his delicious cherries.

name: Celery Gin Sour
garnish: Lime zest twist (discarded) & rest celery stick across rim with a light dusting of celery salt
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Rutte Celery Dry Gin
1⁄3 shot	Bigallet Genepi Grand Tetras
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Celery saccharum (celery syrup)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
1 dash	Celery bitters
review: Genepi adds a touch of herbal sweetness to what is quite literally a Celery Gin Sour.
history: Created in June 2020 by yours truly.

name: Celery Gringo
garnish: Rest celery stick across rim with a light dusting of celery salt
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Rutte Celery Dry Gin
1⁄3 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄4 shot	Manzanilla sherry
5⁄12 shot	Celery saccharum (celery syrup)
1⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A gin sour with faint smoky mezcal, saline and vegetal notes.
history: Created in June 2020 by yours truly.

name: Peach Tea
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Peachtree peach schnapps
1 shot	Cold black breakfast tea
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Black tea tannins and sour citrus juice balance rich fruit peach in this long rum and cognac-laced cocktail.
history: Recipe created in June 2020 by yours truly but inspired by numerous other "Peach Tea" recipes on the Interweb.

name: Paddington
preparation: RINSE chilled glass with absinthe and set to one side. STIR marmalade with rum in base of shaker until marmalade is dissolved. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into absinthe-rinsed glass.
ingredients:
1⁄12 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
2 barspoon	Orange marmalade
1⁄2 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Sweet and sour with citrus tartness and faint absinthe anise.
history: Created Autumn 2008 by David Slape at PDT Bar in New York City soon after the bar opened. David was inspired by a taxidermied black bear on the wall of the bar which was nicknamed Paddington. This recipe is adapted from Jim Meehan's 2011 The PDT Cocktail Book.

name: Mollymock
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Dark/black/blackstrap rum
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
4 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters (optional)
review: Generously flavoured, bittersweet, sweet 'n' sour and Daiquiri-like.

name: The Frank
garnish: Quarter orange slice wheel on rim
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: My equal parts riff on one of Sydney's Maybe Sammy's best-known house cocktails. It is a tad mellower yet retains the drink's bittersweet agave laced aperitivo character.
history:
Adapted from a 2020 recipe created by the folk at Maybe Sammy in Sydney, Australia. The folk at Maybe Sammy pre-batch this cocktail but their recipe for a single-serve is more in line with the following proportions:
12.5 ml Mezcal
12.5 ml Blanco tequila
25 ml Campari
5 ml Amaro Montenegro
12.5 ml Dry vermouth
12.5 ml Sweet vermouth

name: Vanity
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Speyburn 10yo Speyside single malt
1⁄2 shot	Pommeau du Normandie
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
4 fresh	Cranberries (fresh)
review: Apple and lemon juice are renowned for pairing well with Scotch whisky and in the Vanity, this harmonious combination is further enhanced by apple appearing in the deliciously characterful form of Pommeau de Normandie. This cocktail benefits from the sweet and sour fruitiness that fresh cranberries contribute but it's still tasty without them.

name: Flor de Jerez
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Amontillado sherry
1⁄2 shot	Jamaican aged blended rum with funk
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A rum-laced, sherry sour with a balancing splash of rich apricot liqueur.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2009 by Joaquín Simó at Death & Company in New York City, USA.

name: Pearl of Puebla
preparation: Gently MUDDLE (just to bruise) oregano sprigs (stalks & leaves) in base of shaker. ADD other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3 sprig	Oregano (fresh)
1 2⁄3 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
3⁄4 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄6 shot	Pastis
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Agave syrup
review: A herbal riff on Audrey Saunders' French Pearl with mezcal in place of gin.
history: Created in the winter of 2008 by Jim Meehan, this recipe is from his 2011 The PDT Cocktail Book in which he says, "With the help of barman Euclides López, I fashioned a Mexican rendition of Audrey Saunders' French Pearl using two staples of Puebla Cuisine: mezcal and fresh oregano."

name: Brooklyn Heights
preparation: POUR Italian red bitter liqueur into chilled/frozen glass and turn to coat inside of glass. Discard excess and set glass aside. STIR other ingredients with ice and fine strain into red bitter liqueur-rinsed glass.
ingredients:
1⁄12 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Meletti amaro
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Bittersweet with rye whiskey's assertive spirituous spice, this is an aperitivo for those occasions when the pre-dinner drink needs to be a sharpener.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2011 by Maxwell Britten at Jack the Horse Tavern in Brooklyn Heights, New York City, USA. The original recipe calls for Luxardo Amaro Abano but (at the time of writing) this amaro is not available in the UK.

name: Outlaw
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Horse with No Name habanero bourbon
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A cherry brandy habanero-infused whiskey riff on the bourbon-based Scofflaw cocktail.
history: Created in August 2021 by yours truly.

name: Allegheny
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Crème de Mûre liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: I've used a 50/50 mix of dry and bianco vermouths to add some (I believe) much-needed honeyed richness to the all-dry vermouth vintage recipe. Depending on your lemons and crème de mûre, the subtle richness added by splitting the vermouth in this way will hopefully help achieve a perfectly balanced cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide.

name: Pot of Gold
garnish: Dust with edible gold flakes across cocktail's surface
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) to emulsify and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1⁄3 shot	Ginger liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Smooth Irish and peat-smoked Scotch whiskies enlivened with ginger spice and freshened by zesty lemon.

name: Mulled Negroni
garnish: Orange wedge or slice and/or orange zest twist
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Claret red wine
1⁄3 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
review: Red wine, clove-forward falernum and sloe gin add "Mulled" notes to this Negroni.
history: Created yours truly in November 2021 after coming across numerous other Mulled Negroni recipes on the Interweb. None appealed, but I liked the name, so I created my own.

name: Day Bell
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. TOP with sparkling wine.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Ramazzotti amaro
1⁄4 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
1 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Deliciously bittersweet with zesty orange and enlivened by sparkling wine. If you like Negronis then you should try this aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2010 by Joaquín Símo at Death & Company in New York City, USA.

name: Fourth Regiment
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 drop	Celery bitters
review: For this vintage Manhattan riff, I've used two (aromatic and celery) of the three styles of bitters stipulated for this cocktail by both Jacques Straub (1914) and Charles H. Baker Jr. (1939), along with a Creole-style bitters, with which some folk say the Fourth Regiment was originally made. The third style of bitters Straub and Baker stipulate is orange bitters, but I like to add bitter orange oil notes by way of an orange zest twist in place of the lemon twist Straub specifies or Baker's lime twist.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Jacques Straub's 1914 book Drinks.

name: Colonial Ties
preparation: RINSE (coat inside) chilled glass with absinthe and set aside. Add other ingredients to mixing glass, STIR with ice and strain into absinthe-rinsed glass (Sazerac-style, without ice in glass).
ingredients:
1⁄12 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄4 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Jamaican aged blended rum with funk
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Some like to muddle a bitters-soaked brown sugar cube until "smooth paste" to make this cocktail. Depending on your sugar cube, even with a splash of soda water, after what seems like an eternity you may still see sugar crystals rather than paste. Life's too short so I've used 2:1 brown sugar syrup to make this punchy nightcap of a cocktail. One person's paste is another's syrup!
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2014 by Eric Alperin at The Varnish in Los Angeles.

name: Mellow Yellow
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Becherovka liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: A touch of clove-like spice enlivens this otherwise headline "Mellow" golden yellow herbal cocktail.

name: French 1605
garnish: Float small leaf from the tip of a mint sprig
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with sparkling wine/champagne.
ingredients:
1⁄3 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄3 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Chartreuse Élixir Végétal
3 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Chartreuse herbal complexity and richness are soured by lemon and invigorated by brut sparkling wine/champagne in this riff on a French 75.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in March 2021 by Clare Morrow of Cask Liquid Marketing (UK distributors of Chartreuse) for Chartreuse Day, celebrated annually on 16th May.

name: The Vervet
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. Carefully POUR coffee liqueur into centre of the cocktail (it should sink to create a dark layer at the bottom of the cocktail).
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄3 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄2 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
history: The Vervet is a species of monkey with a white body and a black head and is the inspiration for this layered, faintly coffee and banana-influenced riff on a 20th Century cocktail. Fittingly, this cocktail finishes with enlivening coffee. Originally based on Monkey 47 Gin.

name: Rye's Up
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass (no ice in glass).
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
3 drop	Bob's Liquorice bitters
review: This short, rye-based, spirit-forward, and delicately floral "Up" (straight-up/ without ice) cocktail is best enjoyed as a "sharpener" before or after a meal.
history: A contemporary cousin of the Sazerac.

name: Bay Ridge
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄4 shot	La Vieille Prune plum brandy
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: As per the original, I've used a bottled-in-bond strength rye whiskey but some may want to add a splash more of it to this well-balanced Manhattan-style cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2014 by Tom Macy at Clover Club in Brooklyn, New York City, USA, who named his cocktail after a neighbourhood of Brooklyn.

name: Bananarac
preparation: POUR absinthe into chilled glass and swirl to coat (rinse) inside and set aside. STIR other ingredients with ice and strain into absinthe-rinsed glass (without ice).
ingredients:
1⁄12 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Banana fruitiness subtly flavours and lightens a base of rye whiskey and cognac with absinthe adding delicate anise notes.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Natasha David at Nitecap Bar in New York City, USA.

name: Across the Pacific
garnish: Dust with freshly grated nutmeg and lime wheel slice
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Jamaican-style overproof aged pot still rum
1⁄2 shot	Averna Amaro
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
4 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters (optional)
review: Tiki meets the aperitivo/digestivo in this sweet 'n' sour almond daiquiri. Like other daiquiris, this cocktail benefits from dilution so, hence the serve over crushed ice. (Add a splash of water to the recipe if serving on-the-rocks.)
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Meaghan Dorman at Raines Law Room in New York City, USA. Meaghan's original recipe calls for Appleton Reserve and Smith & Cross Jamaican rums.

name: Lulu White
garnish: Pitted green olive dropped into glass
preparation: THROW all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	Ambrato/ambre/amber vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄6 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A delicious bite-sized tequila and absinthe Dry Martini with a pleasing hint of olive-influenced salinity.
history: Adapted from a cocktail made for me in September 2022 by Nate at Lulu White bar in Paris, France. I liked it so much, I had three of them. This, the bar's signature cocktail, is ever-evolving as it changes with each iteration of the menu. My rendition is inspired by the cocktail I enjoyed at Lulu White rather than a reproduction.

name: Elusive Dreams
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Pineapple rum
1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Pineapple juice
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Cinnamon syrup
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
review: A riff on the classic Hotel Nacional Special cocktail with rum-laced, sweet 'n' sour, tropical fruit and delicate cinnamon spice.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Demi Natoli at Patterson House in Nashville, USA.

name: Silver Bay
preparation: POUR first 5 ingredients into a pre-warmed glass, the TOP with boiling water.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Island single malt Scotch whisky
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Creme de Chataigne
1⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1 dash	Whiskey barrel-aged bitters
3 shot	Boiling water
review: Delicately smoky whisky and chestnut liqueur infuse this tasty hot toddy.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in late 2022 by Bobby Hiddleston at Swift bar in London, England. Originally based on Talisker 10 single malt Scotch whisky.

name: Orchard View
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large ice cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
2⁄3 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: If you like Manhattans, you should try this calvados-based, delicately herbal variation served on the rocks.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in February 2023 by Kaitlin Wilkes for Avallen calvados.

name: Peat, Blood, Sweat & Sand
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) & float dehydrated blood orange slice or skewered Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass
ingredients:
1 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
3⁄4 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Blood orange juice
1⁄6 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Faint earthy peaty and bittersweet notes befit the name in this riff on a classic Blood & Sand. Sadly, it's a tad seasonal as this is a lesser cocktail when made with regular orange, rather than blood orange juice.
history: Created in April 2023 by yours truly at The Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Phenoxy Penicillin
garnish: Skewered candied ginger & mist with 3 sprays of peated whisky
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
2⁄3 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Ginger liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄6 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
review: The smoky peated whisky, ginger and honeyed citrus flavours of Sam Ross' original Penicillin with a splash of bittersweet amaro.
history: Created in May 2023 by yours truly at the Clocktower in Rye, England. This riff on a Penicillin cocktail is so named due to 'Phenoxymethylpenicillin' being an antibiotic and 'phenols' being compounds that contribute to the flavour of whisky.

name: Grapevyne
preparation: MUDDLE grapes in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
8 fresh	Green grapes (seedless)
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Ambrato/ambre/amber vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Bepi Tosolini Grappa di Moscato
1⁄6 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Vodka-laced grape juice is delicious in this cocktail with layers of complexity thanks to judicious additions of characterful dry vermouth, Chartreuse, grappa, and absinthe.
history: A riff on the Grape Cocktail. Created by yours truly in May 2023 at The Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Pornstar Bellini
preparation: Cut a fresh passion fruit in half and scoop the seeds and flesh into shaker. Add next 4 ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with sparkling wine.
ingredients:
1 fresh	Passion fruit (fresh)
1⁄3 shot	Passoã passion fruit liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
1⁄6 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
review: The core ingredients in a Porn Star Martini served with the sparkling wine in the glass to produce what's become known as a Pornstar Bellini.

name: Forbidden Fruit Martini
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with sparkling wine.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
2⁄3 shot	Giffard Rhubarbe Liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
1⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
1 2⁄3 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: A calvados-based rhubarb and vanilla sour. The rhubarb and vanilla seem to amplify the flavour of the calvados rather than playing a distinctive role themselves.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in February 2023 by Kaitlin Wilkes for Avallen calvados. Kaitlin's original recipe calls for sparkling dry cider buti've substituted this for brut sparkling wine.

name: Hedgerow
garnish: Skewered lime slice wheel & candied ginger (sail)
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice. Open shaker and POUR cider and ginger beer into shaker. STRAIN into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 shot	Dry cider
1 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: Elegantly fruity and citrussy with enlivening ginger spice.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in February 2023 by Kaitlin Wilkes for Avallen Calvados.

name: Ruby Punch
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients, including lemon peel (Regal shake) with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 swath	Lemon peel
1 1⁄3 shot	Batavia arrack
1 1⁄3 shot	Ruby port
2 shot	Cold black tea
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review:
Arrack provides the funky spirituous base, port adds rich fruitiness, tea lengthens and adds bitter tannins, while sugar and lemon balance each other with classic zesty sweet 'n' sourness. A brilliant alternative to an afternoon cup of tea on a summer's day.

Depending on the sweetness of your port and tannins in your tea, you may need to increase the sugar syrup to 15ml (½oz).
history: A single-serve version of the Ruby Punch in Jerry Thomas' 1862 The Bartender's Guide. I've roughly divided Thomas' punch bowl recipe by 19 to fit a Collins glass

name: White Negroni Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Hayman's Navy Strength Royal Dock Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Blanc quinquina/kina (e.g. Mattei Cap Corse or Kina L'Aéro d'Or)
1⁄4 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Bittersweet and packed with quinine, gentian and zesty lemon.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2022 by Orlando Franklin McCray while bartending in New York City, USA.

name: Red Banana Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Banana rum
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
4 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: How "red" this Daiquiri ends up will depend on your choice of grenadine, but the flavour should be undeniably funky banana.
history: Created in December 2023 by yours truly at The Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: White Monkey
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Orgeat almond liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Milk (whole milk/full 3-4% fat)
2 dash	Dandelion & Burdock Bitters (optional)
review: Pisco shines in this delightfully fresh cocktail that's mellowed by dairy rather than being creamy.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by New York City bartender Tom Richter.

name: Cherry Blossom Sake Martini
garnish: Skewered black olive with cherry blossom when in season
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Akashi-Tai Daiginjo Genshu sake
1 shot	Mancino Vermouth di Torino Sakura
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄6 shot	Cherry blossom/sakura syrup
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Yes, it's a Martini in as much that it has gin and vermouth, but, as the name promises, cherry blossom and sake are the focus.
history: Created in April 2024 by yours truly at the Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Mezcal Porn Star Martini
preparation:
SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

Optionally, separately, POUR champagne into a chilled shot glass to serve on the side. Instruct the drinker to sip alternately from each glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄2 shot	Passoã passion fruit liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
1⁄2 shot	Passion fruit purée
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: A mezcal-laced riff on the classically vanilla vodka-based Porn Star Martini.
history: Recipe by yours truly.

name: Stun Wray
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice, and after shaking, add the apple juice, then strain into glass half-filled with crushed ice. TOP with more crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 shot	White overproof rum
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
4 drop	Bob's Abbotts bitters
1 1⁄3 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review: To better fit a 12oz Collins glass, I've reduced the original spec of this cocktail by a third. However, you'll need properly cold crushed ice (ideally cubes crushed straight from a deep freezer) to ensure your Stun Wray doesn't misfire due to being waterlogged.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR, Oxford, England, who originally used Tempus Fugit Crème de Banane. Jason says, "This cocktail is named after the Star Trek phaser that made its debut in the same 1966 episode as the immortal Captain Kirk."

name: R.N.L.I.
garnish: Lime wedge, paper boat or a miniature lifeboat person
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Gold rum (1-3 years old pot & column blend)
1⁄2 shot	Navy rum (54.5% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Italicus liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water
review:
Gold rum, Navy rum and bergamot liqueur influence this seafarer's Daiquiri. The first four ingredients are an acronym of RNLI (Rum, Navy rum, Lime, Italics).

Please help the R.N.L.I. (Royal National Lifeboat Institution) save lives at sea. Donate at rnli.org.
history: A riff on Julio Cabrera's Daiquiricus, created in July 2024 by yours truly for the R.N.L.I., particularly Emily Leroy-Lewis and the crew at our local Rye Lifeboat Station.

name: Autumn Sweater
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass, preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice.
ingredients:
1 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Averna Amaro
1⁄2 shot	Amaro Nonino Quintessentia
1⁄2 shot	Maple syrup
1 dash	Fee Brothers Turkish Tobacco Bitters
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: As the evenings draw in, it's time to put the fire on and hunker down for winter. Instead, grab an Autumn Sweater to warm body and soul.
history: Adapted from a recipe by Brad Thomas Parsons, published in his 2011 book Bitters: A Spirited History of a Classic Cure-All. Brad's original recipe calls for Urban Moonshine Maple Bitters in place of tobacco bitters.

name: Algonquin
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Pineapple juice
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Classically made with 2 parts whiskey, 1 part dry vermouth, and 1 part pineapple juice, this vintage cocktail is opened and improved by splitting the vermouth to include some bianco vermouth. Creole-style bitters are a must, traditionally one dash but better with two.
history: Adapted from a recipe in G. Selmer Fougner's 1935 Along The Wine Trail : an anthology of wines and spirits, this is one of several 1930s classics attributed to New York City's Algonquin Hotel.

name: Improved Bronx
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 shot	Tangerine / Mandarin / Clementine juice (fresh juice)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Delicate, fragrant fruity notes from freshly squeezed tangerine/mandarin juice freshen this version of the classic Bronx. My recipe for both versions of the Bronx are the same, it's just the use of tangerine/mandarin/clementine orange juice that denotes this "Improved".
history: Bronx cocktail history

name: Cactus Banger
