preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
2⁄3 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Galliano L'Autentico liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A "bangin", golden, sunny-looking and sunny-tasting cocktail.
history:
I don't have any notes as to the origin of this version of the Cactus Banger but as one of the older recipes on my database, its origin is pre-late 1990s.

A Cactus Banger is perhaps better known as being a simple Harvey Wallbanger based on tequila rather than vodka and it is this version that appears in books such as Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide.

name: Chancellor
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 shot	Tawny port
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review:
Complex and sophisticated, scotch whisky-based with rich and dry vinous notes.

Classically, the Chancelor is made with dry vermouth, but even with a rich ruby port, this tends to produce a cocktail that's too dry. I favour a more complex tawny port, and previously, I added 2.5ml of sugar to balance it. Now, instead of sugar, I split the vermouth between dry and bianco vermouths. I also like the above recipe but with the vermouth split three ways: 5ml (1 barspoon) each of dry vermouth, bianco vermouth and rosso vermouth.

Others use only rosso vermouth instead of dry vermouth, which adds much-needed sweetness as well as body and colour. Some also use aromatic bitters, but I like to honour the style of bitters specified by Stanley M. Jones in his 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide.
history:
The Chancellor cocktail most likely originated in London and is named in the "Supplementary List" of cocktails that "space forbids giving the recipes" in William James "Billy" Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Bar Book.

The Chancellor also appears in Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide.

name: Dirty Banana
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with 6oz scoop crushed ice.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
2 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1 fresh	Banana (preferably overripe)
review:
A rum-laced banana milkshake dirtied by coffee liqueur. The riper the banana used in this cocktail, the better. (Brown spots on the banana skin = tasty cocktail.) This cocktail makes for a filling dessert, so consider splitting this recipe between two 10oz Highball glasses and sharing with a friend. Or for a smaller single-serve:

Dirty Banana (half-sized recipe)
Glass: Highball (6oz - 10oz /18cl - 30cl)
Garnish: Banana chunk on rim
Method: BLEND all ingredients with half 6oz scoop crushed ice.
30ml (1oz) Light rum (mellow white/gold 1-3 year old)
15ml (½oz) Coffee liqueur
15ml (½oz) Crème de banana
30ml (1oz) Single cream/half-and-half
1/2 fresh Banana (peeled)
history: A popular cocktail in Jamaica where we discovered this cocktail in the 1990s.

name: Dirty Sanchez
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with ginger beer.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	Tequila agave liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: A Tequila Sour with delicate berry fruit, lengthened and invigorated with ginger beer.
history: Created in 2001 by Phillip Jeffrey and Ian Baldwin at the GE Club in London, England.

name: Golden Cadillac
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄2 shot	Galliano L'Autentico liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: This shaken recipe includes orange juice (classically, it doesn't), giving the otherwise anaemic-looking cocktail its namesake golden hue. Adding orange bitters helps balance and boosts orange flavour.
history:
To quote the bar's own website (poorredsbbq.com), "Poor Red's is world-famous for its Golden Cadillacs. Cadillacs are a blended drink of Galliano liqueur, half and half, white créme de cacao and ice, most delicious! We are the largest consumer of Galliano in the world. Also famous for our award-winning barbecued ribs."

Poor Reds say, " In 1952, a newly engaged couple came to Poor Red's to celebrate their engagement. They asked bartender Frank Klein to create their own special cocktail that would match their newly purchased gold-colored Cadillac. The bartender served the drink in a champagne coupe glass to signify its celebratory nature meant for her and a sidecar glass for him. When you order one Gold Cadillac, you get two glasses.

Galliano noticed the popularity of the Gold Cadillac when their Northern California sales began to increase so they ran an advertising campaign for this drink from 1964 to 1967. The drink became famous around the world."

On Poor Red's bar menu, they call their signature cocktail simply "Gold Cadillac", as does John J. Poister's 1989 The New American Bartender's Guide. However, other vintage cocktail tomes, e.g. Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide, list it as a "Golden Cadillac", and it is by this name that this cocktail is now better known.

name: Jayne Mansfield
garnish: Place strawberry on glass rim with a mint sprig tip replacing the strawberry's leaves
preparation: MUDDLE strawberries in base of shaker. Add next 3 ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into glass. TOP with sparkling wine.
ingredients:
4 fresh	Strawberries (hulled, small & ripe)
1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Fraise des Bois liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 2⁄3 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Fizz is made to accompany strawberries, all the more delicious when laced with rum.
history:
Named after the Hollywood actress, nightclub entertainer and 1950s-60s sex symbol.

Born Vera Jayne Palmer in April 1933, Jayne Mansfield's fame and notoriety were helped by her numerous publicity stunts and flamboyant personal life. Nicknamed "Hollywood's smartest dumb blonde," she enjoyed several box-office successes, won a Golden Globe Award, and, in the sex comedy Promises! Promises! (1963) became the first American actress to perform a nude scene in a major movie.

Tragically, she died aged just 34 (on 29 June 1967) in a car crash in New Orleans.

name: Million Dollar Margarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Agave syrup
4 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters (optional)
review: Although a relatively dry Margarita this particular millionaire benefits from the rich orange notes of a cognac-based orange liqueur.
history: Adapted from a drink discovered in 2006 at Maison 140 Hotel in Los Angeles, USA where we paid a mere $41.14 plus tip for one.

name: Mocha Martini
preparation: SHAKE first four ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. FLOAT cream in centre of drink.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
1⁄2 shot	Irish cream liqueur
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
1⁄2 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: Made with great espresso, this drink is a superb, richly flavoured balance of sweet and bitter.
history: The Espresso Martini story

name: Whisky Butter
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. FLOAT drizzle of Islay malt on the surface of the drink.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄4 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
3⁄4 shot	Warninks Advocaat liqueur
1⁄24 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
review: Creamy and complex Christmassy cocktail. Fino sherry dries, Scotch whisky provides backbone and character while advocaat adds dairy-like creaminess. Chartreuse monastic liqueur adds faint religious significance – drink after all Christmas is meant to celebrate the birth of Christ.
history: Created in December 2014 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Mulata Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
1⁄4 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A classic Daiquiri with aged rum and a hint of chocolate.
history:
Thought to have been created by Constantino (Constante) Ribalaigua Vert at Havana's Floridita bar, but in the Cuban book Bartender's Sixth Sense, the Mulata is said to have been created in the 1940s by one Jose Maria Vazquez.

This cocktail was originally made with Bacardi Elixir, a liqueur made by infusing plums in rum, but since the 1970s crème de cacao liqueur has been used as a substitute.

Production of Bacardi Elixir ended when Bacardi was forced to leave Cuba, but a small batch of around 60 bottles was made to celebrate Bacardi Legacy Competition in April 2013.

See Daiquiri cocktail history

name: Orange Custard Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Warninks Advocaat liqueur
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
6 drop	Bob's Vanilla bitters
review: A smooth creamy orangey dessert cocktail that is surprisingly boozy and far from overly sweet. However, be warned, it is thick and rich - just as a dessert cocktail should be.
history: Created in 2002 by yours truly after rediscovering advocaat on a trip to Amsterdam. This cocktail was originally an "Orange Custard Martini" - every new cocktail was a Martini in those days. Firstly, for reasons of decency, I switched Martini for Cocktail in the name, then, In January 2019, I reduced the amount of advocaat a tad, swapped the now relatively obscure Tuaca liqueur for brandy, and added the vanilla bitters. I think for the better all around.

name: Painkiller
garnish: Dust with freshly grated nutmeg. Garnish with pineapple wedge
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Navy rum (54.5% alc./vol.)
3 shot	Pineapple juice
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Cream of coconut (e.g. Coco Lopez, Re'al etc.)
4 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters (optional)
review: The broadside firepower of navy rum balances sweet pineapple and coconut in what is an all too delicious Tiki-style libation.
history:
From the Soggy Dollar bar on the island of Jost Van Dyke in the British Virgin Islands. The bar's name is logical, as most of the clientele are sailors and there is no dock. Hence they have to swim ashore, often paying for drinks with wet dollars.

A variation on the classic Pina Colada. See our main Piña Colada page for the story behind the classic and for links to numerous other variations.

name: Park Avenue
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄3 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
4 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters (optional)
review:
Very fruity and well-balanced rather than dry or sweet.

The recipe previously on this page was in line with that in the 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide:
50ml (1 2/3oz) Dry gin
20ml (2/3oz) Pineapple juice
10ml (2/3oz) Orange Curaçao
10ml (1/3oz) Rosso (sweet) vermouth
But thanks to a comment by Clarence Castillo (see below), in February 2023 I adopted Ted Haigh's 2009 Park Avenue. Then, a month later, thanks to further encouragement from Clarence, I dropped the gin back a tad and added Daiquiri (roasted pineapple & mint bitters).
history: A degree of mystery surrounds this vintage cocktail, partly due to its first known appearance in a recipe book, Dexter Mason's 1930 The Art of Living, being quite a different recipe to that recognised as a Park Avenue today.

name: Pear Drop
garnish: Pear slice on rim & or serve with pear drop hard candy
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Pear & cognac liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Poire William eau-de-vie
1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Pear juice (freshly pressed)
review: Like the eponymous candy, this after-dinner/late-night cocktail has a full-on tangy pear flavour.
history: Created in 2002 by yours truly.

name: Orinoco cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cachaça
1 1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄3 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄4 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
review: Dry sherry, chocolate and almond add subtle nuances to a base of cachaça and apple juice.
history: Adapted from an originally blended drink created in 2015 by Sergio Padilla at Boca Chica in Barcelona, Spain.

name: Pomegranate Margarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 shot	Pomegranate juice
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Pomegranate and tequila combine harmoniously in this Margarita.
history: Recipe by Simon Difford in 2006.

name: Red Rum 'Martini'
preparation: MUDDLE redcurrants in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
24 fresh	Redcurrants
1 2⁄3 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
review: A beautifully fruity, adult balance of bittersweet flavours.
history:
Created by Jason Scott in 2002 at Oloroso in Edinburgh, Scotland.

This cocktail, which is red and contains rum, is named after Red Rum, the only horse in history to win England's Grand National three times (on his other two attempts, he came second). He became a British hero, appeared on the BBC Sports Personality of the Year show and paraded right up to his death at age 30 in 1995.

name: Rosita
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters (optional)
review: Bittersweet, tequila-based, and Negroni-like. Classically garnished with a lemon zest twist but better with grapefruit.
history:
The origin of this drink remains unknown, but its popularity (like many things in the drinks industry) can be attributed to Gary 'gaz' Regan, even though for some years he was in denial.

The Rosita was introduced to gaz by a fellow cocktail geek back in 2005; who in turn had discovered the recipe in an article written by Terry Sullivan, a fellow drinks writer. Gaz questioned Sullivan as to where he found the recipe, but he could not remember so gaz let the matter drop until 2007 when he made the drink as an aperitif for a few friends round for dinner. Gaz's guests asked the origins of the drink and this led gaz to contact Sullivan again.

This time Sullivan remembered and told gaz that he had found it in The Bartender's Bible. Now many of you will already be smiling as The Bible, published in 1991, was gaz Regan's first book.

Gaz imbibed and wrote about thousands of cocktails over the years so it is understandable that he overlooked his own book. After an embarrassed oh-yeah moment he started rummaging around in the back of the closet of his guest room where an oversized envelope still held his working notes for the book. So it transpired that gaz purloined the recipe from a 1988 edition of Mr. Boston Official Bartender's Guide, but he had added a typical gaz touch, namely a dash of bitters, and predictably a bit more tequila.

The recipe has since been traced back to at 1974 edition of the Mr. Boston Official Bartender's Guide.

name: Slow Comfortable Screw Against The Wall
preparation: STIR first three ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. DRIZZLE sloe gin around surface so it bleeds into drink. FLOAT Galliano.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Southern USA-style liqueur 40% (e.g. Southern Comfort)
3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
1⁄2 shot	Galliano L'Autentico liqueur
review: Galliano adds the wall (as in Harvey Wallbanger) and some herbal peppermint to this Slow Comfortable Screw. Yes, the name's corny but made with fresh orange, this drink is a good brunch or summertime option.
history: More information on the Slow Screw family of cocktails is included on our Slow Screw cocktails page.

name: Spiced Pear
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Pear & cognac liqueur
1 shot	Chairman's Reserve Spiced Rum
1 shot	Pear juice (freshly pressed)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Just as it says on the tin - spiced pear.
history: Created in 2002 by James Stuart-Gammie, Edinburgh, Scotland

name: The Reindeer
garnish: Holly sprig & Luxardo Maraschino cherry (the holly represents the antlers and the cherry the red nose)
preparation:
MUDDLE ginger in base of shaker. Add next three ingredients (all but champagne), SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne.

Spicy sugar syrup
To make your own festive spice syrup: Stir half a cup of hot water and half a cup of sugar in a pan until sugar is dissolved. Add 1 cracked cinnamon stick, ½ a split vanilla pod and 1 teaspoon of cracked Szechuan peppers. Cover for 15 minutes then strain and cool liquid. If using this syrup in the recipe below then use 12.5ml.
ingredients:
2 slice	Fresh ginger root (thumbnail-sized slice)
2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Citroen Vodka
1⁄4 shot	Chili pepper syrup
1⁄12 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
Top up with	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2016 by Ketel One Brand Ambassador, Dave Beatty.

name: Alice Mine
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Medium-dry with luscious orange notes. The orange zest twist is essential to the balance of this late-night sipper.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide.

name: Sir Walter Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄4 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Spirit-forward with faint zesty tartness balanced by delicate rich red fruit sweetness.
history:
The Sir Walter (or Swalter) first appears in Harry MacElhone's 1927 Barflies and Cocktails and is repeated in other regarded tomes such as The Savoy Cocktail Book (1930).

Whether this cocktail honours Sir Walter Raleigh or Sir Walter Scott is a matter of conjecture, but as MacElhone, who heralded from Dundee, Scotland, is thought to be the drinks' creator, many favour Scott as being the protagonist.

name: Ampersand Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A boozy brandy-influenced 'wet' and 'sweet' Martini with a hint of orange. The zesty orange notes help the cleansing attributes of this spirit-forward cocktail, so making it equally suited to the pre-dinner and after-dinner occasions.
history: First published in Albert Stevens Crockett's 1934 Old Waldorf Bar Days.

name: Bloody Bronx Cocktail
garnish: Dehydrated blood orange slice or orange zest twist
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Blood orange juice
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A Bronx made 'bloody' by the use of blood oranges. Fruity yet dry with botanical notes both from the vermouth and the gin.
history: Bronx cocktail history and recipe variations

name: Hoyt's Daiquirí
preparation: Sear two halves of lime with a chef's blow torch and squeeze into a shaker. SHAKE all remaining ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 shot	Lime juice (burnt)
1⁄4 shot	Jägermeisteror other German amaro
1⁄2 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Most unusual and interesting. Recognisably a Daiquiri but with a creamy mouthfeel and great depth of flavour.
history: Created in 2008 by Meimi Sanchez at Bramble, Edinburgh, Scotland.

name: Brooklyn
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Amer Picon
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Perhaps my favourite of the many renditions of the Brooklyn cocktail due to being dry yet made approachable by faint sweet maraschino and bittersweet herbal complexity.
history:
One of the Manhattan variations named after New York's five boroughs.
Brooklyn cocktail history

name: Harold and Maude
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Rose sugar syrup
1⁄6 shot	Lavender sugar syrup
review: Balanced, complex and very, very serious.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2009 by Chase Mallen at Raines Law Rooms in New York City, USA.

name: IVO
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A berry fruity riff on a Perfect Manhattan
history: Named after the logo of Quo Vadis in London, where yours truly is a regular and in December 2009 asked Emma Ramos to make this drink for Charlotte Ashburner, then Chambord's UK Brand Manager. That original recipe was 60ml bourbon, 30ml dry vermouth, 15ml black raspberry liqueur, and 1 dash bitters, but hindsight is a wonderful thing.

name: Palomino Flor
garnish: Short pale yellow stalk and leaf from celery heart
preparation: MUDDLE celery in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Celery juice (freshly extracted)
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄6 shot	Elderflower liqueur
review: Celery imparts subtle vegetal notes in this unusual aperitivo cocktail.
history: Jody Monteith at The Liquorists, Manchester, England.

name: Zubrowka Cocktail
preparation: POUR absinthe into ice-filled glass, top with water and stand to one side. Separately STIR other ingredients with ice. Dump contents of glass and strain stirred drink into the absinthe washed glass.
ingredients:
1⁄3 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 1⁄2 shot	Bison grass vodka
1⁄4 shot	Goldwasser cinnamon schnapps liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: The grassy notes of Zubrówka and delicate cinnamon shine through in this well-balanced and well-integrated delicately spicy vintage cocktail.
history: Adapted from W. J. Tarling's (Bill Tarling) 1937 Café Royal Cocktail Book Coronation Edition in which the invention of this drink is credited to S. T. Yakimovitch.

name: Rapscallion
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) and olive on a stick
preparation: POUR pastis into a chilled ice-fillled glass, TOP with chilled water and leave to stand. Separately, STIR other ingredients with ice. DISCARD contents of glass (pastis, water and ice) and STRAIN contents of stirring glass into pastis-coated glass.
ingredients:
1⁄4 shot	Pastis
1 1⁄2 shot	Speyburn 10yo Speyside single malt
1⁄2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
1⁄4 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Smoky island malts tamed by the Christmas pudding flavours of Pedro Ximénez with pastis adding notes of enlivening anise. To quote Ruby's menu, "An unabashedly smoky, Scottish version of the Manhattan. Talisker single malt whisky and stirred over pedro ximenez sweet sherry with a Ricard pastis rinse. A well-loved signature Ruby Cocktail."
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2007 by Adeline Shepard and Craig Harper at Ruby Bar in Copenhagen, Denmark.

name: Bloody Blood & Sand
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄6 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
3⁄4 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 shot	Blood orange juice
review: A Blood & Sand with the smoky influence of Islay single malt whisky and the rounding citrus notes of blood orange juice.
history: Created in March 2014 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Fruit Cup Spritz
garnish: Half orange slice, lemon slice & mint sprig
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
3 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A light summery spritz with flavours reminiscent of Pimm's.
history:
Created in 2013 by yours truly for Jamie's Italian Bar.

Also see Fruit Cups and Pimm's

name: Affogato Cocktail
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with three cubes ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bepi Tosolini Grappa di Moscato
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
1 scoop	Vanilla ice cream
review: Based on the eponymous classic Italian dessert, this after-dinner cocktail blends coffee and chocolate with ice-cream, appropriately fortified with a splash of grappa.
history: Created in 2013 by yours truly for Jamie Oliver's bars.

name: White Christmas
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 barspoon	Mincemeat
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1⁄4 shot	Gingerbread sugar syrup
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: As the name suggests, this is a Christmassy riff on a White Russian cocktail– the festive feel courtesy of mincemeat and gingerbread syrup.
history: Created in December 2014 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room in London, England.

name: Saison l'Hiver
preparation: MUDDLE clove in base of shaker. Add next 3 ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
1 dried	Clove
1⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
Top up with	Rosé champagne
review: The rich wintery flavours of sloe gin and honey are balanced by lemon juice with clove providing seasonal spice and rosé champagne lifting and refreshing all.
history: Created in September 2014 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room in London, England.

name: Bending Blades cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	Manzanilla sherry
1⁄4 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Pamplemousse liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Tequila-based, zesty and bitter before turning bittersweet. In March 2022, I cut the volume of gentian liqueur from 15ml (½oz) back to 7.5ml (¼oz) so fans of bitter gentian my want to stick with the original spec.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Christopher Day at General Lee's in Los Angeles, USA.

name: Aristotle cocktail
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE mint in base of stirring glass. Add other ingredients, STIR with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3 fresh	Mint leaves
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Kleos Mastiha liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Birch water
4 drop	Bob's Peppermint Bitters
review: The thinking man's mixed drink, this is based on gin with the distinctive flavour of Greek mastiha and lengthened with birch water.
history: Created in August 2015 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Denny & Eleni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 shot	Kleos Mastiha liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1 shot	Birch water
8 drop	Bob's Liquorice bitters
review: Named after Denny Kallivoka and Eleni Nikoloulia, our favourite Greek drinks writers, this whisky based cocktail has a healthy glug of mastiha with birch water. It finishes with liquorice and Islay whisky.
history: Created in August 2015 by yours truly (Simon Difford) at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Minty Pentones cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe
1⁄2 shot	Kleos Mastiha liqueur
4 drop	Bob's Peppermint Bitters
review: Gin's botanical complexity combined with minty and mastiha freshness and a pink hint of cranberry fruitiness makes for a cleansing after-dinner digestif.
history: Created by yours truly in August 2015 at the Cabinet Room in London, England and named after one of my favourite New Orleans' bands, Mark and the Pentones, whose album was playing at the time of the drinks creation.

name: Sailor's Swizzle
garnish: A few dashes Angostura bitters over ice cap crowned with lime zest strings
preparation: POUR ingredients into chilled glass and two-thirds fill with crushed ice. SWIZZLE with a swizzle stick (or churn with a barspoon). Add more crushed ice to fill and SWIZZLE some more. Serve with straws.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
2⁄3 shot	Ruby port
1⁄6 shot	Pimento dram/Allspice liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Port wine is further fortified with golden rum and delicately spiced with Pimento Dram in this long swizzled punch.
history: Created in 2012 by Erik Lorincz at the American Bar, London, England.

name: Ironbound
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cachaça
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Who'd have thought cachaça and apple brandy would make such good bedfellows with herbal liqueur and Creole-style bitters.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Mayur Subbarao of New York, USA. Mayur's original recipe called for bottled-in-bond applejack rather than calvados. The extra punch of applejack dries this cocktail so if using calvados consider reducing the sugar syrup.

name: Picotin
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into a chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
3⁄4 shot	Akvavit / Aquavit
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Americano bianco
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
review: Bright yellow and on the bitter side of bittersweet with aquavit, lemon, gentian and maraschino liqueurs.
history: Created in 2015 by Florian Dubois at Joyeux Bordel in London, England.

name: Greenpoint
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Stirred and boozy with rye whiskey punch and spice smoothed by herbal Yellow Chartreuse and sweet vermouth.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2006 by Michael McIlroy at Milk & Honey in New York City, USA. Michael's original recipe calls for a lemon zest twist, but we prefer an orange zest twist.

name: Trade Winds
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
2⁄3 shot	Coconut water
1⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Coconut water adds dilution and subtly flavours this cognac-based cocktail with sweet vermouth and subtle notes of chocolate and Angostura.
history: Created in 2015 by Daniel Bovey at Be At One, Bristol, England.

name: A Rose By Any Other Name
garnish: Turkish Delight & grate dark chocolate over drink
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Lanique Spirit of Rose liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Crème de violette liqueur
3 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: A dry spirit-led sipper with faint floral and chocolate notes. Perhaps forgo the grated chocolate garnish in favour of a square of dark chocolate balanced on Turkish Delight.
history: Created in 2015 by Sammy Abdalla at The Suburbs, Hoole, Chester, England. Sammy's original recipe calls for Martell Cordon Bluu cognac and La Quintinye Vermouth Rouge.

name: Revolutionary Flip
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE without ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Tawny port
1⁄3 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
1 1⁄3 shot	British bitter ale
1 fresh	Egg (white & yolk)
review: "Full-bodied" both describes this cocktail and how you'll feel after consuming this very tasty meal of a drink.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Markus Olsen at Ziloufs, Islington, London, England.

Markus' original recipe uses equal parts molasses syrup and simple syrup in place of Demerara sugar syrup. It also contained 15ml/ 1/2 oz cream.

name: Titre Provisoire (Provisional Title)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄6 shot	Fig liqueur (crème de figue)
1⁄6 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1 dash	Apple cider vinegar
review: Characterful cognac, herbal Bénédictine and rich fig liqueur are harmoniously balanced by dry vermouth and cider vinegar. This drink is finely balanced but when achieved it sings.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Matt Robertson at Hawksmoor Spitalfields, London, England. Matt's original recipe calls for Martell Cordon Bleu cognac.

name: Mart-Inez
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into a chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
1⁄2 shot	Americano bianco
1⁄2 shot	Barley malt syrup (1:1)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Grape and grain combine harmoniously in this sipping cocktail.
history: Created in 2015 by Matteo Rebuffo at China Tang at Dorchester Hotel, London, England, using Martell Cognac – hence the name.

name: Black Gold
garnish: grapefruit zest twist (digarded), slice truffle & ginseng
preparation: STIR all ingredients in base of shaker until honey dissolves. Add ice, SHAKE and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bacardi Gold rum
2⁄3 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Ginseng liqueur
1 barspoon	Black truffle honey
review:
"I feel that the untameable spirit of Bacardí lives everywhere in nature: truffles, ginseng and herbs all grow out of extremely difficult environments. Just like bartenders, we work at night, are wild, free-spirited, untamed, we pass on positive energy and share good vibes with people, bringing our own distinct flair and 'flavours' to light up the bar; so I believe we bartenders are indeed 'black gold.'"

We say: A honey daiquiri with herbal spice courtesy of Bénédictine and ginseng aperitif. Depending on your ginseng aperitif (we used Kamm & Son but unlikely to be what they use in China) you may want to make that barspoon of honey slightly heaped rather than flat.
history: Chinese BACARDÍ LEGACY 2016 winning cocktail by Choni Song, The Nest, Shanghai.

name: The Seventh Art
preparation: MUDDLE popcorn in base of shaker, add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 cupful	Popcorn
1 2⁄3 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
1⁄3 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Confronted by a wide choice of popcorn at the supermarket I opted for Metcalfe's Honey Bee flavoured popcorn. The honey notes on the corn are very subdued and I wanted to avoid salted popcorn. As for the cocktail, tiny oily droplets from the sweetcorn form a layer on the surface of the drink and as you raise the glass to your lips the aroma of popcorn is surprisingly noticeable. Chartreuse slightly overwhelms the sweetcorn in what is a very enjoyable, Daiquiri-style cocktail.
history: Australian Bacardí Legacy 2016 winning cocktail winning cocktail created by Andrew Bennett at The Classroom in Perth. Andrew's inspiration: "Cuba has a golden history of cinema dating back to 1897 when silent movies were first shown on the island. Known as the 'seventh art,' cinema has been influential in defining the changing Cuban identity and how they view their place in the world. Celebrating this legacy, this cocktail is refreshing, modern and will remind you of your favourite movie experience with that quintessential popcorn flavour, while keeping the classic taste of Bacardí Carta Blanca front and centre."

name: Young Cuban
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄3 shot	Fino sherry
4 sprig	Fresh dill
review: Fresh dill nestles with rich almond, balanced by a touch of zesty citrus, aromatised by fino sherry with rum playing a fortifying role.
history: UK Bacardí Legacy 2015 winning cocktail created by Ally Martin at Peg + Patriot in London, England.

name: Geisha Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Akashi-Tai Daiginjo Genshu sake
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄12 shot	Japanese blended whisky
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A Vodka Martini given a Japanese influence with sake and Japanese whisky. Omit the sugar syrup if you like your Martinis bone dry.
history: Created in November 2016 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Daisy de Santiago
garnish: Seasonal berries & mint sprig dusted with icing sugar or lime wheel (preferably dehydrated)
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. DRIZZLE a spoon of Chartreuse over top of drink.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄6 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
review: Chartreuse adds subtle aromatics to this refreshing herbal Daiquiri/Daisy.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Charles H. Baker, Jr.'s 1939 The Gentleman's Companion volume II – An Exotic Drinking Book.

name: Summer Americano
preparation: STIR first four ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with a splash of tonic water.
ingredients:
1 shot	Rubino vermouth
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
3 drop	Bob's Cardamom bitters
1 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: Aperitif-style, tall and refreshing.
history: Created in May 2015 by Ignacio "Nacho" Vázquez, Spanish Martini Brand Ambassador. Naturally Nacho originally used Martini Bitter.

name: Nineteen Twenty Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Kirschwasser (cherry) eau-de-vie
1⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄6 shot	Groseille (redcurrant) syrup
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Bite-sized and delicately flavoured – the combination of redcurrant syrup and kirsch is almost rose water-like, diluted by dry vermouth with a splash of gin adding botanical complexity.
history: The Nineteen-Twenty Cocktail first appears in Harry McElhone's 1922 Harry's ABC of Mixing Cocktails and also notably in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Yellow Negroni
preparation: POUR all ingredients into serving glass, add ice to fill glass, STIR briefly and serve.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
3⁄4 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
3⁄4 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
review: As the name suggests, this pisco-based, five equal parts, vivid yellow bittersweet aperitif was inspired by the classic Negroni and three of the world's most iconic yellow liqueurs: limoncello, gentian and Chartreuse Jaune.
history: Created 21st January 2017 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Anita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Cachaça (aged 3+ years)
2⁄3 shot	Blood orange juice
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Macadamia nut syrup
history:
Adapted from a recipe created by Thalita Alves in Australia for Campari. Thalita says, "There's only one thing I adore almost as much as mixing beautiful drinks: dancing. Imagining original combinations of ingredients for a cocktail isn't so different from developing a sequence of steps in a well-structured choreography.

"Right foot forward, left foot sweeps in a semi-circle, right foot forward, left foot raised. I still remember how the first choreography I worked on started. I repeated it hundreds of times in front of the mirror, striving for perfect coordination with the other girls. Don't go imagining the corps de ballet at La Scala: we were just an amateur dance company, but we were full of passion and determination.

"But choreographies also need a good story, research, inspiration that comes from somewhere. That was always my favourite part of the entire dance creation process: to choose the message, the idea to be translated into motion. I found a muse that inspired me in piecing together a short act: Anita Garibaldi, the greatest Brazilian heroine, a wonderful mix of romance and strength. That would have been amazing to dance and to watch.

"But I never finished my final work. While working on Anita, I discovered a new Thalita. As a girl who had never gone very far from home, I discovered I had a big dream and a life-long passion to do and see more.
I felt an inexplicable need to seek out new places and suddenly I found myself in an airport for the very first time. I caught a plane to Australia: an unknown country where I had no friends or family, didn't speak the language and had no career. But I knew that this place would be my home.

"I put my creativity to one side for almost 5 years, too busy building my new life. Having gone from job to job, one day I ended up in a cocktail bar. While mixing my first drink I felt that spark from my dancing days again, putting different things together to create a whole new something. My passion was back, albeit in a new shape.

"When I realised I could finally tell stories again, this time in liquid form, I started working on my favourite one: that of Italian revolutionary Giuseppe Garibaldi, who fell in love with Anita, a person of strength and resilience but at the same time also extremely tender and charming. Anita was reborn, as a cocktail.

"I decided to narrate that intercontinental love story through the most emblematic spirits and flavours of the two worlds: Campari and fresh and juicy blood oranges symbolising Italy, Sagatiba Velha and bright green limes for Brazil. I sealed this union with a macadamia nut orgeat to celebrate the country I now call home: Australia. Anita, this symbolic mix of 2 worlds, is garnished with fragrant and aromatic basil leaves to finish.

"This cocktail, like the heroine whose name it bears, has become an icon of something much bigger to me: Australia itself, and all the people that have mixed together over the centuries and moved to this beautiful country to build brand new lives here and, ultimately, make it what it is."

name: A Lucky Roman Americano
preparation:
THROW first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. Top with rosemary soda.

Special ingredient #1: Rosemary soda
ingredients:
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
2 dash	Bob's Peppermint Bitters
Top up with	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
history: Created in 2017 by Luana Bosello in Italy.

name: Black Mesa
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Jamaican-style overproof aged pot still rum
1⁄2 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Pungent, funky and boozy with harmonious rum-dominated bitter sweetness.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Damon Boelte at Grand Army, Brooklyn, New York, USA. Damon's original recipe called for El Dorado 12 year old Demerara rum and Smith & Cross Jamaican rum.

name: Purple Stag
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Jägermeisteror other German amaro
5⁄6 shot	Berry fruit tea (cold)
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Maple syrup
1 barspoon	Blackcurrant jam (preserve)
review: Easy drinking and neither bitter or too sweet, it's hard not to like this rich herbal fruity cocktail.
history: Created in 2017 by Florian Beuren, Jägermeister's UK brand ambassador.

name: Out to Sea
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bacardi 8 year old rum
1 1⁄3 shot	Cold brew coffee
2⁄3 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
3 dash	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Reminiscent of an aged rum-based Espresso Martini (and yes it works when made with freshly brewed espresso coffee rather than cold brew). Fernet Branca and falernum add depth of flavour and their own distinctive personality. A great after-dinner cocktail. The salt influence is subtler than the name might suggest.
history: Created for Bacardí Legacy 2017 by Allen Fang at Barules Cocktail Club in Shanghai, China.

name: Clarita
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bacardi 8 year old rum
1⁄3 shot	Amontillado sherry
1⁄6 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 dash	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Dry (at least with the amontillado sherry) we used, Clarita could be enjoyed as an aperitif or digestive.
history:
The winning Bacardí Legacy 2017 cocktail, created by Ran Van Ongevalle at The Pharmacy I Knokke, Heist, Belgium.

Inspiration: “Clarita is a drink with inspiration from the past, made with knowledge from the present and dreams about the future.

“Clarita is also a reflection of me, the things I love and the things I stand for, approached in the mindset of the Maestros de Ron.

“By precisely blending these ingredients together I wanted to create a family of flavours: high notes, low notes, nutty notes and herbal notes; a true flavour bomb, a true legacy cocktail.”

As Ran’s prize, Bacardi will offer year-long support to further his career as a bartender by creating unique experiences, helping him to gain worldwide recognition for his drink and provide a platform from which he will serve Clarita at some of the finest bars in the world.

name: Playa Fortuna
preparation:
SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

*Special ingredient #1: Coconut cordial – made with equal parts by weight coconut water and white sugar.

*Special ingredient #2: Tartaric acid – made with 1 part cream of tartar and 5 parts water by weight.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
1⁄6 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
4 drop	*Special ingredient #2 (see above)
review: Reminiscent of a coconut and falernum (clove influenced) daquiri.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created for Bacardí Legacy 2017 by Ryan Kent Wainwright at The Ponte / Faith and Flower, Los Angeles, USA.

Inspiration: “The inspiration for this drink was floating in the waves off the Puerto Rican beach of Playa Fortuna while drinking a coconut; taking this idea and using a distinctly Puerto Rican spirit, Bacardí rum, and allowing it to shine.

“I liken it to the apothecary symbol: the spirit is the staff, with the ingredients winding their way around the frame to highlight its strengths but never detract from this very uniquely Bacardí drink. All of this seeks to highlight honesty: an honest product, an honest time and an honest drink.”

name: Sherry Herbst
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
2⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
1⁄3 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Oloroso sherry
review: Subtle vermouth and falernum sweetness takes the edge off this after-dinner whiskey charged, sipper of a cocktail.
history: Adapted from a cocktail discovered in May 2017 at Soho House, Berlin, Germany. Herbst is the German word for autumn/fall and also refers to harvest time so this drink translates as Sherry Harvest.

name: Le Sang Jaune (The Yellow Blood)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain to ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Spirituous apple and rich elderflower with herbal dry vermouth and gentian complexity, finished with the merest hint of anise courtesy of a dash of absinthe.
history: Adapted from a cocktail created in 2017 by Mauricio Barbosa at TUJU in São Paulo, Brazil. Mauricio's original recipe called for 50ml Calvados, 20ml Noilly Prat, 15ml St-Germain, 5ml homemade gentian liqueur and 5 drops absinthe bitters.

name: The Italian Job
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & dehydrated orange wheel
preparation: STIR all the ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Jamaican-style overproof aged pot still rum
3⁄4 shot	Americano bianco
3⁄4 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
3⁄4 shot	Byrrh Grand Quinquina
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Bittersweet and boozy with a dry finish. Striking the right degree of dilution is key to the success of this cocktail – stir a little longer than usual and if using ice straight from the freezer perhaps consider adding a dash of chilled water.
history: Created in 2017 by Joseph Akhavan at Mabel, Paris, France. Joseph's original recipe calls for Smith & Cross Jamaican rum.

name: Ritorno Alle Radici (Back To The Roots)
garnish: Orange zest twist & long cinnamon stick
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
2⁄3 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1 dash	Bob's Chocolate bitters
1 inch	Vanilla pod (sliced)
review: Rich liquid Christmas pudding flavours of Pedro Jimenez laced with scotch whisky and balanced with subtle gentian and chocolate bitterness.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2017 by Elia Doro at Dry Martini Bar, Barcelona, Spain. Elia says, "When I first started to elaborate this cocktail I was thinking how to exalt the bitterness of the gentian, so I decided to make an appetizer, which is typical in my region of Italy and very popular in my city, Padua. As I am in Spain now I used Pedro Jimenez sherry wine as the sweet ingredient, that combined with the scotch will create a nice taste when you start drinking it, and then comes the taste of the Suze that leaves a really nice and soft bitterness."

name: Time for Suze
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into a chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1 1⁄3 shot	Fennel tea
4 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A wonderfully delicate and dry aperitif. Genever provides a bready spirituous base over which flavours of gentian, fennel and absinthe are layered.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2017 by Emily Muscutt at Toto, Newcastle, England.

name: Word by Word
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5 fresh	Mint leaves
1 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
2⁄3 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A bittersweet aperitif-style riff on the classic Last Word cocktail.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2017 by Vitaliy Severinov at El Copitas, Saint-Petersburg, Russia. (Vitaliy's original recipe calls for 15ml Chartreuse Jaune.)
See: Last Word history

name: Day La Vie
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass (preferably a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
2⁄3 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
2⁄3 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Juan Meyer's original recipe calls for equal parts: Redemption rye whiskey, Suze, Amaro de Montenegro, and lemon juice. It's very tasty but I couldn't resist switching and blending whiskies and proportions. Both versions create a bittersweet, aperitif-style cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2017 by Juan Meyer, Norwalk, United States. He told us, "I love Paper Planes, it's my go-to cocktail at any restaurant at any time of day. I also love Suze with its earthy undertones that complement the gentian liqueur, so this is my combination of both."

name: Dutch Orange Cup
garnish: Orange slice, strawberry slices, mint sprig, orange zest twist & borage when in season
preparation: POUR all ingredients into glass half filled with ice. Add an orange slice and a couple of mint leaves from the garnish before filling to the brim with more ice and rest of garnish.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
review: Easy drinking, fruity, summery and gin laced with caramel vermouth freshened by zesty orange.
history: Created in February 2018 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Napoléon Margarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	Mandarine Napoleon liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Agave syrup
8 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters (optional)
review: As the name suggests, this tasty Margarita benefits from a slug of rich mandarin orange liqueur.
history: A variant of the popular Margarita cocktail. A detailed history, along with other variants can be found on our page.

name: First Emperor
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄2 shot	Rhum Clément Blanc
1⁄4 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄4 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Grassy spirituous agricole rhum is mellowed by fruity pineapple, sweet herbal liqueur and vinous herbal vermouth.
history:
Adapted from a drink discovered in March 2018 at Merchant House of Bow Lane, London, England. (The original recipe: 30ml Agricole rhum, 60ml Lillet Blanc, 15ml Yellow Chartreuse and 10ml pineapple syrup, served in a small stemmed wine glass with a single pebble-shaped slither of ice.)

The drink is named after Napoleon Bonaparte (1769-1821) and the following accompanies the drink on the Merchant House's menu, "After rising to the rank of General at the young age of 24, Napoleon later arranged a coup, placing himself as the first Emperor of France. His skill in command led to numerous years of French dominance in Europe and further afield, and his reforms continue to influence our society today."

name: Sage Sazerac
preparation: Rinse chilled glass Pastis and set aside. MUDDLE sage in base of stirring glass. Add other ingredients, STIR with ice and fine strain into the pre-rinsed glass over fresh ice (preferably a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1⁄6 shot	Pastis
3 fresh	Sage leaves
1 2⁄3 shot	Birch spirit/birch eau-de-vie
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 drop	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Subtle notes of pine, pastis and sage combine in this pre-dinner sipper of a cocktail.
history:
Adapted from a drink created in 2017 by Jason Knowles at Hixter Bankside, London, England. His original recipe uses Tarquin's Cornish Pastis and sage infused sugar syrup.

The history of the Sazerac cocktail can be found on our Sazerac cocktail page.

name: Skyline Margarita
garnish: Cayenne-chile rim (4 parts kosher salt, 1 part chile powder & 1 part cayenne), & orange zest twist
preparation:
SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled cayenne-chile salt-rimmed glass.

Special ingredient #1: Blackberry shrub - combine equal parts blackberries, cane sugar and red wine vinegar in a blender, blend until liquefied, then strain out solids.

Special ingredient #2: Cayenne-chile syrup - combine 1 cup sugar, one cup water, 1 teaspoon chile powder, 1 teaspoon cayenne in a saucepan and bring to a simmer. Once desired flavour is achieved, strain out solids. Alternately, use .25 oz simple syrup, a slice of cayenne or other hot pepper, and a pinch of chile powder.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	Patron Citronge
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
1⁄4 shot	*Special ingredient #2 (see above)
review: Recipe supplied by Patrón, who say, “Megan’s cocktail was inspired by Seattle’s abundance of blackberries. A fruity blackberry punch and modern simplicity make the Skyline Margarita created by Seattle’s Megan Radke shine. Keenly balanced sweet blackberry shrub comes together with spicy heat from cayenne and chili powder to complement Patrón Silver’s light pepper notes and crisp finish. Citrus flavors join the star ingredients to make the perfect margarita for enjoying a warm day in the drizzly city.”
history: Created in 2018 by Megan Radke, Seattle, Washington, USA.

name: Cherry Springer
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Sour Cherry Gin
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe
1⁄3 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: We do like a pun, especially a tasty pun. Sweet and sour cherry fortified with gin notes and subtle freshening crème de menthe and delicate chocolate.
history: We’re indebted to Gareth “G” Franklin of Luxardo fame for bringing this brilliantly named recipe, adapted from a drink originally created in 2018 by Filip Palkiewicz at Mercy Brown, Kraków, Poland, to our attention. Naturally, G uses Luxardo’s excellent Sangue Morlacco cherry liqueur when he makes this drink.

name: Accoutrement
garnish: Torrone Stregga Ricoperto di Cioccolato across rim (or brandied cherries)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
3⁄4 shot	Strega liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Rhum Clément Créole Shrubb liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Chris originally garnished this Calvados Sidecar/Applecart-like cocktail with brandied cherries but Strega's excellent chocolates seem a far more fitting accoutrement.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2008 by Chris Hannah at Arnaud's French 75 Bar, New Orleans, USA.

name: Margarita (no added sugar* & low-calorie)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	Agave Sec liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar-free sweetener
1⁄2 pinch	Salt (sea salt)
review:
* BEWARE: Although free of cane sugar and beet sugar, this cocktail contains small amounts of fructose sugars from the agave nectar used in the Agave Sec orange liqueur.

Tasty, zingy, low-calorie and sugar-free. What more can you ask of a Margarita?
history:
Adapted from the classic serve by yours truly (Simon Difford) in January 2019.

Also see Margarita Cocktails - best recipes and history.

name: Naughty Charles
garnish: Lemon zest twist STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄3 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: I first tried this cocktail whilst judging the Heering Classics Challenge 2018 Final and while I loved the flavours it struck me that it was just a smidgen on the sweet side. So, back at my own bar, I experimented with reducing the sweet components. The conclusion, Liam (the drink's creator) nailed it the first time and the proportions he used are the best to make the five ingredients shine. It's not sweet, but it wavers on the sweet side of balanced, so I'd recommend enjoying after a meal.
history: Created 2018 by Liam Doherty-Penzer at Whirly Bird, Sydney, Australia, this cocktail earned him a place in the London final of the Heering Classics Competition. (Liam used J. Walker Black Label for his Scotch and Noilly Prat for his dry vermouth.)

name: Pavoni
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & blue cheese stuffed olive
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Angostura di Amaro
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Sweet and sour with delicate bitterness and a complex cherry flavour, this cocktail is designed to pair with cheese.
history: Created 2018 by Odd Strandbakken at Himkok, Oslo, Norway, this was the winning cocktail in the final of the Heering Classics competition. For the competition, Odd garnished this drink with olives stuffed with Kraftkar cheese, a spicy Norwegian blue cheese judged the Supreme Champion in 2016 World Cheese Awards. And as he says, this cocktail “perfectly pairs with cheese.”

name: The Persuader
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1 shot	Chardonnay (Chablis) white wine
1⁄3 shot	Muyu Chinotto Nero liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Licor 43 Original liqueur
1 shot	Pineapple juice
review:
Named due to this drink's friendly approachability and The Persuaders!, a 1970s British TV series starring Tony Curtis and Roger Moore made brilliant by John Barry's theme music.

This cocktail harnesses rum's affinity to pineapple juice and is Daiquiri-like but with white wine's acidity replacing that of lime juice. Chinotto liqueur adds delicate chocolaty citrus complexity with a touch of rich vanilla liqueur adding balancing sweetness.
history: Created February 2019 by yours truly, this is a riff on the Palermo, a cocktail I came across in 2001 and the first cocktail I encountered that replaced the acidity of citrus fruit with white wine.

name: Picante de la Casa (Soho House Tonic)
garnish: Slice chilli pepper (warn drinker not to eat)
preparation: MUDDLE chilli and coriander/cilantro in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 slice	Red chili pepper (jalapeño/fresno chili (10,000 SHU) deseeded)
3 sprig	Coriander/Cilantro leaves
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
2⁄3 shot	Agave syrup
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Best described as a Tommy's Margarita with added chilli spice and coriander/cilantro.
history: Created by Chris Ojeda at Soho House, West Hollywood, USA, this "House Tonic" is the best-selling cocktail across the Soho Houses around the world, and also has become a popular contemporary classic served in other bars.

name: The Herbalist
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Rutte Celery Dry Gin
1 shot	Celery juice (freshly extracted)
1⁄2 shot	Mentzendorff Kümmel liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Kummel's herbal caraway flavours and botanical gin notes form the backbone of this citrusy celery cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2018 by Jiri Majerik, Bar Manager at Blixen, London, England.

name: Verdita (makes 12 shots)
garnish: Serve alongside a shot glass of tequila
preparation: BLEND all 5 ingredients with stalks but without ice (no need to chop ingredients if your blender is powerful enough) and fine strain into suitable storage container from which to pour into individual shot glass serves. Refrigerate, SHAKE before use and use within 3 days.
ingredients:
10 sprig	Coriander/Cilantro leaves
10 sprig	Mint (fresh) sprigs
1 fresh	Red chili pepper (jalapeño/fresno chili (10,000 SHU) deseeded) (chopped)
15 shot	Pineapple juice
2 pinch	Salt (sea salt)
review: Verde is Spanish for green and Verdita is best described as being a green herbal Sangrita with pineapple adding a hint of tropical fruit and sweetness. Leave the seeds in the Jalapeño if you want spicy and remove if you don't.
history: A traditional accompaniment to tequila in Mexico where it is sipped alternatively.

name: Kingston
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Mentzendorff Kümmel liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Pimento dram/Allspice liqueur
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Caraway (Kummel) and pimento spice (Allspice Dram) shine in this well-aged rum sour.
history: The Kingston is a classic cocktail from the 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book but this recipe is by Frank Caiafa, author of the 2016 The Waldorf Astoria Bar Book, who says, "I've added the touch of lemon juice for a bit of zip, but you could use a couple of dashes of Acid Phosphate or try it without, as they did at The Old Bar [at The Waldorf Astoria]." Frank prefers to use Appleton Reserve for his rum and Combier Kummel.

name: Sweet Tears of Mine
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Salted Caramel syrup
2⁄3 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: The smell of the caramel popcorn garnish as you sip completes this lightly sour caramel, cacao and coffee cocktail.
history: Adapted from a 2019 recipe created by Shavinraj Gopinath at The Iron Fairies, Bangkok, Thailand.

name: Black Espresso
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
1⁄3 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
1⁄6 shot	Kuromitsu Japanese brown sugar syrup
6 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: This riff on a classic Espresso Martini has great depth of flavour with cacao and currant flavours.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2019 by Keisuke KSK Yamamoto at Jeremiah Tokyo in Tokyo, Japan.

name: Landing Gear
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
review: Spiritous and richly fruity with orange and cherry combining harmoniously with cognac.
history: This riff on the classic Burnt Fuselage was created in 2019 by Jason Clapham, Oxford, England.

name: Crazy Crossing
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1⁄12 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Mandarine Napoleon liqueur
review: Bittersweet with herbal botanical complexity.
history: Adapted from a recipe in W. J. Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Cocktail Book where the invention of this cocktail is credited to "F. G. Hunt". We've used a mandarin liqueur, but the original recipe calls for Van Der Hum tangerine liqueur. The original recipe is also shaken rather than stirred. (Our thanks to Jason Clapham of Oxford, England for bringing this recipe to our attention and suggesting the use of Mandarine Napoléon.)

name: The Broady
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
review: An agave influenced riff on a Blood & Sand. Cherry and orange laced with tequila and a smoky hint of mezcal.
history: Created in February 2020 by yours truly for Ian Broad, a lover of cherries known by all at The Rose & Crown in Beckley, East Sussex, as "Broady". After sipping, Ian remarked, "It reminds me of going down a dark alley. The kind of place you shouldn't venture but you can't help going down."

name: Herbaceous Border
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄3 shot	Bigallet Genepi Grand Tetras
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Celery saccharum (celery syrup)
4 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters
review: Genepi and celery add herbal and vegetal flavours (in place of triple sec) to this Margarita riff.
history: Created by yours truly on 11th April 2020 during the Covid-19 lockdown.

name: Celery Wine
garnish: Rest celery stick across rim with a light dusting of celery salt
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Rutte Celery Dry Gin
1⁄3 shot	Grüner Veltliner dry white wine
1⁄3 shot	Celery saccharum (celery syrup)
1⁄12 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1 dash	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Spiritous, vinous and delicately vegetal. One for Martini lovers.
history: Created in June 2020 by yours truly.

name: Banana Daiquiri (shaken)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
6 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters
review: Perhaps better named a Sour Banoffee Daiquiri – what's not to like?
history: Recipe created by yours truly.

name: Xanthia
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
2 dash	Bob's Abbotts bitters
1⁄4 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: A couple of dashes of bitters adds balance and complexity to this herbal gin-laced cherry flavoured after-dinner cocktail.
history: Adapted from Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book which calls for equal parts gin, cherry brandy and Yellow Chartreuse, stipulating to "Shake well and strain into cocktail glass."

name: Thunder In Paradise
garnish: Dashes of Peychaud bitters to colour ice crown & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice and serve with a straw.
ingredients:
1 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Oloroso sherry
5⁄12 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Cream of coconut (e.g. Coco Lopez, Re'al etc.)
review: Sherry, orgeat and cream of coconut are unlikely bedfellows, but all combine harmoniously with lime juice in this rum-laced Tiki-style cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Steve Schneider at Employees Only in New York, USA. Originally based on Caña Brava 7 Year Rum with homemade orgeat syrup.

name: Cantinero Coffee
preparation: THROW all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄6 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Ramazzotti amaro
1⁄6 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
2 dash	Bob's Chocolate bitters
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Jeroen Van Hecke at L'Apereau in Blankenberge, Belgium.

name: In the August Sun
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 shot	White overproof rum
1 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄2 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄3 shot	Cream of coconut (e.g. Coco Lopez, Re'al etc.)
review: Looks like a Pina Colada and indeed tastes a lot like a Pina Colada but overproof rum, fino sherry and falernum ensure this is no ordinary Pina Colada.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Dan Watson at Porco Lounge & Tiki Room in Cleveland, Ohio, USA.

name: Maiden's Blush No.2
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
1⁄6 shot	La Fée Absinthe Blanche
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Raspberry (framboise) sugar syrup
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water
review: A mere spoon of blanche absinthe washes over ten times as much Old Tom gin in this complex sour which is delicately balanced by a splash of raspberry syrup.
history:
Adapted from a recipe in Louis Fouquet's 1896 Bariana: Recueil de toutes boissons americains et anglaises (Bariana: Compendium of all American and English drinks), the second known earliest French cocktail book.

The Maiden's Blush also appears in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book with two versions, No.1 with orange curaçao and No.2 with absinthe and the following recipe:
"1/3 Absinthe
2/3 Dry Gin
1 Teaspoon Grenadine
Shake well and strain into cocktail glass."

Fouquet's recipe calls for 2 parts absinthe to 1 part Old Tom gin while Craddock's stipulates 2 parts gin to 1 part absinthe. Even in Craddock's 2:1, the absinthe dominates the gin so our recipe above uses 10 parts gin to 1 part absinthe. Hence you may want to reduce the gin and up the proportion of absinthe according to taste.

name: Whisky Business
garnish: Lemon slice wheel dusted with Tajin chile seasoning
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Piment d'Espelette chile liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Cinnamon syrup
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A rye sour enlivened with chili and cinnamon spice to warm the cockles.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Meaghan Dorman at Dear Irving in New York City, USA. The lack of a 'e' in Whisky in this cocktails name references it's originally being based on Rittenhouse Rye, one of the few American whiskies to omit the 'e'.

name: Ban-hattan
garnish: Dehydrated banana slice pegged to rim
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Banana (yellow) sugar syrup
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water
review: As the name might suggest, a rye whiskey-based Sweet Manhattan that is lightly sweetened and flavoured with a splash of banana syrup.

name: Naramata
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Pommeau du Normandie
2 dash	Peach bitters
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Brandy and brandy fortified apple sit harmoniously with rich herbal vermouth complexity.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Jamie Boudreau in Seattle, USA. Named after Naramata, a picturesque rural town in British Columbia, Canada.

name: Scotch Adonis
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice)
ingredients:
1 shot	Blended/vatted Scotch malt whisky
1 shot	Oloroso sherry
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Some Scotch whiskies benefit from the influence of maturation in sherry wine-infused casks. However, this cocktail amplifies the fortified wine influence way beyond what's possible from merely the aging process.
history: Adapted from a riff on the classic Adonis promoted by Chivas Regal, this cocktail was originally made with Chivas Extra 13 Sherry Cask Finish.

name: Gaelic Flip
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	The Busker Single Pot Still Irish Whiskey
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Pimento dram/Allspice liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 fresh	Egg (white & yolk)
review: Pot still Irish whiskey character and a touch of pimento dram shine throughout this beautifully balanced flip.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Charles Joly, USA.

name: Damn The Bloody Weather
