preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 1⁄2 shot	Blood orange juice
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Basically, a gin and juice but the orange juice is of the "bloody" variety and amplified by orange curaçao and orange bitters with vermouth adding rich herbal complexity.
history: A bloody good pun on Harry Craddock's Damn-the-Weather in his 1930 The Savoy Cocktail. This cocktail comes to Difford's Guide thanks to a comment left by decerning drinker, Matthew French.

name: Greek Vacation
garnish: Lemon zest twist & basil leaves bouquet
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	O/Purist Tsipouro
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: From the Greek islands to the seaside city of Thessaloniki to historic Athens, Greece is a holiday paradise and I look forward to sipping this delicately honey balanced Tsipouro Sour on my next trip to Greece. In the meantime, perhaps make at home and dream of your next vacation.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Dimitris Karababas at Banana Moon bar in Patra, Greece, this was one of ten winning recipes in the 2021 O/Purist Quest.

name: Sid and Nancy
garnish: Freshly grated nutmeg, cocoa powder & dehydrated banana chip
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	O/Purist Tsipouro
1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
review: Fruity, sweet 'n' sour. A bite-sized tropical-style Greek-laced cocktail for a touch of island escapism in a glass.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Tasos Korakis at Almond Living Well Workshop in Paros, Greece, this was one of ten winning recipes in the 2021 O/Purist Quest. Tasos says, "Using O/Purist Tsipouro as a canvas I tried to portray the 1986 movie, Sid and Nancy, about the life of one of the most iconic couples ever, Sex Pistols bassist Sid Vicious and his girlfriend Nancy Spungen, furthermore my love for Sex Pistols music was also one of my inspirations."

name: Sunset Park
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄4 shot	Chilled water
review: The original recipe calls for a full 2oz (60ml) bottled-in-bond straight rye (without the optional extra splash of water to help with dilution). Just 1/3oz (10ml) less whiskey produces a more approachable but still spirit-forward late-night sipper.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2009 by Michael Madrusan at Milk & Honey in New York City, USA.

name: Colonel Ward
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	White overproof rum
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
review: Rum funk-laced orchard and citrus fruit with medicinal herbal complexity.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England. Originally made with Wray & Nephew overproof rum, this cocktail is named after John Wray's nephew.

name: Blackthorn No. 2 (Homeboy's)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
2⁄3 shot	Tawny port
1⁄3 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Just as Aaron, its creator, describes it, whiskey-laced boozy blackcurrant fruit pastille.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created by Aaron Wall at his Homeboy bar in Islington, London, England where it's one of the signature cocktails. Aaron says, "The Blackthorn cocktail appears in The Savoy Cocktail Book with a gin and an Irish whiskey version, using fortified wine as a modifier. The idea for us was to amplify the berry flavours that you would get from the fortified wine and use a port instead and rounding it off with a little demerara sugar to make this drink finish with a distinct taste of boozy blackcurrant fruit pastille."

While this may be a variation of The Savoy Cocktail Book's Blackthorn it is more properly a riff on Harry Johnson's "Black Thorn" from his 1900 Bartender's Manual which, thanks to William "Cocktail Bill" Boothby's 1930 World's Drinks And How To Mix Them is now known as a Blackthorn No. 3.

name: Greek Espresso Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine stain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	O/Purist Tsipouro
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
2⁄3 shot	Kleos Mastiha liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: The distinctive flavours of tsipouro and mastiha influence this 'Greek' Espresso Martini.
history: Created in October 2021 by yours truly at the Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: Pizzicato Passage
garnish: Orange zest twist & skewered candied ginger
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Amontillado sherry
1 shot	Meletti amaro
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Piment d'Espelette chile liqueur
4 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: Honeyed bittersweetness with bitter chocolate and delicate enlivening chili heat. A tasty and enlivening after-dinner digestivo.
history: Adapted from a cocktail created by Anu Apte-Elford at her Rob Roy bar in Seattle, USA.

name: German Vacation
garnish: Crown with more crushed ice and colour with 3 dashes red Creole-style bitters
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1 shot	Jägermeisteror other German amaro
3⁄4 shot	Ginger liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
review: Rum-laced herbal almond. A refreshing aperitivo or a cleansing digestive.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Sother Teague at his Amor y Amargo bar in New York City, USA.

name: All Jacked Up
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
5⁄6 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
review: Yes, yes, yes, the name, "All Jacked Up" was inspired by the use of 100° proof bottled-in-bond applejack but I've committed sacrilege by using calvados. In the quest for roundness, I also very slightly played down the fernet from the original recipe. Hopefully, the result is still uplifting.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2016 by Jordan Brower at Mayahuel in New York City, USA.

name: Lawrence
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
3 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Some may want to stir this gin-laced aperitivo but it's better enlivened by shaking, as per the original 1933 recipe. Beware, this cocktail benefits from an orange zest twist but not a lemon twist.
history: From a recipe first published in Jacob Abraham Grohusko's 1933 Jack's Manual and kindly adapted for us by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford.

name: Midnight Stroll
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice) and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Ramazzotti amaro
1⁄4 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: An amaro and orange curaçao influenced riff on a Boulevardier.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2016 by Brandon Lockman at Red Star Tavern in Portland, Oregon, USA.

name: Four Flush(er)
garnish: Float dried raspberry or skewered fresh raspberries
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Swedish Punsch liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄24 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄24 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Spicy arrack notes shine in this cocktail that's best described as being rum's answer to a Martini.
history: The "Four Flush Cocktail" appears in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book but I've based our recipe on the "Four Flush(er)" in Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones Complete Barguide.

name: Cyrano
preparation: Cut a large coin-sized lime zest twist disc thick cut so also has flesh of the fruit (Ti' Punch-style) and MUDDLE on base of glass. Add other ingredients, fill glass with ice and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 shot	Rhum J.M. Terroir Volcanique
3⁄4 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1⁄4 shot	Pineapple rum
1⁄6 shot	Pineapple sugar syrup
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A tropical fruit-laced aged agricol Ti' Punch with a touch of bittersweet Italian attitude.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Jonnie Long at Death & Co, The Ramble Hotel, Denver, USA.

name: Islay Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
4 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters
review: An aged rum Daiquiri with smoky peated whisky mellowed by rich honey.
history: Created in January 2022 by yours truly at the Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Roxanne
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	Amaro Santoni
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Strawberry sugar syrup
4 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters
review: What to call a red bittersweet strawberry-influenced aperitivo created while the soundtrack playing is The Police singing "Roxanne (Put on the red light), I loved you since I knew you"?
history: Created by yours truly in January 2022 at the Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: Witch & Broomstick
garnish: Float mint leaf on foaming surface
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY shake (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Monkey 47 Experimentum Series 2y06 Gin
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄6 shot	Strega liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Inspired by the witch on a broomstick on the label of Monkey 47's mint sauce and honey edition (Strega is Italian for witch) and named with a thought to British pub names.
history: Created in March 2022 by yours truly at the Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: Honeymentum
garnish: Float mint leaf or peg to rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 fresh	Mint leaves
1 1⁄2 shot	Monkey 47 Experimentum Series 2y06 Gin
2⁄3 shot	Amontillado sherry
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review: Honeyed gin with vinous sherry, minty freshness and delicate apple fruit.

name: Minty Mellow Yellow
garnish: Float small mint leaf or peg to rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 fresh	Mint leaves
1 shot	Monkey 47 Experimentum Series 2y06 Gin
1⁄4 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: Inspired and created for Monkey 47 Experimentum 2y06. Honey and mint notes in the gin are amplified in this bijou sour with monastic herbal liqueur complexity.
history: Created in March 2022 by yours truly at the Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: West 75th
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with sparkling wine.
ingredients:
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Raspberry (framboise) sugar syrup
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
2 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
review: Fruity, quaffable and balanced rather than sweet, this cocktail cries out for a celebratory occasion. Originally made with lambrusco rather than my preference for prosecco, or ideally rosé prosecco.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2018 by Torrence O'Haire, Corporate Beverage Director at The Gage restaurant in Chicago, USA.

name: Charlie Lindbergh
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄12 shot	Blanc quinquina/kina (e.g. Mattei Cap Corse or Kina L'Aéro d'Or)
1⁄3 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Gin-laced with zesty citrus and rich apricot but made special and balanced by subtle quinine bitterness.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book. Craddock's recipe calls for two now defunct products, Kina Lillet (a quinquina) and Pricota (a British-made apricot liqueur).

name: Kummel Ye Faithful
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄4 shot	Mentzendorff Kümmel liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
4 drop	Bob's Liquorice bitters
review: Intended to be the last drink of the night on Christmas Eve/Day, or indeed any night when you desire a cocktail to transport you to a comfy chair beside a warming fire.
history:
Created on a beautifully warm blue-skied summer's evening in June 2022 by yours truly at the Clocktower in Rye, England. As I said, this is a transportive cocktail. Open fires are optional.

I've since discovered there is a cocktail named "The Kummel Ye Faithful" (made with equal parts gin, kummel, and cream) in the 1929 book Judge Jr. Here's How Again!.

name: Flip the Script
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄6 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
5⁄6 shot	Stout beer
1⁄3 shot	Maple syrup
1 fresh	Egg (white & yolk)
3 dash	Orinoco bitters
review: Irish stout and Irish whiskey combine harmoniously in this rich but balanced flip.
history: Created in 2018 by Robb Collins, Group Head Bartender at London Cocktail Club, London, England, who developed this drink "for the first-ever London Cocktail Club bar takeover, which was at the Exchequer Bar in Dublin, Ireland September 2016. A perfect autumn/winter sip."

name: Snake Eyes
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
2 shot	Coconut water
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Clément Sirop de Canne
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
review: Proof, if it were needed, that mezcal works in tropical/Tiki cocktails.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Ally Marrone (head bartender) and Robby Dow (Beverage director) at Grand Army bar in Brooklyn, New York City, USA.

name: High Octane
preparation: POUR all ingredients into glass. Fill with ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Sage gin
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Bigallet Genepi Grand Tetras
1 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
1 shot	Thomas Henry Pink Grapefruit soda
review: Herbal, citrussy with piney freshness. A palate cleansing and refreshing aperitivo.
history: Created for Engine Gin in November 2022 by yours truly at the Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: Rolls Royce
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Sage gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
4 drop	Boker's bitters
review: A riff on the classic RAC cocktail. Lovingly hand-crafted and highly polished with enough oomph to be a conder in the spirit-forward classics series.
history: Adapted from a recipe in R. de Fleury's 1934 book 1700 Cocktails For The Man Behind The Bar

name: Monkey Bizz
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
4 drop	Bob's Lavender Bitters (optional)
review: Gin-laced aromatised wine with floral elderflower.

name: Sloppy Joe's
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Cognac (brandy)
5⁄6 shot	Tawny port
5⁄6 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄12 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄24 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: Rich and fruity with a balancing brandy backbone. A bite-sized after-dinner or late-night treat that's reminiscent of a very fruity vintage port.
history:
There are two very different vintage cocktails which similar names (the other being Sloppy Joe) that originated at or are named after Sloppy Joe's, a famous bar in Havana, Cuba during the 1930s. Ernest Hemingway was a regular and Sloppy Joe's inspired the fictitious Freddy's Bar in his novel To Have and Have Not.

This recipe adapted from one I found in the variation of the other Sloppy Joe cocktail in Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide.

name: Chocolate Martini
garnish: Square of 70% cacao chocolate pegged to rim
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
3⁄4 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
4 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: As the name suggests, a chocolate-flavoured Martini. The bready notes in the genever help amplify cacao notes.
history: Created in January 2023 thanks to a comment on our Chocolate Vodkatini page (previously named 'Chocolate Martini') by Avery Garnett, a fellow Discerning Drinker.

name: Ve.n.to
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) & skewered white grapes
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass. (When making your honey syrup, ideally dilute honey with chamomile tea rather than just water.)
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bepi Tosolini Grappa di Moscato
1⁄2 shot	Chamomile liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: A balanced and refreshingly cleansing chamomile grappa sour.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Samuele Ambrosi of Grappa Revolution and Leondardo Varesi, founder and bartender at Riva Bar.

name: Hightower
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄24 shot	Giffard Peppermint Pastille crème de menthe
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: An Irish whiskey-based riff on a Gold Rush. The mint notes from the crème de menthe are subtle but really add to this cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Ash Miyasaki at Bar Henry cocktail bar in Echo Park, Los Angeles, USA.

name: Czarina
garnish: Lemon zest twist (expressed & discarded) & dried apricot half on rim
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2 dash	Boker's bitters
review: Vodka-laced apricot with vermouth contributing herbal complexity.
history:
The Czarina cocktail is first mentioned in the "supplementary list" of cocktails in William James "Billy" Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Bar Book. Sadly, as he says in the book, "space forbids giving the recipes," so all we know is that a cocktail of that name was being made in 1937.

A recipe for the Czarina first appears in the 1943 book Cocktail Digest by Oscar Haimo of the Hotel Pierre in New York City, and then in Lucius Beebe's 1946 The Stork Club Bar Book.

name: Almond Negroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Luxardo Bitter Bianco liqueur
1 shot	Ambrato/ambre/amber vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Bitter almond liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄24 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
review: Bittersweet, as you expect from a White Negroni with pleasing dry almond, as the name suggests.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in March 2023 by Jo Cola at Baan Tepa in Bangkapi, Bangkok. Originally made with GIL Gin (a peated rural gin from Calabria, Italy, I've replaced this with a dry gin and a touch of peated Scotch whisky.

name: Black + Gold
garnish: Dehydrated lemon slice wheel with 1 drop of sesame oil on top for aromatics
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Hazelnut liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
5 drop	Sesame oil
review: Subtle and well-integrated hazelnut liqueur and sesame oil add to this honey and bourbon sour.
history: A riff on the Gold Rush created in 2017 by David Rothwhen head bartender at Covina in the Park South Hotel, New York City. (He has since progressed to Beverage Director for HI Hospitality in Florida.)

name: Rhymes With Orange
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Ramazzotti amaro
1⁄6 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
3 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A Sweet Manhattan riff with spiritus rye whiskey underpinned by bittersweet herbal vinous complexity.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2011 by Toby Maloney at The Violet Hour in Chicago, Illinois, USA.

name: Rob Macleod Roy
garnish: Orange zest twist (expressed & discarded) and maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1 shot	Blended/vatted Scotch malt whisky
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
8 drop	Bob's Abbotts bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A Rob Roy with a well-integrated peaty backbone that sits well against the rich vermouth.
history: Created in May 2023 by yours truly for the folks behind Caisteal Chamuis who named this cocktail.

name: Odetta
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Monkey Shoulder Fresh Monkey
3⁄4 shot	Passoã passion fruit liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
1 shot	Pineapple juice
6 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters
review: Tropical fruit balanced by white wine acidity laced with funky/fruity new make spirit. Consider adding a grind or two of black pepper to your shaker to enliven the fruitiness.
history: Created in June 2023 by yours truly at the Clocktower in Rye, England. Named after the singer of the same name whose track Hit Or Miss from her 1970 album Odetta Sings was playing while I was mixing.

name: Monkeys Go Bananas
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Monkey Shoulder Fresh Monkey
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A subtly banana, delicately herbal, funky and grainy take on an Old Fashioned.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Audrey Marculescu of Mobster Bar in Paris, France.

name: King Louis
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably with a clear ice shard).
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Monkey Shoulder Fresh Monkey
5⁄6 shot	Verjuice
2⁄3 shot	Pear liqueur (Poire William)
1⁄3 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
review: Kerry, the creator of this cocktail, describes it as "A juicy wee treat to save you from sizzling over summer, made with a zesty new product from our friends at Monkey Shoulder." The quality of your verjuice will dramatically affect this drink's deliciousness.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Kerry Burgess of Happiness Forgets in London, England.

name: This is Monkey
preparation: STIR first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably a clear ice shard). TOP with rhubarb soda and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Monkey Shoulder Fresh Monkey
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Verjuice
1 2⁄3 shot	Rhubarb soda
review: Brilliantly constructed with new-make spirit and maraschino liqueur just that bit more evident than the other supporting ingredients.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Erik Lorincz of Kwant in London, England. Erik's original recipe was lengthened with London Essence Rhubarb & Cardamom Soda, which sadly is no longer available.

name: Mexican Negroni
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and STIR.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄3 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄3 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review: All the bittersweetness and character you'd expect from a classic Negroni but with tequila and mezcal to the fore.
history: Created by yours truly in June 2023 at The Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: Self-starter
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄4 shot	Blanc quinquina/kina (e.g. Mattei Cap Corse or Kina L'Aéro d'Or)
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Kina aperitif and dashes of absinthe add all-important bitterness to balance this gin-based apricot-flavoured aperitif.
history: The Self-starter was first published in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: 1920 Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1⁄4 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: A rye whiskey's spirituous spice adds backbone to what is essentially a Perfect Manhattan with orange bitters in place of aromatic bitters and garnished with an orange zest rather than a maraschino cherry.
history: Adapted from a cocktail discovered in July 2023 at Cure in New Orleans, USA.

name: Golden Phone
garnish: Lemon zest twist (expressed and discarded) & skewered Luxardo Maraschino Cherries
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄4 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A delightful tequila-based riff on the classic Twentieth Century.
history: A riff on the Twentieth Century by Jim Meehan who also created the 21st Century.

name: Oh My Word
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
3⁄4 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
3⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
3⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2 dash	Lime bitters
review: The lime bitters and lemon oils from the garnish are key to the balance of this riff on the Last Word.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Sother Teague at Amor y Amargo bar in New York City, USA.

name: Blackthorn No. 1
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Dashes of bitters and lemon oils from the garnish are key to this sloe gin-based classic from the turn of the 20th century.
history: This sloe gin/gin version of the Blackthorn cocktail (see Blackthorn No.3 for the whiskey-based version) is first mentioned in a piece titled "New Things in Tipples" in the 21st November 1897 New York Herald as one of three "cocktails which are the products of the fertile imagination of the high card of the Hoffman grill room."

name: Nassau Valley
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Pamplemousse liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Full-bodied and well-balanced with bittersweetness and bright citrus sourness, all playing harmoniously with the characterful rum.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Jason E. Clapham. Originally made with Appleton Estate 8 Reserve Rum, so appropriately named after the valley in Jamaica on the Appleton estate.

name: Tellico Cobbler
garnish: Charred baby corn or corn segment
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. The aroma from the charred corn is a key element of this cocktail.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Tennessee whiskey
2⁄3 shot	Fino sherry
2⁄3 shot	Pineapple sugar syrup
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Looking at the ingredients, you may think this cocktail is sweet, but as Cam Dawson, its creator says, "the sherry really balances it!" Pineapple combines brilliantly with the whiskey and fino sherry.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Cam Dawson, the longstanding UK Jack Daniel's ambassador.

name: Persephone
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Applejack brandy
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Apple brandy and sloe gin sit brilliantly with rosso vermouth in this sour.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2008 by David Slape at PDT in New York City, USA. In ancient Greek mythology, Persephone was the goddess queen of the underworld, wife of the god Haides (Hades).

name: Absinthe Negroni
garnish: Luxardo Maraschino cherry dropped into cocktail
preparation: Spray or rinse chilled glass with absinthe. STIR other ingredients with ice and strain into absinthe-coated glass.
ingredients:
1⁄24 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Savoia Americano Rosso
1⁄4 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
review: Strangely, this bittersweet cocktail suits this receptacle, and it perhaps provokes more attention than a coupe may afford.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2022 by Sarah Morrissey, bar director at Ernesto's Basque Taverna in New York City, USA. The original recipe specifies Aperitivo Cappelletti as the Americano rosso.

name: Improved Vermouth Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Averna Amaro
1⁄4 shot	Amaro Braulio
4 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: An alluringly complex blend of bittersweet, herbal and fruity components that results in a cocktail greater than its parts.
history: Inspired by a modern-day interpretation of the classic Vermouth Cocktail by two of our favourite bartenders/brand ambassadors, Leonardo Leuci (founder and brand ambassador for Del Professore vermouth) and Giorgio Bargiani (assistant director of mixology at The Connaught Bar and global advocate for 1757 Vermouth Di Torino).

name: Bitter Almondo
garnish: Dust with freshly grated nutmeg & float 3 roasted almonds in a line across the surface
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. (There's no need to dry shake to achieve desired foam.)
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Adriatico Bianco almond milk liqueur
1 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
5⁄6 shot	Luxardo Bitter Bianco liqueur
4 drop	Bob's Vanilla bitters
4 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Mezcal fortifies and, depending on your choice of mezcals, provides subtle smokiness, while almond milk liqueur and bitter white liqueur contribute bittersweetness and rich flavours.
history: Created in December 2023 by yours truly at The Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Whiskey Sea
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
6 drop	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
review: Don't be misled by the name, there's no whiskey in this delicious cacao and ripe banana rum sour.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Itzel Gracian at The Manor Bar, Rosewood Miramar Beach Hotel in Montecito, California, USA. Cocktails on the hotel's bar menu are inspired by novels authored by women featuring female protagonists, and this one is named after Ann Howard Creel's The Whiskey Sea, which tells the story of Frieda being swept up by the illegal rum-running business and the handsome Ivy Leaguer.

name: Arbitrary Nature of Time
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1 dash	Xocolatl mole bitters
review: A fruity Boulevardier with cherry brandy moving it from aperitivo to late-night drinking.
history: Created by Maksym Pazuniak at Cure in New Orleans, this cocktail was first published in Rogue Cocktails, self-published in 2009 by Maksym Pazuniak and his colleague Kirk Estopinal.

name: Solomon Grundy
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Lucano amaro
1⁄2 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
4 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Whether a big meal or a big night, this cleansing bittersweet herbal digestive is a great way to finish it, and by Saturday, according to the nursery rhyme, Solomon Grundy was properly finished.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2011 by Dan Long while bartending in Los Angeles. The Solomon Grundy is eponymously named after the supervillain in DC Comics, who, in turn, is named after a 19th-century nursery rhyme.

name: Dónde Estás, Yolanda
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
1 1⁄2 shot	Coconut water
1⁄12 shot	Gomme syrup
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Dry, delicately smoky with subtle coconut.
history: Named after Dónde Estás, Yolanda by Pink Martini. (Dónde Estás, Yolanda is Spanish for 'where are you, Yolanda'.) Created in January 2024 by yours truly at the Clocktower, Rye, England. (I was going to call this cocktail simply Yolanda but then I remembered the Yolanda cocktail in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book. The best names have already been used!)

name: My Tequila Valentine
preparation: SHAKE or STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 1⁄2 shot	Blood orange juice
review: Beautifully balanced tequila and blood orange with a herbal vermouth complexity and delicate bitter notes.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Amy Stewart, author of the Drunken Botanist.

name: Hibiscus Rum Punch
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice, then pour soda into shaker before straining into an ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Jamaican aged blended rum with funk
1 shot	Hibiscus (sorrel) liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Characterful rum rightly provides the backbone to this lightly spiced fruity rum punch.
history: Adapted from a recipe created at Smuggler's Cove in San Fransciso, which in turn was inspired by the traditional Sorrel Punch, enjoyed throughout the Caribbean.

name: Armistice
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2 dash	Whiskey barrel-aged bitters
review: Dry, spirituous and satisfying. A late-night sipper that also works well on-the-rocks.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2011 by Erik Hakkinen at Zig Zag Café in Seattle, Washington, USA.

name: Quadrophenia
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Averna Amaro
1⁄4 shot	Amer Picon
1 dash	Fee Brothers Turkish Tobacco Bitters
review: A Sweet Manhattan on bitter steroids. If you find it a tad punchy then try served on-the-rocks.
history: Adapted form a recipe created 2012 by Julian Goglia, partner and principal bartender at The Pinewood Tippling Room in Decatur, Georgia, USA. The original recipe calls for a house-made alternative to Amer Picon and Old Forester Bohemian Bitters (in place of tobacco bitters).

name: Montana (Jacques Straub, 1913)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Ruby port
1⁄6 shot	Anisette liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: The influence of anisette is surprisingly subtle in this alternative to a Sweet Manhattan. If you want to make this a little drier, use a tawny rather than ruby port.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Jacques Straub's 1913 Straub's Manual of Mixed Drinks. He repeats this recipe a year later in his book, simply named Drinks.

name: Bedford & Grand
garnish: Lemon zest twist expressed and discarded. Adorn with a skewered Luxardo Maraschino Cherry.
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Mancino Vermouth di Torino Chinato
1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A delicious Manhattan-like cocktail that's brilliantly enlivened by chinato and fino sherry with maraschino playing an enhancing role.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2021 by Sebastian Tollius, beverage director at Eleven Madison Park, New York, USA.

name: White Witch
garnish: Spent half lime husk, mint sprigs bouquet and dust with icing sugar. Serve with a straw.
preparation: POUR first 4 ingredients into chilled glass, two-thirds filled with crushed ice and SWIZZLE. Fill glass with more crushed ice and top with soda.
ingredients:
1 shot	White overproof rum
1⁄2 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Overproof rum, orange curaçao and lime are the main influences in this long, refreshing cocktail. However, crème de cacao adds pleasing chocolaty notes.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Victor Bergeron's 1972 Trader Vic's Bartender's Guide.

name: Hazelnut Old Fashioned
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
2⁄3 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄3 shot	Hazelnut sugar syrup
8 drop	Bob's Abbotts bitters
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Just as it says on the tin, an Old Fashioned with subtle hazelnut notes. Hazelnut-flavoured sugar syrup is key to this recipe, which is even tastier when made with a roasted hazelnut syrup.
history: Created in June 2024 by yours truly at the Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: Adonis
garnish: Skewered olive (optional orange zest twist expressed & discarded)
preparation: THROW (or STIR) all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Palo cortado sherry
1 shot	Amontillado sherry
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄12 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review:
Some describe the Adonis as "The sweet version of the Bamboo" but that hardly does this brilliant vintage aperitivo/digestivo, that's off-dry and aromatic justice.

I made the Adonis for Dan to photograph in a vintage Boadas Martini glass as the Boadas Bar's rendition of this classic is the best I've encountered. And thanks to their generosity, I have one of their last 20 original glasses and the knowledge that it's a 'secret' splash of Italian red bitter liqueur that deepens the flavour profile of their Adonis rather than the orange bitters favoured by others.

I really wanted to find a Spanish vermouth that worked best in Adonis or indeed a very expressive Torino sweet vermouth but I found these too domineering and/or overly sweet so I settled on a more standard rosso vermouth. I've also experimented with various styles of sherry and now lean towards a blend of palo cortado and amontillado.
history:
The first known mention of the Adonis in print is in the "Pearls from Billy, the bartender" column in New York's The Sun newspaper on 27th March 1887. The column describes three customers, "three young bloods, with bell-crowned beavers of matchless sheen and silver-headed canes of ultra fashionable immensity who walk into the bar where Billy was bartending and order "Three Adonis cocktails, please." Billy proceeds the confidently make and serve them three cocktails which they drink, pay "fifteen cents each" for and leave. Then it becomes clear that Billy has no idea what an Adonis is. ""What on earth is an Adonis cocktail?" asked the reporter who had watched the incident. "Blessed if I know," said Billy, with an air of perfect frankness; "but I wouldn't be much of a bartender if I let any customer bluff me off with any new-fangled name. I gave them what I always have known as a turf club cocktail, and it suited. The first principle of good bartending is to know how to make everything on earth in the drink line, no matter whether you have ever heard of it before or not.""

This irreverent column doesn't reveal what comprised an Adonis but it does tell us that it was a "new-fangled" cocktail at the time so dating its origin prior to 1897.

It's another 16 years before the Adonis appears in a recipe book, Jacques Straub's 1913 Straub's Manual of Mixed Drinks establishing the recipe as two-thirds Italian (sweet) vermouth to one-third sherry with 2 dashes orange bitters.

name: Banana Bliss
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Oloroso sherry
4 drop	Bob's Abbotts bitters
review: Banana liqueur and brandy go shockingly well together, here toned with sherry and bitters.
history: Adapted from a recipe in W. J. Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Cocktail Book which is credits E. Angerosa with this cocktail's creation.

name: Bellini (Difford's recipe)
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass charged with the prosecco.
ingredients:
2 shot	Peach purée
1⁄3 shot	Peachtree peach schnapps
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
review: It's hard not to like this blend of peaches and sparkling wine. Lemon juice adds balance and a citrusy bite while peach schnapps boosts peachy flavour. If you prefer drier then switch prosecco to brut champagne.
history:
It has long been traditional in Italy to marinade fresh peaches in wine, and the Bellini draws on this tradition by combining prosecco wine with puréed white peaches.

Giuseppe Cipriani created this drink at Harry's Bar in Venice in 1945, fourteen years after he opened his tiny place on the edge of the Grand Canal, not far from Piazza San Marco.

Cipriani named his cocktail after the 15th-century Venetian painter Giovanni Bellini due to the drink's pink hue and the painter's penchant for using rich pinks on his canvases.

Like many other legendary bars around the world, Harry's owes some of its notoriety to being patronised by probably the world's greatest drinker, Ernest Hemingway. It was also the haunt of Sinclair Lewis, Orson Welles, F. Scott Fitzgerald and Dorothy Parker, and continues to attract celebrities to this day. But you don't have to be a celebrity to go to Harry's Bar. Cocktail aficionados from around the world make pilgrimages to the birthplace of the Bellini to sample the original recipe.

White peaches are in season in Italy from May to September, so in Venice, bars that insist on using only fresh peaches rather than frozen purée sell the drink between May and October.

name: Bird of Paradise
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄2 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1 1⁄2 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: If you like tequila and creamy drinks, the two don't mix much better than this.

name: Brandy Alexander
garnish: Express lemon zest twist and discard. Then dust with freshly grated nutmeg.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: This after-dinner classic is rich, creamy and subtly chocolaty.
history:
The original Alexander was gin-based, but in the early 1920s, Harry MacElhone, then a bartender at Ciro's in London, is credited with starting the trend of using brandy in place of gin. What became known as the Brandy Alexander quickly displaced the original gin-based cocktail.

MacElhone's creation of the brandy-based Alexander is supported by the first recipe for such a cocktail appearing in his 1923 Harry of Ciro's ABC of mixing cocktails

name: Hazelnut Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄3 shot	Hazelnut liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: A hazelnut Vodkatini with a hint of chocolate.

name: Lavender Margarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lavender sugar syrup
4 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters (optional)
review: As the name suggests, a floral, lavender-influenced margarita.
history: A riff on the classic Margarita cocktail created in 2006 by yours truly.

name: Long Flight of Stairs
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. Serve with straws.
ingredients:
1 shot	Pear-flavoured vodka
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 shot	Pear & cognac liqueur
2 1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review: A seriously tasty, strong, long drink. The name is a reversal of the London rhyming slang 'apples and pears' (stairs).
history: Created in 2005 by yours truly (Simon Difford) as a homage to the G.E. Club's 'Stairs Martini'.

name: Artist's Special Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1 1⁄2 shot	Oloroso sherry
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Groseille (redcurrant) syrup
review: Irish whiskey is often matured in oloroso sherry seasoned casks so it's no surprise that whiskey and sherry blend harmoniously in this cocktail, with lemon tartness balanced by rich red currant syrup, the key ingredient that makes this cocktail "Special".
history: A voraciously pink Parisian special from the 1920s, this cocktail first appears in print in Harry MacElhone's 1927 Barflies and Cocktails.

name: Mexicano (Hot)
preparation: POUR tequila and liqueur into warmed glass and top with coffee. FLOAT cream over drink.
ingredients:
1 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
Top up with	Filter coffee (hot)
Float lightly whipped	Single cream/half-and-half
review: A spicy, flavour-packed hot coffee. Lightly whip or simply shake cream in container before pouring over the bowl of a spoon. It also helps if the cream is gently warmed.

name: Milk & Honey
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
4 drop	Tonka bitters (optional)
review: Flavoursome Scotch whisky enriched with honey and smoothed with cream.
history: Created in 2002 by yours truly in London, England.

name: Nice Pear
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Pear & cognac liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Poire William eau-de-vie
1 shot	Pear juice (freshly pressed)
review: Despite the "no missus" Frankie Howerd-like, English seaside postcard humour name, this is a very tasteful cocktail – pear and cognac is a delicious flavour combination.
history: Created in 2002 by yours truly.

name: Pooh'tini
preparation: STIR honey with vodka in base of shaker to dissolve honey. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 barspoon	Honey
2 shot	Bison grass vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Camomile tea (cold)
1⁄2 shot	Krupnik spiced honey liqueur
review: Grassy honey with spicy, slightly tannic, camomile finish.
history: Adapted from a drink discovered in 1999 at Lot 61, New York City.

name: Rocky Mountain Rootbeer
preparation: POUR all ingredients into glass and them fill glass with ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Galliano L'Autentico liqueur
4 shot	Cola (e.g. Coca Cola or Pepsi Cola)
1 dash	Bob's Liquorice bitters (optional)
review: Does indeed taste reminiscent of alcoholic root beer.

name: Sgroppino / Sorbetto
garnish: Dust with freshly grated lemon zest
preparation: BLEND all ingredients without additional ice and serve in chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄4 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1 1⁄2 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
2 scoop	Lemon sorbet
review: Smooth and all too easy to quaff. A great dessert.
history: Pronounced 'scroe-pee-noe', this hybrid cocktail and dessert is often served after meals in Venice. The name comes from a vernacular word meaning 'untie', a reference to the belief that it relaxes your stomach after a hearty meal.

name: Snowfall Cocktail
preparation: Take 1/4 a vanilla pod and cut along its length. MUDDLE this in the base of a shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄4 whole	Vanilla pod
1 1⁄2 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: An alcoholic version of a vanilla milkshake with tiny black specs from the vanilla.
history: Originally called a Snowfall Martini and discovered in 2002 at Lot 61, New York City, USA.

name: Knickerbocker
garnish: Squeezed-out half lime shell & seasonal berries: raspberries, blackberries, blueberries
preparation: SHAKE first all ingredients with ice and strain into glass 2/3rd filled with cubed ice. Cap with crushed ice, serve with a straw.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄6 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Raspberry (framboise) sugar syrup
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Fruity and refreshing – a party drink with rum and raspberry flavours predominating. At its best when made with homemade raspberry syrup.
history: The Knickerbocker cocktail first appears in Jerry Thomas' 1862 The Bartender's Guide. For the full story see our Knickerbocker Cocktails page.

name: Wonky Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
1⁄2 shot	Tuaca liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2 dash	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
review: A sweet, wet Vodkatini invigorated with vanilla and grapefruit.
history: Created in 2003 by yours truly (Simon Difford), London, England.

name: Clairvoyant
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice & fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Oloroso sherry
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Hazelnut liqueur
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A hazelnut flavoured variation on the classic Coronation Cocktail
history: Created in 2008 by yours truly in Jerez, Spain and named after Claire Hu, a fellow drinks hack on the same trip who was a fan of hazelnut liqueur.

name: Jalisco Flower
garnish: Grapefruit zest twist &/or edible white flowers
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with champagne/sparkling wine and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1 shot	Grapefruit juice (ruby red)
3 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Subtle, fruity and one of my favourite champagne/sparkling wine cocktails.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2008 by Vincenzo Marianella at Doheny in Los Angeles, USA. (Originally served straight-up in a flute.)

name: Martinez (London spec. with genever)
preparation: STIR ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
review: Bready notes from genever sit brilliantly with the herbal notes of the vermouth. Maraschino notes are subtle but essential to the balance of flavour.
history:
This formula for the vintage classic emerged and became popular in London in early 2008 with the introduction of Antica Formula.
See Martinez cocktail history

name: Fallen Leaves
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Cognac (brandy)
review: Suitably autumnal in colour. Two vermouths and two brandies presented in harmony.
history: Created in 1982 by Charles Schumann in Munich, Germany, and first published in his book American Bar.

name: Bushwick
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into a chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Amer Picon
review: This Italian-American blend is better and even more gripping than Godfather II.
history: Created in 2009 by Phil Ward at Mayahuel in New York City, USA. This riff on the Brooklyn is named after Bushwick, a neighbourhood in the northeast of the New York City borough of Brooklyn. As Amer Picon can be tricky to obtain, Phil recommends Amaro Lucano as a substitute.

name: Cuban Liberal
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄12 shot	Amer Picon
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Light white rum mellowed by Italian vermouth and made interesting with bittersweet French Amer Picon liqueur.
history: Adapted from a drink featured in the La Florida (El Floridita) Cocktails book, this is a riff on El Presidente.

name: Defender Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Crème Yvette liqueur
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: One of those drinks where the bitter oils from the orange zest twist are crucial to its fine balance.
history: Adapted from Albert Stevens Crockett's 1931 Old Waldorf Bar Days which explains, "The name of an American yacht which took care of one of Sir Thomas Lipton's early but seemingly endless Shamrocks". [Shamrock being the name of Sir Thomas Lipton's fleet of America's Cup racing yachts.]

name: Diamondback
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain unto chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄2 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: This potent cocktail marries apple spirit with rye whiskey and rich herbal Chartreuse. An after-dinner/nightcap tipple.
history:
Adapted from Ted Saucier's 1951 Bottoms Up book in which the author calls for two parts rye whiskey, one part applejack and one part yellow Chartreuse. The Diamondback Lounge Cocktail, as its properly named, was the signature drink at the Diamondback Lounge bar which lies within the Lord Baltimore Hotel. This historic 22-story hotel opened in 1928 and still graces the skyline of Baltimore, Maryland to this day, although sadly the Diamondback Lounge has long gone.

The cocktail, and indeed the lounge bar where it originated, are named after the diamondback terrapin, a species of turtle common to the tidal marshlands of America's east coast which, as its name suggests, has a diamond pattern on top of its shell. Since 1932, the turtle has been the University of Maryland's school mascot and is also the Maryland State Reptile.

name: Hocus Pocus
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
review: Bittersweet with gin's botanical complexity and orange zest freshness.
history: Adapted from a drink discovered in 2010 at Forty Four, New York City, USA. Hocus Pocus by the Dutch rock band Focus was a chart-topper both sides of the Atlantic in 1971. Famous for its yodelling, whistling, accordion, and flute, this is a tune that has to heard to be believed. We're fans!

name: Elle Loves
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Vanilla rum/vanilla-infused light rum
1 shot	White Zinfandel rosé wine
1 1⁄4 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: Fruity, very slightly sweet and suitably pink in colour. Best made with a light white rum infused with a vanilla pod, rather than a commercially produced vanilla-flavoured rum.
history: Created 30th January 2014 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room as a Valentine's Day cocktail for Elle Magazine.

name: Red Gemma
preparation: STIR first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne and gently stir.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
1 shot	Shiraz red wine
3 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Red berry flavours with light red wine tannins, liqueur sweetness and botanical depth courtesy of gin, all refreshed with fizz. Berry fizz!
history: Created 5th February 2014 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room in London, England and named after Gemma Monaghan, who incidentally is a Mancunian who supports Liverpool FC.

name: Sangre Dulce Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1 shot	Blood orange juice
1⁄4 shot	Cinnamon syrup
1⁄4 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
review: Mezcal, cinnamon and bittersweet Fernet are big-hitting flavours which combine brilliantly in this characterful yet harmonious cocktail.
history: Created in 2013 by Regina Butler at Blackbird Bar in San Francisco, USA. Regina's original recipe calls for Fernet Vallet, a Mexican amaro that's sadly not available in the UK.

name: Christmas Special No. 1
garnish: Half walnut on rim or rest on the ice
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
1⁄2 shot	Mandarine Napoleon liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Walnut (Nocino) liqueur
review: A great after-dinner cocktail any time of year but particularly appropriate over the festive period due to its ingredients – Pedro Ximénez sherry tastes like Christmas pudding, mandarins are not just for Christmas and walnuts are best cracked whilst watching a Christmas special.
history: Created in December 2013 by yours truly and Paloma Alos at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Fairy Cream
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 1⁄4 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
review: Absinthe sits majestically with cream and chocolate in this indulgent after-dinner cocktail.
history: Created in 2010 by bartending legend Dick Bradsell in London, England.

name: Love Heart
garnish: Half strawberry on rim with Love Heart sweet pegged to rim
preparation: POUR all ingredients into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka (from freezer)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Fraise des Bois liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Parfait Amour liqueur
4 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine (chilled)
review:
This lavender pink drink is everything you (or your partner) might want for a Valentine's tipple. It is the right colour, includes parfait amour liqueur (meaning perfect love) and the all-important champagne sparkle. Good luck.

In case he/she asks, parfait amour is a lilac coloured curaçao (orange) liqueur flavoured with rose petals, vanilla pods and almonds.
history: Created in February 2014 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room in London in England.

name: Right Hand
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & orange slice wheel
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
2 dash	Xocolatl mole bitters
review: This rum-based Negroni may make you wonder why you've been drinking gin Negronis all these years. The Right Hand is usually served straight-up in a coupe but I prefer it tamed by serving on-the-rocks in an old-fashioned glass.
history: Adapted from a recipe created 2007-8 by Michael McIlroy at Milk & Honey in New York City, USA.

name: Quincy Jones
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Byrrh Grand Quinquina
1⁄3 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
2⁄3 shot	Clove & quince syrup (homemade)
2 dash	Orinoco bitters
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Miran Chauhan at Bon Vivant, Edinburgh, Scotland.

name: Le Grand
preparation: STIR first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. TOP with sparkling wine.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Byrrh Grand Quinquina
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 barspoon	Giffard Grenadine syrup
Top up with	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Aromatised wine plays a lead role in this cognac-charged apéritif.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Samuel Rose at Panda & Sons in Edinburgh, Scotland.

name: Bitches' Brew cocktail
garnish: Orange zest twist and Luxardo maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Byrrh Grand Quinquina
3⁄4 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
3⁄4 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	India pale ale (IPA) beer
review: Beer has never tasted so complex - sweet aperitif, dry hoppy IPA beer, bready jenever and cleansing vodka.
history: Created by yours truly on 21st February 2015 at the Cabinet Room, London, England and so named due to its ingredients including beer and Byrrh aperitif (also pronounced 'beer') so "brew" seemed appropriate, helped by the track Bitches Brew on the brilliant 1961 Bitches Brew studio album by Miles Davis, the American jazz trumpeter, composer and bandleader.

name: Greek Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Kleos Mastiha liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Ouzo
review: Mastiha (which after all is a botanically flavoured spirit) combines wonderfully with gin and dry vermouth. A splash of ouzo adds a touch more Greek personality.
history:
Created by yours truly in August 2015 at the Cabinet Room in London, England. (If only I were on a Greek island.)
Martini cocktail history and its evolution

name: The Angel Wore Red
preparation: STIR first 3 ingredients with ice. POUR beer into ice-filled glass and then strain stirred ingredients into glass and lightly stir.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe
2 shot	International lager
review: A most unusual combination of classic Italian red bitter liqueur, bianco vermouth, crème de menthe and lager combine brilliantly in this refreshing aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2015 by Dominic Whisson at the American Bar, The Savoy Hotel, London, England.

name: Moon Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Amontillado sherry
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Crème de Pêche de Vigne liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: Gin and sherry combine harmoniously in this stirred boozy cocktail with a honeyed touch of jammy peach.
history: Created in 2008 by Thomas Waugh at Death & Co., New York City, USA.

name: Roosevelt Cocktail #2
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 dash	Black walnut bitters
review: Rye whiskeys’ strength and spice cuts through and dries the rich sultana notes of PX sherry with the bitters, particularly the walnut bitters, adding flavour and complexity.

name: Sunset Strip
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Tennessee whiskey
1 shot	Giffard Pamplemousse liqueur
1 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
review: Eric Tecosky's original recipe for this cocktail calls for 1.25oz of Jack Daniel's Single Barrel instead of the combination of Tennessee and rye whiskies used here. Being a mix of split base spirits and liqueurs, it was stirred, as you'd expect such a combination. However, somewhat reminiscent of Shakerato, the Sunset Strip seems to benefit from the aeration and extra dilution provided by shaking. Hence, this is the method I've chosen.
history: Adapted from 2015 recipe created by Eric Tecosky at Jones Hollywood, Los Angeles, USA (and courtesy of Gary "gaz" Regan).

name: La Garde de Nuit (The Night's Watch)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 1⁄2 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
3⁄4 shot	Mead
1⁄6 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
review: Cognac with red berry and red wine notes with faint honeycomb.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Matthew Long at Lulu White, Paris, France. Matt’s original recipe called for Chouchen Hydromel mead wine from Brittany and Gentiane de Lure.

name: The Comeback
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Maple shrub (1:1.2 cider vinegar to maple syrup)
review: A complex cocktail with apricot fruit at the forefront and underlying fernet bitterness.
history: Created in 2015 by Constanca Cordeiro at Peg + Patriot, London, England.

name: Rabo-de-Galo
preparation: THROW OR STIR (or even shake) all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cachaça
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1 dash	Hopped grapefruit bitters (optional)
review: The bittersweet herbal notes from the vermouth and Cynar combine harmoniously with the cachaça. Depending on how punchy you like your cocktails you may want to increase or decrease the amount of cachaça (anywhere between 45 and 60ml).
history:
One of the best-known drinks in Brazil, Rabo de Galo originated in the mid-1950s after a Cinzano factory opened in São Paulo, leading to rosso (sweet) vermouth being mixed with the local cachaça.

'Rabo-de-galo' literally translates from Brazilian Portuguese as rooster tail or 'cock tail'. In Brazil, a cocktail is called 'coquetel'. Originally served as a shot in dive bars, which in Brazil are called pés-sujos (literally translates as 'dirty feet'), the proportions and the drink's ingredients vary greatly from bar to bar and region to region, but are generally accepted as being 2/3 cachaça and 1/3 sweet vermouth.

In São Paulo, it is now commonplace for the vermouth to be substituted with Cynar, or (as above) both sweet vermouth and Cynar to be mixed with the cachaça. As the Rabo-de-Galo has transitioned from pés-sujos to cocktail bars, so it has moved from being served straight-up in large tall shot glasses to tumblers and on-the-rocks, as above.

name: Genesis
preparation:
SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).

*Special ingredient #1: All spice & lemon grass syrup
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Bacardi Gold rum
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄3 shot	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A spiced apricot daiquiri. Lemongrass is the stand-out ingredient that makes this cocktail interesting.
history: Polish Bacardí Legacy 2016 winning cocktail by Paweł Rodaszyński, El Koktel, Warsaw. Paweł says, "Don Facundo did not know that the beginning of his work would become a legacy. The light, universal taste of Bacardí rum is known all over the world. We each stand every day before the same opportunity as Facundo - a chance to build our own legacy. In order to achieve it, you need flavours that can inspire. Bacardí Carta Oro, with its vanilla notes, is a perfect match for apricot, lemongrass, lime, and allspice. Create your own legacy!"

name: 18th Century
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Batavia arrack
3⁄4 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
3⁄4 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Sweet 'n' sour with the unmistakable funky twang of Batavia arrack.
history: A riff on the classic 20th Century Cocktail, created in 2008 by Phil Ward at Death & Co., New York City, USA.

name: The Stag
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) with cube of candied ginger
preparation: STIR all ingredients and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Jägermeisteror other German amaro
1⁄3 shot	Lavender sugar syrup
5 drop	Bob's Ginger Bitters
review: Boozy and stirred down. Cognac fortifies and combines harmoniously with the bittersweet herbal and spicy notes of the liqueur. Rich lavender enhances and amplifies these flavours with ginger bitters adding extra zingy spice and toning the blend. Best appreciated as an after-dinner digestif.
history: Created by yours truly in October 2016 at The Cabinet Room, London, after being inspired by the Élysée Treaty cocktail and appreciating how well Jägermeister mixes with brandy.

name: Mexican Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Añejo tequila
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
4 dash	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters
review: Considering tequila is replacing vodka in this French Martini riff, you'd think that when it came to tequila, a blanco tequila would be best suited. However, having tried this and then reposado tequila, unexpectedly I found myself turning towards and favouring añejo as being best suited to this cocktail's tropical and berry fruitiness.
history: Created in February 2017 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Smoking Gun Vesper
garnish: Lemon zest twist & small strip cured smoked pork on a skewer.
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Oak Smoked Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 dash	Jerry Thomas bitters
review: Delicately smoky and almost meaty – be sure to serve with cured meat. A great aperitif cocktail.
history:
Adapted from a drink created in 2016 by Dale DeGroff, King Cocktail, New York City, USA.

This recipe is courtesy of gazregan.com. Dale's original recipe calls for: 1½ oz Chase English Oak Smoked Vodka, ½ oz Tanqueray No. TEN Gin, ¼ oz La Quintinye Vermouth Royal Dry Vermouth and 1 dash Bitter Truth's Jerry Thomas Own Decanter Bitters. Dale's preferred garnish is a small strip cured smoked pork on a skewer.

More information on the story behind Bond's Vesper can be found on our Vesper cocktail page page.

name: Holy Joe Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
review: An Irish whiskey-based, bittersweet aperitif cocktail that works equally well as a nightcap.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2016 by John Robinson, beverage manager at The Hive, Bentonville, Arkansas.

name: The Ribbon
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Fino sherry
1 1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Blood orange liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review: Dry sherry and bitter orange with underlying ripe grape sweetness, The Ribbon makes for a perfect aperitif cocktail.
history:
The Ribbon was created in 2017 at Swift in Soho, London, England, and was originally made with 40% alc./vol. Solerno blood orange liqueur and Cocchi Storico Vermouth di Torino rosso vermouth. My previous interpretation of their recipe comprised:
20ml (2/3oz) Fino sherry
20ml (2/3oz) Cocchi Torino vermouth
10ml (1/3oz) Solerno
10ml Campari liqueur
Due to the demise of the availability of Solerno liqueur in the UK, in August 2022, at Swift Bar in Shoreditch, London, I discovered they had switched to Grand Marner so I also adapted my recipe.

name: For Sake's Sake
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 1⁄2 shot	Akashi-Tai Daiginjo Genshu sake
1⁄3 shot	Italicus liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
review: Being dyslexic, I'm bewildered as to how to spell dyslexic while also amused by sake (the beverage brewed from rice) being spelt the same way as sake (as in for fk's sake!). Hopefully, you'll find this aromatic, subtly orange-influenced sake and rum-based Martini-like cocktail both delightful to drink and easy to spell.
history: Created in April 2017 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: The Rum Pickle
preparation: STIR all ingredients without ice to dissolve sugar. Then STIR with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bacardi Gold rum
2⁄3 shot	Chardonnay (Chablis) white wine
1 barspoon	White balsamic vinegar
1 barspoon	Powdered sugar (white sugar ground in mortar and pestle)
review:
The dry cleansing balsamic vinegar alongside a good buttery Chardonnay and golden rum makes The Rum Pickle a great aperitivo. (Doesn't work nearly so well with a charcoal filtred light white rum.)

Depending on your wine and vinegar, you may need to reduce the amount of vinegar, or up the amount of sugar to achieve a harmonious balance.
history: Created for Bacardí Legacy 2017 by Eetu Topo in Helsinki, Finland. Eetu says, "Rum Pickle represents not just a cocktail, but also a modern Nordic cocktail category that stems from our heritage and tradition when it comes to what we drink and how we eat. The category 'Pickle' consists of a spirit, a lengthener, sugar and vinegar. Using the same ratios it can be replicated to any other form and the result still remains the same - an aperitivo kind of a drink where the vinegar brings the acid that refreshes the drink as well as telling a story about how we in the Nordics have preserved our food for centuries."

name: Celebration (by Grzegorz Nowicki)
preparation:
STIR first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass TOP with prosecco.

*Special ingredient #1: Pineapple cordial made by blending 900g of pineapple flesh with 450g of simple syrup (1:1.5) and straining through a cheesecloth; add 4g tartaric acid.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bacardi Gold rum
1 2⁄3 shot	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 2⁄3 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
review: A splash of prosecco adds vitality to what is a simple, but beautifully balanced rum and pineapple cocktail.
history: Created for Bacardí Legacy 2017 by Grzegorz Nowicki at 6 Cocktails, Warsaw, Poland.

name: The Dandy (by Iain Meldrum)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Speyburn 10yo Speyside single malt
1 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Dry and slightly on the bitter side of bittersweet, single malt scotch, gentian liqueur and dry vermouth sit well together in this appealing aperitif-style cocktail.
history:
