Adapted from a recipe created in 2017 by Iain Meldrum at Michael Neave Kitchen & Whisky Bar in Edinburgh, Scotland. Iain's original recipe called for 25ml single malt scotch (sweet & fruity), 25ml Suze, 25ml Dolin Blanc and 3 drops 5% saline solution.

Iain says, "The Boulevardier cocktail got its name from Parisian urbanites and fashion-followers. This pale, Scotch-based version takes its name from the British (and particularly Scottish Border) word for a man-about-town. It's also a nod to that other famous Scottish product, the Dandy comic."

name: Swiss Watch
garnish: Powdered sugar rim. (Note: Lemon zest can be floated on the drink, halved with the shape of 'V', to show the time 2pm)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled sugar rimmed glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Kirschwasser (cherry) eau-de-vie
1 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: As Peter Konkoly, this cocktail's creator says, it is reminiscent of a Last Word. However, we prefer this tasty drink served on-the-rocks as an aperitif alternative to a Negroni, rather than straight-up as originally specified by Peter.
history: Created in 2017 by Peter Konkoly at The Arts Club, London, England, who describes this as "An alpine variation of The Last Word cocktail, using ingredients found in the Alps (Chartreuse), Switzerland (Kirschwasser) and nearby."

name: Keyser Suze
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
3 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2017 by Chris Grotvedt at The Thief, Oslo, Norway. Chris’ original spec call for 45ml Suze, 45ml Carpano dry vermouth and 3 dash orange bitters. The name is a play on words from the character in the movie The Usual Suspects.

name: Clandestine
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄3 shot	Italicus liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: Honey balances bitter notes of gentian with citrusy bergamot and Scotch spirit. An apéritif of digestif.
history: Created in December 2017 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Canadian Tuxedo
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄2 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
1 1⁄2 shot	Canadian rye whisky
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: On the sour/dry side, this aperitif-style cocktail combines bittersweet amaro and gentian with Canadian rye whisky and citrus sourness.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2017 by Caledonia Wright at Veneto Lounge, Victoria, Canada. Caledonia’s original recipe calls for: ¾oz Suze, ½oz Amaro Abano, 1½oz Lot 40 Rye and ½oz fresh lemon juice.

name: Tezonita
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
3⁄4 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
review: A dry and fairly bitter aperitif-style cocktail combining tequila's herbaceous notes and the herbal flavours of gentian.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2017 by Daniel Kaizen at Calexico Adliya, Adliya, Bahrain for the Olmeca Tahona Society Cocktail Competition 2016. Daniel's original recipe called for 40ml Olmeca Altos Blanco, 25ml Suze and 25ml Belsazar white vermouth.

Daniel says, "It's a delicate drink made as an ode to the Tezontle, the volcanic rock that makes up the Tahona wheel used to crush agave in the traditional method of making tequila. The juxtaposition of being such a light, delicate drink bringing out the bittersweet flavours of the tequila while being quite a punchy agave faithful drink."

name: Fernand x Nando
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc) (infused with coffee beans)
2⁄3 shot	Cachaça
1⁄3 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A bittersweet apéritif combining gentian herbal complexity with attractive coffee, cachaça and calvados spirituous notes.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2017 by Nando Imamura, Hong Kong.

Nando says, "Fernand Moureaux, the genius that believed in create something different than the casual, versus Nando Imamura, bartender, Brazilian-Japanese and married with a French Woman creating flavours around the world. I created this cocktail using French and Brazilian products to celebrate the birth of my 1st baby. I used Suze infused with Brazilian Coffee beans, Cachaça Leblon aged in a French oak for three years and Calvados Cristian Droin VSOP and Angostura Bitters to balance it out."

Namdo's original recipe calls for 30ml Suze infused with Brazilian coffee beans, 20ml Leblon cachaça, 10ml Calvados Cristian Droin VSOP and 2 dashes Angostura Aromatic Bitters.

name: No Borders
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Birch spirit/birch eau-de-vie
2⁄3 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
2⁄3 shot	Italicus liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review: A tasty bittersweet Negroni-style aperitif.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2017 by Emily Couty at Sketch, London, England.

name: Devil Woman
garnish: Hibiscus pickled onion (In a jar of pickled onions, add 50g of dried hibiscus flower to each litre of vinegar and infuse for 3 hours. Double strain vinegar to remove flowers and return to jar.)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄6 shot	Lemon oleo saccharum
1⁄6 shot	Martini Riserva Speciale Bitter
1⁄6 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: Ana Alicia Herrera says of her drink, "The inspiration comes from something I learnt in New Orleans when I first became a bartender. Devil Woman is s new twist on a classic Gibson Martini."
history: Mexican BACARDÍ LEGACY 2018 winning cocktail by Ana Alicia Herrera, Pal Real, Guadalajara, Mexico.

name: Four Poster Red
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 shot	Dolin Chamberyzette
1 shot	Tawny port
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review:
This deep cherry red Negroni-like aperitivo is equally tasty shaken and served straight-up – indeed that's how it was originally made, like a Shakerato. If served shaken, then a white head should cover the drink's surface, or it's not been shaken hard enough. The cocktail should then be consumed before the head fades.

Either shaken or stirred, sweet vermouth/port predominates with bitter liqueur providing balance.
history: Created March 2018 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room in London, England.

name: Polish Pear Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Bison grass vodka
3⁄4 shot	Spiced Pear liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Pear juice (freshly pressed)
review: Pear fruitiness with suitably Martini boozy aromatic vodka.
history: A riff on Dick Bradsell's brilliantly simple Polish Martini by yours truly in May 2018.

name: Yes or Noyau?
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Crème de noyau liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Rainwater/Verdelho (med-dry) madeira wine
review: Bourbon and rye delicately sweetened and delicately flavoured with fruity almond notes with madeira adding light balancing acidity.
history: Created February 2019 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Coconut Rum Punch
garnish: Sprinkle with roasted dehydrated coconut flakes
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	White overproof rum
3⁄4 shot	Coconut sugar syrup
3 shot	Coconut water
5⁄12 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Coconut and rum with a splash of lime are a tried and tested flavour matches. In this case with the added punch of funky overproof Jamaican rum.

name: Clear As Rain
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	Mentzendorff Kümmel liqueur
2 shot	Birch water
1⁄6 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
review: Tequila, kummel and cacao – a trio of powerful flavours diluted and made into a delicate cocktail by birch water.
history: Created in March 2019 by yours truly (Simon Difford) at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Crystal Clear
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Mentzendorff Kümmel liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Italicus liqueur
2 shot	Birch water
review: Subtly citrusy and piney with delicate caraway. Clearly refined.
history: Created in March 2019 by yours truly (Simon Difford) at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Bad Name
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Chamomile liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: Sweet Manhattan-like in style with chamomile liqueur adding its distinctive floral flavour and honeyed sweetness.
history: Created February 2019 by Matteo Landi at Back Door 43, Milan, Italy. So named due to a lack of a better name. Originally made with Cocchi Storico Vermouth di Torino rosso vermouth.

name: Spiced Rum Negroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
2⁄3 shot	Americano bianco
2⁄3 shot	Tempus Fugit Gran Classico Bitter
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Mellow and slightly sweet with flavours of caramel, chocolate and rich orange.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Rogerio Igarashi at Trench Bar in Tokyo, Japan.

name: Smoky Orchard Highball
preparation: STIR first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass glass charged with some of the smoky tonic water, then TOP with more smoky tonic.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Pear liqueur (Poire William)
2 dash	Celery bitters
2 shot	Tonic water (smoked)
review: Savoury, delicately fruity and refreshing with delicate ripe pear, dry gin and celery with a hint of smoke.
history: Created in April 2019 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room in London, England.

name: Bon Vivant's Martini
garnish: Mist with spray of Islay single malt (& optional Cigarillo across the rim)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Tobacco liqueur (not homemade!)
1⁄6 shot	Americano bianco
1 dash	Tea bitters
review: Ideally, this Martini should be accompanied by a cigar which compliments the tobacco liqueur.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2018 by Tom Sipos in Austria. This cocktail was the winning Elit Art of Martini 2018 Global Final in Bilbao, Spain.

name: White Water Ride
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Acqua Bianca liqueur
1⁄3 shot	White overproof rum
2 shot	Coconut water
review: Funky rum and coconut water enveloped in zesty orange, rose and faint minty freshness.
history: Created in February 2020 by yours truly at the Clocktower, Sussex, England.

name: Anurka
preparation: STIR first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. TOP with cider.
ingredients:
1 shot	Martini Riserva Speciale Bitter
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
1 shot	Dry cider
review: Bittersweet with cider harmoniously combining with Italian red bitter liqueur and rosso vermouth.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2016 by Eddie Rudzinskas of Cocktails For You fame. After participating in Martini Ciclismo in 2019 Eddie told us, "This was my winning drink that led me to participate in the Martini Grand Prix in 2016 which introduced me to the Martini Family. Without this, I would've never got on the bike in the first place!"

name: Fourteenth Century
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
1 shot	Americano bianco
1 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A riff on the classic 20th Century based on Black Tears spiced rum and so named due to the Black Death reaping its havoc in the 14th Century.

name: Bubo Bubo
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1⁄2 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
1⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: Bittersweet and whisky-laced but smoothed and mellowed by honeyed richness.
history: Adapted from a cocktail discovered at Le Hibou Bar, Stockholm, Sweden.

name: Rum 'n' It
preparation: STIR all ingredients and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Roasted buckwheat cordial
history: Created in 2020 by Erik Lorincz at Kwānt, London, England. Originally made with Cocchi Storico Vermouth di Torino rosso vermouth.

name: Bergamot Negroni
garnish: Bergamot zest twist (expressed & discarded & lemon leaf (or orange slice)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Oak aged gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Italicus liqueur
review: As the name suggests, subtle bergamot notes influence this dryish Negroni riff.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Naren Young, Creative Director at Dante New York City, USA.

name: American Trilogy
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Applejack brandy bottled-in-bond (50% alc./vol)
5⁄6 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄4 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: To adhere to the original recipe, you should smash a sugar cube and then painstakingly stir this with bitters into a paste. Life is just too short to faff around, so instead, I've used pre-dissolved sugar (syrup). Depending on your personal tastes you may want to reduce this syrup to a mere 5ml or it up to 10ml. Syrup allows you to find your personal sweet spot and then consistently hit it. Once achieved, you've a delicious subtly cider-influenced Rye Old-Fashioned.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2006 by Richard Boccato and Michael McIlroy at Milk & Honey in New York City. By the following year it was a staple at sibling bar Little Branch bar and American Trilogy continues to be a popular cocktail at Attaboy, the bar that occupies the former Milk & Honey site.

Originally built in the glass with a sugar cube and made with three American ingredients, hence the name: rye whisky, applejack and Regan's Orange Bitters.

name: Gustings' Grasshopper
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Cognac (brandy)
5⁄6 shot	Giffard Peppermint Pastille crème de menthe
5⁄6 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
5⁄6 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: Indulgent, minty, creamy, chocolate-laced with cognac. What's not to like?
history: Created by Paul Gustings at Tujague's in New Orleans, USA where it is claimed the classic Grasshopper cocktail was made.

name: Hey Sugar
garnish: Sprinkle dried rose blossom on the surface of the cocktail
preparation: Drip one drop of bitters on each side of the sugar cube plus 2 more drops on the last face [one each for luck]. Drop the bitters-soaked sugar cube into a chilled glass, then pour other ingredients over cube.
ingredients:
1 cube	Sugar cube
6 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters
1⁄3 shot	Elderflower liqueur
4 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Elderflower and dry sparkling wine are a match made in heaven with the bitters-soaked cube seasoning the cocktail with faint bittersweet pineapple and lavender.
history: Created in February 2021 by yours truly and Paloma (my Valentine) for Valentine's Day.

name: Salome
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2 dash	Plum bitters (optional)
review: Equal parts gin, aromatised wine and vermouth combine harmoniously in this "pleasant, clean sippin'" stirred down aperitivo.
history: Eponymously named after an 1891 tragedy by Oscar Wilde, this "exhumed classic" cocktail was brought to our attention by Jason E. Clapham who added the plum bitters, "a greatly needed enhancement". The original recipe, sans bitters, appeared in Hugo Ensslin's 1916 Recipes for Mixed Drinks.

name: Lovely Pear of Coconuts
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Pear liqueur (Poire William)
1⁄3 shot	Coconut rum liqueur (35-40% alc./vol.)
5⁄6 shot	Coconut water
review: As the name implies, this cocktail has a duo of coconut flavours, with pear liqueur and laced with white rum.
history: Created in April 2021 by yours truly at the Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Summa Peto
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Akashi-Tai Daiginjo Genshu sake
5⁄6 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄3 shot	Pear liqueur (Poire William)
review: Delicate, aromatic and Martini-esc with delicate minerality and pear fruitiness.
history: Created in March 2021 by yours truly at the Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: The Bluff
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
2⁄3 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄3 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄3 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
review: A spirituous bittersweet digestif with notes of each of the four ingredients shining in a harmonious way.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Danny Shapiro at Scofflaw in Chicago, USA.

name: Parisian Blonde
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Jamaican aged blended rum with funk
1 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix) (optional)
review: This creamy orange cocktail screams for a funky and characterful rum that needs taming - it's just not the same with a more restrained rum. And, depending on your orange curaçao and personal tastes, you may want to add a touch of additional sugar to the classic three equal parts recipe.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Spicy Manhattan
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Piment d'Espelette chile liqueur
2 dash	Boker's bitters
review: A Sweet Rye Manhattan with a long spicy finish.
history:
Recipe by yours truly but made thanks to a suggestion by Scott Berman, a fellow Discerning Drinker.
Manhattan cocktail history

name: Parthenon Old-Fashioned
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	O/Purist Tsipouro
2⁄3 shot	Navy rum (54.5% alc./vol.)
5⁄12 shot	Vanilla sugar
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Greece is a nation as famous for its seafaring prowess as it is the Parthenon, so it's perhaps fitting to include Navy rum in this Old Fashioned-style tsipouro-based cocktail from Greek city of Lamia. Vanilla is a brilliant touch in this late-night sipper.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Michalis Emmanouil at Degage Bar in Lamia, Greece, this was one of ten winning recipes in the 2021 O/Purist Quest. Michalis says he was inspired by temple of Parthenon in Athens, "built as a temple in honour of goddess Athena, protector of the city as well. In the same way the O/Purist Tsipouro was created by ten successful people from the world of bartending."

name: Silenus
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	O/Purist Tsipouro
1 1⁄3 shot	Riesling wine
1⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1 dash	Soy sauce
review: This cocktail combines a distilled grape spirit with wine (or wines – I used 40ml of one Riesling but the original recipe specifies 28ml Dr. Loosen Demi Sec Riesling and 12ml Dr. Loosen Dry Riesling) and then adds honeyed richness and a touch of savoury soy sauce. It's tricky to nail the perfect balance of wine and honey, and even your choice of soy sauce is crucial. However, patience is rewarded, and once nailed, easily replicated.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Dimitris Kaitalidis at Nectar Distillery in Thessaloniki, Greece, this was one of ten winning recipes in the 2021 O/Purist Quest. Apparently, "Sileni used to be a group of followers of the wine God Dionysus, mythological creatures with ears, tails and horse's hooves. They helped with winemaking and were characterised by drunken joy and ecstasy. Sileni, along with Satyrs and Maenads were Dionysus' entourage during his epic feasts and dances. This drink is pays homage to the God of Wine by using grape distillate O/Purist Tsipouro and wine."

name: Matador
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
5⁄6 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄12 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
review: Best enjoyed as an alternative to a Dry Martini and best as a nightcap. The classic recipe is equal parts tequila, curaçao and dry vermouth, but I like to add a touch more mellowing vermouth and then kick it back up again with the merest splash of mezcal. This adaption was influenced by Jason E. Clapham, who recommended this cocktail to us with the addition of 5ml / 1 spoon of Wray & Nephew overproof rum to give "a bump" to original equal parts recipe.
history: Adapted from a recipe in W. J. Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Cocktail Book.

name: Ice in the Hat
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Becherovka liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe
review: A delightfully refreshingly and cleansing digestif.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR in Oxford, England.

name: Ruby Manhattan
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Tawny port
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Rye whiskey with a touch of apricot and grape fruitiness served short, dry and strong. A delicious nightcap.
history:
Adapted from a cocktail created in the 2000s by Michael Waterhouse at Devin Tavern in New York City, USA.
Manhattan cocktail history

name: Lavorato Secco
garnish: Half orange slice wheel on rim
preparation: POUR first 3 ingredients (all pre-chilled) into chilled glass (no ice) and top with chilled soda water dispensed from a soda gun/siphon.
ingredients:
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 shot	Rabarbaro liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Herboris Amaro Centerbe
2 1⁄2 shot	Soda from siphon
review: Like the original Lavorato Secco served at Milan's Camparino bar, this is bittersweet, herbal, and superbly palate cleansing. The cocktail in the photograph is made using my precious old bottle of Zucca Herboris Amaro Centerbe but as this is near impossible to obtain perhaps substitute with equal parts Centerba Esprit Potabile liqueur and Cynar (a blend not as dry and bitter as Herboris Amaro Centerbe). I double carbonate (WARNING – can be dangerous!) my soda siphon to replicate the effect of the bar's seltzer gun.
history: Adapted from a famous cocktail served at the Camparino Bar in Galleria Vittorio Emanuele, Milan, Italy. The original is made with equal parts Rabarbaro Zucca, Campari, and Zucca Herboris Amaro Centerbe, an ingredient made by Zucca exclusively for Camparino Bar. These first three ingredients are charged with a jet of seltzer water squirted into the glass using a special soda gun. This invigorates the cocktail in a way that soda water simply poured from a bottle doesn't.

name: Luck of the Irish
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
4 drop	Bob's Peppermint Bitters
review: Zippy, refreshing, herbal and cleansing. Best appreciated as an after-dinner digestivo.

name: Queen's Knees
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP up with sparkling wine.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄4 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1 1⁄2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Apple brandy and honey are a natural fit, and they nestle harmoniously with bitter zesty orange and enlivening dry sparkling wine.
history: Adapted from a riff on a Bees Knees created by Stephanie Jordan, self-professed queen bee of Avallen.

name: Funky Banana
garnish: Float dried banana chip or peg to rim
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Cachaça
2⁄3 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
1⁄3 shot	White overproof rum
review: Cachaça and overproof run provide the headline funk to this banana-flavoured spirituous tipple.
history: Created in January 2022 by yours truly at the Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: La Viña
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Amaro Nonino Quintessentia
1 shot	Pale cream sherry (medium/sweet)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Considered by many as a contemporary classic, "The Vineyard" is equal parts rye spicy punch, amaro herbal bittersweetness, and cream sherry richness with a touch of zesty orange oil freshening bitterness. Best appreciated as a digestivo or nightcap.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2009 by Alex Day at Death & Co. in New York City, USA.

name: Old Italian Friend
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bepi Tosolini Grappa di Moscato
2⁄3 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Amaro Santoni
1⁄3 shot	Camomile liqueur
review: Grappa and grapefruit may be the backbone of this bittersweet aperitivo but floral amaro and camomile liqueur provide the top-line flavour.
history: A riff on an Old Friend created in November 2021 by yours truly at the Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Redcoat
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Manzanilla sherry
review: Rich and voluptuous with cognac-laced cherry and vinous complexity.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England, who describes this as "a dashing digestif worthy of the best."

name: Nymph
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Canadian blended whisky
3⁄4 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Just enough apricot to add flavour and richness to a balanced backbone of Canadian whiskey and aromatised wine.
history:
Adapted from a recipe in in William James "Billy" Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Bar Book where this cocktail is credited to "A. F. Lawrence".
Brought to our attention by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford who rebalanced the original equal parts recipe.

name: USS Wondrich
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Amontillado sherry
3⁄4 shot	Pineapple juice
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Chocolate orange liqueur
review: A tiki-inspired riff on the classic Adonis with chocolate orange liqueur. (If a touch too rich for your palate, then split the sherry to equal parts fino and amontillado sherries.)
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Jeff "Beachbum" Berry at his Latitude 29 bar in New Orleans, USA. Named in tribute to David Wondrich, reputedly the first person to request a sherry cocktail at Latitude 29. Incidentally, "USS," meaning "United States Ship," is used as a prefix to the name of a ship to identify it as being a commissioned ship of the United States Navy.

name: Polar Bear
garnish: Float mint leaf or stick to the inside glass rim with a spot of honey
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe
4 drop	Celery bitters
review: Mint notes are subtle in this tequila martini-style spirituous aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2013 for the opening menu of Trick Dog bar in San Francisco, USA where this was originally made with Dolin Blanc vermouth, Tempus Fugit white crème de menthe and a house-made angelica tincture in place of celery bitters. The angelica tincture is made by infusing dried angelica root in high-strength neutral grain alcohol for 48 hours then strained through a coffee filter.

name: Liberal
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄12 shot	Amer Picon
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Spirit-forward and best described as a Manhattan for libertarians, or indeed for anyone of any political persuasion seeking balance.
history: The first known recipe for a Liberal cocktail appears in George Kappeler's 1895 Modern American Drinks. Versions of the Liberal then appear in Thos. Stuart's 1904 Stuart' s Fancy Drinks And How To Mix Them; Jacques Straub's 1913 Straub's Manual of Mixed Drinks; and Albert Stevens Crockett's 1931 Old Waldorf Bar Days.

name: Bourbon Alexander
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
2⁄3 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄2 shot	Coconut liqueur (under 35% alc./vol.)
5⁄6 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: It may be creamy, but this cocktail has a kick. It tastes and looks, much better with a quality white crème de cacao than a dark crème de cacao. A generous splash of sweet, low alcohol strength coconut liqueur surprisingly doesn't overly sweeten and adds nutty depth to the cacao. The nutmeg dusting is critical and much more than a mere garnish.

name: Manhattan Goes Tokyo
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & garnish with skewered candied ginger
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Akashi-Tai Daiginjo Genshu sake
1⁄2 shot	Ginger liqueur
4 drop	Bob's Ginger Bitters
review: A dry and delicately ginger-spiced Manhattan with a touch of Tokyo, courtesy of a slug of Japanese sake.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created by Josh Morton of Barrow's Intense ginger liqueur.
Manhattan cocktail history

name: Gasoline
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Sage gin
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
1⁄6 shot	Kirschwasser (cherry) eau-de-vie
review: Rich blackcurrant fruit balanced by dry vermouth and the flavoursome spirituous notes of gin and kirschwasser. Don't be tempted to stir this cocktail, it's better shaken as aeration and dilution are crucial to its success. Best enjoyed while still foaming.
history: The Gasoline Cocktail first appears in the "Cocktails Round Town" chapter by Arthur Moss in Harry McElhone's 1927 Barflies and Cocktails

name: Pineapple Kingston Negroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1 shot	Pineapple rum
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review: A pineapple rum-influenced riff on Joaquín Simó's Kingston Negroni.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Shelby Allison and Paul McGee at Lost Lake in Chicago, USA.

name: Milady's Martini
garnish: Skewered black olive (at Milady's the olive is purple)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Rosé/rosato vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄12 shot	Amaro Santoni
review: Rosé vermouth contributes almost floral notes to this rosé vermouth and fino sherry-influenced Fifty-Fifty Martini, with a splash of amaro adding a touch of bitter complexity.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2022 by Julie Reiner after she revived Milady's, a vintage Manhattan dive bar that now lives again as a cocktail bar at its original 160 Prince Street at Thompson Street, Soho location. At Milady's you can order this signature cocktail in a "cheeky" mini-size, a three-ounce pour (as above) or as a generous "full-figured" serve.

name: Chef's Kiss
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
review: A riff on a Naked & Famous, this is an impactful kiss, best enjoyed by those who have an infatuation with fernet.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2020 by bartender Jon Pizano at Lazy Bird cocktail bar in The Hoxton Hotel, Chicago, Illnois, USA.

name: Belmont
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Raspberry (framboise) sugar syrup
1⁄6 shot	Framboise/raspberry eau-de-vie
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: A creamy and slightly sweet dessert-style cocktail that's made more serious by the addition of a transformational spoon of raspberry eau-de-vie. (If you choose to use raspberry jam in place of raspberry syrup you'll need two heaped barspoons which should be stirred with the gin prior to adding cream.)
history: Adapted from a recipe in Hugo R. Ensslin's 1917 Recipes for Mixed Drinks (2nd Edition) - it perhaps also features in the 1916 first edition. It's likely this cocktail was created at and is named after the Belmont Hotel which stood at 120 Park Avenue, Manhattan. The hotel opened in 1908, just two years before the nearby Wallick Hotel [see Wallick cocktail] where Ensslin worked from soon after its opening through to the start of Prohibition. It's just a 12-minute walk, through Bryant Square, between the two hotels so it's probable there was a connection between their bartenders.

name: Nico
preparation: STIR first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. TOP with soda water.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄4 shot	Americano bianco
1⁄2 shot	Amaro Braulio
3⁄4 shot	Carbonated/Sparkling/Selzer mineral water
review: Bittersweet, herbal and laced with gin's botanical flavours. Fades with lingering liquorice.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Matty Eggleston at Nico Osteria in Chicago, USA.

name: Bamboo (Difford's 'classic' recipe)
preparation: THROW (or stir) all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄3 shot	Ambrato/ambre/amber vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: I've respected the first-known 1886 recipe which calls for three parts dry sherry to one part vermouth. However, I've split the vermouth between a more full-bodied dry vermouth which better stands up to the sherry, and a bianco vermouth to introduce a touch of sweetness to balance the dry sherry.
history:
Arguably the best-known of all classic sherry cocktails, the Bamboo is also noteworthy due to its lack of base spirit – being simply a mix of sherry and vermouth, sometimes also with dashes of bitters. It's a delicious cocktail but like so many classics there are numerous recipes and conflicting stories as to its origin.

Some say the Bamboo Cocktail was inspired by and named after Bob Cole's 1902 hit song Under the Bamboo Tree but the drink predates the song by more than a decade. It could instead be that the popularity of this cocktail, which by 1900 was commonly featured on cocktail menus and was widely available as a bottled version, inspired the song.

In his 1908 book The World's Drinks And How To Mix Them, William T. "Cocktail Bill" Boothby, a celebrated bartender of the day, credits the drink to Louis Eppinger of the Grand Hotel in Yokohama, Japan. (The hotel was renamed the New Grand in 1913.)

name: Arkwood
preparation: THROW (or stir) all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Gomme syrup
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Aromatic bitters contribute massively to the flavour and hue of this vinous aperitivo. If you like your cocktails bone dry then halve the volume of gomme syrup.
history: The Arkwood Cocktail first appears in the Anonymously written 1895 Bartender's Guide published by The Berner-Mayer Co..

name: Boadas
preparation: THROW all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1 1⁄2 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1⁄6 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄24 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review: I don't know Boadas's recipe for their signature cocktail, and to be honest I'm too polite to ask. And if they told me, I don't think I'd share it as it should remain a cocktail you enjoy at Boadas. Hence, this is very much my interpretation, and given Don Miguel Boadas Parera's Cuban origins it's fitting to use a well-aged Cuban rum (when experimenting I used Havana Club 7). And yes, I tried orange curaçao but found it better with the richness of a cognac-orange liqueur.
history:
Adapted from the signature cocktail, created in 1933 by Don Miguel Boadas Parera for, or soon after, the opening of his bar in Barcelona, Spain.

The original recipe was equal parts Cuban rum (lightly aged - circa 3 year old), Dubonnet Red and orange curaçao. Even with Boadas' theatrical throw, this is not a great cocktail. However, with the 2022 change of ownership of Boadas so this recipe was updated to produce a far more delicious cocktail.

I'm indebted to Boadas for supplying one of their precious original glasses from their collection in which to photograph their signature cocktail.

name: Iz Bananaz
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cachaça
1 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Funky, bittersweet, and very refreshing.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2014 by Robert Krueger at Extra Fancy in Brooklyn, New York City, USA.

name: Harrison Ginsberg's White Negroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Americano bianco
3⁄4 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄6 shot	Verjuice
review: A splash of unripe grape juice helps balance this tasty bittersweet aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2022 by Harrison Ginsberg in New York City, USA.

name: Polka Dot Negroni
garnish: Lemon zest twist (expressed and discarded) & skewered Luxardo maraschino cherry in glass
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
2⁄3 shot	Beefeater Crown Jewel Gin
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
5 drop	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
review: If making with a more standard strength gin then add a splash more but ideally stick to the original recipe (which calls for a third more in volume of each ingredient) and use a 50%+ alcohol by volume gin. The result is a delicious, bite-sized bittersweet aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2016 by Toby Maloney his The Violet Hour bar in Chicago, USA. Tony's original recipe calls for 45ml (1½oz) Salers, 30ml (1oz) Junipero gin, and 30ml (1oz) Dolin Blanc vermouth.

name: Funky Apples
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Monkey Shoulder Fresh Monkey
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Apple/cider eau-de-vie
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: As the creator of this cocktail says, the base spirit shines with "a bangin' mix of high-ester argicole rhum with the clean maltiness of an Irish poitín."
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Barney O'Kane of Little Red Door in Paris.

name: Uncut Gem
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Monkey Shoulder Fresh Monkey
2⁄3 shot	Giffard Crème de Framboise
5⁄6 shot	Pomegranate juice
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Jody's original recipe is stirred but if using freshly pressed pomegranate juice then the cocktail will be cloudy anyway and I prefer this fruity and funky cocktail enlivened by a good shake. I also like it served on-the-rocks.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Jody Buchan, Monkey Shoulder Brand Ambassador, UK North.

name: La Fontaine
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
3⁄4 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Calvados shines in this spirit-forward, Martini-like aperitivo or late-night sipper.
history: Adapted from a recipe "spawn of the Self-Starter and the California Zephyr" created in 2021 by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England.

name: Metexa
preparation: Express the oils of a coin-size grapefruit zest into the base of stirring glass. Add other ingredients, STIR with ice (regal stir) and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 disc	Grapefruit peel/zest
1 1⁄2 shot	Americano bianco
1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	Swedish Punsch liqueur
review: Bitter grapefruit oils replace the quinine bitterness in the original 1930s version of this refreshing aromatised wine and tequila aperitivo.
history: Adapted from Jamie Boudreau's riff on the classic Metexa which first appeared in William James "Billy" Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Bar Book

name: Better Half
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Amontillado sherry
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Chardonnay (Chablis) white wine
1⁄6 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
review: Sherry-based and sherry-led, with vodka, wine and orange liqueur subtly and harmoniously contributing.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Juyoung Kang, head bartender at The Dorsey cocktail bar in the Venetian, Las Vegas, USA.

name: Longines
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Spanish brandy
1⁄2 shot	Aniseed (anise) liqueur
1 shot	Cold black tea
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: The combination of Spanish brandy, strong aniseed liqueur (at least 40% alc./vol.) and black tea give this cocktail a pleasing liquorice flavour with mouth numbing freshness. Traditionally a dulce (sweet) Spanish aniseed liqueur would be used without the added sugar. If using a dry (secco) aniseed liqueur then I'd suggest adding a generous bar spoon of sugar.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in the 1930s-40s by the famous bartender, Constante Ribalaigua Vert at his Floridita bar in Havana, Cuba. The Longines shows his Spanish origins (he was born outside of Barcelona in 1888) with its use of Spanish brandy and (originally) Anis del Mono, a Spanish aniseed liqueur available in two styles, Dulce (sweet) and Secco (dry). The Dulce is by far the most popular style and almost certainly the one used by Constante.

name: Billy Sunday (AKA Amaro Daiquiri)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Amaro Braulio
1 shot	Rabarbaro liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Gomme syrup
review: Big and bittersweet, this cocktail explodes with flavour herbal and citrus flavours. Perhaps more a digestivo than an aperitivo.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Stephanie Andrews for Billy Sunday in Chicago, Illinois, USA. Stephanie's original recipe specifies Sfumato Rabarbaro.

Named for the bar where this cocktail was created, which in turn is named after William Ashley 'Billy' Sunday (1862-1935), a popular outfielder in baseball's National League during the 1880s. Billy Sunday went on to become America's most influential evangelist in the early 20th century, and his sermons influenced the adoption of the Eighteenth Amendment in 1919, leading to Prohibition.

name: Velvet Raspberry Daisy
garnish: Float fresh raspberry in centre of cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. (There's no need to dry shake to achieve desired foam.)
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Adriatico Bianco almond milk liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Framboise/raspberry eau-de-vie
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Crème de Framboise
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Raspberry eau-de-vie and liqueur rounded with almond milk liqueur and balanced with a splash of lime.
history: Created in December 2023 by yours truly at The Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: Christmas Special No. 2
garnish: Orange zest twist expressed and discarded. Adorn with something festive such as a redcurrant sprig
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
1⁄2 shot	Savoia Orancio
1⁄3 shot	Mandarine Napoleon liqueur
review: A "Special" after-dinner cocktail at any time of year but particularly appropriate over the festive period due to its ingredients, particularly Pedro Ximénez sherry, which tastes like Christmas pudding.
history: Created by in December 2023 by yours truly at The Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Old Roma
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Lucano amaro
1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
2 dash	Black walnut bitters
review: A bittersweet, delicately chocolatey Old Fashioned with liquorice-led herbal complexity.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Barlow Gilmore, AKA The Weekend Mixologist.

name: Cantilever
garnish: Lemon zest twist expressed and then pegged to rim
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Lucano amaro
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Byrrh Grand Quinquina
review: Rye whiskey underwrites this delicious digestivo/late-night sipper with waves of delicately bittersweet herbal favours.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Craig Eliason, a Professor of Art History at the University of St. Thomas in Saint Paul, Minnesota, and a keen cocktail aficionado. Craig created this cocktail for the Society of Architectural Historians' 80th Anniversary Celebration. Fittingly, Craig used Amaro Lucano Anniversario edition.

name: Agroni
garnish: Orange zest twist expressed and discarded. Adorn with piece of 70% dark chocolate.
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Rhum J.M. Terroir Volcanique
1⁄2 shot	Rhum Clément Créole Shrubb liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review: An agricole rum-forward riff on a classic Negroni.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Adam Gonna at The Beachcomber (House of Agricole) bar in London, England.

name: Creole Cocktail No. 2
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Bigallet China China Amer
1⁄4 shot	Averna Amaro
review: A whiskey-laced, spirit-forward herbal digestivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Ben Hatch at Elysian Bar in New Orleans, USA.

name: Old Dog, New Tricks
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
1 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A vibrant menthol-like citrus freshness balances heavy, bittersweet herbal and rooty notes. The whopping slug of banana liqueur is surprisingly integrated and is what makes this aperitivo/digestivo special.
history: Adapted from a recipe created at Blythe & Burrows in Portland, Maine, USA.

name: Tuscano
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Amaro Santoni
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Delicately herbal, effervescent and refreshing.
history: This riff on the Americano was suggested in March 2024 by Yorey C, a fellow Discerning Drinker on ourAmericano page. (I've reduced the rosso vermouth to add a balancing splash of dry vermouth.)

name: Charming Man
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1 shot	Pale cream sherry (medium/sweet)
1 shot	Rabarbaro liqueur
2 dash	Xocolatl mole bitters
review: A delicious riff on a Mezcal Negroni created by a particularly charming, talented and fabulous host. Depending on your mood/occasion, you may instead prefer to serve this cocktail over a large cube or chunk of ice in an old-fashioned glass.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2017 by Joaquín Simó at Pouring Ribbons in New York City, USA.

name: Old Pal No. 2
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into an ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Mancino Vermouth di Torino Chinato
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review: On the dry bitter side of bittersweet, it may take three sips before your palette appreciates this Negroni-style aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2016 by Erik Carlson at Bastille Cafe & Bar in Seattle, Portland, USA.

name: Montana (Harry Johnson, 1900)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Anisette liqueur
3 dash	Boker's bitters
review: Sloe gin shines in this cocktail, lifted by subtle aniseed and liquorice notes from a touch of anisette.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Johnson's 1900 Bartender's Manual

name: Old Tom Gin Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
1⁄12 shot	Gomme syrup
1⁄24 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
2 dash	Boker's bitters
review: A delightfully rustic and characterful pre-Martini, Martini.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Jerry Thomas' 1887 Bar-Tender's Guide.

name: Drifter
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Japanese blended whisky
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Amaro Nonino Quintessentia
3 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Whisky-forward with supporting herbal richness.

name: Going Nowhere (but making good time)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
1 shot	Mancino Vermouth di Torino Chinato
1 1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Relatively low in alcohol and delicately bittersweet, this cocktail is suited to repeat orders during an extended aperitivo hour. Gin adds additional botanical fortification to chinato and vermouth.
history: Created in July 2024 for a vermouth seminar at Tales of The Cocktail. Created in Rye, England, to be served in New Orleans, USA, as an example of a vermouth-led aperitivo.

name: Rose (by Johnny Milta)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 shot	Kirschwasser (cherry) eau-de-vie
1⁄6 shot	Groseille (redcurrant) syrup
review: Salmon-pink and wonderfully aromatic with dry vermouth and kirsch with a blast pf fruity redcurrant syrup.
history:
Harry McElhone's 1922 Harry's ABC of mixing cocktails credits this cocktail to "Johny, Chatham Hotel Bar, Paris, 1919" and is referring to a bartender called Johnny Milta.

This recipe is adapted from David A. Embury's 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks.

name: Rose No.3
garnish: Redcurrants, edible rose petal or Luxardo maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Kirschwasser (cherry) eau-de-vie
1⁄3 shot	Groseille (redcurrant) syrup
review: Delicate, aromatic berry and orchard fruit - not too sweet.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Sodden Grape
preparation: MUDDLE grapes in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
7 fresh	Green grapes (seedless)
2 shot	Bison grass vodka
3⁄4 shot	Canadian icewine
review: A 'sod' is a piece of turf. Here 'sodden' refers to the Bison grass, the flavour of which combines well with the grapes and icewine.
history: Created in 2004 by yours truly, London, England.

name: Bamboo (Savoy's 1930 recipe)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: The simplest, one of the best and dryest renditions of the Bamboo cocktail. It may be simple but the combination of vermouth and fino makes for a fabulously complex cocktail.
history: Adapted from Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Fernando
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄6 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Galliano L'Autentico liqueur
review: An unusual, vermouth-based herbal cocktail - very fresh and aromatic.
history:
I came across this cocktail in 2010 at Employees Only in New York City, its birthplace. The recipe I took away from that night called for 30ml (1oz) dry vermouth, 30ml (1oz) rosso/sweet vermouth, 7.5 Galliano, and a mere 5ml (1/6oz) fernet, but I noted: "Originally based only on bianco vermouth with no dry vermouth." I blame their hospitality as it appears their actual recipe for a Fernando is more in keeping with the proportions above.

For all those who liked my previous incarnation, the recipe is 30ml (1oz) dry vermouth, 30ml (1oz) sweet/rosso vermouth, 7.5ml (¼oz) Galliano, and 5ml (1/6oz) fernet.

name: Mr Kappes
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Kirschwasser (cherry) eau-de-vie
1⁄2 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
5⁄12 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
review: Kirschwasser, aromatised wine and sherry sit together harmoniously. I amended, to reduce the volume of serve and make a tad drier in January 2022. The previous recipe, served in a coupe: 60ml kirschwasser, 30ml aromatised wine, and 30ml PX sherry.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2009 by Diana Haider in Frankfurt, Germany.

name: Buttercup
garnish: The original recipe calls for a lemon zest twist but the lemon oils overpower the butterscotch. So if you use a slither of lemon skin on which to nestle a Werther's Original, don't express the lemon's oils over the drink. WARNING: Don't be tempted to use buttercup flowers as they are poisonous. They are also poisonous when eaten by livestock but their acrid taste and the blistering of the mouth they cause mean that animals don't tend to eat them. Interestingly, the toxins degrade when dried, so hay containing dried buttercups is safe for animals to eat.
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Caramel Toffee liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: When made to Lucas Bols original specification: 1 shot Bols Genever, 1 shot Bols Butterscotch liqueur and ¾ shot sweet vermouth, this drink has a great flavour but lacks balls (or perhaps I should say Bols). Hence, the above formula is heavy on the genever with equal parts butterscotch liqueur and sweet vermouth. It's even better with an oude genever rather than a jonge as this amplifies the butterscotch notes.
history: My adaptation of a recipe I discovered in January 2014 at The House of Bols in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

name: Greek Celery Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Kleos Mastiha liqueur
1 shot	Rutte Celery Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Celery juice (freshly extracted)
review: Celery and mastiha pair well, while gin adds a spirituous bite and botanical complexity. A small grind of pepper to finish adds a nuance of spice.
history: A simplified version of a drink promoted by Skinos mastiha by yours truly in August 2015 at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Waterloo
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & float pickled almond
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
1⁄2 shot	Mandarine Napoleon liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Jägermeisteror other German amaro
review: A dry, lightly bitter, aperitif cocktail highlighting the bready notes in genever and the bright zesty freshness of mandarin liqueur.
history:
Created by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

Named after the Battle of Waterloo, which was fought on Sunday 18th June 1815 near the town of Waterloo in present-day Belgium, then part of the Netherlands. The French army commanded by Napoleon Bonaparte was defeated by an Anglo-Allied army commanded by the Duke of Wellington fittingly alongside a Prussian army commanded by Gebhard Leberecht von Blücher, Prince of Wahlstatt. Napoleon's defeat at Waterloo brought his reign as French Emperor to a sudden end.

name: Sleepy Smoker
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into a chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Oak Smoked Vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Manzanilla sherry
1⁄3 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
review: Smoked vodka delicately fortifies dry faintly salty manzanilla sherry with curaçao adding a touch of sweetness and zesty orange freshness.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2016 by Amelia Castro at Polite Provisions, San Diego, CA, USA.

name: She's Like
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Kleos Mastiha liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
3 dash	Celery bitters
review: An unlikely combination of big rich flavours, but when served ice-cold this is either a very interesting Mediterranean aperitivo or a palate cleansing digestivo.
history: Created in 2016 by Ilias Marinakis at 42 Bar, Athens, Greece.

name: Paisley Spritz
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and lightly stir.
ingredients:
2 shot	Chardonnay (Chablis) white wine
1 shot	Drambuie liqueur
Top up with	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
review: The sweet honeyed spice notes of Scottish liqueur combine harmoniously with the gentle acidity of the wine, lengthened and freshened with ginger ale.
history:
Created in October 2013 by Simon Difford at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

Our Spritz page contains information on the history of, and other recipes for, the Spritz family of cocktails.

name: Negrino
garnish: Pink grapefruit wedge/zest twist & scorched rosemary sprig
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and STIR.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
1 shot	Fino sherry
2⁄3 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
review: A riff on the classic Negroni from Vietnam, which brilliantly set the richness of sloe gin against bone dry fino sherry while harnessing the herbal bitterness of gentian. Hit the right dilution, and by the third sip, when your palate has adjusted, you'll not be able to stop sipping this bitter aperitif cocktail.
history: Created in 2017 by Trinh Quan Huy-Philip, a "Travelling Mixologist in Vietnam.

name: Wild & Dirty Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Birch spirit/birch eau-de-vie
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 dash	Lemon bitters
review: Pine (birch) notes mix well with the vermouth in this 2:1 Martini with lemon bitters adding citrus freshness the olive and rosemary sprig garnish adding to the cocktail's aroma and complexity.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2017 by Dean Railton at Vice & Virtue, Leeds, England. Deans original recipe called for 50ml Freya Birch Spirit, 25ml Noilly Prat vermouth and 1 dash lemon bitters.

name: Super Seedy
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1⁄3 shot	Raspberry (framboise) sugar syrup
1⁄12 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
review: Raspberry fruit richness is balanced by bitter botanical complexity in this Irish whiskey-based alternative to an Old-Fashioned.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Jameson Ambassador, Ronan Collins. Ronan’s original recipe specifies Jameson Caskmates Stout Edition.

name: White Grasshopper
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Acqua Bianca liqueur
1 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: Creamy and indulgent but not sickly sweet, with delicate chocolate, rose, mint and zesty orange.
history: Created in 2020 by Salvatore Calabrese at the Donovan Bar in London, England.

name: Pedaling Diplomat
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) & chilled olive (inside glass)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 5⁄6 shot	Ambrato/ambre/amber vermouth
1 1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Muyu Jasmine Verte liqueur
review: Two different dry vermouths and a jasmine liqueur combine to produce an aromatic aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe by Iván Villegas, created after being inspired by Martini Ciclismo 2020 La Classica. Iván says, "As we crossed the villages and cruised the small roads, I was sometimes struck by aromas of pines, flowers and fig trees that triggered my fond memories of long-missed Mediterranean family holidays; so I let this bond with my love for vermouth and then thought of the "Diplomat" classic cocktail since diplomats are always around people from many countries as we were during La Classica."

name: Olimpo
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄6 shot	Italicus liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 dash	Rhubarb bitters
review: A summery light aperitivo.
history: Created in 2020 by Giacomo Giannnotti from Paradiso, Barcelona, Spain.

name: Orchard Keeper
garnish: Float thin apple slice (fresh or dehydrated)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: Apple brandy delicately sweetened and flavoured with honey and aromatised by vermouth.

name: White Grape
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	O/Purist Tsipouro
1 shot	Americano bianco
1 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
review: A bittersweet aperitivo which harnesses tsipouro's and Americano's vinious notes with gentian's bitter herbal flavours.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created by Aggelos Demagos at Unique bar & lounge in Poros Attica, Greece, this was one of ten winning recipes in the 2021 O/Purist Quest.

Aggelos says, "the Canvas for my drink was the encouragement of my company to create a cocktail with O/Purist Tsipouro, combining some of the ingredients I had at home at that time. So, I created White Grape, a tsipouro-based Negroni Bianco."

name: Añogo
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Patrón Añejo tequila
1⁄2 shot	Amontillado sherry
1 2⁄3 shot	Warninks Advocaat liqueur
review: Creamy but not sweet with tequila character shining through. (Añogo is Spanish for 'yearn'.)
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by H. Joseph Ehrmann at Elixir in San Francisco USA. His original recipe doesn't use advocaat at all, instead is made with an eggnog base, made by combining beaten egg yolks with sugar, milk, cream and nutmeg. H. makes this and then lets the mixture age for three months before using it in his Añogo. It's a faff to make the eggnog base so I use advocaat instead. Sorry H.

name: Doubloon
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Pale cream sherry (medium/sweet)
3⁄4 shot	Jamaican-style overproof aged pot still rum
3⁄4 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
review: Rich Spanish cream sherry, pungent Jamaican rum and Italian bittersweet amaro are unlikely bedfellows but combine harmoniously in this late-night sipper.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England.

name: Big Mac
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Speyburn 10yo Speyside single malt
1 shot	Ginger wine
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
history: A volumized riff on a Whisky Mac created in June 2021 by yours truly.

name: Señor Santoni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cachaça
3⁄4 shot	Amaro Santoni
3⁄4 shot	Amontillado sherry
review: This combination of bittersweet liqueur, cachaça and sherry is polarising. I like it! I created it; but I can see that many, perhaps the majority, will hate it. Bet they don't like Marmite either. Poor souls!
history: Created in November 2021 by yours truly at the Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: White Negroni Sbagliato
garnish: Cucumber slice and orange zest twist
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
4 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
review: The lovechild of the White Negroni and Negroni Sbagliato, this bittersweet aperitivo dominated by gentian liqueur so the first couple of sips may be challenging but once past these it's difficult to stop.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2018 by Toby Cecchini and David Moo of The Long Island Bar in Brooklyn, New York City, USA. Not originally made to be served at their bar, but for a Cocktails & Conversations talk with architects Marion Weiss and Michael Manfredi at the American Institute of Architects. It has since become one of the signature cocktails at The Long Island Bar.

name: Hickory
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ambrato/ambre/amber vermouth
1 1⁄2 shot	Rubino vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Amer Picon
review: This aperitivo/digestivo may be low in alcohol but, when made with quality vermouths, it doesn't lack flavour.
history: Adapted from a recipe published in the 1911 book, Beverages de Luxe.

name: Lifetime Ban
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's Navy Strength Royal Dock Gin
1 shot	Fino sherry
1 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
review: A Navy strength gin-charged Bamboo with nutty and toffee notes.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2017 by Dan Greenbaum at The Beagle in New York City, USA.

name: Nutty Tom
garnish: Dried coconut (preferably toasted) slices pegged to rim
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
1 shot	Lucano amaro
1 1⁄3 shot	Coconut water
review: Junpier, liquorice and gin's botanical complexity with bittersweet herbal alpine notes and coconut roundness.
history: Created in March 2024 by yours truly at the Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: Tiki Max
preparation: SHAKE first nine ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. FLOAT overproof rum on drink.
ingredients:
1 shot	Navy rum (54.5% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
6 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄2 shot	Woods rum
review: This drink breaks the golden rule - simple is beautiful. However, it's tasty and packs a punch.
history:
Created in 2008 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

The inspiration for this drink came not from the similarly named discount clothing retailer but the venerable Tiki cocktail itself. Tiki drinks, otherwise known as 'exotics' originated in 1934 when Ernest Raymond Beaumont Gantt, a Louisiana native who had made some money bootlegging rum during Prohibition, opened a bar called Don's Beachcomber in Hollywood and began serving rum based, fruity cocktails. Soon after, Victor 'Trader Vic' Bergeron transformed his restaurant Hinky Dinks into a similar faux Polynesian style. These founding fathers spawned many Tiki imitators and despite a dip in popularity from the 1970s, happily the noughties saw a revival in the fortunes of Tiki.

name: Zombie
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with 6oz scoop of crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
5⁄6 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
2⁄3 shot	Jamaican-style overproof aged pot still rum
1⁄2 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1 shot	Pineapple juice
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
4 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Powerful funky rum and delicate cinnamon spice partially tamed by rich fruit and sweetened clove.
history: Created by Don Beach in 1934 at Don the Beachcomber's in Hollywood, USA. This recipe is adapted from one published in Jeff Berry's Sippin' Safari which Jeff sourced from the 1937 notebook of Beachcomber's waiter Dick Santiago.

name: Surf & Turf
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Manzanilla sherry
1⁄4 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄24 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Dry sherry adds a slight salty 'surf' note to this riff on the classic Turf Club Cocktail.
history:
Created 8th September 2014 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England. I've tweaked the recipe in recent years, the original:
1½ Old Tom gin
¾ Dry vermouth
½ Fino sherry
¼ Orange curacao
1 dash Aromatic bitters
½ chilled water

name: Sangrita
preparation: SHAKE ingredients with ice and strain into shot glass. Serve with a shot of tequila. The drinker can either down the tequila and chase it with sangrita or sip the two drinks alternately.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Tomato juice
1⁄2 shot	Pomegranate juice
1⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
2 drop	Hot pepper sauce (red)
2 dash	Worcestershire sauce
1 pinch	Salt (sea salt)
1 grind	Black pepper
review: In Mexico the quality of the homemade Sangrita can make or break a bar. This recipe is spicy and slightly sweet and perfect for chasing tequila.
history: The name means 'little blood' in Spanish and the drink is served with tequila in every bar in Mexico.

name: Jet Pilot
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with 8oz scoop of crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 shot	Jamaican-style overproof aged pot still rum
3⁄4 shot	Overproof aged rum (not Jamaican style)
3⁄4 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Cinnamon syrup
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A lightly spicy blend of three characterful rums with citrus mellowed by blending with crushed ice.
history: Created circa 1958 by socialite, Steven Crane at his Polynesian-themed Luau Restaurant in Hollywood, USA. The Jet Piolet is a riff of Donn Beach's 1941 The Test Pilot cocktail. The two recipes are very similar but the Jet Pilot benefits from the addition of grapefruit juice and cinnamon syrup.

name: Take a Hike
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
6 fresh	Sage leaves
1 1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄2 shot	Strega liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
4 drop	Hot pepper sauce (red)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Herbal, savoury, spicy and citrusy – this Margarita-like cocktail has something for everyone.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Ramsey Musk, Beverage Director at Accomplice Bar in Los Angeles, USA.

name: Sangaree (Sangria)
garnish: Slices of strawberry, orange and lemon with mint sprig bouquet
preparation: STIR first 6 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with a splash of soda.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Spanish brandy
1⁄2 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
3 shot	Rioja (Crianza) red wine
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄12 shot	Cinnamon syrup
3⁄4 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Summer in a glass. Heavy wine tannins are sweetened, lightened and infused with fruit.
history: This version of the Spanish Sangria was popular in 19th century America. The only real difference is that while a Sangria is usually made in batches, Sangaree are single serve.

name: Reversed Vesper & Tonic 'Martini'
preparation: SHAKE first 7 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with a splash tonic water.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Blanc quinquina/kina (e.g. Mattei Cap Corse or Kina L'Aéro d'Or)
1⁄2 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄6 shot	Becherovka liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: Bittersweet and Martini in style but with the hard edges smoothed and a hint of eastern spice added. Perhaps more a digestivo than an aperitivo.
history:
Created in 2008 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

James Bond named his favourite style of Martini (Vesper) after the beautiful Russian agent Vesper Lynd. This version is 'Reversed' due to the dramatically increased ratio of aromatised wines. Fittingly, my cocktail mixes East and West European ingredients with the introduction of Becherovka. And where there is Becherovka, there should be tonic water (see Be-ton).

I originally made this with 5ml of homemade pomegranate syrup to add much-needed sweetness (to counter kina bitterness) as a fitting blood-like syrup. Swapping to commercial grenadine added too much colour and flavour; hence, now equal parts sugar and grenadine syrup.

name: Bloody Mary (no added sugar & low-calorie)
garnish: Spiked cocktail onion, cherry tomato and lemon wedge with celery stick stirrer (optional salt & pepper rim)
preparation: ROLL (rotate) all ingredients with ice in shaker (rather than shake) and strain into ice-filled glass. Use ice freshly from freezer to fill glass (not ice directly from ice-machine) to avoid unwanted dilution from melting ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3 1⁄2 shot	Tomato juice
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar-free sweetener
2 pinch	Celery salt
3 grind	Black pepper
10 drop	Hot pepper sauce (red)
4 dash	Worcestershire sauce (optional)
review:
With vitamin loaded tomato and lemon juices, this sugar-free, low-calorie Mary is almost a healthy option.

Be sure to use a tomato juice with no added sugar and be aware that adding Worcestershire sauce will also contribute a very small amount of sugar.
history:
Adapted from the classic serve by yours truly (Simon Difford) in January 2019.

Also see Bloody Mary cocktails - how to make, origins and history

name: Jack Pot
garnish: Strawberry with mint sprig crown on rim
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Drambuie liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄4 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄4 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1⁄4 shot	Single malt Welsh whisky
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	British bitter ale
1⁄4 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review:
