Creating this cocktail started with a desire to make a properly British cocktail to toast those special occasions when a fellow Brit wins a sporting event. Fittingly different whiskies in the drink represent England, Ireland, Scotland and Wales. London dry gin, British ale and Drambuie are all obviously British, and with names such as Cox, Granny Smith and Kingston Black, apples are intrinsically a Great British fruit, as indeed is the strawberry (think of Wimbledon), so the obvious garnish.

Handily, Drambuie contains Scotch whisky so naturally mixes well with the other whiskies, and apple juice is a favourite fruit among bartenders to use in whiskey cocktails.

The name is inspired by the Union Jack and also what I thought when I'd successfully combined all the above into one tasty cocktail.
history: Created in August 2013 by Simon Difford at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Celery Gimlet No.2
preparation: MUDDLE celery with salt in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
6 inch	Celery stick (fresh) (chopped)
1 pinch	Celery salt
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄6 shot	White wine vinegar (Chardonnay)
2 dash	Celery bitters
review: Sweet 'n' sour, salt 'n' vinegar served with dry celery gin crunch – a cocktail to awaken your senses.
history: A riff on the classic Gimlet, this recipe is adapted from Naren Young's Celery Gimlet and inspired by salt and vinegar flavours.

name: Atracción Ahumado Margarita
garnish: Lime juice, smoked salt & Tajin seasoning rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
2⁄3 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Piment d'Espelette chile liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Agave syrup
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
4 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A Margarita with a touch of smoky character and plenty of warming oomph. It crossed my mind that whatever "oomph" is in Spanish would be a fitting name for this Margarita, so I hit Google Translate and amusingly it came back with "atracción sexual". Hence, instead of a mere "Smoky Chili Margarita", this became the Atracción Ahumado (Smoky Attraction).
history: Created in October 2021 by yours truly and inspired by Stelios Papadopoulos' Smoky Tommy's Margarita.

name: Undead Gentleman
preparation: POUR absinthe into chilled glass and roll to coat the inside. SHAKE other ingredients with ice and fine strain into absinthe-rinsed glass.
ingredients:
1⁄24 shot	La Fée Absinthe Blanche
1 1⁄2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1 shot	Jamaican-style overproof aged pot still rum
1⁄2 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Cinnamon syrup
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: This riff on Donn Beach's classic Zombie has a tad more gentlemanly refinement in its serve but doesn't hold back in flavour.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Martin Cate at his Smuggler's Cove in San Francisco, USA.

name: Wake Me Up Before You Go-Go
garnish: Dust with chocolate-orange Java salt over 1/3 of cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
1⁄2 shot	Galliano Espresso Coffee liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Oloroso sherry
1⁄4 shot	Lemon oleo saccharum
3 dash	Xocolatl mole bitters
3 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
5 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
history: Created in August 2023 by Nicole Salicetti in New York City, USA, this was the winning cocktail of the Galliano Espresso Martini Competition.

name: The Jackal
garnish: Flamed orange zest twist expressed & discarded
preparation: STIR first 6 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. POUR crème de cassis into centre of cocktail (it should sink to form a red base).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Tennessee whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Mexican corn whisky
1⁄6 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄6 shot	Popcorn sugar syrup
1⁄12 shot	Giffard Piment d'Espelette chile liqueur
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
1⁄4 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
1⁄12 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
review: An expressive riff on an Old Fashioned with a hit of spiced popcorn, served straight-up.
history: Created in November 2023 by yours truly and inspired by The Jackal from Ronny Jordan's 1993 album The Quiet Revolution and the 1973 thriller movie The Day of The Jackal based on the 1971 Frederick Forsyth novel of the same name.

name: Bahama Mama
garnish: Pineapple wedge, Luxardo Maraschino cherry & mint sprigs bouquet
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Jamaican aged blended rum with funk
1⁄4 shot	Jamaican-style overproof aged pot still rum
1⁄4 shot	Coconut rum liqueur (35-40% alc./vol.)
1⁄4 shot	Coconut liqueur (under 35% alc./vol.)
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3 shot	Pineapple juice
review: The holy trinity of rum, coconut and pineapple served in a well-balanced, not overly sweet Tiki-style cocktail.
history:
The bartender most associated with this cocktail is Oswald "Slade" Greenslade, who was born in the Bahamas and worked at the Pink Elephant nightclub. This is where he claims to have created this cocktail in 1963 for three women at his bar who wanted something fruity they'd never had before.

Some question Slade's claims, saying the cocktail appeared on menus in the 1940s-50s, although I've not yet seen evidence of such a menu. However, in September 2024, Slade sent us his original recipe and the story of his Bahama Mama.

Oswald Greenslade's Bahama Mama recipe
1¼ oz Dark Bacardi
1¼ oz Coconut Rum
1 oz Grendene
2 oz Pineapple juice
2 oz Orange juice
4 oz Cracked ice
Shake well and pour into a 12 oz cocktail glass.
Garnish with pineapple, orange slice and cherry.

name: Perfect Blood & Sand
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & skewered Luxardo Maraschino Cherries
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Kirschwasser (cherry) eau-de-vie
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: I'm usually a maximum of five ingredients in a cocktail kind-a-guy, but this Blood & Sand riff with seven ingredients is balanced and tasty. If I were in Asia, where the number eight is lucky, then I'd have also used equal parts orange juice and blood orange juice to keep the number of ingredients lucky.
history: A riff on the classic Blood & Sand cocktail created in August 2014 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room in London, England.

name: Thyme for…
preparation: DASH bitters over sugar cube in stirring glass and MUDDLE cube to crush. ADD other ingredients and stir to dissolve sugar. Add ice and STIR. Fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 cube	Demerara / dark Muscovado / brown sugar
3 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 sprig	Fresh thyme
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
review: It most certainly is! As the name suggests, aromatic thyme subtly influences this spirituous cognac-based cocktail, with Grand Marnier adding rich but delicate zesty orange notes.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Tom Noori at Montpellier Wine Bar, Cheltenham, England

name: Eight Foot Fizz
garnish: Mint sprigs, dried citrus fruit wheels, cinnamon stick and red amaranth leaves, dusted with icing sugar. Place at least 5 pretzels over straw.
preparation:
SHAKE first 6 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda water poured from a height to create a frothy head. Serve with straws.

Special ingredient #1 = Lemon sherbet
Blend the following for a couple minutes and fine strain
600g Caster sugar
600g Super strained lemon juice
20g Lemon zest (removed from fruit with Microplane grater)
5g Maldon sea salt

Special ingredient #2 = Rose water & kiwi syrup
Blend the following and bottle
5g malic acid
100ml Catron kiwi liqueur
100ml Merlet pear liqueur
100ml Money musk coconut
25ml Absinthe
5g Maldon sea salt
100ml Orgeat syrup
50ml Campari
200ml Sugar syrup (1:1)
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
2 shot	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
1 shot	*Special ingredient #2 (see above)
1 shot	Kiwi fruit puree
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
history: Created in 2016 by Andy Mil at The Cocktail Trading Co., London, England.

name: The Ridgwell
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Bourbon whiskey
2⁄3 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
5⁄12 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
5⁄12 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Crème de Mûre liqueur
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Delicately spicy and Manhattan-like in style.
history:
Created in November 2018 at FAM Bar, London, England in memory of Mark Ridgwell, author of Spirits Distilled, respected educator and creator of the Taste & Flavour network of speakers and spirit enthusiasts.

The original recipe is based on Makers Mark (which Mark enthusiastically promoted during his career): 20ml Rittenhouse rye, 25ml FAM blend vermouth (equal parts Carpano Classico, Punt e Mes & Martini rosso) and 5ml Braemble gin liqueur.

name: The Conference
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄6 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 dash	Xocolatl mole bitters
review: As with any good conference, all the participants in this cocktail are heard and their contribution is equally valued. Due to its layering of different spirits to build complexity, some consider this a Tiki-style cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Brian Miller at Death & Company in New York City, USA.

name: Anonymous (But Assertive) Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Horse with No Name habanero bourbon
2⁄3 shot	Mexican corn whisky
1⁄3 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	Giffard Piment d'Espelette chile liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Lemon drizzled grilled sweetcorn with delicate chili spice and citric acidity. Sounds sophisticated but is easy drinking.
history: A riff on Tayēr + Elementary's September 2021 Horse With No Name bottled cocktail by yours truly.

name: Red Thorn
preparation: MUDDLE raspberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5 fresh	Raspberries
1 1⁄2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
5⁄12 shot	Raspberry (framboise) sugar syrup
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄24 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: A raspberry charged variation on the Blackthorn with faint Chartreuse herbal notes.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by bartender Takumi Watanabe. Takumi's original recipe doesn't use fresh raspberries, instead, he uses 15ml homemade raspberry syrup (made with 200ml fresh raspberry juice and 150ml sugar).

name: Grasshopper No. 2
garnish: Dust with grated chocolate and add a mint sprigs bouquet. Serve with a straw.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe
3⁄4 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄4 shot	Brancamenta
1⁄6 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 1⁄4 shot	Double cream / heavy cream
1 pea	Green food colour gel
review: A mezcal and amaro-influenced riff on the classic Grasshopper.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Naren Young at Sweet Liberty in Miami, USA.

name: Fray Wray
garnish: Mint sprigs bouquet & speared dehydrated banana chips
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients (inc. lime wedge) with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 3-5 years
3⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Rhum Clément Blanc
1⁄4 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
1 wedge	Lime (fresh)
review: Banana notes are subtle in this rum and cognac-laced sipper.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Matthew Belanger, when Head Bartender at Donna bar in Brooklyn, New York City, USA.

name: Jersey Quarter
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
2⁄3 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Ginger liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Rye whiskey and apple brandy combine harmoniously to form the backbone of this ginger-spiced, Manhattan alternative.

name: Bill Chandler
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄3 shot	Jamaican aged blended rum with funk
1⁄3 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Rum character shines in this punchy and fruity Daiquiri variation.
history: Adapted from a recipe in G. F. Steele's 1934 My New Cocktail Book. Despite his warning, in pursuit of deliciousness, I've strayed a little away from the exact percentages and even ingredients stipulated Steele's recipe.

name: Daiquiricus
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Italicus liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Rhum Clément Blanc
3⁄4 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
6 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Your choice and alcohol strength of rhum and rum and will dramatically affect this finally balanced and delicious cocktail, along with Martinique rhum it seems fitting to use a lightly aged Cuban rum, if you have access to one.
history: Adapted from the Italicus Daiquiri created by Julio Cabrera at his Cafe La Trova in Miami, USA. Julio's son, Andy Cabrera, made his father's delicious Daiquiri for me after the Art of Italius Aperitivo Challenge in May 2024 with Rome's famous Colosseum as a backdrop.

name: Kris Kringle
garnish: Grapefruit zest twist (expressed & discarded). Adorn with a mini gingerbread man &/or skewered crystallised ginger.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄2 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Gingerbread sugar syrup
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
4 drop	Bob's Vanilla bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Delicately ginger spiced with biscuity creaminess stroking lightly smoky mezcal [your choice of mezcal dependant] with a subtle herbal vanilla.
history: Created by yours truly and named after the Christmasy named Kris Kringle horse who raced in the colours of owner Robert Sangster in the late 1980s and won the Derrinstown Derby Trial for Vincent O'Brien and jockey John Reid.

name: Imperial Bulldog
garnish: Bottle of emptied Underberg upturned into cocktail, raspberry. Mint sprigs bouquet, dehydrated pineapple wedge and lime slice wheel. Serve with a straw.
preparation: MUDDLE raspberries in base of chilled glass and fill glass with crushed ice. SHAKE other ingredients with ice and strain into pre-preprepared glass. Cap with more crushed ice.
ingredients:
6 fresh	Raspberries
2⁄3 shot	Underberg/ Brasilberg
3⁄4 shot	Akvavit / Aquavit
3⁄4 shot	Cachaça
3⁄4 shot	Pineapple juice
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: This cocktail looks better if made to spec with the raspberries in the base of the glass but is fruitier, and arguably better, if you muddle the raspberries in the base of the shaker prior to shaking.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2017 by Jane Danger and Austin Hennelly at Mother of Pearl, a contemporary tiki bar in New York City's East Village which permanently closed in 2020. This cocktail was kindly brought to our attention by David Selle.

name: American Beauty (by David Embury)
garnish: Float mint leaf or red rose petal
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with CRUSHED ICE and fine strain into chilled glass. FLOAT red wine on surface of cocktail.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄6 shot	Claret red wine
review: Both fresh and refreshing. A subtle hint of peppermint gives zing to this cognac-based cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe in David A. Embury's 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks.

name: Dulchin
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Lime cordial (sweetened lime juice)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: This dry, amber coloured, fruity cocktail carries a pisco punch.
history: Drinks historian Dave Wondrich says that this cocktail was created for and named after the wealthy heir of a New York hardware company "who couldn't drink grain spirits and was bored with rum", hence the bartender used pisco, a grape spirit as the base.

name: Fish House Punch #2
garnish: Lemon slice & dust with grated nutmeg
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Crème de Pêche de Vigne liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon oleo saccharum
1 1⁄2 shot	Cold black breakfast tea
review: Over the decades the recipe the Fish House Punch has constantly morphed. The inclusion of cold tea is a contemporary adaptation.

name: Funky Pirate Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	White overproof rum
3⁄4 shot	Navy rum (54.5% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Goldwasser cinnamon schnapps liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water (reduce if wet ice)
review: Spirituous enough for a pirate. Why the name? Well, one of the rums has some 'funk', both rums have nautical connections, the lime protects against scurvy, the cinnamon schnapps liqueur has pieces of gold and grenadine is blood red. Well, seemed appropriate to me!
history: Created in 2004 by yours truly.

name: Strawberry on Acid
preparation: MUDDLE strawberries in base of shaker. Add next 4 ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
3 fresh	Strawberries (hulled, small & ripe)
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Fraise des Bois liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Balsamic vinegar of Modena
1 grind	Black pepper
2 1⁄2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Rich fruity strawberry, balanced and made interesting by vodka, balsamic vinegar and black pepper tingle.
history: Adapted from a cocktail discovered in 2010 at Bordeaux Quay in Bristol, England.

name: Maida Vale
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Originally named the Unripe Manhattan after its creator's website, this Manhattan-style cocktail combines the spice of rye whiskey with sweet bianco vermouth and a dash of orange curaçao.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in January 2011 by Andy Green of Unripe, London, England.

name: Thai Green Cocktail
preparation: MUDDLE first 3 ingredients in base of shaker. SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 inch	Lemongrass stem
7 fresh	Coriander seeds
3 sprig	Coriander/Cilantro leaves
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Coconut sugar syrup
review: Extracting the juice from the stems and leaves of the coriander is key to both the colour and flavour of this fresh-tasting cocktail, inspired by some of the flavours of a Thai Green Curry - only without the chilli heat.
history: Created in September 2014 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England to accompany Spiced Beef and Chilli Blinis.

name: Mr Anthony
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
2⁄3 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄4 shot	Ginger liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
3 drop	Bob's Ginger Bitters
review: A genever-based Penicillin, combining malty gin and honey with subtle ginger warmth and plenty of Scottish island peaty character.
history: Adapted from a drink discovered in February 2014 at Mystique, Amsterdam, Netherlands.

name: Nessie cocktail
garnish: Orange zest twist curled to resemble Nessie
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄4 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Walnut (Nocino) liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
2 dash	Whiskey barrel-aged bitters
review: A Rob Roy (Scotch Manhattan) with walnut liqueur and Pedro Ximénez sherry.
history: Created in January 2015 by yours truly in tribute to the Loch Ness Monster, a.k.a. Nessie, who reputedly inhabits Loch Ness in the Scottish Highlands.

name: Bitter in Brazil
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably large chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cachaça
3⁄4 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 barspoon	Fernet Branca liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water
review: Cachaça based and bittersweet with orange accents and Fernet Branca contributing subtle bitterness.
history: Adapted from a recipe created at The Citizen Wine Bar, Worcester, Massachusetts, USA.

name: Woody cocktail
preparation: MUDDLE mint in base of stirring glass. Add other ingredients, STIR with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3 fresh	Mint leaves
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Kleos Mastiha liqueur
1 shot	Birch water
1⁄4 shot	Fino sherry
8 drop	Bob's Peppermint Bitters
review: Named not after the cheery chap in Cheers or even the Beatles’ Norwegian Wood but due to this particularly Woody cocktail containing birch water and mastiha.
history: Created in August 2015 by yours truly (Simon Difford) at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Miss Moonshine
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Poteen/Poitín
2⁄3 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄3 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄3 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Rosemary sugar syrup (2:1)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Gentian, elderflower and rosemary combine harmoniously, over a Poitín base with aromatised wine.
history: Created in 2014 by Louis Lebaillif at Hawksmoor Air Street, London, England.

name: The Savelberg
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
1⁄3 shot	Poire William eau-de-vie
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Honey
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Boozy with bready genever, pear, citrus and faint rich honey.
history: Created in 2016 by Jan Halfpap at Bar Le Lion, Hamburg, Germany. This riff on the classic Journalist cocktail is named after a Dutch journalist called Robert Savelberg who lives and works in Berlin. Savelberg became famous in Germany due to his critical questioning during a press conference held over the coalition agreement of the new Federal Government in October 2009, and a subsequent satirical movie made by ZDF.

name: Indimenticabili Momenti (Unforgettable Moments)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Moscatel
1⁄6 shot	Strega liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
1⁄6 shot	Cinnamon syrup
review: Slightly sweet with vanilla, cherry and cinnamon, along with complex peppermint and herbal notes from Strega interlaced with cognac.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Renato Pinfildi at presso Bottiglieria, Italy.

name: Venceremos
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
1⁄2 shot	Coconut rum liqueur (35-40% alc./vol.)
5⁄6 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Cucumber juice (freshly extracted)
1⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Sesame oil
review: Coconut, pineapple juice, cucumber and sesame oil combined with light rum makes for a most interesting cocktail.
history:
Bacardí Legacy 2016 winning cocktail creatsed by Chia-An Chan at Angel's Share bar in New York City, USA.

Chia-An says, "I was born into an absolutely alcohol-free family and being a bartender was never my career choice. Yet, life is always full of surprises. Here I stand as a bartender, and I recall that it was the Piña Colada that first introduced me to this sophisticated mixology world.

Venceremos is a unique twist on the Original Bacardí Piña Colada, with the added ingredients of two common Asian food pairings: cucumber and sesame oil. It represents both me and my history; where I am from and where my bartending career began."

name: Carousel
garnish: Chocolate powder or melted dark chocolate rim
preparation:
SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

*Special ingredient #1: Dulce de leche (30ml is approx. 5 bar spoons)
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bacardi Gold rum
1 shot	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
1⁄3 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 pinch	Salt (sea salt)
review: I had to boil a can of condensed milk for three hours to make the dulce de leche but its sweetened caramelised milk flavour is the heart of this unusual cocktail. Rum fortifies with banana, PX sherry and lemon all adding important elements.
history: The Norwegian Bacardí Legacy 2016 winning cocktail created by Moe Aliaff, a freelance bartender in Oslo. Moe says, "The Carousel cocktail is a reinterpretation of a childhood visit to the carnival, a happy time in any child's life! This particular visit was in a time of distress and it signified the beginning of something new, a second chance."

name: Companion
preparation: MUDDLE peppercorns in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
6 whole	Black pepper corns
1 2⁄3 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2 barspoon	Pear purée
1⁄2 shot	Honey
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Rum and pear with honey balancing lemon sourness. Vermouth (Anya's original recipe calls for Noilly Prat dry vermouth) adds complexity and plays an important role.
history: Dutch Bacardí Legacy 2016 winning cocktail by Anya Montague at Mr. Porter, Amsterdam.

name: Guayaba Arabica
preparation:
SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

Special ingredient #1: Coffee scented simple syrup
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
1 shot	Guava juice drink
3⁄4 shot	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
5 sprig	Coriander/Cilantro leaves
1 pinch	Salt (sea salt)
history: The American Bacardí Legacy 2014 winning cocktail created by Naomi Levy at Eastern Standard in Boston, USA.

name: Showgirl Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1⁄2 shot	Ambrato/ambre/amber vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄3 shot	Lanique Spirit of Rose liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
3 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Wonderfully floral – flavours of rose and raspberry dominate with dry vermouth adding balance and complexity.
history:
Created in 2017 at the Beaufort Bar, The Savoy Hotel, London, to celebrate Marilyn Monroe and her stay at the hotel in 1956. The American actress held a press conference at the Hotel where she stayed while in England to film The Prince and the Showgirl with English actor and director Laurence Olivier.

The Beaufort Bar's original recipe calls for an infusion of rosebuds, rose petals and hibiscus flowers and uses Dom Perignon Champagne and a "homemade Aperol Cordial".

name: Brandy Fruit Cup (Difford's Cup No.3)
garnish: Lemon, orange & strawberry slices, mint sprig & borage
preparation: POUR all ingredients into glass. Half fill glass with ice. Add a citrus slice and a couple of mint leaves from garnish before filling to brim with ice. Finish with rest of garnish.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Cognac (brandy)
5⁄6 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
1 2⁄3 shot	Cola (e.g. Coca Cola or Pepsi Cola)
review: Cognac works well in this fruit cup, rounding the other ingredients to present as a more harmonious blend when compared to the same recipe made with gin. However, it's more of a winter's cup, without the freshening edge expected of a summer's fruit cup.
history: Created in June 2017 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England. For more recipes and history see Fruit Cups and Pimm's.

name: Vodka Fruit Cup (Difford's Cup No.6)
garnish: Lemon, orange & strawberry slices, mint sprig & borage
preparation: POUR all ingredients into glass. Half fill glass with ice. Add a citrus slice and a couple of mint leaves from garnish before filling to brim with ice. Finish with rest of garnish.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Ketel One Vodka
5⁄6 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
1 2⁄3 shot	Cola (e.g. Coca Cola or Pepsi Cola)
review: Vodka's clean neutrality allows the fruity flavours in this summery cocktail to shine. Of the original line-up of seven different Pimm's spirit bases, only No.1 (gin-based) still serves but No.6, which had a vodka base, clung onto life longer than the other five.
history: Created in June 2017 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England. For more recipes and history see Fruit Cups and Pimm's.

name: Bourbon Fruit Cup (Difford's Cup No.15)
garnish: Lemon, orange & strawberry slices, mint sprig & borage
preparation: POUR all ingredients into glass. Half fill glass with ice. Add a citrus slice and a couple of mint leaves from garnish before filling to brim with ice. Finish with rest of garnish.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Bourbon whiskey
5⁄6 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
1 2⁄3 shot	Cola (e.g. Coca Cola or Pepsi Cola)
review: All whiskies seem to work well in this fruit cup recipe – bourbon's richness rounds rather than heightens the drink.
history: Created in June 2017 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England. For more recipes and history see Fruit Cups and Pimm's.

name: Slow Comfortable Screw Against a Cold Hard Wall
preparation: STIR first four ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. Then FLOAT Galliano and overproof rum.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
1⁄2 shot	Southern USA-style liqueur 40% (e.g. Southern Comfort)
3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Galliano L'Autentico liqueur
1⁄4 shot	White overproof rum
review: Sloe gin is the 'Slow', Sothern Comfort is the 'Comfortable', vodka and orange juice are the 'Screw' (as in Screwdriver), ice is the 'Cold', overproof rum the 'Hard' and Galliano the 'Wall' (as in Harvey Wallbanger). The result is a much better drink than the sleazy name might suggest, at least it is when freshly squeezed orange juice is used.
history: More information on the Slow Screw family of cocktails is included on our Slow Screw cocktails page.

name: Slow Comfortable Screw Against The Wall With A Bang
preparation: STIR first five ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. Finish with a FLOAT of Galliano.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	White overproof rum
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
1⁄2 shot	Southern USA-style liqueur 40% (e.g. Southern Comfort)
3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Galliano L'Autentico liqueur
review: One of the better Sloe Comfortable Screw derivations - Overproof rum provides the "Bang". Boozy fruity and balanced rather than sweet – what's not to like?
history: More information on the Slow Screw family of cocktails is included on our Slow Screw cocktails page.

name: Dr. Rieux
garnish: Lemon zest twist & demerara sugar rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled and rimmed glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
3⁄4 shot	Swedish Punsch liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Rounded, citrusy and delicately spicy with an attractive underlying funk from Swedish punch.
history: Adapted from a recipe discovered at Vaucluse, New York City, USA. Originally made with Facundo NEO rum.

name: Peat's Dragon
garnish: No garnish (black pepper from the recipe settles and decorates bottom of glass)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Speyburn 10yo Speyside single malt
1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
4 pinch	Black pepper
review: Dry and aromatic with vermouth and aromatised wine, along with rich orange liqueur, gently influencing scotch whisky, enlivened with a subtle black pepper bite.
history: Adapted from a drink discovered in 2017 at The Up & Up, New York City, USA.

name: Swiss Cup 5
preparation: SHAKE first four ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. Top with tonic water and ginger ale.
ingredients:
1 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2⁄3 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
1 1⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
review: Perhaps this would more aptly be named the Alpine Cup. No matter, it's a true Summer Cup in style, well-balanced and refreshing any season of the year.
history: Created by Matt Hollidge @theamateurmixologist on Instagram London / Belfast, UK. "The basis of the cocktail is based on the classic summer / fruit cup recipe, transformed to compliment the flavours of Suze. The 'No 5' is a subtle nod to the history of the drink, where the ordered range created by Pimms (since discontinued) in the 1940s, listed a rye base as the 5th in their range."

name: Mediterranean Margarita
garnish: Chamoy/Tajin rim (if available, use the Mexican condiment Chamoy to moisten the rim of glass, roll in Tajín to lightly coat. Alternately, use citrus juice and any chili-salt combo to create a similar effect.) Finish with a lime zest twist.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled Chamoy/Tajín-rimmed glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	Patron Citronge
1 1⁄2 shot	Amontillado sherry
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Agave syrup
1 barspoon	Orange marmalade
review: Recipe supplied by Patrón, who say, “Citrus and spice shines bright in the Mediterranean Margarita, made for the sights and sounds of Spain. From Yanaida Prado, this modern cocktail takes the smooth oak and light citrus notes of Patrón Reposado over-the-top with punchy orange marmalade, classic lime juice and agave, and deep sherry.”
history: Created in 2018 by Yanaida Prado, Barcelona, Spain.

name: Patchanka
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 barspoon	Orange marmalade
1 pinch	Chili flakes /red pepper flakes
2 dash	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: Lightly bitter, chocolate and coffee with zesty orange. Perfect as an aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Ilaria Bello at Talea Bar, Milan, Italy. (Ilaria's original recipe specifies Oscar.697 Rosso vermouth.)

name: Caribbean Sazerac
preparation: POUR overproof rum into frozen glass, swirl to coat inside and discard excess. SHAKE other ingredients with ice and strain into rinsed glass.
ingredients:
1⁄6 shot	White overproof rum
1 2⁄3 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄6 shot	Rhum Clément Blanc
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄12 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A Caribbean-inspired riff on the classic Sazerac cocktail
history: Created by yours truly but heavily inspired by a recipe created in 2014 by Gareth Fearn at Alberts Bar and Restaurant, Manchester, England.

name: Commander in Chief
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	The Busker Single Pot Still Irish Whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Pommeau du Normandie
1⁄12 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Verjuice
1⁄12 shot	Passion fruit syrup
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Single pot still Irish whiskey gives this Commander backbone while verjuice adds a stiff upper lip, but this Chief has heart and soul in the form of passion fruit, apricot liqueur, and Pommeau de Normandie.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Jillian Vose at The Dead Rabbit, New York City, USA. Jillian's original recipe calls for the whisky to be split between 15ml Redbreast 12-year-old and 30ml Green Spot Irish whiskeys.

name: Lone Oak
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1⁄6 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Pistachio syrup
2 dash	Orinoco bitters
2 fresh	Curry leaf (optional)
review: Herbal Chartreuse, Irish whiskey with zesty lemon and creamy nutty pistachio.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Jillian Vose at the Dead Rabbit in New York City, USA. Jillian's original spec calls for 60ml Jameson Black Barrel Irish whiskey, 7.5ml Green Chartreuse with 22.5ml homemade pistachio syrup:

Homemade pistachio syrup
1. Cover 250 grams raw shelled pistachios with water in a clean nonreactive container and leave to soak for at least 30 minutes.
2. Strain water from pistachios and blend the pistachios while slowly adding 600ml of boiled (but not boiling) hot water.
3. Pulse blend until the mixture reaches a smooth consistency and pour into a clean non-reactive container and leave rest for 2 hours.
4. Strain the mixture using a chinois to produce pistachio milk and discard the solids.
5. Heat and stir the pistachio milk in a saucepan over medium heat with 2 cups white granulated sugar for every 1½ cup of pistachio milk. Continue to heat (do not boil) until the sugar is dissolved.
6. Allow to cool and add dashes of orange flower water to taste.
7. If not using immediately, add high-proof neutral spirit (75% alc./vol.) and store refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 10 days.

name: Number 10
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with prosecco and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	O/Purist Tsipouro
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sour apple liqueur
1 dash	Celery bitters
2 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
review: Prosecco amplifies tsipouro's grape notes with sour apple liqueur adding flavour and freshness.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Angelos Oikonomou at Stardust all day bar in Kastoria, Greece, this was one of ten winning recipes in the 2021 O/Purist Quest. Named after the ten Greek bartenders that collaborated to create O/Purist Tsipouro, Angelos says, "The idea was based on the classic "French 75", aiming at marking its own new path as a modern yet simple and delicious cocktail with tsipouro."

name: Luigi
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Mandarine Napoleon liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1 shot	Tangerine / Mandarin / Clementine (fresh fruit)
1⁄24 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix) (optional)
review: If you don't have tangerines/mandarins then regular orange juice will do, as will triple sec (as per the original recipe) in place of mandarin liqueur, it's that bit better with mandarin. Depending on your citrus fruit and personal tastes, you may want to include or omit the optional additional splash of sugar syrup.
history: A variation on the Bronx, the Luigi Cocktail first appears in Robert Vermeire's 1922 Cocktails: How to Mix Them

name: Mission Bell
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
2⁄3 shot	Savoia Americano Rosso
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Pamplemousse liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄4 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
4 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters
review: Bittersweet grapefruit and mezcal with honeyed roundness.
history: Created September 2021 by yours truly at the Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: Yule Luv It
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Ginger liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
4 drop	Bob's Ginger Bitters
review: Rich orange, delicate ginger spice and herbal complexity with cranberry and lime fruit.
history: Created by yours truly in 2021 thanks to inspiration from the name and ingredients listed for the "Yule Tidings" cocktail on the menu at Porchlight in New York City, USA.

name: Cherry Manhattan
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2⁄3 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
4 drop	Bob's Vanilla bitters
review: "Cherry" may be upfront in the name of this Sweet Manhattan riff but the cherry notes are far from dominant – garnish excluded.
history:
Created by yours truly in January 2022 at the Clocktower in Rye, England.
Manhattan cocktail history

name: Cosmopolitan (1927 recipe)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
2⁄3 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
2⁄3 shot	Swedish Punsch liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: A Cosmopolitan in name but not in style. Instead, this Cosmo is perhaps best described as a delicately spiced Old Fashioned. If serving straight-up, as perhaps originally intended, then, depending on your ice, consider adding a splash of chilled water prior to stirring.
history: This, the first "Cosmopolitan" cocktail in print, appears in the "Cocktails Round Town" chapter by Arthur Moss in Harry McElhone's 1927 Barflies and Cocktails.

name: Ben Barnato
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Pineau des Charentes blanc
1⁄2 shot	Blanc quinquina/kina (e.g. Mattei Cap Corse or Kina L'Aéro d'Or)
1⁄2 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄6 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Delicate honeyed sweet notes are balanced by subtle quinine bitterness and spiritous spice, all laced with grape spirit.
history: Created in February 2023 by yours truly thanks to a comment on our Barney Barnato Cocktail page by a fellow Discerning Drinker called Ben who, due to sourcing issues, had subbed kina aromatised wine for Pineau des Charentes in the recipe. I like the dry quinine notes in the kina so I retained it in this rendition of the Barney Barnato with added Pineau inspired by Ben's comment. Many thanks, Ben.

name: Cherry Bomb No. 2
garnish: Skewered Luxardo Maraschino cherry and green olive
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 5⁄6 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄6 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
1⁄6 shot	Acqua Bianca liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
2 dash	Spiced chocolate bitters
review: A wonderfully complex Cherry Old Fashioned. Kat's original recipe calls for an Acerola cherry juice sugar syrup (1:1) which arguably has more of an apricot than cherry taste. Ideally, you'd make this syrup to make the cocktail but I found cherry brandy (or even equal parts cherry and apricot brandy liqueurs) work well as an alternative, and produce a more radiant cocktail (as photographed).
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2022 by Kat "The Queen of Tequila" Stanley Whyte of the The American Bar at The Savoy in London, England.

name: Ti' Time Daiquiri
garnish: Lime wedge or dehydrated lime slice wheel on rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄6 shot	Rhum Clément Blanc
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Clément Sirop de Canne
1⁄6 shot	Sugar cane juice
4 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters
review: The Ti' Punch meets the Daiquiri.
history: Created in February 2023 by yours truly at The Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: Salt & Pepper Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Manzanilla sherry
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Piment d'Espelette chile liqueur
3 dash	Celery bitters
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2022 by Michael McIlroy at Temple Bar in New York City, USA.

name: Absinthe Colada
garnish: Mint sprigs bouquet & serve with a straw
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. (It pays to stir first 5 ingredients in the tin before adding coconut milk and continuing to stir as you pour this last ingredient to help prevent it from curdling.)
ingredients:
1 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄2 shot	Rhum Clément Blanc
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Peppermint Pastille crème de menthe
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
5⁄6 shot	Cream of coconut (e.g. Coco Lopez, Re'al etc.)
2⁄3 shot	Coconut milk
review: How brilliantly and seductively creamy coconut tames absinthe and rhum agricole makes this colada served frappé dangerous.
history: Adapted from a recipe created at Maison Premiere in Brooklyn, New York City, USA. If pre-preparation allows, in place of coconut cream and coconut milk pre-mix coconut milk & cream made with 3 parts coconut cream to 1 part coconut milk stirred in a pan over low heat. Allow to cool, pour into an airtight container and store in a refrigerator for up to one week.

name: Free to Rome
garnish: Lemon twist, mint leaf & 3 drops of toasted sesame oil (sesame is an allergen!)
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice. SPRAY inside of chilled glass with lemon zest oils. Fine strain cocktail into the aromatised glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Galliano Espresso Coffee liqueur
1 shot	Espresso coffee (cold/chilled)
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1⁄24 shot	Extra virgin olive oil
1 swath	Lemon zest oils
review: Lemon oils dry and add freshness to this Espresso Martini made special by a slash of olive oil and nutty liqueur.
history: Created in August 2023 by Mike Rosenthal in Nashville, USA, this cocktail was the joint 2nd place in the Galliano Espresso Martini Competition.

name: Jane Russell
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄4 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
1 dash	Xocolatl mole bitters
review: A Manhattan-like cocktail, originally served straight-up but is perhaps best-appreciated on-the-rock(s).
history: Adapted from a recipe by New York City bartender Brian Miller. Brain's original recipe uses a combination of two rye whiskeys: 45ml (1½oz) Russell's Reserve Rye and 15ml (½oz) Rittenhouse Rye.

name: Dutch Nemesis
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with sparkling wine.
ingredients:
1 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
3⁄4 shot	Mentzendorff Kümmel liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Pineapple sugar syrup
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 1⁄2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Kümmel shines in this genever and pineapple sour.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Alex Smith at Whitechapel in San Francisco, USA.

name: Beauchamp No. 2
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄6 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Becherovka liqueur
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
4 drop	Bob's Cardamom bitters
review: A split gin-based 2:1 Dry Martini made all the more flavoursome by a splashes of herbal and orange liqueurs.
history: Adapted from Jason E. Clapham's excellent Beauchamp, which is based on high-strength London Dry gin (Beefeater Crown Jewel). I've used a split base of gins to introduce old tom gin's amplified botanicals.

name: Six Cylinder
garnish: Orange zest twist expressed and discarded. Adorn with Skewered Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: A bittersweet aperitivo or digestivo with pleasing subtle rich cherry notes.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide.

name: Practice What You Peach
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Giffard Crème de Pêche de Vigne liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Americano bianco
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Bitter Bianco liqueur
1 dash	Peach bitters
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A gin-laced, bittersweet, peachy fruit aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created at Taste by Niche in St. Louis, USA.

name: Orchard Thief
garnish: Lemon zest twist expressed and discarded. Green apple wedge on rim.
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Fino sherry
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄3 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Pear & cognac liqueur
1 dash	Boker's bitters
review: A Bamboo meets a Chrysanthemum with apple brandy and pear.
history: Created by yours truly in March 2024 after making Chip Tyndale's delicious Orchid Thief. The dyslexic in me said 'orchard' rather than 'orchid'.

name: Bohemian Iced Tea
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Becherovka liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Krupnik spiced honey liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Peachtree peach schnapps
2 1⁄2 shot	Earl Grey tea (cold)
review: A fruity and refreshing drink with surprising flavours.
history: Created by Alex Kammerling at Detroit, London, England. Originally stirred in a tea pot and served in tea cups.

name: Autumn Leaves
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
3⁄4 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Strega liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Whiskey, apple brandy, vermouth and herbal liqueur combine delightfully.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2008 by Jeffrey Morgenthaler at Bel Ami Lounge in Eugene, Oregon. Jeffrey's recipe calls for 22.5ml (¾oz) Wild Turkey rye, 22.5ml (¾oz) Clear Creek apple brandy, 22.5ml (¾oz) Carpano Antica Formula, 7.5ml (¼oz) Strega and 2 dashes of his house made cinnamon tincture.

name: Midnight Over Tennessee
preparation: SHAKE first three ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. Separately SHAKE cream and crème de menthe and carefully strain over drink to layer.
ingredients:
2 shot	Tennessee whiskey
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Peppermint Pastille crème de menthe
1⁄2 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: A great looking tasty dessert cocktail. Whiskey, coffee and chocolate sipped through a layer of minty cream.
history: Created in 2006 by Leon Edwards at Restaurant Bar & Grill, Manchester, England.

name: Shadow Boxer
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cachaça
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Pamplemousse liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Apricot (abricot) eau-de-vie
review: As the name suggests this is a punchy cocktail – spirituous and bittersweet with a long bitter finish. Far from being a crowd-pleaser.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2016 by Ivy Mix at Leyenda, New York City, USA. The original recipe calls for Dolin Dry Vermouth, Giffard Pamplemousse and Blume Apricot Eau de Vie.

name: The Hee Bee Jee Bees
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Honey flavoured vodka
1 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	Agave Sec liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3 drop	Bob's Lavender Bitters
review: A Margarita with a touch of honey vodka and agave enriched orange liqueur.
history: Created in 2010 by yours truly (Simon Difford) at The Cabinet Room, London, England and named after Julio Bermejo & Jacob Briars. Julio is a tequila ambassador and Jacob was promoting 42 Below honey vodka.

name: El Presidente (Sloppy Joe's)
garnish: Lime zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A splash of lime adds zesty citrus balance to this delicate rose-pink tinted rum and vermouth cocktail with a touch of pomegranate contributing fruity sweetness.
history:
El Presidente is one of the best-known classic Cuban cocktails to enter the world's drinking lexicon and during Cuba's 1930s heyday, Sloppy Joe's was one of Havana's most famous bars.

In his 1939 The Gentleman's Companion, Charles H. Baker says (page 99) "Sloppy Joe's own Special is merely the Presidente with the juice of a small lime added, and the twist of lime peel."

name: Made Man
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Fernet Branca adds an almost smoky note to the rye whiskey, Yellow Chartreuse and cherry brandy combo. A great bittersweet after-dinner digestif.
history: Adapted from a drink created by Ali Reynolds at Hawksmoor, London, England where this drink is described as being "A variation on the Manhattan that Mad Men and Goodfellas would have enjoyed at the end of a hard day's work."

name: Manky Panky
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
3⁄4 shot	Shiraz red wine
1⁄4 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Blood orange juice
review: Red berries, red wine and ruby orange subtly fortified with gin and the underlying herbal notes of Fernet Branca.
history: Created 5th February 2014 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England. A fruity riff on Ada 'Coley' Coleman's classic Hanky-Panky.

name: Fresh Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄3 shot	Kleos Mastiha liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
4 drop	Bob's Peppermint Bitters
review: The perfect digestif Martini. Mastiha and white crème de menthe - both renowned for their digestive properties - add cooling freshness to this wet, lightly sweetened Martini.
history:
Created 19th April 2015 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

See: Martini Cocktail and its evolution

name: Claudine cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Armagnac brandy
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Byrrh Grand Quinquina
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Dry and aromatic, the combination of Byrrh and armagnac reveals interesting favours of dried apricot and chocolate.
history: Created in 2015 by Matteo Malisan at 69 Colebrooke Row, London, England.

name: Mediocre
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Vanilla rum/vanilla-infused light rum
1 shot	Mead
1 1⁄4 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄4 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1 dash	Bob's Vanilla bitters
review: Ripe pineapple, rich vanilla and honey laced with rum. The use of mead in this drink inspired the 'Mediocre' name. Best made with a light white rum infused with a vanilla pod, rather than a commercially produced vanilla-flavoured rum.
history: Created in 2016 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Well-fortified
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Moscatel
1 1⁄4 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄4 shot	Bison grass vodka
review: A Bamboo meets a Vodka Martini in this boozy, vodka-laced aromatic aperitif cocktail, so named due to this cocktail packing a trio of fortified wines.
history: Created by yours truly at The Cabinet Room in London, England.

name: The Haole
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with ginger ale, stir and serve.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Pineapple sugar syrup
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
review: Simple but very tasty and refreshing.
history: Thai Bacardí Legacy 2016 winning cocktail winning cocktail by Mitchell Kai Lum, Vertigo & Vertigo Too, Bangkok.

name: Elixir Fizz
preparation:
SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with prosecco and gently stir.

*Special ingredient #1: Homemade vanilla / thyme syrup
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
3⁄4 shot	Rioja (Crianza) red wine
3⁄4 shot	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
review: Red wine and light rum set the base flavours which are overlaid with tart lemon and balancing sweet vanilla and thyme syrup. Prosecco lengthens and invigorates.
history: Cruise ships Bacardi Legacy 2016 winning cocktail by Miroslav Kljajic, Alchemy Bar, Osijek, Croatia. Miroslav says, "The Elixir Fizz was inspired and created in the Alchemy bar where I first fell in love with creating unique beautiful drinks for my guests. Since then, mixology has changed my life. Like alchemy - the process of transforming something ordinary into something extraordinary - I have chosen four simple ingredients to mix with Bacardí and Prosecco to create something special."

name: Dutch Artist's Special
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
1⁄2 shot	Oloroso sherry
1⁄2 shot	Kirschwasser (cherry) eau-de-vie
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Groseille (redcurrant) syrup
review: Bready genever is aromatised with sherry and kirsch while red currant syrup provides the main flavour with its richness balanced by lemon juice.
history:
A riff on the classic Artist's Special cocktail, which is based on Irish Whiskey. The only change is to use Dutch genever instead of whisky – hence the name.

Created in January 2016 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Touchwood
preparation: RINSE chilled glass with vermouth and set aside. STIR other ingredients with ice and strain into rinsed glass.
ingredients:
1⁄12 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 1⁄2 shot	Lowland single malt scotch whisky
1⁄3 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
1⁄3 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
1 pinch	Black pepper
review: Stirred down and boozy, this Lowland single malt-based cocktail is sweetened and made very approachable by Pedro Ximénez sherry, and awakened by a pinch of cracked black pepper. A great late-night sipper.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2016 by Matthew Follent at Bar 1806, Melbourne, Australia, this was one of the drinks that contributed to his winning The Perfect Blend 2016 competition. His original recipe stipulates Auchentoshan Three Wood as the Lowland single malt.

name: Creme Egg Cocktail
garnish: Coat rim of glass with chocolate – use a microwave to melt a few squares of dark chocolate in a saucer and then and dip the rim of the glass into the melted chocolate. Grate chocolate over surface of the drink and add half a Cadbury Creme Egg skewered on a stick. It's easier to cut the chocolate egg when straight from the refrigerator (a good test for how sharp your knife is). Spear the egg with a metal cocktail stick that has been heated in hot water.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
1⁄2 shot	Licor 43 Original liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄2 shot	Warninks Advocaat liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: As befits the name, this chocolate and vanilla vodka-based Easter Egg of a cocktail has both cream and egg – the later in the form of Dutch advocaat.

name: The Last Time (AKA Stop Fiddling With My Drink)
garnish: Square of white chocolate balanced on rim
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Coconut rum liqueur (35-40% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
4 drop	Bob's Vanilla bitters
review: Richly flavoured and yet dry – rum and subtle desiccated coconut with monastic herbal sweetness dried by aromatic fino sherry and vanilla bitters.
history: Created in April 2017 by Paloma, my better half, at the Cabinet Room in London, England. Named after she instructed yours truly to stop trying to make the drink she'd just created better.

name: Curiosity
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bacardi 8 year old rum
2⁄3 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
1⁄3 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄3 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
1⁄6 shot	Earl Grey tea (cold)
review: Reminiscent of an Espresso Martini but with raisiny fruit and distinctive gentiane bitterness. A great after dinner sipper but don't let that stop you enjoying this complex cocktail as an aperitif.
history:
Created for Bacardí Legacy 2017 by Kenny Klein at Maniac Bar, Bad Ischl, Austria

Kenny makes his own vanilla syrup as follows: "Heat 1 part water and add ½ part brown sugar, ½ part white sugar and 2 vanilla pods. Add a pinch of sea salt and slowly cook for 10 minutes, then chill."

Kenny say's, "Through my research into the Bacardí family I discovered that the world-renowned inventor Don Facundo Bacardí and passionate bartenders around the world all have something in common: the curiosity to create something epic and to achieve their own legacy. My drink is inspired by my past Bacardí Legacy compositions and driven by my never-ending curiosity for bartending."

name: Chapeau
preparation:
STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
*Special ingredient #1: Grated liquorice
ingredients:
2 shot	Bacardi 8 year old rum
2⁄3 shot	Blackcurrant / cassis sugar syrup
1⁄3 shot	Balsamic vinegar of Modena
1 pinch	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
1 pinch	Salt (sea salt)
review: The richness of blackcurrant syrup (25ml crème de cassis works well as a substitute) is balanced by the sourness of the vinegar with the liquorice and salt adding umami notes to the rich rum base.
history: The German Bacardí Legacy 2017 winning cocktail created by Christoph Henkel at Shepheard Bar in Cologne, Germany.

name: Apóstol
preparation: FLAME cinnamon powder on a suitable surface and upend snifter glass over smoking cinnamon and leave to capture smoke while mixing ingredients. STIR other ingredients with ice and strain into cinnamon smoked glass.
ingredients:
3 pinch	Cinnamon powder (ground)
1 1⁄3 shot	Bacardi 8 year old rum
1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
review: Rich and cinnamon spiced with chocolatey raisin, this stirred spirituous cocktail is a great after dinner cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created for Bacardí Legacy 2017 by Grace Tsai at Bar 21, Tainan, Taiwan.

name: Psycho Killer Cocktail
preparation:
STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.

Special ingredient: Cocoa nib-infused Campari
Add 2 tablespoons of cocoa nibs to one 70cl or 75cl bottle Campari. Let infuse for one hour and then strain to remove cocoa nibs. Pour back into bottle and mark bottle accordingly.
ingredients:
2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
3⁄4 shot	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: This short bittersweet spirituous cocktail makes for a very tasty aperitif.
history: Created in 2014 by Jillian Vose for the 3rd volume of The Dead Rabbit menu, New York City, USA. Jillian used Redbreast 12 year old Irish whiskey.

name: Sunny Disposition Highball
preparation: STIR first four ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with bitter lemon.
ingredients:
1 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Bitter Lemon
review: A bittersweet lemony aperitif cocktail which is also great on a sunny afternoon - indeed anytime you find yourself with a Sunny Disposition.
history:
Adapted from a recipe sent to us by Christine Lavall, France, who in turn credits "an elderly friend who worked in a bar for many years in France."

Information on Highball cocktails, their history and tips on the perfect serve can be found on our page.

name: Mexican Duchess
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
2⁄3 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Light vermouth amaro (e.g. Cardamaro)
review: Spirituous and lightly vinous with subtle agave notes, bready genever and spicy gin all refreshed by zesty orange curaçao. Five equal parts is a faff to measure for individual cocktails but a dream to batch.
history: A riff on Seth Brammer's excellent Farmer's Tan created in February 2018 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Apples to Oranges Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
3 dash	Combier Elixir
review: Apple and orange laced with bourbon, harmonized by dry vermouth. Spirit-forward and eminently sippable.
history: Adapted from a recipe created 2018 by Tobin Shea at Redbird, Los Angeles, USA.

name: Suzepect Swizzle
preparation: Squeeze grapes to yield 20ml juice and SWIZZLE this with next 3 ingredients in glass half filled with crushed ice. Fill glass with more crushed ice and then FLOAT amaro.
ingredients:
6 fresh	Green grapes (seedless)
1 1⁄3 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Crème de Pêche de Vigne liqueur
8 fresh	Mint leaves
1⁄3 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
review: A bittersweet refreshing drink for a summer's afternoon or an aperitif with grape and peach fruitiness and complexity courtesy of gentian and fresh mint.
history: Created by Linus Morgan at the Tap Room, Kungsholmen, Stockholm, Sweden. Who says, "The name is a wordplay on Suze and suspect, it's a swizzle with nice bitter hit and a nice peach and mint finish.

name: El Patron
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 5⁄6 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
5⁄12 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
1 pinch	Salt (sea salt)
5 drop	Citric acid (10%) solution
review: Chocolate and coffee flavours from the spiced rum are central to this spirit-forward aperitivo/digestivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Jorge A. Conde at Smoke & Mirrors, Singapore. Originally made with Cocchi Storico Vermouth di Torino rosso vermouth.

name: Glee Club Cocktail
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Amontillado sherry
3⁄4 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Framboise/raspberry eau-de-vie
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2 dash	Burlesque bitters
review: Raspberry notes hit your palate first, followed by Chartreuse influenced sherry. Fruity yet spirit-forward and complex.
history:
The Glee Club Cocktail first appeared in Tim Daly's 1903 Daly's Bartenders' Encyclopedia and comprised "2 dashes of orange bitters, 1 dash of yellow Chartreuse, 1 dash of maraschino, 1 wine glass of raspberry wine."

This recipe, adapted from one by Jack McGarry at New York's Dead Rabbit, uses framboise eau-de-vie in place of raspberry wine.

name: Ginger 'Martini'
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Ginger liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
3 drop	Bob's Ginger Bitters
review: A warming medium-dry Vodka Martini with enlivening ginger spice for a cold evening.
history: Created by yours truly (Simon Difford) at the Clocktower, Rye, East Sussex, England.

name: Spiced Alexander
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
3⁄4 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: As the name suggests, this riff on a Brandy Alexander has a delicately spicy finish that cuts through the creaminess.

name: Dante's Old Fashioned Whiskey Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
5⁄6 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
1⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
2 dash	Pimento bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Dashes of bitters just keep this from wavering onto the sweet side of bittersweet. Honey adds delicate richness to rye whiskey and amaro.
history: Adapted from a recipe created at Dante in New York City, USA.

name: Pink Mist
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Italicus liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Amontillado sherry
2 dash	Lemon bitters
review: Softy bittersweet aperitif with zesty bergamot.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Dario Doimo at Mr Coco in Las Vegas, USA. This cocktail was awarded 2nd place in the 2019 Italicus Art of Aperitivo Challenge.

name: Five-Three-Five
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄3 shot	Green melon liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Americano bianco
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: Gin-laced, bittersweet with melon fruit and herbal complexity.
history: Adapted from a recipe by Bob Barron, who says, "I call it The 535," explaining that "535 nm is the wavelength of the centre of the green band in the visible light spectrum."

name: Corn-on-the-Cob
garnish: Grilled baby corn (or Candy Corn) resting on ice
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Mexican corn whisky
3⁄4 shot	Corn/maize liqueur
1 shot	Americano bianco
6 drop	Bob's Coriander Bitters
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Lightly spiced char-roasted corn.
history: Created in January 2021 by yours truly at The Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: High Noon
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Horse with No Name habanero bourbon
1⁄3 shot	Kirschwasser (cherry) eau-de-vie
1⁄3 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A Sweet Manhattan with delicately spiced cherry.
history: A habanero-infused bourbon riff on Shannon Tebay's High Horse cocktail, created in September 2021 by yours truly at the Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Pinky Negroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Savoia Americano Rosso
2⁄3 shot	Ambrato/ambre/amber vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Lanique Spirit of Rose liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Fino sherry
review: Bittersweet and delicately faintly floral.
history: Created in December 2021 by yours truly at The Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Gingerbread Old Fashioned
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Caramel Toffee liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Ginger liqueur
4 drop	Bob's Vanilla bitters
2 drop	Bob's Ginger Bitters
review: Boozy and lightly ginger spiced with vanilla and caramel.
history: Created by yours truly in December 2021 at the Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: Banana Rumhattan
garnish: Float dehydrated banana chip or peg to rim
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Banana rum
1 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
3⁄4 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 drop	Bob's Abbotts bitters
review: Just as it says on the tin, banana-flavoured rum with aged rum and vermouth to create a deliciously banana-flavoured rum Manhattan.
history: Adapted from a recipe by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford and originally based on Discarded Banana Peel Rum and Appleton Signature rum.

name: Bonsai
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
5⁄6 shot	Akashi-Tai Shiraume Ginjo Umeshu
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Piment d'Espelette chile liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Palo cortado sherry
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Savoury and spicy, this is an aperitivo cocktail, that is unless you need a chili-spiced kick-start to your day over breakfast – in which case perhaps rename this Wakey Wakey. Its enlivening spice has a curry-like appeal that makes this cocktail difficult to stop sipping on.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in September 2022 by Juan Jose Orellano Peñalver, a bartender at The Savoy Hotel in London, England. Juan Jose says, he took "inspiration from the Bamboo cocktail, my roots from South of Spain and my travelling time in Asia."

name: Broadwalk Flyer
garnish: Mint sprigs bouquet & dust with freshly grated nutmeg
preparation: POUR all ingredients into class half-filled with crushed ice and swizzle (or churn with barspoon). TOP with more crushed ice.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Cachaça (aged 3+ years)
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Xocolatl mole bitters
review: Sweet and sour with generous cachaça character enhanced by overripe banana and delicate herbal notes.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Damon Boelte at his Grand Army bar in Brooklyn, New York City, USA.
