name: The Tartan
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Highland single malt scotch whisky
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Drambuie liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Ramazzotti amaro
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: The bittersweet lovechild of the Rob Roy and Rusty Nail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2022 by YouTube bartender, Anders Erickson.

name: Villa Viktoria
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Mirabelle (yellow plum) eau-de-vie
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
review: Mirabelle (yellow plum) eau-de-vie add almost floral notes to this excellent Perfect Martini variation.
history: Adapted from a recipe created at Becketts Kopf bar in Berlin, Germany.

name: Savoury Whisky Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Speyburn 10yo Speyside single malt
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Manzanilla sherry
1⁄4 shot	Olive brine (from jarred olives)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: If you've a savoury palate and also like Martinis and single malt scotch whisky then this savoury cocktail may be for you.
history: Created by yours truly in October 2023 at the Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Nutty White
garnish: Float 3 toasted almonds in a line across surface of cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. (There's no need to dry shake to achieve desired foam.)
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Adriatico Bianco almond milk liqueur
1⁄2 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1⁄2 shot	Coconut rum liqueur (35-40% alc./vol.)
1⁄4 shot	Hazelnut liqueur
4 drop	Bob's Vanilla bitters
review: This after-dinner treat is creamy white and very nutty.
history: Created in December 2023 by yours truly.

name: Prizefighter
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
3⁄4 shot	Lucano amaro
1⁄4 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
3 drop	Xocolatl mole bitters
review: Spirit-forward, delicately bittersweet, and (depending on your mezcal) subtly smoky.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 at the Berkshire Room in Chicago, USA.

name: Meditation
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Amontillado sherry
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄6 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: Sherry underpins this brilliantly balanced cocktail with delicate herbal fruity notes.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Charles Christopher Mueller's 1934 Pioneers of Mixing at Elite Bars.

name: Fall Back
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Applejack brandy
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Amaro Nonino Quintessentia
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: A suitably autumnal apple brandy-influenced riff on the Sweet Manhattan with rye spice and herbal bitterness.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2012-17 by Sasha Petraske for the John Dory Oyster Bar in Manhattan, New York City, USA.

name: Sips Adonis
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Rubino vermouth
5⁄6 shot	Palo cortado sherry
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Amaro Santoni
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Delicious and reminiscent of a fortified bittersweet red wine with zesty orange notes.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Simone Caporale and Marc Alvarez at Sips in Barcelona and served at the Amaro Santoni takeover of Double Chicken Please in Manhattan in July 2024. Their original recipe calls for 45ml Martini Rubino vermouth, 25ml Palo Cartado, 20ml Noilly Prat Extra Dry vermouth, and 10ml Santoni.

preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into a chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
3⁄4 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Jamaican aged blended rum with funk
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1 dash	Xocolatl mole bitters
review: Rum and rye-laced, herbal and faintly fudge-like with delicate spice.
history:
Adapted from a cocktail created in 2008 by Ben Sandrof at Drink Bar in Fort Point, Boston, USA. (Sadly, shuttered in January 2024.) This cocktail was perhaps inspired by the bar's Fort Point cocktail.

Not named after Angostura 1919 Rum, this cocktail was originally made with Old Monk Rum, the molasses notes of which inspired the name which references the Great Molasses Disaster of 15th January 1919 when 10 million litre tank of molasses stored for distilling exploded. The ensuing flood drowned and killed many. Coincidently, Prohibition started at the stroke of midnight the next day.

name: Norwegian Wood
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled coupe.
ingredients:
1 shot	Akvavit / Aquavit
1 shot	Applejack brandy bottled-in-bond (50% alc./vol)
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Spirituous, fresh and refreshing with delicious herbal spice.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Jeffrey Morgenthaler at Clyde Common in Portland, Oregon, USA.

name: Champagne Snowball
garnish: Lime zest twist (discarded) & dust with cacao powder
preparation: POUR champagne into chilled glass. SHAKE other 3 ingredients with ice and strain over champagne.
ingredients:
2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
1 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄2 shot	Lime cordial (sweetened lime juice)
2 shot	Warninks Advocaat liqueur
review: Deliciously silky smooth, indulgent, and decadent. Rich thick and creamy advocaat freshened with dry sherry, zesty lime cordial, and invigorated with champagne.
history: The Snowball cocktail was huge in the 1970s and is now enjoying a well-deserved renaissance. This champagne-enhanced version is by yours truly.

name: Byculla
garnish: Slice fresh ginger or candied ginger on rim
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
1 1⁄2 shot	Tawny port
2⁄3 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Ginger liqueur
review: Claret-cum-mulled wine, but hold out for the warming ginger finish.
history: An adaptation of a vintage cocktail recipe of unknown origin. Believed to be named after a neighbourhood in South Mumbai, India.

name: South of Heaven cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Kleos Mastiha liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
3 dash	Celery bitters
review: Bittersweet and refreshing with the very distinctive flavours of mastiha and Fernet Branca.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2013 by George Megalokonomos at Food Mafia, Athens, Greece. This was the winning cocktail in the Mediterranean Cocktails Challenge 2013.

name: Apple Black Royal
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Crème de Mûre liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Sour apple liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
Top up with	Rosé champagne
review: Richly flavoured apple and blackberry fruit liqueurs, bolstered and fortified with calvados, charged and given character with rosé champagne.
history: Created in 2015 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room in London, England.

name: Byrrh Cocktail
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Canadian blended whisky
1 1⁄3 shot	Byrrh Grand Quinquina
1 1⁄3 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1 dash	Peach bitters
review: Canadian blended whisky provides the backbone over which layers of complex French aromatised wine are layered.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Visionario
garnish: Dehydrated orange wheel and lemon zest twist
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bacardi Gold rum
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Martini Riserva Speciale Bitter
1⁄4 shot	Chocolate (dark) sugar syrup
review:
"Visionario is a cocktail that was inspired by the same values that guided Don Facundo Bacardi over 150 years ago: creativity, imagination and determination. These values helped him invent a new style of rum that is still enjoyed today. I dedicate this cocktail to those with passion and a free spirit, who want to make a difference and leave a lasting legacy - just as, I believe, Visionario too can leave a lasting mark and become a classic."

We say: If you like Negronis then you'll love this drink. Golden rum presents a rounder base than gin to build the layers of bitter and vermouth flavours upon with faint sweet chocolate notes bringing all into a balanced complexity. Perhaps serve on-the-rocks.
history: Argentinean BACARDÍ LEGACY 2016 winning cocktail by Maximiliano Yamir Salomon, Isabel Bar, Buenos Aires.

name: Pass the Dutchie
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
1⁄3 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Tawny port
8 drop	Bob's Coriander Bitters
review:
Like a bottle of port, please be sure to pass this cocktail to the left, or at least drink using your left hand. You'll be rewarded with a spirituous bready vinous zesty orange flavoured cocktail that suits late-night imbibing.

Challenging right-handed drinkers to maintain drinking only using their left hand throughout the night makes for a great drinking game. Next round is on the first person to impulsively use the wrong hand.
history:
Created November 2016 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England and originally served on-the-rocks. Updated to a straight-up serve in September 2019.

As for the name, Google "Pass the Dutchie" (with a 't') by Musical Youth. Incidentally, a "dutchie" is a cast iron cooking pot (Dutch oven) and the song lyrics are, "Pass the dutchie 'pon de left 'and side...how does it feel when ya got no food?"

name: Big Fish
garnish: Maraschino cherry on cocktail stick & 2 bay leaves
preparation:
STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.

*Special ingredient #1: Earl Grey syrup made with 10g Dilmah Earl Grey tea, 500ml boiling water and 300g caster sugar.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bacardi 8 year old rum
2⁄3 shot	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
1⁄3 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄12 shot	Sherry vinegar
review: Earl Grey tea, dry sherry and sherry vinegar combine with the aged rum to produce a very interesting drink. Earl Grey flavours linger on the finish.
history: Created for Bacardí Legacy 2017 by Vitaly Alekseyev at The Duchess, Amsterdam

name: Embrasse de la Terre
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
3 dash	Celery bitters
review: This dry spirituous apéritif, Martini-like, cocktail combines malty genever and bitter celery flavours with Yellow Chartreuse richness dried by vermouth.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2017 by Zachary Faden of Mirabelle in Washington D.C., USA. Embrasse de la Terre translates from French to mean 'Kissing the Earth'. This cocktail was the winner of the 2017 Tales of the Cocktail Official Cocktail Competition.

Zachary's original recipe calls for 2 Rutte Old Simon Genever, 1 Dolin Dry Vermouth de Chambéry, ¼ Yellow Chartreuse and 3 dash Bitter Truth Celery Bitters.

name: Beginning of the End
preparation: FLAME an orange zest twist into empty glass to line the inside with smoky oils. Then STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into the pre-prepared glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Amer Picon
1⁄3 shot	Oloroso sherry
review: Burnt orange oils add smoky notes, complexity and balance to this bittersweet drink. A perfect after-dinner cocktail.
history: Created in 2008 by Paul Mathew at The Hide, London, originally for the Boutique Bar Show "Free Spirit" cocktail competition. Based on the classic Fin de Siècle, but using rum in place of gin. Paul's original recipe called for: 45ml Diplomatico Reserva Exclusiva, 15ml Antica Formula, 10ml Amer Picon and Palo Cortado Viejo sherry.

name: The Road Not Taken
garnish: Chamomile flower pegged to rim or lemon zest twist
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Spiced gin
5⁄6 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
5⁄6 shot	Peach aperitif liqueur
2 dash	Boston Bittahs bitters
review: Lightly spiced and bittersweet, a good option for an aperitivo.
history:
Created in 2017 by Joe Macbeth at 400 Rabbits, Nottingham, England. Joe says of his drink, "A nod to Americana and the Robert Frost poem from which it derives its name. A bittersweet dedication to all those who wistfully regret bygone decisions and ponder a life where the grass is greener."

Joe's original recipe calls for: 40 ml Few Spiced American Gin, 25 ml Suze, 25 ml Rinquinquin and 2 dash Chamomile bitters.

name: Reno
preparation: THROW all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄6 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
2⁄3 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
5⁄6 shot	Americano bianco
1⁄6 shot	Italicus liqueur
review: The distinctive flavours of amaro and gentian dominate this bittersweet but mellow aperitif.
history:
Created in 2018 by Giorgio Ferrarese at The Holy Birds restaurant in London, England.

Giorgio says "The story which inspired this cocktail took place during WWII on 21st April 1945, when the allied forces planned to retake Bologna. Polish, English, American and French troops helped Italian partisans to capture the city in a very unusual battlefield, a river called Reno. I used ingredients that remind me of the forces involved in the battle. Amaro Montenegro symbolises the city. Cocchi Americano to celebrate the partisan's movement born in Asti. Italicus represents braveness. And finally, Suze, this sophisticated liqueur de gentian, used to remember the aid received by the allies. Without this strong bitter touch, my cocktail wouldn't be the same, and the battle wouldn't have been won!"

name: Old Gran's Punch
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄6 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1⁄3 shot	Manzanilla sherry
1⁄3 shot	Apple sugar syrup
2 1⁄2 shot	Kombucha
review: Irish whiskey shines in this brilliantly balanced easy-drinking cocktail that will appeal to a wide range of palates.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Jameson Ambassador, Ronan Collins.

Our Punch page details the history of Punch.

name: Once Upon A Time
preparation: THROW all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Blanche armagnac
1 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄12 shot	White wine vinegar (Chardonnay)
review: A short and lightly bitter aperitif-style cocktail with an attractive golden, almost sunny appearance.
history: Adapted from a 2019 recipe by Mattia Lombardi, Amsterdam, this cocktail was inspired by the Negroni and the Brandy Alexander, and a mistake he made during his first bar shift while making them. Mattia says, "The white wine vinegar is a dedication to my colleague and friend Cécile Fayn, as it's her favourite ingredient."

name: Rum Negroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄6 shot	Cachaça
1 shot	Tempus Fugit Gran Classico Bitter
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: I started with a classic three equal parts Negroni, simply subbing rum for gin, but the rum was masked by the bitter liqueur so I boosted rum notes with a splash of cachaça.
history: Inspired by Rogerio Igarashi's Spiced Rum Negroni, recipe by yours truly in August 2019 at The Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Improved Dunlop Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Tawny port
1 shot	Martinique V.S.O.P rum
1⁄6 shot	Clément Sirop de Canne
1 dash	Xocolatl mole bitters
review: Rich and fruity tawny port sits beautifully with aged rhum agricole in this spirit-forward late-night sipper.
history: A 2018 riff on the classic Dunlop Cocktail from The Savoy Cocktail Book by Lulu Martinez of LunaDrinks Inc., USA.

name: Tears in Heaven
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. (Infuse the spiced rum with summer truffle for 24 hours.)
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum (infused with truffle)
5⁄12 shot	Pear liqueur (Poire William)
1⁄3 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
2 dash	Bob's Lavender Bitters
review: A richly flavoured, well-balanced after-dinner cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Giacomo Gianotti at Paradiso, Barcelona, Spain.

name: Circus Circus
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Ambrato/ambre/amber vermouth
2⁄3 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
2⁄3 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe
review: A cleansing, delicately minty, bittersweet and very complex after-dinner digestivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Andrea Gualdi at Maybe Sammy in Sydney, Australia. Andrea's original recipe calls for Tempus Fugit crème de menthe and for the Amaro Montenegro to be infused with spices and this adds a delicious extra something to what is a great drink even without added spice.

name: Emerald Manhattan
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄12 shot	Giffard Peppermint Pastille crème de menthe
4 drop	Bob's Peppermint Bitters
review: An Irish whiskey-based Sweet Manhattan flavoured with a splash of minty emerald-coloured liqueur and peppermint bitters.
history: Manhattan cocktail history

name: Sugar My Plums

preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.

1⁄2 shot	Mirabelle (yellow plum) eau-de-vie
1⁄2 shot	Akashi-Tai Shiraume Ginjo Umeshu
2 dash	Plum bitters
review: Complex grassy flavours of green apple, pear, red grape, and indeed plum. A light, cleansing and aromatic aperitivo.
history: Created by yours truly in May 2021 at the Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Fleur Naturel

ingredients:

1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
5⁄6 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
1 1⁄2 shot	Carbonated/Sparkling/Selzer mineral water

name: Sips Sgroppino
garnish: Float edible flower or freeze-dried raspberry

1⁄2 shot	Italicus liqueur

3 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco

history: Adapted from a recipe created in December 2021 by Marc Alvarez at Sips "drinkery house" in Barcelona, Spain.

name: Appease the Cheese
garnish: Blue cheese stuffed pitted green olive
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.

1 1⁄2 shot	Akashi-Tai Daiginjo Genshu sake
1 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
1⁄2 shot	Italicus liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Mexican corn whisky

history: Created in June 2022 by yours truly at the Clocktower in Rye, England. The name, from Douglas Adams' Hitchhiker's Guide, references this cocktail's delicate style and cheese-stuffed garnish.

name: Coronation Cocktail (Old Waldorf-Astoria's)

3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄12 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur

history: Adapted from a recipe in Albert Stevens-Crockett's 1931 Old Waldorf Bar Days.

name: Lovely Rita
garnish: Float red or pink rose petal
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:

2⁄3 shot	Passoã passion fruit liqueur

history: Created by yours truly at the Clocktower, Rye, England. Named after the song of the same name on The Beatles 1967 album Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Harts Club Band.

name: Epiphany No. 2

name: Blandings
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:

3⁄4 shot	Lucano amaro

history: Created late-2023/early 2024 by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Ewards MCR at Oxford, England.

name: Pirate Queen
preparation: MUDDLE strawberry in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass over a large cube or chunk of block ice.
ingredients:
1 fresh	Strawberries (hulled, small & ripe)
1 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄6 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄12 shot	Ginger syrup
1⁄12 shot	Cinnamon syrup
1 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Lightly spicy with an attractive underlying bready fruitiness from the fresh strawberry and genever.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2014 by Jillian Vose for the 3rd volume of The Dead Rabbit menu, New York City, USA.

name: Bloody Bull
preparation: Add all ingredients to shaker along with ice, then ROLL (rotate rather than shake the shaker) or THROW. Strain into ice-filled glass, preferably with ice fresh from a freezer (rather than ice-machine/ice-well) to avoid unwanted dilution.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 2⁄3 shot	Beef bouillon/Beef Consommé (cold)
1 2⁄3 shot	Tomato juice
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄12 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3 dash	Worcestershire sauce
1 pinch	Celery salt
1 pinch	White pepper (ground)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A beefy Bloody Mary for those seeking a more hearty brunch cocktail. The addition of lemon juice and sugar to balance adds much to this cocktail, as does a can of Baxters Beef Consomme with Cask Aged Sherry.
history:
The Bloody Bull was created in the 1950s by Owen Brennan at Brennan's Restaurant in New Orleans when he decided to beef-up a Bloody Mary by adding house-made beef broth as part of his brunch concept.

Adapted from a recipe in Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide.

name: Top Banana
garnish: Dried banana chip pegged to rim
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur

1⁄12 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura

4 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: Not the simple sweetie the name might suggest. Made with rum, banana, spice, and all things nice.
history: Created in October 2021 by yours truly in the Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: House No. 3
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Manzanilla sherry
1⁄2 shot	Amontillado sherry
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Coconut water
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A quartet of fortified wines add complexity to this spirit-forward aperitivo. Delicious when made with a blended Scotch, but consider using an unpeated island malt to build on the subtle salty notes in the manzanilla.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Vince Bright at Lost Lake in Chicago, USA.

name: Asian Pear Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Akashi-Tai Daiginjo Genshu sake

1⁄3 shot	Poire William eau-de-vie
3⁄4 shot	Pear juice (freshly pressed)
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
4 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Sake and pear with sour complexity.
history: Created in 2002 by yours truly, London, England.

name: Berry Caipirinha
garnish: Stirrer (spoon, wooden lolly stick or stick cut from sugar cane)
preparation:
1. Cut lime in half (from pole to pole) and then slice one of the halves into eight 3-4mm thick half-moon shaped segments and drop into the base of a robust rocks glass.

2. Add 3 bar spoons caster sugar (or ½oz / 15ml sugar syrup 2:1) and MUDDLE.

3. Add mixed berries and MUDDLE some more.

4. When sure fruit juice is fully extracted and the sugar dissolved, transfer the muddled fruit and sugar into serving glass (preferably a 30cl / 10oz highball glass).

5. POUR cachaça (stored in the freezer) into the rocks glass (used to muddle) and swirl to rinse glass before pouring cachaça into serving glass. STIR to ensure all ingredients are well mixed.

6. Crack (rather than crush) four to five large ice cubes using an Ice Tapper and drop into serving glass. STIR before topping with more ice and serve with a stirrer (but no straws).
ingredients:
1⁄2 fresh	Lime (fresh) (chopped)
3 barspoon	Caster/ Superfine/Baker's special sugar (white)
3 fresh	Raspberries
2 fresh	Blackberries
3 fresh	Blueberries (fresh)
1 fresh	Strawberries (hulled, small & ripe)
2 shot	Cachaça (from freezer)
review: A fruity version of the popular Brazilian drink.
history: Caipirinha cocktail history

name: Raspberry Frangipane Spritz
preparation: STIR 5 ingredients (without ice) and strain into ice-filled glass, already charged with prosecco. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Giffard Crème de Framboise
1⁄6 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Vanille de Madagascar
1⁄6 shot	Coconut rum liqueur (35-40% alc./vol.)
1⁄12 shot	Butterscotch liqueur
2 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Just like the eponymously named dessert, this slightly sweet spritz is flavoured with raspberry, almond, vanilla and coconut. Butterscotch liqueur adds a biscuity note.
history:
Created in 2013 by yours truly for Jamie's Italian Bars.
Spritz history and other Spritz cocktails

name: Champagne Piña Colada
preparation: BLEND first 6 ingredients with 4oz scoop of crushed ice (including 15ml/ ½oz champagne) and pour into chilled glass which has been pre-charged with 45ml/ 1½oz of chilled champagne.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄6 shot	Rhum Clément Blanc
2⁄3 shot	Giffard Caribbean Pineapple liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
2 scoop	Coconut sorbet
1 1⁄2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Deliciously creamy pineapple and coconut enlivened by champagne with rum notes shining through.
history:
Adapted from Chris Moore's award-winning signature cocktail which has been served at Coupette, Bethnal Green, London since the French-influenced neighbourhood bar opened in 2017. The recipe's proportions have been tweaked since the bar opened but the ingredients have remained constant:

20ml Bacardi Heritage
10ml Trois Rivières Blanc
40ml Fresh Pineapple Juice
35ml House-made acidic pineapple cordial
3 scoops Coconut Sorbet
60ml Moet & Chandon Brut Imperial

Coconut Sorbet is not easily available in the UK, hence our recipe to make your own. For ease, we've also swapped Coupette's house-made acidic pineapple cordial for pineapple liqueur and rebalanced proportions accordingly. At Coupette, they make their cordial by soaking leftover pineapple skins in sugar syrup overnight and mixing with citric acid.

See Piña Colada history

name: Rumshack Punch
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Navy rum (54.5% alc./vol.)
2⁄3 shot	White overproof rum
1⁄2 shot	Peach purée
1⁄3 shot	Peachtree peach schnapps
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄3 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: Funky rum interlaced with peach, pineapple, lime, and pomegranate fruit. A monster but balanced.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in the 1990s by Dick Bradsell, London, England.

name: Banana Stand
garnish: Originally presented in a banana leaf-wrapped glass bound with brown string but perhaps settle for just the cinnamon stick stirrer.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 shot	Speyburn 10yo Speyside single malt
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄4 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄12 shot	Cinnamon syrup
1⁄12 shot	Pimento dram/Allspice liqueur
review: Smoky whisky-laced, rich, delicately herbal banana. Not as challenging as this drink sounds and considerably tastier.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Zac Overman at Rob Roy in Seattle, USA.

name: Beat Dis
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Vanille de Madagascar
1⁄6 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Giffard Piment d'Espelette chile liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime (fresh)
1⁄3 shot	Beetroot juice
4 drop	Bob's Vanilla bitters
review: Beetroot and vanilla are harmonious flavours, here rum-laced with balancing lime and an enlivening hint of spice.
history: Created November 2021 by yours truly at the Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: Cab Calloway
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Oloroso sherry
1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A sherry-forward, rye whiskey-laced aperitivo with delicate rich apricot.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created by bartender Tiffanie Barrie at One Flew South bar in Atlanta, USA.

Cab Calloway (1907 - 1994) was an American singer, songwriter, bandleader and dancer who was known for his energetic scat singing, particularly in his performance of Minnie the Moocher. He was associated with the Cotton Club in Harlem, known in cocktail circles thanks to Charlie Conolly's book The World Famous Cotton Club: 1939 Book of Mixed Drinks.

name: Raspberry Deluxe Martini
preparation: MUDDLE raspberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
8 fresh	Raspberries
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Framboise/raspberry eau-de-vie
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Crème de Framboise
1⁄6 shot	Pomegranate molasses
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A raspberry-infused sweet vodka martini.
history: Created by yours truly at The Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Passepartout
preparation: Cut a passion fruit in half and scoop flesh from one half into shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 fresh	Passion fruit (fresh)
1 1⁄2 shot	Cachaça
1⁄2 shot	Passoã passion fruit liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Verjuice
2⁄3 shot	Pineapple juice
6 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters
review: The sour, tropical fruity flavour of fresh passion fruit laced with cachaça's grassy tropical notes. Like Jules Verne's Jean Passepartout, this cocktail may help transport you to another place.
history: Created by yours truly in May 2023 at The Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: Thrivemind
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cachaça
3⁄4 shot	Manzanilla sherry
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Rhubarbe Liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 drop	Tiki bitters
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Described by its creator as a "sort of a 50/50 Martini meets a Bamboo."
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2019 by Natasha Bermúdez at Donna cocktail & taco bar in Williamsburg, New York City, USA.

name: Sherry Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Fino sherry
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
1⁄12 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1 dash	Boker's bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Sherry-forward, backed by herbal vermouth with subtle zesty orange. (An additional orange zest twist may be too much.)
history: Created by yours truly at the suggestion of Chris Dimal, a fellow Discerning Drinker.

name: El Presidente (with rhum agricole)
garnish: Lime zest twist expressed and discarded. Float mint leaf/sprig tip or peg to rim

1⁄4 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
