name: Genever Fruit Cup (Difford's Cup No.12)
garnish: Lemon, orange & strawberry slices, mint sprig & borage
preparation: POUR all ingredients into glass. Half fill glass with ice. Add a citrus slice and a couple of mint leaves from garnish before filling to brim with ice. Finish with rest of garnish.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
5⁄6 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
1 2⁄3 shot	Cola (e.g. Coca Cola or Pepsi Cola)
review: Given the use of genever and orange curaçao, this cocktail should be named "Dutch Fruit Cup". Genever's sweet maltiness adds a bready character to this fruit cup.
history: Created in June 2017 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England. For more recipes and history see Fruit Cups and Pimm's.

name: Ohio
preparation: STIR first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄12 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Bigallet China China Amer
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Herbal, bittersweet, zesty and enlivening. A great aperitivo.
history: The Ohio is a classic cocktail from the early 20th century which is thought to have originated in Germany, where it remains popular. This recipe is adapted from one created at Buck & Breck in Berlin.

name: Cafe de Jerez
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Galliano Espresso Coffee liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Spanish brandy
1 1⁄4 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
1⁄2 shot	Salted vanilla syrup
1⁄8 shot	Extra virgin olive oil
1⁄8 shot	Balsamic vinegar of Modena
review: Olive oil, balsamic and salt add pleasing savoury notes to this Spanish-Italian Espresso Martini. As befits the name, the original recipe calls for Spanish brandy, but I also tried and preferred Italian brandy. With a different name, this could be an entirely Italian production.
history: Created in August 2023 by Jonathan Stanyard in Seattle, USA, this cocktail was joint 2nd in the Galliano Espresso Martini Competition.

name: Carmen Miranda
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Lucano amaro
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
2 dash	Jerry Thomas bitters
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Bittersweet and rye whiskey-forward with herbal complexity and subtle overripe banana fruit.
history: Adapted from a recipe (originally served straight-up) created in 2016 at the since-shuttered Park Restaurant and Bar in Cambridge, Massachusetts, USA.

name: Palm Royale Grasshopper
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Peppermint Pastille crème de menthe
1⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Blue Curaçao
1⁄6 shot	Brancamenta
3⁄4 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: A Flying Grasshopper made more befitting of Palm Royale's tasteful extravagance by the addition of minty amaro and blue curaçao.
history: Created by yours truly in May 2024 in tribute to the many Grasshoppers made by Robert Diaz (played by Ricky Martin), the closeted bartender hero, for Maxine Dellacorte-Simmons (played by Kristen Wiig) in the Palm Royale period comedy-drama series which premiered on Apple TV+ in March 2024. Maxine is a social climber striving for lofty status in Palm Beach high society via membership of Palm Royale, the town's exclusive country club and Grasshoppers are her cocktail of choice.

name: 'Two Guns' Miller
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Pamplemousse liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Cinnamon syrup
1 dash	Xocolatl mole bitters
review: Sweet vermouth rounds while pink grapefruit liqueur freshens reposado tequila with gentle but enlivening cinnamon spice and faint bitter chocolate.
history:
Adapted from a recipe discovered in 2015 at Pouring Ribbons, New York City, USA.

This cocktail is named after Harry "Two Guns" Miller, who in the 1920s set up a zoo and the Apache Death Cave tourist attraction in the Arizona town of Canyon Lodge on Route 66. He renamed the town Two Guns and took on the Chief Crazy Thunder persona. However, all did not go to plan. Miller fell out with the couple who owned the land he was renting and on 3rd March 1926 shot the husband during a heated dispute. He was acquitted at the trial but shortly after was mauled by a mountain lion, not once but twice - on two separate occasions. Finally in 1929 fire gutted the attraction.

name: Walter Mondale
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 shot	Amontillado sherry
3⁄4 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Pear liqueur (Poire William)
1⁄12 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
review: A delicious spirit-forward honey, pear and delicately citrusy late-night sipper balanced and made interesting by underlying sherry.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2018 by Adam Gorski, bar manager at Young Joni bar in Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA. A riff on a classic El Presidente, this cocktail is eponymously named after the former Minnesota senator and 42nd Vice President.

name: Vivi
preparation: STIR first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice). TOP with more olive lemonade.
ingredients:
2 shot	Savoia Americano Rosso
1⁄3 shot	Italicus liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Olive lemonade
1 drop	Olive bitters
1 1⁄3 shot	Olive lemonade
review: Meaning "alive" in Italian, Vivi is bittersweet with pleasing savoury olive notes.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Enrico Gonzato at Jumeirah Carlton Tower in London, England.

name: Garibaldino
preparation: STIR first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 shot	Savoia Americano Rosso
1⁄6 shot	Italicus liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Tangerine / Mandarin / Clementine juice (fresh juice)
2 dash	Tonka bitters
1 shot	Fever-Tree White Grape & Apricot Soda
review: Fruity and refreshing yet complex and fairly dry with underlying bitterness.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in December 2021 by the team at Connaught Bar in Mayfair, London, England.

name: Quotidien
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
1 shot	Amontillado sherry
1⁄2 shot	Rhum Clément Blanc
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Crème de Pêche de Vigne liqueur
1 dash	Peach bitters
review: Rum agricole fortifies sherry to produce a spirituous aperitivo or after dinner/late night sipper.
history: Adapted from a recipe by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford. Jason suggests, adding one barspoon of "crème de pêche, for a still gentler version." I have.

name: Gingerbread Tequila Old Fashioned
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Añejo tequila
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Caramel Toffee liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Ginger liqueur
4 drop	Bob's Vanilla bitters
2 drop	Bob's Ginger Bitters
review: Ginger notes are subtle while the caramel combines harmoniously with the aged tequila to make a truly delicious nightcap.
history: A riff on an Añejo Old Fashioned, created in December 2021 by yours truly at the Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Rapid Automobile Cocktail (RAC)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Sage gin
5⁄6 shot	Ambrato/ambre/amber vermouth
5⁄6 shot	Rubino vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Ginger liqueur
4 drop	Bob's Ginger Bitters
review: Ginger fuels this riff on the classic RAC Cocktail with sage and citrus notes from the gin being this cocktail's driving force (or engine).
history: Created by yours truly in December 2022 at The Clocktower in Rye, Sussex.

name: The Other Wine
garnish: Borage/Bourrache flowers or other edible flowers
preparation: POUR all ingredients in carbonation device, CARBONATE, refrigerate and pour into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Monkey Shoulder Fresh Monkey
1 shot	Verjuice
1⁄2 shot	Poire William eau-de-vie
1⁄6 shot	Fino sherry
1 1⁄2 shot	Americano bianco
review: This white wine-like cocktail is aptly named and if you don't have a carbonation device (a SodaStream will do) it's also tasty with all ingredients stirred with ice and strained into an ice-filled glass.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Eric Sabloniere of Blue Bird in Paris, France.

name: Funk The Funky Funk
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. (This is a no-nonsense cocktail so no need for block ice and suchlike. Indeed, it benefits from dilution.)
ingredients:
1 shot	Cachaça
2⁄3 shot	White overproof rum
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Clément Sirop de Canne
1⁄3 shot	Coconut water
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Caribbean Pineapple liqueur
4 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters
review: A funked-up Daiquiri. To properly appreciate, sip while listening to Cantaloop (Flip Fantasia) from the album Hand On The Torch played at 11.
history: Created in October 2022 by yours truly at the Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: Roxie Ray
preparation: MUDDLE strawberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
3 fresh	Strawberries (hulled, small & ripe)
1 shot	White overproof rum
2⁄3 shot	Passoã passion fruit liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Dark/black/blackstrap rum
1⁄6 shot	Amaro Santoni
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Strawberry sugar syrup
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: If you like a Reggae Rum Punch then there's a good chance you'll also like a Roxie Ray.
history: Created in June 2023 by yours truly at The Clocktower, Rye, England. Inspired by singer of the same name and her Lift Me Up on the 2012 Dojo Cuts album Take From Me.

name: Hawaiian Iced Tea
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄12 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
5⁄12 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄12 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
5⁄12 shot	Ketel One Vodka
5⁄12 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
5⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
5⁄12 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 shot	Pineapple juice
review: A quadruplet of spirits infuse this refreshing pineapple and citrus cocktail.

name: Quattro Bianchi
preparation: SHAKE first 8 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Like the Long Island Iced Tea, the Quattro Bianchi uses "all the white spirits in the well" but is a tad dryer than most renditions of the LA Iced Tea.
history: Italian for "four whites," the Quattro Bianchi dates from 1980s and is the Italian answer to the Long Island Iced Tea.

name: Long Island Lemonade
preparation: SHAKE first seven ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with lemonade. Serve with a stirrer.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 shot	Lemonade
review: Surprising dry with sharp zesty citrus, laced with 4 different white spirits and triple sec liqueur, lengthened with lemonade.

name: Lemon Sorbet
preparation: Heat water in pan and add sugar. Gently simmer and stir until sugar dissolves, add lemon juice and the grated rind of 5 lemons and continue to simmer and stir for a few minutes. Take off the heat and allow to cool. Fine strain into a shallow container and stir in liqueur and orange bitters. Beat egg whites and fold into the mix. Place in freezer and store for up to 3-4 days before use.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Chilled water
1 cupful	Caster/ Superfine/Baker's special sugar (white)
1⁄2 cupful	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
5 fresh	Lemon peel
1⁄4 cupful	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
2 barspoon	Orange Bitters by Angostura
2 1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Our favourite recipe for this dessert and occasional cocktail ingredient.

name: Pino Pepe
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with 6oz scoop crushed ice. POUR into glass (or pineapple shell) and serve with straws. If using a pineapple shell, serve with ice cubes.
ingredients:
1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: To quote Trader Vic, "Lethal but smooth - pineapple at its best".
history: Adapted from a recipe in Victor Bergeron's 1972 Trader Vic's Bartender's Guide (Revised Edition).

name: Doheny Pisco Punch
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE (just to bruise) mint in base of shaker. Add next five ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with ginger beer.
ingredients:
12 fresh	Mint leaves
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
2 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
Top up with	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: Vincenzo's twist on the San Franciscan classic.
history:
Adapted from a drink created in 2007 by Vincenzo Marianello at Doheny in Los Angeles, USA.
Pisco Punch cocktail history

name: Amalia (by Robert Kalvans)
preparation: MUDDLE basil in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
12 fresh	Basil leaves
1 2⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
2⁄3 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Passion fruit syrup
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Take a simple Daquiri and add apple juice, fresh basil and passion fruit syrup, plus a splash of egg white to give a foaming head, and you have an Amalia.
history: Adapted from the Latvian Bacardí Legacy 2014 winning cocktail created by Robert Kalvans at Cheers Bar in Riga, Latvia. Robert's original recipe called for 45ml Bacardi Carta Blanca, 20ml apple juice, 20ml passion fruit syrup, 15ml Lime juice, 10ml egg white, and 10 fresh basil leaves.

name: Carondelet
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄6 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
2 dash	Orange blossom water / Orange flower water
2 pinch	Salt (sea salt)
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2011 by Maks Pazuniak at Maison Premiere, New York City, USA.

name: Eye Candy
preparation: MUDDLE ginger in base of shaker. Add next 5 ingredients, shake with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with a splash soda and briefly stir.
ingredients:
3 slice	Fresh ginger root (thumbnail-sized slice)
12 fresh	Mint leaves
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Given the name, the pressure's on for how this (perhaps not appropriately named) cocktail is presented. Beyond the name, this gin-laced ginger-spice forward cocktail has a citrusy elderflower supporting act.
history: Adapted from a recipe created at Touché Lounge and Restaurant in Miami, USA.

name: Amaretto Stone Sour
garnish: Orange zest twist (coin-sized, expressed and then floated)
preparation: SHAKE (Regal Shake) all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) to emulsify and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 swath	Lemon peel
1 2⁄3 shot	Disaronno amaretto
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A Regal Shake adds zesty oils, which, along with citrus juice, balance this almond-flavoured sour.
history: Perhaps the most popular iteration of the many classic Stone Sours. The earliest reference to an Amaretto Stone Sour cocktail historian David Wondrich says he's found is as the "Drink of the Week" in an 1982 newspaper advertisement for the Diamond Supper Club in Menomonie, Wisconsin. Six years later, the Amaretto Stone Sour is one of seven Stone Sours in Vincent Sardi Jr. & George Shea's 1988 Sardi's Bar Guide.

name: Bolero Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into an ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: A beautifully balanced, flavoursome medley of sweet and sour.
history: Adapted from David A. Embury's 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks.

name: Elderflower Collins
garnish: Elderflowers when in season (or lemon slice / Gypsophila (Baby's-Breath)
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
5⁄6 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A hint of elderflower adds interest to the classic Collins cocktail - long, balanced and refreshing.
history: See the history of the Collins cocktail on our Tom Collins page.

name: Golden Fizz No.2
preparation: STIR honey with gin in base of shaker until honey dissolves. Add next three ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with lemonade.
ingredients:
2 barspoon	Honey
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
Top up with	Lemon-lime soda (Sprite/7-Up)
review: More cloudy white than golden but a pleasant, refreshing long drink all the same.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in the late 1990s by Wayne Collins, London, England.

name: Green Fairy
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄6 shot	Chilled water
2⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: A well-balanced Absinthe Sour served straight-up.
history: Created in the 1990s by Dick Bradsell, London, England.

name: Parma Negroni
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with tonic water, briefly stir and serve.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: A long citrusy riff that takes the classic from an early evening cocktail to perhaps one to enjoy on a sunny afternoon.
history:
Discovered in 2005 at Club 97, Hong Kong, China.

The history and other recipes for the Negroni cocktail can be found on our Negroni cocktail page.

name: Ray's Hard Lemonade
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE (just to bruise) mint in base of shaker. Add next four ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda, lightly stir and serve with straws.
ingredients:
7 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Alcoholic lemonade with mint? A vodka mojito? However you describe it, it works.
history: Discovered in 2004 at Spring Street Natural Restaurant, New York City, USA.

name: Velvet Fog
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & dust with grated nutmeg
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄3 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Tangy, fresh and bittersweet.
history: Created by Dale DeGroff in New York City, USA.

name: Bluegrass
preparation: MUDDLE cucumber in base of shaker Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 inch	Cucumber (fresh)
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Cucumber and Bourbon with a hint of bitter sweet orange.
history: Created in 2008 by Hayden Lambert at Merchant Hotel, Belfast, Northern Ireland and named after the bluegrass that grows in Bourbon County where some of the best horses in the world are bred.

name: Judgement Day
preparation: SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1⁄6 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Charles was pretty sour about his experience when he created this very aromatic sour.
history: On 16th May 2008, superstar bartender Charles Vexenat was unjustly jailed in New Orleans during Tales of the Cocktail after his friend Dre dropped a bottle in the Old Absinthe House. Fortunately for Charles he was saved a second day in the slammer by Melanie Asher, owner of Macchu Pisco who bailed them out. This cocktail, created at PDT, New York City, is Charles's tribute to Melanie.

name: Saratoga Cocktail #2
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Dry and robust with cognac character combining well with maraschino and raspberry.

name: South Side Fizz
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and fine strain into (empty) chilled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
7 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄12 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A minty Collins.
history:
Bar legend says the Southside (or South Side) was created during Prohibition, either at a New York City speakeasy called Jack & Charlie's, or at Manhattan's Stork Club, or by Chicago's Southside mobsters to make their bootleg liquor more palatable, while on the other side of town hoodlums enjoyed the Northside (gin and ginger ale).

The truth is more mundane and the Southside evolved from the Mint Julep at Snedecor's Tavern, Long Island in the 1890s when the style of drink known as a Fizz was at the height of its popularity. The club later became the Southside Sportsman's Club. This cocktail is also closely associated with New York's Twenty-One Club.

The South Side Fizz features in Hugo Ensslin's 1916 Recipes for Mixed Drinks but over the decades has morphed into the South Side Rickey served over cracked ice and more recently to the Southside served straight-up without soda.

name: Petruchio Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
2⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Gin-based and bittersweet, this bright orange drink has a foamy head, which may mislead some into thinking it is sweet and easy.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2010 by Jamie Boudreau at his Vessel bar in Seattle, USA.

name: East 8 Hold-up cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
2⁄3 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄6 shot	Passion fruit syrup
review: Vodka-based, fruity and bittersweet with pineapple and passion fruit.
history:
Created in 2010 by Kevin Armstrong at Milk & Honey, London. The name comes from the part of London where Kevin lived, E8, an area where muggings were commonplace.

One night Kevin had just dropped Sam Jeveons off during their taxi ride home and Sam stopped to take a leak. While pissing against a wall with his trousers dropped around his feet, a guy came up behind him, stepped on his trousers and told him to hand over his wallet. Sam ended up chasing the guy with trousers around his ankles. The episode became known as the East 8 Hold Up.

name: Velours de France
garnish: Demerara sugar rim & lemon zest twist (discarded)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into a chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Licor 43 Original liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
4 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄4 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Almond and vanilla liqueur combine harmoniously with cognac with lime juice and bitters adding freshness and balance.
history: Created in 2015 by Edgar Pacheco of World Class Bar Celebrity Cruises, Mexico.

name: Le Château
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1⁄6 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Brandy stirred and served straight-up with a combination of French herbal and Italian bittersweet liqueurs.
history: Created in 2015 by Scott Burgess at Some Place, Liverpool, England.

name: Rosa Picante Margarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Ginger syrup
1 fresh	Jalapeno slice
2 dash	Rose water
review: A refreshing Margarita, with subtle ginger, pepper spice and rose notes. You can substitute half a barspoon of jalapeno oil in place of the jalapeno slice. We found that chilli liqueur also works well.
history: The 2016 Margarita of the Year as selected by Patron tequila.

name: French Diamond
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Maple syrup
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: This citrusy cognac-laced cocktail is fruity and edging towards the sweet side of balanced with maple syrup, lemon and orange juice.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Ciprian Zsraga at The Hoxton Pony, London, England.

name: Black Basil
preparation: MUDDLE basil in base of shaker. Add next 4 ingredients (all but tonic water), SHAKE with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with tonic water and lightly stir.
ingredients:
8 fresh	Basil leaves
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: Light in alcohol, with its basil and zesty lemon flavours, this wholesome looking cocktail makes for a refreshing summer afternoon drink.

name: Amalfitano
preparation: MUDDLE basil in base of shaker. Add next 4 ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with lemonade.
ingredients:
8 fresh	Basil leaves
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 shot	Lemonade
review: Basil, lemon and gin combine harmoniously in this mojito-like summery cooler.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Alessio Aufiero for Pallini Limoncello.

name: Diplomat Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Even with a good dose of sugar this cocktail is on the bitter side of bittersweet.

name: X.Y.Z.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: The original Savoy recipe follows classic Margarita proportions and like the 2:1:1 Margarita is a tad on the sour side. Hence, as with my Margaritas, I like to add a touch of extra sweetness, drops of saline and a dash of bitters. The result is still on the tart side but after a few sips your palate readjusts and tart becomes cleansing.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book. This "rejuvenated classic" was brought to my attention by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford whose preferred recipe (echoes The Savoy spec) is 45ml (1½oz) light white rum, 22.5ml (¾oz) triple sec, and 22.5ml (¾oz) lemon juice.

name: The Big Apple
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Most would pair lemon juice with whiskey but lime sits well with the apple juice in this recipe to produce a very refreshing bourbon aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe featured in the 2022 book, 60-Second Cocktails by Joel Harrison and Neil Ridley.

name: Daybreaker
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2 1⁄2 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
1 1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
6 drop	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
1 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: As the name suggests, this low-alcohol and refreshing cocktail suits breakfast/brunch but is equally fitting for a sunny afternoon or early evening aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Brian Floyd for P6 at the Line Austin Hotel, Austin, Texas, USA.

name: White Linen
garnish: Skewered cucumber ribbon roll (made by twirling a long cucumber ribbon around tweezers)
preparation: MUDDLE cucumber in base of shaker. Add next 4 ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
6 slice	Cucumber (fresh)
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water (chilled)
review: As crisp and clean as white linen with cleansing lime and floral elderflower laced with gin.
history: Adapted from a cocktail created in 2008 by bartender Rene Dominguez at the Ella Dining Room in Sacramento, USA. This cocktail became popular at Shady Lady Saloon, also in Sacramento. (Originally made with a cucumber-forward gin such as Hendrick's.)

name: Vodka Stone Sour
garnish: Skewered half orange slice wheel and Luxardo cherry (sail)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Why have a mere Vodka Sour when you can have a Vodka Stone Sour.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Vincent Sardi Jr. & George Shea's 1988 Sardi's Bar Guide.

name: Absinthe Sour
garnish: Lemon zest twist & Luxardo Maraschino Cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters (optional)
review: A touch of the sours for absinthe lovers.

name: Aviator #1
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. POUR cassis into centre of drink (it should sink).
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
1⁄4 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
review: An Aviation with egg white and a dash of cassis in the bottom but is actually better and more balanced when the cassis is shaken with the other ingredients.

name: Beachcomber
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix) (optional)
review: A Daiquiri with the addition of a dash of triple sec and maraschino.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Patrick Gavin Duffy's 1956 The Official Mixer's Manual.

name: Brighton Punch
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
review: Don't bother trying the version with orange juice but do try halving the quantities and serving straight-up.
history: Popular in the bars of Berlin, Germany.

name: Triple A
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 shot	Chilled water
1 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: So named due to this drink being flavoured with absinthe, apple and almond.
history: Created in 2010 by Dick Bradsell, London, England

name: Cucumber & Mint Martini
preparation: MUDDLE cucumber and mint in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 inch	Cucumber (fresh)
7 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A well balanced fortified salad in a glass - almost healthy.
history: Created in 2004 by David Ramos in the Netherlands.

name: Cumbersome
preparation: MUDDLE cucumber in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into a chilled glass.
ingredients:
4 inch	Cucumber (fresh)
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Interesting and fresh as you like with a pleasant bitterness.
history: Created in 2002 by Shelim Islam at the GE Club, London, England.

name: Detropolitan
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 1⁄2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
review: Yet another twist on the Cosmopolitan.
history: Created at Detroit, London, England.

name: Elixir
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE mint in base of shaker. Add next 3 ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain into ice-filled glasses. TOP with soda, stir and serve with straws.
ingredients:
7 fresh	Mint leaves
1 1⁄2 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A minty, herbal, refreshing summer drink.
history: Created in 2003 by Gian Franco Pola for Capannina in Cremona and Coconuts in Rimini, Italy.

name: Fine & Dandy
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix) (optional)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A Gin Sour sweetened with orange liqueur. Harry Craddock's original 1930 recipe calls for 1 part lemon, 1 part triple sec, and 2 parts gin. Depending on your lemons, this tends to produce an overly sour cocktail, hence I've reduced the citrus and added a touch of sugar.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: French Mule
garnish: Lime wedge or mint sprig bouquet
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled mug or glass whilst also pouring ginger beer.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: This French answer to the vodka-based Moscow Mule uses cognac to make a more robustly flavoured, long, refreshing drink.
history: A variation on the Moscow Mule.

name: Fruit Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: An orange-influenced, sweet and sour whiskey cocktail.

name: Gin Fixed
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass with crushed ice. CHURN (stir) drink with ice and serve with straws.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Sweet and sour with a spirity pineapple twang.

name: Gin-Ger Tom
garnish: Orange slice & Luxardo Maraschino cherry on stick (sail)
preparation: MUDDLE ginger in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 slice	Fresh ginger root (thumbnail-sized slice)
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A Tom Collins with lime and ginger - very refreshing.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2003 by Jamie Terrell at Lab, London, England.

name: Jade Garden
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Jasmine tea (cold)
1 1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Not too dry, nor too sweet, but tasty, balanced and refreshing.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2004 by Michael Butt and Giles Looker of Soulshakers, England.

name: Jasmine
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix) (optional)
review: A slightly sour bittersweet riff on the Pegu Club. The original is just on the tart side of balanced without our addition of the optional spoon of sugar syrup.
history: Created in the mid-1990s by Paul Harrington at Townhouse Bar & Grill in Emeryville, California and named after his college friend, Matt Jasmin, who challenged Paul to "Make me something you've never made before." Inspired by the classic Pegu Club, this cocktail is the result of that challenge. The Jasmine was promoted by its inclusion in his 1998 book Cocktail: The Drinks Bible for the 21st Century.

name: Jubilant
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: A well-balanced aromatic, herbal and fruity sour.
history: Adapted from a recipe attributed to "J. Perosino" in W. J. Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Cocktail Book - Coronation Edition.

name: Kiwi Collins
preparation: Cut kiwi fruit in half, scoop out flesh into base of shaker and MUDDLE. Add next three ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda water.
ingredients:
1 fresh	Kiwi fruit (fresh)
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A fruity adaptation of a Vodka Collins.
history: For the full story behind the origins of the Collins and its many variations see our Collins page.

name: London Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄4 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
3 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
3 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Chilled, diluted and very subtly sweetened gin invigorated by a hint of absinthe and zesty orange.
history: Adapted from a recipe in the 1922 book Cocktails: How to Mix Them by Robert Vermeire who worked at London's Embassy Club. The title page confirms this, saying "By Robert of the Embassy Club" and the book was published in London by Hebert Jenkins Limited.

name: Loud Speaker Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄6 shot	Cognac (brandy)
5⁄12 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
5⁄12 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A gin influenced Sidecar.
history:
Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

Under his recipe: 1/8 lemon juice, 1/8 Cointreau, 3/8 dry gin and 3/8 brandy, Craddock states, "This it is that gives to Radio Announcers their peculiar enunciation. Three of them will produce oscillation, and after five it is possible to reach the osculation stage."

name: Mary Rose
preparation: MUDDLE rosemary in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 fresh	Rosemary sprig
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Gin botanicals with Chartreause's complex herbal notes bolstered by rosemary. Spirituous and lightly sweet. Best enjoyed after dinner.
history: Adapted (We've reduced the volume of each ingredient by 25% from the original recipe) from a recipe created in 1999 by Philip Jeffrey at the Great Eastern Hotel, London, England. Named after King Henry VIII's warship, sunk during an engagement with the French fleet in 1545 and now on display in Portsmouth.

name: Mint Collins
garnish: Mint sprigs bouquet. Serve with a straw.
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE (just to bruise) mint in base of shaker. Add next 3 ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with soda and briefly stir.
ingredients:
12 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A minty John Collins – just as the name suggests.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Victor Bergeron's 1972 Trader Vic's Bartender's Guide (Revised Edition).

name: Mississippi Punch
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 1⁄2 shot	Chilled water
review: Balanced and refreshing. In place of chilled water try cold black tea and up the sugar syrup to 20ml (2/3oz).

name: Momo Special
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE mint (just to bruise) in base of shaker. Add next 3 ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda, lightly stir and serve with straws.
ingredients:
12 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Enrich the minty flavour by macerating the mint in the vodka some hours before making.
history: Created in 1998 by Simon Mainoo at Momo, London, England.

name: Monza
preparation: Cut passion fruit in half and scoop the flesh into shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 fresh	Passion fruit (fresh)
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Often made with up to four times as much bitter liqueur but in such high doses this dominates the other ingredients. Hence in December 2020, thanks to a comment below, we made our recipe more restrained to allow the passion fruit to shine while delivering a relatively dry cocktail.
history: A classic cocktail promoted by Campari and named after the Italian Grand Prix circuit.

name: Orchard Breeze
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
2⁄3 shot	Elderflower liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A refreshing combination of white wine, apple, lime and elderflower laced with vodka.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2002 by Wayne Collins for Maxxium UK.

name: Passion Fruit Collins
preparation: Cut passion fruit in half and scoop out flesh into shaker. Add next three ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda, stir and serve with straws.
ingredients:
2 fresh	Passion fruit (fresh)
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Passion fruit syrup
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: This fruity adaptation of the classic Collins may be a tad sharp for some: if so, add a dash more sugar.
history: For the full story behind the origins of the Collins and its many variations see our Collins page.

name: Passion Fruit Cocktail
preparation: Cut passion fruit in half and scoop out flesh into shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 fresh	Passion fruit (fresh)
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Passion fruit syrup
review: Full-on passion fruit with gin and citrus.
history: Created in 2004 by yours truly.

name: Pisco Punch (Lannes' recipe)
preparation: SHAKE first four ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Pisco's character shines through the sweetened pineapple fruit in this long, refreshing classic.
history:
This recipe is adapted from John Lannes' recipe, owner of the famous Bank Exchange when it closed in 1920.

Our Pisco Punch cocktail page gives a more detailed history of this drink and explains the different recipes.

name: Pogo Stick
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with 6oz scoop crushed ice. Serve with straws.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: To quote Trader Vic, "A refreshing blend of gin with pineapple and grapefruit juice... a real romper".
history: Adapted from a recipe in the 1947-72 Trader Vic's Bartender's Guide by Victor Bergeron.

name: Salty Dog
garnish: Moisten the outside edge of the glass rim with grapefruit juice and then roll in sea salt. Adorn with a grapefruit slice wheel.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 2⁄3 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
4 drop	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
4 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review:
Whether enjoyed with breakfast or as an evening aperitivo, this is a superbly cleansing and refreshing cocktail.

Our previous recipe called for 50ml vodka, 15ml maraschino and 50ml grapefruit juice. I like maraschino but, as many pointed out, it's not traditionally an ingredient in this vintage cocktail.
history: A cocktail from the late 1950s/early 1960s, it's first appearance in a recipe book is in Ted Saucier's 1962 Bottom's Up: New and Revised Edition.

name: Snow White Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. Then DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: The pineapple and egg white ensure that this delightful Daiquiri has an appropriately white frothy head.
history: My adaptation of a classic cocktail.

name: Sensation
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE mint in base of shaker (just to bruise), add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
12 fresh	Mint leaves
1 3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Fresh, fragrant and balanced.
history: The Sensation notably appeared in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Silent Third
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix) (optional)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water) (optional)
review: Citrus sourness drowns the Scotch whisky in the original equal parts recipe of this Sidecar made with Scotch in place of cognac (although, I suspect the likes of Cointreau used to contain more sugar so with a time machine the original spec. may have been balanced, and perhaps rather tasty).
history: The recipe for the Silent Third appears in two 1937 books: William James "Billy" Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Bar Book and Approved Cocktails by The United Kingdom Bartenders' Guild to which Tarling was one of the contributors. The recipe in one book is expressed in fractions and the other as percentages, otherwise they are identical.

name: Stork Club
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura (optional)
review: Orange and gin with a souring splash of lime juice.

name: Vodka Sour
garnish: Lemon slice & Luxardo Maraschino cherry on stick (sail)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters

name: Hotel Georgia Cocktail
garnish: Orange zest twist &/or dust with freshly grated nutmeg
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 5⁄6 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄12 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
6 drop	Orange blossom water / Orange flower water
2⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: An almond gin sour with orange flower water adding a delicate floral note. Lighter and more pleasing than the recipe might suggest.
history:
Adapted from a recipe in Ted Saucier's 1951 Bottoms Up. The original calls for 1oz (30ml) orgeat syrup, which we guess was made to a light 1:1 ratio rather than the richer 2:1 used in the recipe above. Interestingly, Saucier specifies to dry shake, saying "Shake well before adding ice. This gives a nice 'top.'" (I prefer to reverse dry shake as specified in my recipe above.) Saucier's 1951 instruction to dry shake this cocktail is the first known reference to the use of this technique.

The historic 12-story Hotel Georgia opened in downtown Vancouver in 1927 but its signature cocktail, thought to have been created in the mid-1940s, doesn't appear in print until 1951 in Saucier's book. The hotel was refurbished and reopened in 2011 as the Rosewood Hotel Georgia with its original 313 rooms reduced to 155. The hotel is number 11158 in the Canadian Register of Historic Places.

name: The Pan Am Cocktail

ingredients:

1⁄2 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: This citrusy aperitivo has an attractive tartness balanced by rich almond syrup.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Barney Toy at Revelry Bar in Auckland, this was the New Zealand Bacardí Legacy 2015 winning cocktail. During the competition, Barney said, "This drink was inspired by the luxury and style on board Pan American Airway's First Class flight that transported travellers from Florida to Havana in the 1920s and 1930s during Prohibition. The sophisticated elegance and fragrance of the Pan Am Cocktail would have been the perfect welcome complement to sip harmoniously while waiting to escape to an extravagant weekend in Havana, Cuba."

name: John Collins
garnish: Orange slice & Luxardo Maraschino cherry on stick (sail)
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda, stir and serve with straws.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)

review: A refreshing balance of sour lemon and sugar, laced with London dry gin and lengthened with soda. Some know this cocktail as a Tom Collins, understandably so, but a Tom Collins is based on old tom gin, while a John Collins is based on London dry gin. I borrow the wise words of David A. Embury (below) to address this confusion on our Tom Collins page.
history:
It would appear that the Collins morphed from the Gin Punch, a popular drink of the day and its creation and name are attributed to John (or possibly Jim) Collins, head waiter at Limmer's Hotel on Conduit Street in London during the late 1800s. The 'coffee house' of Limmer's Hotel was a true dive bar, popular with sporting types during the 19th century and famous, according to the 1860s memoirs of Captain Gronow (a Victorian writer of four observational tomes) for its Gin Punch as early as 1814.

name: Moscow Mule
garnish: Lime slice, mint sprigs bouquet & straw
preparation: POUR first 3 ingredients into copper mug/glass and stir. Two-thirds fill vessel with cubed ice. TOP with ginger beer and crown with crushed ice.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: "The vodka drink with a kick" is simply vodka and ginger beer with a squeeze of lime served over ice. This drink's all-important enlivening spice is provided by the ginger beer so pick your brand wisely.
history:
Part of the Buck family of cocktails, the Moscow Mule was created in 1941 - 1946 (the date and place of creation are disputed).

John G. Martin had recently (in 1939) acquired the rights to Smirnoff vodka for Heublein, a small Connecticut-based liquor and food distributor. Meanwhile, Jack Morgan, a friend of his and owner of Hollywood's famous British pub, the Cock'n'Bull Saloon on Sunset Strip, was trying to launch his own brand of ginger beer but sales were not going well.

Legend has it that the two men met at New York City's Chatham Bar and hit on the idea of mixing Martin's vodka with Morgan's ginger beer and adding a squeeze of lime (perhaps inspired by the Cuba Libre) to create the Moscow Mule.

Others, most notably Eric Felton in a 2007 article in the Wall Street Journal, say the drink was invented back in Hollywood at the Cock 'n' Bull by Wes Price, its head bartender. Price is said to have created the drink in an attempt to clear an overstock of ginger beer from the pub's basement. He served the new drink to actor Broderick Crawford and so the drink caught on from there.

Wes Price, apparently resigned from the Cock 'n' Bull in 1953 and is quoted as saying "I wasn't truly appreciated. I never got an extra cent for my invention".

What is sure is that the combination of vodka and ginger beer helped both Morgan and Martin shift their products but the cocktail's success is greatly due to its being served in a copper mug specially engraved with a kicking mule. This initiative was driven by a girlfriend of Morgan's who'd recently inherited a copper factory that made the previously poorly selling copper mugs. The success of the Moscow Mule was most fortuitous for all three friends.

By 1947, when Edwin H. Land invented the Polaroid Land Camera, the Moscow Mule was already established on the drinks menus of numerous bars. Martin bought himself one of the instant cameras and went from bar to bar photographing bartenders holding a bottle Smirnoff Vodka in one hand and a copper mule mug in the other. He gave one photograph to the bartender and used a second to show the next neighbouring bar what they were missing out on. The Moscow Mule and the use of the Polaroid Camera was a stroke of marketing genius.

preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.

1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)

history:
Rickeys are a family of cocktails believed to have been created by bartender George A. Williamson in 1880 at Shoemaker's Bar in Washington DC and named after Colonel Joseph Kyle Rickey, a Democratic lobbyist who it is said Williamson witnessed squeeze lime into his whisky before topping his drink with soda. Coincidentally or not, Colonel Rickey purchased the bar in 1883 and became a major importer of limes into the US.

The Gin Rickey cocktail first appeared in print in Harry Johnson's 1900 Bartenders Manual, where he calls for "1 wine glass of Tom or Holland gin if required."

name: Screwdriver (Difford's recipe)
preparation: STIR (preferably with a screwdriver) all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.

2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review:
The temperature at which this drink is served and the freshness of the orange juice are crucial to its success, but it's perhaps better made into a Harvey Wallbanger.

My own preference is to make my Screwdrivers with a whopping 75ml of vodka, 90ml orange juice, 7.5ml rich sugar syrup, and 3 dashes orange bitters. I like the grainy bite the generous measure of vodka adds but it's a punchy drink, so I have cut the vodka back to 60ml and cut back the sugar to 5ml to maintain balance. The only downside to this revised recipe is that the washline may sit a little low in the glass.
history:
Legend has it that this cocktail first appeared in the late 1940s in Iran where parched American oil engineers working in the desert supposedly added orange juice to their vodka and stirred it with the nearest thing to hand, usually a screwdriver which was attached to their work clothes.

This is partly supported by the following reference to the drink in the 24th October 1949 issue of Time Magazine, "In the dimly lighted bar of the sleek Park Hotel, Turkish intelligence agents mingle with American engineers and Balkan refugees, drinking the latest Yankee concoction of vodka and orange juice, called a 'screwdriver'."

history:
The exact origins of this drink are unknown, but its earliest appearance in a cocktail recipe book is in Ted Saucier's 1962 Bottoms Up - New and Revised Edition, which credits its creation to "Ted Majeski, United Press International."

Edward Majeski (1919-1988) was executive editor of the news picture service at United Press International and, according to his obituary in The New York Times, "boasted of never having taken a news picture in his career. But he was celebrated for a keen eye in recognizing a good picture." Apparently, he was also a keen amateur cocktail maker.
