Moscow Mule cocktail history

name: Campirinha
preparation: MUDDLE lime and grapefruit in base of shaker to release juices. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with 6oz scoop crushed ice and pour all without straining into glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 fresh	Lime (fresh) (chopped wedges)
1⁄4 fresh	Ruby red grapefruit (chopped wedges)
2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: This bright red fruit-laden cocktail has the looks to appeal to all, but its bittersweet flavour is more polarising.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2006 by Jamie Lawton at Orchid in Auckland, New Zealand.

name: Especie
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
2⁄3 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water (reduce if wet ice)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Rum-laced and rust coloured with hints of clove and jasmine. A herbal aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2008 by Juraj Ivan at Coq D'Argent in London, England.

name: Patrick Gavin Duffy's Punch
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 2⁄3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A full three ounces of alcohol per serve means this sure packs a tasty punch.
history:
Adapted from the following recipe in Patrick Gavin Duffy's 1934 The Official Mixer's Manual:

"Patrick Gavin Duffy's Punch
Juice of 1 rich Orange
1 Drink Brandy
½ Teaspoon Powdered sugar
½ Glass Benedictine
Shake in ice and pour all into tall glass, decorate with Mint and Fruit in season.
Drink through straw."

name: Santiago al Anochecer
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Agave syrup
review: The same colour as a red sky at night. Bittersweet, Negroni-like and a favourite with shepherds.
history: Created in 2008 by Andrew Coyle at Montpeliers Group, Edinburgh, Scotland. The name literally translates from Spanish as 'Santiago at Dusk'.

name: Union Club Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
5⁄12 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
5⁄12 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 1⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Bittersweet, fruity and complex. A summery aperitivo.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2008 by Jamie Boudreau at Tini Bigs, Seattle, USA and named after a gambling joint Wyatt Earp opened in Seattle in 1899.
The above recipe is scaled back (maintaining relative proportions of ingredients) from the original recipe:
2 oz Bourbon whiskey
½ oz Maraschino liqueur
½ oz Italian red bitter liqueur
1½ oz Orange juice

name: Elder Fashioned
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: "Elder" (elderflower) adds a subtle floral note to bourbon in this riff on a classic Old Fashioned.
history: Created in 2006 by yours truly at The Cabinet Room in London, England.

name: Elder Sour
garnish: Lemon slice & Luxardo Maraschino cherry on stick (sail)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura (optional)
review: So smooth it's almost fluffy. A slightly sweet after-dinner cocktail.
history:
Created in 2006 by yours truly in London, England.

A detailed history of the Sours family of cocktails is available on our Sours cocktails page.

name: Elderflower Cosmo
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Elderflower liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Despite the absence of citrus vodka, orange liqueur and cranberry, this delicate blend is still Cosmopolitan-esque in style.
history:
Created in 2006 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.
Recipes and origin of the Cosmopolitan cocktail

name: Elderflower Daiquiri
garnish: Lime wedge on rim &/or elderflower sprig when in season
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
3⁄4 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Elderflower liqueur adds floral interest to the classic Daiquiri.
history: Created in 2006 by yours truly, London, England.

name: Wash House
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE basil (just to bruise) in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
4 fresh	Basil leaves
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Delicately herbal - simple but refreshing.
history: Adapted from a recipe by Neyah White at Nopa, San Francisco, USA. The building that now houses Nopa was once a laundry, hence the name.

name: Whisky Flower
preparation: DRY SHAKE all ingredients (without ice) SHAKE again with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1 1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Basically an elderflower whisky sour with added interest due to the use of an Islay malt.
history: Created by Robert Williams at Mamasan, Glasgow, Scotland.

name: Noblesse
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
review: A light, sweet and sour, herbal and fruity aperitif cocktail.
history: Recipe adapted from Gary "gaz" Regan's Ardent Spirits November 2010.

name: Penthouse Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A bourbon sour with a touch of maraschino adding an almondy cherry note.
history: Created by Carl Wrangel at the Oak Room, Copenhagen, Denmark.

name: Elderflower Gin Fizz
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chill glass (without ice). TOP with soda.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Elderflower liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Go easy on the size of the glass you use, or this drink will become over-diluted. Due to the lack of ice in the serving, also ensure the soda is well chilled, and preferably use a frozen bottle of gin.

name: Great Chase
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass and stir. (Rather than measuring what is around a barspoon of lemon juice, you may prefer to gently squeeze the lemon wedge garnish prior dropping into the drink.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A lightly elderflower, relatively dry and refreshing spritz-style drink.
history: First promoted by the Chase Distillery late in 2015, the original specification called for Chase Vodka and Chase Elderflower, hence the name.

name: Trinidad Especial
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄3 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: This deep reddy-brown bittersweet drink is based upon sweet almond syrup balancing bitter notes from the Angostura and lime tartness. With a whole shot of Angostura this cocktail is most unusual.
history: Created by Italian Barman, Valentino Bolognese and the winning drink in the Angostura European Cocktail Competition held at Mood Bar, Paris in January 2008.

name: Honey Vodka Collins
preparation: STIR honey with vodka in base of shaker until honey dissolves. ADD other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 barspoon	Honey
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: The honey and lemon combo are reminiscent of a toddy but here served long and iced with cleansing vodka.
history: Also see Collins Cocktails - recipes & history.

name: Tommi's Cocktail
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Chilled water (reduce if wet ice)
review: A delicately bittersweet aperitif cocktail that heroes mezcal complexity.
history: Adapted from a cocktail discovered in 2014 at Wahaca's Mezcalería Cocktail Bar, London, England. This cocktail is named after the fabulous Thomasina "Tommi" Miers OBE, who co-founded the Wahaca chain of Mexican street food restaurants.

name: Le Fizz cocktail
preparation: SHAKE first three ingredients with ice fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with chilled soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Elderflower liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A poor man’s champagne cocktail. Refreshing and, providing consumed whilst still cold, unknowingly boozy.
history: Created in 2013 by Joe McCanta, London, England.

name: Desire
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Elderflower liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Agave syrup
review: An elderflower influenced cognac sour sweetened with agave nectar and served on-the-rocks.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Traverso Alessandro at Mistral lounge bar in Recco, Genova, Italy.

name: PLB
preparation: MUDDLE lemon in base of a sturdy rocks glass and then pour into serving glass. Fill glass with ice, add limoncello and bitters. TOP with tonic and lightly stir.
ingredients:
1⁄4 fresh	Lemon (fresh) (chopped)
1 1⁄3 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
3 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: Long and refreshing with a tart lemony bite.
history: Created in 2015 by Philip Duff for Pallini Limoncello, the initials which comprise this cocktails name are an acronym of Pallini Lemon Bitters.

name: Tremblement de Terre (Earthquake)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
8 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2⁄3 shot	Chilled water (reduce if wet ice)
review: Absinthe adds a liquorice note to this spirit-forward cognac-based cocktail.
history:
Originally equal parts cognac and absinthe, this cocktail is said to have been served at parties by Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec (1864-1901, the French Post-Impressionist.

Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book puts an English spin on "The Earthquake Cocktail" with a recipe that specifies "1/3 Gin, 1/3 Whisky, 1/3 Absinthe, Shake well and serve in a cocktail glass." This recipe is followed by a notation to the name, "So-called because if there should happen to be an earthquake on when you are drinking it, it won't matter." Craddock also notes, "This is a Cocktail whose potency is not to be taken toom lightly, or, for that matter, too frequently!"

name: Absinthe Mojito
preparation: Squeeze and drop lime wedges into glass half-filled with crushed ice. Add mint and absinthe and churn with ice. Fill glass with more crushed ice and TOP with lemonade (or lemon-lime soda).
ingredients:
3 wedge	Lime (fresh)
8 fresh	Mint leaves
5⁄6 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
3 shot	Lemonade
review: Absinthe adds its distinctive aniseed and liquorice notes to a Mojito.
history: Created in 2018 by George Rowley.

name: Parisienne Kiss
garnish: Thin cucumber ribbon placed around inside of glass.
preparation: Half fill glass with ice and place garnish around glass. Add ingredients (squeeze lime wedges and drop into drink) and top with more ice before topping with tonic water.
ingredients:
3 wedge	Lime (fresh)
5⁄6 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters (optional)
3 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: Absinthe, cucumber and lime served long with crisp tonic.
history: Created by George Rowley in 2018, "in honour of Johnny Depp and Hunter S Thompson (my first ever customers) and our 20 year anniversary of starting the absinthe category world revival."

name: St Clemence
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) & mint sprig bouquet
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass charged with half of the tonic water. TOP with rest of tonic.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: A gin-charged alcoholic riff on the classic non-alcoholic Saint Clements cocktail.

name: Coffee Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Just as it says on the tin, a sweet 'n' sour coffee.

name: Coffee Collins
garnish: Lemon wheel slice and Luxardo Maraschino Cherry sail
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Long sweet 'n' sour coffee.

name: Revolver
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix) (optional)
review: Depending on your coffee liqueur, this can be a tad on the dry side so I've added a splash of sugar. Hence, according to your own tastes, you may want to omit/or increase the sugar, and if adding sugar then also consider using muscovado or demerara sugar rather than white sugar syrup.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2004 by Jon Santer at Bruno's in San Francisco, USA. Originally made with Bulleit Bourbon, hence the name, the Revolver became popular after Jon turned his attention across town to Bourbon & Branch.

name: Grapefruit Rickey
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Depending on your grapefruit and how successfully you strike the fine balance between sweet and sour, this can be a deliciously refreshing cocktail. Consider serving with breakfast.

name: Green Ghost
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄3 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Herbal and zesty. I've taken the liberty of adding a splash of sugar to this not too distant relation to the Last Word.
history:
Adapted from the following recipe in the 1937 Café Royal Cocktail Book Coronation Edition which says this cocktail was "Invented by J. B. Hurrell".
"2/3 Seager's Gin
1/6 Lime juice
1/6 Green Chartreuse
Shake"

name: Black Sabbath
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
3⁄4 shot	Averna Amaro
1⁄12 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Smoky peaty notes from Islay single malt whisky dominate this spirit-forward and bittersweet sipper of a cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe (originally based on Laphroaig 10yo) created in 2012 by Alex Smith at Honor Kitchen & Cocktails in Emeryville, California, USA.

name: Last of the Oaxacans
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
3⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A classic equal parts Last Word but with mezcal in place of the usual gin.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2016 by Rick Dobbs at The Last Word bar in Livermore, California, USA.
Last Word history

name: Optimist Old Fashioned
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
4 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: With 60ml of 45% alc./vol. whiskey (depending on your bourbon) and 15ml of 40% alc./vol. liqueur, this is a punchy cocktail. Some may want to drop the bourbon by 10ml or even 15ml for reasons of sobriety (I tried that) but the original 1:4 ratio sits best. (The optimist in me cut the block ice for the pic way too tall.)
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Stephanie Andrews at The Spindle Bar in Charlotte, North Carolina, USA.

name: Written Word
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Recognisably a Last Word but noticeably zestier and not as rich.
history: A riff on a classic Last Word with triple sec replacing maraschino liqueur.

name: Bourbon Mule
garnish: Lime slice, mint sprigs bouquet & straw
preparation: POUR first 3 ingredients into mug/glass and briefly stir. Two-thirds fill glass with cubed ice. TOP with ginger beer and fill mug/glass with a crown of crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
5⁄12 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: A bourbon lime sour lengthened and invigorated by spicy ginger beer.

name: Bitter Bramble
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. DRIZZLE bitter red liqueur over the cocktail (which will bleed through ice as it sinks).
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review: Just as billed, a bitter version of the contemporary classic Bramble.
history: A riff on Dick Bradsell's classic Bramble created in November 2022 by Juan Jose Orellano Peñalver during a Bar Academy in the Caribbean to showcase how to make classic cocktails. Juan Jose's original recipe calls for Arbikie Kirsty's Gin and a serve over cubes or a chunk of block ice.

name: Three Poems
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A cognac sour balanced and flavoured with the rich blackcurrant notes of crème de cassis.
history: Adapted from the Three Hundred Poems cocktail by Chris Brislawn at the suggestion of Simon Stevenson's wife (see the comments on the Three Hundred Poems page), in January 2023. (I took the liberty of reformulating and naming this collaborative cocktail.)

name: Mad MacPeat
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
5⁄6 shot	Cognac (brandy)
5⁄6 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄24 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Peated whisky sits brilliantly with the floral elderflower notes in this late-night sipper. Absinthe plays an important role and I like with as much four times the quarter bar spoon I've stipulated in this recipe.
history: A March 2023 riff on my 2006 In-Seine cocktail at the suggestion of Lucas Fiammiferi, a fellow Discerning Drinker, in a comment on our In-Seine page.

name: Royal Hawaiian
garnish: Skewered pineapple wedge or dehydrated pineapple slice wheel & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
review: A fruity almond gin sour that's reminiscent of Mai Tai served straight-up for gin lovers.
history: The Royal Hawaiian was created in 1948 at the Moana Hotel in Waikiki Beach, Hawaii and first appears in print in Ted Saucier's 1951 Bottoms Up.

name: Skipper
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients and strain into chilled glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Temperature and dilution are key to the success of this cocktail, achieved with a glass filled to the brim with very cold ice chips.
history: A pre-prohibition cocktail from the Big Brass Rail bar at the original Waldorf Astoria Hotel in New York City, USA. Adapted from a recipe first published in Albert Stevens Crockett's 1931 Old Waldorf Bar Days.

name: Absinthe Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2 1⁄2 shot	Chilled water
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Absinthe tamed and served straight-up.
history: Dr. Ordinaire perfected his recipe for absinthe in 1792 and from day one it required the addition of water and sugar to make it palatable.

name: April Shower
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: This mustard coloured, medium dry, cognac-based drink harnesses the uniquely herbal edge of Bénédictine.

name: Bloodhound #2
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
2 1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A dry, tart, refreshing long drink.

name: Brandy Smash
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
7 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Sweetened cognac flavoured with mint. Simple but beautiful.
history: A classic from the 1850s.

name: Buona Sera Shot
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
review: The use of a dry, or at least not so sweet, espresso-style coffee liqueur is essential to the flavour and balance of this rum-laced nutty coffee shot.

name: Caipirovska
preparation: MUDDLE lime wedges in the base of shaker to release juice and oils in its skin. Add vodka and sugar. SHAKE with 6oz scoop crushed ice and pour all without straining into glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 fresh	Lime (fresh) (chopped wedges)
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Vodka replaces cachaça in this Caipirinha-style drink.

name: Copper Illusion
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review: Basically, a Negroni with liqueur replacing sweet vermouth. Like the Italian classic, this is both bitter and sweet.
history: Unknown but brought to my attention in 2005 courtesy of Angus Winchester.

name: Country Breeze
garnish: Seasonal berries or apple slice wheel
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
3 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review: Not too sweet. The gin character shines through the fruit.

name: Gin Fix
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass with crushed ice. CHURN (stir) drink with ice and serve with straws.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A Gin Sour served over crushed ice in a goblet.
history: The fix is an old classic that's very similar to the Daisy.

name: Godfather Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
2⁄3 shot	Disaronno amaretto
2 drop	Boker's bitters (optional)
review: Scotch diluted and delicately sweetened with added almond notes - simple but tasty. Proportions range from equal parts (45ml scotch to 45ml amaretto) to 4:1 (60ml scotch to 15ml amaretto), and even as dry as 8:1 (60ml scotch to 7.5ml amaretto), but we find 3:1 (60ml scotch to 20ml amaretto) is just enough amaretto to take the edge off the scotch and add a pleasing almondy note without overpowering the flavour of the whisky.
history:
The Godfather is one of the enduring classics to emerge from the 1970s. It's basically an Old-Fashioned with attitude – the attitude being: why sweeten with mere sugar when you can use a flavoursome liqueur.

The appearance of the whole 'God damn' cocktail family in Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide, and numerous cocktail books from the 1980s, is testament to the Godfather being a 1970s cocktail. Indeed, this cocktail is eponymously named after the Italian-American Mafia book and film trilogy, The Godfather. Mario Puzo's novel was published in 1969 and Francis Ford Coppola's first film followed in March 1972, the highest-grossing film of the year, and for some years after.

The earliest recipe book mention of the Godfather (and also the Godmother and French Connection) is in Brian F. Rea's 1976 Brian's Booze Guide with one part amaretto to one-and-a-half parts Scotch.

name: Kamikaze
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A bite-sized vodka take on the Margarita.

name: Limoncello Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: If you like the liqueur, you'll love the cocktail.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2005 by Francesco at Mix, New York City, USA.

name: Maple Leaf
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Maple syrup
review: Anything from 10ml (1/3oz) to 15ml (1/2oz) maple syrup works in this recipe, depending on your maple syrup, lemons and personal taste. I've gone for the middle of the road at 12.5ml as for me the trio combines wonderfully with the maple syrup still in something of a supporting role.
history: I suspect this cocktail originated in the USA or the even UK and, as far as I'm aware, (please send me info if you know differently,) this cocktail was always based on bourbon whiskey. If it had been created by a Canadian, where the maple leaf is very much a national symbol, then it's likely a Canadian rye whisky, arguably more appropriate, would have been used.

name: Mauresque
preparation: POUR absinthe and almond syrup into glass. Ideally, serve iced water separately in a small jug (known in France as a 'broc') so the customer can dilute to their own taste. Lastly, add ice to fill the glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2⁄3 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
4 shot	Chilled water
review: Long, refreshing aniseed, liquorice and almond.
history: Pronounced 'Mor-Esk', this classic drink is very popular in the South of France, where it is now commonly made with pastis in place of absinthe. It was originally created by French soldiers serving in the Bataillon d'Afrique during the Algerian campaign of the 1830s and 40s, and was alternatively known as Bureau Arabe after the military department which dealt with local affairs and was said to act like 'an iron fist in a velvet glove'.

name: Miami Beach
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Fruity and frothy topped. Like Baywatch!

name: Nantucket
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
2 1⁄2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Essentially a Seabreeze with rum in place of vodka.
history: Popularised by the USA Cheers Bar chain, this is named after the beautiful island off Cape Cod.

name: Navigator
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
1 1⁄4 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
review: This fruity, grapefruit-led drink is pleasantly bitter and sour.
history: Created in 2005 by Jamie Terrell, London, England.

name: Ole Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Licor 43 Original liqueur
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Cognac and orange with rich vanilla and delicate spice.

name: Passion Fruit Martini (simple)
preparation: Cut 2 passion fruits in half and put one half aside for the garnish. Scoop the flesh out the other 3 halves of fruit into shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 fresh	Passion fruit (fresh)
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Very fruity, slightly sweet, easy drinking and vodka-laced.

name: Seabreeze
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
2 1⁄2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Many don't bother to shake this simple drink, instead simply "building" by pouring ingredients into ice-filled glass and then briefly stirring to mix.
history: Marketing by Absolut Vodka and Ocean Spray helped drive this cocktail's popularity throughout the 1990s but the Seabreeze may have originated in the 1980s or even 1960s along with the Harpoon.

name: Showbiz
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
2⁄3 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
1 1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Sweet cassis soured with grapefruit and fortified with vodka.

name: Testarossa
preparation: POUR all ingredients into glass, then fill with ice.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
3 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Bittersweet liqueur and soda with vodka providing some oomph.

name: Two 'T' Fruity
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄3 shot	Passion fruit syrup
3 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Simple is beautiful - this drink is both. The rawness of vodka is balanced with sweet passion fruit and hints of orange bitters.
history: Created in 2002 at Hush, London, England.

name: American Breakfast
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Maple syrup
review: This citrus fresh bourbon-laced drink would be great with your morning muesli.

name: Beverly Hills Hotel Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Zingy grapefruit sourness balances rich elderflower in this gin-laced cocktail which you might consider enjoying with your breakfast. That's how they rock in Beverly Hills!
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2007 by Philip Spee at The Beverly Hills Hotel, California, USA.

name: Elder & Wiser
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Elderflower liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review: Apple and elderflower combine well with whiskey.
history: Created in 2006 by yours truly and named for its original base, Wiser's Canadian whisky with elder-flower liqueur.

name: Haydenistic
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄6 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
review: Extremely subtle, like a very complex wet Vodkatini.
history: Created in 2007 by Hayden Lambert at The Merchant Hotel, Belfast, Northern Ireland.

name: Parisian Sidecar
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: An elderflower-flavoured Sidecar.
history:
Created in 2006 by yours truly.
Sidecar cocktail history

name: Scottish Gypsy
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
2⁄3 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Scotch and Bénédictine complement each other in this herbal cocktail which is balanced by the addition of bitters.

name: Unicar
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A mismade but fabulously balanced Sidecar inspired this drink.
history: Inspired by a drink discovered in May 2010 at Babel Bar, Hotel du Rome, Berlin, Germany. Named after a combination of 'Sidecar' and 'Ugni-blanc', the grape from which cognac is most commonly made.

name: Bourbon Skin
preparation: Place barspoon in warmed glass. POUR all ingredients into warmed glass and STIR.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3 shot	Boiling water
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Hot, watered down bourbon stirred with orange oils. Simple but very tasty.
history: The only difference between a 'skin' and a 'toddy' is the addition of citrus peel to a skin.

name: Elder Fashion
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and STIR.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Elderflower liqueur
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Spirit-forward and cleansing with gin, floral elderflower with zesty citrus.
history: Created by in 2007 by Phil Ward at Death & Co in New York City, USA.

name: Mexican Squeeze
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and lightly stir.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
4 shot	Lemonade
review: The success of this cocktail is as much about the quality of your tequila as it is about your choice of lemonade. Made well and this Squeeze is zesty, balanced and very refreshing.

name: O' Flower Highball
garnish: Lemon zest twist & mint sprig bouquet
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄3 shot	Elderflower liqueur
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Elderflower liqueur adds a delicate floral note to a scotch whisky highball.
history: For more information on Highball cocktails, their history and tips on the perfect serve.

name: Drink Without A Name
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄12 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
review: To say this nameless cocktail is "spirit-led" is an understatement but, as with a Martini, achieve a sufficiently cold serving temperature and you'll enjoy vodka with orange and delicate herbal nuances.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 1990 by Paul Harrington at The Townhouse, Emeryville, California, USA.

name: Spumoni
preparation: POUR first 2 ingredients into glass and STIR. Add ice and TOP with tonic.
ingredients:
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Ruby red grapefruit
3 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: Bittersweet and citrusy. As good with breakfast as it is as an aperitivo.
history:
Spumoni is a popular low alcohol cocktail in Japan, particularly in Tokyo, so much so that Suntory marketed a canned Spumoni cocktail. Spumoni naturally featured in an episode of the Japanese Bartender anime television series where it was noticed by New York bartender, Jon Mullen who made his own version of the Spumoni at Bar Pisellino. Mullen's version has since become something of a contemporary classic in the USA.

Jon Mullen's Spumoni
Glass: Collins
Garnish: Cracked pink peppercorns
Method: Pour all ingredients into glass and briefly stir to combine.
45 ml (1½ oz) Campari
15 ml (½ oz) Dry gin (originally Neversink Gin)
5 ml (1 barspoon) Pink peppercorn syrup*
45 ml (1½ oz) Tonic water (originally Fever-Tree Indian Tonic)
45 ml (1½ oz) Ruby red grapefruit juice

*To make pink peppercorn syrup, simmer the following for 20 minutes:
1 cup water
1 cup white sugar
1/3 cup muddled pink peppercorns
zest of one ruby red grapefruit
1 tablespoon of grated ginger
Cover and leave to stand until cool, then fine strain into a suitable container such as a Kilner jar. Seal and store refrigerated for up to one month.

name: Garden G&T
garnish: Elderflower blossom when in season, mint sprig bouquet & lime slice
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
3 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: A G&T wit a splash of elderflower liqueur.

name: Elderflower Gimlet
garnish: Half lime wheel slice &/or elderflower blossom when in season
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Gin-laced tart lime balanced and flavoured by rich elderflower liqueur.
history: A riff on the classic Gimlet.

name: Italian Coffee
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) and dust surface with freshly grated nutmeg
preparation: POUR first two ingredients into pre-warmed heat-proof glass. TOP with warmed whipped/shaken cream.
ingredients:
1 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
2 2⁄3 shot	Filter coffee (hot)
1⁄2 shot	Double cream / heavy cream
review: Mildly alcoholic coffee and cream. Beats a regular coffee after a meal.

name: Apparent Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
3⁄4 shot	Elderflower liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Intensely flavoured and bittersweet with rich floral elderflower struggling for attention against assertive citrus and amaro. Originally served straight-up in a sour or coupe glass but better on-the-rocks.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2010 by Bobby Heugel of Anvil Bar and Refuge in Houston, Texas, USA.

name: Italian Espresso Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Averna Amaro
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
review: This low alc./vol. riff on Dick Bradsell's Espresso Martini may lack the oomph of a base spirit but generous amaro does add pleasing herbal bittersweetness.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2022 by Nicholas Boden at Tavernonna Italian Kitchen, Hotel Phillips in Kansas City, Missouri, USA.

name: B & B
preparation: STIR ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
5⁄6 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
review: Honeyed and spiced brandy. Traditionally mixed in equal parts proportions but I prefer slightly drier with a touch more brandy than Bénédictine. The ice will add dilution with time but some, depending on the ice being used, may want to add 10ml (1/3oz) or more chilled water prior to mixing.
history: Bénédictine and various types of brandy have long been mixed together and combo first enters cocktail books in the early 1900s as a pousse-café layered cocktail with the brandy floated over the liqueur.

name: Black Russian
garnish: Lemon slice & Luxardo Maraschino cherry on stick (sail)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
review: This popular cocktail is simple but tasty. Try with just a splash of cola (rather than also with the cream that makes a Colorado Bulldog).
history: Created in 1949 by Gustave Tops, a bartender at Metropolitan Hotel in Brussels, for Perle Skirvin Mesta, the U.S. ambassador to Luxembourg (1949-1953). She was a rich American socialite famous for her lavish parties, and as well as the cocktail, Perle was the inspiration for Irving Berlin's Broadway musical Call Me Madam and she appeared on the cover of TIME magazine in March 1949. She was the original "Hostess with the Mostess."

name: Remsen Cooler
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass and serve with straws.
ingredients:
2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
3 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Scotch and soda for the sophisticate.
history: Originally, circa 1890, it was made with Old Tom gin, but in more recent decades, more commonly based on Scotch whisky. The first recipe book to include a Remsen Cooler was Hon. William Boothby's 1891 Cocktail Boothby's American Bar-Tender.

name: The Surfer
preparation: POUR lemonade into ice-filled glass to two-thirds full. FLOAT cognac over lemonade. Serve with straws and instruct drinker to stir ingredients before drinking.
ingredients:
4 shot	Lemonade
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
review: Simple but tasty and very refreshing. The use of good ice and a quality lemonade is essential to this drink's success.
history: Created in 2008 by yours truly. The original Cognac Surfer is made by floating cognac on mineral water.

name: French Connection
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Disaronno amaretto
review: The apricot and almond notes in amaretto combine perfectly with brandy in this simple cocktail.
history: Named after the 1971 American crime thriller film, The French Connection, this brandy-based cocktail is a sibling of the better-known Scotch whisky-based Godfather. Both cocktails, along with the similar vodka-based Godmother, appear in Brian F. Rea's 1976 Brian's Booze Guide.

name: Tonic Boom
preparation: POUR tonic water into old-fashioned glass. Then POUR gin into shot glass. Instruct drinker to hold gin-filled shot glass directly over surface of tonic water and drop shot into old-fashioned glass and consume.
ingredients:
6 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
review: Essentially a gin and tonic bomb. To quote a Portobello Star regular, "the thinking man's Jager Bomb".
history: Created in 2010 by Edward 'Teddy' McPartland at The Portobello Star, London, England.

name: Vodka Soda
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass and lightly stir (so as not to lose fizz). Don't serve with straws.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
5 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review:
Dry and refreshing with a pleasant minerality.

The proportion of soda water to vodka in this recipe is 2.5 to 1 (a ratio that appears to have the widest appeal) consisting of one 150 ml can of soda water to 60 ml vodka = 210ml plus ice melt total liquid in glass. If using a 12oz glass (350ml to fill level), the ice displacement = approximately 140ml, so ice forms 40% of the contents of the glass. To raise the percentage of ice to the ideal of around 50%, you should use a 14oz Collins glass or a Spanish-style Copa glass.

name: Carajillo
garnish: Float 3 coffee beans on the surface
preparation:
To make a shaken ("shakeado") Carajillo, SHAKE 45ml (1½oz) freshly brewed espresso coffee and 45ml (1½oz) liqueur with ice and fine strain into a chilled coupe glass.

OR, to make a layered ("puesto") Carajillo, POUR 50ml (1 2⁄3oz) liqueur into an ice-filled old-fashioned or stemmed bulbous glass (Copa glass), then carefully float 40ml (1 1⁄3) coffee over the liqueur.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Licor 43 Original liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
review: Carajilo, coffee and liquor or spirit is a popular serve in Mexico. Licor 43 is one of the preferred liqueurs in this cocktail due to its delicately spiced rich vanilla notes combining well with coffee. Your choice of espresso coffee will influence how well the bitter coffee balances the sweet liqueur.
history:
The Carajillo is a Spanish cocktail thought to have been created by Spanish troops in Cuba when the country was a Spanish province, who mixed coffee with rum to give them courage. 'Coraje' means courage in Spanish, and its diminutive form is corajillo. ( In Catalan, the Carajillo is called Cigaló.)

The Carajillo is popular in Spain, where its form varies by region, from simply pouring brandy into an espresso to heating brandy with lemon juice/zest, sugar and cinnamon, then adding coffee. It is also popular in its simplest form in Latin American countries, such as Colombia and Venezuela, and in Cuba, where coffee is mixed with rum rather than brandy.

An American version of the Carajillo combines a double measure of espresso coffee with chocolate liqueur in an ice-filled brandy balloon, topped with whipped cream. Another version is served with a caramelised sugar rim with rum, triple sec, coffee and whipped cream.

However, it is in Mexico where (since circa 2015) the Carajillo has exploded in popularity. Here, it is served shaken ("shakeado") or layered ("puesto").

Its popularity in Mexico has been helped by promotions by Licor 43 Liqueur; by far the most popular liqueur used to make a Carajillo. Indeed, this cocktail was added to Difford's Guide in 2019 due to Licor 43 informing us of its popularity and sending us a glass in which to photograph the layered version.

name: Seven & Seven Highball
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3 1⁄2 shot	Lemon-lime soda (Sprite/7-Up)
review: Whiskey and lemon-lime soda. It might lack sophistication but it's easy and tasty.
history: Traditionally made with Seagram 7 Crown Whiskey topped with 7-Up, this drink propelled Seagram 7 to being America's best-selling spirits brand in 1947, a position it maintained until in the early 1990s and the vodka boom.

name: The Boss
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
5⁄6 shot	Disaronno amaretto
review: Amaretto brilliantly enriches bourbon. I tried adding a couple of dashes of bitters but found myself preferring the simplicity of just the two ingredients.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide:

name: Godchild
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Disaronno amaretto
review: Amaretto delicately flavours and sweetens cognac.
history: One of "The God(father)" trilogy of cocktails, the Godchild is predated by the very similar French Connection. According to Mark Torre's 1987 The Bartenders Cherry, the difference between a Godchild and a French Connection is that a Godchild is made with brandy of unstipulated origin while a French Connection specifically calls for cognac brandy in a Snifter glass.

name: Long Island Iced Tea
preparation: SHAKE first 8 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with cola.
ingredients:
5⁄12 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
5⁄12 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄12 shot	Ketel One Vodka
5⁄12 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
5⁄12 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
5⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
5⁄12 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 shot	Cola (e.g. Coca Cola or Pepsi Cola)
review: A cooling, combination of four different white spirits, triple sec, lemon and lime, crowned with a splash of cola.
history:
This infamous drink reached the height of its popularity in the early 1980s and by 1985 The New York Times reported, "A potent alcoholic drink called Long Island Iced Tea is sweeping the Island's bars as well as watering spots across the country."

Of the many stories surrounding its origin, perhaps the most credible attributes its creation to the 1970s, perhaps 1972, by Robert "Rosebud" Butt at Oak Beach Inn in Babylon, New York. This area of New York State is known as Long Island and the drink resembles an iced tea, so disguising its alcoholic contents – a fact that has many claiming its true origins go back to Prohibition.

name: Banana Flambé
preparation: In a shallow small pan, heat the banana with orange juice, sugar and cinnamon until the banana softens and the orange juice reduces. Add cognac and flambé further. MUDDLE banana in the base of shaker, add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 fresh	Banana (preferably overripe)
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1 barspoon	Caster/ Superfine/Baker's special sugar (white)
2 pinch	Cinnamon powder (ground)
1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Cachaça
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: As Tony says "it's worth it".
history: Created in 2008 by Mauricio 'Tony' Harion from Mixing Bar Consulting, Belo Horizonte, Brazil.

name: Full Monte
preparation: SHAKE first eight ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with champagne, lightly stir and serve with straws.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
Top up with	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Champagne replaces cola and maraschino liqueur replaces triple sec in this sophisticated adaptation of a Long Island Iced Tea.
history: Created by Audrey Saunders at Pegu Club, New York City, USA.

name: Adios, Motherfucker
garnish: Lemon slice & Luxardo Maraschino cherry sail
preparation: SHAKE first 8 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with lemon-lime soda.
ingredients:
5⁄12 shot	Ketel One Vodka
5⁄12 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄12 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
5⁄12 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
5⁄12 shot	De Kuyper Blue Curaçao
5⁄12 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 1⁄3 shot	Lemon-lime soda (Sprite/7-Up)
review: A blued Long Island Iced Tea by both colour and language.

name: Mai Tai (Beaumont-Gantt's)
preparation: Lightly muddle mint in base of shaker (just to bruise). Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
12 fresh	Mint leaves
1 1⁄2 shot	Jamaican-style overproof aged pot still rum
1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
history:
It is claimed that Ernest Raymond Beaumont-Gantt first served this cocktail in 1933 at his Don The Beachcomber's bar in Hollywood, California. This is eleven years earlier than Victor "Trader Vic" Bergeron's Mai Tai origin story.

In his 2014 Potions of the Caribbean, Jeff Berry recounts that Don "told Edward Brownlee [a Tiki-carver and friend of Don] that Vic had derived the Mai Tai's flavour profile from a punch that Vic had particularly liked at the Beachcomber's: "The Q.B. Cooler was the basis for a cocktail he took with him, and he called it the Mai Tai." Fred Fung, who worked as Vic's executive assistant for 41 years, disagrees. "Vic did copy Don The Beachcomber's look. He did go down and copy. But the Mai Tai, he did concoct that, and Carrie Guild did name it."

name: Smoked Salty Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
1 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
1 pinch	Salt (sea salt)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Salty Islay peaty malt and Green Chartreuse influence this Scotch whisky sour.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2014 by Dennis Wolf at Bar Raclette, Puerto Rico.

name: Early Evening Fizz
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discard) Lemon wedge & Luxardo maraschino cherry.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass (no ice in glass). POUR soda into drink slowly from a height in order to build a (Ramos Gin Fizz style) thick foamy head. Serve with a straw.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 pinch	Salt (sea salt)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white
2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Cognac, chartreuse, sloe gin and lemon juice served in a tall foaming fizz – its name inspired by the Morning Glory Fizz.
history: Created in 2015 by Nick Caputo at Sovereign Loss in Brixton, England

name: Conquistador
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄8 shot	Agave syrup
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Aged rum provides oaky richness, while tequila adds earthy minerality to this delicious split spirit base and split citrus sour. I've added a splash of agave syrup to lift this cocktail from perhaps being overly on the sour side.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2008 by Sam Ross at Milk & Honey, New York City, USA. The Conquistador was first published in Jim Meehan's 2011 The PDT Cocktail Book.

name: Long Island Iced Town Hall Tea
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Averna Amaro
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: This spirituous, bittersweet, after-dinner digestivo/late-night sipper is a very different animal to other cocktails that share the Long Island moniker.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2012 by Jamal Robinson at Town Hall restaurant in San Francisco, USA.

name: Flying Tigre Coctel
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water (reduce if wet ice)
review: Light, aromatic and complex - one to sip.
history: Adapted from a recipe in the 1949 edition of Esquire's Handbook for Hosts. The drink is credited to an unnamed Captain serving in the US Marines, Amphibious Group Seven, at Santiago de Cuba in 1942.

name: Jackie O's Rose
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄24 shot	Rose water
4 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: In its simplest form, this is a Daiquiri with added triple sec and rose water - or a Margarita with rum. Whatever, it's a good balance of sweet and sour.
history:
I don't know the origin of this cocktail, but in March 2021, I revisited the recipe to arrive at the above. Our/the original recipe:
60ml (2oz) Light white rum
15ml (½oz) Triple sec
30ml (1oz) Lime juice
15ml (½oz) Sugar syrup
2.5ml (½ spoon) Rosewater

name: Marama Rum Punch
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE mint (just to bruise). Add next five ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with lemonade, lightly stir and serve with straws.
ingredients:
12 fresh	Mint leaves
1 1⁄2 shot	White overproof rum
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
Top up with	Lemon-lime soda (Sprite/7-Up)
review: A tangy, well-balanced punch.

name: Morning Glory
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄6 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Sophisticated and complex - one for sipping.
history: My interpretation of a classic.

name: Tantris Sidecar No.1
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄4 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A Sidecar with extra interest courtesy of Chartreuse, pineapple and Calvados.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2000 by Audrey Saunders at Beacon in New York City, USA.
Sidecar history.

name: Alabazam
preparation: SHAKE first 6 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: This long, fruity cocktail packs a cognac-charged punch, but as the ice melts, it mellows and becomes refreshing.
history: The first known reference to a cocktail of this name appears in Leo-Engel's 1880 American Other Drinks.

name: Blue Hawaii
garnish: Pineapple wedge, Luxardo Maraschino cherry, paper parasol and straw
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
3⁄4 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Blue Curaçao
3 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Aloha!
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 1957 by Harry K. Yee at Henry Kaiser's Hawaiian Village Hotel (latterly the Hilton) in Waikiki, Oahu, Hawaii. The drink, created at the behest of Bols to aid sales of their blue curaçao, is named after the hit song from the 1937 Bing Crosby film, Waikiki Wedding, and not after what is generously described as a "musical-comedy" Elvis Presley 1961 film of the same name. That said, the Elvis film probably contributed to this cocktail's popularity.

name: Cloysters
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice & fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
4 drop	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters (optional)
1⁄4 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: There's a suitable subtle monastic influence to this complex, gin-based, most learned of cocktails.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2007 by John Deragon at PDT bar in New York City, USA. Perhaps named after the Pokémon "Cloyster", this is a gin-heavy riff on the earlier (circa 1970) Cloister cocktail.

garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) to emulsify and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
3⁄4 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Fantastically complex with notes of rum, maraschino, sherry and orange.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2008 by Scott Ingram at MC Bar, Abode Hotel, Glasgow, Scotland. The name is a reference to the year when Facundo M. Bacardi established his first distillery.

name: Smokin Rose
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Lanique Spirit of Rose liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄4 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A Daiquiri riff with Islay malt, rose petal liqueur and vanilla.
history: Created in 2008 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room in London, England.

name: Dopo Cena
preparation: DRY SHAKE all ingredients (without ice). SHAKE again with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1 shot	Kirschwasser (cherry) eau-de-vie
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 barspoon	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix) (2 sugar to 1 water)
1 dash	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Under the white head lies a dessert cocktail (Dopo Cena is Italian for 'after dinner') with aromatic cherry and marzipan flavours.
history: Created by Adrian Gomes, 10 Dollar Shake, Aberdeen, Scotland.

name: Suit & Tai
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients and strain into glass filled with crushed ice and serve with short straws.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Cognac (brandy)
5⁄6 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A Tiki-styled drink based on aged rum and cognac with lime juice, orange liqueur and almond syrup.
history: Created in 2015 by Matthew Neale at Harbour Kitchen, Torquay, England.

name: Elements
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
6 fresh	Basil leaves
1 2⁄3 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄6 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
history: Greek Bacardí Legacy 2014 winning cocktail created by Stelios Papadopoulos at 'Amigos' Mexican Bar-Restaurant in Athens, Greece.

name: Dutch Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: A floral orangey riff on a vodka sour.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Tess Posthumus, Amsterdam, The Netherlands. Tess' original recipe called for orange syrup rather than orange curaçao and sugar syrup.

name: Zima Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bison grass vodka
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Passion fruit syrup
1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
3 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Aromatic and perfumed, bison grass, apple, sour lemon and rich passion fruit combine in this lightly sweet and fruity cocktail.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created by Robb Collins, Group Head Bartender at London Cocktail Club, London, England.

"I created this in 2013 for the Monin 'Twist Your Classics' Competition which I won. To this day I think it's the best drink I have ever created, so light and silky, yet amazing depth of flavour and definitely a drink you can have a few of."

name: The Lemon Peel
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Strega liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Just as the name promises, this tall superbly refreshing cocktail delivers intense zesty citrus but is balanced and quaffable. A drink for a scorching hot summer's afternoon.

name: Art of Choke
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE (just to bruise) mint in base of mixing glass. Add other ingredients, STIR with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
8 fresh	Mint leaves
1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄4 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
1⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A bittersweet cocktail that's best enjoyed as an aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2008 by Kyle Davidson at The Violet Hour in Chicago, USA. As for the name, say it again while remembering the original recipe calls for Cynar, a liqueur flavoured with artichoke leaves.

name: Sahara Cubano
preparation: STIR first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with tonic, FLOAT absinthe and dashes of bitters.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
1 1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Agave syrup
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
1⁄6 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Sip your way through a layer of absinthe to a citrus and cacao influenced rum and tonic. This long drink won't appeal to all but some will dive right in.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Rogerio Igarashi at Bar Trench in Tokyo, Japan.

name: Running Through Orchards
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Spiced Pear liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Vodka-laced pear and cleansing citrus.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Brad Fry of Michael's Restaurant Group in Long Beach, California, USA.

name: Barnum Was Right
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water) (optional)
review: A gin apricot sour balanced and favoured with generous dashes of aromatic bitters.
history:
Named for Barnum Was Right, a 1929 American comedy film released with sounds and also as a silent version for theatres not wired for sound. Only the silent version serves.

Adapted from a recipe in Crosby Gaige's 1941 Crosby Gaige's Cocktail Guide & Ladies' Companion.

name: Byzantine
preparation: MUDDLE basil in base of shaker. Add other ingredients apart from tonic water, SHAKE with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with tonic water.
ingredients:
6 fresh	Basil leaves
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Passion fruit syrup
1⁄2 shot	Lime & lemongrass cordial
2 shot	Pineapple juice
Top up with	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: This fruity, herbal drink is even better made the way Douglas originally intended, with basil infused gin instead of muddled leaves.
history: Created in 2001 by Douglas Ankrah for Akbar, Soho, London, England.

name: Cameron's Kick
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Faintly peaty honeyed whisky with a cleansing hint of lemon, rounded by almond. Classically, egg white is not used, but like many sours, the Cameron's Kick is better with egg white.
history: The Cameron's Kick first appears in Harry MacElhone's 1922 ABC of Mixing Cocktails and is repeated in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Derby Fizz
preparation:
STIR lemon juice and sugar in base of shaker until sugar is dissolved. Add Scotch and orange curaçao, SHAKE with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and slowly pour 2/3rds of the contents of the shaker from a higher than normal height into a chilled empty glass (no ice in glass) while simultaneously pouring soda with your other hand. The cocktail and soda should form a single stream of liquid falling into the glass.

As when pouring a Guinness, to achieve a perfect head on a Derby Fizz, the cocktail should be left to settle for at least a minute before topping off with what remains in the shaker. Ideally, during the settling period, the glass should be placed in a glass froster/fridge/freezer. As the final contents of the shaker are poured into the glass so the head should rise like a soufflé.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 barspoon	Powdered sugar (white sugar ground in mortar and pestle)
2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄4 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Egg white
2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: The "Derby" in the name may suggest Kentucky bourbon and that this fizz should be made with bourbon (indeed it can be), but the nuances of the orange curaçao fit better with Scotch whisky.
history: The Derby Fizz is said to first appear in the 1934 Old Mr. Boston Bartender's Guide, but it's not in the pamphlet-like 1934 edition I own. It is one of the cocktails mentioned in the "supplementary list" in the back of William James "Billy" Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Bar Book but alas without a recipe.

name: Dolce Havana
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A bittersweet, rum-laced melange of Mediterranean fruit.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2000 by Fabrizio Musorella at the Library Bar in the Lanesborough Hotel, London, England.

name: Dyevitchka
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
4 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters (optional)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Pineapple replaces cranberry in this Cosmopolitan-like cocktail.
history: 'Dyevitchka', the Russian word for 'young woman', became known in the West due to its being used in the 1971 novel A Clockwork Orange.

name: Fu Manchu Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe
3⁄4 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: A Natural Daiquiri with a refreshing, clean, citrusy, minty edge.
history: Adapted from a recipe in David A. Embury's 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks.

name: Gin Gin Mule
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into glass. TOP with ginger beer, and then fill glass with ice.
ingredients:
12 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Ginger liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: Zingy ginger and gin's botanical notes make this much more than just another take on the Moscow Mule.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2000 by Audrey Saunders at Beacon, New York City, USA. Audreys's original (and our previous) recipe calls for muddled fresh ginger and sugar syrup (rather than ginger liqueur):
- 2 slice Fresh ginger root (thumbnail-sized)
- 60ml (2oz) Gin
- 15ml (½oz) Lime juice
- 7.5ml (¼oz) Sugar syrup
- 12 fresh Mint leaves
- 82.5ml (2¾oz)Top with Ginger beer

name: Ginger Cocktail
preparation: MUDDLE ginger in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 slice	Fresh ginger root (thumbnail-sized slice)
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Ginger wine
3⁄4 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: This Martini may be served chilled but its flavour is distinctly warming.
history: Discovered in 2003 at Hurricane Bar and Grill, Edinburgh, Scotland.

name: Ginger Mojito
preparation: MUDDLE ginger in base of shaker. Add mint and lightly MUDDLE (just to bruise). Add next three ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into glass filled with crushed ice. TOP with ginger ale.
ingredients:
3 slice	Fresh ginger root (thumbnail-sized slice)
12 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
review: A spiced variation on the classic Mojito.
history: For more recipes, its origins and history, see the Mojito Cocktail.

name: Grand Sazerac
preparation: POUR absinthe into ice-filled glass and TOP with water. Leave the mixture to stand in the glass. Separately, STIR other ingredients with ice. Finally, discard contents of absinthe-washed glass and strain contents of shaker into absinthe-washed glass. (No ice in the finished drink.)
ingredients:
1⁄3 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
Top up with	Chilled water
1 1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
3 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: An orange twist on the classic Sazerac.
history:
Created in 2004 by yours truly in London, England.
Sazerac cocktail history and recipe variations

name: Jack Punch
preparation: Cut passion fruit in half and scoop flesh into shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 fresh	Passion fruit (fresh)
2 shot	Tennessee whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Licor 43 Original liqueur
3 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
