name: Jockey Club
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:

2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura

history:
Adapted from a recipe which first appears in Harry McElhone's 1922 Harry's ABC of Mixing Cocktails and established as being the default recipe thanks to its being repeated by Harry Craddock in his influential 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

However, a "Jockey Club cocktail" is first mentioned in the Friday 1st September 1882 edition of The Greenville Journal as being an alternative name for a Manhattan. Quite different and unrelated cocktails named "Jockey Club" also appear in Edward Spenser's 1903 The Flowing Bowl (equal parts gin and vermouth with gum syrup, Angostura, and raspberry syrup) and Tim Daly's 1903 Daly's Bartenders Encyclopedia (equal parts Jamaican rum and vermouth with dashes of Kümmel , gum syrup and Angostura bitters).

name: Turquoise Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

name: Boxcar
garnish: Sugar rim & orange zest twist (expressed & then discarded)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:

1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)

review: A White Lady in a sugar-rimmed glass with the addition of a dash of grenadine and substituting lime juice for lemon.

name: Embassy Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Jamaican aged blended rum with funk
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: The Daiquiri and Sidecar's lovechild. Some add aromatic bitters, but it's better without, as this allows the rum and brandy interplay to shine. However, like a Daiquiri, the Embassy opens with a touch of dilution, so, depending on your ice, consider adding a splash of water.
history:
Adapted from a recipe in Buzza-Cardozo of Hollywood's 1933 book Hollywood Cocktails: Over 200 Excellent Recipes, this cocktail is thought to have been created at the Prohibition-era Embassy Club in Hollywood, a speakeasy opened in 1928 by Adolph "Eddie" Brandstatter (1886-19400). One of Hollywood's leading restaurateurs, he owned Café Montemartre at 6757 Hollywood Boulevard and his Embassy Club was a private venue exclusive to fee-paying Hollywood stars and glitterati. To quote the Los Angeles Times, " He had the "Brandstatter touch": one part dapper European suavity - he brought a sheen of elegance to the rough-edged Hollywood of the 1920s - and one part straight-up charisma. Wherever Eddie was, that was the party."

However, some believe the Embassy Cocktail was created at the Embassy Club in London rather than any of the numerous American clubs with the same name. Robert Vermeire, author of the 1922 Cocktails: How to Mix Them worked at London's Embassy Club, indeed the title page says "By Robert of the Embassy Club", but his book (published in London) doesn't include a cocktail named Embassy.

The "Embassy Cocktail" does appear in William T. "Cocktail Bill" Boothby's 1934 The World Drinks and how to mix them, but without attribution. Tellingly this book was published in San Francisco, California – the same state where I'm sure this cocktail emerged after the 1928 opening of Hollywood's Embassy Club.

name: Huapala

Created in 2006 by yours truly in London, England.
Sidecar history

name: Comet Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄4 shot	Drambuie liqueur
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: This riff on the Sidecar is lighter, less tart, and altogether more approachable than the original, but some may find it lacks the original's cleansing zesty bite.
history:
Created in 1952 by Eddie "King Cocktail" Clarke at the Albany Club, Albermarle Street, London, England. Made to honour the first-ever jet aircraft to fly a commercial route. The de Havilland DH 106 Comet was developed and manufactured by de Havilland at its Hatfield Aerodrome, Hertfordshire, England. The Comet 1 prototype, registered G-ALYP ("Yoke Peter") first flew on 27th July 1949. This same aircraft, on 2nd May 1952 took off from London bound for Johannesburg on a scheduled BOAC service as the world's first jetliner flight with fare-paying passengers.

Eddie Clarke's original recipe called for Van der Hum, a South African orange liqueur, undoubtedly selected by Eddie due to the destination of that inaugural flight. The use of equal parts triple sec and Drambuie is an accepted substitution but leaves this cocktail on the bitter side, hence I've added a spoon of sugar syrup.

history: Adapted from a recipe discovered in May 2010 at Stagger Lee bar in Berlin, Germany

name: Papa Ghirardelli
preparation: SHAKE first five ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: This cocktail is named after the founder of Ghirardelli Chocolate Company, Domingo Ghirardelli, an Italian-born man who moved to Peru and ran a successful confectionery business and, following the gold rush, ultimately ended up in San Francisco. He went on to found Ghirardely & Girard (later changed to the Ghirardelli Chocolate Company), which has been in continuous operation since 1852. In his own way, Ghirardelli helped build and shape San Francisco, and his company has become synonymous with the city. Ghirardelli Square, which his company-built, has been an official city landmark since 1965.
history: Adapted from a drink which was the signature cocktail of San Francisco Cocktail Week 21-27 September 2010.

history: Yet again I must thank drinks historian David Wondrich for unearthing this drink and its history. It was created by a bartender named Jim Maloney and first appeared in his 1903 book How to Mix Drinks. Maloney patented the name 'Bell-Ringers' as referring to cocktails served in glasses rinsed with apricot brandy.

history:
Created in 2010 by Dick Bradsell at The Pink Chihuahua at El Camion, London, England.

This fluffy little pink drink is named Chihuahua (Spanish: Chihuahueño) after the smallest breed of dog and also the state of Mexico. At El Camion, the front door is painted with an artist's impression of a pink Chihuahua.

name: The Modern

name: Silk Road

name: Northern Glow

2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: A bourbon sour made fruity with cherry brandy.

name: A Few of My Favourite Things
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
1⁄3 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1⁄6 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Bittersweet with zesty citrus, rich sherry, cognac and faint herbal Chartreuse.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Dale Bebington at Hawksmoor Air Street, London, England. Dale’s original recipe specifies Martell Cordon Bleu cognac.

name: Continental Exchange
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Akashi-Tai Shiraume Ginjo Umeshu
5⁄6 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Ginger syrup
1⁄6 shot	Honey
review: Long and refreshing with subtle flavours of apple, lemon, ginger and plum wine combining well with the cognac base.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Kieran Grieves at Bamboo Door in Sheffield, England.

name: Pleasure to Tell
garnish: Orange zest twist & Luxardo maraschino cherry sprayed with chocolate bitters
preparation: STIR first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Disaronno amaretto
4 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: A stirred cognac-based after dinner drink with rich cherry notes and subtle almond and chocolate, freshened with orange oils.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2015 by Jolanta Ewa Malczewska at Holmen Bar in Stavanger, Norway.

name: Grape Expectations
preparation: POUR all ingredients into glass with two-thirds crushed ice and SWIZZLE. Top with crushed ice and serve with a straw.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Lanique Spirit of Rose liqueur

2⁄3 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A rose, Sauvignon Blanc wine, apple and lemon Cognac Swizzle. Fruity, floral and refreshing.
history: Created in 2015 by Ehren Khoo-Steel at The Blind Pig, St Helier, Jersey.

name: The Epicurean
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

1 2⁄3 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
4 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 barspoon	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur

history: French Bacardí Legacy 2016 winning cocktail winning cocktail by Matthieu Henry, Le Comptior De La Bourse, Lyon.

name: Merry Widow Fizz
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and strain into chilled glass (no ice). TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin

1 barspoon	Powdered sugar (white sugar ground in mortar and pestle) (or use 5ml of 2:1 sugar syrup per spoon)

3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water

history: Adapted from a recipe in Stan Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Bar Guide.

name: Witches' Yellow Flip
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Strega liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 fresh	Egg yolk
review: Strega liqueur and citrus juice fortified with cognac flavour this aptly named flip.

name: Like A Lady
preparation: MUDDLE cucumber in base of shaker. ADD other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:

1 1⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)

1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer

Michael says it is "based on one of the first Gin cocktails I ever had during my early days at The Refectory Bar at The Plymouth Gin Distillery. Swapping out orange liqueur to make a simple savoury twist on the classic White Lady."

name: Summer Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into ice-filled glass.

name: Platinum Blond

3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin

Straub's Stone Sour is also differentiated from later renditions by its being frappé.

name: A.B.C. Cocktail
garnish: Lemon zest twist & Luxardo Maraschino cherry

ingredients:

review: A John Collins with lime in place of lemon and sweetened with apple and elderflower liqueurs.
history:
Created in 2004 by yours truly in London, England.
Collins Cocktail history and recipes

name: Beetle Jeuse

history: Created in 2003 by Milo Rodriguez at Raoul's Bar, Oxford, and named after Beetlejuice, the Tim Burton black comedy about a young couple whose premature death leads them to a series of bizarre afterlife exploits.

name: Bishop
preparation: Use a heatproof glass and preheat by filling with boiling water. MUDDLE cloves in the base of shaker. Add boiling water and STIR in honey and other ingredients. Fine strain into glass. (Consider heating in MICROWAVE for twenty seconds to boost temperature).
ingredients:
7 dried	Clove
2 barspoon	Honey
3 shot	Boiling water
2 1⁄2 shot	Tawny port
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A flavoursome and warming variation on mulled wine.
history: Our quick 'n' easy take on this variation of the 18th century Negus - reputedly a favourite of the writer Dr. Johnson. The traditional recipe begins with studding an orange with cloves and roasting it in the oven.

name: Blue Moon Cocktail (1940's recipe)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄3 shot	Crème de violette liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review:
A relation of the Aviation [see history], the Blue Moon features on the back label of Créme Yvette bottles dating from the 1940's. This cocktail became so synonymous with Créme Yvette that when production of the liqueur ceased in 1969 the cocktail was also forgotten. That was until 2010, when Rob Cooper relaunched Créme Yvette, a product formerly made by his father. In so doing he also revived interest in this cocktail. I worked with Rob on St-Germain at this time and I can attest to the efforts and expense he went to, in an effort to authentically replicate his family's liqueur.

However, the Blue Moon is also made with crème de violette liqueur rather than Créme Yvette. Using Crème Yvette creates a pale pink drink (pictured) while crème de violette produces a blue-grey coloured drink that befits its name. The difference in colour leads me to conclude that the Blue Moon was originally made with crème de violette and then reimagined to market Crème Yvette.

Incidentally, blue moon is an astronomical term for the second of two full moons to occur in the same calendar month.
history: This cocktail is said to have been created around 1940 by Oscar Tschirky at Waldorf-Astoria Hotel in Manhattan, New York, USA. Better known as "Oscar of the Waldorf", he was maître d'hôtel at Waldorf-Astoria and is also credited for inventing the Waldorf salad and Eggs Benedict. Although he never worked as a chef, capitalising on his reputation at the hotel, he also authored a cocktail book.

name: Bon Bon

2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
review: Relive your youth and the taste of those big round sweets with this sweet-n-sour lemony cocktail.
history: Adapted from a drink discovered in 2001 at LAB Bar, London, England. The original drink used vanilla vodka.

name: Buena Vida
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:

history: Adapted from a drink created in 2011 by Lee Clinton.

3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)

review: A Scotch Margarita - try it, it works.
history:
Discovered in 2004 at Milk & Honey, London, England.

A variant of the popular Margarita cocktail. A detailed history, along with other variants can be found on our page.

name: Chas
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

review: A wonderfully tangy cocktail with great bourbon personality and hints of almond and orange.
history: Created in 2003 by Murray Stenson at Zig Zag Café, Seattle, USA.

name: Chocolate Sazerac

ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao

history:
Created in 2005 by Tonin Kacaj at Maze, London, England.

The history of the Sazerac cocktail can be found on our Sazerac cocktail page.

name: Citrus Martini

history: Created by Dick Bradsell at Fred's, London, England, in the late 80s.

name: Classic Cocktail

1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)

1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)

history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Algeria
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur

name: Brazilian Cosmopolitan
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

1 shot	Cachaça

1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)

name: Cosmopolitan Cocktail (1934 recipe)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)

review: Reminiscent of a Sidecar and, depending on your syrup, well-balanced.

name: Cruel Intention

name: Dark 'N' Stormy (Difford's recipe)

ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Dark/black/blackstrap rum

history:
The national drink of Bermuda, where ginger beer and Gosling's rum (a brand of dark rum often associated with this cocktail) are produced.

Who first made or named the Dark 'n' Stormy is unknown, but legend has it that it was created, or at least first enjoyed, by British sailors on shore leave in Bermuda after World War I.

name: Deauville (Difford's)

review: A calvados-influenced riff on the Sidecar, or a cognac-influenced riff on the Apple Cart. Either way, served in a more bite-sized portion.
history: My version of the classic Deauville.

name: Easy Tiger

2 slice	Fresh ginger root (thumbnail-sized slice)
2 barspoon	Honey
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Tangy and zesty with rich honey and ginger.
history: Created in 1999 by Alex Kammerling.

name: Eggnog (hot)
preparation: POUR ingredients into heatproof glass and STIR thoroughly. HEAT in microwave oven for a minute (adjust time as appropriate to your oven) and STIR again. Alternatively, mix and warm in pan over heat - do not boil.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 fresh	Egg (white & yolk)
1⁄2 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
2 shot	Milk (whole milk/full 3-4% fat)

name: El Burro
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with ginger beer.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters

name: Mayfair Cocktail
preparation: MUDDLE clove in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 dried	Clove
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Clove adds enlivening spice to this orange and apricot, gin-laced cocktail.
history:
In his 1922 How To Mix Them Robert Vermeire includes the following recipe for the Mayfair Cocktail and crucially also claims that this cocktail is his own creation.

Mayfair Cocktail
Fill the shaker half full of broken ice and add:
  ¼ gill of Dry Gin.
  ¼ gill of plain Orange Juice.
  3 or 4 dashes of Apricot Syrup flavoured with a little Cloves Syrup.
Shake well and strain into a cocktail glass. This cocktail possesses a delicious flavour. I invented it at the Embassy Club in London, 1921. Mayfair is the aristocratic quarter of London, called so because during the reign of Charles II (seventeenth century) they used to hold a yearly fair during the months of May.

This cocktail also appears in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book:

"Mayfair Cocktail
1 Dash Clove Syrup.
¼ Apricot brandy.
¼ Orange juice.
½ Gin.
Shake well and strain into cocktail glass.

name: Merry Widow(er)

history:
The Merry Widow first appears in Hugo R. Ensslin's 1917 Recipes for Mixed Drinks (2nd Edition) (It may have also appeared in his 1916 first edition.) The cocktail also appears in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book and Albert Stevens Crockett's 1935 The Old Waldorf-Astoria Bar Book.

This cocktail takes its name from The Merry Widow Broadway production which opened on 21st October 1907 at the New Amsterdam Theatre. The operetta was premiered in Vienna in 1905, and played all around the world, leading to a ballet version and at least five film versions.

history:
Created in the late 1920s by Harry MacElhone at his Harry's New York Bar in Paris, France. The Monkey Gland takes its name from the work of Dr Serge Voronoff who, convinced that testosterone was vital to a long and healthy life, transplanted monkey testicles onto elderly Frenchmen.

The "Monkey's Gland Cocktail" first appears in MacElhone's 1922 Harry's ABC of Mixing Cocktails (which, sadly, I don't have access to). In his 1923 edition, he specifies the recipe as "1 dash Absinthe, 1 teaspoonful of Grenadine, ½ Orange Juice, ½ Gordon Gin. Shake well, and strain into a cocktail glass. (Invented by the Author and deriving its name from Voronoff's experiments in rejuvenation.)."

name: Pendennis Club Special
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:

history:
Eponymously named after the Pendennis Club in Louisville, Kentucky, the first known reference to this cocktail appears as the Pendennis Club Cocktail in the "Seductive American Cocktails" appendix in William "Cocktail Bill" Boothby's 1908 The World's Drinks and How to Mix Them book with just three ingredients: gin, apricot brandy, and dry vermouth.

By the time it resurfaces in Charles H. Baker Jr.'s 1939 The Gentleman's Companion as "The Pendennis Club's Famous Special" it morphed into a four-ingredient cocktail served over a split fresh kumquat. Modern-day recipes, such as the above, are nearer to Baker's 1939 Pendennis Club Cocktail than Cocktail Bill's 1908 Pendennis Club.

Our recipe, and the drink's newfound popularity, are influenced by a modern-day adaption by Will Elliott at Maison Premiere in Brooklyn, New York City, USA.

name: Sweet Science

name: Test Pilot

history: Created circa 1941 by Donn Beach, this recipe is adapted from a recipe by Victor Bergeron and published in his 1972 Trader Vic's Bartender's Guide.

name: Three Miller
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: A seriously strong drink, in flavour and in alcohol.
history:
The Three Miller is one of several Prohibition-era cocktails whose name references the distance from a shore that a nation's territorial waters. During the 18th century this was established as three nautical miles (5.6 km), the distance a cannonball could be shot from the shore to repel incursions. Hence, during Prohibition, US jurisdiction was limited to three miles offshore so allowing the legal supply of alcohol to parties on board boats just outside territorial waters.

As the number of offshore parties grew, the US negotiated agreements with countries such as the UK and France to recognize the right of the American authorities to enforce Prohibition and anti-smuggling laws to an extended 12-mile limit. Predictably, the parties moved further off-shore. On 29th December 1988, President Reagan extended the territorial waters of the United States to 12 miles from 3 miles.

The notoriety of the three-mile and then 12-mile limit to the reach of the Feds during Prohibition led to the Three Miller/Three Mile Limit, the Twelve Miles Out, and the Twelve Mile Limit cocktails.

This cocktail appears in in Harry MacElhone's 1922 Harry's ABC of Mixing Cocktails and his 1927 Barflies & Cocktails as the "Three Mile Limit Cocktail" and then in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book as the "Three Miller Cocktail."

history: Named after Anton Chekhov's greatest play - a cheery tale of envy and despair. A popular drink in Britain's TGI Friday bars, its origins are unknown.

name: Venus

7 fresh	Raspberries

1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)

name: The Windsor Rose
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

1⁄6 shot	Rose water
review: An orange vodka and rosewater Cosmo.
history: Adapted from a drink discovered in 2005 at The Polo Club Lounge, New Orleans, USA.

name: Zakuski Cocktail

1 inch	Cucumber (fresh)

history: Created in 2008 by yours truly at The Cabinet Room in London, England.

name: Amalia

review: Sip a gooseberry and mint influenced lemon Daiquiri though a foam topping.
history: Created in 2008 by Sam Dean, Mobar, Nottingham England.

name: Cuban Heal
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄4 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1⁄4 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Honey sugar syrup
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters

name: Death In The Gulf Stream

1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)

name: Grand Designs

2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin

review: Not dry, not sweet, just balanced, long and refreshing.
history: Created by Alexandra Fiot at The Lonsdale, London, England.

name: Market Daiquirí

1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)

history: Created in 2008, by Dez O'Connell, London, England

name: Martinez (with London Dry gin)

review:
This Martinez is aromatic, complex and dry. Our previous recipe included dry vermouth to add balance and complexity:
60mml (20z) Drygin
15ml (½oz) Rosso (sweet vermouth
7.5ml (¼) Dry vermouth
5ml (1 barspoon) Maraschino liqueur
1 dah Aromatic bitters
history:
London dry has been the dominant gin style for over 100 years, so by extension was the gin most frequently used to make a Martinez.
See Martinez cocktail history

name: The Mayflower Martini

history: Adapted from a 2008 recipe created by Hans Hilburg at El Pisquerito in Cuzco, Peru.

name: Perfect Lady
garnish: Lemon zest twist (spray and discard) & peach slice
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker, DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Crème de Pêche de Vigne liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: This White Lady riff uses peach liqueur in place of triple sec to make a lighter, fruitier elaboration.
history:
Created in 1936 by Sidney Cox, a bartender at the Grosvenor House, London for The British Empire Cocktail Competition where it took the 1st Prize. That same year a constitutional crisis in the British Empire was caused by King-Emperor Edward VIII's proposal to marry Wallis Simpson, a twice-divorced American socialite. Religious, legal, political, and moral objections were raised due to Mrs Simpson being twice divorced and the marriage was opposed by the King's governments in the United Kingdom and the autonomous Dominions of the British Commonwealth. Despite the opposition, Edward declared his love for Mrs Simpson and his refusal to give her up led to his abdication in December 1936.

He was succeeded by his brother Albert, who took the regal name George VI. Disgraced due to renouncing the throne, Edward was given the title His Royal Highness the Duke of Windsor. He married Mrs Simpson the following year and they remained married until his death 35 years later. She was obviously his 'Perfect Lady'.

name: Satin Sheet
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Agave syrup
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: A spiced margarita-style cocktail.

name: Yokohama
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients and fine strain into chilled glass.

1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin

1⁄24 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Gin and orange with a hint of absinthe.
history: One of the earliest published vodka recipes and credited to Harry MacElhone who also created the Monkey Gland to which this cocktail is practically identical, albeit a splash of vodka. The Yokohama appears in McElhone's 1923 Harry of Ciro's ABC Of Mixing Cocktails.

name: Deauville

3⁄4 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
3⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)

review: The classic recipe omits the sugar syrup, which makes this drink too sour for my taste. Duly sweetened, it is very much in the Sidecar or even Apple Cart vein.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Dream Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix) (optional)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: An after-dinner cocktail with brandy, orange liqueur, and a refreshing burst of absinthe.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Green Glazier
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄4 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄4 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: This cognac-laced herbal and chocolatey bite-sized libation may leave you glazed but pleased - pleasured even.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2008 by Jamie Boudreau at Vessel, Seattle, USA.

name: Jewel
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1⁄6 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: The original recipe, and indeed our old recipe, called for equal parts of the three main ingredients to create a powerful cocktail in both alcohol and flavour. Upping the gin but knocking back the Chartreuse rebalances this classic cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide.

name: Marie Rose
preparation: Strip leaves from rosemary and MUDDLE with grapes in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

1⁄2 sprig	Rosemary sprig
8 fresh	Green grapes (seedless)
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Rosemary spiced gin with grape juice and elderflower: very aromatic.
history: Created in 2007 by Renan Lejeune at Zeta Bar, London, England.

name: Rococoa
garnish: Dust outside of glass with chocolate powder
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄3 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄12 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
4 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
1⁄6 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Subtly smoky chocolate and light rum.
history: Adapted from a drink created by Scott Tyrer at Bibis Italianissimo in Leeds, England.

name: Beggar's Banquet
preparation: SHAKE first four ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with beer.

history: Created in 2010 by Aisha Sharpe in New York City, USA.

name: Grand 'O'

2 1⁄4 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water

1 dash	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)

review: A fruity, zesty, light summery cocktail. Tip - pouring the soda first makes this refreshingly juicy drink easier to mix due to the specific gravities of the ingredients.

name: Merchant of Venice
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo

history: Adapted from a recipe discovered in 2010 at Eclipse Bar in Barcelona, Spain.

name: Netherland Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.

1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix) (optional)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Cognac and orange curaçao are natural partners, here smoothed with egg white and sharpened with a dash of orange bitters. According to tastes, you may want to reduce or omit the sugar syrup, particularly if you are using a particularly sweet orange curaçao liqueur.
history: Created in the early 1900s as the house cocktail at the New Netherland Hotel, on Fifth Avenue (at 59th Street) New York City, which was for a period the tallest hotel in the world.

name: Absinthe Gimlet
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄6 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄2 shot	Lime cordial (sweetened lime juice)
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water
review: A herbal riff on the classic gin-based Gimlet.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2015 by Tara Garnell at The Cabinet Room in London, England after making Charles Vexenat's Green Beast.

name: Creole Contentment
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Sercial (dry) Madeira wine
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water
review: If using a sweeter Madeira such as Verdelho/Rainwater (medium dry) or Bual (medium sweet) you'll need to adjust this finely balanced cocktail. Even Baker himself says it "needs a little trimming". However, dry Sercial Madeira works best to produce a finely balanced complex cocktail.
history: Adapted from Charles H. Baker's 1939 The Gentlemen's Companion .

name: Foxy Lady
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Fraise des Bois liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Best described as a strawberry gin sour, the herbal botanicals in the gin combine well with the sweet strawberry.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2005 by Nicolas Skovgaard at Fox Hotel bar in Copenhagen, Denmark. Nicolas revised this recipe in 2013 to use chamomile tea-infused gin.

name: The Getaway (AKA Cynar Daiquiri)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Dark/black/blackstrap rum
1⁄2 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: The bitter vegetal taste of Cynar turns this Daiquiri into a digestif.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2012 by Wayne Curtis at The Passenger, Washington D.C., USA.

name: Smoked Appletini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice. Smoke with apple and pecan (or other wood) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Honey flavoured vodka
1⁄2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Apple and honey with hints of lemon and clove spice.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2012 by Michael Stringer, Flip-It! Mixology, London.

name: William Porter
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A tart, Manhattan-like combo of Scotch, sweet vermouth and triple sec.
history: Named after William Trotter Porter (1809–1858), an American journalist and editor who founded the Spirit of the Times, a newspaper devoted to sports.

name: Doctor No. 3
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Swedish Punsch liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Tangy Swedish Punch freshened with orange and lemon juice.
history: In his 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks, David A. Embury lists a Doctor No. 3 comprising "One part lemon juice, 1 part orange juice, 2 parts Swedish Punch."

name: Webber Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Citroen Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
1 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: This blackcurrant fruity cocktail has a citrus zing courtesy of the citrus vodka base and the addition of fresh lime juice, the sourness of which adds balance.
history: Created in September 2011 by Jack Webber for the British Brown's Bar & Restaurant chain, it’s since become a favourite on the Brown’s menu where it’s listed under ‘Browns Signature Cocktails’.

name: Londoner (Wood's recipe)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Crème de Mûre liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Rich blackberry fruit liqueur balanced by pink grapefruit and lime juice, with gin fortifying and adding complexity. The flavour is reminiscent of a Bramble served straight-up.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Joe Wood, Cocktail Stars, England and brought to our attention by Gary "gaz" Regan.

name: Tennessee Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Tennessee whiskey
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
history: The Whiskey Sour was first published in Jerry Thomas' How to Mix Drinks or the Bon Vivant's Companion in 1862. The Jack Daniels distillery was established and registered just four years later.

name: The Med
preparation: MUDDLE basil in base of shaker. Add next 3 ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
7 fresh	Basil leaves
1 2⁄3 shot	Kleos Mastiha liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A long summery drink with basil and the distinctive flavour of Greek mastiha.

name: Keyser Söze
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Gin and cognac sit surprisingly well together as base ingredients with gentian and citrus freshness.
history: Keyser Söze is a fictional character and the main protagonist in the 1995 film The Usual Suspects, while Suze, spelt with a 'u', is the bittersweet gentian flavoured liqueur and main protagonist in this cocktail.

name: Foghorn Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE (or stir) all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄12 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Triple sec sweetens dry gin with zesty orange while aromatised wine adds vinous notes. However, it's absinthe that sets this Martini-style cocktail apart. According to bartending convention, this cocktail should be stirred but I much prefer it shaken as when first served this gives the Foghorn a cloudiness that befits its name.
history: A riff on the Corpse Reviver No. 2 created in the Noughties by Ryan Fitzgerald in San Francisco, USA. Absinthe is said to "give the drink an opalescence reminiscent of San Francisco's fog", hence this cocktail's name.

name: Amaro-etti Biscotti
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Disaronno amaretto
2⁄3 shot	Averna Amaro
1⁄6 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
8 drop	Bob's Vanilla bitters
review: Cognac, amaretto and amaro, aromatised with vanilla bitters and Islay single malt.
history: Created in March 2016 by yours truly for Disaronno amaretto.

name: Rachel
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda water and drizzle crème de cassis on surface of drink
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Kwai Feh lychee liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
1⁄6 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
review: Subtle lychee notes shine through this long refreshing cocktail with cognac, lemon and a drizzle of crème de cassis.
history: Created in 2015 by Schwarz Hiltraut, France using Martell V.S.O.P. cognac, this cocktail is named after Jean Martell's wife.

name: Preserve Nippon
preparation: Gently MUDDLE shisho leaf in base of shaker (just to bruise), add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 fresh	Shiso/Perilla leaf
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A vanilla lime cognac sour with Shisho leaf aromatics.
history: Created in 2015 by John Stavroulakis at Zaxari kai Alati Bistrot, Athens, Greece

name: Winter Clove
garnish: Orange zest twist with a flamed clove
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3 whole	Clove
1 1⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Mandarine Napoleon liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
3 dash	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: Zesty mandarin orange and cognac with a hint of smoky peat and clove spice.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Eric Tinca at Love die Late, Great Portland Street, London, England.

name: Night Cap
preparation: Dash bitters over sugar cube in base of mixing glass. Add hot water, crush cube with muddler and stir to dissolve sugar. Add cognac, STIR with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 cube	Demerara / dark Muscovado / brown sugar
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 dash	Bob's Chocolate bitters
1⁄2 shot	Hot water
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
history: Adapted from a 2015 recipe by Gregory Goins at BO Beau Kitchen & Roof Tap, Long Beach, CA 90802, United States

name: Velvet Seine
garnish: Spot 2 drops of Angostura bitters on surface of drink
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Reminiscent of a French Martini without the pineapple juice but with the balancing lemon sourness and an even thicker creamy foamy head thanks to the addition of egg white.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Leigh Brown at Hernando's Hideaway in Warrington, Cheshire, England.

name: Bon Accord
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Lillet-style Rouge light quinquina
1⁄4 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
1 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Based on cognac with half as much scotch, this boozy cocktail is made special by aromatised wine and rich crème de cassis.
history: Created 2015 by Scott Liddle at Strata, Glasgow, Scotland.

name: French Kiss No.3
preparation: MUDDLE raspberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
6 fresh	Raspberries
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Averna Amaro
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
review: Raspberry and rich almond tamed by lime with underlying cognac character.
history: Created in 2015 by Chanelle O Connor at Salomontini Le Resto in London, England.

name: Nouvelle Histoire (New Story)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Green mint (menthe verte)/Peppermint syrup
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: A refreshing citrusy and minty cognac cocktail.
history: Adapted from a created in 2015 by Eric van Oers at Blind Pig London, England.

name: Rose Crescent
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	Island single malt Scotch whisky
1⁄3 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Ginger cordial (non-alcoholic)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Ginger and cognac with underlying whisky and herbal complexity.
history: Created in 2015 by Sean Baylis at La Raza, Cambridge, England

name: A L'Ancienne du Bois (A woody Old Fashioned)
preparation: MUDDLE cherries with bitters and maple syrup in base of glass. Add 3 ice cubes and STIR. Add cognac and 3 more ice cubes and STIR again. Add walnut liqueur and 2 more ice cubes and STIR some more.
ingredients:
5 whole	Maraschino cherry (from jar in syrup)
1 1⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	Walnut (Nocino) liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Maple syrup
4 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Despite the name, this Old Fashioned style drink is more fruity and nutty than it is woody, but it's tasty all the same.
history:
Created in 2015 by Gary Anderson at Gingers Bar at Purnell's Bistro, Birmingham, England, who says, "The drink came from wanting to make a cognac Old Fashioned (hence a l'ancienne). The maple, griottines and Peychaud's bitters were introduced to keep the idea of the cocktail being very French. Bizarrely, the walnut came from attempting a Google search for "maple and cherry" which displayed an antique wood specialist who along with maple and cherry wood also used walnut. Therefore my drink became "A Woody Old Fashioned" or "A L'Ancienne du Bois".
Old-Fashioned cocktail history

name: XOXO
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
1⁄2 shot	Dark chocolate liqueur
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A rich, chocolaty after dinner drink with cognac, pedro ximénez sherry, chocolate and orange liqueurs.
history: Created in 2015 by Josh Powell at Somerset House, Bristol.

name: Mexican Vineyard
preparation: MUDDLE 8 grapes in base of shaker. ADD other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
8 fresh	Green grapes (seedless)
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
2⁄3 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Perhaps best summarised as being an 'Apple and Grape Margarita', the flavours combine harmoniously in this well-balanced cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2005 by Stephen Watts at a cocktail bar somewhere in deepest Nottingham, England.

name: Winter Punch
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) and Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Chairman's Reserve Spiced Rum
3⁄4 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
review: A bourbon and amaretto sour with spiced rum and cranberry.

name: Avenue San Martin
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1⁄2 shot	Amaro CioCiaro
2 barspoon	Honey
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	Ginger syrup
review: Bittersweet and tangy. A cocktail to enjoy as an apéritif with nibbles.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2016 at Bar Hommage, Stockholm, Sweden. This cocktail takes its name from a street in Lima, Peru where the creators of this cocktail once ended up at a bar called Ayahuasca.

name: Tratto Limoncello Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 1⁄2 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Bourbon laced lemon sherbet – a bittersweet aperitif.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Cynthia Tran, Beverage Director at Tratto Restaurant in San Francisco, USA.

name: Dutchess
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Pineapple juice
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄2 shot	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: One of those Angostura heavy (very heavy) cocktails that intuition says shouldn't work, but thanks to the rich balancing properties of almond syrup and pineapple, it is not only balanced but tasty. The genever base justifies the perhaps misspelt name and adds its distinctive character. (The name may come from Dutchess County in New York State).
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2014 by Theo Lieberman of Lantern's Keep and Milk & Honey in New York City, USA.

name: Cucumber Jalapeño Caipirinha
garnish: Stirrer (spoon, wooden lolly stick or stick cut from sugar cane)
preparation:
1. Cut lime in half (from pole to pole) and then slice one of the halves into eight 3-4mm thick half-moon shaped segments and drop into the base of a robust rocks glass.

2. Add 3 bar spoons caster sugar (or ½oz/15ml sugar syrup 2:1) and MUDDLE.

3. Add cucumber and jalapeño and MUDDLE some more.

4. When sure fruit juice is fully extracted and the sugar dissolved, transfer the muddled fruit and sugar into serving glass (preferably a 30cl / 10oz highball glass).

5. POUR cachaça (stored in the freezer) into the rocks glass (used to muddle) and swirl to rinse glass before pouring cachaça into serving glass. STIR to ensure all ingredients are well mixed.

6. Crack (rather than crush) four to five large ice cubes and drop into serving glass. STIR before topping with more ice and serve with a stirrer (but no straws).
ingredients:
1⁄2 fresh	Lime (fresh) (chopped)
3 barspoon	Caster/ Superfine/Baker's special sugar (white)
3 slice	Cucumber (fresh)
1⁄6 inch	Jalapeno slice
2 shot	Cachaça (from freezer)
history: For information on the history and other variations of the Caipirinha, please see our Caipirinha cocktail page.

name: Rosemary Tuck
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 1⁄2 shot	Tawny port
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A refreshing Scotch and port wine nightcap, or perhaps a citrusy whisky aperitif. The Scotch and orange combo puts this drink in the same camp as the classic Blood & Sand.

name: Coffee Coolatta
garnish: Float white tea & coconut foam (make foam using cream whipper with equal parts brewed cold white tea and coconut milk with egg white as protein)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 3⁄4 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Cold brew coffee
review: A dry (some may want to add a touch of sugar syrup) bourbon laced coffee cocktail resplendent with a moustache challenging white tea & coconut head.
history: Created by Chris Amirault at Otium, Los Angeles.

name: Red Earl (by Salvatore Calabrese)
preparation: MUDDLE ginger and then raspberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 slice	Fresh ginger root (thumbnail-sized slice)
10 fresh	Raspberries
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
2⁄3 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix) (optional)
review: Fresh ginger adds a hint of spice which combines well with raspberry fruit in this crowd-pleasing vodka-based cocktail which is freshened by a dash of limoncello.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Salvatore Calabrese – I added half a spoon of sugar to his recipe which you may or not need depending on your raspberries and limoncello.

name: Flor De Don Juan
preparation: MUDDLE basil in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
4 fresh	Basil leaves
1 2⁄3 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
2⁄3 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A basil tequila sour (Margarita if you will) sweetened with elderflower liqueur – basil and elderflower flavours sit well with the tequila and lime.

name: G+T Royale
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and lightly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄6 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄3 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
2 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: A summery aperitif gin cocktail with crisp tonic water and enlivening champagne, flavoured with hints of vanilla and orange.
history: Recipe created in 2017 by Tony Conigliaro with Schweppes 1783 Crisp Tonic Water.

name: The Alchemist
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄6 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
2⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
review: Looking over the liqueur and syrup-dominated recipe, this mezcal-based Margarita meets the Last Word may appear to be sweet. However, the spec is deceiving, and the finished drink is surprisingly balanced, harnessing some big flavours and presenting them harmoniously.
history: Created in 2017 by Sam Fraser at The Rockinghorse in Chichester, England.

name: Black Rum Swizzle
preparation: POUR all ingredients into a glass half filled with crushed ice. SWIZZLE and then fill the glass with more crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Dark/black/blackstrap rum
1 1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄4 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Dark rum adds depth of flavour to this fruity and refreshing cocktail.

name: After Hours
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Mentzendorff Kümmel liqueur
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water
review: Martini-like but with delicate liqueur richness. Lightly spicy and faintly nutty.
history:
Adapted from a recipe by Satvik "Rick" Ahuja, Quarter Bar & Restaurant, Leicester, England.

"I created this drink as gin is usually used in pre-dinner aperitif-style drinks, e.g., Martini, Negroni, G & T etc., or as refreshers in Fizzes, Tom Collinses, Aviations etc. I wanted to create a drink to show how gin could be used to great effect in the after-dinner category where brown spirits usually tend to dominate. Hence my use of a slightly softer yet rooty style of gin [Rick used Plymouth Gin] which marries well with the spice from kummel and the nuttiness of the maraschino also gives it the desired sweetness without making it overly cloying or heavy."

name: Pink Gin Fizz
preparation: SHAKE first four ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda and briefly stir to integrate.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: As the name suggests, this refreshing and fruity long drink is both gin-laced and pink in colour. And yes, it's also fizzy. Well if not out and out fizzy, it is at least invigorated with sparkling water. So perhaps that's why merely fizz rather than fizzy?

name: Pantera Rosa
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 fresh	Raspberries
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Fresh vibrant and fruity. If you like French Martinis you'll also like this.
history: Adapted from a recipe made for us in September 2019 by Mattia Ria at the Blind Pig in Rome, Italy.

name: Giuseppi's Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bepi Tosolini Grappa di Moscato
3⁄4 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A grappa-based sour with faint elderflower.

name: Derby Cocktail
garnish: Mint leaf (float or peg/stick to rim)
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE mint (just to bruise) in base of stirring glass. Add other ingredients, STIR with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2 dash	Peach bitters
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix) (optional)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (optional)
review: This Martini-style classic was originally devoid of sugar syrup but the hint of sweetness mellows the gin and balances the bitters. Alternatively, use Old Tom gin and omit sugar. The splash of chilled water in our recipe helps open and stretch this cocktail.
history: Adapted from Harry MacElhone's 1926 Harry's ABC of Mixing Cocktails where Harry credits this cocktail to "E. G. de Gastreaux of Canal and Vine Streets, Cincinnati, 1903." Harry also says to "Serve with an olive" but this this accoutrement is omitted when the Derby Cocktail later reappears in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Cazador
garnish: Lime zest twist or dehydrated lime wheel slice
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bacardi 8 year old rum
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Maple syrup
1⁄6 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Subtle blackcurrant and anise notes flavour this aged rum maple daiquiri.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by George Hunter, this is the cocktail with which he won the South African final of Bacardi's Legacy bartender's competition, taking him and his cocktail through to the global final.

George created his recipe in Johannesburg, South Africa where Bacardi Ocho is 43% alc./vol. so the above recipe is reformatted for the 40% alc./vol. Bacardi Ocho available in Europe. George's original recipe:
Cazador
60ml Bacardi Ocho
30ml Fresh lime
15ml Maple syrup
10ml Crème de cassis
Absinthe rinse

George told us, "Cazador is my surname in Spanish (Hunter). The cocktail has been created to represent triumph and lessons learnt. Cazador is a symbol to remind people to never give up, to push through the hard times. I started my career as a bar back on minimum wage, I worked hard every single day to learn more and grow as a bartender. The first time I entered Bacardi Legacy, I didn't even make it out the first round. Six years later [2019] I entered again & won the national event in South Africa and get to represent my country on the global stage."

name: Tovarich
garnish: Float a dehydrated lime slice wheel
preparation: DRY SHAKE all ingredients (without ice) to emulsify. SHAKE again with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Mentzendorff Kümmel liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Vodka-laced, delightfully clean and cleansing with kummel's distinctive rich caraway and cumin flavour combining well with lime.
history: Tovarishch, tovarisch or tovarish are all Russian for comrade, friend, colleague or ally. The naming of this cocktail, which first appears in Grosby Gaige's 1944 Standard Cocktail Guide, may have been inspired by Tovaritch, a 1933 play by Jacques Deval.

name: Siesta
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: This bittersweet aperitif cocktail was originally made to be served straight-up in a coupe glass, but we prefer it on-the-rocks.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2006 by Katie Stipe at the Flatiron Lounge in New York City, USA.

name: Watermelon Margarita No.2
garnish: Fresh watermelon wedge on rim or watermelon slices sweets/candy
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Watermelon liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Agave syrup
1⁄2 pinch	Salt (sea salt)
review: Just as the name promises, a watermelon-flavoured margarita.
history: Created in June 2020 by yours truly in Rye, Sussex, England.

name: Pacific Breeze
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 shot	De Kuyper Watermelon liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄2 shot	Lemon-lime soda (Sprite/7-Up)
review: Fruity, light in alcohol and a touch on the sweet side.

name: Midsummer Daydream
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass whilst also pouring tonic water.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Coconut water
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
2 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: There's a double slug of brandy in this dry refreshing long summery aperitivo.

name: Favola
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) & float basil leaf
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Italicus liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Mouth puckering zesty citrus freshness underpinned by gin's botanical complexity.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Alessio Aufiero for Pallini Limoncello.

name: Artichoke Hold
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into a glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Jamaican-style overproof aged pot still rum
3⁄4 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
review: The elderflower is dominated by the other less subtle flavours in this big-flavoured, sweet 'n' sour cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Jeremy Oertel at Donna Bar in Brooklyn, New York City, USA.

name: Fort Lauderdale (by Sam Ross)
garnish: Lemon zest twist or dehydrated lemon wheel
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Apricot liquor and rich almond syrup balanced tart lemon and bitter aperitivo in what's described as a "mash-up of the Third Man and the Bitter Mai-Tai but in coupe form."
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2018 by Sam Ross at Attaboy in New York City, USA.

name: Backstabber
garnish: Root ginger slice or piece of crystalised ginger
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Homemade ginger juice syrup (1:1)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Gin and ginger with ginger's heat mellowed by smoothing egg white.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Boudewijn Vork while working at an Italian restaurant in Noosa, Queensland, Australia. Boudewijn says the reason behind this cocktail's name, "It begins fruity and lenient, but ends sour and spicy. Like you got betrayed, 'a stab in the back'."

name: Extra Sangria
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
2⁄3 shot	Rioja (Crianza) red wine
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: The red wine blends particularly harmoniously when made with a sherry-influenced scotch whisky. Whatever you're Scotch, the traditional Spanish Sangria is tame in comparison.
history: Adapted from a recipe promoted by Chivas Regal (ours has more Scotch), this cocktail was originally made with Chivas Extra 13 Sherry Cask Finish.

name: A Still Dawn
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
5⁄6 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄4 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
1⁄6 shot	Averna Amaro
2 dash	Pear bitters
review: Spirit-forward and bittersweet.

name: Maple Margarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Patrón Añejo tequila
2⁄3 shot	Maple syrup
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Maple syrup works well with whiskey but not so well with blanco tequila. It works better with reposado tequila, but best with añejo tequila. It seems a syrup that oozes out of wood likes wood! Experimentation also proved that a mix of lemon and lime is better than lime on its own in this Margarita.

name: Vanilla Mocha Espresso Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1⁄2 shot	Irish cream liqueur
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Exactly the cocktail the name suggests.
history: A cream liqueur influenced riff on the Espresso Martini.

name: Pan de Muertos
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass/mug filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄6 shot	Pineapple juice
review: A pineapple and almond-influenced Margarita served iced.

name: Upper Cut
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Cachaça
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Cachaça adds an almost banana-like note to this liqueur rather than spirit-based citrusy sour.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Ivy Mix at her Leyenda bar in New York City, USA.

name: Rome With a View
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Herbal bittersweetness with zesty freshness – a long aperitivo with a splash of effervescence.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2008 by Michael McIlroy at Milk & Honey in New York City, USA. Apparently, Michael was inspired by the Triumph of Pompeii cocktail, in turn inspired by Rome is Burning.

name: Dorchester
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
review: A riff on a Last Word with grapefruit juice replacing Chartreuse.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Erik Adkins, Bar Director at the Slanted Door restaurant in San Francisco, USA.

name: Mellow Negroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄6 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1 1⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: As the name suggests, it's a Negroni with the gin-laced punch you'd expect but a little less of the bitterness.
history: Created by yours truly thanks to a comment (on our White Negroni page) by John McLaughlin, a fellow Discerning Drinker, in search of a mellow Negroni recipe.

name: Alpine Swift
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass/tin filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
2⁄3 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
2⁄3 shot	Pineapple juice
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Bittersweet and edging towards the tropical.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2022 by Szomak Palasthy, bars manager at Restaurant and Rooftop Bar in Stratford, London, England.

name: Palomita
garnish: Salt rim &/or grapefruit slice or lime wedge
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with grapefruit soda.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
5⁄6 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Agave syrup
1 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Pink Grapefruit soda
review: Paloma is Spanish for 'dove' and a palomita is a 'little dove'. Given the name it's not surprising that the Palomita is a riff on a Paloma cocktail, swapping out tequila for less assertive vodka.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2018 at Salvation Taco in Manhattan, New York City, USA.

name: Calvados Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Some will debate if a cocktail without rum should carry the name Daiquiri but move past that and this cocktail tastes exactly as its name suggests.

name: Lady Killer
preparation: Cut a passion fruit in half and scoop out flesh into shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 fresh	Passion fruit (fresh)
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Passoã passion fruit liqueur
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
2⁄3 shot	Pineapple juice
review: This gin-laced summery cocktail is fruity yet surprisingly dry.

name: Fresh Side
preparation: SHAKE first 6 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. TOP with ginger beer.
ingredients:
8 fresh	Mint leaves
1 2⁄3 shot	Monkey Shoulder Fresh Monkey
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A spicy cross between a Southside and a Last Word.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Pablo Navas of Mobster Bar in Paris, France.

name: Salty Doggy Style
garnish: Squeeze lime wedge and drop into cocktail
preparation: Half-fill glass with ice and add the first 4 ingredients. STIR, TOP with pink grapefruit soda and then top up ice to fill the glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Passoã passion fruit liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
3 1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A fruity Salty Dog, tamed, groomed and brought to heel.
history: O/ Adapted from a recipe created by Denis Yurco at Boilerman bar, Hamburg, Germany.

name: Orange Crush
preparation: POUR all ingredients into glass. Briefly stir and fill glass with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Oranje Vodka
1 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1 1⁄2 shot	Lemon-lime soda (Sprite/7-Up)
review: A Screwdriver for a hot summer's afternoon.
history: Popular in the American states of Maryland and Delaware. The Harborside Bar & Grill in Ocean City, Maryland, claims to be "Home of the Original Fresh Squeezed Orange Crush".

name: Espresso Margarita
garnish: Orange juice and salt rim. Orange zest twist expressed and discarded. Float 3 coffee beans.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Agave syrup
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: The Espresso Martini meets the Margarita.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Dre Masso in 2016.

name: Perfect Pear
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Poire William eau-de-vie
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A generously flavoured pear drop sour.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 1995 by Marco Dionysos at Saucebox in Portland, Oregon for his ex-wife, Sarah. According to Jim Meehan's PDT Cocktail Book, "He named it the Perfect Pear in honor of their marriage and the King Crimson song 'Three of a Perfect Pair'."

name: Zapatero Old Fashioned
garnish: Orange zest twist & dust with freshly grated cinnamon
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 dash	Xocolatl mole bitters
review: Delicately bittered and spiced mezcal and bourbon, lifted by subtle rich almond.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2013 by Jeremy Lake at Crossroads Kitchen on Melrose Avenue in Los Angeles, USA.

name: Compass Club
garnish: Fresh raspberry floated in foam head
preparation: MUDDLE raspberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) to emulsify and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3 fresh	Raspberries
1 2⁄3 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: A subtly raspberry-influenced Whisky Sour served straight-up.
history: A whisky-based riff on the classically gin-based Clover Club. Discovered in 2024 at Fitz's Bar in London, England, although apparently, this cocktail did not originate there.

name: Charlie Pie
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A small and elegant Negroni variation, served straight-up which benefits from a splash more than dilution than stirring with good ice delivers.
history:
Adapted from a recipe in the 1929 book Cocktails de Paris with the signature beneath attributing its creation to Lucien Gaudin.

Gaudin, an Olympic gold medal-winning French fencer, was a regular customer at a Parian bar called the Le Chevel Pie where a bartender named Charlie created a competition-winning cocktail named Lucien Gaudin in honour of his sporting customer. (Also recorded in Cocktails de Paris). It's surmised that Lucien Gaudin named this cocktail in humorous tribute to 'Charlie', that bartender at Le Chevel Pie.

name: Abacaxi Ricaço
garnish: Cut a straw sized hole in the top of the pineapple shell & replace it as a lid
preparation: Cut the top off a small pineapple and carefully scoop out the flesh from the base to leave a shell with 12mm (½ inch) thick walls. Place the shell in a freezer to chill. Remove the hard core from the pineapple flesh and discard; roughly chop the remaining flesh, add other ingredients and BLEND with one 12oz scoop of crushed ice. Pour into the pineapple shell and serve with straws. (The flesh of one pineapple blended with the following ingredients will fill at least two shells).
ingredients:
1 whole	Pineapple (fresh)
3 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Caster/ Superfine/Baker's special sugar (white)
