review: Looks and tastes great but is a load of hassle to make.
history: Adapted from David Embury's 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks. Pronounced 'Ah-bah-Kah-shee Rich-kah-So', the Portuguese name of this Brazilian drink literally translates as Extra Delicious Pineapple.

name: Absinthe Frappé
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into glass filled with crushed ice. CHURN (stir) and serve with a straw.
ingredients:
1 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄3 shot	Anisette liqueur
1 shot	Chilled water
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Sweet aniseed may not sound appealing but you should try an Absinthe Frappé after a large meal on a summer's night before you decide on this delicious cocktail.
history:
Dating from the early 1870s and said to have been created in 1873/4 by Cayetano Ferrer at Aleix's Coffee House, New Orleans, which consequently became known as The Absinthe Room. Today the establishment is fittingly known as the Old Absinthe House.

George J. Kappeler's 1895 Modern American Drinks – How to mix and Serve All Kinds of Cups and Drinks includes two Absinthe Frappé recipes.

name: Adam & Eve
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Galliano L'Autentico liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Lovers of the Sazerac will appreciate this herbal, bourbon-laced cocktail. Spirit-forward but becomes progressively sweeter as it dilutes.

name: Aggravation
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: If you like Scotch and enjoy creamy drinks, you'll love this.

name: Asian Ginger Cocktail
preparation: MUDDLE ginger in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 slice	Fresh ginger root (thumbnail-sized slice)
2 1⁄4 shot	Akashi-Tai Daiginjo Genshu sake
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Lightly spiced with ginger, distinctly oriental in character.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2004 by Chris Langan of Barnomadics.

name: Bay of Passion
garnish: Skewered lime slice & Luxardo Maraschino cherry sail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Passoã passion fruit liqueur
1 1⁄3 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
2 1⁄2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
review: A passionate Sea Breeze.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Salvatore Calabrese and featured in the 2012 The Complete Home Bartender's Guide.

name: Bella Donna Daiquiri
garnish: Cinnamon powder & sugar rim (moistened with orange juice)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Dark/black/blackstrap rum
1 1⁄2 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Back in 2003, this was the hit cocktail for Difford's Guide staff at the Bellagio, Las Vegas, after working at the Nightclub & Bar Beverage Convention.
history: Adapted from a drink discovered in 2003 at Bellagio in Las Vegas, USA. Whether this cocktail is named after Bella Donna, the 1981 debut solo album by Stevie Nicks, or Atropa belladonna the poisonous plant commonly known as belladonna or deadly nightshade is not recorded.

name: Blue Lagoon
preparation: POUR first 3 ingredients into glass and STIR. Fill glass with ice and TOP with lemon-lime soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	De Kuyper Blue Curaçao
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 1⁄2 shot	Lemon-lime soda (Sprite/7-Up)
review: Lurid blue, easy-drinking zesty citrusy. This cocktail is also known as The Swimming Pool and lounging beside one, or at least imagining you are, is what this cocktail is about.
history:
There are two versions of this bright blue cocktail, both rather better than the film of the same name which despite being panned by the critics was the 9th-highest-grossing film of 1980. Perhaps a young Brooke Shields and a sexually charged plot set on a tropical island paradise helped. But I digress. Back to the drink.

There's also a blended version (see variation) created either sometime in the 1960s, or more specifically in 1972, by Andy MacElhone (son of Harry) at Harry's New York Bar, Paris, France.

We're unaware of anyone claiming to have created this built-in-the-glass/shaken (perhaps later) version of the Blue Lagoon but due to its simplicity, this is now the popular version.

name: Blueberry Cocktail
preparation: MUDDLE blueberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
24 fresh	Blueberries (fresh)
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3⁄4 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
review: Rich blueberry fruit fortified with vodka made more interesting by a splash of wine.

name: Blushin' Russian
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: A White Russian with a hint of almond.

name: Bolshoi Punch
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	White overproof rum
1 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: An innocuous-seeming pink classic - richly flavoured and easy to drink.

name: Boston Flip
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) to emulsify and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
2 shot	Rainwater/Verdelho (med-dry) madeira wine
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 fresh	Egg (white & yolk)
review: A good dusting of freshly grated nutmeg makes this old-school cocktail.

name: Brandy Fizz
preparation: SHAKE first three ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass (without ice). TOP with soda.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
Top up with	Soda from siphon
review: A refreshing and tasty dry drink: cognac and lemon balanced with a little sugar and lengthened with soda.

name: Broadmoor
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Speyburn 10yo Speyside single malt
1⁄3 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Bartending law stipulates that this cocktail be stirred. If law-abiding, stir and serve on the rocks with larger (60ml whisky, 15ml Chartreuse, 10ml sugar, and 2 dashes bitters) measures. However, this digestif is best enjoyed straight-up while still alive and foaming from a good shake.
history: Named after the infamous British mental institution, this recipe is adapted from a cocktail created in 2001 by Swedish bartender Andreas Noren at The Player bar in London, England. It was then popularised at London's Milk & Honey club.

name: Brubaker Old-fashioned
preparation: STIR malt extract in glass with Scotch until malt extract dissolves. Add ice and one shot of Scotch and stir. Add remaining Scotch, sugar and Angostura and stir some more. Add more ice and keep stirring so that ice dilutes the drink.
ingredients:
2 barspoon	Malt extract
2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: If you like Scotch, you should try this extra malty dram. After all that stirring, you'll deserve one.
history:
Created in 2003 by Shelim Islam at the GE Club, London, England. Shelim named this drink after a horse in the sports section of a paper (also a film made in the 1970s starring Robert Redford).
Old-Fashioned cocktail history

name: Bull's Blood
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Orange fruitiness fortified with cognac and white rum. Fruity but not a sweetie.

name: C C Kazi
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 3⁄4 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 3⁄4 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A Rude Cosmo without the liqueur.

name: Calvados Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Apple is somewhat dominated by orange but a pleasing dry, zesty, fruity combo nonetheless.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Captain Collins
garnish: Orange slice & Luxardo Maraschino cherry on stick (sail)
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Canadian blended whisky
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Sweetened, soured and diluted Canadian whisky.
history: See the history of the Collins cocktail on our Tom Collins page.

name: Cheeky Monkey
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1 1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Fire yellow in colour, this drink features the distinctive flavour of Chartreuse with a citrus supporting cast.
history: Created in 2001 by Tony Conigliaro at Isola, Knightsbridge, London, England.

name: Cucumber Sake-Tini
preparation: MUDDLE cucumber in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 inch	Cucumber (fresh)
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Akashi-Tai Daiginjo Genshu sake
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Subtle and dry. Cucumber and sake are made for each other.
history: Created in 2004 by Lisa Ball, London, England.

name: Amsterdam Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Orange-yellow in flavour with genever adding a pleasant spiritous bready backbone to orange fruit. Perhaps serve with marmalade on toast for breakfast.
history: Adapted from Hyma Gale and Gerald F. Marco's 1937 book The How and When.

name: Black Feather
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
5⁄12 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Spirit-forward but with rounded cognac and a hint of orange. For dry palates only. Some may prefer orange curaçao in place of triple sec.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2000 by Robert Hess and published on DrinkBoy.com.

name: Black Jack Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Kirschwasser (cherry) eau-de-vie
1⁄2 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: More burgundy than black but dark fruits of the forest dominate this medium dry cocktail.
history: The name Black Jack traditionally refers to a water bottle made from air dried leather. When the leather was dried it tended to turn black.

name: Bloomsbury Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Licor 43 Original liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: This pinky/rusty drink benefits from a good long stir but the result is an aromatic, medium dry, spicy vanilla Martini.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2003 by Robert Hess and published on DrinkBoy.com

name: Caprice
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A long stir delivers the dilution necessary for this aromatic, delicately spiced and herbal Wet Martini.

name: Charente Collins
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE mint in base of shaker (just to bruise). Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. Serve with straws.
ingredients:
5 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Created in 2005 by Kieran Bailey, The Light Bar, London, England.
history:
Refreshing orange and lemon with a hint of elderflower.

Also see Collins Cocktails - recipes & history.

name: Crossbow
garnish: Orange juice and chocolate powder rim &/or orange zest twist
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
2⁄3 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Surprisingly dry, chocolate and orange laced with gin.
history: Originally a 3-equal parts cocktail, we discovered in 2005 at Bar Opiume, Singapore.

name: The Crow
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: If you use quality pomegranate syrup and have a penchant for Scotch, then you could be pleasantly surprised by this cocktail.
history: The Crow cocktails first appears in Judge Jr.'s 1927 Here's How! Revised Edition and is repeated in Harry Craddock's influential 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Crux
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: The 'crux' of the matter is rarely as tasty as this fruity and none-too-sweet brandy-laced cocktail.
history:
Until I revisited the Crux on 23rd February 2023, our recipe followed the original equal parts proportions with:
30ml (1oz) Cognac
30ml (1oz) Triple sec
30ml (1oz) Dubonnet Red
30ml (1oz) Lemon juice

name: Hot Gin Toddy
preparation: Place bar spoon in empty (ideally warmed glass). POUR all ingredients into glass and then STIR.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 shot	Chilled water
3 shot	Boiling water
review: Warmed and sweetened gin with a hint of orange. (Others prefer a grapefruit zest garnish but there is no accounting.)

name: Blanche Refresher
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. Drizzle Green Chartreuse all over the top of the drink.
ingredients:
1 shot	La Fée Absinthe Blanche
1 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
review: Challenging ingredients, including a whole shot of absinthe, combine to make a very approachable, aptly refreshing cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2013 by Stephen Quainton at B.Y.O.C. Bar, Brighton, England.

name: Dandy Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 1⁄2 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: This complex Manhattan variant is a well-balanced combo of spirit, liqueur and aromatic wine.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Diamond Fizz
preparation: SHAKE first three ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass (without ice). TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
Top up with	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Why top a Gin Fizz with soda when you can use brut sparkling wine?
history: A long lost classic.

name: Dixie Dew
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: A peppermint fresh and zesty orange, bourbon-laced cocktail for late-night sipping.

name: Dutch Courage
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄6 shot	Warninks Advocaat liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review: A refreshing alternative to a traditional English lemonade.
history: Created in 2002 by Alex Kammerling, London, England.

name: El Diablo Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with ginger beer.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: The tequila, rich red berry fruit, lime and ginger aren't exactly a subtle combination but it is one that has proved both popular and enduring.
history: The El Diablo started life as a mere "Diablo" in the "Tropical Specialties" section of Hyman Gale & Gerald F. Marco's 1940 book The How and When.

name: Epestone Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: A pleasant, maroon coloured, blackcurrant-flavoured Daiquiri.

name: Extradition
preparation: MUDDLE strawberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
3 fresh	Strawberries (hulled, small & ripe)
2 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
3⁄4 shot	Passion fruit syrup
review: A light, fruity drink for a summer afternoon.
history: Created in 2001 by Francis Timmons at Detroit bar in London, England.

name: Flirtini #2
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
2 shot	Pineapple juice
Top up with	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: A flirtatious little number that slips down easily.
history: Adapted from a recipe by the New York bartender Dale DeGroff.

name: Floral Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Rose water
review: This aptly named gin Martini is floral but semi-dry and spirit-forward.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2003 at Zander Bar in London, England.

name: Flying Dutchman
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
1⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water
review: A Martini-style genever forward cocktail with bittersweet zesty orange.

name: French 76
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne/sparkling wine.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
Top up with	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: A Vodka Sour topped with sparkling wine. Works well.
history: French 75 history and other recipe variations

name: Gin Berry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
review: Berry flavours combine harmoniously with gin - what an appropriate name.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2004 by Chris Lacey, UK.

name: Hakkatini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review: Balanced bittersweet orange and apple.
history: Adapted from a drink discovered in 2003 at Hakkasan, London, England.

name: Harvard Cooler
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Refreshing and far from too sweet. Lime and sugar enhance the appley spirit.

name: Hawaiian Cosmopolitan
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Sour apple liqueur
1 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Fresh, tangy and distinctly tropical.
history:
Created in 2002 by Wayne Collins, UK.

For more recipes, origins and history behind the Cosmopolitan cocktail, see our Cosmopolitan page.

name: Hemingway
garnish: ¼ lime wheel slice on rim
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄4 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
5⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
5⁄12 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
4 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Delicately sweetened lime and champagne with faint notes of aniseed from the absinthe.
history: A lime influenced riff on Ernest Hemingway's classic Death in the Afternoon. Another version of this cocktail, apparently created at Cantineros' Club, the famous Cuban bar school, calls for a shot of Pernod anis to be poured into a chilled glass and then topped with champagne.

name: The Hive
preparation: STIR honey with vodka until honey dissolves. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 barspoon	Honey
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Krupnik spiced honey liqueur
2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Sour grapefruit balanced by sweet honey.
history: Discovered in 2004 at Circus, London, England.

name: Honey & Marmalade Dram
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: This citrusy drink seems to enrich and enhance the flavour of Scotch.
history: Recipe adapted from the Honeysuckle Daiquiri.

name: The Honeysuckle Orchard
preparation: STIR honey with vodka in base of shaker until honey dissolves. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 barspoon	Honey
2 shot	Bison grass vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A back-to-nature Polish Martini - all the better for it.
history: Discovered in 2005 at The Stanton Social, New York City, USA.

name: Hot Buttered Whiskey
preparation: Place bar spoon in warmed glass. Add ingredients and STIR until butter dissolves.
ingredients:
1 knob	Unsalted butter
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
Top up with	Boiling water
review: Warming and smooth - great on a cold day or whenever you fancy a warming treat.

name: Hot Grog
preparation: Place bar spoon loaded with honey in warmed glass. Add other ingredients and STIR until honey dissolves.
ingredients:
3 barspoon	Honey
1 shot	Navy rum (54.5% alc./vol.)
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 1⁄2 shot	Boiling water
review: Warming, honeyed, pungent rum with a hint of lime.

name: Ice Maiden
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Canadian icewine
3⁄4 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (reduce if wet ice)
review: A subtle Martini with the honeyed flavours of icewine melding with botanicals in the gin and balanced by the acidity of the white wine.
history: Created in 2004 by yours truly, London, England.

name: Illusion
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Green melon liqueur
2 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
review: This medium-sweet, lime green drink is one for a summer's day by the pool.

name: Imperial Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄12 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A Fifty Fifty Martini with faintly rust colour inducing bitters and subtly fruity maraschino.

name: Italian Sun
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
1 1⁄2 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Hazelnut liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Tastes rather like a bon bon (a round, sugar coated, lemon flavoured sweet).
history: Created in 2002 by Dan Spink at Browns, St Martin's Lane, London, England.

name: Jack-in-the-Box
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Smooth 'n' easy pineapple laced with apple brandy. If you like this, then you may also like French Martinis

name: Jamaican Mule
garnish: Lime slice, mint sprigs bouquet & straw
preparation: POUR first 3 ingredients into mug/glass and briefly stir. Two-thirds fill glass with cubed ice. TOP with ginger beer and fill glass with a crown of crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Chairman's Reserve Spiced Rum
5⁄12 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: A spicy rum lime sour, lengthened and invigorated with ginger beer.
history: Moscow Mule history

name: Jenever Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: One of the more delicately flavoured sours.

name: Jolt'ini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 3⁄4 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1 1⁄4 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
1⁄4 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
review: A vanilla-flavoured Espresso Martini.
history: Discovered in 2005 at Degrees in Washington DC, USA.

name: Jose Collins
garnish: Orange slice & Luxardo Maraschino cherry on stick (sail)
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass whilst also pouring soda. .
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: The classic long balance of sweet and sour with tequila adding Mexican spirit.
history: See the history of the Collins cocktail on our Tom Collins page.

name: Kentucky Jewel
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
1 1⁄2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
review: Easy sipping, fruity bourbon.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2004 by Jonathan Lamm at The Admirable Crichton in London, England.

name: Gimlet Cocktail (Charles H. Baker's 1939 recipe)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄6 shot	Lime cordial (sweetened lime juice)
3⁄4 shot	Chilled water
review: Boozy and very subtly flavoured and edging very slightly towards being sweet.
history: Recipe adapted from Charles H. Baker, Jr.'s 1939 The Gentleman's Companion volume II – An Exotic Drinking Book.

name: Koi Yellow
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Raspberry flavoured vodka
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Sherbet raspberry Martini with a sweet and citrus sour finish.
history: The signature drink at Koi Restaurant, Los Angeles, USA.

name: Kool Hand Luke
preparation: MUDDLE lime in base of glass to release juices. POUR other ingredients into glass, add crushed ice and CHURN (stir). Consider serving with a straw.
ingredients:
3⁄4 fresh	Lime (fresh) (cut into segments)
1 1⁄2 shot	Jamaican-style overproof aged pot still rum
5⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: This looks like a Caipirinha and has a similar balance of sweet, sour and spirit. The bitters bring out the spice in the rum, which is every bit as pungent as cachaça.

name: Lemon Drop Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Citroen Vodka
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Sherbety lemon - well-balanced and refreshing, but not really a Martini.
history: An Alternatini (served in a V-shaped glass but not a Martini) that was popular during the 1990s.

name: Lime Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Lime flavoured vodka
1 1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Fresh egg white gives this drink a wonderfully frothy top and smooths the alcohol and lime juice.

name: Limerick
preparation: SHAKE first three ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda water and lightly stir.
ingredients:
2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A long stretched and so refreshing Irish whiskey lime sour.
history: Basically an Irish whiskey Ricky.

name: Lynchburg Lemonade
preparation: POUR first 3 ingredients into glass, add a splash of soda, fill glass with ice and TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Tennessee whiskey
5⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 2⁄3 shot	Lemon-lime soda (Sprite/7-Up)
review: Tangy, light and very easy to drink.
history: Adapted from a recipe created for the Jack Daniel's distillery in - yep, you guessed it - Lynchburg, Tennessee.

name: Mae West cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1⁄4 shot	Green melon liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
review: A rose-coloured, semi-sweet concoction with a cherry, chocolate flavour.

name: Magic Bus
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Tequila-laced cranberry and orange. Our original recipe called for equal parts of all four ingredients but, this particular bus is a tad racier when fueled with a touch more tequila.

name: Mango Collins
preparation: SHAKE first three ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda, stir and serve with straws.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2 shot	Mango purée
1 1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Lemon juice and gin combine with mango in this refreshing tall drink.
history: For the full story behind the origins of the Collins and its many variations see our Collins page.

name: 'Martini' Thyme
preparation: MUDDLE thyme in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 sprig	Lemon thyme (remove stalks)
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A wonderfully fresh herbal Martini with the distinctive taste of Chartreuse. You'll either love it or hate it.
history: A combination of two very similar drinks, that both originally called for thyme infused gin. The first I discovered at The Lobby Bar (One Aldwych, London) and the other came from Tony Conigliaro at Isola, London, England.

name: Matador No.1
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 shot	Pineapple juice
review: A long Margarita-style drink. The lime and tequila work wonders with the pineapple.

name: Mesa Fresca
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
2 1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Sweet and sour tequila and grapefruit.
history: Adapted from a recipe discovered in 2005 at Mesa Grill in New York City, USA.

name: Milk Punch
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Dark/black/blackstrap rum
1⁄2 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
2 1⁄2 shot	Milk (whole milk/full 3-4% fat)
review: The cream, vanilla and sugar tame the cognac and rum.

name: Moonshine Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄12 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: A wet Martini with balanced hints of maraschino and absinthe.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Negus (Hot)
garnish: Dust with grated nutmeg (and optional cinnamon stick)
preparation: Place bar spoon in warmed glass. POUR all ingredients into glass and STIR.
ingredients:
3 shot	Tawny port
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
Top up with	Boiling water
review: A tangy, citrusy hot drink.
history: Colonel Francis Negus was the MP for Ipswich, England from 1717 to 1732. He created this diluted version of the original Bishop.

name: Osmo
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Akashi-Tai Daiginjo Genshu sake
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
review: A sake based Cosmopolitan.
history: Adapted from a drink discovered in 2005 at Mo Bar, Landmark Mandarin Oriental Hotel, Hong Kong.

name: Passion Fruit Daiquiri
preparation: Cut passion fruits in half and scoop out flesh into shaker (saving one half for garnish). Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 fresh	Passion fruit (fresh)
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: The rum character comes through in this tropically fruity cocktail.

name: Peach Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Peachtree peach schnapps
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: A classic Daiquiri with fragrant peach liqueur replacing sugar.

name: Perfect John
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄4 shot	Galliano L'Autentico liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A straight up Harvey Wallbanger with triple sec.

name: Pisco Punch (Prosser's recipe)
preparation: MUDDLE grapes in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
12 fresh	Green grapes (seedless)
2 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄12 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Grape juice and aromatic grape-based spirit paired with pineapple and the merest hint of absinthe.
history:
Jack Koeppler, the bartender at the Buena Vista Café in San Francisco who's also famous for being the first bartender in America to serve Irish Coffee, was given this recipe by the son of its creator, a fellow San Franciscan by the name of Mr Prosser.

Adapted from Mr Prosser's original recipe which is said to have comprised: 2oz white grape juice, 2 oz pisco, 1 spoon pineapple juice and 1 spoon absinthe.

Our Pisco Punch cocktail page gives a more detailed history of this drink and explains the different recipes.

name: Plum Daiquiri
preparation: CUT plum into quarters, remove stone and peel. MUDDLE plum in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 fresh	Plum (stoned & peeled)
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Depending on the ripeness of the plums, you may need to adjust the quantity of sugar.

name: Polly's Special
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Sweet, sour, flavoursome and balanced.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Victor Bergeron's 1947-72 Trader Vic's Bartender's Guide.

name: Pontberry Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Crème de Mûre liqueur
1 2⁄3 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1 dash	Boker's bitters (optional)
review: A light, fruity, easy drinking cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Dick Bradsell in the late 90s for the opening of Agent Provocateur in Pont Street in London, England.

name: President
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: Delicately fruity sweet and sour.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Pulp Fiction
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with lemon-lime soda.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 2⁄3 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
5⁄6 shot	Apple Schnapps liqueur
1 2⁄3 shot	Lemon-lime soda (Sprite/7-Up)
review: Originally made with apple pulp, this drink has a zingy apple taste.
history: Discovered in 2001 at Teatro Club in London, England.

name: Quarter Deck
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: With flavours of prune, toffee, and maple syrup this is a complex after-dinner cocktail.
history: Long lost classic.

name: Quince Sour
garnish: Lemon slice & Luxardo Maraschino cherry on stick (sail)
preparation: STIR quince jam with vodka in base of shaker to dissolve jam. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
3 barspoon	Quince mustard jam
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: The sweet quince both flavours and balances the sour.

name: Raspberry Martini
preparation: MUDDLE raspberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
8 fresh	Raspberries
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Vodka-laced rich berry fruit and dashes of zesty citrus.

name: Resolute
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Simple but tasty. All three flavours are harmonious.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Roman Punch
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. CHURN (stir) drink and top up ice if necessary. Serve with straws. If serving with cubed rather than crushed ice add 1½ shots of chilled water before shaking.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	White overproof rum
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Spirited and refreshing with herbal notes.

name: Ruby 'Martini'
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Citroen Vodka
1 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A sour, citrus-led variation on the Cosmopolitan.
history: Several appearances in episodes of the U.S. hit TV series, Sex And The City, helped this drink become fashionable in 2002, particularly in New York City. It is thought to have originated at the Wave restaurant in Chicago's W Hotel.

name: Le Sang
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2 shot	Rioja (Crianza) red wine
2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: The tannin in the wine balances the fruit and sweetness nicely.
history: French for 'blood', this cocktail is a twist on the classic Spanish Sangria, which also means 'blood'.

name: Santiago Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: This Daiquiri is particularly delicate in its balance between sweet and sour.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Savannah
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Gin and orange with a hint of chocolate - smoothed with egg white.
history:
Adapted from a recipe in the 1949 edition of Esquire's Handbook for Hosts:
"Savannah
Juice of one-half orange
1 jigger Gin
White of egg
Dash Crème de Cacao"

name: Silver Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Dry and aromatic with a hint of maraschino richness.
history:
Adapted from the Silver Cocktail in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book:
"SILVER COCKTAIL.
2 Dashes Maraschino.
2 Dashes Orange Bitters.
½ French Vermouth.
½ Dry Gin.
Shake well and strain into cocktail glass."

name: South China Breeze
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Lychee syrup
3 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Orange and grapefruit with an oriental influence by way of lychee.

name: Sling (Generic Name)
preparation: SHAKE first three ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda or ginger ale.
ingredients:
2 shot	Brandy, whisk(e)y, gin, rum etc.
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water (or ginger ale)
review: Sugar balances the citrus juice while the spirit fortifies and the carbonate lengthens.
history:
The word 'Sling' comes from the German 'schlingen', meaning 'to swallow', and Slings based on a spirit mixed with sugar and water were popularly drunk in the late 1800s.

Slings are similar to Toddies and like Toddies can be served hot. (Toddies, however, are never served cold.) The main difference between a Toddy and a Sling is that Slings are not flavoured by the addition of spices. Also, Toddies tend to be made with plain water, while Slings are charged with water, soda water or ginger ale.

The earliest known definition of 'cocktail' describes it as a bittered sling.

name: Smartini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Citrus with a crispy chocolate edge. A sweetie.

name: Spencer Cocktail
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & speared Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: To quote Harry Craddock, "Very mellifluous: has a fine and rapid action: for morning work."
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Spiked Apple Cider (Hot)
preparation: MUDDLE cloves in base of shaker. Add cognac and apple juice. SHAKE without ice and fine strain into glass. WARM in microwave then FLOAT double cream over drink.
ingredients:
2 dried	Clove
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
Float	Single cream/half-and-half
review: Warming and lightly spiced under a creamy head.
history: Adapted from a drink discovered in 2006 at Double Seven, New York City, USA.

name: Strawberry Martini

ingredients:

2 shot	Ketel One Vodka

history: Originated in London during the late 1990s.

name: Sunshine No. 2
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄4 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: More a sunset but fruity, flavoursome and well-balanced all the same.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Thriller From Vanilla
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Orange and creamy vanilla fortified with a hint of gin.
history: Adapted from a drink discovered in 2003 at Oporto, Leeds, England. The "Thriller in Manila" was what the 1975 heavyweight fight between Muhammad Ali and Smokin' Joe Frazier became known as.

name: Toast & Orange Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 barspoon	Orange marmalade
3 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Bourbon rounded and enhanced by bitter orange and Peychaud's bitters.

name: Toasted Almond
garnish: Dust with cacao powder or freshly ground nutmeg

ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Ketel One Vodka
5⁄6 shot	Disaronno amaretto
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe

review: Slightly sweet but smooth, creamy and definitely toasted.

name: Tuxedo Cocktail No.1 (Savoy & Duffy's recipe)
preparation: Express lemon zest twist into stirring glass. Add other ingredients, STIR with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 twist	Lemon peel
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Bone dry with faint anise and liquorice notes from the absinthe.
history:
Adapted from recipes in The Savoy Cocktail Book (1930) by Harry Craddock and The Official Mixer's Manual (1934 & 1940) by Patrick Gavin Duffy.
Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Vanilla Vodka Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
3⁄4 shot	Licor 43 Original liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: A Vodka Sour with a blast of spicy vanilla.

name: Vavavoom
preparation: POUR ingredients into chilled glass. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
Top up with	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: This drink does indeed give champagne that vavavoom.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2002 by Yannick Miseriaux at The Fifth Floor Bar, Harvey Nichols, London, England, and named after the Renault television advertisements.

name: Wasabi Martini
preparation: Squeeze a pea-sized quantity of wasabi paste onto a barspoon and STIR with vodka until wasabi dissolves. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 pea	Wasabi paste
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: This "Martini" would be more accurately named a Wasabi Vodka Sour, but besides the now-dated name, this child of the early noughties is balanced with attractive spicy heat and a zesty finish.
history:
Created in 2004 by Philippe Guidi at Morton's, London, England.
Martini cocktail and its evolution

name: Watermelon & Basil Cocktail

1 slice	Watermelon (fresh) (chopped)

name: Whisky Fizz

ingredients:
2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
Top up with	Soda from siphon
review: The character of the whisky shines through this refreshing, balanced, sweet and sour drink.

name: Apricot Rickey

1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin

preparation: SHAKE first three ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with lemonade. Lightly stir and serve with straws.

1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)

review: Light, fruity, easy and very refreshing.

2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Smooth and balanced with great rum character. Lime fresh and fruity sweet.
history: Circa 1930s, USA

name: Hot Toddy (brandy & lemon)
garnish: Express and float coin-sized lemon zest twist
preparation: POUR first 3 ingredients in warmed glass and stir. TOP with boiling water while spoon still in glass, briefly stir, garnish and serve.

1⁄3 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)

review: Warms the cockles with cognac and a good dose of citrus.

name: El Presidente Menocal Special

name: Tom Arnold
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka

3⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)

history: This is one of a series of tea-based drinks that were originally named after golfers. It takes its name from the actor and comedian who starred in National Lampoon's Golf Punk.

name: Apple, Cucumber & Elderflower cup
preparation: MUDDLE cucumber in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 inch	Cucumber (fresh)
2 shot	Bison grass vodka
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review: Apple and Zubrówka is a magic combination, as is apple and elderflower. Here these flavoursome combinations are enhanced and freshened by cucumber.
history: Discovered in 2007 at Public Restaurant, New York City, USA.

name: Astor
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Swedish Punsch liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Citrus and the tang of Swedish punch add a distinctive flavour to gin in this tasty vintage cocktail.
history:
Recipe adapted from Albert Stevens Crockett's 1931 The Old Waldorf-Astoria Bar Book where the recipe is accompanied by a notation as to who or what this cocktail is named after, citing "John Jacob" or "William Waldorf", both members of the Astor family, a wealthy American family whose fortune originated in the fur trade and became centred on New York City real estate investments.

John Jacob Astor IV (1864-1912) was the real estate magnate who built New York's Astoria Hotel, "the world's most luxurious hotel" and died as the richest passenger when the RMS Titanic sunk.

William Waldorf "Willy" Astor, 1st Viscount Astor (1848-1919) was John Jacob's cousin and rival who built the original Waldorf Hotel next door to his cousin's hotel. The combined complex became known as the Waldorf-Astoria Hotel.

name: Bobby Burns (Crockett's recipe)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Scotch and vermouth with added depth of flavour courtesy of absinthe and orange bitters.
history: Recipe adapted from Albert Stevens Crockett's 1931 Old Waldorf-Astoria Bar Days where the cocktail is listed as "Robert Burns" accompanied by the following notation, "It may have been named after the celebrated Scotsman. Chances are, however, that it was christened in honour of a cigar salesman, who 'bought' in the Old Bar [at the Waldorf-Astoria]." Robert Burns was a brand of cigars and the name of a cigar shop close to the Waldorf-Astoria Hotel. It could be that the hotel sold these cigars, and the shop's owner was such a good patron of the bar that a cocktail was named in his honour. See Bobby Burns cocktail history for the whole story.

name: El Coco
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Coconut water
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Rum and coconut water with the merest hint of lime.
history: Created in 2008 by Richard Hunt at Mahiki in London, England and named after the coconut palm outside the original Bacardi distillery in Santiago de Cuba.

name: Dutch Master
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄6 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄6 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: It's a vodka and tonic but not like you know it.
history: Created in 2007 by Bruce Borthwick in Fife, Scotland.

name: Elixirita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 shot	Lime (fresh)
1⁄2 shot	Agave syrup
1⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)
review: Basically, a Tommy's Margarita with a splash of cognac served straight-up.
history: Created in 2007 by H. Joseph Ehrmann, this is the signature Margarita at his bar Elixir in San Francisco, USA. He dedicated it to the Boston College Eagles.

name: Final Ward
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
3⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: The Last Word is classically made with gin, maraschino, Chartreuse and lime juice. In this riff, whiskey replaces the gin, and Mr Ward switches citrus fruits from lime to lemon.
history:
Perhaps the best-known riff on the classic Last Word, it was created in 2007 by Phil Ward at Death & Co., New York City, USA.
Last Word history

name: Gin Daisy #3 (Modern long style)
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda and serve with straws.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
2 1⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Fruit and botanicals served long and refreshing.
history: Daisies can be served in a goblet filled with crushed ice, straight up, or, as in this case, long in a Collins glass.

name: Indochine
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Ginger liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Pineapple juice
2 drop	Boker's bitters (optional)
review: Slightly sweet and very frothy. Easy drinking with a ginger kick.
history: Adapted from a drink promoted at the end of 2007 by the owners of Canton Ginger Liqueur.

name: Jägerita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Jägermeisteror other German amaro
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: This Margarita may look a little like liquid mud but is surprisingly tasty with liquorice-forward herbal notes alongside bright citrus.
history: Origin: Created by David Cordoba and made in September 2008 for yours truly and others to try at my Cabinet Room in London. Jeffrey Morgenthaler, who was among the influential bartenders present that night, took the Jägerita back to Portland, Oregon, where he wrote about that night and David's whacky Margarita on JeffreyMorgenthaler.com. Then, in 2014, he included it on the opening menu of his bar, Pépé Le Moko. Thanks to Morgenthaler's influence, the Jägerita has gone on to become a contemporary classic.

name: Lemon Caipirovska
preparation: MUDDLE lemon in base of shaker, add other ingredients and SHAKE with 6oz scoop crushed ice. Pour into glass without straining and serve with straws.
ingredients:
3⁄4 fresh	Lemon (fresh) (chopped wedges)
2 shot	Ketel One Citroen Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A lemon-tastic Caipirovska.
history: Created in 2002 by Tony Conigliaro at Isola, London, England.

name: Maçã Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cachaça
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Subtle combination of cachaça, fresh lime, apple juice and elderflower.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2007 by Jamie Terrell, New York, USA while he was working for Sagatiba. Maçã means apple in Portuguese.

name: Margaret Duffy
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Swedish Punsch liqueur
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Spiced and sweetened cognac.
history: Vintage cocktail of unknown origin.

name: Orange Spur
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Anisette liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Stir well - this bittersweet drink benefits from dilution.
history: Created in 2008 by Don Lee at PDT, New York City, USA.

name: Pineapple Fix
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1 shot	Pineapple juice
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Rum and pineapple are a match made in heaven, here with lemon adding citrus freshness.

name: Port Flip
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 1⁄2 shot	Tawny port
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 fresh	Egg (white & yolk)
review: Old-school and something of a meal in a glass. Well, more of a tasty snack!
history: The "Port Wine Flip" first appears in Jerry Thomas' 1887 Bartender's Guide: How to Mix Drinks, or The Bon Vivant's Companion.

name: Pre Siesta
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Orange liqueurs and bitters flavour this tequila-based, salmon-pink bittersweet cocktail that is perhaps better-served on-the-rocks.
history: Created in 2007 by Rich Hunt at Mahiki in London, England.

name: Smoke of Scotland
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
review: Smoky, with floral and tropical fruit notes from the elderflower liqueur and added complexity from the vermouth and Cynar.
history: Created in 2007 by Vincenzo Marianella at Providence, Los Angeles, USA.

name: Warsaw Pact
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Bison grass vodka
1⁄3 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1 1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review: Fruit and mint flavours combine in this balanced, complex, and yet easy cocktail.
history: Adapted from a drink discovered in 2007 at Paparazzi bar in Warsaw, Poland.

name: Zac's Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Originally made for Zacapa rum which suits lemon rather than lime in a Daiquiri. Daiquiris benefit from dilution and here a dash of apple juice adds a barely perceptible amount of fruit as well.
history: Created in January 2009 by yours truly (Simon Difford) at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Elderflower Manhattan
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Elderflower replaces sweet vermouth in this floral Manhattan.
history:
Created in 2006 by yours truly and originally named Paris Manhattan.
Manhattan cocktail history

name: G & Tea
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with tonic water.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1 shot	Cold black tea
2 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: Dry, floral, long and refreshing.
history: Created in 2006 by yours truly in London, England.

name: Hearst Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A fantastically wet, sweet and aromatic Martini.
history:
This was supposedly a favourite of hacks who worked for the American newspaper magnate, William Randolph Hearst, and is believed to have been created at New York's Waldorf-Astoria. It is nicknamed 'The Disgruntled Journalist' and indeed, is not dissimilar to a Journalist cocktail with extra bitters.
Dry Martini history and evolution

name: Hypnotic Margarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Hpnotiq Tropical liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Liqueurs combine harmoniously with lime and tequila in this tangy, fruity Margarita. However, I remain unconvinced by Hpnotiq.
history: Created in 2005 by Gary Regan at Painter's, Cornwall-on-Hudson, New York, USA.

name: L'amour En Fuite
preparation:
1. POUR absinthe into ice-filled glass, TOP with water and leave to stand.
2. Separately STIR gin, vermouth and elderflower liqueur with ice.
3. DISCARD contents of glass (absinthe, water and ice) and STRAIN contents of mixing glass into absinthe-coated glass. (No ice in glass.)
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Elderflower liqueur
review: Serious yet approachably subtle with hints of vermouth and elderflower dominated by absinthe and gin.
history: Created in 2007 by Jamie Boudreau, Seattle, USA, originally using Lillet. The name comes from a 1979 French film.

name: Lucien Gaudin
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: A vintage French riff on a Negroni. This cocktail is perhaps better, certainly easier drinking when served on-the-rocks.
history:
This vintage cocktail is named after Lucien Gaudin, a French fencer who achieved gold medals with two different weapons at the 1924 Olympics in Paris and the 1928 Olympics in Amsterdam. After retiring from competitive sport, Gaudin became a journalist and also co-owner of Les Films Sportifs, a sports media company noted for producing the film of the 1924 Olympics, now known as "the real Chariots of Fire Olympics." Sadly, the company was not a financial success and Gaudin committed suicide in 1934 following its bankruptcy.

The cocktail, which won the Honorary Cup at the Professional Bartenders Championship in Paris on 2nd February 1929, first appears in the Cocktails de Paris Présentes book, published the same year. This credits the recipe to Charlie of Le Cheval Pie (The Black And White Horse), a Parisian restaurant that operated between 1925 and 1930 where Gaudin is thought to have been a regular.

name: Moonlight Cocktail (Harry Craddock's recipe)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄4 shot	Kirschwasser (cherry) eau-de-vie
1 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
1 1⁄4 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Craddock describes this as 'a very dry cocktail'. It is, but pleasantly so.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Neal's Barbados Cosmopolitan
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
review: Your standard Cosmopolitan made more compelling by a slug of warming Caribbean spirit.
history:
Created in 1985 by Neal Murray at Fog City Diner in San Francisco, USA. This cocktail was added to the menu at BIX, San Francisco in 1988 and was still on the menu in 2006 when I first discovered this riff on a Cosmopolitan.
See: Cosmopolitan cocktail history.

name: The [Pick of] Destiny
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Elderflower liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
3 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Fresh floral orange - just picked.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2007 by Amanda Washington at Rye, San Francisco, USA.

name: Pina Colada Cocktail (Cuban Style)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
4 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: This Colada has no coconut, but it is smooth, balanced and rather tasty.
history: Basically a pineapple-flavoured Daiquiri. This recipe is based on a piece in the December 1922 edition of Travel Magazine, the first known written reference to a Piña Colada, and is what we now refer to as a 'Cuban Style Piña Colada' - one without coconut.

name: Trilby No.2
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
review: Salmon pink in colour and distinctly different in style. One of those drinks you just have to try.

name: Berlin Sour
garnish: Lemon slice & Luxardo Maraschino cherry on stick (sail)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Mentzendorff Kümmel liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: The sweet powerful flavours of kummel and maraschino liqueurs are tamed and harnessed in this sour.
history: Created in 2009 by Thorsten Pannek at Hilton, Frankfurt, Germany.

name: Fibber McGee
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Delicately flavoured, bittersweet grapefruit and sweet vermouth fortified with gin.
history: Adapted from a recipe in David A. Embury's 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks.

name: Hot Tommy
preparation: Place spoon in glass. POUR first 3 ingredients into glass. TOP up with boiling water and STIR until agave nectar dissolves.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Agave syrup
Top up with	Boiling water
review: A Mexican twist on the original winter pick-me-up.
history: Created in December 2009 by Alan Brown of Menzel's Bar, who says of this drink, "Over the busy festive period, feeling full of flu and cold I decided to make a hot toddy to soothe my symptoms. Having no honey to hand I tried using agave nectar instead. This led me to the idea of using tequila and lime instead of lemon (to complement the tequila) with the agave and boiling water. The name for the drink is a Hot Tommy, a nod to the Tommy's Margarita, which makes use of both tequila and agave."

name: Limey Gimlet
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Lime cordial (sweetened lime juice)
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: The two naval spirits sit harmoniously together in this delicately flavoured Gimlet.
history: Created in 2010 by yours truly and named due to the Gimlet's Navy origins and British sailors being nicknamed 'limeys', thanks to mixing their daily rum ration of with lime or lemon juice and sugar to help prevent scurvy. The mixture was known as Grog.

name: A Sinking Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1 1⁄2 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
1⁄6 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
review: Copper red and bitter sweet with wine, elderflower and a touch of cherry liqueur.
history: Created in 2009 by Rich Hunt at Quo Vadis, London, England.

name: Tanglefoot
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Swedish Punsch liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Light rum, lemon and orange juice served short with a tang of Swedish punch.

name: Applejack Rabbit (served long)
garnish: Cinnamon stick and dust with freshly grated cinnamon
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled jar.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Applejack brandy bottled-in-bond (50% alc./vol)
1⁄2 shot	Maple syrup
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Apple brandy sweetened by maple syrup, soured by lemon and lengthened with orange.
history: This on-the-rocks and jarred version of The Savoy Cocktail Book classic Apple Jack Rabbit is adapted from a serve created in 2009 by Dino Koletsas at Bourne & Hollingsworth in London, England.

name: Cablegram
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Ginger syrup
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Whiskey and ginger with a fresh zing of lime.
history: The Cablegram first appears in William "Cocktail" Boothby's 1908 The World's Drinks and How to Mix Them, where it's described as being "A Bourbon Whiskey and Ginger Ale Highball with a little sour added..." This forgotten classic was given a new lease of life in 2009 by Eric Alperin at The Varnish in Los Angeles, USA with a combination of ginger syrup and soda replacing ginger ale and a rye whiskey base adding a touch more kick.

name: Caribeño
preparation: SHAKE all the ingredients with ice and strain into an ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
3 shot	Coconut water
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A Daiquiri that is light on lime and elongated with coconut water. Delicious and very refreshing.
history: Created in 2009 by Martin Cate at Forbidden Island in Alameda, California, USA.

name: Creole Gimlet
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Lime cordial (sweetened lime juice)
1 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Falernum adds a touch of Caribbean spice to this Gimlet.
history: Created in 2009 by Gonçalo de Sousa Monteiro, Berlin, Germany.

name: Dutch Word
garnish: Lime zest twist (discarded) & lime wedge on rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
2⁄3 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
2⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A genever-based variation to the classic Last Word cocktail.
history:
Created in December 2010 by yours truly at The Cabinet Room, London, England.
Last Word history

name: Entwistle's Error
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with tonic water.
ingredients:
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: Long and refreshing with rum character, lemon freshness and tonic water's slightly bitter bite.

name: Fandango
garnish: Mint leaf or mint sprig pegged to rim
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄4 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: A heady mix of gin, vodka and the distinctive herbal flavour of Chartreuse.
history: Adapted from a recipe in a book published in Paris in 1929 titled Cocktails de Paris Presentés Par RIP which credits Georges Robineau from California who won the Honorary Cup at the Professional Bartenders' Championship held in Paris on 2nd February 1929 with this cocktail.

name: Fur Collar
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Apricot brandy adds fruity zingyness to what otherwise would be a Screwdriver served straight-up.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Ted Saucier's 1951 Bottoms Up book.

name: Tropic Thunder
garnish: Dust with freshly ground black pepper
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Crème de Pêche de Vigne liqueur
