1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Pineapple juice
review: Gin, peach, lemon juice and pineapple juice may not seem the most obvious combination but it's a combo that works.
history: Created by Sean Henry at Epernay Champagne Bar, Leeds, England and to quote Sean is "named Tropic Thunder as it aptly describes what to expect on the palate."

name: The Dunaway
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄4 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄2 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A dry sherry-rich aperitivo cocktail.
history: Created in 2010 by Misty Kalkofen at Drink in Boston, USA.

name: Grand Sour
preparation: DRY SHAKE all ingredients (without ice). SHAKE again with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: The rich cognac and orange flavours of Grand Marnier shine in this balanced and flavoursome sour.

name: Hey Hey Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A sidecar-like cocktail with a good balance between sweet (triple sec) and sour (lemon juice), fortified by cognac and smoothed by Lillet Blanc.
history: Hey Hey is a song by Eric Clapton and also a long-running variety television programme on Australian television. However, this cocktail is thought to predate both. The origin of the Hey Hey cocktail is unknown but its original calling for 'Kina Lillet' dates the drink before 1986 as this is when the product's name was changed to Lillet Blanc.

name: Procrastination Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
review: A wet martini flavoured with copious amounts of limoncello (which slightly sweetens and adds surprisingly subtle lemon favours) and a dash of Chartreuse which shines through.
history: Recipe created by Paul Clarke, the Seattle-based cocktail enthusiast behind the excellent cocktailchronicles.com.

name: Special
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Grand Marnier and grapefruit juice provide a flavoursome sweet and sour combination fortified with malty Scotch notes.

name: Pineapple Lassi Cocktail
preparation: MUDDLE cardamom and then pineapple in base of shaker. ADD other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3 whole	Green cardamom pods
3 wedge	Pineapple (fresh) (cored, skinned and chopped)
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Yoghurt liqueur
review: Creamy yoghurty cardamom and pineapple laced with vodka.
history: Created in 2011 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Gentleman's Agreement
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Tennessee whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Amaretto-like almond flavours with Tennessee whiskey balanced with fresh lemon juice and lengthened with refreshing soda.
history: A cocktail originally used by Brown-Forman to promote Gentleman Jack.

name: Coessential
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
8 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄6 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: To quote from the Oxford English Dictionary, "This is done with the help of the hands of consciousness that extend from the spiritual heart and are coessential to it". It is and John Coe did. Thanks again John, this delicate but aromatic drink is dedicated to you.
history: Created in 2011 by yours truly (Simon Difford) at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Le Fume
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄4 shot	Lapsang souchong sugar syrup
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water
review: Peat smoked Islay whisky meets pinewood smoked Chinese tea, fortified with vodka.
history: Adapted from a drink discovered in 2011 at Le Salon Bar at L'Atelier de Joël Robuchon, London, England.

name: Holland House (Kappeler's rye-based)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Spicy rye whiskey delicately sweetened and given an orange accent by a splash of triple sec and heightened with a couple of dashes of bitters. This is a cocktail that benefits from dilution, hence our addition of water, and arguably works better on-the-rocks rather than straight-up.
history:
Recipe adapted from George J. Kappeler's 1895 book Modern American Drinks: How To Mix and Serve All Kinds of Cups and Drinks. Kappeler's recipe stipulates, "Mixing-glass half-full fine ice, two dashes Peychaud bitters, one-half pony Eau de Vie d'Oranges, one and a half pony old rye whiskey, a piece lemon peel. Mix. Moisten the edge of cocktail glass with lemon, dip in sugar. Strain the cocktail into prepared glass."

There are numerous versions of the Holland House, but Kappeler was head barman at the Holland House Hotel so was well placed to recount how the hotel's signature cocktail was made.

Orange eau de vie, or distillate of oranges is not readily available but clear sweetened orange distillate in the shape of triple sec is, hence we have used as a substitute in this drink.

Kappler's book also features a "Holland Gin Cocktail" as follows:
"Mixing-glass half-full fine ice, two dashes Angostura bitters or Peychaud bitters, two dashes gum-syrup, one jigger Holland gin. Mix: strain into a cocktail glass. Add a piece of twisted lemon-peel or a maraschino cherry."

name: Hunter Cocktail
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
2⁄3 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: An after-dinner cocktail with spirituous bourbon, sweetened and mellowed by rich cherry. (We previously had this cocktail served straight-up but it's better on-the-rocks.)
history: The origins of this cocktail are unknown, but its popularity has been much helped by the famous bartender Hidetsugu Ueno San recommending it to guests at his High Five bar in Ginzo, Tokyo, Japan.

name: Shaky Pete's Ginger Brew
glass: Rum barrel mug or pint glass
preparation: Blitz BLEND the first three ingredients with two ice cubes for ten seconds. Fine strain into chilled glass and TOP with beer. See Origin for Pete's original homemade ginger syrup.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 shot	Ginger syrup
4 shot	British bitter ale
review: Imagine a ginger-flavoured shandy with a kick – pretty much describes this gin-laced lemon and ginger-flavoured beer-tail.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2012 by Pete Jeary (aka Shaky Pete) at Hawksmoor, Seven Dials, London, England. Pete's original recipe calls for homemade ginger syrup made by blending 1 kg ginger (peeled and chopped), 1 kg caster sugar and 500ml water fine strained into bottles. Pete uses London Pride beer.

name: Garden, Grain & Grape
preparation: MUDDLE grapes in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, DRY SHAKE (without ice). SHAKE again with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5 fresh	Green grapes (seedless)
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
1 dash	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Pale green lime with frothy white head, this delicate wine and grape flavoured drink is laced with a large splash of vodka.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2012 by Mal Spence at Blythswood Square Hotel, Glasgow, Scotland.

name: La Tour Eiffel
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Bittersweet cognac-influenced palate with lingering flavours of liquorice root, honey, pine and eucalyptus from the Suze.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2007 by Gary "gaz" Regan after a Sazerac-fuelled trip to New Orleans. He was inspired by how the Sazerac might have been if it had originally been created in France rather than New Orleans.

name: Trinidad Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: This deep lurid reddy-brown cocktail won't be to everybody's taste but that's only to be expected with one-and-a-half shots of bitters. However, if you like cough candy then perhaps this cocktail is for you.
history: Created in 2009 by Giuseppe Gonzalez at Clover Club Bar in Brooklyn, USA and inspired by the competition-winning Trinidad Especial by Valentino Bolognese.

name: Sazerac (New Orleans style)
preparation: Ice glass and set to one side. Separately, in another glass stir other ingredients with ice. Discard ice in the now chilled and set glass aside and rinse with absinthe (or Herbsaint). Then strain cocktail into absinthe/Herbsaint washed glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
4 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: While bartenders in other cities have complicated the Sazerac by using a combination of spirits [us included - Difford's Sazerac recipe], in New Orleans they keep it simple: straight rye whiskey with a dash of sugar, stirred and strained into an Herbsaint-washed glass.
history:
The following story originates in Stanley Clisby Arthur's 1937 Famous New Orleans Drinks & how to Mix 'em, and for years, this was accepted as being a true account of the origin of the Sazerac cocktail. However, research by cocktail historian David Wondrich suggests the Sazerac actually originated as a bottled Whiskey Cocktail sold by the Sazerac company. However, "never let the truth stand in the way of a good story."

Brandy-based cocktails were being served in New Orleans before the Sazerac was created, and these early mixed drinks almost certainly included bitters, possibly Stoughton's Bitters, a long-extinct medicinal stomach bitters. The ingredients for the Sazerac have varied over the years, but its flavour has remained distinctive due to one essential ingredient: Peychaud's aromatic bitters, created by Antoine Amedee Peychaud.

His story starts in 1795 when he arrived in New Orleans as a refugee after his father was forced to flee the island of San Domingo and his family's coffee plantation after the slaves rebelled. Antoine grew up to become a pharmacist and bought his own drug and apothecary store at 437 Rue Royale (then No. 123 Royal Street) in 1834. Here, he created an 'American Aromatic Bitter Cordial' and marketed it as a medicinal tonic. Such potions were fashionable then, and there were many similar products.

Antoine also served his bitters mixed with brandy and other liquors, and it has been falsely claimed that the word 'cocktail' originated with Antoine and the measure, known as a 'coquetier', he used to prepare drinks. However, the term "cocktail" first appeared in print in an upstate New York newspaper in 1806 when Antoine was but a child.

Meanwhile, sometime around 1850, Sewell T. Taylor, another New Orleans entrepreneur gave up being a bar owner to move into the liquor business, becoming the local agent for a French cognac company, 'Sazerac-du-Forge et Fils' of Limoges. His bar, the Merchant's Exchange Coffee House at 13 Exchange Alley, was taken over by either Aaron Bird or John B. Schiller.

Exchange Alley used to run between Royal Street and Exchange Place in the French Quarter, where the Wyndham Hotel now stands, a service road under the hotel still links the two streets. It is here, at the Exchange Coffee House, sometime between 1850 and 1859, that the Sazerac Cocktail was created, based on and named after Taylor's Sazerac cognac with Peychaud's aromatic bitters and sugar. The cocktail became the bar's main speciality.

In 1869/70, Thomas H. Handy, the bar's bookkeeper, took over the Exchange Coffee House and renamed it the Sazerac Coffee House after its house cocktail. Meanwhile, Antoine Peychaud fell on hard times and sold his pharmacy store, along with the formula and brand name of his bitters, which Handy acquired in 1873. Having purchased the bar and the bitters required to make its house cocktail, Handy then faced a predicament as cognac, the main ingredient of the Sazerac Cocktail, became hard to obtain.

The phylloxera aphid, a bug which attacks the roots of vines, devastated French vineyards in the late 1860s-1870s and so practically halted cognac production, forcing Handy to change the recipe of the Sazerac Cocktail. He still used the all-important Peychaud's bitters but substituted American-distilled Maryland Club rye whiskey, retaining a dash of cognac. Around this time, perhaps before the change to rye whiskey, a splash of the newly fashionable absinthe was added to the Sazerac. As the cognac became more scarce, so it gradually disappeared from the drink.

To quote from Stanley Clisby Arthur's 1937 Famous New Orleans Drinks & how to mix'em, "The absinthe innovation has been credited to Leon Lamothe who in 1858 was a bartender for Emile Seignouret, Charles Cavaroc & Co., a wine importing firm located in the old Seignouret mansion still standing at 520 Royal Street. More likely it was about 1870 when Lamothe was employed at Pina's restaurant in Burgundy Street that he experimented with absinthe and made the Sazerac what it is today."

Before he died in 1889, Handy disclosed the recipe for his house cocktail to William T. "Cocktail Bill" Boothby who published it in his 1908 book, The World's Drinks and How to Mix Them.

Sazerac (Boothby's recipe)
¾ jigger Whiskey
2 dashes Peychaud
Absinthe to wet glass
½ spoon Sugar syrup
1 slice Lemon peel
Chill cocktail glass, wet with few drops absinthe and toss out. Stir other ingredients well with ice, strain into prepared glass and serve with ice water chaser.

In the 1890s, the Sazerac Company began to bottle and market the Sazerac Cocktail, made with rye whiskey instead of cognac. The cocktail, which continued to be served at the Sazerac Bar, was further adapted in 1912 when absinthe was banned in the US. The Sazerac company started to produce a product called Herbsaint as an absinthe substitute, and although absinthe has been legal in the USA since 2007, most bars in New Orleans continue to make their Sazerac Cocktails with Herbsaint rather than absinthe.

The Sazerac Bar reopened after Prohibition at 300 Carondelet Street. In 1949, Seymour Weiss, the Vice President and Managing Director of the nearby Roosevelt Hotel purchased the rights to use the name Sazerac Bar from the Sazerac Company. He renovated a former Wine and Spirits store on Baronne Street and, on 26th September 1949, opened the new Sazerac Bar. Weiss published that the new bar would abolish its 'men only' rule and welcome women. The move was marketing genius and women flocked to the opening, leading to the event becoming known as 'Storming the Sazerac'.

In 1959, the Sazerac Bar on Baronne Street was closed, and the name transferred to the hotel's Main Bar, which had opened in 1938. Here, the Sazerac Bar remains popular and can be considered the spiritual and actual home of the Sazerac with around 40,000 Sazeracs served there every year. (To allay confusion, the hotel originally opened in 1893 as The Hotel Grunewald, then became The Fairmont, then The Roosevelt before reopening after Hurricane Katrina as The Fairmont.)

In 2007, Ann Tuennerman, then of The New Orleans Culinary and Cultural Preservation Society, lobbied the Louisiana legislature to "Save the Sazerac". The following March, state senator Edwin R. Murray filed a Senate Bill designating the Sazerac as Louisiana's official state cocktail. The bill was defeated on 8 April 2008, but after further debate and lobbying, on 23 June 2008, the Louisiana Legislature passed a bill proclaiming the Sazerac as New Orleans' official cocktail.

name: Wordsmith
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Jamaican-style overproof aged pot still rum
3⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
3⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Punchy pot-still rum with equally powerful Green Chartreuse supported by maraschino liqueur with lime zestiness. Powerful in every respect. (Perhaps split serve between two in Nick & Nora glasses.)
history:
A riff on a Last Word created in 2009 by Chuck Taggart, Los Angeles and named by Dave Stolte.
See: Last Word history

name: The Dandy
preparation: STIR first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Bénédictine adds both saffron flavour and vivid yellow colour to this cognac based cocktail with maraschino contributing fruity notes. Champagne dries and provides effervescence and body to this well-balanced cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe discovered in 2014 at Hawksmoor Spitalfields in London, England. In turn, this apparently comes from a punch served at New York's Waldorf-Astoria in the 1930s.

name: Silent Seven
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Tennessee whiskey
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
history: A riff on the classic 'Silent Third' cocktail first published in the 1937 Cafe Royal Cocktail Book. Originally made with Scotch whisky but perhaps not so silent with rock 'n' roll Tennessee whiskey.

name: Cosmopolis cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Kleos Mastiha liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A riff on a Cosmopolitan with the distinctive Greek influence of mastiha.
history: For more recipes, origins and history behind the Cosmopolitan cocktail, see our Cosmopolitan page.

name: Mastiha Mojito
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. CHURN (stir) with bar spoon. Fill glass with more crushed ice and CHURN some more. Keep adding ice and churning until drink fills glass. Serve with straws.
ingredients:
12 fresh	Mint leaves
1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 1⁄2 shot	Kleos Mastiha liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Mastiha adds a distinctively Greek fresh flavour to this otherwise fairly classic mojito.
history: For more recipes, its origins and history, see the Mojito Cocktail.

name: Mastiha Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Kleos Mastiha liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Some use a whole shot of lemon juice and correspondingly a tad more sugar. It’s also common to add a dash of Angostura bitters but we prefer the refreshing flavour of mastiha unhindered.

name: Sainte Trinite (Holy Trinity)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review:
Cognac, elderflower liqueur and Chartreuse (a trinity indeed) with dashes of bitters and an aromatic citrus twist. This is a boozy cocktail so you may prefer our 25% smaller riff to suit a Nick & Nora rather than the original Coupe glass:
45ml / 1½oz Cognac
15ml / ½oz Elderflower liqueur
10ml / 1/3oz Yellow Chartreuse
1 dash Orange bitters
history: Created by Lewis Roberts at Tariff & Dale in Manchester, England.

name: IS talking
preparation: STIR first ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with tonic.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 1⁄3 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
Top up with	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: A cognac and genever gin and tonic with a sweet zesty orange influence.
history: Created in 2015 by Hans Berendijk at Buster's, Amsterdam, Netherlands.

name: Harry Dean Stanton
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
1 dash	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: The choice and generosity of dash of chocolate bitters is key to the success of this boozy after dinner cocktail. Nail this and the chocolate amplifies fig and raison notes.
history: Created in 2015 by Will Howson at Tonkotsu Mare Street, London, England, and named after the American actor, musician, and singer.

name: Red Haven
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
3⁄4 shot	Ruby port
3⁄4 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Ruby port contributes rich wine notes to this Scotch whisky-based cocktail, with rhubarb amaro contributing complex bittersweet flavours. The Sun Tavern's original spec calls for "oak bitters", but given its "Red" moniker, I opted for Peychaud's Bitters.
history: Adapted from a drink created by Tommy Cummins and discovered in January 2017 at The Sun Tavern, Bethnal Green, London, England, which called for Nardini Rabarbaro Amaro instead of Cynar.

name: Coffee Negroni
garnish: Orange zest twist & float 3 coffee beans
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and lightly stir.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
review: Gin-forward, boozy and bittersweet – as it says on the tin, this is a coffee-influenced Negroni – simple as that.
history: Created in January 2017 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room in London, England.

name: May Vesper
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
5⁄6 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A bone dry and Islay smoked Vesper "may" appeal – certainly worth a try if you're into Martinis and Islay whisky.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created by Angus Waugh in Edinburgh, Scotland who originally made this cocktail with Bruichladdich malt whisky and The Botanist gin. He loves Vespers and enjoys Bruichladdich and Botanist gin, plus they are both made at the same distillery. "With that in mind, I decided to make a Vesper using The Botanist gin and replacing the single measure of vodka in the recipe with a measure of The Classic Laddie (not too peaty). I retained the Lillet Blanc in honour of the "Auld Alliance" between Scotland and France in the 13th to 16th centuries. I call the cocktail the "May Vesper", May being James Bond's Scottish housekeeper in the Fleming novels."
Bond's Vesper Martini story

name: Juan & Jeanne
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
2⁄3 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
2⁄3 shot	Blood orange liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Tequila-based with sour citrus balanced by the rich red wine-like berry flavours of cassis.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2017 by Jeff Berry at Beachbum Berry's Latitude 29, New Orleans, USA which was brought to our attention by gazregan.com where we learnt that "A Mexican base + a French modifier = Juan + Jeanne."

Our recipe says broadly true to Jeff's original proportions, but we've reduced all the ingredients by 12% to suit a medium-sized coupe.

name: Naughty German
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄6 shot	Jägermeisteror other German amaro
1⁄3 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Jägermeister spice and rich cassis combine wonderfully in this after-dinner sipper, with subtle black liquorice and aniseed.
history: Created in 2017 by Florian Beuren, Jägermeister's UK brand ambassador.

name: Le Premier Word
garnish: Lemon zest twist & mist with Islay scotch
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice). TOP with cider and lightly stir.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Medium dry apple cider
review: A cider top eases drinkers into this spirit forward, Chartreuse-heavy riff on the classic Last Word.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2017 by Katherine Boushel at Atwater Cocktail Club in Montréal, Canada. The name (meaning First Word) and indeed the ingredients of this riff on the classic Last Word, reflect Montréal's French and English influences.
Last Word history

name: Hazelnut Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Hazelnut sugar syrup
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: There are two distinctively different types of hazelnut syrup available, the "roasted" version being more intensely flavoured than plain hazelnut syrup. If you use light, charcoal-filtered carta blanca-style rum, I suggest you use plain hazelnut syrup. However, this cocktail is perhaps better with a more flavoursome 'gold' rum and roasted hazelnut syrup.
history: Recipe by yours truly.

name: Washington's Applejack Mule
preparation: SHAKE first three ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with ginger beer and lightly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Applejack brandy bottled-in-bond (50% alc./vol)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
3 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: Take a Moscow Mule and make with apple brandy in place of vodka and you've a Washington's Applejack Mule. Tasty – arguably tastier than a Moscow Mule.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2017 by Jamie Boudreau at Canon, Seattle, USA.

A detailed history of the Moscow Mule cocktail, of which this drink is a variant, can be found on our page.

name: Mandarine Daisy
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Mandarine Napoleon liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Agave syrup
review: "Citrusy and sour" sums up this refreshing gin-laced cocktail with rich mandarin orange liqueur soured by lime.

name: Prospector No.2
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Averna Amaro
1⁄3 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A Sweet Manhattan riff with rich Pedro Ximénez sherry taming bourbon and amaro adding complexity.

name: Passion Fruit Altern'atini (no added sugar & low-cal.)
preparation: Cut passion fruits in half and scoop out flesh into shaker (keep one half for garnish). Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 fresh	Passion fruit (fresh)
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Sugar-free sweetener
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura (optional)
review: A couple of dashes orange bitters helps add a touch of complexity and balance to this vodka-laced fruity cocktail, but beware those bitters may add trace amounts of sugar.
history:
Adapted from the classic serve by yours truly (Simon Difford) in January 2019.

Also see the Martini Cocktail and its evolution.

name: Vodka Collins (no added sugar & low-calorie)
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Sugar-free sweetener
3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Cleansing, easy drinking, sugar-free and just 100 calories.
history:
Adapted from the classic serve by yours truly (Simon Difford) in January 2019.

Also see Collins Cocktails - recipes & history.

name: Pursuit of Happiness
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 dash	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water) (optional)
review: A banana influenced riff on a Scotch Negroni with crème de banana sweetness balanced by bitter notes and faint saltiness. Enjoy as an aperitivo or digestivo.
history: Created in 2018 by Josh Davies at The Hedonist Project in Leeds, England, this cocktail was originally based on Chivas 12 Year Old Scotch, and was created for the 2018 Chivas Masters Competition in London. Josh's original spec calls for this drink to be served over a large ice cube in a coupe. Seems wrong to put a huge chunk of ice in a delicate coupe so we've used an old-fashioned glass.

name: Few Words
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
3 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: This lightly spiced mezcal-laced and cherry flavoured cocktail works equally well as an aperitif or digestif.
history: Created 2018 by Alexey Poltavskiy at Club No. 43, Phuket, Thailand, this cocktail earned him a place in the London final of the Heering Classics Competition.

name: Perfect Storm Highball
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Chairman's Reserve Spiced Rum
1⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: Spiced rum adds vanilla as well as spice to this Mule-style drink.

name: Quill
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Basically a Negroni with dashes of absinthe.
history:
The Quill first appeared in the 1996 edition of Harry's ABC of Mixing Cocktails in which Andrew & Duncan MacElhone added 40+ cocktails to Harry MacElhone original books.

The Quill does not feature in earlier editions of Harry's books and in the 1996 edition his son and grandson credit this recipe to "Frank C. Payne, New York". Payne was one of a group of theatrical press agents who in 1930 formed the Theatrical Press Representatives of America (TPROA) as union to represent their interests, which they publicised through a magazine called The Quill.

name: Watermelon Fizz
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with lemon-lime soda.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	De Kuyper Watermelon liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 1⁄2 shot	Lemon-lime soda (Sprite/7-Up)
review: Tastes as refreshing as it looks. Ripe vodka-laced watermelon, fresh lime, and a splash of invigorating lemon-lime soda.

name: Tea-Quila
preparation: POUR first 3 ingredients into glass and stir to combine. Fill glass with ice and TOP with lemonade.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1 2⁄3 shot	Cold black breakfast tea
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 1⁄2 shot	Lemonade
review: Black tea contributes an almost smoky note to this long tequila-laced cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Giulia Guccurullo from London, England who is the Patrón Perfectionists 2020 Global Winner.

name: White Horse
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Aptly described as being "an herbaceous Scotch sipper."
history: Originally made with the eponymous whisky this classic first appears in William James "Billy" Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Cocktail Book which specifies it should be shaken rather than stirred. Originally created by one "E. Goodall", this cocktail was kindly brought to our attention by Jason E. Clapham and this adaptation is to his recipe.

name: Monte Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Sour, zesty citrus with underling bitterness mellowed by minimal sweetness.

name: Monteleone
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Averna Amaro
2 dash	Cherry bitters
review: A sipper of a cocktail to chase a meal or for late-night contemplation.
history: Adapted from a 2020 recipe (originally served straight-up) by Jason E. Clapham, Oxford, England who told us, "The Monteleone, a Vieux Carré riff named after the Sicilian founder of the hotel where the Vieux Carré was born, in New Orleans – I am guessing he was partial to Averna like most Sicilians I have met."

name: St. Charles Punch
garnish: Seasonal berries and serve with a straw
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Tawny port
3⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: The classic "randy" – port and brandy combo – with tart freshening lemon balanced with a touch of sugar.
history: Adapted from Jerry Thomas' 1862 The Bar-Tenders Guide.

name: Yesterday, Today and Amaro
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1⁄4 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Averna Amaro
review: Bittersweet and spiritous with herbal and subtle chocolate notes. Beware, "boozy" is an understatement, so perhaps split this recipe between two small stemmed glasses rather than one coupe and share the experience with a friend.
history: Recipe created by Brian Kane while Beverage Director at Abe Fisher Restaurant in Philadelphia, USA. This recipe adapted from Brad Thomas Parsons' 2016 book Amaro which includes the following explanation by Brain, "The name pays homage to the history of passing down recipes for amari production from one generation to the next."

name: ItaliCup
preparation: STIR first 3 ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass whilst also pouring soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Italicus liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
3⁄4 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Sour grapefruit and sweet bergamot balance each other in this refreshingly light aperitivo.

name: P & G
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Fino sherry
5⁄6 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Bone dry fino sherry mineral notes are enriched by elderflower and balanced by sour lemon.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2008 by Hayden Lambert at the Merchant Hotel in Belfast, Northern Ireland. A few weeks after creating this cocktail, Hayden entered it into a cocktail competition as the Pomp & Glory cocktail. Your choice of fino and the sourness of your lemons will dramatically influence this delicately balanced cocktail so you may need to adjust proportions accordingly.

Hayden's original recipe calls for:
35 ml Pennyweight fino
25 ml St Germain Elderflower liqueur
7.5 ml freshly squeezed lemon juice
1 dash orange bitters

name: Artist's Gin & Tonic
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Rutte Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
3 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: A G&T with artistic flourishes adding delicate elderflower floral and berry notes.
history:
Created in 2020 by the team at the Bombay Sapphire Distillery, this cocktail's name was inspired by Keïla Urzaiz de Calignon, an accomplished bartender who's also the talented artist who designed the tote bag that accompanies this cocktail in the Cocktail Bundle sold in our UK shop.

Keïla was inspired to make this water collage by focusing on the drink itself and using only the three primary colours blue, red and yellow. Instead of painting the drink, she painted four sheets of paper using the primary colours, blending yellow and blue to make green, and using different proportions of pigments and water to create irregular shades of each colour. She then cut and assembled the pieces to form the shape of the cocktail.

name: Hugo Special
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & pineapple wedge on rim
preparation: MUDDLE orange and pineapple in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 slice	Orange (fresh) (chopped)
3 wedge	Pineapple (fresh)
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: Light and delicate with gin-laced orange and pineapple and subtle, rich, herbal vermouth notes.
history: Adapted from Hugo Ensslin's 1917 Recipes for Mixed-Drinks 2nd edition.

name: Weep No More
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 1⁄4 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Cognac and rich aromatised wine with a touch of maraschino soured by a splash of lime.
history: This "exhumed classic" was brought to our attention by Jason E. Clapham and originally appeared in W. C. Whitfield's 1939 Just Cocktails.

name: Emerald Swizzle
garnish: Mint sprigs bouquet & pineapple wedge on rim
preparation: POUR all ingredients into glass two-thirds filled with crushed ice and SWIZZLE. TOP with more crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1 1⁄2 shot	Coconut milk
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
review: Coconut, pineapple juice and almond laced with herbal liqueur.

name: Blah, Blah, Blah!
preparation: MUDDLE blackberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, shake with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3 fresh	Blackberries
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A fruity late-night cocktail to sip and contemplate. Drinking beer locally brewed from locally grown malt and hops is a very sustainable way to drink. Due to their use of ice and ingredients sourced from much further afield, cocktails are not. However, while beer is a daily staple, cocktails are a special celebratory and luxurious treat. The quest to save the planet is surely worthy of celebration, although to quote another, "All the promises will be nothing but blah, blah, blah..."
history: Created in November 2021 during COP26, the name led to the use of three ingredients: brandy, Bénédictine, and fresh blackberries.

name: Sir Winston
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Whisky usually sits better with lemon rather than lime, but I've tried both in this recipe and lime's distinctive zesty freshness adds to this cocktail, so long as you go easy. Some use as much as 15ml lime but I view 10ml as the limit and 5ml ideal.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Joe Gilmore at The American Bar at London's Savoy Hotel in honour of Winston Churchill, whose mother is often wrongly said to have been present at the Manhattan cocktail's inception.

name: Filibuster
garnish: 3 drops aromatic bitters dotted across cocktail's foaming surface
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Maple syrup
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: A rye whiskey and maple syrup sour served short and straight-up. You'd perhaps have expected this cocktail to be more drawn out.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Erik Adkins, Bar Director at the Slanted Door restaurant in San Francisco, USA.

name: Frenchie
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with grapefruit soda.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
2 shot	Thomas Henry Pink Grapefruit soda
review: Depending on the origin of your choice of ingredients, how "Frenchie" this cocktail is, is questionable, but the result is refreshing, gin-laced and citrus fresh with subtle honeyed floral notes.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Somer Perez of Couture Cocktail Concepts in Los Angeles, USA.

name: Sombretto
garnish: Float red peppercorns or a thin slice of red chili pepper on the drink's foaming surface.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Disaronno amaretto
5⁄6 shot	Giffard Piment d'Espelette chile liqueur
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: This chili-spiced Amaretto Sour originally packed 35ml of chili liqueur. If you're more vindaloo than chicken korma, then go with the original spec., or, if you'er more korma then perhaps go with less than the 25ml I've used.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in October 2020 by Boudewijn Vork at Hotel Boat&Co in Amsterdam, Netherlands. Boudewijn told us, "So I've always really liked the classic Amaretto Sour and I tried to make a twist on it, and after some playing around I found the right taste and specs."

name: Kentucky Flyer
garnish: 2 skewered Luxardo Maraschino Cherries & speared mint sprig bouquet
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: A rye whiskey and maraschino sour, originally made to fill a coupe, but in pursuit of responsible measures, I've reduced by a third to nestle in a Nick & Nora glass.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2011 by Sierra Zimei, cocktail director at Seasons Bar and Lounge in the Four Seasons Hotel in San Francisco, USA. This cocktail's notoriety was helped by its being included in Gary "gaz" Regan's 101 Best New Cocktails of 2011. Originally made with 60ml rye whiskey, 22.5ml maraschino liqueur, and 15ml lemon juice.

name: Wrangler
garnish: Long lemon zest twist & dust with freshly grated nutmeg
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
2 shot	Pale cream sherry (medium/sweet)
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A long almond sherry sour. Cream sherry and almond syrup, freshened with lemon juice and invigorated with soda water.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Mike Jones at Sable Kitchen and Bar in Chicago, USA.

name: Outrigger
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 3-5 years
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Best described as a "Rum Sidecar", like the classic Sidecar this cocktail is a tad on the sour side unless sipped through sugared rim. Altogether a better drink if you forgo the rim and add 2.5ml (half a barspoon) sugar syrup (2:1) so the balance is properly integrated.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Jeff "Beachbum" Berry originally using gold Bajan rum this features in his 2010 book Beachbum Berry Remixed: A Gallery of Tiki Drinks.

name: Pierced Hairy Navel
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
2⁄3 shot	Peachtree peach schnapps
1 1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄3 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
review: Fruity and edging towards the sweet side, tastes better than the name might suggest.
history: Cranberry juice was in its ascendency in the mid-late 1980s when both the Fuzzy Navel (peach schnapps and orange juice) and the Hairy Navel (peach schnapps, orange juice and vodka) where among the most popular 1980s cocktails, so, not surprising, somebody added cranberry juice (and/or cranberry schnapps) to each of these cocktails, so 'piercing' them. Hence, you can have both a Pierced Fuzzy Navel (without vodka) and a Pierced Hairy Navel with vodka. Why settle for mere fuzzy when you can have full-on hairy?

name: Ding-A-Ling
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass over one large ice ball.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1 shot	Dark/black/blackstrap rum
2⁄3 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Rich almond, rum and mezcal with Lemon freshness. Served in a coupe with an ice ball to knock on the side and "ding."
history: Created in January 2022 by yours truly, inspired by hearing the slightly childish but amusing My Ding-A-Ling song play on the radio and wondering what ingredients I could combine with the first letters M (mezcal), D (Dark rum), A (amaretto), and L (lemon).

name: Haut Relievo
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Dark/black/blackstrap rum
1⁄2 shot	Averna Amaro
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: This late-night sipper is a riff on a Red Hook. Dark in colour with a toasty flavour.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2022 by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England. Named after a phrase used by Stephen Maturin to describe a refreshing ingredient in Patrick O'Brian's HMS Surprise. Jason originally based this recipe on Plantation Original Dark rum.

name: Notus
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
6 fresh	Mint leaves
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Kleos Mastiha liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A gin-laced mastiha-led after-dinner refresher made even more refreshing by a gentle burst of mint.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2022 by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England who describes this as "A Greek South Side, named after the god of the south wind."

name: Churchill
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Joe Gilmore made this with lime juice but it's much better with lemon juice. Indeed I'm guilty of also tweaking the proportions of the other ingredients to make this rendition of the Churchill to confirm more to my tastes. Hopefully, Joe would have approved.
history: Named after the legendary Prime Minister, this cocktail was created by Joe Gilmore during his tenure bartending (1940 to 1976) at The Savoy Hotel's American Bar, the oldest surviving cocktail bar in London.

name: Tale Of Two Roberts
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) and shortbread cookie across rim
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: A Rob Roy with a splash of Bénédictine and dashes of absinthe from a Bobby Burns.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in the late 2000's by Frank Caiafa, bars manager of the celebrated Peacock Alley and La Chine restaurants at New York's The Waldorf Astoria Hotel from 2005 until its closure. Frank says this cocktail was a favourite of Gary "gaz" Regan, so much so that he included it in the second edition of his The Joy of Mixolog.

name: Hugo Rickey
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass. STIR briefly and TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
2 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Your choice of grenadine will make or break this Rickey.
history: Eponymously named and created by and Hugo R. Ensslin who included the cocktail in his 1916-17 book Recipes for Mixed Drinks

name: Dragoon
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 3⁄4 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Crème de noyau liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: A smoky bourbon Sazerac sweetened with crème de noyau and served on-the-rocks.
history: Adapted from a recipe by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England.

name: Rosa Rosada Margarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
3⁄4 shot	Lanique Spirit of Rose liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A pale pink, floral Margarita – just as the name suggests.
history: Created in 2023 by yours truly at The Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Dutch Highlander
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Batavia arrack
1⁄4 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: As Jason, the originator of this cocktail, says, "A scotch with some backbone, such as Johnnie Walker Black, is required to stand up to the arrack." That said, you may want to cut the arrack back a tad and up the Bénédictine accordingly – perhaps to 10ml (1/3oz) of each.
history: Adapted from a recipe by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England.

name: 5th Street Finisher
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
3 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Reminiscent of a scotch toddy served cold. Your choice of honey will affect your finished cocktail as much as which Scotch whisky you choose.
history: Adapted from one of the signature cocktails at Speak of the Devil in Ohio, USA since the bar, which is on West 5th Street, opened in 2017.

name: Italian Buck
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with ginger beer.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1 1⁄2 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: A lightly ginger beer spiced, bittersweet aperitivo or digestivo...
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2015 by Jamie Boudreau at Canon in Seattle, USA.

name: Pink Passion Martini
garnish: Float half a fresh passion fruit boat
preparation: Cut passion fruit in half and scoop out flesh into shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 fresh	Passion fruit (fresh)
1 1⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 1⁄3 shot	Passoã passion fruit liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: It's pink, passion fruit flavoured, and surprisingly dry. Fruity doesn't always mean sweet.

name: Sol y Sombra (Sun and Shade)
garnish: Skewered lime wedge and Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. TOP with ginger ale and fill glass with ice.
ingredients:
2 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1⁄2 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
review: Pisco's aromatics form the base of this tall cassis and ginger ale sour.
history: Apparently, this cocktail has been served at Peruvian bullfight arenas since the 1930s.

name: Strawberry Aviation
garnish: Hulled strawberry with mint sprig tip leaves
preparation: MUDDLE strawberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 fresh	Strawberries (hulled, small & ripe)
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Just as the name suggests, only classically an Aviation should include crème de violette so if you feel this is lacking then consider adding 2.5ml (¼ a barspoon)– anymore and the parma violet floral notes overpower the strawberry.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Richard Godwin and published via his The Spirits on Substack, in turn his recipe is a strawberry-infused riff on Takumis Aviation.

name: Knight
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review:
As Jason Clapham, the discerning drinker who brought this cocktail to my attention, says, "it's a Champs-Élysées crossed with Sidecar. What could go wrong?"

If you'd like to cut the above 90ml (3oz) of booze down to Nick & Nora size, then use:
40ml (1⅓oz) Cognac
10 (⅓oz) Orange curaçao
10 (⅓oz) Green Chartreuse
10 (⅓oz) Lemon juice
history: A classic, which originally appeared in David A. Embury's 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks, kindly brought to my attention and rejuvenated by Jason E. Clapham of St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England.

name: Radler
preparation: POUR all ingredients into glass, fill glass with ice and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
3 shot	Pilsner lager
review: Best described as a lager sour served long with soda water. Super refreshing and palate cleansing on a hit afternoon.

name: Regal Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients, including grapefruit zest (Regal Shake), with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 swath	Grapefruit peel/zest
review: Shaking this Daiquiri with a wide grapefruit zest (termed a Regal Shake) has a surprisingly dramatic effect on the finished cocktail, which could be confused for a Grapefruit Daiquiri. The more you sip a Regal Daiquiri, the sourer and zestier it becomes it becomes. This aperitivo eases you in and then puckers you up.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2010 by Theo Lieberman, created at Lantern's Keep in New York City, USA.

name: Almonds in Alameda
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
review: When I first tried this (in November 2023) it seemed familiar but I this combination of ingredients didn't already exist on our database. Not the most exciting cocktail I've added to Difford's Guide but it's well-balanced sweet 'n' sour almond-laced flavour will appeal to many and upset few.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Martin Sheehan-Stross for Tribune Tavern, Oakland, California, USA. Named after nearby neighbouring Alameda, home to distilleries including St. George Spirits, makers of the vodka this cocktail was originally based on.

name: Chirulín
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Cinnamon syrup
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: The aromatics of pisco sit harmoniously with cinnamon spice in this grapefruit sour.
history: Traditionally made with pomelo rather than grapefruit, Chirulín is a Peruvian cocktail with origins traced to the Afro-Peruvian communities of El Ingenio district in Nasca province, Peru.

name: Yellow Mist
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: An apricot and almond Gin Sour.
history: Adapted from a recipe first published in William James "Billy" Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Bar Book.

name: Electric Circus
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Bigallet Genepi Grand Tetras
3⁄4 shot	Green melon liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A bright and bold sour in both flavour and colour.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Chall Gray at his Little Jumbo bar in Asheville, North Carolina, USA.

name: Valentino (vodka-based)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into a chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
4 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A vodka-based riff on the Negroni with its more spirit-forward character taking it into Sweet Martini territory.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in February 1999 by Gary "gaz" Regan and published in his 2001 book, The Joy of Mixology.

name: Hazelnut Espresso No. 2
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
1⁄2 shot	Hazelnut sugar syrup
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Recipe by yours truly in June 2024.
history: Hazelnut flavours sit harmoniously with coffee in this nutty Espresso Martini. Hazelnut-flavoured sugar syrup is key to this recipe, which is even tastier when made with a roasted hazelnut syrup.

name: Maloma
preparation: POUR first 3 ingredients into glass and stir. Add half the mango soda and fill glass with ice. TOP with more mango soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄3 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3 shot	Thomas Henry Mystic Mango
review: As the name suggests, a Paloma with mango soda replacing grapefruit soda, made tastier thanks to a splash of mezcal.
history: Adapted from a cocktail created by Eddie Rudzinskas using Thomas Henry Mystic Mango.

name: Cherry Bomb No. 4
preparation: POUR all ingredients into glass and then fill glass with ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄3 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3 shot	Cherry soda
review: Cherry vanilla bourbon with a balancing hint of lime sourness and freshness.
history: Adapted from a recipe promoted by Three Cents in 2024.

name: Gingerbread Mule
garnish: Skewered crystalised ginger &/or mini gingerbread man atop a summit of crushed ice.
preparation: POUR first 3 ingredients into copper mug/glass and stir. Two-thirds fill vessel with cubed ice. TOP with ginger beer and crown with crushed ice.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Gingerbread sugar syrup
3 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: Want an extra whack of ginger with a touch of cookie in your Moscow Mule, then this is the Mule for you.

name: Absolutely Fabulous
preparation: SHAKE first two ingredients with ice and strain into glass. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1 1⁄2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Easy to quaff – Patsy would love it.
history: Created in 1999 at Monte's Club, London, England, and named after the Absolutely Fabulous television series.

name: A. J.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 2⁄3 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Amazingly simple and beautifully balanced.
history: The initials in the name stand for 'applejack', the American style of apple brandy this drink was originally based upon.

name: Alaska (Savoy recipe)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: In his 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks, David Embury says of the Alaska, "This is also sometimes called the Oriental. It can be greatly improved by using less Chartreuse and adding 1 or 2 parts dry sherry. This is the Nome."
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Apple Breeze
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bison grass vodka
2 1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1 1⁄2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
review: More interesting than the better known Sea Breeze.

name: Apple Crumble No. 2
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Tuaca liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review: Easy to make and equally easy to drink.
history: Created in 2002 by Eion Richards at Bond's Bar, London, England.

name: Arnaud (Parisian Nights)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
review: This flavoursome, three equal parts cocktail has a lightly sweet palate followed by a dry finish. An interesting balance of blackcurrant, vermouth and gin. Some might describe it as "alcoholic Ribena and I've tried upping the gin and reducing the cassis to make drier e.g. 40ml Gin, 30ml Dry vermouth and 20ml Crème de cassis. However, this is best served with equal parts as a dessert Martini at its rich and indulgent best.
history: A classic cocktail named after the pre-war French pianist, singer and stage actress Yvonne Arnaud (1890-1958). A concert pianist as a child she went on to act in musical comedies before switching to non-musical comedy and drama around 1920. She then took dramatic cinematic roles during the 1930s and 40s, continuing to act into the 1950s.

name: Barbara
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1 1⁄2 shot	Milk (whole milk/full 3-4% fat)
review: Creamy and delicately flavoured. The nutmeg garnish plays as important a role as the cacao liqueur.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide.

name: Bessie & Jessie
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 1⁄2 shot	Warninks Advocaat liqueur
2 1⁄2 shot	Milk (whole milk/full 3-4% fat)
review: Malty, creamy and eggy - tasty!

name: The Buck / Gin Buck
preparation: POUR first two ingredients into ice-filled glass and TOP with ginger ale. Stir and serve with straws.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
review: The Buck can be improved by adding a dash of liqueur appropriate to the spirit base. E.g. add a dash of Grand Marnier to a Brandy Buck.

name: Caipirissima
preparation: MUDDLE lime wedges in the base of shaker to release juice and oils in its skin. Add rum and sugar. SHAKE with 6oz scoop crushed ice and pour all without straining into glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 fresh	Lime (fresh) (chopped wedges)
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A Daiquiri-like cocktail made in the style of a Caipirinha.

name: Celery Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 3⁄4 shot	Celery juice (freshly extracted)
review: Celery is usually only tasty when loaded with blue cheese. Vodka also seems to make it rather palatable.
history: Created by Andreas Tsanos at Momos, London, England in 2001.

name: China Beach
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
2⁄3 shot	Ginger liqueur
1 2⁄3 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
review: Dry and lightly spiced.

name: Citrus Caipirovska
preparation: MUDDLE lemon in base of glass. Add other ingredients and fill glass with crushed ice. CHURN drink with bar spoon and serve with short straws.
ingredients:
3⁄4 fresh	Lemon (fresh)
2 shot	Ketel One Citroen Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Superbly refreshing balance of sweet and citrus sourness.

name: Colonel T
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
5⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
2 shot	Pineapple juice
review: Mellow and long with pineapple, apricot and bourbon.

name: Cuppa Joe
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
1 shot	Hazelnut liqueur
review: Nutty coffee fortified with vodka - well balanced.
history:
Created in 2003 at Cellar Bar, New York City, USA.

A variant of an Espresso Martini. See the story behind the Espresso Martini.

name: Absinthe Drip Cocktail (French method)
preparation: POUR absinthe into glass. PLACE cube of sugar on a slotted absinthe spoon resting across the top of the glass. Using an absinthe fountain (or a bottle of chilled mineral water with a small hole in the cap), DRIP iced water over the sugar so it dissolves and drips into the glass. Traditionally the same amount of water is added as absinthe, but full-strength absinthe requires more dilution - Keep dripping until absinthe louches (turns milky white). Add ice, stir and serve.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2 shot	Chilled water
1 cube	Sugar cube
review: Patience is a virtue. Slow dripping of the water is essential to dissolve the entire sugar cube and give the drink enough sweetness to balance the absinthe.
history: This is the traditional method of serving absinthe. It was common until shortly before the First World War, when the drink was banned in most countries.

name: Caipirinha (Contemporary Serve)
preparation: MUDDLE lime wedges in the base of shaker to release juice and oils in its skin. Add cachaça and sugar. SHAKE with 6oz scoop crushed ice and pour all without straining into glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 fresh	Lime (fresh) (chopped wedges)
2 shot	Cachaça
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
history:
In its native Brazil it is usual to serve this drink with cubed ice (actually most usually holly tubular machine ice) but the drink travelled to, and became popular the UK at a time when the use of crushed ice was fashionable, so in this and other 'new' cachaça markets the use of crushed ice has become the norm.

For information on the history and other variations of the Caipirinha, please see our Caipirinha cocktail page.

name: Mezcal Negroni
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and STIR.
ingredients:
1 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: This mezcal-influenced Negroni is an interesting take on the classic, which will be appreciated by mezcal aficionados.
history: Negroni cocktail history and recipe variations

name: Damson in Distress
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Damson liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Damson and amaretto sharpened by lemon juice.
history: Discovered in 2003 at Hush, London, England.

name: Dolce-Amaro
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Disaronno amaretto
review: The very apt name translates as 'bittersweet'.

name: Eastern Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Giffard Mirabelle de Lorraine
1 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review: Light, fragrant and fruity - distinctly oriental.
history: Created in 2003 by Chris Langan, Barnomadics, Scotland.

name: Emerald Martini
garnish: Lemon & lime zest twists (discarded) & mint leaf
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1 shot	Chilled water
2 shot	Lime flavoured vodka
review: A serious drink that's rammed with alcohol and flavour.
history: Discovered in 2005 at Bugsy's Prague, Czech Republic.

name: 57 T-Bird Shot
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Disaronno amaretto
history: A 57 T-bird, or 1957 Ford Thunderbird to give it its full title, immortalised in the Beach Boys' song 'Fun Fun Fun', was the classic car for any 1950s' teenager. Top down, radio up, girl next to you...

name: Flirtini No. 1
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
review: It's a French Martini so hard not to like.
history: Made famous on television's Sex and the City. It is said to have been created in 2003 for Sarah Jessica Parker at Guastavinos in New York City, USA.

name: Full Circle
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Pomegranate juice
2 shot	Pineapple juice
review: Fruity and easy-drinking, yet with complexity from the gin. At least that's how this cocktail tastes when made with pomegranate juice freshly squeezed using a pillar press juicer. (1 pomegranate yields approx. 135ml juice.)
history: Adapted from a drink discovered in 2004 at Mandarin Oriental, New York City, USA. The name is a reference to the bar's location - Columbus Circle, where one of the world's first one-way rotary systems (roundabout) was implemented in 1904.

name: Golden Nail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Southern USA-style liqueur 40% (e.g. Southern Comfort)
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: A warming taste of southern hospitality.

name: Golf Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A 'wet' Martini with bitters.

name: Grape Effect
preparation: MUDDLE grapes in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
12 fresh	Green grapes (seedless)
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Elderflower liqueur
review: Delicately flavoured and heavily laced with rum.

name: Grape Martini
preparation: MUDDLE grapes in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
12 fresh	Green grapes (seedless)
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Simple but remarkably tasty.
history: Created in 2004 by yours truly, London, England.

name: Hair of the Dog
preparation: STIR honey with Scotch until honey dissolves. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3 barspoon	Honey
2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 1⁄2 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: This drink's name and reputation as a hangover cure may lead you to assume it tastes unpleasant. In fact, honey, whisky and cream combine wonderfully.
history: Traditionally drunk as a pick-me-up hangover cure.

name: Iguana Wana
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
2⁄3 shot	Peachtree peach schnapps
2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Orange juice and peach schnapps, laced with vodka.

name: Ink No. 2
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Blue Curaçao
1 1⁄3 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
review: Muscle shell blue in colour. Vodka charged cranberry and orange in flavour.
history: Discovered in 2005 at Halo in Atlanta, Georgia, USA.

name: Jamaican Sunset
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	White overproof rum
1 1⁄4 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
2 1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Overproof rum adds flavour and oomph to cranberry and orange juices.

name: Japanese Slipper
garnish: Luxardo maraschino cherry dropped into drink
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 shot	Green melon liqueur
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Sweet melon, orange liqueur and lemon. A bit of a sweetie, as its lurid green colour might suggest.
history: Created in 1984 by Jean-Paul Bourguignon at Mietta's Restaurant in Melbourne, Australia.

name: Klondike
preparation: POUR ingredients into glass and fill with ice.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 2⁄3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
review: A simple drink but its three-equal parts ingredients combine well.
history: Recipe adapted from A. S. Crockett's 1935 The Old Waldorf-Astoria Bar Book.

name: Lavender & Black Pepper Cocktail
preparation: Pour the syrup into an ice-filled mixing glass. Add the vodka and black pepper. STIR and super-fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄4 shot	Lavender sugar syrup
2 grind	Black pepper
review: Subtly sweetened and lavender flavoured vodka, with a bump and grind of spicy pepper.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2006 by Richard Gillam at the Kenilworth Hotel, Warwickshire, England.

name: Livingstone
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: The classic gin and vermouth Dry Martini made not so dry and a tad more approachable by a splash of sugar.
history: This vintage cocktail is named after Doctor Livingstone, the famous African missionary.

name: Loch Almond Highball
garnish: Amaretti biscuit resting across glass rim & ice
preparation: POUR all ingredients into chilled glass and then fill with ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
5⁄6 shot	Disaronno amaretto
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
review: If you haven't got to grips with Scotch but like amaretto, try this delicately ginger almond combination.

name: Mango Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
2 shot	Mango purée
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Tropical yet potent and refreshing.

name: Marmarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A Margarita with a Marmite rim. After all, yeast extract is slightly salty.
history: Created in 2005 by Simon (Ginger) Warneford at Blanch House, Brighton, England.

name: Mary Queen of Scots
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
2⁄3 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
2⁄3 shot	Drambuie liqueur
