review: Slightly sweet herbal influenced riff on the Rusty Nail.
history:
Adapted from a shaken and straight-up cocktail served in a sugar-rimmed glass with a cherry discovered in 2006 on Kyle Branch's Cocktail Hotel blog.

Mary Stuart, Mary Queen of Scots, was born 8th December 1542 at Linlithgow Place in West Lothian. On February 8th 1587, she was executed in the Great Hall of Fotheringhay.

name: Mayan
garnish: Pineapple wedge on rim &/or float 3 coffee beans
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
review: Tequila, coffee and pineapple combine harmoniously in this medium-dry cocktail.

name: Melon Martini (fresh fruit)
preparation: Cut melon into eight segments and deseed. Cut cubes of flesh from skin of one segment and MUDDLE in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄6 fresh	Melon (Cantaloupe)
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Probably the most popular of all the fresh fruit Martinis.

name: Mrs Robinson #2
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄3 shot	Galliano L'Autentico liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A short Harvey Wallbanger.
history: Adapted from a recipe discovered in 2006 on Kyle Branch's Cocktail Hotel blog.

name: Orange Bloom Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: Fruity, zesty, delicately herbal orange laced with gin. Modern bartending convention is to stir rather than shake this "Martini" but it's better shaken, as stipulated by Harry Cradock.
history: Adapted from the following recipe in Harry Cradock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Paisley Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄6 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: A dry Martini for those with a penchant for Scotch.

name: Parisian Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2⁄3 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
review: Rich cassis tempered by gin and dry vermouth.
history: A drink created in the 1920s to promote crème de cassis. Recipe adapted from Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Pear & Elderflower Fruitini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Pear juice (freshly pressed)
review: Pear and elderflower fortified with vodka.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2001 by Angelo Vieira at St. Martins, London, England.

name: Pink Hound
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: A flavoursome balance of sweet and sour.

name: Pisco Naranja
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
2⁄3 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Aromatic brandy and orange juice pepped and sweetened with a slug of orange liqueur.
history: Based on the traditional Chilean combination of pisco and orange juice.

name: Piscola
garnish: Lime wedge squeezed and dropped into drink
preparation: POUR pisco and bitters into ice-filled glass. TOP with cola and briefly stir.
ingredients:
2 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters (optional)
3 2⁄3 shot	Cola (e.g. Coca Cola or Pepsi Cola)
review: 'Brandy' and cola with a hint of Angostura bitters. Try and see why the Chileans enjoy it.
history: A popular long drink in its native Chile where the 8th of February has been celebrated as Piscola Day since 2003.

name: Red Apple
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Sour apple liqueur
2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
review: As riffs on the Sour Apple Martini go, this one is rather good.

name: Roffignac
preparation: SHAKE first 2 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda, lightly stir and serve with straws.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Giffard Crème de Framboise
2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: This bright red, fruity drink is simple but tasty.
history: This classic cocktail is named after Count Louis Philippe Joseph de Roffignac, Mayor of New Orleans 1820-1828. Roffignac notably introduced streetlights to New Orleans and instigated the laying cobblestones on the roads of the French Quarter.

name: Rusty Nail
preparation: STIR ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Drambuie liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: The liqueur smooths and wonderfully combines with Scotch whisky. The proportions of Scotch to Drambuie vary wildly and are a matter of taste. However, somewhere around 3:1 appears to be preferred by most.
history:
Created in 1942 at a Hawaiian bar for the artist Theodore Anderson but popularized in the 1950s at Club 21 in New York City.

David Wondrich has traced the mixing of scotch whisky and Drambuie liqueur back to 1937 and a drink called B.I.F.. However, given that Drambuie originated in an Edinburgh cellar in 1908 we suspect the combo was first tried decades earlier.

name: Snowball
garnish: Lime zest twist or lime slice
preparation: POUR lemonade and lime juice into ice-filled glass and then the advocaat which will mostly sink though the other ingredients. Lightly stir to integrate while retaining the lemonade's carbonation.
ingredients:
3 1⁄2 shot	Lemonade
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 shot	Warninks Advocaat liqueur
review: Fresh lime juice and lemonade freshens and invigorates creamy advocaat. Try our more luxurious and better Champagne Snowball.
history: Thought to have originated in Britain in the late 1940s or early 1950s, reaching its peak of popularity in the 1970s.

name: Tango Cocktail (from the Bellagio)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄6 shot	Passoã passion fruit liqueur
1 1⁄3 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Passion fruit liqueur, balanced by tart grapefruit and fortified with gin.
history: Adapted from a reipe discovered in 2003 at the Bellagio in Las Vegas, USA.

name: Tatanka
garnish: Apple slice or dehydrated apple slice dusted with cinnamon powder
preparation: POUR all ingredients into glass, then fill with ice and STIR.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bison grass vodka
2 1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: This excellent cocktail's taste is a little reminiscent of Earl Grey tea. It's equally good shaken and served straight-up in a coupe.
history: This Polish cocktail takes its name from Dances With Wolves, the 1990 Western film starring, directed, and produced by Kevin Costner. Tatanka is a Native American word for buffalo and refers to the bison grass-flavoured vodka this cocktail is based on.

name: Tawny-Tini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 2⁄3 shot	Tawny port
1⁄6 shot	Maple syrup
review: Port combines wonderfully with the maple syrup and is fortified by grainy vodka to produce a toffee-flavoured cocktail.

name: Tiki Margarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A simple three-imgrediet almond twist on the classic Margarita.
history:
Created in 2005 by Crispin Somerville and Jasper Eyears at Bar Tiki, Mexico City.
See: Margarita cocktail history

name: Valkyrie Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. Serve with straws.
ingredients:
2 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
review: This sipping drink has a rich vanilla sweet 'n' sour flavour.
history:
Created in 2003 by yours truly (Simon Difford), London, England.

Valkyrie comes from Norse mythology and literally translates as 'chooser of the slain'.

name: The Wentworth
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 1⁄4 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1 1⁄4 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
review: The pleasing tang of bourbon adds backbone to this fruity herbal cocktail.
history: Created in 2003 by Sharon Cooper at the Harvest Restaurant, Pomfret, Connecticut, USA.

name: White Russian Cocktail
garnish: Dust with freshly grated nutmeg (not essential but adds much)
preparation: STIR first 2 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. Carefully FLOAT lightly whipped cream (shake sealed container before pouring).
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review:
One of the best-known cocktails of the modern era, the White Russian, consists of vodka and coffee liqueur served on the rocks, sipped over a silky layer of cream or milk.

A White Russian can be as simple as equal measures vodka, coffee liqueur and fresh cream poured over ice. However, it looks better if you stir at least the first two ingredients and then layer cream on the surface of the drink (as above). Or, some prefer to shake all three ingredients to make a properly integrated cocktail.
history:
Named due to its appearance and vodka base. Smirnoff and Stolichnaya were the main vodka brands at the time, so vodka was associated with Russia.

The White Russian is obviously related to the Black Russian whose origins are thought to date from 1949. However, who first came up with this creamy interpretation and when is unknown.

Mention of the White Russian cocktail in print first appeared in an advertisement for a now long-defunct coffee liqueur called 'Coffee Southern', which ran in the Boston Globe on 21st March 1965, then in California's Oakland Tribune on 21 November 1965. Along with the White Russian, the "Try delicious Coffee Sothern" advert also gives the recipes for 'Coffee and Cointreau', 'Southern Grasshopper' and 'Java Sundae' using the liqueur.

The White Russian strutted its way through the 1970s disco era before its popularity waned in the 80s, only to be rescued and made more popular than ever after being the libation of choice of The Dude in the cult 1998 movie The Big Lebowski. Played by Jeff Bridges, throughout this comedy caper film, Jeffrey "The Dude" Lebowski has little interest or passion for anything other than bowling and drinking White Russians, which he calls a "Caucasian". Over the duration of the film, The Dude consumes seven of the creamy cocktails.

name: Froth Blower Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Salmon-pink and very frothy but surprisingly complex and tasty.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Houla Houla Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
review: Orange generously laced with gin.
history: Adapted from Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Picador
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: The name might be more masculine, but it is still a classic Margarita. This 2:1:1 recipe is a touch on the sour side for most so you may want to add a 5ml (1 bar spoon) of agave or sugar syrup.
history: Yes, you're right! This drink is exactly the same as a classically proportioned Margarita. It was first published in William J. "Billy" Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Bar Book, 16 years before the first written reference to a Margarita.

name: Clubland
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice & fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Dry white port
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Go easy on the bitters, and this is a complex and rewarding Martini-style cocktail.
history: In William James "Billy" Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Bar Book, the creation of this drink is credited to one A. Mackintosh. Originally made with a brand of port called Clubland, hence this drink's name.

name: Flame of Love Martini
preparation: Pour sherry into chilled glass, swirl to coat inside and discard excess. Using a match or lighter, express and ignite the oils from the orange peel so the burnt oil coats the inside of the sherry-coated glass. SHAKE the vodka with ice and fine strain into the coated glass.
ingredients:
1⁄6 shot	Fino sherry
3 twist	Orange zest/swath
2 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
review: Bone dry but fresh and most definitely citrusy.
history:
Created at Chasen's, a legendary Hollywood restaurant that opened in 1936 and was a haunt of movie stars and even royalty until its eventual demise in 1995. The memorabilia that decorated the restaurant was held in storage and in 1997 Maud and Dave Chasen's grandson opened another Chasen's on Beverly Hills' Cañon Drive which sadly failed due to a lack of patrons.

During the original Chasen's heyday, its star-studded clientele enjoyed drinks created by its noted bartender Pepe Ruiz. Of these, the Flame of Love is his most famous creation, partly due to its originally being made for Dean Martin. The legend of this drink is further embellished by Dean dragging his old pal Frank Sinatra to Chasen's to try the drink. The story goes that Frank was so impressed that he ordered one for everyone in the place.
Martini cocktail history

name: Grape Cocktail
preparation: MUDDLE grapes in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass
ingredients:
12 fresh	Green grapes (seedless)
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
review: Green Chartreuse adds extra complexity to what would otherwise be simply vodka-laced grape juice.

name: Hoffman House
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A shaken Wet (5:1) Martini with orange bitters.
history: Apparently the house cocktail at Manhattan's Hoffman House in the 1880s.

name: Hula Hula or Hoola-Hoola Cocktail
garnish: Pineapple wedge on rim with Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Gin and juice - orange with a splash of orange liqueur.
history: Said by some to date from 1934 and to have been created by Ray Buhen, one of Don The Beachcomber's original bartenders. In 1961 Ray opened his own Tiki-Ti Bar in Los Angeles, which today is run by his son and grandson. However, this recipe (spelt Hoola-Hoola) comes from Harry of Ciro's ABC of Mixing Cocktails, published in London in 1923, ten years before Donn Beach opened his Don's Beachcomber bar in Hollywood. So, obviously, Ray Buhen did not create the Hula Hula – although he may have been responsible for changing the spelling and popularising it.

name: Negroski
preparation: Pour ingredients into ice-filled glass and STIR.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review: A Negroni where vodka is substituted for gin.

name: French 77
preparation: POUR first 2 ingredients into chilled glass, and TOP with sparkling wine.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
4 1⁄2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Elderflower liqueur adds flavour to dry sparkling wine while a splash of lemon juice helps balance the rich liqueur.
history:
A floral riff on the classic French 75 created in 2006 by yours truly.
French 75 cocktail history

name: Geisha Mar-Tea-Knee
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Green tea liqueur
1 shot	Jasmine tea (cold)
review: Surprisingly fresh and light, this starts slightly sweet but finishes with refreshing bitter tannins. Tea pearls - hand-rolled balls of tea leaves -make a wonderful garnish.
history: Created in the USA in 2006.

name: Hop Toad #3
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Fresh apricot dessert - all it lacks is a dollop of whipped cream.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Parisian Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
2⁄3 shot	Elderflower liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: Floral vodka with dry vermouth complexity.
history: Created in 2006 by yours truly.

name: Pomme et Sureau
preparation: POUR first 2 ingredients into ice-filled glass, TOP with soda and lightly stir.
ingredients:
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Light, long and refreshing apple and elderflower.
history: Created in 2006 by yours truly. The name is French for 'apple and elderflower'.

name: Scorched Earth
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
review: Dry, very aromatic and bordering on bitter. Interesting but not to everybody's taste. The lemon zest twist makes this cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2006 by Nicholas Hearin at Restaurant Eugene in Atlanta, USA, and first published by Gary "gaz" Regan.

name: Valentino
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into a chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: A variation on the Negroni. More gin and less liqueur and vermouth make for an unusual bittersweet Martini.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in February 1999 by Gary "gaz" Regan and published in his 2001 book, The Joy of Mixology.

name: Carthusian Nail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
3⁄4 shot	Drambuie liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
review: A Chartreuse-influenced riff on the classic Rusty Nail.
history: Created in 2010 by yours truly (Simon Difford) at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Too Ache Sidecar
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 1⁄2 shot	Tuaca liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Tuaca replaces Cointreau in this twist on the Sidecar.
history:
Created in 2009 by yours truly (Simon Difford) at the Cabinet Room, London, England at the insistence of Charlotte Ashburner, UK Tuaca Brand Manager.

See our Sidecar cocktail page for the full story behind the origins of the Sidecar, its history and variations.

name: Absinthe Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: A classic Gin Martini made aniseed fresh with a splash of absinthe. Like me, you may prefer the bite-sized version of this cocktail served straight-up in a Nick & Nora glass with half measures: 75ml (1.25oz) dry gin, 15ml (.5oz) dry vermouth, and 2.5ml (half spoon) absinthe.

name: Death in Venice
preparation: POUR Campari and grapefruit bitters into chilled glass and TOP with Prosecco.
ingredients:
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
3 drop	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
4 1⁄2 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
review: On the bitter side of bittersweet, this is something of a cross between the Italian Spritz and Ernest Hemingway's Death in the Afternoon.
history: Created in 2010 by Tony Conigliaro at 69 Colebrooke Row, London, England.

name: Highlander
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A Scotch whisky-based Sweet Manhattan with orange bitters.
history: A Rob Roy with orange bitters. In his seminal 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks, David Embury notes under his Rob Roy entry, "If orange bitters are used instead of Angostura, this drink is sometimes called the Highland, or the Highland Fling, or the Express. I discovered it as the "Highlander" in 2010 on the menu of the Campbell Apartment in New York City, USA.

name: Conan Doyle
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Island single malt Scotch whisky
1⁄4 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
3 dash	Whiskey barrel-aged bitters
review: A literary riff on a Corn'n'Oil - elementary but tasty. As the ice melts and dilutes this cocktail so the falernum notes amplify and the cocktail mellows and opens.
history: Discovered in 2008 at Tonic Bar in Edinburgh, Scotland. Originally made with Talisker Island single malt Scotch whisky.

name: Presbyterian
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and lightly STIR.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
Top up with	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
review: Basically a Scotch and soda with a delicate hint of ginger spice, the Presbyterian cocktail should be made using Scotch whisky rather than bourbon, rye, Irish whiskey etc..
history:
A traditional British style of Highball using blended Scotch whisky.

The name Presbyterian may come from presbýteros (πρεσβύτερος), the Greek word for 'elder', which incidentally is used 72 times in the New Testament, but the modern Presbyterian Church after which this cocktail is named, originated primarily in Scotland. Indeed, Presbyterian Church government is enacted in the 1707 Acts of Union which created the kingdom of Great Britain.

name: Golden Ivy
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Muscat (Rutherglen) wine
1 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
review: Cognac stirred with rich berry flavours of muscat wine along with the relatively dry berry flavour of cranberry.
history: A Christmas cocktail created in October 2011 by yours truly.

name: Dry Martini (2:1.5 ratio) Sopping Wet
garnish: Chilled olive on stick or lemon zest twist
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura (optional)
review: Herbal vermouth flavours pervade this Sopping Wet Martini.
history: There is considerable debate about the origin of the Martini. See the Martini Cocktail And Its Evolution.

name: Bushranger
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and stain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 1⁄2 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Slightly sweet, this complex cocktail combines flavours of red wine with subtle herbal notes and is fortified with light rum.
history: Unknown. Originally, in the early years of the British settlement of Australia, Bushrangers were runaway convicts who had the survival skills necessary to use the Australian bush as a refuge from the authorities. The term then evolved as the Australian term for a highwayman.

name: Raspberry Daiquiri
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with 1/2 scoop (6oz) crushed ice and serve in chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 1⁄2 shot	Giffard Crème de Framboise
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A crowd-pleasing, slightly sweet blended fruity Daiquiri.

name: Teqroni
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and stir.
ingredients:
1 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: Lighter and slightly sweeter than a classic gin-based Negroni with Italian bitter liqueur. However, this Italian and Mexican trio make for pleasing cross-continental bedfellows.
history: Unknown, but as the same suggests this is simply a tequila-based Negroni.

name: Sanguinello Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
1 shot	Blood orange juice
review: Bitter notes are balanced by sweet, lemony limoncello liqueur with blood orange juice adding citrus freshness.
history: This well-established Italian classic is named after one of the three most common varieties of blood oranges, the Sanguinello orange is native to Spain.

name: Better & Better
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄2 shot	Jamaican-style overproof aged pot still rum
1⁄4 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
review: Initially strong and punchy, but as the name suggests, as the ice melts dilution makes this drink better and better.
history: Created circa 2007 by Jan Warren at 10 Downing in Manhattan, New York City but not popularised until 2012 when he was behind the stick at Dutch Kills, Long Island City. Jan's original recipe calls for Fidencio blanco mezcal.

name: Harvard cocktail #2
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Byrrh Grand Quinquina
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Byrrh combines well with cognac in this variation on the classic Harvard.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2015 by Tony Conigliaro at 69 Colebrooke Row, London, England.

name: Byrrh Cassis
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass in the following order and lightly stir.
ingredients:
3 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
1 1⁄2 shot	Byrrh Grand Quinquina
3⁄4 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
review: Rich berry and red wine flavours are lengthened and enlivened with sparkling water.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Black Diamond #2
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Elderflower liqueur
review: Cognac, vermouth and elderflower liqueur combine harmoniously in this short, boozy cocktail.
history: Created by Pablo Ayos at Ibiza Bartenders Bar School, Ibiza, Spain. Pablo’s recipe originally called for ¾ shot Dos Deus Vermouth,

name: Contessa
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: As Negroni-style cocktails go, the vibrant orange-amber Contessa is nudging being on the sweet side (but no less likeable for it).
history: Adapted from a recipe attributed to John Gertsen at Drink bar in Boston, USA.

name: Il Viaggio
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1 shot	Rabarbaro liqueur
3 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: The ingredients might suggest that this cocktail should be stirred – I tried, but it benefits from the dilution and life that shaking imparts. After some elbow grease, you'll have a delicious bittersweet, herbal almond after-dinner drink.
history: Created in October 2016 by Wouter Bosch, Senior Bartender at The Duchess in Amsterdam, Netherlands. The name is Italian for The Travel.

name: Limoncello Spritz
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
1 1⁄2 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Zesty, almost creamy, lemon enlivened with fizz.
history: A modern addition to the venerable Spritz family of cocktails.

name: Spiked Arnold Palmer
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
4 shot	Cold black tea
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Tea tannins and sour lemon balance the rich limoncello in this refreshing low alcohol cocktail. Perfect for summer.

name: Flat White Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Irish cream liqueur
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
review: Martini drinkers of the gin/vodka and vermouth variety will describe this drink as being all too flat and all too white, but for lovers of flat white coffees and cream liqueurs, this Martini will hit the spot – even though it's not really a Martini.
history: Developed in Australia and New Zealand in the 1980s, a "flat white" is a coffee made by pouring frothy, velvety steamed milk over a double shot of espresso. It is similar to a cappuccino or a latte, but is smaller in volume and with a higher proportion of coffee to milk. As Dick Bradsell's Espresso Martini became a mass-market cocktail in the first half of the Noughties, so the marketers at Baileys Irish Cream started to promote this cocktail.

name: Hairy Navel
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. (Don't be tempted to shake as this detrimentally thins the drink. Instead, consider rolling or throwing.)
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Peachtree peach schnapps
3 1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Fruity and a touch on the sweet side, this is a Screwdriver with added peach schnapps liqueur.
history: The Fuzzy Navel, a mix of peach schappes and orange juice, was named by an adverting agency in 1984 as part of a campaign to support the US launch of De Kuyper Original Peachtree. "Fuzzy" in the name refers to the peach schnapps while "navel" refers to the orange variety of the juice. Given the rise of vodka at the time (Absolut launched in 1980), it was only a matter of time before someone added vodka to the mix, upgrading this cocktail from being merely being "Fluzzy" to "Hairy". The next logical development was to add another popular product at the time, cranberry juice, to make a Pierced Navel cocktail.

name: Orange Witch
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strega liqueur
3 1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)

name: Tuxedo No.4 or Tussetto
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Fino sherry
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Bone dry and aromatic with green grape, citrus and mineral notes. Also consider garnishing this cocktail with an olive – it suits it. This is a tasty riff on a Dry Martini but it has no vermouth (it uses sherry instead) so isn't really a Dry Martini or even a Tuxedo.
history:
Adapted from recipes in Straub's Manual of Mixed Drinks (1913), Jack's Manual 4th Edition (1916) and Old Waldorf Astoria Bar Days (1931) by Albert Stevens Crockett.
Also see: Tuxedo cocktail history

name: Old Fashioned (no sugar & low-calorie)
preparation: STIR half the bourbon with three ice cubes (dry to the touch well-frozen ice, not wet ice) directly in serving glass. Add the rest of bourbon, sugar-free syrup, bitters and two more ice cubes. STIR some more and add another two ice cubes. And if you have room, add more ice before serving.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄3 shot	Sugar-free sweetener
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters (optional)
review:
Despite being made with a dash of sweetener rather than sugar this is a very palatable Old Fashioned and many will not be able to differentiate between the classic sugar-loaded version.

Adding aromatic bitters will help the cocktail's flavour but, depending on the bitters used, is likely to add trace amounts of sugar.
history:
Adapted from the classic serve by yours truly in January 2019.
Old Fashioned cocktail history and recipes

name: Suffragette
garnish: Purple and white edible flowers with dill or other green foliage pegged to rim to represent purple for loyalty and dignity, white for purity, and green for hope.
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Elderflower liqueur
review: A Wet Gin Martini with a touch of elderflower floral richness.

name: Fizzy Peachtree
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Peachtree peach schnapps
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3 1⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: As the name suggests, sparkling peach with delicate lime notes. Light and refreshing.
history: Promoted by De Kuyper in 2019 as the signature cocktail for their Peachtree peach schnapps liqueur.

name: Gangham Spritz
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
1 1⁄2 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
1 1⁄2 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
review: Tastes reminiscent of traditional real lemonade.

name: Gin Agrumi Highball
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Pink Grapefruit soda
history: Citrusy gin and accompanying botanicals, zesty limoncello and grapefruit soda.

name: Spanish Coffee
garnish: Dust with cocoa or cinnamon powder
preparation: POUR liqueur and hot coffee into a warmed glass then FLOAT warmed whipped cream on the surface of the drink.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Licor 43 Original liqueur
6 2⁄3 shot	Filter coffee (hot)
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: Coffee and lightly spiced vanilla smoothed by a creamy top.
history: A cocktail promoted by Licor 43 Liqueur and added to Difford's Guide in 2019.

name: Highland Fling
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: This two-parts scotch to one-part sweet vermouth may be old-school but it remains tasty and the scotch whisky counterpart to a Gin & It.
history: A classic cocktail of unknown origin that is said to date back to the Prohibition period.

name: Tam o' Shanter
garnish: Dust with freshly grated nutmeg & olive
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A Blood & Sand without the blood (cherry brandy) so drier. The dusting of nutmeg is critical to the success of this old-school classic.
history: Named after Scottish Poet Robert Burns' 1790 narrative poem, the origins of this classic cocktail are lost in time.

name: Black Corn & Oil
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
1 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A coffee and cacao spiced rum riff on the classic Corn 'n' Oil.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Uwe Christiansen at Heart of St. Pauli in Hamburg, Germany.

name: White Water Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Acqua Bianca liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Zesty citrus and fresh mint with delicate rose.
history: Created in 2020 by Salvatore "The Maestro" Calabrese at the Donovan Bar, London, England.

name: Grapefruit Mule
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Grapefruit flavoured vodka
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
Top up with	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: A grapefruit riff on the classic Moscow Mule.

name: Hugo Spritz
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
2 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
2⁄3 shot	Elderflower liqueur
5⁄12 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: This recipe is light on elderflower liqueur to make a relatively dry drink. Those after a sweeter version may prefer to follow the standard 3:2:1 Spritz formula with 45ml prosecco, 30ml elderflower and 12.5ml soda.
history:
Pronounced 'Ugo', this spritz-style cocktail was created in 2005 by "Roland 'Ak' Gruber" at his San Zeno wine and cocktail bar in his hometown of South Tyrol in northern Italy. Prior to returning home to open his own bar, Ak had bartended in Switzerland and after closing his bar returned to there. It was while bartending in Switzerland that this cocktail became a well-known contemporary classic.

Ak originally named his drink "Otto" but quickly renamed this riff on a classic Spritz Veneziano. Originally made with lemon balm syrup but at some point, what is now a Hugo changed to being made with more readily available elderflower syrup and then elderflower liqueur.

name: Limoncello Iced Tea
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
3 2⁄3 shot	Cold black breakfast tea
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Lemon iced tea never tasted so good.

name: Tradewinds Negroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Given the slug of aromatic bitters in the recipe, it's not surprising that this riff on a Negroni packs a whack of bitters. However, that whack is subtler and a good deal more enjoyable than you might anticipate.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Justin Elliott at The Townsend, Austin, Texas, USA.

name: Monte Mule
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled mug/glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
4 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: Bittersweet, spicy and enlivening.

name: Ostend Fizz
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Kirschwasser (cherry) eau-de-vie
5⁄12 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: This vintage cocktail was recommended to us by Jason E. Clapham who describes it as "a refreshing long drink for summer gardens in August." We agree.
history:
This cocktail originally appears in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book with equal proportions crème de cassis and kirsch but the recipe we've used comes from W.J. Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Cocktail Book.

It's probable that the Ostend Fizz originated in the Kursaal Casino in Ostend, Belgium. The original beachfront casino opened in 1852 in what was then a popular upper-class resort. The casino was demolished by the German army in World War II and replaced by a modernist building designed by Léon Stynen which was completed in 1953, and, due to its architecture, listed as a monument in 1998.

name: Jim Jam
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Averna Amaro
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Bittersweet with rich jammy apricot and a touch of tart citrus freshness, this cocktail teeters on being sweet but manages to remain balanced.

name: Pompier
preparation: STIR first 2 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass whilst also pouring soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Strike the right balance and there's a note reminiscent of cola. A tad too heavy on the cassis or not quite enough dilution and that cola note turns Ribena-like.
history: French for firefighter, Pompier was a popular cocktail in New York during the late 1930s.

name: Garibaldicus
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Italicus liqueur
4 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Bergamot liqueur and grapefruit juice combine beautifully and while a tasty aperitivo this combo is best served with breakfast.
history: Created in 2019 by Luca Missaglia, Italicus' Global Brand Ambassador.

name: Lemmy
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters (optional)
4 shot	Cola (e.g. Coca Cola or Pepsi Cola)
review: Bourbon and cola with a splash of aromatic bitters. America's answer to Britain's G&T is a sight more rock 'n' roll – or even heavy metal. In contrast the G&T is more Chamber orchestra.
history: Lemmy Kilmister (1945 - 2015), front man of the British heavy metal band Motörhead, was known for drinking Jack or Beam and Coke so spawning the Lemmy, essentially a highball with bourbon, cola +/- bitters.

name: Popinjay
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
3⁄4 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
review: Cognac-laced, richly vinous and delicately herbal.
history: Adapted from a comment left by John McTague in April 2021 on our Little Italy page.

name: Valencia Cocktail No. 1
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
4 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Rich apricot and orange toned by generous dashes of orange bitters and the aromatic bitter oils from an orange zest twist.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Coffee Old Fashioned
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1 1⁄3 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: I've made with rye whisky to deliver that spicy punch but others specify Irish whiskey. However, coffee is the hero in this Old Fashioned so your choice of coffee liqueur will have a bigger impact.

name: Rosy Deacon
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Your choice of sloe gin will greatly influence this gin laced grapefruit sour which can tip from bone dry to slightly sweet.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide.

name: Castro's Pina Colada
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Coconut rum liqueur (35-40% alc./vol.)
4 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Coconut rum and pineapple juice with balancing lime tartness.
history: Created in 2021 thanks to Antonio Castro, a Discerning Drinker who made a Cuban-style Piña Colada with coconut flavoured rum. His name and the cocktail link with Cuba made naming this cocktail easy.

name: Newport
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Crème de noyau liqueur
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Crème de Noyau's fruity, almond-like notes combine with brandy in this late-night sipper.
history: The Newport first appears in R. de Fleury's 1934 book 1700 Cocktails for the Man Behind the Bar with the same recipe repeated in the 1937 The UKBG's Approved Cocktails.

name: Fernet Me Not No. 3
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Bittersweet and sweet 'n' sour. If there were such a thing as a Tiki digestivo, then this would be one, or even it.
history: Unknown.

name: Witches' Tonic
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Strega liqueur
4 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: Strega adds its distinctive herbal and saffron spices notes to a classic Gin & Tonic.

name: Witches' Mule
garnish: Mint sprigs bouquet, lime slice & straw
preparation: POUR all ingredients into glass/mug two-thirds full with cubed ice. Fill glass/mug and crown with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Strega liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: A herbal riff on the classic Moscow Mule.

name: Hummer
garnish: Dust with cacao power & serve with a straw
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with 6oz scoop crushed ice and pour into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
2 scoop	Vanilla ice cream
review: Creamy vanilla iced coffee.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 1968 by Jerome Adams at Bayview Yacht Club in Detroit, USA. His creation proved enduring and the Hummer continues to be a popular Michigan cocktail.

name: Buckaroo
preparation: POUR all ingredients into glass and then fill with ice.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
4 shot	Cola (e.g. Coca Cola or Pepsi Cola)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A bourbon and cola aromatised by a couple of dashes of bitters.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide.

name: Caffè Negroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Mancino Kopi Vermouth
2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review: Coffee-infused vermouth replaces your standard rosso vermouth in this aptly named Negroni variation.

name: Paris Midi
preparation: STIR first 2 ingredients in glass. Add ice to fill glass and TOP with soda water. Briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Superbly refreshing blackcurrant. Perfect for when sitting outside a Parisian café.
history: Adapted from a recipe in the 1934 edition of Bar La Florida Cocktails, the menu booklet of what later became La Floridita.

name: Soufriere Negroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of black ice.
ingredients:
1 shot	Chairman's Reserve Spiced Rum
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
review: Bittersweet and delicately spiced.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Ehren Khoo-Steel at Brass Monkey in Nottingham, England.

name: Buck's Fizz
preparation: POUR half the champagne into a chilled glass, then the orange juice and finally the rest of the champagne.
ingredients:
3 1⁄3 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine (chilled)
1 2⁄3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed) (chilled)
review: A very simple cocktail, but when made with freshly squeezed oranges straight from the refrigerator this is a great brunch drink. (Be sure to fine strain your orange juice.)
history:
Thought to have been created in 1921 by Pat McGarry, first bartender at the Buck's Club, London. Very similar to the Mimosa created in Paris four years later.

The sketchy history of both the Buck's Fizz and Mimosa can be found on our Buck's Fizz and Mimosa cocktail page.

name: Kir Royale
preparation: POUR cassis into glass and TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
4 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Champagne replaces Bourgogne Aligoté white wine in this 'Royal' rendition of Mayor Canon Kir's classic apéritif. Easy to make, easy to drink.
history:
A sparkling version of the Kir Apéritif which is thought to have first been mixed in 1904 at Café George in Dijon, France. It is named after Canon Félix Kir who promoted the mixture while Mayor of Dijon.
Kir and Kir Royale history

name: Mimosa
preparation: POUR half the champagne into ice-filled glass (preferably a chunk of block ice), then POUR orange juice and finally the rest of the champagne.
ingredients:
3 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine (chilled)
3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed) (chilled)
review: Great when made with freshly squeezed orange juice, this cocktail is very similar to the Buck's Fizz, which tends to have a higher proportion of champagne. Also see the Grand Mimosa, basically the same drink charged with orange liqueur.
history:
Thought to have been created in 1925 by Frank Meier at the Ritz Hotel in Paris and named after the Mimosa tropical flowering shrub, Acacia dealbata - perhaps because of its trembling leaves, rather like the gentle fizz of this mixture.

The cocktail made its print debut in Frank Meier's 1936 book, The Artistry of Mixing Drinks titled "Mimosa or Champagne Orange" with the instruction, "In large wineglass, a piece of ice, the juice of one-half Orange; fill with Champagne stir and serve."

In his 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks, David A. Embury writes of this drink, "Just another freak champagne mixture. It is not half bad and the ladies usually like it. Use a good quality domestic champagne, medium dry."

The sketchy history of both the Buck's Fizz and Mimosa can be found on our Buck's Fizz and Mimosa cocktail page.

name: Port Wine Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2 1⁄2 shot	Tawny port
review: Port and brandy served straight-up and dressed up.
history: A classic from the early 1900s.

name: Zaza
preparation: SHAKE (or stir) all ingredients with ice and strain fine into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
review: Zaza is a diminutive of Isabela. However, other than the simplicity of its ingredients, there is nothing diminutive about this classic cocktail.
history: It is named after a French play that was a hit around the verge of the 20th century and was followed by opera and film versions, the Zaza Cocktail appears in Hon. William "Cocktail Bill" Boothby's 1908 The World's Drinks And How To Mix Them.

name: Dubonnet Cocktail No.1
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
review: Simple yet complex. Dry and aromatic.
history: A classic cocktail that was popular in Britain during the 1920s and appeared in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Knicker Dropper Glory
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hazelnut liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Nutty sweetness sharpened with lemon.
history: Created circa 2000 by Jason Fendick, London, England.

name: Mantini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	British bitter ale
review: A gin Martini-style drink made with beer in place of vermouth.

name: Nelson's Blood Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 1⁄2 shot	Ruby port
review: This carpet scary, appropriately named, blood red cocktail balances the rich fruitiness of port with the fortifying complexity of cognac. A popular drink in classic British pubs.
history:
After the Battle of Trafalgar (21 October 1805) when the British Royal Navy demonstrated its navy supremacy by conquering the combined fleets of the French and Spanish Navies the Franco-Spanish fleet lost twenty-two ships without a single British vessel being lost. However, the English lost Admiral Lord Nelson who was mortally wounded during the battle aboard HMS Victory.

To preserve Nelson's body during the return voyage to England, the ship's surgeon ordered that his body be placed in a barrel of French brandy. Although this was lashed to the deck and guarded, stories abound of sailors drinking the brandy out of respect for their commander, Nelson.

name: Mastiha & Tonic
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass and lightly stir.
ingredients:
2 shot	Kleos Mastiha liqueur
4 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: The very distinctive taste of mastiha with freshening tonic water.

name: Rum & IT
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 1⁄2 shot	Italicus liqueur
review: Created in April 2017 by yours truly (Simon Difford) at the Cabinet Room, London, England.
history: I mixed these two ingredients together just to ascertain where to go from there when creating a drink with Italicus. Then do I add a dash of maraschino, curaçao or bitters? I tried numerous liqueurs and bitters but I like the simplicity of this two ingredient cocktail. Now try it with gin – yup, Gin & It also works well. Later, the same mixing session also gave birth to For Sake’s Sake.

name: Gin & IT (Rosolio recipe)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Italicus liqueur
review: Bitter orange peel is a botanical which features in many gins, and in this cocktail a bitter sweet bergamot liqueur is mixed with gin to good effect.
history: One of the cocktails promoted with the launch of Italicus Rosolio di Bergamotto in the summer of 2017.

name: Dark 'n' Stormy Highball
garnish: Squeeze a wedge of lime into drink and drop in as a garnish
preparation:
Integrated version: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
Or, Layered version: POUR ginger beer into ice-filled glass first, then FLOAT rum.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
1 1⁄2 shot	Dark/black/blackstrap rum
review: Refreshing on a hot summer's day and darkly appropriate for Halloween.
history:
The signature drink of Gosling's Black Seal rum and very popular on the brand's home island of Bermuda.
Highball cocktails history

name: The Frank O'Hara
preparation: STIR with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄3 shot	Strega liqueur
review: This ever so simple Martini-style cocktail is surprisingly complex and tasty with the botanicals of both the gin and Italian liqueur combining harmoniously.
history: Probably named after Frank O'Hara, whose 1964 poem The Day Lady Died about the death of Billie Holiday, includes the verse, "and for Mike I just stroll into the Park Lane Liquor Store and ask for a bottle of Strega and then I go back where I came from to 6th Avenue and the tobacconist in the Ziegfeld Theatre and casually ask for a carton of Gauloises and a carton of Picayunes, and a New York Post with her face on it."

name: Vive l'apéritif
garnish: Cucumber slice, and preferably also strawberry, & mint
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
3 1⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: Thirst quenching, refreshing and low in alcohol. A great drink for a summer's afternoon or even before lunch.
history: Adapted from a signature serve promoted by Lillet Blanc as “Lillet Vive”. In French, the word Vive means live or long life, so Lillet Vive means Lillet Life while Vive l'apéritif translates as long live the apéritif.

name: Cucumber & Mint Seltz
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Cucumber & Mint
5 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review:
Light and refreshing. One to serve alongside the cucumber sandwiches!

Also, consider serving as a Spritz: Pour 90ml/3oz Prosecco, 45ml/1.5oz Botanical Cucumber & Mint and 60ml/2oz soda water into an ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
history: One of three signature serves launched in the summer of 2018 to accompany the launch of Ketel One Botanicals.

name: Peach & Orange Blossom Seltz
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Peach & Orange Blossom
5 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review:
Aromatic peach is surprisingly strong in this refreshing and light drink.

Also, consider serving as a Spritz: Pour 90ml/3oz Prosecco, 45ml/1.5oz Peach & Orange Blossom and 60ml/2oz soda water into an ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
history: One of three signature serves launched in the summer of 2018 to accompany the launch of Ketel One Botanicals.

name: Coconut Highball
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
2 2⁄3 shot	Sparkling coconut water
review: Coconut flavours are subtle in this surprisingly dry highball. If you self-carbonate your coconut water then consider also adding a touch of sugar to compensate for the bittering effect of the CO2 on the coconut water, so also enhancing coconut flavours.
history: The history of Highball cocktails and tips on how to make them.

name: Tequesso
preparation: POUR tequila into one shot glass and coffee into the other. Drink tequila first and chase with espresso.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
5⁄6 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
review: A great way to start the day, or end a meal.
history: A popular digestive in the Netherlands where it emerged during the Noughties.

name: Limoncello and Tonic
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
5 shot	Mediterranean tonic water
review: Sharp sherbety zesty lemon and tonic water – it's hard to imagine a more refreshing mix for a summer's day. This drink tastes good with regular tonic water but tastes so much better with Mediterranean tonic water.

name: L'Americano
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Savoia Americano Rosso
1 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Delicately bittersweet and low in alcohol but generously flavoured.
history: A signature cocktail developed in 2021 by Savoia Americano.

name: Pineapple Mimosa
preparation: POUR ingredients into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
3 shot	Pineapple juice
review: Best enjoyed with breakfast, strictly speaking a Mimosa should be served in a wine glass over ice, but flutes are more decadent. If you've a dry palate, use a brut or an extra brut sparkling wine and consider 15ml (½oz) more fizz and 15ml (½oz) less pineapple.
history: "Pineapple Mimosa, anyone?" was the question "uncle" Quentin (Tom Hollander), directed at Tanya McQuoid (Jennifer Coolidge) and Portia (Haley Lu Richardson) during breakfast in Palermo in the penultimate episode of the second series of HBO's The White Lotus. First screened in December 2022, the The White Lotus made the Pineapple Mimosa a popular cocktail in 2023.

name: Pink Panther
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into glass filled with crushed ice. Churn and top with more crushed ice.
ingredients:
2 shot	Adriatico Bianco almond milk liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review: Adapted from a recipe created in 2022 by our friends at Bellaventura Brands, the folk behind Adriatico Amaretto Bianco.
history: Creamy almond (there's no cream) with a pleasing bitter bite.

name: Matcha Bianco
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. (There's no need to dry shake to achieve desired foam.)
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Adriatico Bianco almond milk liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: An almond milk liqueur sour made special by a matcha powder rim.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2022 by our friends at Bellaventura Brands, the folk behind Adriatico Amaretto Bianco.

name: VC (Vermouth & Cassis)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
review: Dry vermouth balances the richness of crème de cassis.
history: The combination of dry vermouth and crème de cassis was most popular in the early 1900s when Noilly Prat featured the combination in a 1919 advertisement campaign.

name: Vermuttino
preparation: POUR ingredients into chilled glass and fill with ice.
ingredients:
2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Select good vermouth, strike the perfect dilution with the freshness of lemon zest twist, and you'll enjoy a delicious aperitivo.
history: Often described as "the original Italian aperitif", this mix of vermouth and soda originated in and remains popular in the bars of Turin, Italy, where the first commercial vermouth was produced in 1786.

name: Barga Kilt
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass (preferably over large chunks of ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1 shot	Nardini Amaro
review: A late-night digestivo, best enjoyed by the fireside.
history: This cocktail was introduced to Difford's Guide via a comment left by Nick Hopewell Smith on our Money in the Bank cocktail page.

name: Cowboy's Cocktail
preparation: POUR into glass - you be careful, mind!
ingredients: 1 1⁄2 shot	Horse with No Name habanero bourbon
review: The cowboy doesn't like his drinks fancy!

name: Texas Iced Tea
preparation: SHAKE first 9 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with cola and serve with a stirrer.
ingredients:
1⁄3 shot	Patrón Añejo tequila
1⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 1⁄2 shot	Cola (e.g. Coca Cola or Pepsi Cola)
review: Packing six different spirits, this Texas Tea is basically a Long Island Iced Tea with bourbon, and packs a suitably large Texan punch, especially if made with 6 x 15ml (½oz) measures of spirit as per the original recipe. If so choose a large (14oz) Collins to accommodate sufficient cola to achieve the desired dilution.

name: Casablanca
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄4 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
4 drop	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Go easy on the aromatic bitters (use drops rather than dashes) or your Casablanca will be more orange than "blanca". Original recipes in The New American Bartender's Guide and Jones' Complete Barguide omit egg white, but this variation on the White Lady tastes and looks better with an appropriately white fluffy head.
history: Eponymously named after Michael Curtiz's 1942 romantic drama movie starring Humphrey Bogart, Ingrid Bergman and Paul Henreid. Filmed and set during World War II, the plot centres around an American expatriate (Bogart) whose love for a women (Bergman) distracts him from helping a Czechoslovak resistance leader (Henreid) escape from the Vichy-controlled city of Casablanca. The women, is the resistance leader's wife and if that were not enough, the script famously delivers lines such as "Play it, Sam," "Of all the gin joints in all the towns in all the world, she walks into mine" and "Here's looking at you kid."

name: Gin Punch No. 2
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. Serve with straws.
ingredients:
3 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
7 fresh	Raspberries
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2 shot	Chilled water
review: Easy on the palate yet incredibly complex. Linseed oil notes of genever shine through.
history: Adapted from Hebert Asbury's 1928 reprint of Jerry Thomas' 1862 How to Mix Drinks, or The Bon Vivant's Companion.

name: Dingo
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Disaronno amaretto
2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Very fruity but with a rum and whiskey kick.

name: Woodside
preparation: MUDDLE pineapple in base of shaker and add other ingredients. DRY SHAKE (without ice), then SHAKE again with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 ring	Pineapple (fresh) (cored, skinned and chopped)
3⁄4 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Ruby port
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth (grapefruit infused)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Delicately fruity, light and fluffy.
history: Created in 2009 by Darren Thrower at The Kenilworth, Warwickshire, England and named after Count Basie's "Jumpin' at the Woodside".

name: Montgomery Slugger
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1⁄4 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Walnut (Nocino) liqueur
3 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Spirit-forward chocolaty nutty coffee.
history: Adapted from a drink discovered in January 2013 at Maison Premiere, Williamsburg, New York.

name: Patrón Señor Sling
garnish: Dehydrated pineapple & lime slices with cherry
preparation: SHAKE first 7 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda and lightly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄3 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Pineapple sugar syrup
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 dash	Bob's Chocolate bitters
2⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Created by Philip Bischoff, bar manager at Singapore’s Four Seasons multi-award winning Hotel Bar, Manhattan. Philip created this drink for Patrón Tequila as part of their activity for London Cocktail Week 2016.

name: Nightmare On Bourbon Street
garnish: Sugar syrup and cinnamon powder rim
preparation: SHAKE first 7 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. FLOAT dashes of bitters.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄6 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Piment d'Espelette chile liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Cinnamon syrup
1⁄6 shot	Maple syrup
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: An enliveningly spiced Whiskey Sour designed to wake you up from your slumber.
history: I came across this cocktail in October 2022 but while I liked the name I didn't like the recipe. Hence, the spec here is my own adaption of somebody else's good idea for a cocktail.

name: Apocalypse Negroni
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Navy Strength Royal Dock Gin
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 dash	3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer or Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water)
6 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Bittersweet and sweet 'n' sour, this straight-up Negroni is designed to have "that extra pinch of acidity that keeps the palate alive and fresh."
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Leonardo Todisco, the global brand ambassador for Strucchi vermouths and bitter.

name: Avenue
preparation: Cut passion fruit in half and scoop flesh into shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 fresh	Passion fruit (fresh)
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄24 shot	Orange blossom water / Orange flower water
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Passion fruit and orange flavours, laced with apple brandy and bourbon. Fruity yet dry.
history: First published in William J. "Billy" Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Bar Book where he credits its creation to "W. G. Crompton."

name: Clover Leaf
garnish: Lemon zest twist expressed & discarded, and garnish with fresh mint leaf
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE mint in base of shaker (just to bruise). Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5 fresh	Mint leaves
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: A Clover Club freshened and made more interesting by the addition of fresh mint, and not just as a garnish.
history:
The Clover Leaf is ostensibly the same as the Clover Club, with various similar recipes coexisting since 1909. The commonly accepted difference between these two very similarly named cocktails comes from Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book where he states a Clover Leaf Cocktail is "The same as Clover Club, with a sprig of fresh Mint on top" and so for most it is merely the decoration that distinguishes the two cocktails apart. However, there's a little more to it than that.

The first known recipe for Clover Leaf appears in Jacob Abraham Grohusko's 1908 Jack's Manual, while the first Clover Club is found in Paul E. Lowe's 1909 book Drinks: how to mix and how to serve. [The Oxford Companion to Spirits And Cocktails references a 1901 Clover Club recipe published in the New York Press on 21st June 1901, but I haven't been able to validate this.]

name: Cool Orchard
preparation: MUDDLE ginger in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 slice	Fresh ginger root (thumbnail-sized slice)
1 1⁄2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Ginger syrup
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Vanille de Madagascar
review: An unusual line up of ingredients combine to make a great drink.
history: Created in 2001 by Douglas Ankrah for Akbar in Soho, London, England

name: Cuban Cocktail No.3
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Like much of the Caribbean, this drink has French influences. Thank goodness for Admiral Rodney.
history: Adapted from Victor Bergeron's Trader Vic's Bartender's Giude (1972) revised edition).

name: Floridita Margarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄4 shot	Lime cordial (sweetened lime juice)
1 1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A blush coloured, Margarita-style drink with a well-matched amalgamation of flavours.
history: Created in 1999 by Robert Plotkin and Raymon Flores of BarMedia, USA.

name: Ginger & Lemongrass Martini
preparation: MUDDLE ginger and lemongrass in base of shaker. Add other ingredients and STIR until honey dissolves. SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 slice	Fresh ginger root (thumbnail-sized slice)
1⁄2 fresh	Lemongrass stem
2 barspoon	Honey
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
3⁄4 shot	Chilled water
review: Consider infusing the lemongrass in gin instead of muddling.
history: Created in 2005 by yours truly (Simon Difford), London, England.

name: Grape Delight
preparation: MUDDLE grapes in base of shaker. Add rest of ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
12 fresh	Red grapes (seedless)
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: This rust coloured drink is fruity and delicate.

name: Great Mughal Martini
preparation: MUDDLE raisins in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
20 dried	Raisins
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3⁄4 shot	Passion fruit syrup
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3 drop	Rose water
1 shot	Lime & lemongrass cordial
review: Douglas' original recipe called for raisin infused boubon and I'd recommend you make this drink that way if time permits.
history: Created in 2001 by Douglas Ankrah for Red Fort, Soho, London, England.

name: Leninade
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) and lemon slice
preparation: SHAKE first 6 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Citroen Vodka
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Orange undertones add citrus depth to the lemon explosion.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created by Dick Bradsell at Fred's bar in London, England, in the late 1980s. His original recipe (1½ shots citrus vodka, ¼ shot triple sec, 1 shot lemon juice, ¼ shot sugar syrup and 3 dashes orange bitters) was served short and straight-up with sugar syrup rather than grenadine.

I added the grenadine and made the Leninade a long drink in July 2013 due to comments from Discerning Drinkers saying the name was suggestive of a long red vodka-based drink.

name: Raspberry Collins
garnish: Skewered raspberries & lemon slice wheel. Serve with a straw.
preparation: MUDDLE raspberries in base of shaker. Add next 5 ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda, briefly stir.
ingredients:
10 fresh	Raspberries
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Crème de Framboise
1 1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura (optional)
3⁄4 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A popular modern-day adaptation of the classic Collins with a whopping 45ml (1½oz) of lemon juice, yet is far from being overly sour. (I've tried reducing the lemon and rebalancing with less sugar but the result is a lesser cocktail.)
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 1999 by Cairbry Hill, London, England.

name: San Francisco
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Long, fruity, slightly sweet and vodka-laced.
history: Unknown, but almost certainly not originally from the city of San Francisco in California. It certainly originated before 1992, as that's when I first encountered this cocktail.

name: Singapore Sling (using Old Tom gin)
garnish: Lemon slice & Luxardo Maraschino cherry on stick (sail)
preparation: SHAKE first six ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda and lightly stir.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Slightly on the dry and sour side, this is decidedly more complex than most Singapore Sling recipes.
history: For more Singapore Sling recipes and the cocktails full story, see our Singapore Sling page.

name: Tennessee Iced Tea
preparation: SHAKE first six ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with cola and serve with straws.
ingredients:
1 shot	Tennessee whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
