Top up with	Cola (e.g. Coca Cola or Pepsi Cola)
review: Whiskey and cola with extra interest courtesy of several other spirits and lemon juice.

name: Love Unit
preparation: MUDDLE pepper in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 slice	Red bell pepper
7 fresh	Basil leaves (thai)
1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Vanilla rum/vanilla-infused light rum
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Delicate, complex and balanced with enough fruit and veg to make your five-a-day.
history: Created by Ryan Magarian, Seattle, USA.

name: Black Tie
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄2 barspoon	Black strap molasses
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Depending on the sweetness of your molasses, you may not need to add sugar syrup.
history: Adapted from a drink created by Mark Lynch at Green 19 in Dublin, Ireland.

name: Bombay Lassi Cocktail
preparation: MUDDLE cardamom in base of shaker. ADD other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 whole	Green cardamom pods
5⁄6 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
1⁄3 shot	Ginger liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Yoghurt (natural)
review: Creamy yet balanced, even slightly tart rather than sweet, with hints of vanilla, cardamom, ginger, and lemon.
history: Created in 2011 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Raita Cocktail
preparation: MUDDLE cardamom, cumin and then cucumber in base of shaker. ADD other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 dried	Green cardamom pods
1⁄2 barspoon	Cumin seeds
1 1⁄2 inch	Cucumber (fresh)
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Yoghurt liqueur
1 pinch	Salt (sea salt)
3 fresh	Mint leaves
review: Fresh cucumber, mint and yoghurt with a hint of cardamom and cumin spice, laced with vodka.
history: Created in 2011 by yours truly (Simon Difford) at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Melon Maple Fizz
preparation: MUDDLE melon in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda water.
ingredients:
4 cube	Melon (Honeydew)
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Green melon liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Maple syrup
1⁄2 shot	Egg white
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Light, fruity and refreshing. Not overly sweet.
history: ADpted from a recipe created in 2014 by Manuel Terron, Midori Global Brand ambassador.

name: Sunny Side Up
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1⁄3 shot	Americano bianco
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Rhubarb bitters
review: Bittersweet zesty citrus and cognac with aromatic wine.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2015 by Christopher McQuillan at Am:pm, Belfast, Northern Ireland.

name: The Burly French Man
preparation: RINSE chilled glass with absinthe and set to one side. STIR other ingredients with ice and strain into absinthe rinsed glass.
ingredients:
1⁄6 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2⁄3 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄3 shot	Damson liqueur
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Boozy and served Sazerac-style, cognac with powerful Chartreuse herbal notes and faintly jammy fruit.
history: Created in 2015 by Tommy Long at the Groucho Club in London, England. Originally made with Cocchi Storico Vermouth di Torino rosso vermouth.

name: Sazeroy
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) & maraschino cherry on stick
preparation: RINSE chilled glass with absinthe. STIR other ingredients with ice and strain into absinthe rinsed glass.
ingredients:
3 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	Lillet-style Rouge light quinquina
1⁄6 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄6 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: A spiritious after dinner sipper which as the name suggests is reminiscent of a Sazerac.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Giovanni Bruno at the Blue Bar at The Berkeley, London, England.

name: Tequila Club
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
2⁄3 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Agave syrup
4 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: The similarity of ingredients in this tequila-based riff on the classic Pegu Club to the Margarita are obvious, so it's not surprising the finished drink is reminiscent of a Margarita, only lighter with the lime notes a lot subtler. As well as the tequila, orange curaçao shines in this drink.
history: Created in February 2017 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room in London, England.

name: Blushing Monk
garnish: Angostura Bitters dash in a single line across top egg white foam to form a brown line representing the rope that ties a monk's robe.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
5⁄12 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄2 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄6 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: An aromatic bittersweet sour with heavy herbal influences.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created by Sam Finch at The Milk Thistle, Bristol, England. Sam says, "The Blushing Monk came from a moment of back bar chaos, with the main intention being to combine Bénédictine with Aperol following the blueprint of a classic sour. Suze became the machinery of balance in the drink, the heavy vegetal notes of the gentian offsetting the sweetness already in the mix whilst reinforcing the light bitterness of the Aperol. Lillet Blanc lifts and brightens whilst the lime brings bold zestiness to the party.

The name simply references the drink's lustily 'blushing' hue and spins on the heritage of the Benedictine Liqueur; a fresh, flirty and suggestively lively flavour experience."

name: Barbacoa
preparation: MUDDLE first 3 ingredients in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, briefly SHAKE with ice and POUR into glass without straining.
ingredients:
3 wedge	Lime (fresh)
3 slice	Red bell pepper
1 slice	Red chili pepper (jalapeño/fresno chili (10,000 SHU) deseeded)
2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄4 shot	Ginger syrup
1⁄2 shot	Agave syrup
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Savoury and lightly spicy with smoky mezcal backbone.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2009 by Julian Cox at Rivera, Los Angeles, USA.

name: Bitter Maid
preparation: MUDDLE cucumber in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 slice	Cucumber (fresh)
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄24 shot	Aniseed (anise) liqueur
5 fresh	Mint leaves
review: A half-ounce of almond syrup is an unlikely ingredient in an aperitivo-style cocktail. Indeed, it's an unlikely recipe but produces an interesting and tasty cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Piotr Kuzmicki in Melbourne, Australia.

name: Igloo
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄3 shot	Crème de violette liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄24 shot	Giffard Peppermint Pastille crème de menthe
1⁄24 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄6 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
history: Adapted from a recipe by Jason E. Clapham of the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England who says this cocktail is so-named due to being based on a drink containing cream called Snowball which appears in W. C. Whitfield's 1939 Just Cocktails.

name: Death By Morning
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & float mint leaf or peg to rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄2 shot	Brancamenta
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1 1⁄2 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
1⁄6 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: With a whopping ¾oz absinthe and ½oz of minty fernet, coupled with 1½oz wake-up call of espresso coffee, this cocktail is assertive but in a surprisingly alluring way. The Vindaloo of Espresso Martinis.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Dzu Nguyen, General Manager at Horsefeather bar in San Francisco, USA.

name: The Fernando
garnish: Half orange wheel slice & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda and then FLOAT dark rum.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 3-5 years
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
1⁄2 shot	Jamaican aged blended rum with funk
review: The dark rum float atop this elongated rum sour makes the first few sips so good that you'll want another to experience the best bit again.
history:
The signature cocktail at The Country Club in Brookline, Massachusetts, the oldest country club in the USA. The cocktail is an upgrade of the club's previous rum float and was created by Fernando Figueroa, who started work at the bar during Easter week in 1990.

The Fernando cocktail became famous in June 2022 when the club was hosting the U.S. Open thanks to a piece by Paul Sullivan featuring the cocktail and its creator in The New York Times. At the club, this cocktail is made with Mount Gay as the base rum and sour mix rather than freshly squeezed juices.

name: Lucky Lucano
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) to emulsify and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Lucano amaro
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Gomme syrup
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A bourbon-laced bittersweet, sweet 'n' sour aperitivo or digestivo with citrus freshness.
history: Created by yours truly in March 2024 and named after Charles "Lucky" Luciano (1897-1962), an Italian-born American gangster "considered the father of modern organized crime in the United States". Lucky Luciano was the first boss of the modern Genovese crime family.

name: King's Cross Cosmo
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Pamplemousse rose (pink grapefruit) syrup
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A gin-based, grapefruit-influenced Cosmopolitan.
history: Created in May 2024 by yours truly to showcase Monin Pink Grapefruit syrup.

name: President Napoleon
garnish: 2 drops aromatic bitters pulled through the foam with a cocktail stick.
preparation: MUDLLE raspberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) to emulsify and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
4 fresh	Raspberries
1 2⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Napoleon tendencies aside, this cocktail is bigger than its diminutive proportions, packed with bourbon-laced, expressive bittersweet fruity sourness. Enjoy and make a pig of yourself!
history: Adapted from a recipe in 2023 by Sam Penton at the Manor Bar in the Rosewood Miramar Beach Hotel, Montecito, California, USA. Sam developed his cocktail, named "Napoleon" after the Marxist pig in George Orwell's 1945 Animal Farm, for a literary villains-themed menu.

name: American Pie Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Apple Schnapps liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Crème de Myrtille liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: This berry and apple pie has a tangy bite.
history: Adapted from a cocktail discovered in the noughties at Oxo Tower Restaurant & Bar, London, England and originally named American Pie Martini.

name: Apricot Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)

1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: This light scarlet classic cocktail combines gin, apricot and lemon juice. The aromatic bitters and lemon zest twist are essential to its balance.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide.

name: Bajan Mojito
preparation: Cut passion fruit in half and scoop flesh into glass. Add mint and gently MUDDLE (just to bruise mint). Add rum, lime juice and crushed ice. CHURN (stir) drink in glass to mix. DRIZZLE passion fruit liqueur and serve with straws.
ingredients:
1 fresh	Passion fruit (fresh)
8 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄4 shot	Passoã passion fruit liqueur
review: A laid-back, fruity, slightly sweet Mojito.
history:
Adapted from a recipe by Wayne Collins, London, England.
See: Mojito cocktail history

name: Bajan Passion

ingredients:

1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄4 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
review: A Daiquiri laced with generous fruit and a touch of vanilla.
history: Created in 2004 by Wayne Collins, London, England.

name: Basil Beauty

1 whole	Passion fruit (fresh)

1⁄2 shot	Coconut sugar syrup
review: Pineapple and passion fruit laced with citrus vodka and infused with hints of lime, basil and coconut.

name: Boston
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin

3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)

3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Gin laced tangy fruit.

name: Capercaillie
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

1 2⁄3 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
5⁄12 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur

history: Adapted from a recipe created in the 1990s by London bartender Wayne Collins. This Scotch whisky-based cocktail is named after a variety of large woodland grouse and sadly UK's Capercaillie population has declined to such a degree that the bird is at risk of extinction.

name: Casanova

3⁄4 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)

name: Cascade
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
6 fresh	Raspberries
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
1⁄6 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
review: Rich raspberry with hints of citrus and vanilla.

name: Allegrottini

3⁄4 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth

history: Adapted from a cocktail discovered in 2005 at the Four Seasons Hotel in Prague, Czech Republic.

name: Blade Runner
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.

2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Jamaican-style overproof aged pot still rum
2 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)

history: Adapted from a cocktail discovered in 2005 at Zoulou Bar, Berlin, Germany.

name: Cuban Cocktail No. 2
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)

1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup

1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura

history: Adapted from a recipe in Victor Bergeron's 1972 Trader Vic's Bartender's Guide.

name: Blanche Corpse Reviver
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	La Fée Absinthe Blanche

3⁄4 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)

review: Blanche absinthe sits surprisingly well in this riff on the classic Corpse Reviver.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2013 by Stephen Quainton at B.Y.O.C. Bar, Brighton, England

See our Corpse Reviver page for the full story behind the origins of the Corpse Reviver, its history and variations on this recipe.

name: Doctor Funk
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Dark/black/blackstrap rum
1⁄6 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)

review: With its very generous dose of rum and absinthe, too many of this rum-laced liquorice-like tasting cocktails and you'll need your very own doctor.
history: Created by Don Beach in the early 1950s at his The Don The Beachcomber restaurant in Palm Springs, this drink is named after Doctor Bernard Funk who was Robert Louis Stevenson's physician in Samoa. The good doctor is said to have concocted and prescribed an absinthe laced limeade so inspiring this cocktail.

name: Flamingo No. 2
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters (optional)
review: This Flamingo's not pink but it is suited to a couple of dashes Creole-style bitters that impart a slight red tinge.

name: Gloom Lifter

name: Georgetown Punch

2⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)

1 shot	Coconut rum liqueur (35-40% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
3⁄4 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A Tiki-style, fruity rum punch.
history: Adapted from a drink discovered in 2005 at Degrees, Washington DC, USA.

name: Gulf Coast Sex on the Beach
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.

1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
3⁄4 shot	Green melon liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1 1⁄2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Golden tan in colour and tropical in flavour, complete with frothy top.
history: Created in 1997 by Roberto Canino and Wayne Collins at Navajo Joe, London, England.

name: Hot Red Blooded Frenchman
preparation: Place bar spoon in warmed glass. Add other ingredients and STIR.
ingredients:
1 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
2 shot	Claret red wine
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
Top up with	Boiling water
review: Warm, fruity red wine - great on a cold night.

name: Inga from Sweden
preparation: MUDDLE strawberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.

review: Inga must like a touch of bitter Italian with her fruit.

name: Jules Delight

review: Sweet fortified strawberries with a cleansing balsamic vinegar bite.
history: Created in 2005 by Julien "Papa Jules" Gualdoni at Trailer Happiness, London, England.

name: Kentucky Colonel No. 2
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.

1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)

1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Peach and bourbon with hints of orange and spice.
history: Created by Morgan Watson of Apartment, Belfast, Northern Ireland.

name: Krakow Tea

ingredients:
12 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Bison grass vodka

3 1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Refreshing and floral with a dry, citrus finish.
history: Created in 2002 by Domhnall Carlin at Apartment, Belfast, Northern Ireland.

name: Lemon Butter Cookie
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Bison grass vodka
5⁄6 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄4 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1 2⁄3 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: An appropriate name for a most unusually flavoured cocktail modelled on the Polish Martini.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2002 by Mark 'Q-Ball' Linnie and Martin Oliver at the Mixing Tin bar in Leeds, England.

name: Luxury Mojito

12 fresh	Mint leaves

history: Mojito cocktail recipes and history.

name: Mint Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
12 fresh	Mint leaves
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Peppermint Pastille crème de menthe
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 1⁄2 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: An after-dinner palate cleanser.

name: Motox

history: Adapted from a drink discovered in 2005 at Mo Bar, Landmark Mandarin Oriental Hotel, Hong Kong.

name: Mrs Robinson #1

8 fresh	Raspberries

review: Rich raspberry fruit laced with bourbon.

name: Mule's Hind Leg

name: Noon

review: This classic cocktail is smooth and aromatic.

name: Orang-A-Tang
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. FLOAT layer of rum over cocktail.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)

review: As the name suggests, orange predominates in this long, tangy, tropical cooler.

2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin

review: A sophisticated, complex balance of orange and gin.

name: Pancho Villa
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)

1⁄4 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Chilled water (reduce if wet ice)
review: Dilution is key to this cocktail so either shake with crushed ice (as per the original recipe) or do as I do and add chilled water. Even then, to quote Victor Bergeron, "This'll tuck you away neatly - and pick you up and throw you right to the floor".
history: Adapted from a recipe in Victor Bergeron's 1972 Trader Vic's Bartender's Guide.

name: Passion Fruit Rum Punch
preparation: Cut passion fruit in half and scoop out flesh into shaker. Add next four ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. CHURN (stir) and then top with sparkling wine.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 fresh	Passion fruit (fresh)
1 1⁄2 shot	White overproof rum
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Passion fruit syrup
1 1⁄2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Rum and fruit combine in this punchy tropical-style drink.
history: Created in 2004 by yours truly.

name: Raspberry Margarita
preparation: MUDDLE raspberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
6 fresh	Raspberries
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Agave syrup
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Just as it says - a raspberry flavoured Margarita.

name: Rude Ginger Cosmopolitan
preparation: MUDDLE ginger in base of shaker. Add the other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 slice	Fresh ginger root (thumbnail-sized slice)
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Lime cordial (sweetened lime juice)
review: To quote Halo's cocktail list, the bar where we discovered this drink, "Looks like a cosmo, goes like a Mexican!"
history:
Created in 2003 by Jeremy Adderley at Halo, Edinburgh, Scotland.

Also see the origin and story behind the Cosmopolitan cocktail.

name: Scorpion
garnish: Orange slice wheel, Gardenia flower & mint sprigs bouquet. Serve with a straw.
preparation: DRY BLEND (without ice) first 5 ingredients on slow setting and add Xanthan gum while continuing to blend. Add half a 7oz scoop of crushed ice and blend again. Pour unstrained into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
3⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 2⁄3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄4 barspoon	Xanthan gum (E415) (optional)
review: A fruity cocktail with a sting in its tail.
history: Created by Victor Bergeron circa 1950s, this recipe is adapted from his 1972 Trader Vic's Bartender's Guide (Revised Edition).

name: Strawberry Daiquiri
garnish: Strawberry (or half if large) on rim with mint sprig tip leaves.
preparation:
MUDDLE strawberries (4 to 7, depending on size) in the base of the shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

NOTE: Strawberry pulp is notorious for blocking strainers and sink wastes. Hence, double straining is essential when making this cocktail, as is the use of a quality Hawthorne strainer (I use one with an extra spring and a wide gauge fine strainer with a large capacity). The Hawthorne strainer should retain most of the fruit pulp, along with the ice in the shaker. Pouring through an additional fine strainer ensures the clarity of the cocktail. Even with the best strainers, the pulp will start to restrict the flow towards the end of the pour and moving your shaker to help the liquid find a new escape route helps. Finally, use a bar spoon to help move the pulp in the fine strainer to allow the last of the cocktail through the strainer. Also, don't be tempted to make two cocktails in one shaker by doubling quantities as this will compound pulp issues. The cocktail is worth the faff!
ingredients:
7 fresh	Strawberries (hulled, small & ripe)
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 grind	Black pepper
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Makes strawberries and cream appear very dull.
history:
A popular cocktail in Cuba where it is known as a Daiquiri de Fresa.
See: Daiquiri cocktail history

name: Tennessee Berry Mule
preparation: MUDDLE raspberries in base of shaker. Add next four ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with ginger beer, lightly stir and serve with straws.
ingredients:
8 fresh	Raspberries
1 1⁄2 shot	Tennessee whiskey
1 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1 1⁄2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: A berry rich cocktail laced with whiskey, flavoured with Amaretto and topped with ginger beer.
history:
Adapted in 2003 from a recipe Alex Kammerling created for TGI Friday's UK. Named partly for the ingredients and partly as a reference to Jack Daniel's proprietor (and nephew), Lemuel Motlow, who took up mule trading during Prohibition.
See: Moscow Mule history.

name: Tootie Fruity Lifesaver
garnish: Tootie Fruity lollypop or 3 Luxardo Maraschino Cherries on a stick rested across the glass rim.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Galliano L'Autentico liqueur
1 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1 shot	Pineapple juice
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Tropical fruit laced with delicate notes of herbal spearmint freshness.
history: Appropriately, this fruity cocktail takes its name from tutti frutti, the Italian for 'all fruits'. Outside Italy, tutti-fruity mainly refers to mixed fruit flavoured ice cream but is also fruit flavoured confectionery. Life Savers are an American brand of ring-shaped hard and soft confectionery created in 1912 by Clarence Crane, a candy maker in Ohio.

name: Triple 'C'
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
5⁄6 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
4 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A chocolate and cranberry alternatini aperitif, for a after-dinner serve, use bianco rather than dry vermouth.
history: Created in 2001 by yours truly and originally called the Chocolate Covered Cranberry Martini - every drink in V-shaped glass was called a 'Martini' in those days.

name: Verdi
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄3 shot	Green melon liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Peachtree peach schnapps
2⁄3 shot	Pineapple juice
2⁄3 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A melange of fruits combine in this slightly sweet, gluggable, short drink.
history: Adapted from a drink discovered in 2002 at the Fifth Floor Bar in Harvey Nichols, London, England.

name: Webster Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix) (optional)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water) (optional)
review: Balanced, or even a tad on the sour side rather than sweet. Indeed, your choice of apricot liqueur will impact the need for added sugar. Adjust accordingly in the pursuit of deliciousness.
history: Adapted form a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: White Lion (David Embury's recipe)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients, including the shell of half a lime, with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 fresh	Lime shell (squeezed/spent lime husk)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix) (optional)
review: Please don't judge this recipe until you have experienced this fruity Daiquiri made homemade "grenadine" (1 part freshly pressed pomegranate juice and 2 parts caster sugar). Then you'll end up with a delicious cocktail with an off-white hue. With commercial grenadine syrup, this cocktail can have a jammy flavour and is likely to be bright cherry red - hardly a 'White' Lion. That said, some prefer cherry red and jammy!
history:
Adapted from a recipe purloined from David Embury's seminal 1948 book, The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks. Embury had a dry palate so we've added a spoon of sugar syrup to his recipe, which, depending on your palate, you may want to reduce or omit this.

Embury does the While Lion an injustice by saying, "This, of course, is simply a White Lady without the egg white and with lime juice in place of lemon". That might sum up his version but the original White Lion in Jerry Thomas' 1862 The Bar-tenders Guide is so much more.

name: Shark's Tooth No.1 (Trader Vic's)
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass whilst also pouring soda water.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	White overproof rum
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Pinky red in colour and heavily influenced by flavoursome overproof rum.
history: Adapted from Victor Bergeron's Trader Vic's 1972 Bartender's Guide (revised edition) where he writes, "One of the first drinks we ever made".

name: Silver Bronx
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
5⁄12 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
5⁄6 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura (optional)
review: A Bronx made 'silver' by the addition of egg white.
history: For the full story behind the Bronx and Bronx variations, please see our Bronx page.

name: Cherry Mariner
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water
review: Rich cherry liqueurs fortified by gin and bittered with a hint of orange.

name: Eastern Raspberry Sidecar
preparation: MUDDLE raspberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
7 fresh	Raspberries
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Akashi-Tai Daiginjo Genshu sake
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Refreshing, fruity, easy drinking.
history:
Created by Ryan Magarian, Seattle, USA.

See our Sidecar cocktail page for the full story behind the origins of the Sidecar, its history and variations.

name: Eastern Sin
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Pineapple juice
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters (optional)
review: Fruity and slightly sweet but toned by Scotch whisky.
history: The Eastern Sin was first published in William James "Billy" Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Bar Book where he credits its creation to J. Stoneham.

name: Flip Williams
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Pear liqueur (Poire William)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 fresh	Egg yolk
review: Velvety smooth with hints of whiskey and pear.
history: Created in 2007 by Julian de Feral at Milk & Honey, London, England.

name: Ginger Snap
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into an ice-filled glass. TOP with ginger ale.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Ginger liqueur
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
review: This balanced Gin Collins is sweetened by ginger and orange liqueurs.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2007 by Gary "gaz" Regan, New York, USA.

name: The Long Shot
garnish: Orange slice & lemon wedge. Serve with a straw.
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain ice-filled glass. TOP with soda and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A simple variation on William Schmidt's Alabazam.
history: Created in 2007 by Julian de Feral at Milk & Honey, London, England.

name: Northern Sun
preparation: MUDDLE ginger in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 slice	Fresh ginger root (thumbnail-sized slice)
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
3 shot	Pear juice (freshly pressed)
1 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Maple syrup
review: Subtle and easy. Hard to believe this drink contains two measures of rum.
history: Recipe adapted 2008 from LCBO Magazine and comes courtesy of Sean Murray of Aurora, Ontario, Canada.

name: Quince Mustard Margarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 barspoon	Quince mustard jam
2 grind	Black pepper
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A wonderfully quince influenced Margarita.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Ryan Magarian in Seattle, USA.

name: Doctor No. 1
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Swedish Punsch liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix) (optional)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
4 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters (optional)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Lime combines well with the aromatic spices in Swedish punch.
history: A recipe for a Doctor Cocktail made with Swedish punch and lime juice first appears in Hugo R. Ensslin's 1917 Recipes for Mixed Drinks (2nd Edition) (It may have also appeared in his 1916 first edition.)

name: Irresistible
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
3⁄4 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Rum-laced, herbal yet delicate with cleansing citrus notes.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide.

name: Rizzo
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Passion fruit syrup
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: The tangy, sharp grapefruit reveals hints of apple spirit smoothed by grenadine.
history: Created in 2006 by Gregor de Gruyther at Ronnie Scott's in London, England, and named for Betty Rizzo, the leader of the Pink Ladies in the film Grease.

name: Screaming Orgasm
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1 1⁄4 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1 1⁄4 shot	Irish cream liqueur
1 1⁄4 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1 1⁄4 shot	Milk (whole milk/full 3-4% fat)
review: As fattening as it is alcoholic, this indugent, creamy dessert in a glass cocktail is served with generous innuendo.
history: One of the best-known cocktails from the 1980s.

name: Waters of Chaos
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
1⁄4 shot	White overproof rum
1⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Robust flavours of overproof rum and Chartreuse combine with Dutch genever in this Last Word-like cocktail.
history: Created by yours truly and named after the words of the track Argha Noah by Nightmares on Wax.

name: Oranjey Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Ketel One Oranje Vodka
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Dry, and yes, very orangey with bittersweet orange complexity.

name: Rhode Island Red
preparation: SHAKE first five ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with ginger beer, lightly stir and serve with straws.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Agave syrup
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
Top up with	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: Tequila with a hint of berry fruit, slightly sweetened with agave nectar, spiced and made long with ginger beer.
history: Created in 2009 by Vincenzo Marianella at Copa d'Oro, Santa Monica, USA.

name: Staffordshire Delight
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A modern day pick-me-up / hair-of-the-dog with a rich, enlivening bittersweet bite.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2010 by Thomas Dalloway, United Kingdom.

name: Lavender Honey Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
3 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: An Irish whiskey sour sweetened with honey and herbal liqueur with Creole bitters adding aromatics.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2006 by Dre Masso at Lonsdale in Notting Hill, London, England.
Sours cocktail history

name: Banana Smoothie
preparation: BLEND ingredients with 6oz scoop of crushed ice. Pour into glass and serve immediately with straws.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Yoghurt liqueur
3 barspoon	Honey
1⁄2 fresh	Banana (preferably overripe)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review: Packed with fruit, this creamy banana flavoured shake is 'hardened' with a double measure of vodka.
history: Created in 2011 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Cantaritos
glass: Cantaritos clay pot or Collins glass
preparation:
If using a Cantaritos clay pot (instead of a collins glass) submerge the pot in cold water to clean the inside and wet the outside clay.

POUR ingredients into ice-filled pot or glass and STIR. Consider serving with straws.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 pinch	Salt (sea salt)
2 shot	Thomas Henry Pink Grapefruit soda
review:
Juicy (freshly squeezed orange, grapefruit and lime) and refreshing slightly salty tequila invigorated with sparkling grapefruit soda.

Wetting the porous clay exterior of the Cantaritos pot not only improves its appearance but as the water evaporates from the outside so it helps keep the contents cold.
history: Commonly made in bars, cafés and even roadside stalls of Jalisco, Mexico. The simple Cantaritos clay pot is often used as a disposable take away container.

name: Teaquila
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cold black tea
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	Honey flavoured vodka
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura (optional)
review: A Mexican iced tea sweetened with honey.
history: Created in 2011 by Mark Cooke and the rest of the team at North Bar, Leeds, England.

name: Wolf Ticket
preparation: MUDDLE peach in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 fresh	Fresh ripe peach (skinned & diced)
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Crème de Pêche de Vigne liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: The ripeness and quality of the peach will make or break this drink. If in season white peaches are preferable.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2013 by Eric Johnson at the Sycamore Den, a 1970s-inspired cocktail lounge in San Diego's Normal Heights neighbourhood, USA.

name: Pink Khaleesi
preparation: MUDDLE peppercorns in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 barspoon	Pink peppercorns
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Kleos Mastiha liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Pretty in pink but with a hint of spice and the distinctive Greek flavour of mastiha.
history: Created in 2015 by yours truly.

name: Deshler Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 1⁄2 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
2 twist	Orange peel
1 twist	Lemon peel
review: A dry Manhattan-like cocktail with zesty citrus. Some will object to the scummy head caused by shaking rather than stirring but a Deshler must be shaken.
history: Cointreau.com (the brand's official website) says, "This is probably the first cocktail created in New York with Cointreau." It first appears in Hugo R. Ensslin's 1916-17 Recipes for Mixed Drinks and is named after the Deshler Hotel in Columbus, Ohio, one of three hotels owned by brothers Louis C. Wallick and Adrian L. Wallick. Ensslin worked at all three but spent most of his career in their The Wallick Hotel in Times Square where it is presumed he created this cocktail.

name: Smokin' Hot Paloma
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with grapefruit soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Piment d'Espelette chile liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Agave syrup
1 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Pink Grapefruit soda
review: Mezcal provides a subtle hint of smokiness while chilli liqueur adds hot spice. The other guests to Paloma's party bring fruity honeyed sweetness.
history: Adapted from a drink discovered in 2015 at Building on Bond in Brooklyn, NYC, USA.

name: Cherry Mojito
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE mint in base of glass (just to bruise). Add the next 4 ingredients to glass and two-thirds fill with crushed ice. CHURN (stir) with bar spoon and then FILL glass with more crushed ice. TOP with soda, briefly churn and serve.
ingredients:
14 fresh	Mint leaves
1 1⁄3 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
2⁄3 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A Mojito with a touch of cherry. Beware, this is no cherry bomb and those looking for something fruitier and sweeter should add 2.5 to 5ml (½ to 1 barspoon) sugar syrup.
history: One of many cherry riffs on the classic Mojito. This one by yours truly in December 2021.

name: Rock of Sages
preparation: MUDDLE cherries in base of shaker. Add sage leaves and lightly bruise with the muddler. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
3 whole	Maraschino cherry (from jar in syrup)
4 fresh	Sage leaves
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 shot	Pineapple juice
1 barspoon	Syrup from Luxardo Maraschino Cherries
review: As the name suggests, sage subtly influences this fruity cognac based cocktail served on the rocks. Fruity and easy.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Dominic Krempels at Archer Street, Soho, London, England. Dominic's original recipe calls for Martell XO cognac and Cocchi Storico Vermouth di Torino rosso vermouth.

name: The Book of Kells
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: A Vieux Carré with more whiskey than cognac, and we're talking Irish whiskey rather than rye or bourbon.
history: Created in 2015 by John Marshall at Melaza Bistro, Woodstock, Vermont, USA.

name: Saronno's Sweetheart
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Disaronno amaretto
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Rhubarb syrup
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Cognac and almond with lemon, apricot and rhubarb.
history: Created in 2015 by Jamie Campbell at The Daffodil Restaurant, Cheltenham, England.

name: Fireplace Fashioned
preparation: POUR whisky and water into ice-filled glass and set aside. Separately, STIR other ingredients with ice. Discard contents of glass and strain stirred cocktail into the chilled Islay whisky washed glass.
ingredients:
1⁄4 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
4 shot	Chilled water
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	Honey sugar syrup
1⁄6 shot	Cinnamon syrup
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Santiago Michelis at Alcoholic Architecture, London, England.

name: Mexica
preparation:
SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.

Special Ingredient #1: Homemade dill syrup
Add 160 grams of dill to 1 litre sugar syrup. Allow to infuse for at least 24 hours, strain and bottle.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
2⁄3 shot	Tangerine / Mandarin / Clementine juice (fresh juice)
1 pinch	Salt (sea salt)
review: Created by Cihan Anadologlu, co-owner of Circle By Cihan Anadologlu in Munich, for Patrón Tequila at London Cocktail Week 2016.

name: El Especialista
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
2⁄3 shot	Fino sherry
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3 barspoon	Caster/ Superfine/Baker's special sugar (white)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 pinch	Salt (sea salt)
review: I love what the dry sherry adds to this Daiquiri, but given the addition of salt perhaps manzanilla sherry would have been more appropriate than fino? Remembering this is a Legacy competition cocktail, the "no garnish" seems a shame.
history: The Italian Bacardí Legacy 2016 winning cocktail created by Livio Morena at Caffè Propaganda in Rome.

name: Last Call
preparation: DRY SHAKE all ingredients (without ice) to emulsify. SHAKE again with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
5⁄12 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
5⁄6 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Cinnamon syrup
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Imagine a Daiquriri with rosso vermouth, pink grapefruit juice, and fluffed with egg white.
history: Adapted from the Argentinean Bacardí Legacy 2013 winning cocktail created by Lucas Lopez at Isabel Bar in Buenos Aires, Argentina. Originally made with Bacardi Carta Blanca rum.

name: Black Forest Sour
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and pour into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Jägermeisteror other German amaro
1⁄6 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Pineapple juice
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Beautifully balanced with complex herbal, berry, pineapple and citrus flavours.

name: French Kiwi & Apple Caipirinha
garnish: Stirrer (spoon, wooden lolly stick or stick cut from sugar cane)
preparation:
1. Cut lime in half (from pole to pole) and then slice one of the halves into eight 3-4mm thick half-moon shaped segments and drop into the base of a robust rocks glass.

2. Add 3 bar spoons caster sugar (or ½oz / 15ml sugar syrup 2:1) and MUDDLE.

3. Add Kiwi fruit and MUDDLE some more.

4. When sure fruit juice is fully extracted and the sugar dissolved, transfer the muddled fruit and sugar into serving glass (preferably a 30cl / 10oz hi-ball glass).

5. POUR cachaça (stored in the freezer) into the rocks glass (used to muddle) and swirl to rinse glass before pouring cachaça into serving glass. Add apple juice and anis liqueur, then STIR to ensure all ingredients are well mixed.

6. Crack (rather than crush) four to five large ice cubes and drop into serving glass. STIR before topping with more ice and serve with a stirrer (but no straws).
ingredients:
1⁄2 fresh	Lime (fresh) (chopped)
3 barspoon	Caster/ Superfine/Baker's special sugar (white)
1⁄2 fresh	Kiwi fruit (fresh)
1⁄6 shot	Aniseed (anise) liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
2 shot	Cachaça (from freezer)
history:
This kiwi and apple flavoured caipirinha is made "French" by the merest hint of anis (aniseed).

For information on the history and other variations of the Caipirinha, please see our Caipirinha cocktail page.

name: Nobile Cocktail
garnish: Lemon slice, mint sprig, raspberry & blackberry
preparation: MUDDLE raspberries in base of shaker. Add next four ingredients (all but bitter lemon), SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with bitter lemon and lightly stir.
ingredients:
8 fresh	Raspberries
2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
2 shot	Thomas Henry Bitter Lemon
review: Fruity but not sweet, with drying bitter lemon. This is a refreshing, low alcohol, aperitif style summery cocktail.

name: Sex On The Beach
preparation: SHAKE first three ingredients (the 'beach' part) with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. Then SHAKE the last three ingredients (the 'sex' part) with ice and strain into glass to sit on top of the 'beach' base layer. Serve with stirrer and instruct drinker to mix layers together before drinking.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Peachtree peach schnapps
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Pineapple juice
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
review:
Sweet fruitiness masks the alcohol in this easy-drinking, long cocktail.

"Sex" is associated with red (e.g.red light district) and is represented in this drink in the form of vodka, cranberry juice, and black raspberry liqueur. These 'sexy' ingredients sit atop the sandy yellow "beach"– consisting of peach schnapps, orange juice, and pineapple juice.

name: Alabama Slammer (long)
garnish: Skewered orange slice & Luxardo Maraschino cherry (sail)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. (Don't be tempted to shake as this detrimentally thins the drink. Instead, consider rolling or throwing.)
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Southern USA-style liqueur 40% (e.g. Southern Comfort)
1⁄2 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A Screwdriver that's flavoured and lightly sweetened with a trio of liqueurs.
history:
Said to have been made famous by American former football quarterback Brett Favre. Just eight weeks after a near-fatal car accident resulting in 30 inches (76 cm) of his small intestine being removed, on 8th September 1990, Favre led Southern Miss to a comeback victory over Alabama. The Alabama coach, Gene Stallings, is quoted as saying, "You can call it a miracle or a legend or whatever you want to. I just know that on that day, Brett Favre was larger than life."

Truth is, the Alabama Slammer was popular in the U.S. a decade before Favre's miracle win and was being served in bars, including T.G.I. Friday's, in the 1980s.

There are numerous recipes for this cocktail dating from the late 1980s, some with orange juice and others with grenadine replacing the sloe gin found in better recipes.

name: Golden Eight
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
2⁄3 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
2⁄3 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: I find the original four equal parts recipe a tad on the sour side so I like to trim back the citrus and also add a few drops of saline. And as is the case we so many Daiquiri-style cocktails, I like to add a splash of dilution.
history: Adapted from the Singaporean Bacardí Legacy 2018 winning cocktail created by Sim Sze Wei at Atlas Bar, originally based on Bacardi Ocho Anos and Carta Blanca rums.

name: Lazy Lover
preparation: MUDDLE cucumber slices and salt in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
3 slice	Cucumber (fresh)
1 pinch	Salt (sea salt)
1 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
3⁄4 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄4 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
1⁄4 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Savoury and lightly bittersweet. An interesting apéritif cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Tess Anne Sawyer at The Up & Up, New York City, USA, which came to us courtesy of gazregan.com.

name: Tuxedo Cocktail No.3 (Lowe & Straub's recipe)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Fino sherry
1 dash	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Although only a spoonful, the sherry used dramatically impacts the finished cocktail. We tried amontillado but found this drink works best with either fino sherry or manzanilla sherries.
history: Adapted from recipes in Drinks As They Are Mixed (1904) by Paul E Lowe and Drinks (1914) by Jacques-Straub.

name: The Bee Bodice
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄6 shot	Ketel One Vodka (infused with lavender)
1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Honey water (1:1)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
2 dash	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
review: Honeyed and floral with a cleansing bitterness.
history: Created by 2017 by Luke Hanson at Dr Inks Curiosities, Exeter, England. Luke says his drink is "a riff on a riff... The Bee's Knees inspired a drink The Bee's Knickers which was on our original and opening menu here at Dr Inks. For our first birthday, we were asked to reinvent them once again and this beauty came to life."

name: Dans Le Jardin (In The Garden)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
4 drop	Chartreuse Élixir Végétal (optional)
review: This bittersweet aperitif-style drink's light green hue and garnish befits its name and uses the tried and tested combo of gentian, gin and lemon juice.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Fred Charlet at La Cabane, Strasbourg, France. Fred says, "With this cocktail, I wanted to remember playing in grandpa's garden hut as a child while my family was sat in the garden enjoying an aperitif. This cocktail is an anthem to our childhood."

name: Fruity Godchild
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄3 shot	Crème de noyau liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Disaronno amaretto
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A riff on a Godfather that's spirituous and delicately sweet almond with faint cherry fruit followed by a surprisingly dry finish.
history: Created in February 2019 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Tearful Chocolate Mojito
preparation:
SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with tonic.

Special ingredient #1: Mint Syrup - lightly muddle 10 mint stems with 250g brown sugar, 250g white caster sugar and 600ml hot water.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
8 fresh	Mint leaves
2⁄3 shot	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
1 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: Chocolatey mint mojito with a crisp tonic dryness.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Din Hassan, Brand Ambassador Black Tears; Singapore.

name: Cranberry Collins
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda water.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Raspberry flavoured vodka
1⁄6 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
5⁄6 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Tangy cranberry and raspberry juice with freshening zesty lemon and a touch of bittersweet herbal complexity.

name: Jimmie Roosevelt
garnish: None "no pineapple, no mint sprig, no cherry garnish"
preparation: Soak sugar cube with Angostura and drop into base of glass. POUR cognac, sugar syrup and champagne over soaked cube. Fill glass with cracked (not crushed) ice and finish with a FLOAT of Chartreuse.
ingredients:
1 whole	Sugar cube
8 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 1⁄2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
1⁄6 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
review: A frappé version of the Classic Champagne Cocktail which is given extra interest courtesy of a Chartreuse float.
history: Created by Charles H. Baker Jr. and friends, in his 1939 The Gentleman's Companion he says, "Champagne Cocktail No. II, which with modestly downcast lash we admit is an origination of our own, & which we christened the Jimmie Roosevelt. Last spring we had the pleasure of turning our house into an oasis, between planes, for Colonel Jimmie Roosevelt and Grant Mason of the Civil Aeronautics Commission... It was warmish, and being a sort of Nephew-in-Law of Paul Garrett, dean of all American Vintners, and present 'father' of Virginia Dare, we brought out 2 bottles of Garett Champagne, and created this one."

name: Robin Redbreast
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Blood orange liqueur
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Vodka-laced blood orange with tangy lime freshness. Reminiscent of a bloody Cosmo.

name: Transcontinental
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄4 shot	Crème de violette liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: The Last Word meets the Aviation somewhere over the French-Italian border.
history: Adapted from a recipe, with the help and input from Tim Ihde (via comments on our Last Word history and variations page) who discovered this cocktail in 2016 at the Brick Farm Tavern in Hopewell, Hopewell, New Jersey, USA, which he says is "an excellent cocktail bar and farm-to-table restaurant."

name: Lady Jane
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
5⁄6 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
5⁄12 shot	Cognac (brandy)
5⁄12 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
5⁄12 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: A tasty spirit-forward after-dinner cocktail with herbal undertones and citrusy freshness.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Susanna McMahon, a keen amateur mixologist and 74-year-old grandmother who says, "This cocktail was created for a very dear lady friend of mine named Jane who adores B&B and rye but had never drunk them together." adding, "Drink to the power of friendship."

Susanna's original recipe called for 20% larger measures of each ingredient than above and used Bénédictine B&B rather than 50% Bénédictine DOM and cognac.

name: Blackthorn No. 2
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄12 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: This low-alcohol digestif is a mashup of William Boothby's and Harry Craddock's 1930 Blackthorn No. 2 recipes with a leaning towards Boothby's. It's jammy with delicate herbal undertones.
history: The recipe for what's now known as the Blackthorn No. 1 appeared in William "Cocktail Bill" Boothby's 1908 World's Drinks And How To Mix Them. This is repeated in the 1930 Swallows edition of Boothby's book, along with three numbered variations, this being number two.

name: Adelaide
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Savoia Americano Rosso
5⁄6 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
3 drop	Bob's Lavender Bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Bittersweet and delicately gin-laced.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Agostino Galli at Lacerba Restaurant in Milan, Italy.

name: Hot Lips
garnish: Salt rim (coat one-third outside of glass with lime juice and salt)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Jalapeño infused blanco tequila
3⁄4 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
1⁄6 shot	Clément Sirop de Canne
review: Unusually, a stirred (not shaken) drink with citrus, and depending on your jalapeños your lips could be merely warmed or scorched. Alternatively, in a quest for ease and consistency, omit the jalapeños from your tequila and omit the 5ml (1/6oz) cane sugar syrup and replace with 10ml chili liqueur. You may also consider shaking rather than stirring!
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2009 by Jessica Gonzalez at Death & Co. in New York City, USA.

name: Humble Pie
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄6 shot	Ginger syrup
1⁄12 shot	Pimento dram/Allspice liqueur
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 grind	Black pepper
review: Apple brandy and scotch whisky with ginger, pimento dram and black pepper spice.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2018 by Sean Hoard, Beverage Director at Pépé le Moko in Portland, Oregon, USA.

name: Holiday Margarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄3 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Pomegranate juice
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Tangerine / Mandarin / Clementine juice (fresh juice)
1⁄6 shot	Agave syrup
review: A fruity limoncello enriched Margarita.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2016 by Duggan McDonnell at Frisson Restaurant in San Francisco, USA.

name: Uptown
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. TOP with sparkling wine.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Ketel One Oranje Vodka
1⁄4 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Agave syrup
2⁄3 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Zest citrus with hints of honeyed almond, enlivened with a splash of dry sparkling wine.

name: Blue On Blue
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
3⁄4 shot	Coconut water
3⁄4 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Blue Curaçao
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Blueberries nestle across a vodka and rum-laced blue lagoon of coconut and cranberry. It may be a "blue drink," but it isn't overly sweet.
history: I came across this cocktail in October 2022, but while I liked the name, I didn't like the recipe. Hence, this spec is my adaption of somebody else's good idea for a cocktail.

name: Golden Glow No.2
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. POUR grenadine into centre of cocktail which should sink to form a red layer in base of glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Dark/black/blackstrap rum
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄12 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
history: Adapted from a recipe in Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide.

name: Fernet Me Not No. 1
preparation: MUDDLE cucumber in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with sparkling wine.
ingredients:
2 slice	Cucumber (fresh)
2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄3 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
review: A riff on a Southside Royal with fernet replacing mint, cucumber and sparkling wine to lift the cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2013 by bartender Terry Cashman at Callooh Callay in Shoreditch, London, England.

name: The Benevolent
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1 shot	Cold brew coffee
1⁄2 shot	Averna Amaro
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
1 dash	Xocolatl mole bitters
review:
This tequila-laced coffee cocktail is relatively light in alcohol and perfect as an aperitivo or digestive.

As a longstanding trustee of the UK's drinks industry charity, which until recently was called The Benevolent, it was the name that drew this cocktail to my attention. The Benevolent was founded in 1986 to support colleagues in the drinks industry in need. Its name was changed to the Drinks Trust in March 2020 to better convey its purpose.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Justin Campbell for Mason restaurant in Santa Monica, USA.

name: Cherry Blossom No. 2
garnish: Skewered maraschino cherry with cherry blossom when in season
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Cherry blossom/sakura syrup
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: A cherry blossom riff on the classic Corpse Reviver No. 2.
history: Created by yours truly in April 2024 at the Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: Sunny Day
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Rhum Clément Blanc
3⁄4 shot	Pamplemousse rose (pink grapefruit) syrup
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
6 drop	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A summery sour laced with rhum agricole.
history: Created in May 2024 by yours truly to showcase Monin Pink Grapefruit syrup.

name: The Communist
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Cherry bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: I've played with the ratios but I'm not sure this sour can be better than a four-out-of-five.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Ted "Dr. Cocktail" Haigh's 2009 book Vintage Spirits and Forgotten Cocktails where he credits "a crude and otherwise quite forgettable cocktail pamphlet from 1933 titled Cocktail Parade."

name: Acapulco
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Fruity and tropical in style and laced with tequila and rum.

name: Almond Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
4 drop	Bob's Vanilla bitters
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water
review: A delicate, almond-flavoured Vodka Martini.
history:
Created in 2005 by yours truly.
Martini cocktail history and variations

name: Amber
garnish: Dust with grated nutmeg & apple wedge
preparation: MUDDLE ginger in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
4 slice	Fresh ginger root (thumbnail-sized slice)
1 1⁄2 shot	Bison grass vodka
4 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Apple Schnapps liqueur
review: A combination of adult flavours in a long, thirst-quenching drink. Also good served straight-up.
history: Created in 2001 by Douglas Ankrah for Akbar at the Red Fort in Soho, London, England.

name: Ambrosia
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into glass, TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
Top up with	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Dry, fortified champers with a hint of apple.

name: Anis'tini
preparation: MUDDLE star anise in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 dried	Star anise
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Black sambuca liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Aniseed (anise) liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Chilled water (reduce if wet ice)
review: Specs of star anise are evident in this aniseedy Martini.
history: Discovered in 2002 at Lot 61, New York City, USA

name: Apricot Sour
preparation: STIR apricot jam (preserve) with bourbon until it dissolves. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 barspoon	Apricot jam (preserve)
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Short and fruity.
history: Created in 2005 by Wayne Collins, London, England.

name: Azure Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cachaça
1⁄4 shot	Goldwasser cinnamon schnapps liqueur
1 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A tangy cocktail that's reminiscent of a cinnamon-laced apple pie. Shame it's not blue.
