history: Ben Reed created this cocktail in 1998 at the Met Bar in London, England. It was originally named the Azure Martini and was made with muddled fresh apple.

name: Banana Colada
preparation: BLEND ingredients with 6oz scoop of crushed ice and serve with paper straws.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
4 shot	Pineapple juice
1 fresh	Banana (preferably overripe)
1 shot	Cream of coconut (e.g. Coco Lopez, Re'al etc.)
review: Don't skimp, use a whole banana per drink for real flavour.
history: See our main Piña Colada page for the story behind the classic and for links to numerous other variations.

name: Bee's Knees (with rum & cream)
preparation: STIR honey with rum until honey dissolves. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 1⁄4 shot	Navy rum (54.5% alc./vol.)
2 barspoon	Honey
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: Smooth and orangey to start, with a rum and honey finish.

name: Berry Nice
preparation: MUDDLE blackberries in base of shaker. Add next three ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain into ice-filled glass whilst also pouring ginger beer.
ingredients:
4 fresh	Blackberries
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
4 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: Rich blackberry flavour with a touch of ginger spice.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2001 in the UK's The Living Room chain of bars.

name: Bikini Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Blue Curaçao
1⁄4 shot	Peachtree peach schnapps
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: A vivid blue combination of lemon, orange and peach laced with gin.
history:
Adapted from a cocktail created in 1999 by Dick Bradsell for an Agent Provocateur swimwear launch.

Invented by designer Louis Réard in July 1946, the bikini swimsuit was named after Bikini Atoll, where the first public test of a nuclear bomb took place four days earlier. At the time, exposing the wearer's navel and buttocks was considered so shocking that no model would wear it, so Réard hired Micheline Bernardini, a nude dancer from the Casino de Paris to model the two-piece swimsuit.

Evolution of the Martini cocktail

name: Black 'N' Blue Caipirovska
preparation: MUDDLE berries in base of glass. Add other ingredients. Fill glass with crushed ice and CHURN (stir) with bar spoon. Serve with straws.
ingredients:
6 fresh	Blackberries
6 fresh	Blueberries (fresh)
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A great fruity twist on the regular Caipirovska.

name: Blueberry Martini
preparation: MUDDLE blueberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
8 fresh	Blueberries (fresh)
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Blueberry/Bilberry liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Vodka-laced rich blueberry with balancing lime freshness.

name: Blush Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Vanille de Madagascar
1⁄2 shot	Disaronno amaretto
2⁄3 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1 1⁄6 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: Drier than it looks, but still one to follow the dessert trolley.
history: Created by Colin William Crowden at Mashed Bar in Leicester, England

name: Brooklyn (St George version)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Basically a bourbon-based Perfect Manhattan with a generous dash of maraschino liqueur. The lack of Amer Picon in this recipe as well as the use of bourbon rather than rye whiskey means it's not what's now generally recognised as being a Brooklyn.
history:
Thought to have originated at the St George Hotel, Brooklyn, New York City, USA.

In his 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks, David Embury says of the Brooklyn, "You will note that the Brooklyn is nothing but a Dry Manhattan with a dash of maraschino. It is supposed to be a specialty of that grand old Brooklyn hotel, the St. George. I would be willing to wager, however, that even in Brooklyn there are at least five to ten times as many Manhattans consumed as there are Brooklyns. Try both and you will understand why."

Brooklyn cocktail history.

name: Caramel Manhattan
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Caramel Toffee liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2⁄3 shot	Pineapple juice
1 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Flavours combine harmoniously with the character of the bourbon still evident.
history:
Adapted from a drink created in 2002 by Nick Strangeway in London, England.
Manhattan cocktail history

name: Caribbean Breeze
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
2 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lime cordial (sweetened lime juice)
review: A long drink with bags of tangy fruit flavours.

name: Chinese Whisper
preparation: MUDDLE ginger in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 slice	Fresh ginger root (thumbnail-sized slice)
2 shot	Ketel One Citroen Vodka
1 shot	Kwai Feh lychee liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Ginger syrup
review: There's more than a whisper of ginger in this spicy cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe discovered in 2003 at Oxo Tower Bar, London, England.

name: Chocolate Puff
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
6 barspoon	Yoghurt (natural)
2 twist	Orange (fresh)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Smooth as you like. The orange is surprisingly evident.
history: Created by Wayne Collins in 2002 for Maxxium UK.

name: Chocolate Sidecar
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
3⁄4 shot	Tawny port
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Cognac-laced chocolate with port wine complexity and sugary richness balanced by lime juice.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2005 by Wayne Collins for Maxxium UK.
Sidecar cocktail history

name: Cider Apple Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice & fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
3⁄4 shot	Apple Schnapps liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: As the name suggests, rich cider flavours with a sharp finish.
history: Created in 1998 by Jamie Terrell at Lab, London, England.

name: Bistro Sidecar
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Tuaca liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Hazelnut liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Although significantly twisted from the classic, this is still recognisably a Sidecar in style.
history:
Adapted from a recipe by chef Kathy Casey Food Studios, Seattle, USA. Kathy's original recipe called for a sugar rim and tangerine juice.

See our Sidecar cocktail page for the full story behind the origins of the Sidecar, its history and variations.

name: Chocolarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
1⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: As the name suggests - a Margarita with chocolate and coffee.
history: Adapted from a recipe discovered in 2005 at Agave, Hong Kong.

name: Columbus Daiquiri
garnish: Lime or apricot wedge on rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: A tangy, apricot flavoured Daiquiri.

name: Derby Daiquiri
preparation: DRY BLEND (without ice) first 4 ingredients and gradually add Xanthan gum while continuing to blend. Add half a 7oz scoop of crushed ice and blend again. Pour into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄4 barspoon	Xanthan gum (E415)
review:
For those seeking the shaken version previously above:
Glass: Coupe
Garnish: Orange zest twist
How to make: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
60ml (2oz) Light white rum
22.5ml (.75oz) Orange juice
15ml (.5oz) Lime juice
7.5 (.25oz) Sugar syrup
history: The Kentucky Derby has long been associated with the Mint Julep and in 1959, the folk behind the Florida Derby turned to a famous local bar in search of a libation to serve at their own racecourse, Gulfstream Park in Hallandale Beach. So, in 1959, Mariano Licudine at The Mai-Kai Polynesian Restaurant and Tiki bar in Oakland Park, Florida, created the Derby, the official cocktail of the Florida Derby.

name: Durango
preparation: SHAKE first three ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
2⁄3 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
2 shot	Thomas Henry Pink Grapefruit soda
6 drop	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters (optional)
review: This sandy coloured drink makes tequila, amaretto and grapefruit into unlikely but harmonious bedfellows.

name: Dutch Breakfast Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Warninks Advocaat liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄6 shot	Galliano L'Autentico liqueur
review: A tasty, aromatic, almost creamy alternative to a fry-up.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2002 by Alex Kammerling, London, England.

name: Emperor's Memoirs
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with ginger beer.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
1⁄4 shot	Ginger cordial (non-alcoholic)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer (chilled)
review: Not particularly alcoholic, but strong in a gingery, spicy way.
history: Created in 2001 by Douglas Ankrah for Akbar, Soho, London, England.

name: French Spring Punch
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with champagne and serve with straws.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Crème de Framboise
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
Top up with	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Not as popular as the Russian Spring Punch but still a modern day London classic.
history: Created by Dick Bradsell and Rodolphe Sorel at Match EC1, London, England, during the late 1990's.

name: Fruit Tree Daiquiri
garnish: Grapefruit zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Syrup from Luxardo Maraschino Cherries
review: Even with a spoon of cherry syrup, this is fruity and balanced rather than sweet with rum holding its own as the dominant flavour.

name: Giuseppe's Habit
preparation: Spray the oils from the two lemon zest twists into the cocktail shaker, wipe them around the rim of the glass and drop them into the shaker, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 fresh	Lemon peel
1 1⁄2 shot	Galliano L'Autentico liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Hazelnut liqueur
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 1⁄4 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review: An intriguing drink that combines hazelnut, orange, apple, aniseed and peppermint.
history: Created in 2002 by Leon Stokes at Zinc Bar & Grill, Birmingham, England.

name: Golden Girl
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1 shot	Pineapple juice
1 shot	Tawny port
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 fresh	Egg (white & yolk)
review: This appropriately named velvety drink is a refined dessert in a glass.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Dale DeGroff in New York City, USA. I've slightly increased the proportions of rum and port from Dale's original recipe.

name: Green Apple & Cucumber Martini
preparation: MUDDLE cucumber in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 inch	Cucumber (fresh)
2 shot	Cucumber flavoured vodka
1⁄2 shot	Sour apple liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Archetypal English flavours. Clean, green and refreshing.
history: Adapted from a recipe discovered in 2003 at Oxo Tower Bar, London, England.

name: Hoa Sua
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Pomegranate juice
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
3⁄4 shot	Akashi-Tai Daiginjo Genshu sake
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Light and easy drinking - the rum flavour shines through.
history: Created in 2005 by yours truly for Hoa Sua catering school in Vietnam using locally available products.

name: Hot Buttered Rum Cocktail
garnish: Cinnamon stick & lemon slice (studded with cloves)
preparation: Place bar spoon loaded with honey in warmed glass. Add other ingredients and STIR until honey and butter are dissolved.
ingredients:
2 barspoon	Honey
1 knob	Unsalted butter
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
2 pinch	Freshly grated nutmeg
Top up with	Boiling water
review:
In his The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks, David Embury says, "The Hot Spiced Rum is bad enough, but the lump of butter is the final insult. It blends with the hot rum just about as satisfactorily as warm olive oil blends with champagne!"

It's rare for us to question Embury but we rather like this slightly oily, warming, spicy toddy. This drink is even better when you use heated dry cider in place of boiling water.

name: Indian Rose
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Rose water
1⁄4 shot	Rose sugar syrup
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Subtle rose hue and flavour
history: Adapted from a drink discovered in 2005 at Mie N Yu, Washington DC, USA.

name: Insomniac
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
2⁄3 shot	Hazelnut liqueur
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
2⁄3 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
2⁄3 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: Wonderfully balanced, creamy and caffeine laced.

name: International Incident
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Irish cream liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1⁄2 shot	Hazelnut liqueur
review: Rich and creamy.

name: Jaded Lady
preparation: SHAKE first four ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. Carefully POUR blue curaçao through centre of drink (it should sink to the bottom).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Warninks Advocaat liqueur
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Blue Curaçao
review: Distinctly Dutch in style, this thick, creamy drink delivers orange, vanilla and more than a hint of gin.
history: Created by yours truly in 1996.

name: Jambouree
preparation: STIR preserve with bourbon in base of shaker until mostly dissolved. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 barspoon	Apricot jam (preserve)
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Rich and jammy flavours balanced by bourbon and lemon juice.

name: Ja-Mora
preparation: SHAKE first four ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
Top up with	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Ja-mora of this fruity champagne cocktail you drink, ja-mora you'll like it.
history: Created by Jamie Terrell and Andres Masso in 1998. Named after 'mora', the Spanish for blackberry. The 'j' and 'a' stand for the names of its two creators.

name: Jean Marc
preparation: MUDDLE mint and ginger in base of shaker. Add next two ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with Appletiser, stir and serve with straws.
ingredients:
2 slice	Fresh ginger root (thumbnail-sized slice)
4 fresh	Mint leaves
1 1⁄2 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄4 shot	Apple Schnapps liqueur
Top up with	Sparkling apple juice
review: Chartreuse combines well with apple, ginger and mint in this summertime drink.
history: Created in 2003 by yours truly after judging a Chartreuse cocktail competition in London and realising which flavours best combine with Chartreuse. Named after my friend, the then President Directeur Général of Chartreuse.

name: Jelly Belly Beany
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
2⁄3 shot	Peachtree peach schnapps
2⁄3 shot	Coconut rum liqueur (35-40% alc./vol.)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water
review: It's a sweetie but you're going to enjoy chewing on it.
history: Created in 2002 at Hush, London, England.

name: Kentucky Dream
preparation: STIR vanilla liqueur and bitters with two ice cubes in a glass. Add half the bourbon and two more ice cubes. Stir some more and add another two ice cubes and the rest of the bourbon. Add the last two ingredients and more ice cubes and stir lots more. The melting and stirring of the ice cubes is essential to the dilution and taste of the drink.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Vanille de Madagascar
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review: Tames bourbon and adds hints of apricot, vanilla and apple.
history: Created in 2002 by Wayne Collins for Maxxium UK.

name: Key Lime Pie #1
garnish: Pie rim - wipe outside edge of glass rim with cream mix (from the float) and dip into crunched-up Graham Cracker or digestive biscuits.
preparation: DRY SHAKE (without ice) cream and vanilla liqueur in a pre-chilled shaker to mix and aerate. Use to rim glass and set the remainder rest aside. SHAKE last 3 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled, rimmed glass. Then carefully float pre-prepared cream and liqueur mix over the cocktail's surface.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Licor 43 Original liqueur (chilled)
2 shot	Single cream/half-and-half (chilled)
1 1⁄2 shot	Coconut rum liqueur (35-40% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: This rich cocktail is great when served as a dessert alternative.
history: Created by Michael Waterhouse, owner of Dylan Prime in New York City, USA.

name: Limey Cosmo
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Lime flavoured vodka
1 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 1⁄4 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lime cordial (sweetened lime juice)
review: If you like Cosmopolitans, you'll love this zesty alternative.
history: Cosmopolitan cocktail history

name: M.G.F.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Ketel One Oranje Vodka
5⁄6 shot	Ketel One Citroen Vodka
5⁄6 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Short and sharp.
history: Discovered in 2003 at Claridge's Bar, London, England.

name: Macka
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
1 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A long fruity drink for parched palates.
history: Famously, the only cocktail, indeed the only drink, served since 1928 at the Damour Colette bar in Lamballe-Armor, Brittany, France. Each customer is only allowed two.

name: Maiden's Blush
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Pale pink (depending on your grenadine), gin-laced rich fruit and subtle lemon sourness.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Malcolm Lowry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	White overproof rum
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: The Daiquiri meets the Margarita in this suitably 'funky' and punchy cocktail.
history: Created by drinks author David Broom. Named after Malcolm Lowry's 1947 novel Under the Volcano which explores a man's battle with alcoholism in Mexico.

name: Mango Margarita (frozen)
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with 6oz scoop of crushed ice. Serve with straws.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	Mango purée
1 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Mango first and Margarita second.

name: The Bomb
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Amontillado sherry
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Pimento dram/Allspice liqueur
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A sherry-led aperitif cocktail. Don't be put off by its murky appearance.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Stan Jones' 1977 Jones Complete Bar Guide.

name: Melon Daiquiri #1 (served 'up')
preparation: Cut melon into 8 segments and deseed. Cut cubes of flesh from skin of one segment and MUDDLE in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄6 fresh	Melon (Cantaloupe)
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Green melon liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A classic Daiquiri with the gentle touch of melon.

name: Met Manhattan
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Butterscotch liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Bourbon and toffee orange. This was originally a shaken drink so in this stirred recipe I've added a splash of water to replicate the dilution imparted by shaking. However, perhaps better to forgo this and serve on-the-rocks in an old-fashioned glass.
history:
A riff on the classic Manhattan cocktail discovered in the 1990s at The Met Bar in Metropolitan Hotel, London, England.
Manhattan cocktail history

name: Mexican 55
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
Top up with	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Suitably hard, yet surprisingly refreshing and sophisticated.
history:
An adaptation of the classic French 75 created in 1988 at La Perla, Paris, France. The name is said to come from Fidel Castro's statement, "Bullets come by vintages, like wine, especially Latin American bullets. Mexican '55 is a good year, '52 not so good."

More information on the history and variants of the French 75 can be found on our page.

name: Million Dollar Cocktail
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) & pineapple wedge on rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Serious, yet superbly smooth and a bit fluffy.
history: Some say this "Million Dollar Cocktail" was created around 1910 by Ngiam Tong Boon at The Long Bar, Raffles Hotel, Singapore. Others maintain it was created in 1894 by Louis Eppinger at The Grand Hotel, Yokohama, Japan. Our money is on Louis, the man many also credit for creating the Bamboo Cocktail.

name: Napoleon
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.

1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1⁄4 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)

history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Opera
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur

2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura

history: The Opera cocktail first appeared in Jacques Straub's 1914 book Drinks. However, the version of the Opera mostly seen today comes from Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Oriental Tartini

1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)

history: Created in 2004 by yours truly.

name: Perfect Alibi

ingredients:

1 1⁄2 shot	Barenjager Honey liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 shot	Jasmine tea (cold)
review: A very unusual and pleasant mix of flavours.
history: Created in 2001 by Douglas Ankrah for Akbar, London, England.

name: Pimm's Cocktail
garnish: Lemon & orange zest twists (discarded) & strawberry on rim
preparation: SHAKE first four ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
2 shot	Fruit cup liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 1⁄2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Luxuriate in this quintessentially English tipple.
history: See our Fruit Cups and Pimm's page for more information.

name: Princeton
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
1⁄2 shot	Tawny port
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix) (optional)
3 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water
review:
Kappeler's 1895 recipe calls for the Old Tom gin and orange bitters to be stirred with ice and strained into a glass, with port poured down the side of the glass so it settles to form a red layer beneath the orange bitters tinted gin.

I've added a spoon (5ml) of sugar syrup to Kappeler's recipe to slightly sweeten the gin (omit if using a sweet old tom) and a splash of water to add some much-needed dilution. I also prefer to abandon the original layering and stir all the ingredients together.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's influential 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Royal Cosmopolitan

1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
Top up with	Brut champagne/sparkling wine

history:
Created in 2003 by Wayne Collins, London, England.

For more recipes, origins and history behind the Cosmopolitan cocktail, see our Cosmopolitan page.

name: Snoopy

name: Tequila'tini

name: Trilby No.1

name: Tropical Daiquiri

1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)

name: Voodoo
garnish: Dust with cinnamon powder (sprinkled through flame)

2 1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: The rich flavour of the aged rum marries well with apple and lime juice.
history: Created in 2002 by Alex Kammerling, London, England.

name: Vowel Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

5⁄6 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
2⁄3 shot	Mentzendorff Kümmel liqueur

name: Wanton Abandon
preparation: MUDDLE strawberries in shaker. Add next three ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
5 fresh	Strawberries (hulled, small & ripe)
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: A crowd-pleaser - looks great and its fruity, balanced flavour will offend few.

name: Ward Eight
garnish: Quarter orange slice wheel & Luxardo Maraschino cherry on stick
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: This is a spirited, sweet and sour combination - like most politicians.
history:
Named after Ward Eight, a voting district of Boston notorious for political corruption. A 1951 Holiday Magazine article, attributes creation of the Ward Eight cocktail to a bartender named Tom Hussion, in November 1898, at Boston's fine-dining restaurant Locke-Ober Café, in honour of Martin Lomasney, who was running for election in Ward Eight. Lomasney, a teetotaller, may not have been at the dinner organised by members of the Hendricks Club of socialites but, while it's possible they toasted him in his absence, contrary to Holiday Magazine the drinks surely weren't mixed by Hussion as he apparently didn't start working at Locke-Ober until 1900.

Another Locke-Ober's bartender, named Billy Kane, may have mixed the first round of Ward Eights for Hendricks Club that night. However, not according to a bartender named Charlie Carter who, in a 1934 letter to G. Selmer Fougner published in his New York Sun "Along the Wine Trail" column, claims he created the Ward Eight to celebrate a 1903 Lomasney election victory.

I have not yet succeeded in verifying the 1951 Holiday Magazine article or the 1934 New York Sun column so I am only repeating what others have written. Frustratingly, I've also not yet been able to access a widely quoted 1907 column in the Boston Herald that claims the cocktail as "the most talked-of drink in Boston."

The cocktail features in the 1913 revised edition of The Cocktail Book - A Sideboard Manual for Gentlemen and, more notably, in Robert Vermeire's 1922 Cocktails: How to Mix Them.

name: Zhivago Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Sour apple liqueur
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Sweet and sour - sweet apple, vanilla and bourbon balanced by sour lime juice.
history: Created in 2002 by Alex Kammerling, London, England.

name: Raspberry Lynchburg
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with lemonade or lime-lime soda. Then, DRIZZLE liqueur around the surface (it will fall through the cocktail, leaving coloured threads).
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Tennessee whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 2⁄3 shot	Lemon-lime soda (Sprite/7-Up)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
review: A berry fruit-influenced riff on a Lynchburg Lemonade.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 1992 by Wayne Collins at Roadhouse, London, England.

name: Balm Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Manzanilla sherry
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	Pimento dram/Allspice liqueur
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Orange-flavoured dry sherry with subtle pimento spice.
history:
Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book:
"BALM COCKTAIL. (6 people)
½ Glass Orange Juice.
½ Glass Cointreau.
3 Glasses Sherry.
1 Dash Orange Bitters.
2 Dashes Pimento Dram Liqueur.
Fill up the shaker with cracked ice, shake and serve with an olive."

name: The Beauty Beneath
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into a chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 3⁄4 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Orange dominates this bittersweet Manhattan, cum-Daiquiri, cum-Negroni.
history: Created in 2008 by Jeffrey Morgenthaler at Bel Ami Lounge, Oregon, USA.

name: Bouquet
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Rose sugar syrup
1⁄4 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Rose delicately flavours gin with a sweet and sour balance provided by honey and lemon.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2005 by Alex Pacumbo at Cocoon, London, England.

name: Cunningham
garnish: Flamed blood orange zest twist (discarded) and skewered Luxardo maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into a chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 3⁄4 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Blood orange juice
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Reminiscent of a Blood and Sand with Bénédictine and lemon juice replacing sweet vermouth.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Marco Dionysos at Tres Agaves, San Francisco, USA and in memory of Johnny Cunningham (1957 - 2003), one of the world's all-time great Scottish fiddlers.

name: Dimi-tini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
7 fresh	Raspberries
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄3 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Like Dimi - this drink's easy to like.
history: Adapted from a recipe by Dimitri Lezinska, London, England.

name: Good Hope Plantation Rum Punch
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda and briefly stir.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Jamaican-style overproof aged pot still rum
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)

2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A classic rum and citrus-laced, generously flavoured, single-serve punch.
history: Originally made at the Good Hope Hotel in Falmouth, Jamaica. The Good Hope is an 18th Century country house set in a 2,000-acre plantation high in the lush landscape of Cockpit Country near Montego Bay.

name: Juniport Fizz
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into empty chilled glass. TOP with soda from a siphon.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Tawny port
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
Top up with	Soda from siphon
review: This straightforward fizz benefits from the unusual combination of gin and port.
history: Created in 2007 by Julian de Feral at Milk & Honey, London, England.

name: Lekker Lekker
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Bison grass vodka
1⁄2 shot	Hazelnut liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄3 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Most unusual with apple, hazelnut and lemon freshness.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Tom Lawman at Snafu in Aberdeen. Lekker Lekker (pronounced 'Laker Laker') is Afrikaans for 'very nice', which is what Tom's South African friend exclaimed when he tasted this drink.

name: Maison Charles Daiquiri

preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
8 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
4 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters
review: Reminiscent of concentrated Mojito.
history: Pronounced 'May-Sawn Sharl', this recipe is adapted from David A. Embury's 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks.

name: Mañana Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Salmon pink in colour, the Mañana has a subtle and delicate rum laced apricot flavour.
history: Mañana, literally meaning 'tomorrow' in Spanish but more usually used to mean some indefinite time in the future. This recipe is adapted from David A. Embury's 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks.

name: Mayfair Cocktail #2
preparation: MUDDLE cloves in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
2 dried	Clove
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Pimento dram/Allspice liqueur
review: Gin with spicy cloves and hints of apricot and orange.

name: Pablo Alvarez de Cañas Special
garnish: Pineapple cubes, Luxardo Maraschino cherry & orange slice
preparation: Place lemon zest in shaker, add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 fresh	Lemon peel
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄6 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Sherry is most prevalent on the palate, but all the other ingredients, including the lemon zest, also contribute to this subtle, balanced and altogether a most unusual cocktail.
history: Recipe adapted from 1937 Bar Florida (later renamed Floridita) menu, Havana, Cuba.

name: Smoking Stallion

1 sprig	Fresh dill
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄6 shot	Maple syrup
review: Subtly herbal and dry with a hint of whisky smokiness.
history: Created in 2008 by Bart Van Ween at a Dutch World Class.

name: Walnut Alexander
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 3⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Walnut (Nocino) liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1⁄4 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: One to accompany the nutty chocolates from the after-dinner selection box.
history:
Created in 2008 by yours truly at The Cabinet Room, London, England.

See our Alexander cocktail page for more information on the origins of the Alexander cocktail.

name: Whiskey Daisy No.2
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. TOP with a splash of soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Light, fresh and fruity. Perfect for a summer's afternoon.
history: Recipe adapted from Harry Johnson's 1888 Harry Johnson's New & Improved Bartender's Manual which also has an illustration of this cocktail (Plate No. 10) served in a stemmed wine glass filled with crushed ice.

name: John Daly
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Citroen Vodka
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 shot	Cold black tea
review: Essentially an alcoholic iced tea, this is bittersweet and refreshing - perfect for a hot afternoon.
history: Named after the American professional golfer noted for his victory in the 1991 PGA Championship and "colourful" personal life.

name: Serendipity (by Colin Field)

ingredients:
8 fresh	Mint leaves
1 1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2⁄3 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Spirity, minty apple invigorated by a splash of champagne.
history: Our adaptation of Colin Field's signature drink. Collin first served this drink on 31 December 1994 at Bar Hemingway Bar in the Paris Ritz Hotel for Jean-Louis Constanza. Upon tasting it, Jean-Louis exclaimed, "Serendipity!"

name: Ragtime
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Ramazzotti amaro
1 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1⁄12 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: This bittersweet drink benefits from the strength of bonded rye whiskey and was originally made with Rittenhouse.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2009 by Jeremy James Thompson at Raines Law Rooms in New York City, USA.

name: Scottish Breakfast
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄2 shot	Maple syrup
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Scotch sweetened with maple syrup, flavoured with calvados and smoothed with cream.
history: Created in 2009 by Erick Castro at Rickhouse, San Francisco, USA.

name: Sketcher's Pet
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Passion fruit syrup
1⁄2 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: A sweet creamy, fruity dessert style cocktail.
history: Created in January 2010 by Zdenek Kestanek at Quo Vadis, London, England for Petek Sketcher.

name: Sweetie Pie
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄4 shot	Pimento dram/Allspice liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 pinch	Salt (sea salt)
review: Bittersweet and most intriguing.
history: Adapted from a drink created by Lydia Reissmueller at Eletaria, New York City, USA.

name: Corpse Reviver No.Blue
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Blue Curaçao
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Considering it's blue, "I quite like it" was the general consensus when we first tried this infamous cocktail. It tastes great when presented with a Jacob Briars' smile accompanied by his booming voice declaring, "I believe you ordered a blue drink."
history: Created in 2007 by Jacob Briars, Queenstown, New Zealand. Around the time a Facebook group started called "A Jihad on all Blue Drinks." This was Jacob's reaction to it. He "blued' the most popular bartenders' drink" at that time, a Corpse Reviver No.2.

name: Irish Rose
garnish: Lemon zest twist & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water (optional)
review: The gentle bite of Irish whiskey soured with lemon and sweetened with pomegranate syrup. The splash of soda which crowns this drink serves to lighten and add a touch of sparkle.
history: A recipe for a Wild Irish Rose cocktail first appears Geo. R. Washburne and Stanley Bronner's 1911 book Beverages De Luxe, "As served at Auditorium Hotel, Chicago, Illinois and attributed to "Samuel Foote, Manager Liquor Department".

name: Voodoo I Do
preparation: MUDDLE pineapple in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 ring	Pineapple (fresh)
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Pineapple, tequila, orange and apricot with a touch of sour lime all presented in a harmonious Tiki-style concoction.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2011 by Michael Layer at the Chapel Bar in Berlin, Germany.

name: South Ireland Sour
preparation: DRY SHAKE all ingredients (without ice). Add ice, SHAKE again and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Feijoa flavoured vodka
1 shot	Stout beer
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Smells of sticking plasters and uses Feijoa and Guinness. Only a Kiwi could create such a drink. Give it a try, it's not as crazy as it sounds.
history:
Created by Jacob Briars at Cocktail World Cup 2007 as a reaction to an Irish bartender who said 42 Below Feijoa Vodka was "undrinkable", to which Jacob responded "in large parts of the world people thought the same about Guinness." So as a joke Jacob made this surprisingly tasty cocktail.

The name is a geographical in-joke. The Irishman was from Cork, in southern Ireland. Cork is part of Munster, and they were in Queenstown, in New Zealand's South Island, which was once known as New Munster. With their flat vowel pronunciation, Kiwis say Island and Ireland in exactly the same way.

name: Subourbon
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 fresh	Blackberries
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A fruity (blackberry and cranberry) long bourbon laced drink with a flavour reminiscent of a fruity, sweet manhattan.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2010 by David Steenkamp at Jamie Oliver’s Barbecoa, London, England. Originally also with a dash of crème de mûre (blackberry) liqueur so sweeter and fruitier.

name: Bénédictine Conversion
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄3 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Bigallet Thym
3⁄4 shot	Chilled water (reduce if wet ice)
review: Tequila and mezcal based with herbal and liqueur and thyme.

name: Archibald Periscope
preparation: SHAKE first three ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with soda and then carefully FLOAT Rioja wine.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Peachtree peach schnapps
3⁄4 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
3⁄4 shot	Chilled water
1⁄2 shot	Rioja (Crianza) red wine
review: Slightly sweet, long and refreshing. To quote the menu at Albert & Pearl where we discovered this cocktail, "a sight for sore eyes".
history: Adapted (considerably) from a drink discovered in 2009 at Albert & Pearl, Islington, London, England.

name: Milanese Breakfast Martini
preparation: STIR marmalade with gin, bitter liqueur and lemon juice in base of shaker to dissolve the marmalade. SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with sparkling wine.
ingredients:
1 barspoon	Orange marmalade
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄6 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄2 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
review: A fruity but dry aperitif drink served 'up' but with a splash of prosecco sparkle.
history: Adapted from a drink originally named Breakfast in Milan by Dawid Steenkamp at Jamie Oliver's Barbecoa in London, England, and inspired by the Negroni and Salvatore's Breakfast Martini.

name: Bridgetown Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
5⁄12 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
5⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
5⁄12 shot	Grapefruit juice (ruby red)
5⁄12 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Rum-laced sweet and sourness with maraschino liqueur brilliantly balancing grapefruit juice.
history: Unknown.

name: Oyster Bay
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. (Be sure to fine-strain your lemon juice when juicing to help the clarity of this cocktail).
ingredients:
2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Citrus notes and dry vermouth subtly influence Scotch in this refined cocktail.
history: Named after Oyster Bay, Long Island. Famous for being the location of Sagamore Hill, US President Theodore Roosevelt's summer White House.

name: Red Opal Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Blood orange liqueur
1 shot	Blood orange juice
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Orange blossom water / Orange flower water
review: The combination of gin, blood orange liqueur, and blood orange juice results in clementine-like flavours with subtle flavours of orange flower water.
history: Adapted from the 1920s classic Opal recipe.

name: King of Orange
garnish: Orange zest twist to resemble a crown
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with prosecco.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
2⁄3 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄6 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
review: Bittersweet, with the richness of Grand Marnier balancing the bitter liqueur and lemon juice. (I'm guilty of rebalancing this cocktail and adding the prosecco.)
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2012 by Dutch bartender Fjalar Goud in honour of King's Day, celebrated across the Netherlands annually on 27th April.

name: Old Mill
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1 shot	Ginger wine
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Peaty Islay malt and calvados combine in this spicy and warming on-the-rocks cocktail.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2014 by Andrea Buttier, an Italian bartender from Bologna working at The Loft, Clapham Common. Andrea originally used Laphroaig 10 year old for his malt with equal parts calvados, 1 shot Stones ginger wine, ½ shot simple syrup and 2 dashes Peychaud bitters.

name: Red Dog Smash
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Tennessee whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 barspoon	Apricot jam (preserve)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Created in 2007 by Cam Dawson, Brighton, England, for the Jack Daniel's Birthday Competition.
history: Jack Daniel was the owner of two saloons in Lynchburg town square, the most famous being the White Rabbit Saloon due to the limited edition bottling of the same name. This cocktail celebrates the lesser known Red Dog Saloon.

name: Wet cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cachaça
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 pinch	Cinnamon powder (ground)
Top up with	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
review: Superbly refreshing. The pinch of cinnamon adds delicate spice which combines well with cachaça and ginger ale.
history: Created in 2015 by Jorge Balbontin, Barcelona, Spain.

name: La Vendangeuse
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) & grapes on stick
preparation: MUDDLE grapes in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
7 fresh	Green grapes (seedless)
1 1⁄2 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Depending on the ripeness of your grapes, and the sweetness of your palate, you may want to stretch to half a shot sugar syrup. Strike the right balance and you’ll be rewarded with a medley of white grapes, white wine and botanical gin freshness with faint, cleansing zesty citrus.

name: Parle-vous Irish cocktail
garnish: Orange zest twist & freshly grated nutmeg
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. (Consider adding a chunk of ice to the glass.)
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: An after-dinner sipper of a cocktail with cognac and Irish whiskey stirred with rich orange and herbal liqueurs.
history: Created in 2015 by Chris Strong at The Luggage Room in London, England.

name: Carré Nouveau
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄4 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
3 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Reminiscent of a Vieux Carré but with aromatised wine replacing rosso vermouth and gentian replacing aromatic bitters.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in February 2016 by Matthias Lataille in London, England.

name: History & Nobility
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water
review: Cognac stirred with orange and apricot liqueurs along with a dash of orange bitters. The original recipe calls for two dashes but go too heavy with your bitters and this subtle drink will be wrecked. Achieving perfect dilution is also key, hence our adding half a shot chilled water (ice allowing of course).
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Daniel Bovey at Be At One, Bristol, England.

name: Quitting Ordinary
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 1⁄2 shot	Earl Grey tea (cold)
1⁄2 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 barspoon	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Earl Grey tea tannins balance rich crème de cassis in this bittersweet, aperitif cocktail.
history: Created in 2015 by Tom Blundell at Cosy Kettle, London, England.

name: Charentes
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Pineau des Charentes rouge
1⁄3 shot	Mentzendorff Kümmel liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Kummel's caraway flavours heavily influence this unusual cognac-based cocktail with Pineau des Charentes and lemon juice.
history: Created in 2015 by Tiarnan O'Gara at MASH, London, England.

name: Coffee Thyme
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled ice.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
5⁄6 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
1⁄6 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 fresh	Fresh thyme
review: A cognac based Espresso Martini with herbal hints of Fernet Branca and thyme.
history: Created in 2015 by Andrew Cotter at Hawksmoor Air Street, London, England.

name: V.S.M. Flip
garnish: Spray glass with gold chocolate spray & grate dark chocolate over drink.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chocolate sprayed glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
2⁄3 shot	Mozart Chocolate Vodka
1⁄6 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1 fresh	Egg (white & yolk)
review: Creamy and velvety chocolate, coffee and cognac.
history: Created in 2015 by Shaun Spurrier at Harvey Nichols Bar, Birmingham, England.

name: Amsterdamage
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
1 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: A genever-based Wet Martini with an orange influence courtesy of triple sec.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Lee Clarke after he and a few friends visited the Bols Museum in Amsterdam. His recipe, a simple variation on a Vodka Martini with equal parts vodka, dry vermouth and triple sec, became the trip's signature cocktail. Given the Amsterdam connection, we thought it appropriate to try using genever in place of vodka with an added dash of orange bitters.

If being in this book, we're not fame enough, in 2023, the Amsterdamage was made on BBC television's Nigella's Amsterdam Christmas Special.

name: Mercado Roma
preparation:
SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably a chunk of block ice).

Special Ingredient #1: Pineapple Ancho Shrub
Blend equal parts pineapple juice and sugar and leave to rest for 2 hours. Add equal parts white wine vinegar and leave for 24 hours. Then add a teaspoon of chipotle sauce and blend.

Special Ingredient #2: Clove Honey
Add equal parts honey, water and a handful of cloves to a pot and heat at 180˚C for 25 minutes stirring constantly.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
1 barspoon	*Special ingredient #2 (see above)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review:
Created by Roberto Berdecia for Patrón Tequila at London Cocktail Week 2016.

Roberto is a co-founder of La Factoría, in San Juan, Puerto Rico.

name: El Murciélago
preparation: SHAKE first three ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with ginger beer and crushed ice. FLOAT dark rum.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
1⁄3 shot	Bacardi Carta Negra Superior
review:
"For my Legacy cocktail, I was inspired by two classic cocktails: the Mai Tai and the Dark and Stormy. My drink honours the first generation of the family Bacardí: Don Facundo Bacardí Massó and sons (Emilio, Facundo and Jose). The roots of the untamable spirit."

We say: Rum laced ginger, almond and lime.
history: Spanish BACARDÍ LEGACY 2016 winning cocktail by Angel Arruñada, Sol Y Mar Café, Fuengirola.

name: Rumbera
garnish: Rose water mist (50/50 Bacardí Carta Blanca to rose water)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Pomegranate juice
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄6 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: This is a crowd-pleasing cocktail - fruity and just a tad on the sweet side, with pomegranate and rich almond biscotti-like flavours dominating.
history: Irish Bacardí Legacy 2016 winning cocktail winning cocktail by Will Lynch of The Exchequer, Dublin.

name: Amado
garnish: Dash Angostura Bitters drawn through foam
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Rose sugar syrup
2⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review:
"Amado means 'sweetheart;' the inspiration behind my drink is my own romantic love story which began with a sour note like lime, but finished with the sweet fragrance of my dream girl, like rose syrup. Of course, it had some bitter times too which seasoned our life and brought us closer, just like the Angostura in this drink. And Bacardí, which is the soul of my cocktail. If this drink soothes your palate, it's a cocktail; but if it soothes your soul, it's a LEGACY."

We say: A rose flavoured daiquiri - what's not to like? We followed the recipe using Monin rose syrup but the result was too sweet and floral. Then we tried 10ml which was a tad too sour. Bang in the middle hit the spot but then we started playing around with Turkish rose water and sugar syrup before remembering this was somebody else's recipe. Cries out for a Turkish delight as a garnish.
history: Indian BACARDÍ LEGACY 2016 winning cocktail by Yogesh Kumar, Delhi Pavilion, ITC Sheraton, Delhi.

name: Wind-up Bird Chronicle
preparation: POUR rum into glass and swirl to coat. POUR the rum from the glass into shaker and set glass aside. Add other ingredients to shaker, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into rum rinsed glass (no ice in glass).
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
5⁄6 shot	Bacardi Carta Negra Superior
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2 barspoon	Caster/ Superfine/Baker's special sugar (white)
history: Thai Bacardí Legacy 2013 winning cocktail created by Suwincha Singsuwan at The St. Regis Bar in Bangkok, Thailand.

name: Jalisco Mint Julep
garnish: Mint sprigs dusted with icing sugar
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into julep cup half-filled with crushed ice. CHURN (stir) the drink with the crushed ice using a bar spoon. Top up the cup with more crushed ice and CHURN again. Crown the drink with some fresh crushed ice, garnish and serve.
ingredients:
12 fresh	Mint leaves
2 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Añejo tequila
2⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 dash	Bob's Lavender Bitters
review: Given the use of tequila, I initially opted for agave syrup over sugar syrup but I found the caramel notes this added somewhat overwhelmed the mint. Instead, perhaps consider using demerara sugar in place of white cane syrup or a mix of the two. To be honest, I found myself preferring the original whiskey-based Mint Julep when tasted against each other but I'd encourage you to give a tequila-based Mint Julep a try, and if you have a better version then please email me at simon@diffordsguide.com.
history:
Created in February 2017 by yours truly (Simon Difford) at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

For the contentious history of the Julep along with its variants, see our Julep page.

name: Manhattan (Sweet with Bitter Chocolate)
garnish: Square of 80% cacao chocolate balanced on rim
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
6 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: Those with a sweet tooth should not be misled by the word "sweet" in the name of this drink, which refers to the use of sweet vermouth in what is a dry but not bone-dry spirituous cocktail. Bourbon provides the backbone, maraschino a faint cherry fruitiness, while the all-important chocolate bitters add, well, bitter chocolate notes. Oh, and there's a dash of dark chocolate liqueur for decadence sake.
history:
Created by yours truly in April 2017 at the Cabinet Room in London, England.
See: Manhattan cocktail history

name: Banana Caipirinha
garnish: Stirrer (spoon, wooden lolly stick or stick cut from sugar cane)
preparation:
1. Cut lime in half (from pole to pole) and then slice one of the halves into eight 3-4mm thick half-moon shaped segments and drop into the base of a robust rocks glass.

2. Add 3 bar spoons caster sugar (or ½oz/15ml sugar syrup 2:1) and MUDDLE.

3. Add slices of banana and MUDDLE some more.

4. When sure fruit juice is fully extracted and the sugar dissolved, transfer the muddled fruit and sugar into serving glass (preferably a 30cl / 10oz highball glass).

5. POUR cachaça (stored in the freezer) into the rocks glass (used to muddle) and swirl to rinse glass before pouring cachaça into serving glass. STIR to ensure all ingredients are well mixed.

6. Use an Ice Tapper to crack (rather than crush) four to five large ice cubes and drop into serving glass. STIR before topping with more ice and serve with a stirrer (but no straws).
ingredients:
1⁄2 fresh	Lime (fresh) (chopped)
1 barspoon	Caster/ Superfine/Baker's special sugar (white)
1⁄3 fresh	Banana (preferably overripe) (chopped)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
2 shot	Cachaça (from freezer)
review: With an overripe banana this drink is delicious, thick and creamy. A meal in itself.
history: For information on the history and other variations of the Caipirinha, please see our Caipirinha cocktail page.

name: Mariel
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Bacardi 8 year old rum
2⁄3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Coconut water
1⁄3 shot	Honey
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: A pleasing and interesting combination of flavours, but slightly on the sweet side and for some drinkers (us) lacks oomph.
history: A Bacardí Legacy 2017 winning cocktail created by Kentaro Satoh at Bar Day Cocktail in Yokohama, Japan.

name: Tropical Pineapple Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into an ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Giffard Caribbean Pineapple liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
4 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters (optional)
review: Pineapple and rich almond flavours add a tropical touch to this refreshing Daiquiri.
history: Adapted from a recipe promoted by Giffard in June 2016 with the launch of their Caribbean Pineapple liqueur.

name: Soixante-Quinze (Washington Herald 1915 recipe)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Applejack brandy bottled-in-bond (50% alc./vol)
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water
review: This 1915 recipe, originally of equal parts gin, applejack and grenadine (1/3 of each to 1/6 lemon juice) makes this Soixante-Quinze (Seventy-Five) a tad on the sweet side (certainly sweet if you are using a proprietary or housemade 2:1 grenadine). However, who knows what brix the original grenadine/pomegranate syrup was, so we've eased back the grenadine to bring modern-day ingredients more into kilter. The resulting drink (which benefits from a splash of water to aid dilution) remains more a fruity, spirituous after-dinner cocktail rather than an aperitif.
history:
Adapted from a 1915 recipe published in The Washington Herald.
See: French 75 history.

name: Pineapple Sour
garnish: Pineapple wedge or dehydrated pineapple slice
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 1⁄3 shot	Giffard Caribbean Pineapple liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Vanille de Madagascar
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Bourbon’s strength and richness of flavour, with tropical pineapple, freshened by citrus.
history: Created in 2017 by Theodoros Spiropoulos, Giffard’s Brand Ambassador in Greece.

name: The Healer
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass (preferably a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄2 shot	Amaro Nonino Quintessentia
1⁄4 shot	Licor 43 Original liqueur
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Bittersweet with cleansing citrus sourness. Vanilla and bourbon notes combine well with gentian. Apéritif in style.
history: Created in 2017 by Juan Meyer, Norwalk, USA, who said of this drink, "One of my regulars came in and said he wants a hot toddy, but he wants it not hot, so I reached for the Suze and this is what I made."

name: Am I Blue?
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with pale ale and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Birch spirit/birch eau-de-vie
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 2⁄3 shot	India pale ale (IPA) beer
review: Long and refreshing, based on India pale ale and birch spirit with grapefruit freshness.
history: Created in 2017 by Thom Solberg at Black Rock in London, England.

name: Suzy & Peat
preparation: MUDDLE cucumber in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 slice	Cucumber (fresh)
1 2⁄3 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄6 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Tarragon sugar syrup (2:1)
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Cucumber vegetal freshness, bittersweet gentian liqueur and peated scotch characterise this aperitivo sour.
history:
Created in 2017 by James Cunningham at Hawksmoor (Seven Dials), London, England. James says, "My head bartender told me that, much to her surprise, super pungent ingredients like Suze and peated scotch where actually great bed fellows. And so began the romance of Suze and peat.

When we put the drink up on the black board at Hawksmoor Seven Dials it simply read: “Suze & Peat by Jim Cunningham”, this made it sound like a) I authored a children’s book and b) that it was definitely one with a happy ending. Suze and peat are a baller couple. The resultant drink is an amazing strange mix of bitter and fresh palate cleansing flavours, the cucumber, tarragon and lime really help to accent Suze's green, grassier notes but don't remove anything from that distinctive bitter kick."

name: Golden Spritz
preparation: STIR first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with cava and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Fino sherry
3⁄4 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄3 shot	Ginger syrup
1 1⁄2 shot	Cava sparkling wine
review: Gin-based with rich ginger balanced by dry sherry, lengthened by apple and invigorated with fizz.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created by Jeff Carmichael at Capa Four Seasons Orlando, USA.
Spritz history

name: Angela Luce
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Strega liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄3 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Fruity and herbal – a refreshingly zingy nightcap.
history: Adapted from a recipe by Silvia Picinato. Named after the eponymous Italian film actress and singer.

name: Witches' Smile
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Strega liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1 1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: This tall vodka-laced drink is lightly herbal, fruity and refreshing.

name: White Lady (no added sugar* & low-calorie)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Agave Sec liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Sugar-free sweetener
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review:
* BEWARE: Although free of cane sugar and beet sugar, this cocktail contains small amounts of fructose sugars from the agave nectar used in the Agave Sec orange liqueur.

Lemon and orange meringue with light gin botanical notes.
history:
Adapted from the classic serve by yours truly (Simon Difford) in January 2019.

For more recipes, its origins and the history behind the White Lady cocktail, see our White Lady cocktail page.

name: Morado
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄6 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄12 shot	Pale cream sherry (medium/sweet)
5⁄12 shot	Giffard Crème de Mûre liqueur
1⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Gin-laced rich PX raisiny sherry, blackberry and coffee combine in this bite-sized after-dinner cocktail.
history: Adapted from a 2019 recipe by Andre Tarantino. His original spec: 35ml Gin Hendriks Orbium, 15ml Lustau East India Sherry, 15ml Créme de Mûre Sauvage Chartreuse, 5ml Borghetti Coffee Liqueur and 2 dashes Peychaud bitters.

name: Banana Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
5⁄12 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
5⁄12 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
5⁄12 shot	Banana tea
2 dash	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: A delicately banana flavoured and sweetened very 'wet' vodkatini.
history: Created summer 2019 by yours truly at the Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: Bywater
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass (optionally over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
3⁄4 shot	Amer Picon
1⁄2 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄6 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: This spirit-forward, herbal and bitter-sweet cocktail was originally served without ice but dilution tames its fire to appeal to a wider audience as an after-dinner digestif.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2008 by Chris Hannah at Arnaud's French 75 Bar, New Orleans, USA.

Original recipe: Stir all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled Nick & Nora glass:
- 52.5ml (1¾oz) Aged rum
- 22.5ml (¾oz) Averna amaro
- 15ml (½oz) Green Chartreuse
- 7.5ml (¼oz) Velvet Falernum
- 2 dashes Regans' orange bitters
- 2 dashes Peychaud's bitters

name: Cuban Sarsaparilla
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with rootbeer.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
8 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
2 1⁄2 shot	Root beer
review: Root beer's vanilla, anise or liquorice notes combine with coffee and cacao rum with underlying bitter and citrus.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Andrew Augustine Lugiman, Barong Bar; Fairmont, Jakarta.

name: Margaret Rose
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: Depending on your lemon juice, this Sidecar-like Daisy may benefit from an additional 2.5ml sugar syrup to balance.
history:
Adapted from a recipe in William James "Billy" Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Cocktail Book where it is credited to "J. W. Fish".
(Our thanks to Jason Clapham of Oxford, England for bringing this recipe to our attention.)

name: Arsenic & Old Lace
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄12 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄12 shot	Crème de violette liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water
review: This Martini-style cocktail needs to be served well stirred in an ice-cold glass. Originally a shaken drink, it benefits from dilution, hence a splash of chilled water in our rendition. Consider adding more water or indeed shaking.
history:
