Named after the eponymous 1939 play by Joseph Kesselring which opened on Broadway in January 1941. The story went on to be made into the 1944 film starring Cary Grant.

This cocktail first appeared in Crosby Gaige's 1941 Cocktail Guide and Ladies' Companion with the following recipe:
"¼ part Absinthe
¾ part Dry gin
3 dashes Cinzano Dry Vermouth
3 dashes Crème de Violette
Shake well with ice and strain into cocktail glass"

name: Tears of Joy
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄3 shot	Cinnamon syrup
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A spicy orange Daquiri with coffee and chocolate. Like most Daiquiris, this cocktail benefits from dilution so, depending on your ice, consider adding a splash of chilled water.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Tess Posthumus at Flying Dutchmen in Amsterdam, The Netherlands.

name: French 40
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients and strain into ice-filled glass whilst also pouring sparkling wine.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 1⁄2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review:
Faintly bittersweet and refreshingly citrusy.
A riff on the classic French 75 named for the 40 botanicals that flavour Amaro Montenegro.

name: Black Fashioned
preparation:
1. Combine all ingredients in a frozen tumbler glass and stir to integrate ground coffee. (Vasilis Kyritsis specifies Colombia coffee as this "gives more acid notes with floral and fruit aftertaste). If you don't have scales to hand then 10 gram of ground coffee has a volume of approx. 30ml in an Easy Jigger
2. Moisten filter paper in a Hario V60 dripper or similar and place over chilled cup. Pour combined ingredients into filter.
3. Patiently wait a couple of minutes while the cocktail drips through the paper and then enjoy.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum (from freezer)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix) (chilled)
10 gram	Ground coffee
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Cold-brew meets cocktail in this deliciously different cocktail. A proper breakfast time pick-me-up.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Vasilis Kyritsis at The Clumsies in Athens, Greece.

name: You're Not My Real Trinidad
garnish: Dust with freshly grated nutmeg & garnish with a mint sprigs bouquet
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄2 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
1 1⁄2 shot	Cream of coconut (e.g. Coco Lopez, Re'al etc.)
2 shot	Pineapple juice
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Bittersweet, spicy and fruity – Reggae Tiki in style, if indeed there is such a cocktail style?
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Kevin Beary at Three Dots and a Dash in Chicago, USA.

name: H.S.L. Special
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄6 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Crème de Mûre liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: A delicately fruity bittersweet sweet 'n' sour aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a cocktail created by and named after Hayden Scott Lambert at his bar, Bramble and Hugo Special this cocktail featured on the opening menu of Above Board back in November 2016.

name: Fall Enzoni
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & skewered red grapes
preparation: MUDDLE grapes in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
5 fresh	Red grapes (seedless)
1 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A riff with rye whiskey punch on the very similar gin-based original Enzoni.
history: This riff on Vincenzo Ericco's original Enzoni is believed to have been created, circa 2012-13 by Richard Boccato for his Dutch Kills bar in Long Island, New York City, USA.

name: Nightcap
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with tonic water.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 2⁄3 shot	Cold brew coffee
1⁄2 shot	Maple syrup
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: Depending on your coffee, the combination with rum, maple and tonic give this tall refreshing Nightcap a chocolaty note.
history: Adapted from a cocktail created in 2019 by Daniel Moik, head bartender at Yours Truly in Hamilton, Bermuda.

name: Tennessee Liplock
preparation: MUDDLE strawberries in base of stirring glass. Add next 3 ingredients, STIR with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with a splash of soda if so desired.
ingredients:
2 fresh	Strawberries (hulled, small & ripe)
2 shot	Tennessee whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Maple syrup
1⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Unusually a fresh muddled fruit cocktail that's stirred rather than shaken. This Valentine's Day cocktail is suitably pink and is garnished with a heart-shaped strawberry. (Apologies for the strawberry in our photo but early Feb is not the best time for strawberries in the UK.)
history: Adapted from a recipe created in January 2021 by Brody Warner, a bartender at Pecker's Bar in Nashville, USA and also the Daddy Rack International Brand Ambassador.

name: Gold Florin
garnish: Lemon spiral or mint sprigs bouquet pegged to rim
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄12 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄12 shot	Strega liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Clément Sirop de Canne
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Spirituous and herbal.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England, this cocktail is based on the Rum Daisy in the 1935 La Florida Bar Book, which omits the Strega. Jason's original recipe is as above but with 60ml rum.

name: Bitter Mai Tai
garnish: Lime slice wheel & mints sprigs bouquet
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into a glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
2⁄3 shot	100% pot still rum (40-45% alc./vol.)
1⁄3 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
review: Just as it says on the tin! Recognisably a Mai Tai and bittersweet.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Jeremy Oertel at Donna Bar in Brooklyn, New York City.

name: Personality a la Roy
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
3⁄4 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water
review: Well, Roy has a personality beyond its stature, so much so that Roy takes dilution well, hence my addition of an optional splash of chilled water.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book. The Savoy recipe calls for Hercules, a sadly long since defunct product that vintage newspaper advertisements for the brand describe as being a "Maté-Wine Apéritif" with an "alcohol strength over 25°." Hence, I've used another wine-based aperitif.

name: Gilroy
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Cherry fruit leads this gin-laced dry and citrussy aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Automobile
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Sage gin
1 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Spirit-forward with gin and Scotch whisky lightly sweetened, softened and aromatised with vermouth.
history:
The makers of Engine Gin discovered the Automobile Cocktail in Frank Meier's 1934 book, The Artistry of Mixing Drinks.
They make Meier's with an absinthe-like Ibiza liquor, saying, "An Automobile Cocktail, a glass of gasoline with a nut in it". So wrote the quirky promotional postcard of Automobile Cocktail, a close relative of Rob Roy. There are several version of it. We have taken the one contained of the Ritz in Paris. To the drink reported by Meier we have made a toe-in, rebalancing it and adding a typical Ibiza liquor which we also soaked our bolt with. At this point the car has become a convertible spider ready to take us along the coasts of Isla Bianca.

name: Frank Lloyd Wright
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄3 shot	Pear liqueur (Poire William)
1⁄6 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄6 shot	Walnut (Nocino) liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: An Old Fashioned-style cocktail with pear and walnut liqueurs along with a touch of peated malt whisky.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2009 by Ian Scalzo at Bourbon & Branch bar in San Francisco, USA. Eponymously named after the noted American architect who designed more than 1,000 structures over his 70-year career. Wright influenced other architects throughout the world who also sought to design in harmony with humanity and the environment, a philosophy he termed "organic architecture". His most famous work, Fallingwater in Pennsylvania was built in 1935, partly over a waterfall, as a weekend retreat house for Liliane and Edgar J. Kaufmann, the owner of Pittsburgh's Kaufmann's Department Store. The property is now a National Historic Landmark.

name: Bottoms Up
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄6 shot	Double cream / heavy cream
1 fresh	Egg yolk
review: A brandy-laced meal with zesty orange cutting through the heaviness of cream.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Ted Saucier's 1951 Bottom's Up, a cocktail book "with illustrations by Twelve of America's Most Distinguished Artists", one of which was Albert "Al" Dorne, who was "one of the best and highest paid in the field of advertising illustration" of his day. It seems he was also a talented mixologist as the book credits this cocktail to Al Dorne.

name: Copenhagen Cocktail 1939
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Rich cherry fortified with gin and given herbal depth by vermouth and aromatic bitters.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Axel Sørensen's black, bar notebook "Lommebogen" ISBN 978-87-995886-0-2. Axel Sørensen, was a bartender at Café de la Reine in Copenhagen during the late 1930s and his granddaughter inherited his pocketbook containing his cocktail recipes and other notes. Henrik Steen Petersen, from the former "Moltkes Bar" in Copenhagen, borrowed this notebook, photographed it and has since published the notebook to make available to all.

name: Martinique
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Rhum J.M. Terroir Volcanique
1⁄6 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: The Hotel Martinique's original signature cocktail was based on Jamaican rum but, given the name, Martinique agricole rum seemed more appropriate. Other than this swap I've respected the line-up of ingredients and arrived at proportions by trial and error.
history: My interpretation of the 1930s signature cocktail from New York City's Hotel Martinique.

name: Harrison Ginsberg's Martinez
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: An aged vermouth-forward, so heavy, New York riff on a Martinez.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2022 by Harrison Ginsberg, Bar Director at Crown Shy restaurant in New York City, USA.

name: Yolanda
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄12 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Rich vermouth-led underpinned by brandy and gin with grenadine adding fruitiness while a mere dash of absinthe adds layers of complexity.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Pink Passion Fruit Daiquiri
garnish: Lime juice and salt rim & float half fresh passion fruit boat
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Passoã passion fruit liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
4 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters
review: Delicately fruity, indeed this is a restrained cocktail all-round, Daiquiri first and passion fruit second.
history: This rendition of a Passion Fruit Daiquiri by yours truly in May 2023.

name: Créme Fresh
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Monkey Shoulder Fresh Monkey
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
review: Will appeal to Negroni drinkers. A full-flavoured, bittersweet aperitivo/digestivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Scott Duncan Simpson of Hoot the Redeemer in Edinburgh, Scotland. Originally made with Cocchi Storico Vermouth di Torino rosso vermouth.

name: African Flower
preparation: STIR (regal stir) all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄6 shot	Amaro CioCiaro
1⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1 swath	Orange peel
review: Bourbon-forward and lightly bittersweet with zesty citrus freshness.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2008 by Becky McFalls at Little Branch in New York City, USA.

name: Honey Deuce
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into glass. TOP with soda and then fill glass with ice. Lastly, add black raspberry liqueur which should bleed through the cocktail as it sinks.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
review: It's the combination of name, tennis tournament and garnish which makes this otherwise very ordinary Vodka Collins sweetened with berry liqueur special.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2016 by Nick Mautone, a highly experienced bartender then working as Grey Goose brand ambassador, which had just become vodka sponsor of the U.S. Open tennis tournament. One evening, soon after being tasked with creating the event's official cocktail, he noticed that honeydew melon balls resembled tiny tennis balls, and with a suitable garnish found, the tall fruity cocktail soon followed. Served in collectable plastic cups, in 2023, some 450,000 Honey Deuce cocktails were made at the U.S. Open, garnished with 1.3 million melon balls.

name: Sloe & Sexy
garnish: 5 drops aromatic bitters (preferably Sexy Bitters) dropped onto surface of cocktail
preparation: DRY SHAKE first 4 ingredients (without ice) Add ice, SHAKE again and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with sparkling wine.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1⁄4 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
1 2⁄3 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: I added egg white to the original recipe to ensure a foamy head to receive and hold the all-important bitters.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Aljosha Moretti at Le Lion Bar de Paris in Hamburg, Germany where it remains one of the bestselling cocktails. Originally based on Rutte Sloe Gin.

Joerg Meyer, the man behind Le Lion Bar de Paris gave us some background information; "A German bartender, Klaus Stephan Rainer from Goldene Bar in Munich, created a "aromatic style" Cocktail Bitter, called Sexy Bitters. I asked Team Le Lion in 2019 to create drinks, featuring this Cocktail Bitters, cause we liked to support our local "underground".

Aljosha Moretti came up with the Sloe & Sexy- a sloe gin and champagne drink featuring Sexy Bitters. And I knew from the second that this creation will become a banger. Champagne cocktail, cool name, accessible and charming taste. So we put it on the menu. If you do not have Sexy Bitters at hand (quite German product) - Change to and Aromatic Bitters. Sey Bitters has a hint of Cinnamon and Tonka Bean shining true."

name: Sweet Lady No. 1
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄3 shot	Peach brandy
1⁄3 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
4 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: Scotch whisky sits brilliantly with chocolate, in this cocktail with peach fruitiness. Despite the liqueurs in this cocktail, it's not a sweetie as it's dried by whisky.

name: Taxi
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄24 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Originally equal parts dry gin and dry vermouth with a splash more absinthe, this super refreshing cocktail is better with the absinthe being forced to shout from backstage and a little extra sweetness provided by splitting the vermouths between equal parts dry and bianco. I've tried using old tom gin and also lemon in place of lime juice but I prefer dry gin and lime juice with lemon reserved for the fragrant garnish.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Jacques Straub's 1913 Straub's Manual of Mixed Drinks.

name: Margariticus
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 shot	Italicus liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Agave syrup
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Naturally, this cocktail also works well with blanco tequila, but as long as your reposado is not overly influenced by vanilla notes, then a good reposado can help round this bergamot Margarita.

name: Cosmic Alaska
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄4 shot	Green melon liqueur
review: Lurid lime green, spirit-forward with herbal melon notes.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Matt Chavez at Coqodaqin in New York City, USA.

name: Camberwell Carrot
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with pink grapefruit soda.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
2 shot	Thomas Henry Pink Grapefruit soda
review: Looks and tastes a little carrot-like.
history:
Created by yours truly and inspired by the Camberwell Carrot in the 1987 film Withnail and I.
Withnail: "Who says it's a Camberwell Carrot?"
Danny: I do. I invented it in Camberwell, and it looks like a carrot."
[Camberwell is a district in South London, England.]

name: Frozen Sake Margarita
preparation: DRY BLEND (without ice) first 4 ingredients on slow setting and gradually add Xanthan gum while continuing to blend. Add half a 2/3 of a 7oz scoop of crushed ice and blend again. Pour into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Akashi-Tai Daiginjo Genshu sake
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
1⁄4 barspoon	Xanthan gum (E415) (optional)
review: Is a "Margarita" without an agave spirit actually a Margarita is worthy of debate, but putting that question aside, this cocktail demonstrates the versatility of sake in cocktails.
history: Adapted from a signature cocktail served at the China Rose Chinese restaurant in Rhinecliff, USA, until it closed circa 2016. Fellow Discerning Drinker Niki La was a patron of the restaurant and fan of this cocktail and shared the recipe with us in 2023, describing it as "the best sake drink I've ever had."

name: Ace
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) to emulsify and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Pleasant, creamy, sweetened gin.

name: Alexander
preparation: DRY SHAKE all ingredients (without ice) to emulsify. SHAKE again with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
3⁄4 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: This gin-laced creamy Alexander has sadly slipped from popularity, partly knocked by its successors, particularly the Brandy Alexander.
history:
The Alexander, comprising gin, crème de cacao and cream, is thought to have originated early in the 20th century, certainly before 1915, evidenced by an equal parts recipe appearing in Hugo Ensslin's 1916 Recipes for Mixed Drinks.

Historian, Barry Popik's website lists several plausible origins for this drink. The first is a cutting from page 11 of the news section of the 3rd October 1915 Philadelphia Inquirer. "The head bartender has even gone so far as to invent an Alexander cocktail, which he is reserving to be served during the World Series." This referred to The Racquet Club and the 1915 World Series, won by Boston beating Philadelphia. The bartender created the drink honouring Philadelphia pitcher Grover Cleveland Alexander (1887-1950).

Alternatively, a 21st March 1929 newspaper column by New York columnist Walter Winchell links the origin of the Alexander cocktail to Troy Alexander, a bartender at a New York pre-Prohibition lobster restaurant called Rector's. It claims that Troy created his eponymously named cocktail for a dinner celebrating a successful advertising campaign.

The advertisement depicted Phoebe Snow, a fictitious railway traveller, wearing a snow-white dress featured in an advertising campaign for the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad (DL&W) to promote the company's use of clean-burning anthracite to fuel its locomotives.

Coal-fuelled trains frequently covered travellers with black soot, but DL&W owned vast anthracite mines in Pennsylvania, so they could legitimately claim that their passengers would arrive clean after a long journey. The first advertisement depicted an image of Phoebe Snow, supposedly a young New York socialite who frequently travelled to Buffalo, New York, wearing a white dress and featured a short poem:

Says Phoebe Snow
about to go
upon a trip to Buffalo
"My gown stays white
from morn till night
Upon the Road of Anthracite"

The popular advertisements first appeared at the turn of the 20th century and ran for nearly 70 years. Phoebe became one of America's most recognized advertising mascots. The Alexander became a Prohibition favourite as the cream and nutmeg garnish helped disguise the rough taste of homemade 'bathtub' gin.

name: Ambrosia Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
5⁄6 shot	Licor 43 Original liqueur
5⁄12 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1 2⁄3 shot	Warninks Advocaat liqueur
review: Easy-drinking but complex with a herbal edge.
history: Created by yours truly and named after the Greek for "elixir of life, the food of the Gods." However, here in the UK, "Ambrosia" is a brand of custard, so advocaat seemed an appropriate ingredient. And if there is a God, he/she/it surely drinks Chartreuse.

name: Apple & Melon Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Sour apple liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Green melon liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: The once ubiquitous Green Apple Martini with extra colour and flavour thanks to a dash of melon liqueur.

name: Apple Mac
garnish: Float thin apple slice (fresh or hydrated)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Ginger wine
6 drop	Bob's Ginger Bitters
review: Scotch, ginger and apple are a threesome that play well together.
history: A 2004 riff on the classic Whisky Mac created by yours truly in London, England.

name: Apple Pie Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bison grass vodka
1⁄2 shot	Goldwasser cinnamon schnapps liqueur
2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
review: There's a good hit of cinnamon in this apple pie.
history: Created in 2000 by Alexia Pau Barrera at Sand Bar, Clapham, England.

name: Atomic Cocktail
preparation: STIR first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. TOP with sparkling wine.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄6 shot	Amontillado sherry
1 1⁄4 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Cognac supercharged with vodka, rounded with sherry and invigorated by champagne. Handle with care.
history: Created in the early 1950s in Las Vegas, USA, then known as the "Atomic City" due to its proximity to the Nevada Test Site (NTS), just 65 miles north of the city. Between 1951 and 1992, NTS was America's leading nuclear weapons test site, with mushroom clouds easily seen up to 100 miles away, leading to increased tourism to Las Vegas. Throughout the 1950s into the early 1960s, the Las Vegas Chamber of Commerce capitalized on the nuclear tests and the spectacle of nuclear clouds and flashes. Casinos hosted "dawn parties" and created atomic-themed cocktails, including this one.

name: Awol
preparation: LAYER in chilled glass by carefully pouring ingredients in the following order. Then FLAME drink and allow to burn for no more than ten seconds before extinguishing flame and consuming. Take extreme care and beware of hot glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Green melon liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	White overproof rum
review: A strong but surprisingly palatable shot.
history: Created in 1993 by Lane Zellman at Louis XVI Restaurant, St. Louis Hotel, New Orleans, USA.

name: Bamboo (with triple sec)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: For sophisticated dry palates - a touch of triple sec takes the dry edge off of fino sherry and dry vermouth.
history: Bamboo Cocktail history

name: Beach Blonde
preparation: BLEND ingredients with 6oz scoop of crushed ice. Pour into glass and serve with straws.
ingredients:
1⁄2 fresh	Banana (preferably overripe)
2 shot	Warninks Advocaat liqueur
2⁄3 shot	White overproof rum
2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Fruity holiday drinking with a satisfying creamy mouthfeel. (This drink is creamy in texture due to egg rather than dairy cream.)
history: Created in 2002 by Alex Kammerling, London, England.

name: Beija Flor Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cachaça
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
2⁄3 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Sharp and quite dry but with a banana twang. Depending on your taste and banana liqueur, you may want to add a splash more liqueur or even sugar syrup.

name: The Big Easy
preparation: SHAKE first three ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with ginger ale.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 3⁄4 shot	Southern USA-style liqueur 40% (e.g. Southern Comfort)
2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
review: Fruity and refreshing with a hint of spice.

name: Black Bison Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Apple Schnapps liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: A fragrant cocktail with a dry finish. As the name suggests, also works well with Zubrowka Bison vodka in place of gin.
history: Adapted from a drink discovered in 2001 at Oxo Tower Bar, London, England.

name: Blinker
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
4 drop	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
review: Back in the 1940s, in his The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks, David Embury said of this drink, "One of a few cocktails using grapefruit juice. Not particularly good but not too bad."
history: First published in Patrick Gavin Duffy's 1934 The Official Mixer's Manual.

name: Blue Velvet Margarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
5⁄12 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
5⁄12 shot	De Kuyper Blue Curaçao
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: May look lurid but is a surprisingly tasty Margarita.
history: Discovered in 2005 at Velvet Margarita Cantina, Los Angeles, USA.

name: Blueberry Daiquiri
preparation: MUDDLE blueberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
20 fresh	Blueberries (fresh)
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Blueberry/Bilberry liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Blueberry juice and liqueur lengthens and sweetens an otherwise classic Daiquiri.
history: Created in 2002 by yours truly in London, England.

name: Bourbon Blush
preparation: MUDDLE strawberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3 fresh	Strawberries (hulled, small & ripe)
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Crème de Framboise
1⁄4 shot	Maple syrup
review: Fresh strawberry, raspberry liqueur and maple syrup combine harmoniously with bourbon.
history: Created in 2003 by Simon King at MJU at Millennium Hotel, London, England.

name: Bourbon Cookie
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1⁄2 shot	Passion fruit syrup
1⁄2 shot	Butterscotch liqueur
review: Looks tame but packs a flavoursome punch.
history: Created in 2002 by Andres Masso, London, England.

name: Brandy Buck
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with ginger ale.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄4 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
review: Lemon juice adds balance to the sweet ginger ale. Brsandy provides the backbone.

name: Butterscotch Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
3⁄4 shot	Butterscotch liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Slightly sweet and very suckable.
history: This child of the 1990s was originally called a Butchscotch Martini.

name: Champagne Cup
preparation: STIR first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne and gently stir.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Syrup from Luxardo Maraschino Cherries
Top up with	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Sweet maraschino helps balance this dry drink.

name: Cherry Mash Sour
garnish: Lemon zest twist & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Tennessee whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: The rich flavour of Tennessee whiskey soured with lemon and sweetened with cherry liqueur.
history: Created by Dale DeGroff when Beverage Manager at the Rainbow Room Promenade Bar, New York City, USA.

name: China Blue Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Kwai Feh lychee liqueur
1 shot	De Kuyper Blue Curaçao
2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: This simple turquoise cocktail tastes more adult and interesting than its colour might suggest.
history: An almost inevitable short adaptation of the original long drink.

name: Chinese Cosmopolitan
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Krupnik spiced honey liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Kwai Feh lychee liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
review: Oriental in name and style - perhaps a tad sweeter than your standard Cosmo.
history:
Discovered in 2003 at Raoul's Bar, Oxford, England.

For more recipes, origins and history behind the Cosmopolitan cocktail, see our Cosmopolitan page.

name: Chocolate Vodkatini
garnish: Sugar syrup and chocolate powder rim
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
4 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: Vodka and chocolate made more interesting with a hint of vermouth.
history: Martini cocktail history and its evolution

name: Claridge Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE or STIR all ingredients with ice & fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
review: Gin for strength, vermouth for dryness and liqueur to sweeten - an interesting combination.
history: This cocktail is first published in Harry McElhone's 1922 book Harry's ABC of Mixing Cocktails where the recipe is credited to "Leon, Bartender, Claridge's Hotel, Champs-Elysées, Paris." The recipe is repeated in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Coconut Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice & fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Coconut rum liqueur (35-40% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Coconut sugar syrup
review: Classic Daiquiri flavour with a pleasing tropical touch.

name: Colorado Bulldog
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with cola.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
3⁄4 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1 shot	Cola (e.g. Coca Cola or Pepsi Cola)
review: This dog's bite is hidden by cream.

name: Corpse Reviver No.1 (Savoy recipe)
preparation: STIR ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Dry and potent. A 'pick-me-up' hangover cure - or possibly put-you-right-back-down-again!
history: Generally credited to Frank Meier, bar manager at the Ritz Bar in Paris during the 1920s and 30s, although he makes no claim to the drink in his 1936 The Artistry of Mixing Drinks. This recipe is adapted from Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Creamy Creamsicle
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Disaronno amaretto
2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Oranje Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: Ultra smooth and creamy. Dessert, anyone?

name: Crème de Café
preparation: SHAKE ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
3⁄4 shot	Sambuca
1 2⁄3 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: Coffee predominates over the creaminess with hints of aniseed and rum.

name: Curdish Cocktail
preparation: STIR lemon curd with gin in base of shaker until curd dissolves. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2 barspoon	Lemon curd
1⁄2 shot	Sour apple liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Beautifully balanced with the tang of lemon curd.
history: Created in 2001 by Tadgh Ryan at West Street, London, England.

name: Apple Manhattan #2
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Apple Schnapps liqueur
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: Exactly as billed, a Manhattan with a hint of apple.
history:
Created in Sweden by Asa Nevestveit and Robert Sorman at Grill in Stockholm, Sweden.
Manhattan cocktail history

name: Asylum Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Aniseed (anise) liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water
review: Seabrook said of this drink, "look like rosy dawn, taste like the milk of Paradise, and make you plenty crazy." He must have been a Pernod lover.
history: Created by William Seabrook, famous for his account of eating human flesh, and first published in Sterling North and Carl Kroch's 1935 So Red the Nose or Breath in the Afternoon.

name: Bermuda Cocktail
garnish: Orange zest twist &/or peach wedge on rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Peachtree peach schnapps
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: Gin with a sweetening touch of peach, orange and pomegranate.
history: Adapted from Victor Bergeron's Trader Vic's Bartender's Guide (1972 revised edition).

name: Bermuda Rose
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Delicate, floral, and aromatic, it has a hint of sweetness but not to offend. Despite the lack of juice in this recipe, don't be tempted to stir rather than shake; this is classically a shaken cocktail, and it's all the better for it. At its best, drink whilst still cloudy from shaking.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Victor Bergeron's 1972 Trader Vic's Bartender's Guide (Revised Edition).

name: Blackthorn No. 4
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1⁄2 shot	Kirschwasser (cherry) eau-de-vie
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: This drink benefits from a long, chilling and diluting stir. The result is Martini in style, fruity yet dry.
history: This, one of the numerous versions of the Blackthorn cocktail, first appears in the 1930 Swallows edition of William "Cocktail Bill" Boothby's World Drinks and How To Prepare Them.

name: Boulevard
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A Manhattan-style cocktail dried by dry vermouth and enriched by cognac-orange liqueur.
history: A classic of unknown origins.

name: Californian Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A medium dry, fragrant orange Martini

name: Club Cocktail (Craddock's recipe)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice & strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: A sweet Martini with a dash of Yellow Chartreuse.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Commodore No. 2
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Bourbon whiskey
5⁄6 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: Lemon juice balances this bourbon and crème de cacco-based red-coloured cocktail that is perhaps best served as an after-dinner cocktail.
history:
The second of two Commodore cocktails in Albert S. Crockett's 1931 Old Waldorf Bar Days, both served frappé. Crockett's Commodore No.1 is rum-based and without crème de cacao liqueur. He stipulates the No.2 recipe as:
"One-third Lemon juice
One-third Bourbon Whiskey
One-third Crème de Cacao
Dash Grenadine Syrup
Frappé in champagne glass"

name: The Currier
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Mentzendorff Kümmel liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Lime cordial (sweetened lime juice)
review: A wonderfully cleansing after-dinner cocktail with bourbon and lime plus hints of caraway and fennel courtesy of Kümmel.
history: Recipe created in July 2006 by Murray Stenson at ZigZag Café, Seattle, USA.

name: Cyder Press
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 shot	Medium dry apple cider
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review: Fresh, fermented and distilled apple juice with a hint of elderflower.
history: Created in 2006 by yours truly (Simon Difford), London, England.

name: Dempsey
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄24 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Depending on your grenadine, this cocktail ranges from blush pink to barely coloured and the flavour will also vary. The colour is immaterial, but nail the balance, with absinthe tamed by grenadine but still assertive, and you've a delightful, spirituous aperitif or late-night sharpener.
history:
Recipe adapted from Robert Vermeire's 1922 Cocktails How to Mix Them. The Dempsey also appears in Harry MacElhone's's Harry's ABC of Mixing Cocktails published the same year and is repeated in his 1923 Harry of Ciro's ABC Of Mixing Cocktails. Both MacElhone's books attribute this cocktail's creation to "Fred. Martin, Casino, Deaville, 1922" while Vermeire says "this drink was introduced at Deauville, 1921." Built in 1912, Casino Barrière de Deauville is an elegant palace of slot machines, crystal chandeliers and marble in Normandy, France.

Vermeire, and indeed the drink's name, reference a boxing match dubbed the "Fight of the Century", which saw Jack Dempsey (world heavyweight champion) knockout Georges Carpentier (world light-heavyweight champion) in the fourth round. The bout took place on 2nd July 1921 at Boyle's Thirty Acres in Jersey City, USA, and was the first boxing fight to produce $1,000,000 dollars in revenue.

name: Devil's Manhattan

ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Southern USA-style liqueur 40% (e.g. Southern Comfort)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: A sweet Manhattan with a hint of the south.
history: Our Manhattan cocktail page features a detailed history and common variants.

name: Diplomat
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & skewered Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth

1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura

history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book. The Diplomat also notably appears in Patrick Gavin Duffy's 1934 The Official Mixer's Manual.

name: Earl Grey Fizz

ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Earl Grey tea (cold)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
Top up with	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Looks like a glass of champagne but has a well-judged little extra something.
history: Created in 2002 by Henry Besant at Lonsdale House, London, England.

name: Eastern Promise
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:

1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur

history: Adapted from a drink discovered in 2004 at Oxo Tower Bar, London, England.

name: Embassy Royal

1⁄2 shot	Drambuie liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)

name: FBI

ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Irish cream liqueur
1 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
3 scoop	Vanilla ice cream
review: Yummy alcoholic milkshake with coffee and whiskey cream.

name: Finnberry Martini

ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Lapponia Lakka Cloudberry
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
review: This berry-influenced 'Martini' can be varied by using other berry liqueurs in the Finnish Lapponia berry range - or try two with 7.5ml (¼oz) of each.
history: Created by yours truly after a trip to Finland in 2002.

name: The Flirt
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)

history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2002 by Dick Bradsell at Lonsdale House in Notting Hill, London, England.

name: Flutter
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
5⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1 1⁄6 shot	Pineapple juice
4 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters (optional)
review: Three ingredients combine harmoniously and, depending on your coffee liqueur, perhaps just the merest tad on the sweet side.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2003 by Tony Coningliaro at Lonsdale House, London, England.

name: Frankenjack
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth

1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur

history: This cocktail is first published in Judge Jr.' 1928 book Here's How! (New & Revised Edition) where the recipe is credited to "the two proprietors of a very, very well-known Speakeasy in New York City." The same recipe is repeated in Harry Craddock's influential 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book, and under the name "Frankenstein Cocktail" in the 1938 book The How and When by Hyman Gale & Gerald F. Marco.

name: Free Town
preparation: SHAKE (or stir) all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 shot	Tawny port
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Great for sipping after dinner.
history: Created in 2004 by Alexandra Fiot at Lonsdale, London, England.

name: Drones Club

history: Adapted from a recipe created in January 2020 by Jason Clapham in Oxford, England. Originally made with Cocchi Storico Vermouth di Torino rosso vermouth.

name: Eider Duck
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

name: Gin Daisy

1⁄4 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)

name: Gingertini

A classic which is thought to have originated sometime in the 1920s.

Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

review: A distinctly tropical cocktail flavoured with mango.
history: Created in 2004 by yours truly (Simon Difford).

name: Marguerite
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄24 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: An equal parts (Fifty-Fifty) Dry Martini with a hint of orange due to the use of orange curaçao, orange bitters and an orange zest twist.
history:
Not to be confused with the much later, tequila-based Margarita, the Marguerite is a gin-based forerunner to the modern-day Dry Martini.

The earliest known Marguerite Cocktail recipe appears in the 1898 book Cocktails... How To Make Them where it tellingly precedes recipes for "Martini Cocktail – No. 1" and "Martini Cocktail – No. 2".

name: Melon Daiquiri (served frozen)
preparation: Cut melon into 8 segments and deseed. Cut cubes of flesh from skin of one segment and place in blender. Add other ingredients and BLEND with half scoop of crushed ice. Serve with straws.

2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Green melon liqueur

review: A cooling, fruity Daiquiri.

name: Michelada
garnish: Coarse sea salt rim - salt the rim of a chilled beer mug by rubbing it with a lime wedge and dipping rim in the coarse salt. Save the lime wedge to squeeze over and drop into finished drink.
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄12 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Hot pepper sauce (red)
1⁄6 shot	Worcestershire sauce
Top up with	Dunkel / dark / black lager
review: Savoury, sweet n sour beer with enlivening chilli heat. On a hot day, if a beer is not refreshing enough, then a Michelada may hit the spot.
history:
Loosely translates as "my cold beer" (mi means 'my', chela is Mexican slang for pint/beer) and ada from helada is cold. This drink, which is popular in Mexico, is thought to have originated there sometime in the 1940s.

There are many variations with Micheladas served with and without ice. It is usually served with light Mexican lager, although we prefer a darker beer. Even the spicy ingredients vary with Worcestershire sauce often omitted, but the hot pepper sauce remains a constant. In Mexico City itself, a Michelada almost always refers to something much simpler than this: 1 shot fresh lime juice in a glass with a salted rim, into which a light lager is poured.

name: Mitch Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bison grass vodka
1 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄4 shot	Peachtree peach schnapps
1⁄4 shot	Passion fruit syrup
review: One of London's contemporary classics. Far from a proper Martini, this is fruity and sweet, but not overly so.
history: Created in 1997 by Giovanni Burdi at Match EC1, London, England.

name: Mudslide
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with a 6oz scoop of crushed ice and serve with straws.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Irish cream liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
3 scoop	Vanilla ice cream
review: A simply scrumptious dessert drink with whiskey cream and coffee.
history:
Legend has it that the Mudslide was created at the Wreck Bar & Grill in Rum Point Club on Grand Cayman Island, although the bar's own website says, "It may have been born elsewhere in the world but we have claimed it as our own! We are the home of the mudslide!" As for the story behind the legend, the folk at the Wreck say:

"Our legend of the Rum Point Mudslide comes from the 1970s when guests came to the bar and asked the bartender for a white Russian. The bartender asked the ingredients; well it is simple vodka, Kahlua and cream. Well the bartender replied, I have Vodka and Kahlua but I don't have any cream but how about some of this Bailey's Irish cream. And thus the mudslide was born at the Wreck Bar at Rum Point Club...

"There have been many variations created over the years and rumor has it that the original trials of this illusive libation contained Vanilla Hagan Daz ice cream. The mudslide recipe was tweaked and the recipe at Rum Point has stayed as it is since the 1980's and served as is it now with Absolut Vodka, Kahlua and Bailey's or Molly's Irish cream a and ice. No fillers, no ice cream nor chocolate, and garnished with cinnamon, a cherry and a shot of Kahlua down the straw!"

name: Oddball Manhattan Dry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.

history:
I first encountered the Oddball Manhattan in London soon after the Millennium and it entered Difford's Guide to Cocktails #2 (published 2002) as a comment under a Dry Manhattan, "Create an Oddball Manhattan by the addition of a few dashes of Green Chartreuse or blue curaçao."

Also see: Manhattan cocktail history

name: Princeton Martini

name: Quarterback
