name: Queen's
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 shot	Pineapple juice
review: Gin-based with vermouth's bittersweet wine notes and pineapple tropical fruitiness. This fruity Martini takes its name from a three-equal parts Perfect Martini being called the Queen. This version not only has pineapple but traditionally 1 part dry vermouth and 1 part rosso vermouth to 2 parts gin. I prefer with a tad less dry vermouth.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Raspberry Caipirinha
garnish: Stirrer (spoon, wooden lolly stick or stick cut from sugar cane)
preparation:
1. Cut lime in half (from pole to pole) and then slice one of the halves into eight 3-4mm thick half-moon shaped segments and drop into the base of a robust rocks glass.

2. Add 3 bar spoons caster sugar (or ½oz / 15ml sugar syrup 2:1) and MUDDLE.

3. Add raspberries and MUDDLE some more.

4. When sure fruit juice is fully extracted and the sugar dissolved, transfer the muddled fruit and sugar into serving glass (preferably a 30cl / 10oz hi-ball glass).

5. POUR cachaça (stored in the freezer) into the rocks glass (used to muddle) and swirl to rinse glass before pouring cachaça into serving glass. STIR to ensure all ingredients are well mixed.

6. Crack (rather than crush) four to five large ice cubes and drop into serving glass. STIR before topping with more ice and serve with a stirrer (but no straws).
ingredients:
1⁄2 fresh	Lime (fresh) (chopped)
3 barspoon	Caster/ Superfine/Baker's special sugar (white)
8 fresh	Raspberries
2 shot	Cachaça (from freezer)
review: A fruity twist on the popular Caipirinha.
history: For information on the history and other variations of the Caipirinha, please see our Caipirinha cocktail page.

name: Raspberry 'Martini' (by Dick Bradsell)
preparation: MUDDLE raspberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
7 fresh	Raspberries
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Giffard Crème de Framboise
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura (optional)
review: Rich raspberry flavour laced with gin.
history: Created in 1997 by Dick Bradsell, London, England and originally named Raspberry Martini.

name: Red Angel 'Martini'
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Shiraz red wine
1 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: A subtly flavoured cocktail with a dry, almost tannic edge.
history: Created in 2001 by Tony Conigliaro at Isola, Knightsbridge, London, England.

name: Rhett Butler
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Southern USA-style liqueur 40% (e.g. Southern Comfort)
1 1⁄2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A simple and well-balanced classic drink.

name: Roulette
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
3⁄4 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
3⁄4 shot	Swedish Punsch liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Balanced apple and spice.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Sage Cocktail
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE (just to bruise) sage in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3 fresh	Sage leaves
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review: Delicate sage and a hint of apple, dried with vermouth and fortified with vodka.

name: Sake-Tini #2
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Akashi-Tai Shiraume Ginjo Umeshu
1⁄2 shot	Akashi-Tai Daiginjo Genshu sake
1 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
review: Salmon-coloured, light and fragrant with plum wine and sake to the fore.
history: Discovered at Nobu Berkeley, London, England.

name: Satsuma Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Oranje Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1 3⁄4 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Tastes like its namesake - hard to believe the recipe comprises almost half apple juice.
history: Adapted from a drink discovered in 2002 at the Fifth Floor Bar, Harvey Nichol's, London, England.

name: Savoy Special No.1
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄24 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: An aromatised 2:1 shaken Dry Martini with a tiny dose of grenadine, which turns this the merest rust-pink, while just a dash of absinthe adds wormwood complexity.
history: Adapted from Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: 75 Cocktail (Vermeire's 1922 recipe)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: Spirituous, dry and fruity, the botanicals in the gin add depth of flavour to the other fruity ingredients.
history: Adapted from a recipe by Henry Tépé of Henry's Bar in Paris, France, originally published in Robert Vermeire's 1922 book Cocktails - How to Mix Them.

name: Sorrel Rum Punch
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. Serve with straws.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	White overproof rum
2 shot	Sorrelade
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: This drink harnesses the flavour of sorrelade and combines it with the traditional strength and bitter sweetness of rum punch. Jamaica in a glass.
history: A classic Jamaican punch using the classic proportions of 'one of sour, two of sweet, three of strong and four of weak.'

name: Sidecar Named Desire
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
3⁄4 shot	Apple Schnapps liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Take a classic Sidecar and add some love interest - apples!
history: See our Sidecar cocktail page for the full story behind the origins of the Sidecar, its history and variations.

name: Singapore Sling (Baker's Formula)
garnish: Lemon slice & Luxardo Maraschino cherry on stick (sail)
preparation: SHAKE first three ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda, lightly stir and serve with straws.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Lacks the citrus of other Singapore Slings but the strength of the gin and dilution cuts and so balances the sweetness of the liqueurs.
history: Singapore Sling history and other versions

name: Sir Charles Punch
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Tawny port
1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Cognac-laced citrusy wine flavours make this somewhat reminiscent of boozy, chilled mulled wine.
history: Adapted from the following recipe in the 1949 Esquire's Handbook For Hosts book.

name: Sir Thomas
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄3 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: Akin to a fruit laced Sweet Manhattan.
history: Created in 2005 by Tom Ward, London, England.

name: Slow Comfortable Screw
preparation: STIR first three ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. FLOAT sloe gin on surface so it bleeds into drink.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Southern USA-style liqueur 40% (e.g. Southern Comfort)
1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3 1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
review: With freshly squeezed juice, this is a sight tastier than its reputation might suggest. Long and refreshing. Spiked fresh orange juice with Southern Comfort and hints of sloe berry fruit.
history: More information on the Slow Screw family of cocktails is included on our Slow Screw cocktails page.

name: Snood Murdekin
preparation: SHAKE first three ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. FLOAT cream over drink.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1⁄4 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: Moreish combination of coffee and raspberries topped with cream.
history: Created in the late 90s by Dick Bradsell at Detroit, London, England for Karin Wiklund and named for the sad, flute-playing Moomin Troll character from the Moomin books by Tove Jansson.

name: Southern Manhattan
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
2⁄3 shot	Southern USA-style liqueur 40% (e.g. Southern Comfort)
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: A Sweet Manhattan with Southern USA style whiskey liqueur and Creole-style bitters adding a hint of southern flavour.
history:
Created in by yours truly in August 2005 for Tales of the Cocktail, New Orleans, USA.
Manhattan cocktail history

name: Southern Mint Cobbler
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE mint (just to bruise) in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into glass filled with crushed ice. Serve with straws.
ingredients:
7 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Southern USA-style liqueur 40% (e.g. Southern Comfort)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Peach purée
review: Very fruity and easy to drink.
history: For information on the fascinating history of Cobblers please see our page.

name: Speyside Cocktail
preparation: MUDDLE grapes in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
7 fresh	Green grapes (seedless)
2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Scotch, grape juice, apricot liqueur and grapefruit may seem an unlikely combo but they get on well together.
history: Discovered in 2004 (originally named Speyside Martini) at Indigo Yard, Edinburgh, Scotland.

name: Steep Flight
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
3⁄4 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Pear & cognac liqueur
2 1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review: "Apples and pears" is the cockney rhyming slang for stairs, hence the flavours in this particular flight.
history: Created in 2005 by yours truly. Incredibly, this cocktail was awarded a Gold in the Long Drink category at the Drinks International Bartender's Challenge on 31st May 2006.

name: Tartini
preparation: MUDDLE raspberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
1 1⁄2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
12 fresh	Raspberries
review: Richly raspberry flavoured.
history: Adapted from a cocktail discovered at the Soho Grand Hotel, New York City, USA during the 1990s.

name: Teddy Bear
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Pear & cognac liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Apple Schnapps liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1 pinch	Cinnamon powder (ground)
review: Light (low in alcohol) and tad on the sweet side, apple and pear with a hint of cinnamon spice.
history: Created in 2002 at The Borough, Edinburgh, Scotland. Originally named after a well-known cockney duo but renamed after the cockney rhyming slang for pear.

name: Tequila Mockingbird
garnish: Float mint leaf or peg to rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Peppermint Pastille crème de menthe
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Minty tequila.
history: Named after Harper Lee's 1960 novel To Kill a Mockingbird, this is thought to have been created sometime in the 1960s.

name: Tequila Sunset
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda and briefly stir
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄6 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A good sweet and sour balance with tequila character seemingly boosted by the honey.

name: Tick-Tack Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄3 shot	Sambuca
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: Strangely enough, tastes like a Tic-Tac mint-flavoured Vodkatini.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2001 by Rodolphe Sorel, London, England. Rodolphe's original recipe omits dry vermouth and comprises 50ml vodka, 12.5ml sambuca, and 12.5ml white crème de menthe.
Evolution of the Martini

name: Toffee Apple
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
2 shot	Giffard Caramel Toffee liqueur
1 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: The taste is just as the name suggests.
history: Created in 2002 by Nick Strangeway, London, England.

name: Valencia Cocktail No. 2
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. TOP with sparkling wine.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
4 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura (optional)
1 1⁄2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Aromatic and fruity - makes Bucks Fizz look a tad sad.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: What The Hell
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Gin and dry apricot. On the 4th of September 2022, I reduced the volume of my previous recipe by 25% and while doing so I omitted sugar syrup from the recipe to be more in keeping with classic versions of this cocktail which call for lemon juice. (I prefer lime.) My previous recipe: 60ml (2oz) gin, 30 (1oz) apricot brandy, 22.5ml (¾oz) dry vermouth, 7.5ml (¼oz) lime juice, 5ml (1 spoon) sugar syrup.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide.

name: White Cosmo
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Citroen Vodka
1 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 1⁄2 shot	White cranberry juice drink
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Just what it says on the tin.
history:
Emerged during 2002 in New York City.

For more recipes, origins and history behind the Cosmopolitan cocktail, see our Cosmopolitan page.

name: Windy Miller
preparation: SHAKE first three ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. TOP with lemonade.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Citroen Vodka
1⁄2 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 shot	Mandarine Napoleon liqueur
Top up with	Lemon-lime soda (Sprite/7-Up)
review: British readers over 40 may remember the children's TV series Trumpton, Chigley and Camberwick Green. If you do, then sing between sips, "Pugh, Pugh, Barney McGrew, Cuthbert, Dibble and Grubb."
history: Discovered in 2000 at Teatro Club in London, England.

name: Winter Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Sour apple liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Reminiscent of an Apple Cart (a Calvados Sidecar), this is simple, balanced and tastes great.

name: Woo Woo
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Peachtree peach schnapps
2 1⁄3 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
2 dash	Peach bitters (optional)
review: Fruity cranberry laced with vodka and sweet peach liqueur. A quaffable cocktail from the 1980s.
history: A Fuzzy Navel with cranberry instead of orange juice.

name: Yellow Parrot
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2⁄3 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1 shot	Chilled water (reduce if wet ice)
review: The aniseed of the absinthe combines well with the other ingredients but dilution is key. A bit of a sweety but a strong old bird.
history: Some say this was created in 1935 by Albert Coleman at The Stork Club, New York City, but the cocktail first appeared in in Robert Vermeire's 1922 Cocktails: How to Mix Them and also notably in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Fix (Generic Name)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Brandy, whisk(e)y, gin, rum etc.
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Fruit juice (often pineapple)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Match the juice and spirit and this formula works every time.
history: A Fix is a classic style of drink that consists of a spirit, lemon juice, and some kind of sweet fruit served short.

name: Gloria
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with sparkling wine.
ingredients:
1 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: A tequila sour topped with champagne or a tequila French 75.

name: Iced Tea Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Earl Grey tea (cold)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Tannic and bittersweet. A refreshing after-dinner cocktail.
history: Created in 2006 by yours truly, London, England.

name: Alberto Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
5⁄6 shot	Fino sherry
5⁄12 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
review: Dry, complex and aromatic. A Fifty-Fifty Martini with a generous dose of fino sherry and a splash of triple sec.
history: First published in William James "Billy" Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Bar Book where the invention of this cocktail is credited to A. J. Smith.

name: Batida de Abacaxi
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cachaça
2 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1 shot	Condensed milk
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: This easy crowd pleaser is creamy, fruity and to taste - only vaguely alcoholic.
history:
The Batida (meaning 'shake') is a traditional Brazilian drink and 'Abacaxi' means pineapple in Portuguese, the official language of Brazil.

Batida is a broad term for a drink usually containing fresh fruit, sugar and/or sweetened condensed milk (leite condensado). They are often blended with crushed ice or shaken and served over crushed ice.

name: Black Strap
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Dark/black/blackstrap rum
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
2 drop	Hot pepper sauce (red)
review: This drink benefits from the dilution, which comes with a lengthy stir.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2007 by Neyah White, San Francisco, USA.

name: Blue Eyed Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄12 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄12 shot	De Kuyper Blue Curaçao
review: A blue-rinsed Vodka Martini with a hint of piney gin.

name: Champagne Pick-Me-Up
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with sparkling wine.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1 2⁄3 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: A subtle hint of biscuity champagne shines through this very quaffable drink.
history: There are many versions of this classic cocktail but I have taken this one from Dale DeGroff's 2008 The Essential Cocktail where Dale credits this recipe to the Ritz Bar in Paris, France, circa 1936.

name: Corpse Reviver No.1 (Gilberg's recipe)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Boozy, complex and delicious with attractive apple notes and faint anise absinthe influences.
history:
In his book The Joy of Mixology, Gary Regan recommends a version of the Corpse Reviver with 2 oz applejack, ¾ oz cognac and ¾ oz sweet vermouth, which he writes was originally created in 2001 by Steve Gilberg, publisher of happyhours.com. This does indeed make a drink strong enough to awaken the dead but those wishing to remain compos mentis may prefer this equal parts version which I created after being inspired by Steve Gilberg's Corpse Reviver.
Corpse Reviver history

name: The Democrat
preparation: SHAKE with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Crème de Pêche de Vigne liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: The base spirit is inspired by Harry Truman, 33rd President, who only drank bourbon and is considered by some to be, "the last great Democrat."
history: Created in 2007 by Jon Santer at Bourbon & Branch, San Francisco, USA as "a kind of ode to the south - a democratic stronghold for so long."

name: East Village Athletic Club
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
3⁄4 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
3⁄4 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Essentially a Last Word with tequila instead of gin.
history: The Last Word, a vintage cocktail classic, was first documented in Ted Saucier's Bottoms Up in 1951 where its creation was attributed to the Detroit Athletic Club. In 2008, the folk at New York's PDT bar tinkered with the recipe to create this drink named after their own hood.

name: Guards
garnish: Orange zest twist (expressed & discarded) and Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Old Guard but this Sweet Martini, which benefits from a splash of orange curaçao, deserves a place on modern cocktail lists.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide.

name: Manchester Special Rum Punch
preparation: STIR honey with rum until honey dissolves. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Jamaican-style overproof aged pot still rum
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Fruity punch.
history: Originally made at the Manchester Hotel, Mandeville, Jamaica. The Manchester Hotel lies in a lush tropical setting in the centre of Jamaica high in the cool mountains of Manchester.

name: Martinez (Orange)
preparation: STIR ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura (optional)
review: Stir well as dilution helps to tame this old-school classic in which bitter orange predominates.
history: See Martinez cocktail history

name: Naranja
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄4 shot	Savoia Orancio
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Rum based twist on the classic Old-Fashioned.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2008 by Chris Edwardes at the Hanbury Club in Brighton, England.

name: Nuez Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1 shot	Walnut (Nocino) liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review: An aged rum Daiquiri with nutty notes.
history: Named after the Spanish for walnut.

name: Original Sin
preparation: POUR absinthe into ice-filled glass and top with water. Leave the mixture to stand in the glass. Separately, STIR all ingredients with ice. Finally discard contents of absinthe-coated glass and fine strain contents of shaker into absinthe washed glass.
ingredients:
1⁄3 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Akashi-Tai Daiginjo Genshu sake
1⁄6 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: Sake and vodka with a delicate hint of honey.
history: Created in 2009 by Spike Marchant and yours truly at the Cabinet Room in London, England.

name: Papa Bear
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Krupnik spiced honey liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: Delicately spiced and honeyed cognac.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2008 by Tim Homewood at Dirty Martini Bar in London, England. Named after an old family friend who passed away. He was known to all of his children as 'daddy bear' so Papa Bear seemed appropriate.

name: The Quingenti
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Apple Schnapps liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Cognac with apple notes and a touch of herbal complexity by way of dry vermouth.
history: Created in 2008 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room in London, England, originally to celebrate the Future 500 initiative - quingenti is Latin for five-hundred.

name: Rusty
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1 1⁄2 shot	Amontillado sherry
1⁄4 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Sherry and rum combine harmoniously with the smoky Islay malt highlighting spicy notes.
history: Created in December 2008 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England. Originally made using Zacapa 23 rum.

name: Delmarva Cocktail No.1
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A minty fresh, dry, whiskey-based palate cleanser.
history:
Created by Ted "Dr. Cocktail" Haigh, who hails from America's Delmarva Peninsula. I believe Ted's original recipe (and certainly our previous rendition of it) comprised:
60ml (2oz) Bourbon
15ml (½oz) Dry vermouth
15ml (½oz) White crème de menthe
15ml (½oz) Lemon juice
I reworked and rebalanced this to the above recipe in August 2022.

name: Flower Power Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Crème de violette liqueur
review: A Dry Martini served super-wet with even more flower power than Austin Powers.
history: Created in 2007 by yours truly in London, England.

name: Gloom Chaser (Embury)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄12 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄24 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Grenadine adds a pink-red hue but absinthe ensures this Martini remains dry. Nonetheless, this drink may chase your gloom (blues) away.
history: Adapted from a recipe David A. Embury's 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks.

name: Greenbelt
preparation: MUDDLE grapes in base of shaker. Add pisco and elderflower liqueur, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with sparkling wine.
ingredients:
10 fresh	Green grapes (seedless)
1 2⁄3 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
5⁄6 shot	Elderflower liqueur
2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine (chilled)
review: Tastes as green and fresh as it looks. Also, floral and refreshing.
history: Created in 2007 by yours truly in London, England.

name: Holland House (Genever-based)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
review: Genever adds its own complexity to this Dutch version of the classic Holland House.
history: This genever-based version of The Holland House was practically unknown before 2008 but it has since been rescued from obscurity.

name: King Cole Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄4 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Fernet-loving folk will appreciate this herbal digestivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Last Straw
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Medium dry apple cider
1 1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review: Three stages of the apple's alcoholic journey, juice, cider and brandy, are sweetened and aromatised by elderflower liqueur.
history: Created in 2006 by yours truly. We used the last straw we had left to sample the first one. Fortunately, there are alternatives to plastic straws.

name: Strawberry & Balsamic Fruitini
preparation: MUDDLE strawberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5 fresh	Strawberries (hulled, small & ripe)
2 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄6 shot	White balsamic vinegar
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Balsamic adds extra bite to vodka-laced strawberries.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2001 at Che Bar, St James's Street, London, and originally named Strawberry & Balsamic Martini. This cocktail was popular in London bars during 2002.

name: Black Nail #1
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Drambuie liqueur
1 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 shot	Honey flavoured vodka
review: A suitably hardened Rusty Nail variation with a full three measures of spirit.
history: Created in 2010 by yours truly (Simon Difford) at The Cabinet Room, London, England and named after New Zealand's All Blacks rugby team.

name: Breakfast Gimlet
preparation: STIR marmalade with gin in base of shaker to dissolve marmalade. Add lemon juice and lime cordial, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄4 shot	Lime cordial (sweetened lime juice)
2 barspoon	Orange marmalade
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Orange marmalade justifies the 'breakfast' prefix and adds complexity to this gimlet.
history: A mashup of the classic Gimlet and Salvatore Calabrese's Breakfast Martini. Created by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Charlie
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A Sweet Manhattan with subtle blackberry and raspberry fruit. Despite the liqueur, this remains spirit-forward and relatively dry.
history: Created in 2009 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room in London England and named for Charlotte Ashburner, then Chambord liqueur's UK brand manager.

name: Culross Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Light rum, aromatic wine served 'up' with the marzipan and almond notes of apricot liqueur. I've used dry vermouth in place of the Kina Lillet in the 1930 recipe.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Si-Mao
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Tennessee whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A whiskey laced shot with a hint of banana.
history: Adapted from a drink discovered in 2010 at Nobu Berkeley, London, England.

name: Waterloo Sunset
preparation: STIR first two ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne. Add raspberry liqueur.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
Top up with	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
review: Fruity, pink champagne.
history: Created in 2008 by Dan Warner, then the Beefeater Global Ambassador, hence originally made using said gin.

name: Amatitan Twist
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Añejo tequila
1⁄4 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
6 drop	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
review: The sublime taste of great añejo tequila mellowed and delicately flavoured with maraschino, chartreuse and grapefruit bitters.
history: Created in 2010 by Dave West at Trio Bar and Grill in Leeds, England.

name: La Bicyclette
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Elderflower liqueur
2 dash	Peach bitters
review: A light and fragrant Sweet Martini style drink with elderflower liqueur and peach bitters.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2008 by Jamie Boudreau, Seattle, USA.

name: Rusty Margarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	Drambuie liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: The rich honeyed notes from Drambuie combine harmoniously with tequila and add an extra dimension to this tasty Margarita. This cocktail is perhaps at its best once the ice has melted to add a little extra dilution.
history:
Created in December 2010 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London.
More Margarita variations and the history of the Margarita

name: Charlie Chaplin Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Dilution is key to this fruity sweet 'n' sour cocktail, hence, depending on your ice, the Charlie Chaplin may benefit from the addition of a splash of water prior to shaking.
history: Created and originally served at New York's old Waldorf-Astoria prior to 1920. This recipe is adapted from Albert Stevens Crockett's 1935 The Old Waldorf-Astoria Bar Book. The drink is named after Sir Charles Spencer 'Charlie' Chaplin (1889-1977), the English slapstick comic actor of the silent film era, who was at the height of his career when this eponymous cocktail was created.

name: Detroit Athletic Club
garnish: Float thin lemon wheel or dehydrated slice of lemon on surface
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
review: Irish whiskey with a splash of sweet vermouth, clove rich falernum and the all-important monastic liqueur.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2010 by Donovan Sornig, Bar Manager at Bol Restaurant, Vail, Colorado. This cocktail was inspired by The Last Word created at the Detroit Athletic Club, which Donovan grew up just four miles away from.

name: Fanhattan
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
1⁄2 shot	Fig liqueur (crème de figue)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Twist on a Manhattan for fig lovers.
history: Created in 2010 by Dan Richards of Host Academy, UK.

name: Stone Place
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: Rum loves fruit, and this rust-pink cocktail has plenty of it.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2010 by Willy Shine at Forty-Four in New York City, USA. This twist on the Ward 8 is named after the street where Shine's parents, who were big Ward 8 imbibers, used to live.

name: Purgatory a la Française
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
2⁄3 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
1⁄6 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
review: This Islay smoke-influenced drink makes for a great nightcap.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2010 by Arthur Combe at Curio Parlour bar in Paris, France.

name: Phish Hook
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
review: Rye whiskey tamed and flavoured by elderflower, Punt E Mes and maraschino.
history: Adapted from a January 2010 recipe courtesy of Jamie Boudreau's spiritsandcocktails.wordpress.com

name: Sargasso
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Martinique V.S.O.P rum
3⁄4 shot	Oloroso sherry
1⁄2 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: This orange-red bitter sweet drink has a dry oaky complexity.
history: Created in 2008 by Don Lee at PDT, New York City, USA.

name: Blue Lassi
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka (infused with vanilla)
1 1⁄2 shot	Yoghurt liqueur
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Blue Curaçao
2 dash	Rose water
review: Baby blue creamy yoghurt with vanilla infused vodka, orange liqueur and aromatic rose water.
history: Created in 2011 by yours truly (Simon Difford) at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Pearlinstrum
garnish: Lime zest twist (and a sprig of elderflower when in season).
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Pear-flavoured vodka
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Elderflower liqueur
review: A pear-flavoured Vodka Martini with delicate, harmonious floral elderflower.
history:
Created in 2012 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

Trying to think of an appropriate 'pear' name, I remembered the Swedish adventurer Per Lindstrand, who, with entrepreneur Richard Branson, was the first to cross the Atlantic Ocean in a hot-air balloon on 2-3 July 1987. The combination of miss remembering his name and my dyslexic spelling gave me Pearlinstrum.

name: Midnight in New York
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Shiraz red wine
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: The success of this cocktail is very dependent on the red wine you use. A lighter earthier style will work better than a voluptuous fruity red.
history: Adapted from a recipe by Trudy Thomas, Liquid Remedy Inc, Phoenix, AZ.

name: Agua De Cuba
preparation: Cut watermelon into 16 segments, chop the flesh from one segment into cubes and MUDDLE in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 slice	Watermelon (fresh) (chopped)
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
2⁄3 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A light, summery, rum-based drink with fresh watermelon and subtle clove spice. We prefer strained into a coupe glass rather than a flute.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2010 by Joey Medrington at Tigerlily, Edinburgh, Scotland.

name: Praline Pecan Pie
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Pecan liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Reminiscent of a pecan-flavoured Sweet Manhattan.
history: Created in December 2010 by Cheri Loughlin, The Intoxicologist, USA.

name: Royalist Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.

1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1 dash	Peach bitters
review: A Manhattan-style cocktail but with dry vermouth and considerably more of it, Bénédictine and peach bitters.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by William James "Billy" Tarling and featured in his 1937 The Café Royal Cocktail Book.

name: Young Man Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: This particular Young Man is essentially a cognac-based Sweet Manhattan with a splash of orange curaçao. I've used rather more curaçao than the "2 Dashes" specified in Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Honey Bee Mine
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) & honeycomb on rim
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄24 shot	Vanilla extract/essence
1 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Honey and vanilla laced with white rum and charged with champagne. Perfect for Valentine's Day.

name: Lychee & Elderflower Spritz
preparation: POUR prosecco and liqueurs into glass. Add ice and TOP with soda.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
5⁄6 shot	Kwai Feh lychee liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Elderflower liqueur
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: As the apt name suggests, this slightly sweet spritz is flavoured with lychee and elderflower liqueurs. East meets west in Italy.
history:
Created in 2013 by yours truly for Jamie's Italian Bar.

name: Sour Cherry Spritz
preparation: POUR prosecco and liqueurs into glass. Add ice. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
5⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
5⁄6 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: The name aptly describes the drink.
history:
Created in 2013, this was a popular drink at Jamie's Italian Bars.
See: Spritz cocktail history

name: Doctor No. 4
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1 1⁄4 shot	Swedish Punsch liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
4 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water) (optional)
review: Retitled 'Swedish Daiquiri', this could be a hit. Aged rum (originally Jamaican rum) combines with tangy Swedish Punch balanced by lime juice. This cocktail loves dilution, so consider adding a splash of water or, perhaps better, serve on-the-rocks.
history: Recipe adapted from Lucius Beebe's 1946 The Stock Club Bar Book.

name: Brits Spritz
garnish: Squeeze grapefruit wedge into drink & add cucumber slice
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and stir.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
5⁄6 shot	Ginseng liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: An elderflower Spritz with depth of flavour and British character courtesy of Kamm & Sons
history:
Created by Alex Kammerling of Kamm & Sons, this is the brand's signature cocktail.

See Spritz cocktail history and more recipes

name: Beetroot & Vanilla Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Beetroot juice
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
review: Just as the name suggests, only the beetroot pervades this otherwise classic Daiquiri more than the vanilla. Consider using vanilla-infused rum.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2014 by Josh Powell at Bar44, Penarth, Wales.

name: Floradora
preparation: SHAKE first three ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with ginger ale and lightly stir.
ingredients:
1 3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Crème de Framboise
2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
review: This pink, gin-based drink is light and fruity with lime juice balancing sweet raspberry liqueur and lengthened with ginger ale. Some make this with raspberry syrup rather than liqueur but why forgo the alcohol?
history:
Dating from the turn of the 20th century, this drink is eponymously named after a successful Edwardian musical comedy that originally opened in London in 1899 and then on Broadway the following year. The show was famous for its chorus line of Florodora Girls, a "sextette of tall, gorgeous damsels, clad in pink walking costumes, black picture hats and carrying frilly parasols [who] swished onto the stage and captivated New York for no other reason than they were utterly stunning."

This cocktail may be named after the Florodora Girls (spelt with three 'o's and one 'a'), but it notably features in Jacques Straub's 1913 Manual of Mixed Drinks as Floradora (spelt with two 'o's and two 'a's) so that's how I've spelt it here.

name: Entente Cordiale Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: This gin laced cocktail is flavoured with apricot liqueur which is balanced and made more complex by dry vermouth. A dash of orange bitters and a light lemon zest twist subtly serve to unify all. (Go easy with the bitters and zest.)

name: Chilcano de Pisco
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and lightly stir.
ingredients:
2 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3 dash	Amargo Chuncho bitters
3 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
review: Pisco and ginger ale made more interesting by a splash of lime juice and a few dashes of Amargo Chuncho bitters.
history: The Chilcano de Pisco is a traditional Peruvian way of serving pisco. Its name should not be confused with the Peruvian fish soup, Chilcano de Pescado, although the drink derived its name from the dish due to the similarity in hue thanks to the colouring effect of the aromatic bitters.

name: Night Vision
preparation: SHAKE first three ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with tonic water.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cachaça
1 shot	Carrot juice (freshly extracted)
1⁄3 shot	Agave syrup
Top up with	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: Cachaça, carrot and tonic water make for a very interesting combo in this drink which is "naturally" sweetened with agave syrup. Perhaps more health shop/juice bar than speakeasy but unusually tasty all the same.
history:
Adapted from a drink originally called "Natural" created in 2015 by Jorge Balbontin, Barcelona, Spain.

Carrots are packed full of Vitamin A, in the form of beta carotene, so are good for the health of our eyes but contrary to popular belief carrots don't help you see in the dark. This urban myth stems from WWII. During the 1940 Blitzkrieg, the Luftwaffe struck the southeast of England under the cover of darkness but The Royal Air Force had the upper hand in the dark skies due to new radar technology. First installed in RAF aircraft in 1939, the secret on-board Airborne Interception Radar (AI) could spot enemy bombers before they reached the English Channel. Not wanting the Germans to develop similar technology, to explain the success of the British pilots, the Ministry of Information spread the myth that they could see in the dark due to eating carrots.

name: Weeski Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Irish whiskey with herbal complexity and zesty orange.
history: Created in 2004 by David Wondrich in Brooklyn, New York City, USA. By popular demand (well, an email and one comment on this website) in June 2020, I reduced the whiskey in this recipe from 60ml to 50ml. (Hope you don't mind David?). However, my own preference is for the original 60ml whiskey but with 15ml Lillet Blanc, 15ml Americano Bianco, and 1 dash orange bitters.

name: Berry Flip
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Giffard Crème de Mûre liqueur
1 2⁄3 shot	Ginger wine
1 fresh	Egg yolk
review: A most unusual brandy-laced flip with rich blackberry and lingering ginger spice. Slightly on the sweet side.
history: Created in 2015 by William Baker at Fu Manchu in Clapham North, London, England.

name: Cherry Velvet
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Vermouth amaro - medium (e.g. Cocchi Vermouth Amaro)
1⁄2 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Rich Pedro Ximénez sherry and Italian amaro add complexity and depth of flavour to luxurious brandy.
history: Created in 2015 by Mickael Lenu at Roka Aldwych in London, England. Mickael's original recipe calls for Martell Cordon Bleu cognac.

name: Le Traite des Pyrenees (The Treaty of the Pyrenees)
preparation: SMOKE the inside of glass with a lightly fragrant cigar and cover. STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into cigar smoked glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 dash	Peach bitters
review: Rich and flavoursome Pedro Ximénez sherry stirred with cognac bitters and delicately influenced by cigar smoke
history: Created in 2015 by Johan Tufvesson at Kosmopol Bar, London, England. Johan’s original recipe calls for Martell XO cognac.

name: B&B Royale
preparation: STIR first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
1 1⁄2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: A crowd pleasing cognac-based cocktail – will appeal to the many and upset few – with the monastic herbal complexity of Bénédictine with rich black raspberry, topped and effervesced with champagne.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2015 by Matthew Eifion Jones at Peppermint in Cardiff, Wales.

name: Charentes Cocktail
preparation: MUDDLE grapes in base of mixing glass. Add other ingredients, STIR with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
7 whole	Green grapes (seedless)
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
5⁄6 shot	Pineau des Charentes rouge
3 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: White grape juice fortified with cognac and lightly sweetened by pineau des charentes with faint hints of chocolate.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Steve Lawson at M.A.S.H, Soho, London, England

name: Brandy Club Cocktail
garnish: Orange & lemon grated zest mixed with caster sugar rim
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Oloroso sherry
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Cognac and zesty orange curacao with sherry. The sugary rim is essential to the balance of this drink.
history: Adapted from a 2015 recipe by Ryu Okada at Kampai Cocktails (a mobile cocktail bar company based in Sussex, England.)

name: Soir d'Ete (Summer Evening)
garnish: Lemon zest twist and fresh lavender sprig/dried lavender blossom
preparation: STIR in all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. (Or strain into ice-filled old-fashioned glass.)
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
2⁄3 shot	Camomile tea (cold) (infused with lavender)
3⁄4 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Fruity cognac with delicate floral tea notes.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Paride Fameli at the Lounge cocktail bar, Novotel London West, England.

name: Chipotle Punch
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄3 shot	Fino sherry
2 barspoon	Chilpotle oleo-saccharum
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Created by José Luis León from Mexico. José is the general manager in Grupo Sicario and is the owner of Baltra and Licoreria Limantour and he created this cocktail for Patrón Tequila as part of their activity at London Cocktail Week 2016.

name: Patrónomy
garnish: Rim glass with black salt. Grapefruit zest twist
preparation:
POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and STIR briefly.

Special Ingredient #1: Gentain eau-de-vie
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
5⁄6 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
2 1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
3 drop	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
review: Created by Remy Savage, the head bartender behind the celebrated Paris cocktail bar Little Red Door, for Patrón Tequila at London Cocktail Week 2016.

name: The Guest
preparation:
STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.

*Special ingredient #1: Ratafia Di Andorno, Rapa Giovanni (Liquore di ciliegie Bere)
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
1⁄2 shot	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
1⁄4 shot	Dark chocolate liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review:
"The Guest is born of the conversations I have had with the regular guests that visit my bar. Building a relationship with them allows me to learn what they like and introduce them to new flavour experiences that open the world of mixology to them. Soon they learn to appreciate different styles of drinks using sweet, sour, bitter, complex and robust ingredients, giving them the confidence to order what they like. The Guest is named for them, and inspired by them. It takes the flavours preferred by my most regular guests and interprets these using my personality as a bartender."

We say: Vaguely reminiscent of a rum laced Black Forest gateau.
history: Mexican BACARDÍ LEGACY 2016 winning cocktail by Pablo 'Pasti' Mangialavori, Limantour, Mexico City.

name: Bittersweet Victory
preparation: THROW all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
1⁄3 shot	Martini Riserva Speciale Bitter
1⁄2 shot	Maple syrup
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review:
"This cocktail symbolizes the highs, lows and successes that everybody, including myself, the Bacardi Company and other companies, will experience or have already experienced in their lifetime. Bittersweet Victory's ingredients mirror this idea: the lows that come with life are reflected through the bitter liquor and lime juice; the highs, on the other hand, can be tasted through the sweetness of the maple syrup. The successes that life brings with it are represented by Bacardí, as the company has surpassed many hurdles in its history to enjoy numerous achievements and personal victories."

We say: Very slightly on the tart side of balanced with rich maple syrup set against bitter aperitivo and lime juice. Rum notes are subdued but have a presence.
history: Austrian BACARDÍ LEGACY 2016 winning cocktail by Stefan Bauer, The Bank Brasserie & Bar, Vienna.

name: The Knight Cup
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
2⁄3 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1⁄3 shot	Pomegranate liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Elizaveta, this cocktails creator, says, "To create my cocktail it was important for me to emphasize the sense of loyalty, tradition and family heritage in Bacardí Carta Blanca. The knight embodies these qualities, as a symbol of nobility, loyalty and honour. The Knight Cap - for those who respect these qualities and also want a little knight's courage."
history: The overall Bacardí Legacy 2013 winning cocktail and the winner of The Russian 2013 Bacardí Legacy, created by Elizaveta Evdokimova, Russia.

name: Blush
preparation:
SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

Special ingredient #1: Cranberry puree
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
1⁄2 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
history: Belarus Bacardí Legacy 2015 winning cocktail by Lizaveta Molyavka, New Project, Minsk

name: Meh-Groni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: This Negroni-inspired cocktail will please mezcal loving bartenders and hardened drinkers (we also loved it) but may challenge other drinkers.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Jesse R. Raines at Vieux Carre, Washington DC, USA. Recipe courtesy of gazregan.com.

name: Around The World With A Negroni
garnish: Pink pepper around glass rim and garnish with a slice of orange and complete with a little wooden spoon with spheres of coffee-flavoured tequila inside.
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Tangerine / Mandarin / Clementine juice (fresh juice)
review: Bittersweet with zesty orange fruitiness.
history: Created by Jennyfer Lee and Jorge Cordero in the Dominican Republic.

name: Killer in Red
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
history: Revealed in January 2017, this is the cocktail after which the Campari Red Diaries’ founding story, Killer in Red is named.

name: Eggs-cellent
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2 shot	Warninks Advocaat liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
8 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: Brandy and advocaat (the eggy element) is a classic and indulgent combo that says Easter and/or Christmas – both spiritual holidays so the addition of Chartreuse is obvious. As this Eggs-cellent cocktail was made for Easter it had to have some chocolate so I added chocolate bitters.
history: Created in April 2017 by yours truly as an Easter Cocktail.

name: Grand Duchess Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄3 shot	Jamaican-style overproof aged pot still rum
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: This vodka-based Tiki-style cocktail is made "funky" by a splash of pot still Jamaican rum while lime juice adds freshness and grenadine adds both a rich hue and sweetness.

name: Blackberry Agave Caipirinha
garnish: Stirrer (spoon, wooden lolly stick or stick cut from sugar cane)
preparation:
1. Cut lime in half (from pole to pole) and then slice one of the halves into eight 3-4mm thick half-moon shaped segments and drop into the base of a robust rocks glass and MUDDLE.

2. Add blackberries and MUDDLE some more.

3. When sure fruit juice is fully extracted and the sugar dissolved, transfer the muddled fruit and sugar into serving glass (preferably a 30cl / 10oz hi-ball glass).

4. Add agave syrup to serving glass.

5. POUR cachaça (stored in the freezer) into the rocks glass (used to muddle) and swirl to rinse glass before pouring cachaça into serving glass. STIR to ensure all ingredients are well mixed.

6. Crack (rather than crush) four to five large ice cubes and drop into serving glass. STIR before topping with more ice and serve with a stirrer (but no straws).
ingredients:
1⁄2 fresh	Lime (fresh) (chopped)
6 fresh	Blackberries
1 shot	Agave syrup
2 shot	Cachaça (from freezer)
review: Sweetening with agave nectar rather than sugar helps set this fruity Caipirinha apart and creates a drink that is very slightly sweet.
history: For information on the history and other variations of the Caipirinha, please see our Caipirinha cocktail page.

name: Scandinavian Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Akvavit / Aquavit
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
4 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters (optional)
review: A caraway-influenced riff on a daiquiri with aquavit replacing rum. Refreshing and suited to a summer's afternoon or an early evening aperitif.
history: Adapted from a 2015 recipe by Kyle Webster at Expatriate, Portland, Oregon, USA. Kyles's original recipe of 2 aquavit, 1 lime juice and ¾ simple syrup (1:1) made from palm sugar.

name: Rum & Raisin Espresso Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
3⁄4 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
3⁄4 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
review: A hint of PX sherry adds the raisin notes to this rum-based riff on Dick Bradsell's Espresso Martini.

name: Pterodactyl Cocktail
preparation: THROW all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄12 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Adapted from a drink created in 2017 by Martyn Lourencoat at Kol Restaurant, Reykjavik, Iceland, who says, "Since cocktail culture is still pretty new in Iceland and people aren't used to gentiane and absinthe in their drinks, I chose the name Pterodactyl because I didn't want guests to connect the name to anything they've had before! The fact that it is difficult to pronounce is an advantage as it is a good talking point for us. Pterodactyl is the name of a species of Pterosaur and so is very hard to come up with expectations on taste from the name!
history: A dry and aromatic aperitif cocktail with a long bittersweet herbal finish. (We prefer with half the amount of absinthe).

name: French Spritz
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and lightly STIR.
ingredients:
1⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
1 1⁄3 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄3 shot	Elderflower liqueur
3 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: This apéritif-style cocktail perfectly fits its name. That said, fans of Italian fizz will be interested to learn how well this spritz works when made with prosecco in place of champagne.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2017 by Fred Charlet at La Cabane in Strasbourg, France, who says of his drink, "The idea was to create a fresh cocktail made with French ingredients: Suze, St Germain and champagne: what else do you need to represent the typically French appetizer. May be a baguette and a béret, but that is not the subject here. I hope you will enjoy this cocktail and don't forget, a good French appetizer always match with French cheese."

See Spritz history and family of cocktails

name: GDPR Cocktail
preparation: MUDDLE raspberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
7 fresh	Raspberries
2 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
history:
GDPR is an acronym for General Data Protection Regulation and this cocktail was created on 25th May 2018 to commemorate the new law coming into effect.

G = Grapefruit juice (preferably pink) 30ml / 1oz
D = Demerara sugar syrup (2:1) 15ml / ½oz
P = Pisco 45ml / 2oz
R = Raspberries 8 fresh

name: Enchanted Field Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Strega liqueur

review: Boozy spicy rye and citrus with minty, menthol, vanilla and piny freshness from a generous slug of Strega liqueur.
