name: Golden Tang
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Strega liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: This vodka-laced cocktail is indeed tangy and golden (well, light orange) with a pleasing banana chew flavour.

name: Harvest Old Fashioned
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: A dry (some may want to up the sugar) spirit-forward riff on a classic Old Fashioned, with rye whiskey providing spirituous spice and calvados appley notes. A tasty after-dinner sipper.
history: Old-Fashioned cocktail history

name: Caipirinha (no added sugar & low-calorie)
garnish: Stirrer (spoon, wooden lolly stick or stick cut from sugar cane)
preparation:
1. Cut lime in half (from pole to pole) and slice on half into 3-4mm thick half-moon shaped segments and drop into the base of a robust rocks glass.

2. Add sweetener and MUDDLE.

3. If using cubed ice straight from the freezer, add chilled water (or optionally add fruit of your choice) and MUDDLE some more. If using watery ice then omit water.

4. When sure muddling has fully extracted fruit juice, POUR the muddled fruit and sweetener into serving glass (preferably a 30cl / 10oz hi-ball glass).

5. POUR cachaça (stored in the freezer) into the rocks glass (the glass used to muddle) and swirl to rinse glass before pouring cachaça into serving glass. STIR to mix with other ingredients.

6. If using cubed ice, crack (rather than crush) four to five large ice cubes and drop into serving glass. STIR before topping with more ice and serve with a stirrer (but no straws).
ingredients:
1⁄2 fresh	Lime (fresh)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar-free sweetener
3⁄4 shot	Chilled water
1 1⁄2 shot	Cachaça
review: Forget those Caipirinhas blighted by crunchy undissolved sugar crystals, this version is sugar-free.
history:
Adapted from the classic Caipirinha by yours truly in January 2019.
Caipirinha cocktail - history, flavours, and how to make

name: La Petite Bouche
garnish: White grapefruit wedge squeezed and dropped in drink as garnish
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
2⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
3 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
3 shot	Mediterranean tonic water
review: Dry and refreshing with gentian bitterness and complexity forming the backbone of this apéritif.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Danny Wilson at Tabouche, Cambridge, England. Danny told us, "Due to me working at Tabouche I tend to like to name drinks around my venue and since this drink is very simplistic, I decided to call it the little mouth in French."

name: Parasol
garnish: Pineapple wedge on rim & dust with freshly grated nutmeg
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Citrusy pineapple, banana and rum. A slightly tart short drink with flavours reminiscent of a San Francisco.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Shannon Mustipher at Glady's in Brooklyn, New York City, USA.

name: Shaft
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. Serve with a straw.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cold brew coffee
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Irish cream liqueur
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
review: Irish cream liqueur adds a creamy mocha note to this Shaft version but some make with cream and others milk, either combining all ingredients prior to pouring or adding milk/cream as a float (as with a White Russian).
history:
Named after private detective John Shaft, the lead character in the 1971 cult movie Shaft, hired by a Harlem gangster to rescue his daughter from the Italian mobsters who kidnapped her. The film's theme song, Theme From Shaft, was an Academy Award-winning hit in its own right.

The creation of the Shaft cocktail, circa 2000, is credited to Mark Smith whilst bartending at The Living Room restaurant in Calgary, Canada, as a built (rather than shaken) caffeinated pick-me-up shot originally consisting simply espresso with a splash of Kahlúa coffee liqueur and skimmed milk.

This cocktail became ubiquitous in Victoria, the capital of British Columbia, Canada, leading many to speculate that this is its true birthplace. Indeed, it was a Victoria resident and fellow Discerning Drinker, Sean Gordon, who first brought the Shaft to my attention in June 2019, saying, "There is a locally invented cocktail/shot called a Shaft", adding "some will sip it but it's most commonly downed in one. It's basically a grownup Jaeger-bomb substitute."

As Sean told me back in 2019, "There's variation from one bar to another". From what I can tell, it seems likely that the original Shaft was created in Calgary and, at some point during its journey to Victoria, the drink morphed with vodka added and Irish cream liqueur often replacing milk. The original espresso coffee base is also widely substituted for cold brew coffee.

name: Picon Punch
preparation: POUR first 2 ingredients into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda (leaving room for the brandy). Briefly stir and then FLOAT brandy.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Amer Picon
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
review: Bittersweet and herbal, a distinctly French aperitif.
history: Thought to have originated at the Noriega Hotel in Bakersfield, California, the Picon Punch has become something of a signature drink of Basque immigrant communities in the USA who have also taken it back to their home region in the French Pyrénées.

name: Public Enemy No.1
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
1⁄2 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1⁄3 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Disaronno amaretto
review: A rich and richly flavoured dessert cocktail highlighting the coffee and cacao flavours of the spiced rum.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Kiki Moka at Union Group; Jakarta. Kiki's original recipe comprised: 30ml Black Tears Spiced Rum, 20ml Cherry Heering, 10ml Luxardo Amaretto and 15ml Cynar.

name: Marshmallow 'Martini'
garnish: Roasted marshmallow & shot of champagne on the side
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
5⁄6 shot	Passion fruit purée
1⁄3 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
1⁄2 fresh	Passion fruit (fresh)
review: Passion fruit and vanilla with a double treat as a garnish.

name: Coco Bongo Club
garnish: Lemon zest twist & half strawberry on rim
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
2 shot	Strawberry flavoured vodka
1⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3 1⁄3 shot	Coconut water
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Refreshing, light and long ripe strawberry and coconut water.

name: Strawberry Dog
garnish: Salt-rimmed glass with grapefruit juice (optional) & half strawberry on rim.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Strawberry flavoured vodka
1 2⁄3 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄6 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄6 shot	Strawberry sugar syrup
review: Rich ripe juicy strawberry and cranberry with zesty grapefruit.

name: Mexican Firing Squad Special
garnish: Orange slice, pineapple wedge & Luxardo maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review:
Tequila dominates this lightly citrusy fairly dry classic. The bitters play a key role in both balance and flavour.

It's worth noting that this drink is a sour served in a highball glass but it is not a Highball and should not be topped with soda. A highball glass should be a max capacity of 10oz / 296ml. Use such a glass filled with ice and this recipe will fill to a good washline without need, or room, for a soda top.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Charles H Baker's 1939 The Gentleman's Companion.

name: Monte Cassino Sunrise
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. POUR grenadine around the surface of the drink. (This should sink to form sunrise effect.)
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bepi Tosolini Grappa di Moscato
1⁄3 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: Long, fruity and juicy with aromatic grappa providing the backbone.

name: Madame Mayahuel
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄2 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1⁄2 shot	Amontillado sherry
1⁄6 shot	Crème de violette liqueur
review: Whether you love or hate this spirit-forward cocktail will firstly be driven by your preference for mezcal and secondly by whether you appreciate this cocktail's floral violet notes, not to mention the sherry and amaro notes.

name: Paloma Negra
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with grapefruit soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
2⁄3 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Pink Grapefruit soda
review: A Paloma with coffee liqueur.

name: Ripe Red Slice
garnish: Fresh watermen wedge on rim or watermelon slices sweets/candy
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Watermelon liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review: It's not only fruity, but also ripe! But not everything that's ripe is sweet!
history: Created 23rd May 2020 by yours truly in Rye, England.

name: Tequila Colada
preparation: POUR all ingredients into glass and stir to combine. Fill glass with ice and serve.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Patrón Añejo tequila
1 2⁄3 shot	Pineapple juice
2 1⁄3 shot	Coconut water
1 pinch	Salt (sea salt)
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Allan Suárez of Mexico who is a Patrón Perfectionists Global Finalist 2020.

name: Salvatore Legacy
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Mentzendorff Kümmel liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Kümmel's bold caraway, cumin and fennel flavours predominate in this cognac-based after-dinner digestive cocktail.
history: Created by Salvatore Calabrese who in October 2012 broke the Guinness World Record for the most expensive cocktail in the world by making this recipe using a 1788 cognac, a 1770 kümmel, an 1860 orange curaçao, and Angostura Bitters from 1900. A total of "733 years of liquid history in one drink, pricing the cocktail at £5,500."

name: Black Magic No.2
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
1 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Two parts amaro to 1 part Islay single malt is a boundary-pushing recipe but with a splash of banana liqueur, the resulting cocktail is balanced and tasty.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Roger Grüter at Angel's Share in Basel, Switzerland. Roger's original recipe calls for Laphroaig 10yo Islay single malt.

name: Detroit Irish Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Tuaca liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
review: There's nothing Irish about this drink, but it's good all the same.
history: Adapted from a drink discovered in 2001 at Detroit in London, England.

name: Marceau
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with splash soda and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Fruity and fresh. The perfect breakfast cocktail.

name: Rackhouse Lemonade
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Tennessee whiskey
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Crème de Pêche de Vigne liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3 shot	Lemonade
review: Perfect to accompany a barbeque. Tennessee whiskey with ripe peach balanced and freshened by tart zesty lemon.
history: Created on 16th December 2020 by yours truly using Daddy Rack Straight Tennessee Whiskey for James Rackham (AKA "Daddy Rack"), the originator of both Daddy Rack Whiskey and the name Rackhouse Lemonade.

name: Saucy Sue
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Sue may not be particularly saucy, but she certainly has spirit – equal parts calvados and cognac with the merest splash of apricot liqueur and a dash of absinthe.
history: This "exhumed classic" was brought to our attention by Jason E. Clapham and originally appeared in Harry Craddock's 1930 Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Beautiful Beth
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. TOP with cola.
ingredients:
1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Coconut rum liqueur (35-40% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 1⁄2 shot	Cola (e.g. Coca Cola or Pepsi Cola)
review: We were recommended this cocktail with the comment that it tastes like an alcoholic "cola cube sweet." It does.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Emma Beare's 2007 501 Must Drink Cocktails. [My thanks to David Cripps for bringing this recipe to my attention in December 2020.]

name: Cameo Kirby
garnish: Skewered raspberry or lime wedge on rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Raspberry (framboise) sugar syrup
review: Rich jammy raspberry brilliantly balances sour lime with gin and vermouth sitting alongside each other as deliciously as ever.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Jacob Abraham Grohusko's 1933 Jack's Bar Manual 5th Edition.

name: Sweetie Darling
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
1 1⁄2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Fruity, rich, fizzy and alcohol-laced. Patsy, you must try it.
history: Adapted from a recipe by Discerning Drinker, Lea Beckerleg, in turn adapted from the 1990s Absolutely Fabulous cocktail

name: Cowboy Spritz
preparation: POUR all ingredients in ice-filled glass and briefly STIR.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Horse with No Name habanero bourbon
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 shot	Cola (e.g. Coca Cola or Pepsi Cola)
review: Whiskey and cola with zesty cowboy attitude.

name: Yellow Jacket (Tequila-based)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
2⁄3 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A slightly sweet tequila-laced after-dinner/late night sipper with rich herbal liqueur and elderflower liqueur. Looks like the kind of cocktail that should be stirred but it's better shaken.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by the team at Employees Only in New York City, USA, this cocktail is named after the yellow jacket wasps that are attracted to agave being processed in Mexican distilleries during the production of tequila and mezcal.

name: Alex Summer
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. (Instead of watermelon juice you can muddle lumps cut from a wedge of fresh watermelon.)
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Watermelon juice
1 shot	Bepi Tosolini Grappa di Moscato
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Grappa adds its distinctive character to this cocktail that's fruity and summery without being sweet.

name: The Swagger
garnish: Grapefruit wedge or slice on rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1⁄2 shot	Rabarbaro liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Pucker-up for this bittersweet, gin-laced and aromatised grapefruit sour.
history: Adapted form a recipe created by Jamie Boudreau at his bar Canon in Seattle, USA.

name: Yellow Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
3⁄4 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Bittersweet and sweet 'n' sour, this aperitif is sure to pucker your taste buds for tasty morsels ahead.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Franck Audoux at the Cravan Café Bar in Paris France. This modern-day cocktail is apparently a version of a 1920s cocktail that was popular along the Riviera.

name: Dorado Old Fashioned
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice or large cube).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1⁄2 shot	Galliano L'Autentico liqueur
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Delicately smoky mezcal and agave caramel notes sit well with rich herbal pepperminty liqueur.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Will Benedetto, beverage director at IGC Hospitality Group in New York City, USA.

name: FERT 61
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. TOP with Prosecco.
ingredients:
1 shot	Savoia Americano Rosso
2⁄3 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
review: Grapefruit freshness and delicate underlying bitterness point this towards being a brunch cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in December 2021 at The Spirit in Milan, Italy. And in case you were wondering, "FERT" is the motto of Italy's royal House of Savoy and this cocktail was created using Savoia Americano Rosso. What these four letters are an acronym of has been lost in the mists of time since its adoption as a motto in the late 1600s. However, many say it stands for Foedere et Religione Tenemur, Latin for 'treaty and religion bind us'.

name: Honeyed Maria Theresa
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: A Margarita balanced by honey and with cranberry replacing orange as the fruity support act to the tequila.
history: A riff on Trader Vic's Maria Theresa by yours truly in January 2022.

name: Wedding Bells
garnish: A pair of skewered Luxardo Maraschino Cherries
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1⁄4 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Gin-laced cherry and orange. I've slightly upped the gin from the original recipe to add structure.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Charles Schumann's 1995 book American Bar.

name: Split Apple Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
2⁄3 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
2⁄3 shot	Americano bianco
review: A Neo-Martini that's suitably spirit-forward as befits the Mar"tini" name and apple flavoured with both apple brandy and apple juice.
history: A riff on the 1990s' Appletini created in January 2021 by yours truly.

name: Wow
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
3⁄4 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
3⁄4 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
review: A trio of spirits tamed by a splash of aromatised wine. Temperature of serve is key so be sure to chill your glass and ideally your ingredients well. Although not classic, I like to serve with an orange zest twist.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book. The Savoy recipe calls for Hercules, a sadly long since defunct product that vintage newspaper advertisements for the brand describe as being a "Maté-Wine Apéritif" with an "alcohol strength over 25°." Hence, I've used another wine-based aperitif.

name: Right Charlie
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water
review: Depending on how sweet or tart your sloe gin is, you may want to add 5ml (1/6oz) sugar syrup.
history: Created thanks to a comment by Brandon John, a Discerning Drinker on our Charlie Chaplin cocktail page saying, "Some joints make this with lemon, which I prefer. The lime tends to overpower it a bit." A Charlie Chaplin should be made with lime, at least according the recipe first specified in Albert Stevens Crockett's 1935 The Old Waldorf-Astoria Bar Book. However, it could very well be the best or "right" way to make a Charlie Chaplin, so a Right Charlie.

name: Mexican Monk
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	Amontillado sherry
1⁄4 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
review: A dry and boozy tequila-laced aperitivo/digestivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Eric Alperin at his bar, Varnish in Los Angeles, USA.

name: Heiress
garnish: Mint sprigs bouquet pegged to rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Peppermint Pastille crème de menthe
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	Giffard Crème de Pêche de Vigne liqueur
review: Best enjoyed as an after-dinner cleanser with gin-laced mint, zesty lemon and delicate peach.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2022 by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England who says, "This vintage-style drink is an enhancement of the rather basic Starboard Light from the Café Royal Cocktail Book. A small amount of Giffard's Crème de Pêche de Vigne serves to bridge the lemon and mint flavours, and lends the drink a hint of elegance.

name: Kill-Devil
garnish: Flaming lime lily pad – cut a coin-sized disc of lime peel and carefully cut/scrape away pith. Float the lime peel boat on the surface of the cocktail, then load the hull with 5 drops of white overproof Jamaican rum and ignite with a match. Instruct drinker to wait until the flame has burnt out before taking a sip.
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Rhum Clément Blanc
1⁄3 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄6 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: This is one boozy little devil, but tasty.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2008 by Erin Williams at Pegu Club in New York City, USA.

name: Golden Glow
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
2⁄3 shot	Galliano L'Autentico liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Drambuie liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Chilled water (reduce if wet ice)
review: The original may have been equal parts gin, 30 Galliano and 30 Drambuie but Scotch whisky sits more harmoniously as the base spirit, so harmoniously that I've added a splash more of it.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide.

name: Cherry Bakewell
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
5⁄6 shot	Disaronno amaretto
5⁄6 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
review: I've seen the same cocktail with equal parts amaretto, cherry brandy and vermouth but's a recipe for an overly sweet cocktail – even for a dessert cocktail. If you're after a less alcoholic dessert then omit the brandy from my recipe, but surely every dessert benefits from a splash of brandy?
history: There are numerous Cherry Bakewell recipes, this one created in December 2022 by yours truly.

name: Chicago Mistake
garnish: Orange zest twist expressed and discarded. Garnish with a skewered orange slice wheel & Luxardo Maraschino cherry.
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Ginger liqueur
1 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
5 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
5 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Intensely flavoured with sweet notes balanced by generous dashes of bitters.
history: Josh Morton, owner/founder of Barrow's Intense Ginger Liqueur, introduced me to this cocktail in January 2023, saying, "It's a great low ABV cocktail that came out of me asking a bartender 7-8 yrs ago for an Intense Manhattan - expecting them to substitute out all or part of the vermouth with Barrow's Intense - instead, they replaced the Whiskey. I didn't think it would work but it's amazing - the Punt e Mes make it. It's also how it got its name."

name: Crown Heights Negroni
garnish: Dehydrated blood red orange slice wheel on rim
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Hibiscus (sorrel) liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review: Originally served straight-up but more approachable when served on-the-rocks.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created by Del Pedro at Tooker Alley in Brooklyn, New Yor City and located on the Prospect Heights side of Crown Heights.

One of numerous cocktails named after New York City boroughs or districts within those boroughs. Crown Heights is a neighbourhood in central Brooklyn.

name: Pisco Punch Collins
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	BarSol Mosto Verde Italia Pisco
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Gomme syrup
2 2⁄3 shot	Pineapple soda
review: The classic Pisco Punch reimagined and as a pineapple soda-charged Collins.

name: Flying Dutchman No. 2
garnish: Dehydrated lemon slice wheel on rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
3⁄4 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A genever (hence "Dutchman")-based Monte Cassino. Even with the genever at twice the proportion of rye whiskey in the equal parts Monte Cassino, the genever is overpowered by the other three ingredients in this very pleasant cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2012 by bar manager Brian MacGregor at Jardinière in Hayes Valley, San Francisco, USA.

name: Bentley Continental
preparation: STIR first 2 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 2⁄3 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A lighter, more sporty Bentley.
history: Created in March 2023 by yours truly at the Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: Metropolitan (1884)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ambrato/ambre/amber vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄12 shot	Gomme syrup
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A dry vermouth-forward brandy Manhattan suited to the pre- or after-dinner occasion.
history: Adapted from a recipe in O. H. Byron's 1884 The Modern Bartenders' Guide. Tellingly, this recipe appears beneath two versions of the Manhattan, the first-known recipe for a Manhattan.

name: Si-Güey
garnish: Orange zest twist expressed and discarded
preparation: STIR first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice). FLOAT peated whisky.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄4 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
3 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1⁄4 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
review: Your nose is greeted by zesty orange then, with the first sip, smoky whisky hits your palate. As you work your way through this late-night sipper, so depleting the whisky float as you sip, the flavour of mellowing orangey tequila grows.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created by late bartending legend Sasha Petraske at his Milk & Honey bar in Manhattan, New York City, USA.

The Si-Güey features in the 2016 book Regarding Cocktails, written by Sasha's wife, Georgette Moger-Petraske, as a tribute to her late husband. Pronounced "see-gwehee" and meaning 'yes dude', 'yeah, dude', 'yeah, man', or 'yeah, mate', "si-güey" is a Mexican slang greeting that Sasha and the other bartenders would say to each other during shifts at Milk & Honey. In the book, Michael Madrusan explains why.

name: Rose Negroni
garnish: Orange slice wheel (preferably dehydrated blood red orange)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Lanique Spirit of Rose liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: Just as it says on the tin, a bittersweet floral Negroni.
history: Added to Difford's Guide in April 2023, this is a cocktail promoted by Lanique Spirit of Rose.

name: Waterfront
garnish: Lime wedge on rim & mint sprigs bouquet
preparation: POUR all ingredients into glass and then fill with ice.
ingredients:
2 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
1 shot	Brancamenta
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: Noted for being the cocktail that packs the most Fernet, this is a brilliant brunch pick-me-up or a refreshing and revitalising digestive.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2008 by Damon Boelte for the opening menu of Prime Meats steakhouse and cocktail bar in Brooklyn, New York City (now shuttered).

name: Frozen Passion Fruit Margarita
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with ¾ of a 7oz scoop of crushed ice and pour into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
2⁄3 shot	Passoã passion fruit liqueur
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Sounds like it may be a sweetie but while this cocktail is both blended and fruity, it is comparatively dry. It's also tasty.

name: Sweet Lady No. 2
garnish: Pineapple wedge and skewered Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. DRIZZLE blue curaçao which will bleed through cocktail as it sinks.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
2⁄3 shot	Coconut liqueur (under 35% alc./vol.)
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Blue Curaçao
review: More subtle in flavour and drier than it looks. A summer cocktail for a day beside the pool.

name: Frozen Honey Deuce
preparation: BLEND first 3 ingredients with 6oz scoop of crushed ice and pour into chilled glass. DRIZZLE black raspberry liqueur around the surface. (This will bleed through the cocktail as it sinks.)
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
review: Starts sour and finishes sweet.
history: A frozen riff on Nick Mautone's original Honey Deuce cocktail created in 2016 for the US Open tennis tournament.

name: Italian Fascination
garnish: Express orange zest twist and discard. Float 3 coffee beans.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Galliano L'Autentico liqueur
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 1⁄4 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: Cream mellows the peppermint-led herbal spirituous notes of Galliano with subtle coffee and orange notes.
history: Created in the 1950s/60s by Donato "Duke" Antone, also credited with creating the Harvey Wallbanger cocktail. The Italian Fascination appears in Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide and Mark Torre's 1984 The Bartender's Cherry.

name: Let's Go Bananas No. 2
preparation: POUR all ingredients into glass and the fill glass with ice.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
4 shot	Pineapple soda
review: Just on the sweet side of bittersweet with crowd-pleasing tropical fruit.
history: Adapted from a recipe promoted by Three Cents in 2024.

name: Cherry Tai
garnish: Mint sprigs bouquet and Luxardo Maraschino Cherries
preparation: POUR all ingredients into glass and then fill glass with ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Jamaican aged blended rum with funk
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3 shot	Cherry soda
review: A soda invigorated cherry sour-laced with funky rum.
history: Adapted from a recipe promoted by Three Cents in 2024.

name: Hédoniste
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into a chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄4 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
2 dash	Lemon bitters
review: "A distant relative of the Widow's Kiss," I prefer this cocktail served on the rocks rather than straight-up.
history: Created late 2023/early 2024 by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Ewards MCR, Oxford, England. Jason's original recipe calls for Merlet Soeurs Cerises.

name: Alice in Wonderland
preparation: POUR all ingredients into chilled glass, fill with ice and TOP with cherry soda.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Watermelon liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3 1⁄2 shot	Cherry soda (chilled)
review: Low in alcohol, delicately bittersweet, and delightfully fruity.

name: Afterburner
preparation: POUR all ingredients into glass, swirl to mix, Flambé and then extinguish flame. Please take care and beware of hot glass rim.
ingredients:
1 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe
1⁄2 shot	White overproof rum
1 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
review: A surprisingly smooth and moreish peppermint-laced drink.

name: Alice From Dallas
preparation: Refrigerate ingredients then LAYER in chilled glass by carefully pouring in the following order.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
review: Coffee and orange spiked with tequila. The trio layer well and combine to make a tasty shot (perhaps stir together and sip to savour the experience rather than downing in one).

name: B-52 Shot
preparation: Refrigerate ingredients then LAYER in chilled glass by carefully pouring in the following order.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1⁄2 shot	Irish cream liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
review: Probably the best-known and most popular shot.
history:
A bartender named Peter Fich is most often credited for creating this cocktail in 1977 while working at the Banff Springs Hotel in Alberta, Canada.

The 1977 date of origin fits when cocktail books of the era are checked. For example, the B-52 doesn't make it into Jones' Complete Barguide, published that very year as "The most comprehensive and up to date collection of drink recipes (4,000)." Ten years on, the B-52, B-53, and B-54 all make it into The Bartender's Cherry published 1987.

Apparently, Fich tended to name his cocktail creations after his favourite bands, their songs, or albums - one such band being The B-52s. The band, which formed in 1976, was named after the beehive hairstyle that adorned vocalist Cindy Wilson, the shape of which resembled the nosecone of the B-52 bomber. The Boeing B-52 Stratofortress, a U.S. high-altitude bomber, was built between 1952 and 1962 and entered service as a long-range nuclear bomber. So this layered shot is named after a band, named after a hairstyle, that's named after a bomber. Hence, the roundabout truth is that this shot takes its name from the B-52 bomber.

name: Bentley
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 1⁄2 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters (optional)
review: Dry, spiced wine impregnated with apple - pretty damn good.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Blueberry Tea
preparation: POUR first two ingredients into glass, top up with tea and stir.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Disaronno amaretto
3⁄4 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
Top up with	Breakfast tea (hot)
review: This does indeed taste just as described on the tin.

name: Brainstorm
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1⁄4 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: Dry vermouth balances the sweet notes of Bénédictine over a spirituous Irish whiskey base.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Hugo R. Ensslin's 1917 Recipes for Mixed Drinks (2nd Edition).

name: China Blue
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Kwai Feh lychee liqueur
1 shot	De Kuyper Blue Curaçao
4 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Looks sweet, but due to a generous splash of grapefruit is actually balanced and refreshing.
history: Emerged in Japan in the late 1990s and still popular along the Pacific Rim.

name: Claret Cobbler

My version of an old classic.

For information on the fascinating history of Cobblers please see our page.

name: Caruso Cocktail

history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book, this cocktail was created at The Savoy for the tenor Enrico Caruso in the early 20th century.

The Mimosa was created in 1925 at the Ritz Hotel in Paris, France. The Grand Mimosa benefits from a splash of Grand Marnier liqueur.

name: Irish Alexander

A variation on the Alaska cocktail, the Nome is mentioned in the Alaska cocktail's entry in David Embury's 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks.

Like the Alaska, the Nome is thought to take its name from its golden colour referencing the gold rush. The Alaska Gold Rush started in the Klondike region of the Yukon in Canada but many prospectors left the Klondike for an area around Nome in west Alaska following the discovery of gold there in 1899.

name: Princess Mary

1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao

history:
Created in London during 1922 by Scottish bartender Harry MacElhone to celebrate H.R.H. Princess Mary's marriage to Lord Lascelles. The year after, Harry MacElhone purchased his eponymously named bar in Paris.

The original recipe featured equal parts of all three ingredients and was first published in Robert Vermeire's 1922 Cocktails – How to Mix Them accompanied by a note to its creation, "Harry, of Ciro's Club, introduced this cocktail in honour of Princess Mary's wedding to Lord Lascelles, February, 1922." Harry repeats this recipe and origin a year later in his own book, Harry of Ciro's A B C of Mixing Cocktails.

name: Astoria

2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura

history:
Recipe adapted from Albert Stevens Crockett's 1931 The Old Waldorf-Astoria Bar Book where the recipe is accompanied by the following notation, "After the big annex to the Old Waldorf, which at its opening, in 1897, became the main part of the establishment."

William Waldorf Astor built the original Waldorf Hotel, which opened in 1893, next door to his aunt's home, on the site of his father's mansion and today's Empire State Building. John Astor persuaded his aunt to move uptown and then built the Astor Hotel. The two hotels were connected and the combined Waldorf-Astoria became the largest hotel in the world at the time.

name: Negroni Sbagliato
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly STIR.
ingredients:
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
2 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
review: This lighter-styled Negroni has some bitterness but lacks the gin punch and character of the original Negroni.
history:
Pronounced 'spal-yacht-oh' which in Italian means "bungled" or "mistaken", this drink was created in the late 1980s by Mirko Stocchetti at his Bar Basso in Milan when making a Negroni he apparently mistakenly reached for a bottle of spumante instead of gin. Unlikely as the mistake might sound, it proved inspired and Negroni Sbagliato cocktails are still served at Bar Basso today with spumante (not prosecco). Sadly, Mirko passed away on the 10th of November 2016, but his family continue to run Bar Basso as a living museum of Milanese bar culture.

If you visit Bar Basso (and you should), ask for your Sbagliato to be served in one of the enormous stemmed chalice glasses. Your cocktail may appear daunting but a giant rectangular ice cube will occupy much of the large glass. Mirko designed this chalice himself back in the 1980s and licensed the design to glassmakers WMF, hence you'll also see the same glasses used in many of Milan's other older bars.

What has long been a cocktail known amongst bartenders became a social media sensation in 2022 thanks to a TikTok video posted by HBO to promote their House of the Dragon series with actor Olivia Cooke asking co-star Emma D'Arcy, "What's your drink of choice?" The response, "A Negroni Sbagliato...with prosecco in it."

Being pedantic, a Negroni Sbagliato is properly made with spumante and not prosecco. This is confused by spumante being the Italian term for sparkling wine and prosecco of course being a distinct style of sparkling wine. However, spumante is also a style of sparkling wine, the most famous spumante being Asti Spumante from Italy's Piemonte region. Spumante tends to be sweeter than Prosecco and lower in alcohol strength, 6% to 10.5% alc./vol versus 9% to 11% alc./vol.

2 Dashes French Vermouth.
