3⁄4 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Kirschwasser (cherry) eau-de-vie
review: Sweet brandy meets dry cherry eau-de-vie in this serious vodka-laced cocktail. Contemporary bartenders may prefer to stir this cocktail but it's classically shaken and all the better for it.
history: Believed to be the first vodka cocktail to appear in print, this first appears in a 1911 book, Beverages de Luxe, published in Louisville, USA. It is thought to have originated at the St. Charles Hotel in New Orleans, USA.

name: Rusty Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Drambuie liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Rich herbal, honeyed notes add a Scottish dimension to the classic Cuban cocktail.
history: Created in December 2010 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Very Rusty Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
2⁄3 shot	Drambuie liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Honey and spice notes from honeyed herbal liqueur add interest to this Aged Daiquiri.
history: Created in December 2010 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Royal Toast
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: Rich cherry liqueur flavours are balanced by dry vermouth and lifted by vodka.
history: Adapted from a recipe "by W. E. Edwards" in the 1937 United Kingdom Bartender' Guild Approved Cocktails.

name: Rosie Lassi Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Yoghurt liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Lanique Spirit of Rose liqueur
review: Creamy vanilla yoghurt with floral rose liqueur fortified with vodka.
history: Created in 2011 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room in London, England.

name: Creamy Vanilla Colada
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1 1⁄2 shot	Yoghurt liqueur
6 drop	Vanilla extract/essence
review: Creamy yoghurt married with aged rum and richly flavoured with vanilla.
history:
Inspired by the classic Pina Colada, this was created in 2011 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.
Piña Colada history and recipes

name: Christmas Velvet Alexander
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) and freshly grated nutmeg
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Warninks Advocaat liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Fino sherry
review: Combining advocaat, gin and fino sherry, this is the ultimate stereotypical English Granny's Christmas Cocktail.
history: A Christmas cocktail inspired by the classic gin-based Alexander and the popular Brandy Alexander. Created in October 2011 by yours truly.

name: Chinato Nail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Drambuie liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Mancino Vermouth di Torino Chinato
review: A riff on the Rusty Nail using Barolo Chinato. Perhaps one for whisky and Negroni fans.
history: Created in 2012 by Simon Difford at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Palmetto Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and stain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: The orange bitters are key to balancing and adding depth to the equal parts aged rum and sweet vermouth. However, go easy with those dashes or bitter orange will dominate this complex cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Sicilian Orange Spritz
preparation: POUR prosecco and liqueur into glass. ADD ice. Top with soda.
ingredients:
3 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
2 shot	Blood orange liqueur
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Zesty, bittersweet blood orange with Prosecco effervescence.
history:
Created in 2013 by yours truly for Jamie's Italian bar.

See Spritz cocktail history and more recipes

name: Parma Violet Spritz
garnish: Small pack of Parma Violet sweets
preparation: POUR prosecco and liqueur into glass. ADD ice. TOP with soda.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
1 2⁄3 shot	Crème de violette liqueur
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Inspired by and garnished with mini Parma Violet sweets, this spritz is flavoured with crème de violette liqueur.
history:
Created in 2013 by yours truly for Jamie's Italian Bars.
History of, and other recipes for, the Spritz family of cocktails

name: Santorini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄4 shot	Ouzo
review: Scotch whisky and sweet vermouth combine harmoniously with ouzo providing subtle and complementary aniseed notes.
history:
Created in December 2014 by yours truly as an adaption of a drink called an Islander created by Gary "gaz" Regan which uses Pernod anise.

Santorini is an island in the southern Aegean Sea and I was inspired to use a combination of whisky and ouzo due to being challenged with demonstrating the mixability of scotch whisky to a group of Greek bartenders in Athens.

name: Atta Boy Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄24 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: The orange zest twist makes or breaks this classic, which when properly balanced lets the gin shine supported by herbal vermouth and delicate sweet pomegranate notes.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Kingston Negroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Jamaican-style overproof aged pot still rum
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
review: The huge character of pungent rum is matched with a bittersweet liqueur and sweet vermouth combo. Not for everyone but a Negroni riff worth trying.
history:
Created in 2013 by Joaquín Simó at Pouring Ribbons in New York City, USA.
See: Negroni cocktail history

name: Jack's Godfather Highball
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Tennessee whiskey
2⁄3 shot	Disaronno amaretto
2 1⁄2 shot	Cola (e.g. Coca Cola or Pepsi Cola)
review: Three popular ingredients combine to make the ultimate Italian American highball. Named, appropriately, after the most famous Italian American of the silver screen. (Not Rocky!)
history: Highball cocktails info, history and tips on the perfect serve

name: Rusty Compass cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
3⁄4 shot	Drambuie liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
review: Peaty Islay single malt whisky lightly sweetened and flavoured with heather honey herbal whisky liqueur and cherry brandy, stirred and served on-the-rocks with an orange zest twist adding zestiness.
history: Based on a drink originally made with Compass Box The Peat Monster Malt Scotch Whisky and served straight-up in coupe.

name: Ionian Spritz
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass and lightly stir.
ingredients:
3 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
2 shot	Kleos Mastiha liqueur
1 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: The Greeks and Italians are separated by the Ionian Sea, in this Spritz both countries come together with Italian Prosecco and Greek Mastiha.
history:
Created in August 2015 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.
See: Spritz cocktail history

name: Cordial Inviter
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Giffard Crème de Pêche de Vigne liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: Peach liqueur adds subtle orchard fruit notes to cognac with dry vermouth balancing and added complex wine and botanical complexity.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Connor O'Doherty at The Maven, Leeds, England.

name: Negroni Bianco Bergamotto
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass and stir.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Italicus liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: Dry with wine like-minerality, zesty bergamot and piney gin notes.
history:
Adapted from a drink promoted with the launch of Italicus Rosolio di Bergamotto in the summer of 2017. Our original recipe comprised four equal parts:
20 ml Dry gin
20 ml Luxardo Bitter Bianco
20 ml Italicus liqueur
20 Bianco vermouth

name: Sloe Gin Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Sloe gin comprises such a large part of this cocktail that the style and quality of your sloe gin will dramatically affect the finished cocktail. Choose well and this is a delicious, well-balanced, wintery cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Stan Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Bar Guide.

name: Koko Colada
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 1⁄4 shot	Coconut rum liqueur (35-40% alc./vol.)
1 1⁄4 shot	Pineapple juice
review: A ridiculously simple, three-equal-parts party cocktail, shaken to produce a pineapple and coconut cocktail fortified with rum and crowned with a foamy head. Off-dry and fruity rather than sweet.
history: Adapted from a recipe promoted by Koko Kanu in 2017 consisting of just equal parts liqueur and pineapple juice.

name: Triangle
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
2⁄3 shot	Poire William eau-de-vie
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
review: A bite-sized bittersweet aperitif-style cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2017 by Daniel Seehuusen at Park, Göteborg, Sweden. Daniel's original recipe called for equal parts Suze, Eau de Vie de Poire de Normandie and Cointreau and he named this cocktail after those three French ingredients: Suze, first presented at the Exposition Universelle in Paris in 1889, Cointreau from Angers and Eau de Vie de Poir from Normandy, which when plotted on a map form a triangle.

name: The Windfall
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Birch spirit/birch eau-de-vie
1⁄3 shot	Armagnac brandy
1 2⁄3 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review: An autumnal-sounding cocktail to be enjoyed in place of a Daiquiri at any time of the year. Yes, it's appley with delicate armagnac undertones and complexity, but it is made interesting by the birch spirit, which gives this drink faint pine, almost smoky bacon notes.
history: Created by Katie Stocks in St Albans, England.

name: Witch Hunt Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strega liqueur
review: This boozy after-dinner sipper of a cocktail is also good, and considerably lighter, with the dilution that comes with serving over crushed ice.

name: Carriaggi Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Kirschwasser (cherry) eau-de-vie
1 shot	Strega liqueur
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: The holy trinity - three equal parts: kirschwasser, Strega liqueur and fresh orange juice. The result is surprisingly spirit-forward, fruity and refreshing.

name: Black Rumhattan
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Dark/black/blackstrap rum
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Dark rum adds molasses-like flavours to this Manhattan riff.

name: Martiki
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Coconut water
1⁄6 shot	Mentzendorff Kümmel liqueur
review: Dry and Martini-like. Assertive kümmel flavours pervade a punchy mix of rum and coconut water.
history: Touted as Tiki's answer to the Dry Martini, this cocktail is purported to have originated at the Luau Restaurant in Beverly Hills, California. Coconut water is a later inspired addition by Ricard Godwin in his 2016 The Spirits book, which calls for 60ml rum, 25ml coconut water and 10ml Kummel.

name: Rum N Coke Float
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
2⁄3 shot	Cola syrup (house made)
2⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: A Rum & Coke but not as you know it.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Ryan Chetiyawardana at Dandelyan in London, England.

name: The Witches
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into a chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Akvavit / Aquavit
1 shot	Manzanilla sherry
1⁄2 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
review: Herbal and complex.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Chantal Tseng at Washington D.C.'s Reading Room. Chantal is inspired to create her "literary cocktails" by works of literature, in this case, the eponymous book by Roald Dahl.

name: Tootsie Roll
garnish: Tootsie Roll chew &/or Luxardo Maraschino Cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
12 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: As the name suggests, this spirit-forward penny chew of a cocktail tastes reminiscent of a Tootsie Roll.
history:
Adapted from a 2015 recipe created by Aisha Sharpe in New York City, USA. Another version of this cocktail, also adapted from a recipe by Aisha Sharpe, calls for 60ml aged rum, 12.5ml maple syrup, and 6 drops of chocolate bitters.

For non-USA readers, a Tootsie Roll is chocolate-flavoured caramel candy that's been made in Chicago, Illinois since 1907 and was the first American "penny candy" to be individually wrapped.

name: Irish Shandy
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
2 1⁄2 shot	Lemonade
2 1⁄2 shot	India pale ale (IPA) beer
review: An IPA lemonade-shandy with a splash of Irish charm.

name: Bald Head
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: This could also be termed a "Perfect Martini" and it could be argued that bald is a perfect hairstyle – at least for us baldies.
history: Adapted from a recipe in David A. Embury's 1948 Fine Art of Mixing Drinks.

name: Coffee & Tonic
preparation: POUR first 2 ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir. LAYER coffee by carefully pouring so sits as a on top of drink.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Italicus liqueur
3 1⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
1⁄6 shot	Cold brew coffee
review: Sipping through the bitter layer of coffee is a great start to this lightly bitter-sweet aperitivo.
history: Created in 2019 by Luca Missaglia, Italicus' Global Brand Ambassador.

name: Bergamot Bamboo
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Italicus liqueur
2 1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A bergamot influenced riff on the classic Bamboo that's best enjoyed as an aperitivo.

name: Grand 75
preparation: SHAKE first 2 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Orange and lemon zestiness enlivened with champagne.
history: A cocktail promoted by Grand Marnier which we became aware of in 2019.

name: Southgate
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Underberg/ Brasilberg
review: An Old Fashioned Whiskey Cocktail made with Underburg bitters.
history:
Adapted from a recipe in Albert Stevens Crockett's 1931 book Ol Waldorf Astoria Bar Days:
"Southgate
One-fourth lump Sugar dissolved in one-half pony of Water
Dash of Boonekamp Bitters
One jigger Whiskey
One piece twisted Lemon Peel"

What are today called Underburg bitters were originally called Underburg Boonekamp Bitters and "One-fourth lump Sugar dissolved in one-half pony of Water" is simply sugar syrup.

name: Algonquin Special
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Tawny port
3⁄4 shot	Fino sherry
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A dash of bitters added to this originally two-ingredient cocktail helps tone what is a tasty apéritif or digestif.
history:
Frank Case (1872–1946) owned and managed the Algonquin Hotel on New York's 44th Street during the heyday of the famed Algonquin Round Table and wrote a number of books about the hotel and its Round Tablers who famously dined there. Knowing this puts the following extract from Crosby Gaige's 1941 Cocktail Guide And Ladies' Companion into context.

"Algonquin is an Indian word that in any language means Case, and Case in the Iroquois tongue means Algonquin. Mr. Case has maintained the prestige of his Forty-fourth Street citadel against all and sundry since time practically began. The Great gather there to lunch and the near-great likewise gather to watch our carnivorous literati at feeding time. They shout with glee when Woollcott drops gouts of gravy or currant jelly on his cummerbund and shudder as Kaufman snarls over a slice of pickled watermelon rind.
    Mr. Case gracefully presents the following combination of food and drink.
Dear Crosby:
    In answer to your request, here is a recipe for a drink very popular at our bar. We call it Algonquin Special–a good enough name. If you do not wish to use the word Algonquin, you can call it Continental or Bodega or most anything.
    Algonquin Special
    (A perfect aperitif)
    ½ jigger Dry Sherry
    1 jigger Tawny Port
    Stir with cube ice. Serve in Sherry glass. Squeeze little orange peel.

And here is a snack that will hold together–that is., it's intended entirely for eating purposes instead of half for eating and half to spill on the rug.
    ¾ cup Cream cheese
    ¼ cup Butter
    ¼ cup chopped Anchovies, very fine
    1 teaspoon chopped Chives
    Mix ingredients well together, spread on toast, cut in 1½ inch length and 1 inch wide.
    If you are affluent and can afford to add a dash of caviar to the mixture, it won't hurt it. Without the caviar, it is still delicious.
Yours sincerely,
Frank Case"

name: Trigger's Neck
preparation: POUR all ingredients in ice-filled glass and briefly STIR.
ingredients:
2 shot	Horse with No Name habanero bourbon
4 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: A Horse's Neck With A Kick cowboy style.

name: Eddie Brown
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄6 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
review: Dry gin and dry aromatised wine enriched with the merest splash of apricot liqueur. (Originally made with Kina Lillet so this drink cocktail benefits from being made with a blend of kina-aromatised-wines.)
history: Adapted from a recipe created in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: My Tokyo 1964
garnish: Orange juice & sugar rim & Luxardo maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Japanese blended whisky
2⁄3 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Sipping from the sugar rim, along with the sweet cherry treat, helps balance this slightly sour citrusy cocktail.
history: Adapted from the signature cocktail at Sachi Bar (basement of Pantechnicon) in Belgravia, London, England. This recipe was created in 2021, the year the Covid delayed 2020 Olympic Games were eventually held in a locked-down Tokyo city. The first time the city hosted the games was 1964.

name: The Witch
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄12 shot	Strega liqueur
4 drop	Bob's Coriander Bitters
review: This witch has a sunny disposition and casts a spirit-forward herbal spell.
history: Adapted from a cocktail discovered in 2021 at Hawksmoor, London, England. The original recipe calls for celery bitters.

name: L'Americano Moderno
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
2 shot	Savoia Americano Rosso
4 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1 1⁄3 shot	Elderberry & hibiscus soda
review: Bittersweet with deep herbal and floral flavours.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in December 2021 by Lorenzo Politano at Aleph Rome Hotel in Rome, Italy.

name: Banana Old Fashioned
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
2⁄3 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
6 drop	Bob's Abbotts bitters
review: The banana notes often found in whisky enhanced with a generous splash of banana liqueur. Don't expect a sweetie, despite the liqueur, this remains a dry, spirituous Old Fashioned.

name: Banana Alexander
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: Brandy-laced creamy banana. What's not to like?
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2016 by Kaleb Cribb at Holeman & Finch Public House in Atlanta, USA.

name: Gage Cobbler
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
1 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Dry sherry minerality with a hint of citrus freshness rounded with honeyed berry fruit.
history: A riff on the classic Sherry Cobbler created in 2020 by Azrhiel Frost, bar manager at The Gage in Chicago, USA.

name: Mellow White Negroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄4 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
review: A White Negroni usually consists of equal parts all three ingredients but this "Mellow" rendition has one-sixth parts bittersweet gentian liqueur.
history: Created thanks to a comment (on our White Negroni page) by John McLaughlin, a fellow Discerning Drinker, in search of a mellow Negroni recipe and suggesting the above.

name: Trois Rivières
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Canadian blended whisky
1⁄2 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
review: Similar to a Quebec cocktail and indeed Trois-Rivières is a Canadian city in the province of Quebec.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Bar Guide.

name: Espresso Iced Coffee
preparation: POUR first 2 ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir. TOP with almond (or oat) milk. (In place of cold brew, make espresso coffee ahead of time, leave to cool and chill in a refrigerator.)
ingredients:
1 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1 2⁄3 shot	Cold brew coffee
1 shot	Almond milk
review: A milky iced coffee.

name: Blue Paradise
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Parfait Amour liqueur
review: This is one of those cocktails where the bitter and aromatic oils from the lemon zest twist is crucial to the balance and overall success of the cocktail. This is a hero cocktail for parfait amour so I've upped its proportion at the expense of the aromatised wine, at least when compared to other interpretations (60ml (2oz) cognac, 30ml (1oz) Dubonnet Red, 4 dashes Parfait Amour) which also call for this classic to be shaken.
history: A vintage cocktail saved from obscurity thanks to its inclusion in Ted "Dr. Cocktail" Haigh's Vintage Spirits and Forgotten Cocktails where he says, "It was the creation of Emil Bauwens, head barman at the Bar Saint-James in Brussels and recorded in his book, Livre de Cocktails."

name: Bandelures
garnish: Half lime wheel slice across rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Rhum Clément Blanc
1 1⁄3 shot	Peach aperitif liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Jason's original recipe calls for 45ml (1½oz) rhum agricole and 30ml (1oz) peach aperitif and I suspect used 40% alc./vol. rhum so I have reformulated to account for my use of 50% rhum agricole.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England. Jason describes this as a "Mood-enhancing rhum agricole plaything."

name: Americano Bianco
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Bitter Bianco liqueur
2 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Long and refreshing. Suited as a summer's aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe shared by Richard Christmas in a comment on our White Americano Cocktail page.

name: Sophisticated Dane
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Akvavit / Aquavit
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: Caraway, spice, spirituous and on the bitter side of bittersweet. If you like Negronis and aquavit then this is for you.
history: A riff on the Rye Boulevardier created in 2021 by Zachary Taylor (and shared with other Discerning Drinkers via our Rye Boulevardier page).

name: Kicker
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
3⁄4 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: One man's 'dash' is another's 'splash'. At least that's how I've interpreted the amount of vermouth in this spirit-forward heavily calvados-influenced sipping cocktail. Would also suit being served over a large cube or chunk of block ice.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Whist
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
3⁄4 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: A pleasant spirit-forward after-dinner cocktail, which I prefer with a generous spray from an orange zest twist but that's perhaps straying away from what this classic should be.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Mexican Lover
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Patrón Añejo tequila
5⁄6 shot	Cognac (brandy)
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: A tequila and brandy-based Manhattan. When I first made this cocktail, I concluded that it needed bitters. It doesn't, but if you do add bitters then vanilla, Boker's, or Abbott's all work better than Angostura or similar aromatic bitters.
history: A forgotten cocktail from the 1980s/90s.

name: Mule-mosa
preparation: POUR all ingredients into chilled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed) (chilled)
1⁄2 shot	Ginger liqueur
4 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine (chilled)
review: A Mimosa given a 'kick' and made more interesting by a splash of intense ginger liqueur – hence the "Mule" in the name.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Josh Morton of Barrow's Intense ginger liqueur.

name: Negroni Rosa
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Amaro Santoni
1 shot	Rosé/rosato vermouth
review: Rose vermouth and a delicately floral amaro add floral notes to this pink-coloured Negroni.

name: Greenhorn
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1 shot	Green melon liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
review: Bittersweet melon laced with tequila.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2022 by Bobby Heugel at his Refuge cocktail bar in Houston, Texas, USA.

name: Calvados Spritz
preparation: POUR ingredients all into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
3 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Elderflower and apple brandy sit harmoniously in this punchy spritz. For a slightly sweeter version substitute prosecco in place of the brut sparkling wine.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in February 2023 by Kaitlin Wilkes for Avallen calvados.

name: Washington Apple
garnish: Apple wedge on rim or float dehydrated red-skinned apple slice
preparation: STIR (or shake) all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Canadian blended whisky
1 shot	Sour apple liqueur
1 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
review: Classically equal parts but better with a splash more whisky, this is an easy-to-like, fruity, juicy crowd-pleasing Old Fashioned-style late-night sipper.
history:
There are over 30 varieties of apple grown in Washington state with by far the majority of them being red-skinned. Established in the late 1880s, Washington's apple orchards nestle in the eastern foothills of the Cascade Mountains, at elevations from 500 to 3,000 feet above sea level.

Apples are big business in Washington with some apple orchards covering 5,000 acres and employing 300 farm workers. Some 40,000 pickers are employed during harvest season across the state.

Urban myth has it, this cocktail was created in the late-1980s after pests decimated much of Washington state's apple orchards leading to mountains of unsellable apples. Seeing this as an opportunity, an entrepreneur named Christof Guycoogan fermented and distilled the spoilt apples to make apple liqueur, which he added to his favourited tipple of Canadian whisky with a splash of cranberry juice.

Turns out, one Randy Woodward has written a whole book about this cocktail, titled Washington Apple Drink and self-published in 2021.

name: Passion Fruit Sangria
garnish: Float half fresh passion fruit boat
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Passoã passion fruit liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Rioja (Crianza) red wine
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
review: Just as you'd expect of anything purporting to be a sangria, fruit-laced and easy-drinking.
history: A passion fruit liqueur-influenced riff on a Sangria created in June 2023 by yours truly.

name: Passion Fruit Spritz
garnish: Spoon of passion fruit seeds and pulp on cocktail
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly STIR.
ingredients:
2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
1 1⁄3 shot	Passoã passion fruit liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: This Spritz needs a brut sparkling wine – most proseccos produce an overly sweet cocktail when used in this spritz.

name: Fairbanks
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1 dash	Boker's bitters
review: Spirit-forward rye whiskey (especially if you are following my preference for 50% alc./vol. straight rye) with a hint of spiced apricot fruitiness. If you don't have Boker's Bitters, regular aromatic bitters also work well and help tone the apricot liqueur.
history:
The Fairbanks first appearance in a cocktail recipe book is in J. A. Grohusko's 1908 Jack's Manual, followed by Jacques Straub's 1914 book Drinks.

Charles Warren Fairbanks (1852 - 1918) was an American politician who served as a senator from Indiana before becoming the 26th Vice President of the United States. As an advisor to President William McKinley, he served on a commission to settle the Alaska boundary dispute, and the city of Fairbanks in Alaska and the Fairbanks North Star Borough within which it lies are named after him. As are Fairbanks in Minnesota, Fairbanks in Oregon, and Fairbanks Township in Michigan.

name: Chanler
preparation: Express oils from lemon peel into stirring glass and drop in (regal stir). Add other ingredients, STIR with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 swath	Lemon peel
2 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: Lemon oils add mouthfeel and a delightful flavour, which combine with the botanicals of the gin and vermouth to preset as almost floral.
history: A pre-prohibition cocktail from the Big Brass Rail bar of the original Waldorf Astoria Hotel in New York City USA named after a regular patron, "Sheriff Bob" Chanler. This recipe adapted from Albert Stevens Crockett's 1931 Old Waldorf Astoria Bar Days.

name: Brainstorm (straight-up)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: A reproportioned version of the pre-Prohibition classic Brainstorm, served straight-up rather than on-the-rocks.
history:
The Brainstorm is a classic which first appeared in Hugo R. Ensslin's 1917 Recipes for Mixed Drinks (2nd Edition) and, like so many of Ensslin's recipes, was repeated in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

Both vintage books stipulate that this cocktail is served on-the-rocks. The now more popular straight-up version (recipe above) originated in 2022 by Al Sotack at Jupiter Disco, a science fiction-inspired cocktail bar in Brooklyn, New York City, USA.
Recipe adapted from Hugo R. Ensslin's 1917 Recipes For Mixed Drinks

name: I Should Coco
garnish: Lime slice wheel and serve with a straw
preparation: BLEND ingredients with a 7oz scoop of crushed ice and pour into glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Adriatico Bianco almond milk liqueur
1 shot	Coconut water
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A low-alcohol, almond, coconut and lime, sorbet-like cocktail that's brilliantly suited to a summer's afternoon/early evening.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2022 by our friends at Bellaventura Brands, the folk behind Adriatico Amaretto Bianco.

name: Cocogroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice.)
ingredients:
1 shot	Coconut rum liqueur (35-40% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: Your choice of coconut rum will significantly impact this riff on a classic Negroni; many so-called "coconut rums" are liqueurs or verging on being liqueurs, so add sweetness to this cocktail.

name: Humble Brag
preparation: THROW all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Dry white port
1 1⁄2 shot	Mancino Vermouth di Torino Sakura
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Delicately floral notes from the vermouth sit brilliantly with the grape notes from the port.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Ramón Clark, bar manager at Deep Dive in Seattle, USA.

name: Montana (Hoffman House, 1905)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Anisette liqueur
2 dash	Boker's bitters
review: Liquorice and subtle aniseed from the anisette emerge through the vermouth's herbal notes.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Charles S. Mahoney's 1905 The Hoffman House Bartender's Guide

name: Alice Mine No. 2
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
3⁄4 shot	Mentzendorff Kümmel liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: You'll need to appreciate kummel to enjoy this long-lost classic. However, if you do, the only question is, do you like this cocktail with more or less Scotch whisky?
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Kirchinato
garnish: Skewered blackberries or Luxardo Maraschino Cherries
preparation: POUR first 2 ingredients into glass and STIR. Add prosecco and then fill glass with ice.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Mancino Vermouth di Torino Chinato
1⁄2 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
3 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
review: This is a sunny afternoon cocktail to challenge the Kir and Kir Royale.

name: Winter Americano
preparation: POUR all ingredients into glass and the fill glass with ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3 shot	Mandarin soda
review: A delightfully zesty bittersweet Americano.
history: Adapted from a recipe promoted by Three Cents in 2024.

name: Americano Branco (Ferroviario)
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
1 1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2 1⁄4 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A bittersweet, cleansing and revitalising digestivo.
history: In Italy this is called an Americano Branco and it is under this name that it features in Elvezio Grassi's 1936 book Mille Misture. Although an Italian aperitivo, it is perhaps more popular in Argentina, particularly the cantinas and cafés of Buenos Aires where it is called a Ferroviario or sometimes a "Fernet con Cinzano".

name: Cherry Cooler
garnish: Luxardo Maraschino Cherry and lime wedge
preparation: POUR all ingredients into chilled glass, fill with ice and TOP with cherry soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cachaça
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
3 1⁄2 shot	Cherry soda (chilled)
review: Cachaça fortifies and adds its distinctive grassy notes to this well-balanced, effervescent cherry sour.

name: Black Velvet
garnish: None (unless drinking to celebrate St. Patrick's Day in which case consider a shamrock or mint leaf)
preparation: Slowly POUR ingredients into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Stout beer
2 1⁄2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Full-bodied stout and delicate dry sparkling wine are an unlikely combination but this classic has stood the test of time. Some may wish to add a barspoon of sugar syrup.
history:
This black sombre cocktail is said to have originated at London's Brook's Club (or others say, Shelbourne Hotel in Dublin, Ireland) in 1861, immediately after the death of HRH Prince Albert, husband of Queen Victoria, of typhoid fever on 14th December. Devastated, the Queen wore black for the rest of her life so this drink's shrouding of sparkling wine with black stout is most appropriate.

However, its origins may date back to an 1830s German cocktail called "Menschenfreund" (meaning philanthropist). And perhaps not coincidently, Prince Albert was born in Bavaria, Germany in 1819.

This cocktail first appears in a cocktail tome, named "Champagne Velvet", in Harry Johnson's 1888 New And Improved Bartender's Manual, written in both English and German.

It was enjoyed by the exuberant Otto von Bismarck, the German Chancellor, so much so that this cocktail is also known as a "Bismarck". It is under this name that it appears in Frank Newman's 104 French-language Recettes des Boissons Anglaises et Americaines.

It is not until Frank-Meier's 1936 The Artistry of Mixing Drinks that the name "Black Velvet" tops the recipe, and even then, German-born Meier lists this as a "BISMARCK or BLACK VELVET" with a recipe that calls for a "split bottle of Guinness" – a "split" was the name for small 187.5ml bottle.

name: Brazen Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Bison grass vodka
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Parfait Amour liqueur
review: Not for the faint hearted - a great combination of grassy bison vodka with violet Parfait Amour.

name: Mango Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Citroen Vodka
1 2⁄3 shot	Mango purée
review: This drink doesn't work nearly so well with plain vodka - if citrus vodka is not available, try using gin.

name: Stone & Gravel
preparation: POUR all ingredients into glass filled with crushed ice and briefly churn (stir).
ingredients:
1 shot	White overproof rum
2 shot	Ginger wine
review: Simple, boozy and surprisingly good.
history: A popular drink in Jamaica.

name: Noshino Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Akashi-Tai Daiginjo Genshu sake
1 1⁄2 shot	Shochu/soju
review: If good quality sake and shochu are used then this can be a great drink. However, it lacks the alcoholic bite I associate with a true Martini, so I much prefer this drink when vodka is used in place of shochu.
history: Adapted from a drink discovered in 2007 at Shochu Lounge, London, England.

name: Stratosphere
preparation: POUR liqueur into glass and TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
1⁄4 shot	Crème de violette liqueur
Top up with	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: A sophisticated Kir Royal.
history: Recipe adapted from The Stork Club Bar Book published 1946 in which Lucius Beebe writes, "Leo Spitzel, captain, asserts that a Stratosphere Cocktail will do wonders for you."

name: Chocolate Stinger
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
2 shot	Mozart Chocolate Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe
review: Chocolate and mint served frappé.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2010 by Klaus St. Rainer at Schumann's Bar, Munich, Germany.

name: IPAlicus
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass and lightly stir.
ingredients:
1 shot	Italicus liqueur
4 shot	India pale ale (IPA) beer
review: Take a citrusy hopped beer and add a tad more citrus in the shape of Rosolio di Bergamotto. The result is predictably citrusy, refreshing and suited to the aperitivo moment rather than a night down the Rose & Crown.
history: One of the drinks promoted with the launch of Italicus Rosolio di Bergamotto in the summer of 2017.

name: Ginger Snap (Fino Sherry & Ginger Ale)
garnish: Lemon zest spiral cut with a channel knife
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and lightly stir.
ingredients:
2 shot	Fino sherry
3 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
review: A light and fabulously refreshing summery aperitivo, that's also perfect for Christmas.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2017 by Tony Conigliaro with Schweppes 1738 Golden Ginger Ale.

name: Rye & Dry
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
4 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
history: So named due being straight rye whiskey served with Canada Dry Ginger Ale.

name: Mujer Negra
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & float roasted coffee bean
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: Coffee and cacao flavours shine in this rum-based aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Ian Burrell, London, England.

name: Marconi
garnish: Lemon zest twist expressed and discarded. Adorn with an apple slice/wedge on the rim or float a dehydrated apple slice.
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: Calvados shines in this spirit-forward nightcap that, despite convention, is perhaps better on the rocks.
history:
Named after Guglielmo Giovanni Maria Marconi (1874 – 1937), an Italian electrical engineer and inventor who's best-known for creating a radio wave-based wireless telegraph system and is credited for being the inventor of radio.

Recipe adapted from Jacques Straub's 1913 Manual of Mixed Drinks.

name: It & T
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass & briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Italicus liqueur
4 shot	Mediterranean tonic water
review: Bergamot liqueur and quinine tonic combine harmoniously in this lightly bitter-sweet aperitivo. Mediterranean tonic water brings out attractive mellow herbal notes in the citrusy liqueur.

name: Savoy Tango
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 1⁄3 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
review: Just two ingredients but, as Jason E. Clapham told me, "a drink that is more than the sum of its parts."
history: Adapted from Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book and kindly brought to my attention by Jason E. Clapham of the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford. The fact that Craddock says it originated at The Savoy, but neither takes credit nor credits a colleague, leads me to suspect this cocktail was created by Ada "Coley" Coleman.

name: Casa Savoia Manhattan
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Savoia Americano Rosso
2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
review: The Manhattan meets an aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Giuseppe Gallo, the creator of Savoia Americano.

name: Hard Start
preparation: POUR ingredients into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur (chilled)
1⁄2 shot	Brancamenta (chilled)
review: Bittersweet, invigorating, and refreshing, it is good served at room temperature but better when the ingredients and glass are chilled.
history: Inspired by his earlier Waterfront, the Hard Start was created in 2009 by Damon Boelte when beverage director at Prime Meats in Brooklyn, New York City. This two-ingredients shot originated during a challenging brunch service when the restaurant's general manager, Bill Mann, who was working a hangover, asked Damon for a pick-me-up. After drinking the shot, Bill said it should be named after the method of starting a bike with a dead battery by rolling down a hill, putting it in gear and popping the clutch. (What we Brits call a 'bump start'.) Hence, Damon named his new shot the Hard Start.

name: Ting 'n' Sting or Ting Wray
preparation: POUR ingredients into chilled glass and fill with ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	White overproof rum
4 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Pink Grapefruit soda
review: Overproof rum sits well with anything fruity, in this case, with a zing of zesty grapefruit. Bring on the sun, sand and the sounds.
history: Ting is a carbonated soft drink flavoured with grapefruit juice (from concentrate) and, in Jamaica, it is often mixed with Wray & Nephew overproof rum to make a Ting Wray or a Ting 'n' Sting. It is also mixed with citrus-flavoured vodka to create a Ving. As they'd say on the BBC, "other brands of grapefruit soda and overproof rum are available."

name: The Lady Wears Red
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. FLOAT champagne foam made by macerating orange zests in champagne overnight, adding gelatin and charging with N2O siphon.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1⁄4 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄6 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄6 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: This 'Lady' is high maintenance but she delivers a complex reward.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2008 by Ben Carlotto at The Voodoo Rooms, Edinburgh, Scotland. The original recipe calls for homemade dry orange syrup made by macerating orange zests in a blend of different sugars with Lillet Blanc and fino sherry. It also calls for homemade citrus bitters, a complex mixture of kaffir lime leaves, various citrus elements, and spices like cardamom and cassia.

name: Mulled Wine
preparation: POUR ingredients into pre-warmed glass and stir.
ingredients:
5 dried	Clove
1 pinch	Freshly grated nutmeg
1 pinch	Cinnamon powder (ground)
1 1⁄2 shot	Tawny port
1 1⁄2 shot	Shiraz red wine
1 wedge	Orange (fresh)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 barspoon	Honey
1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
Top up with	Boiling water
review: Warming, soothing and potent. Better if several servings are made at the same time and the ingredients mixed together and warmed in a saucepan.

name: Behemoth
garnish: Lemon zest twist and drops of walnut bitters on the foam
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Bourbon whiskey
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2⁄3 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
2⁄3 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed) (optional)
1⁄3 shot	Maple syrup (optional)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Tangy, citrus bourbon with a hint of chocolate.
history: This 'monstrous beast' was created in 2004 by yours truly and 'improved' in December 2021.

name: Long Island Spiced Tea
preparation: SHAKE first seven ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with cola, stir and serve with straws.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Chairman's Reserve Spiced Rum
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
Top up with	Cola (e.g. Coca Cola or Pepsi Cola)
review: A contemporary spicy twist on the American classic Long Island Iced Tea.

name: Sandstorm
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Vanille de Madagascar
1 1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Lime cordial (sweetened lime juice)
review: A long, fruity drink featuring well balanced sweet and sourness.
history: Created in 2003 by James Cunningham at Zinc, Glasgow, Scotland, and is named for its cloudy yellow colour.

name: Vampiro
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 shot	Tomato juice
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
7 drop	Hot pepper sauce (red)
1 pinch	Salt (sea salt)
1 grind	Black pepper
review: Something of a supercharged Bloody Maria with a hint of sweet grenadine.
history: The national drink of Mexico where it's often made with pomegranate juice in place of tomato juice and without the grenadine.

name: Habanero
preparation: MUDDLE ginger and chilli in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine-strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 slice	Red chili pepper (jalapeño/fresno chili (10,000 SHU) deseeded) (fine sliced)
1 slice	Fresh ginger root (thumbnail-sized slice)
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Drambuie liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 barspoon	Honey sugar syrup
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: A Daiquiri-style drink with honey, ginger and chilli.
history: Created in 2008 by Giuliano Morandin at The Bar at The Dorchester Hotel, Hotel, London, England.

name: Machine Head
garnish: Luxardo Maraschino cherry & orange zest twist
preparation: POUR all ingredients except tea into mixing glass. SMOKE tea using a chefs smoker and direct smoke into mixing glass. Cover to capture smoke for a minute or so. Remove cover, STIR with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Crème de violette liqueur
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 dash	Xocolatl mole bitters
3 pinch	Lychee rose tea (smoked)
review: Overdo the smoke and your cocktail will start to resemble a cigar. Too little and you may find a tad sweet.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2010 by Jamie Boudreau at Vessel, Seattle, USA.

name: Le Jardin
preparation: SHAKE first 7 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
4 fresh	Blueberries (fresh)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1 dash	Bob's Lavender Bitters
2 1⁄2 shot	Rosé champagne

name: Bloody Caesar

4 shot	Clamato juice
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
7 drop	Hot pepper sauce (red)
3 dash	Worcestershire sauce
2 pinch	Celery salt
2 grind	Black pepper
review: A peculiarly Canadian fishy twist on the classic Bloody Mary.
history:
Virtually every bar in Canada can make you a Bloody Caesar, it's pretty much Canada's national drink. It may seem odd that a drink invented in Canada took the name of Rome's most famous emperor, but though its origins are Canadian its inspiration is very much Italian.

Charged with inventing a signature drink to celebrate the opening of Marco's Italian restaurant at the Calgary Inn in 1969, Walter Chell was inspired by the flavours of Spaghetti Vongole (spaghetti with clams) and named his new cocktail after the Roman emperor.

The typical finish to what Canadians simply call a Caesar is to wet the rim with lemon juice and then dip the glass in celery salt. However, the Caesar actually lends itself to an array of garnishes. Celery and a lime wedge are more traditional, but since the Caesar has become so popular, restaurants and bars have felt the need to customise the garnish to make their version unique, adopting anything from olives and peppers to pickled asparagus and shrimp. Some drinks end up looking more like an appetiser! I've gone for the elegant and deliciously crunchy green bean to garnish ours.

garnish: Small stuffed dead parrot that's passed on, no more, expired and gone to meet 'is maker, a stiff, bereft of life, rests in peace, pushing up the daisies, off the twig, kicked the bucket, shuffled off 'is mortal coil, run down the curtain and joined the bleedin' choir invisible. preparation: BLEND all ingredients with crushed ice and serve with straws.

history:
Created in July 2014 by yours truly after watching Monty Python's famed Dead Parrot Sketch performed by John Cleese and Michael Palin at London's O2 arena.

The use of Lysholm Linie Aquavit and the cocktail's colour is inspired by the "Norwegian Blue" parrot while gin represents British humour. The coconut and loose colada theme comes from the late 1960s/70s when the sketch was originally performed.

In the sketch, the disgruntled customer Mr Praline (played by Cleese) returns a "Norwegian Blue" parrot to the shopkeeper (Michael Palin) explaining, "That parrot is definitely deceased, and when I purchased it not 'alf an hour ago, you assured me that its total lack of movement was due to it bein' tired and shagged out following a prolonged squawk."

name: White Lion
preparation:
1. Peel the zest from the lime prior to squeezing and express 3 zest twists into shaker (also drop spent zests into shaker).
2. Add sugar and lime juice.
3. MUDDLE lime zests with sugar and mix with lime juice until sugar is dissolved.
4. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
3 twist	Lime zest (peel)
3 barspoon	Powdered sugar (white sugar ground in mortar and pestle) (or use 5ml of 2:1 sugar syrup per spoon)

1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Raspberry (framboise) sugar syrup
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
history:
Adapted from the first-known appearance of this recipe in Jerry Thomas' 1862 The Bar-tenders Guide and then repeated in his 1876 and 1887 editions. Jerry Thomas original recipe is for a built drink which does not call for Angostura Bitters. The White Lion first becomes a shaken drink with the addition of Angostura in Jacques Straub's 1913 Straub's Manual of Mixed Drinks (which stipulates 3 dashes Angostura Bitters and 3 dashes raspberry syrup).

Similar White Lion recipes to Jerry Thomas' specification appear in Leo Engel's 1878 American and Other Drinks and Harry Johnson's 1882 and 1888 Harry Johnson's Bartender's Manual, his 1888 edition with the added note "This drink is known for a great number of years in South America." [sic]

This cocktail also features in O.H. Byron's 1884 The Modern Bartender's Guide, George Kappeler's 1895 Modern American Drinks, and then morphs into a quite different White Lion in David Embury's 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks.

name: Three Lions (on the shirt)

review:
A blue-rinsed riff on the Tarling's 1933 competition winning Red Lion, created with the hope of celebrating another English win. There is one orange-flavoured liqueur for each of the three lions. Sip between singing choruses of
"It's coming home, it's coming home,
It's coming football's coming home
It's coming home, it's coming home
It's coming football's coming home."
history:
Created in July 2021 by yours truly and named after the Three Lions song, in turn, named after the emblem of the England football team, worn on the player's shirts since the first international against Scotland in 1872.

Along with the three lions, England's team logo depicts ten rosettes, symbolising the rose of Lancaster, the official emblem of England. Fortuitously, the English Football Association also resides at London's Lancaster Gate. There are ten rosettes to represent the ten regions with a seat on the FA Council.

The three lions emblem derives from the Royal Arms of England, which originated with Richard I (1189–1199), the first of the Plantagenet kings who ruled from 1154. Better known as King Richard the Lionheart, the three lions represented his positions as King of England, Duke of Normandy, and Duke of Aquitaine. The three lions appeared on the Royal Arms of every succeeding monarch.
