3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A herbal honeyed Gin Sour.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in November 2021 by Leandro DiMonriva, The Educated Barfly.

name: Banana Between the Sheets
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A rum and cognac-laced banana sour with far more sophistication than the name might suggest.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Chip Tyndale at Dutch Kills in New York City, USA.

name: Beijo Sour
preparation: MUDDLE raspberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5 fresh	Raspberries
1 2⁄3 shot	Cachaça
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Crème de Framboise
1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A cachaça sour with raspberry and pineapple.
history: Beijo is Brazilian Portuguese for 'kiss'.

name: Pumpkin Toddy
preparation: POUR all ingredients into a preheated glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Applejack brandy
1⁄4 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Pumpkin spice syrup
1⁄4 shot	Maple syrup
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 2⁄3 shot	Boiling water
review: An apple brandy and rye whiskey sour sweetened with pumpkin syrup and maple syrup, lengthened and heated with boiling water.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2008 by Jane Danger at PDT in Manhattan, New York City. First published in Jim Meehan's 2011 The PDT Cocktail Book.

name: Apple Mojito
preparation: ADD first 5 ingredients to glass and two-thirds fill with crushed ice. CHURN (stir) with bar spoon and then FILL glass with more crushed ice. TOP with apple soda, briefly stir and serve.
ingredients:
12 fresh	Mint leaves
1 1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Apple Schnapps liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 1⁄2 shot	Sparkling apple juice
review: An enduring classic given a touch of apple. Those with a sweet tooth may want to add more apple liqueur or even a dash of sugar syrup.
history:
Recipe by yours truly in 2005.
Mojito Cocktail history.

name: Banana Boomer
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Pineapple juice
review: Fortified bubble gum for the young at heart.

name: Basil Grande
preparation: MUDDLE strawberries and basil leaves in shaker base. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into glass. Dust with black pepper.
ingredients:
4 fresh	Strawberries (hulled, small & ripe)
4 fresh	Basil leaves
3⁄4 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
3⁄4 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
review: Fruity, with interest courtesy of the basil and a grind of pepper.
history: Created in 2001 by Jamie Wilkinson at Living Room, Manchester, England.

name: Club Cocktail (Butt's recipe)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice & fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Syrup from Luxardo Maraschino Cherries
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
3⁄4 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: An aromatic, spirited, classical cocktail.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2002 by Michael Butt at Milk & Honey, London, England.

name: Alfonso (Special)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄6 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Dry yet slightly sweet with hints of orange, gin and warm spice.
history: A vintage cocktail of unknown origin that features in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book, William "Cocktail Bill" Boothby's posthumously published 1934 World's Drinks And How To Mix Them; and Victor J. Bergeron's 1972 Trader Vic's Bartender's Guide Revised.

name: Estes
preparation: MUDDLE raspberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 3⁄4 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
1 3⁄4 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Agave syrup
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
7 fresh	Raspberries
review: This rich, fruity long drink is a real crowd pleaser.
history: Created in 2005 by Henry Besant and Andres Masso, London, England, and named in honour of Tomas Estes.

name: French Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Gold rum (1-3 years old pot & column blend)
2⁄3 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 shot	Pineapple juice
8 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters (optional)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A classic Daiquiri made fruity with the addition of black raspberry liqueur and pineapple juice.
history: A riff on the French Martini created in 2009 by yours truly for Charlotte Ashburner, then UK brand manager of Chambord liqueur. Revisited and rebalanced in July 2024.

name: Golden Dawn
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. Carefully POUR grenadine into centre of drink so that it sinks to create a sunrise effect.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄12 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: Although it spoils the sunrise effect, this drink is less tart if the syrup lying on the bottom is stirred into the drink (or, better, included when shaking).
history: Created in September 1930 by Tom Buttery at the Berkeley Hotel, London and first published in William J. "Billy" Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Bar Book. There are now many versions of this classic cocktail (David Embury's The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks lists three), the above recipe is my favourite.

name: Electro Batida
garnish: Desiccated coconut and dehydrated lime wheel
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled coconut shell or collins glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cachaça
1⁄3 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
3 shot	Coconut water
1⁄4 shot	Hazelnut sugar syrup
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Cachaça and coconut water with a touch of hazelnut, lime and subtly smoky mezcal.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2014 by Jorge Balbontin, Vantguard Brand Development Manager.

name: Northern Lights
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bison grass vodka
3⁄4 shot	Apple Schnapps liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Aniseed (anise) liqueur
1 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Wonderfully refreshing: apple and anise served up on a grassy vodka base.
history: Created in 2003 by Stuart 'Holiday' Hudson at MJU Bar, Millennium Hotel, London, England.

name: Pilgrim Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Pimento dram/Allspice liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Whether you serve this hot or cold, it's a delicately spiced drink to warm the cockles.

name: Prickly Pear Mule
preparation: SHAKE first five ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with ginger beer.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Pear & cognac liqueur
1 1⁄4 shot	Poire William eau-de-vie
3 shot	Pear juice (freshly pressed)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
Top up with	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: Subtle pear with ginger spice. Fill the glass with ice and go easy on the ginger beer which can predominate and overpower the pear.
history:
Created in 2002 by yours truly (Simon Difford).

A detailed history of the Moscow Mule cocktail, of which this drink is a variant, can be found on our page.

name: Princess Marina
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄2 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄2 shot	Swedish Punsch liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Chilled water
review: Delicate yet loaded with alcohol and flavour.
history: Created in the late 1920s/early 1930s and named after the Princess Marina, the late mother of The Duke of Kent, Prince Michael of Kent and Princess Alexandra.

name: Reef Juice
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Navy rum (54.5% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: The Reef takes no prisoners! Tangy, fruity, and dangerously moreish.
history: Charles Tobias, the original proprietor of Pusser's Rum, created this drink at the Beach Bar in Fort Lauderdale, Florida. It was a favourite of a friend who crashed his boat on a reef.

name: Sloppy Joe
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A well-balanced combination of sweet and sour.
history:
One of two vintage cocktails that variously appear under the names of Sloppy Joe or Sloppy Joe's. They either originate from or are named after Sloppy Joe's, a famous bar in Havana, Cuba during the 1930s. Ernest Hemingway was a regular and Sloppy Joe's inspired the fictitious Freddy's Bar in his novel To Have and Have Not.
Adapted from a recipe in Stanley M. Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Barguide.

name: Screaming Banana Banshee
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with 6oz scoop of crushed ice and serve with straws.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1 1⁄2 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1 1⁄2 shot	Milk (whole milk/full 3-4% fat)
1⁄2 fresh	Banana (preferably overripe)
review: An alcoholic banana and chocolate milkshake - not too sweet.
history: Without the vodka, this is a plain Banana Banshee.

name: Tilt
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. TOP with bitter lemon.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple flavoured vodka
1⁄2 shot	Coconut rum liqueur (35-40% alc./vol.)
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
Top up with	Thomas Henry Bitter Lemon
review: With a totally tropical taste.

name: Toffee Apple Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Sour apple liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Caramel Toffee liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review: Brandy, gin and vodka-laced apple and rich caramel toffee.
history: Created in 2003 by yours truly.

name: Turkish Delight Cocktail
preparation: DRY SHAKE (without ice) all ingredients. SHAKE again with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄6 shot	Rose water
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Rosewater, honey, chocolate and vanilla provide a distinct flavour of Turkish Delight - fortified with vodka.
history: Created in 2003 by yours truly in London, England.

name: Warsaw Cooler
preparation: STIR honey with vodka in base of shaker until honey dissolves. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bison grass vodka
1⁄2 shot	Chairman's Reserve Spiced Rum
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: Orange, honey, apple and spice laced with Polish Bison grass vodka.
history: Created in 2002 by Morgan Watson of Apartment, Belfast, Northern Ireland.

name: Watermelon Cosmo
preparation: Cut watermelon into 16 segments, chop the flesh from one segment into cubes and MUDDLE in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 slice	Watermelon (fresh)
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Citroen Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Watermelon liqueur
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: It looks a tad pinkier than a standard Cosmo and tastes just as the name suggests.
history: Created in 2003 by Eric Fossard at Cecconi's, London, England. One of many variations on the Cosmopolitan to emerge in the late 1990s and early 2000s.

name: Darlington
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄3 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Blue Curaçao
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Aquamarine blue, this delicately fruity gin-based cocktail is dried by a splash of vermouth and soured by lemon juice.
history: In William James "Billy" Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Cocktail Book (Coronation Edition), the invention of this cocktail is credited to J. B. O'Brien. Made to the proportions specified in Tarling's book, the above recipe would only have 5ml (1/6oz) sugar syrup.

name: Royal Gingersnap
garnish: Cinnamon & sugar rim with orange zest twist (flamed)
preparation: MUDDLE the cherry in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 whole	Maraschino cherry (from jar in syrup)
2 shot	Canadian blended whisky
1 barspoon	Orange marmalade
1⁄4 shot	Ginger liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Riff on an Old-Fashioned.
history: Created by Dale DeGroff, this recipe is adapted from his 2008 book The Essential Cocktail.

name: Thai Red Daiquiri
preparation: MUDDLE pepper in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 slice	Red bell pepper
3 fresh	Basil leaves (thai)
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Coconut water
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Created in December 2008 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.
history: Aged rum, delicately spiced by red pepper and basil.

name: You've Got Mail
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with sparkling wine.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cachaça
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄4 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1 2⁄3 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Superbly refreshing - cachaça and citrus with flavoursome honeyed richness, invigorated with sparkling wine.
history: Adapted from Dave Wondrich's riff on the classic Airmail.

name: East India House
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄3 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄12 shot	Pineapple sugar syrup
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Dry and challenging - rewarding for some.
history: A variation of Harry Johnson's East India Cocktail, Johnson could have also created this in the 19th century. However (as far as I'm aware), a recipe titled East India House doesn't appear in print until Charles H. Baker Jr.'s 1939 The Gentleman's Companion, and this is close to what other vintage books call an East India No. 2 (without the rum in the recipe above).

name: Elysian
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Maple syrup
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
3 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Dry and aromatic, although not for all tastes.
history: Created in 2004 by Mickael Perron at Millbank Lounge Bar, London, England.

name: Fuego Manzana No.2
garnish: Small red chilli (warn drinker not to eat)
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE (just press) chilli pepper in base of shaker to release its flavour. (If you muddle hard then the finished cocktail will be overly spicy). Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 slice	Red chili pepper (jalapeño/fresno chili (10,000 SHU) deseeded)
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	Apple Schnapps liqueur
1 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A hint of chilli heat adds interest to an Apple Margarita, creating a full flavoured contemporary classic.
history: Created by Danny Smith at Che, London, England, initially using rum instead of tequila. 'Fuego Manzana' is Spanish for Fire Apple.

name: The Horseshoe Sling
preparation: SHAKE first five ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
Top up with	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Like its creator, this is upfront and refreshingly different.
history: Adapted from a drink created by Gary "gaz" Regan, New York, USA.

name: Maya Margarita
garnish: Pink river salt rim & lime wedge
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1⁄2 shot	Agave Sec liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Calamansi juice (optional)
review: A tasty Margarita with Grand Marnier, Agave Sec liqueur and orange juice.
history: Created in 2010 by Rob Jameson at Maya Bar, Shanghai, China.

name: The Mulberry
preparation: STIR jam and gin in base of shaker to dissolve jam. Add mint, Pimm's and lemon juice, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with elderflower pressé.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 barspoon	Mulberry jam
7 fresh	Mint leaves
1 shot	Fruit cup liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
Top up with	Elderflower pressé
review: Jammy mulberry fruit, Pimm's and gin freshened with mint and lemon, served on the rocks.
history: Created in 2006 at The Manor House Hotel, Moreton-in-Marsh, Gloucestershire, England. The Manor House Hotel make their mulberry jam using fruit from the Mulberry Tree which grows in the hotel's grounds and is thought to be over 350 years old.

name: Raspberry Smoothie
preparation: BLEND ingredients with a scoop of crushed ice. Pour into glass and serve immediately with straws.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Yoghurt liqueur
3 barspoon	Honey
8 fresh	Raspberries
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Crème de Framboise
1 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review: This soft pink, creamy yoghurt drink is loaded with raspberry fruit and laced with vodka.
history: Created in 2011 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Strawberry Smoothie (Alcoholic)
preparation: BLEND ingredients with 12oz scoop of crushed ice. Pour into glass and serve immediately with straws.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Yoghurt liqueur
3 barspoon	Honey
5 fresh	Strawberries (hulled, small & ripe)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Fraise des Bois liqueur
1 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review: This radiantly coloured creamy strawberry yoghurt drink is sweetened with honey and 'hardened' with vodka.
history: Created in 2011 by yours truly (Simon Difford) at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: The Colonial Cooler
preparation: STIR first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP up with soda.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Amer Picon
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Basically a Gin and It lengthened with soda and spiced with dashes of Amer Picon, Angostura bitters and orange curaçao.
history:
This recipe is adapted from Charles H. Baker's 1939 The Gentlemen's Companion in which Baker explains that he encountered this drink in mid-1920s at the Sandakan Club, North Borneo, during an excursion from the SS Resolute, a round-the-world steamer.

The steamer anchored some 14 miles off shore and Baker and his companions set ashore in two lifeboats, both of which failed to make dry land due to engine trouble. A Borneo prahu "with a sail like a striped butterfly and a gent in a G-string and a headdress" raised the alarm and the adventurers were eventually towed ashore by a British North Borneo Company tug.

"We first went out to the Sandakan Club - there'd be a British Club on Mount Everest if 2 Britishers could stand the cold there! - and had these Coolers, through the courtesy of an American who was sentimental enough to fetch a mint root out with him.

"To 1 jigger of dry gin add the same of Italian vermouth. To this base donate 1 dash of each. Angostura and Amer Picon, and 1 tsp of orange Curaçao. Stir with a goodly lump of ice in a small highball or sour glass, and top off with a squirt of soda garnished with 2 sprigs of mint and a stick of ripe pineapple."

name: Fen Ella
preparation: MUDDLE fennel in stirring glass. Add other ingredients, STIR with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
15 dried	Fennel seeds
2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄2 shot	Apple Schnapps liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄6 shot	Pastis
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Fennel and pastis freshen and delicately flavour Scotch with the merest hint of apple. Best made by infusing the fennel with the scotch whisky for a week or so rather than muddling.
history: Created in July 2013 by Simon Difford at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Punch Back
garnish: Pineapple wedge on rim with cherries on stick
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 shot	Cachaça
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 shot	Coconut water
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Cachaça is the raw, spirity love interest in this rum based coconut and lime punch.
history: Created in May 2013 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England for the National Aids Trust.

name: Pale Charlie
preparation: SHAKE first five ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with ale.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
3 shot	Pale ale
review: Zesty, fruity and refreshing with berry and stone fruit accompanying lime and grapefruit with hoppy pale ale.
history:
Created in 2013 by Michele Mariotti at The American Bar at The Savoy Hotel, London. Michele was one of five finalists in the diffordsguide Beer-tail Competition for London Cocktail Week 2013 held on Friday 9th August 2013 at Simon Difford's Cabinet Room in London.

Michele's drink was inspired by Charlie Chaplin's stay at the Savoy in 1889.

name: Port of Spain cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄2 shot	Pimento dram/Allspice liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Unusual in its bold use of a half shot of Angostura Bitters. In Knee High Bar in Seattle, USA I've tried this cocktail made with a massive one-and-a-half shots. However, half a shot seems more than generous.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2013 by Kyle Mathis at Taste Bar, St. Louis, Missouri, USA.

name: Dirty(ish) Banana cocktail
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with 6oz scoop crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cachaça
1 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1⁄2 fresh	Banana (preferably overripe)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Coffee liqueur, banana and cream laced with cachaça and blended to a creamy icy consistency.
history: Created in 2015 by Jorge Balbontin of Vantguard, Barcelona, Spain.

name: Black Jack
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Byrrh Grand Quinquina
1⁄2 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1⁄2 shot	Amer Picon
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
4 drop	Bob's Liquorice bitters
3⁄4 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: For us Brits, this cocktail rekindles memories of the tuck shop and a black tongue from chewing on far too many Black Jacks. Happily, booze now takes the place of the sugar rush.

name: Le Sang Et Sable
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
2⁄3 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Blood orange juice
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Reminiscent of a cognac-based Blood & Sand.
history: Adapted from a recipe by Toby Cecchini in New York City, USA.

name: Blue Nightcap
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Amontillado sherry
1⁄3 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
1⁄3 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
1⁄2 barspoon	Honey
1 dash	Black walnut bitters
review: Two different sherries, honey and coffee combine with cognac and walnut bitters to produce an after dinner cocktail.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2015 by Vito Nicotra at King Schulz Bar, Kassel, Germany.

name: Velvet Roof
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	Americano bianco
1⁄2 shot	Ginger liqueur
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Cranberry liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Rich berry notes and subtle ginger compliment cognac freshened with lemon and dry aperitif.
history: Created by Adam Murphy at Tavern 219, Palatine, IL, USA

name: Papa Noel
garnish: Cinnamon stick (& originally with a sugar rim)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Honey sugar syrup
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Cognac, aromatic dry vermouth, rich honey, lemon juice and crème de banana with a dash of Angostura.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Vlachakis Marios at A for Athens, Athens, Greece. Vlachakis’ original recipe calls for Martell XO and Martini Ambrato vermouth.

name: Red Head
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Averna Amaro
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Fraise des Bois liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Lavender sugar syrup
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
4 drop	Bob's Lavender Bitters
review: A bittersweet aperitif style cocktail with light strawberry and delicate lavender notes.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Miran Chauhan at The Bon Vivant, Scotland.

name: French Riviera
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 barspoon	Apricot jam (preserve)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Cognac provides the French influence and golden rum the sunny warmth with flavours of apricot, honey and lemon.
history: Created in 2015 by Tom Byrne at Charlotte's W4, Chiswick, London, England.

name: L'apocalypse Ultime (The ultimate Apocalypse)
preparation: STIR first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄3 shot	L'Esprit De June Liqueur
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
2 dash	Boker's bitters
Top up with	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: This cognac and champagne cocktail is dry and boozy with hints of zesty orange.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Alexander Sourmpatis at Spinte at The Whisky Bar, Thessaloniki, Greece. Alexander’s original recipe calls for Martell Cordon Bleu cognac.

name: Chocolat a l'orange (Orange Chocolate)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into a large brandy balloon over a chunk of block ice.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1⁄3 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
5⁄6 dash	Bob's Chocolate bitters
1 whole	Cinnamon stick
1 fresh	Orange peel
review: Cognac stirred with aromatised wine, rich orange liqueur with subtle chocolate, cinnamon and zesty orange.
history: Adapted from a 2015 recipe by Jan Kosler at The Celtic Manor Resort, Coldra Woods, The Usk Valley, Wales. Jan’s original recipe calls for Martell XO Cognac.

name: Yellow Submarine
garnish: Rim glass with fine ground dried parsley and Himalayan salt. Garnish with yellow beet pickles.
preparation:
SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.

Special Ingredient #1 - Yellow Juice with 2 parts yellow beetroot to 1 part yellow bell pepper and 1 part yellow tomato
Special Ingredient #2 - Pepper Falernum made with 1 chile de arbol, 1 jalapeno and 1 bottle Velvet Falernum. Coarsely chop 1 chile de arbol and 1 jalapeno and infuse with a bottle of velvet falernum for 3 days. Strain and re-bottle.
Special Ingredient #3 - Pink Saline Solution. Combine 5 parts water to 1 part Himalayan pink salt. Stir to dissolve and store in a dropper bottle.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
1 1⁄6 shot	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	*Special ingredient #2 (see above)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
4 drop	*Special ingredient #3 (see above)
history: Created in 2016 by Gui Jaroschy, Bars Director for Freehand Hotel and Bar Lab for Patrón Tequila at London Cocktail Week.

name: Hwachae
preparation: Place white rum, watermelon, and pineapple in a shaker and hand blend for 5-10 seconds. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with beer.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
1⁄2 shot	Maple syrup
3 wedge	Watermelon (fresh)
3 wedge	Pineapple (fresh)
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄2 shot	Pilsner lager
review: Who'd have thought watermelon, pineapple, beer, rum, maple syrup and lemon would work so well together? Unusual and refreshing.
history: Singaporean Bacardí Legacy 2016 winning cocktail by Bannie Kang of Anti:dote in Singapore.

name: Reborn Padre Blanco
preparation:
SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice), add beer and pour into glass. Finish with a pinch of salt on top.

*Special ingredient #1: Guava & agave nectar pre-mix
ingredients:
2 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
1 1⁄2 shot	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
5⁄6 shot	Pilsner lager
1 pinch	Salt (sea salt)
review:
"Reborn Padre Blanco is dedicated to Ernest Hemingway who loved to drink a classic Daiquiri from the El Floridita Bar in Cuba. Reborn is a term referring to any person or anything that has existed already, and this year Padre Blanco - my 'Legacy' drink from last year - is reborn with Bacardí Carta Blanca rum and guava to complement the spirit and to represent the fruit bats which Amalia Bacardi insisted were used as a symbol of good health, wealth and family unity. I used agave nectar as Hemingway was a diabetic, and lime balances the sweetness. Egg white and lager symbolize a celebration, refreshment and a new life."

We say: For the "guava & agave nectar pre-mix" we used 30 ml Rubicon guava and 15 ml agave. The finished drink was very fruity, just a smidgeon on the sweet side of balanced but a splash more beer tamed the fruitiness and brought the drink together.
history: Hong Kong BACARDÍ LEGACY 2016 winning cocktail by Kervin Unido, Mr & Mrs Fox.

name: The Optimist
preparation: RINSE chilled glass with Yellow Chartreuse and set aside. SHAKE other ingredients with ice and fine strain into rinsed glass.
ingredients:
1⁄12 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
2 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Ginger syrup
1⁄6 shot	Honey sugar syrup
8 fresh	Basil leaves
history: Hong Kong Bacardí Legacy 2015 winning cocktail by Devender Sehgal, Otto e Mezzo BOMBANA, Hong Kong. Devender's original recipe calls for 10 ml of both homemade ginger and honey syrups.

name: The Viento
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Bacardi 8 year old rum
2⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Strawberry puree
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Agave syrup
1⁄3 shot	Coconut oil
review: Reminiscent of a strawberry and coconut daiquiri.
history:
Created for Bacardí Legacy 2017 by Dave Kerr at The Beaufort bar, Melbourne, Australia.

Inspiration: “It has been 15 years since I served my first drink in a bar, using none other than a Bacardi product. Since then we’ve both grown and innovated; but our legacies will continue to grow and, now, be forever intertwined.

“I wanted to use flavours eschewed by modern bartenders and update them with modern techniques and ingredients. The Viento is not a drink designed to impress other bartenders, it is a flavour combination that should evoke memories of fun whilst challenging the palate to identify modern textures.

“I created a drink to show my own trajectory, but also to help highlight the innovation that has occurred in Bacardí rum’s recent history in parallel with my own career.”

name: El Luchador
preparation:
SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.

*Special ingredient #1: Thyme syrup made infusing 20-30g fresh thyme with 1 litre hot water for around 10 mins, then mixed with 1 kg white sugar.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
5⁄6 shot	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Thyme and Fernet Branca add herbal and medicinal notes this this long, cleansing cocktail.
history:
Created for Bacardí Legacy 2017 by Matías Iriarte, Ginbo Group, Palma de Mallorca, Spain.

Inspiration: “The history of Don Facundo Bacardí and my own history have much in common; we have both had to fight for our dreams. My story is about a man who crossed the Atlantic in turbulent times and went to look for a better life, started from scratch on a paradise island, fell in love with a wonderful woman, founded his company and struggled to achieve his dream.

“El Luchador means ‘the fighter’ - Don Facundo left us his legacy, and now I'm building mine - let's toast the fighters!”

name: Caribbean Colada
garnish: Pineapple, Luxardo Maraschino cherry & paper parasol
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1 shot	Giffard Caribbean Pineapple liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Coconut sugar syrup
1⁄6 shot	Passion fruit syrup
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Rum and pineapple strike up a tropical harmony, helped by coconut, passionfruit and orange.
history: Adapted from a recipe promoted by Giffard in June 2016 with the launch of their Caribbean Pineapple liqueur.

name: Paycheck
preparation: RINSE chilled glass with absinthe and set aside. STIR other ingredients with ice and strain into absinthe rinsed glass.
ingredients:
3 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin (infused with Earl Grey tea)
1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
1⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: Spirituous and aromatic with rich honey notes balancing bitter gentian.
history: Created in 2017 by Jens Küpperbusch, Essen, Germany.

name: Lightness Cocktail
garnish: Lemon zest twist & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Ketel One Citroen Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Strega liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: A citrus vodka sour with Strega and crème de banana.
history: Adapted from a drink discovered at the Icebar, London, England.

name: Eye-opener
preparation: SHAKE and strain all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄6 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Crème de noyau liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
1 fresh	Egg yolk
review: Resembling watery orange custard, this cocktail is surprisingly silky and suited to after-dinner.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Ancient Mariner
garnish: Scored lime wedge & mint sprig bouquet
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1 shot	Dark/black/blackstrap rum
1⁄4 shot	Pimento dram/Allspice liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Characterful and well-aged rums with a blend of citrus and all-important pimento dram. You may swap rums but there's no substitute for the pimento dram.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 1994 by Jeff "Beachbum" Berry, Los Angeles, USA, which featured in his 1998 book Grog Log and subsequent 2010 Beachbum Berry Remixed. Jeff's original recipe calls for 30ml Demerara rum and 30ml dark Jamaican rum. He also specifies white grapefruit juice.

Jeff says he created The Ancient Mariner as an early "attempt to re-create the flavour of our favourite Trader Vic's drink, Vic's version of the Navy Grog – which, in turn, used Don The Beachcomber's even earlier version as a starting point..." "We called it the Ancient Mariner because by the time we finished with it, that's how we felt."

name: Black Cuban
preparation: MUDDLE mint in base of glass. Add next 4 ingredients, STIR with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
6 fresh	Mint leaves
2 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
2⁄3 shot	Lime cordial (sweetened lime juice)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
1 grind	Black pepper
1 2⁄3 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: A cacao and coffee spiced rum riff on an Old Cuban.
history: Recipe created in 2019 by Helder Fortes Silva, Rotterdam, Netherlands. Helder's original recipe uses homemade mint-lime cordial and black pepper tincture.

name: Valentini
garnish: Sugar rimmed glass with half strawberry on rim. Serve with a shot glass of sparkling wine on the side.
preparation: MUDDLE strawberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 fresh	Strawberries (hulled, small & ripe)
1 1⁄2 shot	Raspberry flavoured vodka
1⁄6 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Strawberry sugar syrup
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A rich ripe strawberry and raspberry riff on the Porn Star Martini with lemon freshness and faint saffron.

name: Ají Dulce
preparation: MUDDLE cucumber in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with ginger ale.
ingredients:
3 slice	Cucumber (fresh)
1 1⁄3 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
2⁄3 shot	Fruit cup liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Hot pepper sauce (red)
3 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
review: In South American Spanish ají means 'chili pepper' and dulce means 'sweet', so the name of this drink translates as 'sweet chili pepper'.
history: Created in 2019 by Din Hassan, Singapore.

name: Ojo Negro
garnish: Dehydrated lime slice wheel, mint sprigs bouquet & edible flower
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass/mug.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
1 shot	Coconut rum liqueur (35-40% alc./vol.)
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 shot	Pineapple juice
1 dash	Orange cream citrate
review: Fruity with cacao, coffee, coconut and almond.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Ingo Eifler at Radisson Blue Hotel, Mannheim, Germany (originally with Mahiki Kokoslikör).

Incidentally, Ojo Negro translates from Spanish as Black Eye, a reference to this cocktail being based on Black Tears rum.

name: Crowned King
garnish: Edible fresh flower or dried rose petals
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
1⁄3 shot	Amontillado sherry
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
review: Gin-laced and citrusy with jammy apricot and subtle bitter almond.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Jesse Vida at Atlas in Singapore.

name: A Moment of Silence
preparation: RINSE a chilled glass with red bitter liqueur and set to one side. STIR other ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled, pre-rinsed glass.
ingredients:
1⁄6 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Averna Amaro
1⁄2 shot	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄4 shot	Applejack brandy bottled-in-bond (50% alc./vol)
review:
With a whopping 15ml of bitters on top of 15ml amaro (Italian for bitter) and a punchy 45ml high-proof rye whiskey, this cocktail perhaps would have been better named Momentary Lapse of Reason after the Pink Floyd track. However, the rich apricot brandy rounds and mellows to make this cocktail surprisingly approachable, although still spirituous. Perhaps consider using the following measures to reduce the serve, and so the booze, by a third:
Rinse - 5ml Red bitter liqueur
30ml (1oz) Rye whiskey
20ml (2/3oz) Apricot brandy
10ml (1/3oz) Amaro Averna
10ml (1/3oz) Angostura bitters
5ml (1/6oz) Straight bottled-in-bond applejack
history: This riff on a La Louisiane was created in 2011 by Maks Pazuniak at Cure in New Orleans, USA. Maks is also the originator of the bitters-based Angostura Sour.

name: Cry Baby
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄4 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Turmeric bitters
review: Spiritous, herbal orchard fruit.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2018 by Natasha David at Nitecap bar in New York City, USA.

name: The Anniversary
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
5⁄12 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
5⁄12 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Vibrant in both colour and flavour with rich apricot and grenadine balanced by lemon freshness and charged with spirituous bourbon. Apricot, bourbon and lemon are a harmonious trio enriched with grenadine.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Susanna McMahon, a keen amateur mixologist and 74-year-old grandmother who says, "This drink was created for those who think they do not like bourbon. The apricot brandy works magic on the bourbon, creating a most appealing drink. This is in honor of my in-law's fiftieth wedding anniversary."

name: Unspoken Word
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Horse with No Name habanero bourbon
1⁄2 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
4 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters
review: Citrusy, herbal, fruity, and delicately spiced whiskey riff on a Last Word
history:
Created in October 2021 by yours truly at the Clocktower in Rye, England.
Last Word history

name: Zelenskyy Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice. Separately, STIR vodka and blue curaçao with ice and strain over burnt-yellow layer in glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Passion fruit purée
1⁄3 shot	Peachtree peach schnapps
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Blue Curaçao
5⁄6 shot	Ketel One Vodka
review: Made to resemble the colours of the Ukrainian flag which is said to represent a blue sky over a yellow field of wheat, a reflection of Ukraine being considered Europe's breadbasket. The sunflower is the Ukrainian national flower so the flag also represents a blue sky over sunflowers.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in March 2022 in support of the people of Ukraine by Karol Terejlis, a bartender at Ognisko Restaurant at the Polish Club in South Kensington, London. Funds from sales of the cocktail are donated to Ukraine Crisis Fundraiser. Karol's recipe calls for Kavka Polish vodka.

name: Soft Focus
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
1⁄2 shot	Americano bianco
1⁄4 shot	Poire William eau-de-vie
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Juniper spirit-forward with pear.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2018 by Jeff Baumann at The Great Northern restaurant in Burlington, Vermont, USA.

name: Captain Ron
garnish: Dust with freshly grated cinnamon & garnish with a lemon zest twist
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Martinique V.S.O.P rum
3⁄4 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Bryan Crowder at the Ice Plant Bar in St. Augustine, Florida, USA.

name: Verdita Stargarita (Difford's adaptation)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
5⁄6 shot	Passoã passion fruit liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
5⁄12 shot	Passion fruit purée
1⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: A tequila-laced riff on a Porn Star Martini.
history: Created in 2022 by Dan Gore at Jigger & Jar, the agave spirits-led bar he owns and runs with his partner Claire in the outskirts of Leeds.

name: Red Leg Rebellion
garnish: Dehydrated pineapple slice & Luxardo maraschino cherry with mints sprigs bouquet
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into a glass or julep cup filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄6 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
2⁄3 shot	Rhum Clément Créole Shrubb liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Pineapple sugar syrup
review: Irish whiskey-laced lightly spiced zesty sweet and sour orange and lime.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created at the Bang Bang bar in Teeling Whiskey Distillery in Dublin Ireland. Unsurprisingly, this riff on a Mai Tai was originally based on Teeling Small Batch Irish whiskey.

"Redleg" is a pejorative term to refer to poor white immigrants to the Caribbean islands, particularly Irish immigrants to Barbados forced to work the sugar plantations during the 17th and 18th centuries. The name derives from their sunburnt fair-skinned legs due the strength of the tropical sun.

The injustices suffered by Irish immigrants are remembered in the ballad To Hell or Barbados and in the title of the June 2007 studio album by Irish singer-songwriter Damien Dempsey.

name: Anterograde Amnesia
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into frozen glass (no ice in glass).
ingredients:
1 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
2⁄3 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur

name: Fizz (generic name)
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and strain into chilled glass (no ice in glass). TOP with soda (ideally dispensed from a siphon).
ingredients:
2 shot	Brandy, whisk(e)y, gin, rum etc.
1 shot	Freshly squeezed lemon or lime juice
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (optional)
Top up with	Soda from siphon
review: We recommend the Derby Fizz with its combination of liqueur and spirits over these more traditional versions.
history:
Like the Collins, this mid-19th century classic is basically a sour lengthened with carbonated water and at first glance there is little difference between a Fizz and a Collins. However, there are several distinguishing features.

A Collins should be served in at least a 12 ounce, and ideally a 14 ounce tall glass, while that used for a Fizz should be no bigger than eight ounces. A Collins should be served in an ice-filled glass, while a Fizz should be served in a chilled glass without ice.

A Fizz should also be made using carbonated water from a siphon in preference to soda from bottles or cans. The burst of pressure from the siphon helps build a bubbly head while the tiny bubbles generated give off carbonic acid, benefiting the flavour and the mouth-feel of the drink.

For proportions we have turned to David A. Embury's seminal 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks, in which he recommends:

"1 - or a little less sweet (sugar, fruit syrup, or liqueur),
2 sour (lime or lemon juice),
3 - or a little more - strong (spirituous liquor),
and 4 weak (charged water and ice)."

We've interpreted this as follows:

2 shots spirit (gin, whiskey, vodka, brandy)
1 shot lemon or lime juice,
½ shot sugar syrup,
topped up with soda.
We've also added half a fresh egg white, which technically makes the drink a 'Silver Fizz'.

1⁄2 shot	Milk (whole milk/full 3-4% fat)
review: A little on the sweet side for some but vanilla, coffee and chocolate smoothed with cream is a tasty combination.
history: Created in 2002 by Miranda Dickson, A.K.A. the Vodka Princess, for the UK's Revolution bar chain, where some 500,000 were sold each year.

name: Salty Lychee Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Manzanilla sherry
1⁄2 shot	Lanique Spirit of Rose liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lychee juice drink
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Pale pink in colour and subtle in flavour with gin and the delicately salty tang of manzanilla sherry and drying rich rose and lychee.
history: I created this drink in 2002 after trying Dick Bradsell's Lychee & Rose Petal Martini.

name: Sangria Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Shiraz red wine
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Apple Schnapps liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Crème de Framboise
review: Brandy-based and fruit laced - just like its namesake.
history: Created in 2003 by Angelo Vieira at The Light Bar, St. Martins Hotel, London, England.

name: Shamrock
garnish: Green olive in the glass or mint leaf
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Peppermint Pastille crème de menthe
1⁄4 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: A cocktail best enjoyed as an after-dinner refresher on St. Patrick's Day.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Hugo R. Ensslin's 1917 Recipes for Mixed Drinks (2nd Edition).

name: Silver Fizz
preparation: SHAKE first four ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass (no ice). TOP with soda from siphon.
ingredients:
2 shot	Brandy, whisk(e)y, gin, rum etc.
1 shot	Freshly squeezed lemon or lime juice
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white
Top up with	Soda from siphon
review: For those, like me, who prefer their Gin Fizz with the addition of egg white.
history: A mid-19th century classic.

name: Tango Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
5⁄6 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
review: Beautifully balanced gin-laced herbal complexity with zesty orange.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book. Harry MacElhone's 1929 ABC of Cocktails credits this drinks creation to Harry, a bartender at Palermo, Rue Fontaine, Paris.

name: Trinity
garnish: Orange zest twist expressed & discarded. Adorn with 3 skewered Luxardo Maraschino Cherries.
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe
1⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A Dry Manhattan-based on Scotch with a dash of apricot liqueur and a touch of créme de menthe.
history: Adapted from a recipe in David A. Embury's 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks.

name: Tripleberry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
7 fresh	Raspberries
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Fraise des Bois liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Shiraz red wine
1⁄2 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
review: Rich berry fruit fortified with vodka and tamed by the tannins from a splash of red wine.
history: Created in 2006 by yours truly (Simon Difford).

name: Vanilla & Raspberry Cocktail
preparation: MUDDLE raspberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
12 fresh	Raspberries
2 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
1⁄4 shot	Shiraz red wine
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Exactly that - vanilla and raspberries.
history: Created in 2006 by yours truly (Simon Difford), London, England.

name: Watermelon & Basil Smash
preparation: Cut watermelon into 16 segments, chop the flesh from one segment into cubes and MUDDLE in base of skater. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with ginger ale.
ingredients:
1 slice	Watermelon (fresh)
8 fresh	Basil leaves
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
review: Sweet and sour, long and refreshing with subtle hints of basil, ginger and tequila amongst the fruit.

name: Wilton Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄2 shot	Apple Schnapps liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Goldwasser cinnamon schnapps liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review: Refined cinnamon and apple.
history: A 2003 adaptation of the signature cocktail at The Blue Bar, The Berkeley Hotel, London, England.

name: Wimbledon Martini
garnish: Strawberry in rim crowned with tip of mint sprig.
preparation: MUDDLE strawberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3 fresh	Strawberries (hulled, small & ripe)
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1 1⁄2 shot	Giffard Fraise des Bois liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: Takes some getting through the fine strainer, but when you do it's simply strawberries and cream with the faintest hint of alcohol. Wimbledon is all about strawberries & cream.
history: Created in London sometime during the 1990s when every cocktail served in a V-shaped glass was called a Martini.

name: Toreador
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
5⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	Agave syrup (optional)
4 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters (optional)
review: Apricot brandy replaces triple sec in what otherwise follows the same recipe as a classic Margarita (2 tequila, 1 triple sec, 1 lime juice). As with classic Margaritas, depending on tastes you may want to add 2.5ml (half bar spoon) or more agave syrup.
history: This twist on the Margarita was first published in William J. "Billy" Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Bar Book.

name: Bloodhound #1
preparation: MUDDLE raspberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3 fresh	Raspberries
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
review: Looks like fruity disco drink fodder but is actually surprising dry and strong.
history: Unknown but in his 1922 Mixing Cocktails, Harry MacElhone credits the Duke of Manchester, William Angus Drogo Montagu (1877-1947). The Bloodhound first appears, in a simple form, in William Boothby's 1907 World Drinks, the, in Tom Bullock's 1917 The Ideal Bartender, and perhaps most notably in in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Gin Daisy #2 (Jerry Thomas style)
preparation: SHAKE first four ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with a splash of soda from a siphon.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 Splash	Soda from siphon
review: The rich style of genever combines wonderfully with orange liqueur in this balanced classic.
history: The origins of the Daisy are lost in time but the first written reference to it is in an 1866 novel called 'Gay Life in New York, or Fast Men and Grass Widows' by Henry Llewellyn Williams. This recipe is adapted from Jerry Thomas' 1876 'How to Mix Drinks'.

name: RAC Cocktail
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄12 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A one-to-one Perfect Martini with extra grenadine sweetness and orange bitters adding complexity.
history:
The house cocktail at the Royal Automobile Club in London's Pall Mall. King Edward VII awarded this private members' club its royal title in 1907.

Adapted from a recipe in the 1933 The Green Cocktail Book written by the mysterious" Jimmy".

name: Swedish Rum Punch
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
3⁄4 shot	Swedish Punsch liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
4 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters (optional)
review: A flavoursome Daiquiri-style with the subtle spice of Swedish punch.
history: Created in 2008 by yours truly in London, England.

name: Daiquiri No.2 (El Floridita style)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: Like other Daiquiris, this complex version benefits from dilution so consider adding a dash of water.
history:
The origins of this Daiquiri No. 2 with vermouth and crème de cacao are unknown. Although subtitled "El Floridita-style," this cocktail should not be confused with the Daiquiri No. 2 created by Constantino "Constante" Ribalaïgua Vert, who owned Havana's famous El Floridita from 1918 to 1952.
See: Daiquiri cocktail history

name: Hemingway Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Oranje Vodka
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Vanille de Madagascar
1 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Syrup from Luxardo Maraschino Cherries
review: A fresh and refreshing orange and vanilla influenced Vodkatini.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2005 by Claire Smith, London, England.

name: Skid Row

ingredients:
2 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur

1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Complex, spirit-forward, and bittersweet with apricot liqueur and amaro laced with Dutch genever.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2009 by Eric Alperin at The Varnish in Los Angeles, USA.

name: A Dream to Be
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Tennessee whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Savoia Americano Rosso
3 dash	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2016 by Leon Back at Panda and Sons, Edinburgh for Jack Daniel's Tennessee Calling competition.

name: Italian Milk Punch
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Italian Brandy
1⁄4 shot	Galliano L'Autentico liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Disaronno amaretto
1⁄6 shot	Bepi Tosolini Grappa di Moscato
3 1⁄2 shot	Milk (whole milk/full 3-4% fat)
review: The distinctive flavour of moscato grappa shines through in this milky drink, with amaretto adding rich almond notes and Galliano a touch of peppermint and aniseed.
history: A riff on the classic Milk Punch created in 2011 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Meryl Lynchburg
preparation: SHAKE first four ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (or mug), TOP with soda water
ingredients:
2 shot	Tennessee whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Agave Sec liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Whiskey barrel-aged bitters
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: A long refreshing 'sugar' free whiskey iced tea-style drink.
history: Discovered in 2009 at Underdog Bar, Clapham, London, England.

name: Venetian
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
2 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
1 barspoon	Cartron No. 7 liqueur
1 barspoon	Elderflower cordial
1 barspoon	Picon Biere
review: Burnished copper red and bittersweet with wine and a dash of elderflower, fruit liqueur and bitters.
history: Created in 2009 by Rich Hunt at Quo Vadis in London, England. It is based on the flavours of the spritz, but there are no bubbles of any kind.

name: Messianic Cocktail
garnish: Orange zest twist (and float gold flakes if to hand)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)

1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Ginger and orange are delicately spiced with clove-forward falernum and fortified with golden rum.
history: Messianic means of the Messiah, so perhaps an appropriate name for a Christmas cocktail. Created in October 2011 by yours truly and updated December 2021.

name: Little Smith
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Bison grass vodka
5⁄6 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄2 shot	Difford's Falernum liqueur
1 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1 fresh	Wasabi leaf
review: This apple cocktail is lightly spicy and delicately fragrant with a faint grassiness.
history: Discovered in 2011 at Ubar, Copenhagen, Denmark.

name: El Momento Perfecto
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
2⁄3 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
2⁄3 shot	Byrrh Grand Quinquina
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1 barspoon	Orange marmalade
review: A rum and marmalade Negroni-like drink.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2011 by Daniel Bovey at Sahara Bar in Reading, England.

name: Moonwalk Cocktail
garnish: Orange zest twist (spray & discard) & quarter orange slice on rim
preparation: Drop sugar cube into glass and soak with dashes of grapefruit bitters and orange flower water. POUR liqueur over soaked sugar cube. TOP with champagne. (Build in glass like a classic Champagne Cocktail.)
ingredients:
1 cube	Sugar cube
3 dash	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
2 dash	Orange blossom water / Orange flower water
5⁄6 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
3 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Delicately sweetened champagne with cognac and citrus flavours.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 1969 by Joe Gilmore at The American Bar at The Savoy Hotel, London to commemorate the Apollo 11 moon landing on 20th July 1969.

Speaking to Difford's Guide in January 2012 Joe said, "The moon landings were a big deal to everyone at the time and I thought I've got to make a cocktail for this." Joe, who watched the moon landings repeated on TV when his shift was over, went on to say, "I never got to serve Neil Armstrong personally, but I sent one in a flask to NASA and apparently, it was the first drink he had when he landed. He wrote a letter to me at the Savoy to say thank you." That letter is on display on the wall of the 'museum' to the left as you enter The American Bar.

name: The Ruby Gold
garnish: Float raspberry and dust with grated nutmeg
preparation: DRY SHAKE (without ice) all ingredients. Add ice, SHAKE again with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 3⁄4 shot	Tawny port
2⁄3 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 fresh	Egg yolk
review: A rich after-dinner, dessert-style cocktail.
history: Created in 2010 by Rufus at the Hide Bar, London. England.

name: Huckle my buff
preparation: Gently BLEND all ingredients on a slow speed, then warm in a saucepan, gently stirring with a whisk (or microwave for 30 seconds and stir), POUR into warmed glass. If you make several servings in one batch, keep warm and serve from a sous-vide or heated soup kettle at to 60°C.
ingredients:
1 fresh	Egg yolk
5 shot	Harveys Porter 1859
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄4 shot	Ginger liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
review: To quote Jamie Oliver, "the Huckle-my-buff is not a Dodo, but a Phoenix".
history:
My adaptation of a recipe presented by Jamie Oliver and Jimmy Doherty on Friday 9th August 2013, at the Cabinet Room as their entry to the Difford's Guide Beer-tail Competition for London Cocktail Week 2013.

Also known as Huckle-my-butt and Huckle-and-buff, Huckle-my-buff is an early 18th century hot drink combining gin or cognac and beer. Jamie and Jimmy resurrected the Huckle-my-buff and gave it a modern twist with the use of nitrous oxide and a sous-vide in place of the traditional red-hot poker.

The Jamie and Jimmy recipe was as follows: whisk 1 fresh egg yolk, then slowly whisk in 20 grams muscovado sugar, 35ml cognac, 150ml Harvey's Stout beer and 0.8ml ginger juice. Pour mixture into a soda syphon, close and charge with nitrous oxide (laughing gas/N2O). Gently warm the filled cream whipper to 60°C in a sous-vide (water bath). Discharge warmed syphon into glass. Finish with freshly grated nutmeg.

Originally a punch still drink, Huckle-My-Butt appears in the Ending With "Party Mixes" chapter of W. C. Whitfield's 1941 Here's How Mixed Drinks.

name: Franco Russian Punch
preparation: SHAKE first four ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with champagne and lightly stir.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
2⁄3 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
2 fresh	Raspberries
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
4 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: This long refreshing berry and champagne cocktail is a riff on Dick Bradsell’s Russian Spring Punch.
history: Created in January 2014 for Laurent-Perrier by Sean Ware of the London Cocktail Club, London, England.

name: Bellini Peach Spritz
garnish: Lemon slice or fresh peach wedge
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
3 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
1 1⁄4 shot	Peach purée
1⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Peachtree peach schnapps
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water
review: Basically, a Bellini served on-the-rocks.
history:
Created in 2013 by yours truly for Jamie's Italian Bars.
