name: Willi Wonka cocktail
garnish: White chocolate square and half strawberry
preparation: Muddle strawberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
2 fresh	Strawberries (hulled, small & ripe)
2 shot	Cachaça
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	White chocolate sugar syrup
review: Cachaça and strawberry with subtle hints of lime and chocolate.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2015 by Carlos Londoño at Café Pacifico London.

name: Great Northern
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
2 shot	Akvavit / Aquavit
3⁄4 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: Your choice of honey will greatly influence this drink which harnesses the character of aquavit to great effect with white wine and citrusy notes.
history: Created in 2011 by Jessica Gonzalez at Death & Company in New York City, USA.

name: What's Up, Doc?
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄2 shot	Carrot juice (freshly extracted)
1⁄2 shot	Ginger liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Cinnamon syrup
review: Carrot juice gives this drink an orange hue and combines surprisingly well with gin. Extra flavour and spice comes courtesy of ginger liqueur, lemon juice and cinnamon.
history:
! discovered this drink at The Wayland in Manhattan's East Village. The What's Up, Doc? cocktail became popular across New York City in 2014 with numerous versions using different base spirits such as vodka, rye whiskey and grappa.

"Eh, What's up Doc?" is the catchphrase of Bugs Bunny, the nonchalant cartoon character who stars in the series of animated short films produced by Warner Bros.

name: The Affiliate
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
3⁄4 shot	Fino sherry
3⁄4 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Judicious dashing of orange bitters and hitting the correct dilution will make or break this drink, which is a fine balance between aged rum and rich cherry liqueur versus dry fino sherry and aromatic bitters.
history: Created in 2013 by Charles Joly at The Aviary, Chicago, USA.

name: L'Anniversaire (The Birthday)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	Drambuie liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Raisin sugar syrup (2:1 homemade)
review: Rich yet bittersweet. A good after-dinner digestive.
history: Created in 2015 by Pier Schirru at Century Club in London, England

name: La Palma
preparation: THROW all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
1 1⁄2 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Coconut sugar syrup
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Reminiscent of a well-known coconut rum liqueur but very much drier and more complex with lime adding sourness and bitters playing a crucial role.
history: The Lebanese Bacardí Legacy 2016 winning cocktail by Ayman Zayour, Vivid lounge-bar, Beirut.

name: El Camello Loco
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
3 shot	Pilsner lager
review: Somewhat reminiscent of a Michelada without the spice, this is a very refreshing and enjoyable beer-influenced cocktail. Strangely, the beer makes the lime shine.
history: The Israeli Bacardí Legacy 2016 winning cocktail by Bar Shira, Imperial Craft Cocktail Bar/ La Otra, Tel Aviv.

name: El Puente
garnish: Olive wrapped in a lemon peel & basil
preparation:
MUDDLE olives and basil in base of shaker. ADD other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled copper mug.

*Special ingredient #1: Coriander syrup
ingredients:
2 unit	Black olives
3 fresh	Basil leaves
1 2⁄3 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
1 shot	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: "The scents and flavours of my grandparents' backyard are one of the lasting memories of my childhood. It wasn't until much later when I began travelling that I realised that these characteristics are not unique to Cyprus (which was named after copper). Living in Spain taught me the connection between Mediterranean cuisine, the Spanish love for rum, and therefore their link to the Latin world. These three elements, combined with the romanticism of a childhood backyard, created a 'bridge' in my mind between three worlds. So, I present you El Puente, my own legacy."
history: Cyprian Bacardí Legacy 2016 winning cocktail by Argyris Asleep, Palaia Pineza / Bartó do, Nicosia.

name: Wild Ward
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3 dash	Bob's Cardamom bitters
review: This riff on a Final Ward is both bitter sweet and sweet 'n' sour. It's challenging, complex and a most interesting example of inspired bartending creativity.
history:
Adapted from recipe created in 2016 by Channing Centeno at Momofuku Ko, New York City, USA. "While craving a Final Ward at home, I realized I didn't have any Chartreuse. I subbed in Suze and some cardamom bitters for an added spice. It's now an instant classic at my bar and household."

Channing's original spec is equal parts (¾ oz of each) Suze, lemon juice, rye whiskey, Luxardo Maraschino and 4 dashes cardamom bitters.

name: Green Negroni
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and lightly STIR.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Luxardo Bitter Bianco liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Green melon liqueur
review: Don’t be put off or misled by the lurid green colour or this cocktail, it is both bittersweet and complex. As the name suggests it is based in a classic Negroni but with Green Chartreuse herbal complexity and a dose of rich green melon liqueur.

name: Ginger & Fig Caipirinha
garnish: Stirrer (spoon, wooden lolly stick or stick cut from sugar cane)
preparation:
1. Cut lime in half (from pole to pole) and then slice one of the halves into eight 3-4mm thick half-moon shaped segments and drop into the base of a robust rocks glass.

2. Add 3 bar spoons caster sugar (or ½oz / 15ml sugar syrup 2:1) and MUDDLE.

3. Add fig and MUDDLE some more.

4. When sure fruit juice is fully extracted and the sugar dissolved, transfer the muddled fruit and sugar into serving glass (preferably a 30cl / 10oz highball glass).

5. POUR cachaça (stored in the freezer) and ginger liqueur into the rocks glass (used to muddle) and swirl to rinse glass before pouring cachaça into serving glass. STIR to ensure all ingredients are well mixed.

6. Crack (rather than crush) four to five large ice cubes and drop into serving glass. STIR before topping with more ice and serve with a stirrer (but no straws).
ingredients:
1⁄2 fresh	Lime (fresh) (chopped)
3 barspoon	Caster/ Superfine/Baker's special sugar (white)
1 fresh	Figs (chopped)
1⁄2 shot	Ginger liqueur
2 shot	Cachaça (from freezer)
history: For information on the history and other variations of the Caipirinha, please see our Caipirinha cocktail page.

name: Cuban Pete
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
2⁄3 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Coconut water
8 fresh	Mint leaves
review: A well-balanced chocolatey, minty and subtly coconut daiquiri. Perhaps a tad too many flavours in one drink for some.
history:
Created for Bacardí Legacy 2017 by Ingrid Skaue Øines at To Rom og Kjøkken, Trondheim, Norway.

Ingrid explains the inspiration behind this cocktail: "When I was a little girl growing up in the artic part of Norway, my dream was always to entertain people around me, to be on stage and make people feel good. Today, the bar is my stage. It is the place where I can be all I want to be, entertain, have fun and share stories with my guests.

"The ingredients in 'Cuban Pete' are inspired by the bold Latin- American flavors. The Bacardí Carta Blanca rum is the perfect base to this cocktail, with fresh floral and citrus notes, sweet crème de cacao, combined with coconut water, fresh mint and lime. When you taste 'Cuban Pete' you can feel him shaking his maracas on your pallet. 'Cuban Pete' is about inviting people to have fun and embrace what is in front of them, just like the Bacardí family did for the American people under prohibition."

name: The Joanna
garnish: Small lavender sprigs pegged to rim
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Fino sherry
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
6 drop	Bob's Lavender Bitters
review: Reminiscent of a vodkatini with fino sherry and notes of floral elderflower and lavender.
history: Created in 2017 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room in London, England.

name: Apicius
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Creme de Chataigne
1⁄3 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
review: This digestif cocktail is aromatic and bittersweet with herbal and botanical complexity rounded by rich chestnut liqueur.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2017 by Sam Robertson & Alexander Taylor at Pennyroyal, Cardiff, Wales. They told us, "Apicius is an ancient cookbook which dates back to the 5th century, it provides an insight into the origins of Italian cuisine. Chestnuts, known to aid digestion, were hugely prominent, combined with amaro this cocktail is the perfect after-dinner sipper."

name: Oleo Sacrament
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Tennessee whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Lime oleo saccharum
1⁄3 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
2 dash	Plum bitters
history: Created in November 2017 by Alastair McCarroll, Chamber 36 bar, Liverpool, for Jack Daniel’s Tennessee Calling II.

name: Le Very French 75
garnish: Lemon zest twist & two amarena cherries
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
1 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1 shot	Lillet-style Rouge light quinquina
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄6 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: A dry, bitter apéritif-style riff on the classic French 75. Try with a splash more sparkling wine than suggested in the recipe and/or a spoon of sugar syrup.
history:
Created in 2017 by Regis Laacher at Kremlin in Paris, France. He says of his cocktail, "Basically, a twist of the classic French 75. By adding Lillet Rouge and Suze without simple syrup, you make the drink bitter and dry, the perfect appetizer to start a night out or to kick a party."
More French 75 history and variants

name: Bermuda Triangle
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into a chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Batavia arrack
1⁄2 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
3⁄4 shot	Pineapple juice
1 barspoon	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Pimento bitters
review: As Ralf, the drinks creator, says, "The Batavia plays well with the pineapple and the gomme, and the sherry gives it depth and body" to produce a punch-style cocktail.
history: Created by Ralf Ramirez of The Exhibition Room, Long Beach, CA, at one of Gary "gaz" Regan's excellent educational Cocktail the Country sessions.

name: Cosmopolitan (no added sugar* & low-calorie)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. (Be sure to use naturally sweetened cranberry drink rather than "juice" sweetened with sugar.)
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Citroen Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Agave Sec liqueur
1 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Sugar-free sweetener
review:
* BEWARE: Although
free of cane sugar and beet sugar, this cocktail contains small amounts of fructose sugars from the agave nectar used in the Agave Sec orange liqueur.

The cranberry juice you select and even some vodkas may also introduce unwanted sugar into this cocktail, so choose judiciously. Even unsweetened cranberry juice and even lime juice will contain natural fruit sugars.
history:
Adapted from the classic serve by yours truly in January 2019.
Cosmopolitan cocktail history and development

name: Arancia Spritz
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Soda Water
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
2 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
review: Reminiscent of a Pimm's No.1 Spritz.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2017 by Justin Kaderabek at Monteverde in Chicago, USA.

See Spritz cocktail history and more recipes

name: Callahan's Painkiller
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
2⁄3 shot	Cream of coconut (e.g. Coco Lopez, Re'al etc.)
1⁄3 shot	Lavender sugar syrup
2 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: This riff on the classic Painkiller features the distinctive flavours of coffee and cacao spiced rum.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Michael D Callahan at The Compound Collective, Singapore.

name: Drop By Drop
preparation: STIR first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with beer.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
1⁄3 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
1⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
2 2⁄3 shot	Barrel aged red beer
review: Chocolate, treacle, zesty citrus and spice with faintly smoky beer.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Katalin Bene at Voodoo Reyes - Potions & Botanicals, Geneva, Switzerland.

name: Calvados Mon Amour
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. POUR berry liqueur into the centre of drink to form a sunrise effect.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
3⁄4 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Cinnamon syrup
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
review: Apple brandy, pineapple and orange with a hint of cinnamon and a blast of berry fruit. Sounds sweet and fruity but this cocktail is spirituous and complex.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2006 by Salvatore Damiano, Brand Ambassador & President of United Kingdom Bartenders' Guild.

name: Dairy Milk Chocolate
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
1⁄2 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Perhaps serve with a shot glass of champagne on the side so this cocktail literally contains a "glass and a half". The picture of the glass and a half of milk is still used on Dairy Milk bars, the UK's best-selling chocolate bar, but sadly the slogan was removed after 80 years in 2010 due to contravening European labelling regulations.

name: Sinnerman
preparation: Put 2 spoons of powdered panela sugar in the glass. Add the vermouth and a splash of soda water. Use a barspoon to dissolve the sugar in the water. Add spiced rum, bitters and ice then STIR.
ingredients:
2 barspoon	Powdered panela sugar
1 Splash	Thomas Henry Soda Water
1⁄3 shot	Ambrato/ambre/amber vermouth
1 5⁄6 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
2 dash	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: Sugar spice and all things nice would sum up this drink well if only the name was Niceman rather than Sinnerman. The sugar, in this case, flavoursome Panela sugar, contributes more favour than sweetness to what is a surprisingly dry, coffee and cacao laced drink with rosso vermouth (originally Oscar 697 Vermouth Rosso) adding a touch of richness.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Marco Riccetti at Inside cocktail bar in Torino, Italy.

name: Silent Tears
preparation:
STIR first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with ginger beer.

Special ingredient #1: Spiced brine (made with 100g green chilli or Jalapeño cooked in 100g of water until boiling point and then add 70ml white vinegar and 15g of salt (adjust depending on chilli). Blend and fine strain).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
1⁄2 shot	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
1 1⁄3 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄3 shot	Cucumber syrup
2 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Beer
review: Delicate chilli and ginger spice with vegetal chocolate flavours.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Colin Chia at Nutmeg & Clove, Singapore.

name: Lucky Golden Oranges
preparation: STIR first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with tonic water.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Kumquat liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
Top up with	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: Zippy citrus and floral notes combine in this refreshing riff on a G&T.
history: Adapted from a recipe, originally based on Jinzu Gin with Mancino Sakura vermouth, by Gianluca Capilungo, London, England.

name: Nice Poire Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Pear-flavoured vodka
2⁄3 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: A contemporary balanced and complex Martini with well-integrated fruity and floral flavours.

name: Cherryberry Cherub
preparation: MUDDLE raspberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
5 fresh	Raspberries
1 1⁄2 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Triple Sec (40%)
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄12 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
review: Warning: use of a vanilla-flavoured vodka rather than vodka infused with a vanilla pod (as the recipe intends) can make this fruity summery cocktail a tad candy-like.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Kim van Megen, a Discerning Drinker in Maastricht, The Netherlands.

name: Café Colonial
garnish: Orange zest twist (and serve with a small cup of black coffee in the side)
preparation: Soak sugar cube with chocolate bitters and coffee. MUDDLE cube and STIR until sugar dissolved. Add other ingredients along with ice and STIR. Top with more ice and serve.
ingredients:
1 cube	Sugar cube
5 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
1⁄3 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
2 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
1⁄6 shot	Gingerbread sugar syrup
review: Lightly spicy bittersweet coffee. A good breakfast cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Alberto Martinez at 1862 Dry Bar in Madrid, Spain.

name: All In
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
2⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
review: Spirituous and bittersweet with a underlying chocolaty treat.
history: Adapted from a recipe created at Nitecap in New York City, USA.

name: Cubanero
preparation: STIR spiced rum and jam in the base of a mixing glass until the jam is dissolved. Add cold brew coffee and lime juice, STIR with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably large chunks of ice). TOP with tonic water.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
1 barspoon	Pineapple jam
1 1⁄2 shot	Cold brew coffee
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: Reminiscent of lightly fruity iced coffee with pleasing chocolaty notes.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Jimmy Barrat at Zuma restaurant in Dubai, UAE.

name: Blood, Smoke & Tears
preparation: Smoke chilled glass with a rosemary sprig and leave upturned while making the cocktail to retain smoke. SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into smoked glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
5⁄6 shot	Tawny port
5⁄12 shot	Cinnamon syrup
5⁄12 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: A delicately spicy port influenced Daiquiri smoothed by egg white and aromatised by smoked rosemary. This spiced and port wine combo is perfect for a winter's eve.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Alexander Douglas at Revolution de Cuba bar in Nottingham, England.

name: Blackberry Mint Margarita Julep
garnish: Blackberry & mint sprig bouquet. Serve with straws
preparation: MUDDLE blackberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into cup/glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
5 fresh	Blackberries
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
8 fresh	Mint leaves
review: A mint and blackberry Margarita with honey in place of agave syrup and served Julep-style.

name: Hot Blooded
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Piment d'Espelette chile liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Blood orange juice
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: Chilli pepper-led spirituous spice freshened with lime and blood orange citrus. May make you hot rather than merely warm-blooded.

name: Killer Queen
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	White overproof rum
1 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
1⁄4 shot	Lanique Spirit of Rose liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Jason E. Clapham in Oxford, England.

name: Prelude
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄6 shot	Mentzendorff Kümmel liqueur
1 dash	Celery bitters
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: With delicate but assertive caraway-led herbal undertones, this is a savoury, Martini-style cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Susanna McMahon, a keen amateur mixologist and 74-year-old grandmother. She says, "This is a truly savoury drink without any sweetness at all. I think of it as the perfect complement to before dinner treats or pickled treats such as herring."

name: La Confiture
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1 shot	Pallini Limoncello liqueur
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 barspoon	Orange marmalade
4 drop	Orange cream citrate
review: An explosion of refreshing sweet and sour zesty lemon with a touch of herbal complexity.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Josh Stevens at Lily Blacks in Melbourne, Australia.

name: Rome is Burning
garnish: Flamed orange zest twist (discarded) & skewered Luxardo Maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. TOP with sparkling wine.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
3 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
1 1⁄2 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
review: Originally topped with lambrusco, I've opted for prosecco but some, like me, may prefer champagne or other brut sparkling wine. Whichever you choose, the result is cognac-laced bittersweet herbal and lightly vivacious aperitivo or digestivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe that originated in 2008 at Milk & Honey in New York City, USA.

name: Monsoon Martini
garnish: Dust 1/3rd foam with chilli powder and float coffee bean
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Piment d'Espelette chile liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1 dash	Black walnut bitters
review: If a regular Espresso Martini is not a wake-up call enough, then add some chili to add some spicy heat. Wakey-wakey!
history: Adapted from a recipe discovered at the Dishoom restaurant in Shoreditch, London, England.

name: Wildest Redhead
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large chunk/cube ice). DRIZZLE cherry brandy (which will fall through the cocktail to form a red base to the drink).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄4 shot	Pimento dram/Allspice liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
review: A honeyed Whisky Sour with allspice and a rich cherry base.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2014 by Meaghan Dorman at Lantern's Keep bar in New York City, USA.

name: Rose (English)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: Rose-coloured, gin-laced apricot delicately dried with a little dry vermouth and lemon juice.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Meridian
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Akvavit / Aquavit
2⁄3 shot	Rosé/rosato vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
3 drop	Orange blossom water / Orange flower water
review: Go easy on the orange blossom water – 3 drips from a pipette is plenty. Strike the right balance and you'll have a delicately floral aquavit sour.
history: Adapted from a recipe created at The Quality Chop House restaurant in London and shared by Discerning Drinker, David Teager, via a comment on our Great Northern cocktail page.

name: Prophet in Plain Clothes
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
1 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: The Rob Roy meets the Hanky Panky in this smoky bittersweet digestivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Kraig Rovensky, general manager at Life on Mars in Seattle, Washington, USA. The original recipe calls for Laphroaig 10-year single malt and Amaro Cinpatrazzo.

name: Fitzgerald No. 3
garnish: Orange zest twist expressed and discarded
preparation: POUR all ingredients into ice-filled glass and STIR.
ingredients:
1 shot	Monkey Shoulder Fresh Monkey
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
1⁄3 shot	Luxardo Bitter Bianco liqueur
2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: Bittersweet, wonderfully fresh and enlivening. Enjoy as an aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by La'Mel Clarke of Seed Library in London, England.

name: Frozen Pornstar Martini
garnish: Serve with brut sparkling wine, ideally rosé on the side
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with ¾ of a 7oz scoop of crushed ice and pour into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
1⁄2 shot	Passoã passion fruit liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Passion fruit purée
1⁄3 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
review: A Porn Star Martini adapted to suit a scorchio summer's day.

name: Old Money
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
3⁄4 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	Spiced Pear liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3⁄4 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: An agave spirit, spiced pear and honey sour. I've mixed opinions as to how well pear combines with agave spirits.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Ben Siegel, bartender at Hooch Craft Cocktail Bar in Aspen, Colorado, USA.

name: Pumpkin Spice Calypso
preparation: POUR first 3 ingredients into pre-heated glass. Steam cream (or heat in a milk frother) and pour over the back of a spoon to FLOAT.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
2 1⁄2 shot	Filter coffee (hot)
1⁄4 shot	Pumpkin spice syrup
3⁄4 shot	Single cream/half-and-half (steamed foaming)
review: As the name suggests, pumpkin spice syrup is key to the flavour of this latte-like cocktail.

name: Almond Tiramisu
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. (There's no need to dry shake to achieve desired foam.)
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Adriatico Bianco almond milk liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1 barspoon	Mascarpone cheese (optional)
review: Tastes just as the name suggests and is designed to replace or accompany the dessert of the same name. The optional Mascarpone cheese adds flavour and body to the cocktail. Use a generous bar-spoonful and briefly stir into the cocktail as a good shake should integrate with other ingredients. That said, be sure to fine strain.
history: Adapted from Adam Ennis' 2001 Tiramisu cocktail in December 2023 to use almond milk liqueur.

name: Banana & Almond Milk Daiquiri
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄6 shot	Banana rum
1 1⁄6 shot	Adriatico Bianco almond milk liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Coconut water
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Just as it says on the tin, a banana rum-based Daiquiri with almond milk liqueur, harmonised by a splash of coconut water.
history: Created in December 2023 by yours truly at The Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Captain Cuba
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
3 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Victor's original recipe was made for Bacardi Legacy so calls for a light white rum. Perhaps more importantly, he specifies pomegranate syrup and your choice of syrup, homemade or otherwise, will greatly influence the finished cocktail, as will your crème de cacao which shines.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2010 by Victor Nordelöf at Callooh Callay for Bacardi Legacy and included in Anistatia Miller and Jared Brown's Ramping Up the Classics!

name: Crimson King
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
1⁄4 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
review: Some serve this Boulevardier-style cocktail straight-up but, like the Boulevardier, its delicate chocolate and coffee notes are better appreciated with the additional dilution afforded by being served on the rocks.
history: A cocktail from the early twenty-teens by an unknown creator, perhaps named after the Crimson King, a fictional character created by Stephen King and the main antagonist in the author's eight-volume Dark Tower (1982 - 2004) series, as well as his novels Insomnia (1994) and Black House (2001).

name: Fanciulli
garnish: Orange zest twist expressed & discarded, adorn with skewered Luxardo Maraschino Cherry
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: A Manhattan with extra bitters. While challenging for some, others will enjoy it as a delicious digestivo.
history:
Adapted from a recipe published in Albert Stevens Crockett's 1931 Old Waldorf Bar Days. 'Fanciulli' is slang for 'boys' in Italian, and in Crockett's book, he suggests that this cocktail could have been named for performers in Puccini's La Fanciulla del West opera and then discounts the theory due to the cocktail predating the opera.

Its appearance in Crockett's book suggests this cocktail originated at the Waldorf, and the hotel's former bar manager Frank Caiafa thinks it was named after Francesco Fanciulli, a band leader and composer who lived in New York City after taking over the US Marine Band in 1892.

name: Grappa Luca
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Bepi Tosolini Grappa di Moscato
1 shot	Lucano amaro
3⁄4 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Grappa shines in this bittersweet, sweet 'n' citrus sour, aperitivo or digestivo.
history: Created in March 2024 by yours truly at the Clocktower, Rye, Sussex.

name: Boozy Bijou
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Navy Strength Royal Dock Gin
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄4 shot	Chartreuse Élixir Végétal
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: As the name suggests, this late-night sipper is boozy. Yet, its gin-laced herbal flavours make it hard to stop sipping on.
history: Adapted from a recipe created circa 2023 by Adam George Fournier, beverage director at Spago restaurant in Beverly Hills, California, USA. Adam's recipe calls for Chartreuse VEP Verte and is preferable to the standard Green Chartreuse if available. It also called for Cocchi Storico Vermouth di Torino vermouth.

name: Nut Job
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 1⁄3 shot	Adriatico Bianco almond milk liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Hazelnut sugar syrup
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Black walnut bitters
review: Bourbon-laced almond milk with rich hazelnut and lemon freshness. Hazelnut-flavoured sugar syrup is key to this recipe, which is even tastier when made with a roasted hazelnut syrup.
history: Created in June 2024 by yours truly at the Clocktower in Rye, England. Named after The Nut Job animated heist film starring Surly the squirrel. While the film had mixed reviews, it's a great name for a nutty cocktail. (You didn't think I'd name a cocktail after the term for a foolish or eccentric person, did you?)

name: Ti' Punch Highball
preparation: MUDDLE lime coin in base of glass. Add next 2 ingredients and 4 ice cubes and briefly stir. Add 3 more ice cubes and rest of ingredients, then briefly stir again.
ingredients:
1 disc	Lime zest (peel)
1 1⁄2 shot	Rhum Clément Blanc
1⁄8 shot	Clément Sirop de Canne
2 shot	Coconut water
2 shot	Thomas Henry Tonic Water
review: Grassy rum and coconut with quinine tonic. The first sip may taste overly dry but subsequent sips are all the more refreshing.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Paul McGee at Lost Lake in Chicago, USA.

name: Gingerbread Old Fashioned No. 2
garnish: Mini gingerbread man or skewered crystallised ginger
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄3 shot	Gingerbread sugar syrup
8 drop	Bob's Abbotts bitters
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: The name says it all, a gingerbread-flavoured Old Fashioned.
history: Created in August 2024 by yours truly at the Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Pumpkin Spice Espresso Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
2⁄3 shot	Pumpkin spice syrup
1⁄3 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Just as it says on the tin, a pumpkin spice-flavoured Espresso Martini but mellowed with creamy vanilla.
history: Created in August 2024 by yours truly at the Clocktower, Rye, England.

name: Elmo Cola
garnish: Orange zest twist and skewered Luxardo Maraschino Cherries.
preparation: STIR first 3 ingredients in mixing glass with ice. ADD cola and then strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄4 shot	Syrup from Luxardo Maraschino Cherries
8 drop	Bob's Vanilla bitters
2 shot	Cola (e.g. Coca Cola or Pepsi Cola)
review: An easy-drinking cola, cherry and vanilla-flavoured Old Fashioned.
history: Adapted from the house cocktail served at the St. Elmo Steak House in Indianapolis, USA, since 2012, when hospitality consultant Tim Kirkland introduced it.

name: Bellini-Tini
garnish: Peach wedge on rim or orange zest twist
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Ketel One Vodka
5⁄12 shot	Peachtree peach schnapps
1 2⁄3 shot	Peach purée
3 dash	Peach bitters
review: Peachy! Based on the Bellini, funnily enough.

name: Caipiruva
preparation: MUDDLE lime wedges and grapes in base of shaker to release juices. Add cachaça and sugar. SHAKE with 6oz scoop crushed ice and pour all without straining into glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 fresh	Lime (fresh) (chopped wedges)
4 fresh	Green grapes (seedless)
2 shot	Cachaça
1⁄2 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
review: A grape juice laced twist on the Caipirinha.
history: Created by Dale DeGroff, New York, USA.

name: Chocolate Mint Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe
1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: An after-dinner chocolate mint sweety.

name: Creamsicle
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Oranje Vodka
1 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: A creamy orange number that's surprisingly pleasant.

name: Chatham Hotel Special
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Tawny port
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
1⁄2 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: We've slightly changed the proportions and replaced the original lemon zest garnish with a little extra spice.
history: This mid-1900s classic from New York's Chatham Hotel was resurrected by Ted Haigh in his 2004 book Vintage Spirits & Forgotten Cocktails.

name: Donegal
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Mandarine Napoleon liqueur
1 1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: Aromatised Irish whiskey with cherry and orange.

name: First of July
preparation: MUDDLE blackberries in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
4 fresh	Blackberries
2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
2 shot	Pink grapefruit juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Rich blackberry fruit with a hint of grapefruit acidity.
history: Created on 1st of July by David Guidi at Morton's, London, England.

name: Fly Like a Butterfly
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1⁄2 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: This light, aromatic, sweet and sour beauty has a grown-up, quinine-rich flavour but lacks the 'sting like a bee' finish.
history: Created by yours truly, this is my take on a classic cocktail called a 'Lovely Butterfly' made with the same ingredients.

name: Flying Grasshopper
garnish: Powdered sugar & chocolate powder rim, plus float tip of mint sprig
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Peppermint Pastille crème de menthe
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: Why drink a mere Grasshopper when you could be enjoying a Flying Grasshopper? This creamy after-dinner cocktail is all the better for the splash of vodka, indeed it's arguably better with a splash more vodka. Minty fresh with indulgent chocolate - reminiscent of a choc mint ice-cream.
history: A 1970s or earlier more alcoholic riff on the Grasshopper cocktail. Some, including Stan Jones' 1977 Jones' Complete Bar Guide omit the cream: 1 vodka, ¾ green crème de menthe and ¾ white creme de cacao to make a clear emerald green cocktail.

name: French Tear No. 1
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple juice
4 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters
review: Rum-laced and fruity. Altogether very gluggable.
history: Adapted from a cocktail discovered in 2000 at Quo Vadis in London, England.

name: Cadillac Margarita (AKA Grand Margarita)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Difford's Margarita Bitters (optional)
review: A balanced (far from sweet) and flavoursome Margarita with the rich cognac and orange notes of the liqueur adding to this drink's depth of flavour.
history: The Cadillac Margarita, with Grand Marnier in place of triple sec liqueur, became well known in the 1980s due to being marketed by the Southern California-based El Torito Grill chain of restaurants.

name: Grassy Finnish
preparation: MUDDLE lemongrass in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 fresh	Lemongrass stem
2 shot	Lime flavoured vodka
1 shot	Krupnik spiced honey liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix) (2 sugar to 1 water)
review: Like Finland, this drink is clean, green, wooded and safe, but deep down there's plenty of spice.
history: Created in 2003 by Gerard McCurry at Revolution, UK.

name: Green Tea Cocktail #1
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bison grass vodka
1⁄4 shot	Green banana liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe
1 1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review: It's green and, although it doesn't actually contain any tea, has something of the flavour of alcoholic peppermint tea.

name: Gusto
preparation: MUDDLE grapes in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
7 fresh	Green grapes (seedless)
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	Tequila agave liqueur
2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
review: A pleasing long drink flavoured with apple, grape and tequila.
history: Created in 2003 by Thomas Gillgren at The Kingly Club, London, England.

name: Havana Cobbler
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 shot	Tawny port
1⁄2 shot	Ginger wine
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
review: An unusual, spiced, Daiquiri-like drink.

name: Irish Coffee 'Martini'
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
2 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
1⁄2 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: Forget sipping warm java through a cold head of cream. This 'Martini' version of the classic Irish Coffee offers all the flavour without the moustache.
history:
Created in 2003 by yours truly (Simon Difford) in London, England.

The history and common variants of the Irish Coffee Cocktail are listed on our page.

name: Melon Margarita #1 (served 'up')
preparation: Cut melon into 8 segments and deseed. Cut cubes of flesh from skin of one segment and MUDDLE in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄6 fresh	Melon (Cantaloupe)
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 shot	Green melon liqueur
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Looks like stagnant pond water but tastes fantastic.

name: Old Pal
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
review: Classically an equal parts three-ingredient cocktail comprising: 30ml rye, 30ml bitter liqueur and 30 ml dry vermouth. This produces an overly dry bittersweet spirituous drink. Hence, I prefer the Old Pal with an even split of dry and bianco vermouths so introducing a fourth ingredient and the merest touch more sweetness to tame this Negroni-style sipper.
history: Created in the 1920s by Harry MacElhone at his New York Bar, this rye whisky version of his Boulevardier is named after William "Sparrow" Robinson, then sports editor of The New York Herald in Paris.

name: Grand Élixir
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cachaça
3⁄4 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: The name refers to the inclusion of Yellow Chartreuse which combines well with cachaça in this drink with honey and lemon juice.
history: Adapted from a drink originally served at Franklin Southie (now closed) in Boston, USA.

name: Purple Cosmo
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Citroen Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Parfait Amour liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	White cranberry juice drink
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: If shaken this becomes more of a grey cosmo. The flavour and colour make for an interesting twist.
history: For more recipes, origins and history behind the Cosmopolitan cocktail, see our Cosmopolitan page.

name: Raspberry Mocha'tini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Raspberry flavoured vodka
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Crème de Framboise
1 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
review: Sweet chocolate and raspberry tempered by dry coffee and vodka.
history: Discovered in 2002 at Lot 61, New York City, USA.

name: Robin Hood
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 shot	Apple Schnapps liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime cordial (sweetened lime juice)
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: American readers might consider this an Apple Martini based on rum.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2002 by Tony Conigliaro at The Lonsdale in Notting Hill, London, England.

name: La Rosa Margarita
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Crème de Mûre liqueur
1 shot	Hibiscus tea (cold)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A fruity yet dry, crimson-coloured Margarita

name: Rossini
preparation: MUDDLE strawberries in base of shaker. Add liqueur and lemon juice, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with prosecco and gently stir.
ingredients:
4 fresh	Strawberries (hulled, small & ripe)
1 shot	Giffard Fraise des Bois liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3 1⁄2 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
review: Strawberries seem to complement prosecco even better than white peaches so perhaps order this in preference to a Bellini.
history: Named for the 19th-century Italian opera composer, Gioachino Antonio Rossini. This is one of the most popular Bellini variants in Venice.

name: So So Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: This beautifully balanced, delicately herbal cocktail is so much more than just so-so.
history: The "So So Cocktail" appears in Harry MacElhone's's 1923 Harry of Ciro's ABC Of Mixing Cocktails where he credits this drink to "Mr P. Soso, the popular manager of Kit-Kat Club, London."

name: Star
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄12 shot	Gomme syrup
3 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Apple notes from calvados combine harmoniously with vinous vermouth with creole-style bitters, this Sweet Manhattan-like cocktail's anchoring ingredient.
history:
Said to have been created in the 1870s by a bartender at the legendary Manhattan Club, which once stood at the north corner of 34th Street and 5th Avenue, New York City.

Our recipe is adapted from George J. Kappeler's 1895 Modern American Drinks – How to Mix and Serve All Kinds of Cups and Drinks.

name: Summer Rose Cocktail
preparation: STIR first three ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. POUR grenadine into the centre of the drink. This should settle to form a red layer in the base of the glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄2 shot	Kwai Feh lychee liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: Unless you've a sweet tooth don't mix the red and white layers - sip from the chocolate and lychee top and stop when you hit red.
history: Created in 2003 by Davide Lovison at Isola Bar, London, England.

name: Sunshine No. 1
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1 1⁄3 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: Light, fruity and heading a touch to the sweet side, but could well brighten up your day.
history: Adapted from a recipe in the 1949 edition of Esquire's Handbook for Hosts.

name: Tulip Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Rich but balanced with bags of fruit: apple, apricot and lemon.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Walnut Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Tuaca liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Walnut (Nocino) liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: Nutty but nice.
history: Created in 2005 by yours truly (Simon Difford).

name: Whiskey Squirt
preparation: SHAKE first three ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with soda from a siphon. Serve with straws.
ingredients:
2 shot	Peach purée
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄4 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
Top up with	Soda from siphon
review: Peach combines wonderfully with bourbon and this drink benefits from that marriage.
history: Adapted from a recipe purloined from David Embury's classic book, The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks.

name: Bronze Adonis
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into a chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
1 1⁄2 shot	Ambrato/ambre/amber vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Manzanilla sherry
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A simple yet fabulous twist on the Adonis.
history: Created in 2008 by Julian de Féral at The East Rooms, London, England.

name: Filthy Dirty Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄12 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Olive brine (from jarred olives)
1⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review:
The transition from a mere Dirty Martini to a Filthy Dirty Martini isn't so much about more olive brine but the addition of lime juice. This introduces citrus freshness (beyond the lemon zest twist) and sourness. Using Old Tom rather than London Dry Gin helps offset lime's sourness while bolstering botanical notes to stand up to the 'dirty' ingredients.

Unusually for a cocktail with citrus juice, I recommend you stir this cocktail, but if you prefer your Martinis shaken, then you'll need to dramatically cut back on the vermouth, olive brine and lime juice as shaking amplifies their flavours while masking the gin.
history: A variation of a dry martini. Detailed information can be found on our Dry Martini page.

name: Dutch Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄4 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
1⁄6 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: A modern twist on the classic Dr Martini inspired by a vintage bartender. In his 1882 New and Improved Bartender's Manual Harry Johnson's Martini Cocktail recipe calls for "a dash of curaçao or absinthe, if required."
history: Our Martini cocktail page details its evolution and other common variants.

name: Eureka Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
1⁄6 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A punchy, full-flavoured, veritable basket of fruit.
history: Recipe adapted from a 1935 Bar Florida (later renamed Floridita) menu, Havana, Cuba. "Sherry Brandy" in the menu's recipe is presumed to be a typo for cherry brandy.

name: Falconi
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Tawny port
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Spirit-forward, dry and subtly aromatic. Made more accessable with either bourbon in place of rye and/or ruby port in place of tawny port.

name: Moondream
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Manzanilla sherry
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Crème de Pêche de Vigne liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: Reminiscent of a delicately peach-flavoured Dry Martini.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2008 by Thomas Waugh at Death & Co., New York City, USA.

name: Oriental
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Be warned, this lightly sour, orangey whiskey-based cocktail packs a punch.
history: Adapted from the 1930The Savoy Cocktail Book where author, Harry Craddock, writes of this drink, "In August, 1924, an American Engineer nearly died of fever in the Philippines, and only the extraordinary devotion of Dr. B– saved his life. As an act of gratitude the Engineer gave Dr. B– the recipe of this cocktail." This recipe first appears in Count Benvenito Martini's 1916 book Cocktail Ology.

name: D'Artagnan
preparation: SHAKE first four ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Armagnac brandy
1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1 2⁄3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Use genuine freshly pressed juice and you'll have a tasty Mimosa-style drink.

name: Death By Chocolate
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with 6oz scoop of crushed ice and serve with straws.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Irish cream liqueur
1 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
3 scoop	Chocolate ice cream
review: Unsophisticated but delicious. Don't be cheap - use deluxe ice cream.

name: Dubliner Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A Manhattan variation calling for Irish whiskey instead of bourbon or rye, mixed with equal parts sweet vermouth, orange liqueur and a dash of orange bitters - respectfully Regan's Orange Bitters.
history: Adapted from a recipe by Gary 'gaz' Regan in 1999 in New York, USA.

name: Green Tea Cocktail #2
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Green tea liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Green tea (cold)
review: Exactly what it says on the tin: as subtle and delicate as green tea itself.
history: Created in 2006 by yours truly in London, England.

name: Whisky Cobbler
garnish: Mint sprigs bouquet, dehydrated orange wheel slice & dusting of freshly grated nutmeg. Serve with two straws.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass filled with crushed ice and churn to mix cocktail with ice until outside of glass frosts. Top with more crushed ice to fill glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
1⁄4 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Crème de Pêche de Vigne liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Caribbean Pineapple liqueur
review: Diluted fruity scotch – yum!
history:
Adapted from a recipe in David Embury's 1948 The Fine Art Of Mixing Drinks.
More information on the fascinating history of Cobblers

name: The Bird is the Word No. 1
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
5⁄6 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
5⁄12 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: To quote Fraser Campbell, the drinks creator, "influenced primarily by "The Last Word" with hints of "Yellow Parrot ...and a tequila base."
history:
Adapted from a drink created in May 2010 by Fraser Campbell at Tony Starrs Kitten Club, Melbourne, Australia.
Last Word history

name: Carroll Gardens
preparation: STIR ingredients over ice and strain into a cocktail glass. Squeeze lemon twist over the drink, wipe the rim with the peel and discard.
ingredients:
2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Nardini Amaro
1⁄6 shot	Luxardo Maraschino liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
review: This delightful twist on the Brooklyn is the most Italian American of drinks.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2008-9 by Joaquín Simó at Death & Company in New York City, USA in honour of his local neighbourhood, Brooklyn's Carroll Gardens.

name: Cobble Hill
preparation: MUDDLE cucumber in base of stirring glass. Add other ingredients, STIR with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3 slice	Cucumber (fresh)
2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
review: Sam describes his drink as "a summertime Manhattan. Light and floral, as opposed to the heavy style of the classic Manhattan."
history: Created in 2009 by Sam Ross at Milk & Honey in New York City, USA.

name: New Amsterdam
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
2⁄3 shot	Kirschwasser (cherry) eau-de-vie
1⁄12 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
2 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: A delicately flavoured and lightly balanced genever based drink with hints of kirsch and aromatic Creole bitters.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2006 by Jim Meehan at PDT, New York City, USA. This cocktail features in Jim's 2011 The PDT Cocktail Book.

name: Le Dijonnais Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Galander Fine mustard liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
2 dash	Celery bitters
review: A most unusual cocktail based on a most unusual product - mustard liqueur.
history: Created by Gonçalo de Sousa Monteiro, Berlin, Germany.

name: Treacle No.2
preparation: STIR half the rum with two ice cubes in a chilled glass. Add PX sherry, sugar syrup, bitters, and two more ice cubes. STIR some more and add another two ice cubes and the rest of the rum. STIR some more and add more ice.
ingredients:
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄3 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
1⁄4 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Made to appeal to drinkers who want a cocktail that tastes like Treacle. And it does.
history: Adapted from a 2011 rework of Dick Bradsell's original Treacle by Fraser Campbell at The Alchemist Bar in Melbourne, Australia.

name: Tonka
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Japanese blended whisky
1 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Mozart Chocolate Vodka
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A chocolaty, Japanese whisky-based Manhattan-like drink. Also works well served on-the-rocks.
history: Created in 2010 by Klaus St. Rainer at Schumann's Bar Munich, Germany.

name: New York, New York
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Apple Schnapps liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Whiskey barrel-aged bitters
review: A subtly apple influenced Sweet Manhattan from the Big Apple.
history: Discovered January 2011 at the King Cole Bar & Lounge, New York City, USA.

name: Raspberry Lassi Cocktail
garnish: Raspberries & dust with cracked black pepper
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
8 fresh	Raspberries
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1 shot	Yoghurt liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Crème de Framboise
review: Rich creamy vanilla yoghurt with fresh raspberries and raspberry liqueur fortified with vodka.
history: Created in 2011 by yours truly (Simon Difford) at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Side Err
preparation: POUR ingredients into ice-filled glass and stir.
ingredients:
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄4 shot	Bison grass vodka
1⁄12 shot	Caisteal Chamuis peated scotch whisky
2 3⁄4 shot	Medium dry apple cider
review: This apple delight combines apple brandy, Bison Grass vodka, cider (ideally Devonshire English cider) with a smoky whiff of Islay whisky.
history: Created in August 2011 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room in London, England.

name: Salty Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄6 shot	Caper brine (from jar)
review: As the name suggests, fino sherry and caper brine add saltiness but this 'Salty Martini' also has a distinct nuttiness from the sherry. We'd suggest both a long stir for generous dilution, and serving with grilled almonds.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2009 by Salvatore Calabrese at Fifty in London, England.

name: Christmas Pudding & Custard Cocktail
garnish: Serve chilled Pedro Ximenez sherry on the side
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled coupe glass. POUR chilled Pedro Ximenez sherry into second smaller glass to be served on the side
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Warninks Advocaat liqueur
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
1 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
review: As the name suggests, this drink combines flavours reminiscent of alcoholic custard with Pedro Ximenez sherry resembling liquid Christmas pudding.
history: A Christmas cocktail created in October 2011 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Dutch Blood and Sand
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A light, fragrant style of the classic, normally Scotch whisky-based, Blood and Sand.

name: Montréal
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Aniseed (anise) liqueur
3 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: A sweet rye Manhattan with French Creole influence.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Sips & Apps by Kathy Casey, Chronicle Books, Spring 2009.

name: Stout Fellow
preparation: SHAKE (BEWARE - the stout may be explosive in your shaker so hold both ends more firmly than usual) all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Stout beer
1 shot	Jamaican-style overproof aged pot still rum
1 shot	De Kuyper Crème de Cafe
1⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
review: In a similar style to an Espresso Martini but with very different ingredients including Guinness stout and coffee liqueur in place of espresso coffee.
history:
Created in 2013 by Matthew Coates (M.C.) at Jake's Bar and Still Room, Leeds, England. Matthew was one of five finalists in the Difford's Guide Beer-tail Competition for London Cocktail Week 2013 held on Friday 9th August 2013 at Simon Difford's Cabinet Room in London.

Matthew told us, "The inspiration behind my cocktail comes from my love of all of its components – rum, beer (Guinness) and coffee. I call my drink 'a stout fellow' because it's strong and hearty but also warming and 'friendly'. It also refers to the old Guinness advertising of 'Guinness for strength' encompassing more than one meaning of the word stout."

name: Biscotti Spritz

5⁄6 shot	Butterscotch liqueur
Top up with	Thomas Henry Soda Water

Created in 2013 by yours truly for Jamie's Italian Bar.

Created in 2013 by yours truly for Jamie's Italian Bars.

name: Trident
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Manzanilla sherry
1 shot	Cynar or other carciofo amaro
1 shot	Akvavit / Aquavit
2 dash	Peach bitters

Bone dry and boozy, this cocktail is aimed at those who have a penchant for both sherry and aquavit, not to mention bittersweet artichoke liqueurs - hardly mass market then. Nor are Aston Martin cars but I want one.

Be warned - use the wrong sherry and this drink falls apart - don't be tempted to sub manzanilla with a fino.
history: Robert Hess created this riff on a Negroni in 2002. The Trident name apparently was inspired by the fact that each of the three main ingredients comes from a different seafaring country.

name: Perfectly Paired cocktail

name: Pablo à Paris cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Martinique V.S.O.P rum
2⁄3 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)

2 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe

history:
Adapted from a drink created in March 2015 by Julian de Féral of the Gorgeous Group for Culinaire Bazaar, Paris, France.

Inspired by Picasso and the time he spent in Paris, where at the turn of the 20th century he painted one of his most important and influential masterpieces, Les Demoiselles d'Avognon. As well as being fond of absinthe, Picasso painted a cubist interpretation of a Suze bottle. To quote Julian, "the use of rhum agricole draws parallels between the African influence on Picasso and the culture in Caribbean French colonies." Julian's original recipe calls for Barbancourt 8 rhum agricole, Suze and Dolin Blanc.

name: Batida

history: Originating from Brazil, in Portuguese, batida means shaken or milkshake. Along with the Caipirinha, the Batida could be considered the country's national drink. Both drinks are based on Brazil's national spirit, cachaça.

name: El Magico

SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.

*Special ingredient #1: Honey basil syrup (1:1)
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
5⁄6 shot	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄6 shot	Soy milk
review:
"The El Magico cocktail is dedicated to the Bacardi family during its time in Cuba, where in the early 20th century magic and the occult were very popular. Here, Don Facundo Bacardi become a pioneer of the rum industry; he began to make a softer rum, using a charcoal filter, which at the time people thought must have been Facundo's own magic."

We say: If you are too lazy to make your own honey basil syrup then instead try substituting 7ml Monin basil syrup, 7ml honey syrup and 10ml water. The resulting drink is most unusual and may make you want to experiment with soy milk more. Basil is the lead flavour - giving the finished drink an almost minty freshness. Rum notes are subdued.
history: Russian BACARDÍ LEGACY 2016 winning cocktail by Alexander Kalachev, 15 Bar + Kitchen, Moscow.

name: Gringo's Blood & Sand

name: Susto

"Susto is from the Digestives section of our menu. Local Zapotec tribes of Oaxaca, Mexico, attribute illness to ‘Susto’ – emotional shock. Tribeswomen known as ‘Partera’ provide herbal remedies to ease the suffering."

name: And Now for Something Suze
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) & fresh thyme sprig on floating dehydrated lemon wheel
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄12 shot	Bigallet Thym
review: Gary's original recipe for this dry and spirituous aperitif cocktail calls for Navy strength gin but we found it punchy enough with a gin at 40 – 43% alc./vol..
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2017 by Gary Elliott at Dorcol Distilling and Brewing Co., San Antonio, USA.

Gary's original recipe calls for Plymouth Navy strength gin, a "premium dry vermouth such as Carpano", Suze Suze gentian liqueur and Bigallet Thym. He says, "I fell in love with Suze at first taste. The full-bodied citrus and herbs and the long spicy, bitter finish had me! I frequently use it as a modifier to add richness and a little herbal bitterness to various cocktails. Almost a secret ingredient.

I created this cocktail to highlight the flavors of Suze. After trying multiple styles of gin, I settled on Navy Strength Plymouth Gin. Various London dries and Botanist were also very good. I further experimented with vermouth. Sweet vermouth alone does not work well. A premium dry or a "perfect" with dry and bianco are best. I've been making variations of this cocktail for a few years.

Only recently have I added Bigallet Thym. While totally optional, the Thym enhances the woody notes of the Suze and prolongs the herbal flavors into the finish. Just remember that the Thym is the modifier here. More than 3 or 4 drops will result in a powerful taste of thyme. The nose is lemon and faint herbs. The first flavors are herbal and a touch woody. Juniper follows with continued herbs and just a hint of thyme. The finish is herbal, spicy and clean."

name: The Exotic Teapot

name: MyZo
preparation: MUDDLE chili in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄4 inch	Red chili pepper (jalapeño/fresno chili (10,000 SHU) deseeded)
1 2⁄3 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
5⁄6 shot	Elderflower cordial
5⁄6 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Rich vanilla with sweet elderflower balanced by zesty lemon and enlivened by chilli heat.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2004 by Myles Cunliffe, then a young bartender at Brownes Bar and Restaurant in Brighton, England. This cocktail earned Myles Cunliffe third place in the Stolichnaya sponsored UKBG Cocktail Challenge held in London's Sosho Match bar on 13th June 2004.

Like so many cocktails, even prize-winning cocktails, the MyZo was quickly forgotten. That was until years later when another similar cocktail, the Spicy Fifty, created soon after the competition by the famous bartender Salvatore Calabrese, began to be featured on websites (such as this one) and in books. Indeed, the Spicy Fifty first appeared in our Difford's Guide to Cocktails Twelfth Edition published in 2016. The similarity in ingredients with the Spicy Fifty reminded Myles' of his proud win as a young bartender and that it was Salvatore who presented Myles with his winning cheque [pictured here along with an photo of Dale DeGroff drinking a MyZo].

Myles tells the story, "In 2003 I had been familiar with vanilla vodka and elderflower having played around with that combo for a while, it took a messy chilli filled Sunday afternoon whereby I was trying chilli in everything and this combo worked. Originally it was a long drink (just add soda). I found the Stoli comp on the UKBG website and decided to enter. I submitted the drink and then forgot about it until I received an email from them asking to amend the recipe as it was a short drink recipe (read the comp rules is key to comps) so I removed the soda and resubmitted. This followed with an additional email inviting me to Sosho for the heats. Then the rest shall we say is history. The name however was supposed to be half Myles half Zoe as in MyZo however at the comp I was asked for the inspiration behind the drink (my girlfriend) and the name of my girlfriend (Zoe) and everyone assumed I had named it after her.... (still dining out on that one)."

This story has a happy ending as the MyZo is now not only recognised on this website but also in an letter from Salvatore Damiano, President of the UKBG saying "The United Kingdom Bartenders Guild confirms that the MyZo cocktail by M. Cunliffe has been archived in the UKBG national database." The letter confirms the official recipe as follows:

"MyZo
50 ml Stolichnaya vanilla Vodka,
25 ml fresh lemon juice,
25 ml elderflower cordial
1 cm piece red chilli
shake hard over ice and double strain into chilled cocktail glass"
