name: East Wind
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Dark/black/blackstrap rum
review: A vodka-based alternative to a Sweet Manhattan. Complex herbal vermouth notes fortified with vodka given a hint of extra complexity by a splash of dark rum.

name: St Hubertus Old Fashioned
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄2 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄4 shot	Jägermeisteror other German amaro
1⁄12 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
review: Dry and spirit-forward, as an old-fashioned should be, with hints of liquorice. It's dry, even with the 2.5ml of sugar I've added to Jason's original recipe, and some will want to increase the sugar syrup to 5ml. If you have it, then also try honey syrup rather than sugar syrup as this adds a little something extra.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Jason E. Clapham in Oxford, England.

name: Irish Blonde
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
2⁄3 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Fino sherry
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Dale DeGroff in New York, USA.

name: Eclipse Cocktail (by Harry Craddock)
preparation: Drop pitted black olive into glass and cover with grenadine. STIR gin and sloe gin with ice and carefully strain and slowly pour down the shaft of a bar spoon to layer over grenadine.
ingredients:
1 unit	Black olives
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
review: Gin-laced sweet and tart sloe berry sits over a sweet 'n' savoury base, this Eclipse's final treat.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 1927 to Harry Craddock to celebrate the 1927 total solar eclipse across England that year and first published in his 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Rose Martini
preparation: STIR (or SHAKE) all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Rose sugar syrup
4 drop	Difford's Margarita Bitters
review: Subtly floral and surprisingly dry.

name: Banana Cart
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Chairman's Reserve Spiced Rum
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Cinnamon syrup
1 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: This Cable Car variation harnesses the tried and tested cinnamon and banana flavour combo with zesty lemon and vanilla spiced rum.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England.

name: Black River
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	White overproof rum
2⁄3 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
2⁄3 shot	Amaro (e.g. Montenegro)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Rum funkiness and amaro bitterness combine in the bittersweet after-dinner sipper. For a less potent version use cachaça in place of the over-proof rum.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England. Originally made with Wray & Nephew overproof rum, Jason told us this cocktail is eponymously named for the Black River which runs through the Appleton Estate, where Wray & Nephew is distilled.

name: Painkiller Old Fashioned
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into an ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Pineapple rum
1 shot	Coconut rum liqueur (35-40% alc./vol.)
1⁄4 shot	Pineapple sugar syrup
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A tad on the sweet side, this is a distinctly tropical Rum Old Fashioned.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Sam Patel of @coventrycocktails.

name: Brownie
garnish: Dust with freshly grated nutmeg and garnish with a skewered Luxardo maraschino cherry
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1⁄6 shot	Kirschwasser (cherry) eau-de-vie
review: The same recipe made using white crème de cacao makes a tasty cocktail, but not one that befits the name.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Ted Saucier's 1951 book, Bottoms Up!.

name: Dot (1937 Café Royal)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
review: Apricot and gin dominate this spirit-forward late-night sipper.
history: Adapted from a recipe credited to "G. Matthews" in W. J. Tarling's 1937 The Café Royal Cocktail Book.

name: La Condesa
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Del Maguey Vida Clásico mezcal
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2 dash	Spiced chocolate bitters
review: An late-night, spirituous cocktail to enjoy in place of an Old-Fashioned or Manhattan. The assertive character of mezcal means this cocktail also suits a fuller-bodied 'sweet' vermouth.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Eron Plevon at Alex&nder at Copper & Kings in Louisville, Kentucky, USA.

name: Right-hand Twist
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Chairman's Reserve Spiced Rum
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
review: This spiced rum and PX sherry riff on the classic Negroni is firmly on the bitter side of bittersweet.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Bobby Hiddleston at Swift bar in London, England.

name: L' Italo Americano
preparation: POUR all ingredients into chilled glass and the add ice to fill.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Italicus liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Savoia Americano Rosso
1 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Pink Grapefruit soda
6 drop	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
review: Bittersweet citrus with delicate but assertive underlying herbal complexity and citric acidity.
history: Adapted (I added the grapefruit bitters) from a recipe created in 2023 by our friends at Ital Spirits for the USA launch of Savoia Americano Rosso.

name: Mono Dorado
garnish: Orange zest string cut over cocktail, knotted and dropped into cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Monkey Shoulder Fresh Monkey
1⁄2 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Piment d'Espelette chile liqueur
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Subtly herbal and funky with delicate chili spice.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Cern Bladen-Day of Filthy XIII in Bristol, England. The name translates from Spanish to Golden Monkey.

name: Strawberries & Cream
garnish: Hulled strawberry with mint sprig tip leaves
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 1⁄3 shot	Giffard Fraise des Bois liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: There's a subtle hint of chocolate in this gin-laced Strawberries and Cream.

name: Americano Perfecto
preparation: STIR first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with pilsner and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
4 shot	Pilsner lager
review: This riff on a classic Americano benefits from the use of dual vermouths and swaps out soda for pilsner beer.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Damon Boelte at Prime Meats in Brooklyn, New York City, USA.

name: Fernet Me Not No. 2
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
1 shot	Red/rosso vermouth semi-dry (circa 80gms sugar p/l)
1⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
3 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: You'll need to love fernet liqueur to appreciate this cocktail - if that's you, then you may well love it.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2012 by bartender Florian Minier at Haddington's American Tavern in Austin, Texas.

name: Spooky Tini
garnish: Drizzle chocolate sauce across the upturned glass to form a web-like pattern (to achieve thin lines, it may help to decant your sauce into a squeezy sauce bottle).
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Bourbon whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Irish cream liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Popcorn sugar syrup
1 1⁄2 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: Popcorn-infused creamy whiskey. An indulgent Halloween crowd-pleaser.
history: Popcorn-infused creamy whiskey. A Halloween crowd-pleaser.

name: Time Release
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1 shot	Dry white port
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
1⁄4 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
review: Gin and white port lead with sloe gin and Chartreuse adding their distinctive characteristics.
history: Adapted from a 2015 drink created by Julia Momose, while Beverage Director at GreenRiver restaurant (closed in 2018) in Chicago, USA.

name: Taco Belle
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Bourbon whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Corn/maize liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Piment d'Espelette chile liqueur
2 dash	Lime bitters
review: Toasty corn notes and enlivening chili influence this Old Fashioned-style cocktail.
history:
Created in October 2022 by Brent Roe, a fellow Discerning Drinker who shared his recipe via a comment on the Nixta page on Difford's Guide.

The Taco Belle American restaurant chain takes its name from its founder, Glen Bell who opened Bell's Drive-In and Taco Tia in San Bernardino, California, in 1954. The Taco Bell name was first used in 1962 when he opened his second restaurant in Downey, California. Two years later, Bell turned his restaurant concept into a franchise, and within just three years, there were 100 Taco Bells. Another three years on and there were 325 restaurants. In 2023, the number stood at 8,564 restaurants in 32 different countries.

name: Creole Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Bénédictine D.O.M. liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Amer Picon
review:
This Manhattan-like cocktail is best appreciated as an after-dinner digestivo or late-night sipper. Thanks to the comments below, I have continued to revisit this cocktail, and depending on continued feedback, I will change our recipe above. My own work-in-progress preference is for:
45ml (1½oz) Bonded rye whiskey
45ml (1½oz) Rosso vermouth
10ml (⅓oz) Bénédictine D.O.M.
10ml (⅓oz) Amer Picon
Stirred and strained into a chilled coupe.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Jacques Straub's 1913 Manual of Mixed Drinks. It also notably appears in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: Macouba Old Fashioned
garnish: Orange zest twist expressed and discarded. Dust with freshly grated nutmeg.
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Rhum J.M. Terroir Volcanique
1⁄2 shot	Rhum Clément Créole Shrubb liqueur
3 dash	Angostura Cocoa Bitters
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Orange influences this Old Fashioned but it's the aged agricole rum that dominates and shines.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Joseph Akhavan at his Mabel bar in Paris, France.

name: Post Melon
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄4 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Watermelon sugar syrup
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A Dry Daiquiri with fernet and watermelon syrup. Sounds crazy but I bet this is a cocktail you'll finish.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2022 by Tom Parham at Pennyroyal bar in Cardiff, Wales.

name: Away Colors
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Fernet Branca liqueur
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Banana rum awakened by herbal amaro.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2016 by Zachary Gelnaw-Rubin at Lion Lion Bar (now shuttered) in East Harlem, New York City, USA.

name: Cane & Coco
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. FLOAT aromatic bitters.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Rhum J.M. Terroir Volcanique
1⁄2 shot	Coconut rum liqueur (35-40% alc./vol.)
3 1⁄2 shot	Coconut water
12 drop	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: With quality pressed coconut water, this cocktail is almost creamy, and as the name promises, it tastes of coconut-laced rhum agricole.

name: Tropical Sin
preparation: POUR all ingredients into glass and the fill glass with ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Piment d'Espelette chile liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Coconut liqueur (under 35% alc./vol.)
3 1⁄2 shot	Pineapple soda
review: Alluring tropical fruit with a touch of chili spice.
history: Adapted from a recipe promoted by Three Cents in 2024.

name: Grapeshot
garnish: Lemon zest twist expressed and discharged. Adorn with skewered red grape.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Gold rum (1-3 years old pot & column blend)
1 shot	Red grape juice (e.g. Kedem or Welch's Purple Grape Juice)
1⁄2 shot	Ginger liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Subtle ginger spice in a rum-laced grape sour.
history: This recipe was adapted from one created in 2021 by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR in Oxford, England. Jason formulated it using an old bottling of the King's Ginger, but as this liqueur has since changed, he recommends Crabbie's Ginger Liqueur instead.

name: Pear & Grapefruit Spritz
preparation: POUR all ingredients into chilled glass, briefly stir and fill glass with ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Pear & cognac liqueur
1 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco (chilled)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
3 1⁄2 shot	Thomas Henry Pink Grapefruit soda (chilled)
review: A cognac pear and pink grapefruit spritz balanced by a splash of lemon juice. Yes, I though the same. What's lemon juice doing in a "Pamplemousse Spritz"? So tried with pink grapefruit juice but I prefer this with the zingy sourness of lemon juice.
history: An adaptation of the Belle Pamplemousse Spritz promoted by our friends at Rémy Cointreau USA.

name: Spiced Plantain Negroni
garnish: Slice of plantain or dried banana chip
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Chairman's Reserve Spiced Rum
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Bittersweet orange-red aperitivo
review: A lightly spiced, banana-influenced Negroni that's edging to the sweet side of bittersweet.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Dave Marsland, St. Lucia Distillers Brand Ambassador.

name: Apple Spritz
preparation: POUR first 2 ingredients into glass then TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Apple Schnapps liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Peachtree peach schnapps
3 1⁄2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Sweet, fruity champagne.
history:
Discovered in 2003 at Paramount Hotel in New York City, USA.
Spritz history and the Spritz family of cocktails

name: Black Magic
preparation: MUDDLE grapes in base of shaker. Add liqueur, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
12 fresh	Red grapes (seedless)
1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
3 1⁄2 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Peachier in colour than black but balanced and tasty. Not sweet.

name: Crème Anglaise Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
1 1⁄3 shot	Warninks Advocaat liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: As the name suggests, reminiscent of alcoholic crème anglaise.
history: Created in 2004 by yours truly in London, England.

name: Dolores
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
2 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
1 shot	Fino sherry
review: Aromatic and well balanced, provided you use French-made Dubonnet.
history: A classic. Some recipes include a splash of orange juice.

name: Give me a Dime
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1 shot	Butterscotch liqueur
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: Creamy, sweet and tasty.

name: Honey Wall
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
5⁄6 shot	Tuaca liqueur
5⁄6 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
review: Rum-laced, rich and chocolaty.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2002 by Dick Bradsell at Downstairs at Alfred's in London, England.

name: Mexican Manhattan
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Añejo tequila
1 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 dash	Difford's Margarita Bitters
review: You've tried this with bourbon and rye, now surprise yourself with aged tequila.
history: Manhattan cocktail history

name: Platinum Blonde (creamy)
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
5⁄6 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: This after-dinner sipper maybe creamy but it's balanced rather than sweet with aged rum nuanced by cognac and orange liqueur. Creamy yet sophisticated.

name: El Presidente (sans grenadine)
garnish: Orange zest twist (discarded) & Luxardo maraschino cherry
preparation: STIR ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
review: Bone dry, light and delicate. The sweetness and colour contributed by the maraschino cherry garnish are essential to this drink's success.

name: Princess Mary's Pride
preparation: STIR (or shake) all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
5⁄6 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
5⁄6 shot	Ambrato/ambre/amber vermouth
review: Apple brandy to the fore, followed by aromatised wine.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Harry Craddock on 28th February 1922 to celebrate the wedding of H.R.H. Princess Mary, and published in his 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book where he calls for this cocktail to be shaken rather than stirred.

name: Red Rover
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
3 shot	Shiraz red wine
1 shot	Navy rum (54.5% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
review: Carpet-scarring red with the body of red wine but the palate of a cocktail.

name: Rhubarb & Honey Bellini
preparation: SHAKE rhubarb syrup and honey liqueur with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with Prosecco and gently stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Rhubarb & orange preserve
1 1⁄4 shot	Krupnik spiced honey liqueur
Top up with	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
review: The implausible combination works surprisingly well.
history: A simplified adaptation of a drink created in 2003 by Tony Conigliaro at London's Shumi.

name: Vanilla Sensation
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
1 shot	Sour apple liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: A pleasing vanilla twist on an Apple Martini.
history: Created in 2003 but by whom is unknown.

name: Violet Affinity
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Crème de violette liqueur
1 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: Delicate and surprisingly complex for such a simple drink.
history: Our adaptation of the classic Affinity.

name: Yacht Club
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
review: Rum-laced and slightly sweet with hints of apricot fruit.
history: Adapted from a recipe purloined from David Embury's classic book, The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks.

name: Grand Slam
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Swedish Punsch liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: This after-dinner libation is slightly sweet but wonderfully aromatic.
history: Adapted from a recipe in Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book.

name: The Leavenworth
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
10 drop	Tiki bitters
review: This great cocktail is dramatically influenced by the style of rum used. Francesco's original recipe calls for English Harbour rum.
history: Created in 2008 by Francesco Lafranconi of Southern Wine & Spirits, USA.

name: Oooh Ginger
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Añejo tequila
2⁄3 shot	Ginger liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
review: Subtle ginger spice flavours this dry tequila martini-esque cocktail.
history: Created in March 2008 by Dick Bradsell and yours truly at The Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Grasshopper
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄6 shot	Giffard Peppermint Pastille crème de menthe
1 1⁄6 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1 1⁄6 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: It's hard not to like this creamy slightly sweet minty after-dinner treat.
history:
The Grasshopper is the signature cocktail at Tujague's, the second oldest restaurant in New Orleans, which was opened in 1856 by Guillaume Tujague. Guillaume's sister took over the running of the restaurant when he died in 1912 but a few years later, after her husband's death, she sold Tujague's to Jean-Dominic Castet and his business partner, Philip Guichet, Sr..

Legend has it, in 1919 (or some say during Prohibition in the 1920s), that Philibert Guichet won second prize in a prestigious New York cocktail competition for his Grasshopper cocktail. Sadly, there is no documentary evidence to support this win or his creation of the cocktail.

A recipe for a drink called the Grasshopper, consisting of equal parts crème de menthe layered over crème de cacao appears in William "Cocktail Bill" Boothby's 1908 World's Drinks and How to Mix Them where its creation is attributed to "Harry O'Brien, late of the Palace Hotel, San Francisco."

At some point (perhaps even by Philibert Guichet at Tujague's) cream is added as a third ingredient to the 1908 two-ingredient layered Grasshopper to make the shaken cocktail we recognise today.

Several newspapers from the 1950s point to the modern-day Grasshopper's creation being in the late 1940s in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA, including a piece in the Sunday 19th February 1950 Monroe Morning World (Monroe, Louisiana, USA).

name: Pink Squirrel
garnish: Dust with grated nutmeg and line of Peychaud's bitters across surface.
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Crème de noyau liqueur
1 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1 1⁄2 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: Light pink, sweet and creamy with subtle notes of chocolate, toasted almond and pomegranate.
history:
The Pink Squirrel was created in 1941 by Bryant Sharp at Bryant's Cocktail Lounge in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA. Apparently, the original recipe called for ice cream rather than cream and indeed the Pink Squirrel may have started life as a milkshake spiked with spirits prior to Repeal. Considering it unnecessary, in the 1960s, Bryant's second owner, Pat Malmberg removed the crème de cacao from the original recipe and this is how Bryant's make their Pink Squirrels to this day.

We're indebted to Michael Lazar (AKA Mr. Manhattan) and his Stirred Not Shaken  for researching the origin of this cocktail and there's more detail on Bryant's and the Pink Squirrel on his blog.

name: BBC (by Marian Beke)
garnish: Apple fan or dehydrated apple slice wheel
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Becherovka liqueur
1 dash	Wormwood bitters (optional)
review: Based on the classic B & B cocktail with rum replacing brandy and Becherovka in place of Bénédictine.
history: Created in 2009 by Marian Beke at the Artesian Bar, London, England. The Artesian Bar sits in the Langham Hotel opposite the BBC's Broadcasting House. Indeed, the BBC moved into the Langham after the Broadcasting House was bombed during the Second World War ... they stayed almost 20 years.

name: Woxum
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄2 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
review: The flavour of Chartreuse shines through in this slightly sweet, spirituous cocktail. Historically served straight-up but we prefer on-the-rocks in an old-fashioned glass.
history: Recipe is adapted from Albert Stevens Crockett's 1935 The Old Waldorf-Astoria Bar Book.

name: Molly's Milk
preparation: STIR first two ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. FLOAT whipped cream on drink.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1 1⁄2 shot	Southern USA-style liqueur 40% (e.g. Southern Comfort)

name: Bandera
preparation:
1. POUR tequila to fill first shot glass (caballitos).

2. POUR lime juice to fill second shot glass.

3. To make Sangrita to fill the third glass, SHAKE rest of ingredients with ice and fine strain into glass.
- 15ml (½oz) Tomato juice
- 15ml (½oz) Pomegranate juice
- 7.5ml (¼oz) Orange juice
- 15ml (½oz) Lime juice
- 5ml (spoon) Grenadine syrup
- 2 drop Hot pepper sauce
- 2 dash Worcester sauce
- 1 pinch Salt
- 1 grind Black pepper

4. Instruct the drinker to sip from each of the three glasses alternatively.

Ingredients for all three glasses:
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Silver blanco tequila
2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Tomato juice
1⁄2 shot	Pomegranate juice
1⁄4 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
2 drop	Hot pepper sauce (red)
2 dash	Worcestershire sauce
1 pinch	Salt (sea salt)
1 grind	Black pepper
review: In Mexico the quality of the homemade Sangrita can make or break a bar. The Sangrita in this trio is spicy and slightly sweet.
history:
A popular and classic way of serving tequila in Mexico. Bandera is Spanish for the flag, and the Bandera de México is, of course, green, white and red, hence the three glasses: lime juice (green), Blanco tequila (clear or "white") and Sangrita (red).

The Bandera is also drunk to celebrate Mexican Independence Day with the green lime juice representing the independence movement and the red Sangrita chaser representing the blood of the national heroes. Appropriately, sangrita means 'little blood' in Spanish, and Sangrita is served with tequila in practically every bar in Mexico.

name: Alamagoozlum Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Rutte Old Simon Genever
1⁄2 shot	Jamaican aged blended rum with funk
1⁄2 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄6 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1⁄3 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
2⁄3 shot	Chilled water
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: Tastes reminiscent of Cough Candy with a quintet of big-flavoured ingredients combining harmoniously, including a whopping 5ml (1/6oz) of bitters.
history:
A "Plantation Alamagoozlum" is referenced as "an excellent preventive of colds and chills" in a 1935 column in The Indianapolis News and then as an Alamagoozlum in a 1937 edition of the Louisville, Kentucky, Courier-Journal. However, it most notably features in Charles H. Baker's 1939 The Gentleman's Companion: Around the World with Jigger, Beaker and Flask as "J. Pierpont Morgan's Alamagoozlum, the Personal Mix Credited to that Financier, Philanthropist, & Banker of a Bygone Era."

Baker gives the following recipe "To serve about 5 cocktails: take 1 jigger each of Jamaica rum, gomme syrup, and yellow or green Chartreuse; add ½ pony yellow Curaçao and ½ pony of Angostura bitters. Add 2 scant ponies of Holland gin, the same of water; donate ½ the white of an egg and hard shake with lots of cracked ice. Serve in a Manhattan glass."

As with so many classic cocktails, our recipe is based on David A. Embury's 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks, where Embury says, "This cocktail is supposed to have been a specialty of the elder Morgan of the House of Morgan, which goes to prove as a bartender he was an excellent banker."

Both Charles H. Baker and David Embury credit the creation, or at least this cocktail's notoriety, to John Pierpont Morgan Sr. (1837 - 1913), a Wall Street banker and financier who headed the banking firm that went on to be known as J.P. Morgan and Co., then Morgan, Grenfell & Company.

J. P. Morgan liked to drink in style and frequented New York City's most fashionable clubs, including the Union Club. When his friend, John King, president of Erie Railroad, was blackballed from the Union Club, Morgan resigned and in 1891 established the Metropolitan Club of New York. He commissioned Stanford White to "...build me a club fit for gentlemen, forget the expense..." at One East 60th Street; on the corner of 5th Avenue. As the club's first President, he invited John King to be a charter member.

Top up with	Soda from siphon

On the palate this starts as a nutty sour and finishes with enlivening spice.

Hazelnut-flavoured sugar syrup is key to this recipe, which is even tastier when made with a roasted hazelnut syrup.
