Martin says in his 2016 book Smuggler's Cove, that he created this cocktail "for my old pal Falin Minoru, artist and proprietor of Tiki Kaimuki Fine Boozing Vessels, tiki mugs made in Oakland, California."

name: Asian Mary
preparation: MUDDLE ginger in base of shaker and add vodka. Squeeze wasabi paste onto bar spoon and STIR with vodka and ginger until dissolved. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
3 slice	Fresh ginger root (thumbnail-sized slice)
3 pea	Wasabi paste
3 shot	Ketel One Citroen Vodka
1 barspoon	Soy sauce
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
4 shot	Tomato juice
review: An aptly named Bloody Mary with plenty of Asian spice.
history: Based on the classic Bloody Mary, of which more information can be found on our Bloody Mary cocktail page.

name: Chocolate & Cranberry 'Martini'
garnish: Orange juice, chocolate powder and sugar rim
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
3⁄4 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
4 drop	Bob's Vanilla bitters
review: The chocolate rim sounds naff, but it makes this cocktail.
history: Created in 2003 by yours truly in London, England.

name: DC Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Vanilla rum/vanilla-infused light rum
1⁄4 shot	Hazelnut liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄12 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
4 drop	Bob's Vanilla bitters
review: Vanilla, chocolate and a hint of nut. Enjoy as an altern'atini or add more sugar syrup to make this into a dessert cocktail.
history: Adapted from a cocktail discovered in 2000 at Teatro Club in London, England. Firmly from the age of "altern'atinis."

name: Jerez
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄2 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
1 shot	Peachtree peach schnapps
1 shot	Sauvignon blanc wine
1 shot	La Vieille Prune plum brandy
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Sherry depth and stoned fruit flavours.
history: This drink heralds from one of the noble houses in Spain - well that's what the sherry PR told us, anyway, we've changed the recipe slightly.

name: Peppered Mary
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Pepper flavoured vodka
2 shot	Yellow bell pepper juice
2 shot	Tomato juice
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
7 drop	Hot pepper sauce (red)
1 barspoon	Worcestershire sauce
review: A Bloody Mary with sweet and spicy pepper.

name: Toblerone Cocktail
garnish: Dust surface of drink with dark chocolate powder and place two segments of Toblerone chocolate on rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Vanilla rum/vanilla-infused light rum
1⁄2 shot	Disaronno amaretto
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
1⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1⁄2 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review:
Nibble at the garnish as you sip honeyed, chocolate and almond-flavoured liquid candy. Yumm.

Best made with a gold (1-3 yer old) light rum infused with a vanilla pod, rather than a commercially produced vanilla-flavoured rum.
history: Created in 2003 by yours truly and originally named the Triangular Martini after the triangular Toblerone chocolate bar, which incidentally was invented in 1908 by the Swiss chocolate maker Theodor Tobler. The chocolate bar's name is a blend of Tobler with Torrone, the Italian word for honey-almond nougat, one of its main ingredients.

name: Bitches Brew
preparation: DRY SHAKE all ingredients without ice. Add ice, SHAKE again and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Rhum Clément Blanc
1 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Pimento dram/Allspice liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
1 shot	Egg (white & yolk)
review: This flavoursome flip-style drink comes served with a hint of Caribbean spice.
history: Created in 2008 by Daniel Eun at PDT in New York City, USA.

name: Golden Reign
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1⁄2 shot	Galliano L'Autentico liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1⁄4 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: A lightly creamy, after dinner drink.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2002 by Peter Dorelli at The American Bar at The Savoy Hotel, London, England to celebrate the Queen's golden jubilee.

name: Devil's Horn
garnish: Two chillies on rim to form devil's horns
preparation: Lightly MUDDLE (just press) chilli pepper in base of shaker to release its flavour. (If you muddle hard then the finished cocktail will be overly spicy). Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 slice	Red chili pepper (jalapeño/fresno chili (10,000 SHU) deseeded) (fine sliced)
3 fresh	Raspberries
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
3⁄4 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
1 shot	Honey sugar syrup
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A great balance of sweetness, sourness and spice.
history: Created in 2010 by Roger Vilalta at Banker's Bar, Mandarin Oriental, Barcelona, Spain.

name: Gilbey Vintner's Punch
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. Carefully FLOAT stout.
ingredients:
1 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1 shot	Oloroso sherry
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Orange sherbet
1 shot	Stout beer
history: Created in 2015 by Chris Strong, The Luggage Room, London, England.

name: Belgium Avenue
preparation:
SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

Special ingredient #1: Homemade agave and chamomile syrup
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Bacardi Gold rum
2⁄3 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄2 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
1⁄3 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
history: The Latvian Bacardí Legacy 2015 winning cocktail by Juris Ķēniņš at Mute in Latvia.

name: Slow Comfortable Fuzzy Screw Against the Wall
preparation: STIR first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. FLOAT sloe gin on surface so it bleeds into drink. Finish with Galliano FLOAT.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Southern USA-style liqueur 40% (e.g. Southern Comfort)
1⁄2 shot	Peachtree peach schnapps
3 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
1⁄2 shot	Galliano L'Autentico liqueur
review: Peach schnapps is borrowed from the Fuzzy Navel to influence this member of the Slow Comfortable family, its presence gives this cocktail a distinctive sweet peachy note.

name: Cool Smoke
preparation:
SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled coupe.

Special ingredient #1: Cucumber skin cordial
Special ingredient #2: Pickling liquor
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Tennessee whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Ambrato/ambre/amber vermouth (smoked)
5⁄6 shot	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
1 dash	*Special ingredient #2 (see above)
1 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
1 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
history: Created in November 2017 by Jo Last at The Domino Club, Leeds, UK, for Jack Daniel’s Tennessee Calling II.

name: Leave A Message After The Beep...
garnish: Thyme sprig and Angostura Bitters dashes
preparation:
SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.

Special ingredient #1: Homemade raspberry shrub (6% abv)

Special ingredient #2: Homemade thyme sugar syrup (2:1)
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Tennessee whiskey
2⁄3 shot	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
1⁄3 shot	Rubino vermouth
2⁄3 shot	*Special ingredient #2 (see above)
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
5⁄6 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
history: Created in November 2017 by Josh Davies of The Hedonist Project, Leeds, UK, for Jack Daniel’s Tennessee Calling II.

name: Pinot Grinchio
preparation: SHAKE (briefly) all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Grain Scotch whisky
1⁄3 shot	Pinot Noir red wine
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Fraise des Bois liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Vanilla sugar syrup
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
Top up with	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
review: Jammy strawberry fruit and cream-of-soda vanilla fortified by grain whisky and enlivened by prosecco.
history: Created in 2018 by Robb Collins, Group Head Bartender at London Cocktail Club, London, England, who says this is a "Beautiful drink for Christmas, long, fruity and refreshing, and of course a nice touch of bubbles."

name: Tears & Dreams
garnish: Edible flower & fresh kaffir lime leaf
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
1⁄3 shot	Ratafia de Marseille
1⁄6 shot	Apricot (abricot) eau-de-vie
2⁄3 shot	Pineapple juice
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Cinnamon syrup
review: Fruity but well-balanced with distinctive coffee and cacao flavours from the rum.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Katalin Bene at Voodoo Reyes - Potions & Botanicals in Geneva, Switzerland.

name: Gold El Camino
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄2 shot	Galliano L'Autentico liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Creamy orange tequila with a hint of chocolate, anise and peppermint.
history: A Golden Cadillac with added reposado tequila.

name: On Bended Knee
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Ginger liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 dash	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
3 drop	Bob's Cardamom bitters
review: If a cold cocktail can be warming, then with its generous rye whiskey and ginger liqueur, this is such a cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Susanna McMahon, a keen amateur mixologist and 74-year-old grandmother.

name: Bon Vivant
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Jamaican aged blended rum with funk
2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
1⁄2 shot	Becherovka liqueur
1 dash	Black walnut bitters
1⁄3 shot	Chilled water (omit if using wet ice)
review: Full-bodied like the rum that so influences herbal-influenced this late-night tipple.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England, who says, "Named thus because Jerry Thomas combines brandy and Jamaica rum 2:1 in a number of his famous punches; created with rums like Plantation Xaymaca or Berry Bros. Jamaica Rum in mind."

name: Amer Negroni
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄2 shot	Grapefruit gin
1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄2 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
4 drop	Bob's Grapefruit Bitters
review: Bittersweet zesty grapefruit with delicate apple brandy notes.
history: Adapted from a recipe discovered in January 2021 at The Londoner Hotel in Leicester Square, London, England.

name: Cardamom & Banana Vieux Carré
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Cardamom sugar syrup
4 drop	Bob's Cardamom bitters
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: One of those cocktails where the name aptly describes what's in the glass. Spirit-forward and just nudging towards being a tad on the sweet side.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Anthony Auger at Benne On Eagle restaurant in The Foundry Hotel, Asheville, North Carolina, USA.

name: Tender Nob
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄3 shot	Strega liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Meletti amaro
1⁄12 shot	Hazelnut liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
review: As the ice melts, dilution opens and amplifies this spirit-forward, piney, bittersweet, delicately nutty cocktail.
history:
Named after the area between San Francisco's Tenderloin and Nob Hill neighbourhoods, this cocktail is adapted from a recipe created by Kevin Diedrich at Pacific Cocktail Haven in San Francisco, USA. Kevin's original recipe calls for:
30ml (1oz) Cognac
30 (1oz) Rye whiskey
15 (½oz) Strega
7.5ml (¼oz) Luxardo Amaro Abano
7.5ml (¼oz) walnut orgeat

name: Atonement
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chink of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Dark/black/blackstrap rum
1⁄2 shot	Blanc quinquina/kina (e.g. Mattei Cap Corse or Kina L'Aéro d'Or)
1⁄4 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Orgeat Syrup
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Quinquina and spirituous spice from the whiskey and run balance the rich notes of the raisiny sherry and particularly the nutty orgeat. Dilution also seems key to the success of this combo, hence my preference of serving old-fashioned-style.
history:
Adapted from a cocktail served at Georgia James restaurant in Houston, Texas. The original was served straight-up in a Nick & Nora style glass.

This cocktail was kindly brought to my attention in October 2022 by Frank Rozzelle who was visiting from Louisiana and dined with friends at the steakhouse and described the Atonement as "one of the best cocktails I have ever consumed!" This recipe is my own interpretation rather than an attempt at reproduction.

name: Bijou Blanc
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass Preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's Navy Strength Royal Dock Gin
2⁄3 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
3 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: As the name suggests, a riff on a classic Bijou based on 'white' rather than 'red' vermouths.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2022 by Estelle Bossy at Le Rock in New York City, USA.

name: Bartender's Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
3⁄4 shot	Fino sherry
3⁄4 shot	Dubonnet/French rouge aromatised wine
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Grand Marnier or other cognac orange liqueur
review: This aromatic Martini with a florish has rich orange notes followed by a dry fino sherry finish.

name: Bee Sting
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with ginger ale
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
5⁄6 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1 1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1⁄4 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
review: Delicately spirituous spiced honeyed apple interplay in this long, refreshing cocktail.
history: Adapted from a cocktail discovered in 2005 at The Royal Exchange Grand Café & Bar in London, England.

name: Casablanca No.2
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Ketel One Citroen Vodka
1 shot	Warninks Advocaat liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Galliano L'Autentico liqueur
1 shot	Orange juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: Creamy, citrusy, alcoholic custard.

name: Cherry Alexander
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
1⁄2 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1⁄3 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: A rich Black Forest Gateau-like fruity twist on the creamy classic gin-based Alexander and the popular Brandy Alexander.
history: Created by Wayne Collins for Maxxium UK.

name: Frida's Brow
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄2 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1⁄2 shot	Milk (whole milk/full 3-4% fat)
review: Creamy, sweetened tequila with hints of chocolate.
history: Discovered in 2005 at Velvet Margarita Cantina in Los Angeles, USA.

name: Key Lime
preparation: BLEND all ingredients without ice and serve.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
1 1⁄2 shot	Lime flavoured vodka
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
1⁄2 shot	Lime cordial (sweetened lime juice)
3 scoop	Vanilla ice cream
review: Tangy, smooth and rich! Alcoholic ice-cream for grown-ups.

name: Lychee Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Kwai Feh lychee liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lychee juice drink
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Lychee syrup
review: If you like lychee you'll love this delicate Martini.
history: Adapted from a recipe thought to have been first made in 2001 at Clay, a Korean restaurant in New York City, USA.

name: Koningsdag cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
3⁄4 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Ginger liqueur
1 1⁄2 shot	Carrot juice (freshly extracted)
5 drop	Bob's Coriander Bitters
review: This very Dutch celebratory cocktail was created using Dutch vodka, Dutch orange curacao, and Dutch-made ginger liqueur. Carrot juice provides the all-important orange hue and subtle flavour. For the truly orange King's Day experience, make it with 50% Ketel One vodka and 50% Ketel One Oranje, or even replace vodka with 100% Ketel One Oranje.
history: Created by yours truly in April 2015 in celebration of Koningsdag, a festival held in the Netherlands on 27th April each year when the Dutch dress in orange and party to commemorate their monarch's birthday. Any excuse to party!

name: Melon Collie Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Light white rum (charcoal-filtered 1-4 years old)
3⁄4 shot	Green melon liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Coconut rum liqueur (35-40% alc./vol.)
1⁄4 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1 1⁄2 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: Something of a holiday disco drink but tasty all the same.
history: Created in 2003 by Simon King at MJU, Millenniun Hotel, London, England.

name: Millionaire No.1
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Jamaican-style overproof aged pot still rum
3⁄4 shot	Hayman's Sloe Gin
3⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: High proof pot still rum funk, along with a decent quality apricot brandy and sloe gin is key to the success of this full-flavoured red cocktail.
history:
Recipe adapted from Harry Craddock's 1930 The Savoy Cocktail Book. Craddock also lists a "Millionaire Cocktail (No.2)" as follows:
"1 Dash Anisette
The white of 1 Egg
1/3 Absinthe
2/3 Dry gin
Shake well and strain into cocktail glass."

In his 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks, David Embury's says "At some bars a drink served under the name of "Millionaire" which consists of lime juice, slow gin, and apricot brandy, with a few dashes of Jamaica rum. Since the sloe gin, which is a liqueur, predominates in this drink, I do not regard it as a true cocktail." Embury is more complimentary of what he calls a "Millionaire Royal", proclaiming it to be "a very satisfactory drink."

name: Pepper & Vanilla
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
3⁄4 shot	Pepper flavoured vodka
3⁄4 shot	Tuaca liqueur
1 shot	Licor 43 Original liqueur
1 shot	Yellow bell pepper juice
review: Vanilla and pepper seem to complement each other in a sweet and sour kind of way.
history: Created in 2002 by yours truly (Simon Difford), London, England and originally somewhat dodgily named Pepper & Vanilla'tini. Incidentally, Pieprz i wanilia (which translates as Pepper and Vanilla) was a popular Polish television programme broadcast by TVP. This travel documentary program was broadcast for over 20 years with 300 episodes.

name: Smooth & Creamy
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 shot	Coconut rum liqueur (35-40% alc./vol.)
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
3⁄4 shot	Milk (whole milk/full 3-4% fat)
review: Creamy and moreish.

name: Southern Tea
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1⁄2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1 shot	Southern USA-style liqueur 40% (e.g. Southern Comfort)
2 shot	Earl Grey tea (cold)
review: Sweet fruity flavours balanced by tannic bitterness in the tea.
history: Created in 2002 by yours truly in London, England.

name: Tarte Tatin Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE first three ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. Separately, SHAKE cream and egg white with ice and strain back into shaker. DRY SHAKE (without ice) and carefully pour over back of spoon so as to LAYER over drink.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
3⁄4 shot	Apple Schnapps liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Caramel Toffee liqueur
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1⁄2 shot	Egg white (pasteurised) or Aquafaba (chickpea water) or 3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam cocktail foamer
review: A creamy top hides a vanilla, apple and caramel combo. Inspired by the dessert created by the Tatin sisters, a tart of caramelised apples cooked under a pastry lid.
history: Created in 2003 by yours truly (Simon Difford), London, England.

name: Argha Noah
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄6 shot	Honey sugar syrup
1⁄4 shot	Drambuie liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Oloroso sherry
1⁄2 shot	Cranberry juice (sweetened)
review: Delicately spiced, honeyed and sherried aged rum.
history: Created in January 2009 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Perpetual Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Crème Yvette liqueur
1⁄12 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
4 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: Delicate berry fruit and chocolate influences herbal vinous vermouth.
history:
Recipe adapted from Hugo R. Ensslin's 1917 book Recipes for Mixed Drinks (pape 26):
"½ Italian Vermouth
½ French Vermouth
2 dashes Crème de Cacao
4 dashes Crème Yvette
Shake well in a mixing glass with cracked ice, strain and serve."

name: Greek Piña Colada
preparation: BLEND ingredients crushed ice, pour into glass and serve immediately with straws.
ingredients:
2 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 1⁄2 shot	Yoghurt liqueur
2 wedge	Pineapple (fresh)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Caribbean Pineapple liqueur
1 shot	Coconut rum liqueur (35-40% alc./vol.)
review: A yoghurt and rum based pineapple and coconut drink, and if your blender is sufficiently powerful, with tiny fragments of pineapple shrapnel.
history:
Created in 2011 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England.
Piña Colada cocktail history

name: Mure & Lavender Batida
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with crushed ice and serve with straws.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cachaça
1 2⁄3 shot	Coconut water
1⁄2 shot	Lavender sugar syrup
1⁄4 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
6 fresh	Blackberries
review: As the name suggests this creamy Batida is flavoured with blackberries and lavender.
history: Recipe by Jorge Balbontin, Barcelona, Spain.

name: The Southern Alliance
garnish: Orange zest twist & Luxardo Maraschino Cherries
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably a large chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
2⁄3 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄2 barspoon	Balsamic vinegar of Modena
1 dash	Plum bitters
review: Cognac shines with a delicate fruitiness in this dryish, bittersweet stirred cocktail served on the rocks.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Angelos Bafas at Fabrica Cocktail Bar, Drama, Greece.

name: Late Night
garnish: Dust with freashly grated tonka bean & dried rose petals
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄3 shot	Oloroso sherry
1⁄3 shot	Pear liqueur (Poire William)
1⁄6 shot	Poire William eau-de-vie
2 drop	Bob's Abbotts bitters
review: This spirit-forward stirred cocktail combines fruity pear, dry oloroso sherry and fortifying cognac.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2015 by Claudia Agliano at 34 Restaurant in Mayfair, London, England. Claudia's original recipe specifies 52.5ml Martell XO cognac, 22.5ml poire william liqueur, 15ml oloroso sherry and 3 drops Abbotts bitters.

name: Elixir De Longue Vie (Elixir of Long Life)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Creme de Chataigne
1⁄2 shot	Pineau des Charentes blanc
1⁄6 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
2 dash	Lemon bitters
review: Chestnut, pineau de charente and chartreuse combine with cognac to create a most unusual cocktail with zesty lemon freshness.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 by Kevin Galliano at Big Easy, Covent Garden, London, England.

name: Kawahori
preparation:
SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.

*Special ingredient #1: Yukari rice seasoning
ingredients:
1 barspoon	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
1 1⁄3 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
1⁄3 shot	Akashi-Tai Shiraume Ginjo Umeshu
2 barspoon	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: You'll find plum wine and Yukari powder (which tastes like salty, sweet, fruity black tea leaves and looks a little like black tea) at any specialist Japanese retailer (such as London's Japan Centre). We tried making this drink a few times, with homemade pomegranate syrup as well as commercially available grenadine. How generous the spoon of yukari also greatly affected the outcome. Some of the versions we made were great but the recipe is not fool proof, or the ingredients so easily available outside of Japan.
history: The Japanese Bacardí Legacy 2016 winning cocktail winning cocktail by Masato Sakurai at Ginza Yaemaru in Tokyo.

name: MiAmor
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and fine strain onto chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Bacardi Gold rum
2⁄3 shot	Rosé/rosato vermouth
1⁄12 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review:
"The inspiration for this cocktail is love. There is never a time or place for true love. It happens accidentally, in a heartbeat, in a single flashing moment. The first sip of the cocktail is pink, full of berry aromas, like the first time you saw your loved one. Berries are followed by apricots, to help you to get to know each other. Muscovado sugar smokiness and a floral touch give you wings, so you can do anything for your loved one. And then comes passion... passion that cannot be tamed - like Bacardí. Feel the love!"

We say: We found this drink benefits from being slightly generous when measuring the sugar syrup. The result is a boozy sipper of a cocktail that feels like it should be made with eight year old rum.
history: Estonian BACARDÍ LEGACY 2016 winning cocktail by Angelika Larkina, EBA Koolituskeskus, Tallinn.

name: Original Sin (Gin Joint recipe)
preparation: SWIZZLE all ingredients in a Julep cup with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄2 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	Gentian liqueur (e.g. Suze, Salers etc)
2⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
2⁄3 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Lemon and honey with a touch of bittersweet flavoursome gentian liqueur.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2015 at the Gin Joint, Athens, Greece.

name: Harvest Moon Cocktail (PDT's recipe)
garnish: Coin-shaped and sized orange zest twist
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
3 dash	Bob's Abbotts bitters
review: Stirred down and boozy – very boozy, especially when made with bonded rye and applejack (as per the original recipe) rather than the comparatively subdued calvados used here. However, the cocktail's apple notes, coupled with the subtle herbal complexity of Chartreuse, combine wonderfully in this potent rye whiskey-based after-dinner sipper.
history: Created in 2007 by Daniel Eun at PDT, New York City, USA. Daniels' original recipe, as recounted in Jim Meehan's 2001 The PDT Cocktail Book, uses Wild Turkey rye whiskey and calls for the drink to be served straight-up in a coupe rather than on-the-rocks. However, we prefer with the added dilution from serving over ice. In the book, Jim writes, "This drink looks like the sky during the harvest moon – when reddish-orange moon (the orange twist) rises after sunset."

name: Look for the Silver Lining
preparation: SHAKE first 4 ingredients with ice and strain back into shaker. Add ice-cream and FROSTED DRY SHAKE (without ice) and pour into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bacardi Carta Blanca Superior White Rum
2⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
1 shot	Vanilla ice cream
review: Tangy citrus smoothed with cream, flavoured with vanilla and laced with rum notes.
history: Created for Bacardí Legacy 2017 by Loreta Toska at Theory Bar & More in Athens, Greece. Loreta says, "In life, it is easy to get discouraged and let negativity overcome you... but if you do everything you can, work your hardest and stay positive, you have a shot at a silver lining. Look out for the Silver Lining!"

name: Mai Suit & Tai
garnish: Bowtie, cinnamon stick, maple nut mix, activated charcoal and sugar dusted mint sprig
preparation:
SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.

Special ingredient #1: Homemade almond, pecan, cinnamon and maple syrup orgeat
Special ingredient #2: Smoke & Oak Bitters
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Tennessee whiskey
1⁄3 shot	Italicus liqueur
2⁄3 shot	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
5⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed) (clarified)
3 dash	*Special ingredient #2 (see above)
history: Created in November 2017 by Nathan Larkin at The Fizzy Tarte, Bowness-On-Windermere, UK, for Jack Daniel's Tennessee Calling II.

name: Coming Of Age
preparation:
STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (chuck of block ice).

Special ingredient #1: Toasted coconut husk tincture
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Tennessee whiskey
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Red Bitter Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Coconut sugar syrup
3 dash	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
history: Created in November 2017 by Jack Bishop at Filter & Fox, Liverpool, UK, for Jack Daniel’s Tennessee Calling II.

name: Don's Coco Punch
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
1⁄3 shot	Yellow Chartreuse (or génépy liqueur)
1⁄3 shot	Coconut sugar syrup
2 shot	Pineapple puree
1⁄2 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
review: Reminiscent of a tequila Piña Colada with the merest hint of Chartreuse.

name: Walter's Waltz
garnish: Lemon zest twist (discarded) & apricot wedge/dried apricot half
preparation: SHAKE first four ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass. TOP with cider and briefly stir.
ingredients:
1 1⁄6 shot	Ginseng liqueur
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Mentzendorff Kümmel liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1 2⁄3 shot	Dry cider
review: Medium-dry, herbal, fruity, refreshing and delightfully different. Best served as an aperitivo.
history: Adapted from a drink discovered in 2017 at Marks Bar at Hix, Soho, London, England.

name: Cuban Love
garnish: Fresh or dehydrated pineapple spice & mint springs
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
2 shot	Pineapple verdita
1⁄3 shot	Pimento dram/Allspice liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄2 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
review: Green and herbal (coriander and mint) coffee and pineapple.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2019 by Boo Jing Heng, Tess Bar & Kitchen, Singapore.

name: Peach 'Martini'
garnish: Rosemary sprig & shot of champagne on the side
preparation: MUDDLE peach in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 wedge	Fresh ripe peach (skinned & diced)
1 2⁄3 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
5⁄6 shot	Passion fruit purée
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Rosemary sugar syrup (2:1)
review: A riff on the 'Porn Star Martini' with peach, passion fruit, vanilla and rosemary.

name: Back To The Origin
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
5⁄6 shot	Akashi-Tai Ginjo Yuzushu
1⁄6 shot	Claret red wine
1⁄3 shot	Elderflower liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: Yuzu infused sake dominates this coffee and cacao spiced rum-based cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Nicolas Medicamento at the American Bar at The Savoy, London, England.

name: Nutty New Year
garnish: Hazelnut chocolate chunk balanced across glass rim
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
1⁄2 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄3 shot	Hazelnut sugar syrup
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: An Alexander-style dessert cocktail to see the New Year in with.
history: Created in December 2020 to see in the New Year by Angela Pearce, a Discerning Drinker (who tells us that her husband prefers a Salty New Year - see variant).

name: Fruity Fruit Salad
preparation: MUDDLE grapes in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
7 fresh	Green grapes (seedless)
1 1⁄3 shot	Strawberry flavoured vodka
1 shot	De Kuyper Watermelon liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Poire William eau-de-vie
2 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Bright red and very fruity.
history: Created in June 2020 by yours truly in Rye, Sussex, England.

name: Straight Up In Compton
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Blended Scotch whisky
2⁄3 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
2⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Acidic cocktail mixer
2 dash	Celery bitters
review: Scotch whisky and rich apricot with sour herbal complexity.

name: High Horse
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄2 shot	Kirschwasser (cherry) eau-de-vie
1⁄2 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Although rum is the main ingredient in this cocktail it plays something of a backseat to the more assertive flavours of cherry eau-de-vie and cherry liqueur. The High Horse is best appreciated as an after-dinner drink/nightcap.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Shannon Tebay Sidle at Death & Co. in New York City, USA.

name: Viriana Bracer
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Hayman's London Dry Gin
1⁄2 shot	Bigallet China China Amer
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄12 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe
1 dash	Whiskey barrel-aged bitters
review: Delicate mint and gin-laced bittersweet herbal notes make this a pleasingly boozy aperitivo or digestivo.
history: Adapted from a recipe by Jason E. Clapham at the St. Edward's MCR at Oxford, England who describes this as "a Prince Henry enhancement."

name: Dry Pornstar Martini
garnish: Coin-sized lime zest twist expressed and floated on surface
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Ketel One Vodka
1⁄2 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Bianco Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Passoã passion fruit liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Lime cordial (sweetened lime juice)
review: A Martini-style cocktail first and a Porn Star Martini second with the essential flavours within the contemporary classic presented in a more genuinely Vodkatini form.
history: Created in June 2023 by yours truly at the Clocktower in Rye, England.

name: Long Look Back
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
3⁄4 shot	Japanese blended whisky
3⁄4 shot	Amaro Braulio
1⁄3 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
3 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: When first served, this is a challenging cocktail but time, and with it dilution, has a mellowing effect, producing a heavy but tasty digestivo or late-night sipper.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2018 by Kacie Lambert at Stay Gold (closed in 2019) in New York City, USA.

name: Séamus Plug
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Pear liqueur (Poire William)
1⁄2 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
6 drop	Difford's Daiquiri Bitters
review: Irish whiskey, dry vermouth and pear liqueur cocktail with apple juice. Drops of bitters are crucial to the balance, so if not available, replace them with the oils from a lemon zest twist.
history: Created by yours truly in November 2023. Somebody had to attribute a cocktail to the name!

name: Midnight in Paris
preparation: POUR sparkling wine into chilled glass. STIR next 4 ingredients with ice and strain into sparkling wine-charged glass.
ingredients:
4 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
1⁄4 shot	Cognac (brandy)
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Crème de Mûre liqueur
1⁄12 shot	Hazelnut liqueur
review: A luxuriant fruity and nutty riff on the classic Champagne Cocktail.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2024 by Sam Fraser at Purchases Bar & Restaurant in Chichester, England.

name: Perry Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE first three ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
1 shot	Poire William eau-de-vie
1 shot	Pear & cognac liqueur
2 shot	Pear juice (freshly pressed)
Top up with	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Pear with a hint of sparkle.
history: Created in 2002 by yours truly.

name: Purple Pear Martini
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Bison grass vodka
3⁄4 shot	Poire William eau-de-vie
3⁄4 shot	Crème de violette liqueur
1 shot	Lillet Blanc (or other aromatized wine)
review: Depending on your choice crème de violete, both in hue and flavour, this floral cocktail suits its name.
history: Created in 2002 by yours truly.

name: Sparkling Perry
preparation: SHAKE first three ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne and lightly stir.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Poire William eau-de-vie
3⁄4 shot	Pear & cognac liqueur
1 shot	Pear juice (freshly pressed)
Top up with	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: Reminiscent of perry (pear cider).
history: Created in December 2002 by yours truly (Simon Difford).

name: Kanu-No
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 1⁄4 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
1⁄4 shot	Oloroso sherry
1⁄6 shot	Pale cream sherry (medium/sweet)
1⁄6 shot	Ruby port
review: The rum's sherry notes are heightened by the addition of port and sherry.
history: Adapted from a drink created in 2007 by Mr Ueno at Star Bar, Ginza, Tokyo. Originally served straight-up.

name: Sticky Toffee Fizz
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. TOP with champagne.
ingredients:
1 shot	Chairman's Reserve Spiced Rum
1⁄2 shot	Butterscotch liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Caramel Toffee liqueur
1 2⁄3 shot	Brut champagne/sparkling wine
review: An indulgent champagne cocktail.
history: Inspired by a cocktail discovered at London's Light Bar in September 2014.

name: Nearest & Dearest
preparation: STIR all ingredients and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Tennessee whiskey
2⁄3 shot	Ramazzotti amaro
1⁄3 shot	Tobacco liqueur (not homemade!)
2 dash	Pecan bitters
history: Created in November 2017 by Charlotte Coyle of Filter + Fox, Liverpool, UK, for Jack Daniel’s Tennessee Calling II.

name: For Peggy
preparation:
MUDDLE grapes to extract 30ml juice. SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice filled glass (chunk block ice).

Special ingredient #1: Burnt bay leaf & maple syrup
ingredients:
4 fresh	Green grapes (seedless)
1 1⁄2 shot	Tennessee whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄3 shot	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
history: Created in November 2017 by Shane Kilgarriff of Peggy's Bar, Manchester, UK, for Jack Daniel’s Tennessee Calling II.

name: Cinnamon 'Martini'
garnish: Flamed cinnamon dust & shot of champagne on the side
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 2⁄3 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
5⁄6 shot	Passion fruit purée
1⁄3 shot	Cinnamon syrup
4 drop	Xocolatl mole bitters
review: Vanilla and passion fruit with a touch of cinnamon.

name: Black Hotel
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
3⁄4 shot	Tawny port
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
1⁄2 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: Creamy, chocolaty and delicately spicy with faint rich port fruit.
history: A spiced rum riff on the classic Chatham Hotel Special.

name: Back To Black
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a chunk of block ice).
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
1⁄3 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
1⁄12 shot	Brancamenta
6 whole	Roasted coffee beans
review: Bittersweet with flavours of roasted coffee, cacao and minty freshness.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Thomas Girard, Head bartender at Operation Dagger, Singapore.

name: Celery Nome
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Rutte Celery Dry Gin
2⁄3 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄2 shot	Celery saccharum (celery syrup)
1 dash	Celery bitters
review:
Originally and rather boringly named "Celery Gin Cocktail" until I realised how close it is to David Embury's Nome. My original recipe (photographed) was served in a coupe glass:
60 Celery gin
30 Fino sherry
15 Celery saccharum
history: Created in June 2020 by yours truly.

name: Saz with a Sting
preparation: RINSE chilled glass with rum and set aside. STIR other ingredients with ice and strain into pre-rinsed glass (no ice in glass).
ingredients:
1⁄6 shot	Jamaican aged blended rum with funk
5⁄6 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
5⁄6 shot	Armagnac brandy
5⁄6 shot	Giffard Menthe Pastille white crème de menthe
review: As the name suggests, this is a riff on a Stinger with spirituous Sazerac attitude.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by Deke Dunne, Bar Director at Allegory, a speakeasy bar in the Eaton Hotel, Washington, D.C., USA.

name: Rose (by Albert of the Chatham Bar)
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice & strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
3⁄4 shot	Kirschwasser (cherry) eau-de-vie
1⁄6 shot	Heering Cherry Liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Groseille (redcurrant) syrup
review: Based on dry vermouth with fruity cherry and redcurrant.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by "Albert" of the Chatham Bar featured in the 1929 book, Cocktails de Paris and also in David A. Embury's 1948 The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks.

name: Sketches of Spain
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Oloroso sherry
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	Spanish brandy
1⁄6 shot	Honey syrup (3 honey to 1 water)
review: Best appreciated as a light after-dinner cocktail, perhaps after a properly crispy bottomed paella.
history: Adapted from a recipe created by Kellie Thorn of Atlanta, USA. Kellie's original recipe used only Spanish ingredients, including Spanish vermouth.

name: New Victoria
preparation: SHAKE first 3 ingredients with ice and stain into ice-filled glass(preferably a large cube or chunk of block ice). DRIZZLE banana liqueur.
ingredients:
2 shot	Straight rye whiskey (100 proof /50% alc./vol.)
1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄4 shot	Passoã passion fruit liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
review: A fruity Old Fashioned. They shook rather than stirred it in the 1930s, so "shake it to wake it."
history: Adapted from a recipe in William James "Billy" Tarling's 1937 Café Royal Bar Book where its creation is attributed to "by J. Stephens."

name: Tokyo Bloody Mary
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Akashi-Tai Daiginjo Genshu sake
3 1⁄2 shot	Tomato juice
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄4 shot	Tawny port
7 drop	Hot pepper sauce (red)
3 dash	Worcestershire sauce
1 pinch	Celery salt
1 grind	Black pepper
review: Sake adds an interesting dimension to the traditionally vodka based Bloody Mary. For more information about the history of the Bloody Mary see our Bloody Mary cocktail page.

name: Bananarama
preparation: MUDDLE banana with cachaça and rum in base of shaker. Add other ingredients, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3 slice	Banana (preferably overripe)
1 shot	Cachaça
2⁄3 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 3-5 years
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Corn/maize liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
2 drop	Saline solution 4:1 (20g sea salt to 80g water)
review: Funky cachaça with rum and corn liqueur with the all-important banana flavours contributed by fresh overripe banana and banana liqueur.
history: Created in January 2022 by yours truly at the Clocktower, Rye England.

name: Funky Monkey
preparation: BLEND all ingredients with 6oz scoop of crushed ice and serve with straws.
ingredients:
1 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
3⁄4 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1 shot	Cream of coconut (e.g. Coco Lopez, Re'al etc.)
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
1 shot	Milk (whole milk/full 3-4% fat)
1 fresh	Banana (preferably overripe)
review: Be sure to use a ripe or even over-ripe banana in this tropical style drink.
history: Created in 1998 by Tony Abou-Ganim, Las Vegas, USA.

name: Rum Runner
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass filled with crushed ice.
ingredients:
1 shot	Jamaican aged blended rum with funk
1 shot	Light gold rum (1-3 year old molasses column)
1 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Crème de Mûre liqueur
2 shot	Pineapple juice
1 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
review: Fruity and rounded with a touch of rum funk, rich banana and blackberry.
history: The Holiday Isle Tiki Bar in Islamorada, Florida Keys, USA, claims to be the "home of the Run Runner." Originally named The Hapi Hula Hut, the bar opened in 1969 and was renamed in 1971. As the Holiday Isle's own website says, "Legend has it [so evidence is perhaps sketchy] over 40 years ago the Tiki Bar manager John Elber (Tiki John) had to get rid of an excess of rum and other liqueurs before the arrival of new inventory. Tiki John was challenged to concoct a cocktail that would help use the surplus inventory. So he mixed banana liquor, Meyers rum, brandy and grenadine and named it the Rum Runner" after the liquor smugglers who used the Florida Keys as their base in the early 1900s.

name: Celery Gimlet
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Rutte Celery Dry Gin
1 shot	Celery juice (freshly extracted)
1⁄4 shot	Green Chartreuse (or alternative herbal liqueur)
1⁄3 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄6 shot	Lime cordial (sweetened lime juice)
1⁄6 shot	White wine vinegar (Chardonnay)
2 dash	Celery bitters
review: Occupying the ground between the Gimlet and a shrub with pleasing savoury celery notes adding interest.
history: Created in 2010 by Naren Young at Saxon & Parole, New York City, USA.

name: Black Forest Gateau
preparation: STIR first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. FLOAT cream on drink. (It pays to whip cream first.)
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
2⁄3 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
1⁄4 shot	Kirschwasser (cherry) eau-de-vie
1⁄4 shot	Joseph Cartron Double Crème de Cassis de Bourgogne
1⁄2 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: Dessert by name and dessert by nature: naughty but nice.
history:
Adapted from a recipe created in 2002 at Hush Restaurant in London, England. Hush's recipe lacked three of the essentials in a Black Forest Gâteau: kirsch, cherries and chocolate. Hence, on 28th March 2022, I created the recipe above. Hush's original Black Forest Gâteau recipe:
60 ml Vodka
22.5 ml Chambord liqueur
22.5 ml Crème de fraise
7.5 ml Crème de cassis
22.5 Cream

name: Legend Reviver
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into absinthe misted glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Bacardi 8 year old rum
3⁄4 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth (Star anise infused)
1⁄6 shot	Cinnamon syrup
1⁄12 shot	Caramel sugar syrup
3 drop	Whiskey barrel-aged bitters
1⁄12 shot	La Fée Parisienne absinthe
review: This slightly rich cocktail makes for a good after-dinner drink.
history:
Created for Bacardí Legacy 2017 by Wade Cleophas while working on the Norwegian Escape Cruise Ship. (Wade's recipe calls for 7.5ml caramel/cinnamon syrup but we used 5ml cinnamon and 2.5ml caramel.)

Wade says, "This cocktail was crafted to complement and enhance all that Bacardí Gran Reserva 8 Años rum has to offer. The inspiration comes from a combination of two classic cocktails that perfectly marry carefully selected flavour enhancers. The specific mixture of ingredients reflects the heritage of travel associated with rum."

name: Sleeping Bison-Tini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bison grass vodka
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Pear & cognac liqueur
1 shot	Pear juice (freshly pressed)
1 shot	Apple juice (cloudy & unsweetened)
1 shot	Camomile tea (cold)
review: A light cocktail featuring a melange of subtle flavours.

name: El Tindero
preparation: POUR beer into chilled glass and set aside. SHAKE other ingredients with ice and fine strain into beer charged glass. Finally add ice to glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Pilsner lager
1 2⁄3 shot	Bacardi Gold rum
1 shot	Coconut water
1⁄3 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
1⁄6 shot	Apple cider vinegar
4 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
review: Strangely reminiscent of a 'lager shandy' with very subdued coconut notes. It's a very tasty lager shandy, though.
history: Philippine Bacardí Legacy 2016 winning cocktail by Ohn Richelieu Cruz, Café Enye, Quezon City.

name: 1920s Artist
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Kirschwasser (cherry) eau-de-vie
1⁄2 shot	Oloroso sherry
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Dry Vermouth
1⁄6 shot	Groseille (redcurrant) syrup
1 dash	Peychaud's or other Creole-style bitters
review: Despite its soft salmon pink hue this cocktail is boozy with Irish whiskey and sherry to the fore. Oloroso sherry and dry vermouth balance each other harmoniously with red currant syrup adding flavour and richness.
history: Created in January 2016 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England. This cocktail combines elements from the two best-known vintage cocktails using groseille (redcurrant) syrup. The whiskey element comes from the Artist's Special while the kirsch, sherry and dry vermouth come from the Nineteen-Twenty.

name: Chocolate, Rum & Raisin
garnish: Squares raisin & nut chocolate balanced across rim
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
3⁄4 shot	Giffard Caramel Toffee liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	De Kuyper Brown Crème de Cacao
1⁄12 shot	Pedro Ximénez sherry
5 drop	Bob's Chocolate bitters
review: This cocktail delivers pretty much what it says on the tin – chocolate, rum and raisin. Best enjoyed after dinner with deluxe similarly flavoured chocolate.
history: Created by yours truly in April 2017 at the Cabinet Room, London, England.

name: Admiral's Salute
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Bacardi 8 year old rum
2⁄3 shot	Americano bianco
1⁄3 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄4 shot	Giffard Grenadine syrup
1 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 dash	Peach bitters
review: Making your own grenadine, as per Darren's recipe, will affect the balance and success of this fruity complex cocktail.
history:
Created for Bacardí Legacy 2017 by Darren Miley at Ostro, Auckland, New Zealand.

Darren makes his own grenadine with: 500 ml pomegranate juice, 500 ml sugar syrup, zest of 1 lemon, 1 lime & 1 orange, 5 ml orange blossom water

Darren says, "A salute is a gesture of respect or polite recognition, especially one made to or by a person when arriving or departing. Every day, everywhere on this planet, there are people whose amazing achievements go unnoticed. This cocktail is my tribute to them all, so they, in turn, can raise a glass in salute of those in their world who deserve celebration."

name: Old Tom Gin Fruit Cup (Difford's Cup No.11)
garnish: Lemon, orange & strawberry slices, mint sprig & borage
preparation: POUR all ingredients into glass. Half fill glass with ice. Add a citrus slice and a couple of mint leaves from garnish before filling to brim with ice. Finish with rest of garnish.
ingredients:
5⁄6 shot	Hayman's Old Tom Gin
5⁄6 shot	Orange Curaçao liqueur
5⁄6 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
2 dash	Angostura Aromatic Bitters
1 2⁄3 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
1 2⁄3 shot	Cola (e.g. Coca Cola or Pepsi Cola)
review: It's is possible, indeed probable, that the original Pimm's Cup served in the eponymous London bar was in fact based on old tom gin rather than London dry gin. However, while flavoursome, old tom does inherently produce a sweeter style drink compared to when the same recipe is made with dry gin or other base spirits.
history: Created in June 2017 by yours truly at the Cabinet Room, London, England. For more recipes and history see Fruit Cups and Pimm's.

name: Black Coffee Martini
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Cacao & coffee spiced rum
1⁄6 shot	Crème brûlée syrup
1⁄6 shot	Caramel sugar syrup
1⁄3 shot	Coffee Schnapps liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1 1⁄6 shot	Espresso coffee (freshly brewed & hot)
review: Coffee, cacao and caramel served Espresso Martini-style.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2020 by Nick Tse at Bar Buonasera, Hong Kong.

name: Fresh & Shiny
preparation: SHAKE first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass (preferably over a large cube or chunk of block ice). TOP with ginger ale.
ingredients:
1 1⁄3 shot	Monkey Shoulder Fresh Monkey
1⁄6 shot	Fino sherry
1⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1⁄12 shot	Giffard Banane du Brésil liqueur
4 dash	Xocolatl mole bitters
5⁄6 shot	Thomas Henry Ginger Ale
review: "Fresh" in flavour profile, "Shiny" and new – you won't have had a cocktail quiet like this before. I like to double the measure of banana liqueur to take up to 5ml (1/6oz).
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Ysis Maricourt of Blue Bird in Paris, France.

name: Fresh to Death
preparation: STIR first 5 ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass. TOP with prosecco and add ice.
ingredients:
1 shot	Monkey Shoulder Fresh Monkey
1 shot	Peach juice
1⁄3 shot	De Kuyper Apricot Brandy liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Ginger liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Lime juice (freshly squeezed)
1 1⁄2 shot	Fiol Extra Dry Prosecco
review: A little funky, very fruity and very quaffable.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2023 by Dan Bovey of Hyde Group in Bristol, England.

name: The Socialist
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
3⁄4 shot	Rhum J.M. Terroir Volcanique
3⁄4 shot	Caribbean blended rum aged 6-10 years
3⁄4 shot	Carpano Antica Formula Vermouth
1⁄2 shot	10+ year old blended rum
1⁄8 shot	Pimento dram/Allspice liqueur
3 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: This tasty triple rum Manhattan also works well served on-the-rocks.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2014 at Paper Plane in Atlanta, Georgia, USA.

name: Creamy Bee
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Krupnik spiced honey liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Irish cream liqueur
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
1⁄2 shot	Hazelnut liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Goldwasser cinnamon schnapps liqueur
review: Creamy cinnamon with hints of honey, nuts and berries.
history: Created in 2002 at Hush, London, England and originally made with cinnamon syrup in place of Goldschläger.

name: Réveillon Cocktail
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1⁄2 shot	Pear liqueur (Poire William)
1⁄4 shot	Pimento dram/Allspice liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Punt E Mes vermouth amaro
4 drop	Bob's Abbotts bitters
review: Bittersweet and spicy with underlying warming apple spirit. Originally designed to be served straight-up in a Nick & Nora glass, we think it's better suited to being served on-the-rocks, preferably over a chunk of block ice.
history:
Adapted from a drink created in 2005 by Chuck Taggart, the Los Angeles-based New Orleanian cocktail-loving disc jockey behind GumboPages.com. Chuck reports that after trying the drink for the first time at a 2005 Christmas party, Ted "Dr Cocktail" Haigh declared, "Oh, this is delightful!" adding, "It's like sucking on Santa!"

In French and Portuguese, a réveillon is a long dinner, and often a social gathering, held on the evenings preceding Christmas Day and New Year's Day. In the same way that Americans seem to celebrate St Patrick's Day more fervently than the Irish, Réveillon is particularly celebrated in New Orleans, either due to the city's strong French heritage or it being a damn good excuse for a nosh-up and party.

Réveillon comes from the French word, réveil meaning 'waking' (or 'alarm clock' according to the very literal Google Translate). Why the name? Well, any good party should last through the early hours. Right!

name: Basil Mary
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
7 fresh	Basil leaves
2 shot	Pepper flavoured vodka
4 shot	Tomato juice
8 drop	Hot pepper sauce (red)
1⁄2 shot	Tawny port
4 dash	Worcestershire sauce
1⁄2 barspoon	Horseradish sauce
2 pinch	Celery salt
2 grind	Black pepper
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
review: A particularly spicy Mary with a herbal twist.
history: Discovered in 2004 at Indigo Yard, Edinburgh, Scotland.

name: Bloody Maria
garnish: Salt & pepper rim plus celery stick
preparation: ROLL rather than shake all ingredients in a shaker with ice and strain into ice-filled glass.
ingredients:
2 shot	Patrón Reposado tequila
4 shot	Tomato juice
1⁄2 shot	Lemon juice (freshly squeezed)
8 drop	Hot pepper sauce (red)
4 dash	Worcestershire sauce
1⁄2 barspoon	Horseradish sauce
1⁄2 shot	Tawny port
2 pinch	Celery salt
2 grind	Black pepper
review: Tequila adds interesting flavours to the classic Bloody Mary.
history: Based on the classic Bloody Mary cocktail. For more information please see our page on the Bloody Mary cocktail.

name: Upside-Down Raspberry Cheesecake
preparation:
First Layer: MUDDLE raspberries in base of shaker. Add Chambord, SHAKE with ice and fine strain into centre of glass.

Second Layer: Grate lemon zest into shaker. Add rest of ingredients, SHAKE all ingredients with ice and strain into glass over spoon so as to LAYER over raspberry base.
ingredients:
4 fresh	Raspberries
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
1⁄2 fresh	Lemon peel (grated)
2 shot	Vanilla flavoured vodka
1⁄2 shot	Giffard Vanille de Madagascar
1⁄2 shot	Sugar syrup 'rich' (2 sugar to 1 water, 65.0°Brix)
5 barspoon	Mascarpone cheese
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: Surprisingly, the biscuity top continues to float as you sip the vanilla cream layer right down to the point when you hit the raspberry base.
history: Created in 2003 by yours truly after adapting Wayne Collins' original cheesecake recipe.

name: Mirror Match
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 shot	Calvados / apple brandy / straight applejack
1 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1⁄6 shot	Giffard Parfait Amour liqueur
1⁄4 shot	Jägermeisteror other German amaro
1⁄6 shot	Demerara/Muscovado/brown sugar syrup (2 sugar:1 water)
1 dash	Jerry Thomas bitters
1 dash	Orange Bitters by Angostura
review: Boozy and floral with a hint of sweetness to smooth and harmonise, this after-dinner cocktail, originally served straight-up in a coupe (as presented here) but we prefer ours on-the-rocks.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2017 by Madeleine Rapp at The Dead Rabbit Grocery & Grog in New York, New York City, USA. Drink courtesy of gazregan.com.

name: Fruit and Nut Chocolate Cocktail
preparation: SHAKE all ingredients with ice and fine strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
2⁄3 shot	Raspberry flavoured vodka
1⁄3 shot	Dutch Cacao white crème de cacao
1⁄3 shot	Irish cream liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Hazelnut liqueur
1⁄3 shot	Giffard Framboise de Ronce (raspberry liqueur)
1 shot	Single cream/half-and-half
review: Naughty but nice - one for confectionery lovers.

name: Apple-Jacked
garnish: Orange zest twist & charred cinnamon stick
preparation:
SHAKE all ingredients and strain into ice-filled glass.

Special ingredient #1: Cucumber skin cordia Fortified burnt cinnamon infused honey (240g honey, 10 cinnamon sticks with one end burned, and 50ml Jack Daniels Old No.7, infused for 8 hours at 65°C, remove cinnamon, char one cinnamon stick completely and infuse)

Special ingredient #2: Pickling liquor Citric apple juice (Eager Apple Juice, 2% citric acid by weight)

Special ingredient #3: Ms Betters Batch 42 Aromatic Bitters

Special ingredient #4: Ms Betters Black Pepper & Cardamom Bitters
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	Tennessee whiskey
5⁄6 shot	*Special ingredient #1 (see above)
1 2⁄3 shot	*Special ingredient #2 (see above)
1⁄6 shot	Lemon oleo saccharum
4 drop	*Special ingredient #3 (see above)
4 drop	*Special ingredient #4 (see above)
history: Created in November 2017 by Josh Allen of Tipple Cocktail Bar, Lancaster, UK, for Jack Daniel’s Tennessee Calling II.

name: Towser the Mouser
preparation: STIR all ingredients with ice and strain into chilled glass.
ingredients:
1 1⁄2 shot	The Busker Blended Irish Whiskey
1⁄2 shot	Speyburn 10yo Speyside single malt
1⁄2 shot	Amontillado sherry
1⁄2 shot	Strucchi Rosso Vermouth
1⁄4 shot	Drambuie liqueur
1⁄6 shot	Walnut (Nocino) liqueur
review: An after-dinner/late-night sipper which benefits from a split whisk(e)y base and similarly split fortified wines and liqueurs. Some will prefer served in an old-fashioned glass over a large ice cube.
history: Adapted from a recipe created in 2021 by AlexLynn "Ally" Marone, when head bartender at Grand Army in Brooklyn, New York City, USA.
